projectDetails.name: Build a space biology knowledge engine
projectDetails.summary: A space biology knowledge engine is an integrated digital platform that compiles, organizes, and analyzes biological data from spaceflight experiments to deepen our understanding of how living organisms adapt to space environments. By combining data from diverse sources—such as genomic, proteomic, physiological, and imaging studies—it creates a comprehensive framework for studying the effects of microgravity, radiation, and other space conditions on life. Using advanced data modeling, machine learning, and systems biology approaches, the engine identifies key biological patterns and mechanisms that influence health, growth, and adaptation in space. This knowledge can guide the design of future space missions, improve astronaut health countermeasures, and advance biotechnological innovations for both space and Earth applications.
projectDetails.details:
A space biology knowledge engine is a comprehensive data-driven platform designed to accelerate research on how living systems respond to space environments. It functions as a centralized hub that integrates biological data from spaceflight missions, ground-based analogs, and laboratory experiments. The engine collects and harmonizes diverse datasets—such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, physiology, and imaging—using standardized metadata and ontologies to ensure interoperability. Machine learning algorithms and systems biology tools are then applied to identify patterns, predict biological responses, and uncover molecular mechanisms influenced by microgravity, radiation, and other spaceflight stressors.

The benefits of such an engine include improved accessibility to space biology data, enhanced reproducibility of analyses, and the ability to generate predictive models that inform astronaut health, bioregenerative life support systems, and biotechnology development. Researchers can use the platform to simulate biological processes under space conditions, design optimized experiments, and even identify countermeasures for space-induced health risks.

The intended impact of the project is to transform space biology from a fragmented field into a cohesive, data-integrated discipline—enabling faster discoveries that support long-duration human space exploration and expand biological knowledge for terrestrial applications such as medicine and agriculture.

In terms of development, the project would typically leverage tools like Python and R for data analysis and machine learning, SQL and Neo4j for database management, and Docker or Kubernetes for scalable deployment. APIs (e.g., NASA’s GeneLab API) allow automated data ingestion, while React or Flask can power the web-based user interface. Cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, or NASA’s Open Science Cloud) supports large-scale computation and data storage.

The creativity of the project lies in its interdisciplinary integration—combining space science, bioinformatics, AI, and systems biology into one intelligent platform. It doesn’t just store data; it learns from it, enabling hypothesis generation and predictive modeling that were previously impossible with isolated datasets.

Key factors considered by the team include data standardization, ethical data sharing, scalability, user accessibility, and alignment with existing initiatives such as NASA’s Open Science and FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles. The team also ensured modularity for future expansion, so the engine can evolve as new missions and data types become available.

projectDetails.name: Tesla coil for satellite charging
projectDetails.summary:
Wireless Satellite Charging via Tesla Coil
​A massive, ground-based Tesla coil acts as a powerful, high-frequency transmitter. It generates an extremely high-voltage, oscillating electromagnetic field by creating an electrical resonance between its primary and secondary coils.
projectDetails.details: The Tesla coil is a type of resonant transformer circuit invented by Nikola Tesla. Its main purpose is to generate very high-voltage, low-current, high-frequency alternating current (AC) electricity.primary and secondary coil system to transform relatively low input voltage into extremely high-frequency, high-voltage electricity.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Power Supply: A low-voltage AC source is stepped up by a transformer to a higher voltage.

Primary Circuit: This voltage charges a capacitor, which then discharges through a spark gap into a primary coil (inductor).

Resonance: The primary coil and capacitor form a tuned circuit that oscillates at a high frequency.

Secondary Circuit: The oscillations in the primary coil induce an even higher voltage in the secondary coil (due to resonance and transformer action).

Output: The secondary coil produces very high voltages, creating visible sparks, electrical arcs, or corona discharge into the air.

projectDetails.summary: Space Trash Hack introduces an innovative, autonomous system designed to collect, sort, and recycle waste and debris on Mars, transforming them into reusable resources for future missions. Using an AI "brain" to manage everything, it transforms this waste into vital supplies like fuel, 3D printer filament for making new tools, fertilizer for farms, and construction materials. This creative solution is revolutionary because it creates a circular economy, drastically reducing the need for incredibly expensive shipments from Earth. The intended impact is to enable true self-sufficiency, making permanent human settlement on Mars sustainable, safe, and affordable by ensuring that on the Red Planet, nothing is ever truly considered "waste."

projectDetails.name: Exohunter
projectDetails.summary:
ExoHunt is a machine learning–based project built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to automate the identification of exoplanets using the Kepler dataset. The system leverages a Random Forest Classifier trained on key astrophysical features such as orbital period, planet radius, stellar temperature, and equilibrium temperature to classify celestial objects as Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive. After cleaning and balancing the dataset using SMOTE, ExoHunt achieved an accuracy of ~77%.

The project includes visualizations such as feature importance, confusion matrix, and probability heatmaps to provide transparent insights into model performance. Additionally, an interactive prediction dashboard allows users to input new planetary parameters via sliders to get instant classification results with confidence scores.

Exohunter demonstrates how AI can assist astronomers by rapidly analyzing large-scale exoplanet data, improving discovery efficiency, and supporting the ongoing search for habitable worlds beyond our solar system.
projectDetails.details:
• Our project uses artificial intelligence to find planets beyond our solar system, called exoplanets, by analyzing data from NASA’s Kepler mission. Instead of manually scanning thousands of stars, our model learns patterns from known exoplanets and predicts whether a celestial object is a confirmed planet, a candidate, or a false positive. It cleans and prepares the data, balances the rare exoplanet cases using SMOTE, and trains a Random Forest model. We also made it interactive so anyone can tweak a planet’s properties like its size, orbit, or temperature and see in real time what the AI predicts.
  • Finding new exoplanets is usually slow and painstaking. Our AI speeds up the process, helping astronomers focus on the most promising candidates. It also shows why it makes each prediction, highlighting the most important factors like a planet’s radius, temperature, or orbital period.
  • We built this using Python with libraries like pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, and imblearn. Visualizations were created with matplotlib and seaborn, and the interactive interface uses ipywidgets. All data comes from NASA’s public Kepler exoplanet catalog.
  • This project combines AI with interactivity. It handles the tricky problem of rare exoplanet detection using smart oversampling and makes complex space science accessible and engaging for both researchers and the public.
  • By automating exoplanet discovery, we can explore new worlds faster and more efficiently. Combining AI with astronomy, we hope to inspire more discoveries and make exoplanet science approachable, interactive, and fun.

ExoAI Explorer - Project Summary

What We Developed:
• AI-powered web app that analyzes light curves from NASA's Kepler and TESS missions
• Three deep learning models (Basic CNN, Advanced Multi-Branch, Metadata-Enhanced)
• Explainable AI feature showing which data influenced predictions

How It Addresses the Challenge:

• Processes real NASA data via direct archive integration
• Makes predictions transparent through visual maps
• Supports both professional astronomers and citizen scientists

Why It's Important:
• Accelerates exoplanet discovery by automating tedious manual analysis
• Makes space research accessible to everyone, not just experts
• Builds trust in AI predictions through explainability features
• Helps find potentially habitable worlds faster
projectDetails.details:
Based on my analysis of the codebase, here's a comprehensive overview of the ExoAI Explorer project:

What the Project Does

ExoAI Explorer is an interactive web application that uses artificial intelligence to detect exoplanets from light curve data collected by NASA's Kepler and TESS space missions. The application analyzes stellar brightness patterns over time, looking for the characteristic tiny dips (0.5-2% brightness decrease) that occur when a planet transits in front of its host star.

How It Works

  1. Data Acquisition: Users can upload their own light curve files (CSV/FITS), enter a target star ID to fetch data directly from NASA's archives, use sample data, or process multiple targets in batch mode.
  2. AI Analysis: The application uses deep learning models (1D Convolutional Neural Networks) to analyze the preprocessed light curve data and predict whether an exoplanet is present.
  3. Explainable AI: A unique feature—the system generates saliency maps that visually highlight which specific regions of the light curve influenced the AI's decision, making the "black box" transparent.
  4. Results & Visualization: The app displays the probability of exoplanet presence, classification results, and interactive visualizations of the light curve with transit events highlighted.

Benefits & Intended Impact

For Professional Astronomers:

  • Rapid triage of promising exoplanet candidates from massive survey datasets
  • Multi-mission support (Kepler and TESS)
  • Batch processing for analyzing entire target lists efficiently
  • Explainability features to verify model decisions align with physics

For Citizen Scientists & Students:

  • Accessible interface requiring no programming knowledge
  • Educational tool that teaches transit detection principles through visualization
  • Hands-on experience analyzing real NASA mission data
  • Interactive exploration of different targets and models

Broader Impact:

  • Democratizes exoplanet discovery by making advanced AI tools accessible to a wider audience
  • Accelerates the search for worlds beyond our solar system
  • Thousands of exoplanets remain undiscovered in existing data—this tool helps find them
  • Advances human-AI collaboration in cosmic exploration

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

Programming Languages:

  • Python (primary language for all components)

Frameworks & Libraries:

  • TensorFlow/Keras: Deep learning model development and training
  • Streamlit: Interactive web application framework
  • NumPy: Numerical computations and array operations
  • Pandas: Time-series data manipulation
  • Matplotlib: Data visualization and plotting
  • Scikit-learn: Model evaluation and metrics
  • Lightkurve: NASA Kepler/TESS data access and processing
  • Astroquery: Stellar catalog data queries from MAST

Data Sources:

  • NASA MAST (Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes) Archive
  • Kepler and TESS mission light curve data (FITS format)

Development Environment:

  • Replit (cloud-based development and hosting platform)

Creative & Innovative Aspects

  1. Explainable AI Innovation: Unlike most "black box" AI systems, ExoAI Explorer shows scientists exactly which parts of the light curve influenced the model's decision using gradient-based saliency maps. This builds trust in automated discovery.
    • Basic CNN: Straightforward sequential architecture
    • Advanced Multi-Branch CNN: Separate pathways for detecting global and local transit patterns
    • Metadata-Enhanced CNN: Dual-input model incorporating stellar properties (temperature, radius, mass) for context-aware predictions
  2. Accessibility: Transformed a complex scientific workflow requiring programming expertise into an intuitive point-and-click interface.
  3. Real-Time NASA Data Integration: Direct API access to mission archives enables analysis of actual astronomical observations, not simulated data.
  4. Batch Processing with Parallel Computing: Uses ThreadPoolExecutor to process multiple targets concurrently, suitable for survey-scale analysis.

Team Considerations & Design Decisions

User-Centric Design:

  • Recognized that both professional astronomers and citizen scientists need different levels of detail and control
  • Provided three model complexity levels to balance ease-of-use with advanced capabilities
  • Designed clear visualizations that communicate both to experts and novices

Scientific Rigor:

  • Implemented proper data preprocessing (rolling median detrending, NaN removal, flux normalization) to match scientific standards
  • Used established metrics for transit detection
  • Made explainability a core feature to ensure scientific validation

Scalability & Performance:

  • Modular code architecture separating concerns (data processing, models, explainability, batch processing)
  • Concurrent processing for batch operations
  • Support for multiple data formats and missions

Educational Value:

  • Built-in visualizations teach the principles of transit photometry
  • Sample data allows immediate experimentation without setup
  • Clear labeling and help text throughout the interface

This project represents a bridge between cutting-edge AI technology and practical astronomical research, making the search for distant worlds more efficient, accessible, and trustworthy.

projectDetails.summary:
We developed an automated machine learning pipeline to identify exoplanets from NASA Kepler space telescope data. The system addresses the critical challenge of distinguishing genuine exoplanets from false positives in messy, real-world astronomical datasets. Our solution automatically cleans raw data, handles missing values, and uses intelligent feature selection to identify the most important planetary parameters. A robust Random Forest model then classifies celestial objects as either confirmed exoplanets or false positives with high accuracy.

This work is important because it streamlines the exoplanet discovery process, reducing manual analysis time and providing astronomers with a reliable, automated tool for planetary detection. As astronomical datasets grow exponentially with new missions, such automated systems become essential for efficiently processing vast amounts of telescope data and accelerating the search for habitable worlds beyond our solar system, ultimately contributing to our understanding of planetary formation and the potential for life elsewhere in the universe.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an automated machine learning pipeline that processes NASA Kepler space telescope data to identify exoplanets. The system:

Automated Data Processing: Cleans raw astronomical datasets by handling missing values, removing ambiguous observations, and standardizing features

Intelligent Feature Selection: Uses Random Forest algorithms to automatically identify the most important planetary parameters for detection

Predictive Modeling: Trains ensemble models to classify celestial objects as CONFIRMED exoplanets or FALSE POSITIVES

Accuracy Optimization: Implements sophisticated regularization techniques to prevent overfitting and ensure realistic performance (~96% accuracy)

Workflow: Raw telescope data → Data cleaning → Feature importance analysis → Model training → Prediction & validation

Time Efficiency: Reduces manual analysis from weeks to minutes

Accuracy: Achieves 96% classification accuracy with proven generalization

Accessibility: Makes exoplanet discovery accessible to smaller research institutions

Consistency: Eliminates human bias in planetary classification

Scalability: Can process thousands of observations simultaneously

Accelerate exoplanet discovery for astronomical research

Enable systematic analysis of Kepler and future telescope data (TESS, James Webb)

Support search for habitable planets and potential extraterrestrial life

Democratize space research for universities and institutions with limited resources

STEM education tool for astronomy and data science students

Open-source framework for machine learning in astrophysics

Research reproducibility through transparent methodology

projectDetails.name: Smart Urban Heat Island Monitoring Using IoT and Satellite Data
projectDetails.summary: Our project focuses on Urban Heat Island (UHI) Monitoring, an environmental challenge where metropolitan areas experience higher temperatures than their surrounding rural landscapes due to factors such as reduced vegetation, heat-absorbing surfaces, and anthropogenic emissions. To address this issue, we developed a dual monitoring framework combining IoT sensor networks and satellite data analysis. At the local scale, Arduino and ESP32 microcontrollers with DHT22 sensors provide real-time, site-specific temperature and humidity readings. These insights help identify urban hotspots and assess microclimates. At the broader scale, satellite imagery enables visualization of land surface temperatures and vegetation cover, offering regional patterns of UHI. By integrating ground-level data with satellite observations, our system supports evidence-based urban planning and mitigation strategies, such as increasing green infrastructure and deploying reflective materials. This project is important because it not only highlights the health, energy, and environmental consequences of UHI but also provides scalable, data-driven solutions to reduce risks and enhance urban resilience in a warming climate
projectDetails.details:
Our project focuses on monitoring Urban Heat Islands (UHIs) using a combination of IoT-based local sensing and satellite Earth observation.

How it Works:
We deployed Arduino UNO and ESP32 microcontrollers with DHT22 sensors to capture real-time temperature and humidity data across different urban zones. The Arduino setup provides localized monitoring with immediate OLED display output, while the ESP32 integrates Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to transmit data to the cloud for broader analysis. In parallel, we utilized satellite imagery to study land surface temperatures and vegetation cover, enabling large-scale UHI pattern detection. Integrating both data sources allows a comprehensive view of micro and macro urban climates.

Benefits & Impact:

  • Enables identification of heat hotspots and vulnerable communities.
  • Provides actionable insights for urban planners to design mitigation strategies (e.g., green infrastructure, reflective roofs).
  • Supports climate resilience, public health, and energy efficiency in cities.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Hardware: Arduino UNO, ESP32, DHT22 sensors, OLED display.
  • Software: Arduino IDE, cloud platforms (IoT dashboards), GIS tools, and satellite data visualization (e.g., StoryMaps).
  • Languages: C/C++ (Arduino), Python (for data processing/visualization).

Creativity & Considerations:
We combined low-cost, accessible hardware with advanced data sources to bridge local and global monitoring scales. Our team considered affordability, scalability, and ethical aspects such as data privacy and equitable access. This creative integration ensures the project is practical for small communities while scalable for smart cities

projectDetails.name: Project Farm Buddies
projectDetails.summary: Farm Forward is an AI-powered educational game that teaches sustainable farming using NASA’s Earth observation data. Players act as farmers and make real-time decisions on water management, crop selection, and pest control through interactive missions. The game uses artificial intelligence to analyze datasets like soil moisture (SMAP), rainfall (GPM), and vegetation health (NDVI), providing smart recommendations and feedback. By comparing outcomes made with and without AI assistance, players learn how technology-driven insights improve yield and resource efficiency. Built with React.js, Farm Forward transforms scientific data into an engaging learning experience that promotes climate-smart agriculture and data-driven decision-making for a sustainable future.
projectDetails.details:
Farm Forward is an innovative educational game designed to teach players about sustainable farming practices through NASA’s Earth observation data. The project combines interactive gameplay, scientific learning, and data visualization to help players understand how technology can revolutionize modern agriculture.

The game simulates real-world agricultural challenges, including water management, crop selection, and pest detection, across three mission levels. Each mission encourages players to analyze environmental data—such as soil moisture (SMAP), rainfall (GPM), and vegetation health (NDVI)—and make decisions that impact crop yield and resource usage. This approach transforms complex agricultural science into an engaging and accessible experience for learners of all ages.

Developed using React.js, the project employs an intuitive interface, mock NASA datasets, and dynamic data-driven interactions. Players progress through missions, earn points and achievements, and compare the results of farming decisions made with and without NASA data insights. This gamified method promotes awareness of climate-smart agriculture, demonstrating how data-based strategies can enhance efficiency and sustainability in farming.

Beyond entertainment, Farm Forward serves as an educational tool to empower students, farmers, and the general public with scientific knowledge and technological insight. It shows how real satellite data can influence better agricultural decisions, leading to improved yield, water conservation, and pest control. Future expansions could include real NASA API integration, multiplayer collaboration, and mobile-friendly interfaces, making it a scalable solution for agricultural education worldwide.

projectDetails.name: FUTURE TECHIES
projectDetails.summary:
We developed an interactive web application using Streamlit that helps users estimate the likelihood of adverse weather conditions—such as heat, rain, wind, cold, or discomfort—for any chosen location and date based on NASA POWER climate data (1985–2023).
By selecting a place on an interactive map or typing a location name, users can instantly view probabilities and trends of extreme weather events, including average temperature, rainfall, windspeed, and humidity. The app also provides visual analytics like heatmaps, line charts, and comfort indices, allowing users to understand historical weather patterns.
This solution addresses the challenge by transforming NASA’s long-term Earth observation data into personalized, actionable insights for planners, travelers, and outdoor enthusiasts. It empowers users to make informed decisions for future events, reducing weather-related risks and improving preparedness—all through an intuitive, data-driven interface.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – “Will It Rain On My Parade?”

Our project is an AI-assisted weather probability web application that uses NASA Earth observation data to estimate the likelihood of adverse weather for any location and date. The app analyzes historical NASA POWER data (1985–2023) — including temperature, precipitation, windspeed, humidity, and solar radiation — to calculate probabilities of “very hot,” “very cold,” “very wet,” “very windy,” and “very uncomfortable” conditions.

Users can type a place name or select it on an interactive map, choose a date via a calendar, and instantly receive probability results, visual trends, and comfort indices. The interface also provides heatmaps, charts, and downloadable reports (CSV/Excel) for deeper insights.

We built the project using Python, Streamlit, Folium (maps), Plotly (graphs), and NASA POWER API for data retrieval. The app requires no external hardware and runs fully in a browser.

Our goal is to empower event planners, travelers, and outdoor enthusiasts to make data-driven decisions months in advance. By creatively combining space-based climate data with an intuitive, interactive UI, the project transforms complex Earth observation data into practical, personalized weather intelligence—helping people prepare better for the future.

projectDetails.name: GOODALOCHANA
projectDetails.summary:
Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge “From EarthData to Action: Cloud Computing with Earth Observation Data” by focusing on air pollution prediction using cloud computing, machine learning, and open weather data. Its main goal is to help communities anticipate poor air quality and take precautionary steps to protect their health.

We developed a web-based platform that predicts air pollution levels for the next 24 hours in any selected location. The system analyzes three months of historical weather and air quality data using machine learning models to identify trends and forecast upcoming pollution levels. To collect and process real-time environmental factors like temperature, humidity, and particulate concentrations, the project integrates the MeteorMatics API and WAPI (Weather API).

When predicted pollution levels exceed safe limits, the platform sends users an alert notification, advising them to take preventive actions before going outdoors. Alongside its core functionality, it features a solar system quiz to make learning about environmental and space science engaging for all users.

By combining machine learning, real-time APIs, and user-friendly design, this project turns complex data into simple, actionable insights, empowering individuals to make informed health and environmental decisions.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a web-based pollution prediction platform that uses machine learning and real-time weather APIs to forecast air quality for the next 24 hours. The system collects environmental data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and pollutant concentrations from the MeteorMatics API and WAPI (Weather API). Using the past three months of data, our model identifies patterns in pollution levels and predicts the air quality of a user-selected location. If the forecast indicates unsafe pollution conditions, the website instantly displays an alert notification, encouraging users to take precautionary measures before going outdoors. The site also includes a solar system quiz, combining awareness with engagement to make learning about environmental and space science enjoyable.

This project benefits users by providing early warnings about poor air quality, helping them protect their health and plan their day safely. It transforms complex environmental data into simple, actionable insights, making pollution awareness accessible to everyone. Built using VS Code, Flask, Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, the system emphasizes prediction accuracy, real-time performance, and user-friendliness. Overall, it has a positive impact by promoting health-conscious behavior, inspiring environmental responsibility, and supporting the broader goal of creating cleaner and safer communities.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch Pro - Advanced Global Phenology Platform
projectDetails.summary: BloomWatch Pro is an innovative platform that integrates NASA satellite data with citizen science observations to monitor and predict global flowering patterns. By combining MODIS, VIIRS, and Landsat satellite imagery with data from USA-NPN, GLOBE Observer, GBIF, and iNaturalist, we've created a comprehensive phenology monitoring system. Using Google Gemini AI for analysis, our platform provides real-time visualization, historical analysis, and future projections of flowering events. This addresses the critical need to understand and respond to climate change impacts on plant phenology, which affects ecosystems, agriculture, and biodiversity worldwide. Our tool enables researchers, conservationists, and policymakers to make data-driven decisions for environmental protection and agricultural planning.
projectDetails.details:
BloomWatch Pro is a comprehensive phenology monitoring platform that tracks flowering patterns globally through NASA satellite data and citizen science observations. It works by integrating real-time data from multiple sources, processing it through AI-powered analysis, and presenting it through interactive visualizations including 3D globe, heatmaps, and time-series charts.

The platform offers significant benefits including early warning systems for ecological changes, prediction of phenological mismatches, and insights for agricultural planning and conservation efforts. Its intended impact is to provide researchers, policymakers, and conservationists with tools to understand and respond to climate change effects on plant phenology.

We developed BloomWatch Pro using NASA's MODIS, VIIRS, and Landsat satellite data, integrated with citizen science platforms. The technical stack includes Google Gemini API for AI analysis (92% accuracy), with data processing through ETL pipelines and quality control systems. The visualization layer features interactive 3D mapping capabilities.

Our project is creative in its multidisciplinary approach, combining space-based Earth observation with ground-level citizen science and advanced AI to create a comprehensive monitoring system. We considered factors such as data accessibility, scientific accuracy, user experience, and the need for both real-time monitoring and historical trend analysis.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We utilized Google Gemini API for image analysis and predictive modeling with 92% accuracy. The AI system processes satellite imagery and citizen science photographs to identify species and flowering stages, then generates predictions about future phenological patterns based on historical data and climate models. The AI component also powers our cellular extinction risk predictions, analyzing thermal stress vulnerability, hydraulic failure risk, photosynthetic disruption, and metabolic pathway collapse across thousands of plant species. All AI-generated content and analysis are clearly labeled within our platform interface.

It addresses the challenge of understanding and managing changes in vegetation by harnessing the rich spectral, spatial, and temporal coverage of NASA satellites (like Landsat, EMIT, and PACE).
projectDetails.details:
BloomWatch is an Earth observation application designed to monitor and visualize plant blooming events (phenology) globally. It processes NASA Earth observation data (e.g., from Landsat, EMIT, PACE) to detect bloom timing, duration, and extent. This is often achieved using time-series analysis of vegetation indices (like the Enhanced Bloom Index or NDVI) from satellite imagery to detect color/spectral changes associated with flowering.

The primary goal is to provide a critical bio-indicator of climate and environmental change. The benefits and intended impact include: Ecological insight (understanding plant-pollinator synchronization), Supporting conservation (tracking invasive species and assessing ecosystem health), and Aiding agriculture (predicting crop yields and optimizing resource management).

Tools/Languages/Software As a NASA Space Apps Challenge project, the specific tools vary by team, but development typically involves: Coding Languages like Python (for data analysis, machine learning), JavaScript/HTML/CSS (for web visualization), and languages for mobile app development. Tools/Software include cloud platforms, geospatial libraries (like ArcGIS or Google Earth Engine), and various data visualization frameworks.

Creativity Creativity in BloomWatch projects often lies in developing innovative visualization methods (e.g., interactive maps, VR experiences, time-series animations) or creating predictive models that infer species or ecological implications from the bloom data, offering an original way to make complex satellite data accessible.

Factors Considered Key factors considered by development teams include: Data Resolution (spatial and temporal, to ensure accurate bloom detection), Scalability (the ability to work globally while being useful locally), User Experience (making the visual tool intuitive for specific end-users like farmers or scientists), and Environmental Relevance (addressing a specific monitoring, prediction, or management need)

projectDetails.name: Project INFINITE SHUTTLE
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, INFINITE SHUTTLE, introduces a modular, long-lasting, and upgradable space habitat designed to support 20 crew members for extended missions in orbit or deep space. The habitat is constructed from multiple modules launched separately from Earth and assembled in space like LEGO blocks, allowing flexible expansion, maintenance, and repair.

The design addresses key challenges in modern space habitation—limited lifespan, high repair difficulty, and lack of scalability—by enabling easy upgrades, reconfiguration, and self-sustaining systems. It integrates essential functional zones, including waste management, hygiene, environmental control and life support, food storage, recreation, maintenance, and sleeping areas, all optimized for comfort and efficiency.

INFINITE SHUTTLE is important because it represents a new generation of sustainable space habitats, reducing long-term mission costs while improving crew safety and adaptability. It paves the way for future lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions, promoting a permanent and evolving human presence in space.
projectDetails.details:
INFINITE SHUTTLE is a modular, long-duration space habitat designed to support 20 crew members for orbital or deep-space missions. It works on a Lego-like assembly system, where multiple modules are launched separately from Earth and assembled in orbit using autonomous robotic arms or drones. Each module serves a specific function—such as waste management, hygiene, environmental control and life support, recreation, food storage, maintenance, sleeping, and exercise areas—and can be replaced, upgraded, or expanded easily over time.

The main benefits include long-term usability, easy repair and modification, reduced launch cost, and the ability to adapt to different missions and crew sizes. Its modular design allows quick adaptation for lunar or Martian missions, ensuring sustainability and crew comfort.

The project was developed using AI-assisted design tools (such as ChatGPT, Leonardo.ai, and Canva) for 3D concept modeling, visualization, and presentation design. No physical hardware or complex coding was required at this stage — the focus is on the concept, structure, and functionality.

Our team focused on durability, human well-being, expandability, and resource efficiency. The creativity lies in combining engineering practicality with modular flexibility, envisioning a habitat that can grow and evolve endlessly — truly infinite.

projectDetails.name: Project Raincheck
projectDetails.summary: Project Raincheck is a user-friendly web application that helps individuals make better long-term plans for outdoor events by providing historical weather probabilities. Unlike traditional forecasts, our solution uses decades of real NASA Earth data to answer the question, "What is the chance of rain on my specific date and location?" The app's elegant design makes complex scientific data accessible and actionable, empowering users to make informed decisions for everything from weddings to school trips. Our project's importance lies in its ability to transform NASA's open data into a practical, real-world planning tool for everyday life.
projectDetails.details:
• What does it do or how does it work? The app uses a client-side approach, running entirely within the user's web browser. It leverages the browser's Geolocation API to get the user's latitude and longitude. It then uses this information, along with a user-selected date, to directly query the NASA POWER API. The JavaScript code processes the raw historical precipitation data to calculate the historical probability of rain for that specific day and month. This probability is then presented to the user with a simple percentage and a corresponding visual icon.

projectDetails.name: Toxic Haze of Delhi
projectDetails.summary:
Our project explores the increasing problem of air pollution in Delhi and how satellite technology can be used to study and understand it. Using real data from NASA’s TERRA satellite, we analyzed the levels of pollutants and changes in atmospheric conditions over time. The TERRA satellite carries instruments such as MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), which helps detect aerosols, dust, and smoke particles in the atmosphere.

The main goal of our project was to identify the causes, effects, and patterns of air pollution in Delhi. We observed that the pollution levels rise significantly during the months of October and November, which coincides with crop residue burning (stubble burning) in the neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana. Our analysis showed that the wind direction during this period carries the smoke and particulate matter from these regions toward Delhi, worsening the city’s air quality.

Overall, this project demonstrates how satellite data and scientific analysis can be used effectively to raise environmental awareness and develop sustainable solutions. It reflects the importance of technology in understanding real-world problems and inspiring action to protect our planet.
projectDetails.details:
TOXIC HAZE OF DELHI

We are celebrating TERRA's 25th anniversary and to make it's data useful we created a video showing the air pollution in the capital city of our home country which is Delhi .As we know TERRA have five main instruments, MODIS,CERES,MOPITT,MISR AND ASTER. From these we used MOPITT,MODIS and MISR for detecting the causes of the pollution. With the help of MOPITT we traced the Carbon monoxide levels in the atmosphere of Delhi which was emitted by the Factories ,vehicles and Waste burning during festivals,etc. Using MISR we tracked down the amount of Aerosol in the atmosphere which was one of the main cause for pollution and health issues in Delhi which includes respiratory diseases too. On top of all of these with the information from the FIRMS of NASA and MODIS instrument in the TERRA we found out the big cause for the high pollution. During the post harvesting season on the months of October and November the farmers from the neighboring states burns crop stubbles and the smoke and pollutants from the fire carried by the winds, contributing significantly to its toxic haze. With the data from NASA we showed how the pollution affects Delhi and it's environment. To showcase this we used the GIOVANNI,NASA WORLDVIEW and DAVINCI RESOLVE For video editing.

Project Name: Space Trash Hack: Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars

1.What does it do / how does it work?

Space Trash Hack is an innovative waste management and recycling system designed specifically for Mars colonies. It collects, categorizes, and processes space debris and human-generated waste (plastics, metals, organic matter) into reusable resources. Using a combination of smart sensors, AI-powered sorting, and autonomous robotic arms, the system separates waste efficiently and repurposes it into building materials, energy, or raw inputs for 3D printing.

2.What benefits does it have?

1.Reduces waste accumulation in Mars habitats, keeping the environment clean and sustainable.

2.Converts trash into valuable resources, reducing the need for costly resupply missions from Earth.

3.Supports a circular economy in space exploration by ensuring every resource is reused.

4.Enhances crew safety and comfort by minimizing storage and contamination issues.

3.What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to make Mars settlements more sustainable and self-reliant. By transforming waste into useful materials, Space Trash Hack reduces dependency on Earth and fosters long-term human presence on Mars. Its success could also influence future space missions and even inspire advanced recycling practices back on Earth.

4.What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Chat GPT and our own creativeness.

5.How is your project creative?

1.Adapts Earth-based recycling methods to a completely new environment (Mars).

2.Integrates robotics, AI, and sustainable design into a single system.

3.Introduces the idea of converting waste directly into 3D-printable materials for tools and habitat expansion.

4.Combines futuristic problem-solving with practical engineering to address real challenges of interplanetary living.

6.What factors did your team consider?

1.Harsh environmental conditions on Mars (low gravity, thin atmosphere, temperature extremes).

2.Limited resources and energy—everything must be highly efficient and multi-purpose.

3.Safety and health of astronauts—avoiding contamination from biological waste.

4.Scalability—system should grow as the Mars colony expands.

5.Cost-effectiveness—minimizing reliance on Earth for replacement parts and resupply.

projectDetails.name: Planning from Above: Earth Data for Urban Wellbeing
projectDetails.summary:
"Planning from Above: Earth Data for Urban Wellbeing" explores how urban planners can harness NASA Earth observation data to design smarter, more resilient, and equitable cities in the face of climate change. This project develops a framework for integrating satellite-derived data—such as land surface temperature, air quality, vegetation health, and flood risk—into urban planning strategies.

By using NASA tools like MODIS, ECOSTRESS, OMI, and GRACE, planners can identify vulnerable neighborhoods, track environmental trends, and guide sustainable infrastructure development. For example, satellite heat maps can inform tree planting in heat-prone areas, while air quality data helps target pollution mitigation where it's needed most.

This approach addresses the challenge of balancing urban growth with human and environmental wellbeing. It empowers planners with real-time, high-resolution insights to make data-driven decisions that improve public health, enhance climate resilience, and reduce environmental inequality.

In a rapidly urbanizing and warming world, this project highlights the critical role of Earth science in shaping cities that are not just smarter—but also safer, greener, and more inclusive
projectDetails.details:

It provides planners with real-time, high-resolution insights to target interventions such as urban greening, pollution control, and flood mitigation—improving public health and reducing environmental inequality.

It translates complex satellite data into practical, visual tools for planners—bridging the gap between science and city design in a novel, user-friendly way.

We focused on equity, scalability, data accessibility, and climate relevance to ensure our solution is both impactful and adaptable.

projectDetails.details:
The Genesis Chamber Project: Martian Life Support System 🚀
This project focuses on the Genesis Chamber, a self-contained vertical farm essential for establishing sustainable life on Mars. Its primary goal is to shift colonization from mere survival to thrivability.
Function and Mechanics
The Chamber is an integrated life support and food production unit:
* Energy Generation: High-efficiency solar panels amplify the weak Martian sunlight to power specialized lamps, ensuring a perfect, endless growing day for crops.
* Growing Technique: It uses hydroponics (growing without soil) in vertical racks. A closed-loop system conserves water by precisely injecting nutrient-rich water directly into the plant roots.
* Life Support: The thriving crops act as the colony's lungs, forming a bioregenerative system by absorbing \text{CO}_2 and releasing pure \text{O}_2, continuously replenishing the breathable air.
* Protection: A durable, retractable roof instantly seals the structure against destructive Martian sandstorms.
Impact and Development
The system's success provides a sustained food supply and atmosphere regulation, eliminating reliance on Earth.
* Independent Impact: The Genesis Chamber is the biological and culinary foundation of the colony, proving human expansion into space is possible and self-sufficient.
* Technology: Development relies on Python and C++ for control algorithms, advanced LED arrays and atmospheric sensors for hardware, and CAD for structural design.
* Creativity: The project creatively integrates energy amplification with life support, where food production simultaneously generates breathable air.
* Factors Considered: Design priorities included maximum resource efficiency (especially water and energy) and high system resilience against the extremely hostile Martian environment.

Our project focuses on understanding and visualizing the phenomenon of the Lunar Eclipse, where the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, causing the Moon to appear darkened or reddish in color. Understanding lunar eclipses is important because it enhances awareness of Earth–Moon–Sun relationships, supports astronomy education, and inspires curiosity about space science and exploration. Our project promotes scientific learning through observation, technology, and creativity.
projectDetails.details: Project Title: Lunar IceCube: Prospecting Lunar Ice with a CubeSat What does it do / How does it work? Our project, Lunar IceCube, focuses on exploring and understanding lunar eclipses and the detection of water ice on the Moon through an educational, interactive platform. The system visualizes how Earth, Moon, and Sun alignment causes different types of lunar eclipses—total, partial, and penumbral—while integrating concepts used in CubeSat-based lunar exploration missions. The interactive web model allows users to: Simulate the orbital alignment of the Earth–Moon–Sun system. Observe how varying angles cause different eclipse types. Learn about the significance of such phenomena in understanding the Moon’s composition and illumination patterns—important for detecting lunar ice deposits. It uses real astronomical data and visual simulations to bridge science education and mission design, showing how remote sensing from CubeSats can help analyze lunar surface conditions. Benefits Educational Engagement: Makes complex space phenomena easy to visualize and understand, especially for students and astronomy enthusiasts. Scientific Awareness: Encourages exploration of how space missions (like NASA’s Lunar IceCube) use satellite data to identify water molecules in lunar regolith. Inspiration for Future Missions: Sparks curiosity about planetary science, orbital mechanics, and CubeSat technologies. Public Outreach: Provides an accessible digital platform for learning about eclipses and lunar science without requiring technical expertise. Intended Impact The project’s goal is to democratize access to space science by combining real-world space mission concepts with interactive visualization. By engaging users with dynamic simulations, it helps foster: STEM learning and curiosity about astronomy. Awareness of lunar resources such as water ice and their potential in future human space exploration. A deeper understanding of Earth–Moon–Sun interactions, which are essential for both eclipse science and space navigation. Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (for interactivity and simulation logic). Design Tools: Figma and Canva for layout design and presentation. Data Sources: Public lunar data from NASA’s repositories (e.g., LRO, Lunar IceCube mission). Hosting Platform: GitHub Pages for live deployment and accessibility. Optional Extensions: Python (for data visualization), Three.js (for 3D rendering), and NASA APIs (for real-time lunar data). Creativity and Innovation Lunar IceCube combines scientific accuracy, educational visualization, and creative storytelling. What makes it unique: Blends astronomical data with interactive orbit modeling. Connects real NASA missions (CubeSat-based lunar water detection) with visual learning tools. Uses an elegant, space-themed web interface to simplify celestial mechanics for everyone. Designed to be lightweight, open-source, and scalable for classrooms or public exhibitions. Team Considerations While developing the project, our team focused on: Accessibility: Ensuring the platform works smoothly on browsers and mobile devices. Sustainability: Making it easily extendable with real mission data or 3D simulations in the future. Educational Value: Prioritizing clarity, engagement, and curiosity-driven learning.

projectDetails.name: Project LLUVIA
projectDetails.summary:
"Lluvia" is a highly animated, full-stack web application that provides climate-aware weather predictions by training a unique machine learning model for any location on demand.

Technology: It's built with a React front-end for a fluid, interactive user experience and a Python/FastAPI back-end for powerful data processing.

Core Feature: It uses 20 years of NASA data to train a custom machine learning model on-the-fly for any location, delivering predictions that account for climate trends.

UI/UX: The interface is designed to be immersive, featuring a 3D interactive hero section, scroll-triggered animations, a "glassmorphism" design, and animated data visualizations.
projectDetails.details:
lluvia is a sophisticated, single-location weather analysis tool designed for long-term event planning. It provides users with a deep, climate-aware forecast for any location on Earth for any future date.

It operates on a modern decoupled architecture:

  • Front-End: A highly interactive and visually immersive user interface built with React. Users can select a location by searching or clicking on an interactive map.
  • Back-End: A powerful API built with Python and FastAPI serves as the application's brain.
  • API Communication: When a user requests an analysis, the React front-end sends the location and date to the Python back-end. The back-end then fetches 20 years of historical data from the NASA POWER API, trains a unique Random Forest machine learning model on the spot for that specific location, and performs advanced statistical analysis. The results, including the ML-powered rain probability, are sent back to the front-end to be displayed in a series of animated charts and metrics.

BENEFITS

The primary benefit of lluvia is its ability to provide deep, long-term climatological insights that a standard 10-day weather forecast cannot offer.

  • Climate-Aware Predictions: By training a model on 20 years of data and incorporating the year as a feature, its predictions account for local climate trends, offering a more realistic forecast for a future date.
  • On-Demand, Specific Intelligence: Unlike generic weather apps, it generates a custom analysis tailored to the user's exact coordinates and date, providing highly relevant data.
  • Rich Data Visualization: The application doesn't just provide a single number. It presents data through multiple animated charts (temperature, precipitation, wind) and highlights, making complex historical data easy to understand at a glance.
  • Engaging User Experience: The fluid animations, interactive background, and polished "glassmorphism" design make the process of exploring data enjoyable and intuitive.

INTENDED IMPACT

The intended impact of lluvia is to empower individuals and organizations to make smarter, data-driven decisions when planning future events. By providing a clear and accessible view of historical weather patterns and climate trends, the project aims to:

  • Reduce Weather-Related Risks: Help event planners, farmers, and travelers better anticipate potential weather conditions and mitigate risks.
  • Raise Climate Awareness: By visualizing 20-year trends for any location, the app subtly educates users about the tangible effects of climate change in areas they care about.
  • Democratize Access to Climate Data: Make complex NASA satellite data accessible and understandable to a non-technical audience through a beautiful and user-friendly interface.

Tools, coding languages, software used

The project was developed using standard web development software and does not require specialized hardware.

  • Coding Languages: Python, JavaScript, CSS.
    • FastAPI: For building the high-performance API server.
    • Pandas & NumPy: For data manipulation and analysis.
    • Scikit-learn: For training the Random Forest machine learning model.
    • Geopy: For handling geocoding and reverse-geocoding tasks.
    • Uvicorn: As the ASGI server to run the Python application.
    • React: The core JavaScript library for building the user interface.
    • Framer Motion: For creating the fluid, complex animations throughout the app.
    • React-Leaflet: For the interactive map component.
    • Chart.js & React-Chartjs-2: For creating the animated data visualization charts.
    • Axios: For making API calls from the front-end to the back-end.
    • react-tsparticles: For the interactive, animated background.
  • Software & Environment: Node.js and npm for managing the front-end project, a Python virtual environment (.venv) for the back-end, and a code editor like VS Code.

CREATIVE ASPECT

The creativity of lluvia lies in its fusion of a powerful, on-demand machine learning backend with a highly polished and artistic front-end.

  • On-the-Fly Model Training: Instead of using a single, generalized model, the application trains a new, bespoke ML model for every user request, making each prediction uniquely tailored to the requested location.
  • Immersive Themed UI: The project goes beyond a simple dashboard. It creates an entire themed experience with its interactive rain background, 3D animated "lluvia" logo, and scroll-triggered "glassmorphism" cards, making data exploration feel like an interactive art piece.
  • Data as Art: Components like the FeelRadial gauge and animated chart "drawing" effects transform raw numbers into visually engaging and intuitive displays.
  • Technical Architecture: The choice of a decoupled architecture allows for this high degree of creative freedom on the front-end, a feat not possible with more rigid frameworks like Streamlit.

Factors that we considered

Several key factors were considered during the development process:

  • User Experience First: The primary consideration was creating an interface that was not just functional but also beautiful and engaging. This guided the decision to move from Streamlit to a decoupled React architecture to allow for advanced animations and a custom UI.
  • Data Accuracy and Relevance: We chose to use the official NASA POWER dataset for its reliability. Crucially, we decided to incorporate climate trend analysis to provide predictions that are more relevant for the future than a simple historical average.
  • Performance and Scalability: The back-end was built with FastAPI for its high performance. On the front-end, animations were carefully implemented using Framer Motion and hardware acceleration to ensure a smooth experience.
  • Modularity and Maintainability: The code was intentionally separated into a front-end and back-end, and the front-end was further broken down into reusable components (e.g., GlassCard, MagneticButton, Map). This makes the project easy to understand, debug, and expand in the future.
  • Responsiveness: The design was built to be fully responsive, ensuring a seamless and optimized experience across desktops, tablets, and mobile devices from the start.

projectDetails.details:
BlueBeyond VR is an immersive virtual reality experience that transforms NASA Earth observation datasets into interactive, visually engaging narratives of our planet’s oceans. Users can explore the oceans from a global perspective, dive into plankton blooms, observe coral reefs, witness sea-level rise, and interact with ocean currents and climate phenomena. The VR environment integrates spatial audio, hand-tracking, gaze interaction, and motion controllers to provide a fully interactive and intuitive exploration. NASA datasets such as PACE, SWOT, and GRACE-FO are visualized in real-time, allowing users to experience data as an interactive story, rather than just numbers or charts.

Benefits of the project:

  • Makes complex satellite data accessible and understandable to general audiences, including students, educators, and policymakers.
  • Provides emotional and educational engagement through immersive storytelling.
  • Enables users to explore the invisible aspects of oceans like plankton blooms, microplastics, and underwater currents.
  • Supports climate change awareness by visualizing sea-level rise and ecosystem degradation in a tangible, impactful way.

Intended impact:
BlueBeyond VR seeks to bridge the gap between science and public understanding. By transforming abstract data into interactive experiences, it fosters empathy, awareness, and action regarding ocean health, biodiversity, and climate change. It encourages responsible decision-making and ocean conservation efforts by allowing users to literally step into the oceans’ story. The project also provides an educational tool for K–12 students, universities, and science communicators.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • Software/Platforms: Unity3D, WebXR, Blender (for 3D models), Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop (visual assets)
  • Languages: C# (Unity scripting), HTML/CSS/JavaScript (for WebXR support)
  • Hardware: VR headsets (Oculus Quest, HTC Vive), hand-tracking controllers, optional eye-tracking devices
  • Datasets: NASA Earth observation datasets (PACE, SWOT, GRACE-FO), ocean visualizations, topography and satellite imagery

Creativity of the project:

  • Combines storytelling and science visualization, turning raw NASA datasets into interactive narratives.
  • Immersive VR experience allows users to experience ocean life at macro and micro scales, from space view to plankton level.
  • Integrates interaction mechanics like hand-tracking and gaze-based exploration, making the experience personal and engaging.
  • Blends emotional storytelling with scientific education to leave a lasting impression.

projectDetails.name: Project LUNEXA
projectDetails.summary: Our solution leverages NASA Earth observation data integrated with local urban datasets to build data-driven pathways for healthy and sustainable cities. By combining satellite data on air quality, land surface temperature, vegetation, and water resources with socioeconomic and infrastructure information, we develop predictive and simulation models for pollution, heat islands, flooding, and resource use. These insights are visualized through interactive dashboards and smart city prototypes, enabling real-time decision-making for waste, energy, and water management. The outcome is a framework for resilient urban planning that promotes environmental sustainability, public health, and improved quality of life, while contributing directly to SDGs such as Good Health, Clean Water, Sustainable Cities, and Climate Action.
projectDetails.details:
Our project focuses on creating data-driven pathways for building healthier and more sustainable cities. Using NASA Earth observation data combined with local datasets (such as population density, traffic, waste, and energy usage), we developed predictive models and simulation tools to monitor pollution, urban heat islands, and flooding risks. The project provides interactive dashboards and smart city prototypes that help policymakers and planners make real-time decisions for waste management, water conservation, and energy optimization.

The benefits include reducing pollution-related health risks, improving urban resilience to climate change, and enhancing overall quality of life for residents. The project’s intended impact is to integrate environmental sustainability with human-centered design, directly contributing to SDGs such as Good Health, Clean Water, Sustainable Cities, and Climate Action.

For development, we used Python and R for data processing and modeling, GIS tools (QGIS, ArcGIS) for spatial analysis, and AI/ML frameworks (TensorFlow, Scikit-learn) for predictive modeling. Visualization was achieved through Tableau/Power BI. Creativity in the project comes from combining NASA satellite data with ground-level insights to create actionable solutions that are both technologically robust and socially relevant. Our team carefully considered scalability, adaptability to different urban contexts, and alignment with sustainable development goals.

projectDetails.details:
TEAM METEORITE MINDS | ASTEROID THREAT ANALYSIS AND MITIGATION PLATFORM

An Interactive Web Platform for Asteroid Impact Simulation and Prevention.

OVERVIEW

Welcome to Meteor Madness, an interactive web platform built to address the global challenge of near-Earth object (NEO) threats. Our platform provides users with a suite of tools to visualize asteroid trajectories, simulate impact scenarios, and explore mitigation strategies. By offering a seamless experience that scales from educational exploration to professional analysis, we empower users to engage with one of the most significant challenges facing our planet. Our goal is to make asteroid threat assessment more transparent, understandable, and actionable for a global audience.

PROBLEM STATEMENT (CHALLENGE)

The threat of an asteroid impact, while rare, poses a catastrophic risk to life on Earth. The challenge is to effectively communicate this risk and provide tools for understanding and preparing for such an event. Key difficulties include:

  • Accessibility of Data: Complex astronomical data is often difficult for the public to access and interpret.
  • Understanding Mitigation: The methods for preventing an impact, such as kinetic impactors, are not widely understood.
  • Impact Consequences: Visualizing the potential consequences of an impact is crucial for awareness and planning.

Our platform addresses these challenges by:

  • Providing a user-friendly interface to visualize real-time asteroid data.
  • Offering an interactive kinetic impactor simulator to demonstrate deflection techniques.
  • Predicting and visualizing the location, area, and intensity of a potential impact.

TARGET USERS

  • General Public and Students: Individuals interested in learning about asteroids and space threats.
  • Educators: Teachers and professors seeking interactive tools for STEM education.
  • Researchers and Astronomers: Scientists who require a quick and efficient tool for impact analysis and visualization.
  • Emergency Management and Government Agencies: Professionals who need to understand and plan for potential impact events.

SOLUTION OVERVIEW

The Meteor Madness Platform offers a multi-faceted approach to asteroid threat assessment and mitigation. The platform is built around three core features:

  • Asteroid Position Tracker: Utilizes real-time data to display the current positions of known asteroids, allowing users to explore our solar system's dynamic environment.
  • Kinetic Impactor Simulator with Preventive Measures: An interactive tool that allows users to simulate the process of deflecting an asteroid using a kinetic impactor, providing a hands-on understanding of this key preventive measure.
    *This contains general preventive measures too.

  • Asteroid Impact Tracker: Real-time tracking of near-Earth objects with USGS environmental analysis, historical impact visualization, and interactive mitigation simulation powered by NASA data.


  • Impactor Scope: Asteroid Impact Energy Prediction Model – This tool integrates NASA Near-Earth Object (NEO) parameters with USGS-based physical models to predict the energy and tailored consequences of asteroid impacts.

    *Analysis for Asteroid:

    *Detailed Impact Model: Result Specific to Land Type:

FUTURE SCOPE

  • Integration of More NASA Data: Incorporate a wider range of datasets from NASA missions to enhance the accuracy of our simulations and predictions.
  • Advanced Mitigation Scenarios: Expand the simulator to include other deflection methods, such as gravity tractors and laser ablation.
  • Mobile Application: Develop a mobile version of the platform to make asteroid tracking and threat assessment accessible on the go.
  • AI-Powered Threat Assessment: Implement machine learning models to analyze asteroid data and identify high-risk objects with greater accuracy.
  • Multi-Language Availability : In the future, the website will be usable in multiple regional languages.

projectDetails.details:
Team Metis is proud to present Stellar Stories, an all-in-one interactive web platform designed to make space exploration and astronomy accessible, engaging, and exciting for everyone, especially aspiring young astronomers. Our project is a comprehensive educational tool that blends storytelling, real-time data, and interactive media to create an immersive learning experience.

Main features

  • Journey: An interactive 3D story from the Sun to Earth, covering solar physics, planetary flybys, and the Northern Lights.
  • Nasa Data: Live feeds for Solar Flares (FLR), Coronal Mass Ejections (CME), and more, directly from NASA's DONKI API.
  • Impacts: Real-world awareness sections showing how space weather affects pilots, astronauts, and power grids.
  • Magazine & Games: Illustrated storybooks and an asteroid game to engage younger audiences.
  • Quiz & Reports: Tools to test knowledge and deep-dive into research topics.

Stellar Stories is an interactive educational platform that demystifies space science. It combines a narrative journey from the Sun to Earth with real-time NASA data, games, and resources to make learning accessible and exciting.

Our platform fosters scientific curiosity and serves as a powerful learning tool, highlighting the real-world impact of space weather. We aim to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers while raising public awareness about the importance of monitoring cosmic events for our technologically dependent world.

Our tech stack is built on HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for immersive 3D graphics and Tailwind CSS for styling. We integrated NASA's DONKI API and the WeatherAPI for real-time data.

Our team focused on four key factors:

  • User Engagement: Creating an interactive and visually appealing experience.
  • Educational Integrity: Ensuring all scientific information was accurate and credible.
  • Target Audience: Designing content that appeals to both children and advanced learners aged 10-20, different modules are designed for different age groups.
  • Real-World Relevance: Connecting abstract space concepts to their tangible impacts on Earth.

projectDetails.name: IOT SMART HOME CONTROLER
projectDetails.summary:
This project is a Smart Home Control system built with an ESP32 microcontroller and managed remotely via the Blynk IoT app. It integrates sensors like DHT11 for temperature and humidity, a rain sensor to detect no, medium, and heavy rain through LED indicators, and a PIR motion sensor to automate an LED and fan inside the home. The system smartly combines sensor feedback to automate device control, allowing fans to run manually via the app or automatically based on motion, optimizing comfort and energy use. The rain sensor offers real-time outdoor weather updates useful for irrigation or outdoor activities.

A key enhancement includes using the rain sensor to automatically control windows and drying areas—closing windows or roof shields during heavy rain to prevent water damage to electronics and documents near windows. For clothes drying on terraces, it controls protective covers to avoid wetting after clothes are hung out. This addition makes the system more comprehensive, protecting valuable home assets and adding convenience during rain. The Blynk app integration enables simple, real-time remote control and monitoring, making smart home living accessible and efficient.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do/how does it work?

This smart home control system uses ESP32 with temperature, humidity, rain, and motion sensors to monitor indoor and outdoor conditions. Devices like fans, LEDs, windows, and protective covers are controlled automatically or manually through the Blynk IoT app. Rain sensors trigger window/cover closure and laundry protection in rain.

Benefits

  • Automatic control saves energy and improves comfort.
  • Protects electronics, documents, and clothes from rain and water damage.
  • Simplifies everyday life with remote monitoring/control.

Intended Impact

Enhances home safety, convenience, and resource efficiency, making advanced automation affordable and practical for everyday users.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

  • Programming Language: Embedded C (Arduino IDE)

  • Actuators: LED, fan, motor/servo for windows/covers
  • IoT Platform: Blynk app for remote control and monitoring

Creativity

Rain sensor integration for automatic window and drying cover control is a unique feature. The project blends real-time environmental sensing, IoT, and automation to create a proactive, user-centric solution.

  • Reliable sensor-actuator integration and calibration
  • Simple, user-friendly interface for remote access
  • Security and backup measures for robust operation
  • Low-cost hardware for easy deployment

projectDetails.name: Project MissionNova
projectDetails.summary:
LEO-Swap Hub: The Zero-Knowledge Orbital Economy

(Challenge: Commercializing Low Earth Orbit (LEO) | Team: MissionNova)



The LEO economy is jeopardized by the massive $\text{\$25,000}/\text{kg}$ cost and risk of Earth resupply. We developed LEO-Swap Hub, an interactive digital platform that establishes a *Zero-Knowledge Circular Economy* for co-orbiting commercial space stations (CLDs).



What We Developed: A web prototype of a central Swap Hub for trading critical assets: Life Consumables ($\text{O}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$), Propellant (Hydrazine/Xenon), 3D Filament, and Orbital Replacement Units (ORUs)....etc



How It Addresses the Challenge:

1. Zero-Knowledge Trade: We enforce full anonymity via the Hub’s secure Orbital Trust Protocol (conceptual DLT), neutralizing the risk of commercial espionage.

2. Economic Engine: We use Launch-Cost Credit (LCC) as the exchange medium, tying the swap value directly to the cost of the avoided Earth launch. This is optimized by our Tug Route Planner logic.

Why It Is Important (The Winning Impact):

LEO-Swap Hub is essential software infrastructure for LEO resilience. Our dashboard instantly calculates the Total Cumulative Launch Cost Saved, proving critical operational savings and reducing environmental impact. This system guarantees a sustainable, safe, and commercially viable bridge for humanity’s permanent presence in Low Earth Orbit. (Like a Digital Hypermall as establishing non-Digital one is expensive).
projectDetails.details:
The LEO economy is jeopardized by the massive $\mathbf{\$25,000}/\mathbf{kg}$ cost and risk of Earth-based resupply. We developed LEO-Swap Hub, an interactive digital platform that establishes a Zero-Knowledge Circular Economy for co-orbiting commercial space stations (CLDs).



What It Does & How It Works:

The Hub is a software prototype simulating a central asset depot. Stations access the Hub to anonymously list or request resources, including Life Consumables ($\text{O}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$), Propellant, 3D Filament, and Orbital Replacement Units (ORUs).



The core mechanism is:

1. Zero-Knowledge Trade: All transactions are brokered via the Hub's conceptual Orbital Trust Protocol (DLT) to enforce anonymity. The buyer and seller identities are masked to prevent commercial espionage.

2. Economic Engine: The system uses Launch-Cost Credit (LCC) as the medium of exchange. The LCC value is calculated based on the cost of the avoided Earth launch, validating the trade.



Benefits & Intended Impact:

The project's primary impact is economic sustainability and in-orbit resilience. Our dashboard instantly calculates and visualizes the Total Cumulative Launch Cost Saved, proving critical operational savings for CLD operators. By facilitating resource sharing, we significantly reduce the environmental impact (fewer launches) and guarantee a safer, more stable resource supply.



Tools & Development:

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. Data visualization was achieved using the Chart.js CDN. This stack ensures instant deployment and client-side functionality.



Creativity & Factors Considered:

Our project is creative because it solves a political/commercial problem (lack of trust) with a cryptographic solution (Zero-Knowledge applied to orbital logistics). Key factors considered were: Crew Safety (implementing a non-tradable "Survival Floor"), Economic Viability (using LCC as a driver), and Efficiency (optimizing tug routes with our Tug Route Planner logic).

The final implemented code (HTML/CSS/JS) was manually written, but the conceptual algorithms were AI-assisted in the design phase.

Images and Graphics (Visuals/Presentation): Generative AI tools were used to create the team's avatar, all presentation backgrounds, and the abstract graphics that visualize key concepts (e.g., the LCC scale, the Swap Hub schematic).

🌌 Project Details – AstroHabitat Designer 🚀

✨ What does it do or how does it work?
AstroHabitat Designer is an interactive web application 🖥️🌍 that allows users to design and explore customized space habitats. Users can select planetary environments 🌙🪐 (Mars, Moon, Titan, or orbit), define the number of residents 👩‍🚀👨‍🚀, and set lifestyle preferences 🏠⚡ along with primary activities like research 🔬, farming 🌱, or leisure 🎮. projectDetails.name: weather prediction
projectDetails.summary:
This project is a machine learning–powered weather prediction web application built using Flask, Python, and scikit-learn. It analyzes environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, location, and time to predict the likelihood of rainfall. A logistic regression model is trained on real weather data, balanced and standardized for improved accuracy.

The app provides an interactive web interface where users can input local weather parameters and instantly receive a prediction — either “ Rain Expected” or “No Rain,” along with a probability score.

This project addresses the challenge of accessible, data-driven weather insights without requiring complex meteorological tools. By combining user-friendly design with AI-based prediction, it empowers individuals, farmers, and planners to make more informed decisions about outdoor activities, agriculture, and daily life.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a machine learning–based weather prediction system that forecasts whether it will rain on a given day and time. It works by analyzing key environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, location, and time of day. These inputs are processed through a logistic regression model trained on historical weather data to estimate the probability of rainfall.

The application is built using Python, with Flask serving as the backend framework. We used pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn for data cleaning, preprocessing, and model development. The user interface is designed in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, providing an intuitive web experience. The app can be hosted on platforms such as PythonAnywhere, Render, or Netlify for easy access.

The main benefit of this project is that it offers a quick, data-driven, and easily accessible weather prediction tool that can assist individuals, farmers, and planners in making informed decisions about outdoor activities and agricultural practices.

Our goal was to create a solution that blends machine learning accuracy with real-world usability. We focused on factors like model reliability, user friendliness, and visual appeal to ensure a smooth experience. The creativity lies in integrating predictive analytics into a lightweight, interactive web app that brings the power of AI to everyday weather forecasting.

projectDetails.name: Bloom Watch AI
projectDetails.summary: Bloom Watch AI, an interactive, AI-powered web platform that processes satellite data to detect, monitor, and forecast plant blooming events globally. Users select a location and date range to view bloom detections, hotspot maps, and trends visualized on a world map. Behind the scenes, the system analyzes satellite-derived vegetation indices, soil moisture, and climate data to pinpoint active and emerging blooms. projectDetails.details:
Bloom Watch AI is an AI-powered web platform designed to detect, monitor, and predict plant blooming events worldwide using NASA Earth observation data such as MODIS, Landsat, SMAP, and MERRA-2. The system analyzes vegetation indices, soil moisture, and climate variables to visualize bloom hotspots, trends, and forecasts on an interactive map.

The platform’s frontend is developed using Next.js, providing a fast, responsive, and user-friendly interface. The backend is built with the Firebase SDK, managing authentication, real-time database operations, and cloud storage. Core logic and data processing are implemented in JavaScript, ensuring seamless integration between the client and server.

Bloom Watch AI benefits farmers, ecologists, and conservationists by offering actionable insights for crop planning, biodiversity tracking, and ecosystem health monitoring. The project’s creative aspect lies in transforming complex NASA satellite data into an accessible, real-time visualization tool that engages both professionals and citizen scientists.

Our team focused on usability, data accuracy, and sustainability impact — aiming to make space-based Earth data understandable and useful for addressing agricultural, environmental, and climate challenges.
