projectDetails.name: Exo Lab
projectDetails.summary: In a universe full of undiscovered planets, many dream of finding one, yet few know where to start. Exo Lab was created to guide these explorers. Acting as a mentor in this cosmic journey, the platform suggests stars with unconfirmed exoplanets, inviting users to observe them through their own telescopes. The collected data is then analyzed by Exo Lens, our AI-powered engine trained with NASA datasets, which estimates the probability and characteristics of a potential discovery. Along the way, users can access learning modules explaining real detection methods and experiment in the Exoplanet Lab, where they adjust planetary and system parameters to create it’s appearance and compare their worlds to Earth. Through curiosity, learning, and technology, Exo Lab enables every stargazer to make their discovery and be part of humanity’s grand mission to explore the universe.
projectDetails.details:
Exo Lab

Overview

Exo Lab is an interactive web platform that empowers anyone, from amateur astronomers to professional, to detect and explore exoplanets using real data and AI-driven analysis. Our goal is to bridge the gap between curiosity and scientific discovery by combining education, data analysis, and visual exploration in one cohesive environment.

How It Works

Users begin by learning about exoplanet detection methods through the learning secction.
Then, the platform guides them to promising stars with unconfirmed exoplanets, inviting observations with their own telescopes. The collected data can be uploaded to Exo Lens, our AI engine powered by XGBoost, trained on NASA’s exoplanet datasets, which analyzes the light-curve or brightness data to estimate the probability of an exoplanet’s presence and its basic characteristics.

After analysis, users can visualize results inside a 3D star-system explorer, manipulate orbital parameters, and compare planets through an Earth Similarity Index.

Key Features

  • Home: Welcome to ExoLab, your gateway to exoplanet discovery. Our platform connects amateur astronomers and curious minds with real NASA data and AI-powered analysis tools. Start your journey by exploring detection methods, learning the science behind planetary transits, and discovering where to point your telescope to contribute to actual exoplanet research.
  • Detection Methods: Educational content explaining the physics behind exoplanet detection.
    • Transit Method: When a planet crosses in front of its host star, it blocks a tiny fraction of light, creating a measurable dip in brightness. The transit depth equals (R_planet / R_star)², revealing the planet's size. Jupiter-sized planets block about 1% of starlight, while Earth-sized planets dim stars by only 0.01%. The light curve shows four phases: baseline brightness, gradual dimming (ingress), flat-bottomed transit, and return to baseline (egress). Transit duration and timing reveal orbital period and velocity. Kepler and TESS missions use this method to discover thousands of exoplanets.
    • Radial Velocity Method: Planets gravitationally pull their stars, causing them to wobble. As stars move toward us, their light shifts blue; moving away shifts red. These Doppler shifts measure the star's velocity, which correlates with planet mass. Combined with transit data, this yields planetary density—the key to determining if a world is rocky (5.5 g/cm³), gaseous (< 2 g/cm³), or somewhere between. Ground-based spectrographs can detect wobbles as small as 1 meter per second.
    • Direct Imaging: Photographing exoplanets requires blocking starlight with coronagraphs and correcting atmospheric blur with adaptive optics. This method works best for young, hot gas giants in wide orbits. Images reveal atmospheric composition through spectroscopy, detecting water, methane, and clouds. JWST's infrared capabilities now enable imaging of cooler, older planets previously invisible to telescopes.
    • Gravitational Microlensing: When a star with a planet passes between Earth and a background star, its gravity magnifies the distant star's light. Planets create characteristic spikes in the magnification curve. This method detects planets at enormous distances and reveals that rogue planets ejected from systems may outnumber stars in our galaxy. Each event is unique and never repeats.
  • 3D Explorer: Navigate through interactive three-dimensional representations of planetary systems. Built with Three.js and React Three Fiber, this immersive viewer renders planets with physically-based materials that reflect their composition. Gas giants appear with low metalness and high roughness, while terrestrial worlds show balanced properties. Each planet texture is generated by Google's Imagen AI using a 2000+ character prompt incorporating temperature gradients, atmospheric composition, and stellar type. Orbit controls let you zoom, pan, and rotate freely. Click any planet or star to reveal detailed statistics including mass, radius, orbital period, and discovery method. A realistic starfield of 5000 points surrounds the system, creating an authentic space environment.
  • Planetary Lab:
    • Exoplanet Explorer: Search and discover thousands of star systems containing confirmed and candidate exoplanets. Our real-time integration with NASA's Exoplanet Archive brings you the most up-to-date planetary data available. Use advanced search to find systems by star name or planet designation, or explore curated regions like the Lyra Constellation (Kepler's hunting ground) and the Solar Neighborhood. Each system displays detailed information including stellar properties, planetary parameters, and habitability scores. For unconfirmed candidates, we provide precise celestial coordinates so you can observe them yourself and contribute to their validation.
    • Exoplanet Detector - Feature AI Mode: Input six key parameters from your observations: orbital period, planet radius, transit depth, stellar temperature, stellar radius, and surface gravity. Our XGBoost-trained AI analyzes these features to classify the planet type (Terrestrial, Neptune-like, or Gas Giant), determine if it falls within the habitable zone, and calculate its density. Interactive tooltips guide you through each parameter, making professional-grade analysis accessible to beginners. The system generates a real-time 3D preview of your planet with physically accurate coloring based on temperature and composition.
    • Exoplanet Detector - LightCurve AI Mode: Upload your telescope's brightness measurements as a CSV file containing time-series photometry data. Our machine learning model, trained on TESS and Kepler datasets, analyzes the light curve for transit signatures that indicate an exoplanet's presence. The AI provides a binary prediction (Exoplanet/Not Exoplanet) along with a confidence score. After analysis, view a simulated transit curve showing the four phases: pre-transit baseline, ingress, full transit, and egress. The system calculates transit depth and duration based on physical laws, helping you understand what the data reveals about the planet-star system.
    • Earth Similarity Index: Discover how Earth-like your detected planet truly is. This tool computes the Earth Similarity Index (ESI) using the scientifically validated Schulze-Makuch formula, which weighs planetary radius (57%), escape velocity (26%), and surface temperature (17%). Adjust four sliders to input your planet's characteristics, and watch the ESI score update in real-time. The system automatically categorizes results from "Earth Twin" (>90% similar) to "Not Earth-like" (<40%), while also assessing habitability potential. Individual similarity bars break down how closely radius, density, and temperature match Earth's values. Dynamic range adjustment accommodates extreme exoplanets, with warnings for unusual parameters.
  • About: Learn about our mission to democratize exoplanet discovery and the Cosmic Hackers team from São José do Rio Preto, Brazil. We detail our data sources (TESS, Kepler, JWST, NEOSSat) and explain how our technology stack combines Next.js, FastAPI, XGBoost, and Three.js to create an educational yet scientifically rigorous platform. Discover our goals: reducing the human bottleneck in candidate classification, scaling analysis to 100% of available data, abstracting technical complexity, and implementing continuous learning systems that improve with community feedback. See how Canadian Space Agency contributions through NEOSSat and JWST instruments enable global collaboration in planetary science.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Exo Lab democratizes access to astronomy by guiding users who might not know where to look or how to start.
It shortens the path from interest to contribution, enabling citizen scientists to participate in real research while helping professional astronomers save time in the early stages of exoplanet validation.
The project also fosters STEM education, transforming learning into hands-on exploration.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Next JS, React
  • Backend: FastAPI (Python)

projectDetails.name: Project ExoRAG Team
projectDetails.summary:
ExoRAG is a physics-informed AI system that accelerates exoplanet validation from weeks to milliseconds. We address the critical bottleneck in exoplanet discovery: TESS, Kepler, and K2 missions generate thousands of candidates, but manual validation is slow and resource-intensive.

Our hybrid architecture combines CNN for morphological feature extraction, BiLSTM for temporal dependencies, and attention mechanisms for interpretability. We integrate physics-informed constraints that penalize violations of transit depth, duration, and Keplerian dynamics, ensuring predictions align with astrophysical laws.

A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) layer powered by Qdrant vector database and BGE-M3 embeddings retrieves confirmed transits and NASA literature, providing scientific justifications and anomaly alerts.

Built with FastAPI backend and React dashboard, ExoRAG targets F1 > 0.98 with <100ms latency per light curve, democratizing exoplanet discovery for both professional astronomers and citizen scientists while reducing dependency on labeled data by ~60% through synthetic augmentation.
projectDetails.details:
## 🎯 What It Does

ExoRAG processes photometric light curves from NASA's Kepler, K2, and TESS missions to identify and validate exoplanet transit candidates with unprecedented speed and accuracy. The system:

- Ingests raw light curves and performs automated preprocessing (detrending, outlier removal, normalization)

- Classifies transit signals using a hybrid neural architecture

- Validates predictions against physical constraints (transit depth ≈ (Rp/Rs)², Keplerian dynamics)

- Generates human-readable explanations with scientific references via RAG

- Delivers interactive visualizations with attention maps showing model decision points

## 🌟 Key Benefits

**Speed**: Reduces validation time from weeks to <100ms per light curve

**Accuracy**: Targets F1-score > 0.98 with physics-informed constraints

**Explainability**: RAG layer provides citations to confirmed exoplanets and NASA literature

**Data Efficiency**: Reduces labeled data dependency by ~60% through realistic synthetic injection and SMOTE

**Accessibility**: Interactive dashboard enables both professional astronomers and citizen scientists to participate

## 🔬 How It Works

**Architecture**:

1. **CNN Path**: Captures local morphological features (ingress/egress shapes)

2. **BiLSTM Path**: Models long-range temporal dependencies

3. **Attention Mechanism**: Highlights critical time steps for interpretability

4. **Physics Module**: Enforces astrophysical constraints via composite loss L = L_class + λ·L_physics

5. **RAG Validation**: Retrieves similar confirmed transits and generates contextual explanations

**Data Pipeline**:

- Source: NASA Exoplanet Archive (Kepler DR25, K2, TESS)

- Preprocessing: Lightkurve library for detrending/flattening

- Augmentation: 74/26 synthetic/real ratio with SMOTE for class imbalance

- Cross-mission validation: Train on Kepler, test on TESS/K2

## 🛠️ Technology Stack

**Machine Learning**:

- TensorFlow/PyTorch for model development

- Custom physics-informed loss functions

- SMOTE for class balancing

**Backend**:

- FastAPI for orchestration

- GPU acceleration (RTX) for <100ms inference

- Qdrant vector database for RAG

**Frontend**:

- React dashboard

- Interactive plotly.js visualizations

- Real-time attention map rendering

**Infrastructure**:

- Docker/CUDA containerization

- NASA Earthdata API integration

- Lightkurve for astronomical data processing

## 🎨 Creativity & Innovation

**Physics-Informed ML**: Unlike black-box approaches, we integrate first-principles physics directly into the loss function, ensuring predictions respect fundamental astrophysics

**RAG for Science**: Novel application of Retrieval-Augmented Generation to scientific validation, providing traceable evidence chains

**Hybrid Architecture**: Combines spatial (CNN), temporal (BiLSTM), and attention mechanisms for comprehensive signal analysis

**Synthetic Data Strategy**: Realistic signal injection based on actual stellar parameters, not generic noise

## 📊 Intended Impact

**Short-term**:

- Enable real-time processing of TESS alerts

- Reduce astronomer workload for follow-up observations

- Democratize exoplanet discovery through accessible interface

**Long-term**:

- Scale to future missions (JWST, PLATO, Ariel)

- Integrate Bayesian uncertainty quantification

- Deploy lightweight models for edge/mobile devices

- Foster global citizen science participation

## 🤔 Key Considerations

**Data Imbalance**: Exoplanets are rare (~1% of candidates) - mitigated with SMOTE and careful synthetic injection

**Confounding Signals**: Stellar variability, eclipsing binaries, instrumental artifacts - addressed through physics constraints and multi-feature architecture

**Generalization**: Cross-mission validation ensures model doesn't overfit to specific instrument characteristics

**Interpretability**: Attention maps and RAG explanations crucial for scientific trust and error analysis

**Ethical AI**: Transparent methodology, open data sources, and explainable predictions to maintain scientific rigor

projectDetails.summary:
Guardians of the Blue Planet is a short comic story that transforms NASA’s Terra mission data into an inspiring visual narrative about climate awareness.
The story follows two artificial intelligences, TERRA-IA and ORBIT-IA, who watch over Earth from space. They analyze global temperature and radiation data using instruments from NASA’s Terra satellite—such as MODIS and CERES—to understand how small actions on Earth impact the planet’s health.

Through vivid comic panels and dialogue, the project communicates scientific data in a format that is accessible to all ages, encouraging curiosity and care for our planet.
This project addresses the “Animation Celebration of Terra Data!” challenge by turning environmental data into art and storytelling, proving that science can inspire emotion, empathy, and positive change.

Our goal is simple: turn data into art, and art into awareness.

projectDetails.name: Illustronautas
projectDetails.summary:
1. Urgency: systemic risk and global projections
Urgency is based on the destructive potential of Space Climate. The villain Coronus is the personification of the Class X/ CME (given by NASA), which represents the most severe threat. The risk is systemic: due to our high technology dependence, NOAA projections indicate trillions of dollars in losses and collapse of critical infrastructure (GPS and energy). The project acts as a Knowledge Mitigation Strategy, preparing the next generation for this inevitable event.

2. Scientific and methodological relevance
The relevance lies in the methodological rigor of translating complex data into plot. Each challenge of the Guardians of Tomorrow is based on scientific facts:

- The hero Kenji faces the Geomagnetically Induced Currents (GICs), which cause blackouts.
- Astronaut Aria deals with Atmospheric Drag, which threatens satellites.

The animation not only teaches physics, but shows science in action to protect the planet.

3. Ethical Relevance: The Mission of Equity
The greatest relevance is social. The project addresses the Convergence of Crises (Spatial Climate + inequality), exposing that the risk first affects the vulnerable. The central point is Kenji’s choice to prioritize those most in need, such as Chloé and Mateus. This shapes the critical sense of the young public, ensuring that the ultimate mission of science is equity: that no one be left behind.
projectDetails.details:
The chosen animation project is "Star Stories: The Space Climate Through the Eyes of the Earthlings", executed through the script "The Fury of the Sun and the Social Critique of the Earth".

The story is led by 7 main characters who represent the threat, scientific defense and social impact.

The cosmic villain

CORONUS (The Chaotic Force)

• Archetype: Solar Eruption/CME (coronal mass ejection).

• Personality: Arrogant, impulsive and noisy. He is the physical manifestation of solar plasma.

• Catchphrase: "Tremble, earthlings! The true energy has arrived to turn off your lights!"

The Guardians of the Earth (Heroes of Science)

Dr. SOFIA (The Strategist)

• Archetype: Mission leader and solar scientist.

• Scientific function: Responsible for the detection and command of all defense operations.

• Phrase of Effect: "The Sun has given us the warning. Science will give us the answer. Guardians, it is our time."

ARIA (The Vanguard)

• Archetype: Astronaut.

• Scientific Function: Space Sentry. Protects satellites and the ISS from atmospheric drag.

KENJI (The Protector)

• Archetype: Master of the Electric Grid.

• Scientific Function: Deflects Geomagnetically Induced Currents (GICs) and ensures the distribution of energy with equity.

• Phrase of Effect: "You will not erase my city. Energy always finds a way!"

ELARA (The Navigator)

• Archetype: High altitude pilot.

• Scientific Function: Ensures safe air routes, facing GPS failures and radio blackout.

• Effect Phrase: "Solar turbulence ahead. Passengers, fasten your seat belts. The route is different, but the destination is the same: safety."

BETO (The Foundation)

• Archetype: Farmer of the Future.

• Scientific Function: Ensures logistics and essential supplies, adapting to GPS failure.

• Catchphrase: "Nature always sends its challenges. Sun, rain or plasma. We prepare, and we harvest."

The Affected People (The Reason for the Struggle)

CHLOÉ

• Social Role: Solo Mother, Black.

• Crisis Represented: Fight against drought and water scarcity (Climate Action).

• Impact of the Storm: The failure of the GPS paralyzes the only truck that would rescue.

MATEUS

• Social role: Community leader.

• Crisis Represented: Fight against the advance of the high tide (Climate Inaction).

• Storm Impact: Failure of communication and monitoring systems prevents life-saving relief.

1. Why was this theme chosen?

The theme was selected for fulfilling the challenge in an integral way, but with an amplified social purpose. The script uses the phenomenon of Space Climate (the solar crisis) as a narrative catalyst that exposes and amplifies the inequalities and social vulnerabilities already existing on the planet.

The goal is not only to explain science, but to humanize science. Rather than just saving infrastructure and profit, science heroes are forced to make an explicit ethical choice: use technology to save the lives of the most vulnerable people. Science is, here, portrayed as a tool of equity.

2. Does Animation have a real impact?

Yes, the impact of animation is real and intentional, manifested in three crucial levels for the young audience:

A) Impact on Scientific Literacy

The animation makes accessible and exciting high-risk complex phenomena. The script prepares the audience to understand that the technology is vulnerable to external events, such as Geomagnetically Induced Currents (GICs) and Atmospheric Drag.

B) Impact on the Development of Critical Sense

This is the biggest impact for the young audience. History teaches that technology and infrastructure are not neutral; they always reflect society’s priorities. Kenji’s dilemma ("The system cannot choose who has the right to survive!") aims to develop students' critical sense, encouraging reflection on social justice and equity in the context of a global crisis.

C) Community Preparation

The theme reinforces that the Space Climate community continues to work to understand the needs of those affected and determine ways to mitigate the effects of Space Climate.

3. How does NASA Data Impact the Theme?

The narrative is factual and uses NASA terminology to build the scientific credibility of the story, following the guidelines of telling the story in a unique and factual way.

• Solar Eruption (Class X) and CME: The origin of Coronus. Dr. Sofia identifies the hazard with the correct classification.

• Geomagnetically Induced Currents (GICs): Kenji’s challenge. These parasitic currents invade electrical networks, a real risk of total blackout.

• Atmospheric Drag: Aria’s challenge. Solar heat "inflates" the atmosphere, creating resistance that threatens to bring down satellites.

• Loss of GPS and Radio Signals: The impact on Elara and Beto. The distortion of the signals paralyzes the relief logistics and navigation.

• Magnetosphere and Auroras: The final defense. "Earth’s shield" deflects the plasma, and the absorbed energy is transformed into the "Symphony of the Aurora".

4. What does the young public understand about this topic and why the chosen age group?

The ideal age group is Elementary School II (11 to 15 years).

1. Abstract Reasoning: The public at this age is able to understand the cause and effect relationship at great distances (Sun Earth) and understand the technological impact.

2. Critical and Ethical Sense: It is the phase in which the public develops a sense of justice. They understand the social critique that the most vulnerable people die first, making the ethical dilemma of the script a powerful tool for shaping social consciousness.

3. Scientific Understanding: Concepts such as magnetic field and satellites are studied in Fundamental II, making history an effective form of interdisciplinary education.

5. What is the relevance of this theme to society?

The relevance of the theme is maximum, because it addresses a growing global risk in three pillars:

I. Global Infrastructure Risk

The animation raises awareness of the urgent need to mitigate the risks of solar storms that can cause significant losses due to blackouts, given the high level of technological dependence of modern society.

II. Convergence of Crises

The script demonstrates that an external threat (Space Climate) amplifies an internal threat (Climate Crisis and social inequality). This convergence of crises is the greatest challenge of the 21st century.

III. The Ethical Mission of Science

The theme reinforces that science has a social responsibility. The roadmap reiterates that the purpose of technological advancement is not just to generate profit or convenience, but rather to be a shield of equity, ensuring that in any crisis, the most vulnerable people are not left behind. Science is portrayed as the essential tool for social justice.

projectDetails.name: Rio Preto Verde
projectDetails.summary:
Urban and environmental management faces the challenge of dispersed data and the lack of immediate action to combat crises such as deforestation and wildfires.
We developed Rio Preto Verde, a geospatial web application that transforms NASA/ESA data into Management Intelligence for urban planners and government agencies. Our platform continuously monitors environmental issues (heat spots, emissions, deforestation) using high-resolution sources like NASA Landsat (for the Vegetation Cover Index - NDVI), NASA FIRMS (for real-time Active Fire Alerts), and the LST Model (Land Surface Temperature).
The crucial differentiator is the strategic action suggestion that accompanies every alert, optimizing the response of enforcement agencies in the field. Beyond crisis combat, Rio Preto Verde offers tools for sustainable urban planning, allowing managers to identify ideal areas for city expansion based on integrated environmental metrics.
The project is vital because it transforms the environmental response from reactive to strategic, protecting natural assets and guiding urban development toward a more sustainable future with the power of Earth observation.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction

We are a group of undergraduate technology students with the goal of providing a practical, intuitive, and efficient way to integrate intelligent solutions in the context of urban planning, quality of life, and environmental preservation. To achieve this, we propose a tool capable of using satellite data to monitor areas, notify responsible authorities, and generate potential solutions to assist urban planners — Rio Preto Verde.

Features

When opening Rio Preto Verde, the user is presented, on the left side of the screen, with a general overview of the current situation of the area, based on data collected in real time. Alongside this overview is an interactive map that can be freely navigated. On the map, markers and their corresponding legends are displayed, generated from satellite data processed in real time by NASA and other space agencies.

By scrolling down on the left panel, users can select which markers will be shown on the map. They can also generate a report, access an interface to analyze data for a specific neighborhood, view a national panorama dashboard, or access the Settings and Data section.

Report

By clicking the button to generate a report, the user accesses a section with an executive summary and a panel that details detected issues using satellite data. Quick actions such as generating a PDF or exporting data are also available.

Below this, solutions generated by a trained artificial intelligence are proposed and displayed. If the user clicks Implement Solution, the responsible authorities are notified. By clicking View Full Details, a document with complete information about the proposed solution is opened.

At the bottom of the page, there is an Impact Summary, describing the potential results and benefits of the proposed solutions.

Neighborhood Analysis

This option opens a report focused on a single neighborhood, presenting its specific scenario. It also displays environmental statistics and comparisons between the neighborhood and the city as a whole, as well as trends over time. An AI-generated recommendation is provided for the case of that neighborhood, and a detailed report can be generated.

National Panorama

In this section, users have access to an interactive map for advanced analysis of land cover and use, including biome divisions, water body visualization and more. It also displays graphs from governmental and national sources showing the percentage distribution of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sector, as well as trends in temperature anomalies and deforestation over time.

Settings and Data

In this menu, users can access and review data sources and calibrate the trigger settings for each notification.

Conclusion

In conclusion, Rio Preto Verde is a tool designed to facilitate analysis and decision-making. Through machine learning and the integration of detailed governmental and satellite data, urban planners gain access to a practical, educational, and visual environment for strategic urban planning. projectDetails.name: BIOSPACE EXPLORER
projectDetails.summary:
The BIOSPACE EXPLORER is an immersive web platform designed to democratize the complex knowledge of NASA's Space Biology.
The project solves the challenge of making hundreds of scattered research papers in academic formats accessible, intuitive, and relevant to everyone. The platform offers an interactive exploration experience where the user navigates celestial bodies such as Earth, Mars, and the Moon. Upon selecting a celestial body, the user can:
Explore existing articles, which are visually organized and referenced on the 3D model of the celestial body.
Or, ask a question, and the Artificial Intelligence (AI) will automatically respond with summaries, graphs, and related articles.
This AI is adaptive: it adjusts itself to the user's segment and conversation history, enhancing the relevance of future responses.
The BIOSPACE EXPLORER is crucial because it bridges the gap between science and the public, facilitating data access for students and researchers, increasing the visibility of experiments, and accelerating new discoveries. It is a revolutionary solution that transforms the way we interact with space scientific knowledge.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do and how does it work?

The BioSpace Explorer is an interactive web platform that simplifies and organizes NASA's space biology information. The experience begins with an interactive interface (Home) where the user selects a celestial body (Earth, Mars, or the Moon). Upon entering the celestial body's environment, the user has two interaction options:

  1. Visual Exploration: Existing research articles are mapped and visually organized on the celestial body's 3D model, referenced to the location of origin or study. The user clicks on a point of interest to access a plain-language summary of the article.
  2. AI-Powered Research and Dialogue: The user can ask a specific question. The platform uses an Artificial Intelligence (AI) to analyze NASA data and generate an immediate response, which includes concise summaries, relevant graphs, and the original scientific articles. The AI is adaptive and shapes its future responses and suggestions based on the conversation history and the user's segment of interest.

What are the benefits?

  • Universal Accessibility: Transforms complex and scattered data into easily consumable knowledge, democratizing access to Space Biology.
  • Intuitive Learning: Offers a new and immersive way to learn through the exploration of 3D models, instead of merely reading static documents.
  • Efficiency for Researchers: Researchers and students can quickly find data and correlations using the AI, optimizing search and analysis time.
  • Higher Chance of Investment: The new way of visualizing research through graphs and results provides greater visibility and clarity, which can attract more investment.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The main impact is to transform the relationship between the public and science. The project aims to:

  • Organize and Unify the Database: Through the BIOSPACE EXPLORER, we will organize all the data, transforming it into a structured and relational knowledge base.
  • Accelerate Discovery: By making data more visible and relatable, researchers are expected to make new connections and discoveries more easily.
  • Scientific Literacy: Promote a more informed population regarding the discoveries and challenges of space exploration.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Front-end: React (for the Web Application), with libraries like Three.js and Babylon.js (for rendering the interactive 3D celestial bodies).
  • Back-end: Python (Flask/Django) and Node.js (for API and data processing).
  • AI/Machine Learning: Python with libraries like TensorFlow/PyTorch and integration with LLM (Large Language Models) for adaptive response and article summarization.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and Supabase.
  • Design/Diagramming: Miro (used for mind mapping and design thinking), Canva (for presentation), and CapCut (for video editing).

How creative is your project?

The creativity resides in three pillars:

  1. Immersive Approach: Replacing traditional search with guided space exploration (navigating between Earth, Mars, and the Moon).
  2. Innovative Visualization: Using the celestial bodies themselves as a data interface, visually mapping scientific articles where they are most relevant.
  3. AI as a Mentor: The AI is not just a static chatbot, but a specialized scientific assistant that learns from the user, personalizing and refining responses to suit their knowledge level and interest.

What factors did your team consider?

The team considered the following essential factors:

  • Relevance and Impact: Ensuring the project provided information crucial to investors, scientists, and the general public.
  • User Experience (UX): Prioritizing an intuitive and simplified interface, transforming the complex into something engaging and easy to use.
  • Visualization Innovation: Seeking a new way to present scientific data that was more engaging than standard reports.
  • AI Utilization: Integrating AI not just as a feature, but as the heart of the search system, ensuring fast, contextual, and personalized answers.
  • Mission (Democratization): The main factor was honoring the mission to democratize space biological information.

Future Intentions:

  • Dynamic video to be generated for each question asked to the Artificial Intelligence.
  • Internally process user profile segments to make responses even more assertive for the target audience, thereby having the AI mold its answers.
  • Structured Back-end.
  • Expansion of the Database to also capture other segments of NASA research.
  • Adapt the 3D models' functionalities when the Artificial Intelligence responds to user questions.
  • Creation of Mind Maps in the answers given by Artificial Intelligence, according to the user profile
  • Accurate assessment based on public comments made on articles

projectDetails.name: Project Oceanopoly
projectDetails.summary:
Oceanopoly – A Game to Save the Oceans is a board game inspired by the classic Monopoly, but with a focus on environmental preservation. It educates players about the impacts of plastic pollution on the oceans and the challenges faced by global coastal areas, while promoting awareness-raising actions.

In the game, participants travel across a board representing real coastlines around the world, such as the Brazilian coast, the Great Barrier Reef, and Pacific islands. Each region starts with different levels of plastic pollution, and players must restore them by investing in sustainable solutions such as recycling, marine sanctuaries, and research.

Throughout the game, environmental events, such as increased pollution or volunteer actions, can change the course of the game. The dynamics combine competition and cooperation, challenging players to reduce pollution in areas while making strategic decisions that have a positive impact.

With educational potential and social impact, Oceanopoly is more than a game: it is a creative tool to engage diverse audiences in the fight for ocean preservation and to inspire real change in the world. 🌊♻️
projectDetails.details:
Oceanopoly Concept

An interactive board game where players take on the role of marine scientists, conservationists, or ocean resource managers. The goal is to explore and preserve the ocean, gain knowledge about marine ecosystems, and compete/cooperate to protect important species, such as sharks.

Game Elements

Game Board

Squares replacing traditional Monopoly properties, such as:

Global oceans (e.g., Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and the poles).

Marine ecosystems (corals, mangroves, abyssal zones, etc.).

Marine species (whales, turtles, corals, sharks, etc.).

Conservation projects (protected areas, plastic cleanup initiatives, etc.).

Divisions into thematic actions:

Spaces that provide educational challenges.

Spaces for “environmental events,” such as oil spills or global warming (negative impacts that need to be addressed).

Technology and innovation, where you can “create” scientific tools, such as tracking tags.

Pawns and Characters

Pawns in the shape of marine species (shark, whale, dolphin, turtle, and manatee) or research equipment (ROVs—remotely operated vehicles, submarines, etc.).

Players take on roles such as:

Marine researcher.

Oceanographer.

Environmental activist.

Ocean technology engineer.

Currency

Replace the use of money with the concept of ecosystem preservation or energy points.

Players “pay” or “earn” by contributing to conservation projects or solving environmental problems.

Gameplay

Purchasing regions: Players can purchase ecosystems (such as a coral reef or an abyssal area). Instead of building houses or hotels, they “invest” in conservation and research projects.

Luck and setback cards:

Luck: “Sponsorship received for conservation project,” “Tracking technology improves research.”

Setback: “Environmental disaster: microplastics in the ecosystem,” “Temperature rose and affected the corals.”

Mini interactive educational challenges at specific stops (e.g., questions about ecosystems and interesting facts about sharks).

Cooperation: Include cooperative missions (e.g., cleaning plastic from an ecosystem or protecting sharks from extinction).

Special Editions (Digital Case)

Create an interactive digital version (gamification):

Animated graphics showing real spatial data from NASA, such as ocean currents and marine habitats.

Immersive missions, such as:

Using “satellites” to track sharks and predict their habitats.

Create in-game tracking tags to develop real-time monitoring.

Global rankings to encourage players to compare their “conservation scores.”

Objective

The winner is not the one who “gets rich” the most, but the one who strengthens ecosystems, protects endangered species, and creates innovations for marine conservation the most. In this way, the game teaches the importance of cooperation and environmental responsibility.

Educational Benefits

Environmental awareness: Players learn about the challenges facing marine ecosystems and the impact of human activity.

Science and technology: The integration of spatial data and ideas such as tracking tags helps in understanding how modern science can aid in environmental preservation.

Strategic skills: Planning and decision-making to manage resources (scientific and ecological) in the game.

Value to the community: Promotes empathy for endangered species, such as sharks, by showing their crucial role in the oceans.

Practical Example – Inspiration for Luck/Setback Cards

Scientific Challenge:

“You have received satellite data showing that sharks have migrated to a new area. Track them to earn 50 conservation points.”

Environmental Event:

“An oil spill has occurred in your region: lose 30 conservation points. Help resolve it and earn double on the next turn.”

Innovation:

“Your new electronic tag model improves predator tracking. Earn 40 conservation points!”

Summary

Oceanopoly is a creative and educational way to raise awareness among future generations about the importance of marine conservation while they have fun and learn about science, technology, and sustainability. Depending on the format (board, digital, or both), the game can be optimized for greater global reach and educational impact! 🌍🎮

projectDetails.name: FloodMap
projectDetails.summary: Our project addresses the growing urban flooding problem caused by unplanned city expansion and inadequate drainage infrastructure. We developed a hydrodynamic simulation platform that integrates topographic data (from NASA SRTM), rainfall information (from NASA POWER), and urban land-use features to identify flood-prone areas with high spatial precision. By modeling water flow and accumulation under intense rainfall scenarios, the system generates interactive 3D maps that visualize potential inundation zones. This tool provides valuable insights for urban planners, supporting smarter decisions on land occupation, stormwater management, and the design of retention basins. The project contributes to building more resilient and sustainable cities, especially in regions like Brazil, where recurrent floods severely impact vulnerable communities.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – FloodMap

FloodMap is a simulation and visualization platform designed to identify flood-risk areas by combining topography, rainfall, land use, and urban drainage data. It processes NASA open datasets — such as GPM (precipitation) and SRTM (elevation) — along with local urban data to predict how water accumulates during heavy rain events.

How it works: FloodMap integrates GIS and machine learning to model water flow and display high-risk areas on an interactive map.

Benefits and impact: It supports urban planning and disaster prevention, helping governments and communities make faster, data-driven decisions to reduce damage and save lives.

Tools and technologies: Python, QGIS, TensorFlow, Leaflet.js, and NASA EarthData APIs.

Creativity: Combines real satellite data with predictive modeling and intuitive visualization.

Key considerations: Data accessibility, accuracy of simulations, scalability for different regions, and public usability.

projectDetails.name: Project Solar Whispers
projectDetails.summary: Solar Whispers is an interactive visual story for children and young audiences that explains what space weather is through characters representing elements like the Sun, solar wind, Earth's magnetosphere, and more. The story shows how solar flares, eruptions, and solar wind affect satellites, power grids, auroras, and our daily lives — all told from the perspective of "ears" that can hear the Sun speaking.
projectDetails.details:
Solar Whispers is an interactive digital storybook designed to introduce children and young audiences to the concept of space weather in a fun, visual, and accessible way. The story follows anthropomorphized elements of the Sun, solar wind, Earth's magnetic shield, and other space weather phenomena as characters in a playful narrative.

What does it do?
The storybook presents simplified, science-based explanations of how solar activity — such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar wind — can affect life on Earth. Through engaging visuals and friendly storytelling, it illustrates real-world effects like auroras, satellite disruption, and power outages in a way that younger audiences can easily understand. The project transforms complex scientific data into relatable, character-driven storytelling.
Makes space weather education approachable for K–12 students and general audiences. Promotes STEM interest through creative storytelling. Raises awareness of how space science connects with everyday technologies (GPS, electricity, communication). Can be used by educators in classrooms or outreach activities.

The goal is to demystify space weather and show its relevance to life on Earth. By inspiring curiosity at an early age, Solar Whispers supports long-term interest in space science and Earth–Sun relationships. It helps bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and public understanding through story.

The project creatively transforms scientific data into a narrative format by assigning personality and emotion to elements like the Sun, solar wind, and Earth's magnetic shield. The "ears that listen to the Sun" metaphor invites children to imagine a world where they can hear and feel space weather — making the invisible, visible.

challengeDetails.title: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings

projectDetails.name: Project Space_Girls
projectDetails.summary:
When the sky looks threatening, the truth is your
best defense.
projectDetails.details:
Asteroid Tracker: Your Window to Cosmic Truth

The Asteroid Tracker project, conceived by the innovative minds of Isabella Marinho, Isabelle Delmaschio, and Maria Fernanda Costa of the Space Girls group, emerges as a vital and enlightening response to a growing need in society: to understand and monitor celestial objects that cross our solar system. In a scenario where the sky can pose risks, the fundamental premise of the project is clear and powerful: “When the sky poses risks, the truth is your best defense.”

The Challenge: Navigating the “Meteor Madness”

We live in an age of constant information, but not always clarity, especially when it comes to astronomical phenomena that can generate concern or intense curiosity. The idea for “Asteroid Tracker” was born from the perception of “Meteor Madness,” the natural apprehension and fascination that these celestial bodies arouse. Often, the lack of accurate and accessible data can lead to misinformation or unfounded fears. The challenge, therefore, was to bridge the gap between the complexity of space science and the average citizen, offering transparency and verifiable knowledge.

The Innovative Solution: An App Within Everyone's Reach

Asteroid Tracker is not just a tool; it is a monitoring platform that empowers civil society with reliable information about asteroids and meteors. This intuitive and accessible app aims to demystify the universe around us by providing crucial data in a clear and understandable way for anyone. We believe that knowledge is the key to peace of mind and informed decision-making, and that is exactly what Asteroid Tracker aims to deliver.

The Essence of Reliability: Official NASA Data

The backbone of Asteroid Tracker's credibility lies in its data source. The app relies exclusively on information provided by NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration), the most prestigious and globally recognized space agency. This strategic choice ensures that all data presented to users is official, accurate, and constantly updated, eliminating any room for speculation or unverified information. The use of data such as that from asteroids 2024 YR4 and Vesta demonstrates the system's ability to integrate information about specific celestial bodies, bringing science directly to your device.

Detailed Information for Complete Understanding

To provide a comprehensive and detailed overview, Asteroid Tracker compiles and presents a series of essential attributes for each monitored asteroid or meteor. This information, extracted directly from NASA databases, includes:

Diameter: To give an idea of the object's size.

Mass: Offering insight into its composition and potential impact.

Speed: Essential for understanding the object's trajectory and dynamics in space.

Distance from Earth: One of the most critical pieces of data for assessing proximity and any potential risk.

Orbital Period: Provides information on the regularity of its movement around the Sun.

Imminent Danger: A clear and concise assessment of whether the object poses an imminent threat. This is a direct and crucial indicator for public safety.

Date of Discovery: Contextualizes when the object was first identified, demonstrating the constant vigilance of science.

Probability of Impact: Extremely relevant data that quantifies the risk of collision with Earth.

By centralizing these metrics, Asteroid Tracker not only informs but also educates, allowing users to understand what these numbers mean and how they relate to the safety of our planet. The language used in the app is designed to be accessible, transforming complex scientific data into understandable insights.

Impact on Civil Society: Awareness and Preparedness

Asteroid Tracker transcends the role of a mere informant; it positions itself as a guardian of collective awareness about our place in the cosmos. By offering unrestricted access to high-quality data on asteroids and meteors, the app empowers civil society to:

Understand Real Risks: Distinguish between potential threats and alarmism, based on scientific facts.

Monitor Astronomical Events: Closely follow the trajectory of celestial objects of interest.

Promote Science Education: Spark interest in astronomy and space sciences, encouraging continuous learning.

Ensure Transparency: Ensure that critical information about planetary safety is available to everyone.

In short, Asteroid Tracker is more than an app; it is an essential tool for the modern age, a beacon of reliable information that illuminates the mysteries of space and helps us keep our feet firmly planted on Earth while our eyes turn to the sky. It embodies the vision that, in the face of cosmic challenges, truth is indeed our best and most powerful defense.

projectDetails.name: Maya and the Sun Hiccups
projectDetails.summary:
Story Perspective and Character Development
The story uses the perspective of a person impacted by space weather by focusing on Maya, an 8-year-old farmer's assistant . This perspective is unique and relatable for elementary students.

Character Definition:

Name: Maya

Age: 8

What she does: Helps on a farm, checking soil and planting seeds (corn and sunflowers).

Connection to Space Weather: Her family's farm relies on GPS technology for planting, which is highly susceptible to solar disruptions.

Content and Educational Criteria
The story successfully integrates key scientific concepts in an age-appropriate and engaging manner.

Impacts on Earth (Varying Communities): The story explains how space weather affects multiple, distinct groups, fulfilling a core requirement of the competition:

Farmers (Local Impact): The primary challenge—the GPS disruption causes the tractor to plant in "wiggly snake maze" rows, wasting seeds and time. This is a direct, tangible impact on Maya's life and work.

Challenge & Resolution: Maya's challenge is the disrupted planting. The resolution involves checking the Space Weather Forecast and switching to "the old-fashioned way" of driving, showing how humans adapt to the unpredictable Sun.

Target Audience: The language ("Sun's Wild Hiccups," "wiggly snake maze," "big, noisy crowd yelling") is perfectly suited for elementary school students (the character's age range).
projectDetails.details:
Story Perspective and Character Development

The story uses the required perspective of a person impacted by space weather by focusing on Maya, an 8-year-old farmer's assistant . This perspective is unique and relatable for elementary students.

  • Character Definition:
    • Name: Maya
    • Age: 8
    • What she does: Helps on a farm, checking soil and planting seeds (corn and sunflowers).
    • Connection to Space Weather: Her family's farm relies on GPS technology for planting, which is highly susceptible to solar disruptions.

Content and Educational Criteria

The story successfully integrates key scientific concepts in an age-appropriate and engaging manner.

  • Definition of Space Weather: This is clearly introduced in Part 1 as the Sun having a "huge hiccup" (a Solar Flare) that "spits out huge clouds of energy and tiny particles."
    1. Farmers (Local Impact): The primary challenge—the GPS disruption causes the tractor to plant in "wiggly snake maze" rows, wasting seeds and time. This is a direct, tangible impact on Maya's life and work.
    2. Astronauts/Pilots (Atmospheric/Navigation Impact): Discusses the danger of invisible cosmic rain (particles) and disruption to communication/navigation systems.
    3. Electricians/Power Grid (Global Impact): Explains that a powerful event (a Coronal Mass Ejection, or CME) can cause a blackout, impacting everyday life (lights, computers, refrigerators).
    4. Photographers (Positive Impact): Includes the positive effect of the Aurora Borealis (Northern Lights), showing the full range of space weather results.

Storytelling and Visualization Elements

The narrative uses compelling storytelling and data visualization concepts to make the information understandable.

  • Illustrations/Visualization: The story explicitly calls for three instructional illustrations:
    • A friendly sun with a burst and arrow to Earth (Definition).
    • A tractor in a field showing the contrast between perfect straight rows and curvy, messy rows (The direct, negative impact on farming—an effective data visualization of GPS disruption).
    • A scene showing the aurora and a pilot/astronaut (The varying impacts on different professions).
  • Challenge & Resolution: Maya's challenge is the disrupted planting. The resolution involves checking the Space Weather Forecast and switching to "the old-fashioned way" of driving, showing how humans adapt to the unpredictable Sun.
  • Target Audience: The language ("Sun's Wild Hiccups," "wiggly snake maze," "big, noisy crowd yelling") is perfectly suited for elementary school students (the character's age range).

projectDetails.name: Vai Molhar Meus Planos?
projectDetails.summary: Our project is a personalized web platform that provides users with probabilities of specific weather conditions—such as being very hot, cold, windy, wet, or uncomfortable—for a given date, time, and location. Using NASA’s historical Earth observation data, the system analyzes past weather patterns to estimate the likelihood of certain conditions for future dates, rather than predicting them. Users can specify the purpose of their query, such as planning an outdoor wedding or a hiking trip, and the system, powered by AI, evaluates whether the expected conditions are favorable for that activity. Over time, the platform learns from user feedback, creating personalized comfort profiles to enhance accuracy and user experience. This project helps people make better-informed decisions for long-term outdoor planning, leveraging NASA’s open data to promote accessible and intelligent climate insights.
projectDetails.details:
The platform works by allowing users to log in, select a location, date, and time, and optionally specify an outdoor activity. It then retrieves and analyzes NASA’s historical climate datasets to calculate the probability of adverse conditions for that selection. When no specific activity is provided, the system asks users about their personal comfort level with the presented conditions, gradually building a personalized climate comfort profile.

The project was developed using a combination of web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and TypeScript, with machine learning algorithms assisting in pattern recognition and user preference analysis. We also used NASA’s Earth Science public data to obtain reliable environmental datasets.

The main benefit is enabling users to plan outdoor activities with greater confidence even for dates far in advance, where traditional forecasts are not available. Our project is innovative because it combines personalized AI-driven comfort analysis with statistical weather probability modeling, transforming NASA’s data into practical insights for everyday life.

About Us and Our Mission
We are The Demeter Code, a team passionate about solving real-world challenges at the intersection of technology, data, and sustainability. Our name is inspired by Demeter, the goddess of agriculture, and our mission: to "...

projectDetails.name: The Demeter Code
projectDetails.summary:
We developed FarmVerse, an educational strategy game that transforms planet Earth into an interactive agricultural laboratory. Unlike most farming games that offer fictional land, FarmVerse allows anyone, anywhere, to point to a location on the world map and explore its real agricultural potential, making decisions based on constantly updated, real-time data from NASA.

FarmVerse directly addresses the "NASA Farm Navigators" challenge by centralizing and integrating diverse NASA data in real-time. When a player selects a location, our platform retrieves information on the soil, climate, moisture, and nutrients for that specific area. This complex data is then translated into a gamified and intuitive game experience, teaching the user to make sustainable farming decisions based on real science.

The importance of FarmVerse lies in its ability to democratize and personalize Earth science data. It transforms previously abstract geospatial information into something personal and explorable. By allowing a user to study the agricultural potential of their own neighborhood or a region on the other side of the world, we have created an educational tool that inspires curiosity and teaches the value of space technology for building a more secure and sustainable food future for our planet.
projectDetails.details:
FarmVerse is a strategy and simulation game that transforms planet Earth into an interactive agricultural laboratory. The player's experience begins immersively with a 3D globe, where they can choose literally any location in the world to start their virtual farm. Once a point on the map is selected, our platform fetches and integrates real-time NASA data for that specific coordinate, presenting information on soil, climate, and moisture through a clear dashboard and a heat map that colors the terrain. Based on this information, the player dives into the management cycle: they must plant the most suitable virtual crops for the region, manage a budget, and react to dynamic events like droughts and heavy rains, simulated from real climate data.

The creativity of our project lies in its fundamental premise: instead of a fictional terrain, our game board is planet Earth itself. This hyper-localization approach creates a personal connection and sparks a curiosity that other games in the genre do not offer. We also innovate in the way data is presented, translating complex numbers into visual elements, like the colors that paint the terrain to indicate soil health. For our target audience of university students and small to medium-sized farmers, the benefits are direct: hands-on learning about cultivation, the development of data literacy for making efficient decisions, and a tangible understanding of how precise resource management promotes sustainability.

Our main objective is to create a bridge between NASA's complex space science and the hands of those who farm the land. The impact we seek is, first and foremost, to show that satellite data are practical and accessible tools, not just science fiction, thereby empowering a new generation to trust in technology. On a larger scale, by educating on more efficient and sustainable agricultural practices, FarmVerse aims to actively contribute to global food security.

Throughout the development process, the guiding factor for our decisions was the user experience. Aware that we were dealing with complex data, our challenge was to create an intuitive interface that makes the information understandable for a non-specialized audience. Therefore, we sought a balance between scientific realism and enjoyable gameplay, ensuring that FarmVerse is, above all, an accessible and inspiring educational tool.

For the development of FarmVerse, we utilized a combination of technologies focused on agility. The user interface was built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, while the experience design and prototyping were carried out in Figma. Our development environment was the TRAE IDE. Furthermore, to optimize our workflow, we relied on the support of AI assistants: Gemini AI, ChatGPT, and Copilot to accelerate research and coding, and the Eleven Labs platform for audio generation.

projectDetails.name: Project Trail Tale Flare
projectDetails.summary: Trail Tale Flare is an interactive narrative that explores the impact of solar storms and the role of the Sun in sustaining life. Through the adventures of an alien who crashes in the Amazon after a solar flare, the story brings together science, culture, and creativity. Together with Tainã, a local girl, the alien learns about space weather, biodiversity, and scientific solutions, highlighting the connection between worlds and the importance of cultural exchange and scientific awareness.
projectDetails.details:
Project Objective

To provide the public with an engaging experience that combines:

An understanding of solar storms, their impact on terrestrial technologies, and related phenomena such as the northern lights.

Awareness of the importance of the Sun for life on Earth and ecological cycles.

Appreciation of the cultural and environmental riches of the Amazon, promoting reflection on sustainability and nature.

Plot

Introduction

An alien, traveling in her spaceship through space, suffers an accident caused by intense solar waves and is forced to land on Earth, landing in the middle of the Amazon. Lost and unable to understand what happened, she meets Tainã, a curious local girl who is passionate about the forest and science.

Development

An adventure of learning and friendship:

Breakdown and theft of the ship: While exploring the forest with Tainã, the alien discovers that her ship has been stolen, beginning a search for answers and solutions.

Inspiring characters:

Photographers who capture the natural beauty of the Amazon and show the effects of the Sun in the skies, such as auroras and light phenomena.

Scientists and astronomers who explain in an accessible way the effects of solar storms on terrestrial technology and biodiversity.

Wisdom of the local community, which reveals the deep spiritual and ecological connection with the Sun and nature.

Discovering science: As they learn about solar phenomena and the role of the Sun, the alien and Tainã realize how science and technology can help solve global problems.

Outcome

The journey culminates in the recovery of the alien's spacecraft, with the help of the local community and the new friends she has made on Earth. As she departs for her planet, the alien takes with her a newfound respect for the beauty and complexity of Earth and the role of the Sun, while Tainã and the scientists are inspired by the possibilities of clean and sustainable technology.

Scientific Concepts Covered

Solar storms:

How solar flares and solar winds impact technologies (navigation systems, satellites, and communications).

Aurora phenomena (boreal and austral), caused by the interaction of solar wind with Earth's magnetic field.

The importance of the Sun:

Photosynthesis as the basis of life on Earth.

Ecological cycles, renewable energy, and impact on tropical forests.

Space weather education:

Use of models and smartphones to predict and minimize the impacts of space weather on Earth.

Cultural and Environmental Elements

Amazonian Culture:

Legends about the Sun and its relationship with the cosmos, told by local communities.

The Amazonian view of nature conservation, highlighting the impact of the Sun on local life cycles.

Photography and Art:

Photographers who document the rich biodiversity and starry skies of the Amazon, connecting science and visual inspiration.

Collaboration between worlds:

The relationship between the alien and Tainã represents the exchange of cultures, highlighting the importance of collaboration, unity, and mutual learning.

Implementation and Presentation Formats

The project can be presented in a multimodal way, reaching different audiences through creative formats:

Illustrated e-book:

A digital narrative rich in images that explains both the adventure and the scientific concepts.

Interactive animation:

A short film or interactive animation that shows the impact of solar storms and allows the audience to follow the characters' journey.

Educational platform:

A website or app with educational materials based on the story, addressing science, culture, and sustainability.

Project Impacts

Creative scientific dissemination:

Explaining complex concepts such as space weather using simple language connected to a captivating story.

Environmental awareness:

Promoting a message of Amazon rainforest preservation and the importance of the Sun for ecosystems.

Connection between science and culture:

Inspire young people and adults to see science as part of our daily lives and as a powerful tool for understanding and transformation.

Team and Skills

Our team is made up of individuals with diverse backgrounds, bringing different perspectives and expertise to the project:

Screenwriters and designers: Creation of the storyline and development of striking illustrations.

Educators and scientists: Translation of complex concepts about space weather and the Sun into accessible learning.

Communicators and storytellers: Clear and engaging communication to broaden the project's reach and captivate the audience.

🌍 Conclusion

Trail Tale Flare is a story that blends imagination, science, and culture to explain how space phenomena can directly impact our daily lives while reinforcing the importance of the Sun and biodiversity. The narrative inspires collaboration and mutual learning while educating about space weather and the unique vitality of planet Earth.

These technologies were integrated as creative and technical support resources, allowing for greater efficiency in project development and enhancing the quality of the material produced. projectDetails.summary: Solution to mitigate heat islands in São José do Rio Preto using NASA data, expanding green areas, sustainable infrastructure, and community engagement to improve the urban microclimate.
projectDetails.details:
1. Contextualization

What are thermal refuge spaces?

Thermal refuge spaces are urban areas designed to provide thermal comfort and reduce the impact of extreme temperatures. These spaces include:

Trees and vegetation: They provide shade and cool the environment through evapotranspiration.

Interactive water features: Such as fountains and reflecting pools, which create cooler areas due to evaporation.

Adapted urban infrastructure: Use of less heat-absorbing materials (cool pavement, reflective benches, light-colored areas).

Accessibility for local residents: Designed for well-being, with benches, inclusive access, and located where there is greater movement or vulnerability to heat.

Why São José do Rio Preto?

São José do Rio Preto, with its hot and dry climate, suffers even more from heat islands due to:

High urban density and reduction of green areas in central neighborhoods.

Predominance of urban materials that retain heat, such as concrete and asphalt.

Scarcity of adequate green spaces in areas such as commercial or high-density residential neighborhoods.

Focusing on the creation of thermal refuge spaces will allow for the redesign of the urban microclimate, improving quality of life in the short and medium term and offering a visually attractive and functional solution.

2. Project Objectives

Identify climate hotspots in São José do Rio Preto (areas with the greatest need for thermal refuge, with high population density, low vegetation, and high temperatures).

Design practical interventions that create thermal comfort zones for communities.

Propose sustainable actions based on Earth observation data and urban planning.

3. Project Structure

3.1. Identification of Hotspots

To determine priority locations for thermal refuge spaces, use specific geospatial data and urban indicators:

Land surface temperature (LST):

MODIS or Landsat data to identify areas with higher temperatures.

Indicates vegetation density and helps locate regions with low green coverage.

Identifies urbanized areas and assesses the impact of urbanization.

Rely on urban maps and local information to focus on areas with high foot traffic (e.g., shopping centers, public transportation terminals).

Expected results: A map that combines temperature, vegetation, and population density indices to prioritize critical areas.

3.2. Developing Solutions for Shelters

After identifying the points of greatest thermal vulnerability, it is time to design solutions adapted to the local context. Here are some proposals:

Fundamental Elements of a Thermal Shelter

Green Areas and Tree Planting

Planting large trees (e.g., ipês, sibipirunas) on sidewalks, squares, and bus terminals.

Green roofs and walls on nearby buildings.

Use of native vegetation adapted to the region's climate (low irrigation requirements).

Examples of impact: A mature tree can reduce temperatures by around 2°C to 9°C.

Installation of fountains, water mirrors, or public drinking fountains that generate cool microclimates through evaporation.

Automated irrigation systems to maintain flower beds and vegetated areas.

Replacing dark paving (asphalt) with light-colored surfaces and materials with high thermal reflectivity.

E.g.: Permeable concrete and light-colored tiles.

Inclusion of recycled wood benches in shaded areas.

Pedestrian shelters with high coverage and natural ventilation.

Installation of temporary covers in open spaces, such as squares and terminals.

3.3. Community Integration

Involving the local community in the use, maintenance, and appreciation of spaces is fundamental to the success of the project. You can:

Map local contributions: Create an app or form for residents to point out “hot” spots in the city or suggest spaces for installing shelters.

Environmental awareness: Conduct educational campaigns on the benefits of trees, green spaces, and sustainable behaviors.

3.4. Technologies and Prototyping

You can present a working prototype to demonstrate the feasibility of the project. Some ideas:

Interactive map of hotspots and planned solutions:

Use tools such as Google Earth Engine, QGIS, or Esri ArcGIS to develop maps that combine temperatures, vegetation density, and critical regions.

Develop 2D/3D models with tools such as SketchUp or Figma, showing how thermal shelters will be implemented.

A simple website or app for residents to view proposed interventions and track temperature and vegetation results.

projectDetails.name: Unified Exoplanet Classifier (UEC)
projectDetails.summary:
The volume of data generated by exoplanet-hunting satellites is growing exponentially, creating a strategic challenge for science: the validation of planet candidates. This process is currently fragmented, requiring researchers to master different specialized tools for each dataset produced by satellites such as Kepler and TESS, making it manual, slow, and inefficient.
Our mission with this project is to develop the Unified Exoplanet Classifier (UEC), a unified AI-based software platform designed to automate and enhance the validation of exoplanet candidates. The UEC aims to accelerate scientific discovery, standardize astronomical analyses, and make the validation process more efficient, accurate, and accessible to the research community.
By inputting the parameters of an object believed to be an exoplanet, the UEC links this information to NASA mission datasets and provides supporting visualizations such as the corresponding light curve. The data are then submitted to the appropriate expert model via API, and the platform returns the classification — CONFIRMED or FALSE POSITIVE — with high performance (for instance, over 95.0% F1-Score for TESS mission data).
In this way, the UEC facilitates the prioritization of new targets for studies, follow-up observations, and the publication of scientific results with greater speed and reliability.
projectDetails.details:
The Unified Exoplanet Classifier (UEC) is designed to serve as a facilitator in exoplanet research and validation. By entering parameters of an object believed to be an exoplanet, the system integrates this information with NASA satellite data and provides supportive visualizations, such as the corresponding light curve, aiding in data analysis and interpretation.

Through the UEC interface, users can select their research data source, filter by parameters of interest, or explore previous models and discoveries, expanding opportunities for comparison and learning within the platform. Using examples such as Kepler-186f, users can manually input parameters for customized analysis. By clicking “Classify Objects,” the UEC automatically processes the data and delivers precise results quickly.

Possible outcomes include:

  • Confirmed Exoplanet – the analyzed parameters match those of an already confirmed exoplanet;
  • Exoplanet Candidate – the data indicate a given probability of being an exoplanet;
  • False Positive – the parameters suggest the object does not meet the necessary criteria to be classified as an exoplanet.

Based on these results, users can refine parameters, plan follow-up observations, and support future missions aimed at verifying and studying potential exoplanets.

According to the images below:

Results:

The result may be Confirmed Exoplanet, which means that the analyzed parameters, based on the selected data source, correspond to an exoplanet already confirmed.

The result may also be Exoplanet Candidate, indicating that the parameters analyzed, according to the chosen dataset, have a certain percentage likelihood of being an exoplanet.

Finally, the result could be False Positive, meaning that the analyzed parameters, based on the chosen data source, resemble an exoplanet but do not meet the necessary criteria for confirmation due to inconsistencies or noise in the data.

Lastly, from the results provided by the model, the user can review the obtained parameters, adjust them as needed, and use them to conduct deeper studies, plan complementary observations, and support future missions targeting the possible identified exoplanet.

projectDetails.name: Project Araranauts
projectDetails.summary:
Our project is a colony management game focused on building and maintaining space habitats on distant planets. The player begins with a small crew aboard a mothership with limited resources—food, water, oxygen, and power—and must construct essential structures to ensure survival and happiness.

By simulating the complexity of off-world settlement management, the game raises awareness about the challenges of sustaining human life in space, such as energy distribution, oxygen production, and habitat design. It combines strategic thinking with scientific concepts, promoting understanding of space colonization, sustainability, and human resilience beyond Earth.

projectDetails.summary:
Space Weather – Interactive Educational Game
Embark on an educational adventure that blends science and fun to teach about
space weather! This interactive game offers a progressive experience divided into
three unlockable stages. In the first stage, players explore immersive stories through
three distinct characters: Sofia, an astronaut facing solar radiation in space; João, a
farmer monitoring how solar storms affect his crops on Earth; and Ana, a pilot
navigating the skies during space weather events. Each story is divided into visual
chapters with illustrative images and scientific information about solar phenomena
such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and geomagnetic storms.
After completing all three stories, players unlock a quiz with questions about the
concepts they’ve learned, testing their knowledge of space weather. Finally, upon
completing the quiz, a mini-game is unlocked — a dynamic experience where players
must collect beneficial objects (shields, energy, stars) while avoiding dangerous ones
(meteors, fire, explosions), using a protective shield strategically.
The game is available in three languages (English, Portuguese, and Spanish) and
features a captivating space-themed design with star animations, floating planets,
and space weather elements, creating a complete educational experience about how
the Sun impacts our planet and our daily lives.

projectDetails.name: Echos In Data
projectDetails.summary:
Echoes In Data is a unified machine learning platform that transforms raw exoplanet data from NASA missions such as Kepler, TESS, and K2 into ready-to-use insights.
The project directly addresses the challenge “A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI” by automating the complex and time-consuming steps of data preprocessing, feature selection, and model training.
Through an accessible interface, users can visualize data compatibility, train AI models, and generate predictions — all within one environment.
By leveraging open NASA datasets, the platform enables researchers, students, and enthusiasts to explore planetary candidates more efficiently and collaboratively.
Why it matters: Echoes In Data bridges the gap between raw data and discovery, democratizing access to exoplanet research and empowering a new generation of scientists to accelerate the search for worlds beyond our own.
projectDetails.details:
Echoes In Data unifies raw astronomical data from NASA missions such as Kepler, TESS, and K2, transforming it into an accessible machine learning workflow. The platform automates the key stages of data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, and validation, allowing users to move from raw CSV files to meaningful exoplanet predictions in a single environment.

The interface provides visual feedback on model performance and data compatibility, empowering users to understand, compare, and refine results — even without advanced coding experience.

Developed with Python (pandas, scikit-learn) and an HTML-based visualization layer, the project embodies an open science approach, using public datasets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

Its benefits include faster analysis, reproducible workflows, and a lower barrier of entry for researchers, students, and enthusiasts. The intended impact is to democratize access to exoplanet research, enabling global collaboration in data-driven astronomy.

Creatively, the team designed Echoes In Data to merge automation and education — combining real NASA data with AI models that explain their reasoning through visual outputs.

We focused on scalability, transparency, and accessibility, considering both the scientific needs of researchers and the learning potential for students who dream of discovering worlds beyond our own.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence tools were used solely to support the development process, not to generate core content or scientific results.

  • Text and Ideation: We used AI language models (e.g., ChatGPT) to refine written communication and improve clarity in our project documentation and slide deck. All technical and scientific content was created and validated by our team.
  • Code Assistance: AI was used to accelerate coding efficiency (syntax checks, debugging suggestions) within Python, but the entire data pipeline, ML logic, and visualization scripts were designed, implemented, and tested by the team.
  • No AI-generated media: All visuals and interface designs were original and did not use AI image or video generation tools. No NASA logos, mission identifiers, or branding elements were used or modified.

Our use of AI focused on enhancing productivity and communication, while ensuring all conceptual, scientific, and technical work remained original and human-directed.
