projectDetails.name: Project Climáticos
projectDetails.summary:
Our project presents an educational pixel art animation, hand-drawn and created using only free mobile platforms, that transforms real NASA data into an engaging narrative about the planet. The work combines time-lapses of forests, wildfires, smoke trails, and surface and air comparisons, based on data from the Terra satellite instruments, which this year celebrates its 25th mission anniversary.

The story is narrated as if the satellite itself were telling its experiences over the decades, showing the impact of human activities on the environment and the importance of science in monitoring the planet. The animation blends news segments, reports, and symbolic scenes, contextualizing natural disasters, deforestation, and climate change in different regions.

More than just portraying scientific data, the project aims to translate information into emotion, raising awareness about environmental preservation and inspiring positive actions for the future of Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction


NASA's Terra satellite, in operation for 25 years, is the oldest daily Earth observation satellite and has accumulated over 9,000 days of data, including simultaneous images from five scientific instruments: ASTER, CERES, MISR, MODIS, and MOPITT. This data allows us to study everything from global scientific processes to local environmental events that affect human life.

The project uses this data to create an educational animation that primarily shows the impact of fires and pollution on the world, with a focus on Brazil. We believe that the combination of pixel art, animation, and scientific data can convey the power of environmental awareness, collaboration, and hope in an accessible and visual way.

Exploring the Project Animation


The animation begins with a cat on a sofa who, as he moves, turns on the television. The screen displays the first newspaper, dated December 19, 1999, announcing the launch of the Terra satellite, the first in NASA’s Earth Observing System, with five tools that will allow us to monitor and better understand the planet. The newspaper serves na important role: to historically contextualize the mission and show the public the value of scientific monitoring.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

The animation presents a time-lapse from 2000 to 2025, showing the evolution of data collected by four of the Terra satellite’s instruments: MODIS, MOPITT, CERES, and MISR. This scene aims to demonstrate the magnitude and relevance of scientific monitoring, revealing patterns that would otherwise go unnoticed.[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]



The animation focuses on specific events observed by the Terra satellite, emphasizing the impacts of climate change and human activity on the planet. In Rio Grande do Sul, Terra satellite data records significant climate events, such as the 2024 floods. The extratropical cyclones that hit the east coast of India (2019), the state of Odisha, and southern Bangladesh, highlighting the increasing intensity and frequency of these disasters. The animation then highlights the Puyehue volcano in Chile, whose 2011 eruption released a massive ash cloud that crossed the border into Argentina, causing evacuations and the suspension of flights in the region. These episodes reinforce the essential role of the Terra satellite in monitoring natural phenomena and preventing risks on a continental scale.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]
The scene then shifts to a burning forest. The narrator describes how the fires compromise air quality and then highlights the impacts of this phenomenon on the Amazon rainforest, reinforcing the gravity of the environmental situation depicted. The pixel art images show data collected by the MODIS and MOPITT instruments.[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]
As the climate warms, the air in the forest becomes drier and rivers begin to shrink, as shown in ASTER satellite imagery. This scenario increases the risk of wildfires, turning small fires into large blazes. The material also warns that, with the continued loss of vegetation, the Amazon is approaching a point of no return—a situation in which it would no longer be able to regenerate.

The video concludes by emphasizing that this problem is not exclusive to the Amazon region, but rather a reflection of a global environmental crisis that demands immediate action. The final message conveys hope, reinforcing that, even in the face of chaos, there is still the possibility of renewal. The narrator closes with a call for collective responsibility, reminding us that the planet’s recovery depends on everyone’s collaboration so that, in the future, the Earth can shine again.

What exactly does it do?

The project is na educational animation/documentary that transforms scientific data from the Terra satellite into a visual narrative. It shows the spread of fires, smoke trails, and climate change in Brazil over 25 years, personifying the satellite as the story’s narrator. The animation also includes news-style segments and bilingual subtitles.

How does it work?

Terra data (MODIS, MOPITT, CERES, MISR) is processed and transformed into graphical visualizations, time-lapses, and interactive maps. The narrative combines this information with audio, narration, and video editing, creating na immersive experience that guides the viewer through the environmental impact of wildfires and global warming.

What are the benefits?

• Raising environmental awareness about fires and climate change.

• Accessible science education for different audiences.

• Clear visualization of real data from the Terra satellite, facilitating the understanding of complex phenomena.

• Encouraging actions to preserve and mitigate environmental impacts.

What do you hope to achieve?

• Engaging the public with a compelling narrative based on real data.

• Demonstrating how space science contributes to protecting Earth.

• Providing educational information that encourages conscious attitudes toward climate change.

Conclusion
Our project presents na animated experience that combines science, art, and storytelling to raise awareness about the environmental impacts of fires and pollution in Brazil. By transforming data from the Terra satellite into engaging animations, we demonstrate that each pixel can tell a story and inspire change, uniting creativity and purpose to protect the planet. Using technology to our advantage, we can predict and estimate natural and human-caused disasters, thus helping people take preventive measures to protect both themselves and the Earth.

Behind the Scenes
During the project’s development, we faced significant challenges related to artistic creation, as all the animation and pixel art was hand-crafted using only free mobile platforms. Furthermore, some NASA websites and databases were experiencing temporary outages, making it difficult to access real-time information. Even with these limitations, we were able to leverage the available data and maintain scientific fidelity, creating na educational, engaging, and visually appealing narrative.

Technical Details

Software & Tools: CapCut, FlipaClip, and Ibis Paint

Animation Approach: 2D/3D time-lapses combining data layers, storytelling, and retro pixel art aesthetics.

Narrative Technique: News and report-style segments explaining environmental impacts and possible solutions.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmic Voyager
projectDetails.summary: Cosmic Voyager is an app created for the “Meteor Madness” challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Developed by a creative team on the Lovable platform, the project aims to bring knowledge about meteors and the universe in an interactive, educational, and fun way. The idea arose from the need to bring the public, especially young people, closer to the world of astronomy and the space threats that can impact Earth. With a modern approach, Cosmic Voyager combines technology, fiction, and science to make the user experience immersive and engaging. The project aims to spark interest in space, promote awareness of cosmic events, and show, in an accessible way, how we can learn and prepare for these phenomena.
projectDetails.details:
The Cosmic Voyager app brings together various features to explore the universe and the dangers of meteors.

An AI chat named Robert, which talks with users and answers questions about meteors, planets, and space.

A meteor impact simulation on Earth, where the user can choose the meteor's size and speed and see the effects in real time.

A Earth defense game, challenging players to protect the planet from collisions using strategies and science.

A solar system trivia tab, with interesting facts about planets, moons, and space objects.

A fun and educational quiz to test the user's knowledge of the universe.

The "History of Cosmic Voyage" section, a fictional narrative that tells the origin of the mission, the characters, and the challenges faced by humanity in defending the planet.The app blends entertainment, education, and awareness into a unique experience about the cosmos.

projectDetails.name: Project CyberStorm
projectDetails.summary:
Of course. Here is the English version of the project summary.

StormTracker is a web platform designed to simplify decision-making for outdoor activities. Our project is a functional prototype that, instead of merely presenting raw weather data, analyzes and translates it into a clear recommendation. It uses our custom "Weather Comfort Index" (WCI), an algorithm that evaluates whether conditions are ideal for specific activities like picnics, hikes, or running.

The project addresses the challenge by creatively using open Earth data—specifically, forecast data from Open-Meteo and geolocation from OpenStreetMap—to create a tool with a direct impact on people's daily lives.

Its importance lies in democratizing access to climate information, making it understandable and actionable for the general public. StormTracker empowers users to plan their activities with greater safety and confidence, reducing the risks associated with adverse weather conditions and encouraging a more active lifestyle connected to nature.
projectDetails.details:
Planning outdoor activities often feels like a gamble. Standard weather forecasts provide complex data but fail to answer a simple question: "Is it a good day for my specific plan?"

StormTracker is our solution.

This smart weather advisor transforms raw climate data into clear, actionable advice. Simply enter a location, date, and your chosen activity—like a hike or picnic.

Powered by open data from Open-Meteo and OpenStreetMap, our unique algorithm calculates a "Weather Comfort Index" (WCI). This score provides an instant recommendation, telling you whether to go ahead, be cautious, or reschedule.

With StormTracker, you no longer have to guess. You can make smarter, safer decisions and plan your adventures with confidence.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools (specifically ChatGPT by OpenAI) to assist in brainstorming ideas, refining the user interface design, and writing portions of the code for the StormTracker web application.

AI was used as a collaborative assistant to accelerate development and improve clarity in project documentation and presentation text.

No NASA branding, copyrighted material, or mission identifiers were created or modified using AI.

All datasets and APIs used in the project (NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, and OpenStreetMap) are real and public.

The AI was not used to generate images, videos, or audio for this project.

projectDetails.name: FireWatch
projectDetails.summary:
We have developed an interactive educational experience that uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to explore South America and highlight the critical issue of fires. The platform allows the public to visualize, in real-time, where they are occurring, as well as observe the landscape and fire damage through the unique perspective of SAR.

The project addresses the challenge of low public awareness by translating complex satellite data into an accessible and engaging interface. In it, we not only map fire scars and monitor deforestation, but we also explain the causes of these events, illustrating the human and environmental factors that drive them.

The importance of the project lies in the use of SAR technology, which offers continuous, high-fidelity, day and night monitoring, providing an objective view of the destruction. By combining advanced technology with an educational narrative, our goal is to inform and raise awareness about these fires, and ultimately, offer tools that show the risk of a fire occurring in a specific area and calculate its chance of spreading.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction

Our project is an interactive educational platform that uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to visualize and explain the causes and effects of fires in South America, making complex satellite information accessible to the public.

How it works

Our project is an interactive, real-time educational experience that translates complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into an intuitive and engaging visual interface. Through this platform, the public can visualize where fires are occurring in real-time across South America while also using the unique capabilities of SAR to observe the extent of past fire scars and monitor associated deforestation. Beyond simply displaying data, the tool provides a crucial educational narrative that explains the human and environmental factors causing these fires. Furthermore, the project aims to incorporate predictive analysis tools that can calculate the fire risk level in a specific area and model its potential to spread, evolving from a monitoring platform into a preventative resource.

Benefits

The project's main benefits stem from its innovative use of SAR technology and its focus on public accessibility. A key advantage is its all-weather, 24/7 monitoring; unlike traditional optical satellites, SAR can see through clouds, smoke, and darkness, providing continuous, high-fidelity data. This capability yields an unfiltered, objective view of the destruction on the ground, creating a powerful and unbiased record of events. Crucially, the project's commitment to accessibility transforms this highly technical scientific data into an easy-to-understand format, empowering the general public with critical knowledge that was previously confined to experts.

Impact

The project's core mission is to inform and raise public awareness about the critical threat of fires in South America. By demystifying the data and telling the story behind the destruction, we aim to foster a deeper public understanding of the causes and devastating consequences of these events. This enhanced awareness is intended to encourage proactive engagement in conservation and prevention efforts. Ultimately, the goal is to provide communities and decision-makers with accessible tools to assess risk and mitigate future disasters, turning information into action.

Conclusion

In conclusion, this project serves as a vital bridge between advanced satellite technology and public consciousness. By leveraging the all-weather, objective power of Synthetic Aperture Radar, it transforms complex data from a tool for experts into an accessible narrative for everyone. The platform moves beyond simple monitoring, aiming not only to document the reality of environmental destruction but to foster the understanding and engagement necessary for meaningful conservation. Ultimately, its purpose is to shift the narrative from reaction to foresight, providing the critical tools needed to anticipate, mitigate, and prevent future devastation before it begins.

Technical Details

The development was carried out in JavaScript, using Visual Studio Code as the development environment, with support from fundamental web technologies such as HTML5 and CSS3. For the rendering and manipulation of 3D elements, the Three.js library was used.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used AIs such as Gemini, Copilot, and GPT models throughout several phases of the project, including for assistance with coding, text refinement, and translation. We also used the CapCut AI to narrate our project demonstration.

challengeDetails.title: Through the Radar Looking Glass: Revealing Earth Processes with SAR
challengeDetails.excerpt: Like Alice in Wonderland, let’s travel down the rabbit hole to reveal a world that looks like our planet Earth… but not quite! Using synthetic aperture radar (SAR), we can image the world by emitting radar pulses toward Earth and recording the energy that is reflected back after the signals interact with Earth's surface. Your challenge is to download multi-frequency or multi-polarization SAR data for an interesting study area of your choice –e.g., your hometown, a tropical wetland, ice sheet, forest wildfire, flooded neighborhood, volcano eruption, etc.—and use that data to develop hypotheses about the physical drivers operating there. (Earth Science Division)

challengeDetails.title: Embiggen Your Eyes!
challengeDetails.excerpt: While your cell phone screen can display about three million pixels of information and your eye can receive more than ten million pixels, NASA images from space are even bigger! NASA’s space missions continue to push the boundaries of what is technologically possible, providing high-resolution images and videos of Earth, other planets, and space with billions or even trillions of pixels. Your challenge is to create a platform that allows users to zoom in and out on these massive image datasets, label known features, and discover new patterns. (Astrophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: Solar Impact Simulator X2084
projectDetails.summary:
The X2084 Solar Impact Simulator is an online application designed to simulate asteroid collisions with various planets and moons in our Solar System. The central idea of ​​the project is to gather astronomical and geological information from reliable sources, such as NASA and the U.S. Geological Survey, enabling accurate analyses of potential impacts and defense plans.

With this tool, you can adjust several important physical characteristics, such as the asteroid's size, weight, velocity, and entry angle. It also allows you to select specific targets, such as planets or satellites. You can also use real-world asteroids, such as Vesta, for simulations based on real data.

The system aims to aid decision-making in dangerous situations by offering an easy-to-use interface for municipal managers, civil defense agencies, and scientists to analyze different scenarios for the impact, evacuation, and destruction of near-Earth objects.

Thus, the project seeks to solve the problem presented in the “Impactor-2025” case, offering an interactive and scientifically based way to visualize, study and plan response actions to asteroid impact threats.
projectDetails.details:
O Simulador de Impacto Solar X2084 é uma ferramenta interativa de cunho científico e educativo, que possibilita aos utilizadores:

Funcionalidades Essenciais:
a) Simulação de Colisões com Asteroides:
Possibilidade de arremessar asteroides configuráveis para qualquer planeta do Sistema Solar
Ajuste de atributos realistas: dimensão (10m-10.000m), velocidade (5-70 km/s), material (rocha/metal)
Cálculo físico exato da energia cinética: E = 0.5 × massa × velocidade²
Visualização tridimensional em tempo real, utilizando Three.js com renderização WebGL
b) Conjunto de 8 Planetas Interativos:
Cada planeta apresentando atributos singulares: força da gravidade, atmosfera, diâmetro, natureza (rochoso/gasoso)
Modelos tridimensionais processuais com texturas criadas via algoritmos (crateras, faixas atmosféricas, polos congelados)
Planetas inclusos: Mercúrio, Vénus, Terra, Marte, Júpiter, Saturno, Urano, Netuno

QUAIS VANTAGENS OBTEMOS?

No âmbito Educacional:
Maior percepção das verdadeiras ameaças do espaço que a humanidade enfrenta.
Um jeito divertido de aprender sobre física orbital e como corpos celestes se movem.
Facilidade em entender as proporções gigantescas do universo (distâncias, forças, tamanhos).
Conhecimento sobre sistemas planetários usando dados científicos de verdade.

No campo Científico:
Apresentação de como a defesa do planeta está sendo planejada hoje (como a missão DART da NASA).
Mostrar, de forma visual, o que pode acontecer após um impacto, baseado em modelos da ciência.
Análise de qual tecnologia funciona melhor para evitar desastres.

Na área de Jogos:
Um jeito de ganhar prêmios que estimula a descobrir e aprender.
Avançar ao superar desafios que ensinam ideias científicas.
Ver e entender o que acontece, com números e imagens, para fixar o aprendizado.

QUAL A MUDANÇA QUE O PROJETO QUER GERAR?

Na Sociedade:
Fazer com que mais pessoas, de todas as idades, se interessem por astronomia e pelo espaço.
Tornar as ameaças do espaço mais claras e fáceis de entender para todos.
Incentivar a conversa sobre como proteger o planeta como um problema de todos.

Na Educação:
Uma forma de os professores de física e astronomia mostrarem ideias complicadas na prática.
Aprender fazendo, em vez de só ouvir (aprender na prática).
Ver o que acontece torna as ideias mais fáceis de entender.

projectDetails.name: R.I.C.A
projectDetails.summary: The RICA system (Robotic Intelligent Circular Assistant) was designed as a comprehensive solution for the sustainable management of inorganic waste in extraterrestrial environments, particularly on Mars. Its core purpose is to eliminate the traditional concept of “trash,” transforming all discarded material into reusable resources within a closed-loop production cycle. RICA serves as the central hub of a self-sufficient survival infrastructure, enabling human missions in Jezero Crater to maintain operational capacity for extended periods without relying on resupply from Earth. Through its modular architecture, the system can collect, identify, process, and convert waste into new materials for immediate use—from 3D printing filaments to structural blocks and useful chemical compounds. This represents a revolution in the concept of sustainability beyond Earth, where every gram of material is precious and must be reused to ensure the continuity of human missions.
projectDetails.details:
HOW DOES IT WORK?

RICA operates semi-autonomously, integrating multiple processing modules into a closed-loop recycling circuit. Its structure consists of five interconnected subsystems: automated sorting, thermal and chemical processing, mechanical recycling, additive manufacturing, and a digital materials bank. The process begins with the Automated Sorting Module, where optical and near-infrared (NIR) sensors identify waste types based on their spectral properties. Embedded artificial intelligence continuously learns, improving its recognition and categorization capabilities. Next, the Thermal and Chemical Processing Module performs complex transformations: pyrolysis converts plastics into gases and fuel oils; supercritical water oxidation (SCWO) breaks down organic compounds, recovering pure water and useful gases. The Mechanical Recycling Module melts metals and extrudes polymers to create recyclable filaments, while the Additive Manufacturing Module uses 3D printers to fabricate utensils, tools, and structural components. Finally, the Materials Bank maintains a digital record of all available resources, ensuring traceability and logistical efficiency.

WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS?

RICA offers multiple benefits that impact both environmental sustainability and the operational viability of human missions. First, the system drastically reduces the need for supply transport from Earth, resulting in significant logistical and energy savings. It also promotes crew autonomy, ensuring that essential materials can be continuously regenerated. Another key benefit is psychological: the creative reuse of waste enables the production of comfort items, celebratory elements, and personalized tools—essential for astronaut well-being in isolated environments. There are also substantial technological gains—processes like pyrolysis, solar fusion, and SCWO contribute to the advancement of clean technologies applicable on Earth as well.

WHAT DO YOU HOPE TO ACHIEVE?

RICA’s primary goal is to achieve total self-sufficiency in human missions to Mars. This means creating a system where all resources are continuously regenerated, enabling infinite production cycles and minimizing external dependencies. Additionally, the project aims to establish a replicable model for future space colonies—a circular infrastructure applicable to the Moon, asteroids, and other celestial bodies. The knowledge gained from RICA is also expected to serve as a foundation for developing high-efficiency recycling systems on Earth, enhancing urban and industrial sustainability. Ultimately, the project seeks to demonstrate that circular economies are viable in any environment—even beyond our planet.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, AND HARDWARE USED

RICA’s development integrates a highly complex technological ecosystem. At the software level, the system uses languages like Python and C++ for autonomous module control and sensor data processing. Machine learning models were trained for spectral recognition using frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch. The physical architecture includes high-precision optical sensors, hyperspectral cameras, and robotic actuators for material handling in pressurized environments. The 3D printers operate with multiple extruders for polymers and metals, while the thermal modules are powered by concentrated solar energy and high-efficiency microwaves. The entire system is overseen by an intelligent interface that integrates local and remote control, allowing adjustments via communication with Earth-based command centers.

USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)

Artificial Intelligence is the operational core of RICA. It enables automated waste recognition, recycling process optimization, and adaptive learning based on the environment and available materials. AI uses convolutional neural networks for image and spectral analysis, classifying waste based on composition, density, and reflectance. Additionally, predictive control algorithms adjust temperature, pressure, and energy consumption in real time across processing modules. Continuous learning also enables autonomous maintenance, with the system identifying faults, reorganizing routines, and optimizing robotic handling paths. In essence, AI transforms RICA into a cognitive support entity that learns to operate as a fully independent robotic recycling team.

NASA DATA, PARTNER AGENCIES, AND OTHER SOURCES

The RICA project is grounded in scientific data from sources such as NASA’s Planetary Data System (PDS), the European Space Agency (ESA), and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). These databases provided information on Martian regolith mineral composition, atmospheric conditions, radiation levels, and solar availability. These data were essential for calibrating thermal fusion processes, pressurization, and dust protection. Additionally, NASA computational models were used to simulate operating conditions in Jezero, ensuring RICA could function in low-pressure and extreme temperature environments. Conceptual partnerships with research institutions in sustainability and robotics also contributed to system design and integration improvements. Thus, RICA represents a collaborative effort between science, engineering, and innovation, based on real data and methodologies applied in cutting-edge space missions.

CONCLUSION

RICA symbolizes a convergence of advanced engineering, sustainability, and space exploration. By transforming waste into resources, it redefines the paradigm of human survival beyond Earth, laying the foundation for an interplanetary circular economy. Its implementation in Jezero Crater not only maximizes the operational efficiency of human missions but also creates a legacy of innovation that transcends planetary boundaries. In essence, RICA demonstrates that even in the most hostile environments of the cosmos, intelligence and sustainability can work together to build the future of human presence in space.

projectDetails.name: Echoes of the Sun
projectDetails.summary:
Echoes of the Sun is an interactive story developed to educate children and teenagers about space weather in an engaging way.
The narrative begins in a question-and-answer format, where an astronaut acts as the main narrator, describing his perspective from space.
projectDetails.details:
This is a fun and educational story accessible to all ages, with a special focus on children and teenagers.

The goal is to stimulate cognitive development — including curiosity, attention, and reasoning — while the audience learns about the fascinating world of space weather.

All music and artwork in this project were carefully handcrafted with great dedication and creativity by our team.

Each soundtrack was designed to evoke emotions and immerse the player in the story, while the hand-drawn illustrations bring the world of Echoes of the Sun to life in a unique and special way.

The story is told by an astronaut who, after returning from a research mission on space weather, decides to share his knowledge with students at a school.

- How It Works

The main character of the story is an astronaut who has just returned from a mission studying space weather phenomena.

His perspective and experience in space are key to introducing the topic in an interactive and accessible way.

After returning to Earth, he is invited to give a lecture at a school, where he explains the concept of space weather in a fun and educational setting.


This story takes place in a school environment — a space designed to be both interactive and educational.


The astronaut begins by introducing what space weather is.

The students interact with him through questions and answers. He responds clearly and thoughtfully, encouraging curiosity and understanding.



At the end of the lesson, the astronaut presents a true-or-false challenge based on what the students learned throughout the class.



Benefits:

1. Fun and engaging.

2. Suitable for different levels of knowledge.

3. Interaction with real-world scientific information.


Goals:

1. Democratize the study of space weather.

2. Expand knowledge of space weather among children and young people.


Tools and Software Used

1. ChatGPT

2. Canva

3. FL Studio

4. Krita

projectDetails.name: Project New Era
projectDetails.summary: "The sun's cosmic sneeze” is a children’s storybook that follows two young explorers on an exciting space adventure. During their journey, they uncover the mystery behind the Sun’s “sneezes” — solar eruptions known as Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) — and learn how these events affect Earth. Through a fun and educational narrative, the story introduces readers to the fascinating world of space weather, explaining complex scientific concepts in a simple and engaging way. It highlights how CMEs can cause satellite malfunctions, GPS and Internet disruptions, and even create the aurora borealis, one of nature’s most beautiful light displays. By combining science and imagination, The sun's cosmic sneeze encourages children to explore the wonders of the universe while inspiring a lifelong curiosity for learning.
projectDetails.details:
Currently, the decrease in the habit of reading among children is a growing concern for educators. Much of their time is spent using cell phones, consuming short texts that provide little stimulation for interpretation and critical thinking. This lack of contact with books may, in the future, lead to adults with difficulties in writing, communication, and idea formation.

With this in mind, we at New Era developed The Cosmic Sneeze of the Sun, a children’s storybook created with the support of the Gemini tool, based on prompts developed in ChatGPT. The work aims to stimulate creativity and the habit of reading, presenting, in a playful way, concepts related to space weather.

The story follows Estela and Jimmy, two curious children who, during a game, meet Cosmo, a satellite guardian of space. Throughout the narrative, Cosmo explains in a fun and simple way how space weather influences the Earth and people’s daily lives.

An important feature is the narration function offered by the Gemini platform, which allows access for people with visual impairments, promoting inclusion and accessibility. Thus, the project goes beyond scientific dissemination, also transmitting values such as curiosity, collaboration, and empathy.

Space weather refers to the set of phenomena that occur in space and are influenced by solar activity, such as storms and solar winds. These phenomena can affect satellites, communications, power grids, and space missions, making their study essential for technological safety and the advancement of space exploration. Brazil has stood out internationally for its research and contributions in this field.

⸻

During development, we used Visual Studio for programming and GitHub to host and version the Storybook. We created the project, configured the environment, and began programming, taking advantage of features such as automatic suggestions and debugging.

Then, we created a repository on GitHub, where we recorded the first commit and later sent new updates using the push command. This process ensured organization, version control, and efficient collaboration among team members.

The use of these tools was essential to the success of the project, providing a practical and professional experience in the use of technologies widely adopted in the market.

projectDetails.name: Project Image Explorer
projectDetails.summary:
The "Imager Explorer" is an interactive website designed for the visual exploration of ultra-high-resolution astronomical and satellite images. Its goal is to offer an immersive experience by providing detailed information and allowing users to navigate through gigapixel photographs, such as galaxies and planetary surfaces, with an impressive level of detail.

The main functionality is deep zoom viewing, utilizing OpenSeadragon technology. This ensures smooth navigation without performance loss, even with extremely large images.

Users can select images from a sidebar, where they will find contextual information about each one, including its description, resolution, and capture date. The interface allows users to zoom, pan the image, and explore every detail with precision.

In addition to visual exploration, the site offers an annotation tool. With a double-click, it is possible to add markers on points of interest, inserting labels to identify specific formations. a control panel centralizes the zoom tools and the management of these markers, which can be listed and removed.
projectDetails.details:
"Image Explorer" is an interactive web platform designed to provide an immersive experience for exploring a vast public library of astronomical images. It transforms a simple media search into a dynamic journey of discovery.

How it works:

  1. Search: The user starts by entering a search term related to space (e.g., "Mars," "Andromeda Galaxy," "Hubble").
  2. API Communication: The application takes this term and sends a request to a comprehensive database of space imagery.
  3. Data Retrieval: The database processes the request and sends back a list of relevant images, including their titles, descriptions, and links to various image sizes.
  4. Display Results: The platform displays these results in a clean, scrollable sidebar, showing a small thumbnail and the title for each image.
  5. Immersive Exploration: When the user clicks on an image result, its high-resolution version is loaded into the main viewing area. This viewer is powered by the OpenSeadragon library, a specialized tool that enables a "deep zoom" experience. Instead of loading a massive file at once, it intelligently loads the image in small tiles, allowing the user to seamlessly pan and zoom deep into the details of a planet's surface or a distant nebula with virtually no lag.

## What benefits does it have?

The project offers several key benefits to users:

  • Accessibility to Science: It makes a massive, publicly-funded dataset of scientific and cultural importance easily accessible and engaging for the general public, students, and space enthusiasts.
  • Enhanced Engagement: It moves beyond static image galleries. The deep-zoom functionality encourages active exploration and curiosity, allowing users to discover details and features they would never see in a standard-resolution image.
  • Educational Value: It serves as a powerful and visually compelling educational tool. A teacher can use it to take their class on a tour of the lunar surface, or an amateur astronomer can study the structure of galaxies in breathtaking detail.
  • Inspiration: By bringing the wonders of the cosmos directly to the user's screen in an interactive format, the project aims to inspire awe and foster a greater interest in science, technology, and space exploration.

## What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to democratize the experience of space exploration. We want to break down the barrier between the public and the incredible data collected by space missions. The goal is to make anyone with a web browser feel like they can personally explore the universe, fostering a sense of connection and ownership over humanity's cosmic discoveries. Ultimately, the project seeks to increase scientific literacy and inspire the next generation of explorers, scientists, and dreamers by making space tangible, explorable, and awe-inspiring.

## What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

The project was developed using standard, accessible web technologies, requiring no specialized hardware.

  • Coding Languages:
    • HTML5: For the semantic structure of the web application.
    • CSS3: For all visual styling, layout (using Flexbox), and creating the dark, thematic interface.
    • JavaScript (ES6+): For all the application's logic, including handling user input, API communication (fetch), and DOM manipulation.
    • OpenSeadragon: The core JavaScript library for the high-resolution, deep-zoom image viewer.
    • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Used as the primary local code editor.
    • Live Server (VS Code Extension): A development tool used to run a local server, which was essential for solving browser security (CORS) issues.
    • CodeSandbox: An online IDE that was ultimately used to create a stable, shareable, and hassle-free development environment.
    • Web Browser Developer Tools: (e.g., in Chrome, Edge, Firefox) Used extensively for debugging JavaScript, inspecting network requests, and analyzing the HTML/CSS.

## How is your project creative?

The project's creativity lies in the synthesis and application of existing technologies to create a new user experience.

Instead of just displaying data, we've transformed a database of images into an interactive canvas. The creativity comes from reframing what an image is: it's not just a static picture, but a detailed world to be explored. By integrating a powerful deep-zoom library with a rich data source, we've created an experience that encourages discovery. The simple act of zooming into a vast image of a galaxy to see individual star-forming regions is a creatively designed interaction that makes complex scientific data feel personal and accessible.

## What factors did your team consider?

As a team, we considered several critical factors throughout the development process:

  • User Experience (UX): Our top priority was simplicity and intuitiveness. The interface was designed to be clean and focused on the core experience: search, select, and explore. We deliberately avoided clutter to make the images the heroes of the platform.
  • Performance: We knew that loading gigapixel-sized images would be a major technical hurdle. The decision to use OpenSeadragon was a key strategic factor, ensuring a smooth and responsive experience for the user, regardless of the image's original size.
  • Development Environment Challenges: We encountered and adapted to the common problem of local development server setup. Recognizing this was a point of friction, we strategically migrated to CodeSandbox to create a more stable and accessible development environment, allowing us to focus on the code itself.
  • Debugging and Robustness: We followed a systematic debugging process. When data requests failed, we used the browser's developer tools to inspect network requests, status codes, and console errors to diagnose the problems. This iterative process of testing and fixing was a central factor in creating a functional final product.

projectDetails.summary:
Olá! Somos a equi Plug-in e estamos participando do NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 com um projeto incrível que desenvolvemos. Criamos uma ferramenta visual no Canva que permite desenhar e planejar habitats espaciais de forma simples e intuitiva.
Nossa ideia surgiu quando percebemos que projetar espaços para astronautas viverem é algo complexo, mas que poderia ser mais acessível. Por isso, desenvolvemos um kit de construção digital onde qualquer pessoa pode criar seu próprio habitat espacial.
Na nossa ferramenta, primeiro escolho a forma externa do habitat, depois arrasto os componentes internos como laboratórios, áreas de exercício, cozinha e sistemas de suporte à vida. Organizamos tudo pensando no fluxo de circulação e na eficiência do espaço, que são essenciais quando se vive em ambientes confinados no espaço.
O que mais nos empolga neste projeto é como ele torna o design espacial acessível para todos. Não é preciso ser um engenheiro da NASA para criar algo funcional e interessante! Acreditamos que nossa ferramenta pode ser usada em salas de aula, por entusiastas do espaço e até mesmo por profissionais que querem visualizar ideias rapidamente.
Estamos muito orgulhosos de contribuir com uma solução que pode inspirar outras pessoas a se interessarem por exploração espacial e, quem sabe, ajudar no desenvolvimento de habitats mais eficientes para os astronautas do futuro!
projectDetails.details:
O projeto "Plug-in de Habitat Espacial" foi desenvolvido para o NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025, atendendo ao desafio de criar uma ferramenta visual que permita aos usuários definir a forma/volume de um habitat espacial e explorar possíveis opções de layout.

Problema Abordado

Os habitats espaciais precisam suportar funções críticas como gerenciamento de resíduos, controle térmico, suporte à vida, comunicações, energia e outras necessidades humanas em um ambiente confinado e hostil. O design eficiente desses habitats é fundamental para missões espaciais bem-sucedidas.

Nossa Solução

Desenvolvemos uma ferramenta visual baseada no Canva que permite:

  • Selecionar formas externas de habitats (cilíndricos, infláveis, etc.)
  • Arrastar e soltar componentes internos pré-desenhados
  • Organizar o layout considerando fluxo de circulação e eficiência
  • Compartilhar designs como templates para colaboração
Componentes Principais Analisados
  • Estação de trabalho/laboratório
  • Área de exercícios
  • Cozinha/galeria
  • Banheiro/higiene
  • Estufa hidropônica
  • Sistemas ECLSS (Controle Ambiental e Suporte à Vida)
Impacto

A ferramenta democratiza o design espacial, tornando-o acessível para fins educacionais, engajando o público em missões espaciais, estimulando a inovação através de novas perspectivas e potencialmente contribuindo para o desenvolvimento de habitats mais eficientes.Esta solução atende perfeitamente ao desafio proposto pela NASA, oferecendo uma abordagem interativa e visual para o design de habitats espaciais que pode ser utilizada por pessoas com diferentes níveis de conhecimento técnico.

projectDetails.name: Predadores de Meteoros

Resumo:
 “Predadores de Meteoros” é uma simulação científica em Python que visualiza impactos de asteroides próximos à Terra (NEOs). Com base em dados públicos da NASA, o sistema calcula diâmetro, velocidade, densidade e energia de impacto, gerando um vídeo educativo de ~20 segundos. O projeto aproxima o público da ciência e da Defesa Planetária, mostrando visualmente os riscos e estratégias de mitigação.
 Detalhes:
 Desenvolvido em Python 3.13.7 usando OpenCV e NumPy, o projeto transforma dados reais da NASA NEO API em uma experiência visual interativa. O vídeo “impactor_2025_final2.3.mp4” mostra o movimento de asteroides, estimativas de energia cinética e tamanho de crateras. É educativo, científico e gamificado, reforçando a importância da defesa planetária e da ciência para o público.
Demonstração:
 YouTube (público ou não listado):  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1toZwy_AKiE

Projeto final:
GitHub: https://github.com/PredadoresdeMeteoros/Predadores-de-Asteroides

projectDetails.name: Project Solar Backyard
projectDetails.summary: The project consists in an interactive story aimed at children. The goal is to playfully address solar flares and their impacts on Earth, encouraging players to propose solutions to the problems they encounter. Our project teaches players how one of the many phenomena that exist in space works, but which most people are unaware of.
projectDetails.details:
• What does it exactly do? ⁠A solar flare is a sudden release of energy on the Sun's surface, caused by changes in its magnetic field, usually close to sunspots. These explosions emit intense radiation, charged particles, and electromagnetic waves, and can affect satellites, communications, and electrical networks on Earth. They are classified into A, B, C, M and X - with X being the most intense, as the one recorded by NASA in 2024 (X8.7), one of the largest in the current solar cycle. The educational game presented aims to teach children, in a light and fun way, what solar eruptions are, how they occur and why they are important. Through the character Apollo, the game introduces the theme with interactive questions, colorful visual elements and original soundtrack. This playful approach facilitates understanding and awakens the interest of the little ones in science. In addition, the game addresses topics such as the formation of auroras and how solar eruptions affect our daily life through devices such as GPS and radio, encouraging learning in an engaging and accessible way. How does it work? This game was created with the intention of demystifying the difficulties in learning about solar eruptions.In an interactive and educational environment, children and adolescents can learn how these eruptions occur and what they affect.

As soon as the player enters and goes through a brief animation of the sun, he will find our main character Apollo, who will explain about the eruptions and ask questions with true or false options, with the intention to make players able to delve into the eruptions and understand why it occurs and even what it affects. Each page has an arrow or button that is indicating where the player should click to proceed. Which makes the game even more accessible and easy for our target audience, which are children and adolescents.

At the end it the player solves the problems and answers the correct questions, he is taken to see a northern light!

What are the benefits? 1- Active learning about solar eruptions 2- Everyone can play and learn 3- Stimulation of creativity 4- Contextualization of the content 5- Improvement in cognitive skills 6- Entertainment • What do you hope to achieve? 1- Democratization of the study of solar eruptions 2- Contribution to the dissemination of scientific studies among children and young people What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use to develop your project? 1- Canva. 2- Chat gpt.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used ChatGPT to assist in our research on solar eruptions, to translate our texts into English and to create some images for the game.

Uma equipe formada por estudantes do ensino médio que une diferentes conhecimentos, experiências e visões de mundo em um só propósito: criar soluções inovadoras, guiadas pela nossa identidade e criatividade.

projectDetails.name: Air Quality Intelligence
projectDetails.summary:
Nosso projeto é um aplicativo que atua como um verdadeiro consultor de qualidade do ar, com o objetivo de proteger a saúde das pessoas a partir de informações ambientais confiáveis e acessíveis. Ele transforma dados complexos, como níveis de poluição, temperatura e umidade em recomendações simples e personalizadas, de acordo com a localização e o perfil de cada usuário ou negócio. 
O diferencial do aplicativo está em sua aplicabilidade direta na vida cotidiana, especialmente em situações onde a qualidade do ar pode afetar a saúde de forma crítica. Por exemplo, pais e escolas podem usá-lo para monitorar as condições ambientais e evitar que crianças com histórico de problemas respiratórios participem de atividades ao ar livre em dias de ar impróprio.
Ao permitir o acesso à localização do usuário, o app coleta dados de fontes confiáveis como a NASA e órgãos ambientais locais, processando essas informações em tempo real para gerar um índice que indica se o ar está seguro ou prejudicial. Além disso, oferece previsões diárias, alertas inteligentes e sugestões de atividades seguras, com recomendações específicas para grupos vulneráveis, como crianças, idosos ou pessoas com doenças respiratórias.
O starfield é uma ferramenta de cuidado preventivo, que permite que estabelecimentos melhorem a qualidade do ar de seus ambientes interiores, criando uma rede comunitária de saúde e prevenção.
projectDetails.details:
Starfield: Beyond the map, the solution.

What exactly does this do?

Our project, Starfield, is an environmental intelligence platform that acts as an intelligent air quality advisor. Its primary function is to translate complex scientific data about the environment, sourced from agencies like NASA, into personalized and actionable recommendations to protect the health of citizens and communities. For the general public, it offers predictive alerts and suggestions for safe activities. For businesses and establishments, it goes a step further by providing a clear action plan to improve their indoor air quality and allowing them to verify these actions, creating a network of healthier and more trustworthy spaces for everyone.

What are the benefits?

Starfield is designed to generate a positive and measurable impact on multiple fronts:

  • For Citizens: It offers peace of mind and active health prevention, enabling the safe planning of outdoor activities, reducing pollutant exposure for at-risk groups, and helping to prevent health crises.
  • For Businesses and Institutions: It empowers local establishments with the tools to create safer environments. This serves as a competitive differentiator, strengthening trust and their relationship with the community.
  • For Society: It builds a community-based network for preventive health. By encouraging and validating air quality improvements, the project promotes a more sustainable and resilient future.

What do you hope to achieve?

Our ultimate goal is to move society from simple awareness to effective action. We hope to create a tool that not only informs about the dangers of air pollution but also inspires and enables a behavioral shift, where every citizen and business becomes an active agent in building a healthier environment.

Our motivation is reinforced by a global call to action from the World Health Organization:

"After surviving a pandemic, it is unacceptable to still have 7 million preventable deaths and countless preventable lost years of good health due to air pollution... too many investments are still being sunk into a polluted environment rather than in clean, healthy air,” said Dr. Maria Neira, WHO Director.

To turn this ambition into reality, we designed Starfield with a vision for growth and scalability. First, by generating a 'flywheel effect': each new verified business on the platform makes the app more useful for citizens, and each new citizen increases the incentive for more businesses to join. We plan to accelerate this cycle with community feedback, making our trust network increasingly intelligent. Second, through an evolving trust roadmap: our 'Verified Action' system using photo evidence is the first step. The next phase is integrating with indoor air quality sensors (IoT) for real-time data validation, allowing partners to achieve a 'Gold Standard' seal of credibility.

Ultimately, what we hope to achieve with Starfield is to be part of the solution: to build a future where technology is used to create a network of clean air "oásis," drastically reducing preventable health problems and ensuring that everyone, especially the most vulnerable, can breathe safely.

TECHNOLOGY USED

  • Frontend: React with TypeScript, Vite, React Router, Recharts, Lucide React.
  • Backend: Hono, Cloudflare Workers.
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS, PostCSS.
  • Database and Storage: Cloudflare D1, Cloudflare R2.
  • Platform and Authentication: Cloudflare (Workers, Pages), Google OAuth.

Images and Video: N/A

Code and Data: Artificial Intelligence is the backbone of our development strategy. We integrated it directly into the process of building both the front-end and the back-end.

  • Front-End Development Acceleration: We utilized AI assistants integrated into our no-code development platform to generate User Interface (UI) components, responsive layouts, and interactive prototypes from natural language descriptions. This allowed us to focus on the User Experience (UX) and usability, instead of spending hundreds of hours on manually coding interfaces.
  • Back-End Automation and Optimization: On the server side, AI was employed to model the database schema, generate business logic, and build API endpoints automatically. This not only drastically reduced development time but also minimized the occurrence of human error, resulting in a more robust and scalable system.

Platform and Tools

  • Mocha.js: The framework used for executing automated tests, which were largely generated and structured with the help of AI.

projectDetails.name: The Great Space Weather Adventure
projectDetails.summary: We developed a game for children aged 6 to 12 with the purpose of teaching them about the Sun’s impacts and the events it causes on our planet. It’s a fun and educational adventure where kids can explore our galaxy, and learn about fascinating space phenomena.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

The "The Great Space Weather Adventure" project is an interactive educational game designed to be played directly in a web browser. Its main objective is to teach children aged 6 to 12 about the complex phenomenon of Space Weather in a fun, engaging, and accessible way.

The game covers the following topics:

The Origin: It explains what the solar wind, solar flares, and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are.

The Impacts: It demonstrates how these phenomena affect Earth, impacting essential technologies like satellites (GPS), power grids, aviation, and communications.

The Solutions: It shows the importance of solar monitoring and the preventive actions taken by different professionals to protect our society.

The Beauty: It presents the auroras as one of the beautiful visual effects of space weather.

In summary, it translates a complex scientific topic into a gamified adventure where learning occurs through discovery and decision-making.

How does it work?

The game functions through a narrative journey divided into interactive sections (levels), guiding the player from basic knowledge to practical scenarios:

Personalization: The experience begins with a welcome screen where the player enters their name, which will be used on the final certificate.

Basic Learning: The player is introduced to the concepts by the "Sun" and "Earth," who explain in simple terms what space weather is.

Decision Scenarios: The player takes on the roles of different professionals (astronaut, pilot, farmer, power grid operator) and an everyday person. In each scenario, they receive a space weather alert and must make the correct decision to mitigate the risks.

Gamification: Every correct choice rewards the player with points and helps them level up. Wrong choices result in a loss of points but provide educational feedback explaining the consequences.

Knowledge Validation: At the end of the journey, the player tests everything they've learned in a final quiz.

Reward: Upon completing the game, the player receives a personalized "Space Explorer Certificate" with their name and final score.

What benefits does it have?

The project offers multiple benefits for different audiences:

Accessible Education: It transforms a complex and abstract scientific topic into something tangible and easy for children in the 6 to 12 age range to understand, breaking down learning barriers.

Engagement and Inspiration: It uses gamification elements (points, levels, a certificate) to make learning fun, with the potential to spark an interest in children for careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

Tool for Educators: Being browser-based and scientifically accurate, the game serves as a "ready-to-use" tool that can be easily implemented in classrooms, science museums, and educational programs to complement lessons on space and physics.

Public Awareness: It raises awareness of the real-world impacts of space weather on our increasingly technology-dependent society, highlighting the importance of science and space monitoring.

What do you hope to achieve?

Our main goal is to build a bridge between the complex science of heliophysics and children aged 6 to 12, offering a free, high-quality educational tool that can be used in schools and museums. We hope to transform learning into an exciting adventure, sparking curiosity about the universe and, in the long term, inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers to understand the importance of science for the protection of our technological future.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

The project was developed with the philosophy of being self-contained, portable, and universally accessible. The entire structure, style, and functionality are encapsulated in a single HTML file.

To achieve this, the three fundamental web technologies were used, working together within this single file:

HTML

CSS

JavaScript

Hardware:

No specific hardware is required. The game is designed to run on any device with a modern internet browser (computer, tablet, or smartphone).

Software:

Development was done using only a source code editor and a web browser for testing. For the creation of supporting materials (scripts), generative AI tools were used.

challengeDetails.excerpt: Data from several different space-based exoplanet surveying missions have enabled discovery of thousands of new planets outside our solar system, but most of these exoplanets were identified manually. With advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), it is possible to automatically analyze large sets of data collected by these missions to identify exoplanets. Your challenge is to create an AI/ML model that is trained on one or more of the open-source exoplanet datasets offered by NASA and that can analyze new data to accurately identify exoplanets. (Astrophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: Thiago Duarte: Alone in Space
projectDetails.summary:
My project is an interactive digital story for children that explains, in a fun and visual way, what space weather is and how it affects life on Earth. The narrative is told from the perspective of a solar storm traveling from the Sun to our planet, observing how its impact influences farmers, pilots, astronauts, and power grid operators.

The goal is to turn a complex scientific topic into something accessible, educational, and captivating, combining anime-style digital art with clear and engaging language. The story highlights the importance of Earth’s magnetic field as a “magical protective shield,” inspiring children’s curiosity about astronomy and space physics.

This project addresses the challenge by making space weather knowledge more approachable, fostering scientific curiosity and awareness of how solar phenomena affect our daily lives. It’s important because early science education helps build a new generation of space explorers and innovators.
projectDetails.details:
"Stellar Stories” is an interactive digital story created to teach children about space weather — how solar activity, such as flares and coronal mass ejections, can affect life on Earth. The narrative combines scientific communication and digital art, told from the perspective of the Sun and its “sneeze” traveling toward our planet. Through this fun and imaginative approach, children learn how solar activity influences farmers, pilots, astronauts, and power grids.

The goal of the project is to make complex scientific concepts accessible and engaging, sparking curiosity about astronomy and physics. Its main benefit is educational, raising awareness of how space weather affects everyday technologies and highlighting the importance of observation and protection systems.

To develop the project, tools such as Bing Image Creator were used to generate illustrations, an AI voice generator for narration, and a simple image and video editor to assemble the final digital story.

The creativity of the project lies in combining storytelling, science, and art into a single learning experience. The project was designed to balance scientific accuracy with emotional engagement, encouraging young audiences to see the universe not as something distant, but as a living system that connects us all. 🌞✨
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

In the development of Stellar Stories, we used Artificial Intelligence tools to support the creation and storytelling of the project:

  • Images: all images were generated using Bing Image Creator, with a watermark indicating that they are AI-generated images.
  • Audio: the narration of the story was created with the Eleven Labs voice generation tool, and the use of AI is indicated in the metadata and audio description.

The use of AI allowed us to accelerate the production of visual and audio content while maintaining creativity and the educational focus of the project, without infringing on any NASA logos or elements.

challengeDetails.title: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings
challengeDetails.excerpt: Although the Sun is 93 million miles away from our planet, solar activity can significantly impact our daily lives. “Space weather”—the variations that occur in the space environment between the Sun and Earth—can impact technologies in space and on Earth. Your challenge is to write and illustrate a digital children’s story that explains what space weather is and the varying impacts it has on different people such as farmers, pilots, astronauts, power grid operators, and the general public. You can tell the story from the perspective of a person impacted by space weather or from the point of view of a solar flare or coronal mass ejection (CME) as it approaches Earth. (Heliophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: Project Vacuum Drift
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary: Drift Climate Grid

The Drift Climate Grid is a dynamic and interactive weather dashboard developed by VacuumDrift, built as a single-page application for detailed and intuitive climate analysis. The project redefines how users interpret meteorological data, going beyond basic temperature readings to deliver context, precision, and usability.

Powered by a dedicated climate database, it ensures accurate and consistent forecasts while eliminating time-zone errors. This foundation supports clear visualizations and real-time updates for any region.

Key Features:

Detailed Metrics: Displays temperature, humidity, wind speed, and weather descriptions with expressive emojis for instant readability.

Interactive Map (Leaflet.js): Clicking any location instantly updates all forecasts, refreshing data dynamically.

Comprehensive Climate Breakdown: Offers day classification (comfort level), sun cycle details (sunrise, sunset, daylight duration), and daily practical effects such as outfit tips, skin/hair recommendations, and laundry drying guidance, all derived from real atmospheric variables.

Data Visualization: A Chart.js graph presents weekly max/min temperatures for quick trend recognition.

User Experience: Responsive design, dark/light mode toggle, and minimalist aesthetics optimized for any device.

The Drift Climate Grid turns complex data into personalized, actionable insights, embodying VacuumDrift’s vision of fluid, user-focused technology.
projectDetails.details:
The Drift Climate Grid is an interactive single-page weather dashboard developed by VacuumDrift in response to the challenge of helping users evaluate environmental comfort and adverse weather risks for any time and location. The application transforms raw climate data into meaningful, personalized insights that guide daily decisions and activity planning.

Using a dedicated climate database, the system provides precise forecasts while avoiding common time-zone errors. It presents detailed daily metrics such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and weather descriptions, enhanced with visual emojis for better user interpretation. An interactive map built with Leaflet.js allows users to click any location and instantly refresh forecasts.

To address the challenge’s goal of evaluating “very hot,” “cold,” or “uncomfortable” conditions, the dashboard introduces a Day Classification System that defines comfort levels, sun cycle information, and practical daily effects—such as clothing suggestions, hair/skin care tips, and laundry drying conditions—based on real atmospheric variables.

The app also includes a Chart.js-powered graph for weekly trends, providing a visual understanding of upcoming weather changes. Developed with modern web technologies (JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and responsive design), the project emphasizes creativity, usability, and accessibility through a clean interface and dark/light mode support.

Overall, the Drift Climate Grid converts complex climate data into clear, actionable insights—making weather forecasting more human, accessible, and useful.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
The project Drift Climate Grid (also known as VacuumDrift Weather Flow) utilized Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, specifically Google's Gemini, to accelerate the development of the source code (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) and in the creation of descriptive content.

Code and Data:

  • Front-End Code Generation: The core structure of the weather dashboard, including the layout (Tailwind CSS), the complex data processing functions (K-to-F conversion, weather condition mapping), dynamic UI updates, and the Chart.js integration, were initially generated, optimized, and debugged through iterative prompts with the AI.
  • Key Technical Problem Solving: The AI was instrumental in resolving specific technical challenges, such as implementing the Dark/Light Theme Toggle and fixing the time-zone bug in the date selection input that caused the prediction date to display one day earlier. It also assisted with the integration of the Leaflet.js map for coordinate-based location switching.

Descriptive Text and Metadata:

  • Project Summary and Naming: The project summary detailing the features and its relation to the "VacuumDrift" concept (e.g., naming the project Drift Climate Grid) was generated with the assistance of the AI.
  • Contextual Content: The logic and phrasing for the personalized suggestions, including the Daily Challenge, Attire Suggestion, and Day Classification, were developed and refined with AI assistance.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?
challengeDetails.excerpt: If you’re planning an outdoor event—like a vacation, a hike on a trail, or fishing on a lake—it would be good to know the chances of adverse weather for the time and location you are considering. There are many types of Earth observation data that can provide information on weather conditions for a particular location and day of the year. Your challenge is to construct an app with a personalized interface that enables users to conduct a customized query to tell them the likelihood of “very hot,” “very cold,” “very windy,” “very wet,” or “very uncomfortable” conditions for the location and time they specify. (Earth Science Division)
