projectDetails.name: Project 4° Eletroeletrônica IFSP Sorocaba
projectDetails.summary: Together, we seek to develop a new label model, which will be applied in different species of sharks in order to collect data about the behavior of these animals, as well as extract some information about the marine region in which it is inserted. All this will be done by means of several sensors that will measure the temperature of the sea in that environment, geographical location, depth measurement, detection of movements and capture of sounds produced by them when they are feeding, where an AI, from the audio acquired, would detect the different noises predicting with a certain margin of error, the marine animal that that shark would be feeding on. Our goal is the democratization of these data that are normally difficult to access, thus benefiting several biologists and researchers who need our data for future research, as well as, with the joining of these data, create a predictive system based on IoT, to predict their behavior, future locations and possible species they will feed on.
projectDetails.details:
Disclaimer: For a better experience, use the Desktop within Google Chrome as it has limited functionality on mobile devices.

Introduction

Contemporary studies in marine ecology have benefited strongly from advances in electronic tags (bio-logging tags), which allow remote monitoring of large marine vertebrates such as sharks over long periods (for example, measure depth, temperature and location) (e.g. Pop-off Satellite Archival Tags - PSAT). The integration of additional sensors such as accelerometers, microphones and environmental sensors expands the ability to infer animal behavior and ecological interactions (e.g., feeding behavior, vertical displacements).

However, making this data intuitively accessible to researchers, environmental managers and the general public is still a challenge. Interactive web interfaces and gamified environments can facilitate the spatio-temporal exploration of data, stimulate engagement and transform raw data into understandable narratives (see discussions in geospatial + gamification).

Against this backdrop, our team developed Shark Space, a platform that integrates geospatial visualization, sensory data analysis, ecosystem simulation and educational gamification, focused on monitoring sharks through advanced sensory tags. The objective of this article is to describe the design, architecture, functional modules and challenges associated with implementation, as well as point out future perspectives.

Sharks in Space!

Our journey begins with a broad exploration of the ocean that will guide us on our ecosystems in an educational and intuitive way. In addition to promoting scientific data on these marine animals directed to biologists and researchers.

Shark Space combines three innovative fronts: integrated telemetry, interactive 3D geospatial visualization and ecological gamification. By combining real (or simulated) data from sensory tags with ecosystem simulations and educational quizzes, the platform serves both as a research and teaching tool and as a public awareness tool.

The integration with NASA APIs and real geospatial data reinforces scientific rigor and allows us to situate our users in real environments of global biodiversity. Gamification (simulation + quiz) contributes to fix concepts and arouse interest in oceanography and conservation - in line with trends of "serious games" and gamification of geospatial environments (see discussions on gamification in GIS).

One of the innovations of our project is the use of audio as a basis for an AI as a means of pattern prediction. At this point, we provide an improvement of the existing labels on the market, adding greater autonomy due to the use of piezo-electric technology.

The functionality of our platform is divided as follows: Shark Explorer, Shark Data, Ecosystem Sim, Quiz.

Shark Explorer

In the initial upload, a world map is presented with 20 demarcated strategic points - these locations were defined based on biodiversity data provided by space agencies and global institutes (NASA, GBIF etc.).

By clicking on a point, the user sees an information panel about the ecosystem of that region (for example, typical marine species, oceanographic features) and can trigger an interactive 3D visualization of that area (underwater or coastal).

3D simulation allows free navigation of the camera (angle change, zoom, rotation), visualization of marine models (corals, fish, algae) and overlay of environmental data (temperatures, currents).

Internally, this module invokes NASA APIs to obtain relevant geospatial data (e.g., bathymetry, marine topography, satellite data) in order to enrich the visualization.

Shark Data

We provide five example tags (tags) applied to five distinct species of shark (for example, hammerhead shark, tiger shark, white shark, whale shark, reef shark) - the user can switch between them.

For each label, the interface displays in tables and interactive charts:

  • Maximum and minimum water temperature (during the most recent period)
  • Latitude and longitude of the climb location
  • Depth / height recorded at the time of communication
  • Accelerometer data (motion patterns: intensity, peaks, drift)
  • Timestamp of each read
  • Audio file captured

Predictive analysis of future trajectories - based on topographic modeling algorithms and historical data, the module generates probabilistic maps of possible future routes.

This module allows comparisons between species, time filters (last 24h, last weeks, all history) and export of data in CSV/JSON formats for external use.

Ecosystem Sim

It is a simulation game that combines strategy, ecology and interaction.

The user starts with a world map and can insert marine elements (fish species, sharks, corals, marine vegetation) and pollutants (garbage, microplastics).

There is a 0% to 100% ecosystem health bar that reflects the overall ecological status of the simulated region (based on biomass, diversity, pollution).

Ser’s goal is to maintain high health, balancing species introduction and pollution control.

As a reference for the use of games and simulations for environmental education, other initiatives integrate models and gamification to teach ecosystems and environmental services in an educational context (for example, simulation games of "ecosystem services").

Quiz

The Quiz consists of a game of questions and answers focusing on marine ecology, oceanography, conservation and behavior of sharks and ecosystems.

The quiz has difficulty levels (1 to 10).

For each chosen level, there is a hunger bar that starts at 100%. With each incorrect answer, the bar loses 10%. If the bar reaches 0%, the player loses the game. In addition, at more difficult levels, the bar becomes smaller and smaller (for example, it loses 10% per level).

The questions cover topics such as marine biogeochemical cycles, impacts of marine pollution, fish migration, food behavior, among others.

At the end of each quiz, the user receives a score, ranking and each answer is given an explanation.

Predictive Model

Bayesian model that estimates zones of high probability of shark predation based on simulated environmental and sensory variables, integrating satellite data and biotelemetry in a probabilistic structure for generating dynamic maps of hotspots.

Implemented in PyMC, the model uses Bayesian logistic regression relating environmental variables to the probability of eating behavior.

The prediction identifies the next likely point of displacement, defined by maximizing the probability of occurrence according to the environmental gradient.

Variables:

  • Temperature (°C): regulates metabolism and thermal comfort.
  • Salinity (PSU): influences navigation and prey distribution.
  • Phytoplankton (mg/m 3): biological proxy for prey abundance.
  • Depth (dbar): indicates dive patterns.
  • Minimum temp. (°C): thermal history of the dive.
  • Force G (m/s 2): acceleration associated with hunting.
  • Food consistency: food texture index (1-3).

Results:

Generates continuous probability map: red = high propensity, dark blue = low. Green dots represent current positions and pink lines link to the predicted displacement point.

Explored Problems and Target Audience

We aim to democratize these data that are usually difficult to access, and if they exist today, there is little information available for free access.

In addition, we focus this development mainly directed to biologists and researchers in the area, where we facilitate the study of these people from the availability of these data.

For example, the first public audio capture of a shark in the ocean, was published only in March this year, that is, we ended up having a very small database, thus preventing the effective training of an Artificial Intelligence.

Materials and Methods

O sistema embarcado (“tag”) desenvolvido pela equipe contém os seguintes módulos sensoriais:

  • Pressure Sensor - Paroscientific Digiquartz (2000 dbar). 
  • Temperature Sensor - RBR Solo-T / T-Unit. 
  • Fastloc GPS - Wildlife Computers SPLASH10-F. 
  • Microcontroller - MCU STM32L452RET6. 
  • Accelerometer - ADXL355. 
  • Hydrophone - Teledyne RESON TC8105. 
  • Piezoelectric harvester + power management - LTC3588-1 / LTC3588-2. 
  • Battery - Tadiran SL-2780/S. Long life and high density. 
  • Data storage - Industrial NAND flash (SLC).
  • Housing and fixing - Material: AISI 316L stainless steel. Method of fixing: anti-corrosion nylon screws. Sealing: double seal by Viton O-rings. Bulkheads: sealed coaxial connections and cable passages with IP68 protection.
  • Argos antenna / GPS - integrated L-band (Argos + GPS).
  • Electronics - Regulators: DC-DC step-down/step-up for 3.3 V and 1.8 V. Protection: BMS circuit for secondary batteries (if applicable). Interfaces: UART ↔ Fastloc/Argos; I 2 C/SPI ↔ sensors; SPI/I 2 S ↔ audio ADC.

Remarks: for more information and technical specifications of the components, go to our github.

This type of tag combines characteristics of acoustic transmitters / satellite with dataloggers, a technique used in modern marine telemetry research. The main innovation of our label is the underwater microphone coupling and direct integration with our web platform and simulation module, which requires real-time (or near-real) data processing and robust reception and storage pipelines.

When the tag detects that the shark has emerged or is in a communication zone (for example, breaking of the water-air interface), it starts the data transmission protocol to a satellite, which in turn sends the information obtained to our website. Data sent include:

  • timestamp of the event,
  • geographical location (latitude and longitude) of the animal,
  • recorded depth / height, maximum/ minimum temperature recorded in the session,
  • vector of accelerations in the period (statistical summary or time series),
  • Audio file captured during the session.In the backend, these data packets are received via validated REST APIs and stored in relational database (for tabular data) and file system or object storage (for audio files).

Conclusion and Future

Introducing Shark Space, an innovative web platform that integrates shark-coupled tag sensory data, 3D geospatial visualization, interactive ecological simulations and educational quiz. This multifaceted approach allows researchers, educators and the general public to engage with real or simulated marine behavior data by exploring trajectories, temperature/depth patterns, and ecological environmental impact scenarios.

Although there are technical challenges (energy consumption, acoustic data accuracy, simulation scalability), the initial prototypes proved to be viable and promising as an educational and research support tool. Future extensions and field validations may consolidate the platform as a resource of great value in marine conservation studies, ecological monitoring and knowledge dissemination.

We invite stakeholders to collaborate, test and expand the platform in educational, research and environmental awareness contexts.

Technologies

The web platform adopts the modern client-server architecture (frontend + backend + APIs + database).

Frontend (user interface): HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React. For the development of the web platform in an interactive and creative way.

Backend / API: RESTful services for query of sensory data, history, forecasts and control of the simulation module. The endpoints allow: label selection, time filtering, request of regional maps or 3D models, simulation request, sending of quiz answers, etc.

Integration with external APIs: for the Shark Explorer module, we call NASA’s public APIs - for example, for biodiversity data retrieval, ocean relief or climate data - and import additional geospatial layers (terrain models, ocean cover data) for use in 3D simulation.

We also use Lovable software to create our platform/website and generate the codes. And finally, we use the Conjugator to translate the texts of our document.

challengeDetails.title: Sharks from Space
challengeDetails.excerpt: Earth’s ocean is one of the most powerful habitats in our universe, supporting a range of life that sustains ecosystems and habitability across the globe. It is common to measure photosynthetic activity in the ocean from space, but far more challenging to track top predators. Your challenge is to create a mathematical framework for identifying sharks and predicting their foraging habitats using NASA satellite data, and also to suggest a new conceptual model of a tag (a small electronic device that can be attached to an animal to track and study its movement) that could measure not only where sharks are, but also what they are eating, and in real time transmit that data back to users to enable development of predictive models. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.details:
Project Details: Atena - ISS Legacy Explorer

This project is an interactive and immersive web application designed to celebrate the 25th-anniversary legacy of the International Space Station (ISS). It serves as a digital museum, bringing the history, science, and breathtaking views of the ISS to users through a modern and engaging interface.

What It Does & How It Works

The Atena Project functions as a dynamic single-page application that provides a multi-faceted exploration of the ISS.

  • How it Works: The application is built on a modern web stack. The frontend, created with React, dynamically renders components that fetch and display data. It connects to live public APIs, including the NASA Images API to pull a vast library of official photos and videos, and the Open Notify API to track the real-time location of the ISS over the Earth.
    • A Hero Section with an overlaid menu and a dynamic media carousel or background video to immediately capture user attention.
    • An Interactive Map that displays the current latitude and longitude of the ISS, updating every few seconds.
    • Themed Carousels (both horizontal and vertical) that showcase different aspects of the ISS legacy, such as historic spacewalks (EVAs), the station's assembly, and stunning views from the Cupola module.
    • Media Players that allow users to play videos of missions and experiments directly within the application.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Benefits: The primary benefit is creating a centralized, highly engaging, and educational resource. Instead of static text and disconnected images, the Atena Project weaves together different media formats into a cohesive narrative. It makes learning about the ISS an active experience rather than a passive one.
  • Intended Impact: The project aims to inspire curiosity in space exploration and STEM fields by presenting one of humanity's greatest scientific achievements in a visually compelling and accessible way. By celebrating the 25-year legacy, we hope to educate a new generation about the importance of international collaboration and scientific discovery.

Technology Stack

The project was developed using a combination of modern web technologies:

  • Coding Languages: JavaScript
  • Frontend: React (using the Vite build tool for a fast development environment)
  • Backend: Node.js with the Express.js framework (for serving data from our own database)
  • Database: MySQL / MariaDB (managed via XAMPP)
  • APIs: NASA Images API, Open Notify ISS Location API
  • Software & Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git & GitHub for version control, npm for package management.

Creativity & Innovation

The project's creativity lies in its dynamic storytelling and user experience.

Instead of a traditional, linear webpage, we've created a modular "exhibit." The combination of a real-time tracking map, user-controlled carousels with mixed media (images and videos), and immersive background videos provides a much more fascinating and memorable experience. The innovation is in the synthesis of disparate data sources—live location data, historical images, and mission videos—into a single, cohesive, and interactive interface that tells the story of the ISS from multiple perspectives.

Team Considerations

During development, our team focused on several key factors:

  • User Experience (UX): The primary consideration was to create an interface that was intuitive, visually appealing, and not overwhelming. We prioritized "moviments" and interactivity to keep users engaged.
  • Modularity: We intentionally separated the application into reusable React components (Header, Carousel, ISSMap, Hero, etc.). This makes the code cleaner, easier to maintain, and scalable for future additions.
  • Data Authenticity: We made a conscious decision to source all our media and data from official, reliable sources like the NASA APIs to ensure the content is accurate and authoritative.
  • Responsiveness: While building the layout with modern CSS like Flexbox and responsive units (vw, vh), we kept in mind the need for the application to be accessible on various screen sizes.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
The use of AI can be broken down into the following categories:

  • Code Refactoring and Debugging: The AI's primary role was to assist in debugging complex issues (e.g., Git errors like "non-fast-forward" and "refusing to merge unrelated histories") and to suggest best practices for refactoring. For example, the AI provided guidance on how to convert our initial static HTML and vanilla JavaScript for the carousel and header into modular, reusable React components. This architectural improvement was directed and implemented by our team to enhance the project's quality.
  • Boilerplate and Snippet Generation: We leveraged the AI to generate specific, self-contained code snippets when implementing new features. Examples include the creation of a component for a background video, a custom "YouTube-style" video player, and providing a standard .gitignore file for a React/Vite project. These generated snippets were then integrated and styled by us to fit the project's unique requirements.
  • Code Commenting and Explanation: As part of our workflow, we used the AI to add clear, explanatory comments to code snippets. This helped accelerate our understanding and integration of new patterns (like React Hooks useState and useRef) and ensured our codebase remained well-documented.
  • Project Description and Text Generation: The AI was utilized to help draft and refine the project's descriptive text for this submission, based on a detailed summary, a list of key features, and a clear vision provided by our team.

In summary, all key architectural decisions, feature requests, and the overall project vision were entirely our own. The AI served as a sophisticated tool for troubleshooting, providing targeted examples, and accelerating the implementation of our original ideas and a well amount of work and fun!

challengeDetails.title: International Space Station 25th Anniversary Apps
challengeDetails.excerpt: Crews onboard the International Space Station have many unique opportunities! They witness breathtaking Earth views from the station’s cupola—known as “the window to the world.” ​​They also experience weightlessness and go outside the station on spacewalks, for which they must train extensively in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) at the Sonny Carter Training Facility in Houston, Texas. Your challenge is to create a visual tool that not only helps students and the public understand two of the most prominent sensory experiences on the station (sight and weightlessness) through the lens of the cupola and the NBL, but also informs them how these unique experiences benefit humans on Earth. (Space Operations Mission Directorate)

projectDetails.name: Project Barra de espaço
projectDetails.summary: Our project is an innovative program designed to help researchers easily find NASA articles based on themes, titles, and main keywords. By integrating advanced search and filtering capabilities, the application simplifies access to NASA’s vast database, allowing users to quickly locate relevant information without manually browsing through numerous documents. This solution directly addresses the challenge of time-consuming research, especially when dealing with large and complex datasets. By automating and optimizing the search process, it not only saves time but also increases research accuracy and efficiency. The project is important because it supports scientists, students, and space enthusiasts in exploring NASA’s valuable knowledge base more effectively, encouraging faster discoveries and promoting innovation in space and data-driven research.
projectDetails.details:
Our application allows users to search NASA articles by name and keywords, returning summarized results along with direct links to the original sources. It was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Java, Python, and integrated AI tools such as Gemini, GPT-5, and Suno AI. This project is innovative because it simplifies the process of finding and understanding NASA research materials, helping researchers and the academic community save valuable time. By providing summaries and organized results, our application makes scientific exploration more accessible and efficient.
projectDetails.aiReferences: In our project, we integrated several artificial intelligence tools to enhance both development and functionality. GPT-5 and Gemini were used not only to generate and optimize code but also to summarize NASA articles and improve keyword-based search accuracy. These AIs worked together to automate complex tasks such as content analysis, summarization, and code generation. projectDetails.name: Atmos
projectDetails.summary:
We developed an environmental and climate alert platform that directly addresses the NASA challenge by creating a solution to monitor air quality and protect public health. Our application not only integrates data from multiple sources, such as TEMPO and ground-based measurements, to provide accurate forecasts, but its core innovation is the ability to send critical notifications to users without internet access.

This is crucial for transcending the digital divide and ensuring that vulnerable populations in remote areas receive vital alerts about natural disasters or pollution spikes. The project's scalable architecture, using Docker and n8n, allows for efficient management of data and workflows in the cloud. In doing so, our project transforms Earth observation data into concrete action, offering an inclusive and effective safety tool for everyone.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a platform designed to deliver environmental indicators, such as air quality and UV radiation levels, and more importantly, to issue critical real-time alerts. Its key differentiator is the ability to function for users even without internet access.

The operational proposal is based on a feasibility study to use the network infrastructure of mobile operators to send notifications. Through partnerships, the system would send an alert signal that would be picked up by the application, ensuring the information reaches everyone, regardless of internet connectivity.

The operational proposal explores technologies that do not rely on mobile data. Through partnerships with mobile operators, the system could broadcast alerts using protocols like Cell Broadcast, which is used for national emergency alerts that override cellular traffic, or even mass SMS messages. A secondary explored pathway includes leveraging FM radio signals with RDS (Radio Data System), a technology that embeds small amounts of text data into standard FM broadcasts, reaching devices with active FM receivers.

The main benefit is the democratization of access to vital safety information. It protects populations in remote and vulnerable areas, such as the Amazon, rural zones, or other regions with limited internet infrastructure. The application serves as a prevention tool, allowing users and authorities to act quickly in high-risk situations, such as pollution spikes, or abnormal atmospheric and solar activities.

The intended impact is to save lives and reduce damage by transcending the connectivity barrier. We aim to create a public safety solution that is not just another weather app, but an essential tool that solves the problem of information access in critical moments. The goal is for authorities to use the platform to issue mass alerts effectively, coordinating evacuations and other safety measures for the entire population in an at-risk area.

For the development of the prototype and platform, we used the following technologies:

  • Front-end: Flutter, using the Android Studio IDE.
  • Back-end: Docker for containerization and a low-code approach with the n8n tool for workflow automation.
  • APIs: Consumption and cross-referencing of data from multiple APIs to ensure the accuracy of the indicators.

The project's creativity lies not in displaying the data, but in ensuring its delivery. While conventional applications are entirely dependent on the internet, our solution is innovative for decoupling emergency notifications from the need for a data connection, focusing on reaching the user under any conditions. The proposal to use mobile operator signal infrastructure for this purpose is the project's key innovation, creating a new communication layer for emergencies.

Our team primarily considered the digital divide and the vulnerability of populations in remote areas. We reflected on how current alert systems fail to reach those who need them most because they rely on an internet infrastructure that is not universal. Therefore, the project was designed not to compete with existing applications, but to evolve and serve a critical, neglected niche: the safety of everyone, whether connected or not.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We utilized Artificial Intelligence, specifically Google's Gemini, as a collaborative tool to enhance our productivity and accelerate the development cycle of our project. The use of AI was integrated into three key areas:

Front-End Development

For our Flutter application, Gemini served as a coding assistant. It helped us by:

  • Generating boilerplate code for specific UI components, which saved significant time.
  • Assisting in debugging complex widget structures.
  • Suggesting code optimizations to improve application performance.

Back-End and Workflow Automation

In the back-end, Gemini was instrumental in our low-code workflow building process with n8n. It provided critical guidance on:

  • Structuring complex automation logic.
  • Ensuring the correct parameter formatting required for seamless integration with the various APIs we consumed.

Video Production

Gemini also played a key role in our content creation process, particularly for video production. Its contributions included:

  • Scriptwriting and Storyboarding: Developing initial concepts, scripts, and storyboards for promotional and tutorial videos.
  • Content Refinement: Generating compelling narration and crafting concise on-screen text.
  • Post-Production: Creating optimized video titles, descriptions, and tags to improve discoverability.

By leveraging AI for these tasks, our team was able to streamline technical and creative processes, dedicating more focus to the core innovative aspects of our project.

projectDetails.details:

It makes use of the KOI dataset and the Ensemble-based machine learning - which is to train multiple models in order to achieve the best performance -, having an Accuracy and F1-Score around 92.5%. The data provided by the API is exhibited on the website, being possible to see all the discovered exoplanets and its information, having the option to see advanced information about the planets and dashboards.

Two major factors for the project were to make it acessible for all kind of people and to improve the scientific research. Because of that, there are sections to learn about the subjects mentioned and, for scientists, it is possible to send your own data to be analyzed and classified.

ExoClassifier is both a powerful tool for scientists, as it helps to automatize processes currently manually made, and for general people, serving the purpose of spreading scientific knowledge.

projectDetails.details:
Sunpath: Your Weather-Based Travel Assistant

Our project, Sunpath, is a travel assistant and agenda that helps people plan their trips by providing detailed weather forecasts. It's designed for anyone who loves to travel and wants to avoid being caught off guard by the weather.

How It Works:

Sunpath is a web-based application where users input their destination and travel dates. Using a Python back-end, we fetch real-time weather data from a third-party API. This information is then displayed on a clean, user-friendly interface created with HTML and CSS.

Our Project's Impact:

Sunpath's main goal is to make travel planning easier and more reliable. It empowers travelers to:

  • Plan activities wisely: Know when to schedule outdoor hikes versus indoor museum visits.
  • Pack smartly: Pack the right clothes and gear for any weather condition.
  • Travel safely: Be aware of potential weather hazards.

By minimizing weather-related stress, our app helps ensure a more enjoyable and seamless travel experience.

Tools and Technology:

  • Front-end: HTML and CSS for a simple and intuitive design.
  • Back-end: Python for handling data and API integration.

We believe Sunpath is a creative solution because it tackles a simple but crucial aspect of travel planning that is often overlooked. Our team prioritized user experience, data accuracy, and a scalable design to ensure our project is both effective and ready for future growth.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmora Ltda.
projectDetails.summary:
Our project presents a self-sustaining orbital station designed to integrate human habitation, research, and resource management within a modular ecosystem. The station features interconnected residential domes, agricultural domus for food production, and specialized modules dedicated to energy generation and scientific development. One of its innovative elements is the conceptual use of a Helium-3 reactor module — a detachable and safe energy core that reflects the potential of future fusion-based power systems.

This design addresses the challenge of creating a sustainable and functional habitat capable of long-term autonomy in space. Each section, from residential areas to agricultural units, was carefully modeled to optimize environmental balance, efficient energy use, and human well-being.

By combining architectural design, environmental systems, the project offers a practical and scalable framework for future space settlements. It not only envisions life beyond Earth but also proposes realistic solutions for sustainability, safety, and self-sufficiency in extreme environments.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a comprehensive concept for a self-sustaining orbital station designed to sustain human life, research, and production in space over the long term. It operates as a modular ecosystem comprised of several interconnected sectors—residential domes, agricultural domes, research laboratories, and a future Helium-3-independent power module.

Each section of the station was designed with functional autonomy and ecological integration in mind. The residential domus provide comfortable and adaptive living spaces, featuring retractable furniture and intelligent spatial systems that maximize available volume in artificial gravity environments. The agricultural domus serve as bio-regenerative habitats, capable of producing food and recycling resources, using artificial lighting and partially transparent domes that simulate natural daylight.

The Helium-3 generator module — a conceptual but scientifically grounded feature — represents the potential of future fusion-based power systems. Its modular structure allows it to be safely detached from the main ring in case of malfunction, emphasizing redundancy and safety in energy management.

The project’s intended impact is to demonstrate how architecture, engineering, and digital ecosystems can converge to create sustainable habitats beyond Earth. It seeks to address the challenges of energy autonomy, food production, and mental well-being in isolated environments.

For the development, we used Blender for 3D modeling and AI-assisted tools for conceptual illustration and blueprint generation. All models were designed with technical accuracy, considering spatial proportions, realistic lighting, and ergonomic factors.

Creativity lies in the project’s integrated vision — combining environmental design, energy innovation, and human-centered architecture into a cohesive orbital ecosystem. The team considered factors such as sustainability, modularity, maintenance practicality, and psychological comfort in confined environments.

Ultimately, this project envisions not just a space station, but a prototype for future autonomous habitats around the solar system — scalable, adaptable, and capable of sustaining human life through balance, technology, and design.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence tools were used in our project as creative and technical accelerators, supporting concept development, visualization, and communication — without replacing the human design and decision-making process.

  • ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used as a concept design assistant and technical writing tool. It helped refine the architectural planning of the orbital station, generate technical documentation, and create illustrative visual concepts based on our team’s design specifications. All images generated through AI include visible watermarks identifying them as AI-generated.
  • Veo (Google DeepMind) was used to create short cinematic visualizations of our space station concept. These videos were produced to enhance presentation clarity and engagement and include proper acknowledgment of AI generation in their metadata and captions.
  • Lovable was employed to assist in the website’s structure and layout generation, allowing faster deployment of an interactive interface where our project and documentation can be accessed.

The use of AI in this project was intended to enhance creativity, accelerate prototyping, and improve clarity of communication, not to automate the core reasoning or originality behind the project. Every key design decision — from architectural layout to energy systems — was conceived, validated, and integrated manually by our human team.

All AI-generated assets (visuals, text, and video) comply with the NASA Space Apps Challenge policy: they do not include or modify any NASA branding or mission identifiers, and all such assets are clearly identified as AI-generated both visually and in metadata.

projectDetails.name: Project E.B.M
projectDetails.summary: What if trash could build your future on Mars? Our project turns mission waste into high-performance materials using electromagnetic induction and 3D filament extrusion. Plastics and metals become strong, reusable filament for printing tools and structures—right on the Red Planet. With carbon nanotube treatments, even recycled composites gain new strength. We showcased our concept through a custom-built website (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and used AI to power content, translation, and code. Our vision: a habitat where nothing is wasted, and everything has purpose.
projectDetails.details:
Our project focuses on transforming mission waste into usable materials through electromagnetic induction and 3D filament extrusion, enabling the on-site production of tools and structural components for Martian habitats. Using a system that combines a shredder, electromagnetic inductor, and filament extruder, both plastic and metallic waste—such as aluminum—can be processed into standardized 3D printing filament.

Electromagnetic induction heating allows for efficient and targeted melting of polymers and metals, including aerospace-grade aluminum. The extruded plastic filament undergoes a precise process involving moisture removal, laser-controlled diameter monitoring, and vacuum-sealing to ensure high-quality output for use in additive manufacturing systems like the NASA Refabricator.

To address the challenge of material strength, especially in recycled composites, we propose advanced surface treatments such as electrophoretic deposition of carbon nanotubes, enhancing bonding in carbon fiber-reinforced filaments.

We built a website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to present our concept and technical process. This solution promotes material reusability, reducing waste and supporting sustainable construction during long-duration space missions.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used AI tools to help synthesize and organize research content, as well as to translate technical texts into English. Additionally, AI supported us in the development process by assisting with coding and debugging during the creation of our website. The background artwork of our website was also generated using AI, adding a creative visual layer to our presentation. However, the character illustrations featured in our video are original and hand-drawn by our team, showcasing our artistic contribution to the project.

projectDetails.name: EcoWatch
projectDetails.summary:
EcoWatch is an interactive platform that uses Earth observation data to monitor and visualize environmental patterns related to flowering. We developed a dynamic 3D globe where users can navigate, zoom, and click on any point on the map to automatically generate interactive charts with environmental data from NASA and the Meteomatics API.

Currently, the system displays time series of temperature, absolute humidity, wind speed, solar index, global radiation, and precipitation, enabling quick analyses and regional comparisons. This visualization helps users better understand the climatic factors influencing flowering events, supporting farmers, researchers, and environmental managers in decision-making processes.

EcoWatch meets the BloomWatch challenge by combining science and accessibility, transforming complex datasets into intuitive visual information. In the future, we plan to expand the system to include new phenological indicators and time series–based forecasts, making it an even more comprehensive tool for global environmental monitoring.

GitHub: https://github.com/Fahvihh/ecowatch_
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – EcoWatch (Bloom Watch Challenge)

EcoWatch is a platform developed for the Bloom Watch Challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. Its main goal is to monitor and analyze environmental phenomena related to Earth's phenology, such as flowering, drought, solar radiation, precipitation, and other climatic factors.

The system operates through the integration of environmental and satellite data from public APIs (such as those provided by NASA), displaying them visually and interactively on a global map. Users can click on any region of the planet to view information such as temperature, humidity, wind, drought index, and solar radiation, facilitating the analysis of environmental conditions and the identification of potential ecological impacts.

Key benefits include:

  • Simplified access to complex environmental data.
  • Real-time monitoring to support researchers, farmers, and environmental managers.
  • Easy visualization through intuitive graphs and maps.

The intended impact is to make climate data more accessible and understandable, contributing to sustainable decision-making, agricultural planning, and the preservation of ecosystems affected by climate change.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python, with integration of NASA APIs and libraries for data manipulation and environmental visualization. The design was created in Canva, and the prototype was deployed on Vercel, ensuring a lightweight and accessible interface.

The creative aspect of EcoWatch lies in how it consolidates scattered scientific information into an intuitive and interactive interface, transforming technical data into a visual experience understandable by any user.

During development, the team considered factors such as accessibility, visual clarity, usability, and environmental impact, always aiming to align technology, science, and sustainability.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
During the development of EcoWatch, we used Artificial Intelligence tools such as ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot to accelerate the process of creation, debugging, and code integration.

The AIs were essential for:

  • Generating and correcting code snippets in languages such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python;
  • Assisting in the creation of requests and integration with environmental APIs, including those from NASA;
  • Debugging errors and optimizing the website’s performance;
  • Proposing design and content structure solutions to make the project more intuitive.

A large portion of the website’s code was built with the support of these tools in an iterative manner — that is, the team described the requirements, and the AI generated the base code, which was then manually refined and implemented.

No image, video, or visual element generated by AI uses any NASA brand or identity. All references to AI were properly acknowledged in the project’s documentation and metadata, in accordance with the Space Apps Challenge guidelines.

projectDetails.name: Project Frota Bravo
projectDetails.summary:
For millions of families, air pollution is an invisible enemy invading their homes, attacking everyone's health, especially those with respiratory problems. Current alerts are generic and delayed, informing of a problem that has already taken hold, but without offering a personal defense plan. This generates anxiety, not security.

	Our solution is Atmus Sentinel: a guardian of environmental and personal health. Using NASA Earth observation data, our system not only measures, but predicts the arrival of bad air at your exact location. It translates complex scientific data into clear, preventative, WHO-based action protocols, acting as a "Night Guardian" that alerts you, ensuring a night's safe sleep.

	But the real revolution goes beyond personal protection. The anonymous network of Sentinel devices powers a unique tool for urban planners. For the first time, they don't see a cold map of pollution; they see a real-time map of its human impact (showing in which regions the population's health is being most affected). This intelligence enables truly predictive and preventative urban planning. Planners can measure the success of their actions, such as creating a park, by the direct reduction of health alerts in the community. Aligned with SDGs 3, 4, 13, and 17, our ecosystem creates a partnership between citizens and the city, resulting in smarter, healthier, and more financially sustainable cities. Atmus Sentinel: Protecting people. Empowering the city.
projectDetails.details:
Atmus Sentinel is an IoT device for predictive environmental health alerts, bridging the critical gap highlighted by the lack of actionable guidance to reduce personal exposure to pollution.

Our architecture is designed to use NASA Earth observation data (such as MODIS AOD/PM2.5 products) to generate hyperlocal forecasts. For the hackathon, we processed a real NASA data file to create a scripted JSON file, powering our simulation with realistic PM2.5 pollution scenarios, a key performance indicator in the UAE.

The hardware is a portable prototype (ARDUINO + Humidity/Temperature sensor + RGB LED) which polls our API via Wi-Fi. It interprets the JSON response to control which LEDs to light, translating data into an ambient perception interface.

The backend (Node.js/Express) simulates our intelligence engine, exposing a RESTful endpoint that serves pollution scenarios and action protocols from the JSON file.

For Challenge 7, the anonymous network feeds an aggregated data API via the smartphone app. This provides urban planners with unprecedented metrics on pollution’s impact on public health, aligned with UN SDG, enabling the creation of smarter and healthier cities.

projectDetails.name: ExoLens
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, ExoLens, is an advanced machine learning pipeline designed to accelerate the discovery and validation of exoplanets from NASA's vast datasets. We developed a sophisticated Stacking Ensemble model that leverages a "committee of experts" to achieve high accuracy. It combines the strength of two models: (1) an XGBoost classifier that we optimized with feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning to analyze tabular data, and (2) NASA's ExoMiner Deep Learning model, a specialist in light curve analysis. This hybrid approach directly addresses the challenge by providing a more robust and nuanced vetting system than a single model could achieve.

The importance of ExoLens rests on three pillars: accelerating scientific discovery, by automating the analysis of thousands of candidates; trust, through our integration of Explainable AI (XAI) with the SHAP library, which shows why the model made a decision; and education, with an analysis mode for fictional data that allows for the exploration of hypothetical scenarios. ExoLens is a powerful, transparent, and versatile tool for the next generation of planet hunters.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do and how does it work?


ExoLens is an Artificial Intelligence platform designed to accelerate the discovery and validation of exoplanets from NASA's open data. It functions as an intelligent "second look" for astronomers, analyzing planet candidates and returning a probability of them being real, along with an explanation of its decision.

Its architecture is based on a Stacking Ensemble, an AI "committee of experts" that combines two models:

  1. Logical Specialist (XGBoost): A gradient boosting model that we trained and optimized, specializing in analyzing the statistical and tabular features of a candidate (orbital period, transit depth, planetary radius, etc.), including features we created through engineering.
  2. Visual Specialist (ExoMiner): NASA's Deep Learning model, which is an expert in recognizing visual patterns and subtleties in light curves.

A final Meta-Model analyzes the "opinion" of these two specialists to give a final verdict, resulting in a more robust and accurate prediction. The platform operates in two modes: one for validating real NASA data and another for analyzing "fictitious" data or new observations, using a Nearest Neighbor technique to create a prediction even with incomplete data.

What are its benefits?

ExoLens offers four main benefits:

  1. Enhanced Accuracy: By combining the strengths of a statistical model and a Deep Learning model, our ensemble system is more resilient to errors and achieves higher accuracy than a single model.
  2. Transparency and Trust (Explainable AI): Unlike a "black box," we integrated the SHAP library to generate visual explanations. For each prediction, the user can see exactly which features (e.g., transit depth, SNR) most influenced the model's decision. This is crucial for scientific validation.
  3. Speed and Efficiency: It automates a vetting process that is currently extremely time-consuming and manual, allowing scientists to focus their time on the most promising candidates.
  4. Flexibility and Education: The ability to analyze both real and "fictitious" data makes ExoLens a powerful educational tool, allowing students and enthusiasts to explore "what-if" scenarios and understand what makes a planet candidate viable.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to accelerate the pace of exoplanet discovery and democratize access to astronomical data analysis. By providing a fast, accurate, and, above all, transparent tool, ExoLens aims to reduce the bottleneck in the candidate validation process for the TESS and Kepler missions. In the long term, this could help humanity find new worlds, including potentially habitable planets, more efficiently. Additionally, its educational aspect has the impact of inspiring and empowering the next generation of scientists and astronomers.

What tools, languages, and software were used?

  • Programming Language: Python.
  • Machine Learning Libraries: Pandas (data manipulation), Scikit-learn (for GridSearchCV, LogisticRegression, NearestNeighbors), XGBoost (our main model), and SHAP (for Explainable AI).
  • API Service: Flask, to "wrap" our AI logic in a web server.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Jupyter Notebooks for prototyping, and Git/GitHub for version control and collaboration.

How is the project creative?

The creativity of ExoLens lies in three main innovations:

  1. The Hybrid Architecture: The decision not just to choose one model, but to build a Stacking Ensemble that combines the best of classic Machine Learning (XGBoost) with Deep Learning (ExoMiner) is a sophisticated and creative solution that seeks synergy rather than competition between approaches.
  2. The Solution for Incomplete Data: The implementation of the "fictitious" mode using a Nearest Neighbor search to generate a "proxy" score is a creative and non-trivial solution to a complex problem, allowing the system to function even without all input data.
  3. The Focus on Explanation, not just Prediction: While most projects focus only on accuracy, we made Explainable AI (XAI) a central pillar. The integration of SHAP is not just an "extra" but an essential feature that makes our project creative and truly useful for a scientific audience.

What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered several strategic factors, typical of an agile development environment like a hackathon:

  • Collaboration and Parallel Development: The architecture was designed from the beginning to allow the AI, Backend, and Frontend teams to work in parallel. The creation of a Mock API was a crucial tactical decision to unblock the interface team while the AI models were still being finalized.
  • Time Management: We recognized that training and running all the models on the entire dataset would be time-consuming. We made the strategic decision to work with simulated predictions to validate the complete architecture, ensuring the delivery of a functional end-to-end product.
  • System Robustness: We designed the API to be robust, handling missing columns in the user's input and separating the business logic (TypeScript) from the AI logic (Python) through a microservices architecture.
  • Focus on the End-User: The decision to prioritize XAI and create a didactic mode was based on thinking about who would use the tool (scientists who need trust and students who want to learn).
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence was a foundational and integrated partner throughout the entire lifecycle of our NØise project. We leveraged AI tools across every major phase:

  • Conceptualization & Brainstorming: AI was instrumental in the initial ideation phase, helping us brainstorm core features, identify potential challenges in exoplanet data analysis, and refine our overall project scope and mission.
  • Software Development: Throughout the coding process, we utilized AI assistants like GitHub Copilot for boilerplate code generation, debugging complex algorithms, explaining intricate code blocks, and accelerating the implementation of our Python-based machine learning models.
  • UI/UX Design: We used generative AI to create initial design concepts, visual mockups, and user interface layouts. This allowed us to quickly iterate on the visual identity of our platform and find effective ways to visualize complex data, such as light curves.
  • Content & Communication: AI also played a key role in preparing our project presentation, assisting in drafting documentation, generating scripts for our project video, and refining the text for our pitch.

projectDetails.name: Project Sexto Quasar
projectDetails.summary:
The project focuses on translating complex astronomical themes into light and comprehensible digital experiences, using storytelling as a learning tool.
It was developed as an interactive educational website that introduces children and teenagers to the world of space science through the eyes of Ana, a 9-year-old girl who serves as the main character and narrative voice of the platform.

Through Ana’s curious and creative perspective, users explore how cosmic events — such as solar storms, auroras, or Earth’s magnetic field — directly influence life on our planet.
By combining scientific information with interactive narrative elements, the project transforms space data into an engaging and accessible learning experience.

This approach directly addresses the challenge of making space weather and astronomy understandable to younger generations. It highlights the impact of solar activity on everyday life in a way that is both accurate and imaginative.

Finally, Sexto Quasar is important because it awakens scientific curiosity from an early age, encourages critical and scientific thinking, builds an emotional connection with the universe, and transforms the scientific journey into an inspiring and playful digital experience.
projectDetails.details:
Sexto Quasar is an interactive digital platform that teaches astronomy and space weather concepts through illustrated stories and dynamic visual elements. The narrative, led by the character Ana, guides users through cosmic phenomena in a light and engaging way, combining scientific explanations with interactive visual resources. It works through user participation — reading, observing, and interacting with animations that demonstrate how space events affect Earth.

Its main benefit is the accessibility of scientific knowledge. The project translates technical topics into simple language, making them understandable and appealing to children and teenagers. It also stimulates curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking, turning learning into a playful experience. Moreover, it helps develop an early interest in science and observation of the natural world.

The expected impact is to bring new generations closer to science, inspiring them to explore, question, and understand the universe. Sexto Quasar aims to nurture curious, conscious young minds connected with scientific knowledge, showing that astronomy is not distant, but an essential part of everyday life and our understanding of the planet.

The development of the project involved a combination of design, coding, and collaboration tools. The main tools and platforms used were Visual Studio Code, Microsoft Azure, Porkbun, Mateo Matics API, Gemini API, Miro Team, and GoDaddy.

For programming, the project was developed using Angular for the frontend and NestJS for the backend, ensuring a modern, scalable, and interactive web experience. These technologies were chosen to provide efficient performance, seamless integration between components, and a user-friendly interface for educational storytelling.

The project’s creativity lies in the fusion between scientific communication and a youth-oriented storyline, transforming data and research into a narrative experience that creates an emotional connection with the audience. The team considered factors such as educational accessibility, scientific accuracy, emotional impact, and connection as essential pillars of the design process — ensuring that learning about the universe is as inspiring as observing the stars.

AI was used for both image generation and code development in the project. All visual materials, including illustrations and concept art of cosmic phenomena and the character Ana, were created using Gemini.

In addition, Gemini was also used to support development and assist in resource gathering, contributing to the creation process and improving efficiency. The use of AI was limited to creative and technical assistance, ensuring that all outputs were aligned with the project’s educational and scientific goals.

projectDetails.summary:
Our Pitch Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/17FcICbYeNkSKtd6prQY_ATTPJZDLhpOh/view?usp=sharing
Shift Space is an intelligent weather and air quality monitoring application developed using Flutter for cross-platform accessibility. Our solution addresses the critical need for real-time environmental data by integrating multiple reliable data sources, including Meteomatics API, to provide comprehensive atmospheric insights. The application delivers precise weather forecasts, air quality indexes, and environmental alerts, empowering users to make informed decisions about outdoor activities, health precautions, and daily planning. By combining meteorological data with air pollution metrics, Shift Space creates a unified platform for environmental awareness. Our primary objective is to democratize access to professional-grade weather and air quality information, making it accessible to everyone through an intuitive mobile interface. The app particularly addresses the growing concern about air pollution's impact on public health, providing users with actionable insights to protect themselves and their families. Built with modern Flutter architecture and responsive design, Shift Space represents a significant step toward smarter environmental monitoring, contributing to increased climate awareness and healthier lifestyle choices in our communities.
projectDetails.details:
Shift Space is an innovative environmental monitoring application built upon a sophisticated three-tier architecture designed to deliver highly accurate weather and air quality predictions. At its core, a robust Python API backend acts as the central intelligence, responsible for ingesting real-time meteorological data from a premium source, Meteomatics API. This raw data is then fed into custom machine learning models, which are rigorously trained on extensive historical weather datasets. By analyzing these historical patterns, our ML models generate enhanced, predictive forecasts that surpass the capabilities of traditional weather services, offering users a deeper and more reliable understanding of their environment. The refined insights from the Python API are then consumed by a dynamic Flutter frontend, providing a seamless, cross-platform user experience with intuitive visualizations and personalized alerts.

This advanced approach offers significant benefits, primarily in health protection through precise air quality alerts and smart planning for daily activities. The intended impact of Shift Space is to democratize access to professional-grade environmental intelligence, fostering greater environmental awareness and promoting healthier lifestyle choices within communities. Our project's creativity lies in this machine learning-driven predictive analytics, where historical data is leveraged to provide truly intelligent and actionable insights, rather than just presenting raw information. During development, our team prioritized user-centric design for accessibility, ensured data accuracy and reliability by selecting trusted sources like Meteomatics, focused on performance optimization with Flutter, and built for scalability to accommodate future expansions. Shift Space is more than just a weather app; it's a commitment to empowering individuals with the knowledge to navigate their environment safely and sustainably, bridging the gap between complex scientific data and everyday decision-making.

In addition, it introduces the fundamentals of scientific research, guiding children through the essential steps of the scientific method: identifying a problem, formulating a question, proposing a hypothesis, designing and conducting an experiment, making careful observations, and drawing conclusions.  

By combining storytelling, gamified elements, and interactive activities, the project encourages critical thinking, curiosity, and scientific literacy from an early age. It allows children to learn by doing, making abstract concepts tangible and understandable. Artificial intelligence is used to support character creation and assist in code development, enhancing both the educational and visual aspects of the comic.

Overall, this project aims to inspire a new generation of learners to think critically, question information, and approach problems with a scientific mindset in an engaging and enjoyable format.

projectDetails.name: Project TemporAll
projectDetails.summary: Our program was developed for users who want to plan long-term trips but struggle to find reliable information about the likely weather conditions for their desired travel time and location. We focus on two main problems: first, translating complex meteorological data that a typical person without expert knowledge would not easily understand, and second, mitigating the high risk that comes with finding only short-term forecasts. Often, users plan and pay for a trip far in advance only to have to cancel last minute because they couldn't find adequate climate information beforehand, and the current weather conditions are unsuitable for them. Our program solves this by using NASA data to make a prediction of the possible long-term weather conditions and clearly translates this information into simple terms for the user. This approach directly addresses the "Will it Rain on My Parade?" challenge by leveraging NASA's extensive climate records to build user-centric, actionable travel intelligence. In essence, we are transforming publicly available space and earth science data into actionable, long-term travel intelligence.
projectDetails.details:
1. Project Overview: What is the purpose of the project?
The TemporAll project is a website designed to facilitate access to comprehensive weather and climate information, helping users confidently plan long-term activities, such as trips and events, without the risk of weather disruptions.

2. Key Features: List the features or what the project does.
The project's primary functionality is the ability to search for long-term weather predictions for a specific region and future date chosen by the user.

3. What are the benefits?
The main benefit of the project is its capability to generate long-term climate predictions based on an AI model. This is a key differentiator, as most existing weather tools are severely limited to short-term (day-to-day) forecasts.

4. What is the project's impact?
The project's primary impact is fundamentally shifting the way travel is planned. The tool empowers travelers to move beyond simply looking at past trends and adopt a smarter, data-driven approach that leverages scientific forecasting to maximize their time and money.

1. Enhanced Financial Security Travel is a significant investment.

The tool functions as a safeguard, directly mitigating financial risks.

-* Safer Bookings: It helps travelers avoid spending money on flights and accommodation for periods with a high probability of severe weather, such as heatwaves or intense rain.

-* Reduced Unforeseen Expenses: It helps prevent unexpected costs during the trip, such as having to buy last-minute clothes or dramatically alter plans due to inclement weather.

2. Better Experiences and Less Frustration

A successful trip occurs when reality aligns with expectations. The tool helps ensure that alignment.

-* Optimal Personal Planning: A group planning a long hike can pinpoint the period with the lowest chance of rain. A family can select weeks with the most pleasant temperatures to enjoy the beach.

- * Avoiding Disappointment: It prevents situations where a vacation is spent indoors due to severe rain that, while perhaps uncommon in the past, has become a projected trend for that specific time of year.

3. Greater Control and Climate Adaptation

As the climate changes, the past is no longer a reliable predictor of the future. This tool helps people adapt to this new reality.

* Future-Based Decisions: Users can plan based on "what the weather is likely to be," not just "what it used to be." This provides much greater control over the travel experience.

Summary

In short, the project replaces weather uncertainty with manageable foresight. This gives travelers the confidence required to plan the big moments of their lives well in advance.

5. Technologies Used: Languages, frameworks, libraries, APIs, etc.
The project integrates multiple modern technologies to offer intelligent weather forecasts.

- *Frontend*:

- React with TypeScript

- Tailwind CSS

- Google Maps API (for the interactive map)

- *Backend*:

- Built in Python with FastAPI.

- Uses the NASA POWER LARC API to collect historical weather data.

- Uses the Google Gemini API to provide analyses and descriptions with artificial intelligence.

- The system uses predictive models with Scikit-learn to forecast rain based on historical data.
-* AI Model:

-The system utilizes predictive models built with Scikit-learn to forecast rain probabilities based on historical data.


This combination of APIs and frameworks creates an innovative application that merges climate data, artificial intelligence, and interactive visualization.

6. Why is it creative?
The project is creative because it transforms complex, scientific NASA data—typically accessible only to specialists—into simple, actionable insights for anyone to plan trips well in advance. It uniquely merges climatology, artificial intelligence, and tourism to predict long-term weather trends, going far beyond traditional short-range forecasts. By translating complex space and earth science data into clear, practical language, the system offers security and confidence to the user, making climate science a direct tool for real-world daily decisions.

projectDetails.name: Project TERRA Brasilis
projectDetails.summary: Project TERRA Brasilis offers a hopeful, nature-based path to regenerating degraded lands by repurposing agricultural waste. We were inspired by a real success story in Costa Rica, where discarded orange peels helped revive a forest. Our model uses data from NASA's Terra satellite to connect agricultural industries with local communities in Brazil. Using MODIS instruments, we can find the best spots for these projects: degraded areas right next to agricultural centers. We then use NDVI time-series animations to watch the land heal and to prove the method works. Our project transforms an environmental problem into a powerful solution for capturing carbon, restoring biodiversity, and building stronger communities, all with a clear view from space.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, TERRA Brasilis, is a framework designed to transform agricultural waste into a catalyst for ecological regeneration.

How it works:

  1. Inspiration: We started with the real-world case of 12,000 tons of orange peels being used to successfully reforest 3 hectares of degraded pasture in Costa Rica.
  2. The Brazilian Context: We apply this concept to Brazil, the world's largest producer of oranges, coffee, sugarcane and açaí berry, which generates millions of tons of organic waste annually.
  3. The NASA Data Bridge: Our core innovation is using NASA's Terra satellite data to operationalize this process. We use MODIS Land Cover Type (MCD12Q1) and historical NDVI (MOD13Q1) data to identify degraded lands (e.g., exhausted pastures) located near major agricultural processing plants.
  4. Monitoring and Animation: We then use a time-series of MODIS NDVI data to create compelling animations that visualize the "greening" of the land post-intervention. For detailed analysis, ASTER's high-resolution imagery can provide sharp "before-and-after" snapshots.

Benefits & Impact: This model creates a circular economy, reducing waste disposal costs for businesses while providing communities with valuable compost for soil regeneration and local agriculture. The intended impact is a scalable, low-cost method to combat desertification, increase carbon sequestration, restore biodiversity, and empower local communities.

Tools & Technology:

  • Data Acquisition: We developed a VBA and Python pipeline to automate data fetching from Google Earth Engine, facing challenges with historical data availability that led us to a more focused use of curated NASA data.
  • Data Sources: NASA's Terra satellite (MODIS, ASTER), Landsat program, NASA Worldview, and NASA Earth Observatory.
  • Software: Microsoft Excel (VBA), Python, Google Earth Engine, and video editing software for the final animation.

Creativity: Our creativity lies in connecting a proven, low-tech ecological solution with high-tech NASA satellite monitoring to create a scalable, data-driven framework. The story is told by our original character, an "Orange Astronaut," making the science accessible and engaging.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Throughout the hackathon, we used a diverse suite of AI language and generative models as collaborative partners. They were instrumental in several key areas of our project:

  • Brainstorming, Research & Ideation: We used OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini as interactive mentors. They helped us explore creative angles for our story, connect the scientific dots between ecological case studies, and deepen our understanding of NASA's data products.
  • Data Strategy & Layer Selection: The AIs assisted in identifying the most relevant NASA Terra satellite instruments and data products (like MODIS NDVI and ASTER) to best tell our story, explaining the pros and cons of different satellite sensors and time periods.
  • Code Generation & Debugging: We leveraged the models for the development and troubleshooting of our ambitious VBA and Python scripts. This included generating code snippets and debugging complex API authentication flows for NASA services and the Google Earth Engine.
  • Navigating Technical Systems: The AIs provided crucial guidance on how to work with complex APIs, helping us understand authentication protocols, generate access tokens, and find the correct documentation to legally access the data services.
  • Creative Asset Generation: We explored several generative AI platforms to bring our creative vision to life. We used LMArena.ai and LovArt.ai for initial visual concepts and character design. For our narrator, the "Orange Astronaut," we used prompts developed with the help of LLMs to generate the final character concept.
  • Content Creation and Refinement: We used ChatGPT and Gemini to help draft, refine, and translate our project documentation and pitch. We also explored Google's VEO models for potential video generation concepts and used AI Studio with models like NANO-BANANA for experimental text and content generation tasks.`

projectDetails.name: Project Trinity
projectDetails.summary: We are Team Trinity, a multidisciplinary group of students and professionals in system development. Combining expertise in art, data processing, and software engineering, we created a web application that analyzes the trajectories and physical characteristics of near-Earth objects (NEOs) with potential collision courses toward Earth. Using data from the NEO Coordination Centre (NEO SSA) and NASA’s Small Bodies Database (SBDB), our system shows the possible impact severity of each asteroid, identifying potential natural disasters such as tsunamis, seismic events, and crater formation, and classifying their destructive levels as partial, severe and crater-forming impacts.
projectDetails.details:
The project is a Python web application developed using the Dash library. The data employed are Near-Earth Objects (NEOs), exported from the Small-Body Database Query, an official NASA database that compiles essential information about each object in orbit — such as size, composition, and other technical characteristics collected over decades. Additionally, a NEO Risk list was incorporated, which, when combined with NASA’s data, provides improved assessments of potential threats to the planet.

Our tool offers a comprehensive mapping of more than 1,800 objects near Earth’s orbit. Based on parameters calculated by scientists and astronomers, the system can indicate the estimated dates of potential Earth collisions along with their possible destructive effects.

Furthermore, the program simulates the impacts of a collision, including:

• Formation of the crater at the impact site;

• Zone of severe destruction, involving fires and structural collapse;

• Area of moderate destruction, marked by minor structural damage such as broken windows.

Functionality:

The system is interactive — users can select the orbit of a desired object, and the application displays the corresponding information calculated from the database. It estimates the potential collision date with Earth (and the likelihood of impact using the Palermo Scale) and, based on the object’s physical data (such as size, velocity, and composition), determines the size of the crater and the surrounding destruction radius.

Our program clearly presents to the public the technical information contained in these databases and allows for a better visualization of the potential consequences of asteroid collisions with Earth — helping humanity understand and prepare for the best possible response in the event of an imminent catastrophe.

You can also access our project on: https://meteor-madness-93416373037.europe-west1.run.app/

projectDetails.name: Celestia Leo Certification
projectDetails.summary:
Celestia LEO Certification — Sustainable Space Operations

Celestia LEO Certification is a global standard that evaluates and certifies the sustainability of space operations. It uses the Celestia Space Sustainability Score (CSSS), ranking organizations based on Disposal, Design, Operations, Transparency, and Governance. Its goal is to reduce orbital congestion, limit space debris, and promote fair access to space.

The certification addresses key challenges: orbital congestion in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), risks from inactive satellites and debris, and inequality in space access. By providing a transparent scoring system, Celestia allows emerging nations and smaller organizations to demonstrate sustainability, attract investment, and engage globally.

The CSSS is weighted: Disposal (30%), Design (25%), Operations (25%), Transparency (10%), Governance (10%). Scores determine certification levels: Platinum (≥90), Gold (75–89), Silver (65–74), Bronze (50–64), and Non-Compliant (<50).

Certified organizations gain credibility, visibility, and partnerships. Investors and insurers get a data-driven metric for risk and ESG evaluation. Emerging nations can leverage sustainability for financing or credits.

Managed by an independent non-profit with a blockchain-based public register, Celestia ensures integrity and accountability. It transforms sustainability into a measurable, strategic asset, fostering responsible, equitable, and safe space operations.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Celestia LEO Certification, is a global standard for assessing and certifying the sustainability of space operations. It uses the Celestia Space Sustainability Score (CSSS), a quantitative system that evaluates organizations based on responsible orbital practices and sustainable design. Performance is assessed across five categories: Disposal, Design, Operations, Transparency, and Governance. Each category has a weighted contribution to the total score, determining certification levels: Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze, and Non-Compliant.

The project addresses critical challenges in space: orbital congestion, space debris, and inequality in access to space. Thousands of satellites and tens of thousands of trackable objects in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) increase the risk of collisions and Kessler Syndrome. Inactive satellites and debris threaten both current and future missions. Celestia creates a transparent, measurable system that allows organizations, including emerging nations, to demonstrate sustainability, attract investment, and gain recognition.

Our team integrated NASA data via the NTRS API, enabling real-time access and presentation of scientific and technical reports. This served as a foundation for Celestia, ensuring alignment with aerospace standards, mission documentation practices, and rigorous research methodologies.

Certified organizations gain both digital and physical seals, valid for three years, which enhance credibility, attract investors and partners, and may influence insurance decisions. The certification also allows emerging nations to leverage sustainability for financing or ESG-linked credits.

The project was developed using international frameworks (ISO 24113, Artemis Accords, UNOOSA Outer Space Treaty) and blockchain technology for a publicly auditable registry. Celestia’s creative approach lies in transforming sustainability into a measurable economic and strategic asset, unifying standards, and incentivizing responsible conduct in space. Our team considered technical feasibility, regulatory compliance, environmental impact, and equity to create a practical, scalable, and globally relevant solution.
