projectDetails.name: Artemia: AI Missions
projectDetails.summary:
Artemia is a scientific and strategic simulation game inspired by real NASA technologies and protocols. In it, the player assumes the role of a space base commander responsible for maintaining the balance between oxygen, energy, water, food and psychological well-being of the crew, facing the challenges of surviving in a hostile environment with limited resources. 

Developed based on real data on life support systems (ECLSS), NORS and HPGT pressurized tanks and the Net Habitable Volume (NHV) concept, the project transforms scientific information into playable mechanics. Each module of the habitat (such as oxygen generators, solar panels, batteries, and bio-greenhouses) directly influences the mission's balance, encouraging the player to plan, optimize, and respond to emergencies strategically. 

More than entertainment, Artemia has an educational and inspirational purpose, bringing the public closer to the concepts of science, engineering and space sustainability. 

The game demonstrates how technical and human decisions intertwine to ensure survival on space missions, becoming a playful tool for understanding the real challenges of exploration beyond Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Artemia is an interactive simulator that recreates the experience of managing a sustainable space habitat , combining real-world scientific data with strategic gameplay elements. The system simulates vital variables—such as oxygen, energy, food, water, morale, and available space —that change dynamically as the player builds modules and makes decisions. The goal is to keep the crew alive and productive during missions, facing power outages, resource shortages, and extreme environmental conditions.

The project offers educational and scientific benefits by translating complex engineering and physiological concepts into an accessible and engaging experience. It helps the public understand the workings of NASA's life support systems, such as NORS pressure tanks, electrolytic oxygen generators and solar panels, demonstrating in a practical way how the balance between resource consumption and generation is essential for human survival in space. The intended impact is to inspire new generations of students and enthusiasts to explore topics related to sustainability, space science and self-sufficient habitat design.

The development used React v18.3 Framework (Typescript based) with Tailwind (and GPT-Engineer/Codex for AI support). Project Codebase: ArtemiaSpaceAppsChallenge/straight-from-image

projectDetails.name: Shark Sense
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work? Sharks from Space is an interactive web platform that combines shark occurrence data with NASA Earth observation datasets to explore and visualize the environmental factors shaping shark foraging habitats. The system integrates satellite indicators such as sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll concentration to identify and model regions that sustain ocean productivity and attract sharks. Using historical and environmental data, the platform estimates the probability of shark occurrence by species, revealing where they are most likely to appear.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact? Our mission is to make ocean science engaging, actionable, and educational while supporting shark conservation through data-driven insights. Sharks are key regulators of marine ecosystems, and their decline disrupts oceanic balance. By mapping and predicting shark presence across time and regions, we empower researchers, policymakers, and educators to better understand the environmental dynamics driving shark behavior — ultimately helping to protect critical habitats.

Tools, coding languages, and technologies used We developed the platform using:

  • NASA Earthdata / Earthaccess API to access MODIS and SWOT datasets
  • OBIS & NOAA for shark occurrence and oceanographic data
  • h3 spacial index & LightGBM for spatial analysis and occurrence prediction
  • Vercel for deployment and user accessibility
  • Python / JavaScript (React)

Creativity and innovation Rather than just visualizing data, Sharks from Space transforms environmental and biological datasets into an interactive story of coexistence between sharks and the oceans that sustain them. The inclusion of a probabilistic occurrence model adds a predictive layer, allowing users to explore how environmental shifts might influence shark behavior and distribution. The interface merges scientific exploration with emotional storytelling, making marine science accessible and inspiring.

Team considerations Our team balanced scientific rigor, technical feasibility, and design aesthetics. We focused on integrating reliable, open-access datasets over the last decade to ensure meaningful ecological insights. The platform’s narrative flow and visual interactivity were crafted to help users see — and feel — the unseen dynamics connecting space, ocean productivity, and life beneath the surface.

projectDetails.name: TERRA for Amazônia
projectDetails.summary:
The Amazon rainforest plays a vital role in regulating Earth’s climate and sustaining global biodiversity. However, it faces increasing threats from deforestation and wildfires, many of which are linked to human activity. Our project, Terra for Amazonia, uses satellite data to analyze and visualize fire patterns across the Brazilian Amazon throughout 2024.

We focused on data from NASA’s Terra satellite, launched in 1999 as part of the Earth Observing System. Terra carries five scientific instruments, including MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), which captures daily global images in multiple spectral bands. MODIS detects thermal anomalies—areas emitting unusually high heat—indicating active fires. These detections are processed by FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System), providing near real-time fire locations and intensities.

Using FIRMS data, we created monthly heat maps and animations showing the evolution of fire hotspots across the Legal Amazon region. We also generated statistical visualizations highlighting temporal trends in fire frequency and intensity.

Our goal is to make this information accessible and engaging, helping people understand when and where fires occur and how space technology supports the protection of the world’s largest rainforest.

projectDetails.name: Space Weather Mission
projectDetails.summary: To make the complex topic of space weather accessible and fun for young audiences, we created Space Weather Mission — a digital comic narrative. In it, an astronaut meets a wise alien who playfully explains how solar winds, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections work. The Sun also comes to life as a character — sometimes angry, sometimes kind — making the science more approachable and engaging. In addition to the story, readers actively participate through an interactive quiz, answering questions to help the astronaut safely return to Earth and escape the Sun’s fury. This approach makes learning about space weather both entertaining and educational.
projectDetails.details:
Space Weather Mission  turns the complex topic of space weather into a fun, engaging, and memorable learning experience for young audiences. Using a digital comic format beloved by children, the story follows an astronaut who meets a wise alien and a personified Sun, learning about solar winds, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections through simple metaphors and clear visuals based on NASA data.

The project’s interactivity is central: readers’ choices directly influence the story’s outcome. Answer the challenges correctly, and the astronaut safely returns to Earth, escaping the Sun’s fury. Answer incorrectly, and the mission fails, showing the astronaut floating among the wreckage of the spaceship. This active participation transforms learners from passive spectators into decision-makers, reinforcing understanding through consequences.

Developed entirely in Genially, the project carefully considers language, graphics, font size, and design to match the comprehension level of a non-scientific audience. Space Weather Mission  is creative because it elevates a familiar comic format to deliver real NASA science in an entertaining, interactive, and educational way.

projectDetails.name: Cosmic Weather Tales
projectDetails.summary: Our mission during this challenge was to create a digital children's story. We did this by developing an interactive and immersive interface that invites children and students of all levels to explore Space Weather and its impacts. Through a web solution with intuitive and enjoyable navigation, users interact with three panels, which allow them to choose their Cosmic Narrator, the perspective from which the user explores Space Weather. We transformed the visualization of real data from NASA and partner agencies into clear and entertaining stories, understandable to anyone. The experience is enriched with educational games adapted to each school level, allowing knowledge to be tested in a playful and personalized way. The project aims to promote understanding of Space Weather in a fun, educational way with easy usability and focused on offering the best user experience.
projectDetails.details:
INTRODUCTION:

We are a group of five girls, Technology students and passionate about Science, who seek to create a fun and interactive way to present what Space Weather is and its impacts, through different perspectives, namely:

- Through the eyes of Earthlings: People impacted by Space Weather

- Through the eyes of a Coronal Mass Ejection(CME) heading towards Earth

- Through the eyes of a Solar Flare

Our main goal is simple: to offer children and students of all levels an educational and didactic way to understand Space Weather. We do this through playful and didactic stories based on real data from NASA and partner agencies. To achieve this, we combine our skills in programming, web development, UI/UX design, data analysis, and creativity to create a unique experience in the form of immersive and fun digital storytelling!

Welcome to Cosmic Weather Tales!

HOW DOES IT WORK?

The space journey begins with the home page, where the user clicks an intuitive button to begin their immersive experience.

When clicking the button, the user is surprised by an 8-second animation showing an intense solar storm, arousing curiosity in understanding what that phenomenon represents.

At the end of the animation, the screen background blurs, and an explanatory message about the previous animation appears, introducing the user to Space Weather in a simple and clear way. It also guides the user to the next step of the experience: clicking the button to choose their Cosmic Narrator (the perspective from which they will explore Space Weather).

When you access the Lobby, you'll find three option boxes to choose your Cosmic Narrator, allowing you to explore Space Weather from different perspectives:

- From the perspective of Earthlings

- From the perspective of a CME (Coronal Mass Ejection) heading toward Earth

- From the perspective of a Solar Flare heading toward Earth

Each box you click will transport you to a different view.

1 - First Panel

Clicking on the first panel (through the eyes of Earthlings) takes the user to a new page with a card section, where they can choose which Earthling they want to see. They can choose from: Astronaut, Farmer, Electrical Operator, Pilot, Ordinary Person, Satellite Operator, Space Scientist, Engineer, Forest Ranger, Lifeguard, Fisherman, Photographer, Chef, and Video Game Producer (14 storytelling options ).

Hovering over each card reveals some of the character's characteristics, such as their name, age, and personality.

Once the card is selected, each one leads to a story from different perspectives.

In this example: When clicking on the Astronaut card.

Second Frame

By selecting the second frame, the user embarks on a journey to explore Space Weather through the eyes of Spark, a Solar Flare traveling toward Earth.

Third Frame

By selecting the third frame, the user explores Space Weather from the perspective of Cloe, a CME (Coronal Mass Ejection) traveling toward Earth.

Menu Structure:

On each story page, the user will have access to a game menu, return to the Lobby, and if the story is from the Earthlings' perspective, return to the menu for choosing cards for the different human characters.

Game Structure:

To make the journey even more fun, users will have access to a game menu. The menu organizes games by grade level (Elementary, Middle, and High School), ensuring each user has an experience appropriate to their age and knowledge level.

Level 1 - Explores

For Elementary Students

- Mechanics: A simple word search, in which words are shuffled vertically and horizontally with each entry, ensuring a unique experience with each playthrough.

Level 2 - Astronauts

For Middle School Students

Mechanics: A more complex word search with a larger number of words. Words can also appear in different directions (horizontal, vertical, diagonal, and inverted), and there is a longer introductory text. The shuffling of words at each access ensures a unique and personalized challenge.

Level 3 - Space Cadets

For High School Students

Mechanics: True or false quiz with several questions about Space Weather. For each question, the user can click a button to receive a hint. After answering, the game informs whether the answer is correct or incorrect and provides a detailed explanation. At the end, the user sees the total number of correct answers.

Interface Benefits

By combining science and technology, the project stimulates curiosity and interest in scientific topics in a lighthearted and engaging way. The experience fosters the development of critical thinking and the interpretation of real phenomena, bringing users closer to understanding how the Sun and its events influence Earth. It sparks the imagination, encourages scientific exploration, and demonstrates that learning about space can be fun and transformative.

Conclusion

Ultimately, Cosmic Weather Tales offers an educational and immersive experience that brings children and students of all levels closer to Space Weather and its impacts. Through an interactive interface, engaging narratives, and personalized games, users can explore different perspectives and understand scientific concepts in a dynamic and fun way.

Technical details

To create the website, we used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as development languages, and VS Code as the development environment. We also used Figma to create some title art and correct details in images, and Alight Motion for editing the demo video.

projectDetails.details:
Nosso projeto consiste em um quiz interativo de conscientização contra queimadas, desenvolvido com o objetivo de educar e engajar a população sobre os riscos e impactos das queimadas, além de apresentar soluções práticas para evitá-las. Educação ambiental: Através do quiz, os participantes aprendem sobre as causas, efeitos e prevenção das queimadas.

Engajamento interativo: A abordagem lúdica torna o aprendizado mais atraente, aumentando a retenção de informações.

Consciência social: Incentiva atitudes responsáveis e práticas sustentáveis, contribuindo para a preservação ambiental.

O projeto visa reduzir comportamentos de risco, como queimadas ilegais, e aumentar a conscientização pública sobre a importância de preservar o meio ambiente. Espera-se que ele incentive mudanças de comportamento e inspire iniciativas de educação ambiental em escolas e comunidades.

A criatividade está no formato interativo e educativo, combinando tecnologia e aprendizado ambiental de forma inovadora. O quiz não apenas apresenta informações, mas também desafia os usuários a refletirem sobre suas ações e escolhas, tornando o conteúdo memorável e motivador.

Clareza e objetividade nas perguntas e respostas.

Design atrativo e intuitivo para diferentes faixas etárias.

Inclusão de conteúdos educativos e cientificamente corretos.

projectDetails.name: The Secret Messages of the Sun: The Diary of an Adventurer
projectDetails.summary:
The Secret Messages of the Sun is a digital children’s story created for the Challenge, inspired by the theme “Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings.”

Through the diary of young explorer Laura Elina, readers journey into the heart of the Sun to learn how solar storms, flares, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) affect life on Earth — from power grids to the beautiful auroras in our skies.

The story was born from a father’s conversations with his curious daughter about why the sky shines and how science can explain its mysteries. It turns real NASA solar science into imagination, showing that wonder and knowledge can shine brighter together.

Blending storytelling, science, and AI-assisted illustrations, this project aims to help children discover that even the Sun’s storms carry lessons of courage, curiosity, and balance — the same light that inspires discovery on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
The Secret Messages of the Sun is an illustrated storybook that explains solar storms and their effects on daily life through a child-friendly adventure. Using NASA resources about solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and the Sun–Earth connection, the project merges storytelling with real science.

Inspiration: A few months ago, while following the news, we saw a report about a major power outage in Europe that mentioned a possible link to a solar storm. When I tried to explain it to my wife and daughter, they laughed and said, “We don’t understand anything!” Later, when we saw this NASA challenge, we remembered that moment. That’s when the idea was born — to turn something scientifically complex into something simple, visual, and inspiring. We wanted to spark curiosity in children, who might become the scientists of tomorrow.

How it works: The story uses narrative, illustration, and factual NASA resources to explain real solar phenomena in an imaginative, educational way. It bridges storytelling and science to make learning engaging and memorable.

Benefits: Makes complex space science easy to understand for young readers and families, encouraging curiosity and STEM interest.

Tools: Google Docs, Google Drive, OpenAI ChatGPT 5, and Canva for layout.

Creativity: Blends real NASA solar science with storytelling and family inspiration to teach through imagination.

Impact: Promotes space literacy, family learning, and awareness of how space weather connects us all — showing that even the Sun’s storms can inspire knowledge and wonder.

Team considerations: We focused on accuracy, accessibility, and emotional connection — making sure that scientific facts remained true while the story stayed warm, imaginative, and inspiring for all ages.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI tools were used to assist the creative process, not to replace it.

Specifically:

  • Illustrations: Some illustrations were first hand-drawn in a sketchbook and later enhanced using AI-assisted design tools. Each image was refined manually by the authors to preserve the artistic style and scientific accuracy of the story. This process is transparently credited in the book as “Illustrations by Mario C. Ponciano | AI-Assisted design.”

projectDetails.name: Project cardio space
projectDetails.summary: o presente projeto tem como objetivo desenvolver e validar um protocolo econômico, não- farmacológico e adaptável para a prevenção e redução de riscos cardiovasculares associados à exposição à microgravidade em astronautas. A proposta busca integrar estratégias acessíveis, baseadas em medidas de saúde coletiva e práticas de promoção do bem-estar, que possam ser aplicadas tanto em missões espaciais quanto a sociedade na Terra. Ao unir ciência, inovação e sustentabilidade, o projeto pretende contribuir para a melhoria da saúde cardiovascular em contextos de alta complexidade, garantindo impacto positivo tanto no ambiente espacial quanto no cotidiano de comunidades que enfrentam limitações socioeconômicas e ou falta de especialistas .
projectDetails.details:
O que ele faz ou como funciona?
O projeto desenvolve um protocolo econômico, não-farmacológico e adaptável para prevenir e reduzir riscos cardiovasculares em astronautas expostos à microgravidade, usando triagem clínica, educação em saúde, monitoramento remoto com sensores vestíveis e intervenções como dieta, exercícios com faixas elásticas, regulação do sono e técnicas de relaxamento.

Quais são os benefícios?

  • Redução da pressão arterial e melhora do controle cardiovascular.
  • Melhora de glicemia, perfil lipídico e peso corporal.
  • Menor dependência de medicamentos.
  • Maior bem-estar psicológico e adesão ao tratamento.
  • Solução de baixo custo e sustentável, aplicável tanto no espaço quanto em populações de baixa renda na Terra.

Qual é o impacto pretendido do projeto?
Criar uma estratégia replicável e acessível que beneficie tanto astronautas quanto pessoas em comunidades carentes na Terra, promovendo saúde cardiovascular e reduzindo custos em saúde pública e missões espaciais.

Quais ferramentas, linguagens de programação, hardware ou software você utilizou para desenvolver o seu projeto?

  • Hardware: smartwatch, medidor de pressão arterial, sensor de frequência cardíaca, faixas elásticas de exercício.
  • Software: monitoramento remoto por aplicativos de saúde integrados a dispositivos vestíveis.
  • Não foi necessário uso de linguagens de programação avançadas, mas sim integração de softwares já disponíveis para coleta e análise de dados.

Como é a criatividade do seu projeto?
O diferencial está em unir ciência espacial e saúde pública, criando um protocolo que resolve problemas em ambientes extremos (microgravidade) e ao mesmo tempo oferece benefícios práticos, econômicos e sustentáveis para a Terra.

Quais fatores sua equipe considerou?

  • Impacto da microgravidade sobre o sistema cardiovascular.
  • Necessidade de baixo custo e fácil replicação.
  • Sustentabilidade logística (redução de fármacos e carga enviada ao espaço).
  • Adaptação às condições do espaço e de comunidades de baixa renda.
  • Evidências científicas sobre dieta, exercício, sono e saúde cardiovascular.

projectDetails.name: Project DefesaLogosférica - Galactic Waste Delivery (GWD)
projectDetails.summary:
O Galactic Waste Delivery (GWD) propõe uma estrutura autônoma de coleta, transporte e reaproveitamento de detritos orbitais em órbita baixa da Terra (LEO). Utilizamos uma logística reversa orbital, na qual drones-satélite monitoram, priorizam e interceptam objetos perigosos usando rotas otimizadas. Os itens coletados são levados a uma estação orbital de reciclagem, onde ligas metálicas e compostos são transformados em blocos ou filamentos para impressão 3D, promovendo economia circular espacial.

Essa iniciativa surge em resposta ao crescimento alarmante de lixo espacial: hoje são ~35.000 objetos rastreados pela ESA, sendo ~26.000 fragmentos maiores que 10 cm. Além disso, estima-se que mais de 1,2 milhão de fragmentos entre 1-10 cm e ~130 milhões de fragmentos menores que 1 cm orbitam nosso planeta. Esses detritos representam risco real de colisão para satélites, missões tripuladas e infraestrutura global.

Projetos como o ClearSpace-1, com contrato de ~€86 milhões para remover um objeto de ~112 kg, demonstram que há urgência e mercado para remoção ativa. O GWD vai além: oferecer uma operação contínua, com coleta, entrega segura e reaproveitamento em órbita, mitigando a Síndrome de Kessler, protegendo satélites críticos (GPS, comunicações, Terra observação), e construindo uma infraestrutura sustentável para o futuro da exploração espacial.
projectDetails.details:
Detalhes do Projeto — Galactic Waste Delivery (GWD)

O Galactic Waste Delivery (GWD) é um sistema autônomo de coleta e reciclagem de detritos espaciais em órbita baixa (LEO). O projeto combina um satélite-mãe (mothership) com uma frota de drones-tugs para detectar, capturar e transportar detritos para um módulo de reciclagem orbital, chamado Reforge, que converte o material coletado em feedstock para impressão 3D em microgravidade.

Como funciona:

Detecção e captura: Os drones utilizam sensores LIDAR, câmeras e navegação baseada em visão para localizar e se aproximar de detritos de pequeno e médio porte. Redes, garras articuladas ou laços realizam a captura.

Reciclagem orbital: O módulo Reforge funde metais e produz blocos ou filamentos, permitindo manufatura aditiva diretamente em órbita.

Controle e coordenação: Um sistema de comando autônomo organiza a frota, priorizando objetos de acordo com risco, massa e valor, usando algoritmos de aprendizado de máquina e heurísticas.

Benefícios e impacto:

Reduz o risco de colisões e previne o efeito cascata Kessler, preservando o espaço operacional para satélites e missões futuras.

Gera matéria-prima sustentável em órbita, diminuindo a necessidade de lançamento de metais da Terra.

Oferece solução escalável e modular, permitindo demonstração inicial (POC), expansão da frota e operação comercial contínua.

Tecnologias utilizadas:

Hardware: satélites pequenos (30–80 kg), satélite-mãe (200–600 kg), sensores LIDAR, câmeras, mecanismos de captura e módulo Reforge para impressão 3D.

Software: algoritmos de navegação, controle, coordenação de frota, priorização de detritos e processamento de dados SSA (Space Situational Awareness).

Desenvolvimento: CAD, simulações orbitais, protótipos de captura e reciclagem, testes em bancada e voos parabólicos simulando microgravidade.

Criatividade e diferenciais:

Integra remoção ativa de detritos com reciclagem e manufatura in-orbit, criando um ciclo fechado de reaproveitamento de materiais.

Considera fatores de segurança, regulamentação internacional, custo por kg removido e sustentabilidade a longo prazo.

Permite expansão modular: prova de conceito → demonstração orbital → frota comercial escalável.

projectDetails.details: A úlcera péptica é uma lesão no estômago ou duodeno causada por excesso de ácido ou falha na proteção da mucosa, apresentando sintomas como dor em queimação, náuseas e sangramentos. projectDetails.name: Health in Microgravity – Strategies to Prevent Chronic Diseases in Astronauts
projectDetails.summary: We developed an educational and visual project called "Health in Microgravity – Preventing Chronic Diseases in Astronauts." Our focus is to explain, in a clear and accessible way, how the human body transforms in microgravity and what strategies can help maintain astronaut health during long missions. We created an infographic and slides that highlight the main risks (bone loss, muscle atrophy, cardiovascular changes, and changes in the immune system) and suggest solutions such as nutritional protocols, exercise plans, and others. This work is important because it not only supports safer future missions to the Moon and Mars, but also inspires new applications on Earth, such as improving treatments for osteoporosis, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular disease.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction

Prolonged stays in space cause significant changes in the human body, such as muscle loss, osteopenia, and cardiovascular and immunological changes. This study may not only protect astronauts on future missions to Mars but also lead to advances in the treatment of diseases on Earth (osteoporosis, sarcopenia, heart problems).

Objectives

Our main goal is to provide a way for everyone to visualize in a simple and didactic way how the human body in space can suffer from various health problems and how they can be prevented through many scientific studies.

Development

We developed the project using Canva to create both the slides and the infographic, making the content visually clear and easy to understand.

The infographic is organized into four main sections:

  • Risks of Spaceflight
  • What Can Be Done About It?
  • NASA Studies
  • Curiosities

Both English and Portuguese versions of the infographic and presentation are available in the shared Google Drive folder for accessibility and educational purposes.

Impact

Our project contributes to making scientific knowledge about spaceflight health risks more accessible and understandable to a broad audience. By presenting the information in a clear and visual way, we encourage curiosity about human space exploration while also highlighting connections with health challenges on Earth, such as osteoporosis, muscle loss, and cardiovascular disease. This educational approach can inspire both students and the general public, showing that space research not only supports astronauts on long missions but also benefits medicine and healthcare on our planet.

Conclusion

In conclusion, we highlight the importance of understanding how the human body changes in microgravity and how health strategies can help minimize these effects. Through the infographic and slides, we present the main risks of spaceflight, along with practical solutions such as exercise protocols, balanced nutrition, and remote monitoring.

In addition to contributing to the safety and health of astronauts on long missions, this project also inspires applications on Earth, supporting the treatment of conditions such as osteoporosis, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular disease. The work demonstrates the value of interdisciplinary approaches between space science and health and is designed to be easily understood and accessible to anyone who views it, making the information clear, visual, and intuitive.

projectDetails.name: projeto Respira Bem – Seu Ar, Sua Saúde
projectDetails.summary:
RespiraBem is a technological and scientific project created to monitor air quality in real time, promote environmental awareness, and encourage sustainable practices among the residents of Santa Cruz das Palmeiras and surrounding areas. It arises in response to increasing air pollution and its impacts on health and agriculture, aiming to make scientific data accessible to the population through the integration of science, technology, and environmental citizenship.

The system uses satellite data from NASA (TEMPO, MERRA-2, IMERG, Daymet) and the WHO, combined with ground sensors and networks such as AirNow and Pandora. The information is processed in an interactive app that displays an air quality map, sends health alerts, offers tips and sustainable challenges with rewards, and includes the RespiraBem Agro module, designed for agricultural planning and reducing the impact of pollution on crops.

The project reduces exposure to pollutants, increases environmental awareness, supports smart agribusiness, and encourages eco-friendly behaviors such as recycling and alternative transportation. Developed in Python and JavaScript (React Native), it integrates NASA and WHO APIs and can connect to IoT sensors.

Creative and innovative, RespiraBem transforms complex data into practical actions, bridging science and society, and making Santa Cruz das Palmeiras a model of sustainability and technological innovation.

projectDetails.name: Stellar Minds: How the Human Subconscious Can Drive Space Innovation
projectDetails.summary: The human subconscious is a powerful source of creativity, intuition, and information processing. In extreme environments such as space, where response time, decision-making, and psychological well-being are crucial, understanding and harnessing the mechanisms of the subconscious may be the key to significant advances in technology, mental health, and human performance.
projectDetails.details:
The project aims to better understand the human subconscious and its various applications in space missions. We at Team Rota believe that our subconscious is a rich and underexplored source of knowledge, hiding valuable insights into how our brain functions. Today, with the advent of AI, developing this area of the human brain can help us connect more deeply and accelerate processes in scientific advancement.

Our team considered factors related to human interpersonal relationships. Often, we judge something subconsciously, which can either benefit us or not, depending on the situation. projectDetails.name: Project Teoria&Prática
projectDetails.summary: Aurora Sense é uma solução inteligente que une sensores biométricos, inteligência artificial médica e emocional, e dados espaciais da NASA para monitorar a saúde física e mental em tempo real. O sistema detecta sinais precoces de desequilíbrio, correlaciona fatores ambientais com o bem-estar humano e oferece orientações personalizadas de autocuidado. Inspirado pelo Outubro Rosa, promove prevenção acessível e integrada, conectando corpo, mente e planeta.
projectDetails.details:
Claro, Jennifer! Aqui está a resposta ideal para a seção "Detalhes do Projeto" do formulário do NASA Space Apps Challenge, com base no conteúdo completo do Aurora Sense. Está em inglês, direto e inspirador, pronto para colar na plataforma:

🌌 Detalhes do projeto — Aurora Sense

O Aurora Sense é um sistema inovador que combina sensores biométricos não invasivos, IA médica e emocionale dados da NASA Earth para monitorar a saúde física e mental em tempo real. Ele capacita os usuários a detectar sinais precoces de desequilíbrio, prevenir doenças e entender como os fatores ambientais afetam seu bem-estar.

⚙️ Como funciona

  • Os usuários usam wearables inteligentes (roupas, pulseiras, adesivos) que medem:
    • Temperatura corporal, fluxo sanguíneo, variabilidade da frequência cardíaca (VFC)
    • Níveis de oxigênio, respiração, condutividade da pele (estresse)
    • Microexpressões faciais e tom de voz (via aplicativo)
  • A IA aprende os padrões biológicos e emocionais de cada usuário, detecta os primeiros sinais de condições físicas e mentais e sugere ações personalizadas (respiração, hidratação, repouso, consulta médica).
  • Os dados da NASA Earth (radiação UV, poluição, umidade, temperatura, campos magnéticos) são integrados para correlacionar a saúde com as condições planetárias.
  • O aplicativo Aurora Sense exibe um mapa corporal 3D, radar emocional e alertas personalizados, além de campanhas educacionais como Outubro Rosa e Janeiro Branco.

🌍 Benefícios e impacto

  • Saúde física: detecção precoce de doenças e desequilíbrios fisiológicos
  • Saúde mental: previsão de estresse, ansiedade e esgotamento
  • Saúde ambiental: conexão entre clima e bem-estar humano
  • Educação: Campanhas de conscientização para prevenção e autocuidado
  • Ciência cidadã: mapa global de padrões de saúde e emocionais

O Aurora Sense promove o bem-estar holístico e democratiza o acesso a cuidados preventivos, especialmente em regiões carentes.

🧠 Criatividade e Inovação

  • Primeiro sistema a integrar corpo, mente e meio ambiente em um ecossistema de saúde unificado
  • Usa IA emocional para interpretar voz e expressões para insights de saúde mental
  • Aplica tecnologia espacial ao monitoramento diário da saúde
  • Funciona offline e é movido a energia solar, garantindo acessibilidade e sustentabilidade
  • Permite a ciência cidadã por meio da contribuição anônima de dados

🔧 Ferramentas e tecnologias

  • Hardware: Sensores biométricos e ambientais (ECG, HRV, oxigênio, temperatura, condutividade)
    • React Native (aplicativo móvel)
    • Python + Flask (back-end)
    • TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime (modelos de IA)
    • Reconhecimento de emoções de fala
    • API de dados da Terra da NASA + Mapbox (mapas interativos)

👥 Considerações da equipe

Nossa equipe se concentrou em criar uma solução inclusiva, ética e escalável. Consideramos:

  • Acessibilidade em áreas remotas ou com poucos recursos
  • Sensibilidade cultural na IA emocional
  • Privacidade de dados e consentimento do usuário
  • Integração com dados globais de saúde e clima

O Aurora Sense é mais do que uma ferramenta - é um movimento em direção à saúde inteligente, empática e planetária.

O LOCAL CHANGE é uma plataforma interativa e educativa desenvolvida por Pedro Henrique Duarte do Nascimento, com o objetivo de promover a conscientização ambiental entre crianças, adolescentes e a sociedade em geral. O projeto propõe uma experiência visual e didática que estimula o entendimento sobre o impacto das ações humanas no meio ambiente, aproximando temas científicos de forma acessível e envolvente.

O protótipo apresentado demonstra como a tecnologia — incluindo ferramentas de Inteligência Artificial — pode ser utilizada para facilitar o aprendizado e despertar senso de responsabilidade ecológica. Embora ainda em fase inicial, o sistema visa evoluir com integração de APIs ambientais, bancos de dados complexos e recursos de gamificação, tornando-se uma ferramenta poderosa de educação e transformação social.

Ao unir tecnologia, design interativo e sustentabilidade, o LOCAL CHANGE busca inspirar mudanças reais no comportamento das pessoas e contribuir para um futuro mais consciente e equilibrado com o planeta.
projectDetails.details:
O. O MUDANÇA LOCAL é uma plataforma interativa e educacional desenvolvida para despertar a consciência ambiental de forma visual, acessível e envolvente. Seu principal objetivo é mostrar às pessoas — especialmente crianças e adolescentes — o impacto das ações humanas sobre o meio ambiente, incentivando a reflexão e aprendendo sobre sustentabilidade.

A aplicação funciona por meio de uma interface digital que apresenta versões de diferentes regiões do planeta entre os anos de 2000 e 2020, utilizando imagens ilustrativas de satélite e gráficos dinâmicos. O usuário pode visualizar como o desmame, o crescimento urbano ou as mudanças climáticas alteram o cenário natural ao longo do tempo. As transições automáticas, efeitos visuais e textos educativos feitos a experiência mais imersiva e intuitiva.

Os os benefícios inclusem a educação ambiental de forma prática e lúdica‚ o aumento da consciência coletiva e a formação de uma mentalidade sustentável desde a base da sociedade. O projeto também busca aproximar da tecnologia das causas sociais, mais que inovou e sustentabilidade pode caminhar juntas.

O. O impacto fingido é inspirar as mudanças reais de comportamento e promover o engajamento de jovens em causas ambientais, utilizando a tecnologia como ferramenta de transformação social e educacional.

O prototipo foi desenvolvido com HTML, CSS e JavaScript‚além de conceitos de Inteligência Artificial (IA) aplicados ao design e à geração de conteúdos explicativos. As imagens apresentadas são ilustrativas‚mas demonstram o potencial do sistema quando integrado a APIs ambientais, bancos de dados geoespaciais e ferramentos como NASA/Wikimedia.O.

O projeto é criativo por combinar visualização de dados, contação de histórias e educação ambiental em um formato digital acessível. A ideia é que se qualifique pessoa, independente da idade ou conhecimento técnico, possível visualmente os efeitos das mudanças ambientais.

Durante o desenvolvimento, foram considerados fatores como:

  • Acessibilidade interface para diferentes públicos.
  • Clareza visual e educacional das informações apresentadas.
  • Potencial de Expansão com tecnologias avançadas (IA, Machine Learning, APIs ambientais).
  • Responsabilidade social ao tratar a educação ambiental como base para um futuro mais sustentável.

Em resumo, o MUDANÇA LOCAL não é apenas um site — é uma proposta de transformação, que busca unir ciência, tecnologia e educação para inspirar o cuidado com o planeta.

projectDetails.name: Project $AstroAgro
projectDetails.summary:
Imagine seeing the planet as a large living ecosystem, where each territory reveals where the food on your table comes from and why some regions produce more while others struggle to survive. This is how Farm Navigators begins an interactive ecosystem that combines science, technology, and education to raise awareness about the future of agriculture.
The platform combines a multilingual global map, which shows the actual origin of food and the environmental conditions of each region, with the educational game “Farm Navigators Quiz,” which invites users to make decisions, solve challenges, and understand the impact of their choices on the planet's balance. With each game, players learn in an educational and engaging way how climate, soil, and management are interconnected.
Farm Navigators is more than a game: it is a tool for visibility, traceability, and accessible learning. It translates complex data into simple experiences, bringing the public closer to the reality of agriculture and showing the importance of science in building a sustainable future. By connecting the countryside and the city, it transforms curiosity into knowledge and information into action.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction

Victor lives in the hinterland of Bahia, where the sun beats down on the land and rain is a distant memory. In recent months, he has seen his corn, bean, and tomato crops wither in the intense heat, his reservoirs dry up, and his herd waste away due to lack of water and pasture. Milk production has fallen dramatically, and some of the cattle have died. What was once the family's livelihood and pride has turned into uncertainty.

Without access to reliable climate information or tools to help him plan land use, Victor faces the same dilemma as thousands of Brazilian farmers: how to survive in the face of climate change and scarce resources? Meanwhile, in large cities, few realize the real impact of these losses, and even fewer understand where the food they put on the table comes from. It is in this scenario that Farm Navigators was born.

HOW WE ADDRESSED THE CHALLENGE

Our response to this challenge was the development of "Farm Navigators," a multiplatform digital ecosystem focused on agricultural and environmental education. This tool was created to engage students, farmers, and the general public in an interactive journey through the food production cycle, highlighting how climate, soil, and human decisions directly influence productivity and sustainability.

Through an interactive, multilingual global map, users can visualize the real-world conditions of different agricultural regions, understanding why certain locations produce more, others less, and how climate change affects these outcomes. Integrated with this map, the educational game "Farm Navigators Quiz" encourages active learning by confronting players with real-world agricultural challenges, encouraging informed, data-driven decision-making.

In "AgriFuture," users embark on an educational voyage comprising multiple levels, each consisting of two essential components: a learning phase and an interactive phase.

The journey begins with an immersion into the complexities of agricultural ecosystems, allowing users to understand how climate, soil, and water interconnect to sustain food production.

They then choose a specific country to explore, understanding that agricultural practices and management challenges vary from region to region revealing how factors such as precipitation, soil fertility, and water availability directly influence productivity and sustainability in the field.

The Farm Navigators experience is structured in three interactive phases, which guide the player through a complete journey of modern agriculture—from understanding natural fundamentals to applying intelligent data for sustainable decisions in the field.

Phase 1 – Soil, Climate, and Water

Hidden Forces Beneath the Soil and Sky

In this phase, the player explores the foundations of agricultural life: soil, climate, and water. Supported by NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) and GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) data, the user visualizes how soil moisture, temperature, and rainfall shape land productivity. This stage creates awareness of the balance between natural resources and productivity.

Phase 2 – Vegetation and Crop Health

Seeing Crops Through Space Eyes

Using satellite imagery and vegetation indices such as NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), the player learns to identify crop health, predict disease, and recognize patterns of water stress. This "through the eyes of space" view shows how NASA data helps farmers and researchers make more accurate crop management decisions.

Phase 3 – Farm Management with Data

Smart Decisions, Strong Harvests

Finally, the player takes on the role of farm manager, applying the collected data to plan irrigation, optimize resources, and reduce environmental impacts. This phase encourages critical thinking and data analysis, reinforcing the importance of technology and precision agriculture to ensure strong and sustainable harvests.

This part of the game represents the initial moment of the player's journey, where the central problem of the narrative is presented. The sequence of screens shows an experienced farmer facing increasingly difficult challenges in the fields: droughts that dry out the soil, heavy rains that flood crops, and rapidly spreading pests.

The goal of this introduction is to create emotional connection and contextualize the agricultural reality impacted by climate change, preparing the player to understand the importance of using scientific data in decision-making.

This phase serves as a narrative turning point: the farmer realizes that he can no longer farm in the same way and begins to question—"There must be a better way..."—which sparks the player's curiosity to seek smarter and more sustainable solutions. From this point on, the game invites the user to explore tools based on NASA's open data, demonstrating how information on precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation health can transform the way food is produced and ensure a balance between productivity and environmental preservation.

In short, this part of the game aims to introduce the problem, generate empathy, and motivate action, creating the ideal context for learning about sustainable agriculture and space technology to happen in a natural and engaging way.

HOW WE DEVELOPED THIS PROJECT

🌾 Context: Introduction to Agriculture and Interactive Engagement

After the narrative introduction, where the player experiences the difficulties of farmers facing climate change, the game begins to incorporate fundamental concepts of modern, sustainable agriculture. This transition marks the beginning of active learning, connecting the story to science and real-world NASA data.

  1. In this phase, the player is invited to understand how the balance between soil, climate, and water is essential for agricultural productivity. Concepts such as:
  2. Soil moisture and efficient irrigation, based on data from the NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) mission;
  3. Precipitation and the impact of rainfall on crop management, based on measurements from NASA GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement);
  4. Vegetation health, observed through NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) and other remote sensing variables.
  5. This data is integrated into the gameplay so that the user understands how agricultural decision-making can be guided by real information, transforming scientific knowledge into accessible, practical applications in the field.

🌱 The Agro-Educational Quiz

To reinforce learning, the game introduces an interactive quiz after the presentation of the concepts. This tool has a dual function:

  • To consolidate the knowledge acquired about sustainable agriculture, resource management, and environmental variables;
  • To measure the player's understanding, adapting the difficulty level of subsequent phases based on their performance.

The quiz presents simple, visual questions, such as:

  • "Which data is most useful for predicting a prolonged drought?"
  • "What does NDVI help identify in crops?"

The "Happy Harvest: Learning Through Smart Farming" phase represents the moment when the player puts into practice everything they learned in the previous stages about soil, climate, and vegetation. Here, learning turns into action: the player must manage their harvest strategically, making decisions based on real NASA data, which indicates ideal irrigation conditions, climate, and crop health.

Through simple, visual gameplay, the player understands how modern agriculture depends on the balance between productivity and sustainability. The phase uses data from SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) to represent soil moisture, GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) to indicate rainfall patterns and potential drought periods, and MODIS/NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) to assess crop health and identify the ideal harvest time. Every decision made directly impacts the final outcome: over-irrigating or planting at the wrong time reduces productivity and scores, while good practices—such as efficient water use, crop rotation, and monitoring weather conditions—increase the sustainability score. The feedback system demonstrates the scientific rationale behind each action, teaching the player in a practical way how spatial data analysis can guide real-world choices in the field.

  • The score obtained not only represents harvest success, but also the player's level of environmental and technical awareness. Through educational messages, the game explains why each decision impacts the agricultural ecosystem, reinforcing concepts such as precision agriculture, sustainable management, and the rational use of natural resources.
  • With this, Farm Navigators transforms the act of harvesting into an educational, interactive, and scientific experience. The player learns that producing more doesn't just mean planting and harvesting, but planning, observing, and acting based on evidence—core principles for a sustainable agricultural future aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the innovation and resilience goals advocated by NASA.
  • At the end of this phase, the player understands that the true "happy harvest" is one that arises from knowledge, technology, and harmony with the planet — exactly the vision that NASA encourages by promoting the use of its open data to transform global challenges into opportunities for learning and sustainability.

🛰️ Module – “Global Agricultural Watch Map”

The Global Agricultural Watch Map is a core component of Farm Navigators, designed to translate NASA scientific data into accessible, visually understandable information for the player. This interactive tool works in multiple languages, allowing users from different countries to explore information on crops, climate, and land use worldwide.

The map is powered by NASA Data Layers and presents real-time environmental indicators, including soil moisture, precipitation, surface temperature, and active fires. Each layer represents a set of NASA space missions, such as:

  1. SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) — measures soil moisture and its variation over time;
  2. GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) — records rainfall patterns and precipitation intensity;
  3. MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) — monitors vegetation, temperature, and fire detection;
  4. VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) — captures nighttime and fire data in agricultural areas.

🌍 Educational and Scientific Purpose

The purpose of the map is to democratize access to Earth observation data and show how it can be used to understand and improve global agriculture.

Players can navigate through different regions, compare weather patterns, and observe how soil, vegetation, and crops react to environmental changes.

Furthermore, the map connects to an analytical dashboard (“Global Agricultural Dashboard”) that displays real-time statistics, such as:

  • Global agricultural area monitored (4.8 billion hectares);
  • Crop production (9.9 billion tons in 2023);
  • Economic value of crops (US$3.8 trillion);
  • Active NASA data layers (9 sets with 5 operational satellites).

This data is updated automatically and presented in a simple way, allowing the player to understand how space technology supports agricultural decisions and sustainability policies.

🔍 In-Game Function

Within Farm Navigators, the map functions as a global exploration tool.

By clicking "Click Here to Use the Map," the player enters an environment that simulates the work of a researcher or digital farmer, allowing them to:

  1. View agricultural conditions in different countries;
  2. Analyze the impact of droughts, floods, and wildfires;
  3. Identify critical regions for food security;
  4. Export data and images for comparison and analysis (educational resource in the Export Data & Images tab).

To bring this vision to life, we leveraged material design concepts, implemented a monolithic architecture, and followed an agile development model throughout the project's lifecycle. "Astroagro" is designed to be accessible on cross-platform, achieved through the use of the Dart programming language and the Flutter framework.

Highlighted Features

  • Interactive simulations
  • Real NASA satellite data integration
  • Engaging narratives
  • User-friendly interface
  • Teacher resources, including lesson plans and discussion guides

Benefits

  • Facilitates a profound understanding of agricultural ecosystems and the impact of climate change on soil, crops, and water resources.
  • Empowers students to make informed decisions regarding water conservation and sustainability
  • Enhances critical thinking skills by allowing hands-on experimentation
  • Promotes environmental awareness and inspires the future generation of scientists and conservationists

projectDetails.name: Project BeeMove
projectDetails.summary:
Superbloom events, characterized by the simultaneous flowering of multiple plant species, have become increasingly irregular in recent years due to climate change. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, and shifts in precipitation directly affect flowering cycles and intensity. Understanding and monitoring these changes is essential for identifying vulnerable areas and anticipating long-term impacts.

To address this, NASA’s Worldview Superbloom Visualizations and the “Comparison Between Two Superbloom Seasons” tool were used to analyze differences between the 2020 and 2023 events, detecting areas with reduced blooming intensity and spatial distribution.

Drones complement these observations by capturing high-resolution images of flowering patterns and collecting airborne pollen samples. Repeated analyses establish a reference blooming pattern over time, allowing deviations to be detected. Once critical areas are identified, drones can actively disperse pollen to restore or support flowering.

By integrating satellite imagery, drone monitoring, pollen sampling, and targeted pollen dispersal, the project not only tracks superbloom dynamics but also proposes adaptive strategies to mitigate climate change effects. This combined approach provides large-scale monitoring, biological validation, and actionable interventions, supporting both scientific understanding and practical conservation efforts.
projectDetails.details:
The project monitors superbloom events, which have become increasingly irregular due to climate change. First, NASA’s Worldview Superbloom Visualizations, through the “Comparison Between Two Superbloom Seasons” tool, are used to analyze differences between the 2020 and 2023 events. This allows the detection of areas with reductions in blooming intensity and spatial distribution. To complement these observations, drones are employed for high-resolution image recognition of flowering patterns and for the collection of airborne pollen samples. Repeated analyses make it possible to establish a standard flowering pattern over time. Once this reference is defined, drones can also act as dispersers, releasing pollen in areas identified as having altered blooming patterns.

The project provides large-scale monitoring of flowering changes over time and validates these patterns with pollen data. It also offers a practical way to detect vulnerable regions affected by climate change and makes it possible to actively intervene by using drones to disperse pollen in critical areas.

The intended impact is to better understand and mitigate the effects of climate change on superbloom events. By integrating monitoring and intervention, the project seeks to anticipate changes, reduce the negative impacts of altered flowering cycles, and support strategies for maintaining blooming dynamics over time.

The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for structuring and presenting information, as well as VSCode as the development environment. CapCut and Canva are used to design and edit visual materials and presentations related to the project.

The project is creative because it combines satellite imagery, drone-based monitoring, pollen sampling, and pollen dispersion in a single workflow. It goes beyond monitoring by proposing the active use of drones to disperse pollen, creating an innovative approach that joins detection and intervention.

The system features an electrostatic collection mechanism. The drone-mounted module contains two key stages: the first is a control unit featuring an ESP32 microcontroller, equipped with environmental sensors and a telemetry system. The core of the collector consists of two filters: one at the intake and a second at the exhaust. A specialized circuit board between them generates an electrostatic field. As air passes through, the first filter captures the majority of microparticles, primarily pollen, while the second filter collects any remaining excess, ensuring highly efficient sampling.

To better understand and mitigate the effects of climate change on superblooms. By integrating monitoring and active intervention, the project anticipates ecological changes, reduces the negative impacts of altered flowering cycles, and supports the long-term resilience of these vital natural events.

projectDetails.name: Project Citynauts
projectDetails.summary:
CitySense is an urban intelligence platform that combines IoT and NASA Earth observation data to build a real-time digital twin of the city.
Through a distributed network of ATMOS NODES — solar-powered devices that monitor temperature, humidity, air pressure, and air quality — the system visualizes environmental conditions, predicts risks such as floods and landslides, and notifies citizens and authorities through visual and auditory alerts.
By merging ground-level IoT sensing with satellite data, CitySense helps cities become more resilient, sustainable, and adaptive to climate challenges.
projectDetails.details:
Problem

As climate change intensifies, urban areas are facing a growing frequency of extreme weather events — including floods, landslides, and heat waves — that directly threaten human life, infrastructure, and the environment.
Cities like Salvador, Brazil, exemplify this challenge: complex topography, dense population, and irregular housing increase vulnerability to sudden rainfall, soil saturation, and poor drainage. Yet, most monitoring systems remain centralized, delayed, and disconnected from the daily urban reality.

Today, municipal authorities rely primarily on satellite data, weather stations, and manual field reports, which lack spatial resolution and real-time granularity at the neighborhood level. Many cities also have limited communication infrastructures — so when disasters occur, alerts often fail to reach the communities at risk in time.
This gap between macro-level observation and micro-level response leaves millions exposed to preventable tragedies.

Solution

CitySense bridges this gap by transforming cities into living, data-driven ecosystems that can sense, analyze, and react to environmental changes in real time.
It integrates a distributed network of ATMOS NODES — autonomous, solar-powered IoT devices installed in streets, poles, and public spaces — with Earth observation data from NASA, processed through an intelligent web platform.

Each ATMOS NODE collects hyperlocal climate data (temperature, humidity, air pressure, and air quality) and transmits it via LoRa mesh communication, ensuring the network remains operational even without internet connectivity.
These data streams feed into CitySense, a web-based digital twin that fuses IoT inputs with NASA Earth observation datasets (such as precipitation, soil moisture, and elevation models) to generate a unified urban awareness layer.

The CitySense platform visualizes these insights through an interactive geospatial interface that:

  • Maps real-time environmental conditions across city districts.
  • Predicts flood and landslide risks based on sensor data and NASA climate layers.
  • Automatically triggers localized visual and audio alerts through ATMOS NODES in high-risk areas.
  • Suggests safe evacuation routes and community response actions dynamically.

Each node also acts as a public awareness beacon, displaying environmental conditions through a simple LED indicator (green, yellow, red) and emitting sound alerts for accessibility — allowing citizens to perceive local risks even without smartphones or internet access.

Impact

CitySense provides a new paradigm for urban climate resilience, combining:

  • Ground-truth IoT sensing for precision.
  • NASA Earth observation intelligence for global context.
  • Accessible local feedback for real-world action.

By decentralizing environmental awareness and empowering both authorities and citizens, CitySense transforms reactive emergency management into proactive, community-centered resilience.
It turns the invisible — the state of the air, soil, and weather — into something tangible, visible, and actionable in real time.

projectDetails.name: Agroisland
projectDetails.summary: The main objective of AgroIsland is to be the first player to reach 10 Victory Points (VP), earned by building new farms (1 VP) and upgrading existing ones (2 VP). A bonus of 2 VP is awarded to the player who reforests the most, while excessive deforestation results in a penalty of -1 VP. Players manage three main resources: money ($) for expansion, water (≈) for production and irrigation systems, and carbon credits (C), obtained through sustainable practices such as crop rotation and reforestation. During their turn, players engage in resource production and exchange, followed by expansion and construction actions, which include building new farms. Crucially, the game features an environmental risk mechanism in which the frequency of natural disasters accelerates if deforested biomes outnumber reforested ones. To mitigate this risk and ensure full yield, reforestation is essential and crop rotation is mandatory; failure to rotate crops results in a production penalty, while successful rotation generates valuable carbon credits. Players can also purchase NASA data cards to combat the effects of disasters.

projectDetails.name: Project Ford Enter Senai Cimatec
projectDetails.summary:
Anomatí is a SaaS climate intelligence platform that converts satellite data from NASA, ESA, and NOAA into accessible, actionable insights for farmers, communities, and public managers. By combining decades of reliable climate records with AI and statistical models, Anomatí estimates the probability of extreme events such as droughts, floods, and heatwaves. Unlike traditional weather forecasts, it provides long-term, data-driven risk analyses that support planning and adaptation.

Built on a scalable cloud infrastructure, the platform can handle millions of queries and features inclusive dashboards designed even for users with low digital literacy. Its versatility allows applications across agriculture, water management, public health, civil defense, and outdoor event planning. The project aligns with several UN Sustainable Development Goals, including Zero Hunger (SDG 2) and Climate Action (SDG 13).

With low operational costs and no need for data collection, Anomatí’s business model can include government partnerships, cooperative and insurance integrations, and premium subscriptions. The main challenges involve ensuring accuracy, maintaining simplicity, and defining a sustainable monetization strategy. Technologically viable and socially impactful, Anomatí represents a scalable global solution that democratizes access to climate intelligence and empowers communities to make informed, resilient decisions.
projectDetails.details:
Anomati is an innovative app that revolutionizes planning for outdoor activities, agriculture, navigation, and risk management. Using decades of NASA Earth observation data, Anomati goes beyond standard weather forecasts, focusing on the historical probability of extreme weather and water events over the long term.

At its core is an Intelligent Conversational Climate Assistant (ICCA), which engages with the user, transforming complex data such as flood risk, groundwater levels, air quality, and storm severity into personalized, easy-to-understand suggestions and alerts. From optimizing the best date for an event to guiding crop planting, Anomati empowers users and communities to make informed, proactive decisions, building resilience to climate challenges.

The app will be developed with React Native and will integrate NASA APIs and open AI engines. It also integrates with satellite APIs such as GOES, COSMO, and SIMSAT for accurate and secure data. For greater accessibility, data from up to 3 days of forecasts were made available in cache for consultation and download even offline.

projectDetails.name: Project AstroFarm
projectDetails.summary: Our team, getCodeSpace(), developed AstroFarm for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It's an educational game where players have three days to save their farm from a severe climate crisis. Guided by a NASA astronaut, players use a simplified in-game tablet to interpret real NASA data, like soil moisture and vegetation health maps, learning to turn complex information into sustainable actions such as precision irrigation and soil conservation. The project directly addresses the 'NASA Farm Navigators' challenge by creating an interactive bridge between NASA's Earth observation data and its real-world application in agriculture. AstroFarm translates this high-level technology into an accessible and actionable gameplay loop, demonstrating how data from space can solve problems on the ground. The project's importance lies in demystifying complex climate science and making satellite data accessible to a global audience. It effectively teaches the UN's Sustainable Development Goals—including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 6 (Clean Water), and SDG 13 (Climate Action)—in an engaging format. Ultimately, AstroFarm moves beyond passive learning to empower players with the strategic thinking needed to build a resilient, food-secure future, inspiring a new generation to become proactive stewards of our planet.
projectDetails.details: AstroFarm is an educational simulation game where players are tasked with saving a farm from an imminent climate crisis in just three days. It works by placing the player in the role of a farmer who receives guidance from a NASA astronaut; through an in-game tablet, the player learns to interpret simplified but realistic NASA satellite data on soil moisture and crop health to make critical, sustainable decisions. The benefits of this approach are multifaceted: it demystifies complex scientific data for a general audience, develops problem-solving skills in the context of real-world environmental challenges, and makes learning about the UN's Sustainable Development Goals an engaging and memorable experience. Looking at the bigger picture, the intended impact of the project is to foster a global sense of environmental stewardship and democratize the understanding of how space technology can be used to protect our planet, ultimately inspiring a new generation to pursue solutions that ensure long-term food security and climate resilience. To develop our project, we collected the NASA data and brainstormed about solutions that could solve the problem. Our project is creative in its unique synthesis of a compelling, personal narrative with hard, scientific data, transforming the often dry process of data analysis into an urgent and interactive quest. This gamification of climate science education is our core creative element. Throughout development, our team considered several key factors, primarily user accessibility, ensuring the gameplay and data were intuitive for all ages without sacrificing educational integrity. We also focused on narrative engagement to keep players motivated, and technical feasibility to ensure a polished proof-of-concept could be achieved, all while staying true to the scientific principles behind NASA's data and the global importance of the SDGs.

projectDetails.summary:
GreenOrbit is an interactive educational platform that transforms real NASA satellite data into practical, field-ready decisions. We developed a system that allows farmers to monitor climate conditions in real time, predict natural disasters, and learn sustainable farming techniques. The game uses datasets such as NDVI, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, and GPM to simulate real agricultural scenarios, providing alerts, evacuation routes, and crop recommendations.
The project addresses the challenge of democratizing access to space science and climate data, making complex information accessible and actionable for farmers and students. Its importance lies in reducing agricultural losses, increasing climate resilience, and promoting digital and environmental inclusion, especially in rural areas of Brazil’s Northeast region.
projectDetails.details:
GreenOrbit is a conceptual interactive platform designed to transform real NASA data into an educational and practical tool for farmers. Our goal was to develop the concept, architecture, and functionalities of a system that would use missions such as NDVI, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM, and GFSAD to monitor vegetation health, soil moisture, surface temperature, and precipitation levels—generating climate risk alerts and sustainable management recommendations.

The central idea is an educational farming simulator, where players manage a virtual farm based on historical and real data (1960–2020), learning about irrigation, pest prevention, disaster evacuation routes, and sustainable practices. The project also envisions an interactive community and local marketplace, connecting producers and consumers.

Although we did not develop the full application, we created the concept, visual design, technical structure, and data sources required to make it viable. The planned tools and technologies include NASA Earthdata APIs, Python, Unity, and Google Earth Engine, as well as 2D/3D data visualization.

The expected impact is to democratize access to space science, strengthen climate resilience, and promote environmental and digital education in rural areas. The project is creative by combining data science, gamification, and social purpose, making space-based knowledge accessible and actionable for farming communities

projectDetails.name: Inclusive Technology Identification
projectDetails.summary:
Inclusive Technology Identification (ITI) is an inclusive digital identification and authentication system developed for the “Create Your Own Challenge” category of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. It uses accessible technologies such as QR codes, MIFARE/NFC (RFID) chips, and tracking TAGs, with offline functionality and integration through a web platform.

The project addresses challenges faced by individuals lacking traditional identity documents or digital access, promoting social inclusion in sectors like healthcare, education, and public services. The system follows accessibility guidelines (WCAG) and uses open-source technologies.

It connects with NASA’s space-based capabilities by exploring how trackable identifiers (QR codes or TAGs) could be scanned by satellites or drones in emergency scenarios, helping locate people in disaster zones or remote areas — particularly where infrastructure is limited.

This approach merges simple, low-cost tools with global impact potential, aligning with NASA’s mission to support innovative solutions that improve life on Earth and beyond.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

The “Inclusive Technology Identification” (ITI) project is a digital identification and authentication system designed for social inclusion. It uses QR codes, NFC (MIFARE/RFID) chips, and tracking TAGs to enable secure identification of people without formal documentation. Codes can be read by smartphones, NFC readers, or RFID scanners. The system works offline and syncs when internet is available, with access through a web platform.

What are the benefits?

Provides a digital ID for individuals excluded from traditional systems

Enables access to essential services like healthcare, education, and social aid

Works in areas with limited infrastructure or connectivity

Extremely low cost per user (no biometrics or expensive devices required)

What is the intended impact of the project?

The goal is to promote digital and social inclusion for vulnerable populations, including undocumented people or those in emergency scenarios. The system also supports humanitarian operations, as identifiers can be tracked via sensors, drones, or even satellites in disaster zones — helping locate individuals and ensure access to basic rights.

What tools, programming languages, hardware or software were used?

Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Backend: Node.js or Python (Flask)

Database: Firebase / MongoDB

Hardware: Printed QR codes, NFC chips (MIFARE), low-cost RFID readers

Web platform: Responsive and accessible (WCAG standards)

Spatial integration: Exploration of drone/satellite scanning of tags for emergencies

How is your project creative?

Creativity comes from combining simple, low-cost, accessible technologies (QR, NFC, RFID) with a global-impact mission. The idea of enabling drones or satellites to scan tracking TAGs in isolated or disaster-struck areas is innovative and strongly aligns with NASA’s vision of using space-based technologies to help life on Earth.

What factors did your team consider?

Low-cost per identified person

Digital accessibility (WCAG compliance)

Offline functionality

Privacy and data protection

Usefulness in humanitarian crises

Alignment with NASA’s goal to improve life on Earth using space technologies

projectDetails.summary: The Automated Cleanup System on Mars uses intelligent robots to collect and compact waste on the planet's surface. projectDetails.details:
Automated Waste Management Project on Mars

The Automated Waste Management Project on Mars proposes an innovative and essential solution to ensure the long-term sustainability and autonomy of future human space missions. Facing the current problem of more than 7 tons of accumulated human debris on the Martian surface—composed of discarded hardware, inactive vehicles, and accident remnants—this initiative transforms waste into a valuable resource.

The system operates within a closed-loop circular economy, fully automated and remotely monitored, divided into three main stages:

The Three-Stage Process

Collection and Compaction (On Mars): Autonomous robots, equipped with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced vision systems (like an enhanced Perseverance rover), are responsible for identifying, collecting, and compacting the inorganic debris scattered across the surface.

Transportation (Surface to Orbit): Dedicated transport vehicles efficiently carry the compacted waste from the planet's surface to an orbital processing station.

Processing and Reutilization (In Orbit): At the station, a spacecraft equipped with a metal 3D printer recycles the debris, transforming the waste into construction materials and spare parts.

Impact and Benefits

This project offers crucial benefits that go beyond planetary cleanup:

Space Sustainability: Minimizes the human pollution footprint on another planet, ensuring clean and ethical exploration.

Operational Autonomy: Drastically reduces dependence on Earth for supplies and parts, lowering the costs and mass required for future launches. The ability to produce in situ is vital for long-duration missions.

Risk Mitigation: Decreases the danger of debris damaging sensitive equipment or contaminating crucial scientific samples in the search for life on Mars.

Terrestrial Innovation: The technology for extreme recycling and additive manufacturing (3D Printing) developed to operate autonomously on Mars will serve as a cutting-edge model for the Circular Economy 4.0 on Earth.

In summary, this project turns a liability (waste) into an asset (construction material), paving the way for a permanent, self-sufficient, and responsible human presence in space, while inspiring innovative resource management solutions on our own planet.

projectDetails.details:
Introducing RE-GEN, the next generation of recycling. Our solution is not just a space trash can; it's an autonomous system designed to generate essential resources for missions. The machine is a sustainable space system that enhances NASA's OSCAR technology.

Its main function is to direct and fully utilize gases from inorganic projects, transforming them into essential resources for expeditions:

Oxygen: To reduce cylinder transportation.

Plaster: Internal restoration material for spacecraft and future installations on Mars.

Sulfuric Acid: An agent for leachate mining in Martian soil.

Remaining gases that are not converted into these resources still serve as fuel for the spacecraft. RE-GEN is a model for our sustainable presence beyond Earth, proving that humanity can explore without destroying, as today's waste is tomorrow's infrastructure.
