projectDetails.name: Project Byte Sharks
projectDetails.summary:
The Byte Sharks project develops an intelligent maritime system that integrates NASA satellite data with linked networks to protect shark populations and preserve oceanic balance. The team created an interconnected mesh of smart tracking tags attached to sharks’ dorsal fins, capable of peer-to-peer communication underwater. Each tag shares environmental, positional, and biological data (species, sex, route, ID, nearby sharks), forming a dynamic data network that collectively relays information to surface beacons or satellites.

By combining this distributed sensing network with NASA’s oceanographic variables (SST, SSH, chlorophyll-a, etc.), the project builds a robust spatiotemporal dataset used to train predictive models based on the Inhomogeneous Poisson Point Process (IPP/MaxEnt). These models identify high-probability shark habitats and migratory routes, supporting NGOs in preventing illegal fishing and guiding companies to avoid construction in critical marine zones.

This system enables real-time ecological insight and long-term behavioral discovery — transforming sharks into sentinels of ocean health and advancing both conservation science and sustainable marine development.
projectDetails.details:
In the context of the “Sharks from Space” challenge (NASA Space Apps), the Byte Sharks team proposes an integrated system for monitoring, data assimilation, and prediction to identify shark use areas, migration corridors, and foraging hotspots with low latency and high depth coverage. The system combines: (i) smart tags attached to the dorsal fin forming an underwater mesh network via radio frequency, allowing each shark to act as a node for cooperative route and metadata collection and propagation; (ii) support buoys (beacons) equipped with submerged receivers and surface links that shorten response time by relaying consolidated mesh data to satellites without requiring emergence; and (iii) assimilation of oceanographic variables derived from NASA satellites (e.g., sea surface temperature, dynamic height, chlorophyll-a, gradients, and proxies for fronts/vortices) synchronized with the shared positions/routes across the network.

On top of this flow, we developed a data science pipeline that builds a large-scale presence-environment dataset and trains a spatial predictive model based on an Inhomogeneous Poisson Point Process (IPP), practically implemented via MaxEnt. This approach is consistent for presence-only data, avoiding the common pitfall of interpreting non-observation as ecological absence. The final outputs are probabilistic maps across multiple temporal scales (near-real-time and seasonal) estimating relative occurrence probability and habitat use intensity, along with connectivity indicators between areas (via encounter rates and information diffusion through the mesh).

The proposed system provides value to NGOs and regulatory agencies (protected-area planning, illegal fishing surveillance), to productive sectors (GIS layers to prevent construction in sensitive zones), and to the scientific community (unprecedented submerged behavioral series). The innovation lies in the synergy between a collaborative biological mesh, buoys that bridge coverage gaps, and an interpretable modeling framework — together forming a scalable foundation for evidence-based conservation and coastal/ocean planning.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch

Based on the challenge: BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology

A tool was developed that uses data from NASA, INPE, and CSA to provide the possibility of observing the pulse of environmental life through a simple and accessible idea.

Users can choose how to visualize and what to visualize based on all the data collected on plant flowering, pollen quantity, deforestation, reforestation, and different species in specific regions based on collected data.

We believe that a project like this is important because it translates science into something alive, understandable and actionable, connecting technology and nature so that people can truly see how the planet breathes.
 
This can facilitate learning about phenology, biodiversity, and human impacts, encouraging scientific and environmental interest among young people, schools, and communities. It also unites various data from multiple places in one single location, which few tools can do in an accessible way, thus helping researchers, farmers, environmental managers, specialists, and curious individuals.

projectDetails.name: Safe Journey
projectDetails.summary:
Safe Journey is an intelligent web application designed to improve travel safety by predicting weather-related risks along daily routes. Using data from the NASA POWER API, the system analyzes factors such as rainfall, temperature, and humidity to identify hazardous conditions like heavy rain, extreme heat, or snow. It then displays this information on a simple visual map, showing risk levels (high, moderate, or low) and recommending the safest times and routes to travel.

This solution directly addresses the challenge of reducing uncertainty and danger caused by adverse weather conditions, which contribute to about 21% of traffic accidents in the United States. By transforming complex climate data into clear and accessible insights, Safe Journey empowers users — from drivers and delivery workers to cyclists and pedestrians — to make informed travel decisions.

Developed with React, .NET, AWS, Vercel, and n8n, the project combines reliable data, modern technology, and user-centered design to turn information into safety, confidence, and autonomy for everyone on the move.
projectDetails.details:
Safe Journey is an app that uses data from the NASA POWER API to show weather risks along daily routes, such as heavy rain, extreme heat, or snow. It creates a visual map with risk levels (high, medium, and low), helping users choose the best time and route to travel safely.

The project aims to reduce accidents and increase confidence for everyone on the road — drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians alike.

Technologies used include React, .NET, AWS, Vercel, and n8n. The idea is simple and creative: turn climate data into safety and better travel planning for all.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI tools integrated with n8n to support the analysis of climate data and route predictability. The Google Gemini agent was employed within the automated workflows in n8n to interpret weather patterns, identify potential risks, and generate intelligent recommendations for the safest time to travel.

AI was used exclusively for data analysis and decision support, without creating or modifying any NASA visual or brand elements. All processed information comes from original and verifiable sources, ensuring transparency and accuracy in the results presented by Safe Journey.

projectDetails.name: ExoSense
projectDetails.summary: We built an AI-powered dashboard using NASA exoplanet data to detect, analyze, and visualize new worlds — merging science, technology, and curiosity.
projectDetails.details:
1. Project Overview

ExoSense is an artificial intelligence system designed to identify and visualize potential exoplanets within NASA’s astronomical datasets, such as KOI (Kepler Objects of Interest) and TOI (TESS Objects of Interest).
Our goal is to make the discovery of new worlds beyond our solar system faster, clearer, and more accessible — not only to scientists, but also to students and space enthusiasts around the world.

The project combines machine learning with interactive data visualization, allowing users to explore planetary candidates through an intuitive and engaging web interface.

2. How It Works

ExoSense automatically collects and processes data from NASA’s exoplanet archives. Using a trained neural network, it analyzes key orbital and stellar parameters to predict whether an observed signal likely corresponds to a true exoplanet.

Once the data is processed, the system displays the predictions in a dynamic dashboard where users can interact with visual charts, compare results, and even retrain models with new data.

The workflow includes:

  1. Data acquisition from NASA’s KOI and TOI catalogs.
  2. Cleaning and preprocessing of large-scale astronomical data.
  3. Machine learning inference for exoplanet detection.
  4. Visualization and exploration through an interactive web dashboard.

3. Benefits

  • Accelerated discovery: Automates part of the exoplanet identification process using AI.
  • Data made visual: Transforms complex astronomical data into clear, interactive visuals.
  • Accessible science: Makes exoplanet exploration available to both experts and the public.
  • Educational value: Provides a hands-on platform for learning about data science and astrophysics.
  • Collaboration-friendly: Encourages community research by offering reproducible and transparent tools.

4. Intended Impact

Our vision is to bridge the gap between space science and human curiosity.
ExoSense aims to make exoplanet research faster, more transparent, and more collaborative — empowering researchers to uncover new worlds while inspiring a new generation of scientists.

By providing an approachable, AI-driven environment for data analysis, we hope to:

  • Support ongoing exoplanet discovery missions.
  • Promote data literacy in astrophysics.
  • Encourage the integration of AI into future space research.

5. Tools and Technologies

Languages:
Python (ML and backend) | JavaScript (frontend visualization)

Core Libraries & Frameworks:
TensorFlow, Keras, Pandas, NumPy, Lightkurve, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Flask, and CustomTkinter

Deployment & Environment:
Docker containers ensure portability and reproducibility.

Datasets:
NASA Exoplanet Archive — KOI and TOI catalogs.

Hardware:
Developed on a standard CPU environment, scalable for GPU acceleration.

6. Creativity and Innovation

ExoSense stands out for its ability to combine scientific rigor with accessibility.
While most astrophysical tools are designed for specialists, our project integrates machine learning with a visually intuitive interface that invites anyone to explore the data.

Highlights of our innovation:

  • Real-time predictions through an interactive dashboard.
  • Seamless data-to-visualization workflow.
  • Adaptable neural network pipeline for retraining with new missions.
  • A modern, user-focused design bridging science and creativity.

7. Development Considerations

During development, we focused on:

  • Accuracy and transparency — ensuring reliable model predictions with interpretable metrics.
  • Data quality — careful handling of missing or noisy records in astronomical datasets.
  • User experience — designing clear, responsive visuals that tell a scientific story.
  • Scalability — supporting expansion to larger datasets or future NASA missions.
  • Reproducibility — using Docker for consistent environment setup.
  • Ethical AI use — maintaining traceability in data sources and decision-making.

8. References

  • NASA Exoplanet Archive
  • Kepler Objects of Interest (KOI) Dataset
  • TESS Objects of Interest (TOI) Dataset
  • TensorFlow & Keras Official Documentation
  • NASA Space Apps Hackathon Resources

projectDetails.name: Project Código Estelar
projectDetails.summary:
Our project was created to bring people closer to the universe. NASA holds a vast collection of images, videos, and valuable information about space, but much of this content is difficult for the general public to access. Often, the material is fragmented and presented in highly technical language, which distances those without advanced knowledge in astronomy or physics. This barrier creates frustration and a sense of exclusion, preventing more people from engaging with and learning about the space discoveries that belong to all of humanity.

To address this challenge, we developed a solution that makes exploring the universe more accessible, educational, and inspiring. We created an interactive platform that centralizes access to NASA’s images and news, offering a simple, intuitive, and engaging experience. Through a smart search system and a dynamic visual feed, users can explore space content in a clear and enjoyable way, understanding complex concepts through an educational and visual approach. Our goal is to democratize scientific knowledge, transform the way people learn about space, and inspire new generations to look at the stars with curiosity, understanding, and wonder.
projectDetails.details:
Our project aims to make NASA’s information, images, and news more accessible and understandable to the general public. The proposal seeks to bring people closer to the universe by simplifying access to scientific content and transforming how space knowledge is shared.

The central idea is the creation of an interactive platform that centralizes NASA’s data, images, and updates, offering a simple, intuitive, and educational experience. Through a smart search and a visual feed of news and images, users can explore space in an engaging way, learning about astronomy, science, and technology without needing advanced technical knowledge.

The main benefits include the democratization of scientific information, the encouragement of curiosity and interest in space-related topics, and the promotion of digital inclusion and interactive learning. The intended impact is to inspire new generations to become interested in science and to show that knowledge about the universe can be understood by everyone.

At this stage of development, our team created the semantic model and the functional flowchart that represent how the information would be organized and how users would navigate through the platform. We used Canva as the main tool to design and visualize these concepts.

The creativity of our project lies in combining education, technology, and accessible design, translating NASA’s complex content into a simple and engaging format. We considered key factors such as usability, inclusion, accessibility, clarity in communication, and visual innovation, ensuring that the public can learn about the universe in a meaningful and enjoyable way.

projectDetails.summary: PlantHere is a platform that uses NASA satellite data and geoprocessing algorithms to identify urban heat islands and suggest ideal locations for tree planting.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

PlantHere is an interactive platform that uses NASA satellite data and geoprocessing algorithms to identify urban heat islands and suggest ideal locations for tree planting. The system works by collecting MODIS data via Google Earth Engine, which is processed by a backend built with Flask + Python to generate heat map tiles. These tiles are displayed on an interactive map using a frontend developed with Leaflet.js, allowing users to view real-time critical zones for environmental action.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Strategic planning for urban afforestation.
  • Continuous monitoring of critical heat zones.
  • Targeted tree-planting campaigns in the hottest areas.
  • Community engagement through scientific data.
  • Improved public health and quality of life.

The project aims to transform spatial data into real environmental actions, promoting healthier and more livable cities. In light of the alarming rise in heat-related deaths—such as the 3,830 fatalities recorded in Spain in 2025—PlantHere offers a technological and sustainable response to urban climate challenges.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • Google Earth Engine for MODIS data collection.
  • Flask + Python for image processing.
  • Leaflet.js for interactive visualization.
  • NASA Terra satellite data as the scientific foundation.

Creativity and Team Considerations: The project stands out for creatively merging space technology with local environmental action. By converting satellite imagery into practical tree-planting recommendations, PlantHere bridges science, civic engagement, and public policy. The team considered factors such as:

  • The severity of urban heat islands.
  • The link between deforestation and heat-related mortality.
  • The importance of community involvement.
  • The technical feasibility of integrating geospatial tools.

Every data point analyzed becomes an opportunity to plant a tree in the right place—an innovative approach that unites nature and technology to tackle the climate challenges of modern cities.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):

We incorporated Artificial Intelligence tools at two key stages of the PlantHere project development:

  1. Interface and Frontend Design with Lovable: We used the AI assistant Lovable to accelerate the design of the user interface and user experience. The AI provided layout suggestions, visual organization, and intuitive interaction flows for the interactive map, ensuring accessibility and user engagement. All AI-generated images were modified to include a visible watermark, as required.
  2. Requirements Gathering with Manus: We employed the AI tool Manus to support the gathering and structuring of functional and non-functional requirements. The tool helped simulate user interviews, identify usage patterns, and prioritize features based on urban and environmental data. projectDetails.name: Project Coffe Stain
projectDetails.summary:
Astragate é um portal interativo que transforma o sonho de ser astronauta em uma experiência imersiva e acessível. A jornada começa em um website de narrativa em scrolling que explica a importância da Estação Espacial Internacional (ISS) e das pesquisas da NASA, conduzindo o usuário a duas experiências centrais:

NBL: Mestres da Flutuabilidade (2D): Um jogo que simula o rigoroso treinamento no Laboratório de Flutuabilidade Neutra da NASA. Nele, o jogador interage com os princípios da física para ajustar a flutuabilidade de um astronauta, completando missões que demonstram a complexidade e a importância da preparação para caminhadas espaciais.

Cúpula Virtual (3D): Uma experiência de realidade aumentada, acessada via QR code, que transforma a câmera do celular em uma janela da ISS. O usuário pode observar a Terra em tempo real e interagir com "hotspots" para identificar e documentar eventos imprevisíveis, como furacões e erupções vulcânicas, simulando a tarefa crucial dos astronautas de proteger nosso planeta.

Utilizando recursos e dados da NASA para garantir autenticidade, o Astragate aproxima o público da ciência de forma lúdica, despertando a curiosidade e reforçando por que exploramos o espaço: não para escapar da Terra, mas para melhor compreendê-la e preservá-la.

Astragate: A gateway to the universe.
projectDetails.details:
Um website de narrativa em scrolling que guia o usuário, explicando a importância da International Space Station e conduzindo para uma experiência 2D, um jogo onde o usuário simula o treinamento NBL e uma experiência 3D, onde usamos a câmera do celular para criar uma realidade virtual em que é possível não só ver o espaço sideral a partir de uma cúpula como também interagir com os “hotspots” que simulam a tarefa dos astronautas de identificar e documentar espontaneamente eventos transitórios e imprevisíveis — como furacões, tempestades de poeira, erupções vulcânicas e proliferação de algas — adaptando-se a situações em mudança de uma forma que os satélites pré-programados não conseguem. Tudo isso estimula a curiosidade e o despertar científico nas pessoas.

De forma gamificada você pode simular o treinamento NBL realizado pelos astronautas,interagindo diretamente com os princípios da física da flutuabilidade e os desafios de movimento em um ambiente que mimetiza a ausência de peso. O “NBL: Mestres da Flutuabilidade” é um jogo 2D com diversas missões que ressaltam a importância do treinamento realizado pelos astronautas, essencial para garantir a segurança e o sucesso operacional da exploração espacial humana.

A “Cúpula virtual” é uma realidade virtual aumentada, para utilizá-la o usuário precisa escanear o QR code, transformando a câmera do seu celular em uma cúpula de onde ele poderá observar o espaço sideral EM TEMPO REAL, sentindo-se como os astronautas na ISS. A realidade virtual/aumentada criada, somada aos áudios criam uma verdadeira experiência 3D 

O website 

Mostra a importância dos estudos realizados pela NASA (adicionar)

Direcionamento para os jogos

Um site de narrativa em scrolling que guia o utilizador através dos conceitos com vídeos incorporados, modelos 3D da ISS e do NBL, e visualizações de dados interativas.

Daria para adicionar uma parte com as últimas notícias? Ou as fotos recentes postadas no banco de dados da NASA 

O que vai add:

Deixar os textos comoventes, do sonho de criança e adicionar:

But you know why astronauts go to space?

To make scientific discoveries about the universe, develop innovative technologies that benefit life on Earth, and take the next steps in human exploration, ensuring the future of our species.For example accelerated disease modeling, cancer research, drug development, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine and many more! 

 How do they train to go to space?

The training lasts for years and is extremely rigorous. It includes using flight simulators to practice every detail of the mission, survival tests in extreme locations, and intense physical and psychological preparation to handle the space environment.

What is the importance of the NBL (Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory)?

The NBL is a giant pool essential for spacewalk (EVA) training. The buoyancy in water is the most faithful simulation of weightlessness on Earth, allowing astronauts to safely practice complex tasks.

What is the importance of the Cupola and its effects?

The Cupola has a vital dual function: it is a control station for operating the robotic arm and monitoring spacecraft, and it is also crucial for the astronauts' mental health, connecting them to Earth and combating isolation. Through the Cupola, science meets emotion: it reminds humanity why we explore — not to escape Earth, but to understand and preserve it.

“Como eles treinam para ir para o espaço?”

Localizado no Sonny Carter Training Facility em Houston, Texas, o NBL é a principal instalação da NASA para o treino de astronautas para EVAs. É uma das maiores piscinas interiores do mundo, com 62 metros de comprimento, 31 metros de largura e 12 metros de profundidade, contendo 23.5 milhões de litros de água. No seu interior, estão submersas maquetes em escala real de módulos e componentes da ISS. A prática de utilizar o treino subaquático para simular a ausência de peso remonta ao programa Gemini e foi inspirada pela experiência do astronauta Buzz Aldrin com o mergulho, que reconheceu as semelhanças no movimento e controlo corporal.   

O Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) é uma gigantesca piscina da NASA onde astronautas, usando trajes espaciais completos, treinam para missões. A água cria um ambiente de "flutuabilidade neutra", a melhor simulação em Terra da ausência de peso no espaço. Atingindo a flutuabilidade neutra, os astronautas não afundam nem flutuam. Esse estado permite que eles pratiquem com segurança todos os movimentos complexos e o uso de ferramentas de uma caminhada espacial, preparando-os para o sucesso de missões reais. 

Essa é uma etapa essencial para garantir a segurança e o sucesso operacional da exploração espacial humana, 

O NBL é uma ferramenta de ensaio para garantir que as operações em órbita sejam seguras e bem-sucedidas.

A simulação funciona com base no princípio de Arquimedes. Um astronauta, vestido com um fato espacial de treino, é cuidadosamente equilibrado com uma combinação de pesos e dispositivos de flutuação até atingir a flutuabilidade neutra — um estado em que não afunda nem flutua. Neste estado, o astronauta pode "pairar" a qualquer profundidade na água, permitindo-lhe manipular objetos grandes e praticar tarefas complexas como se estivesse sem peso.   

É crucial compreender que o NBL é um simulador processual, não um simulador sensorial. O seu objetivo principal não é fazer com que um astronauta sinta que está no espaço, mas sim que atue como se estivesse no espaço

The Role of the Cupola: A Window Back to Earth

From the Cupola — the panoramic window of the International Space Station — astronauts see our planet in a way no one else can. This view often triggers the “Overview Effect”, a profound shift in perspective that awakens a deep sense of connection and responsibility for protecting Earth.

Through the Cupola, science meets emotion: it reminds humanity why we explore — not to escape Earth, but to understand and preserve it.

O que é a experiência 2D? (OK)

A experiência 2D gamificada simula o treinamento de astronautas no Laboratório de Flutuabilidade Neutra (NBL). O jogo, "NBL: Mestres da Flutuabilidade", permite que o usuário interaja diretamente com os princípios da física da flutuabilidade e os desafios de movimento em um ambiente que mimetiza a ausência de peso.

O jogador utiliza uma interface intuitiva para "adicionar/remover pesos e flutuadores" a um astronauta 2D submerso na piscina do NBL. O objetivo é alcançar e manter a flutuabilidade neutra, onde o astronauta paira, simulando com precisão a ausência de peso. Através de fases progressivas, o jogador realiza missões como navegar pela maquete 2D da ISS ou completar tarefas de reparo, vivenciando o processo de treinamento que garante a segurança e o sucesso operacional das EVAs (Atividades Extraveiculares). Paineis informativos com recursos audiovisuais (imagens da NASA) são exibidos, explicando a importância de cada aspecto do treinamento do NBL e como ele se traduz em avanços científicos e tecnológicos que beneficiam a vida na Terra.

Este jogo destaca a importância do treinamento rigoroso realizado pela NASA no NBL. Ela desmistifica a "gravidade zero" e mostra que a preparação meticulosa na Terra é fundamental para as missões espaciais, educando sobre a física da flutuabilidade e a precisão necessária para o sucesso da exploração espacial humana.

O que é a experiência 3D (em detalhes e porquê é relevante): 

Ao escanear o QR code o usuário transforma a câmera do seu celular em uma cúpula onde ele poderá observar o espaço sideral EM TEMPO REAL, sentindo-se como os astronautas na ISS. A realidade virtual/aumentada criada, somada aos áudios criarão uma verdadeira experiência 3D 

Além disso, ele poderá aprender mais sobre os estudos realizados pela NASA através de “hotspots” que….. estimulando a curiosidade e o despertar criativo. 

Porquê é relevante?

Porque reduz a distância entre os astronautas e as pessoas. Aproxima a realidade vivida pelos astronautas para o restante da sociedade e ressalta a importância dos estudos realizados pela NASA para cuidar do nosso planeta. 

Como ele resolve o desafio solucionado?

Ele aproxima a experiência que os astronautas possuem para o público geral de maneira lúdica, interessante, interativa, imersiva e gamificada 

 

Teve uso de IA? Como e para que usaram? Quais usaram?

Sim, ChatGPT, Gemini, e as outras

Para gerar a logo Astragate, refinamento do conceito e mecânicas de jogo para a simulação de flutuabilidade, eração e otimização de trechos de código para a lógica de física e interface. Estruturação de textos educativos para os paineis informativos do jogo, garantindo clareza e impacto.

Como usaram os recursos da NASA? Eles te ajudaram? 

Usamos o banco de imagens da NASA para montar os slides, nos inspirar e criar a realidade virtual

Utilizei informações detalhadas e imagens do banco de dados da NASA sobre o Laboratório de Flutuabilidade Neutra (NBL), trajes espaciais e a Estação Espacial Internacional para garantir a precisão e a autenticidade do jogo 2D, tanto visualmente quanto conceitualmente nas explicações educativas.

(Vídeo de 30 seg)                                                                                                               .

"milhares de pessoas sonham em viajar pelo espaço e saber como é ser um astronauta. Agora elas podem!

Através do nosso website, crianças a adultos podem descobrir a importância dos estudos realizados pela NASA e sentir como é a experiência de um astronauta. Através de um jogo 2D poderão simular um treino NBL, experimentando os efeitos da ausência de gravidade total ou parcial. E experienciar como é ver o universo através da cúpula por meio de uma experiência imersiva, transformando seus celulares em verdadeiros portais (gateaways) para o universo. Tudo isso estimula a curiosidade e o despertar criativo e científico. 

Escaneie o QR code e comece agora sua jornada como astronauta, transformando seus sonhos em realidade.

Astragate, a gateway to the universe

(Vídeo de 3min)                                                                                                               .

É o aniversário de 25 anos da estação espacial internacional, mas o presente é seu!

"Em um mundo sem uma Estaçao Espacial Orbital... Ninguém nos alertaria sobre um furacão com horas de antecedência. Sobre Queimadas em massa, Sobre Tsunami." 

E que bom existe a Estaçao Espacial os astronaltas e cientistas, para cuidar do nosso planeta. Há 25 anos podemos nos sentir mais seguros!

Estes astronautas já foram crianças um dia que olhavam para o céu e se perguntavam… Como é ver o planeta lá de cima? Qual será a sensação de voar pelo espaço? De tocar as estrelas?

Este é o sonho de muitos, mas a realidade de poucos...

Ola Sonhadores do espaço, nos Somos a Equipe Coffe Stains e a nossa solução transforma a experiência espacial que é exclusiva aos astronautas — ver a Terra do espaço, flutuar em gravidade zero, ou treinar dentro de uma piscina simulando o espaço — em um portal acessível para todos." 

O grande desafio é: como levar essa curiosidade para qualquer pessoa, em qualquer lugar, de forma acessível e imersiva?

Te apresentamos O Astragate,  uma plataforma interativa e imersiva que te permite realizar o sonho de sentir a experiência vivida por um astronauta. 

Criamos um portal que desperta a curiosidade científica e astronômica, mostrando a importância dos estudos realizados pela NASA e proporcionando duas experiências imersivas repletas de recursos audiovisuais.

 De forma gamificada você pode simular o treinamento NBL, essencial para garantir a segurança e o sucesso operacional da exploração espacial humana, onde os tripulantes experimentam o fenômeno de flutuamento e a sensação de ausência de peso. O “Mestres da Flutuabilidade” é um jogo com diversas missões que permite ajustar a flutuabilidade e perceber os efeitos da gravidade total ou parcial, ressaltando a importância do treinamento realizado pelos astronautas.

Depois de treinados, é hora de decolar! Ao escanear o QR code o usuário transforma seu celular em uma cúpula onde ele poderá observar a Terra e os corpos celestes EM TEMPO REAL, sentindo-se como os astronautas na ISS e vivenciando o “Efeito de Visão geral”.  Esta perspetiva única frequentemente induz uma mudança transformadora nos sistemas de valores, promovendo um profundo sentido de responsabilidade e um desejo de proteger o planeta. Além disso, você poderá aprender mais sobre os estudos realizados pela NASA através da visualização que simulam a tarefa dos astronautas de identificar e documentar espontaneamente eventos transitórios e imprevisíveis — como furacões, tempestades de poeira, erupções vulcânicas e proliferação de algas — adaptando-se a situações em mudança de uma forma que os satélites pré-programados não conseguem. Esses dados têm impacto direto em nosso planeta ao monitorar a resposta a desastres naturais, as mudanças ambientais e até mesmo no planejamento econômico e urbano. Tudo isso estimula a curiosidade e o despertar criativo. 

Escaneie o QR code e comece agora sua jornada como astronauta, transformando seus sonhos em realidade.

Astragate, a gateway to the universe

Storytelling

“Quando eu era apenas uma criança eu olhava para o céu e me perguntava “como será a sensação de voar? De olhar o planeta lá de cima? De estar no céu e tocar as estrelas?”. 

Se assim como eu você sempre sonhou em ter a sensação de viajar pelo espaço sideral… agora você pode! 

Você está a um click/QR code de distância de obter uma experiência imersiva como a de um astronauta 

Abra seu celular, escaneie o QR code e sinta-se como um astronauta dentro da cúpula descobrindo a vastidão do nosso universo!

Astragate, a gateway to the universe”

projectDetails.name: Cosmo Casa Project
projectDetails.summary:
Cosmo Casa, a project that aims to transform the challenge of designing space habitats into a practical and engaging educational experience for students.
The program simulates the complex constraints of space engineering — such as limited space, mission duration, and essential functions — allowing students to apply their knowledge of science and mathematics in real-world scenarios.
Students choose modules, organize the layout of a habitat for the Moon, Mars, or an exoplanet, and visualize how their decisions impact the base’s efficiency and safety.
The system uses a fun competition format and provides detailed feedback to promote interactive learning.
In essence, Cosmo Casa acts as a bridge between educational theory and space exploration, developing critical skills such as creativity and strategic thinking in the next generation of engineers and explorers.
projectDetails.details:
Cosmo Casa is an innovative project designed to transform the design of space habitats into a practical, interactive, and educational experience—serving as a bridge between education and space exploration. Below are the project details based on the provided questions:

What does the project do and how does it work?

Cosmo Casa turns the design of space habitats into a practical and interactive experience, guided by real rules and constraints.

How it works:

Scenario Definition: The teacher begins by defining the mission scenario. This includes choosing the destination (Moon, Mars, or Exoplanet), the number of crew members, and the rocket model. The rocket model specifically imposes volume and weight limits that students must respect.

Design and Organization: Students act as space engineers, clicking and dragging modules they wish to bring into space—such as exercise or food production modules. They must organize the habitat in the most efficient way possible, positioning crucial areas like communication centers and the medical bay.

Testing and Consequences: Students test different layouts and observe in practice how each decision impacts the base’s efficiency and safety.

Competition and Feedback: Learning takes place through a fun competition format, culminating in a ranking of the students who best follow the rules and respect the restrictions. At the end, the system provides detailed feedback, showing what was correct and what could be improved—allowing everyone to learn from both successes and mistakes.

What are the benefits of the project?

Cosmo Casa addresses a dual challenge: the complexity of professional space design software and the lack of practical STEM application among students.

Educational and Practical Benefits:

Simplified Access: It solves the issue of professional software being complex and requiring advanced technical knowledge, which makes quick testing of multiple solutions difficult. Cosmo Casa allows students to experience this challenge in a hands-on and enjoyable way.

Practical Application of STEM: Students actively apply their knowledge of science, mathematics, and technology in real situations where every decision has meaningful consequences.

Interactive Learning: It enables students to learn interactively across scenarios, facing real challenges and understanding the importance of each choice.

Intended Impact:

Preparing the Next Generation: The project aims to prepare the next generation of engineers, scientists, and explorers and also educate students in general

Skill Development: It encourages creativity, autonomy, and strategic thinking.

Transforming the Classroom: By turning the classroom into a laboratory of innovation, education moves beyond theory to become a practical experience that connects learning to the future of space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used to develop the project?

It was developed in Python, using the Flask framework. SQLite was the chosen database, as it's easy to prototype.

How is your project creative?

The project’s creativity lies in its ability to transform a highly complex and technical space engineering task into an accessible and engaging experience for students.

Gamified Engineering: It is creative in the way it guides users through the design of space habitats using real-world rules and constraints in an interactive and competitive format (with rankings).

Realistic and Accessible Simulation: It allows students to experience the challenge of designing a crew habitat in space—where every decision is critical, and even a simple mistake can jeopardize the entire mission.

What factors did your team consider?

In developing Cosmo Casa, the team took into account both the engineering challenges of space habitat design and the educational needs of students.

Engineering and Mission Factors:

Volume and Weight Constraints: Considered the limitations imposed by the chosen rocket model.

Habitat Constraints: Addressed the many real-world limitations of space habitat design, including limited space, number of crew members, mission duration, and the need to include essential functions such as life support, exercise, and critical areas like medical and communication zones.

Educational Factors:

Software Complexity: Acknowledged that existing professional software is complex and requires advanced technical expertise, making it unsuitable for rapid educational testing.

Knowledge Application: Recognized the need to give students the opportunity to apply their STEM knowledge in practical situations with real consequences.

GitHub link: https://github.com/Ricar66/Cosmo-Casa

projectDetails.name: Gaia: Agricultural production balancing system
projectDetails.summary:
The Gaia project, developed for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge , addresses the problem of chronic food insecurity and chaotic urban subutilized that consumes valuable agricultural land in Brazil. It also notes that fertile areas are often subutilized by monocultures, which deplete the soil and don't prioritize local food security.

Gaia proposes an Intelligent Urban Planner solution. This solution uses 
Data Science applied to NASA Earth Science data (soil quality, land use, population density) to perform conflict analysis between urban growth and agricultural land potential. It suggests intelligent reallocation of urban growth to protect high-potential farming areas. The tool's predictive element helps prevent inadequate soil use, projecting scenarios for long-term sustainable growth and hunger eradication.

The proposal includes making Gaia an official public tool for planning agents and allowing citizen participation to complement satellite data. Its impact includes environmental benefits, such as promoting sustainable production systems like Agroforestry , and direct contribution to five UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including Zero Hunger (SDG 2) and Sustainable Cities (SDG 11). The roadmap for Gaia involves phases from Foundation (building the dynamic database with NASA data) to Expansion and Growth (official implementation and scalability).
projectDetails.details:
The Gaia project presents itself as an innovative web tool materialized in a visual and intuitive prototype. Its essence lies in the creative integration of vast NASA Earth science databases, combining crucial information such as soil availability for agriculture, population density, and land use. This data fusion aims to translate complex spatial information into visual and practical solutions for urban and agricultural land management.

The prototype is designed for action and the participation of both public leaders and citizens. Through data analysis, the initial screen delimits municipal regions facing identified problems. These problems are described and, as part of the analysis, immediate solutions are suggested to aid decision-making. In addition to this management view, Gaia encourages community engagement through reporting registration screens, functioning as open channels to receive detailed information from neighborhoods and localities. Citizens can submit data, information, and complaints, complementing the database and obtaining granular statistics that satellites may not accurately capture. To ensure a human and individual focus, the profile screen allows the user to consult previously submitted reports.

Technically, the prototype was built using Next.js, a React framework, with the languages TypeScript and JavaScript, in addition to HTML and Tailwind for the design. This architecture was conceived to answer fundamental questions about how to integrate different NASA data sources to visually demonstrate solutions, what data is essential to solve problems of urban sprawl and agriculture, and how to optimize the user experience.

As a practical result, Gaia proposes intelligent solutions for the reallocation of urban growth and for protecting areas of high agricultural potential that supply regions and can be better utilized for sustainable agriculture models with efficient production. This allows for the prevention of inappropriate land use, pointing the way toward sustainable growth and the eradication of hunger in the municipality. Acting as a solid database for management decisions, the tool can be developed to offer forecasting, comparing data to anticipate problems and design the best solutions, ensuring a long-term vision by simulating scenarios for the city's sustainability.

The intended impact is one of sustainability and transformation. The environmental impact seeks to reorganize monoculture into productive and sustainable areas, such as the agroforestry that Gaia can suggest, increasing biodiversity and regenerating the soil. The sociocultural impact aims to raise public awareness about the importance of sustainable production in solving urban problems. Thus, Gaia contributes directly to balanced urban growth and development with agriculture, the well-being of the population, and the environment.

projectDetails.name: N.A.S.A. Fields
projectDetails.summary:
N.A.S.A (Navigating Agriculture with Satellite Analysis) Fields is an educational web simulation that teaches precision agriculture through an engaging game experience. It combines the economic decision-making system of Virtonomics with the visual, layer-based dashboards of Cities: Skylines, integrating real NASA satellite data—including POWER (climate), SMAP (soil moisture), and LANDSAT (NDVI)—to recreate authentic farming conditions.

Players manage a virtual farm, making choices about irrigation, fertilization, and crop selection while observing how these actions affect yield, carbon balance, and finances. The system converts complex environmental data into visual insights, allowing users to grasp in practical terms how sustainable practices improve profitability and soil health.

By blending gamification with real-world data, N.A.S.A. Fields addresses the challenge of making satellite information understandable and actionable for producers and students, bridging the gap between science and practice. It empowers users to make data-driven agricultural decisions, fosters environmental awareness, and contributes to building a more transparent and credible carbon-smart rural economy.
projectDetails.details:
How does it work

The project integrates satellite imagery data about soil carbon stocks and agricultural practices. Producers input their farm management practices, and the simulator models how adopting sustainable approaches, like regenerative agriculture, would affect their carbon emissions, crop yields, and financial results. By translating complex environmental data into clear insights, the platform shows in practical terms how sustainable actions generate real economic benefits, such as increased carbon credits and long-term productivity. For regulators and policymakers, the system also offers a transparent and efficient tool for monitoring compliance and market integrity. Ultimately, this project guides decision-making, motivates change at the farm level, and builds a more credible and robust carbon market, which can stimulate the market to improve its tools to manage that, such as field-level sensors to provide a more accurate data.

Benefits of the Project

  • Greater transparency and credibility: By using satellite data and technological tools, the project allows for more reliable measurement and monitoring of carbon stocks in the soil, as well as real-time tracking of emissions and sustainable practices. This reduces subjective estimations and promotes trust in the generation of carbon credits.
  • Economic advantages for producers: The simulator demonstrates the financial viability of adopting sustainable and regenerative agricultural practices. Producers are shown how carbon credits can generate an additional source of income, while also improving soil quality and the long-term productivity of their properties.
  • Data-driven decision-making: With a robust database, producers, policymakers, and regulators gain access to quantifiable information that supports informed decisions toward environmentally sustainable practices and compliance with future regulations.
  • Efficiency in monitoring and control: Adoption of advanced technologies (e.g., satellite remote sensing, automated carbon meters) makes oversight over large rural areas possible and cost-effective. This leads to a decrease in regulatory loopholes and increases market integrity.
  • Incentive to innovate and comply: By highlighting both financial and environmental benefits, the project motivates producers to transition from traditional to regenerative agriculture, increasing adherence to sustainable methods even before strict regulation is in place.

 

Intended Impact of the Project

  • Transformation of the rural carbon market: The project aims to set new standards for measuring and certifying carbon credits in agriculture, fostering a more robust, credible, and regulated market.
  • Empowerment and education of producers: By offering accessible simulation tools and information, the project enables rural producers to take a proactive role in sustainable management, encouraging them to adopt practices that benefit both their finances and the environment.
  • Support for policy development: The collected data and continuous monitoring provide a solid foundation for the creation of policies, regulations, and technical norms that promote agricultural sustainability and climate responsibility.
  • Strengthening of environmental compliance: Through the efficient use of monitoring technologies, the project facilitates authorities and institutions to inspect and guide rural activities, closing gaps in regulatory enforcement and enhancing compliance.
  • Long-term sustainability for rural production: Ultimately, the project seeks to demonstrate how sustainable actions add value, preserve resources, and guarantee the viability and success of rural operations for future generations.

1. Lack of oversight and exclusion of agribusiness from obligations

“A law passed by the Brazilian Congress created a regulated carbon trading system, but excluded agribusiness from its main obligations. Rural producers can sell credits without the need to meet reduction targets, as a result of pressure from the rural caucus. The agribusiness sector remains the country’s biggest polluter and, even so, escaped mandatory oversight.”
(Antunes, Claudia. SUMAÚMA, 2024)gov

2. Weaknesses and risks in the voluntary market due to lack of oversight

“In Brazil, many carbon credits are sold without independent auditing or robust verification methods, opening the door to double counting, fraud, and operations with no proven environmental additionality.”
(Antunes, Claudia. SUMAÚMA, 2024)gov

3. Need for advanced monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) methods

“There are still weaknesses in monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) mechanisms in the Brazilian carbon market. Regulatory improvement and the adoption of remote measurement technologies are crucial to ensure environmental integrity and system credibility.”
(Bisinoto, Gustavo D. S. et al. ARACÊ, 2025)senado

4. Political justification and technical difficulty for rural sector oversight

“The technical difficulty of measuring and overseeing agribusiness emissions was the main justification for excluding the sector from the strict rules of the Brazilian Emissions Trading System. The approved bill chose to encourage good practices through voluntary mechanisms, with no direct oversight.”
(Agência Senado, 2023)agro.estadao

5. Importance of technological innovation and databases for efficient oversight

“The development of reliable databases and the implementation of innovative oversight methods, such as satellite data analysis, are essential for the advancement of the regulated carbon market in Brazil.”
(Bisinoto, Gustavo D. S. et al. ARACÊ, 2025)senado

 

Tools, coding languages, hardware and software used.

To develop the project, we combined geospatial analysis platforms, development environments, and design tools that supported both the technical processing and the interactive simulation experience.

·        Tools:

·        Visual Studio Code (VSCode): Main development environment for coding and integration, specifics of the project.

·        Lovable: Used for interface design and user experience prototyping and basic game loop.

·        Software:

·        Google Earth Engine (GEE): Used to retrieve and process satellite imagery, perform temporal analyses, and generate thematic layers.

·        QGIS: Used to inspect, validate, and refine spatial results, as well as create supporting maps.

·        Programming languages:

·        JavaScript/TypeScript: Used to retrieve satellite imagery through GEE and to develop the simulator’s logic and visual layers, enabling interactivity and dynamic feedback. Using Vite, React, shadcn-ui and Tailwind CSS.

·        Python — used to convert GeoTIFF to PNG files, process and enhance satellite image coloration for better visual understanding.

·        Hardware:

·        Standard personal computers for development and testing; heavy processing and data retrieval were handled in the cloud via GEE, minimizing local hardware requirements.

Together, these components created an efficient workflow where GEE and JavaScript powered the data and simulation engine, Python optimized image interpretation, QGIS refined the spatial analysis, and VSCode + Lovable connected technical development with user experience design.

 

 How creative is our project?

Our project’s creativity lies in bridging different worlds: agricultural science, satellite data analysis, and the interactivity of games. Instead of creating another data dashboard, we envisioned farm management as an experience as engaging as games like Civilization or SimCity.

Our main creative choice was to adopt a “macro” view of the farm. This allows producers to make strategic decisions and see their impact over time, crop by crop. The idea is to teach how to translate complex data—such as satellite images—into clear, visual feedback, showing how sustainable practices directly influence the farm’s carbon balance and overall health.

This gamified approach came from a question we had: “Would producers actually want to use a game for this?” The answer came from a real story shared by João (one of our team members), about a young mechanic at his farm who is an enthusiastic Farming Simulator player, turning what he learns in the game into practical, day-to-day farm skills. This helped us see gamification as a powerful tool for education in agribusiness.

 

What factors did our team consider?

Our creative vision was matched by a practical analysis to ensure the solution was feasible and fully focused on the client.

Human Factor and Privacy: The first thing we considered was the user. We decided not to require information about people’s actual financial capital, out of respect for privacy and to avoid any distrust. That’s why we introduced tutorial mode with pre-set values and a free simulation mode, allowing users to enter any values they wish for a more personalized experience.

Technical Feasibility and Data Quality: We evaluated different sources of satellite data for the simulator. By combining NASA data with Sentinel satellites, we found that it would provide higher resolution and allow for more accurate analysis in the simulator.

Strategic Opportunities: Throughout the process, we remained open to new possibilities. The discovery of a contact who works with carbon credit calculations for power plants was a turning point. We recognized this as an important business opportunity and treated it as a priority.

We utilized a variety of Artificial Intelligence tools to accelerate our innovation, research, and development process. Below, we detail how each was applied to the N.A.S.A. Fields project:

  • Brainstorming and Transcription: We used PLAUD AI to record and transcribe our brainstorming sessions, ensuring no ideas were lost and allowing for a more efficient analysis of the discussions.
    • ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity AI were used extensively to expand on initial concepts, explore different approaches to gamification, research carbon calculation methodologies, and understand the specifics of satellite data from sources like Landsat and Sentinel.
    • Claude AI was used as a complementary research tool to deepen our knowledge of regenerative agriculture practices and to structure the project's documentation.
  • Platform Development: We employed the Lovable AI platform to assist in the creation and development of our simulator's interface, streamlining the prototyping process and the construction of the software's visual elements.

projectDetails.name: Project Iron Shark
projectDetails.summary:
Our project combines satellite Earth observation and in-situ sensing to understand and predict shark foraging habitats. We developed a mathematical framework that integrates NASA datasets — PACE (phytoplankton composition), SWOT (ocean surface topography), and SST (sea surface temperature) — to generate daily predictive maps of shark feeding hotspots. These maps highlight oceanic fronts, eddies, and productive zones that attract prey and, consequently, sharks.

To complement and validate these models, we proposed an innovative electronic tag equipped with a hydrophone, GPS, and onboard AI capable of detecting feeding events through acoustic signatures analyzed by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). When a bite-like pattern is identified, the tag transmits data in real time, linking satellite-derived predictions with actual shark behavior.

This dual approach — space-based prediction + smart-tag validation — advances marine conservation, supports sustainable fisheries, and demonstrates how NASA’s open data can drive actionable science to protect apex predators and maintain ocean ecosystem health.
projectDetails.details:
Our project predicts shark foraging hotspots by combining NASA satellite data with machine learning and an innovative bioacoustic tag. The workflow integrates SST (MUR GHRSST) to detect thermal fronts, PACE OCI to identify phytoplankton composition, and SWOT to map ocean surface topography that reveals eddies and fronts.

Using Python (NumPy, Xarray, Matplotlib, and XGBoost), we built a data pipeline that preprocesses these datasets, computes gradients, and generates daily GeoTIFF probability maps of potential feeding zones. These maps visualize where environmental conditions align to attract prey and, consequently, sharks.

To validate these predictions, we designed a smart electronic tag equipped with a hydrophone, microcontroller (ESP32), and low-power LoRa/Satellite transmitter. The tag applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to underwater sounds to detect bite-like acoustic signatures, transmitting GPS-tagged data in real time.

The project’s creativity lies in closing the feedback loop between space and sea — satellite-derived models guide conservation and fishing efforts, while real-world acoustic detections refine the model over time. This synergy between remote sensing, artificial intelligence, and embedded systems showcases how NASA’s open data can be transformed into actionable science for marine conservation, sustainable fisheries, and ocean education.

Intended impact: support marine protected area planning, reduce shark bycatch, and inspire new generations to apply space technology to ecological challenges on Earth.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI was used in three complementary ways in our project:

1. Scientific Modeling:
We implemented a machine learning model (XGBoost) trained on multi-sensor NASA satellite data (SST, PACE, SWOT) to generate predictive maps of shark foraging habitats. The algorithm learns statistical relationships between oceanographic variables and known shark presence to identify likely feeding hotspots.

2. Smart Tag Concept:
The proposed electronic tag integrates an onboard AI model for real-time acoustic classification. It processes underwater audio through Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and a lightweight neural network to detect bite-like patterns indicating feeding events.

3. AI-assisted Documentation:
Generative AI tools (ChatGPT) were used only to refine English writing, structure documentation, and improve readability. All scientific analysis, data processing, and modeling work were fully designed, implemented, and validated by the team.

All AI-generated materials (text, images, or code snippets) were reviewed, edited, and integrated by human contributors, ensuring original scientific intent and compliance with NASA Space Apps guidelines.

projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary – AgroSpace Quiz

AgroSpace Quiz is an educational game that transforms real NASA satellite data into accessible knowledge for farmers, students, and agricultural professionals. Its goal is to teach, in a simple and interactive way, how to interpret and apply space-based information for sustainable agriculture.

Using APIs such as NASA POWER, SMAP, MODIS/Landsat, and EONET, the game provides data on climate, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation, and extreme weather events, allowing players to simulate agricultural decisions based on real data from their own region.

Through multiple-choice questions, players learn how to:

Analyze climate history and plan irrigation;

Interpret vegetation indices (NDVI);

Reduce water and energy waste;

Prepare for droughts and floods using NASA alerts.

AgroSpace Quiz combines education, science, and gamification in a multilingual platform (Portuguese, English, and Spanish), accessible via browser and mobile devices.
With a modern interface, educational feedback, and smart geolocation, it turns complex data into practical and sustainable decisions for the field.

Impact:
The project promotes the use of space technology to improve agricultural productivity, reduce environmental impact, and democratize access to NASA’s scientific data, empowering smart agriculture on a global scale.
projectDetails.details:
🧩 What it does / How it works

AgroSpace Quiz is an educational game that uses real NASA satellite data to teach farmers, students, and agricultural technicians how to make data-driven and sustainable decisions in the field.
The player enters their geographic location, and the system retrieves regional data through NASA APIs (POWER, SMAP, MODIS/Landsat, EONET).
This information is transformed into interactive quiz questions that simulate real-world farming scenarios—such as when to irrigate, how to interpret vegetation indices (NDVI), or how to respond to extreme weather.
Each answer provides immediate educational feedback, showing how space data influences real agricultural practices.

🌱 Benefits

  • Accessible education: teaches complex scientific data in a simple, gamified way.
  • Sustainability: helps farmers reduce waste of water, energy, and resources.
  • Smarter decisions: promotes data-based planning using real climate and soil information.
  • Digital inclusion: free, multilingual platform (Portuguese, English, and Spanish).
  • Environmental awareness: demonstrates how climate and soil affect crop health.

🌍 Intended impact

AgroSpace Quiz aims to democratize access to NASA’s space-based data, promoting more sustainable and efficient agriculture worldwide.
Expected impacts include:

  • Up to 50% reduction in water and energy waste on farms;
  • Improved productivity through use of historical environmental data;
  • Digital empowerment for rural farmers and students;
  • Global awareness about climate change and sustainable resource use.

💻 Tools, programming languages, and technologies

  • Frontend: React.js with Hooks and Tailwind CSS
  • Backend / APIs: integration with NASA POWER, SMAP, MODIS, and EONET
  • Geolocation: Navigator Geolocation API (GPS)
  • Design: Lucide React Icons + CSS animations
  • Multilingual support: i18n (Portuguese, English, Spanish)
  • Platform: Web App / Progressive Web App (works online and offline)
  • Database (optional): local JSON or Supabase for future scalability

💡 Creativity

AgroSpace Quiz turns complex scientific space data into a fun, interactive learning experience.
It is the first multilingual quiz that uses real NASA data to simulate real-world agricultural decisions, combining data science, education, and sustainability through gamification.
The interface is modern and engaging, with maps, animations, and visual feedback that make learning dynamic and enjoyable.

🧠 Key factors considered by the team

  • Ease of use: accessible to anyone with a smartphone or computer.
  • Low cost: fully free and lightweight.
  • Scalability: easily expandable with new questions, crops, and regions.
  • Social relevance: designed for farmers who rarely have access to scientific tools.
  • UN SDG alignment: contributes to Goals #2 (Zero Hunger) and #13 (Climate Action).
  • Real-world application: teaches decisions that can be immediately applied in farming.

projectDetails.summary:
SatelliteHub, a Global Orbital Data Platform via API , aiming to democratize access to powerful, yet currently inaccessible, space data. The project addresses challenges like data fragmentation, technical barriers, and prohibitive costs associated with orbital data. SatelliteHub acts as the "AWS of Space Data" , unifying and normalizing data from multiple sources, including NASA and ESA satellites, commercial partners, and Eventually its own constellation of metallic and biodegradable wooden nanosatellites.

The core of the solution is a simple REST API with SDKs in 5+ languages, dramatically reducing integration time from six months to six lines of code. The platform also features automated processing (NDVI, etc.), AI for analysis, and a no-code web dashboard. This is important because it enables over 100 verticals, from AgTech and Environmental Monitoring to Smart Cities and Defense, to finally leverage satellite data for precision agriculture, real-time deforestation alerts, risk management, and more. Lambda Lovers' moat is its combination of API-first, multi-source data, superior developer experience, and a commitment to orbital sustainability with carbon-negative wooden satellites.
projectDetails.details:
Project Ybyrá: The Global Orbital Data Platform

The Ybyrá project, developed by Lambda Lovers, is an ambitious Global Orbital Data Platform and SDK designed to revolutionize access to satellite and geospatial data. Positioned as the "Leading Cloud Platform for Space Data," Ybyrá’s core mission is to make Earth Observation (EO) data universally accessible, easy to use, and directly available to developers and enterprises worldwide.

Core Offering and Architecture

Decentralized Data and LEO Satellite APIs

Unlike traditional systems that centralize data within a single entity like NASA, Ybyrá's approach is fundamentally decentralized and developer-centric:

  • SDK with Decentralized Data: The Ybyrá Software Development Kit (SDK) provides a streamlined interface for accessing a vast, distributed network of geospatial data. The data itself is not solely centralized within NASA's systems; instead, Ybyrá aggregates, normalizes, and delivers data from a multitude of independent global sources.
  • LEO Satellite APIs: The platform leverages Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, including its own planned constellation, to provide high-frequency, near-real-time data access via its REST APIs. This architecture ensures speed, global coverage, and resilience.

Universal Data Unification

Ybyrá acts as a powerful middleware layer, unifying and simplifying access to a diverse and growing range of orbital data sources:

  • Public Sources: Integrates data from key public missions like NASA (Landsat, MODIS) and ESA (Sentinel-2, Copernicus).
  • Commercial Partnerships: Includes high-quality data from commercial providers such as Planet and Spire.
  • Ybyrá Constellation: Future integration of data from its own planned satellite network.

Seamless Functionality

Ybyrá’s platform automates the complex, time-consuming tasks associated with processing geospatial data:

  • The platform not only unifies multi-source data but also automatically normalizes and processes it, generating valuable analytics like NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) and NDRE (Normalized Difference Red Edge).
  • Simplicity and Speed: Users can access this unified and processed data easily via a simple REST API (JSON output) or comprehensive SDKs available in principal programming languages. This developer-first approach dramatically reduces the integration time from an estimated six months to just six lines of code.

Creativity and Unique Differentiators

Sustainability and Environmental Moat

Ybyrá is building a robust sustainability moat through groundbreaking, eco-conscious technology:

  • The World's First Biodegradable Satellite: The project plans to launch the world's first commercial-use biodegradable wooden satellite. This design is engineered to be 100% biodegradable upon re-entry and is carbon negative, setting a new standard for sustainable space operations and mitigating the growing problem of space debris.

Data Quality and Coverage Advantage

To surpass current public and commercial offerings, Ybyrá is investing in its own infrastructure:

  • Premium Resolution and Daily Coverage: Developing its own constellation allows Ybyrá to offer a premium resolution of 5 meters and guarantee daily coverage of the planet, significantly improving upon the temporal and spatial quality of current public data sources.

Technology and Partnerships

The platform is built on a foundation of robust technology and strategic alliances:

  • Technology Stack: The core platform leverages an API-first architecture with comprehensive SDKs for multiple languages, all backed by scalable cloud infrastructure.
  • Key Partnerships: The project is supported by collaborations with established institutions, including NASA CSLI (CubeSat Launch Initiative) and INPE (Brazil’s National Institute for Space Research) for satellite development and data integration.

Vision

The Lambda Lovers team has set a bold target, aiming for a valuation of US$ 1 Billion+ by 2029, cementing Ybyrá’s position as the definitive infrastructure layer for the global geospatial economy.

projectDetails.name: Flowering View
projectDetails.summary: We chose the Bloomwatch challenge because it aligned with the personal experiences and interests of our group members. With a focus on economic and humanitarian development, we created a website to serve the agricultural sector by aiming to increase rural productivity. Our site allows anyone to view regional pollen data and serves as an educational tool, explaining the benefits of pollination for plants. Our project's goal is to improve the quality of both planting and flowering, making it an important initiative for agricultural development.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an innovative solution that transforms NASA's remote sensing data into actionable intelligence to solve a global challenge: the desynchronization between agricultural flowering and pollinators, which threatens food security and causes massive economic losses. Our platform continuously processes NASA's Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to generate a high-precision, dynamic map of crop health and status. Based on this, our predictive system issues strategic alerts to farmers, enabling them to optimize their operations and ensure effective pollination.

To achieve this precision, we integrated an artificial intelligence ecosystem where models like Gemini and GPT are used to enrich our agricultural crop data, while a Cloud AI-based architecture ensures the real-time integration and delivery of alerts. The direct impact is the strengthening of food security and the promotion of a more resilient and sustainable agriculture, with the potential to reverse billions of dollars in annual losses within the global agricultural sector.

The key innovation of this project is the democratization of access to space technology. We are converting a NASA scientific asset, previously restricted to specialists, into a predictive and intuitive tool placed directly in the hands of farmers. Our initiative was conceived with a global vision, focusing on usability and socioeconomic impact, demonstrating how the collaboration between NASA's space science and artificial intelligence can generate scalable solutions for urgent humanitarian challenges.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We utilize a combination of AI technologies, including cloud-based AI, Comet AI, and general-purpose chatbots like Gemini and GPT. These AI systems are employed to gather specific data on various plants, such as primary crops and their cultivated areas and translate everting to english. Furthermore, we leverage cloud AI to develop our website and integrate NASA's Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) data, ensuring it is continuously updated.

projectDetails.name: Lightcurve Scan
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a fully automated pipeline for the analysis of real Kepler mission light curves, focused on detecting and characterizing planetary transits in a simple, scalable, and reproducible way.

Using official data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive, we filtered a balanced set of 500 confirmed and 500 candidate exoplanets. Their light curves were automatically downloaded using Lightkurve, then preprocessed to remove outliers, normalize flux, and clean noise. We applied the Box Least Squares (BLS) algorithm to detect periodic transit signals and visualize them through folded light curves.

The result is a functional prototype that generates transit plots, summary outputs, and a CSV with transit parameters—ready for further scientific analysis or machine learning applications.

Our project addresses the challenge by making complex astrophysical data accessible to anyone with a browser and Google Colab, without requiring powerful hardware or prior domain expertise. It empowers students, citizen scientists, and researchers to explore real space data and contribute to exoplanet discovery.

This prototype lays the foundation for scalable, democratized exoplanet transit detection—opening the door to broader participation in space science.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do and how does it work?
ExoDetect is a fully automated pipeline that downloads, cleans, and analyzes real light curves from the Kepler mission to detect potential exoplanet transits. It uses official NASA data (from the Exoplanet Archive), Lightkurve for data access, and the Box Least Squares (BLS) algorithm to identify transit-like signals. The pipeline saves the results as visual plots and a CSV summary for easy inspection and downstream use.

What benefits does it have?
The main benefit is accessibility: our tool allows anyone with a Google account to run real exoplanet transit detection experiments—no need for high-end hardware or local software setup. It’s ideal for education, citizen science, and rapid prototyping of exoplanet detection methods.

What is the intended impact of the project?
We aim to democratize access to real space data, enabling students and enthusiasts around the world to explore planetary science hands-on. Our solution lowers the entry barrier to exoplanet research, fostering scientific curiosity and literacy in space exploration.

What tools and technologies were used?

- Languages & Libraries: Python, Lightkurve, Pandas, Matplotlib, Astropy, NumPy

- Environment: Google Colab (free GPU/CPU access in-browser)

- Data Sources: NASA Exoplanet Archive (Kepler), via manually curated .csv file

- Algorithms: Box Least Squares for transit detection

- Outputs: .png light curves, .csv results table, and intermediate .fits storage

What makes it creative?
Unlike most academic pipelines, ExoDetect is simplified, modular, and educational. It maintains scientific rigor while being friendly to non-experts. It’s designed to be both a tool and a learning platform, offering transparency, interactivity, and ease of experimentation.

What factors did your team consider?
We prioritized:

- Official data only (no simulations)

- Equal balance of confirmed vs candidate planets

- Fast setup and clear outputs for non-specialists

- Scalability (can extend to TESS, K2, or future missions)

- Reproducibility (notebooks can be forked and reused easily)

The project is creative because it combines advanced generative AI and machine learning techniques with interactive visualizations, allowing users to explore relationships between articles dynamically and intuitively.
