projectDetails.name: Exo.AI
projectDetails.summary: Exo.AI automates exoplanet discovery using NASA's Kepler, K2, and TESS mission data through advanced machine learning. Ensemble Models (HistGradientBoosting + RandomForest) were trained on 21,000+ samples with 65+ advanced engineered features. The system provides explainable AI via SHAP analysis, enabling scientists to understand model decisions. We automatically detect known exoplanets with 99.5% similarity matching and offer comprehensive comparison tools with confirmed exoplanets, transforming manual identification into automated classification. Exo.AI democratizes exoplanet discovery through an intuitive web interface that allows researchers and enthusiasts to analyze candidate data, visualize planetary characteristics, and prioritize follow-up observations. The platform processes batch data, ranks candidates by scientific interest, and offers real-time model training capabilities. Built with FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and containerized deployment, Exo.AI accelerates the discovery of worlds beyond our solar system by providing transparent, automated exoplanet identification for both scientific research and educational exploration.
projectDetails.details:
Project Overview

Exo.AI is an advanced system for analysis and exoplanet detection that uses AI to identify possible exoplanet candidates orbiting distant stars. This project represents an end-to-end ML solution that combines exploratory analysis of NASA satellite datasets (Kepler, TESS and K2), advanced feature engineering based on physics real context, advanced modeling techniques like imputation and strategic data unification of all missions did by NASA. Therefore, we're abstracting all complex logic to a simple and modern interface that both users and scientists can use to achieve your objectives, studying, exploring, researching, you decide!

1. Exploratory Analysis of Data

To extract valuable information from raw photometric data and other types of datas, we've implemented a exploratory data analysis (EDA) and feature engineering pipeline for exoplanet catalogs from Kepler, TESS, and K2 missions. The workflow is designed to unify heterogeneous catalogs, derive physically meaningful features, and prepare the data for robust modeling and imputation.

1.1. Data Unification from Different Sources

We've started by implementing an canonical mapping system to unify data from all three missions (K2, Kepler, TESS) each one with different nomenclatures, types and distinct formates. The main identifiers extracted from NASA's exoplanet data includes: Identification Rows, Orbital Informations, Planet Dimessions & Mass, Transit Geometry, Astrometry / Photometry Essentials, Signal / Quality. And then, based on those features we divided into two categories of features, FEATURES_MAP and CRITICAL_FEATURES.

After mapping critical features, we decide to analyze missingness to visualize gaps on datasets and possible actions to pré-process our new features. This heatmap exhibes an abroad visualization to understand how null or nan data appears on dataset. This leverages us to implement posterior imputation or physical derivative features to achieve high metrics on our model perfomance.

1.2. Derived Features

To enhance our model performance we leverage an abroad study on physics and astronomical context and have mapped some physics features on our feature engineering processing, we've added physics variables on our data set

  • Planet Surface Gravity : g = G * M / R²;
  • Stellar Luminosity in AU: (R/Rsun)^2 * (Teff/5772 K) ^ 4;
  • Semi Major Axis of Plannetary Orbit in AU: if 'semi_major_axis_au' missing estimate via Kepler's third law (P in days, Mstar in Msun): a(AU) = ( (P/365.25)^2 * Mstar) ^(1/3) ;
  • Incident Flux Recalculated: Recompute insolation using luminosity and a (S_earth);
  • Equilibrium Temperature: Theoric temp if planet was a black body in radioactive equilibrium: Teq = Teff * sqrt (R * / (2a)) * ( 1 - A) ^ (1/4) with A=0 (Zero albedo) Planet absorving 100% of light;
  • Planetary Density: Relation between mass and volume.

1.3. Heavy-Tail Variable Distribution (Pre-Imputation)

This image show two critical features of project Exo.AI before imputation revealing important patterns about quality and nature of astronomical data from NASA missions.

  • Planet Insolation Earth Combined: Shows an unimodal distribution with skew positive;
  • Transit Depth: Shows a complex multimodal distribution

This image demonstrate the inherit complexity of astronomical real data and justify the sofistication of our pipeline. Distributions mutimodais and outliers presences shows why that was necessary.

1.4. KNN Imputation

Later we've implemented an imputation system KNN based on physic similarity to reduce missingness from ~60% to ~5% without lose performance and maintaining a clean dataset without deviate values. The target variable is a binary label based on the disposition field, where both "CONFIRMED" and "CANDIDATE" are treated as positive classes. After encoding, the positive class rate is about 39%, indicating some class imbalance.

2. Modeling

2.1. Baseline Modeline with HistGradientBoosting

The remaining features were split into numeric and categorical sets. Categorical variables with low cardinality were one-hot encoded, while high-cardinality ones were skipped for simplicity. The baseline model uses HistGradientBoostingClassifier. This model achieved strong performance with an ROC-AUC of ~0.935 and PR-AUC of ~0.921. A default probability threshold of 0.5 yielded good but improvable results. Precision-recall tradeoffs were analyzed, and an optimized threshold was selected to maximize recall under a precision constraint (≥ 0.85).

2.3. Model Calibration & Interpretation

A calibration curve showed that the model was fairly well-calibrated, but not perfect. Calibration wasn't explicitly applied, though it's suggested for production environments.

2.4. Cross-Validation & Ensemble Modeling

A 10-fold stratified cross-validation confirmed the robustness of the baseline model with consistent ROC-AUC and PR-AUC across folds. To improve performance, a secondary model using RandomForestClassifier was trained, and its output was averaged with the gradient boosting model to form a simple ensemble. This ensemble slightly improved performance (ROC-AUC to ~0.940 and PR-AUC to ~0.925), demonstrating the benefit of combining models. An additional threshold optimization was performed for the ensemble, further refining performance under the same precision constraint.

2.5. Final Resume ML Layer

At final we transformed 21.224 samples with 65 astronomical features into a world-class machine learning model for exoplanet detection. With a hybrid and scientifically validated approach, it achieved ROC-AUC of 0.983, recall of 95.9% and precision of 96.9%, prioritizing not losing real candidates. The optimized set, combined with a robust analysis of errors and feature importance, guarantees performance, interpretability and generalization. This model is the technical core that underpins Exo.AI's entire intelligent API — accelerating discoveries with scientific confidence.

Following is our architecture of modeling pipeline:

3. Backend API & Deployment

We delivered a production-grade, RESTful API system that abstracts complex machine learning workflows into clean, intuitive endpoints. Built on FastAPI and structured under the versioned path /api/v1/, the architecture is modular, scalable, and tailored to meet the needs of both general users and expert scientists in the domain of exoplanet discovery and validation.

3.1. API Structure & Modular Design

At the heart of Exo.AI is a router-based architecture that organizes endpoints by functionality. This design promotes clarity, testability, and maintainability, supporting both ease of use and extensibility as the system evolves.

3.2. Prediction Module

3.2.1 Prediction Module — /api/v1/predict/

The prediction module serves as the gateway for model inference, offering dual interfaces depending on user expertise.

  • POST /predict/user: Designed for non-specialist users, this interface simplifies predictions using only 7 essential features. It includes automatic imputation, a quality scoring mechanism based on data integrity, and seamless persistence to the database.
  • POST /predict/scientist: Tailored for expert users, this endpoint exposes the full power of the model with access to over 65 engineered features. It performs granular quality diagnostics and stores rich scientific metadata along with each prediction.
3.2.2. Explainability Module — /api/v1/explain/

To ensure transparency, Exo.AI integrates real-time explainability using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations).

  • POST /explain/user and POST /explain/scientist return visual and numerical explanations that highlight which features influenced a given prediction the most.
3.2.3. Comparison Module — /api/v1/compare/

This unique scientific utility contextualizes a predicted candidate by identifying similar, confirmed exoplanets.

  • POST /compare/user returns a list of analog planets based on internal similarity algorithms, providing meaningful references for follow-up study.
3.2.4. Batch Processing Module — /api/v1/batch/

Exo.AI empowers large-scale analysis through its batch processing engine.

  • POST /batch/process and POST /batch/process-csv allow users to submit multiple candidates via structured data or CSV files, supporting automatic feature mapping and ranking by scientific interest.
3.2.5. Scientific Dashboard Module — /api/v1/dashboard/

To bridge predictions with visual insights, the dashboard module offers rich interfaces for researchers.

  • GET /dashboard/scientific/{prediction_id} serves interactive views tied to prediction results, enabling detailed exploration of input values, predictions, explanations, and comparative context.

3.3. API Deployment / Model Deployments

3.4. Summary & Value Proposition

Exo.AI goes beyond a traditional ML backend, it’s a full-stack scientific inference engine with:

  • Dual-access modeling pipelines (user vs. scientist)
  • Integrated explainability
  • Contextual comparison
  • Batch processing for large campaigns
  • Automated quality diagnostics
  • Full transparency and auditability

Whether integrated into a scientific pipeline via API calls or exposed to frontend dashboards, Exo.AI delivers high-performance ML capabilities tailored to real-world astronomy applications.

4. Frontend Webapp

The frontend Exo.AI represents an synthesis refined between modern technology, immersive design and scientific accessibility. Built on Next and React, the system was developed with focus on perfomance, scalability using TypeScript to guarantee security.

In a simplified way how are we doing the predictions based no user story...

4.1. Dual Interface Design

Dive into the dual-mode system. Explain the simplified experience for general users and the advanced, data-rich interface for scientists. Highlight how this reflects thoughtful UX design. Beyond this, we're bringing educational content, scroll-based animations, space-themed UI, infromativa sections to keep users engaged and leraning.

4.2. Integration with the Backend API

Narrate how the frontend communicates with the backend securely and efficiently using Axios, TypeScript interfaces, and schema validation via Zod. Emphasize the robustness of the integration.

5. Main Technologies

Backend Frameworks
  • FastAPI 0.100.0 - Modern and fast web framework
  • Python 3.11 - Programming language
  • Pydantic 2.0 - Data validation
  • Uvicorn - ASGI server
Frontend Frameworks
  • NextJS
  • React
  • Typescript
Machine Learning
  • Scikit-Learn 1.4.0 - ML library
  • Pandas 2.0 - Data manipulation
  • NumPy 1.24 - Numerical computing
  • Joblib 1.3 - Model serialization
Database
  • PostgreSQL 15 - Primary database
  • SQLAlchemy 2.0 - ORM
  • Psycopg2 - PostgreSQL driver
Visualization & Analysis
  • Matplotlib 3.7 - Data visualization
  • Seaborn 0.12 - Statistical visualization
Containerization
  • Docker - Containerization
  • Docker Compose - Service orchestration
Deployment
  • Azure (API, ACR e Webapp)
  • Supabase (PostgreSQL)
  • GoDaddy (DNS)

projectDetails.name: Project Ratelitte
projectDetails.summary:
Ratelitte is an educational RPG where anthropomorphic mice embark on a space adventure to explore exoplanets and learn about artificial intelligence. The game integrates real data from NASA’s Exoplanet Archive, using it to generate in-game dialogues, decisions, and scientific challenges that teach players how exoplanets are discovered — including methods such as the transit method.

Our goal is to make complex scientific topics, like exoplanet exploration and AI, accessible and engaging for children, especially in underprivileged schools. By combining storytelling, gamification, and real NASA data, Ratelitte turns learning into an interactive journey of curiosity and discovery.

The project addresses the challenge by demonstrating how AI and machine learning can support science education while reflecting NASA’s mission to inspire the next generation of explorers. Ratelitte shows that even the smallest explorers — like our space mice — can reach the stars.
projectDetails.details:
Ratelitte is an interactive educational RPG developed with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, designed to teach players about exoplanets and artificial intelligence through a fun and accessible experience. In the game, players control small space-faring mice on missions to explore distant worlds.

The game integrates real data from NASA’s Exoplanet Archive API, using it to dynamically generate in-game dialogues and decision-making scenarios. This allows players to learn about exoplanet detection methods, such as the transit method, while understanding how AI and machine learning assist scientists in identifying new worlds.

By merging gameplay with real scientific data, Ratelitte promotes curiosity, scientific literacy, and digital education — particularly for students in under-resourced communities. The project’s intended impact is to make complex space science topics approachable through storytelling, exploration, and interactivity.

Our team focused on creativity, accessibility, and education. We wanted to show that science can be playful, inclusive, and inspiring — and that even small explorers can reach the stars.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Text and dialogue generation: AI tools (such as ChatGPT) were used to create and refine in-game dialogues, scientific explanations, and educational prompts about exoplanets and AI. All narrative content was reviewed and edited by the team to ensure scientific accuracy and accessibility.

Visual design: Some concept art and character ideas were prototyped using AI-assisted image generation for inspiration. All AI-generated images include visible watermarks to comply with NASA Space Apps requirements.

Code assistance: AI tools were used to assist in writing and debugging HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code, improving workflow efficiency while maintaining human oversight and originality in design and logic.

No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were used or modified in any AI-generated materials. All content was created to respect NASA’s brand integrity and emphasize educational value.

projectDetails.summary: This children's book tells the story of Mari, a curious 8-year-old girl who notices strange things happening throughout her day, like her radio crackling and her GPS failing. After seeing colorful lights dancing in the sky, she decides to investigate and "travels" to space in her imagination to discover what's behind it all. Upon her return, she feels like a true space scientist and shares her discoveries with her friends, explaining in simple terms how the Sun, our giant star, influences our planet.

To develop the project, we used a creative approach that combined storytelling with scientific information adapted for children. Creativity manifested itself in the creation of the character Mari and her journey of discovery, illustrating how imagination can be a portal to knowledge.

projectDetails.name: GeoFarm
projectDetails.summary: As the global population continues to grow, concerns about food security have become one of the central challenges of the twenty-first century. The GeoFarm initiative proposes an innovative solution centered on improving existing agricultural practices rather than expanding production areas. Through the development of Farm Navigators, an interactive educational simulation, GeoFarm aims to democratize access to scientific data and provide farmers with insights into soil conditions, irrigation, and crop management. By integrating NASA’s Earth observation datasets, the project transforms complex geospatial information into an intuitive, interactive tool that fosters agricultural literacy, sustainable practices, and data-driven decision-making among farmers across different regions of the world.
projectDetails.details:
Farm Navigators is conceived as a digital platform that merges gamification with scientific modeling to simulate realistic agricultural environments. Using NASA’s environmental monitoring data, such as the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission for soil moisture content, the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) for vegetation and land surface temperature, and the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission for rainfall distribution, the simulation recreates authentic farming conditions across multiple geographic zones. Within this environment, players can experiment with different cultivation strategies, including crop rotation, irrigation management, and fertilization techniques, while observing the resulting impacts on soil quality, productivity, and ecosystem balance. The platform thus functions as both an educational tool and a decision-support system, bridging the gap between scientific data and agricultural application.

The principal issue addressed by this project is the limited agricultural knowledge among farmers regarding soil properties, irrigation optimization, fertilization balance, and climate-related factors affecting crop performance. This gap in understanding often leads to inefficient management, crop losses, soil degradation, and pest infestations, ultimately compromising both productivity and food quality. Additionally, there is a significant technological divide: older farmers, who represent a large portion of the agricultural workforce, often encounter difficulties adopting digital tools that could enhance their operations.

The GeoFarm project seeks to address this challenge by translating complex scientific datasets into an accessible, interactive, and educational interface. The platform integrates real NASA satellite data with simplified geospatial models, allowing users to visualize soil fertility, climate variations, and environmental conditions in real time. Farmers and students can simulate decision-making processes, such as selecting crop types, adjusting irrigation schedules, or applying fertilizers, and immediately observe how these actions affect yield, resource efficiency, and ecological stability.



By merging scientific rigor with gamified learning, Farm Navigators fosters engagement and comprehension even among non-technical users. Moreover, it encourages collaboration between younger, tech-savvy farmers and older producers, promoting knowledge transfer across generations. The solution thus functions as both a learning environment and a bridge between scientific data and practical agricultural management.

The foundation of Farm Navigators lies in the integration of high-resolution environmental data derived from multiple NASA missions and complementary global databases. The SMAP mission provides near-real-time measurements of soil moisture and freeze-thaw conditions, essential for identifying optimal planting periods and irrigation strategies. The MODIS sensors, aboard NASA’s Terra and Aqua satellites, supply detailed information on land surface temperature, vegetation indices (NDVI), and evapotranspiration (parameters critical to understanding plant health and water use efficiency). The GPM mission contributes global precipitation data, improving modeling accuracy for water availability and irrigation planning. These datasets are complemented by records from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), which include soil texture classifications, crop distributions, and productivity indexes.

From a global perspective, the agri-tech market is rapidly expanding, with projections indicating it will grow to almost USD 80 billion by 2030. Within this context, there is increasing demand for digital tools that integrate sustainability, data analytics, and education. By aligning its mission with initiatives such as NASA Harvest and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), GeoFarm positions itself as a socially impactful and scientifically grounded project. The expected long-term outcomes include improved agricultural literacy, greater resilience to climate variability, and the democratization of access to environmental intelligence. By connecting satellite-derived data to local decision-making, Farm Navigators empowers farmers to produce more efficiently, preserve natural resources, and actively participate in building a sustainable global food system.

projectDetails.name: Project Halo
projectDetails.summary:
Halo is an intelligent assistant that helps users decide if the weather is favorable for tours or trips at the desired location and data. It combines weather data from NASA and partners with artificial intelligence for specific, personalized, and accessible activities.

The interface is simple: users can type or speak what they want to do, and the system checks the weather conditions (rain, extreme heat, cold, wind, humidity, or discomfort). If the weather is ideal, Halo confirms and suggests the best way to enjoy it. If not, it offers indoor alternatives, new data, or locations.

Furthermore, the app learns from user history, generating increasingly accurate recommendations. It also sends engagement notifications, such as "Today is a great day for that hike you wanted," and collects feedback after the event.

With this, Halo not only answers "will it rain at my stop?" but transforms the question into an opportunity for better, inclusive, and safe planned experiences.
projectDetails.details:
Halo works as a weather-based activity planner. Users enter their desired activities, and the system, based on Earth observation data (NASA and partners), assesses whether conditions are suitable. If not, it offers alternative options, whether in other locations, dates, or indoor activities.

Values:

  • Facilitates travel and outing planning.
  • Helps users avoid frustrations and weather risks.
  • Intelligently promotes leisure and tourism.
  • Personalization. Learns from user history and preferences to deliver increasingly relevant suggestions.
  • Time & cost savings. Minimizes wasted trips and last-minute rebookings by recommending the best time/place.
  • Environmental awareness. Suggests lower-impact alternatives and can nudge users toward sustainable choices (e.g., closer locations, off-peak times).
  • Community & social value. Supports group planning, shared activities, and optional social challenges that build local engagement.

Intended impact:

The purpose of Halo is to bridge the gap between complex meteorological data and everyday decision-making, transforming weather information into a practical tool for improving people’s lives. By providing clear, personalized, and accessible insights, Halo empowers users to plan their activities with confidence, safety, and convenience. Its mission is to make weather intelligence an inclusive resource available to everyone, regardless of technical knowledge or physical ability while promoting well-being, social engagement, and sustainable outdoor experiences. In essence, Halo strives to create a future where weather data is not just information, but a meaningful part of how people connect with their environment and make better choices in their daily lives.

Market Validation

Concept validation survey results - response distribution

Age range

Current city / residence

How often do you rely on weather?

Activities most affected by weather

Have plans been disrupted by weather?

Where do you check the weather?

Which features are most useful?

Which of these features would you find most useful?

We conducted a targeted validation survey with our core audience young adults and adult outdoor and travel enthusiasts to confirm that Halo addresses a real need and to prioritize features for the MVP. The survey was administered online and combined closed questions (preferences, likelihood of use, notification and privacy tolerances) with open-ended questions that captured qualitative perceptions and user suggestions. The results show strong support for the concept: 85% of respondents expressed approval of the project and its core features, providing clear quantitative confirmation that Halo resonates with the target audience and validating our MVP priorities.

Survey link (form):
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/156qIwd5wDdIkq1kBjBCFC7yz6R4sG0D9nhLDuIdQsTY/edit?ts=68e2e836#responses

Functionalities

  • Intelligent Weather Planning
    Users can input or speak the type of activity they wish to perform, and Halo automatically analyzes weather conditions such as temperature, rain probability, humidity, wind, thermal sensation, and UV index — based on Earth observation data (NASA and partners). The system then determines whether the conditions are favorable and provides tailored recommendations.
  • Adaptive Suggestions and Alternatives
    If weather conditions are not ideal for the chosen activity, Halo suggests alternative solutions, including new dates, nearby locations with better conditions, or indoor activities aligned with the user’s interests.
  • Personalized Notifications and Recommendations
    The app proactively engages users with intelligent notifications like: “Today is the perfect day for that hike you planned.” It also collects feedback after each activity to improve future recommendations.
  • Accessibility-Centered Design
    Built according to WCAG standards, Halo includes full compatibility with screen readers, voice navigation, adjustable contrast, and audio descriptions — ensuring that users of all abilities can navigate and access information independently and safely.
  • Rolling Map
    One of Halo’s most innovative features is the Rolling Map, an interactive map tool that allows users to select a specific location directly by pointing or dragging a marker. This enables precise planning, letting users explore different areas, analyze weather conditions for each region, and customize activity locations dynamically — similar to the flexibility of platforms like Airbnb. This feature greatly enhances the planning experience by turning static weather data into an interactive and exploratory tool.
  • Activity History & Feedback Loop
    Halo keeps a history of past activities and their corresponding weather conditions, allowing users to review, learn, and plan better future outings. The feedback system continuously improves the accuracy of recommendations.
  • Future Gamification Layer (Upcoming)
    The platform will include a gamified experience with badges, streaks, and group achievements that reward consistent use and collaborative activities. This layer aims to foster engagement, encourage safe planning, and create a community-driven experience.

Data Privacy, Ethics & Compliance

  • Explicit opt-in for location, voice recording and history storage.
  • User controls for deleting history and disabling learning features.
  • Minimization: only store data necessary for personalization; anonymize aggregated datasets used for model training.
  • Clear disclosure when content (audio/images/text) is AI-generated and metadata tags for provenance.
  • Accessibility and privacy principles embedded in design.

Evaluation & Metrics

  • Recommendation accuracy (ML validation against historical events).
  • User acceptance rate of recommendations.
  • Post-activity satisfaction (NPS / feedback).
  • Accessibility metrics (Lighthouse accessibility score, results from screen-reader tests).
  • Engagement & retention (DAU/MAU, badge adoption for gamification rollout).

Accessibility:

Built on the standards of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), Halo ensures an inclusive experience for all users. The app offers full compatibility with screen readers, voice navigation, adjustable contrast, and audio descriptions of visual elements. Each feature was designed so that people of all kinds can access weather information independently and safely. 

Technologies used:

  • Integrations: Weather APIs and NASA data..
  • Prototyping: Figma, Miro (flows).

Plus — Future Gamification (badges & collaborative rewards)

  • Badges: Tiered achievements (bronze/silver/gold) for first uses, repeated safe activities, completion of safety checklists and micro-learning modules.
  • Social Challenges & Team Badges: Optional group activities with shared badges to encourage safe, coordinated outings.
  • Partner Incentives: Opt-in integrations with local businesses for discounts tied to verified badge milestones.

projectDetails.name: Nacle - article finder
projectDetails.details:
Project Details

Our project addresses a key challenge in NASA’s Space Biology domain: connecting 607 scientific articles with hundreds of Open Science Data (OSDs) efficiently and meaningfully.
Currently, researchers must manually search for connections between publications and datasets — a process that is time-consuming, biased, and often overlooks emerging research gaps (the so-called “vaults”).

What It Does & How It Works

The platform provides a semantic exploration portal that:

  • Summarizes each article using AI-based text extraction.
  • Relates scientific articles to NASA OSDs through vector embeddings and cosine similarity.
  • Detects knowledge gaps (“Vaults”) — underexplored topics or disconnected areas — based on network metrics such as match density, coverage, and recency.

Users can navigate through three main tabs:

  1. Articles – searchable catalog with summaries, match visualization, and related OSDs.
  2. OSDs – dataset directory with metadata, author/contacts, and top related articles.
  3. Vaults – visual map of semantic gaps with VaultScore, metrics, and missing thematic factors.

Benefits & Impact

The portal accelerates discovery by revealing hidden connections and underexplored areas in space biology. It supports researchers, data curators, and program managers in identifying promising research directions, linking studies to open data, and prioritizing future investigations.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: Next.js (TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Framer Motion, Lucide-react.
  • Backend & Data Processing: Python for data analysis, web scraping, and semantic preprocessing.
  • Data: JSON-based structures linking Article ↔ OSD (stored in all_matches.json), enriched with embeddings (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
  • Architecture: ingestion → normalization (synonyms, entity linking) → embedding generation → bipartite graph of matches → vault detection.








Creativity & Design Factors

We focused on usability and clarity: clean data visualization, responsive graphs, and intuitive navigation across Articles, OSDs, and Vaults.
Our system is creative because it doesn’t just match text — it builds a living semantic network of articles and datasets, surfacing relationships and “matches” that humans would miss.
Each Vault reveals an actionable insight: a gap that could represent the next frontier for space biology research.

Considerations

  • Semantic normalization ensures that different terms (e.g., “Drosophila melanogaster” ≈ “fruit fly”) resolve to the same concept.
  • Usability testing emphasized quick comprehension, minimal clicks to insight, and visual explainability.
  • The VaultScore formula is adjustable, allowing future collaboration with domain experts to refine scientific relevance.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
How we used Artificial Intelligence (AI) in our project

We used Artificial Intelligence as a core analytical component to summarize scientific articles and generate semantic keywords that support the correlation between Articles ↔ OSDs (Open Science Data).

Specifically, AI was applied in the following steps:

  1. Article Summarization:
    We used AI-based text models (LLMs) to create concise and reliable summaries of each scientific article. These summaries were generated from the article’s title, abstract, and key sections extracted during preprocessing.
  2. Keyword & Factor Extraction:
    The same models were used to identify and normalize important scientific entities (e.g., organisms, techniques, conditions, missions).
    These AI-generated keywords serve as semantic anchors to link related articles and OSDs.
  3. Similarity & Matching:
    The AI-generated keywords and summaries were combined with text embeddings (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2) to compute semantic similarity (cosine distance) between articles and OSDs, producing the network of matches stored in all_matches.json.
  4. Vault Detection (Emerging Gaps):
    AI indirectly supports the “Vault” feature — areas of low semantic connectivity detected through metrics derived from the embedding graph — highlighting potential research opportunities.

All AI outputs were used strictly for data summarization and semantic linking, not for branding, UI design, or media content.
No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were generated or modified by AI tools.

projectDetails.name: DataSharks
projectDetails.summary:
Our project introduces an innovative and intelligent system for shark monitoring and data analysis, integrating smart acoustic tags with a predictive analytics platform.

Currently, there is a major gap in the availability of tools capable of predicting, processing, and analyzing shark data collected by tags in an integrated way. This limitation prevents researchers from fully understanding sharks’ behavioral, migratory, and ecological patterns — which are crucial for conservation and marine protection efforts.

Our platform addresses this challenge by using accelerometer, temperature, and GPS data to analyze and predict shark behavior, distinguishing between hunting, resting, and migration patterns, while also identifying potential breeding habitats based on temperature and environmental variations.

The data captured by the tags are transmitted acoustically to underwater receivers and then sent via surface buoys to satellites, which forward them to our cloud platform. There, advanced predictive models process the information to generate interactive visualization maps, allowing near real-time tracking and behavioral insights.

This approach aims not only to enhance scientific research but also to strengthen marine conservation and coastal safety strategies, making shark monitoring smarter, more automated, and sustainable.
projectDetails.details:
Our project proposes an intelligent platform for shark behavior prediction and monitoring, designed to analyze, forecast, and visualize data collected by smart tags attached to sharks.

🧩 Problem

There is currently a lack of integrated tools capable of processing and predicting shark behavior — such as movement, migration, hunting, and reproduction — using real sensor data.
This gap limits marine research, conservation efforts, and our understanding of ocean ecosystems.

⚙️ How It Works

The acoustic smart tags collect environmental and behavioral data — including acceleration, depth, temperature, and location.
Data are transmitted via underwater acoustic signals to receivers, relayed to surface buoys, and then sent to satellites.
Once in the cloud platform, the information is processed by machine learning models that generate behavioral insights and predictions.

Key components:

  • Accelerometer → detects activity patterns such as hunting, resting, and swimming.
  • Location sensor → tracks migratory routes and habitat zones.
  • Temperature sensor → identifies breeding areas and thermal preferences.
  • Predictive models → forecast movements and environmental interactions.
  • Interactive maps → visualize real-time behavior and conservation zones.

🌊 Benefits

  • Enables data-driven, predictive insights into shark behavior.
  • Supports scientists and conservationists with visual dashboards and analytics.
  • Promotes marine conservation policies, reducing extinction risk and coastal incidents.
  • Encourages global collaboration by integrating oceanographic data into a unified network.

🚀 Intended Impact

We aim to build a global network of intelligent marine data, where each tag contributes to collective ocean knowledge.
Expected impacts include:

  • Enhancing conservation strategies by identifying key habitats and migration corridors.
  • Preventing shark-human incidents through predictive mapping.
  • Providing reliable scientific data for research institutions and environmental agencies.

🤖 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage

AI was fundamental in three areas:

  1. VEO (Gemini) and Google NANO — used to generate images, videos, and app prototypes (with AI watermark).
  2. Data processing — machine learning handled large NASA satellite datasets to identify key correlations.
  3. Coordinate management — AI-assisted mapping and prediction of shark activity zones.

📡 Satellite Data Sources

NASA – OB.DAAC

  • Aqua MODIS Level-3 Chlorophyll (CHL)
    • North: -6.95531 | South: -9.81641 | East: -32.37553 | West: -35.55819

These datasets are essential to understand shark population dynamics — phytoplankton, the base of the oceanic food web, strongly affects prey availability and predator behavior.

COPERNICUS – Global Ocean Physics Analysis and Forecast

Variables:

  • Salinity, Temperature, Depth
    Daily resolution (0.49m–266.04m depth) allows for vertical stratification analysis, revealing thermoclines and salinity gradients crucial for understanding shark physiology.

💻 Tools, Languages & Technologies

  • Hardware: Acoustic tags, underwater receivers, satellite buoys.
  • Backend: Python.
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
  • Design & UX: Figma, Gemini VEO, Google NANO.

Our project combines AI, satellite data, and marine technology into a single predictive system — turning raw ocean data into actionable knowledge for research and conservation.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
In our project, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was strategically applied in three key stages of development:

  1. Data Processing and Analysis:
    Due to the large volume of data provided by NASA — including satellite coordinates and oceanographic information — AI models were used to assist in data preprocessing and cleaning, ensuring accuracy and efficiency during analysis. AI also helped manage and interpret shark location coordinates, enabling the identification of behavioral patterns such as migration, rest, and hunting, based on accelerometer and temperature sensor readings.
  2. Image and Video Generation for the App:
    To visually represent the platform and its functionality, we used Gemini with VEO and Google NANO to generate AI-based images and videos of the app and its data visualizations. All AI-generated content includes a visible watermark, following the NASA challenge guidelines to indicate its artificial origin.
  3. Design Optimization and Creativity:
    AI was also used to enhance the design process, helping simulate oceanographic data visualization scenarios and ensure a user interface that is both intuitive and scientifically accurate.

These AI tools were employed purely for creative and technical support, without using or modifying any NASA logos, symbols, or mission identifiers, as per challenge requirements.

projectDetails.name: BlooMap - Software masons
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Bloomap, is an interactive web application designed to visualize and monitor the health of global vegetation.

It directly addresses the "BloomWatch" challenge by transforming complex Earth observation data from the Sentinel-2 satellite into intuitive, actionable insights. With a single click on our map-based interface, users instantly receive key metrics such as the current bloom status, recent trends, and a historical analysis of the selected area's vegetation.

The importance of Bloomap lies in its ability to democratize access to critical environmental data. It empowers a diverse range of users—from farmers optimizing crop management and public health officials predicting allergy seasons, to scientists monitoring biodiversity and climate change impacts. By simplifying complex science, Bloomap provides a vital tool for making informed decisions that support sustainable agriculture, public health, and the conservation of our planet's ecosystems.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Bloomap is a full-stack web platform that provides an on-demand, user-friendly analysis of vegetation health and plant blooming for any location on Earth.

Our solution works through a seamless user journey. First, the user is greeted by an engaging splash screen while our performant Next.js application initializes. They are then presented with a full-screen, interactive map powered by Leaflet.js. Using a responsive radius slider, the user can define the precise scope of their area of interest. A single click on the map triggers our robust NestJS backend, which queries a STAC API for recent Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and the OpenStreetMap Nominatim API for reverse geocoding. This complex satellite data is processed in seconds by our backend to calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), a key scientific indicator of plant health. From this NDVI score, we derive our user-friendly metrics (status, trend, and historical data), which are then displayed back to the user in a smoothly animated modal built with Framer Motion, providing an instant and intuitive diagnostic of the area's vegetation.

What benefits does it have?

The primary benefits of Bloomap are accessibility, speed, versatility, and user experience.

  • Accessibility: It translates raw, complex scientific data into simple, actionable indicators (e.g., "Status: High," "Trend: Rising") that anyone can understand, removing the barrier to entry for engaging with Earth observation data.
  • Speed: Our optimized full-stack architecture provides near real-time insights with a single click, eliminating the need for users to have expertise in finding and processing geospatial data.
  • Versatility: The platform is designed to serve a wide range of applications, from precision agriculture and public health monitoring to environmental science and education.
  • Engaging User Experience: Unlike raw data tools, we focused on creating a polished and enjoyable experience with smooth animations, a clean interface, and interactive controls like the radius slider.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The primary intended impact of Bloomap is the democratization of Earth observation data, empowering individuals and organizations to make data-driven decisions about our planet. We aim to:

  • Empower Agriculture: Enable farmers to practice more sustainable farming by optimizing resource use based on real-time crop health.
  • Enhance Public Health: Allow authorities to anticipate high-pollen seasons by monitoring regional vegetation peaks, improving the quality of life for allergy sufferers.
  • Support Environmental Science: Provide an accessible tool for scientists, students, and conservationists to monitor biodiversity and the effects of climate change on local and global scales.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Our technology stack was chosen for performance, scalability, and a unified developer experience using TypeScript across the board.

  • Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Leaflet.js (for interactive maps), Framer Motion (for polished UI animations), and Tailwind CSS for styling.
  • Backend: NestJS (a Node.js framework), TypeScript.
  • APIs & Data: European Space Agency (ESA) Sentinel-2 data accessed via a STAC-compliant API, and the OpenStreetMap Nominatim API for reverse geocoding.
  • Core Language: TypeScript.
  • Development Tools: Git for version control and Visual Studio Code.

How is your project creative?

Bloomap's creativity lies in the synthesis of a complex backend data pipeline with a polished, performant, and feature-rich frontend. Our primary innovation is the radical simplification of the user experience. We creatively combined two distinct data sources (satellite imagery and geocoding) into one seamless output. The entire process—querying satellites, processing imagery, calculating indices, and fetching location data—is executed in seconds and is completely abstracted from the user. The final experience is reduced to the simplest possible action—a single click—to gain powerful insights, enhanced by interactive controls like the radius slider and fluid animations that make data exploration feel intuitive and engaging.

What factors did your team consider?

  • User-Centric & Engaging Design: Our top priority was an interface that required zero prior knowledge of geospatial science. We incorporated features like a splash screen, animated modals, and interactive controls to make the experience not just easy, but enjoyable.
  • Performance Optimization: This was a key concern, leading us to use Next.js's dynamic imports to client-side load the heavy map component, ensuring a fast initial page load and a smooth user experience.
  • Data Relevance: We chose Sentinel-2 data for its excellent balance of spatial resolution and temporal frequency, making it ideal for monitoring dynamic changes in vegetation.
  • Scalability: We used robust and modern frameworks (NestJS, Next.js) and implemented backend caching for geocoding requests to ensure the application is fast and can handle future growth.
  • Feasibility: We focused on a core, high-impact feature set that was ambitious yet realistically achievable within the hackathon's timeframe, ensuring we delivered a polished and functional product.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Yes, we utilized Artificial Intelligence to support and accelerate our project's development.

  • Code Development: During development, we consulted AI models, including Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, at key moments. These tools assisted in generating specific code snippets and suggesting optimizations for certain functions. This approach increased our development speed and helped ensure the solidity of the final code, allowing our team to focus more time on the core architecture and the unique logic of the Bloomap platform.
  • Documentation and Narrative: To ensure our project's vision was communicated effectively, we used Google's Gemini as a creative assistant to help us draft and refine our project descriptions and pitch. This process helped us to better articulate our team's original ideas and the overall vision for our project, ensuring the final text was clear, compelling, and impactful.

projectDetails.name: Project Plêiades
projectDetails.summary:
Plêiades é um aplicativo mobile desenvolvido em React Native (Expo) que ajuda usuários a planejarem atividades ao ar livre de forma mais segura e inteligente. Ele utiliza dados históricos da NASA POWER API para calcular probabilidades de calor, frio, chuva, vento, umidade e desconforto térmico em qualquer localidade do planeta.

O app permite que o usuário consulte condições passadas e tendências recentes, filtrando por horários e perfis de atividade (praia, trilha, pesca, fotografia ou urbano). Além disso, conta com o recurso de Check-in Climático Comunitário, onde pessoas registram como realmente estava o tempo em determinado lugar e momento, enriquecendo a base de dados e validando os modelos históricos.

Com isso, Plêiades busca não só melhorar o planejamento cotidiano, mas também contribuir para a ciência cidadã, incentivando uma rede colaborativa de dados climáticos locais. A solução oferece impacto direto na vida das pessoas, reduz riscos em atividades externas e promove a conscientização sobre as mudanças climáticas globais.
projectDetails.details:
O Plêiades funciona como um planejador climático inteligente. Ele cruza dados abertos da NASA com preferências do usuário e devolve análises claras em forma de gráficos e percentuais, indicando as melhores datas para atividades ao ar livre.

Entre os principais benefícios estão:

  • Segurança: ajuda a evitar exposição a condições severas de calor, chuva ou vento.
  • Praticidade: sugere automaticamente os dias mais adequados nos próximos 7 dias.
  • Colaboração: permite check-ins comunitários, simulando um banco de dados enriquecido por observações humanas.
  • Educação climática: conscientiza usuários sobre padrões climáticos locais e globais.

Tecnologias utilizadas: React Native + Expo, TypeScript, NASA POWER API, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, AsyncStorage, Expo Router e Expo Location.

Criatividade: além de processar dados históricos, o projeto introduz um conceito de gamificação futura com check-ins colaborativos, estimulando engajamento e melhorando continuamente a qualidade dos dados.

Nosso time considerou impacto social, clareza de uso, acessibilidade, integração com dados confiáveis e potencial de expansão para outros contextos.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Utilizamos inteligência artificial como ferramenta de apoio ao desenvolvimento, especificamente para:

  • Apoio na escrita de documentação e README (revisão de clareza e formatação).
  • Sugestões de otimização de código em etapas de prototipagem.
  • Geração de wireframes ilustrativos para apresentação (quando indicado como imagem AI).

Nenhum modelo AI foi usado para substituir a lógica principal ou manipular os dados da NASA. Todas as decisões técnicas e implementações de código foram feitas pelo time, com IA atuando apenas como acelerador de criatividade e comunicação.

projectDetails.name: Recyclonauts
projectDetails.summary:
Recyclonauts is an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) designed to revolutionize waste management on Mars through intelligent and sustainable recycling. Built as an interactive prototype in Figma and Web Programming, the system digitally simulates the identification, cleaning, and recycling of inorganic materials, such as beverage packaging, during long-duration space missions.

By integrating artificial intelligence for material recognition and an intuitive user interface for astronauts, Recyclonauts ensures efficient classification and transformation of waste into reusable components, including aluminum-based parts, wiring, and metal alloys. This solution directly addresses the “SpaceTrash Hack: Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars” challenge by demonstrating how circular economy principles and automation can reduce dependence on Earth-supplied materials, minimize waste accumulation, and enhance mission autonomy.

Beyond simulation, Recyclonauts promotes self-sustainability and environmental responsibility, offering a new perspective on how space crews can reuse local resources, turning “trash” into essential materials for maintenance, repairs, and even radiation shielding, a crucial step toward sustainable human settlement on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction:

Recyclonauts is an MVP developed to optimize waste management in space missions. The project simulates, through an interactive interface created in Figma, the process of identifying, cleaning, and recycling inorganic materials such as aluminum packaging.

By combining artificial intelligence and circular economy principles, the system guides astronauts in transforming waste into new useful components, reducing dependence on Earth-supplied resources and promoting sustainability in Martian operations.

How does it work?

The user places the item on the machine's conveyor belt with an attached screen. The system triggers the scanner and automatically identifies the material type.

The user answers whether there is internal residue (yes/no). If so, the system follows the cleaning protocol step-by-step before allowing recycling.

After determining whether there is internal residue, the user chooses Recycle, Reuse, or Discard. If Recycle is selected, the system generates possible product options from that material.

The user selects the desired product (e.g., gear).

Upon startup, the system takes the item to the processing line and displays a tracking screen with: Input / Expected Output / Destination / Current Status and a progress bar for each step.

Typical Steps Shown and What Each One Does:

  1. Shredding & Preparation — mechanical removal of the plastic layer.
  2. Transport to Chamber / Isolation — isolation for safe processing.
  3. Argon Purge — removal of O₂ to prevent oxidation.
  4. Pyrolysis / Polymer Decomposition — degrades organic layers (if applicable).
  5. Separation & Melting — separation of metals and melting of aluminum.
  6. Controlled Pouring / Casting — preparation of the feedstock (billets/granules).
  7. Rapid Cooling & Granulation — production of granules or filaments as needed.
  8. Additive Manufacturing / 3D Printing — printing / manufacturing of the final part.

The screen highlights the current step, time remaining per step, and any safety alarms (temperature, leakage, contamination).

At the end of processing, the user sees the confirmation screen with a photo of the final product.

The product is automatically added to the astronaut's Local Resource Inventory (LRI) with metadata: quantity, lifetime and usage history.

Benefits:

Reduction of Earth Supply Dependence (Mass Savings):The main benefit is the drastic reduction of Launch Mass (MLM). Every gram of aluminum recycled in situ on Mars represents mass that no longer needs to be transported, freeing cargo capacity for other critical supplies or scientific equipment.

Autonomous Additive Manufacturing (ISRU): The R.A.M.S. system enables immediate, local production of vital components through Additive Manufacturing (3D printing). This includes critical spare parts, specialized tools, and even radiation shielding materials, minimizing mission downtime and ensuring the operational autonomy of the base and maintenance systems (Scenario 1).

Waste Management and Safety: The equipment eliminates the accumulation of bulky debris within facilities, mitigating environmental contamination risks and maintaining habitat cleanliness. The processed aluminum is transformed from inert waste into a high-value resource—crucial for mission longevity.

Creativity / Innovation:

In an environment as challenging as Mars, where every gram of material and every unit of energy is precious, our proposal stands out by transforming a critical problem — the accumulation of inorganic waste — into a solution for another equally vital challenge: the manufacturing autonomy of the colony. We did not simply develop a recycling system; we created a closed-loop, intelligent cycle that redefines the concept of sustainability in extraterrestrial environments.

The core of our innovation lies in the integrated approach we adopted. While conventional solutions focus on a single aspect of the problem, our system acts on three fronts simultaneously: waste management, production of strategic inputs, and on-demand manufacturing. The distinction begins with the non-combustion pyrolysis process used for food packaging, which preserves the habitat’s oxygen — an invaluable resource on Mars — while generating energetic byproducts that are reused in the process itself, creating a circular efficiency rarely seen even in terrestrial systems.

However, the true revolution lies in the final product we chose to prioritize: aluminum filaments for 3D printing. This strategic decision transforms our system from a simple recycling device into a universal factory of possibilities. Instead of producing specific, limited objects, we generate the raw material that allows astronauts to manufacture any necessary part — from a broken tool to a complex life-support component. This flexibility directly addresses one of the greatest vulnerabilities of long-duration missions: the unpredictability of repair and adaptation needs.

The fully automated process, with a “place and forget” interface, represents another innovative leap. Astronauts — scientists and engineers of various specializations — don’t need to become metallurgy experts. They simply deposit used packaging, select the desired program, and retrieve the filament ready for printing — with all process complexity managed by intelligent control systems.

Technologies and Tools:

  • Figma (Design)
  • Claude Code Sonnet 4.5 (Programming tool)
  • Google Colab (Data Tool and Python)
  • VS Code (HTML, CSS and JS)
  • GitHub Copilot (Programming tool)
  • Deepseek (Text Summary)
  • Sora (Video Generate)
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro (Text Summary and Translate)
  • Chat GPT 5 (Text Summary and Translate)
  • Trello (Project Management)

3D Printing Machines Used on Mars

Waste Materials Recycling for In-Space Manufacturin

Regolith-Polymer 3D Printing (KSC-TOPS-88)

The large amount of garbage on Mars:

https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240004915/downloads/SeattleMuseumofFlight_April2024.pdf (Slide 31)

Expected Results:

The operational impact of this solution is transformative. Every kilogram of packaging recycled means less launch mass from Earth in spare parts. Every tool printed locally eliminates months of waiting time and provides immediate responsiveness to emergencies. Beyond environmental sustainability, we are proposing operational sustainability — the colony’s ability to sustain, adapt, and thrive using resources already available on-site.

This approach not only solves immediate waste management challenges but also lays the foundation for a true Martian circular economy. We present not just a product, but a manufacturing ecosystem that evolves and adapts with the colony — where today’s “trash” becomes tomorrow’s tool and the safety of the day after.

projectDetails.name: Project ReMars Spectral
projectDetails.summary:
ReMars Spectral: Hyperspectral Intelligence for Sustainable Recycling on Mars 
(Integrating CRISM Spectral Science with ReMars Circular Resource Systems)

ReMars Spectral combines hyperspectral imaging and artificial intelligence to detect, classify, and recycle inorganic waste on Martian missions. Inspired by CRISM, which maps minerals across multiple spectral bands, the system adapts these techniques to characterize plastics. Through advanced spectral demixing and AI classification, it accurately identifies and separates polymeric materials, enabling efficient recycling and additive manufacturing via 3D printing for a self-sustaining human habitation ecosystem on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
Methodology: CRISM-Based Spectral Detection for Waste Classification

The ReMars Spectral system employs a detection and classification framework inspired by the Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)—an instrument recognized for its ability to map mineralogical diversity on the Martian surface through detailed hyperspectral imaging. While CRISM was designed to identify minerals such as sulfates, clays, and oxides in the 0.36–3.92 µm wavelength range, ReMars Spectral adapts these analytical foundations to characterize inorganic and polymeric waste generated during manned missions.

1. Spectral Data Acquisition

Custom hyperspectral sensors capture reflectance data from waste samples in the visible and near-infrared bands, simulating the spectral resolution and sensitivity of CRISM. These spectral signatures are recorded for a wide variety of materials—including polymers, metal alloys, glass fragments, and composite waste—under controlled Martian atmosphere and illumination conditions.

2. Spectral Preprocessing and Calibration

The raw spectral data undergo calibration procedures analogous to CRISM's Directed Observation Mode, including correction for instrumental noise, solar incidence angle, and atmospheric CO₂ scattering. The result is a normalized reflectance cube optimized for spectral feature extraction.

3. Spectral Unmixing and Machine Learning Classification

ReMars Spectral applies linear spectral unmixing algorithms combined with machine learning classifiers (e.g., Support Vector Machines and Neural Networks) to decompose mixed spectral signatures into identifiable components. This enables the discrimination of polymeric compounds—such as polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polystyrene (PS), and polyester—from other inorganic or metallic waste.

4. Smart Recycling Pathways

After classifying materials, the system directs them to specific recycling routes within the ReMars infrastructure.

5. Integration with the ReMars Circular Economy Framework

The hyperspectral sensing process is fully integrated with the ReMars circular system through an AI-based control interface that continuously updates spectral libraries and optimizes recycling efficiency. This allows real-time adaptation to material variability and operating conditions on Mars, ensuring up to a 45% improvement in classification accuracy and a reduction in sorting errors by almost half compared to traditional optical methods.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Results and Expected Impact

The ReMars Spectral system—which integrates hyperspectral intelligence inspired by CRISM data processing—enables a new standard in circular resource management for Martian missions. By combining spectral analysis, AI-driven classification, and in-situ recycling technologies, the system transforms mission waste into vital resources that enhance habitat autonomy, sustainability, and resilience.

The main expected results of the project include: 

60-80% reduction in total waste volume, achieved through precise hyperspectral sorting and multipath recycling.

Production of plastic composites, serving as construction materials, thermal insulation, tools and utilities.

Leveraging spectral mapping principles derived from CRISM, ReMars Spectral achieves up to 45% higher classification accuracy compared to conventional optical sorting. This accuracy minimizes resource loss, optimizes recycling workflows, and ensures a sustainable circular economy model—transforming waste into a strategic asset for survival and innovation on Mars.

projectDetails.name: Air QMBA: Quality Monitoring and Bridge Assistant
projectDetails.summary:
This project introduces an advanced platform designed to monitor and forecast air quality using real-time data from multiple sources, including NASA's TEMPO satellite, local sensors, and meteorological information. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, the platform provides personalized alerts and actionable insights to help individuals and governments mitigate the health risks of air pollution. Predictive capabilities allow for early intervention and informed decision-making in response to pollution spikes.

The platform is user-friendly, offering an intuitive interface that helps individuals monitor local air quality and make better decisions regarding outdoor activities. Additionally, the system supports governments and public health organizations, equipping them with tools to take swift actions and implement data-driven measures. The ultimate goal is to increase access to reliable air quality data, raise global awareness, and improve environmental health for communities worldwide.
projectDetails.details:
INTRODUCTION

Air pollution is one of the most pressing threats to public health, silently affecting billions of people every day. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), in 2021 alone, poor air quality was linked to more than 8.1 million deaths worldwide, underscoring the scale and urgency of the crisis. Beyond mortality, polluted air reduces quality of life, aggravates respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, and disproportionately impacts vulnerable populations. The WHO reports that 99% of the world’s population breathes air that exceeds safe quality limits, exposing communities to severe health risks such as strokes, heart disease, and chronic respiratory conditions. These alarming realities highlight the critical need for accessible, reliable tools that can transform complex environmental data into actionable insights for communities worldwide.

THE PROBLEM

On October 12, 2023, the city of Manaus, Brazil, recorded a PM2.5 concentration of 314.99 µg/m³ — more than 20 times the World Health Organization’s recommended limit of 15 µg/m³.

To better understand the magnitude of this number, the Air Quality Index (AQI) categorizes air pollution from “Good” to “Hazardous,” with values above 300 considered extremely dangerous.

The toxic haze, fueled by widespread Amazon wildfires, blanketed vast areas and triggered a surge in respiratory illnesses.

The map below illustrates how widespread fire activity across the Amazon released massive amounts of particulate matter, contributing to the toxic haze observed in Manaus.

This case is not isolated. Similar crises, though often less severe, occur around the globe. According to the WHO, 99% of the world’s population breathes air that exceeds safe quality limits, exposing communities to strokes, heart disease, and chronic respiratory conditions. Beyond human health, polluted air intensifies wildfires, worsens droughts, and accelerates climate change — making air pollution one of the most urgent and pervasive environmental challenges of our time.

SOLUTION

The case of Manaus on October 12, 2023, dramatically illustrates the impact of extreme air pollution spikes. With a PM2.5 concentration exceeding 314.99 µg/m³, more than 20 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended limit of 15 µg/m³, the city faced a respiratory health crisis and a major public health challenge. This event, exacerbated by wildfires in the Amazon, served as a wake-up call for the urgent need for real-time monitoring and forecasting tools that allow both individuals and authorities to make informed and rapid decisions. Given that 99% of the global population breathes air that exceeds safe pollution levels, according to the WHO, our solution emerges to bridge the gap in information and forecasting, providing individuals with the tools to protect themselves proactively while helping governments act quickly to safeguard public health.

Based on the urgent needs identified in the Manaus scenario and the global air pollution challenge, we have developed an integrated, accessible application that combines cutting-edge technologies, such as satellite data, local ground-based sensors, meteorological information, and artificial intelligence (AI) to deliver:

a. Real-Time Monitoring:
The app provides a real-time view of air quality, displaying updated data on pollutants such as PM2.5, NO₂, O₃, and others. This allows users to immediately know the pollution levels around them, helping to prevent respiratory diseases and promote informed decision-making.

b. Personalized Alerts and Forecasts:
Using machine learning algorithms, the app predicts pollution spikes, forecasting air quality fluctuations over the coming days. Additionally, it provides personalized alerts tailored to the health profile of each user (e.g., sensitive groups like the elderly, children, and asthmatics). For instance, when dangerous levels of pollutants are detected, the app sends alerts recommending actions such as avoiding outdoor activities or wearing a mask.

c. Community Panel and Public Campaigns:
The app integrates a Community Panel, where users can report local air quality concerns, share observations, and receive feedback from other community members. This panel also includes public health alerts and campaigns that highlight key issues and solutions, such as government actions or awareness programs. It helps to facilitate community-driven efforts in improving air quality and encourages active engagement in local environmental protection initiatives.

d. AI-Powered Intelligent Assistant:
The platform also features an AI-powered assistant that interacts with users, providing personalized recommendations based on real-time air quality data. The assistant responds to queries like “Is it safe to run today?” and suggests actions based on local conditions, user health profiles, and pollution forecasts. This feature aims to empower individuals to make better, data-driven decisions for their health and well-being, ensuring proactive responses to air quality changes.

e. Education and Awareness:
The app includes an educational section on the effects of air pollution on health and the environment. Using infographics, explanatory videos, and interactive quizzes, the app seeks to increase public awareness, helping people understand the importance of monitoring air quality and how to protect their health.onitoring air quality and how to protect their health.

HOW IT WORKS

Our platform operates by integrating real-time data from satellites, ground-based sensors, and meteorological information to provide an accurate view of air quality and predict pollution spikes. This data is collected via public APIs, such as the AirNOW and WEkEO API, sensor networks like OpenAQ, and climatic data obtained from reliable meteorological sources. Once collected, the data undergoes complex processing and validation, ensuring both accuracy and reliability. The use of machine learning algorithms in the backend allows the app to predict air quality variations based on historical patterns and local weather conditions.

1. Data Collection

The app collects data in real time from various sources to help map global and local air quality:

Satellite Data(WEkEO and AIRNOW): The satellite provides detailed data on atmospheric gases such as NO₂, PM2.5, formaldehyde, and ozone (O₃). This data is crucial for understanding global pollution levels and providing up-to-date information for the app.

Ground-Based Sensors (OpenAQ): Sensors scattered across urban and rural regions provide real-time air quality data (e.g., PM2.5, NO₂, CO). These data points are essential to complement satellite information, offering a more accurate and localized view of pollution.

Meteorological Data: Temperature, humidity, and wind speed directly affect the dispersion of pollutants. The app integrates these data points to adjust predictions, ensuring that air quality is more accurately represented based on weather conditions.

2. Data Processing and Validation

After data collection, the platform undergoes a cross-validation process between sources (satellites and local sensors) to ensure there are no discrepancies in measurements and that the data is consistent.

Real-Time Cross-Validation: The system compares data from satellites with local sensor data to correct inconsistencies and ensure accuracy. The system adjusts data in real time based on new inputs, always maintaining the reliability of the information.

3. Air Quality Prediction

At the heart of the solution is the accurate prediction of pollution using machine learning algorithms. We utilize predictive models to forecast pollution levels at different times, helping to anticipate fluctuations in air quality.

Machine Learning (AI): The platform uses machine learning algorithms to analyze historical and current data to predict pollution spikes. These models are trained to identify pollution patterns and forecast upcoming increases in pollutants like PM2.5, NO₂, and O₃. This allows for advanced notifications to users and authorities about dangerous spikes, such as those caused by wildfires or heavy traffic.

Pollution Spike Predictions: The app uses predictive model data and weather forecasts to anticipate pollution events. The system predicts air quality fluctuations, informing users about the best times for outdoor activities and when to avoid contact with pollutants.

4. Alerts and Notifications

Based on predictions, the app sends personalized alerts according to each user’s health profile (e.g., elderly, asthmatic). Alerts are sent when pollution levels reach critical values, notifying users of the need for precautions.

Personalized Alerts: The app sends push notifications whenever pollution levels exceed safe limits. For example, users with respiratory conditions may receive alerts before a PM2.5 spike, suggesting they avoid outdoor activities or wear masks.

5. User Interface

The user interface has been designed to be intuitive, enabling anyone to easily access air quality information and forecasts clearly.

Screen 1 – Interactive Map: The interactive map interface displays real-time air quality information, allowing users to view local pollution levels and the forecast of fluctuations. The app uses Google Maps API or Leaflet to display data in interactive layers.


Screen 2 – Personalized Local Panel: The panel provides personalized alerts, air quality charts, and daily forecasts. It also offers health tips based on the user’s profile.

Screen 3 – Intelligent Assistant: The intelligent assistant interface uses AI to interact with users, responding to questions like “Is it safe to run today?” and providing personalized recommendations based on local data.

Screen 4 – Local History:
The Local History screen allows users to review past air quality data, providing a historical view of pollution levels and trends in their area. This screen displays data in charts and graphs, enabling users to track the air quality over time and analyze patterns for better future decisions.


Screen 5 – Community Panel:
The Community Panel enables users to share local air quality concerns, report events (e.g., fires, industrial activity), and contribute to community-driven solutions. This screen includes public health alerts, campaigns, and shared observations, fostering local collaboration in improving air quality. It also highlights important public health initiatives and governmental actions.

6. Technologies Used

Integration of AirNOW, WEkEO, and OpenAQ APIs. Cloud storage (Google Cloud, AWS). The use of Groq API for AI enables fast processing of large-scale machine learning tasks, enhancing the real-time prediction capabilities of the app.

Frontend: Development with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; Leaflet for the interactive map.

CONCLUSION

Air pollution is an urgent global crisis that affects millions of lives every day. Through the integration of cutting-edge technologies, such as satellite data, local sensors, meteorological information, and artificial intelligence, our platform provides a powerful tool for individuals and governments alike to monitor, predict, and respond to air quality challenges. By offering real-time monitoring, personalized alerts, and community-driven solutions, we aim to empower people to make informed decisions about their health and contribute to improving air quality at the local level.

Our solution not only addresses immediate health risks posed by poor air quality but also supports long-term environmental sustainability by fostering awareness, collaboration, and data-driven action. With the ability to predict pollution spikes, inform users in real time, and equip authorities with actionable insights, we are confident that our platform will play a vital role in combating air pollution and improving the quality of life for communities worldwide. Together, we can make the air we breathe safer, healthier, and more sustainable for all.
