projectDetails.name: WINI
projectDetails.summary: SeaReal is an Augmented Reality experience that transforms NASA observational data into an interactive ocean timeline. By pointing their phone camera, the user "summons" marine creatures that represent past, present, and future states of the ocean, observing environmental changes translated into vivid visualizations (water color, particles, sea level rise). The backend processes PACE, SWOT, and GRACE-FO products to generate data-derived textures/overlays. 3D models and animations are created in Blender and exported as glTF. Python + OpenCV handle marker/scene detection and overlay logic. The experience is short (2–4 minutes per narrative), accessible (captions, seated mode, safe palettes), and designed for schools, museums, and events, connecting science to a wide audience and turning raw data into empathy and action.
projectDetails.details:
SeaReal converts NASA observational products into AR experiences that make visible oceanic changes over time. The user points the device's camera; a local/server pipeline delivers optimized visual overlays and 3D models that represent the state of the ocean in that decade. The timeline control allows for smooth transitions (interpolation) between states reconstructed from real data.

Technical Pipeline — Step-by-Step

Data Acquisition (Pre-processing)

  • Download selected products (e.g., chlorophyll/phytoplankton, sea level height, salinity, OLR) via Earthdata/PO.DAAC/GRACE portals.
  • Suggested tool: Python scripts (netCDF4, xarray) to automate downloads and extract relevant layers.

Data Transformation into Visual Assets

  • Generate derived maps (e.g., temperature anomalies, chlorophyll index) with Python (xarray, numpy, matplotlib).
  • Export textures (PNG) and small sets of points/particles (CSV/JSON) for runtime use.

Modeling and Animation

  • 3D models of creatures and animations created in Blender; export as glTF with LODs (Levels of Detail) and compressed animations. (Blender → glTF for WebAR/mobile).

AR Integration / Runtime

  • OpenCV (in Python for prototyping, or in WASM for web): marker/scene detection, camera calibration, and pose estimation for model placement.
  • Rendering of models and textures over the camera feed (e.g., three.js / WebGL for WebAR, or a native layer with OpenCV + OpenGL in the mobile prototype).
  • Timeline control: UI slider for transitioning between decades; each position loads a specific texture/particles/model.

Spatial Audio and UI

  • Simple spatial audio (Web Audio API or native engine) mapped to data changes (e.g., pitch increases with temperature).
  • Captions, information panels, and accessibility buttons.

Distribution

  • WebAR (GitHub Pages) for maximum reach; native builds if required (future).

Tools / Libraries (Suggested Versions)

  • Python: 3.10+; xarray, netCDF4, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, Pillow.
  • OpenCV: 4.x (for marker detection, calibration) — can use OpenCV Python for prototyping.
  • Blender: 3.x (modeling, animation, glTF export).
  • Web / Optional Runtime: three.js, GLTFLoader, WebXR/AR.js (if migrating to WebAR).
  • Service: GitHub + GitHub Pages for demo / public repository.

Benefits and Impact

  • Visual and emotional education on ocean changes.
  • Accessible to schools and the general public (requires no remote sensing expertise).
  • Modular tool: new NASA datasets can be integrated without rewriting the engine.

Creativity / Differentiation

  • “Ocean Pokémon”: creatures that visually change along the timeline; visual metaphors (water color = health, particles = pollution).
  • Direct integration of real NASA data for enhanced credibility.

Design and Team Considerations

  • Data source transparency (credits and links).
  • Balance scientific veracity with legibility for a lay audience.
  • Asset optimization for common devices (LOD, compressed textures).

Accessibility

  • Full captions and removable text panels.
  • Color palettes safe for color-blind users.
  • Seated mode; touch/gesture control; 360-video alternative for users without AR hardware.

Performance & Optimizations

  • Export glTF models with Draco compression, KTX2 textures, use LODs.
  • Bake shadows and lighting when possible; reduce vertex count.
  • Data pre-processing in Python to reduce runtime cost.

Licensing & Credits

  • Include NASA credits and links to used datasets (see "NASA Data" section).
  • Respect terms of use for datasets (Earthdata/PO.DAAC/GRACE).

projectDetails.name: Memento Mori: O Despertar do Sol
projectDetails.summary:
Em um futuro próximo, a Terra agoniza — não apenas por causas humanas, mas por uma força antiga e consciente despertando no coração do Sol. Divindades esquecidas começam a se manifestar enquanto o cientista Dr. Adrian Kael, da agência AURION, investiga uma anomalia solar que desafia toda lógica.

A trama mistura ficção científica sombria, fantasia teológica e mistério investigativo, conduzida através de um dossiê narrativo (livro) e um site interativo (AURION). O leitor assume o papel de investigador indireto, conectando relatórios, arquivos corrompidos e enigmas criptografados. Cada pista decifrada revela fragmentos do enredo e a verdade sobre o Sol Vivo, entidade divina que manipulou todos os eventos desde o início.

O projeto une literatura e tecnologia, com puzzles e dados científicos reais da NASA, explorando o clima espacial e seus efeitos sobre a Terra. Ao mesmo tempo, questiona os limites entre razão e fé, ética e sobrevivência, ciência e divindade.

No fim, a revelação é inevitável: o apocalipse não é destruição, mas reengenharia — e o maior erro não está na fórmula, mas no próprio humano.
projectDetails.details:
Projeto Narrativo: MEMENTO MORI – O Despertar do Sol

1. Conceito Central

Uma narrativa imersiva e investigativa, ambientada em um futuro próximo do universo Memento Mori, onde a Terra está morrendo — não apenas por consequências humanas e causas naturais, mas por forças muito mais antigas e conscientes.

Divindades antigas, anteriormente adormecidas, começam a se manifestar sob formas sutis e disfarçadas.

O leitor assume o papel de investigador indireto, reunindo pistas espalhadas entre o livro físico/digital e um site interativo, que contém arquivos, relatórios e fragmentos de dados ocultos.

A história mistura ficção científica sombria + fantasia teológica + mistério investigativo, revelando gradualmente que as “anomalias científicas” são, na verdade, manifestações sobrenaturais, culminando em uma revelação surpreendente sobre o verdadeiro fim do mundo.

2. Estrutura do Projeto

Livro

  • Apresentado como dossiê narrativo: relatórios, diários, transcrições, correspondências e dados corrompidos.
  • O protagonista, Dr. Adrian Kael, é cientista cético, racional e traumatizado, conduzindo a investigação de uma anomalia solar e climática.
  • Ao longo dos capítulos, eventos e pistas sugerem causas sobrenaturais, mas sem confirmação imediata.
  • A descoberta do divino é gradual, permitindo que o leitor perceba sinais antes mesmo do protagonista.
  • O clímax revela que uma divindade aparentemente confiável (Sol Vivo) manipulou tudo desde o início, e que os humanos por trás da AURION/NEBULA também têm agendas ocultas.

Site Interativo

  • Funciona como extensão do livro, oferecendo documentos citados na narrativa: relatórios, imagens, áudios, vídeos e códigos.
  • Alguns arquivos contêm pistas ocultas, criptografadas ou corrompidas, revelando informações não explícitas no livro.
  • Puzzles, coordenadas e enigmas misturam dados científicos (NASA, astronomia, física) e simbologia mística (runas, sigilos, idiomas antigos).
  • Certos conteúdos só se desbloqueiam quando o leitor conecta dados do livro, encontrando senhas ou padrões ocultos em trechos de texto

projectDetails.details:
The Aura project is an artificial intelligence system that monitors air quality using satellite data. It processes this information and provides users with simple and quick feedback about air quality, as well as personalized tips and precautions based on their health conditions — for example, for risk groups such as children, pregnant women, and people with respiratory issues.

The Aura project aims to improve the quality of life for people with respiratory problems by promoting health and well-being. It also helps users anticipate and prevent the worsening of their symptoms, avoiding health risks through better decision-making.

Figma – Used to design our interactive website.

N8N – A low-code automation tool used to develop the AI agent.

Groq – The AI technology that powers our intelligent agent.

Our project brings innovation to the field of personal health prevention and care by using AI to promote ease, comfort, and speed in everyday decision-making.

In developing this project, we focused on practicality, agility, and accessibility to make complex and detailed information available to everyone in a simple and objective way.

projectDetails.name: Project Condado
projectDetails.summary:
Nossa equipe desenvolveu um plano estratégico e realista para a vida em Marte, focado em segurança e autossustentabilidade. O projeto se baseia em duas fases de missão. Na primeira, um foguete não tripulado enviará maquinário e robôs para iniciar a construção do habitat, além de sondas que irão identificar as melhores localizações para cavernas e para extrair gelo do subsolo. Apenas na segunda fase, a tripulação partirá para Marte, com o habitat pré-pronto, garantindo sua segurança desde o início.
Desenvolvemos dois tipos de habitats, um na superfície e outro no subsolo, garantindo redundância e resiliência à missão. O primeiro, será construído com partes da espaçonave, sendo enterrado no solo marciano para proteção contra radiação e variações de temperatura. O segundo habitat será um abrigo inflável e tambem com partes da espaçonave dentro de uma caverna, um conceito já estudado para bases lunares, que oferece proteção natural ainda maior. Para a autossustentabilidade, a base contará com um ecossistema circular fechado, onde a aquaponia e a criação de insetos garantirão um ciclo alimentar contínuo. A energia será fornecida por pequenos reatores modulares (SMRs) reaproveitados do próprio foguete. 
link de apresentação https://www.canva.com/design/DAG07qAUebE/GKrRr3Zxegp6NUXgIAp4Nw/view?utm_content=DAG07qAUebE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h0c8b0a82a2
projectDetails.details:
O nosso projeto é um plano estratégico para estabelecer uma presença humana sustentável em Marte. O plano se baseia em uma abordagem de duas fases: primeiro, o envio de maquinário e materiais para a construção de um habitat, e, em seguida, a viagem da tripulação. A construção do habitat seria feita com dois modelos complementares, um na superfície e outro no subsolo. O habitat na superfície, em estilo "casa de hobbit", usaria as partes da espaçonave e o solo marciano (regolito) para se proteger de radiação, variações de temperatura e meteoritos. O habitat subterrâneo, inspirado no conceito do arquiteto Thomas Herzig para bases lunares, seria uma estrutura inflável montada no interior de cavernas naturais. A base funcionaria com um ecossistema autossustentável, usando aquaponia e a criação de insetos para produzir alimento,

Para desenvolver este projeto, consideramos uma ampla gama de fatores técnicos e logísticos. Utilizaremos maquinário robótico para escavação e construção, sondas como a Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) e a sonda Phoenix para análise de solo e localização de gelo. A base contará com sistemas de purificação de água e pequenos reatores modulares (SMRs) para energia. A maior parte do trabalho de construção seria feita por robôs e impressoras 3D, minimizando a exposição humana

projectDetails.name: Project ECHO: Exoplanet Classification Hub - Online
projectDetails.summary:
The project developed is ECHO (Exoplanet Classification Hub - Online), a full-stack web platform designed to streamline the classification and analysis of data from observations using the transit method.

ECHO addresses the primary challenge in astronomy: the exponential volume of data generated by missions like Kepler and TESS, which renders traditional analysis and visual inspection impractical. It overcomes this by applying advanced computational methods based on machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). The platform uses a processing pipeline that ingests data from sources like NExA/MAST, performs feature engineering, and utilizes Parallel Classification. This includes using AutoGluon for automated binary classification (Confirmed Exoplanet vs. False Positive) of tabular data and a Deep Learning CNN for multi-target classification of TESS light curves.

ECHO is important because its intended impact is to democratize access to advanced exoplanet analysis through a user-friendly, open-source tool. The use of a modern, efficient web architecture ensures a seamless and low-latency user experience even when dealing with large datasets. Furthermore, the system incorporates a full Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) lifecycle, using Docker and a CI/CD pipeline to rapidly update and reliably test new scientific models against real-world data, supporting the wider astronomy community.
projectDetails.details:
ECHO (Exoplanet Classification Hub - Online) is a full-stack web platform designed to streamline the classification and analysis of exoplanet data. Its primary function is to serve as a fast, accessible interface for processing the astronomical data and presenting the results derived from multiple methods.

The system operates through a seamless integration of a data pipeline and a production-ready web application.

1. Data Pipeline (ETL and Feature Engineering): Data is sourced from official sources such as NExA/MAST. Raw exoplanet data is merged, cleaned, and transformed using a Python Jupyter Notebook. This crucial step involves handling missing values, performing feature selection, preparing the binary target variable (converting candidate status to 0 or 1 numerical labels), and applying scaling and normalization to numerical features.

2. Parallel Classification: The processed data undergoes classification using advanced AI/ML techniques:

  • AutoML Classification (Tabular Data): Python code utilizes the AutoGluon TabularPredictor to automate the process of binary classification (determining if a signal is a Confirmed Exoplanet or a False Positive). AutoGluon automatically handles missing data, performs feature engineering, trains and evaluates multiple models simultaneously, conducts hyperparameter tuning, and creates a highly accurate ensemble model.
  • Deep Learning Classification (Light Curve Data): A parallel classification stream uses a Deep Learning approach, specifically a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), to analyze time series light curve data from TESS. This model, implemented using TensorFlow and Keras, performs Multi-Target Classification. (this solution was explored, as seen in the project's public code base, but not implemented into the final application due to time constraints).

3. Deployment and Web Application: The resulting trained models are crucial deployable artifacts. A TensorFlow.js Conversion step ensures model parameters are integrated into the NodeJS-based web application. The frontend and server-side logic, built with SvelteKit and TypeScript, provides a highly responsive user experience by consuming the deployed model and data via a RESTful interface.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main benefit of the project is the creation of a unified, high-performance tool for exoplanet data analysis. By using a modern, fast framework like SvelteKit and a high-efficiency server like Caddy, the project is intended to provide a seamless and low-latency user experience. The intended impact is to democratize access to advanced exoplanet analysis by offering a user-friendly, open-source tool. By integrating machine learning with traditional classification and a robust deployment system (CI/CD), ECHO establishes a template for rapidly updating and testing new scientific models against real-world data, thereby supporting the wider astronomy community.

How is your Project Creative?

The project's creativity lies in its modern, unified, and simplified architecture.

Furthermore, the architecture is designed for low-overhead deployment. Using SQLite eliminates external database dependencies, allowing the entire application to be highly portable and easily deployed as a single container via Docker. Caddy is used for High-Efficiency Serving, which separates static file delivery and proxy concerns, offloading demanding tasks like security and delivery of large assets (such as .fits files) from the core application logic.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Lifecycle: Creating a robust continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. This pipeline automatically validates new models via Integration Testing, packages them into a Docker Image, and rolls them out to Azure Cloud without manual intervention, ensuring the platform can rapidly integrate the latest scientific models.
  • Data Quality: Accounting for the fact that astronomical data is often incomplete by implementing strategies for handling missing values (e.g., mean, median, or zero imputation) and performing feature selection to reduce noise.
  • Accelerated Model Development: Leveraging AI/AutoML (AutoGluon) to accelerate model development by automatically finding superior model configurations for the project's classification requirements.

The team is using the domain and Azure cloud credits provided by the spaceappschallenge 2025.

We thank the organizers for the support.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools were utilized in the project to adhere to NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, focusing on accelerating development, ensuring code quality, and optimizing the Machine Learning (ML) model selection.

Code and Data Processing

AI assistance was applied to non-core tasks to enhance efficiency and methodological rigor:

  • Code Review and Refinement: AI tools were used to review existing Python code (specifically sections for data cleaning, preprocessing, and the Keras model definition) to verify adherence to best practices and to confirm the correct implementation of standard data science techniques. This served to accelerate the documentation process and improve the quality of the data preprocessing scripts.
    1. To help validate the training configuration and interpret the output of the ML model, ensuring the process followed standard methodological practices for binary classification on tabular data.
    2. We utilized an Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) framework, AutoGluon, to efficiently search for and find the optimal model configuration (including the best algorithm, hyperparameters, and ensemble) for the binary classification task. This usage was crucial to ensure a superior model setup was not overlooked.

This targeted use of AI allowed the team to maintain focus on the core scientific challenge of exoplanet classification while ensuring the clarity and quality of the supporting technical assets.

The AI tools used to assist in the above tasks were:

  • Gemini (a helpful AI assistant built by Google)
  • ChatGPT (by OpenAI)
  • AutoGluon (Automated Machine Learning framework)

Ao final, um prompt transforma os resultados em imagens do próprio cenário do usuário, reforçando o aprendizado. O projeto ataca a complexidade de projetar habitats para Lua/Marte sob restrições reais (volume, massa, ISRU, autonomia, microgravidade), integrando saúde, ergonomia, logística, radiação, sono, sustentabilidade e trabalho. Entrega educação acessível, rigor técnico e ferramenta prática de decisão. Diferenciais: foco humano (Enfermagem + Farmácia), escalabilidade e alinhamento ao Space Apps. Baseado em NASA/TP-2020-220505, ESDMD-001 (2024), MMPACT (AIAA 2021), IEEE 2023 e Stromgren et al.
projectDetails.details:
O FUTURE 2.0 é uma plataforma educativa e interativa que transforma diretrizes técnicas da NASA em experiências compreensíveis para qualquer público. O projeto combina um site autoexplicativo (com conteúdo curado, visual e comparativo) com uma planilha interativa (que orienta escolhas e gera diagnóstico automático) e um conjunto de prompts prontos para criar imagens dos cenários definidos pelo usuário. O resultado é um fluxo completo: aprender, decidir e visualizar — deixando claro por que e como projetar um habitat fora da Terra com foco no ser humano.

O problema que atacamos

Projetar habitats para Lua, Marte e ambientes de trânsito orbital exige equilibrar saúde, ergonomia, manutenção, logística, radiação, energia e sustentabilidade sob restrições reais de volume, massa, ISRU, autonomia e operação em microgravidade. A grande barreira é traduzir critérios complexos em decisões compreensíveis e justificáveis, permitindo que estudantes, profissionais e público leigo enxerguem impactos concretos das escolhas de design.

Nossa solução: site educativo

No site (https://newworldspaceapps.blogspot.com/), as páginas temáticas explicam, em linguagem clara e visual, o que muda fora da Terra: água, resíduos, higiene, ergonomia, sono, saúde e exercícios, radiação, trabalho, logística, controle ambiental e sustentabilidade/ISRU. Cada página compara “Terra vs. Espaço” e apresenta boas práticas fundamentadas em documentos oficiais. Aplicamos um filtro de qualidade nos melhores materiais, consolidamos e organizamos as informações e tornamos o conteúdo acessível por meio de exemplos, glossário e ilustrações.

Nossa solução: planilha interativa

A planilha foi projetada para conduzir o usuário por cenários reais (Lua, Marte, Trânsito, Órbita; estruturas metálicas, infláveis, híbridas e ISRU/rególito), permitindo definir prioridades e avaliar implicações. Ao final, a automação gera um diagnóstico com três níveis de status — adequado, atenção e crítico — destacando pontos fortes, riscos e melhorias recomendadas em áreas como alimentação, controle ambiental, ergonomia, higiene, logística, manutenção, psicologia e lazer, radiação, saúde e exercícios, sono, sustentabilidade/ISRU e trabalho. Um dashboard resume resultados e a lógica de priorização, facilitando comparação entre habitats.

Do diagnóstico à visualização: prompts para imagens

Depois de preencher a planilha, o usuário recebe um prompt pronto para ser colado em uma IA generativa. Esse prompt usa os resultados do relatório e produz imagens comparativas (trípticos “Adequado | Atenção | Crítico”) com o mesmo personagem e o mesmo habitat, respeitando condições de microgravidade e boas práticas (contenção, fluxos de ar, “water walls”, arnês, etc.). Assim, o público vê suas próprias escolhas ganhando forma, o que reforça o aprendizado e acelera discussões técnicas.

Fluxo de uso recomendado

O caminho sugerido é simples e pedagógico. Primeiro, aprender no site, compreendendo conceitos e diferenças essenciais entre Terra e Espaço. Em seguida, escolher na planilha os cenários e prioridades, ajustando pesos conforme a missão. Depois, diagnosticar com base no relatório automático, que aponta onde melhorar e por quê. Por fim, visualizar com os prompts, gerando imagens do próprio cenário para uso em aulas, apresentações e revisão de design.

O que o FUTURE 2.0 entrega

A plataforma entrega educação científica acessível, rigor técnico e uma ferramenta prática de simulação e decisão. Ao mesmo tempo, promove engajamento com imagens sob medida do cenário do usuário e reprodutibilidade do processo em diferentes turmas, pesquisas e eventos. Professores e avaliadores enxergam valor pedagógico e aplicabilidade direta; estudantes e público leigo ganham clareza e motivação.

Diferenciais que convencem a banca

O FUTURE 2.0 traduz diretrizes da NASA em ação concreta, mantendo equilíbrio entre ciência e acessibilidade. A abordagem é centrada no humano, com ênfase em saúde, ergonomia, privacidade, sono e bem-estar psicológico — um diferencial sustentado pelas formações de Enfermagem (Eduardo) e Farmácia (Gabriel). O projeto é escalável (novos habitats, destinos, integração com IA e 3D), transferível para ensino e pesquisa, e está totalmente alinhado ao objetivo do Space Apps: criar uma ferramenta visual que ajude a pensar, projetar e entender habitats espaciais.

projectDetails.name: ANGA: Active and Collaborative Air Quality Monitoring System
projectDetails.summary:
ANGA is an intuitive web platform designed to combat the "invisibility" of air pollution, especially in regions without official monitoring—such as most parts of Brazil. By leveraging data from NASA, the OpenAQ network, and other sources, our platform provides real-time air quality forecasts and alerts for any location.
Our key differentiator lies in citizen science innovation: we empower users to become active sensors, using their smartphone cameras to capture daytime atmospheric visibility and nighttime sky clarity during bright moon phases. These collaborative data, processed by our Artificial Intelligence, help create a hyperlocal and more accurate air quality map, with the ultimate goal of protecting public health, informing environmental policies, and fostering a more aware and engaged society.
projectDetails.details:
WHAT DOES THIS EXACTLY DO?

ANGA translates complex atmospheric data from satellites and sensors into simple, actionable information for everyday citizens. It displays the Air Quality Index (AQI) in real time, provides 24-hour forecasts, and issues health alerts. Above all, it creates a collaborative monitoring network, filling the gaps left by the lack of official measurement stations.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

The platform operates through a cloud-based client–server architecture:

Frontend (Web Application): Users access ANGA through their web browser. The application requests their geolocation.

Backend (Python Server): The server receives the coordinates and orchestrates data collection, making calls to multiple APIs.

Data Collection:

  • OpenAQ: Retrieves real monitoring data from nearby ground stations.
    • Daytime Measurement: By pointing their camera toward the horizon, users send an image to the backend. A Computer Vision AI analyzes contrast loss to estimate particulate pollution.
    • Nighttime Measurement: On ideal nights (identified via weather and astronomy APIs), users capture the moon’s light halo, which our AI correlates with atmospheric clarity.

Artificial Intelligence: A Machine Learning model in the backend processes all these datasets — real, derived, and collaborative — to generate a localized and accurate 24-hour AQI forecast.

Visualization: The frontend receives all consolidated data from the backend and displays it intuitively through dashboards, tables, alerts, and an interactive map.

WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS OF THIS?
  • Public Health: Provides real-time alerts that enable at-risk populations (children, the elderly, and people with asthma) to take protective measures.
  • Democratization of Information: Delivers air quality data to millions of Brazilians living in “data deserts”, areas without official monitoring.
  • Foundation for Public Policy: Builds a robust dataset that can be used by municipalities and state governments to develop more effective environmental policies.
  • Awareness and Engagement: Transforms citizens into active participants in monitoring their environment, fostering a culture of environmental responsibility.
WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS OF THIS?

We aim to create the most comprehensive and collaborative air quality map in Brazil, making the invisible, visible. Our goal is for people in any city to be able to consult ANGA and make informed decisions to protect their health — just as farmers rely on weather forecasts to guide their actions.

FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION

Integration with Wearables: Connect with smartwatches and fitness bands to cross-reference user health data (such as heart rate and physical activity) with pollution levels.

Enhanced Health Alerts: Allow users to voluntarily input pre-existing health conditions (such as asthma or COPD) to receive more specific and personalized alerts.

Gamification: Introduce a points, badges, and rewards system to encourage continuous user participation in citizen science data collection.

WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGE, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE WERE USED?
  • Backend: Python (using the Flask framework).
  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, and pure JavaScript (Vanilla JS).
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS for fast and responsive design, combined with custom CSS.
  • Maps: Leaflet.js.
  • Data Sources (APIs): OpenAQ API, and data/concepts from NASA’s TEMPO and Pandora projects.
  • Infrastructure: Cloud hosting on Render.com, utilizing serverless functions for image processing.
  • Artificial Intelligence (Planned): Python libraries such as TensorFlow or PyTorch for Machine Learning and Computer Vision models.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub.

projectDetails.name: Project T.A.R.D.I.S
projectDetails.summary:
TARDIS Voyager is an interactive web application designed to bring planetary exploration to everyone's fingertips. We developed a platform featuring high-resolution, explorable maps of the Moon, Mars, and Earth, bridging the gap between complex scientific data and public engagement.

To address the challenge of making space education interactive, our application combines curated, historical guided tours—highlighting iconic locations like Apollo landing sites and rover paths—with a dynamic, community-driven annotation system. This allows users not only to learn from established facts but also to contribute their own points of interest, fostering a collaborative discovery environment.

The project is important because it transforms passive learning into an active journey. By providing an accessible and engaging tool, TARDIS Voyager aims to democratize planetary science, spark curiosity in space exploration, and serve as a valuable educational resource for students, enthusiasts, and researchers alike.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

TARDIS Voyager is a web-based, interactive cartography platform that allows users to explore detailed maps of the Moon, Mars, and Earth. The application operates in two primary modes: exploration and contribution.

In exploration mode, users can select a planet and embark on curated guided tours of significant historical and geological landmarks, such as the Apollo landing sites or the Valles Marineris canyon on Mars. For the keen-eyed explorer, we've also hidden several Easter eggs throughout the maps, rewarding curiosity with unique references and fun discoveries. An animated rover visually connects the main tour points, creating a narrative journey that encourages both structured learning and playful exploration.

In contribution mode, users can add their own discoveries to the map. By clicking on any location, they can create a persistent annotation with a title, description, and author name. This user-generated data is saved to our database and becomes visible to the entire community. The frontend, built with Next.js and React, dynamically fetches map tiles and annotation data from a backend API. All annotations are displayed on an interactive Leaflet map and are also listed in a filterable side panel for easy navigation.

What benefits does it have?

The primary benefit of TARDIS Voyager is that it transforms planetary science from a passive, academic subject into an active, engaging experience.

  • Educational Benefit: It serves as a powerful visual learning tool for students and educators, turning abstract coordinates and mission logs into tangible points on a map.
  • Community Engagement: It fosters a collaborative environment where space enthusiasts can share knowledge and discoveries, creating a rich, user-generated library of planetary points of interest.
  • Accessibility: As a web-based platform, it democratizes access to high-resolution planetary data, requiring no specialized software or hardware—only a web browser.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our intended impact is to spark curiosity and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers. As a rocketry team, our passion is hands-on science, and we wanted to build a tool that reflects that spirit. We aim for TARDIS Voyager to become a living, collaborative atlas—a constantly evolving resource used for both formal education in classrooms and informal discovery at home. By making the exploration of other worlds feel personal and interactive, we hope to lower the barrier to entry for space science and make the cosmos feel a little closer.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Our project was developed using a modern, full-stack TypeScript approach:

  • Frontend Framework: Next.js with React
  • Language: TypeScript
  • Mapping Library: Leaflet.js with React-Leaflet for component integration.
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS for a utility-first design system, complemented by shadcn/ui for accessible, pre-built components.
  • Backend: Next.js API Routes, providing a serverless backend environment.
  • Database & ORM: PostgreSQL (hosted on Neon) for our relational database, with Prisma serving as our type-safe Object-Relational Mapper.
  • API Validation: Zod for robust schema validation on our API endpoints.
  • Version Control & Deployment: Git and GitHub for version control, with the project deployed on Vercel.

How is your project creative?

Our creativity lies in the synthesis of two distinct concepts: the authoritative, curated historical tour and the dynamic, user-generated "wiki-map." Instead of just presenting established data, we created a platform where official history and community curiosity coexist and enrich each other. The animated rover is another creative touch that transforms simple navigation from a functional click into a narrative journey, making the experience more story-driven. We also creatively combined multiple data sources (map tiles, historical points, and user annotations) into a single, cohesive user interface that feels intuitive and unified.

What factors did your team consider?

Throughout the development process, our team prioritized several key factors:

  • User Experience (UX): A seamless and intuitive interface was paramount. We focused on making navigation, tour controls, and annotation creation as straightforward as possible, ensuring the platform is usable for all ages and technical skill levels.
  • Performance: Loading high-resolution map tiles and a potentially large number of annotations can be resource-intensive. We considered performance from the start, using Next.js features like dynamic imports for the map component and efficient data-fetching strategies to ensure a smooth experience.
  • Scalability: We designed the backend to be serverless and the database to be robust, anticipating that the number of user annotations could grow significantly.
  • Data Integrity: To ensure the quality of user-submitted data, we implemented server-side validation using Zod, preventing malformed or incomplete data from entering our database.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence tools were utilized to accelerate development and enhance creative aspects of the TARDIS Voyager project. Our team leveraged AI as a collaborative partner to support our original vision and execution. The specific uses are detailed below:

  • Video Production: The script, narrative structure, and storyboard concepts for our project demonstration video were developed with the assistance of Perplexity AI. The tool was used to brainstorm compelling ways to present our application's features and to refine the descriptive text, ensuring a clear and impactful final presentation.
  • Logo Design and Branding: We used Copilot's image generation capabilities to brainstorm and iterate on concepts for the TARDIS Voyager project logo.
  • Code and Development Assistance: ChatGPT was integrated into our development environment, serving as an AI pair programmer. It helping to identify potential bugs, which significantly streamlined our coding workflow. Additionally, we consulted with large language models like Google's Gemini for debugging CSS layout issues, refactoring code, and generating documentation text.

In all instances, AI-generated content was reviewed, selected, and heavily modified by our team to fit the unique goals and technical requirements of our project. AI served as a tool to augment our skills, not to replace the core problem-solving and creative direction driven by our team.

projectDetails.name: Rio 40° App
projectDetails.summary:
Rio 40° is an interactive educational app created to celebrate the 25th anniversary of NASA’s Terra satellite. Using data from Terra’s MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) instrument, the project visualizes how the surface temperature of Rio de Janeiro has changed over the past 25 years. Through animated storytelling, the app connects satellite observations with real urban experiences, showing how deforestation, urban growth, and reduced vegetation contribute to the rise of local heat islands.

The experience guides users through three dimensions — past, present, and future — combining scientific data with human impact. It highlights how NASA’s continuous Earth observation helps us understand and adapt to climate change on a local scale.

By transforming complex MODIS datasets into an accessible, emotional narrative, Rio 40° reinforces the mission of Terra: to reveal how our planet evolves — and remind us that what happens on Earth is visible from space.
projectDetails.details:
Rio 40° is an interactive storytelling app that transforms 25 years of data from NASA’s Terra satellite into an immersive visual experience about urban heat and climate change in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

The app uses observations from Terra’s MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) instrument to illustrate how the city’s surface temperature has evolved between 2000 and 2025. Users can explore animated sections that reveal the past (historical temperature rise), present (urban heat maps), and future (scientific projections), supported by accessible explanations and practical insights on how local actions can mitigate heat impacts.

The project’s main goal is to make complex satellite data understandable and emotional, connecting global science to the daily lives of citizens. It encourages environmental awareness and community engagement through storytelling and visual design.

Tools used: Figma (interactive prototype and animations), Illustrator (visual elements), and NASA Earthdata resources (MODIS datasets and references).

Creative approach: By combining UX research, graphic design, and scientific storytelling, Rio 40° bridges the gap between data and emotion. It transforms raw satellite measurements into a narrative that celebrates the Terra mission’s legacy and inspires collective action for a more resilient urban future.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence was used as a supporting creative and research tool throughout the development of Rio 40°, primarily to accelerate ideation and enhance visual storytelling.

- Concept development and writing assistance: AI tools (ChatGPT by OpenAI) were used to help refine the English and Portuguese copywriting, summarize scientific sources from NASA’s MODIS data, and structure the UX storytelling in a clear and educational tone.

- No NASA logos or design elements were created or modified using AI. All NASA references are cited directly from official NASA data sources and documentation.

AI was used solely to enhance creative communication — not to generate or modify scientific data. The project’s datasets, facts, and references come exclusively from NASA’s MODIS and Terra mission databases.

projectDetails.aiReferences:
1. Data Analysis and Prediction

AI processes complex NASA satellite data (like SMAP, MODIS, GPM, ECOSTRESS) to:

  • Predict soil moisture, rainfall, and crop health
  • Forecast crop yield and detect early drought or flood risks
  • Identify optimal sowing and harvesting periods

2. Smart Decision Support

AI models analyze environmental conditions to give real-time recommendations for:

  • Irrigation scheduling (when and how much to water)
  • Fertilizer optimization (based on soil and weather data)
  • Pest and disease detection using image-based analysis (NDVI & vegetation indices)

3. AI Mentor (AgriBot)

An AI-powered chatbot helps farmers by:

  • Answering questions in simple language
  • Translating NASA data into practical advice
  • Providing personalized suggestions based on farm location and crop type

4. Predictive & Adaptive Learning

  • AI learns continuously from user data and changing environmental conditions
  • Improves accuracy of predictions and advice over time
  • Adapts to regional weather and soil variations

5. Visualization & Accessibility

  • AI converts raw satellite data into easy-to-understand visuals
  • Provides color-coded maps for soil health, water stress, and vegetation health
  • Makes complex scientific data accessible to farmers and students

(Space Operations Mission Directorate)

projectDetails.name: Project AInigma
projectDetails.summary:
We built an educational farm simulation that: 
● Lets users manage a virtual farm (planting, irrigating, fertilizing, raising livestock). 
● Integrates NASA Earth data in real time for soil moisture, rainfall, vegetation, and 
temperature. 
● Shows the impact of every decision: on crop yield, water use, and environmental 
health. 
● Provides feedback and mini-tutorials so players learn why their decisions worked or 
failed. 
This way, users aren’t just playing a game — they’re learning how data-driven, sustainable 
practices shape real agriculture.
projectDetails.details: 1. User selects a farm plot (real or simulated). 2. Game fetches NASA satellite data for that location. 3. User chooses actions: irrigate, fertilize, plant, feed livestock. 4. Simulation engine calculates outcomes: crop growth, soil health, environmental impact. 5. User sees results in graphs, visuals, and sustainability scores. 6. Tutorials explain the science behind the outcome. 7. Loop repeats for days/seasons, teaching strategy and sustainability.

(Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: Bio Verse
projectDetails.summary:
**Summary:**
Our project is a **smart web application** that integrates **AI, knowledge graphs, and NASA’s biological research data** to simplify complex space experiments. It allows users to **search intelligently** (e.g., “plant root growth in microgravity”), get **AI-generated summaries** of experiment findings, and **visualize research progress** through interactive dashboards with a futuristic UI.

The platform acts as a **centralized hub for biological insights**, accelerating the understanding of how **microgravity and radiation affect life**. By making scientific data more accessible and interactive, it supports **sustainable food growth** and helps **lay the foundation for future space habitats**, empowering both researchers and learners to explore space biology for humanity’s future.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an AI-powered web application designed to make NASA’s biological and space research data more accessible, understandable, and interactive. It combines Artificial Intelligence, Knowledge Graphs, and GenLabs data to help users explore and visualize experiments related to microgravity, radiation, and plant growth in space.

How It Works:
  • Smart Search: Users can type queries like “plant root growth in microgravity” to instantly access connected experiments, research papers, and findings.
  • AI Summaries: A built-in AI model processes complex scientific information and converts it into easy-to-understand summaries and insights.
  • Visualization Dashboard: An interactive dashboard displays the timeline, relationships, and evolution of experiments using modern 3D and graph-based visualizations.
Benefits & Impact:
  • Acts as a centralized hub for biological insights, integrating scattered NASA datasets.
  • Enables faster understanding of the effects of microgravity and radiation on living organisms.
  • Promotes interactive learning and discovery for scientists, students, and space enthusiasts.
  • Contributes to sustainable food growth in space and supports the foundation for future space habitats.
Tools & Technologies Used:
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React.js (for dynamic and futuristic UI).
  • Backend: Python (Flask/FastAPI) with REST APIs.
  • AI & Data: OpenAI APIs, NASA GeneLab datasets, and vector databases for smart search.
  • Visualization: D3.js / Plotly for data visualization and graph mapping.
  • Design: Figma for dashboard mockups and interface design.
Creativity & Design Thinking:

The creativity lies in combining AI summarization with knowledge graphs to form a living, evolving ecosystem of biological research. The futuristic UI and interactive visualizations make scientific data engaging, intuitive, and educational.

Team Considerations:

While designing, we focused on:

  • Accessibility and ease of understanding for non-experts.
  • Scalability for integrating future NASA datasets.
  • Ethical AI use and data transparency.
  • Time efficiency—ensuring the prototype can be built and functional within the hackathon duration.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI-Powered Smart Search:
We used OpenAI’s language models to interpret natural language queries and map them to relevant NASA GeneLab experiments via a knowledge graph.

projectDetails.name: NASA Space Biology Knowledge Engine
projectDetails.summary:
The NASA Space Biology Research Platform is an AI-powered web application designed to analyze, summarize, and visualize NASA’s space biology research publications. It leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to process over 600 bioscience papers, generating clear summaries, extracting key findings, and presenting data through interactive visualizations and an intelligent chatbot interface.

This solution addresses the challenge of navigating NASA’s vast, complex biological datasets by transforming unstructured research into accessible insights. Scientists, mission planners, and researchers can now quickly explore experiment results, identify research gaps, and gain a deeper understanding of how living systems respond to space environments.

By combining spaCy, PyTextRank, and Google Gemini AI, the platform enhances data accessibility and supports evidence-based decision-making for future Moon and Mars missions. This project demonstrates how AI can accelerate discovery and promote open science within NASA’s space exploration efforts.
projectDetails.details:
The NASA Space Biology Research Platform is an AI-powered web application that analyzes, summarizes, and visualizes NASA’s bioscience research. It processes hundreds of space biology publications to help scientists and mission planners easily explore how living systems respond to the space environment.

The platform uses a hybrid AI summarization system combining spaCy, PyTextRank, and Google Gemini AI to extract key information and generate clear, concise summaries. It also provides interactive charts and an AI chatbot that allow users to explore experiment results and ask scientific questions in real time.

This project offers significant benefits, including faster access to critical research findings, data-driven decision-making, and improved collaboration among researchers. It reduces analysis time by over 80%, making NASA’s vast data more understandable and actionable.

Developed with React, FastAPI, Python, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, the system demonstrates creativity through its combination of natural language processing, generative AI, and interactive visualization. The team focused on accuracy, usability, and scalability, ensuring the tool is both scientifically valid and accessible for future space exploration research.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our project makes extensive and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence to enhance data analysis, summarization, and user interaction.

  • Text Summarization: We used Google Gemini AI in combination with spaCy and PyTextRank to generate hybrid summaries of NASA’s bioscience research publications. Gemini AI rewrites extracted scientific text into concise, human-readable summaries without altering factual content.
  • Conversational Assistant: The platform includes an AI-powered chatbot using Gemini to provide context-aware answers about research findings.
  • Data Extraction: NLP tools identify keywords, scientific terms, and numerical data for visualization.
  • AI Transparency: All AI-generated text (summaries and chat responses) is clearly labeled within the application interface, ensuring users understand which content is AI-assisted.
  • No AI-Generated Media: No AI-generated images, videos, or NASA-branded graphics were used in the project.

The use of AI accelerated innovation, improved accessibility, and enabled intelligent summarization of complex scientific information.

Space Learning Universe is an interactive web-based platform designed to make space education engaging, immersive, and accessible to all. Our project transforms traditional learning into a gamified experience featuring space quizzes, exploration missions, and AR-based solar system simulations powered by real NASA data. Users can embark on virtual missions, earn XP, and climb leaderboards while uncovering fascinating facts about the cosmos.

projectDetails.details:
Project Details – Space Learning Universe

Space Learning Universe is an interactive education platform that transforms the way people learn about space. The system combines gamified quizzes, exploration missions, and an AR-based solar system experience to make astronomy both fun and informative. Users can test their knowledge, earn XP, and climb a global leaderboard while exploring real-time data fetched directly from NASA APIs.

Our project works by integrating multiple modules — quiz engine, mission tracker, user authentication, and a live NASA data fetcher — within a web app built using Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, and EJS. The AR experience is designed to visualize celestial bodies in 3D, helping learners grasp complex concepts visually.

The benefits include increased curiosity for space, accessible education for all age groups, and a more engaging alternative to traditional learning methods. The intended impact is to inspire students to explore STEM fields while having fun discovering the universe.

We focused on creativity, engagement, and accessibility, ensuring that learning feels like play, not homework. By blending real-world NASA data, gamification, and modern web tech, Space Learning Universe stands as a creative step toward the future of space education.

projectDetails.name: RainAlert - Event Planner & Forecaster
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, RainAlert – Event Planner &  Forecaster , is a web-based weather monitoring system that provides real-time rain alerts, agricultural guidance, and event planning assistance. Using NASA POWER API for daily precipitation data and the Open-Meteo API for hourly forecasts, our system delivers accurate, location-based weather predictions.

The backend, built with Java Spring Boot, stores weather data in MySQL, while the HTML/CSS frontend presents an interactive dashboard accessible via http://localhost:8080. Users receive alerts when predicted rainfall exceeds customizable thresholds, enabling farmers to protect crops, communities to plan outdoor events, and decision-makers to minimize weather-related disruptions.

This project addresses the challenge by integrating global satellite data with real-time local forecasts, providing actionable insights for communities vulnerable to rainfall. Its importance lies in preventing losses, enhancing preparedness, and making weather information accessible to all, especially in agricultural and event planning contexts.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a web-based Rain Alert and Weather-Forecasting System that helps farmers, community members, and event organizers prepare for rainfall.

The system integrates NASA’s POWER API (https://power.larc.nasa.gov/) to access daily satellite-based precipitation data (PRECTOTCORR parameter) and combines it with the Open-Meteo Weather API (https://open-meteo.com/) to provide hourly rainfall predictions.

How It Works

  1. The backend, built with Java Spring Boot, fetches precipitation data from NASA POWER and hourly forecast data from Open-Meteo.
  2. Data is processed and stored in a MySQL database.
  3. The HTML/CSS frontend displays a browser-based dashboard served from http://localhost:8080.
  4. The dashboard shows daily and hourly forecasts, visual trends, and sends alerts when predicted rainfall crosses a threshold.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Provides early rain warnings for farmers to protect crops and plan irrigation.
  • Helps event planners and communities reduce disruptions caused by sudden rainfall.
  • Combines satellite data (NASA) with real-time API data (Open-Meteo) for improved accuracy.
  • Lightweight dashboard designed to be accessible on low-bandwidth connections.

Tools & Technologies

  • Backend: Java Spring Boot
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS
    • NASA POWER API – https://power.larc.nasa.gov/
      – Example call: …parameters=PRECTOTCORR…
    • Open-Meteo API – https://open-meteo.com/
  • Runs on: Browser at http://localhost:8080
  • Other Tools: [add IDE such as IntelliJ IDEA or VS Code]

Creativity

We creatively integrated satellite-based precipitation data from NASA with live hourly forecasts to provide actionable, local rain alerts.
The web app uses open APIs, lightweight frontend design, and simple setup instructions, making it cost-effective, scalable, and easy for rural communities to use.

Factors Considered

  • Accuracy and reliability of precipitation forecasts
  • Ease of setup for hackathon judges (includes README + SQL dump)
  • Simple UI for quick decision-making in emergencies
  • Data privacy and security (API keys excluded from the shared code)

projectDetails.name: Project CodeSharks
projectDetails.summary:
Our project is a Django-based web application that helps users explore and analyze NASA’s Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. SAR satellites can capture Earth’s surface even at night or through clouds — this makes it very useful for tracking floods, deforestation, land changes, and natural disasters.

The software doesn’t need any hardware. It connects to public NASA and Copernicus APIs to fetch real satellite images, processes them using Python tools, and shows them interactively on a web map interface built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, and Leaflet.js.

This project supports environmental monitoring, disaster management, and research by giving everyone easy access to complex satellite data in a simple, user-friendly dashboard.
projectDetails.details: Our project, NASA SAR Data Viewer, is a Django-based web application that allows users to view and analyze Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite data from NASA and Copernicus. It works by fetching real-time radar images through public APIs and displaying them on an interactive map using Leaflet.js. The tool helps monitor floods, deforestation, and land changes, even at night or through clouds. Built using Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap, it requires no hardware. The project promotes environmental awareness and disaster management, offering a creative, user-friendly, and accessible way to explore complex Earth observation data.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support and accelerate the development process of our project, NASA SAR Data Viewer. AI was primarily utilized for data analysis, image enhancement, and project content generation. Machine learning models helped identify environmental changes such as flooded regions, vegetation loss, and land deformation from SAR satellite images by analyzing pixel variations over time. We also used AI-based Python libraries to automate preprocessing of radar data, including noise reduction and image classification. Additionally, AI-assisted writing tools were used to refine documentation, generate clear project descriptions, and enhance user interface text. All AI-generated content (text and code suggestions) was verified, edited, and approved manually by our team to ensure accuracy, originality, and compliance with the NASA Space Apps guidelines. No NASA branding or design elements were modified or used through AI tools.

projectDetails.name: Space Biology Search Engine
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, "Space Biology Search Engine," is an AI-powered web application designed to make NASA's bioscience research more accessible. It allows users to search for scientific papers and then "talk" to them using a chatbot to get clear, synthesized answers.

It offers following features :
1. Interactive Search: Users can search for NASA research papers using keywords.
2. AI-Powered Chat: A chatbot is trained on the user's selected papers, allowing them to ask questions and get answers directly from the source material.
3. Grounded Answers: The chatbot's knowledge is strictly limited to the selected papers, ensuring answers are accurate and verifiable.
4. Modern Tech Stack: The project uses a Python Flask backend for its API and a dynamic HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. The AI component leverages sentence-transformers for understanding text and the high-speed Groq API for generating answers, with a local model as a fallback.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do and how does it work :


This project is a bio-search engine backend that allows users to search for reserach papers, specifically from the NASA NTRS API, and then train a chatbot on the contain of those papers to answer questions. Here's a breakdown:

  1. Search: It uses the NASA NTRS API to find paper based on user-provided keywords.
  2. Training: It downlaods the PDF files of the papers, extracts the text, and chunks the text into smaller segments. It then uses a sentence transformer model to create embedings (numerical representations) of these text chunks. These embeddings are stored in a FAISS index, which allows for efficient similarity searching.
  3. Question Answering: When a user asks a question, the question is also embedded using the same sentence transformer model. The FAISS index is then used to find the text chunks that are most similar to the question. These chunks are used as context for a large langugae model (LLM) to generate an answer. It attempts to use the Groq API for a high-quality response and falls back to a local LLM (GPT4All) if the API is unavailable or fails.
  4. Job Management: The training process is handled in a backgeound thread, and the status of the training job is tracked via files in the jobs directory.
  5. Session Management: Trained models are stored in the sessions folder, using a unique session ID. This allows users to have multiple different "chatbots" trained on different sets of papers.
What benefits does it have :
  • Information Retrieval: Quickly find relebant research papers from the NASA NTRS API.
  • Knowledge Synthesis: The chatbot can synthesize information from multiple papers to answer user questions, potentially providing insigjts that would be difficult to obtain by reading the papers individually.
  • Accessibility: Makes complex research more accessible to a wider audience by providing a conversational interface.
  • Local Fallback: Offers a local LLM fallback, ensuring functionality even without a reliable internet connection or API key.
Intended impact of the project :

The project aims to make scientific research more accessible and easier to understand. It could be used by researchers to quickly find and synthesize information, or by students to learn about a particulaar topic. By providing a convrrsational interface to research papers, the project could lower the barrier to entry for anyone interested in learning about science and technology.

Tool, languages, and hardware or softwares :
  • Coding Language: Python
    • Flask: For creating the web API.
    • Flask-CORS: For handling Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS).
    • Requests: For making HTTP requests to the NASA NTRS API and downloading PDFs.
    • pdfplumber: For extracting text from PDF files.
    • Sentence Transformers: For generating sentence embeddings.
    • FAISS: For efficient similarity searching.
    • GPT4All: For running a local LLM.
    • Groq: For using the Groq API.
    • python-dotenv: For loading environment variabls.
    • Groq API (Mixtral-8x7b-32768): Primary LLM for generating answers.
    • GPT4All (orca-mini-3b-gguf2-q4_0.gguf): Local LLM as a fallback.
    • Docker: To containerise the application
Creativity of the project :

The project is creative in its combinatino of existing tools and technologys to create a newer solution for accessing and understanding scientific research. Specifically, it combines:

  • A search engine (NASA NTRS API)
  • PDF text extraciton
  • Sentence embeddings for semantic search
  • A FAISS index for efficient retrieval
  • A large language model for question answering
  • A job queue for background processing
  • A local LLM fallback

This combination of technologies allows users to interact with research papers in a new and intuitive way.

Factors that were considers while making the project :
  • Performance: The projrct uses FAISS for efficient similarity searching and background threads for long-running tasks to ensure responsiveness.
  • Scalability: The project is designed to be scaiable, as the FAISS index can handle large datasets and the background job queue can handle many training requests.
  • Reliability: The project includes error handling and logging to ensure that it is reliable. It also includes a local LLM fallback in case the Groq API is unavailable.
  • Usability: The project provides a simple and intuitive API for users to search for papers, train chatbots, and ask questions.
  • Cost: The project uses a local LLM as a fallback to reduce the cost of using the Groq API.
  • Containerisation: The project is designed to be run in a containerised environment. The docker file makes sure that the cache directory, and models directory, are setup correctly.
  • API Key Security: The project uses environment variables to store the Groq API key, which improves security.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology
projectDetails.summary:
BloomTrack India

A decision-support platform that monitors and predicts large-scale vegetation blooms by fusing NASA Earth Observation data (Landsat, MODIS) with citizen science. Built on Google Earth Engine, our algorithms analyze Vegetation Indices (NDVI) and unique spectral signatures to identify specific mass flowering events beyond simple greenness.

Our interactive web platform delivers a real-time bloom probability heatmap, a community validation layer for crowdsourced photos, and historical trend analysis tools.

This provides actionable intelligence for key stakeholders:
• Agriculture: Forecasting peak mustard crop flowering for optimized harvests.
• Ecology: Tracking the spread of invasive species like Lantana camara.
• Public Health: Predicting high-pollen seasons in cities for public health alerts.

Designed for scalability, our MVP will demonstrate the concept on the mustard farming use case. BloomTrack translates complex satellite data into tangible solutions for India's critical economic and environmental challenges.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: BloomTrack India

Last Updated: October 5, 2025

1. Project Summary (Elevator Pitch)

BloomTrack India is a web-based geospatial platform designed to monitor, predict, and analyze large-scale vegetation blooms across the Indian subcontinent. By creating a novel fusion of NASA's robust Earth Observation (EO) data with community-driven citizen science, our project translates complex satellite imagery into actionable intelligence for key stakeholders in agriculture, ecology, and public health.

2. The Problem Statement

Several sectors in India face challenges due to a lack of timely and scalable data on vegetation phenology (the timing of seasonal events like flowering).

  • For Farmers: Mustard farmers in states like Rajasthan and Punjab lack precise tools to predict the peak flowering period, which is critical for planning honeybee pollination services and optimizing harvest timing.
  • For Ecologists: Conservation authorities struggle with the manual, resource-intensive process of tracking the spread of invasive alien species, such as Lantana camara, which often outcompete native flora.
  • For Public Health: Urban citizens, especially in cities with extensive green cover like Bangalore, face seasonal health risks from high pollen concentrations, with little to no advance warning.

3. Our Solution

BloomTrack India addresses these challenges by providing a centralized, user-friendly platform that integrates top-down satellite analysis with bottom-up community validation.

Our platform processes petabytes of NASA satellite data to identify signals of mass flowering events. This data is then visualized on an interactive map, providing users with historical context, real-time insights, and predictive forecasts.

4. Key Features

MVP (Minimum Viable Product) - Focus for Oct 5, 2025

  • Interactive Map Interface: A map of India where users can navigate and select points of interest.
  • Historical NDVI Charting: On clicking any point on the map, the platform fetches and displays a historical NDVI (plant health) chart for that specific location, showing vegetation cycles over the past few years.
  • Basic Citizen Science Upload: A simple form allowing a user to drop a pin on the map and upload a photo of a real-world bloom, which is stored in a database with its coordinates.

Full Version (Future Features)

  • Dynamic Bloom Probability Layer: A real-time heatmap showing areas with a high statistical probability of a mass bloom event occurring.
  • Advanced Spectral Signature Analysis: An algorithm trained to detect the specific "color signature" of target species like mustard crops or invasive Lantana.
  • Predictive Alerts System: An automated notification system that sends alerts to subscribed users (e.g., "High pollen warning for Bangalore" or "Peak mustard bloom expected in Alwar district in 7-10 days").

5. Technical Architecture

  1. Data Source: NASA's Landsat (30m, historical depth) and MODIS/VIIRS (daily, temporal frequency) archives.
  2. Data Processing: Google Earth Engine (GEE) is used for all heavy-duty, cloud-based geospatial processing and analysis.
  3. Backend API: A Python (Flask/FastAPI) server acts as the middleman. The frontend requests data from this API. The API then queries Google Earth Engine for NDVI/bloom data and the citizen science database for user submissions.
  4. Frontend: A JavaScript-based web application using Leaflet.js for mapping and Chart.js for data visualization.
  5. Database: A cloud-based database like Supabase or Firebase is used to store all citizen science submissions (photos, coordinates, comments).

6. Technology Stack

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Chart.js
  • Backend: Python (Flask or FastAPI)
  • Geospatial Engine: Google Earth Engine API
  • Database: Supabase / Google Firebase
  • Version Control: Git & GitHub
  • Secrets Management: Environment variables (for handling serviceAccountKey.json safely)

7. Project Roadmap

  • Phase 1: Hackathon MVP (Oct 5, 2025):
    • Goal: Prove the core concept.
    • Deliverable: A working web app focused on the mustard farming use case. Users can click on a farm in Rajasthan and see its historical NDVI chart. Basic photo upload is functional.
    • Goal: Build out the full version features.
    • Tasks: Develop the heatmap layer, integrate citizen science pins onto the map, and refine the UI/UX.
    • Goal: Implement predictive models and species-specific algorithms.
    • Tasks: Develop and validate the Lantana camara spectral signature model and the Bangalore pollen prediction model. Scale the backend to handle more users and larger query areas.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Yes, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was utilized as a key tool in the development of the BloomTrack India project. Specifically, we used Google's Gemini, a large language model, as a collaborative assistant throughout the project lifecycle. Our usage can be categorized as follows:

1. Project Scoping, Planning, and Idea Refinement: The initial concept for BloomTrack India was brainstormed with the AI to refine the value proposition, define the specific use cases (for farmers, ecologists, and public health), and structure the idea into a coherent project plan. The AI helped formulate the project roadmap, breaking it down into a feasible Minimum Viable Product (MVP) for the hackathon and outlining features for future development.

2. Technical Guidance and Architecture: Gemini was used as a technical consultant to suggest a viable technology stack (Python, Flask, Leaflet.js, Google Earth Engine API, etc.) and to outline the project's technical architecture. This included defining the data flow from the frontend user interface to our backend API and the Google Earth Engine processing platform.

3. Code Debugging and Best Practices: A critical part of our development involved troubleshooting a Git security issue where a secret key (serviceAccountKey.json) was accidentally committed. The AI provided a precise, step-by-step command-line guide to safely remove the key from the Git history. Furthermore, it educated us on security best practices, providing code examples and instructions for using .gitignore and environment variables to manage sensitive credentials safely.

4. Documentation and Content Generation: The AI assisted in drafting, refining, and formatting all project documentation. This includes the various summaries, the detailed project description for our GitHub README, and this AI usage disclosure statement itself.

Summary of Intent and Execution: In all instances, the AI served as a tool to accelerate our workflow, provide expert knowledge, and help us overcome technical hurdles. The original project idea, all final strategic decisions, and the entirety of the executed code were driven and implemented by the human team members. The AI acted as a 'pair programmer' and 'project planning assistant,' enabling us to build a more robust and well-documented project within the hackathon's timeframe.

projectDetails.name: A world Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
projectDetails.summary: We developed an AI-powered automated exoplanet detection system that integrates data from NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS missions into a unified pipeline for classifying exoplanet candidates with high accuracy and full explainability. The system addresses the critical bottleneck in exoplanet discovery, where thousands of candidates await confirmation due to reliance on slow, manual analysis of light curves, by replacing it with an ensemble machine learning architecture combining Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, and Neural Networks. This approach not only accelerates classification from weeks to seconds but also ensures robustness through weighted soft voting and transparency via SHAP explainability, allowing scientists to understand the features driving each prediction. Our solution is important because it overcomes mission-specific limitations of existing AI tools, handles class imbalance with SMOTE oversampling, and provides an interactive web interface for researchers, students, and citizen scientists to explore real exoplanet data. Built on open-source technologies like React.js, Flask, and Scikit-learn, the system is scalable and future-ready for upcoming space telescope missions, empowering the next generation of AI-assisted space exploration.
projectDetails.details:
The project is an AI-powered automated exoplanet detection system that analyzes light curve data from NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS missions to classify celestial signals as confirmed exoplanets or false positives. It works by first ingesting raw mission data, then applying a unified preprocessing pipeline to clean, normalize, and standardize features across missions, followed by classification using an ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, and Neural Networks combined via weighted soft voting for optimal accuracy. Real-time predictions are enhanced with SHAP explainability, which visualizes the contribution of each stellar feature to the model’s decision, ensuring transparency and scientific trust.Our-Solution-Intelligent-Exoplanet-Detection.pptx

Key benefits include drastically reducing analysis time from weeks to seconds, enabling scalable processing of thousands of candidates through asynchronous batch handling, and overcoming class imbalance using SMOTE oversampling. The intended impact is to accelerate exoplanet discovery by empowering NASA researchers, astrophysics students, and citizen scientists with a transparent, cross-mission compatible tool that supports future space telescope integration.Our-Solution-Intelligent-Exoplanet-Detection.pptx

Developed using React.js and Bootstrap for the frontend, Flask for the backend, and Plotly.js for visualization, the system leverages Scikit-learn, XGBoost, and MongoDB for machine learning and data management. Its creativity lies in unifying disparate mission datasets into a single AI pipeline while providing interpretable results—a critical advancement over black-box models. The team considered factors such as computational efficiency, model overfitting (addressed via k-fold cross-validation), and mission-specific data incompatibilities, resolving them through adaptive preprocessing and model caching
projectDetails.aiReferences:
The project utilized Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a core component for automated exoplanet detection, leveraging ensemble machine learning models including Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, and Neural Networks to classify exoplanet candidates from NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS mission data. AI was employed to process light curve data, with the system applying SMOTE synthetic oversampling to address class imbalance and using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for model interpretability, ensuring transparent and scientifically valid predictions. The AI models were trained and optimized using Scikit-learn and XGBoost libraries, with hyperparameter tuning performed via GridSearchCV to maximize accuracy.Our-Solution-Intelligent-Exoplanet-Detection.pptx

Code generation and development workflows were conducted manually by the team without reliance on generative AI tools, and all software components—including the Flask backend, React.js frontend, and data processing pipelines—were original implementations. No AI-generated images, videos, or audio were used in the project deliverables, and all visualizations were created using Plotly.js from model outputs without AI assistance. The use of AI in this project adheres to NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines by focusing on open scientific data and ensuring that AI serves as a tool for accelerating discovery while maintaining transparency, originality, and human oversight in the development process.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch
projectDetails.summary: BloomWatch is an Earth observation based application designed to monitor, analyze, and visualize global flowering patterns (phenology) using satellite and ground data. Its main goal is to understand when, where, and how plants bloom across different regions and seasons, helping scientists, farmers, and environmentalists study the effects of climate change, ecosystem health, and agricultural productivity
projectDetails.details:
Description:
BloomWatch is an AI-powered web tool that visualizes and predicts plant blooming events using NASA’s Earth observation data. Through an interactive map, users can select any country, state, or city to view bloom status, analyze vegetation trends, compare regions, and forecast upcoming bloom seasons.

Impact:
It supports farmers in crop planning, ecologists in biodiversity tracking, and public health experts in predicting pollen impacts bridging science and sustainability.

Tools Used:
Firebase, Google Maps API, TensorFlow.js, NASA POWER, MODIS, Landsat, and VIIRS datasets.

Innovation:
Combines real-time satellite insights with AI predictions to make global vegetation intelligence accessible and actionable for agriculture, ecology, and conservation.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Primary areas where AI is utilized:

  1. Botanical Analysis and Species Suggestion:
    • Where it happens: This is the core AI feature on the Map, Dashboard, and Analysis pages.
    • How it works: When you request an analysis for a region, the application sends historical climate and vegetation data (as a proxy) to the AI model. The AI is prompted to analyze this data and, based on the specific geography and climate patterns, suggest suitable flower species, explain their ecological significance, and describe their potential human impact.
    • Compliance: This falls under "Code and data". The application acknowledges AI generation directly in the user interface. For example, the analysis results are presented in cards clearly labeled "AI Botanical Analysis" or "AI Prediction," making it obvious to the user that the content is machine-generated.
    • Where it happens: On the Climate page.
    • How it works: After viewing the climate and vegetation charts, you can click "Generate Short Reply." This action sends the chart data to the AI, which is instructed to produce a simple, narrative summary of the key trends in the data.
    • Compliance: This also falls under "Code and data". The UI presents the output under a clear heading like "Analysis Summary," and the action is initiated by a button with a "Wand" icon and text like "Generate," indicating an intelligent process is taking place.
