projectDetails.name: Build a Space Biology Knowledge Engine
projectDetails.summary: We created the NASA AI Bioscience Explorer, a dynamic knowledge engine, to speed up future human space exploration. NASA has produced enormous volumes of space biology data over the years, but this data is scattered and challenging for researchers to efficiently query. By developing an intelligent dashboard that makes use of knowledge graphs and artificial intelligence, our project tackles this difficulty. A vast collection of NASA bioscience publications are ingested, processed, and summarized by this tool, which then arranges the results in an easy-to-use, explorable interface. The effects and outcomes of decades of life science research carried out in space are now readily navigable by users. This is important because it turns a disorganized archive into intelligence that can be used. Our platform enables scientists and mission planners to make better decisions by providing access to this abundance of information, protecting astronauts' health and safety as we get ready for trips to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
projectDetails.details:
To accelerate future human space exploration, we developed the NASA AI Bioscience Explorer, a dynamic knowledge engine designed to centralize and interpret decades of complex research. NASA has generated vast amounts of space biology data, but this information is dispersed and difficult for researchers to effectively query. Our project addresses this challenge with a Next.js 14 web application that leverages Google's Gemini AI to create an intelligent exploration platform.

Built with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion, the application ingests NASA bioscience publications and uses its AI core to analyze research abstracts. It automatically generates concise summaries, assesses the impact on human spaceflight, and extracts key findings. Users interact with this processed data through an intuitive, responsive dashboard and an interactive knowledge graph, all presented within a futuristic, deep-space NASA-style interface. This creative fusion of advanced AI with an immersive user experience makes complex data not just accessible, but engaging.

The primary benefit is the transformation of a scattered archive into actionable intelligence. By making this wealth of information easily navigable, our platform empowers scientists and mission planners to make more informed decisions, directly impacting the health and safety of astronauts as we prepare for missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
As the main tool for data analysis and content creation, artificial intelligence is a fundamental part of the NASA AI Bioscience Explorer. Our usage of AI is open and essential to the operation of the project.

We specifically made use of Google's Gemini AI in the methods listed below:

AI for Summarization and Data Analysis: The Gemini AI model receives text abstracts from NASA bioscience publications via the application's backend. In order to read, comprehend, and digest the intricate scientific content, the AI is instructed to assume the role of a space bioscience specialist.

The AI model does more than simply summarize; it also pulls important information and provides it in a structured JSON format. The mission, the organism under study, the main conclusions, and any possible ramifications for upcoming human space travel are all listed here.

AI for Content Generation: Gemini AI creates all of the summaries, impact analyses, and keyword tags that are shown on the interactive dashboard. The user interface is filled with this AI-generated information, which makes the raw data comprehensible and accessible.

AI-Powered Knowledge Graph: The structured data produced by the AI's examination of the source articles is the source of the connections and insights shown in the knowledge graph.

projectDetails.name: NASA Space Biology Knowledge Engine
projectDetails.summary: Our project is an AI-powered web platform enabling instant, smart access to NASA’s space biology research. We built a dashboard that ingests 600+ NASA bioscience publications and lets users ask natural-language questions to get evidence-based, cited answers in seconds. Using advanced AI—including Google Gemini API, LangChain, Convex vector search, and NASA’s own open datasets—we turn decades of static reporting into search, insight, and actionable knowledge. Our tool helps scientists, mission planners, and students rapidly find experimental evidence, discover research gaps, and accelerate breakthroughs for Moon and Mars exploration. This solution democratizes space biology knowledge, maximizes NASA’s data value, and enables deeper, faster, more collaborative space science
projectDetails.details:
• What does it do?
    • Provides instant question-answering and semantic search over all NASA bioscience publications.
    • Upload CSV/list of publications—our system crawls articles, parses and chunks text, stores in Convex vector DB using Gemini embeddings, supports AI-powered Q&A using LangChain.
    • Saves weeks or months of manual literature review.
    • Identifies knowledge gaps, trends, co-authorships for space mission planners.
    • Allows any user (scientist or student) to ask “How does microgravity affect heart tissue?” and get a high-quality, cited answer.
    • Next.js (frontend), Convex (backend DB), LangChain, Google Gemini API, Cheerio, PapaParse, Vercel hosting.
    • Unified semantic search + Q&A for a niche scientific domain never before indexed this way.
    • Multi-modal ingestion: both HTML articles and PDFs.
    • Bulk 600+ ingestion, automatic metadata, AI-enhanced insights/analytics.
    • Chose this challenge due to its global scientific/educational value and to maximize public impact using true open data.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
• All text-based Q&A, search, and document chunking are powered by Google Gemini API and LangChain (AI code and embeddings).
  • Some answers are generated or summarized with generative LLMs (Gemini).
  • No NASA logos were used in AI-generated visuals or video.
  • If AI-generated images/video were used, a visible watermark “AI generated” was added.
  • All AI contributions and tools are clearly acknowledged here and in our documentation.

projectDetails.details:
Project Overview

NASA Solar System Explorer is an interactive web-based platform that transforms complex NASA space data into an engaging, educational experience. It allows users to explore our solar system through a dynamic 3D visualization with real NASA research data integration.

🔧 What It Does & How It Works

Core Functionality:

  • Interactive 3D Solar System: Real-time rendering of planets orbiting the sun with accurate relative speeds
  • Click-to-Explore Interface: Users can click any celestial body to zoom in and access detailed NASA research data
  • Real NASA Data Integration: Fetches high-resolution images and scientific data directly from NASA APIs
  • Multi-layer Visualization: Toggle between different data views (topography, temperature, geology, satellite)
  • Time Travel Feature: Explore how our understanding of planets evolved from 2010-2025

Technical Workflow:

  1. Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript with Canvas/WebGL for 3D rendering
    • User interacts with 3D model → System fetches relevant NASA data → Displays in contextual panels
    • Real-time physics simulation for orbital mechanics
    • Progressive loading of high-resolution imagery

💡 Benefits & Features

Educational Benefits:

  • Democratizes Space Science: Makes NASA research accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts
  • Interactive Learning: Transforms passive learning into active exploration
  • Multi-sensory Experience: Combines visual, interactive, and informational elements

Specific AI Contributions:

  3. Educational Content: Assisted in compiling accurate planetary information from verified sources

projectDetails.name: AstraSeek
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, AstraSeek, is an AI-powered platform designed to classify potential exoplanets using open NASA datasets from Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. The tool applies machine learning models to evaluate orbital, stellar, and transit features, predicting whether a planet is a confirmed exoplanet, candidate, or false positive.

AstraSeek directly addresses the challenge of managing and interpreting the massive volume of astronomical data collected by space missions. Instead of requiring extensive manual analysis, the system streamlines discovery by offering automated, reliable classifications through an easy-to-use web interface.

This project is important because exoplanet identification is key to advancing our understanding of habitable worlds and the potential for life beyond Earth. By making AI-driven classification accessible to both researchers and enthusiasts, AstraSeek helps accelerate scientific discovery and fosters public engagement in space exploration.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, AstraSeek, is an AI-powered web application that classifies exoplanets into three categories: confirmed, candidate, or false positive. Using open NASA datasets (Kepler, K2, TESS), the system evaluates planetary and stellar parameters such as orbital period, radius, transit duration, and star temperature.

We developed the entire project in JavaScript, building both the machine learning model and the web interface in the same ecosystem. The frontend was created with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, while Firebase was used for authentication and backend support. The AI model is implemented in JavaScript (TensorFlow.js) to run predictions directly in the browser, making it lightweight and accessible.

The benefits include real-time classification of planets without requiring heavy installations or external servers. This makes AstraSeek useful for both researchers and space enthusiasts who want quick, interactive insights.

The intended impact is to simplify exoplanet detection, accelerate discovery, and spark curiosity about habitable worlds beyond Earth. Our team focused on accuracy, usability, and creativity by combining space science with web-based AI, delivering a project that is both technically innovative and publicly engaging.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Our project, AstraSeek, used AI in the following ways:

  • AI-Lite Model Integration: We used an AI-Lite API to power the exoplanet classification model in JavaScript. This enabled us to run predictions on planetary data (orbital period, radius, transit duration, star temperature) and classify planets as confirmed, candidate, or false positives in real time.
  • AI for Documentation Support: We used an AI documentation API to help generate structured project documentation, summaries, and descriptions, which accelerated our writing process while ensuring clarity and completeness.

We did not use AI to modify NASA datasets or branding. All datasets came directly from official NASA archives (Kepler, K2, TESS). Any AI-assisted text generation has been acknowledged, and no AI-generated images, videos, or audio were used.

projectDetails.name: future  Weather Prediction  Portal
projectDetails.summary:
Weather Probability Portal ( Team : NextGenMinds)

The Weather Probability Portal is an AI-powered web application that helps users predict and visualize the probability of weather conditions—such as rainfall, temperature, wind speed, humidity, or snowfall—for any location and date they select.

Using NASA Earth Observation data (from resources like Giovanni, GES DISC OPeNDAP, Worldview, and Earthdata Search), the platform analyzes historical and real-time datasets to provide location-specific weather insights and future climate probabilities.

Users can log in securely, search a location by name, pincode, or map marker, and select a date and time for their planned outdoor event or trip. The dashboard then displays detailed weather probabilities, distances, and AI-based activity recommendations (e.g., “High snowfall probability—try skiing or snowboarding”).

The system also allows users to download results in CSV or JSON format for further analysis. With an intuitive UI, AI-driven insights, and NASA’s reliable data backbone, the Weather Probability Portal goes beyond basic forecasts to empower smarter outdoor planning and decision-making.
projectDetails.details:
Weather Probability Portal

What does it do / How does it work?

The Weather Probability Portal is an AI-powered web application that predicts and visualizes the probability of weather conditions—such as rainfall, temperature, windspeed, humidity, and snowfall—for any selected location and date.
Users can log in securely using their credentials and search a destination by typing its name, entering a pincode, or marking a location on an interactive map. The system uses NASA Earth Observation data (from Giovanni, GES DISC OPeNDAP, Worldview, and Earthdata Search) to fetch climate datasets. AI models analyze this data to calculate weather probabilities for future dates.
The dashboard then visualizes the data through interactive charts, maps, and probability indicators. It also suggests activity recommendations based on the weather (e.g., “Rain likely—carry waterproof gear” or “High snow probability—try skiing”).

What benefits does it have?

  • Helps travelers, event planners, and outdoor enthusiasts make smarter scheduling decisions.
  • Uses NASA’s reliable datasets for high accuracy and credibility.
  • Offers personalized insights based on real-time and historical data.
  • Reduces risks by warning users about extreme weather conditions.
  • Enables data download in CSV or JSON for further analysis and reporting.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to make outdoor activity planning safer and more informed by using satellite-driven climate intelligence. By leveraging NASA’s open data, it raises awareness about climate variability and environmental change, empowering communities and individuals to plan responsibly. It also encourages data transparency and open science by making processed results downloadable and easy to understand.

What tools, coding languages, and technologies were used?

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React.js, TailwindCSS
  • Backend: Node.js, Express.js
  • Database: MongoDB / Firebase for user data and search history
  • AI & Data Processing: Python (Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow/Scikit-learn)
  • APIs & Data Sources: NASA GES DISC OPeNDAP, Giovanni, Worldview, Earthdata Search
  • Map Integration: Leaflet.js / Mapbox API
  • Hosting & Deployment: Vercel / Render / GitHub Pages

How is your project creative?

  • Combines AI prediction models with NASA’s Earth data to deliver probabilistic weather forecasting months in advance—beyond traditional apps.
  • Offers multi-input location selection (pincode, text search, or map pin).
  • Integrates interactive visualization dashboards for easy interpretation of complex data.
  • Suggests weather-based activity recommendations to keep the experience engaging and practical.
  • Allows import/export of data for open collaboration and further analysis.

What factors did your team consider?

  • User experience: Simple and visually appealing UI for non-technical users.
  • Accuracy: Selection of reliable NASA datasets for temperature, precipitation, and wind parameters.
  • Scalability: Modular code structure and cloud-based architecture for future expansion.
  • Accessibility: Works across devices and browsers.
  • Sustainability: Encourages eco-conscious travel planning and outdoor safety awareness.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our project, Weather Probability Portal (NextGenMinds), integrates Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to enhance prediction accuracy, optimize data visualization, and deliver intelligent user recommendations. Below are the specific ways AI was utilized:

  1. AI in Weather Probability Analysis:
    • Used machine learning models (Random Forest, LSTM, and Regression algorithms) in Python to analyze NASA’s historical Earth observation data (temperature, precipitation, humidity, windspeed).
    • The AI models calculate probabilistic forecasts for future dates and determine likelihood percentages for extreme weather events (e.g., “70% chance of heavy rain”).
    • A rule-based and AI-enhanced module suggests activities or precautions based on the predicted weather (e.g., “High snow probability — consider skiing” or “High UV index — wear sunscreen”).
    • Used ChatGPT (OpenAI GPT-5) for idea validation, optimization of code structure, and generation of descriptive text content such as summaries and project documentation.
    • AI-generated documentation and visuals (if any) include visible watermarks and metadata acknowledgments as per NASA’s guidelines.
    • Implemented AI-based data smoothing and trend recognition to automatically highlight anomalies and important weather patterns on the user dashboard.

All AI-generated content, models, or media have been clearly acknowledged and documented. The intent of AI usage in this project is to accelerate innovation, improve prediction accuracy, and enhance user experience, while maintaining full transparency about its application.

projectDetails.name: Project Terra Data Animation
projectDetails.summary:
Our project showcases a dynamic visualization of NASA’s Terra satellite datasets through a synchronized animation that highlights key environmental transformations on Earth — including vegetation growth, temperature variation, and ice cover changes. We developed a Python-based video pipeline using MoviePy and PIL, integrating multiple dataset clips, transitions, and animated motion of the Terra satellite to create a cohesive narrative of Earth observation data.

By visually representing how Terra observes our planet’s climate and surface dynamics, the project bridges the gap between raw satellite data and public understanding.

This project is important because it raises awareness about environmental change and demonstrates how open-source tools and real NASA datasets can be used to communicate science through motion and storytelling.
projectDetails.details:
Our project visualizes real NASA Terra satellite data through a seamless animation that highlights key environmental phenomena such as ice cover, vegetation growth, and temperature variations. The system works by combining multiple image datasets into short clips, synchronizing them with audio, and animating the Terra satellite’s movement across the screen to represent data transitions.

We developed the project using Python, with core libraries including MoviePy for video processing, PIL for image handling, and NumPy for efficient frame manipulation. The animation was designed to run smoothly, automatically adjusting clip durations to match the corresponding audio. The final output delivers a cohesive and informative video that illustrates Earth’s dynamic systems as captured by Terra.

The project’s main benefit lies in making complex satellite data accessible, engaging, and visually intuitive. By transforming static datasets into animated storytelling, we help bridge the gap between scientific research and public understanding.

Creatively, the project balances data accuracy with visual aesthetics, using motion and timing to emphasize environmental changes. Our team carefully considered clarity, synchronization, educational value, and viewer engagement to ensure that the animation both informs and inspires audiences to appreciate Earth observation technology.

projectDetails.name: AstraTwin : Astronaut Health Digital Twin
projectDetails.summary:
Astronaut Health Digital Twin  is a web-based simulation tool that predicts how astronauts’ health changes during long-duration space missions. It focuses on three main risks: muscle loss, bone density loss, and radiation exposure.

Users can input mission parameters such as duration, daily exercise, and shielding levels, and the app generates interactive graphs showing how each health factor evolves over time. This allows astronauts, mission planners, and researchers to explore “what-if” scenarios — for example, how increasing exercise or improving shielding can reduce health risks.
projectDetails.details:
The project is simple, visual, and predictive, making complex space medicine data easy to understand. It also has potential for future expansion to include mental health, nutrition, wearable sensors, and AI-driven personalized recommendations.

How it works-

Users can input mission parameters such as duration, daily exercise, and shielding levels, and the app generates interactive graphs showing how each health factor evolves over time. This allows astronauts, mission planners, and researchers to explore “what-if” scenarios — for example, how increasing exercise or improving shielding can reduce health risks.

It’s a futuristic, interactive tool that helps plan safer space missions while also offering insights relevant to healthcare on Earth.

projectDetails.name: NASA TEMPO Satellite Air Quality Monitoring
projectDetails.summary:
NASA TEMPO Satellite Air Quality Monitoring

The NASA TEMPO Satellite Air Quality Monitoring project by Team S3 SQUAD focuses on leveraging NASA’s TEMPO satellite data to visualize real-time air quality across North America. The application fetches pollutant data such as Ozone (O₃), Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂), and Particulate Matter (PM₂.₅) through NASA’s API and transforms it into interactive maps, charts, and dashboards.

This system empowers citizens, researchers, and policymakers with accessible, localized, and real-time air quality insights. It includes forecasting trends, health alerts, and supports offline/local data processing for enhanced accessibility and data privacy.

By turning complex satellite datasets into a simple, user-friendly visualization platform, the project promotes environmental awareness, public health monitoring, and data-driven decision-making for cleaner, healthier communities.
projectDetails.details:
🚀 Project Details – NASA TEMPO Satellite Air Quality Monitoring

Our project, NASA TEMPO Satellite Air Quality Monitoring, is designed to process and visualize real-time air pollution data captured by NASA’s TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) satellite. The system retrieves pollutant data such as Ozone (O₃), Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂), and Particulate Matter (PM₂.₅) through the NASA TEMPO API, processes it locally, and displays it via a dynamic web dashboard.

🛰️ How It Works

The application follows a structured data flow:

  1. Data Fetching: Air quality data is fetched from the NASA TEMPO API.
  2. Backend Processing: Using Node.js or Python (Flask), the data is cleaned, parsed, and structured for analysis.
  3. Storage & Caching: The processed data is stored temporarily (e.g., in memory or local cache) for quick retrieval.
  4. Visualization: A frontend interface built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript displays pollutant levels on interactive maps, charts, and heatmaps.
  5. Alerts & Forecasting: The system generates smart alerts when air quality exceeds healthy thresholds and uses predictive algorithms to forecast pollution trends.

💡 Benefits & Intended Impact

The project aims to make complex satellite air quality data accessible and actionable for everyone — from policymakers to ordinary citizens.

  • Health Awareness: Provides real-time alerts about poor air quality to prevent exposure to harmful pollutants.
  • Environmental Insights: Enables local and regional pollution tracking to support research and policy-making.
  • Data Accessibility: Simplifies access to NASA’s high-quality datasets for education, awareness, and innovation.
  • Community Empowerment: Helps communities monitor environmental conditions and take informed action toward sustainability.

🧠 Tools, Languages, and Technologies

  • Backend: Node.js / Python (Flask)
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • Data Source: NASA TEMPO API
  • Visualization: Charts.js, Heatmap.js, custom JavaScript maps
  • Storage: Local cache / Redis (for fast retrieval)
  • Optional Cloud/Offline Support: Local processing ensures usability without internet dependency

🎨 Creativity & Innovation

What makes this project unique is its ability to transform complex satellite data into a simple, intuitive interface that anyone can understand.
We prioritized user experience, designing clear visuals and real-time interactivity that bridges the gap between space-based science and everyday decision-making.
The project also introduces an offline/local mode, ensuring accessibility even in low-connectivity regions — a rare feature among space-data applications.

⚙️ Team Considerations

During development, our team focused on:

  • Accuracy: Validating pollutant data consistency from NASA TEMPO API.
  • Performance: Implementing lightweight data caching for faster updates.
  • User Experience: Designing an intuitive, accessible dashboard for diverse audiences.
  • Scalability: Planning future expansion to global coverage and mobile platforms.
  • Ethics & Privacy: Ensuring no personal data is collected and local processing is supported for user safety.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools were used in a limited capacity to support the development and presentation of our project. Specifically:

  • Documentation & Content Enhancement: We used ChatGPT (OpenAI) to refine the project’s written descriptions, summaries, and technical explanations for clarity and conciseness.
  • No AI-Generated Code, Data, Images, Videos, or Audio were used in the project. All source code, visualizations, and data processing logic were created entirely by our team.
  • The AI assistance was strictly for improving documentation quality and presentation flow — not for generating or altering any core technical or scientific components.

All project functionalities, APIs, and datasets are original, manually implemented, and based on NASA TEMPO satellite data.

projectDetails.name: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
projectDetails.summary:
ExoSight Finder is an AI-powered web application that automates exoplanet detection from stellar light curves collected by NASA's Kepler and TESS missions. Our solution addresses the challenge of manually analyzing thousands of light curves by deploying an ensemble machine learning model (CNN + Random Forest) trained on 5,302+ labeled light curve datasets.

Users upload light curve data (CSV/FITS format), and our system automatically preprocesses the data (normalization, outlier removal, gap interpolation) and runs ML inference to classify exoplanet candidates with confidence scores. The application features interactive visualizations including transit markers, phase-folded curves, and a real-time 3D orbital viewer built with Three.js that displays the exoplanet system with habitable zone overlays.

Key innovations include a discoveries gallery with advanced filtering, a model performance dashboard showing 94.8% accuracy metrics, and export capabilities for further research. ExoSight Finder democratizes exoplanet discovery by making professional-grade detection tools accessible through an intuitive web interface, enabling both researchers and citizen scientists to contribute to NASA's exoplanet catalog expansion.
projectDetails.details:
ExoSight Finder is a full-stack web application that automates exoplanet detection from stellar light curves using machine learning, making professional-grade astronomical analysis accessible through an intuitive interface.

HOW IT WORKS:

The system accepts light curve data files (CSV/FITS format) from NASA's Kepler and TESS missions. Upon upload, our preprocessing pipeline normalizes flux values, removes statistical outliers beyond 2-sigma thresholds, interpolates missing data points, and applies SMOTE for class balancing. The processed data is analyzed by an ensemble ML model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for temporal pattern recognition and Random Forest classifiers for feature-based detection. The model outputs classification results (CANDIDATE vs FALSE_POSITIVE), confidence scores, and key planetary parameters including orbital period, transit depth, and estimated planet radius.

BENEFITS & IMPACT:

- Accelerates Discovery: Automates analysis that traditionally takes hours per light curve, enabling rapid screening of thousands of stellar observations

- Democratizes Research: Makes advanced detection tools accessible to citizen scientists, educators, and researchers without specialized astronomical software

- Educational Value: Interactive visualizations help users understand the transit method and exoplanet characteristics

- Scalable Analysis: Can process batch datasets for large-scale surveys

- Open Source: Full codebase available for community contribution and research validation

TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION:

Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite for fast development and optimal performance. Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui component library provides a modern, accessible interface optimized for both desktop and mobile devices. Three.js with React Three Fiber powers the 3D orbital visualization, rendering planetary systems with realistic orbital mechanics, habitable zone overlays, and size comparisons against Earth and Jupiter.

Backend API: Python-based RESTful API (FastAPI framework recommended) handles file uploads, executes preprocessing pipelines using NumPy and Pandas, and runs ML inference with TensorFlow/PyTorch models. The ensemble approach combines CNN architectures (encoding-decoding pathways) with gradient boosting algorithms for 94.8% accuracy on validation datasets.

Data Processing: Leverages the Lightkurve Python library for standardized light curve manipulation, following NASA Kepler/TESS data format specifications. Preprocessing implements normalization via PDCSAP flux corrections, linear interpolation for gap-filling, and statistical outlier rejection.

Machine Learning: Models trained on 5,302+ labeled Kepler Objects of Interest (KOI) and TESS candidate datasets from NASA's Exoplanet Archive. Training methodology includes transfer learning from Kepler to TESS data, data augmentation through synthetic transit injection, and cross-validation across multiple stellar types.

Visualization: Recharts/Plotly.js for interactive time-series plots with zoom/pan capabilities. Custom WebGL shaders for smooth 3D rendering. Responsive design ensures functionality across device sizes from smartphones to large displays.

CREATIVE ASPECTS:

- Real-time 3D orbital mechanics simulation with physics-accurate animations

- Gamification elements including discovery badges and achievement tracking

- Progressive disclosure UI design that guides users from simple upload to advanced analysis

- Dark space-themed aesthetic with cyan/purple accent colors evoking astronomical imaging

- Export functionality generates publication-ready reports with annotated light curves

TEAM CONSIDERATIONS:

- Accessibility: WCAG AA compliance, keyboard navigation, screen reader support

- Performance: Lazy loading for heavy 3D components, code splitting by route, optimized bundle sizes

- Scalability: Stateless API design for horizontal scaling, caching strategies for repeated analyses

- User Experience: Loading skeletons during processing, clear error messages, contextual help tooltips

- Data Privacy: Client-side validation, no storage of uploaded data without consent

- Open Science: MIT license, comprehensive documentation, reproducible analysis pipelines

VALIDATION:

Results compared against NASA's confirmed exoplanet catalog show 92.1% precision and 89.7% recall on test sets. The system successfully identifies known transiting exoplanets and flags previously unconfirmed candidates for further investigation.

FUTURE ROADMAP:

Integration with NASA Exoplanet Watch API for community collaboration, transit timing variation analysis for multi-planet system detection, automated habitability scoring using
projectDetails.aiReferences:
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE USAGE DISCLOSURE:

We utilized AI tools at multiple stages of development to accelerate implementation while maintaining full creative control and scientific accuracy. All AI-generated content was reviewed, validated, and modified by our team.

1. FRONTEND DEVELOPMENT:

- Tool: Lovable.dev (AI-powered web application builder)

- Usage: Generated initial React component structures, Tailwind CSS layouts, and responsive design patterns from natural language prompts describing desired UI/UX features

- Modification: All generated components were manually reviewed and customized for exoplanet-specific features, accessibility improvements, and performance optimization

* Code completion suggestions for boilerplate TypeScript/React patterns

* Writing unit test templates for preprocessing pipelines

- Modification: All generated code was tested, refactored, and documented by team members

- Percentage: Approximately 30% of utility code had AI-assisted generation; all ML model architecture and training code was human-designed

3. DOCUMENTATION:

* Generating initial README structure and installation instructions

* Creating API endpoint documentation templates

* Drafting user guide content explaining the transit method

- Modification: All documentation reviewed for technical accuracy and customized with project-specific details

4. DESIGN ASSETS:

- Tools: None (no AI-generated images or videos used)

- All icons, favicons, and visual assets sourced from open-source libraries (Lucide React icons) or created manually

- No NASA logos or branding modified or generated via AI

5. AUDIO/VIDEO:

- No AI-generated audio used

- Demo video/presentation created manually through screen recording/slide design

- No AI voice-over or synthetic media

6. DATA & MACHINE LEARNING:

- Training Data: 100% sourced from NASA public datasets (Kepler, TESS missions)

- Model Architecture: Human-designed CNN and Random Forest ensemble

- No synthetic training data generated via AI; only real astronomical observations used

- Preprocessing algorithms based on peer-reviewed astronomical research methodologies

7. PROJECT PLANNING & IDEATION:

- Tools: ChatGPT-4, Claude AI

- Usage: Brainstorming feature priorities, exploring technical architecture options, researching ML approaches for time-series classification

- All final decisions and implementations made by team members

TRANSPARENCY COMMITMENT:

- All AI-assisted code includes comments indicating origin (e.g., "// Generated with GitHub Copilot, modified for exoplanet detection")

- README.md contains dedicated section acknowledging AI tool usage

- Source code repository history preserves human modifications to AI-generated content

- No proprietary NASA data or restricted materials were processed by AI tools

ORIGINAL CONTRIBUTIONS:

- Complete ML model training and validation pipeline

- Domain-specific astronomical data preprocessing algorithms

- 3D orbital mechanics visualization and physics simulation

- Scientific interpretation of results and parameter extraction

- User experience design tailored to astronomical research workflows

- Integration of NASA data sources and API design

This project exemplifies responsible AI usage: leveraging tools to accelerate development velocity while ensuring all domain expertise, scientific accuracy, and creative vision remained human-driven.

projectDetails.name: Team Name- Starcoders :-    Challenge:- Bloomwatch- An Earth Observation Application for  Global Flowering Phenology
projectDetails.summary:
Bloom Watch is a web-based platform that visualizes, monitors, and predicts global plant blooming events using NASA Earth observation data. The project harnesses datasets from MODIS (NDVI/EVI) and NASA POWER to detect vegetation changes and identify bloom phases over time. By combining these datasets with simple AI-driven analysis, the tool generates an interactive “Bloom Map” that displays current and predicted blooming intensity across the globe.

This project supports NASA’s mission to understand Earth’s dynamic systems by providing insights into plant phenology, which is critical for agriculture, biodiversity, and climate studies. Bloom Watch empowers farmers to optimize crop cycles, assists researchers in studying environmental patterns, and helps communities monitor ecological health. It translates complex satellite data into accessible visual insights, encouraging sustainable decision-making for a greener planet. 🌍🌸
projectDetails.details: What does it do? Bloom Watch uses NASA satellite data to track and visualize vegetation bloom events worldwide. It processes NDVI and weather data to determine when and where plants are entering bloom stages. How does it work? NASA APIs provide real-time vegetation and climate data → backend processes patterns → AI model predicts bloom → frontend visualizes global map and time trends. Benefits & Impact: Supports sustainable agriculture and climate adaptation. Enables scientists to study plant phenology and environmental shifts. Helps farmers predict planting and harvesting periods. Tools, Languages, and Stack: Frontend: React.js, Leaflet / Mapbox Backend: Node.js / Express Database: Firebase / MongoDB Machine Learning: Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow) APIs: MODIS, NASA POWER, NASA GIBS Creativity: Transforms complex NASA datasets into an intuitive, human-friendly visualization tool that connects space data to local ecosystems and communities. Key Factors Considered: Data accessibility, visualization clarity, prediction accuracy, and usability for both researchers and farmers.

Users can enter their city, and the app provides a clear climate risk assessment categorized as Low, Moderate, or High, helping farmers anticipate extreme weather events. The app features a user-friendly interface with a sidebar navigation menu, offering quick access to sections like Home, Climate Risk, Crop Advice, Alerts, and Settings. TerraGuard aims to empower farmers with actionable insights, reduce crop loss due to unexpected weather, and enhance sustainable farming practices. By integrating global climate data and presenting it in a localized, easy-to-understand manner, TerraGuard bridges the gap between advanced meteorological information and everyday agricultural decision-making. The project demonstrates practical use of APIs, JSON parsing, Android UI design, and asynchronous network operations, making it both an educational and socially impactful solution.
projectDetails.details:

The project demonstrates creativity by integrating global NASA climate data into a local, actionable format for farmers, addressing agricultural challenges and promoting sustainable practices. projectDetails.details: A code was designed to download files from Internet and save them to a specific file. Another program was used to extract keywords from these downloaded files, and to summarize these files too. The summarized data and the keywords were saved in a JSON file. Using such a platform is easier, not only for the users, but also for the coders, as it is as easy as downloading the pdf just to add more data. This project would impact scientists, As it would save a lot of their time instead of going through the Internet to search for individual sites. We used javascript library balloon graph to make the knowledge graph. We used html, json and php in our website. One of the major factors considered while making the program was ease of usage for every user.

projectDetails.name: ISS Legacy Explorer — Celebrating 25 Years of the International Space Station
projectDetails.summary:
ISS Legacy Explorer is an interactive full-stack web application created to commemorate 25 years of the International Space Station (ISS) — a symbol of global unity, scientific innovation, and human exploration. Our project showcases the evolution and impact of the ISS through multiple engaging modules designed to educate and inspire.

The application features a real-time ISS Tracker using live satellite API data, allowing users to view the station’s current position, altitude, and velocity on an interactive map. It also includes an interactive mission timeline, an experiment explorer highlighting major scientific studies conducted in space, an astronaut directory with search and filter capabilities, and an analytics dashboard that visualizes data through dynamic charts. To make learning fun, a quiz module tests users’ knowledge about space and ISS history.

This project addresses the challenge of making complex space data accessible and engaging to the public. By combining technology, education, and creativity, ISS Legacy Explorer demonstrates how space research aboard the ISS continues to shape life on Earth and inspire future generations of explorers.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, ISS Legacy Explorer, is a full-stack interactive web application that celebrates 25 years of the International Space Station (ISS) by combining real-time data, visualization, and education in a single platform.

The system allows users to:

  • Track the ISS live using real-time satellite API data, showing latitude, longitude, velocity, altitude, and current location on a Leaflet.js map.
  • Explore a timeline of the ISS’s major milestones and missions.
  • Discover scientific experiments conducted aboard the ISS, categorized by fields such as biology, physics, earth observation, and technology.
  • Learn about astronauts from various countries using an interactive search and filter system.
  • View data analytics through a dynamic dashboard built with Chart.js, and test knowledge through a quiz module.

We developed this project using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, Chart.js, Leaflet.js, and APIs for live tracking. The backend can integrate with Node.js and Express for data handling and scalability.

The project’s creativity lies in how it transforms complex space data into an engaging educational experience, combining science, design, and interactivity.

Our team focused on user experience, accuracy, and visual appeal, ensuring that the application not only informs but also inspires curiosity about space research. The intended impact is to make space exploration accessible, interactive, and inspiring for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

projectDetails.name: ExoMind AI
projectDetails.summary:
ExoMind: Exoplanet Classification Platform
ExoMind is a secure, full-stack web platform developed to provide astronomers with rapid, AI-driven preliminary disposition for Exoplanet Candidates (KOIs). The core of the system is a Python Flask API hosting an optimized Random Forest Classifier model, which is fed input via an intuitive web interface.

The platform directly addresses the challenge of astronomical data overload and the bottleneck of manual review. By instantly transforming raw orbital and physical parameters into a highly confident prediction (Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive), it acts as a powerful preliminary filter.

ExoMind is critical because it significantly improves efficiency and focus. It enables researchers to prioritize their limited time and valuable telescope resources exclusively on the highest-confidence candidates, thus fundamentally accelerating the rate of exoplanet discovery and confirmation.
projectDetails.details:
ExoMind: Exoplanet Classification Platform (Concise)

ExoMind is a secure, full-stack platform that provides rapid, AI-driven preliminary disposition for Exoplanet Candidates (KOIs).

Functionality & Smart AI Use: The system uses a focused Random Forest Classifier hosted on a Python/Flask API. The core innovation is the smart preprocessing pipeline that accepts only 10 essential parameters from the user and automatically transforms them into the 72 features required by the model (using Scaler and Imputer objects). This is AI used precisely where needed, abstracting complexity for the researcher.

Impact: ExoMind acts as an immediate, automated filter. By instantly providing a prediction and confidence score, it allows human astronomers to prioritize limited telescope time and resources on the most promising candidates, thereby accelerating the rate of exoplanet discovery.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

We approached AI with a philosophy of precision and necessity:

  1. Core Classification: Custom-trained Random Forest Classifier used for the single, complex task of identifying non-linear patterns in astronomical data.
  2. Model Reliability: Scaler and Imputer objects integrated into the API ensure data consistency and model reliability by correctly transforming raw user inputs into the model's required feature format.
  3. Generative AI: No external generative AI tools (LLMs, image generators, etc.) were used to create any visual assets, audio, or core application code.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our utilization of Artificial Intelligence includes:

  1. Core Classification Model: We developed a custom-trained Random Forest Classifier (a supervised machine learning model) using the Scikit-learn library. This model is responsible for the single, complex task of identifying non-linear patterns across 72 calculated features to assign a preliminary disposition (CONFIRMED, CANDIDATE, or FALSE POSITIVE) to an exoplanet.
  2. Model Reliability Pipeline: We integrated pre-fitted Scaler and Imputer objects directly into our Flask API. This intelligent preprocessing pipeline automatically normalizes user-provided data and handles missing values, ensuring the raw input is correctly and consistently transformed into the 72 features the model expects. This guarantees model reliability and efficiency in a live application.
  3. Generative AI: No external generative AI tools (LLMs, image generators, or audio tools) were used to create any visual assets, audio, or core application code. All application logic, frontend design, and API structure were created by the team.

projectDetails.name: Aerometics
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Forecast: Clean Skies, is an innovative web application that predicts and visualizes real-time air quality by integrating NASA’s TEMPO satellite data, ground-based measurements (OpenAQ, Pandora), and weather information (OpenWeatherMap). The platform provides users with accurate, location-based AQI forecasts, empowering individuals, schools, and policymakers to make informed health and environmental decisions.

Through an intuitive dashboard featuring interactive maps, pollutant overlays, and dynamic charts, users can monitor current air conditions, view short-term forecasts, and receive alerts when pollution levels exceed safety thresholds. The backend processes satellite and ground data, validates it, and stores it in a PostgreSQL + PostGIS database for efficient geospatial queries.

By combining multiple data sources, our system bridges the gap between space-based monitoring and local ground realities. The result is a scientifically reliable, user-friendly, and scalable platform that transforms complex Earth observation data into actionable insights — helping communities plan daily activities, reduce exposure risks, and contribute to cleaner, safer skies.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

Our project, Forecast: Clean Skies, is a web-based air quality forecasting platform that integrates NASA’s TEMPO satellite data, ground-based sensors (OpenAQ, Pandora), and weather datasets (OpenWeatherMap) to deliver accurate, real-time, and predictive insights into air pollution levels. The system continuously fetches and processes data from these sources, validates it, and displays interactive visualizations such as AQI maps, pollutant trends, and short-term forecasts on a user-friendly dashboard.

How it works:
The backend collects satellite and ground measurements, processes them through a data pipeline, and stores them in a PostgreSQL + PostGIS database for geospatial analysis. The frontend, built using React.js, renders this data on interactive maps and graphs. Users can view local forecasts, explore historical data, and receive alerts when pollution exceeds health limits.

Benefits & Impact:
The platform promotes public health awareness and environmental decision-making by providing timely, location-based air quality predictions. It helps individuals plan outdoor activities safely and assists policymakers in monitoring pollution patterns.

Tools & Technologies:

  • Frontend: React.js, Leaflet.js, Chart.js
  • Backend: Node.js (Express)
  • Database: PostgreSQL + PostGIS
  • APIs: NASA TEMPO, OpenAQ, OpenWeatherMap

Creativity & Considerations:
Our team focused on creating a scientifically grounded, visually engaging, and accessible tool that bridges the gap between complex NASA Earth data and public usability. We prioritized accuracy, scalability, and real-time responsiveness while ensuring the design remains intuitive and inclusive for all users.

projectDetails.name: Atmos - AI-Powered Weather Forecasting
projectDetails.summary: Atmos is an AI-powered weather forecasting platform designed to help users plan outdoor events with confidence. The application addresses the challenge of predicting adverse weather conditions by providing personalized weather risk assessments for specific locations and times. Users can access features like Quick Check for instant risk evaluation, Time Optimizer to find optimal weather windows, Live Nowcast for real-time satellite/radar data with 90-minute predictions, Route Risk Mapper for analyzing weather along event routes, and Event Scheduler with automated weather alerts. The platform uses NASA Earth observation data combined with machine learning to deliver accurate, location-specific forecasts, helping users avoid 'very hot,' 'very cold,' 'very windy,' 'very wet,' or 'very uncomfortable' conditions for their outdoor activities.
projectDetails.details:
WHAT IT DOES:

Atmos is a comprehensive weather intelligence platform with five integrated features:

1. Quick Check - Provides instant weather risk assessment for any location and date, displaying detailed metrics including temperature, precipitation, wind speed, and overall risk level with color-coded indicators.

2. Time Optimizer - Uses advanced algorithms to analyze multiple time windows and recommend the optimal slots with lowest weather risks based on user-defined tolerance levels for rain, wind, and temperature.

3. Live Nowcast - Displays real-time weather conditions with interactive map layers showing precipitation, clouds, temperature, and wind patterns. Features 90-minute forecast timeline with frame-by-frame predictions.

4. Route Risk Mapper - Allows users to draw custom routes on a map and analyzes weather risks along each segment, color-coding them by risk level (low/medium/high).

5. Event Scheduler - Enables users to save events and receive automated weather alerts 2 hours before if conditions become risky.

BENEFITS & IMPACT:

- Helps event planners, outdoor enthusiasts, and travelers make informed decisions

- Reduces weather-related cancellations and safety risks

- Provides personalized risk assessments based on individual tolerance levels

- Combines multiple data sources for comprehensive weather intelligence

- User-friendly interface accessible on web and mobile

TECHNOLOGIES USED:

- Frontend: React.js, Next.js for responsive web application

- Mapping: Leaflet.js for interactive maps with real-time weather overlays

- Data Sources: NASA Earth observation data, OpenWeatherMap API, CartoDB for base maps

- Backend: Node.js for API integration and data processing

- Deployment: Vercel for hosting and continuous deployment

- Authentication: User authentication system for personalized preferences

CREATIVE ASPECTS:

- Innovative risk tolerance customization allowing users to set their own thresholds

- Interactive route drawing tool for path-specific weather analysis

- Real-time nowcasting with frame-by-frame animation

- Integrated alert system with advance notifications

- Clean, intuitive UI design with clear visual risk indicators

KEY FACTORS CONSIDERED:

- User experience and accessibility for non-technical users

- Real-time data accuracy and reliability

- Mobile responsiveness for on-the-go access

- Data privacy and user preferences management

- Scalability to handle multiple users and locations globally
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI and machine learning technologies were utilized in the following aspects of the Atmos project:

1. Weather Risk Prediction Algorithm: Machine learning models were used to analyze historical weather patterns and predict risk levels for future dates and locations. The AI processes multiple weather parameters (temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity) to generate composite risk scores.

2. Time Optimization Engine: AI algorithms analyze multiple time windows across a specified date range to recommend optimal slots with the lowest weather risks. The system learns from historical weather data patterns to make accurate predictions.

3. Nowcast Predictions: Machine learning models process real-time satellite and radar data to generate 90-minute short-term forecasts with frame-by-frame predictions.

4. Route Risk Analysis: AI algorithms analyze weather conditions along custom-drawn routes, segmenting the path and calculating risk levels for each segment based on predicted weather conditions.

5. Code Assistance: AI coding assistants were used to help debug code, suggest optimizations, and generate boilerplate code for certain features. All AI-generated code was reviewed, tested, and modified by team members.

6. UI/UX Design Assistance: AI tools provided suggestions for color schemes, layout improvements, and accessibility enhancements.

All core logic, architecture decisions, and creative implementations were designed and executed by the team members. AI was used as a tool to accelerate development, not replace human creativity and decision-making.

projectDetails.details:
Terra Satellite: 25 Years of Earth Science — User Manual 🌍🛰️

This guide will help you navigate and interact with the Terra Satellite Earth Science Data website. The site is designed to showcase 25 years of data collected by the NASA Terra satellite and its five onboard instruments.

1. Overview

The website is divided into four main sections, accessible via the top navigation bar:

Home: A dynamic introduction featuring a rotatable 3D Earth model and an overview of the mission.

Data: Interactive charts demonstrating long-term trends in global climate data (Temperature, CO

2

​

Levels, Ice Coverage, and Vegetation).

Query: A custom form that simulates querying satellite data for a specific date and location.

Impact: Story-driven content explaining how the Terra satellite's data affects real-world issues like climate change, air quality, and biodiversity.

2. Home Section

The Home section features the main title, mission summary, and a dynamic 3D Earth visualization.

2.1. Interacting with the 3D Earth Model

The stylized globe displays simulated Earth data (like atmospheric and heat overlays).

Rotation: Click and drag (or touch and drag on mobile) the globe to rotate it horizontally and vertically.

Zoom: Use your mouse scroll wheel (or pinch-to-zoom on mobile devices) to zoom in and out of the Earth.

Information Overlay: The "heat-overlay" animation pulsing on the globe visually represents data like rising temperatures or atmospheric CO

2

​

.

2.2. Sticky Instrument Navigation

As you scroll down the page, a sticky navigation bar appears at the top. This bar highlights the five major instruments on the Terra satellite.

Instrument Icon Primary Role (Simulation)

ASTER <i class="fas fa-mountain"></i> High-resolution land surface temperature, emissivity, and elevation.

CERES <i class="fas fa-cloud-sun"></i> Measures Earth's radiation budget (solar energy reflected/emitted).

MISR <i class="fas fa-camera"></i> Multi-angle imaging to study aerosols, clouds, and surface properties.

MODIS <i class="fas fa-globe-americas"></i> Large-scale, moderate-resolution data on the land, atmosphere, and oceans.

MOPITT <i class="fas fa-smog"></i> Monitors atmospheric pollution, specifically carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations.

Export to Sheets

Selecting an Instrument: Click on any instrument card. While this action is primarily for demonstration, in a fully functional application, it would filter or load data specific to that instrument.

3. Data Visualization Section

This section displays historical trends derived from Terra and related NASA mission data.

3.1. Viewing Data Charts

Use the four buttons to switch between different long-term visualizations:

Temperature: Shows global temperature anomaly over time.

CO

2

​

Levels: Shows the rise in atmospheric CO

2

​

(parts per million).

Ice Coverage: Shows the trend in Arctic sea ice extent (million square kilometers).

Vegetation: Shows changes in the Global Vegetation Index (NDVI), indicating planetary "greenness."

Chart Interaction: Hover over the line on any chart to see the specific data value and year.

Timeline: The animated progress bar at the bottom visually represents the timeline of data acquisition from the Terra launch year (1999) up to the present (2024).

4. Custom Data Query Section

Use this tool to simulate requesting specific, localized satellite data for any date from December 18, 1999, to the current date.

4.1. Submitting a Query

Date: Select a date between 1999-12-18 and today.

Location: Enter a geographical location (e.g., "New York, USA").

Latitude/Longitude: Enter the coordinates for the center of your search area.

Latitude: -90 to 90

Longitude: -180 to 180

Dataset: Select one of the available environmental variables (e.g., Temperature, Aerosol Optical Depth, Cloud Properties).

Area Size (km): Enter a radius for the data search (1-100 km).

4.2. Viewing Results

Click the "Query Data" button.

The page will display a Query Results box with simulated data for the selected location, date, and dataset.

Value: The simulated or mock measurement (e.g., temperature in °C, NDVI value).

Unit: The corresponding unit of measurement (e.g., °C, NDVI, g/kg).

Quality: The simulated data quality rating ("Good" in this demo).

Note: Due to API access limitations, the data returned is a highly simplified, often mocked, result to demonstrate functionality, not real-time satellite data.

5. Impact Stories Section

This section provides narrative examples of how Terra's data contributes to scientific understanding and real-world policy.

5.1. Exploring the Impact

Three key impact areas are detailed:

Climate Change & Extreme Weather

Air Quality & Public Health

Ecosystems & Biodiversity

"Learn More" Button: Click the "Learn More" button under any story to open a pop-up window (Modal) with a more detailed explanation of Terra's role in that area.

Closing the Modal: Click the '×' icon in the top right corner or click anywhere outside the pop-up window to close it.

projectDetails.name: AstroGuard
projectDetails.summary:
AstroGuard is our solution for the "Meteor Madness" challenge, a unified planetary defense hub designed to make Near-Earth Object (NEO) data accessible to everyone. We developed a live web platform that uses NASA’s NeoWs API to provide real-time tracking of asteroids, a personal watchlist for monitoring specific threats, and an engaging "Astro Quiz" for education.

Our project directly addresses the challenge by tackling the disconnection between NASA's trajectory data and USGS's terrestrial data. Our future vision is an Impact Simulation module that will fuse these datasets to visualize the real-world consequences of an impact.

This is important because AstroGuard bridges the critical gap between complex scientific data and public understanding. It democratizes knowledge about planetary defense, raises global awareness of potential NEO threats, and provides a powerful educational tool to inspire the next generation of scientists and astronomers.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?


AstroGuard is a unified web platform designed to be a "Planetary Defense Hub." Its primary function is to make the complex science of Near-Earth Object (NEO) tracking and impact risk assessment accessible, understandable, and engaging for everyone.

How it Works:

The platform operates on a simple yet powerful architecture:

  1. User Interaction: A user interacts with the platform's front end, for example, by searching for a specific asteroid or using our smart filters to find potentially hazardous objects.
  2. Validation & Processing: Our backend validates the user's input. Valid requests are passed to the application layer, which contains the core logic of our system.
  3. Data Aggregation: The application layer communicates with external services, primarily the NASA NeoWs (Near Earth Object Web Service) API, to fetch real-time data on asteroid trajectories, sizes, and velocities.
  4. Visualization: This processed data is then presented to the user on an intuitive dashboard, featuring interactive lists, visualizations of orbital paths, and key statistics.
  5. Personalization: Using Firebase Authentication and a Firestore database, users can create secure accounts to save specific asteroids to a personal "Watchlist" for continuous monitoring.

In its future phase, the platform will fuse this NASA data with geological and demographic data from the USGS to simulate and visualize the real-world consequences of an impact.

What benefits does it have?

AstroGuard offers several key benefits:

  • Democratizes Data: It breaks down the barrier between complex scientific data and the general public, turning abstract numbers into clear, visual information.
  • Bridges Siloed Information: It provides a single point of access for information that is currently disconnected (e.g., NASA's orbital data and USGS's terrestrial data), creating a more holistic view of potential threats.
  • Promotes Education & Awareness: Through features like the "Astro Quiz Challenge," it makes learning about astronomy and planetary science engaging and fun, increasing public awareness of NEOs.
  • Provides a Decision-Support Framework: While user-friendly, the platform is built on accurate scientific data, providing a powerful tool for students, researchers, and even policymakers to visualize scenarios and support informed discussions about planetary defense.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our intended impact is to shift the public perception of asteroid threats from the realm of science fiction to a matter of scientific preparedness. We aim to:

  1. Raise Global Awareness: Create a more informed global citizenry that understands the nature of NEOs and the importance of planetary defense initiatives.
  2. Empower Through Education: Serve as an engaging STEM tool for students and enthusiasts, fostering a deeper interest in space science and data analysis.
  3. Foster Proactive Dialogue: By clearly visualizing potential impact scenarios, we hope to encourage proactive conversations among the public and policymakers about mitigation strategies and funding for detection programs.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

AstroGuard was developed using a modern, scalable tech stack.

  • Frontend: React, HTML5, CSS3
  • Backend: Typescript and Firebase for serverless functions and authentication.
  • Database: Firebase Realtime Database and Firestore for flexible and real-time data storage.
  • APIs: NASA NeoWs (Near Earth Object Web Service) API for all asteroid data.
  • Software & Version Control: VS Code as our primary IDE and Git/GitHub for collaborative development and version control.
  • Hardware: The project was developed on standard consumer laptops and requires no specialized hardware to run or access, as it is a web-based platform.

How is your project creative?

The creativity of AstroGuard lies in its synthesis and presentation of information:

  1. Innovative Data Fusion: Our core creative concept is the fusion of two distinct types of data: extraterrestrial (asteroid trajectories from NASA) and terrestrial (geographical and population data from USGS). This combination to create public-facing impact visualizations has not been done before in an accessible tool.
  2. Gamification of Complex Science: We creatively tackled the challenge of public education by integrating a gamified "Astro Quiz Challenge." This transforms passive data consumption into an active and enjoyable learning experience.
  3. User-Centric Design: Rather than building another expert-only tool, we creatively focused on the user experience for the non-expert, ensuring the design is intuitive and the information is presented with clarity, bridging the gap between scientists and the public.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several critical factors during development:

  • Data Reliability: We exclusively used official, well-documented data sources like the NASA API to ensure the information presented is accurate and trustworthy.
  • User Accessibility: A primary consideration was making the platform accessible to a broad audience, regardless of their scientific background. This influenced every UI/UX decision.
  • Scalability and Future-Proofing: We chose a technical architecture (React, Firebase, Python) that is highly scalable, allowing for the seamless integration of future modules like the Impact Simulator, machine learning-based threat prediction, and even AR/VR visualizations.
  • Feasibility for a Hackathon: We prioritized the development of a functional and polished Minimum Viable Product (MVP) to demonstrate the core concept effectively within the timeframe, while laying out a clear and ambitious roadmap for future development.

projectDetails.summary:
Embark on a journey with Vesta, your personal guide to the cosmos. Vesta brings the universe to your fingertips with an immersive 3D solar system, allowing you to explore planets, track asteroids, and witness the breathtaking dynamics of our galaxy in a stunning virtual reality experience. Engage with interactive quizzes and cosmic challenges to expand your astronomical knowledge and curiosity.

Vesta makes learning fun and engaging with gamified simulations like the "Minecraft Extinction" event, where you can experience the aftermath of a catastrophic asteroid impact. Predict meteor trajectories, explore global impact zones on interactive maps, and receive timely notifications about upcoming celestial events and discoveries.

Powered by generative AI, Vesta can summarize complex astronomical documents, explain space phenomena in simple language, and answer your cosmic questions in real time. Integrated with ArcGIS, users can visualize realistic 3D elevation maps of terrain and impact regions, while mobile AR and VR modes allow you to simulate asteroid strikes directly in your surroundings, blending science with imagination.

Vesta is not just an app; it’s a living, breathing window to the universe—an educational adventure designed to make space exploration thrilling, interactive, and accessible to everyone on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Website link - https://www.vesta.select

What does it do or how does it work?

Vesta is an interactive educational platform that brings the wonders of the cosmos to your fingertips. It provides a comprehensive and engaging experience for learning about our solar system, asteroids, and the potential threats they pose. The application works by combining real-time data from astronomical sources with immersive 3D visualizations, interactive simulations, and gamified learning modules. Users can explore a detailed model of the solar system, track near-earth objects, and even simulate asteroid impacts to understand their potential consequences. The platform also includes an augmented reality (AR) feature that allows users to bring celestial bodies into their own environment, creating a truly immersive learning experience.

What benefits does it have?

The primary benefit of Vesta is that it makes learning about space and planetary defense accessible, engaging, and fun for people of all ages. By transforming complex scientific data into interactive experiences, Vesta helps users grasp difficult concepts more easily. It provides a safe and entertaining environment to learn about the potential dangers of asteroid impacts and the importance of scientific research in this field. The platform's gamified approach encourages continuous learning and exploration, fostering a deeper appreciation for science and technology.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of Vesta is to raise global awareness about the importance of planetary defense and to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronomers. By providing a platform that is both educational and entertaining, we hope to spark curiosity and encourage more people to take an interest in space exploration and scientific research. In the long run, we believe that a more informed public can lead to greater support for scientific initiatives aimed at protecting our planet from potential cosmic threats.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Vesta is a web-based application developed using a modern tech stack:

Frontend: React, Vite 3D Graphics: Three.js  Mapping: Leaflet, ArcGIS  Programming Language: JavaScript*   Hardware: The application is designed to run on standard desktop and mobile browsers. The AR features require a smartphone or tablet with a camera.

How is your project creative?

Vesta's creativity lies in its unique blend of scientific education and interactive entertainment. We have combined real-world astronomical data with cutting-edge web technologies to create an experience that is both informative and captivating. The use of gamification, AR, and VR sets Vesta apart from traditional educational resources. Instead of just reading about space, users can experience it, interact with it, and even play a role in protecting it. This multi-sensory approach to learning is what makes Vesta a truly creative and innovative project.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several key factors during the development of Vesta:

User Engagement: We wanted to create an experience that would keep users coming back. This is why we incorporated gamification, interactive quizzes, and social media sharing features. Scientific Accuracy: While we wanted the application to be fun, we also made sure that the information presented is accurate and up-to-date. We use data from reliable astronomical sources to ensure the credibility of our platform. Accessibility: We designed Vesta to be accessible to a wide audience, regardless of their scientific background. The application is easy to use and the concepts are explained in a clear and concise manner. Scalability: We built the application with scalability in mind, allowing for the future addition of new features, data sources, and learning modules.

projectDetails.name: Project THE ASTRO-QUARQET
projectDetails.summary:
Our project is designed to spark curiosity about space, rockets, and aerospace among the next generation by combining education with interactive gameplay. We developed a set of engaging games where children can learn about rocket launches, space weather, and missions in a fun, hands-on way. Players explore how inputs like fuel, weight, and design affect rocket success, while also discovering concepts such as sustainability and ISRO’s vision for space exploration.

By gamifying complex scientific ideas, we make them approachable and exciting for young learners. This directly addresses the challenge of inspiring future explorers and scientists, as children not only play but also build a foundation in space science and aerospace. Our mission is to nurture early interest in space, encourage strong fundamentals, and connect players to the bigger picture of human exploration and planetary care.

This project is important because the curiosity we ignite today can grow into the innovations and breakthroughs of tomorrow.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do / how does it work?
Our project is an educational game platform designed to introduce children and young learners to space science, rockets, and aerospace. Players interact with simple rocket launch simulators, balance inputs such as weight, fuel, and design, and explore challenges inspired by real missions and space weather data. The project uses NASA’s DONKI API to bring real-time space weather insights into the learning experience.

What benefits does it have?

  • Makes complex STEM and aerospace concepts easy and fun to understand.
  • Encourages curiosity and early learning about space missions.
  • Provides hands-on interaction with concepts like sustainability, rocket dynamics, and space weather.

Intended impact
We aim to inspire the next generation to take an interest in space exploration, build strong foundations in aerospace and science, and connect them with real-world missions. The project encourages children to see themselves as future scientists, astronauts, and innovators.

Tools, coding languages, and software

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React for UI interactivity).
  • Backend/APIs: NASA DONKI API (for space weather), Python (for logic & integration).
  • Design: Canva, Figma (for game visuals and presentation).

Creativity
Our project merges education with play. By gamifying real scientific principles and space data, we create an engaging experience that both teaches and entertains. Unlike traditional educational resources, our approach is interactive, visually appealing, and connected to real NASA datasets.

Factors considered

  • Accessibility for children (simple language, fun visuals, intuitive design).
  • Scientific accuracy, while keeping the experience playful.
  • Sustainability and awareness of Earth’s environment alongside space exploration.
  • Aligning with ISRO and NASA’s vision to inspire future space explorers.

Our project TerraVision is an AI-powered interactive 3D visualization portal built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. It displays real-time weather, CO pollution, and environmental data across 36 districts of Maharashtra, India.

The system uses Globe.gl, Web Speech API, and JavaScript to provide a NASA-style experience, featuring a Jarvis-like AI voice that narrates live environmental insights.

TerraVision demonstrates how AI narration and visualization can transform raw NASA climate data into interactive awareness tools for sustainable development.
