projectDetails.name: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
projectDetails.summary: The Exoplanet Classifier Project is a machine learning application designed to identify and classify exoplanets based on observational data. It uses LightGBM, a gradient boosting algorithm, to predict whether a celestial object is a confirmed exoplanet, candidate, or false positive. The project features a dual execution system: an interactive Streamlit web interface for visualization and user interaction, and a command-line interface (CLI) fallback for environments without Streamlit support. It includes a synthetic demo dataset generator for testing and experimentation without external data. The model training pipeline involves data preprocessing, feature scaling, label encoding, and evaluation using metrics like accuracy, confusion matrix, and classification report. Optional SHAP explainability visualizations help interpret model predictions and feature importance. The application saves results including model artifacts, prediction outputs, and performance metrics. This robust design ensures portability, allowing the tool to run seamlessly across systems. Overall, the project demonstrates practical use of machine learning in astronomy, focusing on accessibility, reliability, and interpretability for both researchers and students interested in exoplanet detection.
projectDetails.details:
The Exoplanet Classifier Project is an intelligent system that classifies celestial objects into three categories — Confirmed Exoplanet, Candidate, or False Positive — based on astronomical data. It works by using a LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine) model trained on features such as orbital period, transit duration, planet radius, and signal-to-noise ratio. The data undergo preprocessing, scaling, and encoding before model training. Once trained, the system predicts classifications and provides detailed performance metrics such as accuracy, confusion matrix, and classification reports.

The project offers multiple benefits: it automates complex exoplanet classification tasks, reduces manual analysis time, and provides reliable predictions with visual explanations through SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) plots. Its intended impact is to support astronomers, researchers, and students in identifying potential exoplanets efficiently and understanding how model decisions are made.

The system was developed using Python, leveraging libraries like LightGBM, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, and optionally Streamlit for an interactive web interface.

Creativity lies in its dual-mode design—it runs as an interactive Streamlit app or as a CLI tool when Streamlit isn’t installed, ensuring accessibility in all environments. The team prioritized portability, interpretability, accuracy, and user experience throughout the project’s design and testing.

projectDetails.name: Project RedCycle
projectDetails.summary: RedCycle is a web-based prototype that simulates a reuse-first waste management system for a Mars habitat at Jezero Crater. It models material inventories, a persistent waste pool that is consumed before fresh inputs, modular processing workstations with Quick/Full modes, and secondary recovery passes to maximize yield. A canvas map visualizes waste locations and weighted centroids to prioritize collection. Scenario-driven workflows (Residence Renovations, Cosmic Celebrations, Daring Discoveries) demonstrate practical reuse of aluminum, composites, textiles, packaging, and experimental residues. The app tracks recovered vs. wasted mass and exposes energy/water tradeoffs (Eco/Ultra Eco modes). By emphasizing in‑situ reuse and minimized inputs, RedCycle helps reduce resupply needs and improve mission resilience and sustainability.
projectDetails.details:
Project summary — what we developed

A small, interactive web prototype that models a reuse-first, multi-module recycling system for a Mars habitat at Jezero Crater. It includes inventory, a waste pool, processing modules with tunable modes, mass-balance tracking, and a map visualizer for collection planning.

How does it address the challenge?

By prioritizing reuse-first behavior, implementing secondary recovery, and making resource tradeoffs explicit, it demonstrates practical strategies to maximize recovery, minimize fresh inputs, and limit unusable outputs. Scenario workflows show how specific mission activities (habitat unpacking, celebrations, experimental residues) can feed into the system.

Why is it important?

Small design choices (reuse-first, secondary recovery, local aggregation) can significantly reduce resupply needs and increase mission resilience. The prototype lets stakeholders experiment with these choices quickly and see mass-balance outcomes.

Tools / code / hardware used:

  • Frontend: React + TypeScript, Vite dev server
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS utilities and shadcn UI components
  • Map & visualization: Canvas-based component with DOM tooltip overlay
  • Local persistence: browser localStorage
  • Development environment: Node.js, npm
  • Hosting: vercel

How is the project creative?

It adapts simple, real-world circular economy patterns to the constraints of an off-world habitat. The wastePool reuse-first policy and the map-centroid visualization make the prototype practical: they combine process optimization with spatial planning in a compact, educational tool.

What factors were considered?

Mass balance, energy and water tradeoffs, crew time, local collection logistics, regenerative reuse (wastePool), and safety (avoid incineration, avoid PFAS/microplastics). We also assumed continuous electricity and limited water available, matching the challenge guidance.

projectDetails.name: Project Algorythm
projectDetails.summary:
We created a Methane Monitoring and Awareness App to make the invisible visible. Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas, more than 80 times stronger than CO₂, but it often goes unnoticed because we can’t see or smell it. It leaks silently from rice fields, livestock, landfills, and energy facilities, contributing massively to climate change.

Our app brings this hidden problem to light by using satellite data to show methane levels on a simple, interactive world map. People can zoom into their own region, check daily or weekly trends, and see clear alerts when levels rise above normal. What was once raw scientific data is now transformed into something anyone — farmers, students, families, or policymakers — can understand.

This project matters because awareness is the first step toward action. If we can see methane, we can reduce it. Farmers can adopt better practices, communities can demand cleaner surroundings, and governments can respond faster to leaks. By making climate data human-friendly, we hope to empower people everywhere to play a role in protecting our shared future.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a Methane Monitoring and Awareness Web App designed to make greenhouse gas emissions visible and understandable to everyone. It works by pulling satellite-based methane data and displaying it on an interactive global map. Users can zoom into regions, see color-coded methane concentrations, track daily and weekly trends, and receive alerts when abnormal spikes occur.

The main benefit is accessibility — instead of complex scientific platforms, the public gets simple visuals they can easily understand. Farmers can learn how their practices affect methane, communities gain awareness of pollution in their surroundings, researchers and NGOs get an open tool to study trends, and governments can identify hotspots for targeted climate action.

The intended impact is to raise awareness, inspire action, and support climate solutions. Since methane is 80 times more powerful than CO₂ in the short term, reducing it has immediate benefits for slowing global warming.

We developed the app using Firebase (Firestore, Functions, Hosting) for the backend, React.js for the frontend, and integrated Google Maps API for visualization. Data is sourced from Google Earth Engine’s Sentinel-5P methane dataset.

Our project is creative because it bridges advanced satellite science with a human-centered interface. We considered simplicity, clarity, and inclusivity — ensuring that even someone with no scientific background can use the app, understand the data, and feel empowered to act.

  • Increasing efficiency: Automating the exoplanet hunting process frees up scientists to focus on more detailed analyses and atmospheric characterization of the most promising candidates.

projectDetails.name: Cellexis : RAG Based NASA Bioscience Search Engine
projectDetails.summary:
Cellexis is a smart research platform that transforms the access to NASA bioscience research publications using cutting-edge AI technologies. The platform uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), knowledge graphs, and natural language processing to allow researchers to navigate and analyze challenging biological data sets from space missions.
Key Innovation:
Cellexis revolutionizes how scientists engage with scientific literature through semantic search, natural language question-answering, and interactive knowledge graph visualization. A user can query, for instance, "How does microgravity influence immune response?" and get contextual answers with automatic citations.
Technical Accomplishment: Constructed with a new React/TypeScript frontend and FastAPI backend, featuring Google Gemini AI, Neo4j graph database, and vector embeddings for smart document retrieval.
Impact: Our project solves the main problem of information overload in scientific research by making NASA's large bioscience knowledge base more accessible, easier to understand and discover for the public, which in turn will help in speeding space biology research and enabling new scientific breakthroughs through RAG powered insights, and knowledge graphs created with the help of Neo4j auradb. Research scholars, scientists and even the public can make use of this easy to use app for boosting their scientific knowledge. Also the project is completely scalable.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works

Core Functionality:

Cellexis converts static NASA bioscience research papers into a smart, queryable knowledge system. The platform processes PDF documents via an advanced AI pipeline that:

1. Document Ingestion: Pulls text from NASA bioscience PDFs with PDFPlumber

2. Embedding Generation: Generates vector representations via Sentence Transformers

3. Knowledge Graph Construction: Automatically extracts biological entities and relationships via NLP and stores them in Neo4j

4. Smart Retrieval: Applies FAISS vector similarity search to locate appropriate document pieces

5. AI-Driven Responses: Employs Google Gemini AI to construct contextual responses with citations

User Experience:

• Natural language search ("How does microgravity influence immune response?")

• Interactive knowledge graph display revealing research linkages

• Voice commands for hands-free interaction

• Side-by-side paper comparison features

• Intelligent bookmarking and export options

Benefits & Intended Impact

Immediate Benefits:

• Time Efficiency: Relevant data can be discovered in seconds, not hours

• Discovery Enhancement: Discovers unseen relationships between research topics through graph visualization

• Accessibility: Provides access to complicated scientific literature via natural language queries

• Citation Accuracy: Automated citation creation with relevance score

Broader Impact:

• Accelerated Research: Quicker literature reviews leave more time for the actual experimentation

• Cross-Disciplinary Insights: Knowledge graphs uncover novel insights between disparate biological systems

• Space Biology Advancement: Improved access to NASA's research hastens comprehension of life in space

• Educational Value: Renders space biology research more accessible to students and early-career scientists

Technical Stack & Tools

Frontend Technologies:

• React 18.3.1 with TypeScript for type-safe coding

• Vite for rapid development and optimized builds

• Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui for clean, responsive UI

• Cytoscape.js for interactive visualization of graphs

• Firebase Authentication for safe user management

• Web Speech API for voice command functionality

Backend Technologies:

• FastAPI (Python 3.8+) for performance-oriented API building

• Google Gemini AI for natural language generation

• Sentence Transformers for document embeddings

• FAISS for vector similarity search with great efficiency

• Neo4j graph database for knowledge representation

• PDFPlumber for text extraction from documents

Infrastructure & Deployment:

• Frontend: Netlify/Vercel for hosting the static site

• Backend: Render for containerized API deployment

• Database: Neo4j AuraDB (cloud) for scalable graph storage

• Authentication: Firebase Auth for secure user sessions

Creative Aspects

1. Multimodal Interface Design:

• Integrated visual (graph), textual (search), and auditory (voice) interfaces

• Smooth transitions between various modes of interaction

• Progressive Web App features for offline interaction

2. Deep AI Integration:

• Innovative merging of RAG with knowledge graphs for richer context

• Real-time entity recognition and relationship mapping

• Context-aware and relevance-based citation scoring

3. User Experience Innovation:

• Voice-operated research with voice-activated commands ("Hey Cellexis")

• Fullscreen exploration and dynamic filtering modes

• Smart bookmarking with integration of personal notes

4. Cross-Document Intelligence:

• Multi-document agreement detection in paper comparison

• Automatic cross-referencing throughout the entire knowledge base

• Temporal analysis of research evolution over time

Team Considerations & Design Decisions

Scalability Factors:

• Independent scaling with microservices architecture

• Large document set optimization with vector database

• Efficient caching solutions for high-hit rate information

User-Centric Design:

• Responsive layout ensuring usability on any screen

• Gradual reveal of advanced features

• Minimization of cognitive load using intuitive flow for scholars

Performance Optimization:

• Lazy loading of large knowledge graphs

• Debounced searching to reduce API calls

• Client-side caching of results for lookup-intensive results

Security & Privacy:

• JWT authentication with refresh tokens

• CORS configuration securing cross-origin requests

• Sensitive information environment variable management

Accessibility & Inclusion:

• Voice control for mobility-impaired users

• High contrast modes for visual accessibility enhancement

• Keyboard navigation facilitation throughout the interface

Data Quality & Reliability:

• Automated citation validation and scoring

• Confidence indicators for AI-generated responses

• Version control of documents for updates and corrections

The project is a thoughtful balance between cutting-edge AI capability and down-to-earth usability, designed particularly to address the particular requirements of space biology researchers to efficiently explore the vast repository of NASA knowledge.

projectDetails.name: AquaSense: Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring with Interactive Map
projectDetails.summary:
We developed AquaSense, an IoT-based system that monitors water quality in real time and visualizes it on an interactive web map. Using an ESP32 device connected to sensors for temperature, TDS, and turbidity, our system collects live readings and sends them to a cloud-hosted dashboard. The dashboard displays the data dynamically, marking the device’s location on a map and indicating whether the water is safe, moderate, or unsafe.

This project addresses the challenge of environmental monitoring and data accessibility by providing instant, location-based insights into water quality, which can help authorities, researchers, and communities take timely action. It is important because water quality directly affects human health, agriculture, and aquatic ecosystems. By combining IoT, cloud services, and interactive visualisation, AquaSense provides a scalable, low-cost solution for monitoring water sources globally.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do / How does it work?

AquaSense monitors water quality in real time using an ESP32 IoT device connected to sensors for temperature, TDS, and turbidity. The device sends readings to a cloud-hosted Flask web dashboard, which displays the data dynamically on an interactive map. Each device’s location is marked, and water quality is categorized as safe, moderate, or unsafe based on sensor thresholds. The system updates every few seconds, providing live insights into water conditions.

Benefits

  • Provides real-time monitoring of water bodies.
  • Helps authorities, researchers, and communities identify unsafe water quickly.
  • Eliminates manual water testing and reporting delays.
  • Scalable — additional devices can be added easily to monitor multiple locations.

Intended Impact

AquaSense aims to improve environmental awareness and safety by offering instant, location-specific water quality information. It can assist in preventing waterborne diseases, protecting aquatic ecosystems, and supporting sustainable water management.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Hardware: ESP32 Dev Module, Temperature Sensor (DS18B20), TDS Sensor, Turbidity Sensor, Laptop/Power source
  • Software / Programming: Arduino IDE (C++), Python (Flask for backend), HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the dashboard
  • Cloud / Deployment: Render.com for hosting the live web dashboard

Creativity

  • Combines IoT sensors, cloud computing, and interactive mapping for a holistic solution.
  • Live location-based visualization makes water monitoring accessible and intuitive.
  • Lightweight and low-cost, allowing easy deployment in multiple areas.

Factors Considered by the Team

  • Accuracy of sensor readings for reliable water quality categorization.
  • Live visualization to make data immediately actionable.
  • Scalability for multiple devices and locations.
  • Usability — the dashboard is simple, clear, and mobile-friendly.
  • Low-cost, real-time IoT solution for communities with limited resources.

projectDetails.name: Project ARRAKIS
projectDetails.summary:
AgriSmart Decision-Maker is an interactive farming simulation designed to teach players the importance of data-driven decision-making in agriculture. Inspired by NASA’s open agricultural and climate datasets, the game challenges players to manage crop health across a simulated farming season by interpreting environmental clues and making strategic daily choices. Each in-game day presents abstracted data, such as soil moisture, rainfall, and temperature, requiring players to decide whether to irrigate, fertilize, or wait.

Behind the scenes, each scenario has a hidden optimal action based on real scientific parameters. Correct decisions improve crop health, while poor ones lead to penalties, reflecting real-world agricultural risks. The player must maintain positive crop health over multiple days to win.

Through this simple yet engaging decision loop, AgriSmart promotes awareness of sustainable farming, efficient water usage, and adaptive planning under uncertainty. It also introduces the educational potential of integrating real-world data into gaming to make complex concepts in environmental science and agriculture accessible and enjoyable.

Ultimately, AgriSmart Decision-Maker merges science, strategy, and sustainability — empowering players to think like modern farmers and appreciate how informed, data-based actions can shape the future of global food security.
projectDetails.details:
How it works:
AgriSmart Decision-Maker is a data-driven farming simulation that allows players to experience the challenges of managing crops under uncertain environmental conditions. Each game day presents soil and weather clues — such as moisture, temperature, and rainfall — while the true numerical data remains hidden. Players must analyze the provided information and choose between three actions: Irrigate, Fertilize, or Wait. The game evaluates each choice against a hidden “correct action” and adjusts crop health accordingly, creating a dynamic learning loop of analysis, decision, and feedback.

Benefits:
The game simplifies real agricultural data into an engaging and educational experience. It helps players understand sustainable resource management, smart irrigation, and the importance of using data for better farming outcomes. It also fosters critical thinking, environmental awareness, and strategic planning skills.

Intended Impact:
AgriSmart aims to promote awareness of sustainable farming practices and demonstrate how technology and data science can optimize agriculture. It bridges the gap between scientific data and everyday understanding, making agricultural education interactive and accessible.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used:
Data refined using Excel, Unreal Engine (for game dev), and NASA’s open agricultural datasets for realism. The project was prototyped in PyCharm..

Creativity & Design Considerations:
The team focused on simplicity, clarity, and realism — designing a game that educates while entertaining. Factors like balanced difficulty and meaningful feedback were carefully considered to create a blend of learning, challenge, and enjoyment.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch - Global Flower Bloom Exploration Platform
projectDetails.summary:
BloomWatch is an innovative Earth observation platform that combines NASA satellite data with advanced AI technology to monitor, visualize, and explain global flower blooming events. The platform features an interactive 3D globe interface where users can explore real-time bloom patterns worldwide and receive AI-generated ecological explanations.

The project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by creating a sophisticated solution for tracking and understanding plant phenology. It integrates multiple cutting-edge technologies: MapLibre GL JS for 3D globe visualization, AI-powered flower recognition from uploaded images, and intelligent bloom explanations generated by CrewAI agents. The platform's RAG-powered chatbot provides context-aware responses using a vector database of bloom-related information, ensuring accurate and relevant assistance to users.

BloomWatch serves diverse stakeholders: scientists tracking phenology shifts, farmers identifying optimal crop windows, conservationists locating flowering hotspots, and tourists planning flower-viewing trips. By combining real-time web research integration (SerpAPI and NewsAPI), monthly bloom predictions, and abundance visualization, the platform makes space technology accessible for both scientific research and public engagement.
projectDetails.details:
What it does & How it works: BloomWatch is an Earth observation platform that monitors and visualizes global flower blooming events through a sophisticated workflow:

  1. Users interact with a 3D globe interface to select regions and flowers of interest
  2. The platform processes this input through multiple AI agents working in parallel
  3. It combines NASA satellite data with real-time web research to generate comprehensive bloom information
  4. Users can upload flower images for AI-powered identification
  5. The system provides monthly predictions and abundance visualizations using color-coded overlays

  • Scientists can track global phenology shifts
  • Farmers can identify optimal crop bloom windows

  • Tourists can plan flower-viewing trips

challengeDetails.title: Your Home in Space: The Habitat Layout Creator
challengeDetails.excerpt: Space habitats are “homes in space” that keep crew members healthy and able to execute their mission. projectDetails.details:
The Cosmic Navigator is a dynamic, adaptive educational application built with Flutter and Dart that makes complex astronomical data accessible and engaging for users across different knowledge levels.

What It Does & How It Works

The core challenge addressed was making abstract astronomical data relatable and scalable based on the user's level of comprehension. We solved this by implementing a Theme Age system (Explorer, Scientist, Philosopher) that dynamically scales the content.

The app displays 50 interactive space facts and detailed mission information. When a user selects a Theme Age, the app instantly updates the analogy provided for each fact (e.g., comparing a distance to "LEGO bricks" for an Explorer or "Astronomical Units" for a Philosopher). Key features include:

  • Adaptive Content Scaling: Content adapts based on the user's selected knowledge theme.
  • Voyager 1 Deep Dive: Dedicated, interactive panels for the mission's timeline, statistics, instruments, and the Golden Record contents.
  • Themed Quiz Challenge: A functioning quiz system to test knowledge across different difficulty levels.

Impact and Tools

The project serves as an educational tool, transforming static, overwhelming data into an adaptive learning experience. It ensures that complex concepts, like interstellar distance or black hole mass, are effectively communicated to all users, fostering curiosity and scientific literacy.

  • Primary Technologies: Flutter (Dart), Riverpod (State Management), GoRouter (Navigation).
  • Creative Factor: The dynamic, tri-level analogy system that personalizes the data display for each user's stage of curiosity.

projectDetails.summary:
Project name: Meteor Madness
Challenge: The project addresses the potential threat posed by a newly identified near-Earth asteroid, "Impactor-2025," and the need for tools that help the public and decision-makers understand and mitigate such risks.
Problem: Integrating NASA's near-Earth object data with environmental and geological information from the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) is complex. Existing tools often lack user-friendly interfaces for simulating impact effects and evaluating mitigation strategies.
Solution: Develop an interactive visualization and simulation tool that integrates real-time NASA and USGS datasets. The tool will enable users to model hypothetical asteroid impact scenarios, predict outcomes (e.g., impact zones, seismic events, tsunamis), and explore potential mitigation strategies.
projectDetails.details:
• Features:
    • Data integration: Seamlessly combines NASA's asteroid parameter data (size, velocity, trajectory) with USGS datasets on topography, seismic activity, and tsunami zones.
    • Interactive visualizations: Includes dynamic visuals like animated orbital paths and 2D impact zone maps.
    • Simulation capabilities: Accurately models asteroid trajectories, calculates impact energy, and estimates environmental effects.
    • Mitigation scenario analysis: Allows users to input variables and test potential deflection strategies, such as kinetic impactors, to visualize the outcomes.
    • Educational focus: Incorporates gamification and storytelling to engage users and communicate complex astronomical threats in an accessible way.
  • Impact: This tool aims to enhance global asteroid risk management by bridging the gap between scientific data and actionable insights for scientists, policymakers, and the public.

About the team and challenge.

We first knew about the NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE when our teacher, Jiya Miss

told us about it . All of us are in class 7. We were very excited... Some of us decided to

make a team of four, the Astroblazers. The members in this team are Jovana Anna

Santo, Sesha Venugopal, Feba Gheevarghese, Allen Abraham Jacob. We decided to

choose the topic “ Meteor Madness”. Teamwork was never a problem here. We decided

to divide our work equally.

About the Game (What exactly the project does?)

This project also has a fun and interactive video game that consists of three levels. We

used the coding platform Pictoblox to develop our games. We used information from

Google, NASA, and Wikipedia. Our game reflects on the problems faced by astronaut

once they launch into the outer space. We have divided the game into 3 levels and one

member has done the starting and one has done the end of the game. After each level, a

meteor appears.

Sesha Venugopal did the starting and ending is done by Feba Gheevarghese. In

the begining a meteor will come and say the introduction. It includes a lot of information

about meteors, meteoroids, meteorite, meteor showers, different colors of meteors

and different type of meteoroids based on composition. It also tells that meteors are of

different types based on their appearance and the type of meteors are Fireball,

Earthgrazers, Bolide and Superbolide. It also tells us about different type of meteorite

based on their composition, they are: Iron meteorite, stony meteorite and iron-stony

meteorite. It also explain briefly about these types. The name of this game is “Meteor

Bot” and it consist of three levels. Your challenge is to pass the three levels to reach your

meteor . At last a meteor will come and say hope you enjoy the game, their is one more

meteor called Fireball meteor and fireball meteor will come and explain itself. Beware!!

This game may be far advanced than you think. Enjoy and have fun with the game.

How does it works?

The 1st level of the the game is done by Allen Abraham Jacob. It shows a

meteor that was hiding and it is showing after a random time. There will be having a slide

which tell about the rules to play the game. The meteor is controlled by the left and right

arrows. The player can gain points by shooting it. The game is also having timer and a

decoy which can reduce the player’s time if touched. Eg : If the score is =17 or timer =0

then the game will end. Remember that this is the 1st level.

The 2nd level of the game has been also done by Sesha Venugopal. It

shows the rocket being attacked by a blackhole. First there will be a few slides

explaining the instructions of the game. The rocket is controlled by the tip of the index

finger. Every time the rocket touches the black hole the life of the spaceship will reduce

by 1. If the life of the spaceship is 4, the above rocket will be able to meet its forgot

Chelyabinsk, a bolide meteor. If the life of the rocket is below 4 the game will restart. If

the player get to meet the meteor, it will explain about itself. Enjoy and have fun. The life

of the rocket is 10 and the blackhole will attack the player 15 times. Then, at last a

astronaut will come and tell you some things and then the level will end with a

congratulations slide.

The 3rd and the hardest level has been made by Jovana Anna Santo. It

shows a spaceship being attacked by loop. There are some rules and regulations which

explains how to play this game. You have to use your nose to move the spaceship away

from the loop. This is the hardest level in this game. You can’t get an meteor as a reward

even if lose, instead you have to play the game again, there if you win, you will get the

reward (super bolide).. The information about the meteor has been provided.

This project will help people to understand the seriousness of this situation

interactively and enjoyably so that the information will get stuck to their heads. We have

Our project has a clear presentation that explains what our project does, its

Our team member Feba Gheevarghese made the detailed project description whereas

Vote of thanks.

Big thanks to our school, Mar Thoma Residential School, Thiruvalla for the great

Mrs. Jiya Jaison and Ms. Asiya Beevi for their extensive and valuable suggestions and

great support during the entire project. We also thank God Almighty for His guidance

and strength.

Thank You!!

projectDetails.name: NASA Ag Data Explorer
projectDetails.summary:
NASA Ag Data Explorer is a prototype web application developed to provide agricultural stakeholders with an integrated view of critical hydrological data from space and ground sources. We developed an interactive Leaflet-based map interface that acts as a fusion center for SMAP soil moisture, NASA/USDA Global Soil Moisture, and GRACE-FO mass change data.

The project addresses the challenge by making disparate, complex NASA datasets accessible and actionable. By allowing users to visualize these layers together, select a specific area, and generate a time-series chart and area statistics (e.g., average soil moisture), it rapidly transforms raw satellite observations into crucial agricultural insights.

This is important because it enables data-driven decision-making regarding irrigation scheduling, drought assessment, and water resource management, especially in regions lacking extensive ground-based monitoring. It acts as a powerful, user-friendly tool to mitigate climate risks and improve crop yields.
projectDetails.details:
What it Does and How it Works

The NASA Ag Data Explorer is an interactive web-based mapping application that fuses multiple NASA and USDA hydrological datasets into a single, user-friendly interface for agricultural decision-making.

  • Data Integration: It visualizes SMAP soil moisture, NASA/USDA Global Soil Moisture, and GRACE-FO mass change (total water storage) as transparent map layers.
  • Analysis: Users can draw a selection rectangle (Shift + Drag) on the map to define an area of interest (e.g., a farm or region).
  • Visualization: It generates real-time statistics (e.g., average soil moisture) and a time-series chart for that specific area, effectively turning complex raster data into actionable trends.
  • Ground Truthing: It allows users to upload field CSV data (lat, lon, soil_moisture) to plot their own ground measurements alongside satellite observations.

Creativity and Factors Considered

  • Creativity: The project's main creative contribution is the fusion of SMAP and GRACE-FO data (representing surface and deep water resources, respectively) into a single analytical dashboard. This comprehensive hydrological view, combined with the intuitive "Shift+Drag" area-based analysis, simplifies complex Earth science for agricultural users who typically only use surface-level data.
    • User Experience (UX): Prioritized a clean, dark-mode interface and simple button controls to ensure easy use, even with minimal technical knowledge.
    • Data Latency: The architecture is designed to handle temporal data by allowing date selection, simulating the need to query specific days from NASA archives.
    • Accessibility: Ensured the tool can be run locally via a browser (index.html), making it easy to deploy and test without needing dedicated servers initially.
    • Scalability: Used placeholder functions (makeGibLayer) to clearly define where live NASA API calls (WMS/WMTS/WCS endpoints) need to be integrated for a fully operational product.

projectDetails.name: StratSense
projectDetails.summary:
StratSense is an innovative data-driven platform designed to monitor and analyze stratospheric patterns using satellite and ground-based sensor data. Our project focuses on improving the understanding of atmospheric composition, temperature fluctuations, and aerosol distribution in the stratosphere — key factors influencing climate and weather prediction. By integrating datasets from NASA’s open sources and applying machine learning algorithms, StratSense identifies anomalies, visualizes stratospheric changes in real time, and provides insights for climate researchers and environmental agencies.

We developed a web-based dashboard that simplifies complex data into accessible visuals and predictive analytics. The system highlights critical atmospheric trends that could support early warnings for climate irregularities and contribute to sustainable environmental policy-making. StratSense addresses the challenge by transforming raw satellite data into meaningful, actionable intelligence — bridging the gap between data accessibility and global climate awareness.
projectDetails.details:
StratSense is an innovative atmospheric intelligence platform that monitors and analyzes stratospheric patterns using satellite and ground-based data. It focuses on identifying temperature variations, aerosol concentrations, and ozone fluctuations — all of which play a crucial role in understanding climate behavior and predicting atmospheric trends.

The system collects data from NASA’s open APIs and other scientific sources, processes it through machine learning models, and visualizes the results in an interactive web dashboard. Users can explore real-time changes in stratospheric conditions through maps, dynamic graphs, and predictive models that highlight anomalies or trends.

StratSense transforms complex satellite data into clear, actionable insights that can help researchers, policymakers, and educators make informed decisions about climate adaptation and environmental protection. By bridging the gap between scientific data and usability, it encourages a deeper understanding of how stratospheric shifts impact weather and ecosystems on Earth.

The project’s creativity lies in its ability to combine scientific accuracy with accessibility. Our team designed StratSense with a focus on reliability, user engagement, and environmental impact — transforming raw data into a meaningful, educational, and sustainable digital tool for atmospheric awareness.

🌌 A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
🚀 Introduction

The universe has always inspired curiosity about whether life exists beyond Earth. The discovery of exoplanets—planets orbiting stars outside our solar system—has opened new frontiers in astronomy. Yet, detecting these distant worlds is challenging due to the massive datasets generated by space telescopes such as Kepler, TESS, and JWST. Manually analyzing these light curves is time-consuming and prone to errors.

Our project, “A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI,” leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to automate the identification of potential exoplanets. By using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), we can detect subtle patterns in stellar brightness indicative of planetary transits, reducing human effort and increasing detection accuracy. This project merges astronomy with modern computing to accelerate scientific discovery and engage students, researchers, and enthusiasts worldwide.

projectDetails.details:
🌦️ Project Details – Kerala-Themed Interactive Weather Dashboard

🌀 What does it do / How does it work?

The Kerala-Themed Interactive Weather Dashboard is a smart web application that provides real-time and forecasted weather information for any global location.
Users can:

  • Search for a city by name,
  • Enter latitude and longitude, or
  • Select a location directly on an interactive map.

The backend (built with FastAPI) fetches weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API, processes it, and sends clean, formatted results to the frontend.
The frontend (built with React) then displays weather metrics like temperature, humidity, wind speed, and conditions through colorful Kerala-inspired visuals and animations.

🌞 What benefits does it have?

  • Instant, accurate weather updates from anywhere in the world.
  • User-friendly and engaging interface that makes weather tracking enjoyable.
  • Forecast visualization helps users plan for future days.
  • Encourages regional design creativity, merging local aesthetics with modern tech.
  • Can be extended for disaster alerts, agriculture planning, or tourism applications in Kerala and beyond.

The project aims to make weather information more accessible, interactive, and culturally relatable.
By blending Kerala’s cultural design elements with AI-powered weather insights, the app creates a bridge between technology and local identity.
Its educational and functional aspects make it ideal for students, travelers, and weather enthusiasts.
Ultimately, it promotes the idea that regional art and global data can coexist beautifully in technology-driven products.

projectDetails.name: Biological Knowledge Space Engine
projectDetails.summary:
We developed the Space Biology Knowledge Engine, a prototype platform that makes NASA’s space biology data and research rapidly searchable, understandable, and actionable. Using retrieval-augmented AI, our system ingests scientific papers, NASA technical reports, and experiment datasets, then delivers concise answers to natural-language questions such as “Which immune cells change after long-duration spaceflight?” Each answer is grounded in evidence and linked directly to its source, ensuring transparency and reliability.

This addresses the challenge of navigating vast, fragmented biological knowledge relevant to human spaceflight and space crop research. By integrating metadata (mission, organism, hardware, assay type) and highlighting evidence, the tool accelerates literature discovery, mission planning, and educational use.

Its importance lies in enabling faster, evidence-based decisions for astronaut health, countermeasure development, and bioregenerative life support. Ultimately, it helps bridge the gap between scattered data and actionable insights for future exploration missions. This provides fast, evidence-backed answers to space biology questions using NASA’s open data and literature. Our prototype combines semantic retrieval with short, provenance-rich answers so researchers and mission planners can get reliable, cited summaries in seconds.
projectDetails.details:
We developed the Space Biology Knowledge Engine, a prototype platform that makes NASA’s space biology data and research rapidly searchable, understandable, and actionable. Using retrieval-augmented AI, our system ingests scientific papers, NASA technical reports, and experiment datasets, then delivers concise answers to natural-language questions such as “Which immune cells change after long-duration spaceflight?” Each answer is grounded in evidence and linked directly to its source, ensuring transparency and reliability.

This addresses the challenge of navigating vast, fragmented biological knowledge relevant to human spaceflight and space crop research. By integrating metadata (mission, organism, hardware, assay type) and highlighting evidence, the tool accelerates literature discovery, mission planning, and educational use.

Its importance lies in enabling faster, evidence-based decisions for astronaut health, countermeasure development, and bioregenerative life support. Ultimately, it helps bridge the gap between scattered data and actionable insights for future exploration missions.

Here’s a structured write-up (within 200 words) that answers each of those submission questions clearly:

Benefits & Impact
The Space Biology Knowledge Engine makes NASA’s vast but scattered biological data easier to access, interpret, and apply. Researchers, mission planners, and educators benefit from fast, evidence-based answers that reduce time spent searching and lower the risk of overlooking critical findings. The intended impact is to accelerate countermeasure discovery for astronaut health, improve space crop research for sustainable missions, and inspire students by providing clear, interactive access to authentic NASA data.

Tools & Technologies
We built the prototype with Python (FastAPI, Streamlit) for backend and UI, React + Tailwind for web components, FAISS/Elasticsearch for retrieval, and sentence-transformer embeddings for semantic search. Sources included PubMed abstracts, NASA Technical Reports Server entries, and GEO dataset metadata. We containerized the pipeline with Docker for portability.

Creativity & Considerations
Our creativity lies in combining retrieval-augmented generation with a curated ontology of space-biology entities (organism, hardware, mission) to give both human-readable answers and structured metadata links. We considered accuracy (avoiding hallucinations), evidence provenance, data licensing, biosecurity (sensitive protocols), and usability for non-experts. The result is a novel, reliable bridge between open NASA data and practical insight for future space exploration.

projectDetails.name: Project Astrons
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, *Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars*, focuses on developing an innovative, closed-loop recycling system designed specifically for the harsh and resource-scarce environment of Mars. We created a modular recycling unit capable of processing a wide variety of waste—plastics, metals, organic matter—into reusable materials that support life-sustaining operations, such as habitat construction, 3D printing, and food production.

This solution addresses the critical challenge of sustainability for long-term Mars missions, where resupply from Earth is limited and costly. By efficiently reusing available materials, the system minimizes waste, conserves essential resources, and supports a self-sufficient Martian colony.

Our project is important because it aligns with the goals of space exploration and colonization: resilience, efficiency, and independence. A reliable recycling infrastructure is essential for maintaining a healthy, habitable environment on Mars, ensuring mission success, and paving the way for future interplanetary settlements.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars

Our project introduces a smart, modular recycling system engineered specifically for Martian environments. The system is designed to handle various types of waste generated during space missions, including plastics, metals, organic matter, and packaging materials. It utilizes advanced sorting algorithms, automated robotic arms, and high-efficiency compactors to separate, process, and repurpose materials into usable resources such as construction components, filament for 3D printing, and nutrient-rich compost for hydroponics.

We used a combination of Python for automation and system logic, Arduino for sensor integration and robotic control, and CAD software (such as Fusion 360) for designing the physical components of the unit. Our prototype also integrates machine learning to optimize sorting accuracy over time based on the waste profiles encountered on Mars.

The project benefits include waste reduction, resource conservation, and increased self-sufficiency for Martian colonies. It also decreases the need for costly and infrequent resupply missions from Earth.

Creativity was key in designing a solution tailored to Mars' constraints: limited energy, low gravity, and extreme environmental conditions. Our team considered factors such as energy efficiency, repairability, modularity, and long-term durability to ensure the system’s success in supporting sustainable life on the Red Planet.

projectDetails.name: Neural Explorer : Finding Earth 2.0
projectDetails.summary:
This project, “Neural Explorer : Finding Earth 2.0,” focuses on finding planets outside our solar system by analyzing the brightness of stars.
We created synthetic star data (light curves) showing how brightness changes when a planet passes in front of a star — called a transit.
A neural network model was trained using this data to detect transits automatically.
It was tested on real NASA data and achieved high accuracy.
The project shows how AI can make exoplanet discovery faster, more efficient, and highly reliable for future space research.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Neural Explorer: Finding Earth 2.0, implements a machine learning solution to detect exoplanet transits by analyzing stellar light curves. A transit occurs when a planet passes in front of its host star, producing a small dip in brightness. Detecting such signals in large telescope datasets is challenging due to noise and the massive data volume.

To address this, we generated over 2,000 synthetic light curves with configurable transit parameters such as depth, duration, and position. Realistic Gaussian noise was added to simulate telescope conditions. A neural network classifier, built with TensorFlow/Keras, was then trained to distinguish between light curves with and without planetary transits. The model architecture includes two hidden layers with dropout regularization, optimized with Adam and binary cross-entropy loss.

The system achieved excellent results, converging within five epochs with 100% validation accuracy, and demonstrated reliable predictions on unseen test data. Visualizations were produced to showcase sample light curves, training history, and prediction outcomes. The trained model can also be applied to new datasets, including real NASA observations, to support exoplanet discovery.

This project highlights how AI can accelerate the search for habitable planets by providing a fast, scalable, and accurate detection method. By combining synthetic data generation, neural networks, and NASA datasets, it demonstrates the potential of AI-driven exploration in the quest to discover Earth-like worlds beyond our solar system.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI was a core component of this project. We implemented a neural network classifier using Keras to automatically detect exoplanet transit signals in light curve data. The model was trained on a synthetic dataset that included both transit and non-transit events with realistic telescope noise.

AI was also used to analyze and classify unseen test light curves, achieving high accuracy and demonstrating the ability to scale to real NASA data. Additionally, we used an AI assistant (ChatGPT) to help generate documentation and provide code structuring suggestions, which we then refined and implemented manually.

All AI-generated contributions (code suggestions, documentation support) have been acknowledged here, and the final model, training, and results were built and verified by the team.

projectDetails.name: METEOR MADNESS : AN AI POWERED SKY INTERPRETER
projectDetails.summary: Meteor Madness is an AI-powered sky interpreter designed to help people identify what they see in the night sky — whether it’s a meteor, star, or satellite — simply by uploading a photo. The app analyzes the image to label stars and constellations, detect streaks, and classify them accurately. Using tools like Astrometry.net for plate solving, OpenCV for meteor detection, and Astropy for star mapping, it can even identify which meteor shower a streak belongs to, such as the Perseids. This project aims to support both astronomy enthusiasts and researchers by offering quick, accurate classification of celestial events. In the future, the team envisions a real-time mobile app that makes sky interpretation accessible to everyone — turning night-sky photos into meaningful cosmic insights.
projectDetails.details: Meteor Madness is an AI-powered tool that identifies stars, meteors, and satellites from night-sky photos using advanced image processing and astronomy data. It works through a streamlined process — plate solving, streak detection, and object classification — to provide instant results. The project uses a Python-based backend with an AI detection engine for classification, data processing modules for star mapping and catalog cross-checking, and a Streamlit web app frontend for a simple, interactive user experience. Combining OpenCV, Astropy, and Astrometry.net, Meteor Madness creatively bridges AI and astronomy to make celestial analysis accurate, accessible, and educational for everyone.

projectDetails.name: Project SKYVYN
projectDetails.summary: If you’re planning an outdoor event—like a vacation, a hike on a trail, or fishing on a lake—it would be good to know the chances of adverse weather for the time and location you are considering. There are many types of Earth observation data that can provide information on weather conditions for a particular location and day of the year. projectDetails.details: “Skyvyn is a smart weather app that helps people plan outdoor events by predicting temperature, humidity, wind, and rain chances. With a simple, mobile-friendly interface, users get personalized comfort insights and rain probability in seconds.”
projectDetails.aiReferences:
• Machine Learning Model (XGBoost)
    • You trained an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model, which is a powerful AI algorithm for predictive tasks.
    • It captures non-linear patterns and seasonal variations in weather data better than simple regression models.
    • The model takes historical NASA POWER data (10+ years) along with location/time inputs.
    • It predicts future temperature, humidity, rainfall probability, and comfort level for the user’s chosen event time and place.
    • You applied AI techniques like cyclical encoding (sin/cos for seasonal patterns), lag features, and normalization to convert raw NASA weather data into meaningful inputs the model can learn from.
    • AI classifies the predicted temperature into categories like “very hot,” “very cold,” or “comfortable,” based on user’s preferred conditions.
    • This personalization makes the app user-centered instead of generic weather apps

projectDetails.name: Project ASTRUM
projectDetails.summary:
NASA CLIMASENSE is a web-based climate information platform designed to provide real-time and forecasted weather data for any location, helping users make informed decisions for outdoor activities and events.

The system features a secure login and sign-up interface, ensuring personalized user experiences. Upon successful login, users are directed to a Weather Dashboard where they can input a city and view live climate data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, and weather conditions.

The dashboard integrates with a free OpenWeatherMap API to fetch and display accurate weather data. It includes:

📅 Date and Time selection to view conditions at specific times.

🌦 Real-time weather summary with clear iconography.

📊 Interactive bar charts generated using Chart.js, visualizing temperature, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation.

📈 8-day forecast table to help users plan ahead.

The clean and modern Bootstrap-based UI makes the application accessible and responsive across devices. This project demonstrates practical use of PHP (backend) and HTML/CSS/JavaScript (frontend) technologies to build a functional climate monitoring tool.
projectDetails.details:
NASA CLIMASENSE is a web-based climate forecasting platform designed to help users access real-time and future weather information for any location by simply entering the city name. The platform features a secure login and sign-up system that allows users to create an account and access a personalized dashboard. Once logged in, users can view detailed weather data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation, all fetched using the OpenWeatherMap API. This information is displayed in a clean, organized interface, enhanced with interactive charts that make it easy to visualize hourly and daily forecasts. The system provides real-time updates and extended forecasts, helping users plan outdoor activities like vacations, hikes, or events with greater confidence.

The main benefit of NASA CLIMASENSE is that it simplifies climate data and makes it actionable for everyday use. It enables users to plan efficiently by providing accurate weather information in an accessible format. The intended impact of this project is to increase climate awareness, support informed decision-making, and demonstrate how open-source weather data and NASA’s Earth observation concepts can be used to build meaningful public tools.

The project was developed using PHP for backend logic and API handling, HTML and CSS for structure and design, and JavaScript with Chart.js for data visualization. Bootstrap was used to ensure a responsive and user-friendly interface. During development, the team focused on data accuracy, user experience, security, scalability, and accessibility. By combining real-time weather data with interactive visualization and user authentication, NASA CLIMASENSE offers a creative and innovative solution that can be expanded to include features like alerts for extreme weather conditions.

projectDetails.details:
Cosmic Dashboard is a dynamic, all-in-one web application designed to make space exploration accessible and engaging. Built with vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet.js, it consolidates real-time data from multiple NASA APIs—including those for asteroids (NeoWs), daily pictures (APOD), and Earth imagery (EPIC)—into a unified, user-friendly interface.

The project addresses the challenge of data fragmentation by providing a single portal where users can track near-Earth asteroids, view the live ISS location, search NASA’s vast media library, and explore historical space events for any given day. A personalization system with user accounts allows users to save their favorite discoveries, curating their own journey through the cosmos.

This dashboard is important because it transforms complex scientific data into an interactive educational tool. The project's creativity lies in its synthesis of disparate data streams into a cohesive and engaging user experience. By democratizing access to public space information, the Cosmic Dashboard aims to foster curiosity and inspire the next generation of explorers, scientists, and engineers, making the wonders of our universe tangible for everyone

Artificial Intelligence (Google Gemini) was a foundational tool in this project, serving as a development partner to accelerate the entire lifecycle from concept to deployment. Beyond initial creation, the AI was critical for troubleshooting, diagnosing runtime JavaScript errors and API-related issues like HTTP status codes. It also assisted in refining features, such as converting a static data source to a live API call, and helped draft all project descriptions, summaries, and technical explanations, making it an invaluable collaborator for rapid prototyping and iteration.

projectDetails.name: Project Axis
projectDetails.summary: The search for Earth-like exoplanets is one of the most exciting frontiers in space exploration. While thousands of exoplanets have been discovered, identifying those that may support life remains a complex challenge. Existing databases and tools are often designed for researchers and can be overwhelming for students or enthusiasts. This app aims to bridge that gap by providing a simple, user-friendly platform to explore, filter, and visualize potentially habitable exoplanets. By making space data more accessible and interactive, the app not only supports research but also inspires curiosity and learning in the field of astronomy.
projectDetails.details: As the discovery of exoplanets continues to grow rapidly, there is a clear need for a tool that helps make sense of this vast and complex data. Most existing platforms are designed for experts and are not accessible to students, educators, or the general public. Our app solves this by providing a clean, interactive, and intelligent way to search for Earth-like planets using scientific criteria such as size, temperature, and distance from their star.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI helps the app move beyond just displaying data — it interprets, predicts, and adapts, making the search for Earth-like worlds faster, smarter, and more insightful.

1. Habitability Prediction

AI models can analyze large datasets of exoplanet characteristics (mass, radius, temperature, orbital distance, etc.) and predict the likelihood of a planet being Earth-like or habitable. This helps prioritize planets for deeper study.

2. Pattern Recognition

AI can detect hidden patterns in massive astronomical datasets that may be missed by traditional methods. For example, it can spot Earth-like traits among thousands of planets discovered by Kepler or TESS.

3. Data Cleaning and Classification

Exoplanet data is often noisy or incomplete. AI can clean and classify this data automatically, improving the reliability of search results.

4. User Personalization

The app can use AI to personalize results for users — showing planets based on their interests, past searches, or specific research goals.

5. Real-Time Updates and Learning

Machine Learning (ML) algorithms can be trained to learn from new discoveries and update the app’s scoring models in real time, making it smarter over time.

projectDetails.name: NilayaSrishti
projectDetails.summary: A NASA-grade space habitat design platform that makes complex aerospace engineering accessible. Design realistic space stations for Moon, Mars, and deep space missions using real mathematical validation and professional engineering standards.
projectDetails.details:
NilayaSrishti (निलयसृष्टि - "Creating Cosmic Dwellings") is a NASA-grade space habitat design platform that democratizes complex aerospace engineering through an intuitive web-based interface. Built with React 18.2 and Three.js, the platform enables students, educators, and engineers to design realistic space stations for lunar, Martian, and deep space missions using real mathematical validation based on NASA-STD-3001 Human Systems Integration Requirements. Users can select from six geometric habitat shapes (cylinder, capsule, sphere, dome, torus, cube) and populate them with 12 NASA-compliant module types, each with scientifically validated volume requirements that scale with crew size and mission duration. The system performs real-time calculations using accurate geometric formulas—from simple boxes (V = L×W×H) to complex toruses (V = 2π²Rr²)—ensuring every design meets the 15 m³ per crew minimum and includes a 20% safety buffer standard in aerospace engineering. Nine professional presets based on real space agency concepts (ISS-inspired, Mars Base, Lunar Gateway) provide starting points, while features like extreme zoom (0.5m to 500m range), drag-and-drop module placement, double-click editing, and JSON export/import enable sophisticated design workflows without requiring backend infrastructure.

The project's creative approach bridges the gap between educational accessibility and professional rigor by combining a retro Minecraft-inspired aesthetic with NASA-grade calculations, making space engineering approachable without sacrificing accuracy. Our team carefully considered human factors in space (minimum sleeping space of 2.5 m³ per crew, adjacency recommendations for module placement, critical vs. optional modules), educational impact (teaching 3D geometry, volume calculations, and mission planning concepts), and practical usability (no installation required, works offline, presentation mode with hidden errors, sidebar toggle for maximum workspace). The intended impact is threefold: empowering STEM education by making complex engineering concepts interactive and fun, supporting preliminary mission design with a tool rigorous enough for concept development yet simple enough for rapid iteration, and inspiring the next generation of aerospace engineers by giving them the tools to start designing humanity's future homes in space today. By making NASA-standard habitat design accessible through any web browser, NilayaSrishti transforms space architecture from an exclusive domain into an inclusive platform where anyone can contribute to building tomorrow's cosmic dwellings.
projectDetails.aiReferences: NilayaSrishti is an original concept created by our team. The project name, Sanskrit etymology, retro gaming aesthetic, module library design, preset configurations, and overall user experience are entirely human-designed. AI tools served only as coding assistants to implement our vision more efficiently, similar to how developers use Stack Overflow or documentation—they accelerated implementation but did not generate the creative direction or core functionality.

projectDetails.name: Your home in space: The Habitat creator
projectDetails.summary:
This interactive web tool enables users to design and visualize space habitat layouts for NASA's Artemis program and future Mars missions. The simulator features a single cylindrical deck with multiple internal layers, each representing different functional zones like living quarters, work areas, and life support systems.

Users can switch between 3D, top-down, and side views to examine their habitat designs from different perspectives. The tool includes eight functional areas with specific space requirements based on crew size. Layers can be resized intuitively by dragging handles, and sectors automatically reposition around each layer's circumference.

Real-time calculations show space utilization efficiency with color-coded feedback. Mission parameters like crew size and deck diameter can be adjusted to explore different design scenarios. The simulator provides immediate visual feedback on layout adequacy, helping users optimize habitat designs for various mission durations and crew sizes while considering real-world constraints like launch vehicle limitations.

projectDetails.details:
# Project Details: Meteor Madness Challenge

## What It Does & How It Works

Meteor Madness Challenge is an interactive educational platform that gamifies space science learning through AI-powered meteor exploration. The system works by:

**Interactive Learning Modules**: Users engage with four meteor types through 3D visualizations, interactive simulations, and virtual laboratory environments. The platform uses Three.js for realistic 3D rendering of meteor compositions and orbital mechanics.

**AI-Driven Personalization**: Machine learning algorithms analyze user performance in real-time, adjusting content difficulty and suggesting personalized learning paths. The AI tracks progress through meteor identification challenges, impact prediction games, and composition analysis tasks.

**NASA Data Integration**: The platform is trained exclusively on authentic NASA datasets, including meteor composition data, orbital parameters, and impact records from sources like the Meteoritical Society database and NASA's Planetary Data System.

## Benefits

- **Accessible STEM Education**: Makes complex astronomical concepts understandable through gamification

- **Personalized Learning**: Adapts to individual student pace and comprehension levels

- **Scientific Accuracy**: NASA-verified data ensures educational content reliability

- **Engagement Boost**: Game elements increase motivation and knowledge retention

- **Scalable Platform**: Web-based accessibility requires no special hardware

## Intended Impact

- **Educational**: Increase student participation in space science by 300% through engaging content

- **Inspirational**: Demonstrate AI capabilities to younger generations as both users and future developers

- **Scientific Literacy**: Improve public understanding of meteor science and planetary defense

- **Career Pathway**: Spark interest in STEM fields, particularly astronomy and data science

## Development Tools & Technologies

**Frontend Development**:

- HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ES6+

- Three.js for 3D graphics and animations

- GSAP for smooth animations and transitions

- WebGL for hardware-accelerated graphics

**AI & Backend**:

- Python with scikit-learn for machine learning algorithms

- TensorFlow.js for browser-based AI processing

- NASA API integrations for real-time data

- Firebase for user analytics and progress tracking

**Design & UX**:

- Adobe Creative Suite for UI/UX design

- Blender for 3D meteor models

- Responsive design frameworks for cross-device compatibility

## Creativity & Innovation

**Unique Approach**: Combining authentic NASA data with gaming mechanics creates an unprecedented educational experience. The platform transforms passive learning into active discovery.

**Technical Innovation**:

- Real-time 3D meteor visualization using WebGL

- AI algorithms that adapt to learning patterns

- Browser-based processing eliminates need for downloads or installations

**Educational Creativity**:

- Mission-based learning structure mimicking real scientific exploration

- Virtual meteor hunting with realistic detection simulations

- Collaborative challenges encouraging peer learning

## Team Considerations

**Accessibility**: Designed for diverse learning abilities and age groups (12+)

**Scientific Integrity**: All content verified against NASA databases and peer-reviewed research

**User Experience**: Intuitive interface requiring minimal technical knowledge

**Performance**: Optimized for various devices and internet connection speeds

**Safety**: COPPA-compliant data handling for younger users

**Scalability**: Architecture supports simultaneous users without performance degradation

**Future-Proofing**: Modular design allows easy content updates and feature additions

The project successfully bridges entertainment and education while maintaining scientific rigor, demonstrating that AI can be both a creative tool and an educational accelerator when grounded in verified scientific data.

projectDetails.name: Project Big Bang
projectDetails.summary:
Project Sentinel is a NASA-inspired, interactive web simulator designed to educate the public and inform policy on planetary defense.
It allows users to select real asteroid data (from NASA JPL) and visualize potential impact scenarios in a dynamic, 3D environment using the Three.js framework.
The core of the project is a rigorous Physics Engine that calculates impact energy, models crater formation, and simulates the devastating Impact Zones (Fireball, Blast Wave, Thermal Radiation).
Ultimately, Project Sentinel enhances public awareness and preparedness by visualizing the immediate, regional, and long-term effects of an impact, and modeling various Mitigation Strategies (like the Kinetic Impactor and Gravity Tractor).
projectDetails.details:
The project titled Big Bang: Meteor Madness — Asteroid Impact Simulator is an interactive web application that demonstrates how an asteroid impact could affect Earth. Users can adjust factors such as the asteroid’s size, speed, impact angle, and lead time to see how these parameters influence the energy released, crater size, casualties, and overall damage. The simulator also allows users to experiment with different defense techniques, including kinetic impactors, nuclear deflection, and gravity tractors.

This project helps people understand real asteroid threats and the importance of planetary defense. It simplifies complex physics concepts through visual and interactive simulations, making learning both engaging and informative. The main goal is to raise awareness about how science and technology can be used to prevent potential asteroid disasters.

The simulator was developed using React and TypeScript for interactivity, along with Tailwind CSS and ShadCN UI for modern design. The Sonner library was used for real-time notifications, and physics-based calculations were implemented to determine impact energy, crater formation, and deflection requirements.

The project combines scientific accuracy with creativity, offering an enjoyable learning experience while maintaining realism. It focuses on clarity, interactivity, and user engagement. In the future, the simulator aims to include real NASA asteroid data and advanced 3D visualizations to make it even more realistic and educational.

Live demo: https://orbit-defense-sim.lovable.app

Project Summary – BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology

BloomWatch is an innovative Earth observation platform designed to monitor and analyze global flowering patterns using satellite imagery, climate data, and machine learning. We developed an interactive web and mobile application that detects flowering stages of vegetation across regions, visualizes seasonal trends, and predicts upcoming bloom periods. By integrating remote sensing data (such as NDVI and temperature indices) with AI-driven phenology models, BloomWatch provides real-time insights into how climate change, weather anomalies, and land-use patterns influence flowering cycles.

This solution directly addresses the challenge of tracking global flowering phenology—a key ecological indicator vital for agriculture, biodiversity, and climate research. Understanding bloom dynamics helps scientists, farmers, and policymakers anticipate pollination periods, crop yields, and ecosystem shifts. BloomWatch makes large-scale phenological monitoring accessible and actionable, supporting sustainable environmental decision-making worldwide.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology

BloomWatch is an innovative Earth observation web application designed to monitor, visualize, and predict global flowering patterns using remote sensing and climate data. The platform focuses on understanding flowering phenology—the study of seasonal plant life cycle events—and how these are affected by climate change and environmental conditions.

The system processes satellite imagery and climate datasets to detect flowering phases of vegetation across regions. It analyzes parameters such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), temperature, and rainfall to identify bloom trends and generate interactive, real-time visualizations. Users can explore global flowering maps, time-lapse animations, and predictive graphs that reveal seasonal variations and climate impacts.

BloomWatch was developed using React with Vite for a fast and modular development environment. The technologies used include JSX, JavaScript (JS), CSS, and JSON. React components handle the user interface, while JSON files manage structured environmental data and API responses. CSS is used for responsive design and clean data visualization layouts.

The application’s benefits include aiding researchers, farmers, and environmental organizations in tracking phenological shifts, predicting blooming periods, and assessing the ecological impact of global warming. It supports sustainable agriculture, biodiversity conservation, and climate monitoring by translating complex datasets into accessible visual insights.

BloomWatch’s creativity lies in its fusion of AI-driven data processing, satellite analysis, and intuitive visual design. The project emphasizes usability, scalability, and scientific accuracy, ensuring it can serve both academic and practical environmental needs. The team considered factors like data integrity, cross-platform performance, user accessibility, and global relevance, resulting in a unique tool that bridges technology and environmental awareness.

The story intertwines science and mythology to describe the birth of a star, personified as Stella.

In the Nebula Forest, a cloud of gas and dust, Stella—a small wisp of matter—dreams of shining brightly. Guided by Eldorion, an old, fading star, she learns that to become a star, she must gather strength through gravity and endure immense pressure and heat.

As she collects dust and gas, her core grows hotter until, after eons of struggle, nuclear fusion ignites, and Stella awakens as a radiant new star. Her light fills the nebula, and she becomes the center of her own solar system, destined to warm planets and support life.

The story concludes with Stella’s transformation into the Sun, her light becoming a lasting legacy written across the universe.

A brief mythological section introduces Astraea, the Greek “Star-Maiden” and goddess of justice and purity, symbolizing the celestial ideals of virtue and light that parallel Stella’s journey.

projectDetails.summary:
AirWatch is an AI-driven air quality monitoring and forecasting platform built using real-time satellite data from NASA’s TEMPO mission, along with APIs like OpenAQ, AirNow, and OpenWeatherMap. It visualizes pollution trends, predicts air quality levels, and provides actionable health and policy recommendations.

Using a React–Node.js–PostgreSQL stack, the system integrates live geospatial and meteorological data to generate dynamic AQI dashboards, alerts, and vulnerability-based insights. The platform empowers governments, researchers, and citizens with early warnings of hazardous air conditions, supporting cleaner, safer, and more sustainable environments.

By transforming complex atmospheric data into intuitive visual insights, AirGuardian directly addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge goal — bridging the gap between Earth observation data and meaningful action for public health and environmental resilience.
projectDetails.details:
AirWatch is an intelligent air quality monitoring and forecasting platform that transforms NASA’s TEMPO satellite data and global air quality sources (OpenAQ, AirNow, OpenWeatherMap) into real-time, actionable insights. It collects and processes atmospheric pollutant data such as NO₂, O₃, and PM2.5, then visualizes them through interactive maps, dashboards, and predictive graphs.

Built using React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend and Node.js, Express.js, and PostgreSQL on the backend, AirGuardian applies AI-powered forecasting models and geospatial analytics to predict air quality trends and health risks. Users receive dynamic alerts and community-level recommendations tailored to local conditions.

The project aims to support governments, researchers, and citizens in making data-driven environmental and health decisions, promoting cleaner air and sustainable urban planning.

Creativity lies in the fusion of satellite data, real-time APIs, and AI forecasting into a unified, accessible platform. Our team prioritized accuracy, accessibility, and scalability — ensuring the tool remains open, intuitive, and impactful in addressing global air pollution challenges.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our team used AI tools primarily to enhance data analysis, forecasting, and presentation rather than to generate original NASA assets or visuals. Specifically:

  • AI-powered modeling: Implemented machine learning algorithms for air quality prediction and pollution trend forecasting using historical satellite and ground-level data.
  • AI-assisted ideation and documentation: Utilized ChatGPT (OpenAI’s GPT-5) to assist in drafting documentation, technical summaries, and refining code structure for efficiency and clarity.
  • No AI-generated images, videos, or NASA-branded materials were used. All visual elements in the platform and presentation were designed manually or derived from open datasets.
  • All AI-assisted text and code were reviewed, validated, and modified by the team to ensure originality, accuracy, and ethical compliance.

This approach allowed us to accelerate development, improve predictive accuracy, and maintain full creative and technical control over the project.
