projectDetails.name: Aurora Chaser: Life Under Space Weather
projectDetails.summary:
For this project, I developed a creative educational story titled Aurora Chaser: A Space Weather Story. The narrative is told from the perspective of Maya, a young photographer who chases auroras caused by space weather events such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Through her experiences, readers learn what space weather is, how it impacts Earth, and how it influences the lives and work of people in different fields—from photographers and pilots to farmers and engineers.

This project addresses the challenge of making complex scientific concepts like space weather relatable and engaging for students. By using storytelling, it connects real-world impacts—such as communication disruptions, GPS failures, and the creation of auroras—to everyday experiences.

It is important because space weather affects technology and daily life in ways that are often overlooked. Presenting the topic through a personal and visually compelling perspective helps inspire curiosity, build awareness, and make space science accessible to learners of all ages.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Aurora Chaser: A Space Weather Story, transforms complex space weather science into an engaging and relatable narrative. It works by combining storytelling, visuals, and educational content to explain phenomena such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and their impacts on Earth. Instead of abstract data alone, the project frames the science through the perspective of a young photographer, Maya, whose life and work are directly influenced by auroras and the challenges of space weather.

The primary benefit is accessibility—students and general audiences can connect scientific concepts to real-world experiences. This approach makes it easier to understand not only the beauty of auroras but also the risks space weather poses to technology, communication systems, and daily life.

The intended impact is to raise awareness about space weather, inspire curiosity about space science, and highlight its relevance to society. We developed the project using presentation tools and creative writing methods rather than heavy technical coding or hardware. However, the format can be expanded to include multimedia, animations, or interactive features in the future.

The creativity lies in turning data and science into a personal, humancentered story that resonates across age groups. Our team considered educational clarity, relatability, scientific accuracy, and storytelling appeal to ensure the project was both informative and inspiring.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
This project was guided entirely by human creativity and decision-making. While a large language model was consulted, its role was strictly supportive and never creative. All ideas, storylines, and final content were conceived, developed, and authored by our team.

The AI’s contributions were limited to:

  • Organizational Help: After our team generated all concepts and themes, the AI was occasionally used to sort through notes or assist with simple keyword checks.
  • Writing Assistance: Every section of the narrative was written by humans. At times, the AI was used in the way one might use a thesaurus—to suggest alternative phrasing or to confirm grammatical accuracy.
  • Proofreading: The AI provided light editing support, flagging typos or minor grammar issues, comparable to built-in tools in standard word processors.
  • Clerical Formatting: It was also used for basic formatting of summaries and slides to streamline document preparation.

projectDetails.name: Milo: Earth's Cosmic Visitor
projectDetails.summary:
In this project, we created an innovative educational storybook called "Milo: Earth's Cosmic Visitor", where we presented space weather through Milo, a coronal mass ejection (CME), to children and general audiences. The book describes the impact of space weather events like solar eruptions on Earth by causing auroras, interfering with satellites, GPS technology, power grids, and even astronauts in space. By combining science and storytelling, Milo's adventure is able to make such difficult concepts both entertaining and accessible.

This project solves the problem of science communication, particularly the challenge of describing intangible, vast cosmic phenomena to young audiences in a way that it seems close to them. Through storytelling and pictures, the project bridges scientific fact and human experience, like farmers observing GPS malfunctions or kids marveling at auroras.

Its value is in raising awareness of space weather—a natural but powerful force that impacts modern technology and everyday life. By presenting it as a story, the project stokes curiosity, scientific literacy, and wonder about the universe, inspiring future learners to explore the relationship between the Sun, Earth, and humanity.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details

Our project, “Milo: Earth’s Cosmic Visitor,” is an illustrated educational storybook designed to explain space weather and its effects on Earth in a fun, relatable way. The story follows Milo, a coronal mass ejection (CME), on his journey from the Sun to Earth. Through narrative and visuals, readers learn how CMEs interact with Earth’s magnetic field, creating auroras while also affecting satellites, GPS, power grids, and astronauts.

How it works:

  • The project simplifies scientific concepts using storytelling and characters.
  • Illustrations visualize Milo’s journey, helping audiences imagine phenomena that are otherwise invisible.
  • A structured 5-page story format balances science facts with engaging fiction.

Benefits:

  • Makes complex science accessible to children, students, and non-experts.
  • Encourages curiosity about astronomy, space weather, and Earth-Sun connections.
  • Supports teachers and science communicators by providing an approachable learning tool.

Intended Impact:
The project aims to improve public awareness of space weather, highlighting both its beauty (auroras) and challenges (technological disruptions). By sparking interest in young audiences, it fosters early scientific literacy and inspires the next generation of explorers and innovators.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Story development & editing: ChatGPT (for narrative structure, refinement).
  • Design & visuals: AI-based illustration tools to generate images of Milo, auroras, and cosmic scenes.
  • Presentation: Google Slides (for project formatting and sharing).

Creativity:
The project is creative because it transforms a highly technical scientific topic into a character-driven adventure that blends facts with imagination. By personifying a CME as “Milo,” the story creates an emotional connection to cosmic phenomena, making science memorable.

Factors Considered:

  • Scientific accuracy vs. storytelling simplicity.
  • Age-appropriate language for children while keeping facts intact.
  • Visual appeal through colorful imagery of auroras, space travel, and the Sun.
  • Real-world relevance—showing how space weather impacts farmers, pilots, astronauts, and everyday technology

  • Design Support: AI assisted in structuring the story into a 5-page illustrated storybook format, balancing text with visuals for maximum impact.

projectDetails.name: Project Galaxy Questers
projectDetails.summary: Exo System is an advanced telescope-integrated platform designed to detect, analyze& classify exoplanets using artificial intelligence. It connects with a telescope-like machine& provides users with an interactive touchscreen interface to scan and explore the night sky. The AI engine processes real-time telescope images to identify celestial bodies, distinguishing confirmed exoplanets, potential exoplanets& non-planetary objects with high accuracy. Then it calculates and displays essential planetary parameters like distance from Earth, orbital distance, orbital period, planetary size, radius, surface temperature, and the type of host star. Each planet is further classified as rocky, gaseous or icy giving users a clearer picture of its nature. A feature of the system is its habitability score, rated on a scale of 0 to 100, which considers orbital position, star type, estimated temperature, size, and potential for liquid water or atmosphere. This score is categorized into 5 ranges: very low, low, moderate, high and very high, enabling easy assessment of life-supporting potential. It also supports automatic image capture when exoplanets are identified, tagging each image with its calculated data and metadata for accuracy. The data are securely stored in cloud servers, providing backup and enabling users to access their findings anytime. The app maintains an observation log, recording the date, time, planetary data, images& habitability scores for future comparisons and analysis.

projectDetails.details:
🌍 NASA Space Apps Challenge Proposal

Project Title: Urban Vitality Dashboard — The A.C.T.I.O.N. Framework for Climate-Resilient Cities

---

🧩 The Challenge: Unsustainable Urban Growth Under Climate Change

Cities are growing faster than ever — but this growth is increasingly unsustainable.

Urban expansion intensifies heatwaves, floods, and pollution, while straining energy, water, and land resources. These environmental pressures translate directly into reduced human wellbeing, particularly in vulnerable communities.

🔑 Pain Points for Urban Planners

1. Siloed & Static Data – Reliance on outdated land-use maps, infrequent census updates, and isolated environmental datasets.

2. Reactive vs. Proactive Planning – Urban responses often occur after disasters like floods or heatwaves.

3. The Trade-off Fallacy – The belief that economic growth must come at the cost of environmental health.

4. Lack of Quantitative Wellbeing Metrics – Limited ability to measure neighborhood “health” beyond GDP or income.

---

🚀 Our Solution: The A.C.T.I.O.N. Framework

A data-driven urban planning system that integrates NASA Earth observation data to assess, correlate, target, implement, optimize, and nurture sustainable city development.

The framework powers the Urban Vitality Dashboard, an interactive decision-support platform for planners and the public.

---

🔬 A.C.T.I.O.N. Framework Breakdown

Phase Objective NASA Data Used Example Output

1. ASSESS Diagnose environmental & social baselines Landsat (LULC), MODIS (LST), GEDI (canopy height), GRACE-FO (groundwater), Sentinel-5P (air pollution) Heat, vegetation, water, and air-quality maps

2. CORRELATE Identify links between environment & inequality LST + income + health + flood data overlays "District X is 5°C hotter and 40% less green than average."

3. TARGET Prioritize intervention zones Composite indices of vulnerability Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) map

4. IMPLEMENT Design data-informed interventions Landsat & Sentinel-1 (SAR) for urban growth modeling Scenario modeling for new developments

5. OPTIMIZE Monitor outcomes & efficiency MODIS/VIIRS (night lights), SMAP (soil moisture), Landsat NDVI Real-time performance monitoring

6. NURTURE Engage & empower citizens Open data from dashboard Public portal for awareness & participation

---

🛰 NASA Earth Observation Data Utilized

Dataset Use Case

Landsat 8/9 (USGS) Land use/land cover, NDVI, urban heat mapping

MODIS (Terra/Aqua) Land surface temperature (LST) trends

Sentinel-2 (ESA) Fine-scale vegetation and impervious surface mapping

GEDI (ISS) Tree canopy height and urban green infrastructure assessment

GRACE-FO Groundwater and water resource stress

SMAP Soil moisture and water-use efficiency

Sentinel-5P (Tropomi) Air quality indicators (NO₂, PM2.5, CO)

VIIRS Nighttime lights as proxy for energy use and economic activity

Together, these datasets provide a continuous, global, and multidimensional picture of urban systems — enabling planners to see cities as dynamic, living entities.

---

🏙 Prototype: The Urban Vitality Dashboard

Core Features

🗺 Interactive Map Interface: Toggle layers such as Urban Heat Island, NDVI, Air Quality, Flood Risk, and Climate Vulnerability Index.

🔍 Scenario Planner: Users can draw new development zones and instantly visualize projected heat or vegetation impact.

📊 Real-Time Optimization: Track citywide trends via satellite data updates (NDVI, LST, night lights).

👥 Public Participation Module: Open dashboard for citizens to explore their neighborhood data and contribute to greening projects.

Prototyping Tools:

Google Earth Engine – Data preprocessing and analysis

Kepler.gl / Mapbox – Visualization

Python (Flask) – Backend modeling

React + D3.js – Interactive dashboard UI

---

🌡 Example Use Case: The “Heat & Inequity” Problem in Veridia City

1. ASSESS: Landsat data reveals extreme Urban Heat Islands (UHI) in low-income district Brickwell.

2. CORRELATE: Overlaid with income and health data → Brickwell has higher poverty, elderly population, and triple the heat-stroke cases of affluent Hilltop.

3. TARGET: Brickwell ranked #1 in Climate Vulnerability Index.

4. IMPLEMENT: Using GEDI canopy data and SMAP soil moisture, planners design a tree-planting and “cool roof” campaign.

5. OPTIMIZE: Two years later, Landsat LST shows a 2°C temperature drop and NDVI confirms canopy growth.

6. NURTURE: Citizens view improvements on the dashboard — fostering trust and ongoing engagement.

---

💥 Expected Impact

🌡 Reduce Urban Heat Islands by targeting green infrastructure in high-risk zones.

💧 Enhance Water Sustainability through GRACE-FO and SMAP-informed irrigation policies.

🌳 Improve Urban Livability by measuring wellbeing beyond GDP — through environmental, social, and health data integration.

🤝 Promote Climate Justice by identifying and addressing environmental inequities.

🛰 Advance NASA’s Mission by demonstrating real-world applications of satellite data for global urban resilience.

---

🧭 Next Steps

1. Develop a minimum viable product (MVP) dashboard prototype for one pilot city.

2. Integrate real-time data feeds from NASA APIs and Copernicus services.

3. Collaborate with urban planning agencies and citizen science groups to test usability.

4. Expand to regional and global scales through modular design and open-source deployment.

---

✳ Mission Statement

> “Urban Vitality Dashboard transforms NASA’s Earth data into an actionable compass for cities — ensuring that growth and wellbeing thrive together under a changing climate.”

projectDetails.name: Impactor 25
projectDetails.summary:
Impactor 25 is an interactive asteroid impact simulation platform. It lets users select real NASA-tracked asteroids or enter custom parameters, choose any location on Earth, and simulate the physical and societal effects of an asteroid impact. The app combines NASA data, physics-based calculations, and AI-powered analysis to estimate crater size, energy released, destruction radius, affected cities, and secondary effects like tsunamis and earthquakes. Results are visualized with dynamic maps and detailed breakdowns.

This project addresses the challenge of understanding and communicating asteroid impact risks by making complex science accessible and interactive. It supports education, outreach, and research, helping users explore “what if” scenarios and grasp both local and global consequences. Impactor 25 is important for raising awareness about planetary defense, fostering scientific literacy, and demonstrating the value of combining open data, physics, and AI for real-world challenges.
projectDetails.details:
Impactor 25 is an interactive web platform that simulates asteroid impacts on Earth using real NASA data, physics-based models, and AI-powered analysis. Users can select actual near-Earth asteroids or input custom parameters, choose any location, and instantly visualize the effects of an impact—including crater size, energy released, destruction radius, affected cities, and secondary effects like tsunamis and earthquakes.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Impactor 25 makes complex planetary science accessible and engaging for the public, educators, and researchers. It helps users understand the risks and consequences of asteroid impacts, supports science outreach, and raises awareness about planetary defense. By combining real data and advanced modeling, it empowers users to explore “what if” scenarios and fosters scientific literacy.

Tools & Technologies:

  • Next.js and React for the frontend and UI
  • Tailwind CSS for styling
  • Framer Motion and GSAP for animations
  • NASA NEO API for asteroid data
  • Google Gemini API for AI-enhanced impact analysis
  • Custom physics models for calculations

Creativity & Team Considerations:
The project creatively blends open data, physics, and AI to deliver accurate, visually compelling simulations. The team focused on clarity, accessibility, and scientific rigor, ensuring results are both reliable and easy to understand. The UI uses a modern, monochrome theme and the Orbitron font for a space-inspired look, while interactive maps and dynamic cards make the experience immersive and educational.

**How does it address the challenge?**

Mediguardian addresses the challenges faced by the elderly by providing:

* **Medicine Reminder System**: Allows users to set specific times for medication, sending mobile alerts to remind them.
Emergency Alert System: In case of a medical emergency, users can press a button to instantly send an SMS or email to pre-specified contacts, alerting family or caregivers for immediate help.
SOS Button: A quick distress signal that notifies contacts instantly.

Why is it important?
As the elderly population grows, ensuring their health and safety becomes paramount. The platform's user-friendly design ensures that elderly users can navigate without confusion, promoting independence and reducing reliance on others.
projectDetails.details:
Mediguardian is a user friendly web application designed specifically for senior citizens, with a focus on healthcare management ,medication reminders ,and emergency alert systems . The platform aims to support elderly users - especially grandparents - by ensuring they never miss important medications and have immediate access to help in emergency situations .

The project begins with a login/input page, where users are required to enter their Name ,Age , Disease, select whether they are a critical or normal medical case .This information helps personalize the features and ensure appropriate responses in case of emergency.

Once logged in, the user gains access to the main dashboard, which provides several key functionalities:

MEDICINE REMINDER SYSTEM :

Users can set specific times for taking medicines . When the time arrives, the system sends a ringing alert on their mobile to remind them.

SET MEDICINE TIMINGS:

This feature allows us to caregivers to schedule medicine times daily. It helps in maintaining consistency and avoiding missed doses.

EMERGENCY ALERT SYSTEMS :

In case of any medical emergency, users can press a button to instantly send an SMS or email to a pre- specified contact ,alerting family or care givers for immediate help .

🆘 SOS BUTTON :

The SOS button is the most important feature, allowing uses to send a quick distress signal with just one tap . It triggers emergency help and notifies contacts instantly.

Call ambulance - Direct access to ambulance services.

Food -A requested button for meals or care give us assistance .

Emergency button – Another quick access help button for non medical emergency.

Simple UI/UX tailored for elderly users.

projectDetails.name: A WORLD  AWAY HUNTING FROM EXOPLANET WITH AI
projectDetails.summary: In this project, we explored how artificial intelligence can help discover exoplanets—planets orbiting stars beyond our solar system. Using datasets provided by NASA, we analyzed light curves of distant stars to detect the tiny dips in brightness that indicate an exoplanet passing in front of its star. We implemented a machine learning approach, training a Random Forest Classifier to distinguish between stars with and without exoplanets. Our model processed and scaled the data, learned from patterns in stellar light curves, and successfully predicted potential exoplanet candidates. The final output was visualized as a Kepler-style diagram, highlighting detected exoplanet signals. This project demonstrates how AI accelerates the search for worlds beyond Earth, turning vast astronomical data into meaningful discoveries.
projectDetails.details:
🌌 Project Title: A Planet Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with Artificial Intelligence --- 🧠 Project Theme: Artificial Intelligence in Space Exploration --- 🪐 Problem Statement: With the vastness of our universe, billions of stars and planets exist beyond our solar system. However, identifying exoplanets (planets orbiting other stars) is a massive challenge due to the sheer volume of astronomical data. Traditional observation methods are slow and prone to human error. This project uses AI and Machine Learning to analyze light curve data from space telescopes like Kepler and TESS to detect exoplanets automatically and efficiently. --- 🎯 Project Objective: To develop an AI-based system capable of identifying potential exoplanets by analyzing light curves — graphs showing how a star’s brightness changes over time — using neural networks and pattern recognition techniques. --- 🔍 Key Idea: When a planet passes (or transits) in front of its host star, the star’s brightness dips slightly. By training an AI model to recognize these dips in light intensity, we can automatically detect planetary transits, helping astronomers discover new worlds faster and with higher accuracy. --- 🧩 Methodology: 1. Data Collection: Obtain light curve datasets from NASA’s Kepler or TESS missions. Each dataset contains time vs. brightness values for stars. 2. Data Preprocessing: Normalize the brightness values. Remove noise using signal processing techniques. Label known exoplanet data for training. 3. Model Development: Use a Neural Network (CNN or RNN) to identify transit patterns. Train the model with thousands of sample light curves. 4. Model Testing and Validation: Test on unseen star data. Evaluate accuracy, precision, and F1-score. 5. Visualization: Plot detected light curves and highlight possible transits. 6. Output: List of stars showing potential exoplanet signatures. Prediction confidence (e.g., 95% chance of exoplanet). --- 🧰 Tools & Technologies Used: Python TensorFlow / Keras – for neural network modeling Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn – for data handling and visualization Scikit-learn – for evaluation metrics Google Colab / Jupyter Notebook – development platform --- 🚀 Expected Outcome: An AI model capable of identifying exoplanets based on star brightness variations. Faster, more reliable detection of exoplanet candidates compared to traditional human analysis. A visual dashboard displaying the detected transits. --- 🌍 Impact: This project contributes to the field of astroinformatics by combining data science and astronomy. It can accelerate the discovery of Earth-like planets, advancing humanity’s quest to find life beyond our solar system. --- 👩‍💻 Team Members: Sanjay Kumar – Team Leader Gopal – Data Analyst Saran sadaippan – AI Model Developer

The RTX 4050 GPU accelerates neural network computations, significantly reducing training time. The combination of fast SSD storage and DDR5 memory ensures quick data loading and model performance during large dataset training. The system efficiently handles real-time visualization of light curves and transit plots.

projectDetails.details:
AeroCast: TEMPO Satellite-Powered Air Quality Forecasting

AeroCast is an end-to-end cloud-based platform for near real-time air quality forecasting, leveraging Machine Learning (ML) to fuse data from next-generation satellite instrumentation, ground-truth sensors, and hyperlocal weather conditions. Our goal is to provide timely, location-specific PM$_{2.5}$ predictions to empower proactive health decisions.

Key Innovations and Hackathon Deliverables

  1. Multi-Source Data Fusion Pipeline: We built a robust Python pipeline to ingest, clean, and align three disparate data sources:
    • TEMPO Satellite Data: Provides Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2​) column density (a key pollution precursor).
    • OpenWeatherMap: Supplies real-time weather features (temperature, wind speed/direction).
    • OpenAQ Ground Sensors: Provides PM2.5​ ground truth for model calibration.
  2. Spatial Machine Learning Core: Our system uses Haversine-based nearest neighbor search to accurately link satellite and weather data points to the closest available ground-truth sensor PM2.5​ measurements. This combined dataset is used to train a Linear Regression model that predicts future PM2.5​ levels.
  3. Deployable Web Service: The model is deployed via a Flask web backend (app_backend.py) that serves predictions to a dashboard frontend (index.html) featuring a Leaflet map. Users can click any location to immediately get an AQI forecast derived directly from the model output and nearest features.

Impact Statement

AeroCast demonstrates the rapid prototyping of an operational solution capable of transforming high-volume, global satellite data into actionable local health information. This system overcomes the scarcity of ground-based air quality sensors by using ML to translate ubiquitous satellite observations into precise ground-level predictions.

Technologies Used

  • Data/ML: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn (Linear Regression, BallTree for spatial search).
  • APIs: OpenAQ, OpenWeatherMap, TEMPO (.nc file handling).
  • Deployment: Flask (Backend), HTML/JavaScript/Tailwind CSS/Leaflet (Frontend).

projectDetails.name: Project Guardians of Galaxy
projectDetails.summary: This project presents "Flara’s Visit from the Sun," a simple and engaging story for children aged 8–15 that explains space weather and its effects on Earth. The story follows Flara—a playful spark from the Sun—as she travels to Earth as a solar flare, interacts with Earth's magnetosphere, and touches the lives of astronauts, pilots, farmers, and power grid operators. By weaving scientific concepts into a friendly narrative, the project makes complex topics like solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and their impact on technology and daily life easy to understand for young readers. This approach addresses the challenge by bridging the gap between technical heliophysics and everyday experiences, sparking curiosity while helping students recognize the real-world importance of space weather. Understanding space weather is crucial as it affects communication systems, navigation tools, electrical grids, and even creates the beautiful auroras, directly connecting children’s lives to the Sun’s distant activity.
projectDetails.details:
This project uses storytelling to teach children about space weather and its effects on people and technology. The story explains how energy from the Sun, like solar flares, travels to Earth and interacts with our planet’s protective magnetosphere. As the character Flara journeys from the Sun to Earth, young readers see how space weather can impact astronauts in space, pilots flying planes, farmers using GPS, and workers maintaining power grids. The narrative highlights both problems (technology interference) and wonders (auroras) caused by space weather.

The main benefit is making complex science easy and interesting for children, helping them relate solar activity to their own world. The project encourages curiosity and awareness of how the Sun and space weather affect everyday life. Its intended impact is to improve science literacy among children and help them see connections between space and Earth.

This digital story was designed for use in presentations and e-learning. Text was crafted using clear, simple language and divided into sections for easy adaptation to slides. Illustrations can be added using drawing tools or software like PowerPoint, Canva, or children’s art applications. No advanced coding or hardware is required; the project leverages creative writing and basic digital illustration.

Creativity came from turning heliophysics into a personal adventure through a character kids can identify with, making science feel friendly and close to home. The team focused on clarity, relevance, age-appropriate language, and storytelling appeal to ensure the project would inspire young learners.
projectDetails.aiReferences: AI was used to develop this project by generating the narrative content, simplifying scientific concepts, and organizing the story into age-appropriate language and sections. AI also assisted in structuring the story for use in presentations and providing clear summaries and project details. These AI-generated elements helped transform complex heliophysics ideas into a creative, engaging, and easy-to-understand story for children.

“The Blue Dot”
The Blue Dot is a literature-based storytelling project inspired by NASA’s breathtaking imagery of Earth and space exploration. It tells the story of a small satellite named Hope-3 that, after drifting through the darkness of space, turns back and rediscovers our planet — sending a final message: “Home detected.” Through short narration, visuals, and sound, the project connects science and emotion, reminding humanity of the beauty and fragility of our only home. By using NASA’s open data and real imagery from missions like Voyager and Apollo, The Blue Dot blends creativity with technology to inspire curiosity and a deeper appreciation for Earth among people of all ages.
projectDetails.details:
Project Title: The Blue Dot

Team Members: Neeraj V V (Leader), Alan Sebastian, Alwin, Amal

Project Overview:
The Blue Dot is a literature-based storytelling project inspired by the true journey of Voyager 1 and its final observations of Earth. Through the fictional satellite Hope-3, we dramatize Voyager 1’s last moments, culminating in the timeless message: “Home detected.” Using NASA’s open-source imagery and archival data, we blend science with emotion, creating a cinematic narrative that inspires curiosity and reflection on the fragility of Earth.

Objectives:

- Highlight Voyager 1’s mission and significance.

- Translate scientific data into an accessible, emotional story.

- Inspire interest in space exploration and environmental awareness.

- Demonstrate creative use of NASA imagery and data.

Neeraj V V: Led the project, conceptualized the narrative, aligned scientific data with creative storytelling, and managed the final presentation.
Alan Sebastian: Researched Voyager 1, compiled mission data, and ensured accuracy in visuals and narrative.
Alwin: Designed visuals, slides, and presentation flow, integrating images with the narrative.
Amal: Handled audio, narration, sound effects, and synchronized voiceovers with visuals.

Collaboration:
The team maintained continuous communication, holding brainstorming sessions and coordinating research, visuals, and audio to ensure a polished, cohesive project.

Outcome:
The Blue Dot successfully combines science and storytelling, evoking reflection on Earth’s beauty and fragility. The team’s collaboration and expertise produced a compelling, scientifically accurate, and emotionally engaging submission for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

projectDetails.name: Backwater Guardian: Vembanad Lake - A Satellite-Based Screening Tool to Guide Water Quality Investigations
projectDetails.summary: Backwater Guardian is a satellite-based screening tool developed to enhance water quality monitoring in Vembanad Lake. Traditional manual sampling methods are slow, costly, and cover only limited areas, making it difficult to detect pollution or algal blooms in time. This project uses Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite data processed through Google Earth Engine to identify potential problem zones using spectral indices such as NDWI for water detection, NDCI for algal concentration, and additional indicators for turbidity and anomalies. The results are visualized through an interactive Streamlit dashboard, allowing field teams to efficiently locate and prioritize sampling sites. By transforming monitoring from random sampling to intelligence-driven fieldwork, Backwater Guardian saves time and resources while enabling early warning of water quality issues.
projectDetails.details:
The Backwater Guardian project is a satellite-based tool designed to assist in the monitoring of water quality in Vembanad Lake, India, by leveraging advanced geospatial technologies and satellite imagery. The tool uses data from the Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites, which provide high-resolution (10-meter) imagery every five days, enabling near real-time monitoring of the lake's water quality. The core functionality of the project revolves around using spectral indices such as the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) and the Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI), which allow for the identification of water bodies and the detection of algal blooms. In addition to these, the system flags turbidity and anomalies in water quality using data from the red and near-infrared (NIR) bands of the satellite imagery.

The project operates on the Google Earth Engine platform, which processes vast amounts of satellite data, making it possible to generate cloud-free composite images for analysis. This platform also enables the efficient identification of potential hotspots where water quality issues are most likely to occur, thus helping field teams focus their sampling efforts on priority areas rather than conducting exhaustive manual checks across the entire lake. The results are presented through a user-friendly web dashboard, built using Streamlit, which visualizes spatial and temporal data, helping researchers and conservationists make informed, data-driven decisions.

The Backwater Guardian tool has significant benefits. Primarily, it improves the efficiency of water quality monitoring by reducing the need for costly and resource-intensive field sampling. Traditional monitoring methods often struggle to keep up with the vast expanse of large water bodies like Vembanad Lake, where manual data collection can be slow and limited. By providing a real-time, intelligence-driven solution, the project optimizes resource allocation, helping field teams focus on areas that require urgent attention. The tool also supports early warning by identifying potential water quality issues before they become visible crises, such as algal blooms, turbidity, or pollution events, allowing for proactive intervention.

The intended impact of the project is to transform water quality monitoring from a reactive, labor-intensive task into a proactive and efficient process. This will lead to smarter resource management, reducing operational costs while enhancing the effectiveness of conservation efforts. It also holds the potential for scaling to other water bodies worldwide, improving freshwater management in regions where monitoring is challenging due to limited resources or large areas to cover.

The tools and technologies used in the development of Backwater Guardian include Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite data, Google Earth Engine for processing and analysis, Streamlit for creating the interactive dashboard, and Python for coding the backend and integrating the data. The backend is responsible for fetching and processing the satellite data, conducting analysis, and transforming the results into actionable insights. This includes implementing algorithms to calculate indices like NDWI and NDCI, as well as anomaly detection to flag areas requiring field attention. On the frontend, the Streamlit framework provides a simple yet powerful interface for displaying maps, charts, and actionable insights, ensuring that the tool is user-friendly for field teams with limited technical experience. The dashboard allows users to visualize potential hotspots, track temporal changes in water quality, and prioritize areas for field visits.

The project is also designed to be scalable and collaborative, with future plans to work with local agencies to calibrate the system using ground-truth measurements, enhancing the accuracy of the predictions. The creativity of the project lies in its ability to harness satellite data and geospatial analysis to address a local environmental problem, which traditionally relied on manual and limited monitoring methods. By combining satellite-based data collection with real-time decision-making tools, the project offers a unique, scalable, and data-driven solution to water quality monitoring in Vembanad Lake and beyond. Factors such as resource constraints, user-friendliness, and scalability were central to its development, ensuring that it can be easily adopted and expanded for wider use.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch – Turning NASA Space Data into Early Warnings for Harmful Algal Blooms
projectDetails.summary:
Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) are growing rapidly across oceans, lakes, and rivers due to pollution and climate change. These blooms threaten marine life, fisheries, tourism, and human health by releasing toxins and depleting oxygen in water.

BloomWatch is a web-based monitoring and early-warning platform that integrates NASA satellite data (MODIS Aqua and VIIRS) with citizen science inputs to detect and forecast harmful algal blooms in near real time. Using satellite-derived chlorophyll concentration, ocean color, and AI-based pattern recognition, BloomWatch identifies bloom risk zones and visualizes them on an interactive map dashboard.

The platform also enables citizens to submit on-ground photos and observations, strengthening the validation of NASA data and promoting community engagement. By combining space-based data and local insights, BloomWatch aims to Predict, Protect, and Prevent — safeguarding water quality, ecosystems, and livelihoods.
projectDetails.details:
Project Description: BloomWatch – Turning NASA Space Data into Early Warnings for Harmful Algal Blooms

Overview
BloomWatch is a web-based monitoring and early-warning system that detects and predicts Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) by integrating NASA satellite data, AI-based analysis, and citizen science reports. It transforms space-borne chlorophyll and ocean color data into actionable insights for environmental agencies, researchers, and the public.

How It Works

  1. Data Integration: BloomWatch collects and visualizes satellite data from NASA’s MODIS Aqua and VIIRS missions through NASA Worldview. These datasets show chlorophyll concentration and color variations that indicate possible bloom activity.
  2. AI-Based Prediction: A simple machine-learning model (prototyped in Python) analyzes pixel color intensity and chlorophyll values to estimate bloom probability in a given water region.
  3. Citizen Reporting: Users can upload local water photos, coordinates, and short descriptions through the web interface, helping validate NASA data in near real time.
  4. Visualization Dashboard: All bloom detections appear on an interactive map that displays risk levels, severity filters, and recent alerts.
  5. Early Warning Alerts: When bloom probability crosses a threshold, the system flags the area as “High Risk,” enabling early response and awareness.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • 🌊 Environmental: Enables early action to reduce ecosystem damage and fish kills.
  • 💧 Public Health: Provides timely alerts to prevent human exposure to toxic waters.
  • 💼 Economic: Protects fisheries and tourism industries from bloom-related losses.
  • 🌍 Global Insight: Supports climate monitoring and contributes to UN SDG 6 (Clean Water) and SDG 14 (Life Below Water).
  • 🧠 Educational: Encourages citizen participation and data literacy in environmental monitoring.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Figma – UI/UX prototype design
  • HTML / React (optional demo) – frontend mock-up
  • NASA Worldview & EarthData – satellite visualization and data retrieval
  • Google Earth Engine (planned) – for chlorophyll time-series analysis

No external hardware was used; all components are software-based for accessibility and scalability.

Creativity and Design Approach
Our team designed BloomWatch to merge space technology and community science. The creative element lies in linking NASA’s large-scale satellite data with on-ground citizen inputs, forming a hybrid system that is predictive, participatory, and planet-focused.

We prioritized:

  • Usability – simple dashboard and reporting interface
  • Scientific credibility – real NASA data and indicators
  • Scalability – modular design that can expand to other environmental hazards (oil spills, coral bleaching, etc.)

Vision

“To transform space data into actionable insights that protect water, life, and the planet.”
Predict • Protect • Prevent

BloomWatch was entirely designed and developed using Figma for the user interface and prototype screens.

AI was used only for idea structuring and text drafting during documentation and presentation preparation. Specifically, OpenAI’s ChatGPT was used to help refine descriptions and improve clarity in project summaries and presentation slides.

No AI-generated images, audio, or video content were used. All visuals were created manually in Figma or sourced directly from official NASA Worldview satellite imagery.

projectDetails.summary: LeafBot is an AI-driven solution designed to monitor and enhance air quality using intelligent insights from plant-based data. projectDetails.details:
Our project LeafBot is an AI-powered web application created to promote sustainable living by identifying the most effective air-purifying plants. It helps users choose the right plants to improve indoor and outdoor air quality by analyzing environmental factors such as pollutant levels, oxygen release capacity, and surrounding conditions. By using scientific data from NASA’s Clean Air Study along with extended plant datasets, LeafBot recommends species that can significantly reduce harmful pollutants and increase oxygen levels, contributing to a cleaner and healthier environment.

The application uses machine learning models built with Python and scikit-learn to analyze plant data and provide intelligent recommendations. Its interactive interface, developed using Flask, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, allows users to easily explore plant information through data visualizations powered by Power BI. These visual insights help users understand the environmental benefits of each plant, making scientific information accessible and engaging for the general public.

Our team designed LeafBot with the goal of merging technology and environmental awareness to inspire real-world change. By integrating AI, data analytics, and sustainability, LeafBot goes beyond just being a web app—it becomes an educational platform that encourages green choices. Ultimately, the project aims to support community well-being, raise environmental consciousness, and foster a future where technology and nature work together to restore ecological balance.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used Artificial Intelligence tools to enhance both the data processing and analytical capabilities of our project LeafBot. The core of our system relies on AI-based models trained using scikit-learn, which analyze extensive plant datasets to identify and recommend the most effective air-purifying species. These models consider multiple environmental parameters such as pollutant type, air quality index, and oxygen release rate to deliver accurate and meaningful plant suggestions tailored to user needs.

projectDetails.name: Project HASHIRAS
projectDetails.summary:
Aerthys-The aqi partner

Air pollution is one of the most pressing challenges for public health today, affecting millions globally. Our project transforms NASA’s TEMPO satellite observations into actionable air quality forecasts, helping people plan their day safely and limit exposure to harmful pollutants.

TEMPO, launched by NASA, provides high-resolution hourly observations of air pollution across North America, allowing us to see real-time atmospheric conditions in unprecedented detail. We combine this satellite data with historical trends to train a Random Forest machine learning model, which predicts air quality for the next 24 hours. The predictions are simple and intuitive: Good, Moderate, or Hazardous, so anyone can understand and act on the information.

To make our forecasts meaningful, we display hourly trends, enabling users to plan outdoor activities safely. While the current system runs locally, the design is scalable to cloud platforms, so it can process massive datasets from TEMPO and provide real-time predictions for larger regions.

What makes our solution truly impactful is the direct benefit to human health. By providing clear, reliable air quality forecasts, we empower communities to protect themselves and their families, making our cities safer and more informed.

In short, our project bridges NASA’s TEMPO satellite data with everyday public health action, turning complex satellite information into a lifesaving, practical tool.

Probability of temperatures exceeding a heat threshold

Likelihood of heavy rain or high wind

Discomfort index based on temperature and humidity

web-based platform that helps users evaluate the likelihood of extreme or uncomfortable weather conditions for any selected date and location. StellarCast is a web platform developed by Team Hasta la Vista for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025.

The team developed a solution combining a Lunar Weather Forecast and a Moon Phase Calendar. The platform aims to solve the challenge of making lunar observation accessible and educational by consolidating hard-to-find, real-time lunar data and viewing conditions in one place.

What Was Developed?

StellarCast features two main modules:

    The Moon Phase Calendar displays the moon phase for each date with names (e.g., New Moon, Full Moon) in a simple, interactive interface, helping users plan observations.

The Lunar Weather App displays temperature, humidity, cloud cover, and visibility using NASA Open APIs for real-time data, enabling users to make informed decisions for outdoor activities.

Addressing the Challenge

StellarCast addresses the challenge by providing a platform built for clarity and connection with the cosmos. It makes complex lunar concepts easier to visualize and understand, and delivers an activity-specific weather forecast by interpreting data relevant to the user's need for lunar observation.

Importance

The project is important because it makes space and lunar science engaging for the public and aids educators, astronomers, and enthusiasts globally. It's described as "Bringing the Moon closer — through weather, data, and design".

projectDetails.summary:
Guardian Angel Emergency Response System

Our team developed a comprehensive real-time emergency response platform that revolutionizes how emergency services coordinate and respond to critical situations. The system features four distinct role-based dashboards: Citizens can instantly report emergencies and receive safety alerts, Dispatchers manage incoming calls and coordinate resources, Drivers navigate optimized routes with live tracking, and Hospitals prepare for incoming patients with real-time updates.

Our platform addresses critical challenges in emergency response: delayed communication, inefficient resource allocation, and lack of real-time coordination between stakeholders. By integrating live ambulance tracking, interactive maps with user geolocation, and real-time data synchronization, response times are significantly reduced while improving coordination accuracy.

This system is vital because every second counts in emergencies. Traditional systems rely on fragmented communication channels, leading to delays that can cost lives. Guardian Angel creates a unified ecosystem where all stakeholders have instant access to critical information, enabling faster, more coordinated emergency responses that save lives.
projectDetails.details:
What it does and how it works: Our Guardian Angel system is a real-time emergency response platform that creates a unified communication network between four key stakeholders: citizens, emergency dispatchers, ambulance drivers, and hospitals. The system operates through role-based dashboards with live map integration, enabling instant emergency reporting, real-time ambulance tracking, and coordinated response management. Citizens can report emergencies with one click, dispatchers can assign and track ambulances in real-time, drivers receive optimized navigation with live updates, and hospitals can prepare resources based on incoming patient data.

Benefits and intended impact: The platform dramatically reduces emergency response times by eliminating communication delays and coordination gaps. Real-time data sharing ensures all stakeholders have instant access to critical information, leading to faster medical interventions and potentially saving lives. The system also optimizes resource allocation, reduces ambulance idle time, and provides hospitals with advance patient preparation time, ultimately improving overall emergency care quality and efficiency.

Technology stack:

  • Frontend: React 19.2.0 with modern hooks and state management
  • Routing: React Router DOM for seamless navigation
  • Maps: Leaflet.js with React-Leaflet for interactive real-time mapping
  • UI Components: Lucide React icons with custom Tailwind-inspired styling
  • Real-time simulation: Custom JavaScript classes mimicking WebSocket behavior
  • Development tools: Create React App, npm package management
  • Version control: Git with comprehensive commit history

Creative innovations: Our team implemented several creative solutions: live ambulance trail visualization showing movement history, dynamic status indicators with real-time updates, user geolocation integration for precise emergency reporting, and a realistic data simulation system that mimics real-world emergency scenarios. The role-based authentication system automatically redirects users to specialized dashboards, creating an intuitive user experience tailored to each stakeholder's needs.

Factors considered by our team: We prioritized user experience across different roles, ensuring each dashboard provides relevant information without overwhelming users. Performance optimization was crucial for real-time updates, so we implemented efficient state management and selective re-rendering. Accessibility considerations included clear visual indicators, intuitive navigation, and mobile-responsive design. We also focused on scalability, designing the architecture to easily integrate with actual backend APIs and real emergency services databases when deployed in production environments.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
No AI-Generated Media:

  • No AI-generated images, videos, or audio were used in this project
  • All visual designs and UI layouts were created by the development team
  • Map integration uses standard Leaflet.js library without AI-generated content

Transparency Statement: AI tools were used as programming assistants to accelerate development and provide code suggestions, but all core concepts, user experience design, emergency response logic, and system architecture were entirely conceived and designed by our development team. The AI served as a coding productivity tool rather than a creative or conceptual contributor.

Our project, “Data Pathways to Healthy Cities and Human Settlements,” focuses on using Earth observation (EO) and urban data to improve the health, sustainability, and livability of urban areas. projectDetails.details:
The project "Data Pathways to Healthy Cities and Human Settlements" focuses on leveraging data and technology to improve the health, well-being, and sustainability of urban environments.

Function and Mechanism

The project works by creating an integrated data ecosystem that collects, processes, and analyzes diverse datasets related to urban life and public

  • Data Collection: Gathers information from various sources, including IoT sensors (air quality, noise levels, traffic), administrative data (hospital records, city planning documents), social media, surveys, and satellite imagery.
  • Data Pathways: Uses data pipelines to ensure secure, standardized, and real-time flow of information into a central data warehouse or cloud-based platform.
  • Analysis and Modeling: Employs machine learning (ML) and geospatial analysis to identify patterns, predict health risks (e.g., pollution hot spots, disease outbreaks), model the impact of urban policies (e.g., new park construction), and generate actionable insights.
  • Visualization and Dissemination: Presents complex data through interactive dashboards and easy-to-understand visualizations for policymakers, urban planners, healthcare providers, and the public.

projectDetails.name: SPACE FARMING: An Intelligent Microgravity Growth Controlling System   Mimicking neural intelligence in plant tropic response
projectDetails.summary: The presentation “Space Farming: An Intelligent Microgravity Growth Controlling System” This explores how plants can be cultivated in space or on Mars using an AI-based growth simulation system. It begins by explaining gravitropism, where plants on Earth use gravity to guide root and shoot growth, and how in microgravity, this mechanism fails, causing disoriented growth. To study this, scientists use a clinostat to simulate zero gravity by rotating plants continuously. The project proposes an Intelligent Plant Growth System that uses sensors, AI, and computer vision to control factors like light (phototropism), touch (thigmotropism), and water (hydrotropism), allowing optimal growth even in microgravity. The setup includes a growth chamber with automated nutrient delivery, disease detection, pollination assistance, and circadian rhythm synchronization with Mars’ day-night cycle. Overall, it envisions a self-sustaining smart greenhouse that mimics natural growth stimuli to make sustainable space farming possible on Mars or future space stations.
projectDetails.details: Our project, SPACE FARMING: An Intelligent Microgravity Growth Controlling System, is designed to simulate and guide plant growth in microgravity environments by mimicking neural intelligence in plant tropic responses. It works by integrating AI-driven control of phototropism, hydrotropism, and thigmotropism within a sealed protective dome, using sensors, computer vision, and machine learning to monitor and adjust environmental variables like light, moisture, and nutrients in real time. This system benefits space missions by enabling sustainable agriculture in zero-gravity conditions, supporting long-term human habitation on Mars or the Moon. The intended impact is to revolutionize space farming by ensuring reliable food production beyond Earth, leveraging Mars’s Earth-like day cycle and resource-rich regolith. We developed the project using tools like high-resolution cameras, nutrient sensors, AI algorithms, and a clinostat to simulate microgravity, with coding likely in Python and embedded systems for automation. Creativity shines through our use of intelligent stimuli simulation, automated pollination, and multi-plant coordination. Our team considered factors such as plant physiology, space constraints, environmental hazards, and the need for closed-loop autonomy to ensure resilience and scalability in extraterrestrial agriculture.

projectDetails.name: Project Hydrofusion
projectDetails.summary: "Appachan and the Sun's Sneeze" is a heartwarming tale of resilience, tradition, and intergenerational learning. When a solar flare disrupts Thomas Appachan's GPS-guided tractor, Jumbo, he turns to traditional farming methods learned from his childhood in Kerala, India. With his granddaughter Maya's help, Appachan uses his fingers to check soil moisture and a rope to plant straight rows. Despite the setback, they successfully plant pepper seeds and irrigate the dry patches. The story highlights the impact of space weather on modern technology and the importance of preserving traditional skills. Appachan's experiences showcase the value of combining modern technology with traditional wisdom. The bond between Appachan and Maya is a central theme, as they work together to overcome challenges and learn from each other. The story celebrates the human spirit, intergenerational learning, and the importance of traditional knowledge in modern times. It's a delightful tale of resilience, adaptability, and the power of human ingenuity.
projectDetails.details:
Modern farms today use advanced technologies like GPS-guided tractors, satellite-based navigation, and soil sensors to increase efficiency and reduce waste. GPS, or Global Positioning System, works through signals sent from satellites orbiting Earth. These signals help tractors drive in straight lines, plant seeds accurately, and deliver the right amount of water and fertilizer to each section of the field. Soil moisture and nutrient sensors collect real-time data from the ground, helping farmers decide when and where crops need irrigation or care.

This combination of satellite guidance and smart sensors is known as precision agriculture. It saves time, fuel, and resources while improving crop yield and protecting the environment. Farmers can cover large areas quickly and use fewer inputs like water and fertilizer, reducing both cost and pollution. In addition, GPS mapping helps track crop growth and detect problems early. Overall, these technologies make farming more sustainable, data-driven, and productive by combining scientific innovation with practical decision-making, ensuring food security for the future.

projectDetails.summary:
Our solution transforms complex Earth and ocean data into immersive, interactive experiences that make scientific information accessible and engaging for everyone.
Using NASA’s open datasets, we create visual stories and VR simulations that allow users to explore changes from the depths of the oceans to the heights of the atmosphere.

Through data visualization, storytelling, and virtual reality, we help bridge the gap between scientific discovery and public understanding, inspiring action and awareness about our planet’s interconnected systems.
projectDetails.details:
🧠 1. What does it do or how does it work?

This project is an Arduino-based smart monitoring system designed to detect and alert users to environmental and safety hazards in real time.
It continuously measures:

  • Temperature and Humidity using the DHT11 sensor
  • Distance using the Ultrasonic sensor (HC-SR04) for obstacle or level detection
  • Fire/Flame presence using the Flame sensor
  • Vibration or shock using a Vibration switch sensor

When any abnormal condition is detected—such as high temperature, fire, vibration, or object detection—the buzzer and RGB LED provide audio-visual alerts. Data readings are displayed on a TM1637 4-digit display.

🌍 2. What benefits does it have?

  • Early Warning System: Detects fire, vibration (possible earthquakes or break-ins), or obstacles early.
  • Low Cost: Uses affordable components and simple wiring.
  • Automation: Reduces the need for constant human monitoring.
  • Scalable: Can be expanded to include more sensors (like gas or motion).
  • Educational Value: Helps students learn IoT and embedded systems concepts.

💡 3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to:

  • Enhance safety in homes, schools, and laboratories by providing real-time hazard alerts.
  • Promote awareness about environmental monitoring and smart safety systems.
  • Encourage innovation by demonstrating how simple electronics can solve real-world problems.

It can be applied in smart homes, industrial monitoring, and disaster management systems.

🛠️ 4. Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used

Hardware:

  • Arduino Uno R3
  • DHT11 Sensor (Temperature & Humidity)
  • Ultrasonic Sensor HC-SR04
  • Flame Sensor (IR-based)
  • Vibration Sensor (SW-420 or similar)
  • RGB LED Module
  • Active Buzzer
  • TM1637 4-digit Display
  • Jumper Wires and Breadboard

Software:

  • Arduino IDE
    • DHT.h for temperature & humidity
    • TM1637Display.h for display control

Programming Language:

  • C/C++ (Arduino programming language)

🎨 5. How is your project creative?

  • It combines multiple sensors into one unified monitoring system.
  • Uses color-coded RGB LED alerts (e.g., red for fire, blue for normal, green for safe).
  • Displays live readings in an easy-to-read digital format.
  • Can be enhanced with wireless modules (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth) for IoT applications.

⚙️ 6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Safety: Ensure electrical components are connected correctly.
  • Accuracy: Proper calibration of sensors.
  • Power efficiency: Use 5V components to minimize power use.
  • Ease of use: Simple display and buzzer alerts for quick understanding.
  • Scalability: Ability to add new sensors in the future (e.g., MQ135 for air quality).
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI tools (ChatGPT by OpenAI) to assist in the research, code generation, documentation writing, and idea refinement stages of our project. Specifically:

  • Code: AI was used to help generate and debug Arduino code for integrating multiple sensors (DHT11, Ultrasonic Sensor, Flame Sensor, Vibration Sensor, RGB LED, and Buzzer) with the Arduino Uno board.
  • Documentation: AI assisted in drafting and refining the project explanation, benefits, and technical descriptions.
  • Design Support: AI was used to brainstorm and structure system flow, data display logic, and component interaction.

All AI-generated content was reviewed, tested, and verified by the team to ensure accuracy, originality, and functionality. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were used or modified in AI-generated materials.

projectDetails.name: AirAware: Real-Time Air Quality Forecasting
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, AirAware, is a web-based platform that delivers real-time air quality maps and forecasts for North America.

We developed this solution to address the critical data gap that exists between sparse ground-level monitoring and broad satellite observations. AirAware addresses this challenge by integrating and fusing multiple data sources: NASA's high-resolution TEMPO satellite data, ground-based sensor data from networks like AirNow, and weather data from NOAA/NWS. Our processing engine uses machine learning models to combine these streams, generating accurate short-term (24-72 hour) air quality predictions.

This project is important because it transforms complex data into actionable insights for public health protection, allowing individuals to reduce their exposure to pollutants. It also provides data-driven tools for more effective environmental policy and enhances scientific research, ultimately empowering communities to breathe cleaner air.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

AirAware is a web-based platform designed to generate real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) maps and forecasts. It works by integrating multiple data sources and processing them through a four-step pipeline:

  • Data Collection: The system gathers data from three main sources:
    • NASA's TEMPO satellite for broad, hourly, high-resolution coverage of pollutants like NO2​, O3​, and aerosols.
    • Ground-based air quality sensors from networks like AirNow and the EPA.
    • Weather information from APIs provided by NOAA/NWS.
  • Processing & Fusion: Machine Learning models are used to combine and fuse these multi-source data streams.
  • Prediction Engine: The system generates short-term air quality forecasts for the next 24-72 hours.
  • Frontend Delivery: The forecasts are delivered to users through interactive maps, graphs, and notifications on the web platform.

What benefits does it have?

The project provides several key benefits:

  • Public Health Protection: It delivers early warnings that allow individuals, especially vulnerable populations, to reduce their exposure to air pollution.
  • Policy & Management: The platform provides data-driven insights that can be used for effective environmental management and regulatory decisions.
  • Research Enhancement: It serves as a powerful tool for researchers who model and study pollution using real TEMPO data.
  • Scalability: While designed for local use, the system can be scaled to provide continent-wide coverage.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The project's goal is to bridge the significant gap between satellite observations and real-time, ground-level air quality forecasts. The intended impact is to transform NASA's TEMPO data into actionable insights, empowering people and communities to breathe cleaner air.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

The core tech stack listed in the presentation includes:

  • Backend: FastAPI, Python, PostgreSQL
  • Frontend: React (Next.js)
  • Machine Learning: PyTorch, XGBoost
  • Mapping: Mapbox

How is your project creative?

The project's creativity lies in its approach to solving the problem of a "Data Gap". It creatively combines three distinct types of data—high-resolution satellite imagery (TEMPO), precise ground-level sensor readings (AirNow/EPA), and contextual weather information (NOAA/NWS)—and uses machine learning to fuse them into a single, accurate predictive model. This multi-source data fusion is an innovative way to create a more comprehensive and reliable air quality forecast than any single source could provide alone.

What factors did your team consider?

The team considered three primary challenges when developing the project:

  • Health Crisis: The fact that air pollution affects millions globally, leading to severe health issues.
  • Limited Monitoring: The problem that current ground stations are sparse and region-specific, which limits comprehensive coverage.
  • Data Gap: The significant gap that exists between satellite observations and real-time, ground-level air quality forecasts.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
• Data Fusion: The central use of AI is in the "Processing & Fusion" stage of the project's workflow. Machine Learning models are utilized to combine and fuse data from the project's multiple sources, which include NASA's TEMPO satellite, ground sensors, and weather APIs.
  • Specific Technologies: The project's core tech stack explicitly lists machine learning and deep learning tools. This includes XGBoost, a gradient boosting library, and PyTorch, a deep learning framework, both used within the Python programming language.
  • Future AI Implementation: The project's future roadmap includes plans to implement "Personalised AI Analysis". This feature intends to use AI-driven analysis to provide individualized pollution exposure risk assessments.

projectDetails.name: Eco Mars
projectDetails.summary: This Ecomars project is highly commendable for its thoughtful integration of sustainability and closed-loop systems, essential for long-term human survival on Mars. The innovative approach of converting human sweat, urine, and solid waste into water and fertilizer demonstrates practical resource recycling vital for self-sufficiency in an extraterrestrial environment.Additionally, incorporating small greenery plants not only supports oxygen production through photosynthesis but also enhances mental well-being for inhabitants by bringing a touch of Earth’s natural environment into the habitat.Using accessible materials like thermocol, cardboard, and aluminum foil for the model makes the concept tangible and easy to demonstrate, showing creativity and practicality in prototyping space habitation ideas.Overall, the project smartly combines ecological principles with space engineering concepts, positioning it as a valuable contribution toward sustainable human presence on Mars. This concept could inspire further developments and innovations in space habitat design.
projectDetails.details: This project imagines a conceptual Mars habitat that functions as an artificial natural ecosystem where human metabolic waste and Martian soil resources are recycled to sustain life-support systems. It includes subunits for converting sweat and urine into purified water, processing solid human waste into fertilizer, extracting water from Martian soil and purifying it for drinking, and growing plants within a controlled habitat. The habitat structure is envisioned as a closed-loop ecological system mimicked physically in a model made of thermocol, aluminum foil, glue, and plastic tape with labeled subunits showing flow and connection pathways.The purpose of this project is to creatively explore how a sustainable living environment might function on Mars, integrating biological and mechanical processes in a compact habitat. The model is meant for educational and conceptual demonstration, illustrating challenges and possible solutions for human survival in an extraterrestrial environment.It is important to emphasize that this project is based on fiction and creativity rather than current practical implementation or real-world engineering. It serves as a speculative exploration of ideas, inspired by ongoing research but assembled in an imaginative way to visualize potential closed-loop life support on Mars. The materials (thermocol and aluminum foil) and the simplified system units represent an abstract physical realization rather than a fully functional device or habitat.Thus, this project merges scientific thinking with artistic expression to communicate complex systems through an accessible physical model, fostering awareness and discussion about space habitation challenges while relying heavily on conceptual imagination rather than operational reality.Such fictional models and ideas often inspire real research but remain originally creative and educational tools rather than ready-to-deploy technologies .

projectDetails.name: Celestial Compass
projectDetails.summary:
We have developed Celestial Compass, an interactive web application designed to make astronomy accessible and engaging for everyone. The app allows users to explore upcoming celestial events visible from their location, track the International Space Station (ISS) in real time, and view NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD). Users can search for any city to receive location-specific event data, with events sorted by date and detailed information available via an interactive modal.

Celestial Compass addresses the challenge of connecting people with space phenomena in a simple and visually appealing way. By integrating real-time tracking, daily cosmic highlights, and location-based event information, it provides a comprehensive platform for users to explore the universe from their own home.

The project is important because it fosters scientific curiosity and astronomical awareness, turning complex space data into an engaging learning experience. Its responsive design ensures usability across devices, and interactive components encourage users to actively engage with the cosmos. By bridging the gap between raw astronomical data and user-friendly visualization, Celestial Compass inspires exploration, education, and a deeper appreciation for the universe.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:
Celestial Compass is an interactive web application that allows users to explore the cosmos from their own location. The app provides three main features:

  1. Sky Events: Users can search for any city to see upcoming celestial events, such as meteor showers, eclipses, and planetary alignments. Events are sorted by date and can be clicked to view detailed information in a modal.
  2. ISS Tracker: Displays the real-time location of the International Space Station on a map, letting users follow its path across the sky.
  3. Cosmic Feature of the Day: Fetches NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) to highlight significant cosmic phenomena, including images or videos with explanations.

Benefits and Impact:
The project makes astronomy accessible, educational, and engaging for the general public. By combining location-based data, real-time tracking, and daily cosmic highlights, it helps users develop a deeper understanding of space events and encourages curiosity about the universe. Its responsive and interactive interface ensures usability across devices.

Technical Details:

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS
  • State Management: useState, useEffect
  • APIs: Custom backend endpoints for APOD and event data
  • Other Tools: Modal popups, sortable event lists, interactive maps

Creativity and Considerations:
The project integrates multiple sources of space-related data into one unified platform, emphasizing user experience and visual appeal. Factors considered included ease of navigation, real-time accuracy, responsiveness, and making astronomy engaging for both beginners and enthusiasts.

projectDetails.name: URBAN ECHO – AI-Driven Digital Twin for Healthy & Resilient Cities
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a project that leverages NASA Earth observation data to address the challenge of balancing city growth with the wellbeing of both people and the environment amidst climate change. As climate change introduces new complexities in maintaining societal and environmental wellbeing in cities, monitoring natural resources, ecosystems, and infrastructure is crucial to ensure a high quality of life. With over half of the global population residing in cities, ensuring quality of life in these urban areas is vital.

Our project demonstrates how urban planners can utilize NASA Earth observation data to develop smart strategies for city growth. By integrating this data, urban planners can make informed decisions that promote sustainable development, minimize environmental impact, and enhance the wellbeing of city dwellers. This approach supports balanced growth by considering both human needs and environmental health, addressing the challenges posed by climate change in urban settings.
projectDetails.details:
URBAN ECHO is a digital twin platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into actionable insights for city planners. It fetches satellite data (heat, vegetation, air quality, rainfall, flooding, population), processes it with AI models, and simulates different urban growth scenarios. Planners can test “What-if” pathways (e.g., increasing green cover, smart density) and visualize results in an interactive dashboard, which also generates a City Health & Resilience Index.

Benefits:

  • Provides real-time urban health insights using NASA data.
  • Helps planners predict climate risks such as heat islands, pollution, and flooding.
  • Supports informed decision-making with scenario simulations.
  • Produces actionable policy recommendations for resilience and health.
  • Makes complex Earth data accessible and actionable through visual dashboards.

Intended Impact:

  • Enable sustainable, resilient, and healthy urban futures.
  • Help cities proactively address climate risks and improve public health.
  • Contribute to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for sustainable cities and climate action.
  • Scale globally to empower 50+ cities with data-driven urban planning.

Creativity:
URBAN ECHO is unique because it combines AI + Earth data + simulation into a single digital twin framework. The “What-if” simulator is innovative, allowing planners to explore interventions before implementation. The Health & Resilience Index translates technical data into understandable metrics for policymakers.

Factors Considered by the Team:

  • Scalability to global cities.
  • Usability for planners via intuitive dashboards.
  • Integration of citizen health data for localized accuracy.
  • Alignment with international datasets (WHO, UN-Habitat).
  • Long-term adaptability with predictive urban health alerts.

StellaFab represents a paradigm shift in space exploration, merging orbital manufacturing with advanced astronomical research in a single platform. It overcomes decades-old constraints—high costs, launch limitations, and inability to repair or modify space instruments—by moving manufacturing into orbit and creating modular, reconfigurable telescopes. This approach drastically reduces costs and expands access to space research.

For centuries, humanity has explored the cosmos with ever more sophisticated instruments, yet Earth’s gravity well has limited our capabilities. Rockets restrict size, introduce vibrations, and make launches costly. StellaFab eliminates these barriers by sending raw materials and manufacturing capabilities to space, building telescopes optimized for the orbital environment. This enables instruments of unprecedented scale and flexibility. These telescopes simultaneously conduct groundbreaking research across multiple disciplines, from exoplanet detection to galactic mapping, opening new frontiers in cosmic discovery.
