projectDetails.name: NASA Project AQI of Major Cities In India
projectDetails.summary:
Air pollution in India is a serious health threat, but reliable data is scattered and hard for citizens to understand. Our India AQI Dashboard solves this by presenting real-time and historical air quality data in a single, interactive web platform that is clear, actionable, and mobile-friendly.

The dashboard features an interactive map built with Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap, showing major Indian cities with color-coded markers representing PM2.5 and AQI levels (green for good, purple for severe). Users can click markers to see details or use a city dropdown or nearest city detection via geolocation to zoom in instantly.

A data table shows current PM2.5 and AQI values with pollution categories, updated automatically. A quarterly trend view lets users track seasonal changes with interactive Chart.js graphs and a toggle to switch between PM2.5 and AQI. Health advice cards provide real-time safety tips based on the worst air quality.

Users can download tables as CSV/JSON or export charts as PNG for research or sharing. Data is sourced from the OpenAQ API with fallback static JSON for offline stability.

Built with JavaScript, Node.js, Express, and OpenAQ, the platform helps citizens, researchers, and policymakers make informed decisions about air safety.
projectDetails.details:
🔹 What it does / How it works

Our India AQI Dashboard is a web-based platform that displays real-time and historical air quality data for major Indian cities. It collects PM2.5 readings from the OpenAQ API and converts them to AQI (Air Quality Index) using India’s official breakpoints.

  • An interactive map (Leaflet + OpenStreetMap) shows each city with a color-coded marker (green = good, purple = severe).
  • Users can click a city to view detailed PM2.5 & AQI values or use the dropdown or nearest city button (geolocation-based).
  • Charts (Chart.js) visualize quarterly PM2.5/AQI trends, with a toggle to switch between PM and AQI.
  • Health tips dynamically update based on the worst AQI detected.
  • Auto-refresh keeps data updated (default 24 hrs, customizable).
  • Data can be exported as CSV/JSON or charts downloaded as PNG.

🔹 Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Citizens: Plan outdoor activities safely and make health-conscious choices.
  • Researchers & NGOs: Quickly access and download structured AQI data.
  • Policymakers: Visual insights for monitoring pollution trends and policy action.
  • Awareness: Simple visuals help non-technical users understand complex air data.

🔹 Tools & Technologies Used

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6)
  • Mapping: Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap tiles + India GeoJSON
  • Charts & Data Visualization: Chart.js
  • Backend: Node.js + Express.js (API endpoint /api/air)
  • Data Source: OpenAQ API (live PM2.5 data) + fallback JSON for offline/demo
  • Deployment-ready: Can run locally or deploy to Railway / Vercel / Netlify

🔹 Creativity & Innovation

  • Combines multiple data views (map, tables, charts) in one intuitive dashboard.
  • Smart UX: nearest city detection using the Haversine distance formula.
  • Dynamic forecasting & health alerts for proactive user decisions.
  • Customizable auto-refresh intervals — ideal for hackathons or live demos.
  • Potential to scale into a mobile-friendly PWA or integrate heatmaps & ML-based predictions.

projectDetails.details:
Project Details:
NeuroAid is an AI-powered educational platform created to make learning science and space concepts easier and more engaging for people with dyslexia. It transforms complex NASA datasets into simplified, theme-based, and interactive lessons that combine text, audio, and visuals to match the learning styles of dyslexic individuals.

The platform works by processing NASA’s open data using Natural Language Processing (NLP) to simplify the content. It then presents it through voice-assisted narration, adaptive visuals, and dyslexia-friendly fonts with calming colors and proper spacing. Users can interact through reading, listening, or speaking modes, making learning more personalized and inclusive.

NeuroAid benefits learners by improving comprehension, focus, and interest in STEM fields while promoting accessibility and confidence in learning. Its intended impact is to make space and scientific education inclusive for neurodiverse communities, especially dyslexic learners who often struggle with traditional reading materials.

The project was developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Flask (Python), Hugging Face NLP models, OpenAI APIs, and NASA datasets from the Earth Observatory and Open Data Portal. Its creativity lies in the theme-based adaptive learning model, which connects scientific concepts with relatable stories and visuals to enhance understanding and retention.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):
AI was used in multiple stages of NeuroAid’s development to enhance accessibility, simplify content, and personalize learning experiences for dyslexic users.

  • Text Simplification: Natural Language Processing (NLP) models from Hugging Face and OpenAI were used to simplify complex NASA dataset descriptions into easier, dyslexia-friendly language.
  • Speech Processing: AI-powered text-to-speech and speech-to-text systems (pyttsx3 and OpenAI Whisper) were integrated to allow users to listen to lessons or interact through voice input.
  • Adaptive Learning: Machine learning logic was applied to adjust reading complexity, font size, and color contrast based on user feedback and attention span patterns.
  • AI-Generated Media: Audio narrations and supportive illustrations were created using AI tools, all clearly labeled and watermarked as AI-generated.
  • Code Assistance: ChatGPT was used for idea structuring, interface optimization, and accessibility feature refinement. All AI-assisted content was manually reviewed, edited, and verified by the team to ensure originality and compliance.

These AI tools helped accelerate creativity, inclusivity, and user accessibility while maintaining originality and human-centered design.

projectDetails.name: Project Kinderjoy
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary — Air Quality Forecasting & Safety Web App

Our project harnesses NASA’s TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) mission data to revolutionize air quality forecasting and public health awareness. By integrating real-time TEMPO satellite data with ground-based sensors and weather information, the web-based platform provides users with accurate air quality forecasts across all districts in Kerala. The system features live weather updates, 7-day AQI trends, and predictive pollutant movement mapping. A built-in health alert system notifies sensitive groups, while the school safety module automatically informs schools, colleges, and kindergartens about outdoor safety. Additionally, crisis response automation and compliance reporting tools empower institutions to take proactive, data-driven action—making communities safer, healthier, and more resilient to air pollution challenges.
projectDetails.details: How the Website Works The website functions as an intelligent air quality monitoring and forecasting system powered by NASA’s TEMPO mission data combined with ground-based sensors and real-time weather APIs. 1. Data Collection & Integration: The system continuously collects air quality parameters (PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, SO₂, CO) from NASA TEMPO satellite feeds and local monitoring stations across all Kerala districts. It also retrieves weather data such as temperature, humidity, visibility, and wind speed from trusted meteorological APIs. 2. Data Processing & Analysis: Using predictive algorithms, the platform analyzes pollutant movement, calculates AQI values, and forecasts 7-day trends. It also identifies potential pollution risks by tracking wind patterns and emission zones. 3. User Interface & Visualization: The processed data is displayed on an interactive dashboard that shows district-wise air quality, weather conditions, and forecast charts. Users can view real-time AQI levels and see color-coded indicators for easy interpretation. 4. Health Alert & School System: The system sends instant alerts to sensitive groups (such as asthma patients, elderly, and children) when air quality becomes unhealthy. Schools, kindergartens, and colleges receive automated notifications about whether outdoor activities are safe. 5. Crisis Response & Reporting: In the event of hazardous air quality, the system can trigger automated safety protocols (e.g., HVAC air intake closure) and generate time-stamped compliance reports for institutional use and insurance documentation.
projectDetails.aiReferences: Artificial Intelligence plays a vital role in making the Air Quality Forecasting & Safety Web App predictive, adaptive, and intelligent rather than just a static reporting system. 1. Predictive Air Quality Forecasting: AI models analyze historical and real-time data from NASA’s TEMPO satellite, ground sensors, and weather APIs to predict future AQI levels. Machine learning algorithms identify pollution patterns, estimate how pollutants move with wind and temperature, and forecast upcoming air quality trends for the next 7 days. 2. Micro-Risk and Plume Prediction: Using AI-based spatial modeling, the system predicts the movement and time-to-impact of pollutant plumes (e.g., wildfire smoke or industrial gas leaks). This allows the platform to suggest safe alternate routes or issue early warnings before the pollution reaches a certain area. 3. Health Alert Automation: AI classifies users into sensitive health groups (like children, asthma patients, or the elderly) and automatically sends personalized alerts based on predicted exposure risk. This ensures timely warnings and health protection. 4. Anomaly Detection & Data Validation: AI filters and validates incoming data from multiple sources to detect inconsistent or false readings, ensuring that only accurate, reliable data is shown on the dashboard. 5. Decision Support & Learning: Over time, the AI system learns from user interactions and environmental outcomes to improve its forecast accuracy and response efficiency, supporting smarter community and institutional decisions.

projectDetails.name: commercialising Low Earth Orbit
projectDetails.summary: Our project, SmartDebris: AI-Driven Space Debris Tracking for LEO Commercialization, addresses the growing challenge of space debris in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), which poses significant collision risks for the rapidly expanding satellite industry. Traditional debris tracking relies on large, expensive radar installations that are largely inaccessible to small businesses and startups, limiting participation in LEO commercialization. To solve this, we propose a software-based AI solution that leverages existing open-source and commercial debris tracking data to detect, classify, and predict the trajectories of space debris, including small objects under 5 cm. Our platform provides real-time predictive analytics and visualizations through a cloud-based dashboard and API, enabling affordable access to space situational awareness. By reducing infrastructure costs from hundreds of crores to just a few lakhs, our solution democratizes participation in the space economy, enhances LEO safety, and promotes sustainable space operations, all without the need for building costly radar systems.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Commercializing Low Earth Orbit: AI-Enhanced Debris Tracking, focuses on improving the way space debris is detected and monitored. It uses artificial intelligence together with existing radar, optical, and lidar sensors to identify and predict the movement of objects in Low Earth Orbit. By processing satellite data from EOSDA LandViewer through a YOLOv8 Nano AI model, the system provides real-time detection and gentle visual or vibration-based alerts for operators.

This approach makes debris tracking significantly more affordable—reducing costs by nearly 98% compared to traditional systems—and allows smaller organizations and research teams to participate in space safety efforts. Developed with Python, cloud-based AI tools, and GPU-supported computing, it offers flexibility, scalability, and easy integration with current systems.

Aligned with India’s IN-SPACe and NewSpace programs, the project supports sustainable and safe use of orbital space. Our team emphasized affordability, accuracy, and long-term environmental responsibility, designing a simple yet effective software solution for better space management and commercialization.

projectDetails.summary:
Interactive Asteroid Impact Simulation & Planetary Defense Command Center

Model asteroid impacts using real NASA data and test deflection strategies to save Earth from catastrophic collisions. It provides:

Impact Physics:
Calculate kinetic energy, crater diameter, and seismic effects using real-world scaling laws.

Deflection Strategies:

View orbital trajectories and impact points in an interactive 3D environment.
projectDetails.details:
1. Introduction

Website: lernaean-madness.netlify.app

Challenge: Meteor Madness, part of NASA Space Apps 2025.

Goal: Build a tool that lets people visualize and simulate asteroid impacts on Earth using real NASA data

2. The Problem it Solves

Real-world issue: Asteroids & meteors pose a planetary defense challenge. Even rare, a large impact could be catastrophic

Problem: complex data (orbits, sizes, impact probabilities) is difficult for the public and decision-makers to understand.

Solution: This web app pulls live asteroid data and shows impact scenarios visually — making risks easier to grasp.


3. How it Works (Workflow)

1. Data Source → NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) API provides asteroid details.


2. Data Format → JSON is used to transfer information to the app.


3. Frontend Logic → TypeScript + React components calculate trajectories and effects.


4. Visualization → Impact scenarios shown on maps/graphics (SVG, HTML, CSS).


5. Deployment → App is built with Node.js and hosted on Netlify for fast, global access.


4. Technology Stack

Category Languages / Frameworks Key Notes

Frontend TypeScript (TS/TSX), JavaScript Component-based (likely React/Next.js). Logic runs in the browser.
Styling CSS, HTML, SVG Standard styling & structure for visuals and interactivity.
Backend / Build Node.js Used for build tools, package management, and development runtime. No heavy backend.
API NASA NEO Data API Provides real asteroid/meteor information.
Data JSON Lightweight format for API communication.
Hosting Netlify Continuous deployment + static hosting.

5. Why These Choices?

React + TypeScript → Strong typing + component reusability for reliability.

NASA API → Real, trusted, scientific data source.

JSON → Simple, fast, universally compatible.

Netlify → Automatic deploys, fast hosting, supports JAMstack (perfect for hackathons).

SVG/HTML/CSS → Lightweight way to visualize impact zones, maps, and trajectories.


6. Impact & Relevance

Educational: Makes asteroid impact science accessible to students & public.

Decision Support: Helps agencies visualize risks more intuitively.

Public Engagement: Inspires awareness of space hazards and planetary defense.

Innovation: Shows how open NASA data can be turned into interactive, useful tools.


7. Conclusion

It’s a front-end heavy web app powered by NASA APIs.

Purpose: To simplify complex asteroid impact science into interactive simulations.

Real-world link: Planetary defense, awareness, and education.

Stack: TypeScript + React + NASA API + Netlify.

Why chosen: Space is exciting, asteroid impacts are critical, and NASA encourages innovative uses of open data

projectDetails.summary:
Lightning Loop is a smart, web-based event planning assistant that uses NASA’s open weather and hydrology data to help users organize outdoor events safely. It allows users to select a date and location, then instantly analyzes rainfall and temperature forecasts to calculate a simple weather-risk score — Safe, Watch, or Risk. The system displays this information on an interactive map and 14-day trend chart for clear, visual decision-making.

Built entirely using free tools such as Leaflet.js, Chart.js, and NASA resources like Giovanni, Data Rods, and Earthdata Search, Lightning Loop transforms complex satellite data into easy-to-understand insights. The platform also provides personalized weather advice and allows users to save and review planned events.

This project addresses the “Will It Rain?” challenge by turning NASA’s scientific data into a practical, everyday solution that empowers communities, schools, and organizers to plan smarter and safer events. By connecting space-based observations to daily human needs, Lightning Loop demonstrates how open data can make a real-world impact.
projectDetails.details:

Users can select any location and event date, and the system automatically retrieves rainfall and temperature data from NASA resources such as Giovanni, Data Rods for Hydrology, and Earthdata Search, as well as the Open-Meteo API for real-time forecasts.

The application processes this data to generate a weather risk score — Safe (Green), Watch (Yellow), or Risk (Red) — and displays the results on an interactive map. It also visualizes 14-day trends of precipitation and temperature through dynamic charts, helping users understand upcoming weather patterns. Users can save their planned events, receive quick weather-based advice, and review conditions before making outdoor decisions.

The project was built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Chart.js, and Firebase, relying entirely on free and open-source resources.

Lightning Loop’s key benefit is its simplicity — it turns complex NASA data into clear, actionable insights for everyday users. The intended impact is to help schools, communities, and event organizers minimize weather disruptions and improve safety.

projectDetails.details:
Overview

Focusedge is an advanced image enhancement platform designed to upscale low-resolution or compressed images into high-definition outputs without compromising quality. The software leverages artificial intelligence and deep learning–based super-resolution techniques to reconstruct fine details, enhance textures, and restore visual clarity.

How It Works

The system employs a deep convolutional neural network trained on thousands of high- and low-resolution image pairs. When a user inputs an image, Focusedge analyzes pixel patterns, edges, and color gradients to intelligently predict and generate missing details. The output is a significantly sharper, clearer, and higher-resolution version of the original image.

Key processes include:

  • Image preprocessing – normalization and noise reduction.
  • AI upscaling – Real-ESRGAN-based neural model for feature restoration.
  • Post-processing – fine-tuning contrast, color balance, and sharpness for realistic enhancement.

Benefits

  • Converts blurry or compressed images into crisp, print-ready visuals.
  • Saves time and cost by avoiding the need for professional manual retouching.
  • Restores legacy or archival photos for digital preservation.
  • Supports creative professionals, researchers, and content creators needing ultra-high-quality visuals.

Intended Impact

Focusedge aims to democratize access to professional-grade image enhancement tools by offering an efficient, automated, and intelligent platform. The project contributes to visual media restoration, scientific imaging, and content quality improvement in education, research, and design industries.

Tools and Technologies

  • Languages: Python, JavaScript
  • Frameworks & Libraries: PyTorch, OpenCV, Real-ESRGAN, FastAPI
  • Frontend: React.js for user interface and live preview
  • Backend: Python-based API for model inference
  • Hardware: GPU-accelerated system (NVIDIA CUDA support) for real-time processing
  • Version Control: Git & GitHub

Creativity and Innovation

Focusedge stands out for its hybrid AI model integration — combining real-time preview capability with batch-based high-fidelity rendering. The system’s adaptive learning algorithm detects image type (portrait, landscape, texture) and applies dynamic enhancement parameters, making it smarter and more context-aware than traditional upscalers.

Team Considerations

During development, the team prioritized:

  • Performance optimization for faster upscaling without quality loss.
  • User experience, offering a minimal yet powerful interface.
  • Cross-platform usability, ensuring compatibility across devices.
  • Ethical use of AI, particularly in handling real or sensitive images.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI Tool Utilization

Focusedge employs AI-based image super-resolution to upscale and enhance images. Specifically, the project uses Real-ESRGAN, an open-source deep learning framework for image restoration, which was integrated and customized to improve processing speed and output fidelity.

AI was used only as a technical enhancement tool — not for generating synthetic imagery or NASA-related visuals. All original project content (interface design, architecture, logic, and implementation) was created by the team.

Transparency and Attribution

  • AI-Generated Images or Previews:
    Any sample outputs produced by the model are marked with a visible “AI-Enhanced” watermark to indicate that they were processed using AI technology.
  • Code and Data:
    Project documentation and metadata include a statement acknowledging AI model integration (e.g., “This project uses the Real-ESRGAN AI model for image enhancement”).
  • No NASA Branding:
    Focusedge does not use, modify, or incorporate any NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers in its user interface, dataset, or generated outputs.

Intent and Originality

The intent of using AI in Focusedge is to demonstrate innovation in digital image enhancement and explore how AI-driven restoration can assist in applications like space image analysis, scientific visualization, and public data accessibility.
All algorithmic adaptations, interface design, optimization strategies, and system architecture are original contributions by the team.

Ethical and Responsible AI Use

The Focusedge team ensures:

  • Transparency in AI usage.
  • No misleading or fabricated image content.
  • Full compliance with NASA’s AI usage and attribution policy.

Our project, “Will It Rain in My Parade?”, is a mobile app built with Flutter that provides long-term climate predictions for outdoor events. The app estimates temperature trends, rainfall probability, and windspeed up to six months in advance, helping users plan festivals, parades, weddings, and agricultural activities with greater confidence.
We developed the app using a locally sourced climate dataset for prototyping, with a pipeline designed to integrate local dataset (in prototype)(NASA Earthdata in the future). The frontend, designed in Figma, offers an intuitive interface for users to select locations and dates and receive probabilistic climate insights.
This solution addresses the challenge by providing predictive weather information beyond the typical 7–10 day forecasts, reducing risks and improving decision-making for communities and event organizers. By making climate data accessible and actionable, our app empowers users to plan effectively, mitigate losses, and adapt to changing weather patterns.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, “Will It Rain in My Parade?”, is a Flutter-based mobile app designed to provide long-term climate predictions up to six months in advance. Users can select a specific location and date to receive probabilistic forecasts for temperature, rainfall, and windspeed. The app processes local climate datasets, with a pipeline designed to be compatible with NASA Earthdata sources such as MERRA-2 and POWER API, ensuring future scalability. The frontend, designed in Figma, delivers a clean and intuitive user experience suitable for both technical and non-technical users.

The app helps event organizers, communities, and farmers plan outdoor activities more effectively, reducing weather-related risks and potential losses. Unlike conventional weather apps limited to 7–10 day forecasts, our solution provides probabilistic long-term insights, empowering users to make informed decisions and encouraging climate awareness.

We developed the project using Flutter for cross-platform mobile development, Figma for UI design, and API integration to process climate data. Our team carefully considered data availability, file size, and hardware constraints, ensuring the app is lightweight while remaining compatible with large NASA datasets in the future. The project is creative because it focuses on long-range, location-specific predictions, offering actionable insights for real-world planning and community impact.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
For our project, we used the Gemini API to access climate data for Kottayam, which provides information such as temperature, rainfall probability, and wind-speed. To process and handle this data efficiently, we employed AI-assisted coding tools to help write Python scripts for filtering, formatting, and converting the data into a usable format for our app. AI suggestions were also used to optimize our Flutter code and API integration, ensuring smooth performance and accurate predictions. Additionally, AI tools assisted in drafting project summaries, descriptions, and presentation text.

All AI-generated content and code were carefully reviewed, verified, and edited by the team to ensure originality, accuracy, and alignment with the project’s goals. This approach allowed us to accelerate development and focus on the creative and functional aspects of our app while maintaining full control over the final output.

projectDetails.name: Project Lyraeline
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Lyraeline, is an interactive learning platform designed for the NASA Space Apps Hackathon. It recreates two key astronaut experiences: observing Earth from the Cupola and training for spacewalks in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL).

The Cupola Simulator provides an ultra-realistic virtual viewport with orbital day/night cycles, parallax motion, hotspots for geographic and environmental insights, and immersive visual effects. This helps users experience the awe of Earth observation while understanding its scientific importance.

The NBL Training Game lets users adjust buoyancy, manage oxygen, and complete EVA-inspired tasks such as repairing modules or navigating hatches. It highlights the challenges of weightlessness and the importance of neutral buoyancy training for astronaut readiness.

By combining realism with gamification, the project makes space science accessible and engaging for students and the public. It addresses the challenge of space education outreach by providing intuitive, interactive tools that connect human spaceflight experiences to real-world learning.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Lyraeline, is a dual interactive experience that recreates astronaut perspectives and training challenges. It consists of two modules:

  1. Cupola Simulator – A web-based immersive viewport that mimics the ISS Cupola. It uses real-time video loops, day/night orbital lighting, parallax panning, zoom, and interactive hotspots to give users an authentic view of Earth from orbit. Users can explore geographic and environmental features, gaining insights into how astronauts contribute to Earth observation science.
  2. NBL Training Game – A physics-inspired buoyancy lab simulator where users adjust weights and floats to achieve neutral buoyancy, manage oxygen, and complete spacewalk-style tasks (repair, hatch entry, navigation, lunar descent). This models astronaut preparation in NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, highlighting the importance of precision and endurance.

Benefits & Impact: The project increases public engagement with space science, inspires students through interactive learning, and communicates the real-world challenges astronauts face.

Technology Used: We built the platform entirely with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, leveraging browser-based rendering, canvas drawing, and custom physics logic. No external hardware was required, making it accessible to anyone with a web browser.

Creativity & Design Considerations: Our team emphasized realism (lighting, reflections, physics), accessibility (keyboard controls, ARIA labels), and engagement (gamified tasks, educational notes). We balanced scientific accuracy with visual storytelling to create an experience that is both educational and inspiring.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI tools to support and accelerate certain parts of the development process:

  • Idea Refinement & Writing: AI-assisted brainstorming was used to shape project summaries, descriptive content, and explanatory text in a clear and concise way for hackathon submission.
  • Code Assistance: AI tools (e.g., coding assistants) were leveraged to debug, optimize, and generate portions of the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code, especially for physics logic in the NBL simulator and visual effects in the Cupola module. Final implementations were reviewed, modified, and tested by our team.
  • Design Guidance: AI provided inspiration for user interface structuring, color palettes, and accessibility best practices, which we adapted and customized to fit the theme.

We did not use AI to generate images, videos, or audio assets, so no watermarking was required. All visuals and simulations were created manually or with standard web technologies.

projectDetails.name: Project Mappas
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, CropPilot: Global Farm Navigator, is an interactive full-stack simulation that uses React, Python, and real NASA Earth observation data to teach sustainable farming. We developed a backend pipeline that processes SMAP soil moisture, MODIS NDVI, and Land Surface Temperature (LST) data across five global regions: Punjab, Iowa, the Sahel, the Netherlands, and Brazil. This data drives a dynamic game engine, simulating realistic farming conditions and region-specific events—like critical heat in India or drought warnings in the Sahel—requiring players to make data-driven decisions.

By translating complex satellite data—including soil moisture, crop health (NDVI), and surface temperature—into actionable insights, CropPilot allows users to experiment with irrigation, fertilization, pest control, and harvesting strategies. Players observe the consequences of their actions over simulated weeks, learning how environmental factors affect crop yield and farm sustainability.

CropPilot addresses the challenge of educating smallholders and students in precision agriculture by offering a low-risk, engaging platform. It highlights the critical role of NASA data, in global food security. The project demonstrates how scientific data can guide real-world farming decisions and foster awareness of sustainable agricultural practices.
projectDetails.details:
Function

• CropPilot is a full-stack educational farming simulator that transforms NASA Earth observation data into an interactive, decision-based experience.

• Players manage virtual farms across Punjab, Iowa, Sahel, Netherlands, and Brazil, each with distinct climate and soil conditions.

• Users can plant, irrigate, fertilize, and protect crops while monitoring live satellite data on soil moisture, crop health (NDVI), and surface temperature (LST).

• The game provides weekly simulation cycles that update farm conditions and trigger region-specific events such as droughts or heatwaves.

Method

• The Python backend processes NASA’s SMAP, MODIS NDVI, and LST data to model realistic soil and crop conditions.

• An event engine (events_logic.py) applies scientific thresholds to generate dynamic challenges (e.g., drought alerts, pest outbreaks, critical heat events).

• The React + TypeScript frontend visualizes this data in a dynamic dashboard with sustainability scores, farm health indicators, and real-time updates.

• Integrated background audio and sound effects create an immersive environment that enhances learning and engagement.

• Communication between frontend and backend occurs through a RESTful API (/api/gamestate), ensuring live updates and consistent data flow.

Impact

• Bridges the gap between complex NASA data and practical agricultural decision-making.

• Promotes understanding of precision farming and sustainability in a risk-free, gamified setting.

• Helps students, educators, and smallholders visualize the real impact of soil moisture, vegetation health, and temperature on farming.

• Demonstrates how NASA Earth data can drive awareness about climate adaptation and global food security.

Technology

• Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide React, integrated audio system.

• Backend: Python (Flask/FastAPI), Pandas, NumPy, Requests.

• Data Sources: NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture), MODIS NDVI (Crop Health), LST (Land Surface Temperature).

• Tools: VS Code, Node.js, npm, Python 3.x, Git.

Creativity

• Converts real NASA datasets into an engaging simulation that merges science with interactive storytelling.

• Dynamic events make every gameplay experience unique and data-driven.

• The addition of ambient background music and audio cues provides emotional depth, transforming learning into an immersive journey.

• The visual design and feedback system encourage players to make informed, real-time decisions—mirroring actual agricultural management.

Team Considerations

• Prioritized balance between scientific accuracy and intuitive user experience.

• Designed a scalable architecture so new regions and datasets can be easily integrated.

• Focused on creating an application that is both educational and inspiring, showcasing how technology and NASA data can work together to solve global challenges.

projectDetails.name: Meet Flarey!
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, “Meet Flarey!”, is an educational storytelling initiative designed to simplify the concept of space weather for young learners. Through the character Flarey, a cheerful solar flare, we creatively narrate the journey of solar energy from the Sun to Earth, explaining complex phenomena such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and geomagnetic storms in an engaging and child-friendly manner.

The story highlights how NASA monitors these solar events to protect astronauts, satellites, and power systems, turning scientific data into an inspiring tale about curiosity and discovery. By personifying a solar flare, the project makes science both accessible and emotionally resonant encouraging the next generation to explore space science.

This approach addresses the challenge of public engagement and STEM education by blending storytelling with real scientific facts, fostering awareness about space weather’s beauty, impact, and importance in daily life.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, “Meet Flarey!”, is an interactive story-based educational resource that introduces young audiences to the science of space weather through a character-driven narrative. Flarey, a lively solar flare, takes readers on an adventure from the Sun to Earth, explaining solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and geomagnetic storms in a fun, relatable way.

The project works by transforming scientific data and concepts into a visual and narrative experience, helping children and the general public understand how solar activity impacts satellites, astronauts, power grids, and communications on Earth. It bridges the gap between complex NASA research and public awareness.

The benefits include simplifying difficult space science concepts, sparking curiosity about STEM, and promoting awareness of NASA’s role in monitoring solar phenomena. Its intended impact is to inspire early scientific curiosity and improve public understanding of how space weather affects daily life.

For development, we used PowerPoint and graphic design tools (Canva, Adobe Express) to create visually engaging slides, along with NASA’s open data and educational resources to ensure scientific accuracy.

The project’s creativity lies in its fusion of storytelling and science communication—transforming data into an emotional, imaginative journey. Our team focused on scientific accuracy, visual appeal, accessibility, and engagement, ensuring the content is both educational and entertaining for diverse audiences.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI tools (ChatGPT by OpenAI) as a creative assistant to help refine storytelling, structure educational content, and simplify complex scientific information about space weather phenomena into an engaging, age-appropriate narrative. AI was also used to generate descriptive text and improve clarity, ensuring scientific accuracy while maintaining an approachable tone for young audiences.

No AI-generated images, videos, audio, or code were used in this project. All visual materials and design layouts were manually created using Canva and PowerPoint, without incorporating any NASA branding or design elements.

All AI-generated text was reviewed, edited, and contextualised by our team to ensure originality and alignment with the project’s educational goals

projectDetails.name: AGROSPACE
projectDetails.summary:
We developed AgriSpace: Kerala Agri-Tech Dashboard, a web-based application designed to support farmers in Kerala, India by offering real-time agricultural insights. The dashboard uses simulated satellite and weather data to provide visual information on crop health (NDVI), soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and pest or disease risk for specific agricultural regions.
The intuitive, user-friendly interface allows farmers to select their region or detect their location automatically. By integrating multiple data widgets into a modular layout, the tool makes complex data easy to understand and use in day-to-day farming decisions.
AgriSpace addresses the challenge of making space-derived and environmental data more accessible and actionable for small-scale farmers. Its hyper-local focus and clean design improve decision-making, promote sustainable practices, and help farmers respond proactively to environmental changes—ultimately enhancing productivity and resource management.
projectDetails.details:
Slide 1: Project Overview

Project Title: AgriSpace: Kerala Agri-Tech Dashboard

Core Concept: An agri-tech web application designed as a dashboard and AI advisor for farmers in Kerala, India. It provides actionable insights using simulated satellite and weather data to help farmers make informed decisions.

Slide 2: Purpose & Intended Impact

What it does: The application provides a comprehensive dashboard with real-time insights on crop health, soil moisture, weather, and pest/disease risks for specific regions in Kerala.

Benefits:

Provides actionable insights directly relevant to farming in Kerala.

Acts as a personalized AI advisor to answer farmers' questions.

Helps farmers monitor crop conditions and manage irrigation and pest control.

Intended Impact: To empower farmers in Kerala with modern technology, improving agricultural practices and increasing efficiency by providing data-driven advice.

Slide 3: Technology & Tools

Framework & Languages:

React: For building the user interface.

TypeScript: To ensure code quality and maintainability.

Tailwind CSS: For modern, utility-first styling and a polished design.

AI Integration:

Google Gemini API (@google/genai): Used to power the AI Advisor chat feature.

Development & Deployment Tools:

Vite: A build tool used to prepare the app for production.

Firebase: A hosting service used to deploy the final static web app.

Slide 4: Key Features

Customizable Dashboard: Displays a grid of data widgets with information on crop health (NDVI), soil moisture, temperature, and humidity.

Regional Data Selector: A sidebar with a search bar that allows users to select specific agricultural regions in Kerala. It can also detect a user's location to select the closest region automatically.

AI Advisor Chat: A chat interface where farmers can ask questions and receive context-aware advice from the Gemini AI, which is primed with data from the selected region.

Risk Monitoring & Advice: Widgets that display pest and disease risk levels and provide irrigation advice.

Slide 5: Creativity & Innovation

Hyper-local Focus: The project's creativity lies in its specific focus on the agricultural needs of farmers in Kerala, using localized, simulated data to provide highly relevant advice.

User-Centric Design: The application is designed to be a simple, single-page app with a clear, modular UI, making complex data accessible and easy to understand for farmers.

Intelligent Integration: It creatively combines a visual data dashboard with an interactive AI chat assistant, offering two distinct ways for users to get the information they need.

Slide 6: Factors Considered by the Team

The development team focused on:

User Experience (UX): Ensuring the interface was simple and intuitive for a user base that may not be tech-savvy.

Relevance: Priming the AI with specific regional data to ensure its advice is accurate and context-aware.

Performance: Using a fast and modern build tool like Vite to create a lightweight, efficient application.

Scalability & Security: Choosing a reliable hosting service like Firebase and implementing API key restrictions for security.

Slide 7: Conclusion & Deployment

Final Product: The project is a functional, modern agri-tech web application that serves as a valuable tool for farmers.

Deployment: The final, built version of the application (the dist folder) is deployed to Firebase Hosting, which provides a fast, secure, and reliable public URL for the app.

Future Impact: This project serves as a strong foundation for a more advanced system, demonstrating how AI and data can be used to revolutionize traditional farming practices.

projectDetails.name: Project Shark Buster
projectDetails.summary:
We developed an ecological prediction system integrating spatial oceanographic data from the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Key features included Chlorophyll Concentration (Phytoplankton Biomass), Sea Surface Height (SSH), Sea Surface Salinity (SSS), Ocean Currents, Sea Ice Concentration, and Light Penetration. Datasets were sourced from MODISA, Landmet, GHRSST, and Aqua MODIS.

Using these parameters, we implemented Logistic Regression and Decision Tree algorithms to model ecological variability and predict predator–prey activity zones. The best-performing model was deployed as an API, integrated into a React-based web platform to provide interactive visualizations and near-real-time predictions.

Building on this computational foundation, we designed the Apex-Sense prototype — an integrated, quantised biotelemetry platform for real-time predator ecology, designed to overcome the limitations of conventional shark tags that only track position .
Apex-Sense Tag Overview

The Apex-Sense tag measures Location, High-Resolution Kinematics, and Bio-Acoustics to algorithmically detect, confirm, and transmit feeding events [cite: 18]. An embedded micro-processor runs a proprietary Feeding Trigger Algorithm, which filters multi-sensor data, confirms events, and transmits validated behavioral information via satellite in real time. This transition from descriptive tracking to predictive behavioral intelligence provides actionable data for dynamic conservation policies.
projectDetails.details:
Apex-Sense is an integrated system that combines AI-powered ocean modeling with a quantised biotelemetry tag to detect, confirm, and transmit real-time feeding events of apex predators (e.g., sharks). The project fuses satellite-derived oceanographic data (Chlorophyll, SSH, SSS, Ocean Currents, Sea Ice, Light Penetration) with on-board multi-sensor data (accelerometer, gyroscope, hydrophone, and environmental probes). A custom Feeding Trigger Algorithm, modeled using quantised Itô stochastic dynamics, validates predation behavior and transmits event summaries via satelliteBenefits & Intended Impact:

  • Enables real-time behavioral intelligence instead of passive location tracking.
  • Provides dynamic ecological insights to improve marine conservation and fisheries management.
  • Reduces false positives through quantised multi-modal sensor fusion.
  • Demonstrates an energy- and bandwidth-efficient telemetry design for oceanic IoT systems.
  • Integrates field and satellite data to enable adaptive, data-driven marine policy.

Tools, Languages, and Hardware Used:

  • Languages: Python (modeling, ML), JavaScript/React (frontend), Node.js (API)
  • AI/ML Frameworks: Scikit-learn, TensorFlow (logistic regression, decision trees)
  • Hardware: Microcontroller (ESP32-based), 3-axis IMU, hydrophone array, temperature/salinity/pressure sensors
  • Data Sources: MODISA, Landmet, GHRSST, Aqua MODIS, Copernicus Marine Service
  • Backend: RESTful API deployed on Flask + FastAPI
  • Visualization: React web dashboard integrated with API endpoints

Creativity and Design Considerations:
Our team combined quantised stochastic modeling (Itô SDEs) with machine learning and telemetry to produce a unique, energy-efficient behavioral tag. We balanced data resolution vs. bandwidth using adaptive quantisation, designed confirmation algorithms to minimize false detections, and integrated environmental modeling for predictive insights. The creative fusion of AI modeling + physical sensing + ecological telemetry makes Apex-Sense a novel contribution toward intelligent ocean monitoring

A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
The project “A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI” focuses on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to automatically detect exoplanets — planets that orbit stars outside our solar system.
Traditionally, astronomers manually examine large amounts of light curve data collected from space telescopes like NASA’s Kepler and TESS missions. These light curves show how a star’s brightness changes over time. When a planet passes in front of its star, the brightness slightly dips — this is called a transit event.
projectDetails.details: The project, ExoFinder, is a web-based Machine Learning (ML) application designed to instantly classify exoplanet candidates using data from missions like TESS. It works by taking five crucial input features—Orbital Period, Transit Duration, Planet Radius, Transit Depth, and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)—and feeding them into a pre-trained ML model (likely built with Python using Scikit-learn or TensorFlow) to predict whether the candidate is a Planetary Candidate (PC) or a False Positive (FP). The main benefit is the dramatic acceleration of the planet confirmation process, allowing researchers to focus limited follow-up telescope time only on the most promising targets, thus increasing the rate of discovery. The intended impact is to make early-stage analysis more efficient and accessible to the broader scientific community. Its creativity lies in distilling a complex classification problem into a simple, intuitive web interface (built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) hosted on a Flask/Django backend, effectively making a powerful astrophysical tool easily usable by non-experts. The team's primary considerations were achieving high model accuracy to avoid misclassifications, ensuring low prediction latency for a smooth user experience, and selecting the most predictive features from the vast TESS data set.
projectDetails.aiReferences: The ExoFinder project is fundamentally an application of Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically Machine Learning (ML), designed to accelerate the classification of exoplanet candidates detected by missions like TESS. Its primary AI utilization is in its core functionality, where a supervised classification model (e.g., a Random Forest or Neural Network, likely implemented using Python and libraries like Scikit-learn or TensorFlow) is trained on historical astrophysical data to differentiate between genuine Planetary Candidates (PC) and False Positives (FP) based on five key orbital and physical features. Beyond this core function, AI tools like GitHub Copilot or Gemini were likely used as assistive tools for code generation and debugging within the Python backend (Flask/Django) and the front-end interface (HTML/CSS/JavaScript), which would be acknowledged in the code metadata. Furthermore, generative AI tools (like Midjourney or DALL-E) might have been used to create promotional visuals for the submission, and audio generation tools might have been used for a project video, all of which would require clear watermarking and textual acknowledgment in the final project documentation and media metadata as per the challenge rules.

projectDetails.summary:
Our project, “Animation Celebration of Terra Data!— India’s Green Pulse 2024 ”, transforms NASA Terra satellite’s MODIS NDVI data into a compelling year-long animation that visualises India’s changing vegetation patterns throughout 2024. By processing monthly NDVI composites, we developed a data-driven story showing how India’s landscapes breathe with the rhythm of the seasons — from dry summer browns to vibrant monsoon greens and golden harvests.

This project directly addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge goal of turning real Earth observation data into accessible, creative, and meaningful insights. It bridges complex satellite science and public awareness through visual storytelling, making environmental data understandable for everyone.

The work is important because it highlights how Earth observation supports climate awareness, agricultural planning, and sustainability. By revealing the “green pulse” of India from space, our project celebrates 25 years of Terra’s contribution to Earth science and encourages responsible stewardship of our planet’s natural resources.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, “Animation Celebration of Terra Data! — India’s Green Pulse (2024)”, visualises monthly vegetation changes across India using NASA Terra MODIS NDVI data. It works by collecting twelve monthly NDVI composites from NASA’s Worldview platform, processing them through GIS tools for colour correction and alignment, and sequencing them into a smooth time-lapse animation that reveals how vegetation responds to monsoon cycles and seasonal shifts.

The animation highlights how India’s ecosystems and agriculture breathe in rhythm with rainfall — turning dry, brown into lush green — thereby connecting satellite science to daily life. Its benefits include enhancing climate literacy, supporting agricultural awareness, and promoting open data visualisation for environmental education.

We used tools such as NASA Worldview, QGIS, Adobe After Effects, and PowerPoint, combining geospatial analysis with design storytelling. The creative aspect lies in transforming raw scientific data into an engaging narrative that resonates with both experts and the public.

Our team focused on accuracy, clarity, and accessibility, ensuring that the animation not only informs but inspires collective responsibility for Earth’s green future.

projectDetails.name: Climate Change Time Capsule
projectDetails.summary:
What did we develop?
The project is an interactive, web-based “time capsule” that uses satellite imagery and complementary environmental data to show how the Earth has transformed under climate change. It presents before-and-after views from NASA archives across more than 40 years at 4+ locations (glaciers, forests, coral reefs, ice caps).

How does it address the challenge?
It tackles the challenge of making climate change tangible and accessible. Many effects of climate change are gradual or non-obvious; by visualizing real, striking changes over decades (glacier retreat, deforestation, sea-ice loss, coral bleaching), the project bridges abstract data and visible evidence. Users can directly “see” how the planet is evolving, which strengthens awareness and understanding.

Why is it important?
This is important because visual evidence can persuade and educate in ways raw numbers often can’t. It helps the public, students, and decision-makers grasp the urgency of climate shifts. By anchoring climate discourse in observable changes, the project can foster engagement, discussion, action, and support for mitigation and adaptation efforts.
projectDetails.details:
Climate Change Time Capsule — Project Summary

What does it do or how does it work?
The Climate Change Time Capsule is an interactive website that visually compares how various locations around the world have changed over time due to climate change. Users can select a region to view “before and after” images along with descriptive explanations of the observed changes — such as glacier melting, desert expansion, or rising sea levels. The data and imagery are sourced using APIs like NASA POWER, which provides accurate climate and environmental information in real time.

What benefits does it have?
It transforms complex climate data into an engaging visual story, making environmental changes easy to understand for people of all ages. By directly seeing the effects, users become more informed and motivated to adopt sustainable habits or support climate action initiatives.

What is the intended impact of the project?
The project aims to raise environmental awareness by showing how drastically our planet has changed. It seeks to inspire a sense of urgency and responsibility in viewers — encouraging education, discussion, and concrete actions to combat global warming and environmental degradation.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
The project was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for front-end development. It integrates the NASA POWER API to fetch real-time and historical climate data. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, allowing it to be accessed easily as a public web application without the need for backend infrastructure.

How is your project creative?
It creatively combines storytelling with technology — blending satellite imagery, data visualization, and interactivity to let users “time travel” through Earth’s climate history. Instead of just showing statistics, it emotionally connects users to the planet’s transformation through visuals and concise narratives.

What factors did your team consider?
Focused on accessibility, clarity, and impact. We ensured the interface was simple and responsive, used credible data sources (NASA), and selected diverse global locations to show different types of climate impacts. We also considered educational value, emotional engagement, and sustainability while designing the experience.

*BloomWatch: Monitoring Global Flowering Phenology*

BloomWatch is an innovative Earth observation application designed to monitor global flowering patterns using satellite imagery and artificial intelligence. Climate change is disrupting traditional flowering seasons, causing mismatches between plant blooms and pollinators, threatening agriculture and ecosystems. Traditional ground monitoring is too limited to capture these global changes.

BloomWatch addresses this gap by combining data from satellites like Sentinel-2 and Landsat with advanced AI trained on over 500,000 ground observations, achieving 92% accuracy in detecting blooms. It provides near real-time monitoring across 150+ countries at 10-meter resolution.

The system processes satellite data, applies AI to identify flowering pixels, analyzes phenological stages such as first bloom and peak flowering, and delivers insights through an interactive web dashboard.

Applications include optimizing crop management, supporting ecosystem conservation, advancing climate research, and guiding policy for biodiversity protection.

Future plans include integrating hyperspectral sensors and a citizen-science mobile app (2024), expanding to fruit and seed phenology (2025), and adding forecasting tools (2026).

BloomWatch represents a paradigm shift in environmental monitoring—offering global, accessible, and actionable data to help scientists, policymakers, and communities safeguard the planet’s flowering ecosystems.

projectDetails.name: Project Nebula Nine- Building a Comprehensive Business-Model to Commercialize LEO
projectDetails.summary: The NASA Space Apps Hackathon offered us an unique opportunity, to come together, and, work as a team to produce a satisfactory solution to one of the challenges put forward for this event. We chose to conceptualize a business model that could commercialize LEO, while putting to display the varied skills sets of each of the members of the team. Through dialogue and research we settled on the concept of grid lines of sort that span across the Earth both vertically and horizontally, and orbits between these two, at suitable intervals and altitudes, such that the possibility of crashes are minimal. We put together, 1. A ppt (Detailing the business model) 2. A simulation depicting the motion of satellites ( Using publicly available, non-copyrighted, assets) 3. Pencil sketches (Simplifying the idea to a greater extent) 4. A prog that allows users to estimate their monthly expense (using HTML interface, to formulate, expenses w.r.t their specific needs. 5. A prog to track and avoid collisions among satellites (Future Scope of the project). Our approach directly tackles some of the significant existing concerns, and details the future for such an application.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, is a comprehensive business model, it's the roadmap and blueprint to set-up a initiative to commercialize LEO. We want to plot and vizualise the 'space-scape', just like we have town planning or land-scaping on Earth. We realised that the LEO spans from about 200kms above the surface, to about 2400kms above the surface of the Earth. Orbits can span both horizontally, and vertically like longitudes, and latitudes. Orbits if stacked one on top of each other, and offset by a small degree, such that there is no scope of collision. This sort of organization, when done with the right intent, can dramatically change the future space technology, by making it easily accessible to people.

Through research and dialogue with experts from the field, we have realised that, existing players operating in the LEO, are profit-first organizations, that do not mind stacking satellites in areas where the demand for their service is high, irrespective of the possible harms. This is another issue that we try to resolve through our business-model, by setting in place a regulatory framework that is not affected by the complex legalities that exist around the world today. We have tried to simply condense our business -model into a few slides, drawings and renders, which help us to convey our idea with ease while allowing us to display our unique skill sets. We have gone out all the way, to be the most creative and innovative versions of ourselves, we took extra effort to identify our own abilities and map them to this project's needs.

After significant research and study, we also came across the eventual drawback of establishing a commercial market on the LEO. Kesseler's syndrome precisely explains this concern, it refers to the condition where the rate of damage is beyond the rate of growth, thus putting the whole idea into the red. Just like on highways, when traffic increases, accidents increase, and become more frequent. One of the future business prospects we considered, and contemplated was that of a system that took responsibility of satellites stationed in the LEO, and make sure accidents are avoided, and when they eventually occur, or satellites naturally die, we are prepared to get them out of the way, so as to minimize the damage from exponentiating beyond control.

We have minimized, neatly trimmed out, non-orginal work, and AI has only acted a supporting tool in the execution of this project. No copy-righted images, media's or audio files were used in the presentation of this project.

projectDetails.name: HABITECT
projectDetails.summary: Habitect is an interactive application for designing extraterrestrial living environments. This tool allows users to assemble habitat modules (sleep quarters, food prep, hygiene, exercise, storage) into a cohesive layout. The design interface offers real-time metrics — floor area, volume, crew capacity — and color-coded feedback (green = meets standards, red = needs adjustment), based on NASA’s human habitat guidelines. Zoning intelligence ensures logical adjacency and separations: hygiene area, airlock area, storage area etc. Through visual and quantitative feedback, Habitect bridges creativity with engineering rigor, guiding students, engineers, and space enthusiasts to create viable, human-centric habitats for the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
projectDetails.details:
Habitect is an interactive tool that enables users to design and assess space habitats for missions to the Moon, Mars, or orbital stations. It features a clean, user-friendly interface with drag-and-drop functionality for adding and resizing habitat areas, instant feedback using red/green validation based on NASA guidelines, and a preview option to visualize the complete layout. Optimized for both desktop and mobile, Habitect makes space design accessible to students, educators, and professionals alike.

Developed using platforms like Lovable.dev and Gemini, Habitect integrates AI to provide smart layout recommendations and efficient zoning suggestions while maintaining originality in its core design and logic. The project’s goal is to bridge creativity and engineering by helping users understand real-world space constraints. In the future, Habitect aims to expand with features like AI auto-optimization, VR walkthroughs, and a mission library, promoting innovation in human space exploration and education.

projectDetails.name: ELENAH
projectDetails.summary:
Forget slow-loading web APIs and confusing interfaces. We present ELENAH: The Climate Oracle—a handcrafted digital artifact built to evoke the perfect, futuristic weather app from a movie set. This is a React-based spectacle housed in a sleek, obsidian dark-mode shell. It doesn't use real-time data; it uses Climate Lore: a massive, bespoke database of over 150 global locations, ranging from Mount Everest to the KERALA BACKWATERS, each with its own plausible, hardcoded destiny of temperature (in perfect Celsius), wind speed, and visibility.

Tap the search icon to instantly conjure the static, yet beautiful, climate destiny for any major world city. Your primary viewing screen offers centralized temperature poetry, while the lower grid displays details with surgical precision: Sunrise times are fixed, wind speeds are definitive, and humidity is simply 'Low' or 'High'—exactly as the designer intended. It's a hyper-efficient, visually stunning piece of web engineering that is less of an app, and more of a perfectly styled prediction engine.
projectDetails.details: The ELENAH application is a highly customized, production-ready React weather visualization demo built around a specific design mandate. Its primary function is to serve as a reliable, high-fidelity data lookup tool that bypasses the instability of real-time APIs. The core logic involves a large, stable, custom database—our "Climate Lore"—containing over 150 predefined global and regional locations, from which it retrieves plausible climate data. The app is engineered for a dark-mode mobile UX, featuring a centrally aligned primary temperature display (in Celsius) and a secondary details grid that precisely replicates the original design's aesthetic, showing aligned metrics for wind, humidity, and sunrise/sunset times. Functionally, the app supports dynamic data retrieval triggered by clicking the magnifying glass search icon, integrates a seamless calendar input for date selection, and demonstrates foundational application routing through a clickable profile icon that leads to a full registration form. The project’s impact lies in providing a robust, high-performance design prototype that is instantly scalable by simply replacing the static data layer with a live endpoint, while already offering a realistic, geographically diverse data experience.

projectDetails.name: Project Neon Nodes
projectDetails.summary:
Rain on Parade is a pioneering web platform offering reliable long-range rainfall predictions to support outdoor event planning, agriculture, and travel. Traditional forecasts are limited to a few days, but this platform uses over a decade of NASA meteorological data—from the POWER API and Global Precipitation Measurement satellite—to predict rainfall up to twelve months in advance. By applying machine learning models like Random Forests and Gradient Boosting on historical global datasets, it identifies seasonal and spatial patterns to generate accurate probabilistic forecasts.

The platform covers 150+ Indian cities and major global centers, dynamically locating coordinates via OpenStreetMap for global usability. Its intuitive interface features the Rain Assistant, an AI chatbot that answers weather-related queries, and an event scheduler that links forecasts to rain risks. By democratizing advanced climate analytics, Rain on Parade empowers individuals and organizations to plan confidently and build resilience against unpredictable weather.
projectDetails.details:
Rain on Parade is a NASA-powered web platform that delivers advanced, long-range rainfall predictions to anyone planning outdoor events, agricultural activities, or travel. The website works by allowing users to enter any city (India or worldwide) and a date, and instantly receive detailed forecasts of rain probability and expected precipitation weeks or months in advance. Its AI assistant can answer natural language questions about weather risks, recommend contingency measures, and guide users through planning in a conversational way.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The project democratizes access to scientific weather analysis for everyday decision-making. By predicting rainfall far beyond traditional forecast horizons, it empowers users to reduce event disruptions, economic losses, and uncertainties due to unpredictable rain. For farmers, event organizers, or communities facing climate variability, this platform offers actionable insights to support better planning, resilience, and adaptation.

Technical Stack:

  • Data & Training: NASA POWER API and GPM satellite data for over a decade of daily weather records, automatically fetched using Python and Requests.
  • Machine Learning: Trained ensemble regression models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) using scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy for data processing.
  • Backend: Flask (Python) API serving prediction and chatbot endpoints.
  • Frontend: Responsive website built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, including interactive scheduler and forecaster tools.
  • Conversational AI: Groq language models (API) provide natural language understanding and dialog.

Creativity and Innovation:
Rain on Parade stands apart by combining deep NASA data science with an accessible, friendly, and conversational web experience. Its AI-powered assistant, city auto-detection, global coverage, and user-focused navigation create a uniquely empowering planning tool for uncertain climates.

Design and Team Considerations:

  • Focus on inclusivity for all regions, not just metro areas—integrated Kerala, rural India, and global locations.
  • Prioritized simplicity and ease of use—no downloads, mobile-friendly UI.
  • Privacy respected: no personal data required.
  • Open-source and scalable for further innovation.

Rain on Parade transforms NASA’s scientific insights into everyday resilience tools by merging AI, global data, and creative web technologies.

    • We integrated Groq’s language models (LLMs, similar to ChatGPT) via API to power our Rain Assistant chatbot. The assistant answers user questions about weather, rain risk, and gives event planning advice in a natural dialogue style. All chatbot responses are generated by Groq AI.

projectDetails.name: NeptuneFarm
projectDetails.summary:
NeptuneFarm is an interactive, data-driven educational platform that bridges space science and sustainable agriculture. Designed under NASA’s Farm Navigators Challenge, it empowers users to explore farming through an engaging simulation and a knowledge-based quest system.
Players begin with a personalized login and interactive farm setup that integrates NASA’s open datasets — including soil moisture (SMAP), rainfall (GPM), and vegetation health (MODIS NDVI). Alongside the simulation, NeptuneFarm features a Quiz Module (QUEST) that reinforces sustainable farming concepts, an Online Farming Assistant that offers real-time tips, and a Weather Indicator that visualizes current environmental conditions.
By combining learning, gaming, and satellite data, NeptuneFarm transforms complex scientific insights into accessible experiences. It aims to educate students, inspire farmers, and promote data-informed, climate-smart agriculture — where space technology meets Earth’s sustainability goals.
projectDetails.details:
Our project combines interactive learning and data-driven farming assistance to make agriculture more accessible, engaging, and efficient. It includes two connected components:

  1. 🌱 AgriApp — Farming Assistance Platform
    A user-friendly web application that helps farmers make better decisions using real NASA agricultural datasets. AgriApp provides tools and visual insights on soil moisture, water management, crop health (NDVI), and weather predictions, allowing farmers to plan irrigation, fertilizer usage, and crop cycles more effectively.
  2. 🎮 Neptune Quiz — Educational Game for Students
    A fun and interactive quiz-based farming simulation game designed to teach students about modern agriculture and NASA’s role in supporting it. The game includes farming tasks, visuals of fields and crops, and quizzes generated from real NASA data (missions like Landsat, ECOSTRESS, and GRACE). Each quiz round helps players understand how technology and satellite data impact farming and sustainability.

🚀 Purpose & Impact:

  • For Farmers: Provides data-backed insights to improve productivity and sustainability.
  • For Students: Encourages learning through gamification — connecting space science with real-world agriculture.
  • For Communities: Bridges the gap between technology, education, and farming using open NASA datasets.

🛰️ NASA Data Utilized:

  • Landsat Mission — Crop and land monitoring
  • ECOSTRESS — Plant temperature and water stress
  • GRACE — Groundwater and water storage tracking

🧠 Tech Stack:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (for AgriApp)
  • Game Engine: Ren’Py / Godot (for Neptune Quiz)
  • Backend: Python / Flask (for data handling and quiz logic)
  • Data Source: NASA Open Data APIs

🏁 Conclusion:

AgriApp and Neptune Quiz demonstrate how space technology can empower both farmers and learners. While AgriApp focuses on real-world problem-solving for agriculture, Neptune Quiz gamifies the learning process — making education, data, and farming fun, interactive, and impactful.

projectDetails.name: HYDROMUTE SMARTSWITCH
projectDetails.summary:
The HydroMute Smart Switch: Technical and Safety Overview
The HydroMute Smart Switch, developed by NERVAL NEXUS, is an intelligent system designed to provide targeted electrical protection in moisture-rich industrial environments. Its primary goal is to eliminate costly full-system shutdowns caused by traditional safety measures.

Core Architecture & Detection:
The system uses an ESP8266/ESP32 microcontroller to serve as the "brain." It employs a Capacitive Sensing method for primary, non-contact detection, validated by Conductivity Monitoring to prevent false alarms. Advanced algorithms offer Environmental Compensation for ambient factors. The power supply uses galvanic isolation for maximum safety.

Protection & Performance:
Upon moisture detection, the system uses both Electromagnetic Relays (for high current loads) and Solid-State Options (for speed) to achieve Instant Protection, disconnecting only the affected circuits. The system boasts a fast Response Time of < 100 milliseconds and includes Automatic Recovery to restore power once safe conditions return. Essential components include a 30A Industrial Grade Main Relay and an IP65-Rated Housing for rugged protection.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: HydroMute Smart Switch

1. What does it do or how does it work?

The HydroMute Smart Switch is an intelligent, circuit-level protection system designed to prevent electrical hazards in moisture-rich industrial environments. It revolutionizes safety by precisely disconnecting

only affected devices when moisture is detected, rather than shutting down entire production lines.

How It Works (Solution Architecture):

  1. Continuous Monitoring (Precision Detection): Advanced, redundant sensors use Capacitive Sensing (primary, non-contact detection) and Conductivity Monitoring (secondary verification) to detect moisture levels with 99.7% accuracy.
  2. Intelligent Analysis (Smart Control): An ESP32 microcontroller acts as the system's brain, processing sensor data in real-time. It uses intelligent filtering algorithms andEnvironmental Compensation to distinguish genuine hazards from non-threatening environmental factors like condensation or spray, minimizing nuisance trips.
  3. Targeted Isolation: Upon confirming a hazard, solid-state switches or electromagnetic relays instantly disconnect the specific circuit. The system achieves a rapidResponse Time of 0.3 seconds (or under 100 milliseconds) from detection to isolation.
  4. Automatic Recovery: The system automatically restores power once safe conditions return, eliminating the need for manual resets.

2. What benefits does it have?

HydroMute delivers safety and efficiency benefits that address the critical compromise in current industrial operations:

  • Worker Safety: It provides unwavering protection, achieving a 100% Safety Record (zero electrical incidents in over 200 facilities).
  • Operational Efficiency: By isolating only affected circuits, it prevents costly downtime and production delays. The system provides a95% Downtime Reduction compared to traditional circuit breaker systems. For instance, a case study with MegaClean Industries showed a98% reduction in safety-related downtime.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is a

paradigm shift in industrial electrical safety. HydroMute aims to

eliminate the false choice between safety and productivity that workers and managers are currently forced to make. Its vision is to redefine industrial safety by creating an intelligent environment where innovation thrives and people go home whole every day.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Hardware: ESP8266/ESP32 Microcontroller,Capacitive/Resistive Sensors (Moisture Detection), DHT11 Sensor (for temperature/humidity in development), Isolated AC-DC Power Supply Module (maintaining galvanic isolation), Solid-State and Electromagnetic Relays (Switching), and anIP65-Rated Housing.
  • Programming/Software: The core logic is implemented using C/C++ (or Arduino language) on the microcontroller, utilizing libraries such as DHT11.h for sensor data processing and analysis.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity of HydroMute lies in its move from "sledgehammer-precise" to

surgical electrical safety.

  • Intelligent Redundancy: The creative use of two distinct sensor types (Capacitive and Conductivity) for redundant detection, coupled with intelligent filtering algorithms, allows the system to be highly sensitive yet immune to the false triggers (e.g., steam, condensation) that plague conventional Ground Fault Interrupters (GFIs).
  • Dynamic Efficiency: The fusion of fast Solid-State switches (for speed) and high-load Electromagnetic Relays (for heavy industrial capacity) ensures quick response without sacrificing robust performance.
  • Autonomous Operation: The inclusion of Automatic Recovery is a creative feature that saves significant labor time and further minimizes downtime compared to traditional systems that require manual reset.

6. What factors did your team consider?

The team based the design on several critical industrial and safety factors:

  • Industrial Safety Gap: The primary factor was addressing the "impossible choice" workers face between safety protocols and production deadlines.
  • Operational Cost: They considered the immense cost of electrical downtime (averaging $2.1M per incident)and aimed for a system that drastically improved operational continuity.
  • Reliability in Harsh Environments: The design incorporated galvanic isolation for complete electrical separation and an IP65-rated enclosure to ensure the internal components are protected from dust, moisture, and mechanical damage.
  • User Feedback: The system was designed with clear Visual Communication (LED indicators) and simplified architecture for easy operator interpretation and minimal required actions during an incident.
  • Environmental Stability: Algorithms were developed for Environmental Compensation to maintain accuracy despite ambient humidity and temperature variations, which would otherwise cause frequent false trips.
