projectDetails.name: Project NexHack
projectDetails.summary: This project is a data-driven application that monitors flood risks and microbial health hazards in Kochi, Kerala. By combining NASA Earth observation datasets (such as precipitation, soil moisture, and flood mapping) with local ward-level data (rainfall, drainage, water stagnation, and health reports), the app identifies areas where stagnant water is likely to persist after floods. These stagnant zones often become hotspots for microbial growth, leading to outbreaks of waterborne and vector-borne diseases such as cholera, leptospirosis, and dengue. The app provides ward-wise alerts and early warnings for citizens, health workers, and municipal authorities, enabling them to take timely preventive actions like water treatment, sanitation drives, and medical readiness. By bridging climate data and public health insights, this project strengthens urban resilience and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3 – Good Health, SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities, and SDG 13 – Climate Action).o
projectDetails.details:
FloodSense Microbial Kochi – Project Details

What it does / How it works:
FloodSense is an app that predicts flood risks and microbial hazards in Kochi, Kerala. It combines NASA satellite data (rainfall, soil moisture, water levels) with local ward maps to calculate where stagnant water may lead to microbial growth. The app shows ward-wise risk levels on an interactive map and sends alerts to citizens and authorities.

Benefits:

  • Helps prevent waterborne and vector-borne diseases after floods.
  • Allows authorities to prioritize sanitation and health measures.
  • Informs citizens about high-risk areas for safety.

Intended Impact:
The app reduces post-flood disease outbreaks, protects public health, and makes Kochi more resilient to climate disasters. It can later be scaled to other flood-prone areas.

Tools / Languages / Software:

  • Python for backend and risk calculations
  • FastAPI for API
  • JavaScript + Leaflet.js for interactive maps
  • NASA datasets: rainfall, soil moisture, water levels
  • Optional: React for frontend, SQLite/PostgreSQL for data storage

Creativity:

  • Combines flood prediction with microbial risk, a rarely addressed problem.
  • Turns global NASA data into ward-level, actionable alerts.
  • Provides an easy-to-understand map for citizens and authorities.

Factors Considered:

  • Local flood and stagnant water patterns
  • Health risks and disease-prone areas
  • Data availability and scalability
  • Alignment with SDGs (Health, Sustainable Cities, Climate Action)

projectDetails.name: Project AgroBuilders and modern farming
projectDetails.summary: AgroBuilders is an educational web application designed to bridge the gap between complex environmental data and practical, sustainable farming. Faced with challenges like climate change, resource depletion, and a knowledge gap in modern technology, the agricultural community needs accessible tools to improve practices. AgroBuilders addresses this by simulating farming scenarios and providing data-driven insights through a user-friendly platform. It leverages open-source data from NASA and other providers to offer actionable advice on everything from pest identification to satellite-based crop health analysis. The project's core mission is to educate farmers, students, and enthusiasts on how to use technology to foster innovative and sustainable agricultural methods, making complex data understandable and actionable for a non-scientific audience.
projectDetails.details:
The Problem

Traditional farming faces numerous obstacles that limit productivity and sustainability:

Knowledge Gap: Many farmers, particularly in small-scale operations, lack access to or training for modern technological tools and data analytics.

Resource Inefficiency: Outdated methods can lead to the overuse of water, fertilizers, and pesticides, increasing costs and environmental impact.

Climate Uncertainty: Changing weather patterns make it difficult to rely on traditional farming calendars, leading to crop failures and financial strain.

Data Complexity: While vast amounts of environmental data are available, they are often too complex for practical, on-the-ground application without interpretation.

The Solution: AgroBuilders Web App

AgroBuilders is a comprehensive, smart-farming assistant that translates complex data into easy-to-understand advice. Its key features include:

Pest & Disease Identification: Users can upload a photo of a plant, and the app uses an AI model to identify potential issues and suggest treatments.

Weather & Climate Advisory: Provides real-time weather data, a 7-day forecast, and AI-generated farming advice based on location-specific climate conditions.

Soil Analysis (pH & Moisture): Allows users to log soil pH and moisture levels to receive AI-driven analysis on nutrient availability, crop suitability, and irrigation needs.

Satellite Imagery Analysis: An interactive map allows users to select a specific plot of land. The tool then simulates a crop health analysis based on satellite data concepts, identifying potential stress areas.

Drone Spraying & Field Mapping: Users can upload a field image, select specific grid sectors needing attention, and generate a targeted drone spraying plan.

Farm Management & Optimization: A local data-logging tool for tracking farm inputs, labor, and sales, with an AI feature that provides suggestions to improve profitability.

Live website: https://karthikkkmurali.github.io/AgriBuilders/
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI is integrated into both the development process and the core functionality of the AgroBuilders application.

Code Generation & Development: AI, specifically large language models like Gemini, was utilized throughout the development lifecycle. This included:

Code Snippet Generation: Generating JavaScript functions for API calls, data processing, and UI manipulation.

Debugging: Assisting in identifying and resolving bugs in the code.

Prototyping: Rapidly creating the HTML and CSS structure for new features.

Content & Prompt Engineering: Writing the text for the application and crafting the detailed prompts sent to the Gemini API for analysis.

Application Features: The "smarts" of the smart-farming assistant are powered by the Gemini model:

Image Recognition: In the "Pest & Disease Identification" feature, the AI analyzes user-uploaded images to identify problems.

Data Interpretation & Analysis: For features like "Weather Advisory," "Soil pH Analysis," and "Farm Optimization," the application sends structured data (weather forecasts, pH values, financial logs) to the AI, which then generates tailored, actionable advice.

Simulated Analysis: In the "Satellite Imagery" and "Drone Spraying" sections, the AI provides a simulated analysis based on the selected location and user inputs, educating the user on how an expert would interpret such data.

The dashboard aggregates and visualizes data on air quality, water quality, greenspace distribution, and population growth, allowing city planners and policymakers to identify environmental disparities across districts.

projectDetails.details:
Our project, Urban Intellect: City Health Dashboard, is an interactive platform that processes NASA Earth observation resources and translates them into actionable insights for urban planning. It collects data on air quality, water quality, greenspace availability, and population growth, and then visualizes these metrics through intuitive charts and maps. Users can compare districts, identify underserved areas, and explore sustainable growth scenarios.

The main benefit is making complex satellite data understandable and actionable for city governments, urban planners, and citizens. It highlights disparities such as pollution hotspots or unequal greenspace access and suggests interventions like reclamation of land, preservation of parks, or improved connectivity.

The intended impact is to support healthier, more sustainable, and equitable cities by bridging the gap between scientific data and local action.

We used Python for data processing, JavaScript (Chart.js + Tailwind CSS) for visualizations, and HTML/CSS for the interface. The backend script processes data into a processed_data.json file, which powers the live dashboard.

Creativity comes from combining real NASA data pathways with engaging design, providing not just numbers but context-driven recommendations. Our team considered accessibility, clarity, and real-world usability to maximize impact.

  • Code generation & debugging: Assisted in writing and refining HTML, CSS, JavaScript (Chart.js, Tailwind), and Python scripts to ensure smooth data visualization and interactivity.
  • Content drafting: Helped draft project summaries, descriptions, and explanations in a clear, concise way for presentation materials.

All AI-generated outputs were reviewed, tested, and validated by the team before integration. No NASA logos, mission identifiers, or branding elements were used or altered.

We did not use AI to fabricate scientific data; the underlying datasets come from NASA Earth observation resources and open-source urban metrics. AI was only used to accelerate development and communication.

projectDetails.name: ASTRO VERSE
projectDetails.summary:
Astroverse is an interactive web-based platform designed to make space exploration accessible, engaging, and educational for everyone. Addressing NASA’s challenge of complex and scattered space data, Astroverse transforms raw scientific information into an immersive 3D experience. The platform allows users to explore planets, stars, moons, and dwarf planets through revolving 3D models, each paired with accurate facts, histories, and characteristics.

The frontend is developed using React + Vite for high performance, styled with Tailwind CSS, and enhanced with Three.js for realistic 3D visualizations and Framer Motion for fluid animations. Users can search and filter celestial bodies and view detailed data within a clean, responsive interface.

The backend is powered by Flask (Python 3.11+), integrating Google’s Gemini API to refine and generate planet descriptions dynamically. Data is managed through local JSON storage augmented with AI content. The platform is hosted using Render/Fly.io for backend services and Vercel/Netlify for frontend deployment.

Astroverse bridges the gap between science and curiosity, offering an innovative tool for students, researchers, and enthusiasts to explore the universe in an intuitive way — merging technology, AI, and astronomy into one captivating digital experience.
projectDetails.details:
Astroverse is an interactive web-based platform that reimagines how people explore space. NASA provides vast amounts of high-quality data about celestial bodies, but much of it is highly technical, complex, and scattered across multiple sources. Astroverse bridges this gap by transforming raw NASA data into immersive 3D visual experiences, enabling anyone—students, educators, or enthusiasts—to understand and appreciate the wonders of the universe.

The platform allows users to explore planets, moons, stars, and dwarf planets through revolving 3D models enhanced with real NASA textures. Each object includes dynamically generated descriptions powered by Google’s Gemini AI, which refines scientific data into accurate, engaging, and easy-to-understand summaries. Users can search for any celestial body, view real-time planetary data, and experience the universe in motion.

Astroverse was developed using React + Vite for a high-performance frontend, Tailwind CSS for responsive design, Three.js for 3D visualizations, and Framer Motion for smooth transitions. The Flask (Python) backend manages data, APIs, and AI integration, while deployment was handled via Vercel and Render.

The project’s creativity lies in merging AI, education, and visualization to make space exploration both scientific and aesthetic. It simplifies complex space information, promotes curiosity, and provides an engaging learning experience for users worldwide.

Our team focused on accessibility, accuracy, and storytelling—ensuring Astroverse doesn’t just present facts, but narrates the story of our cosmos in a way that’s immersive and inspiring. By combining technology and imagination, Astroverse makes the universe not just observable, but truly explorable.

projectDetails.name: Space Weather Adventure-Stellar Stories
projectDetails.summary:
Space Weather Adventure is an interactive educational website that brings space weather concepts to life through engaging narratives and interactive elements. We developed four character-driven stories—a pilot, farmer, CME, and astronaut—that demonstrate how solar activity impacts different aspects of life on Earth and in space. The project addresses NASA's challenge by making complex space weather phenomena accessible and relatable to diverse audiences through immersive storytelling, text-to-speech functionality, interactive quizzes, and comprehensive scientific explanations.

This initiative is important because it bridges the gap between scientific research and public understanding, helping people recognize how space weather affects modern technology, agriculture, aviation, and space exploration. By transforming abstract concepts into tangible experiences, we're fostering greater awareness of space weather's real-world implications and inspiring the next generation of space scientists and informed citizens.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works

Space Weather Adventure is an interactive web-based educational platform that uses character-driven storytelling to explain space weather phenomena. The website features four distinct perspectives:

  • Captain Sky, an airline pilot experiencing navigation disruptions
  • Farmer Green, dealing with GPS failures in precision agriculture
  • Sparky the CME, personifying a coronal mass ejection's journey from Sun to Earth
  • Astronaut Alex, experiencing space weather directly from the International Space Station

Each story combines narrative text, visual elements, and interactive components including text-to-speech functionality that highlights words as they're read aloud. The platform also includes an educational quiz, comprehensive resource library, and scientific explanations that break down complex concepts into understandable terms.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Benefits:

  • Makes abstract space weather concepts tangible and relatable through real-world scenarios
  • Provides multiple learning modalities (visual, auditory, interactive) to accommodate different learning styles
  • Offers accessible scientific content that requires no prior knowledge
  • Creates emotional connection through character stories, enhancing knowledge retention

Intended Impact:

  • Increase public awareness of space weather's real-world impacts on technology and daily life
  • Inspire student interest in space science and STEM careers
  • Bridge the gap between NASA's space weather research and public understanding
  • Prepare future generations for living and working in an increasingly technology-dependent world affected by space weather

Technical Implementation

Tools & Technologies:

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (vanilla)
  • Styling: Custom CSS with CSS variables for consistent theming
  • Interactivity: Native Web Speech API for text-to-speech functionality
  • Graphics: Unsplash API for high-quality space imagery
  • Icons: Font Awesome for consistent iconography
  • Responsive Design: Mobile-first approach with CSS media queries

No external frameworks or libraries were used, ensuring fast loading times and broad compatibility across devices and browsers.

Creative Elements

Creative Approach:

  • Personification of space weather through "Sparky the CME" makes abstract concepts memorable
  • Multiple perspective storytelling shows how the same phenomenon affects different people
  • Interactive text highlighting synchronized with speech creates an engaging reading experience
  • Space-themed visual design with animated stars and nebula effects creates immersive atmosphere
  • Gradual complexity - starting with simple stories and building to detailed scientific explanations

Design Considerations

Our team prioritized:

  • Accessibility: Text-to-speech functionality, color contrast compliance, keyboard navigation
  • User Experience: Intuitive navigation, clear visual hierarchy, responsive design for all devices
  • Educational Value: Accurate scientific content presented in engaging, approachable ways
  • Performance: Lightweight codebase for fast loading, even with limited bandwidth
  • Scalability: Modular design allowing easy addition of new stories or perspectives
  • Cross-generational appeal: Content that engages both students and adults

The project successfully transforms NASA's vital space weather research into an engaging, educational experience that demonstrates how solar activity connects to our daily lives on Earth.

projectDetails.name: M.A.R.S (Material And Resourse Salvage)
projectDetails.summary: Imagine you're on Mars and you're living in a big tent. Everything you needed to build that tent and live there came in a giant box. Now, the tent is built, but you have this huge pile of wrapping, foam, and metal frames left over. You can't just throw it out, and you can't ask Earth to send you a screwdriver if one breaks. Our project, the M.A.R.S. Bench, is like a magical workbench from a video game. You feed all that leftover trash into one side of the bench, and it acts like a super-smart recycling machine. It shreds it, melts it, and presses it. On the other end, it has a 3D printer that can use that old trash material to print out a brand new screwdriver, a plate for your food, or even a brick to make your tent stronger. We're turning useless garbage into life-saving tools right there on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works

The M.A.R.S. Bench is an integrated, semi-autonomous workstation designed to solve the critical issue of inorganic waste accumulation on long-duration missions to Mars. Faced with the generation of over 12,000 kg of trash and the prohibitive cost of resupply from Earth, our project reframes waste not as a liability, but as a high-value, on-site resource.

The Bench operates on a three-stage process that turns trash into mission-critical assets:

  1. The Deconstructor: The first stage receives various waste inputs, from foam packaging and fabrics to plastic containers. It uses powerful shredders to pulverize the material into a uniform, manageable feedstock. Integrated optical and density scanners then automatically sort the feedstock into different bins for processing.
  2. The Forge: This module handles mixed, complex materials that are difficult to recycle traditionally. It uses intense heat and pressure to thermally compress the shredded feedstock into dense, durable blocks and sheets. By mixing the material with Martian regolith, the Forge creates a novel composite we call "Ferro-Crete," perfect for construction, insulation, and radiation shielding.
  3. The Fabricator: This is the high-precision module. It takes pure, sorted polymer feedstock from the Deconstructor, melts it, and extrudes it into standard 3D printer filament. An integrated 3D printer then uses this filament to fabricate custom tools, replacement parts for equipment, scientific instruments, and daily-use items on demand.

Project Benefits

The M.A.R.S. Bench provides a multitude of benefits essential for the success and sustainability of Martian exploration:

  • Drastic Cost Reduction via Launch Mass Offset: The single greatest expense of a Mars mission is launch mass. By manufacturing essential items on-site from existing materials, the Bench eliminates the need to launch countless kilograms of spare parts and supplies, saving hundreds of millions of dollars.
  • Enhanced Crew Autonomy and Safety: The Bench acts as mission insurance. It empowers astronauts to solve unforeseen problems by fabricating solutions in real-time, drastically reducing their dependence on a supply line that is months or years away.
  • Increased Mission Capability: Astronauts are no longer limited by the tools they brought with them. They can design and create new instruments for unexpected scientific opportunities, making the mission more adaptive and productive.
  • Long-Term Sustainability: The project establishes a true, closed-loop circular economy on Mars. It sets a foundational standard for how future off-world settlements can live off the land and minimize their environmental footprint.

Intended Impact

The intended impact of the M.A.R.S. Bench is to fundamentally shift the paradigm of space exploration from one of reliance to one of self-sufficiency. In the short term, it ensures the safety and success of the first human missions to Mars. In the long term, it serves as the cornerstone technology for sustainable colonization. The Bench is not just a recycling machine; it is the first step toward building a true industrial fabrication ecosystem on another world, enabling us to build our future on Mars with the materials of Mars.

Development & Technology

As this is a conceptual project for a hackathon, we utilized modern digital tools to develop the idea, design the presentation, and create the project narrative.

  • Software & Languages:
    • Presentation: Microsoft PowerPoint was used for the final presentation.
    • Automation: Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) was used to programmatically generate the presentation structure, ensuring speed and consistency.
    • Design & Visualization: Diagrams.net was used for creating the schematic blueprints and process flowcharts. Visual assets were sourced from the official NASA Image Library and edited using Canva.
  • Research & Data: Our project was developed directly from the NASA Space Apps Challenge documentation, incorporating all listed waste materials and constraints. We referenced the material properties of the MGS-1 Mars Global Simulant to inform the design of the "Ferro-Crete" composite.

How is Your Project Creative?

Our project's creativity lies in its narrative framing and its integrated systems approach.

  1. Thematic Innovation: Instead of presenting a simple recycling system, we framed it through the compelling narrative of the "resourceful engineer," inspired by classic science fiction like Dead Space. This transforms a practical problem into an engaging story of survival and ingenuity, making the concept more memorable and impactful.
  2. Integrated Systems Thinking: Rather than designing a single machine for a single purpose, we created a holistic, multi-functional platform. The innovative two-pathway system—using the Forge for low-grade, high-volume output and the Fabricator for high-value, high-precision output—is a creative solution that addresses the full spectrum of waste materials, something single-purpose machines cannot do.

Factors Considered by the Team

Our design was driven by the specific constraints and realities of a Martian mission:

  • Astronaut Time: Recognizing that crew time is the most valuable resource on Mars, we designed the Bench to be semi-autonomous. The "load and go" principle ensures that astronauts are not bogged down with complex recycling tasks.
  • Safety: We explicitly avoided incineration, which is hazardous in a closed environment and was forbidden by the challenge. Our mechanical and thermal processes are designed to produce no toxic emissions or harmful byproducts.
  • Resource Availability: The design maximizes the use of abundant resources (continuous electricity from the habitat, unlimited Martian regolith) while conserving scarce ones.
  • Practicality and Modularity: The Bench is conceived as a modular system. It provides the essential functions needed for an initial mission but can be expanded with new modules in the future as a settlement grows.

Project Report – NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025
Team: Nova Genesis | School: Nirmala Public School

Healthcare efficiency is critical for patient survival, yet hospitals often face challenges such as disorganized medicine storage, delays in emergencies, inefficient record-keeping, and improper biomedical waste disposal. These issues compromise patient safety, waste staff time, and pose environmental hazards.

Our team developed the Advanced Medicine Trolley with Integrated Smart Dustbin System, designed to improve hospital workflow, ensure systematic medicine storage, provide record-keeping space, and enable safe waste segregation. The trolley includes transparent compartments, a registration/digital space, and a five-color coded smart dustbin system aligned with global biomedical waste standards. 

Key features include: organized drawers, smart dustbin sensors with indicators, portability with swivel wheels, and scope for IoT/AI integration. The trolley enhances efficiency, reduces errors, promotes sustainability, and is scalable for clinics, hospitals, rural health centers, medical camps, and even space healthcare systems.

Future scope includes AI-enabled medicine tracking, IoT-based real-time monitoring, robotic automation for hazardous waste, and hospital management integration.

In conclusion, this innovation bridges efficiency, sustainability, and adaptability, offering a practical yet futuristic solution to improve patient care and biomedical safety.
projectDetails.details:

  • Time-efficiency during emergencies.

  • Sustainability and scalability across different healthcare environments.

projectDetails.name: Project Novaspark
projectDetails.summary:
Our team developed a comprehensive full-stack climate visualization platform that transforms complex NASA satellite data into actionable insights for understanding global weather patterns and climate trends. We built a system that processes 25 years of MERRA-2 climate data to provide interactive forecasts for temperature, precipitation, wind, snowfall, and air quality across any location worldwide.

Our solution addresses the critical challenge of making sophisticated climate science accessible by combining advanced backend data processing with an intuitive frontend interface. We integrated Google Gemini AI for intelligent weather classification and natural language explanations, while our parallel processing architecture ensures fast, reliable performance. The platform features multiple interactive map views, real-time graph generation, and seamless 2D/3D visualization capabilities.

This project is important because it democratizes climate understanding, helping diverse users—from travelers to agricultural planners—make informed decisions based on reliable climate intelligence. By bridging the gap between raw satellite data and practical weather insights, our team has created a tool that empowers better anticipation and adaptation to changing global climate conditions.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: WeatherDoc - AI-Powered Climate Intelligence Platform

What It Does & How It Works:

WeatherDoc is a comprehensive full-stack web application that processes 25 years of NASA MERRA-2 satellite data to deliver intelligent climate analysis and weather forecasting. The system accepts user-specified global coordinates and dates, then leverages parallel processing architecture to extract and analyze five key climate variables: temperature, precipitation, wind patterns, snowfall, and air quality index. Our multi-stage backend processes coordinate normalization for global coverage, concurrent data extraction from NetCDF datasets, automated graph generation showing historical trends (2000-2025), and AI-powered classification using Google Gemini that provides natural language explanations of weather phenomena.

Key Benefits:

- Democratized Access: Makes sophisticated climate science understandable through intuitive visualizations and plain-language AI explanations

- Comprehensive Analysis: Delivers multi-dimensional weather assessment across five critical environmental factors

- Historical Intelligence: Provides 25-year trend data to distinguish between temporary weather events and long-term climate patterns

- Global Scalability: Processes any location worldwide with intelligent coordinate handling and normalization

Intended Impact:

WeatherDoc aims to bridge the gap between complex meteorological data and practical decision-making for diverse users including travelers, agricultural planners, event organizers, and environmental researchers. By providing accessible climate intelligence, we empower better planning and adaptation strategies in an era of increasing climate volatility, ultimately contributing to more informed environmental stewardship and climate resilience.

Technical Implementation:

- Backend: Python, Flask, xArray, NumPy, Matplotlib, Concurrent Futures for parallel processing

- AI Integration: Google Gemini API for intelligent weather classification and natural language generation

- Data Sources: NASA MERRA-2 datasets (M2IMNPASM, M2TMNXFLX, M2TMNXAER) covering 2000-2025

- Frontend: React.js with interactive Leaflet/Google Maps, 2D/3D visualization libraries

- Architecture: RESTful API design with thread-safe operations and optimized file management

Creative Elements:

Our team's innovation lies in the seamless integration of multiple complex systems: real-time climate data processing, AI-powered natural language classification, and interactive geospatial visualization. We developed a unique coordinate normalization system that handles global coverage gaps, implemented parallel processing for computational efficiency, and created an AI classification system that goes beyond simple thresholds to understand nuanced "very uncomfortable" conditions combining multiple environmental factors.

Design Considerations:

Our team prioritized user experience through responsive design that works across all devices, implemented efficient memory management for large dataset handling, ensured accessibility through multiple map view modes (standard, satellite, night, topographical), and built robust error handling for edge cases in global coordinate processing. We also focused on scalability through our parallel architecture and maintainability through clean, documented code structure.

projectDetails.details: NASA Township Odyssey is an interactive, gamified web application that transforms NASA’s open Earth data into a township-building simulation. Players are challenged with real satellite-based questions derived from APIs such as MODIS (vegetation), SMAP (soil moisture), GPM (rainfall), and POWER (solar energy). The intended impact is to raise awareness about environmental sustainability and demonstrate how space-based data supports smart farming and climate resilience. projectDetails.name: ParadeGuard
projectDetails.summary: ParadeGuard is a data-driven weather risk dashboard built for NASA’s “Will It Rain on My Parade?” challenge. It provides users with location-specific insights on the likelihood of adverse weather—such as extreme heat, rainfall, wind, or poor visibility—using multi-source data from NASA and integrated APIs (Google Weather, Meteostat, Open-Meteo). The platform combines historical climatology and live forecasts to compute a weighted composite risk score (Rain 40%, Temperature 25%, Wind 20%, Visibility 15%). Users can search any location, select a date, and visualize risks through interactive charts, maps, and comfort indices. The interface, developed with Streamlit and Python, supports CSV/JSON data export and real-time analytics with caching and fallback APIs for performance reliability. ParadeGuard empowers event organizers, outdoor enthusiasts, and planners to make informed, data-backed decisions about timing and preparedness, turning decades of NASA weather data into a simple, actionable forecast planning tool.

Accurate location and forecast data for any place and time.

Risk scoring (0–100) based on rain, temperature comfort, wind, and visibility.

Interactive visualizations using Plotly and pydeck.

Data exports in CSV or JSON formats.


It caches API responses for speed, runs efficiently (<2 s), and includes fallbacks for reliability. Designed as an analytical tool, ParadeGuard helps users anticipate and mitigate weather disruptions using scientific data and NASA-aligned methodology.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology
projectDetails.summary:
BloomWatch (Bloomscope) is a literature-based project that explores how NASA’s Earth observation data can help us understand when and where flowers bloom around the world. By combining insights from satellite missions like Landsat, MODIS, and RADARSAT, along with ground reports from citizen scientists through the GLOBE Observer App, the project proposes a unified framework for tracking global flowering events.

This concept directly responds to NASA’s BloomWatch challenge by showing how different types of Earth data—optical, radar, and hyperspectral—can work together to reveal nature’s blooming patterns. Beyond science, Bloomscope highlights how climate change influences these natural rhythms and how technology can make them visible to everyone.

In essence, it’s about using space-based data to tell Earth’s seasonal stories—helping researchers, farmers, and everyday people stay connected to the living patterns of our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Bloomscope (BloomWatch) is a literature-based research project that explores how NASA’s Earth observation data can be used to study global flowering phenology—the timing and spread of blooming events across ecosystems. Instead of building a system, the project compiles and analyzes existing research, datasets, and methodologies to propose a unified conceptual framework for global bloom monitoring.

Through a detailed review of resources such as NASA’s GLOBE Observer App, MODIS and Landsat missions, RADARSAT Constellation data, and hyperspectral flower studies, Bloomscope examines how each dataset contributes to understanding vegetation patterns. The study emphasizes the integration of optical, radar, and ground-based observations to enhance the reliability of bloom detection models and reduce the limitations found in isolated approaches.

This project’s creative aspect lies in synthesizing scientific and technological insights into a single conceptual model that bridges gaps between disciplines—remote sensing, ecology, and citizen science. It offers a structured overview of how multi-sensor data could be harmonized for consistent global analysis.

The intended impact is educational and scientific: to help future researchers, environmental scientists, and data developers design effective bloom-monitoring systems based on existing literature. By highlighting challenges such as data integration, cloud interference, and validation gaps, Bloomscope provides a clear roadmap for advancing research in flowering phenology.

Ultimately, this literature-based project transforms scattered research into a cohesive vision for global environmental observation—a blueprint for turning data into discovery.

projectDetails.name: Palantir
projectDetails.summary: An enhanced, interactive web-based asteroid impact simulator that visualizes the devastating effects of asteroid collisions with Earth. This tool provides real-time physics calculations and beautiful visualizations to help understand the scale and consequences of asteroid impacts. It transforms raw data from NASA's APIs into a powerful educational and decision-support tool. Palantir provides an intuitive and engaging 3D platform to explore NEO data. The web-based platform is designed to be accessible to a broad audience, regardless of their technical expertise. The "Custom Asteroid" feature makes learning about asteroid threats an engaging and interactive experience. Palantir also have Mitigation Strategy Simulation features to simulate deflection strategies, such as kinetic impactors or gravity tractors.
projectDetails.details:
What it Does and How it Works

Palantir simulates asteroid impact scenarios by allowing a user to:

  1. Set Parameters: Use a control panel to specify the asteroid's properties, including its Diameter (10m - 10km), Impact Velocity (11-72 km/s), Impact Angle (15° - 90°), and Composition (Iron, Stone, Ice, or Carbon-rich).
    • Crater Formation
    • Fireball Radius
    • Air Blast Radius
    • Thermal Radiation (3rd-degree burn radius)
    • Seismic Effects (Richter scale magnitude)

Project Benefits and Intended Impact

The primary intended impact of the Palantir project is educational and to raise planetary defense awareness.

  • Educational Value: It helps users, students, and the general public understand the devastating power and true scale of asteroid impacts, how different parameters affect the outcomes, and the physics involved.
  • Mitigation Awareness: It underscores the crucial importance of asteroid detection and deflection programs by providing a tangible demonstration of "what if" scenarios.
  • Predictive Tool: While simplified, it uses real NASA and USGS datasets to provide credible predictions of consequences, which can be useful for initial scenario planning or discussion.

Tools and Technologies

The project utilizes web-standard and popular open-source technologies:

  • Coding Languages: HTML5 (semantic structure), CSS3 (styling, modern animations, and effects), Three.js(create and render 3D graphics and animations), and Vanilla JavaScript (physics engine and calculations).
    • Leaflet.js: Used for interactive map rendering.
    • OpenStreetMap: Provides the world map tiles.
  • Datasets: It uses real NASA and USGS datasets for its calculations.

Project Creativity

The creativity of this project lies in its comprehensive integration of complex scientific data with a highly visual, interactive, and user-friendly web interface:

  • Interactive and Accessible Visualization: It takes complex physics equations (like crater scaling laws and blast wave propagation) and translates them into a simple "point and click" web experience, making the science accessible to a non-specialist audience.
  • Modern UI/UX: It features a "Dark space-themed" design with modern aesthetics like Glassmorphism effects, smooth animations, and transitions, which enhance user engagement compared to traditional, purely data-driven simulators.
  • Contextualization: The inclusion of Famous Asteroid Presets (e.g., Tunguska, Chelyabinsk) and Energy Comparisons (e.g., TNT equivalent) is a creative way to give context to the simulated numbers, making the impact calculations more meaningful.

projectDetails.name: Project NOLA
projectDetails.summary:
NØLA is an advanced AI-driven satellite network designed to revolutionize the way we explore and visualize space. Combining artificial intelligence, real-time data processing, and immersive VR technology, NØLA creates a bridge between the cosmos and human experience. Each satellite in the NØLA constellation is equipped with high-resolution imaging sensors and an autonomous AI core capable of analyzing celestial patterns, mapping constellations, and tracking cosmic movements with extraordinary precision.

The collected data is processed and streamed directly into 360° VR environments, allowing users to witness Earth, stars, and galactic structures from orbit in real time. Through adaptive algorithms, NØLA optimizes satellite positioning, manages communication links, and enhances image clarity without human intervention. Its smart energy system, powered by solar efficiency modules, ensures sustainable operation across all orbits.

NØLA’s vision extends beyond observation—it aims to create an evolving digital map of the universe, accessible to researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide. By merging AI autonomy, constellation mapping, and virtual reality streaming, NØLA transforms traditional space exploration into an interactive and data-rich experience, opening a new era where anyone can explore the universe—virtually, intelligently, and in breathtaking detail.
projectDetails.details:
How NØLA Works

1. Satellite Network & Launch
NØLA begins with a constellation of AI-powered nanosatellites launched into Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Each satellite is equipped with high-resolution panoramic cameras, thermal sensors, and a compact AI computing module. These satellites form a synchronized orbital network, constantly communicating and sharing data with one another.

2. AI Data Processing
Once in orbit, each satellite captures real-time space and Earth visuals — stars, planets, and even atmospheric layers. The onboard AI instantly analyzes this data, detecting constellations, object movements, and celestial alignments. This minimizes the need for ground control, as the AI autonomously manages orientation, focus, and image clarity.

3. Constellation Mapping
The captured visuals are compiled to form a dynamic 3D star map. NØLA’s neural algorithms identify and update constellation positions using reference patterns and live movement tracking. This creates a constantly evolving AI-generated map of the night sky.

4. VR Streaming Pipeline
The processed 360° visuals are encoded and streamed directly to Earth through ultra-low latency transmission. Users with VR headsets or compatible devices can enter a real-time virtual environment, viewing Earth, stars, and orbits as if they were in space themselves.

5. Ground Integration & Learning Loop
Back on Earth, the ground AI hub collects data from all satellites, comparing predictions with actual movement patterns. The system continuously learns, updates its models, and sends optimized parameters back to the satellites. This closed learning loop helps NØLA evolve, becoming more precise with every orbit.

6. Sustainable Power System
Each satellite uses solar adaptive panels that rotate toward sunlight for maximum energy capture. Combined with low-power AI chips and temperature-regulated systems, NØLA maintains long-term efficiency with minimal maintenance.

projectDetails.name: The Unknown
projectDetails.summary:
In our project, “A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI,” we developed an advanced machine learning system to identify exoplanets from NASA’s publicly available datasets. Using the Kepler KOI dataset, we performed rigorous preprocessing, feature selection, and class balancing to ensure robust training. We trained five models—Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Network, and an unsupervised SVM—and combined them into a weighted ensemble to maximize accuracy and generalization. The ensemble model was validated not only on the Kepler dataset but also on additional NASA datasets, demonstrating strong transfer learning and minimal overfitting.

We then deployed the system through a user-friendly web dashboard, allowing researchers to analyze single entries or large CSV datasets, with detailed predictions and confidence scores supporting fuzzy classification. This tool streamlines exoplanet discovery, empowers scientists to prioritize high-confidence candidates, and bridges theoretical knowledge with practical AI applications, addressing NASA’s challenge of accelerating exoplanet identification efficiently and accurately.
projectDetails.details:
How it works:
Our project, “The Unknown: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI,” identifies exoplanets from NASA datasets using advanced machine learning techniques. The name “The Unknown” reflects our mission to explore the countless stars in the universe—most of which remain uncharted and mysterious—and help scientists discover worlds that are hidden or unknown.

We first preprocessed the Kepler KOI dataset, selecting only the most informative features and handling class imbalance using SMOTE and random oversampling. Without balancing, models would have been biased toward the majority class (non-planetary candidates), misclassifying the smaller but critical planetary data.

We trained five models—Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Network (supervised), and Support Vector Machine (unsupervised). The unsupervised SVM identifies planetary patterns as anomalies, complementing the supervised models. A weighted ensemble approach was then applied, giving slightly higher weight to the SVM, producing a single, accurate, and efficient model.

Benefits and Impact:
The ensemble model generalizes well across multiple NASA datasets, reducing false positives and negatives. Researchers can analyze individual stars or bulk CSV datasets using our web dashboard, which provides predictions along with confidence scores. This fuzzy classification enables scientists to prioritize high-confidence planetary candidates, accelerating exoplanet discovery and supporting data-driven decisions.

Transfer Learning in Our Project:
After training the ensemble model on the Kepler KOI dataset, we validated it using samples from the other two NASA datasets. Despite being trained on a single dataset, the model performed exceptionally well on unseen data, demonstrating strong generalization. This mimics transfer learning, where knowledge gained from one dataset is applied to related datasets, reducing overfitting and increasing model reliability.

Impact:
By using this transfer learning-like method, our system can handle diverse astronomical data, making it practical for real-world research where new datasets continuously emerge. It highlights the adaptability of our AI approach in exoplanet discovery, showing that our models are not limited to the dataset they were trained on.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS
  • Backend: Flask (Python)
  • Machine Learning: scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow/Keras
  • Data Handling: Pandas, NumPy
  • Deployment: Web-based interactive dashboard for real-time testing

Creativity and Considerations:

  • Combined supervised and unsupervised approaches to improve anomaly detection.
  • Weighted ensemble reduces computation while maximizing accuracy.
  • Developed an intuitive dashboard to make advanced ML accessible to non-technical users.
  • Addressed class imbalance, feature redundancy, and real-world scalability to ensure practical usability for NASA scientists.

Intended Impact:
Our project bridges AI with practical astronomy, helping researchers efficiently identify and prioritize exoplanets from massive datasets, potentially accelerating discoveries in the search for new worlds, and enabling exploration of “The Unknown.”

projectDetails.details:
BloomWatch is a web-based Earth observation dashboard that visualizes global flowering patterns using NASA satellite data.
It processes vegetation indices and phenology datasets (such as NDVI/EVI from MODIS or VIIRS) to detect “blooming events” and map them on an interactive world view.

It:

  1. Fetches satellite-based vegetation data from NASA Earth APIs.
  2. Applies filtering and thresholding techniques to detect areas with high flower reflectance patterns.
  3. Displays these regions as “Bloom Hotspots” on a global interactive map.
  4. Provides a timeline and species explorer, allowing users to track how bloom timing shifts across regions and seasons.

Benefits:

  • Climate Change Insight:
    Helps monitor how flowering cycles are shifting globally — key indicators of climate-driven changes.
  • Biodiversity & Ecology Support:
    Aids scientists and conservationists studying pollinator cycles, species interactions, and ecosystem health.
  • Agriculture Aid:
    Farmers and planners can use bloom timelines to forecast pollination windows and seasonal crop behaviors.
  • Educational & Public Awareness Tool:
    Makes complex NASA data understandable and visually engaging for students and the general public.

Development Stack:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React.js
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS, custom animations
  • Mapping: Leaflet.js
  • Data: NASA Earth Observation APIs (MODIS/VIIRS vegetation indices, phenology datasets)
  • Deployment: Vercel

projectDetails.name: ExoQuest
projectDetails.summary:
ExoQuest is an AI-powered web application designed to make abstract exoplanet data engaging and visual. The core idea is to let users explore distant worlds created on demand.

The application works by fetching scientifically plausible parameters (like temperature, star type, and radius) and uses procedural generation—a fast, pure JavaScript technique—to instantly create a unique, 3D equirectangular planet texture. This texture is mapped onto a sphere rendered with Three.js, providing a smooth, interactive, and mobile-friendly visualization.

Key features include a detailed ANALYSIS REPORT, a rule-based Habitability Score, and a Galaxy Logbook utilizing localStorage to save and track discoveries across user sessions. ExoQuest successfully transforms complex astronomical numbers into a tangible, visually rich exploration experience.
projectDetails.details:
The project is ExoQuest: AI-Powered Exoplanet Explorer, a web application that transforms abstract astronomical data into an interactive, visual, and educational experience.

🚀 Project Overview: ExoQuest

ExoQuest is a front-end web application that allows users to "explore" newly discovered or generated exoplanets in a futuristic, mission-control style interface.

How It Works

The core flow is driven by procedural generation linked to scientific parameters:

  1. Data Fetch: The app pulls data for a random exoplanet from an internal mock catalog (simulating data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive). This data includes key metrics like Equilibrium Temperature (Teq​), Radius, and Star Type.
  2. Visualization: The planet's data (especially temperature and planet type) is fed into a pure JavaScript function that algorithmically generates a unique, color-coded texture. For instance, a high temperature results in a dark, reddish texture (like a lava world), while a low temperature results in blue and white colors (ice world).
  3. 3D Rendering: The generated texture is applied to a sphere rendered using Three.js, which rotates smoothly in a simulated space environment.
  4. Analysis: The system calculates a Habitability Score (0-100%) based on scientific rules (e.g., is the temperature in the liquid water range? Is the planet rocky or a gas giant?).
  5. Persistence: Users can save their discoveries to the Galaxy Logbook, which uses the browser's localStorage to save the planet data across sessions.

Benefits, Creativity, and Impact

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Scientific Accessibility: The primary impact is making complex, numerical astronomical data accessible and visually compelling to the general public. It translates scientific facts into a tangible 3D visualization.
  • Engagement and Education: It offers an engaging, gamified way to learn about planetary diversity, the Habitable Zone, and exoplanetary classification.
  • Promoting Data Visualization: The project showcases how generative techniques can be used to visualize data for which no direct photographic evidence exists.

Creativity

ExoQuest's creativity lies in its Procedural-Scientific Linkage. Instead of using slow, generic AI image generators, the visualization is directly—and instantly—controlled by the planet's fundamental physics. A planet's appearance is a direct, visible output of its temperature and size, ensuring every generated world is scientifically plausible yet visually unique. The entire experience is packaged in a unique, responsive Mission Control UI aesthetic.

Factors Considered by the Team

  1. Speed and Stability: We prioritized a fast, stable experience. This led us to drop external AI APIs (like DALL-E/Stable Diffusion) and the external SimplexNoise library in favor of pure JavaScript procedural generation, ensuring near-instantaneous load times and eliminating external failure points.
  2. Scientific Integrity: We based the mock data, the procedural color palettes, and the Habitability Score rules on known astronomical principles (e.g., distinguishing gas giants from rocky worlds, using the Celsius/Kelvin liquid water range).
  3. User Interface: We focused on a dark, high-contrast, futuristic Mission Control theme, optimizing readability and visual appeal to reinforce the exploration theme.

projectDetails.name: Home in space
projectDetails.summary:
The project is an AI-assisted visual design tool for creating and evaluating space habitat layouts for lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions. It allows users to build modular habitats, define dimensions, assign functional zones, and receive automated scientific feedback. The system calculates total usable volume, area per crew member, storage capacity, path lengths, and mass constraints while checking zoning compliance, accessibility, and redundancy under simulated emergency scenarios.

AI evaluates 2D layouts to ensure functional efficiency, proper adjacency of rooms, and compliance with human-factor and engineering standards. The tool incorporates key habitat systems such as life support, thermal control, radiation shielding, power, waste management, and emergency egress.

Designed to be both educational and analytical, it helps users understand the trade-offs in space habitat design while providing quantitative validation and feedback. The project supports NASA’s Artemis goals by enabling users to explore, optimize, and test sustainable off-Earth living environments.
projectDetails.details:
DETAILED PROJECT SUMMARY

The project is a comprehensive AI-driven visual habitat design and evaluation tool built to assist in the conceptualization, analysis, and optimization of space habitats for lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions under NASA’s Artemis and future Mars campaigns. It focuses on integrating human, structural, and environmental factors into a single interactive system that allows both students and professionals to create scientifically credible and operationally feasible space habitat layouts.

Purpose and Objectives

The primary goal is to enable users to design and assess space habitats that can sustain human life for extended durations in extraterrestrial environments. The tool simplifies the complex process of habitat layout design by providing an interactive workspace where users can:

  1. Construct habitat modules using defined geometric forms (metallic, inflatable, or in-situ manufactured).
  2. Assign functional areas such as sleeping quarters, control stations, hygiene modules, and life support systems.
  3. Automatically calculate key parameters like usable volume, crew capacity, and resource requirements.
  4. Receive intelligent feedback from an integrated AI system that checks compliance with NASA’s standards for habitability, safety, and mission sustainability.

Scientific and Engineering Calculations

  1. Total Usable Volume (NHV)
    • Calculated as the difference between the total geometric volume of the habitat and the cumulative volume of all installed equipment and structures.
    • Provides accurate estimates of free, livable space within each module and for the entire station.
    • Derived by dividing NHV by the number of crew members.
    • Compared against NASA’s recommended minimum volumetric allowances to ensure sufficient habitability and avoid overcrowding.
    • Computes total area and volume devoted to food, water, tools, and other supplies.
    • Evaluates if storage allocations meet the operational demands for crew size and mission duration.
    • Measures the distance and arrangement between connected modules.
    • Identifies inefficient or overly long travel routes that may reduce crew productivity and increase fatigue.
    • The AI evaluates 2D top-view layouts to ensure proper adjacency of functional areas (e.g., separating noisy zones like gyms from sleep quarters).
    • Checks that hygiene, food prep, and medical zones follow ergonomic and operational best practices.
    • The AI runs multiple emergency scenarios (e.g., fire, hull breach, system failure) to evaluate whether critical pathways and backups are sufficient.
    • Determines which rooms or systems require duplicate components or alternate routes.
    • Each object and module is assigned an estimated mass.
    • The system performs binary checks to ensure the total mass does not exceed launch or landing payload capacities.
    • Calculates power, life support, and thermal regulation requirements based on crew count, mission duration, and installed systems.
    • Ensures that the energy demand is balanced with power generation and storage capacity.
    • Analyzes the 2D layout to confirm that all equipment, airlocks, and control points are physically reachable for maintenance and inspection.
  2. Crew Time Efficiency
  • Evaluates how long it takes for crew to move between critical zones (e.g., control → airlock → med bay).
  • Suggests optimized connector lengths to balance accessibility with zoning needs.

Functional and Structural Components

Each habitat can contain multiple specialized areas including:

  • Sleep Quarters – Personal or shared compartments for crew rest.
  • Galley / Wardroom – Cooking, dining, and social zones.
  • Hygiene Module – Toilets, washing, and basic bathing systems.
  • Control Station – Core for navigation, communication, and monitoring.
  • Life Support and Power Rooms – Housing for CO₂ scrubbers, O₂ tanks, and electrical systems.
  • Airlock and EVA Suit Bay – Entry/exit point for external missions.
  • Medical Bay – Treatment and emergency care.
  • Exercise Area – Countermeasures against microgravity health risks.
  • Storage Rooms – For food, tools, and spare equipment.
  • Maintenance Workshop – Repair and fabrication activities.
  • Science Lab – Dedicated area for experiments and research.
  • Radiation Shelter – Shielded space for high-radiation events.
  • Plant Growth Chamber – For biological life support and food production.

System and AI Integration

The integrated AI acts as both an evaluator and an advisor, analyzing user-created layouts through structured prompts and quantitative models. It provides:

  • Real-time numerical feedback on usable volume, NHV, and per-crew space.
  • Zoning validation through adjacency rules and human-factor mapping.
  • Emergency and redundancy evaluation, simulating structural and resource failures.
  • Optimization suggestions for path efficiency, mass balance, and system redundancy.
  • Visual feedback indicators (green = compliant, red = non-compliant) for quick interpretation.

Scientific Relevance

The tool incorporates fundamental parameters relevant to real-world habitat design:

  • Human factors (privacy, noise, lighting cycles, hygiene, and work efficiency).
  • Engineering limits (mass, power, structure, radiation, and thermal control).
  • Operational realism (redundancy, maintainability, and egress under stress).
    It bridges the gap between conceptual design and engineering evaluation, enabling users to learn through simulation while adhering to NASA’s standards for human spaceflight safety and comfort.

Intended Use Cases

  • Educational Platform: Helps students explore principles of human space habitation and engineering constraints.
  • Professional Concept Tool: Allows engineers and mission planners to visualize and validate early-stage habitat concepts.
  • Gamified Sandbox: Engages broader audiences by combining scientific accuracy with creativity and interactivity.

Impact and Innovation

This project delivers a unified platform that blends interactive design, quantitative analysis, and AI-assisted evaluation, making it easier and faster to develop feasible habitat concepts. It promotes scientific literacy, encourages engineering creativity, and supports NASA’s broader vision of sustainable human presence on the Moon and Mars.

By combining visual interactivity with real scientific logic and automated assessment, this tool transforms complex habitat engineering into an accessible, educational, and practical experience.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
DETAILED PROJECT SUMMARY

This project is an AI-assisted habitat design and analysis system created to simulate, construct, and evaluate space habitation environments such as lunar bases, Martian habitats, or orbital stations. The system combines a 3D modular design interface with AI-driven evaluation algorithms to ensure scientific accuracy, human-factor compliance, and mission readiness.

1. System Overview

Users can construct habitat layouts using a 3D layout editor, where rooms are represented as modular cubes or cylindrical connectors. Each module can be assigned specific functions such as crew quarters, laboratory, life support, storage, or medical bay.
The AI subsystem automatically performs technical and ergonomic assessments based on geometry, layout, and crew configuration.

2. AI INTEGRATION AND FUNCTIONAL ROLES

A. Spatial & Structural Analysis

AI analyzes the 2D and 3D layout maps to:

  • Detect unusable or cramped spaces using volume subtraction logic:
    Usable Volume = Total Volume of Habitat – Volume of Objects
  • Compare usable space per crew member with NASA’s recommended Net Habitable Volume (NHV) standards.
  • Provide feedback highlighting any zones below acceptable comfort thresholds or where human movement is restricted.

B. Human Factor & Crew Efficiency Evaluation

AI calculates:

  • Area per Crew Member = NHV / Crew Size
  • Path Length Between Zones, analyzing connector distances to ensure efficient movement.
  • Crew Time Efficiency, by detecting if long or redundant corridors increase travel time unnecessarily.

The AI gives qualitative feedback, identifying layouts that optimize crew mobility and workflow.

C. Zoning & Functional Compliance

Using 2D layout image analysis, AI verifies that:

  • Living zones, work zones, and hazardous zones maintain safe distances.
  • Egress routes and maintenance access points follow zoning rules.
  • Environmental systems and access routes comply with redundancy and emergency regulations.

It cross-references with preset zoning compliance prompts (aligned with NASA/ESA design logic).

D. Redundancy & Emergency Scenario Simulation

AI runs multi-scenario redundancy tests, simulating:

  • Fire in a zone
  • Pressure loss in a connector
  • Power failure or blocked exits

It checks if the layout allows:

  • Safe egress through alternate routes
  • Survival with available backup systems and storage

AI also determines resource redundancy, evaluating whether extra consumables and spares exist for a given crew and mission duration.

E. Resource & Storage Management

AI calculates:

  • Storage area and volume used for food, water, and equipment.
  • Compares it with the expected consumption rate per crew member and mission length.
  • Flags deficits or excesses in storage planning.

Formula used:
Total Storage Volume = Volume of all designated storage zones

3. Mass & Load Estimation

AI assists in mass constraint calculations by:

  • Estimating approximate weights for every component and human.
  • Summing them to compute total payload mass.
  • Comparing this with launch vehicle payload limits.
    If the payload exceeds threshold, AI provides mass-reduction suggestions.

4. Environmental & Life Support Load Calculation

AI estimates the Environmental Control Load (ECL) by:

  • Analyzing total crew count, oxygen/CO₂ balance, and thermal loads.
  • Predicting if the habitat’s energy and thermal systems can sustain environmental conditions.
  • Suggesting energy redistribution or increased life-support redundancy if limits are breached.

5. Maintainability & Accessibility

AI reviews the layout map and checks:

  • Whether all systems (airlocks, valves, panels) are reachable for maintenance.
  • If connectors allow internal movement between zones.
  • Whether emergency tools and repair stations are logically placed.

6. AI-Driven Feedback Mechanism

After performing all calculations and spatial evaluations, the AI provides:

  1. Numerical outputs (volume, path lengths, crew ratios).
  2. Comparative assessments against NASA standards.
  3. Textual feedback identifying design flaws, bottlenecks, and optimization paths.

Optional:

  • Haptic feedback can be given in VR mode to simulate path-length effort or cramped regions.

7. Scientific Relevance

This AI-based tool ensures that space habitat concepts are not only visually accurate but also scientifically validated. It mirrors the analytical process NASA engineers use when evaluating habitat modules, redundancy systems, and ergonomic layouts — making it both a professional engineering simulation and an educational research tool.

8. Core Benefit

The AI system reduces human workload by automating:

  • Volume, mass, and energy calculations
  • Ergonomic validation
  • Emergency scenario testing
  • Compliance checking

This allows human designers to focus on innovation and creativity, while AI ensures scientific consistency and mission safety.

projectDetails.name: Space Trash Hack: Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars
projectDetails.summary:
The SpaceTrash Hack project tackles one of the most pressing sustainability challenges in long-duration space missions: inorganic waste management. During a hypothetical three-year Mars mission, astronauts could generate over 12,000 kg of waste—including plastics, packaging, and textiles—which are impractical to store or return to Earth.
Our solution proposes a compact, solar-powered system that converts this waste into 3D printing filament. This filament can be used to manufacture tools, spare parts, and structural components directly on Mars, reducing payload mass and promoting in-situ resource utilization (ISRU). The process includes waste collection, sorting, shredding, extrusion, and quality control, culminating in functional printed products.
An energy and cost analysis reveals that filament extrusion is the most resource-intensive stage, but the overall system remains viable with renewable energy inputs. While challenges such as filament quality and throughput exist, the benefits—zero-waste operations, reduced Earth dependency, and enhanced mission sustainability—make this approach a promising leap toward self-sufficient extraterrestrial living.
projectDetails.details: Our project, Mars 3D Recycling Unit, transforms inorganic waste generated by astronauts on Mars into usable 3D printing filament. The system collects and sorts waste, pre-processes it by cleaning and shredding, and then extrudes it into filament for 3D printing tools, spare parts, and habitat components. This closed-loop approach reduces reliance on Earth supplies, minimizes waste accumulation, and enhances mission sustainability. Using hardware like extruders and 3D printers . The project adapts to Martian conditions with energy efficiency and safety in mind. By combining recycling and manufacturing in a single workflow, our project fosters self-sufficiency, innovation, and long-term exploration sustainability

projectDetails.summary:
The Weather Prediction Platform for Vulnerable Communities is designed with a strong focus on accessibility, accuracy, and real-time responsiveness. It offers a suite of key features including real-time weather data aggregation from trusted sources like NASA Earthdata and OpenWeatherMap, long-range 45-day weather forecasts powered by machine learning, and targeted disaster risk assessments for events such as floods, tsunamis, and hurricanes. The platform includes a location-aware alert system that automatically tailors notifications and warnings based on user location, a dark-themed NASA-inspired user interface for better visual comfort, and a dedicated admin portal for system oversight and data management.

From a technical perspective, the system architecture is modular and scalable. The frontend is built using React and Material-UI to ensure a responsive and intuitive user experience. The backend, developed with Node.js and Express, handles core functionality such as API routing, user authentication, and data management. A separate Python-based ML microservice, powered by FastAPI along with libraries like scikit-learn and TensorFlow, processes weather data and generates predictive models. PostgreSQL serves as the primary relational database, managing all user, alert, and forecast data. The entire platform is containerized using Docker to streamline development, deployment, and scalability across different environments.

projectDetails.name: Project SARKEET
projectDetails.summary:
Earth and the Solar System as our Cosmic "Home": This element deals with our local astronomical community.

The Solar System: It consists of the Sun (our star), the eight planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), dwarf planets (such as Pluto), moons, asteroids, and comets.

Earth's Protective Environment: The Earth is shielded by its atmosphere and the heliosphere—a huge magnetic bubble generated by the Sun that protects the entire solar system from extreme interstellar radiation. It's this special environment that has enabled life to thrive.

Humanity's Future in Space and Adaptation to the Cosmos: This is the space exploration and settling part.

Space Exploration: The continuing effort to launch instruments and human beings outside of Earth's atmosphere in order to study the universe, expand our understanding, and locate new resources.

Living in Space: Study (most commonly on the International Space Station, ISS) of how astronauts adjust to the harsh environment of space, overcoming difficulties such as weightlessness, radiation, isolation, and establishing a sustainable "space culture" for long-term spaceflight to places like the Moon and Mars.

Space Settlement: The permanent human presence living and working in communities around the solar system, using resources from asteroids or the Moon for the betterment of humanity and the protection of the Earth's environment.
projectDetails.details:
The spacecraft is located at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 , which is a gravitationally stable location approximately 1.5 million km away from Earth in the direction of the Sun. It offers an unobstructed view of the Sun and the solar wind approaching it.It employs a highly advanced instrument set to capture and quantify Energetic Neutral Atoms (ENAs). These are formed when the charged particles of the solar wind hit interstellar medium particles at the heliosphere's boundary. By charting the direction and energy of the ENAs, researchers are able to construct a 3D map of the boundary zone.

2. What are its advantages?

Enhanced Space Weather Prediction: IMAP delivers near-real-time measurements of the solar wind and high-energy particles, providing approximately 30 minutes of warning for potentially damaging space weather activity on the way to Earth.Technology and Astronaut Protection: The information assists in creating improved models to foresee space weather effects, which can cause power grid disruptions on Earth, harm satellites, and be a health threat to astronauts on long-duration flights.Understanding Planetary Habitability: By examining how our star's shield is created and its dynamic evolution, scientists can gain valuable insights on how other star systems' "heliospheres" shield exoplanets, supporting the search for life beyond our galaxy.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Scientific Impact: To fundamentally enhance our knowledge of heliophysics—how the solar system engages with the local galactic environment—and solve key questions regarding how particles get energized and transported around our cosmic home.Societal Impact: To contribute to improving the safety and resilience of contemporary technological infrastructure (communication, navigation, power systems) at risk from extreme solar activity.

4. What instruments, programming languages, equipment, or software did you use to create your project?

Hardware: The IMAP spacecraft itself, and its advanced package of particle detectors, magnetometers, and dust analyzers.Location/Orbit: The L1Lagrange Point.Technology/Data: Energetic Neutral Atom (ENA) detection. The information is analyzed through sophisticated computational and analytical models, normally employing languages such as Python and MATLAB, which are the norm for space science data analysis.

5. Why is your project creative?

The essence of creativity is in the way of mapping the heliosphere:Indirect "Seeing": IMAP is not able to see the edge of the heliosphere directly in a classical sense. It outsmarts by picking up Energetic Neutral Atoms (ENAs)—charged particles that have "neutralized" themselves—carrying it straight to the spacecraft. This converts the invisible boundary collision into a readable signature, basically using atomic messengers from the edge of the solar system to map out its boundaries.

6. What were some of the factors your team took into consideration?

Location: Choosing the L1moment was essential for ongoing, upstream monitoring of the solar wind.Instrumentation: Making the instruments sensitive enough to detect very low-flux particles over billions of miles away.Miniaturization: Creating a full suite of instruments that could be hosted on a single spacecraft.Longevity and Autonomy: Building the spacecraft to function automatically and dependably for extended years in deep space, out of reach from convenient repair or servicing.

projectDetails.name: Project SentiTech Squad
projectDetails.summary:
The Terra Satellite, launched by NASA in December 1999, is one of the most important Earth-observing missions. Its main goal is to study how the Earth’s atmosphere, land, and oceans interact and affect the global climate.

Terra carries five key instruments—MODIS, MISR, CERES, ASTER, and MOPITT—which together collect data on temperature, air quality, vegetation, clouds, and energy balance. This information helps scientists monitor environmental changes across the planet.

Over the years, Terra has made major discoveries, including tracking deforestation, melting ice caps, urban growth, wildfires, and pollution patterns. Its long-term observations have greatly improved understanding of climate change and the effects of human activities on Earth’s ecosystems.

As part of NASA’s Earth Observing System (EOS), Terra’s data continues to guide scientists and policymakers in addressing global environmental challenges. The mission has become a cornerstone of modern Earth science, highlighting both the beauty and fragility of our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Our team, consisting of five 8th-grade students, created a presentation and video about NASA’s Terra Satellite, focusing on its purpose, instruments, and major achievements.

Our project highlights Terra’s major milestones, including its launch, first global data collection, and over 20 years of continuous service. We also explored how Terra’s discoveries have revealed deforestation, melting ice caps, air pollution, and global temperature rise, helping scientists and policymakers address environmental challenges.

Through our presentation and video, we aim to celebrate Terra’s legacy and inspire others to appreciate how technology and teamwork can help us understand and protect our planet.

projectDetails.name: Project SilentVoice
projectDetails.summary:
SilentVoice is a communication system designed for individuals with ALS, Locked-In Syndrome (LIS), or severe stroke patients who find it difficult to move, gesture, or speak. By detecting the blinks of a person, SilentVoice converts them into clear, spoken or written messages in real-time. Users can communicate silently and effectively, and even control smart devices in their environment through personalized commands.

This solution directly addresses the challenge of enabling communication for those completely unable to interact using conventional methods. SilentVoice empowers users to express themselves independently, participate in daily life, and regain a sense of autonomy. Its significance lies in enhancing accessibility, fostering inclusion, and improving the quality of life for individuals facing extreme communication barriers.
projectDetails.details:
What it does / How it works:
SilentVoice enables communication for individuals with ALS, Locked-In Syndrome (LIS), or severe stroke who cannot move, gesture, or speak. It detects subtle cues such as eye movements or blinks and converts them into clear, written or spoken messages in real-time. Users can also control smart devices in their environment using customizable commands, allowing them to interact with their surroundings independently.

Benefits:

  • Allows complete non-verbal communication for users with extreme mobility restrictions.
  • Restores autonomy and reduces dependence on caregivers.
  • Improves social interaction, emotional expression, and participation in daily life.
  • Enhances accessibility and inclusion for severely disabled individuals.

Intended Impact:
SilentVoice aims to empower people who cannot speak or move, helping them regain a voice and control over their environment. It promotes independence, reduces isolation, and improves quality of life for users with severe communication barriers.

Tools, Languages, Hardware, and Software Used:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Socket.IO (JS client)
  • Backend: Python + Flask, Flask-Socket.IO
  • ML and Computer Vision: Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, TensorFlow/Scikit-learn
  • IOT and Hardware: ESP32, GPIO Control, Jumper wires + LEDs

Creativity:
The project creatively addresses communication for users who are completely non-verbal and unable to perform gestures, a group often neglected by conventional assistive technologies. SilentVoice combines intuitive interaction, environmental control, and real-time communication in a single seamless system.

Team Considerations:

  • Ease of use and minimal cognitive load for users.
  • Safety and reliability for real-time communication and device control.
  • Customization for individual needs and comfort.
