projectDetails.name: AIRE
projectDetails.summary:
Aire is a comprehensive planning platform designed to build climate resilience in fast-growing cities. The platform uniquely integrates Earth Observation data, crowdsourced community feedback, and intelligent AI tools to transform urban planning. It analyzes critical environmental layers—including heat risk, flood zones, air quality, and land use change—to provide actionable insights.

A core feature, the GeoAdapt module, delivers hyper-local guidance on climate-adapted building design, agricultural practices, and disaster preparedness. By offering role-based dashboards for planners, city leaders, and residents, Aire validates satellite data with on-the-ground knowledge. The ultimate goal is to foster safer, greener neighborhoods, optimize infrastructure investments, and empower communities to grow wisely in the face of environmental challenges. Aire helps build smarter cities for both people and the planet.
projectDetails.details:
Project Vision and Core Mission

Aire is a sophisticated, one-stop urban planning platform engineered to empower fast-growing cities in their fight against climate change. The core mission is to build urban resilience by seamlessly integrating three critical streams of information:

  1. High-resolution satellite data (Earth Observation).
  2. On-the-ground human intelligence (Community Input).
  3. Advanced analytics and forecasting (Smart Tools).

By harmonizing these elements, Aire provides city planners, municipal leaders, and residents with the data-driven insights needed to design and adapt their environments for a sustainable and secure future. The project's philosophy is rooted in "smart planning for people and planet," ensuring that urban growth is equitable, environmentally conscious, and resilient to future shocks.

Platform Architecture: The Four Core Modules

Aire's functionality is delivered through four deeply integrated modules that form a comprehensive urban planning ecosystem.

  • 1. Earth Observation Layers: This module serves as the foundational data engine of the platform. It aggregates and processes near real-time data from a variety of public and private satellite constellations. This raw data is then translated into clear, actionable, and map-based visualizations, allowing users to understand complex environmental dynamics at a glance.
  • 2. Planning & Decision Tools: This is the analytical brain of the platform. It equips urban planners with a powerful suite of tools to move from data to decisions. These tools use predictive analytics and machine learning to model the potential impacts of different planning choices, helping to de-risk investments and optimize for resilience.
  • 3. Community Feedback Portal: Acting as the "human sensor network," this module bridges the gap between high-level satellite data and localized, real-world conditions. It is a user-friendly, mobile-first interface that empowers residents to become active participants in the urban planning process, ensuring that solutions are context-aware and address genuine community needs.
  • 4. GeoAdapt Module: This unique module synthesizes information from all other parts of the platform to provide hyper-local, climate-aware guidance. It moves beyond just identifying risks to offering concrete, evidence-based recommendations for living, building, and farming in a changing environment.

Detailed Module Functionality

Earth Observation Layers

This module provides a multi-layered view of the urban environment by integrating data from various specialized satellite missions:

  • Heat Risk Zones: Utilizes thermal data from satellites like MODIS and Landsat to identify urban heat islands—areas where asphalt and buildings trap heat—which are critical for public health planning.
  • Flood-Prone Areas: Combines soil moisture data from SMAP with precipitation data from the GPM mission to map areas with high flood risk, both from overflowing rivers and surface water accumulation.
  • Air Quality Monitoring: Leverages sensors on satellites like Aura and the Sentinel-5P to track concentrations of pollutants such as NO₂, SO₂, and particulate matter, identifying pollution hotspots.
  • Vegetation Index (NDVI): Calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index to assess the health and density of green spaces, crucial for monitoring urban parks and green belts.
  • Land Use & Urban Expansion: Employs datasets like the Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) and SEDAC to track how the city is growing, monitor informal settlements, and analyze land consumption patterns.
  • Population Density & Growth: Integrates data from WorldPop and other demographic sources to visualize population distribution and growth trends, which is essential for infrastructure and service planning.

Planning & Decision Tools

Users can leverage these tools to build a more resilient city:

  • Zoning Recommendation Engine: An AI-powered tool that analyzes environmental risk layers (flooding, landslides, heat) and suggests optimal zoning regulations. For example, it might recommend restricting residential construction in high-risk floodplains and instead zoning those areas for parks or recreational use.
  • Infrastructure Gap Analyzer: This tool overlays existing infrastructure maps (e.g., storm drains, public transit, hospitals) with population density and climate vulnerability data to pinpoint critical service gaps. It can answer questions like, "Which neighborhoods lack sufficient storm drainage to handle a 50-year flood event?"
  • Climate Vulnerability Scorecard: A comprehensive assessment tool that assigns a vulnerability score to different city zones based on a weighted combination of environmental risks, population density, and socio-economic factors. This helps leaders prioritize investments in the most vulnerable communities.
  • Scenario Simulator: An interactive tool that allows planners to model the future. Users can adjust variables like "projected sea-level rise" or "population growth rate" to simulate different scenarios and visualize their potential impact on the city's infrastructure and resources, enabling proactive rather than reactive planning.

Community Feedback Portal

This module fosters a collaborative planning environment:

  • Crowdsourced Issue Reporting: Through a simple mobile app, residents can report local issues by dropping a pin on a map. They can tag the issue (e.g., "blocked drain," "extreme heat," "air pollution smell"), upload a photo, and add a brief description.
  • Data Validation and Ground-Truthing: This citizen-generated data is invaluable for validating satellite observations. For instance, a cluster of resident reports about localized flooding after a storm can confirm and refine the flood-risk models generated from satellite data.
  • Targeted Local Action: City agencies can monitor this real-time feedback to dispatch maintenance crews, issue localized health warnings (e.g., for heat or air quality), or identify the need for small-scale infrastructure improvements like planting more street trees or installing a new public water fountain.

GeoAdapt Module

This is Aire's most innovative feature, providing actionable, location-specific intelligence:

  • Historical Climate and Disaster Analysis: The module analyzes decades of climate data to identify trends (e.g., rising average temperatures, decreasing rainfall) and catalogues historical disaster events (floods, landslides) to understand an area's specific risk profile.
    • Building Design: Recommends architectural styles suited to the local climate, such as houses on stilts in flood-prone areas or buildings with green roofs to mitigate heat.
    • Farming Practices: Suggests crop types that are resilient to changing rainfall patterns or advises on optimal irrigation techniques.
    • Lifestyle & Safety: Provides practical tips for residents, such as evacuation routes for floods or the locations of public cooling centers during a heatwave.

User Experience and Application

Interactive Dashboard & User Roles

The Aire platform is accessible via a web-based dashboard with a clean, map-centric interface. Key features include toggleable data layers, clickable zones for detailed reports, and color-coded risk overlays. To serve different stakeholders, Aire provides distinct user modes:

  • Planner Mode: Unrestricted access to all data layers and the full suite of planning and simulation tools.
  • Leader Mode: Provides high-level executive summaries, key performance indicators, and budget impact reports for mayors and city managers.
  • Resident Mode: A simplified interface focused on local insights, community reporting, and receiving safety alerts.
  • Agency Mode: Tailored for specific bodies like environmental agencies, focusing on ecosystem health, pollution monitoring, and long-term environmental trends.

Use Case: Kanjirapalli, Kerala

To illustrate its practical application, consider a use case for Kanjirapalli, a region susceptible to heavy rainfall and landslides:

  1. Risk Identification: Aire's Earth Observation layers would identify steep, deforested slopes with soil types prone to saturation, flagging them as high-risk landslide zones.
  2. Adaptive Housing: The GeoAdapt module would analyze this risk and recommend slope-stable housing designs, such as terraced construction and deep-rooted vegetation for soil stabilization, discouraging conventional designs in these areas.
  3. Resilient Agriculture: By mapping historical and projected rainfall trends, Aire could advise local farmers on transitioning to crops that are more tolerant of intense rain and help plan the placement of check dams to manage water runoff.
  4. Public Safety: The platform would identify optimal locations for shaded community walkways and public hydration stations based on heat island data and pedestrian traffic patterns, enhancing public health and safety.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is integral to the core functionality of the Aire platform, enabling it to move from simple data visualization to predictive and prescriptive analytics. Here is how AI is used:

  • Predictive Risk & Probability Analysis: The GeoAdapt module uses machine learning models, particularly time-series forecasting and regression analysis, to predict the future likelihood and intensity of climate-related events. For example, it analyzes historical rainfall, soil moisture, and geological data to forecast landslide probability under different future climate scenarios.
  • Zoning Recommendation Engine: This tool is powered by a classification algorithm. The AI analyzes multiple layers of data—such as flood risk, heat vulnerability, population density, and existing infrastructure—to recommend the most suitable land use zoning (e.g., residential, commercial, green space) for specific parcels, optimizing for safety and climate resilience.
  • Scenario Simulator: Our simulation tools leverage AI to model the complex, cascading impacts of planning decisions. When a planner proposes a new development, the AI simulates its potential effects on local air quality, traffic patterns, urban heat island intensity, and storm-water runoff, providing a holistic impact assessment before any ground is broken.
  • Satellite Image Processing and Feature Extraction: On the back end, we use computer vision algorithms (specifically, Convolutional Neural Networks - CNNs) for automated feature extraction from raw satellite imagery. This allows us to automatically classify land use, detect the expansion of informal settlements, and monitor changes in vegetation cover (deforestation or greening) in near real-time.

projectDetails.summary:
We developed Defend Earth: Impactor-2025, an interactive asteroid impact simulator designed to be both user-friendly for the public and scientifically rigorous for experts. The platform integrates real datasets from NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) API and USGS geospatial resources to model asteroid trajectories, impact consequences, and mitigation strategies.

The tool offers two modes:

Play Mode engages the public with simple sliders and visual storytelling, letting users adjust asteroid size, speed, or deflection and instantly see 3D impact simulations, craters, and tsunami maps.
Pro Mode provides scientists and policymakers with advanced dashboards, accurate orbital mechanics, and hazard overlays for decision-making, including the ability to export impact reports and test deflection scenarios.

This project addresses the challenge of making complex asteroid threat data accessible, educational, and actionable. By combining intuitive design with real science, Defend Earth bridges the gap between public engagement and professional preparedness — empowering everyone to better understand and respond to planetary defence challenges.

MAIN OBJECTIVE : MAKING A VERY SIMPLE USER FRIENDLY APP CONSISTING BOTH COMPLEX AND SIMPLE IDEAS!
projectDetails.details:
What it does / how it works:
Defend Earth: Impactor-2025 is an interactive web-based simulator that models asteroid impact scenarios and mitigation strategies. It integrates real-time asteroid data from NASA’s NEO API with environmental datasets from the USGS. Users can explore asteroid trajectories in 3D, simulate impact outcomes such as crater size, blast radius, and tsunamis, and test deflection strategies like kinetic impactors or gravity tractors.

Benefits and intended impact:
The project makes asteroid threats understandable to the public while giving scientists and policymakers a rigorous decision-support tool. It raises public awareness through gamified interaction while enabling experts to visualize risks, assess consequences, and plan responses. By bridging education and science, it helps both inspire and prepare society for real planetary defense challenges.

Tools and technologies:
We used Python (Flask/FastAPI) for backend simulation, JavaScript with Three.js and D3.js for visualizations, and MapLibre/Leaflet for impact zone mapping. Data integration relied on NASA NeoWs and USGS DEM/topography datasets.

Creativity and design choices:
The project is unique in its dual-layer approach:

  • Play Mode simplifies science into an accessible, game-like experience with intuitive sliders and visual storytelling.
  • Pro Mode provides detailed dashboards, exportable reports, and advanced simulation accuracy.

Our team prioritized clarity, accessibility, and engagement — from choosing clean fonts and user-friendly controls to ensuring scientific validity — to create a tool that is both fun and functional at the highest level.

projectDetails.name: Project EXOPLANET
projectDetails.summary:
The Necessity: A Data Deluge 
Modern exoplanet-hunting missions, like NASA's Kepler Space Telescope and the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), monitor hundreds of thousands of stars simultaneously for years. This generates an astronomical amount of data.

Massive Volume: TESS alone generates terabytes of data, creating millions of "light curves" (graphs of a star's brightness over time). It's physically impossible for human astronomers to manually inspect every single one.

Tiny Signals: The signal of a transiting exoplanet—the dimming of a star's light as a planet passes in front of it—is incredibly faint. It's like trying to detect the dimming of a car's headlight when a fruit fly passes in front of it from a mile away.

Complex Noise: This faint signal is often buried in "noise." The star itself might have sunspots or flares that cause its brightness to vary, or the satellite's instruments might have subtle errors. Distinguishing a true exoplanet transit from this noise is extremely difficult. so we developed an ML using ensemble .
projectDetails.details: It's smarter at handling the specific challenges of exoplanet data. It can see the faint, hidden patterns in the noise, work at a scale humans cannot, and do so with unwavering consistency, ultimately accelerating the pace of cosmic discovery.

projectDetails.name: SpaceCast
projectDetails.summary: SpaceCast is an innovative climate change early warning system that harnesses the power of NASA’s space-based satellite data and artificial intelligence to predict and alert communities about climate-driven hazards such as droughts, floods, heatwaves, and sea-level rise. Built using tools like Google Earth Engine, Python, and React/Streamlit for visualization, SpaceCast ensures that satellite data can be processed, analyzed, and communicated efficiently in real time. The platform is cloud-deployed and scalable, capable of reaching even the most remote areas with limited infrastructure.

PlanetGuard 2.0 is an advanced, modular web application that combines AI, satellite data, and geospatial analytics to predict, monitor, and respond to natural disasters such as floods, wildfires, and earthquakes. By transforming complex satellite data into actionable intelligence, PlanetGuard 2.0 empowers decision-makers to plan smarter, respond faster, and build more resilient communities in the face of increasing climate challenges.
projectDetails.details: PlanetGuard 2.0 is an AI-powered web application that predicts and responds to natural disasters such as floods, wildfires, and earthquakes. projectDetails.name: Project TECH TRIB3

projectDetails.details:
Project Overview & Functionality

The NASA Space Biology Knowledge Engine is a full-stack web application that turns NASA's complex Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) into an accessible, interactive dashboard.

It has a React front-end that provides a dynamic user interface and a Python/Flask back-end that serves as a smart middleware. The back-end calls multiple live NASA APIs, processes, cleans, and unifies the data before sending it to the front-end in a simple format. This leads to benefits like better efficiency for researchers and easier access for a wider audience, making a dense scientific repository straightforward to search and explore.

Intended Impact

The project's goal is to speed up scientific discovery and help with future mission planning. By making this data available to more people, we allow a larger community to gain insights into the biological effects of spaceflight, which is essential for designing safer long-duration missions.

Technology Stack

Front-End: React.js, React Router, Vite, JavaScript, CSS

Back-End: Python, Flask, Flask-CORS, Requests

Development: VS Code, Git, npm, and pip with venv for package management.

Creative Approach & Key Considerations

Our project's creativity comes from its user-focused design for a data-heavy problem. Instead of just showing raw data, we aimed to create a guided journey of discovery for the user.

A major decision was to use our back-end as an abstraction layer. This "translator" simplifies the complexity of multiple, inconsistent NASA APIs into a single, clear API for our application to use. During development, we faced real-world issues like unreliable external APIs and inconsistent data formats. Our answer was to build a strong back-end that filters and standardizes data, ensuring a smooth user experience despite the messy source data.

projectDetails.name: India's breathing crisis
projectDetails.summary:
Project Overview
This project utilizes multi-year NASA MODIS satellite data (2018–2024) to analyze Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) across the Indian Subcontinent. AOD reflects atmospheric aerosol loading, including both air pollutants (smog, smoke) and natural particles (dust, sea salt).

Objectives

Seasonal Cycle: Characterize sharp, predictable shifts in air quality driven by India’s monsoonal climate.

Pollution Hotspots: Identify persistent high-AOD regions, particularly over the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) during winter.

Key Drivers: Correlate AOD patterns with the monsoon “washout” effect, pre-monsoon dust storms, and post-monsoon pollution from crop burning and stagnant air.

Yearly Variations: Examine inter-annual changes, notably the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown, which caused an unprecedented temporary drop in anthropogenic AOD.

Findings (Visualized)

Monsoon Cleansing (Jul–Sep): AOD reaches annual lows (blue/green tones) as rainfall removes aerosols.

Winter Pollution Peak (Oct–Feb): AOD surges (red/brown tones) across the IGP due to biomass burning, heating, and trapped emissions.

2020 Anomaly: April 2020 data reveal a short-lived but remarkable improvement in air quality during lockdown.

Conclusion
India’s air quality is governed by intertwined climatic and human factors. While the monsoon offers a natural reset, the recurring high AOD during dry seasons—especially over the IGP—highlights the urgent need for sustained, multi-sectoral emission control efforts.
projectDetails.details:
This project leverages multi-year satellite observations from NASA’s Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) aboard the Terra and Aqua satellites to study Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) variations across the Indian Subcontinent from 2018 to 2024. AOD represents the concentration of aerosols—tiny solid or liquid particles suspended in the atmosphere—arising from both anthropogenic sources (pollution, biomass burning) and natural processes (dust storms, sea spray).

Objectives:

  1. Seasonal Cycle:
    Analyze the characteristic seasonal variations in AOD linked to India’s monsoonal climate, identifying the cyclical rise and fall of aerosol concentrations.
    • Monsoon washout effect (aerosol cleansing by rainfall)
    • Pre-monsoon dust storms from arid regions
    • Post-monsoon biomass burning and emission trapping during stagnant weather
  2. Yearly Variations:
    Examine inter-annual AOD changes, highlighting the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown as a unique period of significantly reduced anthropogenic emissions.

Findings (Visualized through MODIS Data):

  • Monsoon Cleansing (Jul–Sep):
    AOD values drop to their annual minimums (visible as blue/green tones in maps) due to intense rainfall that efficiently removes atmospheric aerosols.
  • Winter Pollution Peak (Oct–Feb):
    Elevated AOD levels (red/brown tones) dominate the IGP region, driven by crop residue burning, increased heating emissions, and limited atmospheric dispersion.
  • 2020 Anomaly:
    April 2020 imagery shows a temporary but dramatic improvement in air quality during the national lockdown, illustrating the direct impact of reduced human activity on atmospheric clarity.

Conclusion:

India’s atmospheric aerosol patterns are shaped by the dynamic interplay between climatic cycles and human activities. The monsoon season serves as a natural atmospheric “reset,” while dry-season peaks—especially over the IGP—underscore persistent air quality challenges. Long-term solutions demand integrated emission control strategies across sectors to achieve sustained improvements in regional air quality.

projectDetails.name: Vanishing White-Terra Antarctica
projectDetails.summary:
“Vanishing White-Terra Antarctica” is an animated story celebrating 25 years of NASA’s Terra satellite observations by showcasing the dramatic changes in Antarctica’s ice cover. Using data from Terra's five instruments—MODIS, CERES, MOPITT, MISR, and ASTER—we illustrate how rising temperatures and human activities are accelerating ice melt and contributing to sea level rise.

This project aims to transform complex satellite data into a captivating narrative, making Earth science more accessible and highlighting the impacts of polar change. By blending science and storytelling, “Vanishing White” honors Terra’s legacy and inspires reflection on the future of our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Here’s a detailed write-up (around 200 words) that you can use or adapt for your project submission:

Project Details – “Vanishing White-Terra Antarctica”

Vanishing White is an animated data story that visualizes 25 years of Terra satellite observations to show how Antarctica’s ice has changed over time. The project integrates datasets from all five Terra instruments — MODIS (snow cover), CERES (energy budget), MOPITT (carbon emissions), MISR (multi-angle imagery), and ASTER (high-resolution glacier views). These data layers are transformed into time-lapse animations and visual overlays that narrate the connection between ice loss, global warming, and rising sea levels.

The animation was developed using NASA’s Worldview, Panoply, and Google Earth Engine for data visualization, and assembled with InVideo AI and Adobe After Effects for storytelling and cinematic rendering.

Its benefits include making complex climate data visually accessible, promoting public understanding of Earth system science, and inspiring action on climate resilience.

The project’s creativity lies in merging real satellite data with artistic storytelling — turning scientific insights into an emotional visual journey. Our team focused on accuracy, narrative clarity, and global relevance, ensuring that Terra’s long-term legacy was portrayed not just as data, but as a story of our planet’s transformation.

projectDetails.name: Exoplanet Probability: Hunting for Worlds with AI
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary – ExoPredict

ExoPredict is an AI-powered platform designed to identify potential exoplanets using NASA Kepler mission data. The system integrates a **machine learning model (XGBoost)** trained on 41 stellar and orbital features to predict the likelihood of an exoplanet’s existence. Built with **FastAPI** on the backend and **React** on the frontend, ExoPredict offers an intuitive interface with three prediction modes — **KepID Search**, **Custom Feature Input**, and **CSV Upload** — enabling both researchers and enthusiasts to explore celestial data efficiently.

This project addresses the challenge of analyzing massive astronomical datasets by automating the classification process and improving accessibility to complex scientific models. Its importance lies in **accelerating exoplanet discovery**, promoting **open science**, and bridging the gap between **astronomy, AI, and education** — empowering users to engage with real NASA data through a user-friendly and transparent predictive system.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – ExoPredict: AI-Powered Exoplanet Detection System

Overview

ExoPredict is an AI-powered web application designed to identify and visualize potential exoplanets using NASA’s open exoplanet datasets. It combines machine learning, data visualization, and a user-friendly interface to assist researchers, students, and enthusiasts in analyzing space data efficiently.

The system provides an interactive UI built with React that allows users to upload exoplanet data, run real-time AI predictions, and visualize results through clean and insightful charts.

How It Works

  1. Data Input: Users upload datasets (for example, NASA Kepler or TESS datasets) in .csv format.
  2. Data Preprocessing: The system cleans and normalizes the data before model evaluation.
  3. AI Prediction: The pre-trained machine learning model classifies each celestial object as a potential exoplanet or non-exoplanet based on astrophysical parameters.
  4. Visualization: The interface displays analytical insights — confidence levels, distributions, and potential planetary patterns — through charts and tables.
  5. Results Export: Users can download the analyzed results for further study.

Benefits and Impact

  • Accelerates Exoplanet Discovery: Enables faster analysis of massive datasets that would take days to process manually.
  • Supports Citizen Science: Makes space research accessible to everyone, not just professional astronomers.
  • Promotes STEM Learning: Encourages students to explore AI applications in astrophysics.
  • Enhances Data Transparency: Utilizes NASA’s public datasets to encourage open research collaboration.

Tools, Languages, and Frameworks

  • Frontend: React, TailwindCSS, Recharts, shadcn/ui
  • Backend / AI: Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn (Random Forest, Logistic Regression)
  • Dataset Sources: NASA Exoplanet Archive, Kepler Mission Data
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub
  • Deployment: Vercel or Render

Creativity and Design

ExoPredict stands out for its fusion of science and design—translating complex space data into an intuitive, visually engaging dashboard. The project emphasizes accessibility and clarity, ensuring that even non-experts can understand and explore exoplanet data.

The UI is designed with a modern, space-inspired aesthetic, featuring a minimal color palette, data-focused visualization, and responsive layouts.

Team Considerations

During development, the team focused on:

  • Data accuracy and integrity to ensure reliable AI predictions.
  • Scalability to make the platform expandable for future datasets or missions.
  • User experience to provide a simple yet powerful interface for diverse audiences.
  • Open-source collaboration so that researchers and students can contribute to improving the model.

Intended Impact

The project aims to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and astrophysics, empowering people worldwide to participate in the search for worlds beyond our own.
By democratizing access to exoplanet research, ExoPredict supports NASA’s mission of expanding knowledge and fostering innovation for a better understanding of our universe.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Our project, ExoPredict, integrates Artificial Intelligence in two primary areas:

  1. Machine Learning Model Development:
    • We used AI techniques such as supervised learning (Random Forest and Logistic Regression models) to classify celestial bodies as potential exoplanets or non-exoplanets based on NASA’s open datasets (Kepler and TESS).
    • The models were trained and evaluated using Python libraries such as scikit-learn and pandas.
    • These models form the analytical core of the project, providing automated predictions that accelerate data-driven discovery.
    • AI-assisted tools (such as ChatGPT) were used to streamline code structuring, improve documentation clarity, and enhance user interface text.
    • All AI-generated content was reviewed, modified, and validated by our team to ensure technical accuracy and originality.

No AI-generated images, videos, or audio were used in the project.
All visual elements, datasets, and model outputs are derived from NASA’s open-source data and our own design work.

projectDetails.summary:
The project "Bio Space Stations: Pioneering Human Health in Orbit" developed an integrated biological space habitat system designed to address the adverse effects of spaceflight on human health. It combines modular labs with lab-on-a-chip biosensors, AI-driven health monitoring, radiation-shielded habitats, artificial gravity rings, and regenerative agriculture to support long-term human missions. This design continuously monitors neurological, immune, metabolic, and reproductive health, mitigating the impacts of microgravity and radiation through personalized countermeasures and sustainable ecosystems.

The project tackles critical challenges like neurological impairment, immune suppression, musculoskeletal degradation, and reproductive risks, which are major barriers to prolonged space exploration. Its importance lies in enabling safer, more resilient human presence in space, laying the foundation for sustainable colonization of Mars and beyond. Leveraging advanced technologies and synthetic biology, it transforms hostile space environments into life-supporting habitats, pioneering the future of deep space travel and human resilience.
projectDetails.details:
The project "Bio Space Stations: Pioneering Human Health in Orbit" by The Junction Brains aims to design innovative space habitats that address the biological challenges faced by astronauts during deep space missions.

What it does and how it works

The project explores the impacts of spaceflight on neurological, immune, metabolic, musculoskeletal, microbial, reproductive, and genetic systems, and develops solutions like modular labs with lab-on-a-chip biosensors, radiation-shielded habitats using water walls, artificial gravity rings, and regenerative agriculture zones. These components work together to continuously monitor health parameters, mitigate radiation and microgravity effects, and sustain long-term human life in space through closed-loop ecosystems and adaptive countermeasures.

Benefits and intended impact

It offers preventive and personalized health monitoring, protection against space radiation, maintenance of musculoskeletal and neurological functions, and sustainable food production in space. The intended impact is to create autonomous, self-sustaining bio space stations enabling safe, long-duration human space exploration and Mars colonization while enhancing astronaut resilience and well-being.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, software

The project incorporates cutting-edge technologies such as lab-on-a-chip devices, wearable biosensors, AI-driven gene expression and health monitoring algorithms, quantum sensing, and neural brain-computer interfaces. The lab-on-a-chip systems process biological data for real-time analysis. AI and machine learning models adapt and personalize countermeasures. Hardware includes radiation-shielding water walls and rotating habitats for artificial gravity simulation.

Creativity

The project is creative in integrating biology, synthetic biology, and ecology with advanced technology to transform harsh space environments into sustainable habitats. It leverages novel living architecture concepts, genetic engineering for radiation resistance, modular AI labs, and closed-loop regenerative systems that recycle resources and optimize health dynamically.

Factors considered by the team

The team considered biological impacts of microgravity and radiation on various systems, psychological well-being, reproductive challenges, metabolic and musculoskeletal degradation, microbial dynamics, and ecological sustainability. Ethical AI use, crew autonomy, habitat modularity, multi-generational safety, and resource efficiency were key considerations in designing adaptive, scalable solutions.

In summary, this project is a biological revolution in space habitation aimed at enabling resilient, self-sustaining human presence on Mars and beyond through integrated technology, biology, and ecological engineering.

projectDetails.name: Chrysalis Aurelia
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary – Chrysalis Aurelia.      
We, Team Phoenix Protocol, developed Chrysalis Aurelia, an intelligent recycling system designed to turn mixed plastic waste into reusable polymer sheets. Our project combines QR-code waste verification, ultrasonic sensors, a nichrome-wire heating plate, and advanced air filters to create a safe and efficient recycling process. It even includes automatic lid locking, temperature monitoring, and smoke filtration to make sure the system is both safe and sustainable.
We created this system to address the “Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars” challenge, where recycling must work under extreme Martian conditions like dust, low gravity, radiation, and limited energy. Our design can adapt to these challenges using solar power or by converting Martian radiation into energy.
This project is important because it changes how we look at waste. Instead of throwing plastics away, we can reuse them to make strong sheets that can be used for insulation, flooring, packaging, or even construction support on Mars. Our goal is to build a future where humans can live sustainably both on Earth and beyond — by transforming pollution into potential, and waste into wealth.
projectDetails.details:
PROJECT DETAILS – CHRYSALIS AURELIA

What Does It Do
CHRYSALIS AURELIA is designed to automate the recycling of mixed plastic waste, especially in extraterrestrial environments like Mars. The concept converts uncut plastics into thin, reusable sheets using controlled heat and compression. These sheets could be reused for insulation, surface covering, or as feedstock for future 3D printing, transforming plastic waste into a valuable resource.

How Does It Work
The system concept includes a metal container and automated pressing mechanism integrated with temperature sensors that would detect the melting points of different plastics. A nichrome-based heating plate would melt and compress the plastic at controlled temperatures. Toxic fumes are planned to be filtered through a carbon filtration unit and a compact HEPA H13 mini-filter. The simulated working is programmed in PictoBlox, with the usage of chatgpt and gemini for researching about new components, concepts and considerations .Meta AI was used to create backdrops (images) for the pictoblox codes.The entire mechanism's structure is currently demonstrated in Tinkercad simulation, showing sensor readings, lid operations, heating, and filtration virtually.

Benefits
The project concept enables on-site recycling of plastic waste, reduces environmental impact, and could lower dependence on Earth-based resupply. It produces reusable materials suitable for space missions and terrestrial applications while promoting energy-efficient waste processing.

Intended Impact
This system aims to establish a self-reliant circular recycling process adaptable for Mars and Earth. By turning plastic pollution into practical materials, it contributes to sustainable living and supports the development of long-term extraterrestrial habitats.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used
We used PictoBlox for automation and AI control, ChatGPT and Gemini for the research of new concepts, contents etc,and Meta AI for creating images (3 images). The hardware structure simulation concept includes a nichrome heating plate, temperature sensors, automated pressing unit, and carbon + HEPA H13 filters. All hardware operations and interactions are currently demonstrated through Tinkercad simulations, including sensor readings, lid control, heating, and filtration.

How the Project Was Created
We researched Martian environmental conditions and plastic melting behaviours, then designed the recycling unit conceptually. Using Tinkercad, we created simulations to showcase how the system would operate, including sensor-triggered heating, compression, and filtration. This approach allows us to demonstrate the project effectively without physical hardware investment.

Factors Considered
We focused on energy efficiency, safety, material suitability, adaptability to low-pressure and temperature variations, and sustainability. Simulations ensured that the system design is practical, safe, and capable of producing reusable materials under realistic extraterrestrial conditions.

projectDetails.details:
Project Details: NASA Bioscience AI Dashboard

The NASA Bioscience AI Dashboard is an innovative platform designed to centralize and analyze decades of NASA’s bioscience research. Over the years, NASA has conducted numerous experiments to study the effects of space environments on humans, plants, microbes, and animals. However, this valuable data is scattered across many databases and publications, making it difficult for researchers to find and use effectively. Our project addresses this problem by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to organize, summarize, and visualize bioscience data in one interactive dashboard.

The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) to automatically read and summarize research papers, identify key findings, and classify studies based on themes. It then builds a knowledge graph to map connections between experiments, species, missions, and biological effects. The interactive dashboard allows users to explore these relationships visually, search by topic, and gain insights quickly.

The project’s main benefits include improved accessibility to NASA’s bioscience information, faster discovery of relevant studies, and better collaboration between scientists from different fields. By simplifying access to complex data, it helps researchers generate new hypotheses and supports future Moon and Mars missions by enhancing understanding of how space conditions affect living organisms.

The system is developed using Python and JavaScript, with Hugging Face Transformers and spaCy for NLP, Neo4j for knowledge graphs, and Plotly Dash or Streamlit for visualization. Data is sourced from NASA’s open-access bioscience repositories.

This project is creative because it combines AI, knowledge graphs, and visualization to make scientific data truly interactive. Our team focused on accuracy, usability, scalability, and ethical AI use. Ultimately, the NASA Bioscience AI Dashboard transforms how space bioscience research is accessed and understood, paving the way for sustainable human space exploration.

Our project focuses on creating a sustainable and scalable ecosystem in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) that supports research, manufacturing, and satellite servicing. As NASA transitions from operator to customer, the goal is to empower private entities to make space more accessible and commercially viable.
The proposed LEO Microfactory and Servicing Hub integrates modular R&D pods for pharmaceuticals, materials science, and electronics fabrication, along with robotic satellite servicing and refueling systems. projectDetails.details: Our project, “Making LEO Accessible & Viable,” aims to design a sustainable ecosystem in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) where research, manufacturing, and satellite servicing can coexist. The core concept is a LEO Microfactory and Servicing Hub — a modular orbital platform equipped with R&D pods and robotic servicing arms. How it Works: The microfactory modules serve as plug-and-play research pods that can be leased by private firms or research institutions. These pods are designed for material science, pharmaceutical, and electronics experiments in microgravity. The servicing hub uses robotic systems to inspect, refuel, and repair satellites — extending their operational life and reducing debris. Benefits & Impact: Reduces launch and maintenance costs for small and medium players. Extends satellite lifetimes and decreases orbital debris. Promotes sustainable space commercialization and research opportunities. Supports NASA’s vision of transitioning to a customer-driven LEO economy. Tools & Technologies Used: We used CAD modeling tools (Fusion 360 & SolidWorks) for module design, Blender for visualization, and Python-based simulation tools for orbital dynamics and cost estimation. Presentation and documentation were developed using Canva, PowerPoint, and Figma for visualization. Creativity & Team Considerations: Our design emphasizes scalability, modularity, and sustainability — ensuring environmental responsibility and global accessibility. We considered economic viability, environmental impact, and technical feasibility to align with NASA’s sustainability goals while envisioning a future orbital business park that democratizes access to space.

projectDetails.name: ROUTLEDGE
projectDetails.summary: We developed an automated brick loading system that uses an escalator mechanism integrated into a truck to streamline the brick-loading process in brick-making factories. Traditionally, loading bricks is time-consuming and labor-intensive, requiring workers to manually lift and stack heavy bricks into trucks. Our solution replaces this with a motorized conveyor system that automatically lifts and loads bricks, reducing manual labor, increasing safety, and cutting loading time by more than half. This innovation directly addresses key challenges in the industry, such as low efficiency, high labor costs, and worker fatigue or injury. It is especially beneficial for small to medium-sized factories looking for affordable automation solutions. The system is designed to be durable, easy to operate, and scalable, making it a practical improvement for real-world factory conditions. By automating a single but essential step in the production chain, our project contributes to higher productivity safer work places , and a more mordern and sustainable brick manufacturing process.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: Automated Brick-Loading System

1. What does it do or how does it work?

  • What it does: The project is an innovative transport solution designed to significantly streamline the final stage of the brick-making process—loading finished bricks onto delivery trucks.
  • How it works: We have replaced the standard, manual-opening tailgate of a conventional delivery truck with a robust, motorized escalator-style conveyor belt system.
    • Integration: The conveyor mechanism is permanently mounted and structurally integrated into the vehicle's body, designed to withstand the weight and abrasive nature of the bricks.
    • Operation: Bricks are placed directly onto the running conveyor from the factory's final staging area. The system automatically lifts the bricks and deposits them neatly and efficiently into the truck bed, evenly distributing the load without the need for human personnel inside the truck.
    • Power: The system is powered by the vehicle's engine (via a Power Take-Off/PTO) or an auxiliary power unit (APU) for reliability.

2. What benefits does it have?

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to modernize and increase the scalability of brick-making factories, particularly in regions where labor is still the primary method.

  • Economic Impact: To provide a clear Return on Investment (ROI) for factory owners through cost savings on wages and faster turnaround times, allowing trucks to complete more delivery cycles per day.
  • Social Impact: To shift the role of factory workers from strenuous manual labor to supervisory and machine-operation roles, improving job quality and worker longevity.
  • Industry Impact: To establish a new standard for logistics in the clay, cement, and other block-manufacturing sectors.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Since this is a mechanical engineering project, the focus was on hardware and design software:

  • Hardware:
    • Custom-fabricated steel conveyor structure (High-Tensile Steel).
    • Industrial-grade Electric or Hydraulic Motors (for the conveyor drive).
    • Heavy-duty rubber or modular plastic belting designed for abrasive materials.
    • Sensor array (e.g., proximity sensors) to monitor the brick flow and prevent jamming.
  • Software/Tools:
    • Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Software (e.g., SolidWorks or Autodesk Inventor) for modeling the mechanism and integration with the truck chassis.
    • Finite Element Analysis (FEA) Software to simulate stress and load bearing on the structure.
    • Basic PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) or Microcontroller for controlling the motor speed, direction, and sensor feedback.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity lies in the novel integration of an established technology (the conveyor belt) into a mobile logistics platform (the truck) to solve an industry-specific problem.

  • Recontextualization: Conveyors are common in stationary factories, but integrating one as the primary, permanent, and functional part of a delivery truck is a unique approach to mobile loading.
  • System Design: The design addresses the unique challenge of distributing the load evenly within the truck bed—something a simple static conveyor cannot do—by potentially using a traversing head or adjustable boom angle, making the solution elegant and practical.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Load Balancing & Vehicle Dynamics: Ensuring the weight and placement of the escalator mechanism did not compromise the truck's stability, axle load limits, or road legality.
  • Durability & Maintenance: Selecting materials that could withstand constant exposure to dust, heavy loads, and outdoor environments with minimal maintenance.
  • Power Efficiency: Designing a system that could operate effectively without draining excessive power from the truck's engine or requiring overly large auxiliary batteries.
  • Adaptability: Designing the system to be retrofittable or easily adapted to various common truck chassis models used globally in the industry.
  • Brick Protection: Ensuring the conveyor speed and drop height were optimized to minimize impact and prevent costly brick damage.

projectDetails.name: God's Eye
projectDetails.summary:
God’s Eye is an AI-powered crowd management and evacuation system designed to enhance safety in large public gatherings. It uses YOLOv8-based computer vision to detect and count people in real-time, providing accurate crowd density analytics from short video feeds. The system also integrates Google Gemini AI to generate optimized venue layouts, helping organizers visualize safe entry and exit routes.

By combining live headcounts with intelligent layout planning, God’s Eye predicts bottlenecks and high-risk zones before they become critical. The platform’s web-based dashboard displays real-time crowd flow, alerts, and automatic rerouting suggestions—empowering authorities to make proactive decisions during emergencies.

This solution addresses the growing global challenge of crowd-related disasters by transforming surveillance footage into actionable safety intelligence. Ultimately, God’s Eye provides the situational awareness and reaction time needed to save lives in densely populated environments.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an AI-powered crowd analysis and management system designed to help event organizers and safety teams monitor and control crowd density in real-time. Using computer vision and video analysis, the system automatically detects and counts people entering or exiting a monitored area. This enables dynamic crowd flow assessment, early detection of congestion, and optimized emergency response.

The system works by processing short video feeds (up to 8 seconds each) captured at key entry gates. It uses YOLO-based object detection models to identify individuals and track movement frame by frame. The processed data is displayed on a web-based dashboard that visualizes live counts, flow direction, and crowd trends for situational awareness.

Our goal is to assist authorities in preventing overcrowding incidents, ensuring safe entry/exit flow, and enabling data-driven decision-making during large public events.

Tools, Technologies & Development

  • Languages: Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • Frameworks/Libraries: OpenCV, Ultralytics YOLOv8, FastAPI, Pandas, Plotly
  • Environment: Anaconda (Python 3.13), Localhost Web Interface
  • AI Tools: Google Gemini API (for generating schematic venue layouts)
  • Visualization: Custom-built dashboard with live charts and video display

Key Benefits

  • Real-time people counting and density tracking
  • Helps identify crowding risks before they become dangerous
  • AI-assisted layout generation for event planning
  • Scalable and lightweight for portable deployments

Creativity & Design Considerations

Our team focused on real-world applicability, AI ethics, and modularity.

  • We avoided unnecessary facial recognition to ensure privacy.
  • The layout AI focuses on schematic planning, not surveillance.
  • The dashboard design prioritizes clarity, accessibility, and responsiveness.

  1. Computer Vision (YOLOv8) –
    Used for detecting and counting individuals in short crowd videos.

projectDetails.name: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings
projectDetails.summary:
Stellar Stories is an interactive, educational web platform designed to teach students about space weather — how solar flares, CMEs, and geomagnetic storms affect Earth and human life. The website adapts its content based on the learner’s school level (Elementary, Middle, or High School), providing personalized storytelling, visuals, narration, and quizzes.

Built using React, Node.js, and MongoDB, it combines playful design, voice narration (Google TTS), interactive animations (Lottie), and real NASA data to make complex space science engaging and easy to understand.

The project addresses the challenge of making scientific literacy accessible and fun, turning space weather concepts into relatable human stories — from astronauts to farmers. By merging technology, education, and storytelling, Stellar Stories inspires curiosity, encourages STEM learning, and helps young minds connect with the science of our Sun and planet.
projectDetails.details:
“Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings” is an interactive storytelling website that simplifies complex space weather concepts for students of all ages. When a user enters the site, they select their school level (Elementary, Middle, or High School) — and the platform dynamically adapts the storytelling style, visuals, narration, and quiz difficulty based on that level.

The website explains how solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and geomagnetic storms affect daily life on Earth — from astronauts and pilots to farmers and children — through animated stories, interactive diagrams, and real NASA space weather data.

Technically, the platform is built using React.js (frontend), TailwindCSS and Framer Motion for responsive design and animation, and Node.js with Express.js (backend) connected to a MongoDB database for storing student progress and quiz results. Google Cloud Text-to-Speech generates natural narration, while NASA APIs provide authentic real-time data on solar activity and auroras.

The project’s goal is to bridge science and imagination, turning learning into an adventure. It encourages curiosity about Earth–Sun interactions and promotes STEM education in an engaging, age-appropriate way.

Creative Aspect: The fusion of storytelling, adaptive learning, gamification, and real scientific data makes this an immersive, playful, and educational experience that helps young learners see space science through human eyes.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI tools were used as assistive and creative accelerators in the development of Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings.

  1. Voice Narration:
    We integrated Google Cloud Text-to-Speech (TTS) to generate clear and age-appropriate narration voices for each school level — soft and story-like for elementary students, and formal yet engaging for higher levels. All narration audio is AI-generated and properly acknowledged in the metadata.
  2. Content Enhancement & Idea Structuring:
    AI-assisted writing tools (e.g., ChatGPT) were used to help refine storytelling flow, generate quiz questions, and simplify scientific explanations into age-appropriate language while ensuring factual accuracy.
  3. Image and Animation Guidance:
    AI-based image suggestion tools were used to generate initial concepts for background illustrations and character ideas. These AI-generated visuals were later recreated and adapted with appropriate watermarks and credits.

No NASA logos or official branding elements were used or modified in any AI-generated content. The AI was employed solely to enhance creativity, accessibility, and engagement, not to replace human input or originality.

projectDetails.name: Project Trivox
projectDetails.summary: Our project focuses on developing a machine learning model capable of identifying exoplanets using publicly available NASA datasets from missions such as Kepler, K2, and TESS. Traditionally, exoplanet detection relied on manual analysis of light curve data, which is time-consuming and prone to human error. By applying AI and ML techniques, our model automates this process, classifying celestial bodies as confirmed exoplanets, candidates, or false positives based on parameters like orbital period, transit duration, and planetary radius. The trained model is integrated into a simple web interface built using HTML and CSS, allowing users to upload new data and instantly receive predictions. This project addresses NASA’s challenge of improving the efficiency and accuracy of exoplanet discovery while making the process accessible to researchers and enthusiasts alike. It demonstrates how AI can accelerate scientific exploration and contribute to future space discoveries.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an AI-powered system designed to automatically identify exoplanets from NASA’s open-source datasets, such as those from the Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. Using parameters like orbital period, planetary radius, and transit duration, the model classifies each celestial object as a confirmed exoplanet, candidate, or false positive.

We developed the project using Python in Google Colab, leveraging machine learning libraries such as Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib. The model was trained and tested on preprocessed NASA data, and its accuracy was optimized through scaling and hyperparameter tuning. The trained model was then exported as a .pkl file, which can be connected to a frontend interface built using HTML and CSS to make predictions interactively.

This project reduces manual effort in exoplanet identification, accelerates research, and enables both scientists and students to explore astronomical data intuitively. Its creativity lies in merging AI with space science and presenting complex data analysis through a simple, accessible web interface.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to automatically classify celestial objects as exoplanets, candidates, or false positives based on NASA’s open-source datasets. Our AI model was trained on features such as orbital period, transit duration, planetary radius, and other observational parameters. We implemented algorithms like Logistic Regression and Random Forest Classifier using Python’s Scikit-learn library in Google Colab.

The AI model learns patterns from historical data and applies them to new or unseen data to make accurate predictions. This approach eliminates manual classification, improves detection accuracy, and allows faster discovery of potential exoplanets.

challengeDetails.title: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI
challengeDetails.excerpt: Data from several different space-based exoplanet surveying missions have enabled discovery of thousands of new planets outside our solar system, but most of these exoplanets were identified manually. Your challenge is to create an AI/ML model that is trained on one or more of the open-source exoplanet datasets offered by NASA and that can analyze new data to accurately identify exoplanets. (Astrophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: NASA DATA EXPLORATION IN AGRICULTURAL

This project explores how NASA’s satellite data and Earth observation technologies are transforming modern agriculture. With growing challenges like climate change, soil degradation, and water scarcity, farmers and scientists need accurate, large-scale environmental information. NASA provides this through its Earth Science Division and various satellite missions that monitor land, water, and atmosphere conditions around the globe.Key NASA missions such as Landsat, MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), and SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) supply vital data on crop health, soil moisture, drought conditions, vegetation cover, and land use patterns. By analyzing this data, researchers can track seasonal changes, predict crop yields, and improve decision-making in precision farming.

NASA’s initiative, NASA Harvest, demonstrates the practical application of these tools by collaborating with global partners to enhance food security, sustainability, and resilience in agriculture.
Additionally, tools like NASA Worldview, Giovanni, and Earthdata Search make satellite data accessible to users worldwide, supporting educational, governmental, and commercial efforts.

projectDetails.name: Project Aurora
projectDetails.summary: The Aurora Project is an interactive web platform that blends real-time space weather data with community storytelling. Built with Django, the system fetches live solar and geomagnetic data from NOAA APIs to predict aurora visibility and send alerts to users. When significant space weather events occur, the platform automatically creates event threads where users can share photos, videos, and personal experiences of witnessing auroras and other space weather effects. This creates a crowdsourced historical archive where each solar storm is documented through both scientific data and human stories. The platform features timeline visualizations of past events, interactive maps showing aurora visibility zones, and a social layer that connects celestial phenomena with terrestrial experiences, making space weather accessible and meaningful to the general public.
projectDetails.details:
Aurora Project - Detailed Project Overview

What It Does & How It Works

The Aurora Project is a Django-based web platform that integrates real-time space weather monitoring with community engagement. The system automatically fetches solar wind data, Kp indices, and geomagnetic activity from NOAA APIs to predict aurora visibility probabilities. When significant space weather events occur (like coronal mass ejections or geomagnetic storms), the platform creates dedicated event threads where users can share their experiences through photos, videos, and stories. The backend processes scientific data while the frontend displays interactive timelines, aurora prediction maps, and user-generated content galleries.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Educational Value: Makes complex space weather concepts accessible to the general public
  • Scientific Contribution: Creates a crowdsourced database linking solar activity with terrestrial observations
  • Community Building: Connects astronomy enthusiasts, photographers, and scientists worldwide
  • Historical Preservation: Documents space weather events through both data and human experiences
  • Real-time Utility: Provides practical aurora prediction alerts for photographers and sky-watchers

Technical Stack

  • Backend: Django (Python) with REST API endpoints
  • Data Sources: NOAA SWPC, OVATION Aurora Forecast APIs
  • Frontend: HTML/CSS/JavaScript with Leaflet.js for maps and Chart.js for data visualization
  • Database: PostgreSQL with PostGIS for location data
  • Task Processing: Celery for background data fetching and alert generation
  • File Storage: AWS S3 for user-uploaded media
  • Notifications: WebPush API for real-time aurora alerts

Creative Elements

  • Dual Perspective: Bridges the gap between scientific data and human experience
  • Event-Based Storytelling: Automatically generates "time capsules" for each significant space weather event
  • Crowdsourced Verification: Allows users to confirm aurora predictions with actual sightings
  • Interactive Timeline: Visualizes the relationship between solar activity and public observations over time

Key Considerations

  • Data Accuracy: Implemented data validation and source verification for scientific integrity
  • User Experience: Designed intuitive interfaces for both data-heavy displays and social features
  • Scalability: Built to handle increased traffic during major space weather events
  • Accessibility: Ensured compatibility with screen readers and mobile devices for field use
  • Privacy: Implemented robust media upload permissions and location privacy controls
  • Scientific Value: Maintained data standards suitable for potential research applications

The project transforms abstract space weather data into tangible, human-centered experiences while maintaining scientific rigor and educational value.

projectDetails.summary:
Our project,

CHRONO-SHIFT, created by Team Vajram, is an educational app that performs time dilation calculation and determines potentially habitable planets.

It solves the problem that complex scientific principles such as time dilation are hard to grasp for the majority of individuals. Our app makes this phenomenon—a fundamental aspect of Einstein's relativity —easy to understand by using interactive simulations, space visualizations, learning modules, and quizzes. Individuals can learn how both.

This work is significant because humanity is on the cusp of interstellar travel. Our app offers tools to methodically discover and map humanity's next home, making time dilation a theoretical limitation instead of a calculated variable for future space flight. It empowers users with the information to comprehend our universe and our place in it.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details: CHRONO-SHIFT

What is it or how does it work ?

CHRONO-SHIFT is an interactive web application to make abstruse astrophysical phenomena, mainly time dilation, intuitive and help in the quest for habitable exoplanets . The app operates in a client-server model, retrieving real-time data dynamically from different space APIs . People may engage with a Time Dilation Engine to model the experience of velocity and gravity on time, from astronauts aboard the ISS to theoretical models near black holes such as Gargantua . Outside simulations, it has "Space Surf" for solar system visualization in real time , "Celestialpedia" for a cosmic objects knowledge base learning modules for detailed study and challenges to test understanding and knowledge gaining .

What are the benefits?

The main advantages of CHRONO-SHIFT are:

Educational Accessibility: It converts abstract scientific theories into interactive and comprehensible experiences, making astrophysics accessible to a larger community of people other than scientists.

Improved Knowledge of Space Travel: By depicting time dilation, the app provides an understanding that time is a quantifiable factor in upcoming interstellar travels, not an impassable obstacle.

Inspiration for Generations to Come: By making users familiar with the marvels of space and the scientific complications of exploration, it seeks to spark interest in STEM studies.

Data-Driven Discovery: It offers tools and data to methodically scrutinize and discover possible worlds to live, advancing the common human quest for our next home.

What is the desired outcome of the project?

The intended impact of CHRONO-SHIFT is to empower users with a deeper understanding of the universe, particularly regarding the nuances of time and space in the context of interstellar travel. We aim to foster a scientifically literate public that can grasp concepts vital for humanity's future in space In the end, the project aims to add to the conversation and work of mapping systematically and discovering humanity's next home for habitation, translating abstract scientific concepts into concrete, understandable knowledge for everyone.

What coding languages, hardware, software, or tools did you use to create your project?

Coding Languages: JavaScript (for React and Node.js)

Frameworks/Libraries:

Frontend: React.js for the UI.

Backend: Node.js for server functionality and API management.

3D Visualization: WebGL (most probably through a library such as Three.js to allow easier interaction) for displaying interactive space environments).

Database: (Referenced in presentation) Holds data regarding celestial objects and user progress.

APIs: Space APIs to receive real-time satellite information, cosmic information, and celestial object data.

Deployment : GitHub for version control and Netlify for continuous deployment and hosting.

Security: HTTPS, JWT authentication, and encrypted data exchange.

Why is your project creative?

CHRONO-SHIFT is creative in a number of ways:

Narrative Integration: It doesn't simply show data; it tells a story around humanity's greatest questions: "How does time act in space?" and "Where do we go next?".

Interactive Storytelling : Through the use of interactive visualizations and simulations (such as the black hole example), it provides users with active experience of scientific principles instead of passive reading.

Gamified Learning : Incorporating challenges and quizzes innovatively enhances learning and motivates users.

Visual Appeal : Through WebGL rendering of beautiful 3D visualizations of space environments and objects, it beautifies the user interface and renders intricate subjects visually appealing .

Integrated Approach : It innovatively integrates educational materials (learning modules, Celestialpedia) with discovery instruments (Space Surf, Time Dilation Engine) to deliver an immersive and holistic platform.

What were some of the key considerations your team had ?

Team Vajram took various important considerations into account during development:

User Experience (UX) : Placing emphasis on a simple, interactive, and easy-to-use interface to make otherwise complicated subjects accessible to users of all ages and technical proficiencies.

Scientific Accuracy : Having all simulations, data, and descriptions conform to the established scientific rules, specifically Einstein's relativity theories for time dilation .

Data Integrity : Gathering good and up-to-date data from trusted space APIs.

Performance : Optimizing the app for seamless performance, particularly for 3D visualizations (WebGL), on different devices.

Scalability : Creating the architecture to enable future expansion, including more features, modules, and data without major overhauls.

Security : Putting in place features such as HTTPS and JWT authentication to secure user information and provide secure interactions .

projectDetails.details:
EcoFarm Simulator is an interactive web-based educational game that transforms NASA’s open datasets into a hands-on learning experience about sustainable agriculture. It uses real environmental data—such as soil moisture, temperature, rainfall, and vegetation indices (NDVI)—to simulate realistic farming conditions. Players analyze this data to make informed decisions on irrigation, fertilization, and livestock management, and the game visualizes how these choices affect crop growth, yield, and long-term sustainability.

The platform aims to make complex scientific data accessible and engaging for learners. By integrating NASA’s Earth observation data, EcoFarm helps users understand how real-world environmental factors influence agricultural outcomes and resource management. The intended impact is to promote data-driven decision-making, encourage sustainable farming practices, and build awareness of climate-smart agriculture.

The game was developed using React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for the front end, integrated with NASA Power API for live environmental data. Leaflet maps visualize geospatial datasets, and Firebase supports data storage and authentication.

Creatively, EcoFarm gamifies scientific learning—turning satellite data into interactive decision-making challenges. The team focused on usability, educational value, and visual appeal to ensure that both students and farmers can learn about sustainability in an engaging, impactful way

projectDetails.details:
VyoMeds is a responsive web application developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 – Create Your Own Challenge category. The project addresses the issue of limited visibility and accessibility of medicines for patients in Kerala, India.

VyoMeds allows users to upload a prescription image, from which medicine names are extracted using dummy OCR data. The user can then search for medicines case-insensitively (e.g., “Paracetamol” or “paracetamol”) and instantly view nearby pharmacies on a Kerala-specific Google Map. Each pharmacy listing shows stock availability, prices, and distance, helping users choose the most convenient option.

Pharmacies have a dedicated dashboard that automatically updates their stock in real time as sales or restocks occur (simulated in the prototype). The system also provides notifications to patients when medicines become available nearby.

Tools & Technologies Used:

Frontend: React.js, Tailwind CSS

Backend: Node.js with dummy JSON data

APIs: Google Maps JavaScript API (restricted to Kerala), Geolocation API

OCR (Simulated): Dummy data; future upgrade with Tesseract.js or Google Cloud Vision

Version Control & Deployment: GitHub, Vercel

Intended Impact & Benefits:

VyoMeds bridges the gap between patients and pharmacies, making access to essential medicines faster, location-based, and reliable. It reduces the time patients spend searching for medicines and empowers pharmacies to manage their inventory efficiently.

Creativity & Design Approach:

The project combines AI-driven medicine recognition (future OCR integration), real-time stock synchronization, and map-based visualization to create an accessible digital healthcare tool tailored to Kerala’s geography. The interface was designed to be clean, mobile-friendly, and intuitive, ensuring ease of use for all age groups.

projectDetails.summary:
AeroShield uses Earth Observation data + cloud computing to create a global predictive system that warns about dangerous air quality and sky conditions in real time.
-A web-based application that forecasts air quality.
-Clear visualizations of complex information, such as air quality forecasts, that includes landscape features.
-Proactive user alerts about potential health risks related to poor air quality.
-User-centric design
projectDetails.details:
What does it do / How does it work?

AeroShield Dashboard is a real-time air quality monitoring web application that allows users to visualize and understand the Air Quality Index (AQI) of any location worldwide.

It combines interactive maps, charts, and live environmental data using the OpenWeatherMap Air Pollution API.
Here’s how it works:

  1. Interactive Map (Leaflet.js):
    Users can click anywhere on the map or search for a city to retrieve AQI data.
    • A color-coded card displays AQI levels (Good → Hazardous).
    • A 24-hour trend chart (Chart.js) visualizes historical air quality changes.
    • A heatmap overlay shows pollution intensity across major cities.
  2. Dark/Light Theme Toggle:
    The UI automatically adapts to user preference for visual comfort.

What benefits does it have?

  • Educational Insight: Helps users understand local and global air quality trends.
  • Health Awareness: Displays alerts when pollution levels are unsafe.
  • Decision Support: Encourages safe outdoor planning based on real-time AQI.
  • Accessibility: Works in browsers on desktop and mobile; no installation required.


    Intended Impact

The project aims to raise environmental awareness by providing clear, visual access to air pollution data.
Intended impacts include:

  • Encouraging individuals and policymakers to make environmentally conscious choices.
  • Empowering communities to track pollution hotspots.
  • Supporting sustainability education by showing how air quality fluctuates with time and location.


    Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used

Frontend:

  • HTML5 – for structure
  • CSS3 – for responsive, themed design
  • JavaScript (ES6) – for dynamic interactivity
  • Leaflet.js – for maps and heatmap visualization
  • Chart.js – for historical AQI chart plotting

Backend:

  • Node.js + Express.js – for handling API requests securely (server.js)
  • CORS & dotenv – to handle environment variables and cross-origin requests
  • OpenWeatherMap API – for AQI and pollution data

Other Libraries:

  • Leaflet Heatmap Plugin – to visualize regional air quality intensity
  • Leaflet GeoSearch – to allow search-based location input
  • Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) – for reverse geocoding

Hardware/Software Requirements:

  • Runs on any device with a modern browser
  • Optional local Node.js server for proxying API calls

    Creativity and Innovation
  • Interactive Environmental Visualization: Combines mapping, live data, and analytics into one intuitive interface.
  • Smooth Animated Panels: The right-hand info panel slides in with soft transitions using CSS animations.
  • Adaptive Dark/Light Mode: Enhances usability and aesthetics dynamically.
  • Data-Driven Alerts: Displays automatic “⚠ Health Alert” when AQI exceeds safe levels.
  • Geo-aware Design: Integrates user geolocation and open data for personalized insights.

Design and Team Considerations

When developing the project, the team considered:

  1. Accuracy: Using reliable data from OpenWeatherMap.
  2. Performance: Efficient fetching, caching, and rendering of data.
  3. User Experience: Clean design with accessible controls and readable data.
  4. Scalability: Modular JavaScript files for future features (e.g., more pollutants, predictive models).
  5. Accessibility: Simple color coding and clear text for all AQI levels.
  6. Privacy: No personal data stored; geolocation is optional and user-triggered

  • Text and Content:
