projectDetails.name: Sharpedo – Shark Tracking & Conservation App
projectDetails.summary:
Sharpedo is an advanced marine monitoring solution that transforms sharks into real-time ocean data collectors. Each shark is equipped with a Location Tag and a Bio-Nutri Sensor. The Location Tag tracks migratory routes, temperature, and depth, while the Bio-Nutri Sensor analyzes dietary intake, identifying the shark’s food composition, including proteins, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. Together, they transmit live data to satellites for processing and visualization through an AI-based dashboard.
By merging movement and nutritional data, Sharpedo helps scientists understand shark health, ecosystem balance, and climate impacts on marine life. The insights support conservation efforts, predict ecological shifts, and promote sustainable marine resource management — turning sharks into sentinels of the sea.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – Sharpedo

Sharpedo is an AI-powered marine monitoring system that transforms sharks into mobile ocean explorers. Each shark is equipped with two core components:

  • Location Tag – a GPS-based satellite tracker embedded on the shark's Main Fin that records real-time movement, migration routes, regular hotspots and breeding hotspots, depth, and temperature.
  • Bio-Nutri Sensor – a compact biosensor capsule placed in it internal abdomen that analyzes the shark’s diet, identifying nutrient composition such as proteins, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals.

The data is transmitted via satellite to an integrated dashboard, where AI and data visualization tools analyze and display patterns of movement and nutrition across time and regions. This enables scientists to monitor food web dynamics, detect ecosystem shifts, and assess ocean health indicators.

Benefits & Impact:
Sharpedo provides continuous, non-invasive ocean data collection, improving understanding of marine biodiversity, pollution impacts, and climate-driven behavioral changes in sharks. By linking animal movement with environmental and dietary data, Sharpedo helps predict ecological changes before they become critical.

Tech Stack:

  • Hardware: Location Tag (GPS + satellite uplink), Bio-Nutri Sensor (diet/nutrient biosensor)
  • Software & Tools: Python, Figma, Satellite API integration, and a cloud-based AI dashboard (built with Flask + React), Vibe coding with Google Gemini and Perplexity Ai,
  • Data Analysis: Real-time telemetry processing, AI pattern recognition, and oceanic data mapping.

Creativity & Design Factors:
Our team focused on sustainability, energy efficiency, and minimal animal disturbance. The sensors are lightweight, hydrodynamic, and solar-assisted. Sharpedo bridges biology, AI, and space-based data systems to create a smarter, interconnected approach to ocean conservation.

projectDetails.name: AquaSmart - Saving every drop with smart technology
projectDetails.summary:
• Our project AquaSmart – Smart AI+ IoT Water Tracker is designed to reduce water wastage in apartment complexes.

• It is an AI and IoT-based monitoring system that tracks real-time water usage using smart flow sensors.

• The system detects leaks and sends instant alerts to residents through a mobile app dashboard.

• Data is transmitted via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth to the cloud for processing and analysis.

• Machine Learning algorithms analyze consumption patterns, detect abnormalities, and predict future water usage.

• This project directly addresses the urban water scarcity challenge faced by many cities.

• AquaSmart helps by identifying wastage early and supporting responsible water management in apartments.

• It promotes sustainable living through predictive analytics, gamification, and real-time monitoring.

• The system is practical, scalable, and user-friendly, making it suitable for widespread adoption in urban communities.
projectDetails.details:
What the Project Does / How It Works

• In Bengaluru, rapid urbanization, over-dependence on borewells, and groundwater depletion have created a severe water crisis.
• AquaSmart is an AI + IoT-based Smart Water Tracker for apartment complexes.
• IoT flow sensors continuously measure water usage across apartments.
• Data is transmitted via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth to a central hub (ESP32/Arduino).
• The system uses cloud analytics and machine learning to detect leaks and unusual consumption.
• Users receive real-time alerts and can monitor usage through a mobile app dashboard.
• The app provides usage graphs, leak alerts, bill estimation, and predictive insights.

Benefits
• Reduces water wastage through early leak detection and usage awareness.
• Saves costs with accurate consumption tracking and bill prediction.
• Promotes sustainability in urban areas facing water scarcity.
• Encourages responsible usage through gamified features like leaderboards.
• Improves management efficiency for apartment communities and facilities teams.

Intended Impact
• Minimize 30–40% of apartment water loss caused by leaks and overuse.
• Support sustainable water management in drought-prone cities like Bengaluru.
• Build awareness about individual water consumption habits.
• Help communities achieve long-term water conservation goals.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used
• Hardware Components: Flow Sensor, ESP32 / Arduino, Wi-Fi Module
• Backend: Python / Node.js
• Database: Firebase / AWS
• Analytics: Machine Learning–based anomaly detection for leaks
• Application Layer: Flutter / React Native (Mobile App)
• Visualization Tools: Grafana / ThingSpeak

Creativity and Innovation
• Unique “Fitbit for Water” concept that tracks and improves water usage habits.
• AI-driven analytics for real-time insights and predictive maintenance.
• Combines IoT hardware, cloud computing, and gamification for engagement.
• Scalable design for both small apartments and large housing communities.

Team Considerations
• Focused on practical implementation and cost-effectiveness.
• Designed a user-friendly app interface for residents and management.
• Ensured data security and privacy in cloud storage and analytics.
• Prioritized sustainability and social impact in every design choice.

projectDetails.name: SkyScope Advanced - Weather Forecast Dashboard
projectDetails.summary:
Planning outdoor activities months in advance is uncertain due to limited long-term weather insights. To address this, our team developed SkyScope – Advanced Weather Forecast Dashboard, leveraging NASA’s Earth observation data and machine learning to provide detailed forecasts for any location and date.

SkyScope integrates the NASA POWER API, offering decades of environmental data such as temperature, precipitation, wind speed, and air quality. A Random Forest model estimates precipitation patterns and generates meaningful weather predictions. Gemini AI produces human-friendly weather summaries and AI-generated activity suggestions based on predicted conditions.

Users can enter a city or drop a pin on the map and select a date, viewing all key metrics—including temperature, precipitation, wind, air quality—along with AI-generated activity suggestions and a separate weather summary. The dashboard also shows a 5-month temperature trend, allows CSV download for analysis, and supports Augmented Reality (AR) for immersive exploration.

By combining NASA’s historical climate data with machine learning and AI, SkyScope transforms complex datasets into actionable insights. It empowers travelers, event organizers, and outdoor enthusiasts to plan confidently, make informed decisions, and stay aware of long-term climate patterns. SkyScope simplifies preparation, enhances safety, and helps people make the most of their outdoor activities.
projectDetails.details:
Inspiration

You’re planning a hike, picnic, or outdoor adventure months in advance. You’ve mapped the route, packed your gear, and set the date—but suddenly it rains, or the heat becomes unbearable. That uncertainty can ruin even the best-laid plans. SkyScope – Advanced Weather Forecast Dashboard ensures you’re never caught off guard by the weather.

What SkyScope Does

SkyScope allows users to enter a city or drop a pin on a map and pick any future date. Instantly, you can view temperature, precipitation, wind, air quality, and an overall weather summary. It provides AI-generated activity suggestions, a 5-month temperature trend graph, downloadable CSV data, and Augmented Reality (AR) visualizations for a fully immersive experience.

How It Works

Our backend in Python using Flask fetches data from NASA POWER API. A Random Forest machine learning model predicts precipitation, while Gemini AI generates concise, human-friendly weather summaries and activity suggestions. The frontend, built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, delivers interactive charts, smooth navigation, and dynamic visuals.

Benefits and Impact

SkyScope transforms complex Earth observation data into actionable insights, helping travelers, hikers, and outdoor planners make informed decisions. Users can plan confidently, avoid adverse weather, and maximize outdoor enjoyment. It also promotes awareness of long-term climate patterns.

Tools and Technologies

Python, Flask, Random Forest ML, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Chart.js, NASA POWER API, Gemini AI, Echo3D.

Creativity and Considerations

SkyScope is more than a weather app—it’s a personalized, interactive, and immersive outdoor planning companion. We focused on accuracy, usability, interactivity, and visual appeal so users can plan smartly and enjoy adventures safely.

SKY MAP - An interactive map displaying exoplanets across the universe, with clickable details for each one. Includes a database of exoplanets and graphs showing the Discovery Timeline and Methods used.

ML LAB - This has an predictive AI/ML Model on the basis of exoplanet's database in terms of %, also listing its characteristics.

EXO-JOURNEY: An interactive learning module where you choose a path and explore information with images and questions to learn the basics.

projectDetails.details:
This project has 3 main functions and 2 submain functions which are very important and those are

MAIN FUNCTIONS

  • Sky Map
  • ML Lab
  • Exo-Journey

SUBMAIN FUNCTIONS

  • Glossary
  • Cosmo

Let us first move to MAIN FUNCTIONS

SKY MAP

This platform features an interactive, zoomable map of confirmed exoplanets located across the known universe. Each exoplanet on the map is clickable, revealing in-depth data such as its name, discovery method, distance from Earth, host star characteristics, orbital parameters, size, and potential habitability. Integrated with a robust exoplanet database, the platform also includes dynamic graphs that visualize the timeline of exoplanet discoveries over the years and categorize them based on the detection methods used—such as transit, radial velocity, direct imaging, and more. Together, these tools provide users with a comprehensive, visually engaging way to explore the progress of exoplanetary science and understand the diversity of worlds beyond our solar system.

ML LAB

This platform includes a predictive AI/ML model that analyzes the exoplanet database to estimate the likelihood of key characteristics—such as habitability, atmosphere type, or orbital stability—in percentage terms. It also provides detailed listings of each exoplanet’s physical and orbital properties used in the prediction process.

EXO-JOURNEY

This interactive learning module offers a branching, user-driven experience where learners can choose their own educational path based on interest or knowledge level. As users progress, they are guided through a series of structured content blocks featuring high-quality visuals, descriptive explanations, and interactive questions. These questions are designed not only to assess understanding but also to reinforce key concepts. The module covers foundational topics related to exoplanets—such as planetary formation, detection methods, orbital mechanics, and habitability—making it an engaging tool for building essential knowledge in space science.

Now let us move on to SUBMAIN FUNCTIONS

GLOSSARY

This section serves as a glossary, providing clear definitions and explanations for all the key terms used throughout the website. It’s designed to support new learners and clarify unfamiliar or complex vocabulary, making the content more accessible and easier to understand.

COSMO

An integrated chatbot designed to assist users by answering questions about the website’s content, features, terminology, and any related topics. It serves as a virtual guide, helping users navigate the platform, understand complex terms, and make the most of their learning experience.

This is our whole project.

Explore. Learn. Discover. The universe is just a click away.

We developed TerraVerse, an interactive, animation-driven web application designed to transform complex Earth science data into engaging, intuitive visual experiences. Built with Lovable AI and enhanced with open NASA datasets, TerraVerse allows users to explore environmental and climate phenomena—such as temperature trends, emissions patterns, and atmospheric changes—through dynamic globe and map visualizations.

The project directly addresses the challenge of making NASA’s vast open data more accessible and meaningful to the public. Instead of raw datasets or static charts, TerraVerse translates scientific information into animations that users can see and interact with, helping them understand how Earth’s systems are changing over time.

This is important because global issues like climate change, deforestation, and rising emissions can feel abstract and distant. By visualizing them in real time and at a planetary scale, TerraVerse bridges science and storytelling—empowering educators, students, policymakers, and the general public to connect with the data, build awareness, and inspire informed action.

projectDetails.name: Project StellarMorph
projectDetails.summary: We developed Stellar Stories, an interactive storytelling platform that transforms complex NASA space weather data into human-centered narratives and immersive experiences. Instead of raw numbers, users encounter stories, visuals, and cultural perspectives that show how cosmic events like solar flares, auroras, and geomagnetic storms affect life on Earth. Our system pulls data from NASA APIs, processes it through AI storytelling models, and delivers outputs in multiple styles — scientific, poetic, cultural, or casual. Paired with dynamic visualizations (maps, aurora animations, 3D space weather displays) and immersive AR/VR simulations, the platform makes space weather relatable, engaging, and unforgettable. The project directly addresses the challenge: space weather is powerful but invisible to most people. By blending science, storytelling, and technology, Stellar Stories bridges the gap between expert data and public understanding. This is important because space weather isn’t just science — it impacts communications, navigation, satellites, power grids, and even daily life on Earth. By giving it a “human voice,” Stellar Stories turns invisible cosmic forces into shared experiences, inspiring awareness, curiosity, and preparedness for our collective future under the Sun.
projectDetails.details:
Stellar Stories is an interactive digital platform that transforms complex NASA space weather data into meaningful stories, visuals, and immersive experiences. It collects live data from NASA’s space weather APIs — such as solar flares, geomagnetic storms, and aurora forecasts — and processes it through an AI storytelling engine. This engine converts technical data into engaging human-centered narratives, allowing users to see, hear, and feel space weather as if they were part of it. The data is then visualized using interactive 3D maps, aurora displays, and AR/VR simulations, creating a bridge between science and storytelling.

Benefits & Impact:

The project makes invisible cosmic phenomena visible and relatable. It helps people understand how space weather affects our communication systems, power grids, satellites, and even the skies above us. By turning data into experiences, it promotes public awareness, scientific curiosity, and educational outreach, especially among students and non-scientists. The intended impact is to inspire a deeper appreciation for the Sun-Earth connection and to prepare society to recognize the real-world effects of space weather.

Tools, Languages & Software:

Frontend Development: React / Flutter for web and mobile app interface

Visualization: D3.js and Three.js for interactive 2D and 3D graphics

Immersive Layer: Unity / Web XR for AR & VR storytelling

AI Storytelling Engine: Natural language model for narrative generation

Data Source: NASA Open APIs (space weather, solar activity, aurora alerts)

Hosting: Cloud-based platform for real-time updates and scalability

Creativity & Innovation:

Our innovation lies in giving space weather a human voice. While most solutions visualize data, Stellar Stories brings emotions, culture, and imagination into science — combining NASA’s accuracy with human creativity. The mix of AI-generated stories, real-time data, and immersive experiences transforms abstract scientific information into living, interactive tales of the cosmos.

Factors considered by the team:

We focused on accessibility, engagement, and education. Our goal was to make the experience enjoyable for everyone — from students to space enthusiasts — regardless of their scientific background. We also prioritized scalability, user-friendly design, and integration with NASA’s reliable datasets to ensure scientific credibility along with creative expression.

I developed an interactive ocean currents visualization tool that transforms complex marine data into an intuitive animated heat map. This React-based application displays real-time current patterns with temperature-based color coding, directional indicators, and interactive tooltips showing detailed metrics like speed, strength, and temperature.

The tool directly addresses the challenge of interpreting complex oceanographic data by making it visually accessible and engaging. Users can quickly identify temperature gradients, current strengths, and flow patterns through animated visual representations rather than raw numbers.

This is critically important because understanding ocean currents is vital for climate science, marine navigation, fisheries management, and predicting weather patterns. By democratizing access to this complex data through an intuitive interface, the tool supports better decision-making for researchers, policymakers, and maritime industries while raising public awareness about ocean dynamics and climate change impacts.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details

OceanFlow Viz: Interactive Ocean Currents Visualization Platform

What It Does & How It Works:
OceanFlow Viz is an interactive web application that transforms complex oceanographic data into an intuitive animated heat map. The system displays ocean currents as dynamic, color-coded points on a gradient ocean background, where each point represents a current with specific characteristics. The visualization uses:

  • Temperature-based coloring (blue for cold → red for hot)
  • Size variations to indicate current strength (weak to very-strong)
  • Animated direction indicators showing flow patterns
  • Interactive tooltips revealing detailed metrics on hover
  • Real-time statistics summarizing overall conditions

The platform processes geographical data with position coordinates (x, y percentages), temperature readings, speed measurements, and directional information to create a comprehensive marine current map.

Benefits:

  • Accessibility: Makes complex ocean data understandable to non-experts
  • Real-time Monitoring: Provides immediate visual feedback on current patterns
  • Educational Value: Helps students and researchers grasp ocean dynamics quickly
  • Decision Support: Aids maritime industries in route planning and safety

Intended Impact:
Our project aims to bridge the gap between complex scientific data and practical understanding, supporting climate research, marine conservation efforts, and sustainable ocean resource management. By making ocean current patterns visually accessible, we hope to contribute to better environmental decision-making and public awareness about ocean health.

Technical Implementation:

  • Frontend: React with TypeScript for type-safe development
  • Animation: Framer Motion for smooth, engaging visual effects
  • UI Components: Custom design system with Card, Badge elements
  • Icons: Lucide React for consistent iconography
  • Data Visualization: Custom heat mapping algorithms with interactive elements

Creative Elements:

  • Dynamic Ocean Texture: Animated wave patterns create an immersive underwater environment
  • Pulsing Effects: Current points pulse with shadow animations to draw attention
  • Interactive Experience: Hover effects with detailed tooltips and scale transformations
  • Multi-dimensional Data: Simultaneously represents temperature, speed, strength, and direction in a single view

Team Considerations:
Our development process prioritized:

  • User Experience: Intuitive design requiring minimal explanation
  • Performance: Smooth animations even with multiple data points
  • Accessibility: Clear color contrast and interactive elements
  • Scalability: Component-based architecture for easy feature expansion
  • Scientific Accuracy: Proper data representation and measurement units
  • Visual Appeal: Engaging design that maintains professional credibility

The project successfully merges scientific rigor with engaging visualization, creating a tool that serves both educational and professional marine science applications.

projectDetails.name: Project Stellar 🚀
projectDetails.summary:
NASA Stellars is an interactive data intelligence platform built to aggregate, analyze, and visualize space biology information from diverse sources, including NASA archives, PubMed, and other open scientific repositories. Its mission is to help researchers, educators, and students explore how spaceflight conditions influence organisms, genes, and biological systems.

The platform unifies these datasets into a dynamic knowledge graph enhanced with interactive visualizations. Users can intuitively search, filter, and discover relationships between missions, experiments, and biological entities. By addressing the issue of fragmented and dispersed space biology data, NASA Stellars provides a centralized, user-friendly environment for turning complex datasets into actionable insights.

This project plays a vital role in bridging the gap between raw data and meaningful discovery. It accelerates space biology research, supports educational exploration, and promotes public engagement with NASA’s life sciences initiatives. Ultimately, NASA Stellars contributes to preparing humanity for future long-duration space missions by deepening our understanding of how life adapts beyond Earth.
projectDetails.details:
NASA Stellars developed an interactive visualization platform that converts NASA’s complex satellite data into understandable, real-world insights about environmental changes on Earth. The system highlights key factors such as temperature shifts, deforestation trends, ocean color variations, and atmospheric gas levels, making it easier for everyone — from students to scientists — to grasp how our planet is evolving.

How It Works:

  • NASA satellite data is collected from sources like EOSDIS, MODIS, and Earthdata.
  • Data is preprocessed and cleaned using Python and MATLAB for precision.
  • AI-assisted tools (Perplexity Pro, Cursor, and ChatGPT) help analyze, summarize, and visualize data efficiently.
  • Results are displayed through an intuitive, web-based dashboard, allowing users to explore changes over time, compare regions, and understand environmental interactions.

Benefits & Impact:

  • Makes complex satellite data accessible and engaging for the public.
  • Encourages data-driven environmental awareness and education.
  • Helps researchers and policymakers identify regional trends and anomalies faster.
  • Promotes sustainability awareness through data storytelling.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used:

  • Languages: Python, MATLAB, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • AI Tools: Perplexity Pro, Cursor, ChatGPT (GPT-5)
  • Visualization Tools: Plotly, Matplotlib, Google Earth API
  • Data Sources: NASA EOSDIS, MODIS, Earthdata Portal
  • Frameworks: Flask (for backend integration)

Creativity and Design Factors:
The project stands out for transforming raw scientific data into interactive environmental storytelling. The creative use of AI-assisted summarization, combined with minimalist design and accessible visual layouts, ensures that even non-experts can explore NASA’s observations meaningfully.

projectDetails.name: Ocean Pulse
projectDetails.summary:
48 hours and NASA’s ocean data. Thrilled to share the result of our sprint at the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025: Ocean Pulse.

It’s a React-based platform designed to turn complex oceanographic datasets into real-time hazard alerts. But we didn't stop there. To maximize educational impact, we built a similar model that includes interactive 3D models of oceans, satellites, and the solar system, complete with speech narration to explain the data.

This dramatically raised the technical challenge. We weren't just showing charts; we were rendering heavy 3D visualizations. Integrating NASA's GHRSST data alongside these complex models and still hitting sub-2-second load times (solved with lazy-loading and smart caching) was intense.

The real win wasn't just the code, it was the mindset shift. The best solutions bridge scientific accuracy with deep user accessibility. This meant optimizing those heavy 3D models and speech tracks to work smoothly on 2G networks and supporting multilingual interfaces. 
It forces you to prioritize people over raw features. That's the design constraint that truly matters.
projectDetails.details:
OceanPulse is a React-based platform developed at the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025.

What it Does: It transforms complex NASA GHRSST sea surface temperature data into two critical tools:

  1. Real-Time Hazard Alerts for coastal communities (e.g., warnings for potential red tides or severe weather).
  2. Interactive 3D Educational Models (oceans, satellites, solar system) with speech narration to improve scientific literacy.

The Key Challenge & Solution: The technical difficulty lay in integrating and rendering both high-volume NASA data and heavy 3D models while maintaining sub-2-second load times. The team overcame this using lazy-loaded components and smart caching strategies.

Intended Impact & Big Lesson: The primary goal is to provide life-saving, accessible information globally. The biggest lesson was that true impact means designing for accessibility first—ensuring the platform is usable on basic 2G networks and supports multilingual interfaces, thus prioritizing people over features.

Tools Used: The core development used React.js, JavaScript, Mapbox/Leaflet, and NASA's GHRSST data.

projectDetails.name: TerraQuest -  Exploring New Worlds with AI-Powered Exoplanet Discovery
projectDetails.summary: TerraQuest is a compact research and demo web app that combines a React + TypeScript frontend with a Flask backend to explore exoplanet properties. I developed lightweight, prototype models — a RandomForest-based habitability predictor, a planet classifier, and a transit light-curve visualizer — and wired them to REST endpoints so users can analyze parameters, get classification probabilities, and generate transit plots (base64 images). The tool addresses the challenge of rapid experimentation: it lets researchers and educators iterate on inputs, visualize results, and compare model outputs without heavy infrastructure. It's important because it lowers the barrier to exploring exoplanet hypotheses, teaching core concepts (habitable zones, transit detection), and prototyping more robust models or deployed services down the line.
projectDetails.details:
TerraQuest is a lightweight research and demo toolkit for exploring exoplanet science through interactive analysis and visualization. It pairs a React + TypeScript frontend with a Flask backend that exposes REST endpoints for habitability prediction, planet classification, transit light-curve generation, and combined analysis. The backend contains compact prototype models implemented in Python using NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn (RandomForest), and Matplotlib; the transit visualizer returns base64 PNGs that the frontend decodes and displays.

Benefits and intended impact: it lowers the barrier to rapid experimentation and teaching by providing an easy-to-run, end-to-end environment (frontend UI + backend models) so researchers, students, and educators can quickly test hypotheses, explore parameter sensitivity, and visualize transit signatures without heavy infra. The project emphasizes reproducible demos and fast iteration rather than production-grade science, making it ideal for prototyping new models or classroom labs.

Tools & implementation details: React, TypeScript, axios on the frontend; Flask, Python 3.10+, scikit-learn, NumPy, SciPy, and Matplotlib on the backend. Start scripts (start_app.ps1, start_app.bat, start_app.js) and PowerShell-friendly docs speed setup on Windows. No special hardware is required (CPU-only).

Creativity & design choices: synthetic training data for quick model bootstrapping, a hand-rolled but instructive transit generator, and tight UI/API integration to make scientific concepts (habitable zone, ESI, transit depth) interactive. Practical considerations included developer ergonomics (venv, clear README, CORS), reproducibility, and making results interpretable for non-experts.

projectDetails.name: Project Teach heads
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Space BlackJack, is a space-themed educational game inspired by the classic card game BlackJack. We developed an interactive web-based game that teaches players about probability, risk assessment, and decision-making — key skills used in real space missions.

Instead of playing with traditional cards, players manage space resources such as fuel, oxygen, and power. Each round simulates mission-critical choices, like deciding whether to “hit” (take more risk) or “stand” (play it safe) while striving to complete their space mission successfully.

By blending game mechanics with NASA space data and STEM concepts, Space BlackJack makes learning about space exploration fun and accessible. It encourages players to think like astronauts and mission planners, developing analytical thinking and strategic decision-making skills essential for the future of space science.
projectDetails.details: Space BlackJack is an interactive, space-themed educational game inspired by the classic card game BlackJack. projectDetails.name: Project - Akasha
projectDetails.summary: The presentation “A World Away Hunting for Exoplanets with AI – The 2025 Challenge” explores how artificial intelligence is revolutionizing the search for planets beyond our solar system. With over 6,000 exoplanets discovered since the 1990s through missions like Kepler and TESS, the volume of astronomical data has grown exponentially. Traditional manual analysis cannot keep pace with the terabytes of daily data and the faint, noise-covered planetary signals. The upcoming NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 invites global teams to design AI/ML solutions that can automatically detect exoplanets from vast datasets. Participants—ranging from coders and scientists to storytellers—will gain access to open NASA data and computing resources, encouraging innovation and STEM collaboration. AI plays a crucial role in processing light curves, spectroscopy, and high-contrast imaging to separate genuine planetary signals from stellar or instrumental noise. Success stories include AI uncovering hundreds of hidden exoplanets in Kepler data and ESA’s Ariel Data Challenge advancing atmospheric analysis. The project not only accelerates our understanding of planetary formation and habitability but also contributes to broader domains like climate science and medical imaging. By democratizing participation and promoting interdisciplinary learning, this initiative aims to inspire the next generation of space scientists and innovators, uniting humanity in the quest to discover new worlds beyond Earth.
projectDetails.details: The project “A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI” explores how artificial intelligence and machine learning can revolutionize the discovery of planets beyond our solar system. With space missions like Kepler, TESS, and the upcoming Ariel generating terabytes of data daily, traditional manual detection methods are too slow to process and identify faint exoplanetary signals buried in stellar noise. This project aims to develop AI/ML models that automatically detect exoplanets by analyzing light curves and spectroscopic data with greater precision and speed. Using NASA’s open exoplanet datasets, algorithms such as CNNs and RNNs are trained to distinguish genuine planetary transits from instrumental or cosmic noise, significantly reducing false positives. The initiative aligns with the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025, encouraging global collaboration among coders, scientists, and innovators to accelerate space discovery. Beyond astronomy, the AI techniques developed here have broader applications in fields like climate science and medical imaging, while inspiring the next generation of STEM leaders to push the boundaries of space exploration.

projectDetails.name: ORBIS: Mars Inorganic Waste Recycling System
projectDetails.summary:
It is designed as an integrated flowchart that combines electrical, mechanical, and control systems to turn complex waste streams (like plastics or composite materials) into usable feedstock. The core structure starts with a centralized 240VAC Electrical Power distribution panel, which branches out to three main operational subsystems.

The system features Mechanical Loads (Shredder/Grinder and Sorter motors) and Heating Zones (Furnace/Melter PID control) for material transformation. Crucially, it incorporates dedicated HVAC and Control Systems for safety and precision, including VOC and dust sensors, HEPA filtration, and a central PLC/HMI. The final process flow culminates in Energy Recovery and a VOC & Dust Scrubber, with an essential Emergency Stop as the ultimate safety override.

The overall goal is a closed-loop system emphasizing safety, environmental control, and efficient resource recovery.
projectDetails.details:
Project Orbis is a conceptual Advanced Waste Mangement System designed to achieve circularity by converting complex refuse (like waste plastics or composites) into usable pellets, filaments, or molds.

The system functions via tightly integrated Electrical, Mechanical, and Control phases. The process begins with secured 240VAC distribution, feeding motors for Shredding and Grinding, and three PID-controlled Furnace Heater Zones for thermal processing. The system's intelligence comes from the Control System (PLC/HMI), which monitors critical parameters using VOC and Dust Sensors. Safety is paramount, with enclosure fans, HEPA filtration, and a centralized Emergency Stop Relay.

The primary intended impact is environmental—mitigating landfill waste while creating a sustainable, high-quality feedstock for manufacturing. It is creative in its holistic integration of safety and environmental controls (like the VOC & Dust Scrubber) directly into the thermal process loop. Development was conceptual, focusing on Flowchart Logic and system layout, using Mermaid.js and basic HTML/CSS/JavaScript for visualization, prioritizing modularity and operator safety as key factors.

projectDetails.name: From EarthData to Action: Cloud Computing with Earth Observation Data for Predicting Cleaner, Safer Skies
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, AQI.Earth, is a cutting-edge, AI-powered air quality intelligence platform designed to make environmental insights accessible, engaging, and data-driven. It combines real-time AQI visualization, geospatial mapping, and a WhatsApp-based conversational assistant to help users understand air quality trends locally and globally.

The platform is fully containerized and deployed using Docker on our custom domain, ensuring high scalability, modularity, and rapid deployment. Built using Next.js, FastAPI, MongoDB, and Leaflet map, openweathermap, AQI.Earth fetches global air quality data through APIs and visualizes pollutant concentrations, temperature layers, and forecast trends in a highly interactive 3D interface.

Our integrated WhatsApp Bot (+1 number) allows users to query AQI data, pollutant breakdowns, and forecasts simply by sending a message—making environmental data accessible even without visiting the website.

This solution directly addresses the challenge of environmental data awareness by transforming complex sensor data into meaningful insights for citizens, researchers, and policymakers. The system’s AI-driven approach, seamless cross-platform integration, and focus on user experience make it a scalable and impactful innovation toward cleaner air and smarter urban living.
projectDetails.details:
AQI.Earth is an AI-powered air quality intelligence platform that transforms raw sensor and API data into meaningful insights for the public. It fetches real-time global air quality data from APIs (e.g., OpenWeather, WAQI, NASA POWER) and integrates pollutant concentrations, weather variables, and forecast layers. These datasets are then visualized on an interactive geospatial map built with Leaflet and 3D layers, allowing users to explore AQI trends globally and locally.
Additionally, a WhatsApp conversational assistant enables users to query AQI data, pollutant breakdowns, and future forecasts without needing to access the website.

What benefits does it have?

  • Accessibility: Citizens can understand complex AQI metrics through simple visualizations or chatbot queries.
  • Engagement: Gamified and interactive 3D interfaces make environmental monitoring intuitive and appealing.
  • Awareness: Helps policymakers, researchers, and everyday users interpret environmental data for smarter decisions.
  • Cross-platform reach: WhatsApp bot integration extends accessibility to communities with limited web access.

What is the intended impact of the project?
The project aims to bridge the gap between raw environmental data and actionable insights. By making air quality intelligence engaging and accessible, AQI.Earth hopes to:

  • Drive awareness about air pollution at local and global scales.
  • Encourage policy-driven action for urban air quality improvement.
  • Provide researchers and NGOs with a scalable data platform for environmental analysis.
  • Empower citizens to make daily lifestyle choices (e.g., outdoor activities, commuting) based on real AQI information.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use to develop our project?

  • Frontend: Next.js (for interactive web interface, 3D rendering, map visualizations)
  • Backend: FastAPI (for efficient API management and AI model serving)

projectDetails.name: Project team Zephyr
projectDetails.summary:
Planning outdoor activities, from a family vacation to a mountain hike, involves significant uncertainty due to unpredictable weather. Standard forecasts provide general outlooks but fail to offer personalized risk assessments based on an individual's comfort and safety thresholds. This gap often leads to cancelled plans or, worse, exposure to dangerous conditions.

AeroCast is a personalized weather risk assessment application designed to bridge this gap. Leveraging decades of historical climate data and real-time Earth observation feeds from NASA (e.g., GOES, MODIS) and NOAA, AeroCast calculates the historical probability of adverse conditions for any user-specified location and date on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
AeroCast is a personalized weather risk assessment tool designed to help users confidently plan outdoor activities. Instead of a generic forecast, our app allows users to input a location, date, and their own custom thresholds for conditions like "very hot" or "very windy."

Leveraging historical NASA and NOAA Earth observation data, AeroCast calculates the precise probability of encountering those user-defined conditions. This creative approach shifts from simple forecasting to providing a personalized, probabilistic risk analysis. Built with Python and React, our project makes complex climate data accessible, enhancing user safety and decision-making for any adventure.

projectDetails.name: Project TechQuilla
projectDetails.summary:
Our project is an interactive platform designed to aggregate, analyze, and visualize space biology data from multiple sources such as NASA archives, PubMed, and other open datasets. The goal is to help researchers, educators, and students uncover meaningful insights about how spaceflight affects organisms, genes, and biological processes.

By integrating these datasets into a knowledge graph with interactive visualizations, the platform allows users to search, filter, and explore connections across missions, experiments, and organisms. This directly addresses the challenge of navigating fragmented biological data by providing a centralized, user-friendly tool that makes complex information accessible and actionable.

The importance of this project lies in its ability to bridge the gap between raw space biology data and practical understanding. It not only accelerates research but also empowers educators and learners by making cutting-edge space science more approachable. Ultimately, our project contributes to advancing biological research in space, supporting future long-duration missions, and fostering public engagement with NASA’s scientific endeavors.
projectDetails.details:
NASA-TechQuilla is an interactive platform designed to make space biology data more accessible, understandable, and actionable. It works by aggregating datasets from NASA archives, PubMed, and other open sources, then transforming them into a knowledge graph enriched with interactive visualizations. Users can search, filter, and explore relationships between organisms, genes, missions, and biological experiments in an intuitive interface.

How it works

  • Data is collected from open APIs and repositories.
  • The platform structures this data into interconnected entities (organisms, missions, experiments).
  • A knowledge graph engine enables semantic linking and discovery.
  • Visual dashboards present the data through charts, graphs, and interactive exploration.
  • Users can run queries, compare results, and even export findings.

Benefits

  • Researchers: Accelerates discovery by integrating fragmented datasets.
  • Educators & Students: Makes complex biological concepts more approachable.
  • NASA & Scientific Community: Provides insights useful for planning long-duration missions.
  • General Public: Increases awareness and engagement with space biology.

Intended Impact
NASA-TechQUilla bridges the gap between raw datasets and meaningful insights, helping scientists better understand how living organisms adapt to space. This can inform future missions, astronaut health, and even applications for biology on Earth.

Tools & Technologies

  • Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, D3.js for data visualization
  • Backend: Node.js with Express, GraphQL for flexible queries
  • Database: MongoDB with Mongoose for schema-driven data storage
  • DevOps: Docker for containerization, GitHub Actions for CI/CD
  • Other Libraries: Material UI for styling, Apollo for GraphQL integration

Creativity & Team Considerations
The creativity lies in presenting scientific data in a way that feels like storytelling. Instead of static tables, we built an exploratory system that allows users to interact with the data and discover unexpected connections. Our team focused on:

  • Accessibility (making it useful for both experts and learners)
  • Scalability (ability to add new datasets and features)
  • Engagement (interactive visuals instead of dense text)
  • Reliability (ensuring data consistency and proper integration)

Ultimately, NASA-TechQUilla combines data science, web development, and creative design to transform complex biological information into a platform that informs, educates, and inspires.

projectDetails.name: UrbanScope signifies a data-driven initiative to comprehensively monitor and improve urban environments. It reflects our commitment to harnessing Earth observation data for building resilient, healthy, and sustainable cities.
projectDetails.summary:
UrbanScope is an avant-garde digital platform that harnesses NASA Earth observation data—such as MODIS, Landsat, and Sentinel—integrated with cutting-edge geospatial analytics to illuminate critical urban health challenges, including intensifying heat islands, deteriorating air quality, and insufficient green space. Utilizing robust cloud architecture, the platform delivers seamless, scalable processing of voluminous datasets, while offering sophisticated visualization tools such as 3D urban models and temporal satellite imagery to expose microclimatic disparities and vegetation deficits.

Designed with user-centric precision, UrbanScope enables stakeholders to interrogate multifaceted environmental metrics—ranging from air pollutant concentrations to vegetation indices—fostering evidence-based urban resilience and sustainability strategies. Its interactive features promote civic engagement by empowering communities to report localized environmental concerns and validate data accuracy. UrbanScope epitomizes an indispensable resource for advancing environmental justice, catalyzing adaptive urban planning, and enhancing public health in the face of escalating anthropogenic and climatic pressures
projectDetails.details:
Here’s your content with key phrases and ideas highlighted for emphasis — suitable for a presentation, report, or visual slide version:

Problem:

Urban environments increasingly suffer from the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, wherein metropolitan areas endure significantly elevated temperatures compared to their rural hinterlands. This arises from anthropogenic modification of natural landscapes, replaced by impervious surfaces such as concrete, asphalt, and dense building materials with high thermal mass and low albedo, which absorb, retain, and slowly release heat, especially during nighttime.

The crisis worsens with the loss of urban greenery—trees, parks, and vegetation that provide evapotranspiration and natural shading. The “urban canyon effect”, caused by tall buildings and narrow streets, reflects solar radiation and impedes airflow, while vehicular, industrial, and domestic waste heat further intensifies local warming.

These factors lead to severe health impacts—heat-related illnesses, respiratory and cardiovascular problems, increased energy consumption, deteriorating air quality, and widening socio-economic disparities as vulnerable communities bear the brunt. Additionally, UHI disrupts meteorological patterns, alters rainfall, and degrades water quality through thermal pollution.

With rapid urban expansion, climate change acceleration, and environmental injustice, there is an urgent need to quantify, visualise, and mitigate urban heat. Without action, UHIs will continue to erode urban resilience, threatening human welfare and ecological balance.

Solution:

UrbanScope represents a revolution in urban environmental management, merging NASA’s Earth-observing satellite data with advanced data analytics to uncover spatial and temporal patterns of urban heat, air pollution, and vegetation loss with unprecedented precision.

By leveraging AI-driven predictive modelling and cloud-native deployment, UrbanScope enables anticipatory action against heat stress and pollution events. Its immersive 3D visual interface converts complex datasets into intuitive insights, empowering data-informed urban design and climate adaptation.

Through community-centric modules and participatory sensing, citizens provide hyperlocal data, enhancing accuracy and fostering inclusive climate governance. This democratisation of data ensures that marginalised communities play an active role in resilient urban planning.

Built on sustainability and resilience, UrbanScope not only diagnoses urban environmental challenges but also guides mitigation strategies, helping cities withstand climate change and unplanned urbanisation. It stands as a fusion of scientific rigour and social responsibility, dedicated to creating vibrant, healthy, and equitable human settlements.

projectDetails.details:
Our project, Parade Weather Planner, is a web-based application that predicts and evaluates outdoor weather conditions to help users make informed decisions when planning events. Designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 under the theme “Will It Rain on My Parade?”, it leverages live weather data to determine whether conditions are very hot, very cold, very windy, very wet, or very uncomfortable.

- How It Works

The app takes the user’s selected location and date, retrieves real-time data from the OpenWeatherMap API, and processes it to calculate key parameters such as:

1.Temperature (for hot/cold comfort zones)

2.Wind speed (for windy conditions)

3.Humidity and precipitation probability (for wet/uncomfortable weather)

4.Cloud coverage (for general comfort prediction)

Based on these metrics, the system evaluates a comfort index, classifying weather into categories like Ideal for outdoor events, Caution advised, or Unfavorable conditions. The interface visually displays the forecast, comfort score, and tailored suggestions such as “carry an umbrella” or “avoid outdoor activities.”

- Tools and Technologies Used

Our team used a combination of front-end web technologies and real-time weather APIs:

1.HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript – for the responsive and interactive user interface

2.OpenWeatherMap API – for real-time weather data retrieval

3.GitHub Pages – for project hosting and live deployment

4.VS Code – for development and version control integration

This tech stack allowed us to build a fast, accessible, and lightweight solution that requires no installation—just a browser.

- Benefits and Impact

The Parade Weather Planner provides an easy-to-use solution for people planning outdoor activities such as parades, picnics, hikes, or sports events. It translates complex meteorological data into clear, human-centered insights, helping users

1.Avoid unsafe weather conditions

2.Optimize event timing and location

3.Reduce weather-related disruptions

By promoting weather awareness and preparedness, our project supports community resilience and aligns with NASA’s mission to use Earth observation data for public good.

-Creativity and Design

We focused on creating a minimalistic, visually engaging, and intuitive interface that appeals to general users. Our innovation lies in combining data analysis with emotional design—translating scientific information into personalized and relatable terms like “very comfortable” or “uncomfortable.”

- Team Insights

As “The Last MINUTE,” we combined coding, data visualization, and UI/UX design skills to deliver a working prototype within limited time. We prioritized simplicity, accessibility, and relevance to NASA’s Earth Science goals—turning weather data into actionable decisions.

projectDetails.name: Sunny the Solar Flare’s Big Adventure: A Space Weather Storybook
projectDetails.summary:
I created the entertaining and instructive children's book Sunny the Solar Flare's Big Adventure – A NASA Space Weather Storybook, which uses storytelling to introduce the idea of space weather. In order to demonstrate how space weather affects astronauts, aircraft, farmers, power grids, and even produces the beauty of auroras, the story follows "Sunny," a friendly solar flare, on his journey from the Sun to Earth.

Making difficult scientific subjects like solar flares, CME's, and geomagnetic storms approachable and entertaining for young students is the challenge this project attempts to solve. The book bridges the gap between early education and science communication by fusing narrative storytelling, vibrant illustrations, and accurate scientific fact boxes.

Space weather is significant because it impacts satellites, communication, transportation, and power systems, all of which have an impact on day-to-day life on Earth. Teaching kids about these unseen but potent forces not only piques their interest in science and space travel, but it also increases their understanding of how international cooperation—including that of NASA, NOAA, EMBRACE, and others—keeps our planet safe.
projectDetails.details:
1) What does it do?

The project is Sunny the Solar Flare's Big Adventure, a children's book that uses the perspective of a character named Sunny to explain space weather. It provides accurate, practical science while distilling difficult scientific ideas—such as solar flares, CME's, and auroras—into an entertaining story that children can grasp.

2) What benefits does it have?

a)Makes complex science interesting and suitable for young learners.

b)Increases understanding of how space weather impacts daily life (aviation, power, GPS).

c)Provides educators, parents, and teachers with an accessible STEM resource.

d)Encourages young children to consider science, space exploration, and collaboration.

3) What is the intended impact of the project?

The intention is to stimulate young students' curiosity and interest in STEM subjects, particularly space science. Children are also better able to understand how science and technology shield Earth from space weather problems.

4) What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

a)ChatGPT (text generation): For writing and refining the story in a kid-friendly style.

b)Gemini Nano Banana: For creating colorful illustrations of Sunny, astronauts, satellites, and auroras.

c)Gamma AI : To develop an engaging project demo presentation.

d)Microsoft Designer: For formatting and polishing the final storybook pages and slides.

e)Publuu: It is website that I used to convert my Stotybook which was in a form of PDF to a Flipbook.

5) How is your project creative?

Sunny the Solar Flare’s Big Adventure is innovative because it personifies a solar flare and takes readers on a journey from the Sun to Earth through the vibrant character of Sunny, rather than merely presenting facts.

A Science/Data Fact Box and a storytelling section are combined on each page so that readers can learn factual, accurate information from NASA, NOAA, and other international space agencies while also enjoying the story. The learning process is engaging and reliable because of this blending of fact and fiction.

I ended the story with "The Flare Poem" a creative synopsis in straightforward, rhythmic verses that uses rhyme and imagination to further bolster the main ideas, to make it even more captivating.

6) What factors did your team consider?

Sunny the Solar Flare's Big Adventure was entirely my own creation, so I meticulously planned every step to strike a balance between originality, precision, and educational value. The primary elements I took into account were:

Scientific Accuracy: Verifying that all information regarding space weather, CMEs, and solar flares originated from reputable NASA and NOAA sources. In addition to being accurate, I wanted the story to be entertaining.

Educational Value: Ensuring that the narrative imparts knowledge about how space weather impacts technology, people's daily lives, and Earth.

Age Appropriateness: Crafting the narrative in a straightforward, captivating style that kids can grasp without sacrificing the science's true meaning.

Creativity and Engagement: To make the story memorable and emotionally uplifting, Sunny's personality was added, visual scenes were created, and a poem was concluded.

projectDetails.name: Project The Livable City Initiative
projectDetails.summary:
The project developed by The Livable City Initiative is The Urban Heat Island (UHI) Mitigation and Green Equity Initiative, which is fundamentally a data-driven decision framework and a Geo-Smart Growth Atlas prototype.
We developed the Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (UHVI) by fusing NASA Earth Observation (EO) data—specifically Landsat LST (heat), Landsat NDVI (vegetation), and TEMPO (\text{NO}_2)—with socio-economic data.
This project directly addresses the challenge by identifying the exact neighborhoods suffering most from the UHI effect and Green Equity deficits. The UHVI guides the city to implement smart strategies like Cool Corridors, targeted tree planting (15% NDVI increase goal), and Air Quality Buffers. It is important because it shifts urban planning from reactive general policy to proactive, precise, and equitable investment, ensuring that climate resilience and improved public health benefit the most vulnerable populations first.
projectDetails.details: Project Overview: The Livable City Initiative The Urban Heat Island (UHI) Mitigation and Green Equity Initiative developed by The Livable City Initiative is a data-driven decision framework and an intended Geo-Smart Growth Atlas prototype designed to make urban planning equitable and climate-resilient. Functionality and Mechanism Our project works by fusing multiple data streams into a single, actionable index: * Assessment Tool (The UHVI): We built the Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (UHVI) by combining geospatial data layers. The primary inputs are Landsat Land Surface Temperature (LST) to identify heat hotspots and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to measure the existing tree canopy. This identifies the "Greenspace Deficit Map". * Stressors Integration: We integrate data from TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions) on \text{NO}_2 and \text{O}_3 concentrations to pinpoint air pollution sources. We also use VNP46 (Black Marble) to track uncontrolled urban sprawl (impervious surface expansion). * Actionable Strategies: The UHVI directly translates into policy actions for city departments, including defining Cool Corridors for reflective pavement and mandating Green Equity Plan investments. Benefits and Intended Impact The project's impact is focused on improving both environmental health and social equity: * Public Health: Lower LST leads to reduced heat-related illness and decreased peak energy demand. This directly addresses the heat-related public health crisis. * Green Equity: It resolves the issue of heat burden being unequally distributed by directing new tree planting (targeting a \mathbf{15\% \text{ increase in NDVI}}) to the most heat-vulnerable, low-canopy neighborhoods. * Sustainable Growth: It guides development away from high-LST/flood-risk zones, using VNP46 data to define Urban Growth Boundaries and prevent sprawl. * Environmental: Leads to improved local air quality (monitored via TEMPO) and reduced stormwater runoff. Tools and Creativity * Tools/Software: The project relies on NASA Earth Observation data from Landsat, TEMPO, and VNP46. Development requires Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software (e.g., ArcGIS or QGIS) and coding languages (likely Python or R) for data processing and index calculation. * Creativity: The project's creativity lies in its holistic data fusion—combining heat (LST), vegetation (NDVI), air pollution (TEMPO), and urban growth (VNP46) into a single, weighted Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (UHVI). This makes the project highly prescriptive and eliminates political guesswork by providing a unified, objective map for equitable resource allocation. Factors Considered The team considered several crucial factors beyond just heat: * Equity: Ensuring that resource allocation is mandatory for underserved communities. * Public Health: Directly linking LST data to tracking heat-related hospitalizations. * Sustainability: Guiding long-term growth by restricting development in environmentally sensitive and high-risk zones. * Accountability: Establishing clear Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) verified by NASA data (e.g., 2^{\circ} \text{C} decrease in LST, 15\% increase in NDVI). * Stakeholder Integration: Designing mechanisms for resident validation through a Community Heat Watch program.

projectDetails.name: AeroVolt
projectDetails.summary:
The Martian energy crisis—caused by the thin atmosphere, weak sunlight, and intense radiation—threatens both missions and human survival.

The Mars Power Hub 1000 is the solution: a closed-loop energy rover that autonomously generates, stores, and redistributes power on the Red Planet.

Key Features of the Mars Power Hub 1000
This next-generation rover is engineered for sustainability and self-sufficiency in Mars' harsh environment. Its core innovation is a regenerative power cycle managed by the LH₂ & ElectroTech System and Fuel & LOX Cryodistribution Storage, which minimizes waste and maximizes efficiency.

It's equipped for extreme durability and operational stability, featuring:

Radiation Shielding for component protection.

A Water Purificator Stack for essential life support.

An Integrated Environmental Sensor Suite for real-time analysis.

A Modular Power Distribution Unit to support habitats.

A Primary S-Band Satellite Dish for secure comms.

Mission control monitors and regulates the rover via the PowerHub Web Interface developed by our team. By providing reliable, renewable, and autonomous energy, the Mars Power Hub 1000 is fundamental to establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
Project Name: AeroVolt

The Martian Energy Crisis:

Title: Sustainable Power for Permanent Mars Exploration: The Closed-Loop Hub

The Problem: Limitations of Current Energy Systems

  1. Weak Sunlight & Dust Storms
    • Mars receives 60% less sunlight than Earth due to its greater distance from the Sun.
    • Solar panels, though useful, become highly unreliable during Martian nights (which last ~12 hours) and especially during planet-wide dust storms.
    • These storms can persist for weeks to months, blanketing the surface in thick dust that almost completely blocks sunlight.
    • As a result, solar-powered systems cannot ensure consistent energy for rovers, habitats, or scientific operations.
    • Current missions rely heavily on Earth-shipped energy systems:
      • Batteries: Provide temporary storage but must be recharged and eventually degrade.
      • Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs): Supply long-lived but low power output (typically tens to hundreds of watts).
    • Transporting fuel, batteries, or additional RTGs from Earth is prohibitively expensive and drastically limits mission scalability.
    • This dependency makes long-duration human exploration or colonization unsustainable.
    • Future Martian operations (habitats, laboratories, mining equipment, long-range rovers, agriculture modules) will require continuous, high-power energy in the kilowatt range.
    • Existing technologies (solar + RTGs) cannot meet these demands at scale.
    • Without a breakthrough energy system, Mars missions will remain limited in scope and duration.

The Solution: Transition to ISRU-Based High-Power Systems

The long-term vision for Mars exploration demands a paradigm shift: moving away from fragile, imported, low-output energy sources toward a self-sustaining Martian energy grid built on In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).

  • ISRU Advantage: Instead of relying on Earth, ISRU harnesses resources already available on Mars.
    • Ice → Water → Electrolysis → Hydrogen + Oxygen
    • Hydrogen + Oxygen → Fuel Cell → Water + Electricity + Heat

Power Hub 1000 (PH-1000)

*What it does / How it works:*

AeroVolt addresses the Martian Energy Crisis by introducing the *Closed-Loop Hydrogen (CLH) Power Hub, a self-sustaining energy system that leverages Martian water ice. The system cycles **Ice → Water → Electrolysis → Hydrogen → Fuel Cell → Water* to provide continuous, high-density power. Our prototype, *Power Hub 1000 (PH-1000)*, is a next-gen rover that autonomously generates, manages, and distributes energy while recycling resources.

*Key Features:*

* *Electrolysis Unit:* Extracts H₂ and O₂ from Martian water ice.

* *Fuel Cells:* Convert H₂ + O₂ back into water, generating electricity and heat at ~50–60% efficiency.

* *Resource Recycling:* Produces both energy and essential life-support outputs (H₂O and O₂).

* *Integrated Systems:* Includes environmental sensors, water purification, satellite communication, cryogenic storage, radiation shielding, and modular power distribution.

* *PowerHub Web Interface:* Enables mission control to monitor and regulate systems in real time.

*Benefits & Impact:*

* *Reliable:* Operates during long Martian nights and global dust storms, unlike solar.

* *Scalable:* Supports habitats, rovers, and scientific equipment with high-kilowatt power.

* *Sustainable:* Reduces dependency on Earth-supplied batteries or RTGs, lowering mission costs.

* *Foundational:* Establishes a closed-loop energy economy for future Martian settlements.

*Tools, Languages, and Development:*

* *Prototype Development:* CAD modeling, simulation tools, and hardware prototyping for rover design.

* *Software:* PowerHub Web Interface built with *HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React.js)* for monitoring and control.

* *Simulation & Analysis:* Python for system modeling, efficiency simulations, and data handling.

* *Electrochemical System Modeling:* MATLAB and open-source physics simulators for fuel cell and electrolysis performance testing.

*Creativity & Design Considerations:*

* Designed for *autonomy and durability* in extreme Martian conditions.

* Balances *energy generation, storage, and distribution* in one resilient rover.

* Integrates *dual-use systems* (power + life support).

* Modular approach allows *expansion into Martian infrastructure* (habitats, research bases).

* Considered *logistics, scalability, redundancy, and human survival needs* in design.

*Intended Impact:*

The Power Hub 1000 is more than a rover—it’s the *core of a Martian energy ecosystem*, enabling sustainable human exploration and long-term settlement on Mars. By solving the reliability and scalability gaps in current Martian power systems, AeroVolt lays the groundwork for humanity’s future beyond Earth.

Power Hub 1000 (Back view)

Power Hub 1000 (Interior components)

PowerHub Web page

web page link :

https://getmocha.com/apps/0199b3c0-cd7b-7c59-85ba-b94a9df1dcc2

The *PowerHub web page* is the digital command and monitoring center for AeroVolt’s Power Hub 1000 (PH-1000) rover and supporting Martian systems. It is designed to provide mission control and researchers with *real-time visibility, live updates, and seamless control* of all critical energy operations.

*Key Features:*

* *Live Data Feed:* Continuously streams telemetry from rovers and the PH-1000, including power generation, fuel cell performance, electrolysis status, water recycling, and atmospheric sensor data.

* *Dashboard Interface:* A clean, interactive dashboard built for quick situational awareness with graphical displays of power levels, resource storage (H₂, O₂, H₂O), and system health.

* *Alerts & Notifications:* Automatically flags anomalies such as low storage levels, efficiency drops, or environmental hazards.

* *Communication Link:* Integrates with the PH-1000’s satellite dish for secure, low-latency updates across Martian infrastructure.

* *Remote Control & Regulation:* Allows operators to adjust system parameters, manage power distribution, and initiate emergency protocols directly from the interface.

* *Scalability:* Supports integration with multiple rovers, habitats, and Martian outposts, making it adaptable for long-term settlement operations.

*Technology Stack:*

* *Frontend:* HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React.js) for responsive, real-time UI.

* *Backend:* Node.js for handling live rover data streams.

* *Data Handling:* APIs and socket-based communication for real-time synchronization.

* *Visualization:* Interactive charts and graphs to translate raw telemetry into actionable insights.

*Impact:*

The PowerHub web page ensures *transparency, reliability, and control* of Martian energy systems. By centralizing live updates, environmental monitoring, and energy management into one platform, it acts as the *digital backbone* of AeroVolt’s closed-loop hydrogen power solution—empowering mission control to maintain operational stability on Mars.
