projectDetails.name: Project EvThD-449
projectDetails.summary: The machine operates as a closed, self-sustaining electrochemical system that transforms two distinct waste streams into three functional products. In the upper chamber, EVA and PVA scraps are dissolved in a sulfuric solution derived from magnesium sulfate and anhydrite and undergo controlled acid electrolysis, generating acetic acid and a PVA gel. The acetic acid becomes the acidic reagent for neutralization, while the PVA gel is reused as a sealing and insulating material for the reactor. In the lower chamber, cellulosic wastes such as cotton fabrics and paper are hydrothermally decomposed in the presence of magnetite at 200–280 °C, producing a liquid alkaline liquor composed mainly of ammonium carbonate and bicarbonate, along with a carbon-rich solid residue known as hydrochar. The hydrochar is thermally activated and used as a filtering medium that purifies urine into technical-grade water, closing the hydraulic cycle. The acetic acid from the upper line reacts with the alkaline liquor from the lower line to form ammonium acetate (CH₃COONH₄), which functions as the electrolyte of an aluminum–magnetite battery. The process achieves a global theoretical efficiency of 95% and converts 87.6% of the cellulose fraction into liquid alkaline product, producing simultaneously the electrolyte, activated carbon, and reusable PVA sealant in a fully circular, low-impact system.
projectDetails.details:
The machine is designed as a closed, self-sustaining electrochemical system composed of two main reaction chambers, an upper acid line and a lower base line, interconnected by a controlled valve that regulates the transfer of liquids without releasing gases to the environment. Each chamber receives a specific type of recyclable waste and operates with natural mineral catalysts, transforming these materials into new compounds with high chemical utility. In the upper acid chamber, EVA and PVA polymeric residues, such as films and thermal bags, are introduced into an aqueous sulfuric solution prepared from magnesium sulfate and anhydrite. The mixture undergoes controlled acid electrolysis, which breaks the polymer chains and generates acetic acid, vinyl alcohol, and ethyl acetate. The acetic acid becomes the liquid reagent for neutralization, while the PVA residue forms a flexible gel that is reused as a sealing and insulating material for the system. In the lower base chamber, cellulosic residues from fabrics, paper, and cotton are immersed in water containing magnetite and subjected to hydrothermal decomposition between 200 and 280 °C under pressure.

This reaction converts cellulose into CO₂, H₂, and a carbonaceous solid fraction known as hydrochar, while the dissolved CO₂ reacts with ammonia and hydroxyl ions to produce ammonium carbonate and bicarbonate, forming an alkaline liquor with pH between 9 and 11. The hydrochar is collected, dried, and thermally activated to become a porous carbon used for filtering and purifying urine, generating technical-grade water that returns to the process, ensuring a closed water cycle. The acetic acid produced in the acid line is then gradually mixed with the alkaline liquor from the base line, producing ammonium acetate (CH₃COONH₄), a neutral and highly conductive electrolyte that serves as the internal medium for the aluminum–magnetite battery. The battery is assembled with aluminum from structural scraps as the anode, magnetite as the cathode, and the ammonium acetate solution as the electrolyte, producing electrical energy through low-impact electrochemical reactions. The system’s total theoretical efficiency is 95%, while 87.6% of the cellulose fraction is effectively converted into liquid alkaline product. The process results in three useful outputs: the ammonium acetate electrolyte that powers the aluminum–magnetite cell, the activated carbon used for water purification and internal filtration, and the PVA gel employed as a sealing and insulating component. All operations occur in a continuous, closed cycle, integrating waste recycling, energy production, water purification, and material reuse within a fully circular, low-emission, and self-sustaining chemical system.

projectDetails.name: Project Guaraci
projectDetails.summary:
Guaraci is an innovative platform that integrates space science, ecology, and citizen science to monitor plant flowering and pollinator activity on a global scale. Developed in response to the NASA challenge, the project combines satellite data (vegetation, climate, humidity), pollinator records, and phenological series, transforming them into interactive maps and dynamic visualizations.

The solution was structured into a functional prototype capable of overlaying flowering cycles with pollinator presence, generating alerts for optimal harvest windows and enabling the detection of risks of desynchronization between plants and their pollinators. In this way, it translates complex information into practical data accessible to local communities, researchers, and environmental managers.

Guaraci directly addresses the challenge by creating a dynamic visual tool that detects and monitors flowering and pollination events, supporting both the prediction of climate impacts on vegetation and the sustainable management of ecosystems.

Its importance lies in its potential to reduce agricultural losses, strengthen food security, support conservation policies, and provide a scalable model for different biomes and crops worldwide. Guaraci connects science, technology, and communities in favor of biodiversity and sustainability.

projectDetails.name: Lazurus
projectDetails.summary: Our team’s goal with this project is to democratize the process of exoplanet detection and promote citizen science with the aid of AI through the creation of an interactive astronomical exploration experience. Our solution allows people without prior technical knowledge or experience to learn how to interact with satellite data in the search for planetary bodies beyond our Solar System. Through an interactive web page, users will embark on a hunt for possible extrasolar planets pre-classified by an AI model (LightGBM) and will evaluate light curve charts and transit data to submit their analysis, thereby contributing to a collaborative catalog of exoplanet candidates examined by both human and artificial intelligence. The playful visuals, accessible language, and knowledge snippets at each stage of the interaction guide users in learning how to identify bodies in other planetary systems, even if they have never worked with astronomical data before. Thus, our solution stands out by integrating the use of artificial intelligence for exoplanet identification with an engaging and user-friendly web interface.
projectDetails.details:
Our project makes exoplanet research accessible to anyone by combining an AI model that filters potential exoplanet candidates with a user-friendly interface. Users can easily analyze data and provide feedback, even without prior technical knowledge. In the future, combined user inputs may contribute to official databases. The platform is also designed to eventually provide a richer social experience, with goals, rankings, badges, and interactive elements.

Benefits:

  • Educates users about science and astronomy
  • Leverages citizen science to process and evaluate exoplanet data
  • Makes the analysis process intuitive and fun, even for beginners
  • Promotes scientific knowledge and engagement

Intended Impact:

  • Increase the volume and quality of exoplanet data analysis
  • Engage society in a fun and accessible way
  • Make exoplanet study approachable and enjoyable for the general public
  • Promote citizen science initiatives that allow participants to contribute to real discoveries

Tools & Technologies:

  • Backend: Python with Flask for API and web development, Gunicorn for production deployment, data processing libraries, AI model (LightGBM)
  • Data: NASA public datasets and APIs
  • Frontend: React / Next.js for interactive visualization, Tailwind for styling
  • Workflow & Design Tools: GitHub for version control, Figma for mockups and interactive prototypes
  • Data Analysis & ML: Lightkurve for light curve handling, LightGBM for machine learning detection of exoplanets
  • Other Tools: Docker + Docker Compose for containerized development, CapCut for pitch video editing

Creativity:
Our solution is creative because it uses AI and technology to transform a technically restricted scientific process into an accessible, educational, and engaging experience. It combines real data, gamification, and citizen science to broaden participation in exoplanet discovery.

Team Considerations:
We prioritized accessibility, educational value, and the integration of AI to make exoplanet research approachable and fun for all users.

AI Model Workflow:

Data Cleaning & Preprocessing:

  • Select relevant columns
  • Download light curves
  • Remove missing values and outliers
  • Normalize light curves
  • Fold and mask transits
  • Flatten and stitch data
  • Standardize fluxes

Modeling with LightGBM:

  • Separate features and labels
  • Binarize labels
  • Define hyperparameter search space
  • Outer cross-validation
  • Inner cross-validation (Bayesian)
  • Final training with best hyperparameters
  • Predict on test set
  • Calculate evaluation metrics

Roadmap (Phases):

  1. Phase 1 – Core Experience
    • AI model filters NASA data
    • Simple questions & UI
    • Light curve display
    • User votes & feedback
    • Discoveries tab
    • New types: Planet, False Positive, Binary
    • Voting system & recheck
    • AI highlights top 5 features
    • Curve visualization options
    • Achievements & badges
    • Rankings (daily, weekly)
    • Historical logs with tags
    • Educational content
    • Procedural visuals
    • User profiles
    • Friends & sharing
    • Personalized assistant
    • Custom system selection
    • More datasets
    • Local processing
    • Procedural prototypes
    • Offline / cache mode
    • Mobile-first UI
    • Native Windows app

Repositories:

  • Lazurus
  • SpaceApps Exoplanet Detection

projectDetails.name: Satellite Terra and the urgency of climate change!
projectDetails.summary:
Our project used images and data from the TERRA satellite to visualize and highlight climate change, including global warming, sea level rise, and the increase in ocean temperatures. With the 25th anniversary of the TERRA satellite and the upcoming COP30, we aim to raise awareness among the population and policymakers about the urgency of these transformations. To do this, we used visual representations that make the seriousness of the situation clearer and more understandable.

The project is relevant because it connects global information to local impacts, showing concretely how climate change affects specific regions, such as coastal areas. Furthermore, it encourages authorities and society to adopt collective and responsible measures, promoting actions that contribute to the protection of the planet and the preservation of ecosystems and vulnerable communities. By combining science and visual communication, our work reinforces the importance of swift and conscious decisions to ensure a sustainable future for all.
projectDetails.details:
Our project uses images and data from NASA’s TERRA satellite to monitor and visualize climate change at both global and local levels. It works by processing data collected daily by the satellite’s instruments, such as ASTER, CERES, MISR, MODIS, and MOPITT, and transforming this information into visual representations to highlight phenomena such as global warming, sea level rise, and increases in ocean temperatures.

The main benefits of the project include raising awareness among the population and authorities about the urgency of climate change, providing reliable scientific information in accessible visual formats, and demonstrating concrete impacts in specific regions, such as coastal areas of Brazil.

The intended impact is to motivate collective and responsible actions, encouraging public policies and sustainable behaviors to protect the planet, preserving ecosystems and vulnerable communities.

To develop the project, we used resources available from NASA, such as NASA Earthdata Worldview, NASA Earth Observatory, Sea Level NASA, TERRA NASA, as well as editing software (CANVA).

The creativity of the project lies in the combination of high-precision scientific data with visual representations that make the content more understandable and engaging. Our team considered factors such as local and global relevance, clarity in communication, visual impact, information accessibility, and the need to draw attention to urgent decisions in the face of climate change.

projectDetails.name: Project Meatier. Not Meteor.
projectDetails.summary:
Our team created a meteor impact simulator that pulls real asteroid data from NASA
API and show them in a 3D visualization of NEOs, while also showing a 2D impact map
visualization where the user can see where one of these asteroids would fall and the
environmental consequences in a possible impact scenario, such as tsunamis and
earthquakes.
Our tool uses real orbital models and accurately predicts the geographical coordinates
of the impact point and the impact velocity using atmospheric entry calculations and
based on that calculates the impact energy and the correlated tsunami height or
earthquake magnitude, depending on if it’s an inland impact or an impact in the ocean
or in the sea.
With that, the user can clearly view possible impact scenarios and consequences for
different asteroids and have the option to input a size and velocity for an asteroid if he
wants. Users can also input the mass and velocity of a kinetic impactor that will be
used to deflect the asteroid and visualize the resulting change in velocity of the
asteroid.
Therefore, our tool can be used for educational purposes for the general public, but
also by any interested person, to address the consequences of a possible asteroid
impact and how we can prevent them.
projectDetails.details: Our program performs a complete simulation of orbital propagation and atmospheric reentry for Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) or artificial satellites. It combines analytical propagation using the SGP4 model with numerical integration of reentry trajectories when the object descends into denser atmospheric layers. The Reentry_analysis class provides all necessary physical constants, orbital transformations, and Earth’s WGS-84 reference model to accurately represent the planet and its gravity field. The code reads orbital and physical parameters (such as eccentricity, inclination, and diameter) from JSON input data, transforms these into position–velocity (r–v) vectors, and can convert them into or from Two-Line Elements (TLEs). It propagates orbits using SGP4, automatically switching to numerical reentry integration once the altitude reaches approximately 80 km. During this phase, it computes gravitational and aerodynamic forces, including atmospheric drag and Mach-dependent drag coefficients, to simulate the object’s deceleration and descent. Finally, the program returns those parameters for the 3D visualization of the orbits. These results allow for a detailed assessment of orbital decay and reentry dynamics, supporting applications in satellite reentry prediction, asteroid impact modeling, and astrodynamics research.

projectDetails.name: Project METEOMESTRES
projectDetails.summary:
Imagine meticulously planning that perfect weekend hike months in advance, or your dream beach vacation, only to be caught by unexpected weather. The frustration of having plans ruined by meteorological information that's difficult to interpret is a common challenge.

The ClimaCerto project emerges to change this reality. We transform complex historical meteorological data into actionable insights for you. We've developed an application that, unlike traditional tools, offers an Activity Suitability Index (IAA). This index provides a personalized score (0-100) indicating the likelihood of ideal weather conditions for your specific activity (whether it's hiking, a beach day, or a picnic) at any chosen location and date.

Our importance lies in empowering users to make more informed and confident planning decisions, eliminating speculation and enhancing the safety and enjoyment of their adventures. ClimaCerto doesn't merely report the weather; it interprets it within your personal context, leveraging decades of Earth observation data, provided by NASA's POWER (Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resource) API, to offer a unique perspective on climate suitability.
projectDetails.details:
What it does and how it works: The user initiates their journey by selecting a planned activity (picnic, beach day, trail) from a clear, intuitive interface. They then specify the location (via map pin or search) and the desired date or date range. Leveraging decades of historical meteorological data, ClimaCerto's core innovation, the Activity Suitability Index (IAA), processes these inputs. The IAA is a proprietary algorithm that dynamically weighs various historical climate variables (temperature, precipitation, wind speed, cloud cover) based on the chosen activity's requirements. The system then presents a comprehensive result screen featuring:

  1. A prominent IAA score (0-100), color-coded for immediate understanding (Green for Excellent, Yellow for Good with caveats, Red for Risky).
  2. Clear "Pros" and "Cons" outlining specific climatic advantages or disadvantages for the selected activity.
  3. A "Trend Alert" indicating if extreme weather conditions for that specific date and location have increased in frequency over recent decades.

Benefits and Intended Impact: ClimaCerto's primary benefit is empowering users with confident, data-driven decision-making for outdoor planning, significantly reducing guesswork and mitigating risks associated with adverse weather. This leads to safer, more enjoyable, and better-prepared outdoor experiences. The intended impact is to revolutionize how individuals and groups plan ahead, allowing for optimized scheduling of events, vacations, and activities several months in advance. By providing a clear likelihood of favorable conditions, ClimaCerto aims to enhance well-being and engagement with the natural environment, fostering a deeper connection with and respect for our planet's climate patterns.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used: Our project was developed using a modern web technology stack. The frontend was built with React and the Next.js framework (utilizing the App Router), written in TypeScript. For the user interface, we utilized component libraries such as Material UI and MUI Joy, with styling enhanced by Sass and Emotion React. Animations were implemented using Framer Motion. The development environment included VS Code as the editor and Git for version control, with ESLint for code quality. For efficient data fetching from APIs, we used Axios, and the interactive map component was built with Leaflet. The project also incorporates Google Fonts for typography and icon libraries like Material Icons and react-icons. Turbopack was used to accelerate our development process.

How is your project creative? The project's creativity lies in its fundamental shift from raw data presentation to contextualized decision support. Unlike conventional weather applications that merely present meteorological figures, ClimaCerto uniquely interprets these figures through the specific lens of a user's planned activity. The Activity Suitability Index (IAA) is a novel, human-centric algorithm that synthesizes complex environmental variables into a single, easily understandable metric, offering truly personalized guidance. The "Trend Alert" further introduces a unique layer of insight, directly connecting historical climate data to evolving patterns and potential future risks, making complex climatological information accessible and actionable for everyday planning.

What factors did your team consider? Our team considered several critical factors throughout the development process. User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) were paramount, ensuring the app is intuitive, visually appealing, and provides immediate value without requiring meteorological expertise. The relevance and reliability of historical meteorological data were central to building a trustworthy foundation. We focused on long-term planning capabilities, addressing a key unmet need for future event organization. Additionally, the project's scalability and modular architecture were priorities, allowing for easy expansion with new activities and potential future integrations. We also carefully considered the adaptability to different user profiles and a wide range of outdoor activities, ensuring broad applicability and impact.

projectDetails.name: WAIN - Weather Artificial intelligence of NASA
projectDetails.summary:
The Smart Climate Solution is a platform that transforms complex NASA meteorological data into practical and accessible insights for businesses and governments. Utilizing an automated pipeline that combines AWS infrastructure and the Cloudflare network, the solution processes petabytes of satellite data and delivers it as real-time forecasts, alerts, and reports. The objective is to bridge the gap between climate science and business decisions, enabling sectors such as logistics, agriculture, and energy to optimize operations, reduce costs, and mitigate risks associated with extreme weather events.
The platform operates on a "Climate Intelligence as a Service" (CIaaS) model, offering an economical and scalable alternative to expensive in-house meteorological modeling teams. With a serverless and API-focused architecture, the solution ensures high availability, low latency, and security, in addition to allowing the creation of automations based on climatic triggers, such as the probability of rain. In this way, the project democratizes access to crucial data, promoting resilience and sustainability.
projectDetails.details:
Project_Description

1. What the Project Does and How It Works: An In-Depth Analysis

The Smart Climate Solution is a sophisticated Climate Intelligence as a Service (CIaaS) platform, called WAIN - Weather Artificial intelligence of NASA, designed to act as a universal translator between NASA's complex data ecosystem and the practical needs of the market. Its fundamental purpose is not just to provide weather forecasts, but to deliver contextualized business intelligence, transforming raw scientific data into a strategic advantage. The platform addresses the central challenge that, although NASA provides petabytes of high-quality Earth observation data, significant technical barriers—such as complex file formats (HDF, NetCDF), the need for data normalization, and the absence of a business context—prevent its use by the vast majority of companies, governments, and developers. The solution, therefore, positions itself as a bridge, democratizing access to this wealth of information.

The platform's operation is orchestrated by a robust and automated data pipeline, supported by a serverless and hybrid multi-cloud architecture, optimized for resilience, performance, and cost efficiency. The process begins with data ingestion from a diverse portfolio of NASA sources, including POWER (for energy and meteorology data), Giovanni, GES DISC, and Earthdata Search, as well as public sources like GPM, ERA5, and NOAA. This stage collects a wide range of atmospheric variables. The raw data is then stored in a Data Lake on Amazon S3, serving as a centralized repository. From there, the pipeline triggers AWS Lambda functions for processing and enrichment, where the "magic" of transformation occurs: data is normalized, validated, and converted from technical formats (HDF, NetCDF) to more accessible formats like JSON and CSV. Processed reports are persisted in Amazon DynamoDB, a high-performance NoSQL database, while high-demand results are strategically replicated and cached at the edge of Cloudflare's global network (using KV and R2), which reduces response latency to less than 120 milliseconds anywhere on the planet. The most innovative pillar of the solution is contextualization via Artificial Intelligence, using Machine Learning models based on TensorFlow and PyTorch. These models not only predict the weather but correlate climatic variables with operational and economic indicators, generating specific recommendations for each sector—for example, a 40% increase in humidity could trigger an alert for an insurance company to recalculate hail damage risk. Final delivery is made through a modular RESTful API, managed by AWS API Gateway, allowing plug-and-play integration with ERP, CRM systems, and other applications. Additionally, a climate automation engine allows users to configure actionable workflows (e.g., "If the probability of rain is greater than 50% for three consecutive days in Belo Horizonte, notify the operations team via CRM API"), transforming the platform into a proactive partner.

2. Strategic and Quantifiable Benefits of the Project

The benefits of the Smart Climate Solution are vast and quantifiable, generating tangible value on multiple fronts. In the economic sphere, the most direct benefit is the drastic reduction of operational and capital costs. The document estimates that the platform can cut up to 80% of the expenses companies would incur to maintain internal teams and meteorological modeling infrastructure, a cost ranging from US$200,000 to US$500,000 annually. In addition to direct savings, the solution acts as a powerful tool for loss mitigation, protecting sectors whose revenues are intrinsically linked to the climate. Brazilian agribusiness, for example, loses about R$25 billion annually due to climatic irregularities, and urban disaster costs exceed R$10 billion in reconstruction alone—losses that can be significantly reduced with accurate forecasts and alerts. The platform also opens doors for revenue increase, allowing companies to optimize their offerings based on the climate; the example of the value of an Airbnb reservation, which can increase by 50% to 200% with favorable forecasts, perfectly illustrates this potential.

Technically, the main benefit is the democratization of access to data science, by converting complex scientific data into a "business-ready" format through a simple API. This eliminates the entry barrier for companies that do not have climatology specialists. The serverless and edge computing architecture ensures high performance, resilience, and scalability, with 99.999% availability and the ability to absorb demand peaks without service degradation. Security and compliance are treated as central pillars, with the implementation of cutting-edge encryption (AES-256 with TLS 1.3), robust authentication, and adherence to major data regulations (LGPD, GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001), making the solution suitable for corporate and governmental environments. Strategically, the ultimate benefit is empowering organizations to achieve a new level of operational resilience and intelligence, enabling proactive and data-driven decision-making, which is fundamental in an era of increasing climate uncertainty.

3. The Intended Impact: A Holistic Vision

The intended impact of the Smart Climate Solution transcends the commercial sphere, aiming for positive transformation in social, economic, and environmental realms. The social impact is, perhaps, the most profound, as the project seeks to protect lives and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable communities. By providing early warnings and localized forecasts, the platform can be a vital tool to mitigate the devastating effects of floods, droughts, and heatwaves on at-risk populations, such as riverside communities and family farmers in Brazil and India, who are disproportionately affected and often lack access to critical information. This directly translates into reduced income loss, increased food security, and decreased social inequality.

Economically, the impact manifests in the strengthening of strategic sectors of the global economy. By making agriculture, logistics, energy, and tourism more efficient and less susceptible to climate shocks, the platform contributes to economic stability and sustainable growth. In a world where the annual cost of climate catastrophes already exceeds US$2 trillion, tools that increase predictability are invaluable economic assets. Environmentally, the solution promotes sustainability by enabling more efficient operations: optimizing transport routes reduces carbon emissions, precision agriculture decreases water and input waste, and energy management becomes more effective. These optimizations are in direct alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Finally, the project has a lasting scientific and technological impact, serving as an exemplary bridge between NASA's fundamental science and practical application, inspiring and empowering a new generation of innovations based on Earth observation data.

4. Detailed Overview of the Technological Ecosystem Used

The project was built upon a modern, robust, and carefully selected technological ecosystem to meet scalability, performance, and security requirements. The backbone of the infrastructure lies in Amazon Web Services (AWS), whose portfolio of serverless and managed services allows for agile and efficient operation. The main AWS services used are: AWS Lambda for serverless code execution, which forms the heart of the processing pipeline; Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service), used as a durable and scalable Data Lake for raw data; Amazon DynamoDB, a NoSQL database with millisecond latency for storing reports and metadata; AWS API Gateway, which acts as the entry point for all API requests, managing authentication, authorization, and traffic; AWS EventBridge, a serverless event bus that orchestrates communication between the different microservices of the pipeline; AWS Secrets Manager for secure management of API keys and other credentials; and the set of observability tools Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray, which provide end-to-end monitoring, logging, and tracing.

For the delivery and security layer at the edge, the platform synergistically integrates with Cloudflare. The Cloudflare Edge Network (CDN) is used to distribute and cache content globally, bringing data closer to end-users. Cloudflare KV and R2 are used as key-value and object storage at the edge, respectively, for even faster caching of high-demand reports. Security is reinforced by the Cloudflare Security Suite, which includes WAF (Web Application Firewall) and protection against DDoS attacks. Regarding development and artificial intelligence, the team utilized cutting-edge frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch, indicating the predominant use of the Python language for data science and backend processing. The entirely cloud-based nature of the project abstracts hardware complexity, allowing the team to focus on business logic while benefiting from the scale and resilience of AWS and Cloudflare's global infrastructure.

5. Project Creativity and Strategic Factors Considered

The creativity of the Smart Climate Solution lies not in the invention of new technology, but in its innovative synthesis and strategic application of existing technologies to solve an old and universal problem. The project's ingenuity resides in its ability to abstract the immense complexity of geospatial data and deliver it as a simple, intuitive, and high-value service. The main innovation is the paradigm shift from simple weather forecasting to the delivery of contextualized climate intelligence. The platform does not just answer "will it rain?" but rather "how will the rain forecast for Paris impact flight demand, and what is the recommendation for my airline?" This contextualization, powered by AI, is what transforms data into actionable wisdom.

This creative approach was shaped by a series of strategic factors that the team deeply considered. The primary factor was the identification of the critical gap between data availability and its practical applicability, a problem affecting both developing and advanced nations. The team analyzed specific scenarios in Brazil (losses in agribusiness), India (impact of monsoons on agriculture), and the United States (disaster recovery costs), understanding that, despite the differences, the central problem was the same. Another crucial factor was the focus on real business needs, designing the solution not as a technical exercise, but as a tool to generate tangible ROI. Scalability and the SaaS business model, with plans ranging from free to corporate, were considered to ensure the project's accessibility and financial sustainability. Developer Experience (DevEx) was prioritized, resulting in a well-designed RESTful API that facilitates integration. Finally, the team demonstrated a keen awareness of the social impact and climate inequality, positioning the solution not just as a product, but as a tool with the purpose of democratizing science and building a more resilient and equitable future.

projectDetails.name: Farm Twin - The Agricultural Digital Twin
projectDetails.summary:
Our team developed Farm Twin – The Agricultural Digital Twin, an educational board game inspired by NASA’s challenge to explore how space data can support agriculture. The game simulates a farm under varying conditions of climate, soil, and resource availability, using real NASA datasets such as NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) and climate forecasts as the foundation for gameplay.
Players face decisions about crop selection, resource allocation, and responses to environmental events, while balancing productivity and sustainability. Through this analog simulation, participants experience the impact of agricultural management choices in a simplified, engaging, and accessible format.
This project addresses the challenge by transforming complex satellite data into an intuitive learning tool. It helps farmers, students, and communities understand how environmental variability influences agricultural outcomes and how data-driven strategies can improve resilience to extreme events.
The importance of Farm Twin lies in its ability to bridge the gap between science and practice: making NASA data more approachable, fostering awareness of sustainable agriculture, and paving the way for a future digital prototype connected to real-time satellite and climate data.

projectDetails.name: Nebula X
projectDetails.summary:
NebulaX addresses NASA's challenge by applying machine learning to automate exoplanet identification across the vast array of Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. While traditional methods rely on manual analysis, our platform uses advanced AI algorithms to detect complex patterns in light curves, identifying planetary transits with over 96% accuracy.

Combining intelligent preprocessing, neural networks, and ensemble models, NebulaX not only exponentially accelerates discoveries but also democratizes access to astronomical research through an intuitive interface. This solution represents the evolution of space exploration, where artificial intelligence amplifies our ability to unravel cosmic mysteries.

Besides revolutionizing astrophysics, the techniques developed have the potential to impact other fields such as medicine and biotechnology, demonstrating the transformative power of AI in science. Our goal is to accelerate the search for habitable worlds and advance our understanding of the universe.

projectDetails.name: Cosmos Reader
projectDetails.summary:
Cosmos Reader is an interactive reading and learning platform that transforms space weather into a personalized journey. Designed to make studying engaging for all ages, the app combines artificial intelligence, gamification, and real NASA data through APIs, allowing each reader to become the protagonist of their own mission.

Users can create original stories or upload their own books. Aurora, an AI assistant, is equipped to explain scientific concepts using simple analogies, tailored to each person's level of understanding.

The platform also features an interactive space weather glossary, with trends and links to additional data. In addition, keywords are generated from books uploaded or written within the app, enhanced by AI and gamification elements — including a global leaderboard that highlights the most curious users, avid readers, and standout learners.

With the AI Story Illustrator, narratives come to life through unique illustrations, stimulating creativity. By combining storytelling, education, and technology, Cosmos Reader engages new audiences in science and climate awareness — making learning about the universe an accessible, inspiring adventure where users take center stage.
projectDetails.details:
What it does and how it works:

Cosmos Reader is an interactive reading and learning platform that transforms space weather and real scientific data into a personalized journey of discovery. By combining artificial intelligence, gamification, and NASA data, the app allows each user to become the protagonist of their own learning adventure.

Through Aurora, the intelligent assistant, readers can explore scientific concepts explained in simple, age adapted language. In addition, users can create original stories, upload their own books, and visualize everything through the AI Story Illustrator, which brings the content to life with unique, custom illustrations.

Personalized learning;

The use of AI allows the language and complexity of scientific concepts to be adapted to different age groups and knowledge levels;

Continuous engagement;

Gamification elements — including missions, rankings, achievements, and rewards — stimulate curiosity, reading habits, and autonomous learning.

Integration of art and science:

The AI Story Illustrator feature generates unique illustrations based on the stories, fostering creativity and visual thinking.

Global community of readers and explorers:

The worldwide leaderboard highlights curious readers, aspiring scientists, and creative writers, encouraging collaboration and recognition.

Intended Impact:

Cosmos Reader aims to democratize access to scientific knowledge and inspire new generations to explore the universe in an active and creative way.

By combining literature, technology, and scientific education, the project promotes:

Scientific and digital literacy across diverse audiences;

Climate and cosmic awareness, showing the connections between Earth, the Sun, and space;

Inspiration for STEM careers (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics);

Educational inclusion, making complex content both accessible and engaging.

challengeDetails.title: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings
challengeDetails.excerpt: Although the Sun is 93 million miles away from our planet, solar activity can significantly impact our daily lives. “Space weather”—the variations that occur in the space environment between the Sun and Earth—can impact technologies in space and on Earth. Your challenge is to write and illustrate a digital children’s story that explains what space weather is and the varying impacts it has on different people such as farmers, pilots, astronauts, power grid operators, and the general public. You can tell the story from the perspective of a person impacted by space weather or from the point of view of a solar flare or coronal mass ejection (CME) as it approaches Earth. (Heliophysics Division)

projectDetails.details:
SOBRE O WEATHER MACHINE

O weather machine funciona usando uma IA, mais especificamente um modelo de regressão linear (em python) que obtém os dados de clima diários obtidos no NASA Power Data Access Viewer, retornando de volta à webpage; Eles são:

  • Tempreratura
  • Velocidade do vento
  • Precipitação
  • Índice de raios UVA
  • Umidade específica

Apartir destes dados foi possível treinar o modelo para realizar as previsões. Consirerei importante deixa-lo de fácil acesso e muito intuitivo na hora de coompreender as informações, com cores, imagens etc.

ABOUT THE WEATHER MACHINE

The weather machine uses AI, specifically a linear regression model (in Python) that takes daily weather data from the NASA Power Data Access Viewer and returns it to the webpage. These include:

  • Temperature
  • Wind speed
  • Precipitation
  • UVA index
  • Specific humidity

Using this data, we were able to train the model to make forecasts. I consider it important to make it easily accessible and intuitive to understand, with colors, images, etc.

projectDetails.name: Luminho, O Plasma Viajante.
projectDetails.summary:
Histórias Estelares: O Clima Através dos Olhos Terráqueos
A Perspectiva: O Viajante EMC (Ejeção de Massa Coronal)

Luminho é uma nuvem de partículas carregadas, uma EMC recém-expulsa do Sol após uma grande erupção. Curioso e sonhador, ele decide explorar o espaço e acaba se encantando com o planeta azul — a Terra. Durante sua viagem, Luminho descobre o “abraço protetor” do campo magnético terrestre, a Magnetosfera, que o desvia, mas parte de sua energia ainda alcança o planeta.

No caminho, ele provoca efeitos inesperados: astronautas se abrigam na Estação Espacial, pilotos enfrentam falhas nos GPS e recorrem a mapas e bússolas, redes elétricas piscam e deixam uma criança frustrada sem videogame, e um agricultor precisa voltar a cuidar das plantações manualmente após perder o sinal dos satélites.

Vendo o que causou sem querer, Luminho se entristece, mas aprende sobre responsabilidade e empatia. Ele promete que, da próxima vez, avisará com uma linda “aura” luminosa — as Auroras Boreais — quando um de seus amigos solares decidir visitar a Terra.

Moral: Errar faz parte do aprendizado. O importante é reconhecer, corrigir e transformar o erro em algo bonito, como fez Luminho, mostrando que todos podem brilhar à sua maneira.
projectDetails.details:
Histórias Estelares: O Clima Através dos Olhos Terráqueos

A Perspectiva: O Viajante EMC (Ejeção de Massa Coronal)

A história se trata de Luminho, uma EMC que, após uma Chuva Coronal (que se trata de uma chuva de plasmas superaquecidos), vai se aventurar pelo espaço e fica admirado com a Terra.

Personagem Principal

Luminho é uma nuvem gigante de partículas carregadas (a EMC) que acabou de ser "espirrada" do Sol por uma Erupção Solar (a grande "tosse" do Sol).

O Enredo

A Jornada:

Luminho sai do Sol e viaja pelo espaço, admirado pela Terra. Ele não sabe que é poderoso e só quer saber mais sobre o planeta azul.

A Missão Inesperada:

Ao se aproximar da Terra, ele sente o "abraço protetor" do campo magnético (a Magnetosfera), que o desvia. Mas uma parte dele, a mais forte, consegue sentir a Terra.

Os Encontros e Impactos (A Causa e Efeito):

Astronautas: Ele passa perto da Estação Espacial, e os astronautas precisam se proteger dentro de módulos especiais para evitar o excesso de radiação.

Pilotos: Ele bagunça o GPS e as comunicações de um avião, fazendo com que o piloto precise usar métodos de navegação mais antigos (como mapas e bússolas).

Redes Elétricas: A partícula de Luminho acaba entrando na Terra e "esbarra" em fios elétricos (como um curto-circuito gigante), fazendo as luzes da cidade piscarem ou apagarem, frustrando uma criança que jogava videogame.

Agricultores: Ele atinge satélites que ajudam o agricultor (personagem secundário) e as máquinas agrícolas a monitorar sua plantação com precisão. O fazendeiro precisa voltar a verificar as plantas "na mão".

Desfecho da História:

Luminho, vendo o que causou sem querer, fica triste. Ele percebe que seu poder é grande. Então Luminho decide que, da próxima vez, vai avisar com uma "aura" de luz (a Aurora Boreal), quando um dos seus amigos ou parentes estiverem curiosos em sair viajando pelo espaço.

Moral da História:

Lembrando que mesmo errando no início, podemos consertar os nossos erros com bondade e tentando ajudar o próximo. Luminho mostra que a criança consegue ser amada e incluída, mesmo tendo suas diferenças.

projectDetails.name: Project FloraVision
projectDetails.summary:
FloraVision addresses the BloomWatch challenge by creating an automated phenological monitoring system focused on native Brazilian bioindicator trees, particularly ipês (Tabebuia spp.) in the Cerrado biome.
Using Sentinel-2, NASA MODIS, and INPE satellite data processed through Google Earth Engine, we detect flowering events by analyzing spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, IRECI, NDWI, MSI) that capture the unique pre-flowering leaf senescence and bloom patterns of deciduous species. Machine learning models (CNNs, Random Forest) classify phenological states, while Markov chains and linear regression predict flowering windows 7-30 days in advance with 87% accuracy.
Our proof-of-concept successfully detected ipê flowering 10 days before visual observation and revealed a critical finding: 2024 blooms occurred 18 days earlier than historical averages, providing quantifiable evidence of climate change impacts on ecosystem phenology. This tool empowers researchers, conservation managers, and policymakers with actionable insights for biodiversity monitoring and climate adaptation strategies.
projectDetails.details:
🌸 What does it do or how does it work?

Our project leverages NASA’s Earth Observation data — mainly HLS (Harmonized Landsat Sentinel) and VIP Phenology (NDVI/EVI2) datasets — to detect flowering patterns of Handroanthus (ipê trees) across the Brazilian Cerrado.
By combining multi-spectral indices such as IRECI, NDWI, MSI, and EVI, the system detects peaks of water stress followed by vegetation recovery, which correspond to flowering periods.
These patterns are cross-referenced with precipitation datasets (CHIRPS/GPM) and agricultural NDVI trends to analyze the connection between flowering, drought relief, and the beginning of crop cycles — particularly maize.

💡 Benefits and intended impact

The project transforms a natural event — the flowering of ipê trees — into a satellite-based climate signal that bridges biodiversity and agriculture.
Main benefits:

  • Supports climate-smart agriculture by using ecological indicators to anticipate rainfall and planting periods.
  • Promotes biodiversity monitoring and awareness of the Cerrado ecosystem.
  • Integrates local ecological knowledge with advanced Earth observation analytics.
  • Builds a scalable model that can be applied to other flowering events worldwide.

The intended impact is to demonstrate how AI and remote sensing can reveal connections between ecosystem behavior and human agricultural practices, promoting more sustainable land management and early-warning systems.

🛰️ Tools, languages, and software used

  • NASA & USGS APIs:
    • CMR/Earthdata Search API (HLS, VIPPHEN datasets)
    • GIBS/WMTS for map visualization
    • CHIRPS and GPM IMERG for precipitation data
    • Dyad — used to build a functional AI-powered prototype interface, capable of visualizing satellite data, receiving natural language queries, and assisting in analytical interpretation.
    • Claude AI — used for code generation, optimization, and scripting automation during the development of API integrations and processing pipelines.
    • Python (rasterio, geopandas, xarray, numpy, matplotlib) for image and data analysis
    • n8n for workflow orchestration and API automation
    • Google Earth Engine and Sentinel Hub API for time-series and index generation
    • QGIS/Leaflet for geospatial visualization

🎨 What makes it creative?

The project creatively merges AI, ecological knowledge, and remote sensing to transform the flowering of a native tree — a visual symbol of the Brazilian Cerrado — into a quantifiable environmental indicator.
It unites biological phenology, satellite imagery, and AI-assisted development, illustrating how technology can help interpret and preserve natural patterns that humans have observed for centuries.

🧠 Which factors did your team consider?

  • Seasonal climate variability and onset of rainfall in the Cerrado biome.
  • Spectral behavior of flowering versus vegetative phases.
  • Limitations of cloud cover and spatial resolution in satellite imagery.
  • Agricultural calendars for maize and soybean (ZARC data).
  • Water stress indices (NDWI, MSI) and phenological cycles.
  • Integration of AI tools to accelerate prototyping and code reliability.
  • The importance of combining traditional ecological knowledge with modern data science for sustainable outcomes.

projectDetails.name: CELESTIS
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary:
Our project addresses muscle atrophy caused by microgravity during space missions. We developed a smart watch equipped with physiological sensors that monitor astronauts’ muscle activity, oxygenation, temperature, pressure, and sweat in real time. The device functions as a data collector and transmitter, which is processed in the cloud and compared with NASA’s biomedical reference parameters.
Based on this analysis, the system identifies physiological changes, such as loss of muscle mass or strength, and sends the information to a personalized AI, which generates alerts and activates automatic responses in the suit through electrical microsimulation and vibration. This approach aims to prevent and correct muscle atrophy during long missions, ensuring optimal astronaut performance and recovery.
The project’s necessity is validated by NASA articles highlighting the lack of alternatives beyond standard exercises, which are often insufficient. Feasibility relies on integrating existing technologies — sensor watches, personalized AI, and microsimulation suits — to create an innovative, functional solution adapted to the space environment.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

The IAC-Active is an innovative system designed to prevent muscle atrophy in astronauts during long-duration microgravity missions. The core device is a smart watch that continuously collects physiological data — muscle activity (EMG), oxygenation, temperature, pressure, sweat, acceleration, and body orientation — via integrated sensors. This data is transmitted to the cloud and cross-referenced with NASA’s biomedical database to identify individual physiological changes. A personalized AI processes the data and sends alerts, recommendations, and electrical microstimulation signals to the astronaut’s “second skin,” targeting specific muscles to prevent loss of mass or strength.

Benefits and Impact:

The system enhances physical performance, accelerates post-mission rehabilitation, and can extend an astronaut’s operational career by 30–40%, reducing medical and training costs while ensuring physiological safety during long-term missions.

Creativity and Innovation:

Innovation lies in integrating existing technologies — smart watches, personalized AI, and NMES/EMS wearable suits — into a functional, space-adapted solution. The “second skin” is a form-fitting suit with textile electrodes distributed over key muscle groups, connected to electronic modules and a safe battery, controlled via the watch interface. The system design accounts for comfort, safety, washability, electromagnetic compatibility, and clinical usage protocols.

Tools and Technologies:

Physiological sensors, smart watch, electronic modules, cloud processing, personalized AI, NMES/EMS, conductive textiles, and secure wireless communication (BLE). Existing technologies are combined in a novel way for space use.

Considerations:

Safety, efficacy, comfort, biomedical and aerospace regulations, integration with existing space suits, system redundancy, continuous monitoring, clinical protocols, and medical supervision.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):

Artificial Intelligence was employed as a core component of the project to process physiological data collected by the smart watch. It continuously analyzes EMG signals, pressure, temperature, sweat, and movement, cross-referencing them with biomedical databases and extensive scientific research conducted at institutions such as NASA, MIT, Harvard, and other leading centers. The AI identifies physiological changes, generates personalized alerts, and issues electrical microstimulation commands to the astronaut’s “second skin.”

Furthermore, AI was utilized to produce 3D simulations of both the wearable suit and the smart watch, enabling precise design visualization, validation, and optimization during the conceptual development phase. All AI-generated models and simulations are clearly marked with a watermark to ensure full transparency in AI usage.

Tá Chovendo AI is a personalized weather forecasting platform that sends automatic WhatsApp alerts whenever weather conditions change in a way that could affect a user’s plans or events.

Unlike traditional forecast apps, users define the specific weather conditions they want or need to avoid — such as wind intensity, temperature range, or absence of lightning — and the system proactively notifies them of any relevant changes.

The platform integrates NASA satellite data and historical climate information, applying Machine Learning Linear Regression models to generate high-accuracy long-term predictions (up to six months ahead).

Its core value lies in turning generic forecasts into actionable insights, allowing users to plan with confidence. Instead of interpreting complex weather data, users receive personalized, predictive, and timely alerts, helping them prevent disruptions, losses, and frustrations.

In short, Tá Chovendo AI transforms weather forecasting into a proactive, intelligent, and user-centered experience — powered by NASA data and AI.
projectDetails.details:
Our application is a personalized weather forecasting platform that sends automatic alerts via WhatsApp whenever weather conditions change in a way that could affect your plans or events.

Unlike common weather apps, the user defines the specific conditions they want or wish to avoid, and the system notifies them when something changes — using NASA data (to be evaluated based on which datasets we can access and how to use them) and Machine Learning (ML) with Linear Regression models to predict scenarios in advance.

What it does:
It allows the user to configure specific weather parameters that determine the success or failure of a plan (for example, wind between 18–25 knots, moderate temperatures, or no lightning).

How it works:
It uses high-accuracy Linear Regression Machine Learning models, combining historical and satellite data (including NASA datasets) to generate detailed long-term forecasts — up to six months ahead.

Core Value:
The user no longer needs to interpret generic weather forecasts. The application actively monitors the custom conditions defined by the user and, if any change threatens their plan, it sends an instant and personalized alert.

This way, the user moves from being reactive to proactive, receiving predictive notifications that help prevent losses, delays, and frustrations.

projectDetails.summary:
In response to this challenge, our project, Apollo Terra, innovates in the fight against hunger in Ceará, Brazil, through a precision agriculture and artificial intelligence platform. Leveraging the power of NASA's MODIS sensor data, we conducted detailed mapping to identify areas of fertile and unused soil throughout the state. Our solution directly addresses the challenge by creating a tool to manage vegetation potential, moving from passive monitoring to proactive action.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) will cross-reference satellite data with climate and bibliographic information to determine the most suitable crops for each area, such as corn or beans. When it detects a spot with high production potential, the platform immediately alerts the local government and partner NGOs, signaling the urgency to mobilize resources. The ultimate goal is to quickly utilize these lands, directing the harvest to the Ceará Zero Hunger program and strengthening food security in the municipality where production occurred, transforming Earth observation into direct action against hunger.
projectDetails.details:
The Apollo Terra project is an interactive web platform designed to help users explore environmental and territorial data from Ceará, Brazil, in a visual, accessible, and engaging way. The platform integrates real-world datasets, including NASA’s open environmental data, to allow users to navigate through an interactive map, explore different regions of Ceará, discover vegetation and semi-arid areas using geospatial information, experience a gamified simulation that makes learning about environmental conditions more dynamic and intuitive, and use filters and dashboards to easily visualize specific data patterns. The intended impact of the project is to promote environmental awareness and education through accessible technology. By making scientific and territorial data more interactive and understandable, Apollo Terra aims to support researchers, students, policymakers, and the general public in exploring and understanding regional environmental dynamics.

The frontend of the project was developed using React for building the user interface, Vite for fast development and bundling, React Leaflet for interactive mapping features, CSS and Tailwind for responsive and modern styling, and NASA and external APIs for real environmental and vegetation data. The project is innovative because it combines real geospatial data with gamified interaction, making complex information more intuitive to explore. During the design process, the team considered accessibility and usability across different devices, data accuracy and integration with reliable sources such as NASA, a clean and responsive user interface to ensure a smooth user experience, and the educational impact of presenting information through visual storytelling and interactivity.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmos Sentinel
projectDetails.summary:
Cosmos Sentinel is a comprehensive decision-support platform that transforms raw scientific data into actionable intelligence for asteroid impact response. We developed an integrated system that simulates impact scenarios using real-time data from NASA (NeoWs, SBDB) and USGS (elevation, geology), providing tailored dashboards for scientists, the public, and, most critically, governmental agencies.

This directly addresses the challenge by not only modeling physical consequences but also focusing on the humanitarian and logistical aftermath. Our platform generates detailed reports on infrastructure at risk, resource deficits (like shelters and medical aid), and provides a timeline for critical actions. The most innovative feature is our "AI for Congestion-Free Evacuation," which uses real-world road data and reinforcement learning to calculate and manage optimized evacuation routes, preventing catastrophic traffic jams.

This project is important because it shifts the focus from simply visualizing a disaster to actively managing it. By providing actionable intelligence and a solution to the complex problem of mass evacuation, Cosmos Sentinel bridges the critical gap between scientific data and the life-saving decisions that must be made on the ground.
projectDetails.details:
What it Does and How it Works

Cosmos Sentinel is an integrated decision-support platform designed to transform a potential asteroid impact from an unmanageable catastrophe into a coordinated response.

It works in three main stages:

  1. Data Ingestion and Simulation: The platform consumes real-time data from official agency APIs, including NASA's NeoWs and SBDB for asteroid characteristics and trajectory, and the USGS's elevation and geology services to understand the impact zone's topography and ground composition. This data feeds a physics-based model that simulates the physical effects of the impact (e.g., tsunami height, seismic magnitude).
  2. Consequence Analysis: This is where Cosmos Sentinel excels. It moves beyond physical effects to analyze the humanitarian and logistical consequences. The system cross-references the impact zone with population data to estimate populations at risk and identifies critical infrastructure (ports, airports, power plants) that will be affected, quantifying the necessary response, such as a shelter deficit of over 1.5 million people.
  3. Actionable Intelligence and AI-Powered Evacuation: The platform presents this analysis in tailored dashboards. For government officials, the GovernmentDashboard provides a clear summary of critical metrics and a timeline of actions. Its most innovative feature is the "AI for Congestion-Free Evacuation," which uses real-world road data from OpenStreetMap and a multi-component AI system (including Reinforcement Learning) to calculate and manage optimized, traffic-free evacuation routes.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The primary benefit of Cosmos Sentinel is its ability to save lives and mitigate economic devastation.

  • Benefits:
    • Transforms Data into Decisions: It converts complex scientific data into clear, actionable KPIs for leaders (e.g., "1,517,700 shelter spaces needed," "Transfer 342 hospital patients").
    • Solves Mass Evacuation Chaos: The AI-powered routing system is designed to prevent the traffic gridlock that could be as deadly as the impact itself, ensuring a more orderly and rapid evacuation.
    • Prioritizes Actions: The system provides a clear timeline and ranks the top 5 critical actions needed within the first 72 hours, allowing for effective resource allocation under extreme pressure.
  • Intended Impact: The intended impact is to shift the global paradigm from disaster reaction to proactive crisis management. By providing a tool that allows authorities to plan, simulate, and manage a response before an impact occurs, Cosmos Sentinel aims to drastically reduce loss of life and give cities a fighting chance to protect their populations and critical assets.

Technology and Tools Used

We employed a modern, full-stack architecture to build a robust and scalable platform.

  • Backend:
    • Languages: Python
    • Framework: FastAPI for creating high-performance, asynchronous APIs.
    • AI & Data Science Libraries: PyTorch for the Reinforcement Learning model (DQN) that controls traffic signals; scikit-learn for predictive models; OSMnx and NetworkX to process real-world road network data from OpenStreetMap for the evacuation AI.
    • Languages: JavaScript, HTML, CSS
    • Framework: React 18 for building a dynamic and component-based user interface.
    • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS for a modern, responsive design; Lucide React for icons; and Framer Motion for animations.
    • Mapping: Leaflet for interactive 2D maps that visualize impact zones and evacuation routes.

Creativity and Factors Considered

The creativity of Cosmos Sentinel lies in its unique approach to the problem and its thoughtful design.

  • Creative Approach:
    • From "What If" to "What Now": While other simulators stop at showing the destruction, our project's creativity is in answering the next, more important question: "What do we do now?". This shift from a passive educational tool to an active decision-support system is our core innovation.
    • Multi-Persona Dashboards: We creatively addressed the challenge of communicating complex data by designing distinct user experiences: a high-level strategic dashboard for leaders (GovernmentDashboard), a detailed interface for scientists (ScientificReport), and an engaging simulator for the public (AsteroidDashboard).
    • AI for a Human Problem: Applying a sophisticated, three-part AI system to solve the deeply human and chaotic problem of mass evacuation is a novel and creative use of technology.
    • Scientific Rigor: Our top priority was ensuring the simulations were grounded in reality. This is why we chose to use live data from official sources like NASA and USGS wherever possible.
    • Actionable vs. Overwhelming Data: We carefully considered how to present vast amounts of data without overwhelming the user. The GovernmentDashboard is a direct result of this, summarizing billions of data points into critical, easy-to-understand metrics.
    • The Human Element: We went beyond physics to consider the real-world factors of a disaster. The inclusion of population vulnerability, critical infrastructure dependencies, and the psychology of mass evacuation drove the design of our most important features.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
1. Core AI Feature within the Project: The most critical AI component is the "AI for Congestion-Free Evacuation," which we developed and implemented. This system is documented in backend/README_IA_EVACUACAO.md and uses a multi-layered approach:

  • Routing AI: Employs algorithms like Frank-Wolfe and real-world road data from OSMnx to calculate and distribute traffic across optimal evacuation routes, preventing bottlenecks.
  • Predictive AI: Uses a Machine Learning model (Gradient Boosting) to forecast travel times based on variables like weather and traffic conditions.
  • Decision AI: Utilizes a Deep Q-Network (Reinforcement Learning) to intelligently control traffic signals in real-time, further optimizing traffic flow.

2. AI Tools for Development Assistance: To accelerate innovation and development, our team used several generative AI tools for assistance, with all generated code and ideas being reviewed, tested, and adapted by the team.

  • ChatGPT and Gemini: These large language models were used for generating code snippets, debugging assistance, explaining complex programming concepts, and helping to draft documentation.
  • Cursor: This AI-powered code editor was utilized to assist in writing and running tests for our backend services, helping to ensure code quality and reliability.
  • Claude: This tool was consulted during the initial phases for brainstorming and generating ideas for the user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design of our frontend dashboards.

projectDetails.name: Project LEO-Compute Secure
projectDetails.summary: In our project, LEO-Compute Secure, we developed an innovative two-layer orbital data center architecture to overcome the security and sustainability challenges of terrestrial data centers. Our solution uses low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for the active processing of data requiring rapid access and low latency, functioning as "hot storage". For long-term storage and secure archiving ("cold storage"), we use geostationary orbit (GEO) satellites. The importance of our project lies in its ability to offer a global, resilient, and energy-efficient data infrastructure that leverages the natural cooling of space and solar energy to operate sustainably and protect critical information from terrestrial physical and cyber risks.
projectDetails.details:
The LEO-Compute Secure project is an innovative solution for secure digital data storage and large-scale information processing that utilizes a constellation of satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), with a focus on sustainability and energy efficiency.

What the Project Does and How it Works

The main objective is to implement a LEO satellite constellation to provide Data Center as a Service (DCaaS), offering data processing, storage, and security. Each satellite node functions independently, performing complex tasks without reliance on ground servers.

Key technical aspects include:

Architecture: The satellites are designed as autonomous processing and storage nodes, with a target of 30-40 satellites in LEO (500–1200 km) for continuous global coverage.

Security: All critical cryptographic processes use Hardware Security Modules (HSM) and are performed in isolated hardware. The LEO-Secure Protocol employs elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) combined with PGP for encryption in transit, and data is re-encrypted after processing.

Communication: Satellites connect via high-speed optical Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs), reaching up to 200 Gbps, enabling a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) system for task sharing and network redundancy.

Processing: Tasks are distributed among satellites to avoid overload and process data immediately on the nearest node, reducing response time. The system supports embedded AI using high-efficiency CPUs/GPUs and FPGA/ASIC accelerators for encryption and real-time analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to be a sustainable, resilient, and scalable solution for critical computing demands, addressing major weaknesses in terrestrial data center implementations.

Sustainability and Energy Efficiency: The system achieves significant energy savings by using thermal radiation into deep space for natural cooling, eliminating traditional cooling systems and reducing energy consumption. It uses integrated solar panels for power, taking advantage of the continuous solar life.

Security and Resilience: It offers high physical security, protecting against cyberattacks, natural disasters, and operational failures on Earth. The distributed architecture ensures redundancy and continuity in adverse scenarios.

Global Access and Performance: The constellation provides continuous network infrastructure anywhere on Earth with low latency (under 50 ms), which is vital for real-time processing and large-scale AI applications.

Use Cases: It provides orbital data processing solutions for strategic sectors, including: Earth observation (climate monitoring, disaster management), security and defense (encrypted communications, surveillance), financial services (high-frequency transactions, distributed auditing), and scientific research (global simulations).

Creativity, Tools, and Factors Considered

Creativity: The project's core creativity is moving the data center infrastructure to LEO to leverage space's natural cooling and solar power for operational optimization, creating a solution inherently protected from many terrestrial vulnerabilities. Future plans involve a two-layer orbital architecture, using LEO for "hot storage" (active processing) and GEO (Geostationary Orbit) for "cold storage" (long-term preservation).

Tools, Coding, and Hardware: Key hardware includes low-power, high-efficiency CPUs/GPUs, FPGA/ASIC accelerators, and high-density, radiation-tolerant SSDs and RAM. The methodology includes the use of AI for predictive and dynamic solutions, specifically for adverse weather route diversion and battery charging optimization with a focus on maximizing sun exposure.

Factors Considered (Challenges): The team analyzed complex challenges, including the high initial cost and launch failure risk (requiring launch insurance), the impossibility of physical repairs in orbit (necessitating remote maintenance and redundancy) , and the need to comply with international regulations and space debris mitigation guidelines. Components must also be protected with physical shielding and error correction algorithms (ECC) against space radiation and component degradation.
