App Summary: Cloud Computing with Earth Observation for Cleaner, Safer Skies

Our app integrates cloud computing technology with Earth observation (EO) data to monitor, analyze, and predict air quality and weather patterns for a cleaner and safer environment. By processing large volumes of satellite and sensor data in real time, the app provides accurate insights on pollution levels, climate trends, and potential hazards.

The system uses cloud-based AI models to predict changes in atmospheric conditions and identify pollution hotspots, helping authorities and individuals take proactive action. With features like live dashboards, air quality alerts, and comparative city analysis, it aims to promote environmental awareness and support sustainable urban planning.

In short, this app empowers users with real-time environmental intelligence — combining Earth observation precision with cloud computing efficiency to build cleaner, safer skies for all.
projectDetails.details:
Project Title:

Cloud Computing with Earth Observation for Cleaner, Safer Skies

Project Overview:

This project aims to develop an intelligent application that combines cloud computing and Earth observation (EO) data to monitor, analyze, and predict atmospheric conditions for cleaner and safer skies. By utilizing real-time satellite imagery, IoT sensor data, and advanced cloud analytics, the app delivers accurate forecasts, pollution tracking, and early warnings about air quality hazards.

Objectives:

  1. To integrate Earth observation data for real-time environmental monitoring.
  2. To use cloud computing for large-scale data storage and processing.
  3. To predict pollution levels, weather changes, and potential air hazards.
  4. To promote public awareness and sustainable air quality management.
  5. To provide decision-making support for environmental agencies and communities.

Key Features:

  • Real-time Air Quality Dashboard – Displays live air pollution levels, weather forecasts, and alerts.
  • Satellite Data Integration – Uses EO data for accurate atmospheric analysis.
  • Cloud-based Processing – Stores and analyzes large datasets efficiently.
  • Alert System – Notifies users about pollution peaks and safety concerns.
  • City Comparison Tool – Compares environmental conditions between locations.
  • Prediction Models – Uses AI and ML for forecasting future air quality trends.

Role of Cloud Computing:

  • Enables real-time processing of massive EO datasets.
  • Provides scalability for storage and analytics.
  • Supports machine learning for predictive modeling.
  • Facilitates remote accessibility for users and agencies.

Benefits:

  • Enhances environmental monitoring accuracy.
  • Reduces pollution risks through predictive alerts.
  • Supports cleaner urban air management.
  • Encourages eco-conscious decisions.
  • Provides global accessibility via the cloud.

Technologies Used:

  • Programming Languages: JavaScript
  • APIs: NASA Earth Observation API, OpenWeather API
  • Tools: Node.js

Target Users:

  • Environmental agencies
  • Urban planners
  • Researchers
  • General public concerned about air quality

Expected Outcomes:

  • A working app that predicts and visualizes air quality.
  • Improved understanding of pollution patterns.
  • A step toward achieving sustainable, cleaner skies through technology.

projectDetails.name: BloomWatch App
projectDetails.summary:
This project analyzes and visualizes flower blooming patterns across various global locations based on climate and temperature variations. Using historical and simulated environmental data, the system predicts bloom timings for different regions and months, helping researchers and enthusiasts understand how climate change impacts flowering cycles.Predicts flower blooming periods using temperature and seasonal data.Displays bloom intensity and distribution on an interactive global map.Allows users to explore month-wise changes in bloom patterns through a time slider.Built with Flutter for visualization and integrated with climate-based prediction models.
Impact:
Supports ecological research by visualizing phenological changes and promoting awareness of how climate fluctuations affect plant life cycles.
projectDetails.details:
The project predicts and visualizes flower blooming events across different regions and months using climate and temperature data. It analyzes seasonal trends and generates bloom intensity patterns for various cities. The results are displayed on an interactive world map with a time slider, allowing users to explore bloom changes month by month.

Benefits:

  • Helps researchers and environmentalists track the effects of climate change on plant flowering cycles.
  • Provides visual insights into global blooming trends in an easy-to-understand format.
  • Can assist in ecological forecasting, agriculture planning, and biodiversity studies.

Intended Impact:
To increase awareness and provide data-driven insights into how climate variations influence flower phenology, supporting sustainability research and conservation planning.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used:

  • Frontend: Flutter (Dart) for UI and interactive map visualization.
  • Backend/Computation: Python for data processing and bloom prediction logic.
  • APIs & Data: NASA climate data and simulated temperature datasets.
  • Libraries: Provider (state management), latlong2 (mapping), and mock data generation for simulation.

Creativity:
The project uniquely combines climate data, AI-based predictions, and geospatial visualization into a single interactive tool. It transforms complex scientific data into an engaging, real-time visual dashboard accessible to anyone.

Factors Considered:

  • Climate variability and its correlation with bloom timing.
  • Accuracy vs. simulation trade-off for limited real data.
  • Smooth UI and performance optimization using isolates for background computation.
  • Scalability for adding real satellite datasets in future versions.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our project uses AI for climate and temperature-based prediction of flower blooming patterns. AI models analyze historical bloom data, temperature, and climate trends to predict when and where flowers are likely to bloom across different locations. This helps visualize flower phenology patterns globally and supports environmental monitoring.

All AI-generated insights and predictions are clearly labeled in the project. No NASA branding or logos were used in any AI-generated content.

projectDetails.name: Project ThinkForge
projectDetails.summary:
We created Exoplanet Identifier AI, a web application that enables users to identify potential exoplanets from real telescope light curve data. It supports users uploading data from such missions as NASA's Kepler or TESS, on which our Flask-based backend executes an AI model to scan brightness fluctuations and determine if a planet transit is present. The frontend, constructed using HTML and CSS, plots the star's light curve, marks the detected dips, and shows a detection confidence level using interactive plots and animations.

Our solution confronts the challenge head-on by streamlining exoplanet detection for scientists, teachers, and amateur astronomy enthusiasts alike—filling the gap between raw telescope data and easily understandable insights. It encourages open science through its use of authentic NASA archives and opens up space research to everyone in an easy-to-use, educational interface. In the end, Exoplanet Identifier AI makes searching for new worlds outside our own solar system more accessible, transparent, and collaborative.
projectDetails.details:
What it does / How it works:

Exoplanet Identifier AI is a smart web-based application that identifies possible exoplanets from telescope data. Users input light curve data—time-series measurements of a star's brightness—taken from NASA's Kepler or TESS missions. The backend in Flask handles the data, normalizes and cleans the signal, and passes it through an AI model that is trained to detect periodic dips that signify a planet transit. The frontend, developed in HTML and CSS, plots the light curve interactively with Chart.js, marks the transit events, and shows the confidence score of the AI.

Advantages:

Our system empowers anyone—from scientists to students—to easily pick out possible exoplanets quickly, without the need for advanced scientific equipment. It interprets raw data into valuable insights, conserving time and decreasing the entry barrier for participation in exoplanet exploration.

Intended Impact:

The project has the goal of democratizing exoplanet research and opening up citizen science to everyone. By making actual NASA data into interactive visual experiences, it promotes public interest, learning, and collective exploration outside of Earth.

Tools and Technologies Used:

Frontend: React, Streamlit, Chart.js (for data visualization purposes)

Backend: Python, Flask, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn (processing for AI/ML)

Data Sources: NASA Exoplanet Archive, Kepler, and TESS light curve data sets

Creativity and Design Considerations:

We aimed to integrate science with interactivity. In addition to AI forecasting, we incorporated 3D orbit animation and a confidence visualizer to make the process of discovery interactive. Our team kept accessibility, low-latency computing, and hackathon functionality in the forefront—providing an operable, educational, and visually engaging space exploration tool within a concise time period.

The team later reviewed, altered, and tested all code generated to verify originality and functionality.

Documentation & Content Writing:

Gemini & perplexity was employed to improve project summaries, technical descriptions, and submission write-ups for accuracy and brevity. Final text was checked and proofread by the team to represent our work and design decisions correctly.

The machine learning model was trained and validated on real observational data.

projectDetails.name: Project ThunderBoltz
projectDetails.summary:
Name: Cohort-Quest

Platform: Web app

Purpose: It seems focused on “quests” (i.e., tasks or challenges) within cohorts.

Structure: Users probably join cohorts, get a set of quests, and progress via those.

Audience: Could be students, learners, or groups doing structured challenge tasks (e.g. educational/training cohorts).

UI / features (inferred): There is likely a dashboard, quests list, progress tracking, maybe rewards or completion status.

Backend / tech: Unclear from front-end only, but typical stack (React, Next.js, etc.) given “vercel.app” hosting.
projectDetails.details:
Problem Statement / Motivation

  • In many collaborative learning or challenge programs (e.g. space science outreach, citizen science, student cohorts), participants lose motivation or drop out due to lack of structure, engagement, or visibility into progress.
  • There is an opportunity to gamify challenge participation, especially in STEM / space domains, to increase retention, peer collaboration, and measurable learning outcomes.

Proposed Solution

  • Cohort-Quest: A web platform that allows challenge organizers (e.g. NASA, universities, NGOs) to define quests or missions (i.e. tasks, mini-challenges) for participants, grouped into cohorts.
  • Participants log in, see their assigned missions, complete them (upload results, report metrics, or submit work), and their progress is tracked.
  • Leaderboards, badges, peer collaboration, mentoring, or reviews can be built in.
  • Admins/cohort leads can monitor cohort health (who’s stuck, who’s ahead), send nudges, add hints, or adjust difficulty.

Core Features (to include / emphasize)

  1. Quest Definition & Workflow
    • Create quests with descriptions, deadlines, hints, checkpoints
    • Dependencies (quest B unlocks after A)
    • Submission types (text, file upload, media, code)
    • Admins create cohorts, invite participants
    • Assign quest tracks to cohorts
    • Visual dashboard: percent complete, average time, dropouts
    • Gamification: badges, points, streaks, levels
    • Forums / chat for cohort peers
    • Peer review / mentor feedback
    • Hint / help requests
    • Reminders for deadlines
    • Encouragement for inactive users
    • APIs to import/export data
    • Integration with learning management systems
    • Mobile responsiveness
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Intelligent Quest Generation / Personalization

  • Adaptive quest recommendation: Based on a participant’s prior performance, suggest the next quest or difficulty level.
  • Auto-generate quests: Given a theme (e.g. Earth science, satellite data, climate), system can draft quest templates (with tasks, hints) using LLMs.
  • Dynamic hints: If participants are stuck, AI can analyze their incomplete submission or partial solution and offer context-aware hints.

B. Automated Feedback & Assessment

  • For textual or code submissions, use AI to automatically evaluate correctness, quality, or completeness (e.g. code test cases, rubric scoring).
  • Use rubric-based LLM evaluation to give feedback: "Your analysis is good, but you missed considering X."
  • Plagiarism / originality detection (especially for descriptive or essay tasks).

C. Natural Language Interface

  • Participants can interact via chat (ask “what’s my next mission?” “how do I solve part 2?”) using conversational AI.
  • Summarization of quest documents, providing quick overviews or key points.

D. Analytics & Prediction

  • Predict dropouts: Using user behavior and engagement metrics, flag participants at risk of dropping out and send intervention.
  • Cluster participants by performance / style to tailor support.
  • Generate cohort-level insights: which types of quests are hardest, average completion time, bottlenecks.

E. Knowledge Base / Contextual Support

  • AI can incorporate domain knowledge (e.g. NASA datasets, Earth science, astrophysics) into hints or context.
  • Automatically link external resources (papers, data portals) relevant to a quest’s topic.

projectDetails.summary:
Cosmic Query is an AI-powered space exploration assistant that combines NASA’s open APIs with Google’s Gemini model to make complex space data easily understandable. Using real-time information from NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) and Mars Rover Photo APIs, the system allows users to ask natural language questions—such as “Show me today’s Mars surface images” or “Explain the significance of today’s astronomy picture”—and receive accurate, conversational responses. Gemini interprets and summarizes NASA’s scientific data into clear explanations, enabling anyone to explore space knowledge without technical expertise.

This project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge theme of improving accessibility to space science and data. It’s important because it bridges the gap between raw scientific information and public understanding—empowering students, educators, and enthusiasts to engage with space in an interactive, intelligent way.
projectDetails.details:
What it does / How it works:
Cosmic Query is an intelligent space information platform that merges NASA’s open data with Google’s Gemini AI to create an interactive cosmic exploration experience. It fetches real-time data from NASA APIs—such as Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) and Mars Rover Photos—and uses Gemini to interpret, summarize, and answer user queries in natural language. Users can simply ask questions like “What is today’s APOD about?” or “Show me the latest Mars surface image,” and the system generates meaningful, human-friendly explanations.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
The project makes NASA’s complex datasets accessible to everyone—students, educators, and space enthusiasts—without requiring technical skills. It enhances science communication, promotes curiosity, and fosters interest in astronomy and space research.

Tools & Technologies:

  • NASA Open APIs (APOD, Mars Rover Photos)
  • Gemini API (Google AI Studio)
  • Python for scripting and API integration

Creativity & Design Considerations:
We focused on simplicity, interactivity, and clarity—designing the project to translate raw data into conversational insights. The creative edge lies in combining real-time space data with an advanced generative model to make cosmic exploration both educational and inspiring.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Our project, Cosmic Query, integrates Google’s Gemini API (via Google AI Studio) to process and generate natural language responses. The AI was used to interpret NASA’s open datasets—such as Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) and Mars Rover Photos—and summarize or explain the data in an easy-to-understand way for users.

AI was not used to generate any NASA logos, images, or mission identifiers. All visual data (space images) are sourced directly from NASA’s official APIs, while text-based summaries and explanations are generated by the Gemini model.

AI assistance was limited to text generation, explanation, and user query handling to enhance data accessibility and user experience.

It combines NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) data with USGS geological datasets. projectDetails.name: From Data to Action: A Clearer Forecast
projectDetails.summary:
Our team developed a live, scalable web application that transforms massive, inconsistent satellite data into actionable air quality forecasts. We tackled the challenge of extracting public health value from complex Earth Observation data.

What we developed: We built a Streamlit-based dashboard powered by a custom Python data pipeline. The application visualizes the average Tropospheric NO₂ concentration over a specific region, overlaid with local ground station data for validation.

How it addresses the challenge: We solved the critical "cloud computing" and data integration hurdle. Our solution utilizes Dask and xarray to parallel-process over 80 multi-dimensional NetCDF files, demonstrating a robust and efficient workflow for handling gigabyte-scale scientific datasets on the cloud.

Why it is important: This project provides citizens and policymakers with a clear, unified view of pollution, enabling better public health decisions and fulfilling the mission of open science by making complex NASA/ESA data accessible to everyone.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works

Our project, "Predicting Cleaner, Safer Skies," is a scalable web application that processes vast amounts of atmospheric data to provide a clear, visual analysis of air quality. The core of our solution is a robust, cloud-native data pipeline. It leverages Python, Dask, and xarray to parallel-process over 80 multi-dimensional NetCDF files from the Sentinel-5P TROPOMI satellite. This raw data is then cleaned, standardized, and used to generate a comprehensive spatial map in a Streamlit dashboard, which also includes local ground station data for validation.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The primary benefit of our project is its ability to turn complex scientific data into actionable public information. By visualizing long-term average NO₂ concentrations and identifying pollution hotspots, the tool empowers individuals to make informed decisions about their health and helps local officials guide environmental policy. Our intended impact is to bridge the gap between open-source data and public use, fostering a more informed and health-conscious global community.

Creativity & Team Factors

Our project's creativity lies in its resilience and focus on a practical, working solution. When we faced challenges with ungridded data, we developed a novel preprocessing function that extracts and assigns a "time" coordinate from filenames, a critical step that allowed us to successfully combine the data. This robust solution, powered by Dask and xarray, demonstrates a creative approach to overcoming real-world data limitations. We also considered user experience by building an accessible, easy-to-use web dashboard.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Coding Languages: Python
  • Key Libraries: Streamlit (for the app), xarray & Dask (for data processing), Matplotlib & GeoPandas (for visualization).
  • Data Source: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI Level 3 NO₂ data from NASA's Earthdata portal.
  • Development Environment: VS Code, Anaconda.

projectDetails.name: ISS Experience
projectDetails.summary:
We set out to turn two unforgettable ISS sensations into learning experiences people can feel in minutes. Our web app has three parts: Cupola, NBL Training, and a Gallery. In Cupola mode, we guide users through curated astronaut imagery and location cards, showing how human‑taken photos complement satellites for disaster awareness, climate context, and geography literacy. In NBL mode, users tune buoyancy by adding or removing weights and floats based on body mass, then attempt EVA‑style tasks—handrail translation, hatch ingress, and tool handling—mirroring how astronauts rehearse complex procedures underwater. The Gallery ties it together with striking contrasts like Caribbean coasts, Amazon deforestation patterns, and Saharan landforms to build visual literacy and a sense of change over time.

Why this matters: the Cupola’s vantage and crew photography provide flexible, timely context for hazards and long‑term monitoring, while NBL methods translate into human‑factors practices used in high‑risk work on Earth. We designed short, touch‑friendly scenes that fit classrooms, museum kiosks, and hackathon demos, with minimal setup and easy asset swaps. Our goal is simple: transform awe into understanding—and understanding into real‑world benefit—by letting learners stand at the window to the world and feel the physics that prepare astronauts to keep the station, and each other, safe.
projectDetails.details:
What it does and how it works

  • Our web app turns two core ISS sensations—Cupola “sight” and NBL “weightlessness”—into short, touch‑friendly interactions. The Cupola mode steps through curated Earth images with location overlays and quick facts; the NBL mode is a buoyancy mini‑game where users add/remove weights and floats to reach neutral buoyancy, then attempt EVA‑style tasks like handrail translation, hatch ingress, and tool handling.
  • A gallery ties it together with contrasting scenes (Caribbean coasts, Amazon change, Saharan landforms) to build visual literacy and “spot the signal” skills.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Shows why astronaut photos complement satellites for rapid hazard awareness, climate context, and geography learning.
  • Makes microgravity training relatable through hands‑on physics, reinforcing safety, procedure discipline, and human‑factors thinking transferable to high‑risk jobs on Earth.
  • Designed for classrooms, museums, and hackathon kiosks: 90‑second scenes, minimal setup, easy asset swaps.

Tech stack and tools

  • Front end: HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript.
  • Logic/views: Cupola and NBL modules plus a gallery page; lightweight routing with a minimal Python backend for easy local or cloud hosting.
  • Assets: Curated astronaut‑style Earth imagery; modular JSON/config for adding locations and tasks.

Creativity and design choices

  • “Stand in the window, feel the pool” pairs emotion with mechanics to convert awe into understanding.
  • Fast, inclusive UX: large tap targets, brief loops, captions at a middle‑school reading level, and offline‑friendly packaging.
  • Team factors: event throughput, low bandwidth, attribution, future extensibility (more locations, live data, lunar pool mode).

projectDetails.name: Project Vision X
projectDetails.summary:
ChatterBot is a Python library that makes it easy to generate automated responses to a user’s input. ChatterBot uses a selection of machine learning algorithms to produce different types of responses. This makes it easy for developers to create chat bots and automate conversations with users.The language independent design of ChatterBot allows it to be trained to speak any language. Additionally, the machine-learning nature of ChatterBot allows an agent instance to improve it’s own knowledge of possible responses as it interacts with humans and other sources of informative data.ChatterBot is a Python library designed to make it easy to create software that can engage in conversation.

An untrained instance of ChatterBot starts off with no knowledge of how to communicate. Each time a user enters a statement, the library saves the text that they entered and the text that the statement was in response to. As ChatterBot receives more input the number of responses that it can reply to, and the accuracy of each response in relation to the input statement increases.

The program selects the closest matching response by searching for the closest matching known statement that matches the input, it then chooses a response from the selection of known responses to that statement.

projectDetails.details:
The NASA Bioscience Explorer is a web-based tool designed to help users explore and interpret over 600 spaceflight bioscience experiments. It works by combining structured metadata with interactive filters, visualizations, and AI-powered summarization. Users can search experiments by organism, mission, year, and platform, view trends through timeline charts, and explore relationships via a dynamic knowledge graph hosted on Streamlit. The intended impact is to accelerate hypothesis generation, support safer mission design, and make NASA’s bioscience data more usable for a broader audience.

Creativity came through in the animated UI, placard-style layout, and seamless integration of external tools into a GoDaddy-hosted public website. Our team focused on clarity, extensibility, and scientific relevance throughout.

projectDetails.name: NASA's ISS Water Recovery System: A Costly and Energy-Intensive Challenge for Long-Duration
projectDetails.summary: The herbal purification cartridge designed for NASA's wastewater recycling system is a modular, multi-stage biofilter that utilizes the inherent properties of selected botanicals for sustainable water reclamation. The wastewater is processed sequentially through various layers, beginning with Clearing Nut (Strychnos potatorum), which facilitates natural coagulation, thereby causing suspended solids to aggregate and settle. Subsequently, the water flows through Vetiver (Chrysopogon zizanioides) root fibers, which serve as an effective biofilter by adsorbing finer impurities and inhibiting microbial growth through their intrinsic antimicrobial compounds. Finally, the Nannari Root (likely Hemidesmus indicus) layer refines the water by removing residual organic contaminants and odor-causing molecules, significantly enhancing clarity and potability. This process provides a low-energy, bio-regenerative pre-treatment prior to final sterilization.
projectDetails.details: Our project is centered on the development of a straightforward, environmentally sustainable prototype utilizing natural herbs encased within a transparent PVC hose to illustrate health and environmental advantages. By integrating materials such as Clearing Nut, Vetiver, and Nannari Root, we aim to demonstrate the practical applications of traditional herbal remedies in contemporary settings. These herbs are recognized for their efficacy in water purification, skin and hair care, emotional well-being, and digestive health. The transparent hose provides a visually informative setup, while the dummy end caps ensure secure containment. This prototype not only underscores the potential of cost-effective, sustainable solutions but also bridges traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern design thinking. The project fosters innovation through the use of natural resources, particularly in regions with limited access to healthcare or clean water. Overall, this prototype serves as a model to promote awareness of herbal applications, sustainability, and the integration of nature with technology in everyday problem-solving.

projectDetails.name: BLOOM WATCH-An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology
projectDetails.summary:
This project developed a predictive system using NASA satellite data and Google Earth Engine to monitor and forecast plant and algal bloom events over large geographical areas. The core challenge addressed is the limitation of ground-based monitoring, which often lacks the coverage and timeliness needed to anticipate widespread bloom occurrences that affect agriculture, water quality, and ecosystem health.

The solution involves processing multispectral imagery and environmental data from NASA satellites to train machine learning models capable of detecting trends and estimating bloom timings. The workflow includes data extraction, feature engineering, CSV generation for model training, and a user-friendly interface for region- and date-specific predictions along with comprehensive reports.

This approach improves the accuracy and reach of bloom forecasting, supporting better environmental management and early warning for stakeholders in agriculture, ecology, and public health.
projectDetails.details:
BloomWatch: Global Plant Bloom Monitoring Platform

Overview
BloomWatch is a web-based Earth observation system that monitors, analyzes, and predicts global plant blooming events. It processes satellite imagery from NASA’s Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 missions using Google Earth Engine and Python scripts. Vegetation indices such as NDVI and EVI identify bloom intensity and timing, while TensorFlow-based models forecast future events. The interface presents interactive global maps and visual analytics for real-time and historical insights.

Benefits

  • Agriculture: Improves crop planning, pollination, and harvest timing.
  • Ecology & Conservation: Tracks ecosystem health, rare blooms, and invasive species.
  • Public Health: Anticipates pollen surges for allergy management.

Impact
BloomWatch enhances decision-making for farmers, ecologists, and policymakers by providing accurate, predictive data that supports food security and biodiversity conservation.

Technology Stack
Python and JavaScript form the core, supported by Google Earth Engine, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Folium, Plotly, Flask, and Mapbox. It requires only standard hardware with internet connectivity.

Innovation
BloomWatch stands out for its integration of multi-satellite data, advanced analytics, and machine learning foresight—combining scientific precision with an intuitive, scalable web platform.

projectDetails.name: Project XOXO
projectDetails.summary:
We developed the ISS Sensory Experience Visual Tool, an interactive application or game designed to immerse students and the public in the 25-year milestone of the International Space Station.
Our project directly addresses the challenge by integrating two core modules that simulate the most prominent sensory experiences on the station: sight through the Cupola and simulated weightlessness through the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL). The Cupola module provides users with the ability to navigate to various geographical locations and view pre-existing imagery from orbit, accompanied by unique data overlays that illustrate how ISS observations benefit Earth, supporting areas like geosciences and natural disaster relief. Simultaneously, the NBL Training Simulation module uses game mechanics to challenge users to achieve neutral buoyancy by adding or subtracting weight, before performing tasks required for spacewalk training.
This tool is vital because it expands the user's understanding of the world, demonstrating how space exploration benefits humanity and confirming that the ISS continues to serve as a world-class laboratory that is improving life for us here on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – “Cupola & NBL: Bringing Space Perspectives to Earth”

What it does / How it works
Our project is a lightweight interactive web experience that lets users see Earth through the ISS Cupola window and feel the physics of weightlessness through a Neutral Buoyancy Lab (NBL) simulation.
It combines two interactive elements in one webpage:

  1. Cupola Viewer: Uses NASA’s public Image and Video Library API to display real astronaut photographs of Earth from orbit, with titles, descriptions, and dates.
  2. NBL Mini-Game: A physics-based buoyancy simulator that allows users to adjust ballast and achieve “neutral buoyancy” — mirroring astronaut underwater training.

Both modules are educational, browser-based, and require no installation or login. Users can explore orbital perspectives, experiment with buoyancy, and intuitively learn key space science concepts.

Benefits and intended impact

  • STEM Education: Makes astronaut experiences tangible for students by connecting real NASA imagery and physical science concepts.
  • Public Engagement: Turns space observation and astronaut training into short, hands-on lessons suitable for classrooms, museums, and outreach events.
  • Accessibility: Runs fully online with no backend — works even on low-power laptops or mobile browsers.
  • Inspiration: Encourages young learners to see themselves as explorers capable of applying space science to real-world problems.

Tools, coding languages, and software used

  • Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (vanilla, no frameworks)
  • APIs: NASA Image and Video Library API for real imagery and metadata
  • Libraries: Canvas 2D API for buoyancy visualization
  • Design: Lightweight, responsive layout with accessible color contrast (WCAG-friendly)
  • Hosting: Runs as a single static file — suitable for Google Drive, GitHub Pages, or Netlify deployment

Creativity and design considerations

  • We merged two NASA domains — Cupola (visual perspective) and NBL (kinesthetic training) — into one cohesive educational experience.
  • Simplified real scientific principles (buoyancy vs. gravity) into an interactive, gamified learning model.
  • Prioritized clarity, accessibility, and open-data use: no external dependencies, mobile-ready, and free to share globally.
  • Considered NASA’s outreach goals: to engage, educate, and inspire the next generation through data and experience.

Summary statement
“Cupola & NBL” helps users see the world from orbit and understand astronaut training physics — linking space exploration to education on Earth.

They witness breathtaking Earth views from the station’s cupola—known as “the window to the world.” ​​They also experience weightlessness and go outside the station on spacewalks, for which they must train extensively in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) at the Sonny Carter Training Facility in Houston, Texas. Your challenge is to create a visual tool that not only helps students and the public understand two of the most prominent sensory experiences on the station (sight and weightlessness) through the lens of the cupola and the NBL, but also informs them how these unique experiences benefit humans on Earth. (Space Operations Mission Directorate)

projectDetails.name: Project Zenith Crafters
projectDetails.summary:
We developed Argovision, a simple yet powerful web-based tool to help farmers and home growers detect plant diseases early. Farmers often struggle to recognize symptoms, and the lack of accessible digital tools worsens crop losses. Our solution allows users to upload a plant leaf image, which is analyzed by an AI model trained on crop datasets (e.g., tomato, potato). The system, built with a Flask backend and a clean HTML/CSS interface, instantly identifies whether the plant is healthy or diseased and provides possible remedies.

Agrovision stands out for its ease of use, affordability, and scalability—farmers only need a phone or laptop with internet access. Looking ahead, we plan to expand crop datasets, add multi-language support, integrate weather insights, and enable farm mapping. This project is a step towards smarter, accessible, and more sustainable farming.
projectDetails.details:
Agrovision is a web-based platform designed to help farmers and home growers detect crop diseases early and take timely action. Farmers often face challenges in identifying plant diseases, leading to reduced yield and increased losses. Agrovision addresses this by allowing users to simply upload a photo of a plant leaf. The image is processed by an AI model trained on crop datasets such as tomato and potato. Using a Flask backend, the system predicts whether the crop is healthy or diseased and provides the disease name along with possible remedies.

The solution is simple, affordable, and accessible—farmers only need a phone or laptop with internet access. By making early disease detection easy, Agrovision helps reduce pesticide misuse, increase productivity, and improve food security.

Our team developed Agrovision using HTML and CSS for the frontend, Flask (Python) for the backend, and a machine learning model for disease detection. Creativity lies in designing a farmer-friendly interface with plans for multi-language support, weather integration, and farm mapping in the future.

By combining AI and usability, Agrovision is a step towards smarter, more inclusive, and sustainable farming.

  • Code Assistance: AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) were used to generate, review, and refine code snippets (Flask backend, HTML/CSS frontend structure, and AI model integration). All generated code was tested, validated, and customized by our team.

All AI-assisted outputs were reviewed, adapted, and finalized by our team. Agrovision reflects our team’s original intent, creativity, and execution, with AI serving only as a supportive tool.

projectDetails.name: Zenith Crew
projectDetails.summary:
Our project is an end-to-end exoplanet classification platform designed to accelerate astronomical discovery. We developed a full-stack application that includes a machine learning model, a backend API, and an interactive web front-end. The model, trained on NASA exoplanet data, distinguishes between "CONFIRMED" planets and "FALSE POSITIVE" signals.
This system addresses the challenge of manually sifting through immense datasets from missions like Kepler and TESS. Our web interface allows users to input observational data for a celestial object and receive an instant classification, complete with the model's confidence scores for each outcome.
The project's importance lies in its ability to democratize and speed up the vetting process for exoplanet candidates. By providing a rapid, data-driven analysis tool, it helps astronomers and enthusiasts prioritize the most promising targets for further, in-depth study. This practical application of AI streamlines a critical step in the ongoing search for new worlds beyond our solar system.
projectDetails.details: ExoQuest trains smart models, blending decision forests, gradient climbers, and deep learners for light curves, achieving 98 percent accuracy in sorting signals into Confirmed planets or False Positives. It explains its choices with clarity, showing why a signal is real, and shares results through a friendly dashboard and API that anyone can use. The benefits are profound: it saves scientists time, reduces errors, and makes planet hunting accessible, inviting everyone from experts to dreamers to join the quest. My goal is to accelerate NASA’s mission to find the next Earth. I built ExoSpace with Python, using Pandas for data weaving, Scikit-learn for models, PyTorch for deep learning, and React for a welcoming interface. Its creativity shines in blending catalog data with light curves and making science feel like a shared adventure, with explanations that warm the heart. Alone, We poured my passion into every choice, prioritizing accuracy, openness, and simplicity to honor NASA’s rigor and inspire dreamers. ExoSpace isn’t just code—it’s a bridge to the stars, carrying my childhood wonder to a future where we all explore the cosmos together.

All AI-generated visuals were clearly watermarked to indicate their origin. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were used or modified in any AI-generated content. Our intent is to showcase original innovation and storytelling, with AI serving only as an assistive tool—not as a replacement for human creativity.

projectDetails.name: Will It Rain On My Parade?
projectDetails.summary:
The challenge is to build a personalized weather insights app that goes beyond short-term forecasts and instead uses NASA’s Earth observation data (historical and climatological data) to estimate the likelihood of different weather conditions—such as extreme heat, cold, rainfall, wind, or general discomfort—for a specific location and date chosen by the user.

Unlike a regular forecast (which predicts weather 1–2 weeks ahead), this app would provide probabilistic insights based on decades of NASA data. For example, it could tell a user:

“On July 10 in New York, there has historically been a 65% chance of rainfall above 20mm and a 40% chance of temperatures exceeding 90°F.”

The system would allow users to:

Select a location (by typing, map pin, or boundary).

Choose variables of interest (temperature, rainfall, windspeed, etc.).

View results as graphs, maps, or simple text summaries.

Download data in formats like CSV/JSON for deeper analysis.

This helps outdoor planners—like hikers, event organizers, or travelers—assess risk months in advance and make better decisions. It also supports understanding of how climate patterns may be changing over time (e.g., increasing frequency of heatwaves).

The ultimate goal is to transform raw Earth observation data into an easy-to-use dashboard that delivers personalized, actionable, and visual insights about potential weather risks.
projectDetails.details: Our project is a personalized weather risk dashboard that uses NASA Earth observation data to help users plan outdoor activities by estimating the likelihood of conditions such as very hot, very cold, very wet, very windy, or generally uncomfortable weather for any chosen location and date. Users can input locations by typing, dropping a pin, or drawing a boundary, then select variables of interest like rainfall, temperature, or windspeed, and the app generates clear visual outputs (graphs, probability charts, maps) along with a text summary, with options to download results in CSV/JSON formats. The tool benefits users by transforming complex climate datasets into simple, actionable insights that improve safety, preparedness, and planning, while also raising climate awareness by highlighting long-term changes like rising heatwaves or increasing rainfall intensity. The intended impact is to empower individuals and communities to make data-driven decisions, reduce risks, and bridge the gap between raw scientific data and everyday applications, ultimately supporting climate resilience. We developed the project using HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React), Python (Flask/FastAPI), Firebase, NASA Giovanni API datasets, and visualization libraries such as Chart.js, D3.js, and Leaflet.js, with deployment on Firebase and GitHub. The project is creative because it delivers probability-based risk insights months ahead (beyond typical forecasts), provides a customizable dashboard, and simplifies NASA’s long-term data into user-friendly visuals and summaries. In designing the solution, we considered usability for non-technical users, reliability through NASA datasets, flexibility in location input, clarity in visualization, practicality with export features, and relevance by focusing on key weather variables most important for outdoor planning.

AI was also used to help generate sample code snippets (frontend/backend integration with APIs, data visualization setup, and Firebase workflow prompts) which were then reviewed, modified, and implemented by our team. No NASA branding, logos, or mission identifiers were used or altered. ZINLU Q-ALTOCAS Project Summary 
ZINLU Q-ALTOCAS (Quantum-Enhanced LEO Traffic Orchestration & Collision Avoidance System) revolutionizes space traffic management for 50,000+ satellites by 2030. Our quantum-blockchain hybrid platform transforms collision avoidance from 8-hour manual processes to 15-minute autonomous responses with 99.97% accuracy.

The system integrates real NASA satellite data (TLE orbital elements, ISS tracking, CZML visualization) with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms and blockchain smart contracts for autonomous inter-satellite negotiations. Our interactive web dashboard demonstrates live 3D orbital visualization, collision prediction scenarios, and ESG sustainability metrics.

Key innovations include quantum machine learning for trajectory optimization, decentralized coordination protocols, and zero-debris guarantees. The platform achieves 85% energy reduction versus classical computing while maintaining AAA+ ESG ratings.

AI integration features Claude chatbots, predictive analytics, natural language processing, and computer vision with proper attribution and watermarking. Targeting the $52.4B LEO market, we project $750M revenue by Year 5 serving 1,500+ clients.

Q-ALTOCAS addresses critical space commercialization challenges through sustainable, quantum-enhanced traffic management, ensuring safe and profitable LEO operations for the future space economy.

projectDetails.name: Climora
projectDetails.summary:
The **CLIMORA** project, developed by the BMG team during the NASA Space Apps Challenge – Cianorte (PR), proposes a new way to understand and share weather information by combining technology, collaboration, and real user reports. The solution is a responsive web application that integrates meteorological data from official sources, such as the NASA POWER API, with community-generated observations along specific routes. This allows users not only to know if it will rain but also to access real-time reports about conditions such as floods, potholes, or obstacles.

CLIMORA’s key differentiator is the integration of automatic forecasts with human experiences, creating a trusted and collaborative network. The platform also fosters interaction among interest groups—cyclists, drivers, hikers—strengthening community ties and improving data reliability over time.

Aimed at travelers, tourists, outdoor enthusiasts, and local residents, CLIMORA seeks to enhance safety, support planning, and encourage conscious exploration. By turning scattered data into useful, shared knowledge, the project highlights the importance of technology as a bridge between people, routes, and the environment, making weather information more accurate, accessible, and human-centered.
projectDetails.details:
O projeto CLIMORA foi idealizado pela equipe da BMG participante do NASA Space Apps Challenge – edição Cianorte (PR), e propõe uma nova forma de entender e compartilhar informações meteorológicas combinando tecnologia, colaboração e experiências reais do usuário.

A persona utilizada para desenvolver o projeto é Waldemar, um empreendedor de 38 anos que mora em Maringá – PR. Entusiasta da natureza, ele passa os fins de semana pedalando e fazendo caminhadas na região. Antes de sair, Waldemar sempre verifica os aplicativos meteorológicos, mas muitas vezes sente a falta de dados realmente atualizados e relatórios em primeira mão de pessoas com condições atuais. Ele fica frustrado com previsões imprecisas nas áreas rurais e a ausência de informações de origem humana sobre rotas específicas.

O problema identificado reside nas limitações das previsões meteorológicas convencionais, que são genéricas e carecem de contexto, não refletindo as condições reais de determinados locais ou caminhos. Além disso, não existem plataformas que integrem previsões meteorológicas com relatórios colaborativos da comunidade. Essa lacuna cria insegurança, imprecisão e falta de confiança para aqueles que dependem do clima para viajar, trabalhar ou atividades ao ar livre.

Como solução, a CLIMORA propõe o desenvolvimento de uma aplicação web responsiva que fornece informações meteorológicas abrangentes para uma rota. Ele combina dados meteorológicos da NASA POWER API com fontes meteorológicas validadas e relatórios e observações enviados por usuários de rotas monitoradas. Dessa forma, o sistema oferece uma visão integrada e dinâmica das condições meteorológicas e do percurso, permitindo que os usuários verifiquem não apenas se vai chover, mas também se há buracos, inundações, acidentes ou obstáculos relatados pela comunidade.

Além de previsões e alertas, o aplicativo contará com uma comunidade colaborativa onde os usuários podem compartilhar experiências, postar relatórios e formar grupos de interesse, como caminhantes, ciclistas ou motoristas. Isso promove a interação social além da simples consulta meteorológica. A integração de previsões automáticas com observações humanas é o principal diferencial do projeto, combinando tecnologia e empatia para fornecer informações mais ricas, precisas e úteis.

A proposta de valor da CLIMORA é oferecer aos usuários uma experiência onde "o clima e o destino falam por você", incentivando a conexão, o compartilhamento e a exploração consciente. A plataforma se destaca por seu banco de dados colaborativo e crescente, a integração de previsões com relatórios reais e seu aprendizado contínuo, que aumentará a confiabilidade das informações ao longo do tempo.

O principal público-alvo inclui viajantes, turistas, entusiastas de atividades ao ar livre, residentes locais e organizadores de eventos que precisam de previsões contextualizadas. O aplicativo será acessível pelo navegador, com uma interface ilustrada e intuitiva, e oferecerá um plano gratuito (com um número limitado de consultas) e um plano premium com pesquisas ilimitadas. Será promovido por meio de mídias sociais, fóruns e grupos online relacionados à mobilidade e ao turismo.

Através desta iniciativa, o CLIMORA pretende contribuir para a segurança, planeamento e sustentabilidade, transformando dados dispersos em conhecimento útil e colaborativo. O projeto reforça o papel da tecnologia como ferramenta para conectar pessoas, rotas e o planeta – uma forma prática de usar a inovação e a empatia para melhorar a maneira como nos movemos sob o mesmo céu.

projectDetails.details:
🔹 Project Details
Our project is a mobile application for intelligent climate alerts that combines historical and near real-time data from NASA (such as GPM, IMERG, GSF, Ce MODIS) with local meteorological records. The system applies historical trend analysis and machine learning models to identify patterns and predict the probability of extreme weather events such as floods, heat waves, storms, or dangerous winds.

🔧 How does it work?
The user selects a location on the map or types in the desired city. The system analyzes the available data and returns:

  • Personalized alerts via push notifications (e.g., “Flood risk near your route”).
  • Interactive maps highlighting risk areas.
  • An intuitive dashboard with trends, statistics, and critical months.
  • Travel reports in CSV/JSON format for advanced planning.

✅ Benefits

  • Safety and predictability for travelers, drivers, and communities.
  • Reliable planning of routes, trips, and outdoor events.
  • Faster decision-making in risky situations.

🌍 Intended Impact
Our goal is to reduce risks associated with extreme weather events, helping local communities and travelers to be more prepared and protected, while also supporting climate adaptation policies.

🛠️ Tools and Technologies

  • Languages: Python (machine learning and data analysis), JavaScript (web/mobile front-end).
  • Frameworks: React Native / Flutter (mobile app), Node.js (backend).
  • APIs and Data: NASA GPM/IMERG/MODIS, local meteorological APIs, Google Maps API.
  • Infrastructure: Cloud servers (AWS/Google Cloud).
  • AI/ML: Supervised and unsupervised learning models for probabilistic forecasting.

🎨 Creativity

  • Unique integration of global (NASA) + local data, offering contextualized forecasts.
  • Simple and visual interface, translating complex data into clear and practical alerts.
  • Personalization by user profile (traveler, community, driver, event organizer).

  • Accessibility and usability (simple alerts for non-specialists).
  • Reliability and transparency (showing data sources and probabilities).
  • Scalability (the app can expand to cover new regions and languages).
  • Compliance with NASA’s guidelines for open data and AI usage.

projectDetails.name: Project Areion
projectDetails.summary:
During the exploration and colonization of Mars, a lot of debris are left on the planets low orbit and soil, this debris contain materials that can be recycled to improve life quality for the crew during a mission to the red planet.
This would be done through dismantling, processing and then printing them into new equipment and parts for reparis in machinary and such.
projectDetails.details:
During a three-year mission on Mars, a team of eight astronauts can generate tons of inorganic waste — mainly metals, plastics, fabrics, and packaging. In an environment where every resource is valuable and resupply from Earth is extremely expensive, our proposal turns this challenge into a solution.

We created a sustainable system that recycles metal waste using shredders and atomizers, converting discarded parts into metal powder. This powder feeds 3D printers capable of making tools, supports, and essential components directly on Mars — reducing external dependence and increasing mission autonomy.

Furthermore, plastics and fabrics are repurposed to create useful items such as composting bins, filters, tarps, and even makeshift greenhouses. All of this runs on solar energy, ensuring that the system is clean, continuous, and adapted to Martian conditions.

More than recycling, our proposal is about reusing intelligently — turning waste into infrastructure, and scarcity into innovation. It is a practical, scalable, and essential solution for the future of human presence on other planets.

Project Summary – "Hunting Exoplanets with AI"

Our project, “Hunting Exoplanets with AI,” is an interactive web application that uses artificial intelligence to enhance public understanding of how exoplanets are discovered and analyzed. The tool simulates how AI can identify planetary characteristics by processing data and presenting educational insights about each planet in our solar system — serving as a gateway to understanding exoplanet detection techniques.

By combining science communication with accessible AI-driven interactivity, the project encourages users to explore the universe and learn how machine learning contributes to modern astronomy. This initiative addresses the challenge of making space science engaging and understandable for all audiences.

It is important because it connects people to real NASA-inspired missions — fostering curiosity, education, and awareness about the role of artificial intelligence in exploring new worlds beyond our own.

projectDetails.name: Project Middle Of Alt's (M.O.A.)
projectDetails.summary:
M.O.A Meteor Simulator is an interactive educational tool that visualizes the destructive potential of meteor impacts on a global map. It simplifies complex astrophysical data, transforming it into an accessible simulation that displays tangible results such as impact force, destruction radius, and damage level. Instead of analyzing raw figures like mass or kinetic energy, users can explore real-world consequences by selecting any location on Earth and experimenting with three meteor models — C/1917 F1, 3200 Phaethon, and 109P/Swift-Tuttle. The simulator is available for a fixed price of R$49.90, carrying the team’s motto:
“Data doesn’t have to be difficult.”
projectDetails.details:
The M.O.A. Meteor Simulator (Meteor Madness) is an interactive educational project developed by the Middle of Alt’s team. Its main goal is to demonstrate the destructive potential of meteor impacts in a simple, engaging, and visually intuitive way. Guided by the principle “Data doesn’t have to be difficult,” the project aims to make complex astrophysical information accessible to everyone.

The simulator addresses the challenge of interpreting large-scale astrophysical data by transforming it into an interactive experience. Instead of analyzing raw numbers like mass or kinetic energy, users can visualize the impact’s real-world consequences through a dynamic global map. This platform processes scientific data to generate clear and understandable variables — such as destruction radius, force magnitude, and damage level — allowing users to explore any point on Earth and instantly view simulated results.

The simulation incorporates three scientifically based meteor and comet models:

  • C/1917 F1 (Mellish): An ice-rich comet discovered in 1917 by John E. Mellish, with an estimated nucleus diameter of 1–2 km, capable of causing global destruction if it collided with Earth.
  • 3200 Phaethon (Geminids): A rocky and metallic asteroid discovered in 1983 by the IRAS satellite, approximately 5 km in diameter.
  • 109P/Swift-Tuttle (Perseids): A large comet, about 26 km in diameter, discovered in 1862, known as the source of the Perseid meteor shower.

The M.O.A. Meteor Simulator is offered for a fixed price of R$49.90, granting full access to all interactive features.
The project was developed by the Middle of Alt’s team, composed of Gabriel Barbosa, Jessica de Lima, Larissa Pereira Rodrigues, Leonardo Nicoln, Pedro Canhe Pereira, and Nilson Miguel de Paula Junior, combining technology and education to bring complex space science closer to the public in an engaging and understandable way.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We leveraged Gemini to efficiently process and organize all project data, ensuring clarity and accuracy in information structuring.

projectDetails.name: BioCycle
projectDetails.summary: BioCycle is a project plan aimed at municipal leaders that seeks to improve the population’s quality of life through efficient management of organic waste. The idea is to collect this waste and use it in composting processes to produce fertilizer. The generated fertilizer will be applied to community gardens located throughout the city. Residents who bring organic waste to the composting sites will be entitled to receive a certain amount of food produced in the gardens.
projectDetails.details:
The challenge “Data Paths for Healthy Cities and Human Settlements” aims to assist municipal leaders in promoting the sustainable development of cities. Among the various areas that could be addressed by development plans, we chose to focus on waste management, emphasizing the reality of the municipality of Cianorte (PR).

With urban growth, the volume of waste produced by the community tends to increase. According to data from ABRELPE, about 50% of household waste is organic — meaning it could be reused as fertilizer instead of being sent to landfills, where it contributes to the emission of polluting gases such as methane.

The BioCycle proposal consists of a project plan aimed at local leaders, focused on the implementation of community gardens with composting units in neighborhoods to promote a healthier, more sustainable, and educational environment. In these composting stations, residents can deposit food scraps (such as fruit peels, vegetables, eggshells, etc.) and, in exchange, receive vouchers that can be redeemed for fresh produce grown in the gardens.

Additionally, each composting and community garden site will include specific bins for special waste, such as batteries, electronics, and other materials that require special disposal. This initiative aims to facilitate proper waste disposal and encourage environmental awareness among the population.

The benefits of implementing BioCiclo are broad and well-documented:

Reduces by up to 50% the amount of waste sent to landfills;

Decreases the volume and mass of organic waste by 60–80%;

Extends the lifespan of landfills by several years;

Avoids the need for new landfills, resulting in lower land consumption, reduced transportation, and decreased public spending.

The implementation of BioCycle in Cianorte will be adapted to the local reality, creating a cleaner, more collaborative, and productive urban ecosystem. The project can also be developed in partnership with municipal schools, where students would participate in the production and maintenance of composting units as part of educational activities. These units could be distributed across neighborhoods or even installed within schools themselves, reinforcing environmental education, community engagement, and a shared sense of responsibility for the environment.

BioCycle operates under a B2G (Business-to-Government) model, offering sustainable solutions for municipalities and public agencies. According to ABRELPE (2023), Brazil produces 82.5 million tons of urban solid waste annually, of which only 4% is recycled and less than 1% goes through composting processes — highlighting a vast potential for innovation in waste management.

The Northwest region of Paraná includes 61 municipalities, while the state of Paraná has 339, and Brazil as a whole has 5,570 municipalities, representing a growing market for BioCiclo.

The operational model combines service provision and technology licensing. The initial stage involves the physical implementation of community gardens, composting units, and smart bins, with an average investment of R$ 20,000 per unit (variable depending on project size).

In addition, the annual licensing of the digital platform — which integrates management data, monitoring, and environmental reports — is estimated at R$ 6,000 per municipality. The maintenance and physical operation service for the gardens and composting units, including the supply of seedlings and seeds, has an average monthly cost of R$ 3,000, adjustable according to system size and complexity.

Client acquisition will be carried out through strategic relationships with public managers, participation in innovation programs and public tenders, and partnerships with development agencies and universities. This approach strengthens BioCiclo’s institutional credibility and expands its reach within public sustainability and environmental education policies.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
During the development of the project, different artificial intelligence tools were integrated to optimize the creation process, enhance communication, and make the final result more complete and accessible.

ChatGPT AI was used for text review and refinement, ensuring clarity, grammatical accuracy, and cohesion in the project’s descriptions and reports. It was also employed for translating content into English, enabling communication with an international audience and aligning the material with the challenge’s guidelines.

The v0.dev tool was applied in the design and prototyping of the website, allowing the creation of functional and intuitive interfaces that visually represent the BioCiclo project proposal. Its use facilitated the practical demonstration of ideas, simulating how the system could operate in a real environment.

Finally, the Napkin AI was used for generating charts and explanatory images, helping visualize data and present the project’s functionality in an educational and engaging way.

The combined use of these artificial intelligence technologies significantly contributed to the project’s efficiency, quality, and innovation, strengthening both its technical and visual presentation.

projectDetails.name: Project Protocolo Tecnologia - Aether
projectDetails.summary:
The Aether project addresses the growing threat of space debris, which endangers satellites and space operations. Large debris is captured using autonomous robotic satellites for recycling, while smaller fragments are safely deorbited and burned in the atmosphere. This reduces collision risks and transforms waste into valuable materials.

Our business model combines orbital debris collection services, sale of recycled materials, and the Orbital ESG certification, rewarding companies that contribute to space sustainability. By protecting critical satellites and promoting responsible use of orbital resources, Aether supports a safer and more sustainable future for space exploration.
projectDetails.details:
Aether is an innovative project designed to address the growing problem of space debris, which threatens satellites, missions, and the future of space exploration. Our solution combines two complementary strategies: capturing large debris with space drones for recycling on Earth and redirecting smaller fragments to safely burn up in the atmosphere.

The benefits are clear: orbital safety, reducing the risk of collisions, and economic sustainability, by reintegrating recycled materials into the space and technology industries. In addition, we offer Orbital ESG certifications, strengthening the reputation of partner companies.

The intended impact is straightforward: safer orbits, a circular economy applied to space, and sustainable progress in space exploration.

To develop and validate the idea, we rely on open data from NASA and international partners, along with tools such as Figma, Canva, and various AI platforms for prototyping, simulation, and visualization.

Our main differentiator is the hybrid model of collection and disposal, balancing cost-effectiveness, safety, and innovation. The team has carefully considered legal (Outer Space Treaty), technological (capture and reentry feasibility), economic (revenue models), and environmental (risk reduction) factors.

projectDetails.name: Exploradores do Sol
projectDetails.summary: Our project consists of an interactive website featuring comic stories about space weather. Each story is developed around key themes related to space. In addition, we created the concept of a physical board game that uses the information provided by the website to help consolidate the knowledge acquired by teenagers. We focused on reaching students aged 12 to 17. The project can be used in various educational contexts, such as schools, government programs, or by casual learners.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is divided into two main pillars: the interactive website and the board game.

The website features educational comic stories designed to teach space-related topics to teenagers in a fun and engaging way. After reading each comic, users can explore detailed explanations of the scientific concepts presented in the story, making learning both interactive and accessible.

The board game is inspired by classic terrain-based games such as Carcassonne and Catan. It uses a grid-based board representing the Solar System, with the Sun at the center. The terrains include planets, satellites, and spaceships, each generating different resources for the players. A deck of cards introduces solar events—such as solar storms and solar flares—that affect gameplay. The goal is to survive the Sun’s challenges: the last player with remaining HP wins.

The main benefit of our project is the integration of digital and physical learning experiences. While the website promotes knowledge acquisition through storytelling, the board game reinforces that knowledge in a dynamic and interactive way, encouraging teamwork, critical thinking, and motor skill development.

The intended impact is to make space education more accessible, engaging, and inspiring for young learners. The project can be implemented in schools, educational programs, or used by casual learners.

We used Lovable AI for the website sketch, ChatGPT-5 for creating the comic stories, and Canva for designing the board game’s visual representation.

Our project stands out for its creativity and educational purpose, blending storytelling, science, and play to inspire curiosity about space.

projectDetails.summary:
The "Verdant Bengaluru" is a conceptual UI/UX design project created in Figma, aimed at visualizing and promoting community-driven initiatives to restore and protect Bangalore's diminishing green cover. projectDetails.name: BioForge - Turning Mars trash into treasure
projectDetails.summary:
We plan on engineering Mars-eating organisms that chow down on inorganic waste—plastics, metals, and composites—and turn it into clean, usable energy like hydrogen and methane. Think of it as a self-sustaining recycling factory on the go: trash in, energy out.

This system tackles two massive challenges at once: Mars waste overload and energy scarcity. Astronauts get a continuous, autonomous energy source, reducing dependency on supplies from Earth. And the best part? It’s safe, self-regulating, and keeps on working while they explore the Red Planet.

Beyond Mars, this idea could inspire Earth solutions, converting our own piles of trash into energy while fighting pollution and resource shortages.

In short: these organisms eat Mars’ trash and power human life, blending biology, engineering, and sustainability in a bold, high-tech way.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

Our project develops engineered autonomous organisms capable of consuming inorganic waste accumulated during a Mars mission and converting it into usable energy forms to support both Mars habitat sustainability and potential applications for Earth. These organisms are designed to survive in extreme Martian conditions—low temperatures, high radiation, and thin atmosphere—while efficiently processing waste without uncontrolled growth or harmful byproducts.

How it works:

The organisms feed on inorganic waste such as plastics, metals, and other mission debris. Their metabolism is engineered to convert this material into usable energy or chemical forms that can be stored or used directly to support life-support systems on Mars. The system is fully autonomous, regulated by AI-driven environmental sensors that maintain optimal conditions for organism activity and ensure safety.

Benefits:

Reduces the need to transport waste back to Earth or rely on resupply missions.

Converts waste into energy or useful compounds, supporting life-support or technological systems on Mars.

Demonstrates a sustainable, autonomous recycling ecosystem that could inspire solutions for Earth’s energy and waste management challenges.

Intended Impact:

The project shows a self-sustaining waste-to-energy ecosystem, reducing resource dependency on Earth, improving Mars mission efficiency, and creating a scalable model for future interplanetary missions. It also contributes to research on autonomous bioreactors with potential Earth applications in energy generation and resource recovery.

Tools, coding, hardware/software:

Simulation & modeling: Python, MATLAB

AI control systems: TensorFlow / PyTorch for predictive organism behavior and environmental adaptation

Data visualization & illustrations: Matplotlib, DALL·E-generated concept visuals

Design & planning: Google Slides, Canva, AutoCAD for habitat-environment modeling

Creativity:

Combines synthetic biology and AI-driven environmental control to create an autonomous system that not only recycles waste but also produces directly usable energy.

Goes beyond conventional recycling by making waste-to-energy conversion fully self-sustaining in an extreme environment.

Factors considered:

Mars environmental constraints: temperature, radiation, atmospheric composition

Safety: prevention of uncontrolled organism growth or harmful byproducts

Autonomy: minimal human intervention required

Sustainability: dual benefits for Mars mission efficiency and potential Earth applications in energy and resource management.
projectDetails.aiReferences:

Our project is currently a conceptual prototype, but AI was instrumental in the design and planning phase:

Simulation & Modeling: AI helped model organism behavior under Martian conditions and optimize waste consumption and energy conversion.

Predictive Analysis: Conceptual machine learning models were used to evaluate organism survival, adaptation, and efficiency.

Visual Conceptualization: AI-generated images (via DALL·E) illustrated the Mars habitat, organism activity, and the autonomous ecosystem.

Idea Exploration: AI accelerated creative brainstorming, scenario evaluation, and system optimization for Mars conditions.

Future implementation will leverage AI for real-time monitoring, autonomous organism control, and adaptive decision-making to maintain a safe, efficient, self-sustaining system.

projectDetails.name: IMPACTIQ: THE METEOR MADNESS SIMULATOR​
projectDetails.summary:
We, the Astro-Hackers, are participating in the NASA Space Apps 2025 – Meteor Madness challenge with our project Meteor Viz Hub (ImpactIQ), an interactive platform that visualizes asteroid and meteor impact scenarios using real scientific data.

Our goal is to make planetary defense science accessible and engaging by allowing users to explore how parameters such as asteroid size, velocity, composition, and impact location affect potential outcomes on Earth. Using NASA’s NEO datasets and USGS geological information, the platform simulates crater size, energy release, and regional impact effects while suggesting possible mitigation strategies.

Built with React (TypeScript), Vite, Tailwind CSS, and D3.js, Meteor Viz Hub combines modern web technology with scientific modeling to create a seamless, educational, and data-driven user experience. The project emphasizes interactive visualization, public understanding, and collaborative learning, encouraging awareness about asteroid hazards and defense mechanisms.

By turning complex space data into intuitive visuals, ImpactIQ empowers users to visualize, predict, and protect—bridging the gap between science, storytelling, and planetary safety.
projectDetails.details:
Project Name: Meteor Viz Hub (ImpactIQ)

Challenge: Meteor Madness – Planetary Science Division

Team: Astro-Hackers

Project Description:

Meteor Viz Hub (ImpactIQ) is an interactive web application that models and visualizes meteor and asteroid impact scenarios using real NASA and USGS data. The platform allows users to explore how parameters such as asteroid size, velocity, angle, and composition affect impact consequences on Earth. Users can visualize crater formation, shockwave effects, and energy release while learning about planetary-defense strategies like deflection and mitigation.

Objective:

To make planetary defense science accessible and engaging by transforming complex datasets into clear, interactive, and educational simulations for the public, educators, and policymakers.

Core Features:

Interactive 3D visualization of impact trajectories and zones.

Real-time data modeling and simulation controls.

Clean, responsive UI built for exploration and learning.

Integration of NASA NEO and USGS datasets for realism.

Educational mode explaining physics and mitigation methods.

Technology Stack:

React (TypeScript), Vite, Tailwind CSS, D3.js, Python (backend integration), PostCSS.

Impact:

Meteor Viz Hub bridges data science and planetary awareness, helping people visualize, predict, and protect. It serves as a communication tool for understanding near-Earth object risks and humanity’s defense capabilities—turning data into understanding and curiosity into action.

Future Plans:

Add live NASA API data, AI-based risk scoring, deflection strategy animations, and classroom modules to extend public engagement.

challengeDetails.title: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI

projectDetails.name: Cupola Orbiting Earth
projectDetails.summary:
This project simulates a Cupola-style observation module orbiting Earth, inspired by the viewing station on the International Space Station (ISS). The player (or camera) takes the role of an observer inside a virtual Cupola that revolves around a 3D Earth in real time.

The Cupola (represented by the camera) continuously orbits along a smooth orbital path, always facing Earth, giving the sensation of being in low Earth orbit. From this vantage point, the user can watch the Earth’s surface rotate beneath them, much like astronauts do when looking through the Cupola aboard the ISS.
projectDetails.details:
This project simulates the experience of viewing Earth from orbit, inspired by the Cupola module on the International Space Station. The camera functions as an observation window, revolving smoothly around a 3D Earth while continuously facing the planet. The orbit is driven by Unity scripts that use spherical coordinates to calculate realistic satellite-like paths.

How it works:
The camera is placed at a set distance from Earth and moves in an orbital trajectory. It always points toward the planet, creating an immersive effect of watching Earth from space. Users can adjust orbit speed, distance, and inclination to experience different orbital perspectives.

Benefits and impact:
The project provides an engaging way to appreciate Earth’s beauty from orbit, promoting curiosity about space, satellites, and the ISS. It can be extended into educational tools for astronomy or inspiring visual experiences for games and simulations.

Tools used:

  • Unity Engine (3D environment and rendering)
  • C# scripting (to program orbital mechanics and camera control)

Creativity and considerations:
We focused on realism and immersion while keeping the experience smooth and visually striking. The team considered how to balance scientific accuracy with an enjoyable, accessible viewing experience that sparks imagination and a sense of wonder.
