projectDetails.details:
🌌 AstroBuddy – Your Personal AI Space Companion 🚀

By Team BeastMode | Built with React, TypeScript & Supabase

Welcome to AstroBuddy, an AI-powered space companion developed during our first-ever hackathon – the NASA Space Apps Challenge 🌍🛰️

Crafted by Team BeastMode, AstroBuddy is a web-based application designed to make space exploration fun, accessible, and interactive for everyone. Whether you're a curious student, an astronomy enthusiast, or just someone who looks up at the stars and wonders — AstroBuddy is here to guide you through the cosmos.

🛠️ Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React + TypeScript ⚛️ (self & help of ai) ~ VS Code
  • Backend / Realtime DB: Supabase (hosted backend postgres database, real time sync)
  • APIs: NASA Open APIs, OpenAI for AI chatbot & quiz generation
  • Other Tools: Three.js (for 3D solar system), CSS Modules for styling, figma ai, loveable ai, replit

✨ Key Features

  • 🤖 AstroBuddy Chatbot – Ask space-related questions and get intelligent answers in real-time using OpenAI and live NASA data.
  • 🌌 3D Interactive Solar System – Explore planets and their stats in a beautifully rendered 3D model.
  • ❓ Quiz Generator – Test your space knowledge with dynamically generated quizzes powered by AI.
  • ☁️ Live NASA Data Integration – Pulls real-time data like Astronomy Picture of the Day, ISS location, and Mars weather.
  • ♿ Accessible, Responsive UI – Built with a user-first mindset, designed to work across all desktop devices.

🎯 Purpose & Inspiration

This project was born out of passion, curiosity, and the excitement of building something meaningful in just 3 hours. It’s our take on what knowledge and skills applied, how AI and open space data can empower people to learn and interact with the universe like never before.

We believe learning should be interactive, data-driven, and fun — and that’s exactly what AstroBuddy aims to be.

🚧 Status

This is a hackathon (Project) and a work-in-progress. We plan to polish and improve it after the event based on feedback and future goals.

🙌 Credits

  • 🚀 Project by Team BeastMode
  • 💡 Submitted for NASA Space Apps Challenge
  • ❤️ Built with love, coffee, and a lot of debugging

Uniqueness/Project creativity

  • Your uniqueness compared to other projects lies in:
  1. All-in-one ecosystem – Instead of focusing on just a chatbot, or just a 3D solar system, AstroBuddy combines AI conversation, real-time NASA data, quizzes, and 3D visualization into one seamless platform.
  2. AI-powered learning – The quiz generator powered by OpenAI isn’t just static questions—it adapts, educates, and explains answers with fun facts, making learning personalized.
  3. Accessibility-first design – While many hackathon projects skip WCAG compliance, you’ve included screen-reader support, keyboard navigation, and mobile-first UI for inclusivity.
  4. Engagement focus – Gamification (quizzes + scores), interactive 3D models, and live space weather make it more than a utility—it’s an experience.

Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known

Accessibility + UI:

projectDetails.details:
Vision

Luma A circadian health app that transforms NASA’s space sleep science into daily guidance for everyone on Earth.

The Problem

Over 60% of people worldwide suffer from poor sleep, fatigue, and irregular routines.

Misaligned circadian rhythms → reduced focus, health issues, and stress.

Astronauts face extreme circadian disruption (16 sunsets/day).

NASA’s research exists but is not accessible to the public in actionable form.

The Solution

Luma makes NASA science actionable for everyday life.

Personalized Circadian Coaching: Align sleep & wake times with natural light cycles using NASA solar & lunar data.

Behavioral Nudges: Timely guidance on sunlight, moonlight, meals, and meditation.

Adaptive Feedback: Tracks sleep, evaluates circadian alignment, and adjusts suggestions to optimize energy and health.

Engaging NASA Rewards: Users earn space knowledge, ISS insights, and Earth science facts by following healthy routines.

Science that keeps astronauts performing in orbit now empowers people to live healthier, more energized lives on Earth.

App Workflow

1️⃣ Set Your Space Schedule & Location – User enters location, bedtime, and wake time for personalized guidance.

2️⃣ NASA-Powered Guidance – Fetches sunlight, moonlight, and solar data specific to location.

3️⃣ Offline Smart Alarms – Wake up with NASA space sounds + motivational messages:

“Good morning! Astronauts wake at the same time daily — you’re on track!”

4️⃣ Morning Check-In – Record mood, energy, and sleep quality in 3 taps.

5️⃣ Daily Nudges – Push notifications for sunlight, moonlight, and meditation breaks.

6️⃣ Circadian Reports – Visual insights, sleep efficiency, and recommended adjustments.

7️⃣ NASA Rewards – Unlock space facts, ISS stories, and Earth science insights.

Key Features

Offline Smart Alarms — reliable anytime, anywhere.

NASA Space Sound Library — unique wake-up experience.

Dynamic Light Nudges — location-based notifications for sunlight & moonlight exposure.

Interactive Morning Check-Ins — feed adaptive recommendations.

Personalized Circadian Reports — visual score & actionable insights.

NASA Rewards System — learn about space, ISS routines, and Earth science.

Lifestyle Guidance Tools — meditation prompts, meal timing suggestions, and activity nudges.

Adaptive AI Suggestions — learns patterns to refine sleep/wake guidance and lifestyle recommendations.

Technical Architecture & Data

Data Sources & Usage:

NASA POWER API → sunlight, daylight cycles → plan alarms & light nudges.

NASA JPL Horizons → moon phases → optimize bedtime & relaxation routines.

NASA Sound Library → offline alarm tones.

NASA Open Data Portal → unlockable rewards (space facts, Earth science insights)

Stack: - Frontend : Flutter/React Native

- Backend : Firebase +offline DB

- AI : adapative lifestyle recommendations

Impact & Future

Global Public Health Impact – Better sleep, improved focus, mental clarity, energy, and overall wellness. NASA Legacy in Your Hands – Every user experiences astronaut-grade circadian science.

projectDetails.name: Project Blue Planet Coders
projectDetails.summary:
Our project focuses on NASA’s Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP), a mission designed to study the heliosphere, the protective bubble around our solar system that shields Earth from harmful cosmic radiation. We developed a comprehensive 7-slide presentation that explains IMAP’s mission, launch, orbit, scientific objectives, instruments, global collaboration, and its significance for space exploration.

By visualizing IMAP’s instruments and mapping techniques, our project addresses the challenge of making complex space science accessible and understandable to students, scientists, and the public. It highlights how IMAP provides real-time space weather data, aids in astronaut safety for Moon and Mars missions, and advances our understanding of cosmic particle acceleration.

This project is important because it communicates the critical role of IMAP in protecting Earth, supporting future deep-space exploration, and fostering global scientific collaboration. By combining detailed information with engaging visuals, our presentation ensures that the impact of IMAP is clear, inspiring, and educational for a wide audience.
projectDetails.details:
How it works:
The presentation uses detailed narration, captions, and 3D visuals to illustrate how IMAP detects energetic neutral atoms, measures solar wind particles, observes magnetic fields, and maps the heliosphere’s boundary in 3D. It visualizes IMAP’s instruments, particle flows, and data transmission in an interactive and engaging way.

Benefits:

  • Educates the public about space science and heliophysics.
  • Highlights IMAP’s role in protecting Earth and astronauts from cosmic radiation.
  • Demonstrates the mission’s contribution to space weather forecasting, deep space exploration, and global scientific collaboration.

Intended Impact:

  • Inspire students and enthusiasts about heliophysics and interstellar science.
  • Provide a clear understanding of IMAP’s scientific goals, instruments, and data usage.
  • Showcase the importance of international collaboration in space exploration.

Tools & Technologies:

  • Gamma.ai for creating the interactive PPT slides.
  • InVideo.ai for 3D animation and narration storyboard planning.
  • Graphics, diagrams, and captions to make the presentation visually engaging.

Creativity:

  • Combined detailed scientific data with cinematic 3D visuals for storytelling.
  • Simplified complex concepts for a broader audience while maintaining scientific accuracy.
  • Integrated team branding and NASA Space Apps Challenge logos for professionalism.

Team Considerations:

  • Ensured scientific accuracy of IMAP mission details.
  • Designed content to be visually engaging and educational.
  • Balanced technical depth with public accessibility.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI-powered tools to create and enhance our project:

  • InVideo.ai: For generating 3D animations and narration storyboards, converting the IMAP mission script into engaging video visuals.
  • Gamma.ai: For designing and auto-generating visually appealing presentation slides from detailed content.
  • AI-driven captioning and visual suggestions: To ensure scientific concepts were represented accurately and clearly in the slides and video.

These AI tools allowed us to transform complex space science data into an accessible, interactive, and professional presentation, saving time and enhancing creativity.

projectDetails.name: Animation Celebration of terra data
projectDetails.summary: For my project, I developed a PowerPoint presentation titled “Animation Celebration of Terra Data.” The presentation focuses on celebrating and visualizing the power of Earth data through engaging animations and creative storytelling. It highlights how Terra satellite data helps scientists monitor Earth’s systems like climate, vegetation, and atmosphere to better understand environmental changes. This project addresses the challenge of making complex satellite data more accessible and appealing to the public, especially students and young learners. By combining animation and scientific insight, it transforms technical data into an educational and visually captivating experience. This is important because it bridges the gap between science and society encouraging awareness, curiosity, and appreciation for how space technology helps protect our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Animation Celebration of Terra Data, transforms NASA’s Terra satellite data into an animated storytelling experience. The aim is to make Earth observation data more engaging, understandable, and visually appealing to students and the general public. We created a PowerPoint-based animation that showcases how Terra data helps track environmental changes such as temperature shifts, forest cover loss, and air quality patterns.

The project addresses the challenge of scientific communication how to make complex satellite information accessible to everyone. By using creative animation, we bridge the gap between data and understanding, turning numbers and graphs into visual stories about our planet’s health.

We used PowerPoint, Canva, and NASA Earthdata resources to develop the project. These tools allowed us to design animations, infographics, and data visuals. The creative aspect lies in blending art, design, and science to raise environmental awareness and inspire action for a sustainable future.
projectDetails.aiReferences: I used AI tools such as ChatGPT to help with idea generation, content refinement, and summarizing complex concepts about Terra satellite data in a more engaging way. Canva’s AI-based design suggestions were also used to improve the visual presentation and animation flow. These tools helped make the project more creative, clear, and visually appealing, while I ensured that all content remained original and accurate to NASA’s data sources.

projectDetails.name: Project CODE ERROR
projectDetails.summary:
Asteroid Alert: NASA Space Apps Project
The Asteroid Alert is a beginner-friendly web dashboard for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, tracking near-Earth asteroids using NASA's free NEO API. It displays the next 7 days' close approaches in a responsive Bootstrap table—showing name, date, distance (km), size, and hazard status—with a Chart.js bar chart visualizing distances (color-coded for hazards). If no threats, it reassures "Earth is safe!" Built in under 8 hours with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript (no backend), it fetches data via fetch() and handles errors gracefully. Demo via browser or GitHub Pages; uses DEMO_KEY for API (upgrade for production).
projectDetails.details: What it does/how it works: Asteroid Alert is a simple, web-based dashboard that fetches real-time data from NASA's Near-Earth Object (NEO) API to display upcoming asteroid close approaches to Earth over the next 7 days. Users open the index.html file in a browser, where vanilla JavaScript uses fetch() to query the API (e.g., with DEMO_KEY), processes the JSON response, and populates a responsive Bootstrap table with details like asteroid name, close approach date, distance (in km), estimated size (in km), and hazard status (badges: red for "Yes", green for "No"). A Chart.js bar chart visualizes distances over time, color-coded by hazard level. If no asteroids are detected, it displays "Earth is safe!" for reassurance. No backend or installs needed—runs locally or on GitHub Pages.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Benefits and intended impact: It democratizes access to NASA's open data, raising public awareness of planetary defense without requiring technical expertise. Benefits include educational value (e.g., STEM learning on space threats), real-time monitoring (tracks 10-50 asteroids/week), and promotion of citizen science. The impact is to empower individuals to engage with space exploration, fostering a proactive mindset toward NEO risks (e.g., low-probability impacts like 1 in 300,000). It aligns with "Space for Earth" themes, potentially inspiring community alerts or policy discussions on asteroid detection.

Tools, coding languages, hardware/software used: Built with HTML (structure), CSS (dark space-themed styling: black background, blue accents), and vanilla JavaScript (API logic, data processing, chart generation). Libraries: Bootstrap (responsive UI), Chart.js (visualizations). No hardware beyond a standard laptop; software: VS Code editor, Chrome browser for testing. NASA's free NEO API as data source. Total development: 4-8 hours solo.

Creativity: The creativity lies in simplifying complex NASA data into an intuitive, no-setup dashboard—transforming raw JSON into an engaging, color-coded experience (e.g., hazard badges and scaled charts for readability). Unlike dense API docs, it adds user-friendly touches like safety messages and responsive design, making planetary defense feel accessible and fun, like a "space weather" app.

Team factors considered: As a solo developer, factors included time constraints (quick prototype for challenge), accessibility (mobile-friendly, no logins), and ethical use of public data (attributing NASA fully). Prioritized open-source sharing (GitHub) for collaboration, error handling for unreliable API loads, and educational focus over advanced features to maximize impact within scope.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

N/A. The core project code, dashboard, and visuals (screenshots from manual browser testing) were developed manually using standard web tools. AI was not used for code generation, data processing, images, videos, or audio in the project itself. Planning documents (e.g., PPT outlines) were created with human input only.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmic trio
projectDetails.summary:
The AI Frontier: Real-Time Space Weather Defense

This presentation outlines NASA's critical strategy for mitigating the existential threat posed by solar activity to our technological infrastructure and deep space exploration endeavors. Our dependence on orbiting assets (GPS, communications) and global power grids necessitates a paradigm shift from historical data modeling to real-time, predictive intelligence.

The core of this strategy is the application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, exemplified by the Surya Heliophysics Foundation Model—a collaboration with industry partners like IBM. Trained on petabytes of high-resolution data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Surya acts as a force multiplier, achieving a 16% improvement in solar flare prediction accuracy and pioneering the generation of visual forecasts with up to two hours of lead time.

This advanced capability moves us toward realizing a "Digital Twin" of the Sun, transforming complex data into immediate, actionable, and visual intelligence. This capability is not just about protecting technology; it is a matter of life and death for future human exploration. For astronauts on missions to the Moon and Mars, accurate space weather predictions will be vital for their survival. By leveraging AI, NASA is building the next generation of space defense, securing not only our assets on Earth but also our place as a space faring nation.
projectDetails.details:
This is an excellent set of analytical questions that addresses the core technology and strategy behind the presentation outline.

Here are the answers to your questions, framed around the central project of the presentation: the AI-Driven Space Weather Forecasting System (specifically referencing the Surya Heliophysics Foundation Model) and the concept of the Digital Twin of the Sun.

1. What does it do or how does it work?

The project develops a new paradigm for space weather prediction by shifting from traditional, time-intensive physics simulations to real-time, data-driven forecasting using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).1

How it Works (The Surya Model):

  • Training Data: The core model (like NASA/IBM’s Surya) is a Foundation Model trained on massive, curated, high-resolution datasets, specifically petabytes of continuous solar observations from spacecraft like the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), spanning nearly a full solar cycle.
  • Feature Extraction: The model utilizes Deep Learning (specifically Convolutional Neural Networks, or CNNs) to analyze the raw imagery and magnetic field data.2 It autonomously learns and identifies subtle, complex pre-cursor patterns in the Sun's active regions that precede solar flares and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs).3
  • Output Generation: Unlike traditional classification models that only output a "yes/no" flare prediction, this system generates a visual prediction—a high-resolution image showing where and how the solar flare or CME is likely to occur, often with two hours of lead time.4
  • Digital Twin: This predictive capability is integrated into a Digital Twin of the Sun-Earth system (as proposed in the outline), which is a dynamic, animated, and physics-informed simulation that visualizes the threat path to Earth and orbiting assets in real-time.5

2. What benefits does it have?

The benefits are measured across three critical domains: operational efficiency, national security, and human safety.

<colgroup><col><col><col></colgroup>

Domain

Key Benefit

Metric / Detail

Operational & PredictiveIncreased Forecast Accuracy

Achieves up to a

16% improvement

in solar flare classification accuracy.

Operational & PredictiveExtended Lead Time

Provides an unprecedented

two-hour lead time

for solar flare predictions, allowing for defensive maneuvers.

National SecurityInfrastructure Protection

Enables pre-emptive actions (e.g., disconnecting power grids, switching satellites to safe mode) to protect GPS, telecommunications, and high-voltage power grids from damage.

Deep Space ExplorationAstronaut Safety

Provides critical, timely warnings of Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) events, which are vital for astronaut survival on missions to the Moon (Artemis) and Mars.

Scientific AdvancementComputational Efficiency

Generates forecasts at a fraction of the computational cost and time compared to running full physics-based models on supercomputers.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is transformative, aiming to elevate space weather forecasting from a research function to an essential, proactive space defense capability.

  • Securing Technological Civilization: The primary impact is to safeguard the technological bedrock of modern society (finance, transport, communication) against natural, high-impact events.
  • Enabling Deep Space Missions: By providing reliable, high-fidelity radiation warnings, the project directly supports the human exploration goals of the Artemis program and subsequent Mars missions.6
  • Democratizing Science: By releasing the AI models (like Surya) and the associated datasets as open-source, the project accelerates heliophysics research globally, allowing universities, startups, and international partners to build specialized applications on NASA’s foundation.
  • Developing Next-Gen Forecasting: The project creates a flexible, scalable infrastructure that can rapidly integrate data from future missions (like Parker Solar Probe and upcoming L1 monitors), ensuring that NASA maintains its preeminence in space domain awareness.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The development of a project of this scale requires a robust, high-performance, and scalable technology stack:

  • Coding Languages: Python is the primary language, given its dominance in the data science and ML ecosystem.7
    • Deep Learning Libraries: TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Keras for building, training, and deploying the deep neural networks (CNNs).
    • Data Handling: Specialized libraries for processing massive geospatial/heliophysics data, often integrated with tools like IBM’s TerraTorch for foundation models.
    • Deployment: Open-source platforms like Hugging Face and GitHub are used to share the final model and code with the global scientific community.8
    • High-Performance Computing (HPC): Training the model on petabytes of data requires extensive use of supercomputing resources, such as those available at the NASA Center for Climate Simulation (NCCS).
    • Accelerators: Heavy reliance on GPUs (Graphics Processing Units), often provided by partners like NVIDIA, to drastically reduce the training and inference time.

5. How is your project creative?

The project is creative in its approach to integrating scientific rigor with cutting-edge AI architecture:

  • Visual Forecasting: The most creative aspect is the ability to generate a predicted image of a solar flare's location and structure up to two hours in advance, rather than just a simple probability score. This is a novel use of generative AI in heliophysics.
  • The Digital Twin Concept: Using advanced data visualization and animation to integrate the AI predictions into a single, comprehensive, dynamic simulation of the Sun-Earth environment. This moves the prediction out of static charts and into an immersive, actionable 3D operational dashboard.
  • Foundation Model Architecture: Applying the concept of a "Foundation Model" (a single large model trained for an entire scientific domain) to solar physics is a creative scaling of AI capabilities, maximizing the knowledge extracted from 9+ years of continuous observational data.9

6. What factors did your team consider?

The team had to balance scientific accuracy, operational necessity, and technological constraints:

  • Data Scalability: The factor of managing and efficiently processing petabytes of high-resolution image data was a critical technical constraint, requiring custom solutions to handle the vast scale.10
  • The Rarity Problem: Major, dangerous solar events are rare. The team had to consider how to train the model effectively when the most critical events (X-class flares) make up a tiny fraction of the dataset. This required advanced techniques like explainable AI (XAI) and sophisticated data augmentation.
  • Speed and Latency: For the forecast to be useful, it must be delivered quickly. The model must operate faster than the solar phenomena it predicts, requiring optimization for low-latency deployment in operational environments.
  • Model Interpretability (Explainability): Because the forecasts impact critical infrastructure and human life, the team needed to ensure the model wasn't a "black box." Scientific confidence requires knowing why the AI made a certain prediction, driving the need for Explainable AI techniques.
  • Open Access: To maximize scientific utility and impact, the team considered the necessity of making the model and data open-source, involving decisions about licensing and community support (using platforms like Hugging Face).

🛰️ Project Summary – AeroSense: NASA TEMPO Air Quality Forecasting App
Our project, AeroSense, is a web-based application designed to forecast and monitor air quality using NASA’s TEMPO satellite data, ground-based sensor data (OpenAQ, Pandora), and real-time weather information. The app integrates these diverse datasets to provide accurate, localized Air Quality Index (AQI) forecasts and health alerts for users across North America.
AeroSense visualizes pollution trends through interactive maps, graphs, and dashboards, enabling users to understand how environmental and weather factors influence air quality. It proactively notifies communities of unhealthy conditions and offers preventive recommendations to reduce exposure.
By combining satellite and ground-level observations, AeroSense bridges the gap between scientific data and public awareness—helping policymakers, health-sensitive populations, and the general public make informed, timely decisions. This tool directly supports NASA’s goal of leveraging Earth observation data to improve public health, enhance environmental management, and promote clean-air awareness.
projectDetails.details:
AeroSense is an intelligent web-based platform that forecasts and visualizes air quality using NASA’s TEMPO satellite data, ground-based air monitoring networks (OpenAQ, Pandora), and weather APIs (OpenWeatherMap). The system collects real-time atmospheric data—including pollutants such as NO₂, O₃, and PM2.5—then integrates and analyzes them to produce accurate Air Quality Index (AQI) predictions.

The app features an interactive dashboard and map visualization that display pollution trends, weather influence, and health alerts. Users receive proactive notifications when air quality becomes unhealthy, along with preventive health recommendations.

Developed using React (frontend), FastAPI (backend), and PostgreSQL (database), AeroSense leverages Python-based data processing and machine learning models (LSTM forecasting) to predict pollutant trends. The project’s creative approach lies in combining satellite and ground-level insights for real-time environmental awareness, bridging the gap between complex Earth observation data and actionable community guidance.

Our team focused on accuracy, usability, scalability, and public impact, ensuring the app serves both citizens and policymakers in making informed air-quality decisions.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmos Innovators
projectDetails.summary:
Problem: Lack of early, data-driven prediction systems for natural disasters.
Solution: A unified AI platform that integrates live satellite data (NASA + NOAA) with trained machine learning models to predict wildfires, floods, and landslides hours or days before they occur.
Outcome: An open, extensible, and deployable system offering proactive disaster risk forecasting — bridging space data and real-world impact.                                                          ## 🚀 Solution Overview

The *AI Disaster Prediction System* is an intelligent platform that predicts *wildfires, floods, and landslides up to 24 hours in advance, using **real-time NASA and NOAA satellite data* combined with *machine learning models* trained on historical climate and geospatial datasets.
projectDetails.details:
How It Works

Data Ingestion:

The system continuously fetches real-time climate and environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, precipitation, and soil moisture from:

🌞 NASA POWER API (surface temperature, humidity, radiation)

🌧 NOAA GFS API (rainfall, pressure, soil moisture)

AI Forecasting:

Trained machine learning models (e.g., Random Forest Regressors) analyze patterns in these inputs and predict risk levels for upcoming 6, 12, and 24 hours.

Prediction Output:

The API produces results in GeoJSON format, ready for integration into:

3D visualizations (e.g., React + Three.js dashboards)

GIS mapping tools (ArcGIS, QGIS)

Early warning systems and dashboards

User Query:

Developers or disaster agencies can query the API directly:

/api/ai/predict/fires?lat=12.97&lon=77.59

→ Returns wildfire risk forecast for that region (and similarly for floods/landslides).

🌦 Predictive Capabilities

Disaster Type Input Data Output

🔥 Wildfire Temperature, humidity, vegetation index, rainfall Predicted fire risk (0–1 scale)

🌊 Flood Rainfall intensity, soil moisture Flood probability score

🏔 Landslide Rainfall, soil moisture, vegetation coverage Landslide risk forecast

🌍 Impact

✅ Provides 6–24 hour advance forecasts of disaster risk

✅ Enables real-time monitoring and visualization

✅ Scalable across multiple geographies and data sources

✅ Empowers governments, NGOs, and emergency services for early response AI and Machine Learning Models

Three separate AI models specialize in different disasters, all trained using scikit-learn:

🔥 Wildfire Model

Algorithm: Random Forest Regressor

Inputs: Temperature, humidity, vegetation index, rainfall

Output: Fire risk score (0–1)

Purpose: Detects potential fire ignition conditions.

🌊 Flood Model

Algorithm: Gradient Boosting or Random Forest

Inputs: Rainfall intensity, soil moisture, cumulative precipitation

Output: Flood risk probability

Purpose: Predicts water overflow or flash-flood zones.

🏔 Landslide Model

Algorithm: Decision Tree or Logistic Regression

Inputs: Rainfall, soil moisture, slope, vegetation

Output: Landslide likelihood

Purpose: Evaluates terrain stability after prolonged rainfall.

Each model learns from historical satellite and ground datasets, discovering relationships between environmental factors and disaster events. Trained models are saved as .pkl files in the /models folder for fast inference.https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/)
projectDetails.aiReferences:
# 🧠 Use of Artificial Intelligence in the AI Disaster Prediction System

Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a *central and transformative role* in the AI Disaster Prediction System. The project’s primary goal is to forecast *wildfires, floods, and landslides* several hours or days in advance using real-time satellite and environmental data from NASA and NOAA. Achieving this requires more than simple statistical analysis — it depends on AI’s capability to detect complex, nonlinear patterns in massive datasets and make reliable predictive inferences about the likelihood of future disasters.

---

## 1. Role of AI in Disaster Forecasting

Traditional disaster management systems are *reactive, relying on ground sensors, satellite imagery, and human observation to identify events *after they begin. AI changes this paradigm by making disaster management *proactive*.

Through machine learning algorithms, the system can:

* *Learn patterns* from historical environmental data (temperature, humidity, rainfall, vegetation index, soil moisture, etc.).

* *Correlate variables* to identify conditions that precede a disaster.

* *Predict risk levels* at specific locations and times before an event occurs.

* Continuously *update predictions* as new data streams in from NASA and NOAA APIs.

This predictive intelligence enables early warnings — potentially saving thousands of lives and reducing economic damage.

---

## 2. Machine Learning Foundations

The system uses *supervised learning*, where historical datasets containing both environmental parameters and recorded disaster events are used to train AI models. Each disaster type — wildfire, flood, and landslide — has its own specialized model, since the factors that trigger these events differ significantly.

### 🔥 Wildfire Prediction Model

The wildfire model learns relationships between:

* Temperature and relative humidity (dryness indicators)

* Rainfall (recent precipitation affects vegetation moisture)

* Vegetation coverage (density and flammability)

A *Random Forest Regressor*, a powerful ensemble learning algorithm, is employed. It creates multiple decision trees that collectively learn how environmental conditions influence the likelihood of a fire. This ensemble approach reduces overfitting and provides robust predictions even with noisy satellite data.

### 🌊 Flood Prediction Model

For floods, AI focuses on:

* Cumulative rainfall over time

* Soil moisture levels

* Rainfall intensity forecasts from NOAA GFS data

By analyzing temporal changes in these variables, the flood model predicts how close an area is to saturation and potential overflow, offering forecasts for 6, 12, and 24-hour horizons.

### 🏔 Landslide Prediction Model

Landslide prediction integrates:

* Continuous rainfall (especially in hilly or mountainous regions)

* Soil saturation (from surface moisture data)

* Vegetation density (root strength and soil stability)

Machine learning helps identify combinations of these factors that have historically preceded landslides, turning them into probabilistic forecasts for new locations and timeframes.

---

## 3. Data Sources and AI Integration

AI is most effective when it has *accurate and timely data*. The system integrates two key global data sources:

1. *NASA POWER API*

Provides real-time temperature, humidity, solar radiation, and precipitation correction data. These variables help determine atmospheric and surface conditions that contribute to disaster formation.

2. *NOAA GFS (Global Forecast System)*

Supplies high-resolution forecasts for precipitation, soil moisture, and pressure. These predictive datasets enhance the AI models by offering insights into future environmental conditions, not just current ones.

By combining *observed data (NASA)* and *forecasted data (NOAA), the system allows AI to model both the **current state* and *expected evolution* of weather conditions — enabling true predictive capability.

---

## 4. Model Training and Deployment Pipeline

The AI development process in the project follows four main stages:

### (a) *Data Collection and Preprocessing*

Historical datasets are gathered from open repositories (NASA MODIS, ERA5, USGS, Copernicus). These datasets undergo cleaning, normalization, and feature extraction to prepare inputs for training.

### (b) *Model Training*

The Random Forest algorithm is trained on labeled data — for example, past instances where wildfires occurred versus where they did not. The model learns statistical correlations that indicate increased risk.

### (c) *Model Evaluation*

Each model’s accuracy is tested using metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R² score. Cross-validation ensures the models generalize well to unseen data.

### (d) *Model Deployment*

Trained models are serialized using joblib and stored in the /models directory as .pkl files. The FastAPI backend loads these models dynamically to generate predictions based on live NASA and NOAA data queries.

This pipeline enables *real-time AI inference* — users can request predictions for any latitude and longitude, and receive disaster risk forecasts instantly in GeoJSON format.

---

## 5. AI Decision Process (Inference)

When a user queries the API (e.g., requesting wildfire predictions for Bengaluru), the backend performs the following AI-driven operations:

1. *Fetch Live Data:* NASA and NOAA APIs provide the most recent and forecasted data for that location.

2. *Preprocess Input:* The data is structured into a feature vector containing temperature, humidity, rainfall, soil moisture, and vegetation index.

3. *Model Inference:* The relevant AI model (e.g., wildfire.pkl) processes this input to compute a risk score between 0 and 1.

4. *GeoJSON Output:* Results are returned as a geospatial JSON object for easy visualization on 3D maps or GIS dashboards.

This fully automated AI pipeline transforms raw environmental data into actionable risk intelligence.

---

## 6. Advantages of Using AI

The use of AI offers several advantages compared to conventional methods:

* *Predictive Intelligence:* Enables forecasting rather than post-event detection.

* *Scalability:* Can cover entire countries or continents by leveraging global satellite data.

* *Adaptability:* Models can retrain as new data becomes available, improving accuracy.

* *Automation:* Requires minimal human intervention once deployed.

* *Integration:* Compatible with visualization tools, mobile dashboards, and early warning systems.

AI acts as the *analytical brain* of the system — continuously learning, adjusting, and providing early alerts that can be directly translated into preparedness actions.

---

## 7. Future AI Enhancements

Planned improvements include:

* Integration of *Deep Learning (LSTM networks)* for sequence-based temporal forecasting.

* Use of *computer vision* on satellite imagery to detect vegetation dryness and flood extent.

* Application of *transfer learning* to adapt models across regions with limited local data.

* Real-time *reinforcement learning* to improve predictions based on ground truth feedback.

These advancements will evolve the system from a predictive engine to an *autonomous environmental intelligence platform*.

---

## 8. Conclusion

In summary, Artificial Intelligence is the *core enabler* that transforms this project from a weather-based monitoring tool into a *predictive early-warning system. By learning from the Earth’s past and analyzing its present state through satellite data, AI can **forecast the future behavior of natural systems* with remarkable precision.

Through this project, AI demonstrates its potential to bridge *space technology and humanitarian impact, providing a scientific foundation for **disaster resilience, preparedness, and climate adaptation* across the globe.

---

projectDetails.name: SPACE TIME COMMUNICATION
projectDetails.summary: Quantum communication promises to revolutionize space missions by enabling faster, secure communication over vast distances. Through quantum entanglement, data could potentially be transmitted instantaneously, bypassing the limits of light speed and eliminating communication delays. Additionally, quantum key distribution (QKD) ensures highly secure transmission, protecting sensitive information from interference. Investing in quantum technology will be key to shaping the future of space exploration, offering breakthroughs that could enhance both the speed and security of deep-space communication.
projectDetails.details: Quantum entanglement presents a groundbreaking approach to communication, particularly in the context of space exploration, where traditional methods are limited by the vast distances between celestial bodies. Entanglement allows two particles to be linked in such a way that the state of one particle is instantaneously reflected in the state of the other, regardless of the distance separating them. This non-locality could potentially enable faster-than-light communication, bypassing the time delays that currently hinder long-distance space communication. Additionally, quantum communication utilizes secure data transmission through quantum channels, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to protect information from eavesdropping. Any attempt to intercept or measure the quantum states would disturb the system, alerting the sender to the presence of an intruder, thus ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of transmitted data. With continued advancements in quantum technologies, this method of communication could revolutionize not only space missions but also the security and efficiency of all future interplanetary and interstellar communications.

# NASA-project
Seeing & Floating: Cupola and NBL Interactive
Project Description
This project is an interactive educational web experience inspired by NASA's International Space Station (ISS) modules, the Cupola and the Neutral Buoyancy Lab (NBL). It simulates two key sensory experiences that astronauts have on the ISS: viewing Earth through the Cupola's panoramic windows and practicing floating and weightlessness in the NBL underwater training facility. The project uses public NASA media to provide an immersive outreach experience aimed at STEM education.

Features
Interactive panoramic Cupola window simulation showcasing Earth views and space.

Simulated layer highlights like wildfire monitoring, city light mapping, and atmospheric features.
projectDetails.details:
# NASA-project

Seeing & Floating: Cupola and NBL Interactive

Project Description

This project is an interactive educational web experience inspired by NASA's International Space Station (ISS) modules, the Cupola and the Neutral Buoyancy Lab (NBL). It simulates two key sensory experiences that astronauts have on the ISS: viewing Earth through the Cupola's panoramic windows and practicing floating and weightlessness in the NBL underwater training facility. The project uses public NASA media to provide an immersive outreach experience aimed at STEM education.

Features

Interactive panoramic Cupola window simulation showcasing Earth views and space.

Simulated layer highlights like wildfire monitoring, city light mapping, and atmospheric features.

Video content showcasing astronaut training and Earth observation.

Interactive gravity slider to demonstrate how astronauts float more freely in microgravity.

Toggle views between Cupola sight and NBL weightlessness training.

Quick facts and lesson ideas to enhance educational use.

Responsive and visually engaging with an orange-purple theme.

Technologies Used

HTML5, CSS3 (with custom theming and gradients)

JavaScript for DOM interactivity and event handling

Video integration for multimedia display

Public NASA images and videos (public domain)

Installation

Clone or download the repository.

Open the index.html or main HTML file in a modern web browser.

No additional server or installation steps required.

Usage

Use navigation buttons to switch between Cupola view and NBL simulation.

Interact with the panorama by dragging horizontally to look around.

Adjust the gravity slider to see the astronaut float differently.

Explore layer toggles to visualize different Earth monitoring data.

Play embedded videos for more context on astronaut training and Earth benefits.

Contribution Guidelines

This project is for educational and outreach purposes inspired by NASA media. Contributions should focus on improving interactivity, educational content, accessibility, and visual design. Please submit issues or pull requests with clear descriptions.

License

This project uses NASA public domain images and videos. The code and additional content are shared for educational use only. Please credit NASA for media assets when used externally.

challengeDetails.title: International Space Station 25th Anniversary Apps
challengeDetails.excerpt: Crews onboard the International Space Station have many unique opportunities! They witness breathtaking Earth views from the station’s cupola—known as “the window to the world.” ​​They also experience weightlessness and go outside the station on spacewalks, for which they must train extensively in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) at the Sonny Carter Training Facility in Houston, Texas. (Space Operations Mission Directorate)

projectDetails.name: Dhritvan Space Lab
projectDetails.summary: The Space Weather Adventure tells the story of Ravi, a curious boy from a space-loving family. His father, Professor Pixel, teaches using holograms; his mother, Captain Skywave, is a pilot; his grandfather, Farmer Orbit, uses GPS-guided tractors; and his brother, Kiran, is an astronaut. Ravi’s magical friends—Sunny the Sun, Maggie the magnetic shield, and Aurora the sky artist—help explain how space weather affects Earth. When Sunny sneezes a giant solar flare, chaos follows: GPS fails, radios go silent, holograms flicker, and Kiran faces rising radiation in space. Maggie and Aurora work together to protect Earth, restoring order with dazzling auroras. That evening, the family shares a virtual dinner with Kiran, learning about real historical solar storms like the 1859 Carrington Event and the 1989 Quebec blackout. Through the adventure, Ravi learns that understanding space weather helps everyone stay safe—and that the Sun connects all of Earth and space in one cosmic family.

challengeDetails.title: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings
challengeDetails.excerpt: Although the Sun is 93 million miles away from our planet, solar activity can significantly impact our daily lives. “Space weather”—the variations that occur in the space environment between the Sun and Earth—can impact technologies in space and on Earth. Your challenge is to write and illustrate a digital children’s story that explains what space weather is and the varying impacts it has on different people such as farmers, pilots, astronauts, power grid operators, and the general public. You can tell the story from the perspective of a person impacted by space weather or from the point of view of a solar flare or coronal mass ejection (CME) as it approaches Earth. (Heliophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: Project Errorz
projectDetails.summary:
The Astronaut Health Multimodal AI Chatbot is an intelligent system designed to monitor and manage astronaut health during long-duration space missions. It allows astronauts to input vital parameters such as blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood sugar, and body temperature. The AI analyzes these readings in real time, providing health feedback, alerts for abnormal values, and guidance based on an integrated space biology knowledge base.

This system effectively acts as a Space Biology Knowledge Engine, converting raw biological data into actionable insights. It addresses the critical challenge of maintaining astronaut health in isolated environments, where immediate medical support is unavailable, by enabling self-monitoring, preventive care, and informed decision-making.

The project is important because it enhances mission safety, promotes autonomous health management, and educates astronauts on biological responses in microgravity. Beyond space applications, it demonstrates how AI can support remote healthcare, emergency monitoring, and personalized health guidance, making it a significant step toward integrating artificial intelligence with human biology for extreme environments.
projectDetails.details:
What it does / How it works:
The Astronaut Health Multimodal AI Chatbot collects vital health parameters from astronauts — such as blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, sugar levels, and temperature — either through manual input or connected sensors. The AI analyzes the data in real time, identifies abnormalities, and provides personalized health feedback and guidance. It also includes a knowledge base with space biology manuals, allowing astronauts to understand the biological impact of their readings and take preventive measures. The system functions as a Space Biology Knowledge Engine, converting raw data into actionable insights.

Benefits:

  • Real-time health monitoring and alerts
  • Personalized suggestions for maintaining astronaut health
  • Promotes self-care and safety in isolated environments
  • Reduces reliance on Earth-based medical teams
  • Supports education on space biology and preventive measures

Intended impact:
The project ensures astronaut well-being during long-duration missions, enhances mission safety, and provides a model for AI-assisted health monitoring in remote or extreme environments.

Tools, coding languages, hardware/software used:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • Backend: Node.js (for AI/logic simulation, if extended)
  • Platform: Web-based interface (runs in browser)
  • Optional hardware: Vital signs sensors for real-time input

Creativity:
The project combines AI, interactive chatbot design, and space biology knowledge to create a novel, multimodal tool for autonomous health management.

Factors considered:

  • Safety and reliability of health monitoring
  • User-friendly interface for astronauts in microgravity
  • Integration of biological knowledge for preventive care
  • Realistic parameters for space missions (e.g., vitals under microgravity conditions)
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of AI in the project:

  • The chatbot logic and health analysis responses were designed and generated with the assistance of AI tools, which helped in formulating realistic astronaut health feedback based on input parameters.
  • AI was used to suggest and structure the knowledge base content for space biology protocols, ensuring clarity and accuracy in guidance.
  • The project uses AI algorithms to evaluate vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, sugar, and temperature) and generate personalized health recommendations.
  • All AI-generated text content has been reviewed, modified, and adapted to maintain originality, context, and applicability to space health monitoring.
  • Code snippets and logic structures were developed with guidance from AI-assisted tools for faster prototyping and organization.

projectDetails.name: Project FULL METAL ALCHEMIST
projectDetails.summary:
Our project “Meteoroid Madness” was created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. The challenge focuses on understanding the behavior, impact, and visualization of meteoroids in our solar system. As a team of second-year students, we developed an interactive web application that helps users visualize meteoroid activity, their composition, and potential impact on Earth and other celestial bodies.

The web app uses data visualization to explain how meteoroids form, travel through space, and burn up as meteors upon entering planetary atmospheres. Through dynamic charts and animations, users can explore real-time simulations showing the frequency and trajectory of meteoroids based on scientific datasets. We also included educational sections that explain key topics such as asteroid belts, meteor showers, and impact craters, making complex space phenomena accessible to students and the general public.

Our goal was to create a visually engaging and educational platform that promotes curiosity about space science. By combining research, creativity, and teamwork, “Meteoroid Madness” demonstrates how simple web technologies can bring space data to life and inspire the next generation of explorers and innovators.
projectDetails.details: Meteoroid Madness is a web-based visualization project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025. Our aim was to simplify and illustrate complex meteoroid-related data through interactive visuals. The website presents information about meteoroid origins, trajectories, compositions, and impacts using dynamic charts and animations. It allows users to explore how meteoroids move through space and interact with planetary atmospheres. The project was built using basic web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, focusing on education, engagement, and accessibility. It helps learners and enthusiasts better understand space phenomena through an intuitive and interactive interface.
projectDetails.aiReferences: In Meteoroid Madness, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was integrated to enhance data analysis and visualization accuracy. AI models were used to predict meteoroid trajectories and estimate their potential impact areas using available NASA datasets. Machine learning algorithms helped identify patterns in meteoroid density, speed, and composition across different regions of space. Additionally, AI-powered visualizations made the data more interactive and educational for users. By applying AI, our project transforms complex scientific information into simple, understandable insights, allowing users to explore and learn about meteoroids dynamically while highlighting how AI can support space research and public awareness.

challengeDetails.title: Meteor Madness
challengeDetails.excerpt: A newly identified near-Earth asteroid, "Impactor-2025," poses a potential threat to Earth, but do we have the tools to enable the public and decision makers to understand and mitigate its risks? NASA datasets include information about known asteroids and the United States Geological Survey provides critical information that could enable modeling the effects of asteroid impacts, but this data needs to be integrated to enable effective visualization and decision making. Your challenge is to develop an interactive visualization and simulation tool that uses real data to help users model asteroid impact scenarios, predict consequences, and evaluate potential mitigation strategies. (Planetary Science Division)

projectDetails.name: Mobility system of mass rover
projectDetails.summary: Our project focuses on developing a mobility system for a Mars rover capable of traversing the planet’s rough and uneven terrain. We designed a lightweight, durable suspension and wheel mechanism that enhances stability, traction, and maneuverability across rocky surfaces and slopes. The system addresses the challenge of maintaining balance and movement efficiency under reduced Martian gravity and unpredictable obstacles. By improving mobility, the rover can explore larger areas, collect more data, and operate for longer durations. This innovation is crucial for future Mars missions, ensuring reliable performance and contributing to successful planetary exploration.
projectDetails.details:
Our project focuses on developing an efficient mobility system for a Mars rover, designed to navigate challenging Martian terrains such as rocks, sand, and slopes. The system works by integrating six-wheel independent suspension and rocker-bogie mechanism, allowing the rover to maintain stability and traction even on uneven surfaces.

The main benefit of this design is enhanced mobility and obstacle-handling capability, ensuring smooth exploration and data collection in harsh environments. The intended impact of this project is to support future Mars missions by improving rover endurance, adaptability, and scientific reach.

We utilized CAD tools (like SolidWorks) for mechanical design, Arduino/ROS for control systems, and Python and C++ for programming sensors and motor coordination. The hardware includes DC motors, servo systems, sensors, and microcontrollers.

Our project stands out for its innovative use of lightweight materials, energy efficiency, and adaptive motion algorithms. As a team, we considered factors such as terrain type, energy consumption, weight balance, and reliability to ensure practical performance on Mars-like surfaces.

projectDetails.name: ClearSkies { simple, powerful, health-focused}
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, ClearSkies, is an integrated web-based forecasting platform that leverages NASA’s TEMPO mission data, ground-based air quality observations, and meteorological inputs to deliver timely, location-specific air quality insights. The system transforms complex Earth observation datasets into accessible, actionable information, empowering individuals and communities to make informed health and lifestyle decisions.

Beyond visualizing pollution trends, ClearSkies provides proactive alerts during periods of elevated risk, tailoring notifications to vulnerable populations such as children, the elderly, and those with respiratory conditions. Its architecture is designed to seamlessly scale from local deployment to cloud-based infrastructure, ensuring adaptability, reliability, and broad accessibility.

This initiative directly addresses the challenge by bridging the gap between satellite science and public health action. By converting environmental intelligence into practical guidance, ClearSkies aspires to reduce pollutant exposure, foster healthier communities, and contribute to a cleaner, safer atmosphere for all.
projectDetails.details:
ClearSkies: Hyper-Local Air Quality Forecast - Project Summary

🎯 Core Functionality & How It Works

  • Goal: Provide fast, hyper-local air quality forecasts up to four hours in advance, addressing issues of generalization and delay in current reports.
    1. NASA TEMPO Satellite Data (NO2​): Tracks macro-level pollution plumes and movement.
    2. Local Ground Station Readings (PM2.5​): Measures immediate, street-level health impact.
    3. Local Weather Data (Wind Speed/Direction): Serves as the predictive variable to model plume movement.
  • Output: The final forecast is displayed on a live, interactive, color-coded dashboard built on a no-code platform.

✨ Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Actionable Warnings: Translates complex AQI numbers into immediate, clear advice (e.g., "High Risk: Stay Indoors").
  • 4-Hour Forecast: Provides a crucial time window for the public and health officials to take preventative action.
  • Hyper-Local Accuracy: Improves reliability by combining the regional "big picture" (TEMPO) with local "ground truth" (PM2.5​).
  • Intended Impact: Improve public health decision-making and reduce pollutant exposure by offering timely, granular information.

🛠️ Tools & Technology

  • Data Extraction (Low-Code): Python (using libraries like Pandas, xarray) for processing complex TEMPO files.
  • Data Integration (Low-Code/No-Code): Google Sheets used as a central database to fuse TEMPO data, ground readings, and weather data.
  • Visualization (No-Code): Looker Studio (Google) used to create the final interactive map and dashboard with conditional formatting.

💡 Creative & Design Factors

  • Data Fusion Innovation: Creatively merges large-scale, complex satellite data with simple, local data using an intermediate programmatic step, making the former accessible to no-code platforms.
  • Focus on Prediction: The inclusion of wind data for a 4-hour forward forecast adds a critical, high-value feature beyond simple current visualization.
  • Accessibility: Building the final user interface on a common, no-code platform (Looker Studio) ensures the powerful NASA data is accessible to the general public.
  • Design Factor: Prioritized low latency and actionability (clear health alerts) in the design process.

Microgravity Meal Planner Project Details

Project Overview:
The Microgravity Meal Planner is a web-based application designed to provide personalized nutrition plans for astronauts in microgravity environments. 

Key Features:
1. Today's Meal Plan: Customized meal plans tailored to individual astronaut needs and mission requirements.
2. Nutrient Tracker: Monitoring of essential nutrients to ensure balanced intake.
3. Meal Reminders: Timely reminders for meals to maintain a regular eating schedule.
4. Food and Health Tracking: Logging of food consumption and tracking of health metrics.
5. Nutrient Analysis: Detailed analysis of nutritional intake to optimize health.
6. Review and Feedback: Regular reviews and feedback mechanisms to improve meal planning and nutrition.
7. Profile Details: Personalized profiles for astronauts with dietary preferences, health metrics, and mission details.

Objectives:
1. Provide personalized nutrition plans for astronauts.
2. Monitor and track nutrient intake and health metrics.
3. Support astronauts' busy schedules with meal reminders.
4. Offer a user-friendly interface for easy navigation and data entry.

Target Audience:
Astronauts and space agencies seeking to optimize nutrition and health during space missions.

Expected Outcomes:

1. Improved astronaut health and performance.
2. Enhanced nutrition planning and tracking.
3. Increased efficiency and productivity during space missions.
projectDetails.details:
Microgravity Meal Planner: A Nutrition Solution for Astronauts

The Microgravity Meal Planner is an innovative web application designed to provide personalized nutrition plans for astronauts in microgravity environments. Our project aims to ensure astronauts receive the necessary nutrients to maintain optimal health and performance during space missions.

How it Works:

1. User Input: Astronauts input their dietary preferences, health metrics, and mission details.

2. Meal Planning: Our AI-powered algorithm generates a customized meal plan, taking into account nutritional needs, food preferences, and mission requirements.

3. Nutrient Tracking: The app tracks nutrient intake and provides detailed reports.

4. Meal Reminders: Timely reminders for meals to maintain a regular eating schedule.

Benefits:

- Improved Health: Personalized nutrition plans ensure astronauts receive necessary nutrients.

- Increased Efficiency: Meal planning and reminders save time and reduce stress.

- Enhanced Performance: Optimal nutrition supports astronauts' physical and mental performance.

Intended Impact:

Our project aims to support the health and well-being of astronauts during space missions, contributing to the success of space exploration.

Tools and Technologies :

- Design Tools: Figma, Canva, and Miro for wireframing, UI/UX design, and collaboration.

Creativity:

Our project incorporates AI-powered meal planning, providing a unique and innovative solution for astronauts' nutritional needs.

Factors Considered:

- Nutritional Requirements: Astronauts' specific dietary needs in microgravity environments.

- Food Preferences: Individual preferences and dietary restrictions.

- Mission Requirements: Meal planning tailored to mission duration, type, and specific requirements.

By providing personalized nutrition plans and tracking features, the Microgravity Meal Planner app supports the health and well-being of astronauts, contributing to the success of space missions.

projectDetails.name: Project Horizon Narrators
projectDetails.summary:
“Deep Dive: From Universe to Ocean” is an immersive, 3D virtual reality experience that takes users on a journey from the cosmos to Earth’s oceans. Starting with a panoramic view of the universe, users can explore planets through interactive 3D models with narration and audio. Selecting Earth reveals its five major oceans, each glowing with real NASA satellite data layers such as temperature, currents, and chlorophyll concentration. Users can dive into each ocean, encountering diverse marine creatures in a fully interactive underwater environment. Data visualizations are seamlessly integrated, providing an engaging, educational experience that makes complex scientific information accessible to non-experts.

This project addresses NASA’s challenge by transforming raw Earth observation data into a visually compelling, story-driven experience. By bridging space, Earth, and oceans, it fosters curiosity, ocean literacy, and climate awareness, helping users connect emotionally to our planet’s dynamic systems while inspiring exploration and scientific understanding.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

Deep Dive: From Universe to Ocean is an immersive 3D virtual reality experience that lets users explore the universe, planets, and Earth’s oceans in a story-driven environment. The project begins with a panoramic universe view where users can search for any planet, view interactive 3D models, and listen to narrated descriptions. Selecting Earth highlights its five oceans, which users can click to dive underwater. Beneath the waves, users encounter diverse marine creatures while real NASA satellite data, including sea surface temperature, ocean currents, and chlorophyll levels, are visualized interactively. Spatial audio enhances immersion and storytelling.

The project benefits users by transforming complex scientific data into an engaging, accessible experience. It promotes ocean literacy, climate awareness, and curiosity about space and Earth. Creativity comes from combining 3D visualization, interactive exploration, and audio narration into a cohesive journey.

Tools & Technologies:

  • 3D & VR: Three.js
  • Data Sources: NASA MODIS, SeaWiFS, SWOT, GOES datasets
  • Visuals & Design: Blender, sketchfab
  • Audio: elevenlabs

The team carefully considered user experience, accessibility, scientific accuracy, and visual storytelling, ensuring the project is both educational and immersive.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
• Narration TTS for planet/ocean audio
    • Generate natural voice tracks per planet (or dynamic narration). Tools: Azure Cognitive Services TTS, Google Cloud TTS, Amazon Polly, OpenAI TTS. Export MP3 and wire into existing audio button.
    • Use generative models to create higher‑quality or varied planet/ocean textures. Tools: Stable Diffusion (inpainting), StyleGAN, Generative adversarial nets; or Real-ESRGAN for upscaling existing textures.
    • Denoise and normalize narration and ambient audio. Tools: RNNoise, Adobe Enhance, open-source ML denoisers.
    • Produce captions, tags and descriptions for textures/models (for READMEs and search). Tools: BLIP / CLIP, Vision transformers.
    • Upscale low-res maps with Real-ESRGAN or ESRGAN to improve appearance without replacing art.
    • Create multiple LODs automatically and pick best for performance. Tools: commercial/opensource LOD generators; research ML tools for remeshing or Houdini/Blender plugins.

challengeDetails.title: Deep Dive: Immersive Data Stories from Ocean to Sky
challengeDetails.excerpt: Satellite observations reveal insights about our dynamic home planet to scientists, but people without a remote sensing background often find the stories within these datasets difficult to access. NASA’s open data policy makes these observations available to everyone—scientists and non-scientists alike. Your challenge is to build a short, immersive, virtual reality (VR) experience that leverages NASA’s Earth observation datasets and visualizations to bring stories about our planet’s oceans to life, connecting a broad audience to this data, its beauty, and its impact. Using visuals, spatial audio, and even interactive elements, your VR experience can enable users to dive deeper into Earth’s unfolding ocean story. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: 25 Years of warming - Terra's view of changing planet
projectDetails.summary:
Between 2000 and 2025, global land surface temperatures have shown a clear upward trend.
NASA’s Terra MODIS satellite data reveals that:

Average land temperatures have increased by roughly 0.8–1.0 °C in many regions.

Warmer zones (shown in orange and red on the maps) have expanded across continents.

Polar areas, South Asia, and parts of Africa show the most significant warming.
This steady rise reflects the ongoing effects of greenhouse gas emissions, deforestation, and urbanization.
projectDetails.details:
This project visually demonstrates how Earth’s land surface temperature has changed between 2000 and 2025 using NASA’s Terra MODIS satellite data.
It collects global temperature maps from NASA’s Worldview platform, arranges them chronologically, and presents them as an animated video showing the progression of global warming.
Each slide in the video represents a different year, supported by narration and subtitles that explain the environmental changes.
The result is a clear, data-driven visualization of how our planet is heating up over time.

challengeDetails.title: Sharks from Space
challengeDetails.excerpt: Earth’s ocean is one of the most powerful habitats in our universe, supporting a range of life that sustains ecosystems and habitability across the globe. It is common to measure photosynthetic activity in the ocean from space, but far more challenging to track top predators. projectDetails.name: Meteo Minds
projectDetails.summary:
I developed a responsive Weather Dashboard that provides 7-day forecasts for any city worldwide. Users can select a city by typing or interacting with an interactive map, and view key weather details including temperature, chance of rain, and UV index. The app also offers personalized activity recommendations based on the forecast, helping users plan their day or events effectively.

A key feature is the Smart Weather Chatbot, which answers natural-language questions about rain, temperature, UV levels, and suggested activities. Unlike basic weather apps, the chatbot can respond to queries about specific days of the week, giving users detailed, actionable advice.

This project addresses the challenge of making weather information accessible and actionable, especially for planning outdoor activities. By combining interactive visualization with AI-powered guidance, it empowers users to make informed decisions, reduce weather-related surprises, and improve daily planning.
projectDetails.details:
How it works:
The Weather Dashboard is a responsive web application that provides 7-day weather forecasts for any city worldwide. Users can select a city either by typing it into a text field or clicking on an interactive map powered by Leaflet.js. The app displays key weather information such as temperature, chance of rain, and UV index. It also features personalized recommendations for outdoor activities based on the forecast.

The Smart Weather Chatbot allows users to ask natural-language questions like “Should I carry an umbrella today?” or “Is it sunny on Friday?” and provides day-specific weather-aware responses. It interprets queries, fetches relevant forecast data, and gives actionable advice.

Benefits:

  • Helps users plan daily activities or events with confidence
  • Reduces surprises caused by unexpected weather
  • Educates users about UV safety and weather patterns
  • Provides an interactive and engaging experience through chatbot interaction

Tools and Technologies:

  • Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • APIs & Libraries: Weather API for forecasts, Leaflet.js for maps, Chart.js for rain trends
  • Software: Any modern browser, no special hardware required

Creativity:

  • The chatbot can respond to specific days of the week, not just today
  • Interactive map selection adds a visual and intuitive element
  • Focused on user-friendly experience and actionable insights

Team Considerations:

  • Ensuring accurate weather information
  • Presenting data visually and intuitively
  • Making recommendations safe and practical for outdoor activities
  • Balancing interactivity with performance and responsiveness

projectDetails.name: Project MIRAI_6
projectDetails.details:
Project Summary (The What & Why)

Project Name: *Space Biology Knowledge Engine (Team MIRAI\_6)*

| Detail | Description |

| *The Core Problem* | NASA possesses *608+ space bioscience publications* (abstracts/titles) on how life is affected by space. This knowledge is currently *unstructured*, making it inefficient and time-consuming for scientists and mission planners to query, synthesize, and use for critical decisions. |

| *The Goal* | To transform this massive collection of raw, unstructured text into a *structured, queryable database* and a *dynamic web application* (dashboard) using AI and Knowledge Graphs. |

| *Target Audience* | *Mission Architects* (for actionable countermeasures), *Program Managers* (for identifying funding gaps), and *Scientists* (for generating new hypotheses). |

| *Core Deliverables* | 1. *AI-Tagged Dataset:* Publications are tagged with Organism, Environment, and Impact. |

| | 2. *Dynamic Dashboard (Streamlit):* Allows interactive search, filtering, and visualization. |

| | 3. *Actionable Summaries:* Provides concise, decision-ready takeaways from complex studies. |

| | 4. *Knowledge Gap Identification:* Visualizes research connections to pinpoint where more studies are urgently needed for a safe Mars mission. |

Project Details (The Tools & Scope)

| Category | Detail |

| *Scope of Data* | Titles and Abstracts from *608 NASA Bioscience Publications* (provided by the challenge). |

| *Primary Programming Language* | *Python* (used for all data processing, AI/NLP, and web application logic). |

| *Data Processing / Storage* | *Pandas* (for tabular data manipulation and cleaning) and *Standard Data Structures* (for the database model). |

| *Core AI/NLP Tool* | *spaCy / NLTK* (for Named Entity Recognition and text processing). |

| *Knowledge Graph Tool* | *NetworkX* (Python library for constructing and analyzing the graph connections). |

| *Web Application / Dashboard* | *Streamlit* (Python framework for quickly deploying the dashboard as a functional web application). |

| *Team Name* | *MIRAI\_6* |
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI Used in This Project

The project leverages several AI and data science techniques, primarily falling under the umbrella of *Natural Language Processing, which is a key branch of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML).

AI/ML Technique Purpose in Project Tool/Implementation

| *Natural Language Processing (NLP)* | *Core Function:* Used to read, interpret, and structure the unstructured text data (Titles and Abstracts). | Python libraries: spaCy, NLTK, or a simplified, fine-tuned *Large Language Model

| *Named Entity Recognition (NER)* | *AI Feature Extraction:* Identifies and classifies key information from the text into predefined categories (entities). | The custom NLP model identifies: *Organisms* (Mus musculus), *Environments* (Microgravity), and *Biological Impacts* (Bone Density). |

| *Text Summarization (Extractive/Abstractive)* | *Actionable Insights:* Used to distill the detailed abstract text into a concise, single-sentence summary suitable for Mission Planners. | A rule-based system or a simple LLM prompt to generate the "Actionable Summary." |

| *Knowledge Graph Construction* | *Data Structuring:* Not AI per se, but a critical AI-enabling structure. It models the *relationships* found by the NLP/NER step. | Python library: NetworkX. Used to connect nodes like [Organism] $\rightarrow$ [Impact] $\rightarrow$ [Environment]. |

| *Clustering/Topic Modeling* | (Optional but Powerful): Used to group similar papers together to identify broad themes or *areas of consensus/disagreement*. | Libraries like Scikit-learn or Gensim. |

projectDetails.name: Project NASA Aspirants
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Global Bloom Detector, tackles a critical environmental problem — the lack of efficient, automated systems to detect and monitor vegetation bloom events across diverse ecosystems like deserts, coastal zones, and agricultural lands. Bloom events indicate ecosystem vitality, food security, and climate resilience, yet they often go unnoticed or unquantified until after major environmental changes occur.
Our solution uses NASA’s free and open satellite data, including MODIS NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) and GPM precipitation datasets, to identify bloom onset, peak, and decline through advanced time-series analysis and machine learning models. Users can upload a region or polygon, and the system automatically detects bloom events, visualizes patterns on interactive maps, and generates summary analytics in CSV, GeoTIFF, or GeoJSON formats. This gives researchers, policymakers, and farmers actionable insights into vegetation health and climate interactions.
Looking into the future, our project could evolve into a global early warning system for vegetation and ecosystem change — helping predict crop yield shifts, desertification risks, and coastal ecosystem responses to climate events. By leveraging NASA’s Earth observation data, Global Bloom Detector bridges science, technology, and sustainability — empowering humanity to better understand and protect our planet’s green heartbeat.

projectDetails.name: Project Orbit spacex
projectDetails.summary:
This simulation models the autonomous behavior of a Mars rover navigating harsh terrain while detecting and recovering from faults in real time. 

It blends embedded system principles with intelligent pathfinding and diagnostic logging to showcase mission-critical reliability.
projectDetails.details:
Project Title: Mars Rover Simulation – Autonomy, Fault Recovery & Terrain Intelligence

Our project simulates a Mars rover navigating autonomously across diverse Martian terrains while handling real-time faults and logging telemetry data. It models realistic rover behavior under harsh conditions using a modular, embedded-first architecture. The rover uses an A* pathfinding algorithm enhanced with terrain scoring to avoid hazards like craters, steep slopes, and sand traps. Fault scenarios—such as sensor dropout, wheel stall, communication loss, and ICD mismatches—are injected during runtime, triggering recovery routines like terrain re-scans, rerouting, and protocol fallback. Telemetry logs track rover position, terrain type, and battery consumption in real time.

Benefits:

  • Prepares for real-world deployment by simulating mission-critical reliability
  • Enables testing of autonomous decision-making and fault recovery strategies
  • Offers a scalable architecture suitable for embedded rover systems
  • Provides audit-ready telemetry logs and fault diagnostics

Intended Impact:

  • Enhance fault-tolerant autonomy for planetary exploration
  • Inspire future rover designs with robust navigation and recovery logic
  • Provide a testbed for embedded diagnostics and protocol abstraction
  • Demonstrate how simulation can accelerate innovation in space robotics

Tools, Languages, and Software Used:

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Simulation Logic: A* algorithm with dynamic terrain scoring
  • Embedded Concepts: Watchdog timers, buffer-safe diagnostics, CAN/USB telemetry logging
  • Protocol Handling: ICD version-aware wrappers, flexible array buffers
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used Microsoft Copilot to accelerate architecture refinement, documentation clarity, and presentation strategy. Specifically:

  • Code and Data: Copilot assisted in structuring the A* pathfinding algorithm, fault recovery logic, and telemetry logging format. All AI-assisted code is annotated and acknowledged in comments and metadata.
  • Documentation: AI helped polish technical descriptions, organize system architecture, and format fault tables and telemetry logs for clarity.
  • Presentation: Copilot supported slide formatting and narrative flow, ensuring our simulation goals and embedded-first design were clearly communicated.
