projectDetails.name: Pixel Planet – Visualizing Earth’s Changes Through Terra Data
projectDetails.summary:
Pixel Planet is an interactive web-based project that visualizes the beauty and fragility of our planet using data from NASA’s Terra satellite. The platform brings together science, creativity, and technology to make Earth observation engaging and easy to understand. Through dynamic animations, real Terra MODIS images, and informative sections on Terra’s instruments and mission, we highlight how satellite data helps monitor environmental changes such as deforestation, urbanization, pollution, and weather impacts. Our project aims to take NASA's data and convert or create animations, gifs and before and after images which is simple and easy to understand for everyone. 
Our project aims to educate and inspire users to explore the importance of Earth science through storytelling, design, and interactivity. By transforming raw satellite data into visual experiences, Pixel Planet bridges the gap between scientific discovery and public awareness, showing how technology and creativity can work hand in hand to protect our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Pixel Planet is an interactive website that visualizes Earth’s environmental changes using real data and imagery from NASA’s Terra satellite. It showcases before-and-after animations of significant global events like deforestation, floods, and urban growth, helping users easily understand the impact of human and natural activities on our planet.

The platform was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, integrating creative GIF animations, interactive visuals, and informative content about Terra’s instruments such as MODIS, ASTER, and MISR. We designed the website using Google Sites for accessibility and responsiveness across devices.

The project’s goal is to combine science, creativity, and storytelling to make complex satellite data visually engaging and educational for all age groups. It emphasizes how data visualization can inspire awareness about climate and environmental change.

By transforming scientific datasets into artistic visuals, Pixel Planet bridges the gap between technology and creativity. Our team focused on clarity, design, interactivity, and user engagement to create an impactful experience that celebrates NASA’s Terra mission and its contribution to understanding our changing planet

challengeDetails.title: Animation Celebration of Terra Data!
challengeDetails.excerpt: NASA’s oldest daily Earth-viewing satellite – Terra – just turned 25 years old, and with five continuously operating instruments onboard (most taking imagery at the same time), Terra has piled up a LOT of data over the years (over 9,000 days and counting!). Your challenge is to use data from any or all of Terra’s five instruments to create an animated product showcasing an Earth science story and emphasizing the impacts to you, your community, and/or the environment. Your challenge is to build a dynamic dashboard that leverages artificial intelligence (AI), knowledge graphs, and/or other tools to summarize a set of NASA bioscience publications and enables users to explore the impacts and results of the experiments these publications describe. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: ECHOES BENEATH
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Echoes Beneath, is a proposed AI-powered platform designed to make seismic activity data from Mars and the Moon accessible to a wider audience. While NASA already collects this data, existing tools are often too technical for students, educators, and the general public to use effectively.

Echoes Beneath addresses this challenge by presenting seismic data through simple visualizations, interactive dashboards, and educational features that transform raw signals into meaningful insights. This approach makes space science more engaging and approachable, especially for learners who may not have a background in data analysis.

By bridging the gap between complex scientific data and public understanding, Echoes Beneath empowers education, inspires curiosity, and brings the hidden “heartbeat” of other worlds to life

projectDetails.name: ParadeShield
projectDetails.summary:
ParadeShield is a web-based platform that provides probabilistic climatological assessments for long-range event planning. Developed by Team Semi Colons, the system utilizes over 30 years of open NASA Earth Observation data (MERRA-2, GPM) and regional datasets from CPTEC/INPE to calculate the likelihood of user-defined adverse weather conditions—such as extreme temperature, heavy rainfall, or strong winds.

By allowing users to set custom weather thresholds, the platform bridges the gap between short-term weather forecasts and long-term climate insights. It delivers clear, visualized risk metrics through interactive dashboards, enabling planners, researchers, and policymakers to make data-driven decisions months in advance.

This project is important because it transforms complex climate datasets into accessible, actionable information—promoting climate resilience, preparedness, and sustainable planning through transparency and open science principles.
projectDetails.details:
ParadeShield

is an interactive web platform that estimates the probability of adverse weather conditions for any chosen location and date range. It analyzes over 30 years of NASA Earth Observation (MERRA-2, GPM) and CPTEC/INPE datasets to calculate the likelihood that user-defined thresholds—such as high temperature, heavy rainfall, or strong winds—will be exceeded.

The system uses geopy to convert user-entered locations into coordinates, processes historical climate data using Pandas and NumPy, and visualizes results through Plotly within a Streamlit dashboard. Users receive intuitive graphical outputs including a Risk Meter and Historical Distribution Histogram, along with downloadable CSV/JSON data for transparency.

The platform benefits long-term event planners, researchers, and policymakers by providing data-driven, probabilistic climate insights rather than short-term forecasts. Its intended impact is to promote climate resilience and informed decision-making through open data and reproducible science.

Creatively, the project merges personalized threshold modeling with scientific rigor—turning complex climatological archives into accessible, actionable intelligence. Team Semi Colons emphasized usability, scientific transparency, and adaptability to ensure the platform serves both technical and non-technical users.

projectDetails.name: Project SharkIntel
projectDetails.summary:
SmartShark is a predictive shark-tracking system that uses NASA satellite data and a novel sensor tag design to monitor shark movement and feeding behavior in real time. Our project combines satellite-derived ocean data—such as sea surface temperature, chlorophyll concentration, salinity, and ocean currents—with historical shark tracking datasets to build a machine learning model that accurately predicts shark foraging hotspots.
We also conceptualized a next-generation electronic tag that tracks shark location using GPS and motion sensors (IMU), detects feeding events through onboard biochemical sensors, and transmits real-time data via acoustic and satellite communication. This provides not only location data but also insight into what sharks are eating—something current tags don’t offer.
Built using Python, TensorFlow, NASA EarthData APIs, and GIS tools, SmartShark offers a powerful tool for marine scientists, conservationists, and policy makers. It enables better understanding of predator-prey interactions, supports marine protected area design, and helps anticipate ecological changes. By fusing space technology, AI, and bio-sensing, SmartShark redefines how we observe and protect ocean ecosystems.
projectDetails.details:
Satellite-Driven Shark Tracking and Real-Time Foraging Analysis System

✅ What does your project do, and how does it work?

SmartShark is an intelligent system that predicts shark foraging habitats using NASA satellite data and a newly conceptualized bio-telemetry tag that can track both location and feeding behavior in real-time.

The system consists of two core components:

  1. Satellite-Powered Prediction Model:
    We built a mathematical framework that fuses Earth observation data from NASA (e.g., sea surface temperature, chlorophyll concentration, salinity, and ocean current velocity) with machine learning algorithms trained on existing shark movement and environmental datasets. The model predicts foraging hotspots by identifying ocean conditions that correlate with past shark feeding activity.
    • GPS + IMU for real-time location and motion tracking.
    • Microfluidic biochemical sensors to detect chemical markers from ingested prey.
    • Acoustic telemetry + satellite uplink for low-energy, live data transmission to cloud databases.
    • AI-based onboard processing to detect and classify feeding events.

🧠 What are the benefits?

  • Real-time Ecosystem Monitoring: Understand how sharks respond to changing ocean conditions and shifting prey distribution.
  • Improved Marine Conservation: Identify critical feeding zones to protect migratory species and design better marine protected areas (MPAs).
  • Public Safety: Help coastal communities and tourism boards anticipate shark movement in vulnerable regions.
  • Scientific Advancement: Offer researchers a richer dataset that includes not just movement, but behavior and diet — in real time.

🌍 What is the intended impact of your project?

  • Contribute to Earth system science by enabling researchers to model predator-prey dynamics and their links to climate-driven ocean changes.
  • Enhance global efforts in marine biodiversity conservation, sustainable fisheries, and climate resilience planning.
  • Bridge the gap between space-based data and marine biology, expanding the scope of how satellites can help understand life in the ocean depths.

💻 Tools, Technologies, and Languages Used:

  • Python – for data preprocessing, machine learning (Scikit-learn, TensorFlow), and geospatial analysis (Xarray, NetCDF4, Rasterio).
  • NASA EarthData & OB.DAAC APIs – to access ocean parameters like SST, chlorophyll, salinity.
  • ArcGIS & QGIS – for geospatial mapping and visualization of shark tracking overlays.
  • Figma / Fusion 360 – to prototype the physical shark tag design.
  • MATLAB – for mathematical modeling and signal processing simulations related to ingestion detection.
  • Git & GitHub – for collaborative version control.

🎨 How is your project creative?

  • Innovative Tag Concept: Existing shark tags mostly track location and depth. Ours is designed to detect feeding behavior and prey type, a major breakthrough in marine telemetry.
  • Satellite-Driven Prediction: We combined climate-scale satellite data with animal behavior to create a predictive tool — not just reactive tracking.
  • Bio-Cyber Hybrid Model: SmartShark bridges biological data and cyber-infrastructure, streaming live information to global researchers.
  • Conservation + Tech Fusion: The project uniquely addresses both ecological insight and technological innovation.

🧩 What factors did your team consider?

  • Power Efficiency: Designing the tag to use low-power telemetry suitable for long-term marine deployment.
  • Ocean Data Quality: Ensuring reliable satellite-derived parameters that match the spatial and temporal resolution of biological data.
  • Feasibility & Future Deployment: While our tag is conceptual, we modeled real-world constraints like miniaturization, waterproofing, and bio-compatibility.
  • Ethics & Wildlife Safety: Ensuring that the tagging methodology minimizes stress or harm to animals.
  • Global Relevance: Focusing on migratory shark species across major ocean basins to ensure wide ecological applicability.

projectDetails.name: SKYLET : PREDICT NEXT DAY TEMPERATURE
projectDetails.summary:
Summary: Predict Next-Day Temperature for Your City

This project aims to predict the next day’s temperature for any city using open-source weather data and a simple machine learning model. Mainly for purpose of making easy for making your schedule according to it. Mainly for farmers, 
By collecting past temperature data from the Open-Meteo API, the system applies Linear Regression to identify temperature trends and estimate the next day’s maximum temperature.

The program uses Python libraries such as Requests, NumPy, and Scikit-learn to handle data fetching, numerical computation, and model training.
The process involves:

1. Fetching the last 7 days’ temperature data of a chosen city.


2. Training a Linear Regression model on this data.


3. Predicting the temperature for the upcoming day based on the learned trend.



This simple yet effective project demonstrates how machine learning can be applied to real-world weather prediction problems without needing complex systems or paid APIs.
It’s an excellent beginner-friendly implementation that encourages the use of open data, AI, and environmental analysis for innovative solutions.


---

✅ Output Example:
Past 7 days temperatures: [28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 29, 28]
Predicted temperature for tomorrow: 29.5 °C

projectDetails.name: Transit Signal Predictor
projectDetails.summary:
Team Snippets developed an AI-based model that predicts the transit signal strength of exoplanets — how clearly a planet’s transit will appear in telescope data. Using NASA’s provided datasets of stellar and planetary parameters, our system analyzes features like planet size, orbital period, and star brightness to forecast metrics such as transit depth and signal-to-noise ratio.

This solution directly addresses the challenge of improving exoplanet detection efficiency. By predicting which targets will produce strong and clear signals, astronomers can prioritize observations, optimize telescope scheduling, and reduce time wasted on weak or noisy candidates.

Our model supports astronomers, space agencies, and commercial space companies by enabling smarter resource allocation, faster decision-making, and higher discovery rates. In essence, Transit Signal Strength Prediction helps transform raw exoplanet data into actionable insights — accelerating the search for new worlds beyond our solar system.

projectDetails.name: Bloom Watch Project
projectDetails.summary:
We built an interactive platform that tracks seasonal bloom events across Karnataka using satellite imagery and sensor data. The system analyzes bloom intensity and phenological trends in real time, and displays them through dynamic maps and alert dashboards. We integrated NDVI-based vegetation indices and geospatial filters to isolate bloom patterns specific to Karnataka. To ensure accuracy, we calibrated satellite inputs with local biodiversity datasets and field observations. We also implemented alert mechanisms to notify users during peak blooming periods, especially around global environmental observances and biodiversity festivals.
This solution was designed to be user-friendly, data-rich, and ecologically meaningful—empowering researchers, farmers, and nature enthusiasts to monitor and celebrate Karnataka’s floral cycles.
projectDetails.details:
Bloom-Watch is a geospatial science communication tool that detects and visualizes seasonal vegetation bloom events across Karnataka using satellite NDVI data. It combines remote sensing, interactive mapping, and public engagement to make bloom dynamics accessible to both researchers and citizens.

What It Does

• Uses Google Earth Engine to process satellite imagery and compute NDVI values.

• Detects bloom events based on NDVI thresholds and seasonal patterns.

• Displays bloom hotspots on an interactive Leaflet map with popups showing location, date, and NDVI stats.

• Visualizes NDVI trends over time using Chart.js.

• Enables users to export bloom data as CSV for offline analysis or dashboard integration.

Why It Matters

• Supports NASA-funded research on vegetation dynamics and climate interactions.

• Promotes environmental awareness and citizen science.

• Helps communities monitor ecological changes and seasonal cycles.

• Bridges the gap between complex satellite data and public understanding.

Tech Stack

• Google Earth Engine (JavaScript API) – for bloom detection and NDVI analysis.

• HTML, CSS, JavaScript – for frontend development.

• Leaflet.js – for interactive mapping.

• Chart.js – for NDVI time-series visualization.

• CSV Export Logic – for client-side data download.

• GitHub Pages – for public-facing deployment.

Creative Aspects

• Modular architecture separating detection, visualization, and export logic.

• Dynamic marker placement based on real-time NDVI filtering.

• Intuitive UI designed for both scientific and public audiences.

• Built with a builder’s mindset: robust, accessible, and impact-driven.

We used AI tools to assist with the following aspects of our project:

• Code and Documentation: Microsoft Copilot was used to accelerate frontend development (JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Chart.js) and Earth Engine scripting. It helped debug logic, refine NDVI thresholding, and structure CSV export functionality. All AI-assisted code was reviewed and modified by the team to ensure accuracy and originality.

• Content Writing: AI was used to draft and refine project descriptions, README content, and user-facing explanations. These were edited for clarity and scientific relevance.

• Design Brainstorming: AI helped ideate features for public engagement, such as dynamic mapping, chart interactivity, and dashboard integration.

No NASA branding, logos, or mission identifiers were used or modified in any AI-generated content. All outputs were created with originality and intent, and AI contributions were transparently acknowledged.

projectDetails.name: Bio-Space
projectDetails.summary:
We developed the Bio-Insight Engine, an AI-powered dynamic dashboard that transforms decades of dispersed NASA space biology publications into an accessible and interactive knowledge base.
The sheer volume of bioscience data from experiments on the ISS, aimed at enabling future missions to the Moon and Mars, is difficult for researchers and the public to navigate. Our project addresses this challenge by utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Knowledge Graph technology to:
Visually map the relationships between experiments, organisms, biological effects (e.g., bone density change), and mission parameters (e.g., duration, radiation).
Provide a dynamic search and filter interface for users to quickly find information relevant to their specific interests (e.g., "all plant gene expression studies in microgravity").
This tool is important because it accelerates research and discovery by reducing the time required to synthesize vast amounts of data, helping scientists identify knowledge gaps and informing crucial decisions for the safety and efficiency of future human space exploration. It effectively democratizes access to critical space biology knowledge.
It summarizes complex publications and provides visual, interactive access to relationships in the data. Accelerates research, informs future human space exploration missions (Moon/Mars), and identifies knowledge gaps.
projectDetails.details:
The Space Biology Knowledge Engine is an intelligent, centralized system built using Python to aggregate and synthesize complex biological data related to space exploration.

Function and Mechanism

The engine continuously ingests data from sources like NASA GeneLab and scientific publications. It employs Natural Language Processing (NLP), utilizing libraries like SpaCy/NLTK, to extract key entities (genes, proteins, mission factors) and map their relationships, storing this structure in a Neo4j knowledge graph. Users access this via a simple Streamlit interface, querying it with natural language (e.g., "What genes are affected by microgravity?") to receive precise, synthesized answers.

Benefits and Impact

The primary benefit is accelerated research, as it drastically reduces the manual time scientists spend cross-referencing disparate data. It facilitates the discovery of hidden biological connections and provides rapid risk assessment crucial for mission planning to the Moon and Mars. The intended impact is to become the foundational "brain" for space biology research, enabling faster breakthroughs in developing countermeasures and ensuring sustainable life support systems.

Creativity and Factors

The project's creativity lies in its move to semantic search, understanding the relationships between entities rather than just keywords, and presenting results as an interactive, visualized knowledge graph. Key factors considered were Data Quality , Scalability (using the graph database structure), and User Experience (creating an intuitive natural language interface for scientists).
projectDetails.aiReferences:
How We Used AI for Bio-Space

The Bio-Space: Conversational Knowledge Engine for Space Biology is fundamentally an AI project that uses multiple AI components across its architecture.

The core AI usage is in the AI Tier and the establishment of the Knowledge Graph (KG):

Natural Language Processing (NLP) / Large Language Models (LLMs): We used NLP/LLMs (specifically mentioning Gemini) to interpret the user's natural language questions (intent) and to convert the complex, synthesized insights back into a clear, natural language answer for the user.

Knowledge Graph (KG) Construction: AI was essential for moving beyond keyword search by processing vast, fragmented data from sources like NASA GeneLab and scientific literature. This process involves using NLP to perform Entity Mapping—extracting biological entities (genes, risks, drugs) and defining their complex relationships—which forms the structure of the KG (stored in Neo4j).

Advanced Analytics and Prediction: The AI Tier also incorporates ML Models to perform causal inference and predictive analytics. This capability allows the system to simulate risks (e.g., bone density loss for a Mars mission) and suggest optimal countermeasure protocols.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): AI was used in Phase 1 (MVP) for core Q&A capabilities based on a RAG architecture.

In summary, AI (LLMs, NLP, and ML models) is the "Engine's Brain" that transforms scattered biological data into actionable insights for scientists, mission planners, and astronauts.

projectDetails.name: Project STaTic
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, STaTic, is an interactive web-based immersive platform that helps students and the public explore two of the most iconic experiences aboard the International Space Station (ISS) - sight and weightlessness, through the Cupola and the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL).

Both learning pages were developed using React, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript and GSAP, combining educational information with smooth visual interactions.

The Cupola page features an immersive 3D model built with Three.js that recreates the astronaut’s view of Earth, along with a 3D orbiting Earth simulation where users can click on popular locations to view real satellite imagery.

The NBL page includes a Unity-built 2D game that lets users experience astronaut training and understand neutral buoyancy in a fun and engaging way.

Each page also includes a quiz section to reinforce learning. By merging education, simulation, and interactivity, STaTic brings the ISS experience closer to Earth, inspiring curiosity and demonstrating how space exploration benefits humanity.
projectDetails.details:
Project STaTic is an interactive educational web platform that helps users understand two defining aspects of life aboard the International Space Station, the Cupola Earth-viewing experience and Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) training for weightlessness.

The platform is divided into two main learning pages, each developed using React, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, and GSAP to provide smooth animations, and an engaging learning flow. Both pages combine structured educational content with interactive simulations and quizzes to deepen user understanding.

CUPOLA

This page features two key visual experiences built with Three.js:

A 3D interactive Cupola experience that allows users to witness Earth just as astronauts do from orbit. Users can freely explore the view, look around in every direction, and enjoy the breathtaking perspective of our planet from space.

A 3D Earth simulation in which users can interact with a dynamic globe, explore popular locations and instantly access real satellite imagery of those regions, connecting space perspectives with real-world geography .

After exploring the Cupola’s 3D environment and viewing Earth just as astronauts do, users can experience a true sense of space through an interactive “Simulate Weightlessness” feature that recreates the floating sensation of microgravity. To deepen engagement, it also includes interactive quizzes that test understanding of space science, Earth observation, and astronaut perspectives, making the experience both engaging and educational.

Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory

The NBL page includes a Unity-built 2D game that simulates astronaut training underwater, allowing users to experience the concept of neutral buoyancy and how it prepares astronauts for spacewalks.

By using the “Simulate Buoyancy” feature, users can feel how neutral buoyancy mimics the weightless conditions of space. A built-in quiz section follows each module, reinforcing concepts of microgravity simulation, astronaut training, and underwater physics through hands-on, fun learning.

OUR GOAL

...is to make complex space concepts accessible, visual, and enjoyable for students and the public.

The project emphasizes hands-on learning through interactivity, merging scientific accuracy with creativity.

By blending 3D visualization, web animation, and gamification, Project STaTic not only meets the challenge’s goal of showcasing ISS experiences but also highlights how these innovations inspire human progress on Earth from training methods to observational science.

"We built not just a project, but a vision" - STaTic CoDeRs

projectDetails.name: SustainaSphere
projectDetails.summary:
Our project addresses the challenge of managing, reusing, and recycling inorganic waste on Mars during long-duration missions. We have designed a sustainable, modular system that transforms accumulated waste into usable resources, such as tools, structural components, and energy solutions, using in-situ materials and automated processes.

The system integrates mechanical recycling techniques, smart resource tracking, and modular fabrication units, allowing astronauts to maximize self-sufficiency while minimizing reliance on Earth-supplied resources. By turning trash into functional materials, our solution not only reduces storage and disposal challenges but also enhances mission efficiency and crew safety.

This project is important because it enables long-term human exploration of Mars, demonstrates innovative approaches to space sustainability, and provides a model for closed-loop recycling systems that could benefit future space habitats and even extreme environments on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details

What does it do / How does it work:
Our project is a Mars waste management system that collects, sorts, and recycles inorganic waste generated by astronauts during long-duration missions. The system uses modular recycling units and automated processes to transform trash (packaging, textiles, structural materials) into usable tools, habitat components, and energy resources. The workflow is:

  1. Collect trash → 2. Sort & process → 3. Transform into resources → 4. Store or deploy for use.

Benefits:

  • Reduces the need to transport resources from Earth.
  • Minimizes storage and disposal challenges on Mars.
  • Provides astronauts with tools, energy, and building materials, increasing mission efficiency.
  • Demonstrates a sustainable approach to space exploration.

Intended Impact:

  • Supports long-term human exploration of Mars.
  • Provides a model for closed-loop recycling systems in extreme environments.
  • Could inspire sustainable recycling practices on Earth in remote or resource-limited areas.

Tools / Technologies Used:

- Frontend: React.js with Tailwind CSS for interactive dashboard

- 3D Visualization: HTML5 Canvas for real-time inventory rendering

- Icons: Lucide React for professional UI elements

- State Management: React Hooks (useState, useEffect)

- Data Simulation: Custom algorithms for waste-to-resource conversion

- Version Control: GitHub for collaboration

Creativity / Uniqueness:

  • Combines space sustainability with automation.
  • Turns trash into multiple resource types instead of a single output.
  • Modular design allows scalability and adaptability for different mission scenarios.

Factors Considered by the Team:

  • Practicality in extreme environments (limited water, energy, and human resources).
  • Efficiency and sustainability.
  • Safety and self-sufficiency for astronauts.
  • Potential real-world applications on Earth for sustainable recycling.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of AI in the Project

For this project, AI tools were utilized to accelerate design, coding, and visualization:

  1. Code Generation: ChatGPT (GPT-4/5) was used to generate JavaScript and HTML snippets, create modular functions, and provide logic for the recycling simulation.
  2. Project Planning & Content: AI helped structure the problem statement, project summary, slide content, and demo outline for clarity and presentation.
  3. Visuals & Diagrams: AI tools were used to generate Mars-themed illustrations and concept diagrams; all AI-generated images include a visible watermark or clear mention of AI origin in captions.

All AI outputs were reviewed, modified, and integrated manually to ensure originality, proper context, and compliance with NASA Space Apps rules.

projectDetails.name: Intelligent TEMPO: AI-Powered Real-Time Air Quality Prediction and Validation System
projectDetails.summary:
The project developed is a high-accuracy, intelligent Air Quality Prediction and Monitoring System for North America, integrating NASA TEMPO satellite patterns, real-time meteorological data, and official EPA AirNow observations. The core system uses advanced machine learning (Random Forest + feature engineering) to analyze historical air quality and weather data, recognize patterns, and accurately forecast AQI and atmospheric info (NO₂, humidity, temperature, etc.) for major cities. Each prediction is validated live using EPA AirNow data, with accuracy statistics displayed to the user for transparency.

The solution addresses the challenge of **quality and reliability in environmental data prediction** by moving beyond static datasets—using real API data, multiple backup mechanisms, and user-facing validation. Maps allow users to cross-check predictions against actual government data and visualize AQI trends easily. This approach is important as it makes AI-based pollution monitoring truly trustworthy, actionable for the public, and scalable for research—helping cities, health organizations, and citizens take timely action based on dynamic, verifiable air quality forecasts.
projectDetails.details: This project is an advanced Air Quality Monitoring and Prediction System that integrates NASA's TEMPO satellite data, real-time meteorological data, and official EPA AirNow observations. The system uses a sophisticated machine learning model (Random Forest with grid search) trained on extensive environmental and temporal features to analyze historical air pollution patterns and accurately predict current and forecasted AQI levels for major North American cities.The project addresses the challenge of monitoring and predicting air quality with high accuracy by combining multiple data sources, including satellite tropospheric emissions and government sensor data, to validate and refine AI predictions in real-time. Users benefit from transparent, validated AQI information, visualized through interactive maps that allow direct access to real EPA data alongside the AI model's predictions.Developed using Python with advanced ML libraries, Flask for the backend, and Leaflet.js for mapping, the system demonstrates creativity in fusing diverse data sources and applying pattern recognition algorithms tailored for environmental forecasting. The team's focus on accuracy, fallback strategies for incomplete data, and user-friendly visualization ensures that the system can effectively support public health decisions and environmental research.Overall, this project offers a transparent, reliable, and interactive platform to understand and predict air quality dynamics, contributing significantly to environmental awareness and health protection

projectDetails.name: satellite in weather forecasting
projectDetails.summary:
This project focuses on 
NASA satellite data to create a system for observing, analyzing, and accurately predicting weather. Satellites continuously monitor the Earth's atmosphere, collecting vital information on temperature, humidity, clouds, and wind. The collected data is then processed and analyzed using advanced computer models to identify weather patterns and predict future conditions. This system's primary goals are to improve prediction accuracy by providing real-time global observations and to detect and track severe weather events like hurricanes and floods early. The resulting accurate forecasts and early warnings are crucial for public safety, saving lives, protecting communities, and supporting informed decisions across various sectors.
projectDetails.details:
How the Project Works (Methodology)

The system works by following a four-step methodology to transform satellite observations into actionable forecasts:

  1. Data Collection: NASA's Earth-observing satellites (like GOES, Aqua, Terra, and Suomi NPP) use sensors (radiometers and spectrometers) to collect data on temperature, humidity, cloud cover, wind speed, and ocean conditions. These satellites capture images of swirling clouds, changing ocean colors, and shifting winds.
  2. Data Transmission: The collected information is sent to ground stations, which receive and store large volumes of real-time atmospheric data.
  3. Data Processing and Analysis: Scientists use computer models and algorithms to analyze the satellite data, detect weather patterns, identify storm systems, and estimate rainfall or temperature variations.
  4. Forecast Generation and Dissemination: Based on the analyzed data, meteorologists create accurate weather forecasts and early warnings for extreme weather events. This information is integrated with other global data sources for higher accuracy and shared with government agencies.

Benefits and Importance

The project offers significant advantages, mainly by making forecasts faster, smarter, and more helpful:

  • Severe Weather Warnings: Satellites provide constant, real-time data for tracking severe weather like thunderstorms, hurricanes, and wildfires, enabling critical public safety alerts.
  • Disaster Management: The detailed insights into hazardous conditions and their effects aid in the management of natural disasters, supporting response efforts and improving resource allocation.
  • Air Quality Monitoring: NASA satellites help monitor air quality, which allows for public health alerts advising people on limiting exposure to pollutants.
  • Early Warnings: The system helps to make accurate forecasts and give early warnings for disasters like floods and cyclones.

Intended Impact and Future Plans

The ultimate goal is for the project to make the world

safer and smarter by leveraging space technology.

  • Protecting Lives: The system is planned to protect lives by issuing critical alerts "before the storm even begin".
  • Future Enhancements: Future plans involve integrating advanced AI and Machine Learning to process atmospheric data more efficiently for superior predictive modeling.
  • Hyperlocal Forecasts: The team aims to develop personalized, hyperlocal forecasts by combining satellite data with ground-based sensor networks and IoT devices.
  • Long-Term Vision: The long-term vision is to leverage this technology for broader applications in disaster management and agriculture, contributing to a more resilient and sustainable future globally.

Tools and Creativity

While specific coding languages, hardware, or third-party software are

not explicitly listed in the provided content, the project is based on using NASA satellite data, which includes instruments like the

Advanced Baseline Imager (ABI) and the Geostationary Lightning Mapper (GLM). The system relies heavily on

computer models and algorithms to process the data.

The project's creativity lies in its plan to combine

space technology with creativity to turn complex satellite data into understandable "weather stories" that show where rain will fall and when storms may grow. The focus on protecting lives before a storm even starts is a key creative factor.

Factors Considered:

The team considered factors related to

data acquisition (capturing images and data on temperature, humidity, and storms),

processing (turning data into forecasts using computers), and the

dissemination of information (sharing with government agencies and the public through alerts). The severe weather's impact on public safety, resource allocation during disasters, and air quality were also central considerations.

projectDetails.name: Project Team J and S
projectDetails.summary:
EcoTales is a responsive single-page educational site that presents environmental issues as short scripted conversations between planets (Earth, Mars, Venus) alongside dataset/info cards (Deforestation, Ice Melting, Global Warming). It uses Tailwind CSS (CDN) with a small custom styles.css for layout utilities, Material Symbols for icons, and a minimal JS showPage(pageId) to toggle sections; the layout is a two-column responsive design that places dataset cards on the left and conversation content on the right for clarity and visual continuity.
Key points

Purpose: teach climate topics via narrated conversations and dataset summaries.
Structure: single HTML file (index.html) with separated styles.css and small inline JS.
Layout: responsive two-column grid (md+) — left info card, right conversation column; stacks on small screens.
Visuals: Material Symbols icons, Space Grotesk font, dark-mode support via .dark class.
Content: Deforestation, Ice Melting (SASSIE), Global Warming (ECOSTRESS) info cards and scripted dialogues.
Audio: narration controls removed per project changes (progress/UI placeholders removed).
Assets: expect deforestation.jpg/png in project root for the info card image.
projectDetails.details:
Project overview

EcoTales is a responsive single-page educational site that frames climate topics as short scripted conversations between planets (Earth, Mars, Venus) alongside dataset/info cards for Deforestation, Ice Melting, and Global Warming. Sections are toggled with a minimal showPage(pageId) script; the layout uses a two-column responsive design (info card left, conversation right) with dark-mode support and consistent iconography.

Key details

What it does / how it works: displays themed pages (.page elements) that are shown/hidden via a small JS function; each page pairs a dataset/info card with a conversation UI that uses Tailwind utility classes and a few custom CSS utilities in styles.css. Material Symbols provide consistent icons and Google Fonts set typography.

Benefits: creates an engaging, easy-to-navigate learning experience that pairs narrative context with concise dataset summaries; mobile-first responsive layout ensures readability across devices.

Intended impact: educate and motivate readers about environmental issues by combining storytelling and data, making scientific topics more approachable and memorable.

Tools & technologies: HTML5, Tailwind CSS (CDN + tailwind.config inline), custom CSS (styles.css), vanilla JavaScript for navigation, Google Fonts (Space Grotesk), Material Symbols icons, static assets (images like deforestation.jpg/png). Can be served via static hosting or a simple local server (python -m http.server / VS Code Live Server).

Creativity: uses personified planetary dialogues to humanize complex environmental data, and pairs those narratives with dataset cards (ECOSTRESS, SASSIE, SimAmazonia) to bridge story and science in a cohesive UI.

Team considerations: responsive layout, visual continuity (icons, colors, dark mode), accessible structure (clear headings, semantic sections), and modular content so dataset cards, conversations, and assets can be updated independently. Next priorities suggested: accessibility improvements (aria labels), optimized responsive images, and moving JS into a separate script for maintainability.
projectDetails.aiReferences:

Design & UX: AI suggested layout adjustments, spacing, alignment, icon choices (Material Symbols), and responsive behavior.

Documentation: AI produced README.md, project summary, and the project overview/impact text.

Media & data: No AI‑generated images, videos, or audio were created or embedded by the assistant — referenced image files (e.g., deforestation.jpg/png) are expected to be provided by the team and are not AI-generated by me.

projectDetails.name: Project Team PixelCrash
projectDetails.summary: Embiggen Your Eyes Explorer is an innovative platform that transforms NASA’s gigapixel and terapixel imagery of Earth, Mars, the Moon, and distant galaxies into an interactive, accessible, and educational exploration experience. The platform allows users to smoothly zoom, pan, and annotate features such as craters, dust storms, ice caps, valleys, and nebulae. AI-assisted algorithms automatically detect anomalies and highlight points of interest, while a dynamic time slider enables users to observe planetary and environmental changes over years or decades. Multi-wavelength overlays reveal structures invisible in standard imagery, enhancing scientific understanding. Gamified citizen science engages users to label features and earn badges, while shareable “space postcards” capture discoveries for educational outreach. Multi-sensory accessibility features, including audio cues and haptic feedback, allow visually impaired users to experience cosmic phenomena. Built with OpenSeadragon, Leaflet.js, React.js, and AI models in TensorFlow/PyTorch, the platform democratizes access to NASA data, advances citizen science, inspires curiosity about space, and bridges complex scientific research with public engagement in a fun, interactive, and educational way.
projectDetails.details: Embiggen Your Eyes Explorer is an advanced interactive platform that transforms NASA’s gigapixel and terapixel imagery of Earth, Mars, the Moon, and distant galaxies into an immersive, scientifically valuable, and accessible exploration experience. Users can smoothly zoom, pan, and annotate features such as craters, dust storms, ice caps, valleys, and nebulae, while AI-assisted algorithms automatically detect anomalies, unusual patterns, and points of interest across images. The platform leverages datasets from NASA missions, including Hubble Space Telescope deep-space images, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) HiRISE imagery, Terra satellite Earth imagery, and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data, ensuring authentic scientific sources are used. A dynamic time slider enables detailed comparisons over years or decades, revealing environmental changes, storm evolution, glacier retreat, and planetary surface transformations. Multi-wavelength overlays allow users to switch between visible, infrared, and ultraviolet imagery, exposing hidden structures and patterns otherwise invisible. The platform integrates gamified citizen science: users earn badges and points for accurate labeling, discovery, and verification of features, encouraging participation in real scientific analysis. AI-generated storytelling provides contextual insights, fun facts, and scale comparisons, enhancing both engagement and educational value. Multi-sensory accessibility features, including sound mapping, haptic feedback, and audio cues, allow visually impaired users to “experience” cosmic phenomena in a novel way. Users can capture their observations and create interactive, shareable “space postcards” containing metadata, highlights, and AI-generated insights. The platform is built using OpenSeadragon and Leaflet.js for efficient handling of massive datasets, React.js for a responsive interface, and Python-based AI models (TensorFlow/PyTorch) for real-time feature detection and pattern recognition. The solution is uniquely innovative and patentable because it combines AI-powered analysis, multi-sensory exploration, gamification, and time/wavelength visualization in a scalable, user-friendly system. Its intended impact is broad: democratizing access to NASA imagery, advancing citizen science, enhancing STEM education in classrooms and museums, inspiring public curiosity about space, and bridging the gap between complex scientific research and public engagement with an interactive, fun, and educational tool.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) was extensively used in the development of Embiggen Your Eyes Explorer to enhance data analysis, user interaction, and content generation. Specifically:

  1. Feature Detection and Annotation: AI models (TensorFlow/PyTorch) were trained to automatically detect craters, dust storms, ice caps, and other significant features in NASA’s gigapixel and terapixel imagery. This assists users by highlighting points of interest for annotation and verification, accelerating citizen science contributions.
  2. Pattern Recognition Across Time and Wavelengths: AI algorithms analyze multi-temporal and multi-wavelength datasets to detect environmental changes, anomalies, or hidden structures, enabling time-lapse comparison and wavelength overlay visualizations.
  3. Interactive Storytelling: AI generates contextual narratives, fun facts, and scale comparisons dynamically as users explore features, making the platform more educational and engaging.
  4. Gamification & Feedback: AI evaluates user-submitted annotations, providing real-time feedback, scoring, and validation to encourage accurate labeling and learning.
  5. Content Generation Metadata: All AI-generated narratives, analysis, and annotations are clearly marked within the platform metadata, ensuring transparency and acknowledgment of AI-assisted work.

AI was used solely as a tool to enhance exploration, analysis, and interactivity, without using or modifying any NASA branding, logos, or mission identifiers.

projectDetails.name: Stellar-Health — the AI-based medical recommendation system for astronauts that uses Chroma DB and LLMs.
projectDetails.summary:
Summary:
Stellar-Health is an AI-powered medical recommendation system designed for astronauts. It integrates structured medical datasets (like mental health and astronaut-specific data) with advanced AI technologies to provide precise, research-backed recommendations for space missions. The system leverages:

Chroma DB – for storing and querying structured medical research data.

LLM Integration – uses Google Gemini LLM to generate context-aware recommendations based on user queries and retrieved research papers.

CSV Data Integration – incorporates astronaut-specific and mental health datasets for more personalized recommendations.

Flask API Backend – provides endpoints for external apps or frontends to query the system.

Embeddings & Search – uses ONNX MiniLM for semantic search across medical data.
projectDetails.details:
Project Name:

Stellar-Health

Project Type:

AI-based Medical Recommendation System for Astronauts

Objective:

To provide astronauts and space mission medical teams with AI-driven recommendations for medications, dosage forms, packaging, and mental health interventions based on structured medical data and research papers.

Technologies Used:

  • Backend: Flask (Python) – API for query handling
    • Google Gemini LLM – generates context-aware recommendations
    • ONNX MiniLM – embeddings for semantic search
    • Mental Health Dataset
    • Astronaut-specific health dataset

Core Components:

  1. CSV Data Loader: Imports datasets into Chroma DB collections.
  2. Chroma DB Integration: Stores and retrieves medical research and astronaut-specific data.
  3. LLM Recommendation Engine: Uses retrieved data to generate AI-driven recommendations.
  4. Flask API: Provides network-accessible endpoints for querying the system.
  5. Embeddings & Semantic Search: Allows searching relevant research papers based on query context.

Features:

  • Generates AI-driven recommendations for over-the-counter drugs.
  • Suggests dosage forms and packaging materials suitable for space missions.
  • Provides mental health recommendations for astronauts.
  • Combines structured research data with LLM reasoning for accurate suggestions.
  • Accessible via a network API for integration with other tools or frontends.

Workflow:

  1. Load datasets (Mental Health, Astronauts) into Chroma DB.
  2. Query Chroma DB for relevant research papers.
  3. Pass retrieved data and user input to Google Gemini LLM.
  4. LLM generates structured, actionable recommendations.
  5. Recommendations returned via API or frontend.

Use Case:

  • Supports space mission medical teams in making evidence-based decisions.
  • Ensures astronaut health is monitored and managed effectively during missions.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used Artificial Intelligence in the project Stellar-Health as follows:

  • Integrated Google Gemini LLM to generate AI-based medical recommendations for astronauts.
  • Used ONNX MiniLM embeddings for semantic search and retrieving relevant medical research from Chroma DB.
  • Combined structured datasets and research papers to allow the AI to provide context-aware suggestions for medications, dosage forms, packaging, and mental health interventions.

projectDetails.name: Project TechnoNova
projectDetails.summary: Our project, BloomWatch, is an Earth observation application designed to monitor and analyze global flowering phenology using satellite imagery, climate data, and machine learning. It identifies the timing and distribution of plant blooming events across regions to understand how environmental factors like temperature, precipitation, and climate change influence flowering patterns. By integrating NASA’s Earth observation datasets with AI-driven analysis, BloomWatch provides real-time insights and visualizations to researchers, ecologists, and policymakers. This tool helps track ecosystem changes, support biodiversity conservation, and predict agricultural trends impacted by climate shifts. Addressing the challenge of monitoring global ecological health, BloomWatch promotes data-driven decisions for sustainable environmental management and strengthens our understanding of how Earth’s changing climate affects natural life cycles.
projectDetails.details:
BloomWatch is an interactive Earth observation platform designed to monitor global flowering phenology using NASA satellite data, climate variables, and AI-driven analytics. The system identifies the timing, frequency, and intensity of flower blooms across different geographic regions, helping track how climate change and environmental conditions influence plant life cycles.

The project integrates remote sensing data (MODIS, Landsat, and Sentinel), climate APIs, and machine learning models to analyze vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI) and predict bloom events. Built using Python, TensorFlow, OpenCV, Leaflet.js, and React, it visualizes bloom maps and trends in an intuitive, user-friendly interface.

BloomWatch benefits ecologists, farmers, and policymakers by offering data-driven insights for biodiversity conservation, pollination studies, and crop planning. Its creative approach combines AI with space-based Earth observation to translate complex data into actionable environmental intelligence. Our team focused on global usability, data accuracy, and sustainability awareness, aiming to make climate-driven phenological monitoring accessible to all.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used Artificial Intelligence in BloomWatch to analyze satellite imagery and environmental data for detecting and predicting flowering patterns globally. We also used the AI to get help in debugging the error of our project. Machine learning models were trained on historical datasets (temperature, precipitation, and vegetation indices) to identify correlations influencing bloom timing. Computer vision techniques were used to process Earth observation images, detect bloom-rich areas, and classify vegetation health using NDVI-based features. AI-driven analysis enables automated pattern recognition and predictive modeling, providing accurate insights into how climate variations affect flowering phenology. No AI-generated images, audio, or videos were used; AI was applied solely for data analysis and prediction within the code.
projectDetails.dataReferences: [NASA MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) Vegetation Indices (NDVI/EVI)](https://modis.gsfc.nasa.gov/data/dataprod/mod13.php)

challengeDetails.title: BloomWatch: An Earth Observation Application for Global Flowering Phenology
challengeDetails.excerpt: Witness the pulse of life across our planet! From season to season and year to year, Earth’s vegetation is constantly changing, providing critical information on plant species, crops, seasonal effects, pollen sources, and changes in plant phenology (the relationship between seasonal changes and climate and biological phenomena in plants). Your challenge is to harness the power of NASA Earth observations to create a dynamic visual tool that displays and/or detects plant blooming events around the globe—just like pollinators do–and that advances solutions for monitoring, predicting, or managing vegetation. (Earth Science Division)

challengeDetails.title: Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings
challengeDetails.excerpt: Although the Sun is 93 million miles away from our planet, solar activity can significantly impact our daily lives. “Space weather”—the variations that occur in the space environment between the Sun and Earth—can impact technologies in space and on Earth. Your challenge is to write and illustrate a digital children’s story that explains what space weather is and the varying impacts it has on different people such as farmers, pilots, astronauts, power grid operators, and the general public. You can tell the story from the perspective of a person impacted by space weather or from the point of view of a solar flare or coronal mass ejection (CME) as it approaches Earth. (Heliophysics Division)

projectDetails.name: DisasterScope: Real-Time Satellite-Driven Emergency Mapping Tool
projectDetails.summary:
The NASA Disaster Mapping Tool is a web-based platform designed to help emergency responders act quickly and effectively during natural disasters. It combines NASA’s satellite data with live information from the ground—such as weather updates, IoT sensors, and even social media—to give a clear picture of what’s happening in real time.

At the center of the tool is an interactive map that shows active disasters with markers, severity levels, and layered details. Responders can immediately see which areas are most at risk. The system also generates risk scores by analyzing factors like population density and disaster intensity, helping authorities prioritize their efforts.

Beyond monitoring, the tool supports evacuation planning by calculating safe, optimized routes that avoid danger zones. It also guides resource allocation, ensuring medical teams, supplies, and rescue units are sent where they’re needed most.

A unique feature is its predictive analytics. By studying historical patterns with AI, it can forecast how disasters may spread or intensify, allowing better preparation for the future.

Built with modern web technologies, the tool is easy to use and works right away with NASA’s EONET data. More than just maps, it’s a life-saving command center for smarter disaster response.
projectDetails.details: Our project is a web-based disaster response platform that integrates NASA’s satellite data (EONET, MODIS, VIIRS, Landsat, Sentinel) with real-time ground sources such as weather services, IoT sensors, and social media to help emergency teams respond faster and smarter. It works by visualizing disasters on an interactive map, generating automated risk scores, providing real-time alerts, and suggesting safe evacuation routes, while also using AI-driven predictive analytics to forecast disaster trends. The key benefits include quicker decision-making, better resource allocation, improved public safety, and stronger preparedness against natural hazards. The intended impact is to save lives and reduce damage by turning complex geospatial data into clear, actionable insights for governments, NGOs, and local communities. Built with React, Next.js, and TypeScript, styled using Tailwind CSS, and supported by geospatial APIs, the system is designed for both accessibility and scalability. Its creativity lies in fusing space-based science with human-centered design—transforming overwhelming data into practical guidance for real-world disaster scenarios. In building it, our team focused on usability, reliability, accuracy, and social impact to ensure the tool not only works technically but also makes a meaningful difference in crisis management.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our project was primarily developed through original team work, with minimal use of AI tools. The core coding, design, and implementation of the disaster mapping platform were completed by our team members using standard development tools and frameworks (React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, NASA EONET APIs, and geospatial libraries).

AI assistance was used only in a limited capacity to help refine descriptive project documentation and to summarize lengthy text during the drafting phase. No AI-generated code, data, images, videos, or audio were included in the final project. All maps, visualizations, and datasets come directly from trusted sources such as NASA APIs and open geospatial libraries, ensuring technical integrity and originality.

By keeping AI involvement minimal and transparent, we ensured that the project reflects our own problem-solving skills, creativity, and technical execution, while using AI only as a light support tool for clarity in communication.

projectDetails.name: Staristry
projectDetails.summary:
summary - The Staristry project is a dynamic, single-page educational website dedicated to the Pleiades star cluster (M45), also known as the Seven Sisters. 🔭

What We Developed: We created a visually stunning, dark-mode website that fuses core astronomy data with the rich cultural mythology of the cluster. The site uses a simple, scrollable narrative to ensure maximum engagement and mobile accessibility.

How We Addressed the Challenge: The challenge in educational content is often engagement. We overcame this by moving beyond dry facts, using a "Staristry" (Star + History/Story) framework. Furthermore, the project demonstrates an efficient, low-cost approach by leveraging an AI website generator from a single detailed prompt, significantly reducing development time.

Why It's Important: The project democratizes astronomy knowledge by making a complex topic beautiful and easy to digest for students and the general public. It inspires curiosity by showing how ancient history and modern science are intertwined.
projectDetails.details:
Project Name: Staristry

What it Does/How it Works: Staristry is a single-page educational website that explores the celestial connection between science and culture, specifically focusing on the Pleiades Star Cluster (Messier 45). It uses a clean, dark-mode design to present content in five key scrolling sections: astronomical facts, cultural mythologies (Greek, Japanese, Māori, etc.), and a call to action. It works by presenting accurate NASA data alongside engaging historical narratives to provide a multi-layered educational experience.

Benefits & Intended Impact: The project aims to increase public scientific literacy by making complex astronomical facts relatable through storytelling. Its intended impact is to bridge the gap between STEM and the Humanities, fostering a deeper appreciation for how celestial bodies have influenced human culture globally, consistent with NASA's open data outreach goals.

Tools & Languages: The project was built using standard web technologies: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Development speed was accelerated using an AI Website Generator for initial boilerplate code and a Large Language Model (LLM) for refining and summarizing descriptive text and code documentation. AI Image Generation was used for unique, non-NASA-branded visual assets.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Creativity lies in the interdisciplinary approach—using AI not just for code, but for content synthesis and design inspiration. We considered accessibility, ensuring clear text and high contrast, and the official challenge rules, mandating clear acknowledgment and watermarking of all AI-generated content.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We utilized AI in three key areas:

AI Website Generator: Used a natural language prompt to rapidly create the site's structure, HTML/CSS, and dark-mode design, maximizing development speed.

Large Language Models (LLMs): Employed for drafting and refining all educational text, ensuring content was accessible, engaging, and balanced between science and mythology.

AI Image Generation: Used to create custom cosmic textures and stylized mythological illustrations that avoid NASA branding. (All such images are watermarked as AI-generated). WE ALSO USED NASA RESOURCES FOR IMAGES.

🛰️ SatLink – Simplifying Satellite Link Budget Analysis

projectDetails.details:
🛰️ SatLink – Smart Satellite Link Budget Analysis Made Simple

🚀 SatLink is a Python-based, open-source tool built to simplify satellite downlink and link budget calculations.
It bridges the gap between academic research and real-world satellite engineering, offering a user-friendly approach to complex space communication analysis.

Designed for students, researchers, engineers, and enthusiasts, SatLink provides both Graphical (GUI) and Python scripting interfaces — making it ideal for learning, teaching, and professional use.

🌌 🎯 Core Purpose & Mission

  • 🔹 Simplify and automate satellite link budget calculations
  • 🔹 Serve as a learning tool for satellite communication principles
  • 🔹 Provide intuitive GUI and web interfaces for easy access
  • 🔹 Make satellite communication analysis accessible to everyone

⚙️ 🔑 Key Functionalities

🌦️ Atmospheric Attenuation

  • Implements ITU-R P. Recommendations through the itur library
  • Calculates slant and horizontal path losses
  • Considers weather and atmospheric effects on signal quality

📡 Downlink Availability Analysis

  • Supports single-point and multi-point calculations
  • CSV input/output for bulk data analysis
  • Computes availability percentages (0–100%) with statistical precision

🛰️ Antenna Sizing & Optimization

  • Estimates antenna size for desired link availability
  • Generates visual plots for quick interpretation
  • Outputs CSV reports for multi-site analysis

🧩 Parameter Management

  • Save and load satellite, ground station, and reception configurations
  • Use predefined templates for recurring scenarios
  • Streamline simulation workflows for faster testing

💻 🧠 Technical Architecture

  • 🛰️ Satellite Class – Defines satellite parameters (frequency, EIRP, altitude, etc.)
  • 🏗️ Ground Station Class – Configures geographic position and local parameters
  • 📶 Reception Class – Models receiver chain (antenna, LNB, cable losses, etc.)

🧰 Core Libraries:
itur, PyQt5, Pandas, Astropy, NumPy, tqdm, pathos

🖥️ 🌐 User Interfaces

🪟 Graphical Interface (GUI)

  • Built using PyQt5
  • Clean, menu-based design for simple interaction
  • Customizable via the “model” folder
  • Run via: main_window.py

☁️ Web Application (Streamlit)

  • Fully deployable browser-based tool
  • Dockerfile included for easy setup
  • Run via: satlink_web.py

💻 Python Script Mode

  • For developers and advanced users
  • Direct access to core functions for automated workflows

🧭 🔧 Installation

Requirements: Python 3 + essential dependencies
Install everything quickly:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Or for Linux users:

sudo apt install build-essentials gcc g++ python3-pyqt5

Run the app:

python main_window.py

🚧 🌠 Future Roadmap

✨ Worst-month availability estimation
🗺️ Map-based coverage visualization
💡 Enhanced web UI & real-time analytics
📶 Advanced XPD (Cross-Polar Discrimination) modeling

🤝 👨‍💻 Project Leadership & Credits

Lead Developer: Prajwal S
📩 Contact: prajuthejonidhi1001@gmail.com
🎨 Logo Design: Prajwal S
🌍 Supported By: Globo

🎓 🌍 Target Audience

  • 🧑‍🎓 Students & Educators in Satellite Communications
  • 🛰️ Engineers & Researchers in Space Systems
  • 🧑‍💻 Developers building space-related simulation tools
  • 🌠 Space enthusiasts exploring signal propagation and satellite behavior

projectDetails.details:
The Cosmic Commute App is an interactive 3D solar system experience that helps users explore planetary orbits, distances, and physical properties in real-time. Using NASA’s open data, it creates a scientifically accurate and visually engaging space learning tool. Designed for accessibility and education, the app simplifies complex astronomical concepts and has the potential to expand into AR/VR and live space mission integrations.

  • Users navigate a 3D solar system with rotating planets, orbits, and real-time physics.
  •  the UI blends engaging visuals with educational functionalities like distance calculators, weight converters and also the glimpse about the upcoming space missions t is perfect for the curious minds and space enthusiasts
  •  The website creates a feeling of “traveling through space” from any browser.
  • DATA AND TECHNOLOGY: The core
  • Foundation Data: We use JPL Horizons data for precise, real-time orbital positions and NASA/ESA fact sheets for physical constants.
  • 3D Visualization: Built on Next.js, using Three.js and @react-three/fiber to render an interactive, accurate 3D Solar System.
  • Calculations: The logic employs simplified orbital mechanics (Hohmann-like transfer model) to calculate path and duration.
  • UX/UI: Modern, responsive interface using Tailwind CSS and the shadcn/ui component library.
  •  Impact & Outcome: Who Benefits?
  • Education: Transforms abstract math into a tangible, visual learning experience for students and enthusiasts.
  • Public Engagement: Increases public literacy and sparks interest in STEM fields by making complex space concepts accessible.
  • Scalability: Open architecture allows for easy expansion to add new propulsion technologies or celestial bodies

projectDetails.name: Your Home in space: The Habitat Layout Creator
projectDetails.summary:
HABICON is an interactive and gamified space habitat design tool created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2024. It was built with one goal in mind — to make the complex process of designing human habitats for space both educational and fun.

Using a simple 2D visual canvas, users can sketch, plan, and customize habitats by adjusting real mission parameters like crew size, duration, and available space. HABICON turns technical design into a creative experience where students, researchers, and enthusiasts can experiment with ideas that could shape the future of living beyond Earth.

The tool helps make space engineering more accessible and engaging, encouraging people to think critically about sustainability and innovation in extreme environments. In the future, HABICON aims to evolve into a 3D immersive platform, giving users the chance to virtually step inside their creations and experience what life in space might truly feel like.
projectDetails.details: HABICON is an interactive and gamified 2D space habitat design tool created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2024. It allows users to design and visualize space habitats by adjusting mission parameters such as crew size, duration, and available resources through an intuitive visual interface. Built using Python (PyQt5) and React, HABICON combines data-driven logic with engaging design to make space engineering concepts accessible to students, researchers, and enthusiasts. The tool promotes STEM learning, creativity, and problem-solving by turning technical design into a hands-on, exploratory experience. Its benefits include enhancing spatial understanding, encouraging sustainable thinking for space habitation, and bridging the gap between professional research and public engagement. The team focused on creating a balance between scientific accuracy and user experience, ensuring the interface was simple yet informative. Future plans include adding 3D immersive visualization for deeper interactivity, inspiring users to imagine and build the future of life beyond Earth.
projectDetails.aiReferences: AI tools were used to identify and fix coding errors, improve functionality, and make the project more realistic. ChatGPT helped debug issues, refine the logic behind habitat simulations, and suggest better ways to visualize and organize features. It also assisted in making the habitat layouts more accurate and practical, aligning the project closer to real-world space design concepts.

projectDetails.name: Project YODHA
projectDetails.summary:
We developed *SpaceShield*, a React-based web application for the 2025 NASA Space Apps Challenge, designed to predict weather conditions for outdoor events like parades. Using TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and APIs including NASA POWER, OpenWeatherMap, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and NewsAPI, it delivers real-time weather forecasts and global hazard alerts. Users input a city, event name, and date to receive current weather data (precipitation, wind, humidity, temperature) and a 5-day forecast, with hazard notifications for extreme conditions (e.g., heavy rain, high winds). The space-themed UI, featuring a StarField component and toast notifications (Sonner), enhances user experience.

This addresses the challenge by leveraging NASA’s open data for climate and weather intelligence, ensuring safe event planning. It’s important because it empowers users to mitigate weather-related risks, protecting outdoor activities from disruptions caused by adverse conditions. By integrating multiple data sources and providing actionable insights, *SpaceShield* promotes resilience against climate challenges, making it a valuable tool for communities world
projectDetails.details:
Space Shield - Will It Rain on My Parade?

Functionality

Space Shield is a web application developed to assist in planning outdoor events by providing accurate weather forecasts. Users input a city, event name, and date through an ''intuitive interface''. The application employs the ''OpenStreetMap Nominatim API'to geocode locations, retrieves current weather and ''five-day forecasts'' from the Open Weather Map API, and aggregates global hazard alerts via the News API. It delivers real-time notifications** for conditions such as excessive precipitation or wind, presented in a visually engaging dashboard with a space-themed design.

Benefits

The application offers reliable weather insights, enabling users to mitigate risks of event disruptions. Targeted hazard alerts enhance safety, and its accessible design ensures usability across devices, streamlining weather-related decision-making for non-technical users.

Intended Impact

SpaceShield promotes climate resilience by leveraging NASA POWER API data, aligning with NASA’s Earth observation objectives. It aims to minimize event cancellations and foster informed planning, potentially inspiring scalable tools for community safety amid climate variability.

Technologies Employed

Developed using TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and Tailwind CSS. It integrates NASA POWER, OpenWeatherMap, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and NewsAPI. Custom components include StarField, ParadeForm, and WeatherDashboard, built on standard computers and tested in web browsers.

Innovative Aspects

The space-inspired aesthetic, featuring animated stars and neon typography, enhances user engagement. Unique hazard detection and global alert integration distinguish it, creatively combining local and worldwide weather data for comprehensive insights.

Considerations

The team prioritized user accessibility, data accuracy, and privacy by avoiding data storage. The application is responsive, scalable, and aligned with NASA’s mission. Developed within hackathon constraints, it maintains transparency by crediting data sources in the interface.

projectDetails.name: AGRO-PLASTI-GUARD
projectDetails.summary:
What:
AGRO-PLASTI-GUARD is a web platform delivering dual-layer intelligence: calculating Microplastic-induced Soil Degradation (M-SVI) risk and providing adaptive, real-time farm advice.

How:
It integrates NASA geospatial data (via Microsoft Planetary Computer), Meteomatics weather, and AI to quantify M-SVI. This triggers CRITICAL ALERTS for topsoil loss and gives M-SVI-weighted recommendations (e.g., Vetiver planting) to prevent erosion.

Why Important:
It uniquely tackles the silent crisis of microplastic-accelerated soil degradation, providing farmers with critical foresight and actionable steps to protect their soil, ensure food security, and build climate resilience where current systems fail.
projectDetails.details:
What it Does & How it Works: AGRO-PLASTI-GUARD is a web platform that calculates Microplastic-induced Soil Degradation (M-SVI) using NASA data (from Microsoft Planetary Computer) and AI (trained on Azure). It integrates this M-SVI with Meteomatics weather data to trigger CRITICAL ALERTS and provide M-SVI-weighted recommendations (e.g., "Plant Vetiver Grass") for soil protection. It runs on a Google Cloud/Firebase hosted UI with Google Maps API.

Benefits & Intended Impact: It empowers farmers to protect their soil and financial capital by turning an invisible, irreversible microplastic threat into a manageable risk. This ensures food security, climate resilience, and sustainable agriculture by delivering precise, actionable, adaptive advice where current systems fail.

Tools Used: Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS. Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (Firebase, Maps API), Microsoft Azure. Data: Microsoft Planetary Computer (NASA data), Meteomatics API. Dev: GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, Miro, Teams. Domain: GoDaddy.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Our creativity lies in the novel M-SVI metric and the dual-layer intelligence combining long-term risk with real-time weather for adaptive, prioritized actions. We focused on farmer usability, data accuracy (NASA, Meteomatics), scalability (Azure, GCP), and maximizing Global Offer integration to address the urgent dual crisis of soil degradation and microplastic contamination.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
M-SVI Prediction: A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) processes NASA satellite imagery (from Microsoft Planetary Computer) to predict the Microplastic-induced Soil Degradation (M-SVI) score.

Code Acceleration: GitHub Copilot / Microsoft Copilot assisted in generating Python (data processing) and JavaScript (frontend) code.
