projectDetails.name: B.A.S.I.S - Building Assistant & Simulation Intelligence System
projectDetails.summary:
The B.A.S.I.S. (Building Assistant & Simulation Intelligence System) project revolutionizes space habitat design by making it more accessible, collaborative, and innovative. Traditionally, habitat creation relies on small groups of experts, leading to slow and costly development. B.A.S.I.S. overcomes this by offering an open-source, educational, and space engineering software aimed at higher education and research.

It enables users to design habitats for extreme planetary environments using an AI Co-Pilot trained with constantly updated data from NASA and other agencies. The interface supports 2D and 3D modeling with real-time calculations of mass, volume, energy, and thermal parameters. An environmental simulation module tests structural durability under harsh conditions, while its modular system allows independent component design.

The core innovation is its multifunctional AI, which acts as an interactive mentor—encouraging critical thinking, detecting design flaws, and providing access to validated engineering templates. Moreover, B.A.S.I.S. promotes global collaboration by inviting users with promising projects to submit them for peer review within an international scientific network. Approved proposals can be forwarded to space agencies.

By integrating artificial intelligence, research, and education, B.A.S.I.S. transforms space habitat design into a dynamic, inclusive, and globally connected experience.
projectDetails.details:
Detalhes do Projeto B.A.S.I.S.

O B.A.S.I.S. é um Software Educacional e de Engenharia Espacial de código aberto de nível ensino superior, focado na concepção e no design modular de habitats em ambientes planetários adversos. Ele se propõe a democratizar o desenvolvimento de habitats espaciais, superando o funil de desenvolvimento restrito atual.

O que o B.A.S.I.S. faz e como funciona?

O software funciona em duas camadas principais: uma Interface de Design Intuitiva e Modular e uma Inteligência Artificial Co-Piloto (IA) multifuncional.

  1. Interface de Design e Engenharia:
    • Criação 2D e 3D: Inspirada em softwares CAD contemporâneos (como SolidWorks ou SolidEdge/FreeCAD), a interface permite aos usuários criar plantas e esquemas bidimensionais (2D) e, em seguida, fazer sua extrusão para modelos tridimensionais (3D).
      • Massa total.
      • Volume pressurizado.
      • Demanda energética estimada.
      • Área de superfície para análise térmica.
      • Entre outros mais complexos.
    • Módulo de Simulação: Integra um módulo para modelar as condições ambientais extremas do planeta-alvo. Isso permite avaliar a durabilidade, vida útil dos materiais e resistência estrutural do habitat contra eventos extremos.
    • A IA é o diferencial estratégico do B.A.S.I.S., treinada com um repositório de dados da NASA e de outras agências.
    • Instigação e Resolução de Problemas: Em vez de dar respostas diretas, a IA formula perguntas analíticas baseadas no projeto, forçando o usuário a conceber ativamente a solução, estimulando o raciocínio crítico.
    • Detecção Proativa de Falhas: Identifica e aponta falhas no projeto que seriam normalmente ignoradas, exercitando a capacidade de aplicação do conhecimento do usuário em cenários complexos.
    • Base de Conhecimento e Templates: Atua como um banco de dados dinâmico, permitindo a consulta a ideias existentes, testadas e validadas por agências, facilitando o uso de templates ou soluções de engenharia reconhecidas.

Benefícios e Impacto Pretendido

Benefícios

  • Democratização da Engenharia Espacial: Reduz a dependência de um pequeno grupo de especialistas, abrindo o campo para estudantes e uma comunidade global de inovadores.
  • Aceleração do Ciclo de Desenvolvimento: Transforma o processo de design longo e caro, tornando-o mais acessível e rápido através da assistência da IA e da natureza de código aberto.
  • Desenvolvimento de Habilidades: Promove ativamente o desenvolvimento do raciocínio crítico e de capacidades técnicas ao desafiar o usuário a resolver problemas propostos pela IA.
  • Redução de Riscos/Custos: Permite a experimentação de baixo custo e a detecção precoce de falhas através da simulação e da análise proativa da IA.
  • Convergência Academia-Indústria: Fornece aos estudantes de engenharia a ferramenta de que precisam para aplicar a teoria a desafios espaciais do mundo real.

Impacto Pretendido

O principal impacto é a geração de soluções inovadoras e inéditas para habitats espaciais.

  • Contribuição Científica Formal: O software visa a criar um mecanismo de validação global para propostas de alto valor. Se a IA classificar uma solução como inovadora e a simulação interna validar, o usuário pode liberá-la para uma rede de revisão por pares de cientistas e engenheiros voluntários.
  • Encaminhamento Formal: Soluções validadas e endossadas pela comunidade técnica do B.A.S.I.S. ganharão o aval para serem encaminhadas como Propostas Formais à NASA ou à agência espacial pertinente. Isso maximiza a convergência de talentos globais e permite que novas perspectivas alimentem a inovação na engenharia espacial.

Aspectos Técnicos e Criatividade

Ferramentas, Linguagens e Software Utilizados

Embora o projeto seja uma proposta, a natureza e as funcionalidades implicam o uso de ferramentas específicas, o que demonstra a viabilidade da ideia:

  • Linguagens de Programação:
    • Para a Interface e Lógica Central: Linguagens como C++ (para performance) ou Python (para prototipagem e integração da IA), combinadas com frameworks de interface gráfica (ex: Qt, Tkinter) ou game engines (ex: Unity, Unreal Engine) para a visualização 3D.
    • Para a IA Co-Piloto: Python seria ideal, utilizando bibliotecas de Machine Learning como TensorFlow ou PyTorch para o treinamento e a implementação do modelo de IA (provavelmente um modelo de linguagem ou raciocínio baseado em regras e dados técnicos).
    • Design/Visualização 3D: Bibliotecas de código aberto como OpenCASCADE Technology ou o uso de engines de jogos.
    • Simulação: Bibliotecas para computação física e simulação numérica para modelar as condições planetárias e a resistência estrutural (ex: NumPy/SciPy para cálculos).
    • Repositório de Dados: O uso de um repositório de dados da NASA e outras agências é crucial para treinar a IA.

Criatividade do Projeto

A criatividade do B.A.S.I.S. é excepcionalmente alta e estratégica, pois reside no papel que a IA desempenha no processo de design e no modelo de contribuição científica.

  • IA como "Professor" e "Desafiador": A maior inovação é afastar a IA do modelo de "solucionador" direto para o modelo de "mentor" ou "instigador". Ao formular perguntas analíticas e apontar falhas sem dar a solução, o B.A.S.I.S. estimula a solução ativa de problemas e o desenvolvimento de raciocínio crítico no usuário. Isso transforma o software em uma ferramenta de aprendizado de nível avançado.
  • Modelo de Validação Colaborativa: A criação de uma ponte entre o software e a agência espacial por meio de uma rede de revisão por pares voluntária global é um mecanismo de inovação criativo e prático. Ele garante que ideias promissoras, geradas por um grupo diversificado de usuários, recebam a validação técnica formal necessária para serem consideradas por agências como a NASA.

Fatores Considerados pela Equipe

A equipe considerou múltiplos fatores para garantir que o projeto fosse relevante, viável e impactante:

  1. O Funil Restritivo de Engenharia Espacial: O principal fator de problema, reconhecendo que a exploração espacial precisa de mais mentes e um processo mais rápido e barato.
  2. Necessidade Educacional/Acadêmica: A carência de ferramentas práticas para estudantes de engenharia aplicarem conhecimentos a desafios espaciais. O projeto visa preencher essa lacuna.

projectDetails.name: Trail Weather AI
projectDetails.summary:
TrailWeather AI is a route-based weather intelligence tool that redefines how travelers and field teams plan their journeys. 

Instead of static forecasts for single points, it analyzes the entire route between a start and destination, calculating segment-by-segment weather conditions based on when the user will actually reach each location. Using NASA POWER’s climate data - temperature, precipitation, wind, radiation, and soil moisture - the system provides time-synchronized, route-aware insights that reveal localized risks and microclimates often missed by traditional apps. 

Built in 48 hours during NASA Space Apps, our prototype combines React, Leaflet, and NASA APIs to turn complex satellite data into a simple, visual, and actionable forecast map. This approach empowers hikers, cyclists, and professionals to make safer, better-informed decisions - showcasing how space-based Earth observation can directly improve safety and planning on the ground.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TrailWeather AI is a route-based weather intelligence tool that transforms how travelers understand environmental conditions along their journey. Unlike conventional weather apps that provide point forecasts, our prototype takes a start and end location, generates the optimal route between them, and delivers segment-by-segment weather insights based on when the user will actually be at each location.

How it works:

  1. Temporal Mapping: Users specify their travel date and average speed. The system calculates when they'll reach each segment of the route.
  2. Route Planning: Users input point A (start) and point B (destination). The system uses Leaflet's routing capabilities to generate the optimal path.
    • Temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOT), and wind speed (WS10M)
    • Atmospheric pressure (SLP) and cloud coverage (CLD_AMT)
    • Solar and infrared radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, ALLSKY_SFC_LW_DWN)
    • Soil moisture at multiple depths (GWETTOP, GWETROOT, GWETPROF)
  3. Weather Prediction: Using historical patterns from NASA's data, we extrapolate conditions for the travel date and generate segment-specific forecasts.
  4. Visual Intelligence: The route is displayed on an interactive map with intuitive emoji indicators showing weather conditions at each segment. Hovering over any emoji reveals detailed meteorological information for that specific location and time.

What benefits does it have?

Route-centric awareness: Instead of checking weather at arbitrary points, travelers see conditions evolving along their actual path, revealing microclimates and localized hazards they would otherwise miss.

Time-synchronized forecasts: By accounting for travel speed, the system shows what conditions will be like when you're actually there, not just generic daily forecasts.

Actionable insights: The visual map interface makes it immediately clear which segments might be challenging, enabling better planning decisions (alternate timing, route adjustments, or additional preparation).

NASA data accessibility: We transform NASA's rich Earth observation datasets into practical, user-friendly guidance for everyday travelers, demonstrating the real-world value of space agency research.

What is the intended impact?

For recreational users: Hikers, cyclists, and road trippers gain safer, more informed journey planning, reducing exposure to unexpected weather hazards.

For professional operations: Event organizers, search and rescue teams, and field researchers can make better go/no-go decisions and optimize timing to balance safety with mission success.

For the broader community: By making NASA's Earth observation data accessible and actionable, we demonstrate how space-based science directly improves ground-level decision-making and safety.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

Frontend & Visualization:

  • React for the web application interface
  • Leaflet for interactive mapping and route generation
  • JavaScript for data processing and user interactions

Data Source:

  • NASA POWER API as the primary meteorological data source
  • Real historical climate data across 12 key parameters (atmospheric, radiation, and soil moisture variables)

Development & Collaboration:

  • Git/GitHub for version control and team collaboration (https://github.com/hcsilva/path-wise-chatter)
  • 48-hour hackathon sprint with a multidisciplinary team

Team Composition:

  • Developers (frontend implementation and API integration)
  • Data Scientists (weather data analysis and extrapolation logic)
  • Designer (user experience and visual interface)

How is the project creative?

Route as the forecast object: We fundamentally reconceived weather forecasting. Instead of "what's the weather in location X?", we answer "what weather will I experience traveling from A to B at time T and speed V?"

Temporal intelligence: By incorporating travel speed and departure time, we create a personalized weather timeline that matches the user's actual experience, not abstract area forecasts.

NASA data democratization: We bridge the gap between high-fidelity Earth observation datasets and everyday decision-making, making space agency research immediately useful to regular travelers.

Minimalist but informative UI: Emoji-based visual indicators provide instant comprehension, while detailed data remains one hover away—balancing simplicity with depth.

Rapid prototyping approach: In 48 hours, we proved the concept end-to-end: real NASA data, real routing, real user interface - demonstrating both technical feasibility and user value.

What factors did the team consider?

Data reliability and honesty: We use NASA POWER's validated historical data and clearly communicate that forecasts are extrapolations based on historical patterns, not real-time predictions. This keeps expectations realistic while demonstrating the approach's potential.

User experience: We prioritized an intuitive interface that non-technical users can understand immediately. Weather complexity is hidden behind simple visual indicators, with details available on demand.

Scalability path: While our 48-hour prototype queries NASA POWER directly from the frontend, we designed with awareness of how this could evolve (backend caching, machine learning models like LSTM for sophisticated temporal predictions, ensemble forecasting).

Practical constraints: We focused on core functionality that proves the concept rather than trying to build a production-ready system in 48 hours. The working prototype demonstrates value and feasibility for future development.

Team collaboration: With developers, data scientists, and designers working in parallel, we maximized our limited time by clearly dividing responsibilities while maintaining constant communication.

Open source and transparency: Our GitHub repository documents our approach and makes the project accessible for review, learning, and potential future development by the community.

Future Vision: While our current prototype uses historical extrapolation, the architecture is designed to accommodate machine learning models (such as LSTM networks) that could learn terrain-aware, temporal patterns from NASA's multi-parameter datasets, providing increasingly sophisticated forecasts as the system evolves.

projectDetails.name: Project ExoIA
projectDetails.summary:
We are ExoIA.
Our project offers a solution to the exoplanet discovery process, which is currently manual, time-consuming, and faces several challenges such as stellar noise and analytical complexity.

We have developed software that uses artificial intelligence to discover new exoplanets — assisting both researchers in the field with detection and cataloging of known planets, and the general public who wish to learn more about this area.

Our solution analyzes images and data from space telescopes in the background, and whenever a new exoplanet is discovered, it is automatically cataloged on our website — for instance, the fictional discovery of Kepler-186 b.

This will make the discovery of new exoplanets faster and help build a larger and more comprehensive database.
We count on your support to invest in our project and help make this advancement a reality.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details – EXOIA

What it does and how it works:
EXOIA is an Artificial Intelligence system designed to interpret astronomical data in real time and automatically identify new exoplanets from observations made by space telescopes such as the James Webb Space Telescope and the Kepler Telescope.
The system uses machine learning models and one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (CNN-1D) to analyze light curves and detect small brightness variations in stars — the so-called planetary transits.
When a user searches for the name of a star through the interface, EXOIA accesses public data from these missions, displays all known exoplanets associated with that star, and simultaneously processes recent data to identify potential new exoplanets not yet cataloged.

Project benefits:

  • Automates the exoplanet discovery process, reducing analysis time from weeks to minutes.
  • Increases scientific accuracy, decreasing false positives by combining supervised AI models with anomaly-detection neural networks.
  • Democratizes access to astronomical research, allowing scientists, students, and enthusiasts to explore space data in an accessible and visual way.
  • Creates an interactive scientific exploration environment, where users can visually track monitored stars and discoveries in real time.

Intended impact:
The main goal of EXOIA is to make exoplanetary research faster, more open, and collaborative.
By interpreting live data and presenting results intuitively, the project aims to:

  • Support scientists in the initial screening of exoplanet candidates;
  • Encourage science education, integrating AI and astronomy into dynamic learning experiences;
  • Foster new discoveries through continuous learning that detects subtle signals potentially indicating yet-unconfirmed planets.

Tools, languages, and technologies used:

  • Programming Languages: Python (for Machine Learning and backend), JavaScript/React (for the interactive web interface).
  • Libraries and Frameworks:
    • TensorFlow and PyTorch (AI modeling);
    • Scikit-learn and LightGBM (post-processing and false-positive reduction);
    • Plotly and Three.js (3D visualization and interactive star maps).
  • Data Sources: NASA Exoplanet Archive, Kepler/TESS Light Curves, JWST Open Data.
  • Infrastructure: NASA public APIs and a real-time data analysis pipeline hosted in the cloud (Google Colab / Hugging Face Spaces for prototyping).

Creativity and uniqueness:
EXOIA combines automatic interpretation of space data, active discovery of new exoplanets, and personalized interactive visualization — something unprecedented in a single platform.
Unlike traditional solutions that only query static databases, EXOIA interprets raw data (light curves and images) and continuously learns from new observations.
Moreover, the intuitive interface makes the project accessible to both researchers and the general public, merging science, technology, and design in an innovative way.

Factors considered by the team:
During development, the EXOIA team considered:

  • Scientific accuracy, validating models with real data from Kepler and TESS;
  • Usability and visual clarity, ensuring any user can easily understand the results;
  • Scalability, allowing the system to process new data as future space missions become available;
  • Ethics and transparency, with open-source code and public access to discoveries and datasets;
  • Technological sustainability, using only free tools and platforms to ensure project reproducibility.

projectDetails.name: Project Lama
projectDetails.summary:
Our project proposes the development of a centrifuge aboard a spacecraft to generate artificial gravity. The goal is to reduce the negative effects of microgravity on living organisms, such as bone and muscle loss, cardiac alterations, and physiological stress, which are common in long-duration space missions.
The solution consists of a rotating ring that uses centrifugal force to simulate Earth's gravity. Tests with biological models indicate that artificial gravity helps maintain the health and normal behavior of organisms, providing important data for future long-duration human missions, such as trips to Mars or the Moon.
This project addresses the challenge of maintaining the health of living beings in space, offering a practical and innovative solution to microgravity-related problems. Its importance lies in allowing astronauts to remain healthy and functional during extended missions, as well as contributing to advances in artificial gravity research and space biology.
projectDetails.details: Our project develops a centrifuge aboard a spacecraft to generate artificial gravity, using a rotating ring to simulate Earth-like conditions. This helps reduce the negative effects of microgravity on living organisms, such as bone and muscle loss, cardiovascular changes, and physiological stress. The design was created with physics simulations and CAD software, considering rotation speed, gravity levels, organism adaptation, and structural safety. By maintaining health and normal behavior in space, our project offers a practical and innovative solution for long-duration missions, contributing to advances in space biology and artificial gravity research.

projectDetails.name: Project Mars Treasures
projectDetails.summary:
Imagine a space mission with no inorganic waste. Mars Treasures transforms the 12,600 kg an eight-person crew would generate on a three-year Mars round trip into an opportunity for sustainability, science, and culture. We repurpose debris by turning potential waste into cultural and scientific heritage. Our mission is to market these materials in advance to museums, collectors, and enthusiasts, funding their safe return to Earth through an online auction. The earnings from selling the debris are reinvested in R&D for more effective space waste management and in purchasing carbon credits to offset the mission’s emissions. Through this project, space debris ceases to be merely a cost and becomes an opportunity for financial return—supporting NASA’s missions while promoting sustainability and cultural preservation.
By turning space waste into heritage, Mars Treasures redefines the relationship between exploration, sustainability, and memory.
projectDetails.details:
Mars Treasures is an innovative solution designed to address the challenge of inorganic waste management on long-duration space missions by transforming these materials into valuable cultural and scientific heritage. It reimagines space debris not as a liability, but as a self-sustaining resource for future exploration.

Our project targets the thousands of kilograms of non-biodegradable materials—such as packaging, textiles, polymers, and metallic components—generated by a crew. For a typical three-year Mars mission with an eight-person crew, this amounts to approximately 12,600 kg of inorganic waste. Instead of being discarded, these items are pre-cataloged and linked to specific mission milestones and crew activities. Upon a controlled return to Earth, they undergo a rigorous process of decontamination, certification, and documentation to ensure their integrity. Subsequently, these certified artifacts are auctioned on a dedicated online platform, marketed to museums, collectors, and space enthusiasts. The revenue generated is strategically allocated to create a circular funding model. Mars Treasures would manage the auction platform and all on-Earth logistics, while partnering with a space agency like NASA for the return transport. This crucial return-to-Earth capability is already being established by fully reusable launch systems, like SpaceX's Starship, which are designed to bring large payloads back from deep space.

The project offers multifaceted benefits. Economically, it creates a self-funding mechanism to cover the significant costs of return logistics, material preservation, and mission insurance. For scientific advancement, it generates revenue by providing authenticated, space-flown materials for study, with proceeds directly funding further research into sustainable space operations and materials science. Environmentally, it directly addresses the "leave no trace" principle on other celestial bodies and finances the purchase of carbon credits to offset the mission’s terrestrial emissions. Culturally, it preserves the tangible history of human space exploration, turning discarded items into powerful artifacts that tell the story of our journey beyond Earth. The intended impact is to fundamentally redefine the relationship between space exploration, sustainability, and collective memory, proving that even what we leave behind can narrate our progress.

To develop this concept, our team utilized a multi-tool approach. We built a detailed financial model using Google Sheets, which incorporated data from NASA’s environmental reports, SpaceX’s published logistics costs, and academic studies on space economics. This model allowed us to project financial scenarios, material recovery costs, and auction-based revenue. Key factors considered in our feasibility analysis include: the logistical cost-per-gram for return missions; overhead, indirect costs, and mission failure insurance; taxes, regulatory compliance, and equipment costs; and the total carbon footprint of on-Earth operations and the current market price for carbon credits. To refine our technical documentation and enhance the clarity of our project proposal, we employed ChatGPT as a writing and structuring assistant.

The creative essence of Mars Treasures lies in its interdisciplinary approach, merging sustainability, economics, and cultural preservation. It challenges the conventional, disposable mindset of exploration by proposing that every mission material possesses intrinsic symbolic and scientific value. By turning space waste into heritage, Mars Treasures ensures that the story of humanity's expansion into the cosmos is one of responsibility and reverence.
projectDetails.aiReferences: Our team leveraged ChatGPT as a comprehensive AI assistant. We utilized its capabilities for both text and image generation. It was instrumental in brainstorming, synthesizing complex ideas, and refining our technical documentation for clarity. We also used its integrated DALL-E 3 model to create all artistic depictions for the project, including conceptual illustrations and mockups of the packaged artifacts.

projectDetails.name: Project Pluvia
projectDetails.summary:
Pluvia is a web application that helps people prepare for the weather rather than simply predict it. Using more than 30 years of NASA POWER historical climate data, it analyzes temperature, precipitation, and wind to calculate averages and probabilities for any chosen date and location.

Users can enter a future date, a place, and optionally what they plan to do, such as a wedding, a trip, or agricultural work. Pluvia then provides clear visual data and personalized insights powered by artificial intelligence. These insights help users think ahead and adapt their plans, for example, suggesting alternative activities for a rainy day, reinforcing decorations for windy conditions, or reminding travelers to bring suitable clothing.

By transforming NASA’s open data into practical guidance, Pluvia empowers people to plan confidently, make smarter decisions, and ensure their events, trips, and projects succeed even when the weather does not go as expected.
projectDetails.details:
How It Works

Pluvia uses NASA’s POWER API, which provides over 30 years of global historical climate data.
When a user enters a date, location, and optionally a description of their plan, the backend retrieves the same calendar day across all those years (for example, every December 15 from 1981 to 2024).

It then calculates the historical averages for temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. These results are combined with the user’s inputs and processed through an AI model (Llama-3.3-70B), which generates short natural-language insights that help users plan and adapt.

Examples include:
“It may be windy on that day, secure decorations and check your audio equipment,”
or
“Rain is frequent in the afternoon, plan indoor activities for that time.”

Benefits and Impact

Pluvia helps people prepare instead of predict. It gives users confidence to plan important events, trips, or agricultural activities using long-term statistical context rather than short-term forecasts.
This can reduce stress, avoid financial losses from cancellations, and make planning more resilient to climate uncertainty.

By turning NASA’s open climate data into practical and accessible insights, Pluvia helps users make smarter, data-driven decisions about the moments that matter most.

Tools and Technologies

  • Frontend: Next.js, deployed on Vercel
  • Main API backend: written in Zig, hosted on a self-managed VPS
  • AI service: Cloudflare Worker integrating Llama-3.3-70B
  • Data source: NASA POWER API
  • Repository: https://github.com/orgs/PluviaProject/repositories

Creativity and Considerations

We wanted Pluvia to bridge rigorous science and everyday life. Using a low-level language like Zig for the backend allowed us to explore performance and learning opportunities, while separating the AI service into its own worker improved scalability. Our focus was on creating something innovative, practical, and beautifully simple, helping people plan with science, not guesswork.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence was used in two main areas of our project:

1. Insight Generation

Pluvia integrates the Llama-3.3-70B model through the Groq API to generate personalized insights and natural-language summaries for users. After retrieving and averaging 30 years of NASA POWER climate data for the selected date and location, the results and user inputs are sent to the model, which produces concise, human-like recommendations.
In case the daily usage limit of the Groq free plan is reached, the system automatically switches to OpenRouter.ai (using the same model) as a fallback provider to ensure uninterrupted AI service.

2. Visual Assets

A few illustrative images used in the presentation PDF were generated using AI tools to visualize concepts such as weather-related events. All AI-generated images include a visible watermark indicating their artificial origin, following the Space Apps Challenge rules.

No NASA branding, logos, or mission identifiers were used or modified in any AI-generated content.

projectDetails.name: Project Demeter
projectDetails.summary:
Demeter is a web-based platform that provides agricultural producers with real-time air quality insights and 7-day predictive forecasts to protect crop health and optimize yields. By integrating data from NASA satellites and atmospheric sensors, Demeter monitors critical pollutants (CO₂, O₃, NO₂, SO₂, etc.) and environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, wind, AOD) that directly impact agricultural productivity.
Users register their fields and crop types (soy, corn, wheat, etc.) to receive tailored notifications and actionable recommendations for irrigation, pesticide application, and harvest timing. The threshold-based classification system (good/moderate/poor) makes complex environmental data accessible to farmers of all technical levels.
By democratizing advanced environmental monitoring, Demeter enables proactive crop management amid increasing air pollution and climate variability, supporting sustainable farming practices and food security worldwide.
projectDetails.details:
Through reality's looking glass

Imagine a rice farmer in rural Brazil, waking before dawn to check her fields. She's done everything the traditional way: timed her planting perfectly, managed her water with precision, selected the best seeds its cooperative could offer. Yet season after season, her yields keep declining. She consults with neighbors, checks the soil, adjusts her irrigation schedule. Nothing explains the loss. The culprit isn't in the ground—it's in the air above her head, invisible and unmeasured.

This is the story playing out across thousands of small and mid-sized farms worldwide. Air pollution, atmospheric shifts, and global warming changing variables that farmers can't see are quietly eroding agricultural productivity. According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and Fatma Kunt, the estimate is that grain production will decrease 20% to 30% due to the impact of air pollution. While large industrial farms have access to sophisticated monitoring systems and agronomic consultants, the backbone of global food production—small farmers—are left guessing in the dark.

Project Demeter was born from recognizing this profound gap. We asked ourselves: What if we could put NASA's most advanced atmospheric observation technology directly into the hands of every farmer who needs it? What if space-age science could become as practical as checking the weather forecast? Demeter is a React-based app that integrates, analyzes and treats the Air Quality Indexes received data, making them accessible and understandable for everyone, independent of the literacy rate.

At its core, Demeter is a translator, it speaks two languages fluently. On one side, it communicates with NASA's TEMPO Air Quality Observation satellites, accessing a constant stream of atmospheric data: aerosol concentrations, nitrogen oxide levels, ozone profiles, humidity patterns, atmospheric radiation. This is the language of atmospheric science, expressed in parts per billion and spectral measurements.

On the other side, Demeter speaks the language of farming, and more importantly, the language of farmers. It understands that a rice paddy needs humid air like lungs need oxygen, while date palms are engineered by nature for arid climates. It knows that certain ozone levels can damage leafy vegetables but leave root crops unaffected. This knowledge comes from a simplified but powerful neural network, built with TensorFlow and scikit-learn, that learns from each farmer's specific crop profile and regional conditions.

When a farmer sets up Demeter, they're not entering abstract data—they're describing their livelihood. "I grow tomatoes on three hectares." "My corn is in the flowering stage." "I have citrus trees that are ten years old." The system takes these human parameters and begins watching the sky on their behalf, cross-referencing real-time atmospheric data against crop-specific vulnerability patterns.

Red alert: what and how?

The magic happens when Demeter spots danger. Perhaps nitrogen oxide levels are spiking in a pattern that historically correlates with reduced photosynthesis in wheat. Maybe aerosol concentrations suggest an air quality event that could stress fruit development. The neural network processes these patterns and sends a notification—not in scientific jargon, but in actionable language: "Air dryness alert: Consider delaying fertilizer application for at least 48 hours" or "Elevated ozone levels detected: Sensitive crops may need additional irrigation."

We realized early on that creating powerful technology wasn't enough. The most sophisticated app in the world is worthless if farmers don't trust it, can't understand it, or can't access it. That's why Demeter's architecture extends far beyond code.

The technical foundation is deliberately robust yet accessible. Python handles the backend data processing, interfacing directly with NASA's TEMPO API to pull fresh atmospheric observations. PostgreSQL databases store both the streaming satellite data and each farmer's unique crop parameters, enabling truly personalized predictions. Firebase Cloud Messaging powers the alert system, ensuring notifications reach farmers even in areas with spotty connectivity. The React Native frontend works seamlessly on both iOS and Android, including older devices that are more common in rural areas.

But here's where Demeter becomes truly innovative: we built a bridge between digital and physical infrastructure. Through partnerships with institutions like Brazil's EMBRAPA and the USDA-ARS, as well as local rural unions and NGOs, we've created a network of access points where farmers can engage with Demeter even without personal smartphones or digital literacy. A farmer can visit a local agricultural extension office, where a trusted advisor — someone who speaks their language and understands their region — helps them interpret their atmospheric data and adjust their farming practices accordingly.

This hybrid model respects a fundamental truth about agricultural communities: knowledge flows through relationships, not just through apps. By embedding Demeter within existing support networks, we're not trying to replace traditional agricultural wisdom—we're augmenting it with a dimension that was previously invisible.

Ripples become waves under data analysis

The intended impact of Demeter operates on multiple scales, like ripples spreading across water. At the individual level, a farmer gains the ability to make proactive decisions rather than reactive repairs. Instead of discovering crop damage after an air quality event, they receive advance warning (as redundant as that sounds) and can take protective measures—adjusting irrigation, delaying certain treatments, or preparing for reduced yields in specific plots.

Scale this up across thousands of farms, and the ripples become waves. Regional agricultural productivity increases as more farmers optimize their resource allocation based on atmospheric conditions. Water isn't wasted trying to compensate for air quality stress. Fertilizers are applied when crops can actually utilize them effectively. The economic impact compounds: fewer crop losses mean more stable incomes for farming families and more reliable food supplies for local communities.

The Good Earth: knowledge construction through traditions

The deepest impact might be psychological and cultural. Farmers are notoriously skilled at reading their environment—they understand wind, soil, water, sunlight with an intimacy that comes from generations of observation. Demeter adds a new sense to this expertise: the ability to "see" air quality. Over time, this builds climate resilience not just through immediate adaptations, but by making farming communities aware of environmental patterns they never had access to before.

When a farming cooperative in rural India starts comparing notes about how their Demeter alerts correlate with crop outcomes, they're building collective knowledge. When a father in Kenya shows his daughter how atmospheric data predicted the need to protect their coffee plants, he's passing down a new kind of agricultural wisdom. This is how Demeter contributes to global food security, not just by preventing crop losses, but by fundamentally expanding what farmers know about the world their crops grow in.

Demeter's creativity isn't just in the technology, it's in the recognition that the most underexplored dimension of agricultural science isn't only in the soil or the seed, but also in the air. While countless platforms forecast weather or analyze soil conditions, we're the first to make atmospheric quality a core agricultural tool accessible to everyday farmers.

The innovation is also in our refusal to follow the typical tech development playbook: we didn't build an app and hope farmers would find it. We didn't create a generic platform that treats all crops and all farmers the same. Instead, we built an adaptive system that learns from each user, respects varying levels of digital access, and works within the social fabric of agricultural communities rather than trying to disrupt it.

Most importantly, Demeter proves that space technology doesn't have to stay in space. NASA's satellites were looking down at our fields all along—we just needed to build the bridge that helps farmers look back up and understand what they're seeing. In doing so, we're turning the invisible visible, making the complex simple, and transforming cutting-edge atmospheric science into something as practical and essential as checking whether it's going to rain.

projectDetails.name: Sponge City
projectDetails.summary: In 2024, southern Brazil faced its worst flooding disaster, highlighting the urgent need for resilient urban planning. Our team developed Sponge City, a platform leveraging NASA’s Earth observation data to transform urban centers into sponge cities that mitigate flood risks. By analyzing real-time data, Sponge City identifies optimal locations for green infrastructure, such as rain gardens and permeable pavements, which absorb rainwater to prevent floods and restore ecosystems. The platform integrates strategic planning with real-time monitoring, delivering precise, actionable solutions to urban planners. This addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by using open data to tackle climate-driven disasters, specifically flooding in vulnerable regions like Rio Grande do Sul. Sponge City is critical because it empowers communities to adapt to extreme weather, enhancing urban resilience and sustainability. By streamlining decision-making and promoting eco-friendly infrastructure, it helps prevent future disasters and supports healthier ecosystems, ensuring safer cities for all.
projectDetails.details:
Sponge City Project Summary

Sponge City is a versatile platform designed to enhance urban resilience against flooding and climate-driven disasters worldwide. While it draws on data from real-world examples, such as the 2024 floods in southern Brazil to demonstrate its capabilities, the system is built for global application, analyzing topographic, hydrological, and environmental data from NASA’s Earth observation databases to identify optimal locations for green infrastructure. This includes permeable pavements, rain gardens, and vegetated roofs that absorb rainwater, mitigate flooding, and support ecosystem restoration. Utilizing artificial intelligence to make the calculations and pinpointing, the platform provides real-time analytics, strategic planning tools, and actionable recommendations, enabling urban planners, policymakers, and communities to make informed decisions efficiently.

The system was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScrip, and React, for the user interface; Figma for prototyping; and Gemini for generating visualizations and textual content. This combination ensures an accessible and intuitive experience. Benefits encompass reduced flood risks, improved water management, enhanced biodiversity, and cost-effective urban adaptations. The intended impact is to empower global cities to combat escalating climate challenges, fostering sustainable development and preventing disasters on a planetary scale.

Our project’s creativity lies in its innovative fusion of NASA open data with AI-driven insights and dynamic, user-centric visualizations, allowing for customizable scenarios and predictive modeling. For expansions, Sponge City supports integration with additional datasets (e.g., from local sensors or satellite networks), scalability to regional or national levels, and modular features for user-contributed data, enabling collaborative global resilience efforts. Our team considered factors such as data accuracy and privacy, cross-cultural accessibility, interoperability with existing urban planning tools, environmental equity, and long-term adaptability to ensure the platform’s viability and inclusivity across diverse contexts.

projectDetails.summary:
We are Tecnoway Falcon 9, and our project is about solar flares, powerful explosions on the Sun that release intense energy and can impact Earth. To address the challenge of making space science accessible and engaging, we developed an educational experience that combines scientific explanation with a creative comic strip (HQ).
Our goal was to explain what solar flares are, how they happen, their effects on satellites, GPS, and communication systems, and how they can even cause auroras or power outages. We used NASA resources like the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) to ensure accurate and up-to-date information.
We also used AI-generated images and Google Translate voice for character narration. This mix of science and creativity makes space weather easier to understand—especially for students and young audiences.
projectDetails.details: Our project aims to explain in a simple and creative way what solar flares are, their types (solar flares and coronal mass ejections), how they occur, and the impacts they can have on Earth, such as interference with satellites, GPS, communications, and even blackouts. To achieve this, we developed an educational presentation that includes an animated comic strip made in Scratch, narrated using Google Translate's voice, images generated by artificial intelligence, and content based on reliable NASA sources (such as SDO and SOHO). Our focus was to make a scientific topic accessible and interesting to young audiences, combining technology, art, and science. The project aims to increase interest in astronomy and raise awareness of the importance of space weather. The team considered factors such as accessible language, use of reliable data, visual creativity, and interactivity to make learning more engaging and effective.

projectDetails.name: Adventures in Space Weather
projectDetails.summary:
We created a digital children's story titled “Adventures in Space Weather”, which explains in a fun and accessible way what space weather is, including its phenomena (like solar flares and coronal mass ejections) and their impacts on Earth. The story follows a pilot and co-pilot who experience a sudden failure in their aircraft's instruments caused by a solar storm. Based on data from NASA the narrative shows how these events can disrupt satellites, power grids, GPS systems, and communication networks.

During the flight, the characters explain these effects and end their journey admiring a beautiful aurora borealis, a phenomenon that occurs when solar particles hit Earth’s atmosphere. The story is lighthearted, educational, and grounded in real science.

Our goal is to teach children about space weather early on, encouraging critical thinking and scientific awareness. According to NASA and NOAA, space weather already affects several key sectors, and the adults of the future will need to understand and manage these challenges. We believe stories like this are a first step toward preparing the next generation.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, titled “Adventures in Space Weather,” is a digital children’s story aimed at explaining space weather and its effects on Earth in an accessible and engaging way, based on scientific information from NASA and INPE. Our team, Tecnoway Saturn V, is a robotics team from Brazil composed of six members, who collaboratively developed this project.

According to NASA (2024), space weather refers to “conditions in space that can influence the performance and reliability of space and terrestrial systems.” The solar flares and coronal mass ejections featured in our story “release massive amounts of energetic particles and radiation that can impact human technology on Earth and in space” (NASA, 2024).

Our narrative follows a pilot and co-pilot who experience instrument failures caused by a solar storm, illustrating how space weather “can affect GPS navigation systems, power grids, and communications, leading to significant economic and social impacts” (NOAA, 2024). The story also highlights the formation of the aurora borealis, described by NASA (2024) as “one of the most spectacular visual manifestations of space weather.”

For the creation of the script and images, we used the OpenAI ChatGPT artificial intelligence tool, which helped us develop the text, initial illustrations, and also to translate scientific texts from English to Portuguese. The animation was manually created using the Canva platform, ensuring an attractive and didactic visual presentation. The narrator’s voice was generated using an AI text-to-speech tool within Canva, while the voices of the pilot, co-pilot, Sun, and Earth characters were recorded by members of our team, bringing emotion and personality to the story.

Our goal is to raise awareness about space weather from early childhood, preparing future generations to understand and cope with the effects of this phenomenon. As stated by INPE (2024), space weather “directly affects the country’s critical infrastructure and essential technological systems.” The combination of accurate science, accessible narrative, and innovative technology makes this project an educational and engaging tool that unites learning and entertainment.
projectDetails.aiReferences: For our project, we utilized Artificial Intelligence tools extensively to enhance creativity and efficiency. Specifically, we used OpenAI's ChatGPT to assist in scriptwriting, generating story dialogue, and translating scientific texts from English to Portuguese. Additionally, ChatGPT helped create initial image concepts which were further refined manually. The animation sequences were crafted using Canva, where we also used its AI-powered text-to-speech tool to generate the narrator's voice. The voices of other characters—such as the pilot, co-pilot, Sun, and Earth—were performed by our team members to add a personal touch. All AI-generated images include visible watermarks as required, and audio metadata acknowledge the use of AI for narration. This blend of AI assistance and human creativity allowed us to produce an educational and engaging digital story while maintaining originality and adherence to NASA’s guidelines.

node.excerpt: AIRTH uses NASA data and climate sensors to predict and fight air pollution.Drones and IoT devices react in real time to clean and regenerate the air.

projectDetails.name: AIRTH
projectDetails.summary:
Project Summary – AIRTH: Earth’s Breathing Network

AIRTH is an autonomous system that transforms NASA Earth data into real-world action. Using NASA TEMPO satellite data combined with ground air quality sensors (OpenAQ) and meteorological inputs (Open-Meteo, OpenWeather), AIRTH predicts air pollution events before they happen.

When atmospheric risks are detected, AI algorithms automatically deploy drones to release natural biochemical compounds that neutralize toxic gases and particulate matter, while IoT devices activate air filters and micro-sprayers in affected zones.

Built with Python, TensorFlow, React, and AWS, AIRTH integrates real-time forecasting, visualization, and automated response — creating a closed loop of detection, decision, and regeneration.

This project directly addresses the TEMPO challenge by connecting Earth observation data with practical, automated mitigation, reducing exposure to pollutants and protecting both ecosystems and human health. AIRTH turns air monitoring into air healing — helping our planet breathe again.
projectDetails.details:
What it does / How it works:
AIRTH is an autonomous system that predicts and reacts to air pollution in real time. It integrates NASA TEMPO satellite data, ground-based sensors (OpenAQ), and meteorological data (Open-Meteo, OpenWeather) to detect toxic changes in the atmosphere. When critical levels are predicted, drones release natural biochemical compounds that neutralize gases like NO₂ and SO₂, while IoT devices on the ground activate air filters and micro-sprayers in affected zones.

Benefits:
AIRTH acts before pollution causes damage — protecting both crops and communities. It prevents respiratory risks, reduces agricultural losses, and promotes cleaner, safer skies through automated action, not just monitoring.

Intended Impact:
By turning satellite data into direct environmental response, AIRTH bridges the gap between Earth observation and real-world intervention. It aims to create a global network capable of reducing pollution peaks, preserving ecosystems, and improving public health.

Creativity & Considerations:
AIRTH transforms data into action — using predictive AI and biocompatible chemistry to clean the air. The team focused on automation, sustainability, and real-time response, ensuring every alert leads to an immediate reaction. It’s not just about understanding pollution — it’s about healing it.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):
AIRTH uses AI to analyze and predict air quality patterns by processing NASA TEMPO, OpenAQ, and meteorological data. Machine learning models (TensorFlow) identify pollution trends and trigger automated environmental responses, such as drone deployment and IoT activation.

projectDetails.name: Urban Connect (Project The Big Bang Hypothesis)
projectDetails.summary:
NASA sends millions of climate data points every day, but they arrive in technical language, in English, and far from the reality of those planning our cities.

UrbanConnect transforms this into a more accessible, practical language. And with our chatbot Deimos, that data becomes real-world solutions, guiding users with engineering and urban planning recommendations based on cutting-edge science.

The future of cities is already being observed from space. UrbanConnect brings that future down to earth, and turns it into action.
projectDetails.details:
Development Report – UrbanConnect Project

1. General Context

During the event, our team began developing UrbanConnect, a web platform focused on improving accessibility to weather and environmental data provided by NASA.

The main goal of the project is to translate technical and complex information into clear, accessible, and applicable content for the Brazilian reality, promoting intelligent solutions in engineering and urban planning.

2. First Day of the Event

On the first day, we completed approximately 55% of the UrbanConnect project’s programming.

The activities focused on:

Structuring the main web page;

Initial integration with the database.

Identified Problem

During the initial analyses, we identified an informational paradox:

NASA made available around 30,000 sets of environmental and weather data. However:

The files were in a technical and foreign language;

The availability was temporary (only two days);

The data, while extremely valuable, were not easily understood by Brazilian professionals without specific technical training.

This situation reflects a recurring issue: crucial information about climate and the environment is available but inaccessible in terms of language and local context.

In practice, areas such as engineering and urban planning still base decisions on historical data, when it would be far more efficient to use real-time climate projections and analyses supported by cutting-edge technology.

3. Team Mission

The mission of the UrbanConnect team is to make NASA’s climate and environmental data accessible, integrated, and useful for the Brazilian public.

The proposal consists of gathering all the information in a unified digital environment featuring:

Translation and simplification of technical data;

Interactive and intuitive visualization;

Direct applicability in areas such as urban planning, infrastructure, and sustainability.

4. Second Day of the Event

On the second day, we finalized the platform’s development and prepared the presentation script.

Activities included refining the web interface, running functional tests, and preparing a 30-second pitch for the final presentation.

5. Developed Solution: UrbanConnect

UrbanConnect is a collaborative web platform that connects people, communities, and professionals through translated and contextualized climate data.

Main Features

User registration and simplified access to consolidated data (no need to manipulate complex spreadsheets);

Visualization of interactive charts and information;

Tools for building intelligent urban and environmental strategies;

Chatbot Deimos, a virtual assistant providing technical support and solutions in engineering and urban planning.

Differential

UrbanConnect closes the information loop:

Real NASA data → Translation and simplification → Brazilian contextualization → Practical actions.

6. Technologies Used

The application was developed using a modern and scalable technology stack:

Languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript

Frameworks: (React and Node.js) Two frameworks focused on code optimization and organization

Database: Firebase

Data Exchange Format: JSON

These technologies provided a solid, secure, and expandable foundation for the platform.

7. Future Perspectives

During the event, a proposal emerged to expand the Deimos chatbot, transforming it into an intelligent system based on a neural network capable of learning from the integrated climate and environmental data.

Although we had previously developed some “neurons” in an earlier project, full implementation was not possible in this context. Nevertheless, these prototypes serve as a proof of concept, demonstrating the technical feasibility and development potential of UrbanConnect and Deimos to incorporate continuous learning artificial intelligence.

This evolution would allow Deimos to autonomously interpret complex data, identify climate patterns, and generate practical recommendations for urban planners, public managers, and engineers — precisely the audience that currently faces barriers in accessing, interpreting, and applying official data such as NASA’s.

With more development time and institutional support — such as from an organization like NASA — it would be possible to build a robust neural network capable of assimilating the agency’s datasets, producing predictive analyses, and providing increasingly accurate and contextualized recommendations.

Furthermore, if scientific and governmental institutions adopted platforms like this, they could filter, interpret, and apply their data in real time — democratizing access to scientific information, accelerating decision-making processes, and increasing efficiency in urban and environmental planning.

8. Conclusion

The UrbanConnect project made significant progress throughout the event:

On the first day, we structured more than half of the application;

On the second day, we completed the development, planned, and delivered the final pitch.

The initiative reinforces the importance of making scientific information accessible and demonstrates the potential of technology and artificial intelligence to translate complex data into concrete actions aimed at a sustainable urban and environmental future.

projectDetails.name: MarsCycle
projectDetails.summary:
Summary
MarsCycle is an autonomous closed-loop circular economy system for Mars, tackling non-metabolic waste management in long-duration missions. For an 8-person crew over 3 years, 12,600 kg of inorganic waste (plastics 38%, metals 28%, electronics 17%) accumulates, costing $126M in resupply. We developed a 4-layer robotic ecosystem: satellite mapping dispatches C-Robin collectors to gather waste; S-Robin sorters categorize it; AI (MarsMind) optimizes processing via pyrolysis/H₂-O₂ furnaces; and fabrication units (3D printing/CNC) reuse materials into habitat tools. Powered by solar and ISRU (MOXIE-integrated O₂), it achieves >90% recycling, slashing Earth dependency. Built with Next.js/FastAPI/DeepSeek AI, it's creative in blending NASA simulant data (MGS-1) with real-time web dashboards for control. This ensures sustainable Jezero Crater operations, vital for Artemis/Mars goals.
projectDetails.details:
MarsCycle revolutionizes waste management on Mars by creating a fully autonomous, self-sustaining circular economy that transforms inorganic trash into mission-critical resources, minimizing human intervention and Earth resupply. It works through a seamless 4-layer architecture: Layer 1 uses satellite hyperspectral imaging (inspired by Perseverance's Jezero Crater data) for 24/7 waste mapping, dispatching solar-powered C-Robin (Collector Robot Bin) rovers to autonomously navigate regolith terrain, identify materials via AI vision (LiDAR/RGB sensors), and transport up to 20kg payloads to the central hub. There, S-Robin (Sorter) arms employ spectrometry for precise separation into type-specific containers (e.g., HDPE plastics, aluminum metals). Layer 2's processing hub applies pyrolysis/fusion (fueled by H₂ from plastic syngas + MOXIE-produced O₂) to purify materials, with AI quality checks ensuring 95% accuracy. Layer 3 fabricates via multi-material 3D printing, robotic injection molding, and CNC machining, producing items like habitat bricks (HDPE + MGS-1 regolith) or tool replacements. Layer 4's MarsMind AI (DeepSeek R1 LLM) predicts needs, optimizes energy (e.g., solar windows), and distributes via adaptive logistics, closing the loop with >90% recycling.

Benefits include massive cost savings ($10,000/kg avoided), reduced mission risks from waste hazards, and enhanced sustainability—reusing 70% electronics for repairs and integrating ISRU for zero-waste ops. The intended impact is enabling permanent Mars colonies, aligning with NASA's Artemis program by proving scalable self-sufficiency in extreme environments (low pressure, -60°C temps, radiation).

We used Python (FastAPI backend, Pandas for NASA data processing) and JavaScript (Next.js/React frontend with Three.js for 3D Jezero simulations, Recharts for Sankey metrics) as coding languages; hardware simulations via OpenCV for robot vision; software like Ollama/LangChain for local AI, SQLite for inventory DB, and Vercel/Railway for deployment—no custom hardware built, but designed for rad-hard rovers. Creativity shines in "Robin" bots (pun on "robot bin") with personality-driven simulations (e.g., "efficient" vs. "exploratory" behaviors) and hybrid H₂-O₂ furnaces from plastic-derived fuels, blending real NASA waste categories with predictive ML for "what-if" recycling scenarios.

Our team (threeeo) considered factors like Mars' dusty regolith (vibration dust mitigation), energy constraints (solar/RTG backups), AI reliability (human overrides, 6-month maintenance), ethical ISRU (no organics), and scalability—prioritizing offline-capable, modular design for 48h hack feasibility while grounding in sources like Non-Metabolic Waste Categories and Waste Management Options for Long-Duration Missions.

Hefest is a project whose core purpose is to transform raw data into clear, organized, and accessible information, aimed at understanding urban and territorial realities. It addresses a common challenge in the public sector: the abundance of available data, which is often dispersed, technical, and difficult for managers and decision-makers to interpret.

More than simply providing numbers, Hefest seeks to give context and meaning to the information, enabling a multi-dimensional understanding of reality—social, economic, environmental, and structural. In this way, the software serves as a bridge between technical data and practical action, accelerating strategy formulation and policy execution.
By prioritizing accessibility and transparency, Hefest strengthens trust between government and society, reducing the risk of misinterpretation or manipulation. In short, it is a strategic tool for territorial and urban analysis.

Scalable platform, allowing the inclusion of new indicators and features.

projectDetails.name: Project Digitalis
projectDetails.summary:
We developed an app capable of recognizing plants through the use of AI.

The app works by capturing a photo of a flower, which, if uploaded, can be recognized through AI.

It fits the challenge because the app identifies and analyzes plant flowering.

It is extremely important because it fits the current scenario for honey producers (beekeepers) and for use by academic researchers.
projectDetails.details:
We created a comprehensive application called Bloom Map, designed to monitor flowers and support beekeepers in the northwestern region of Paraná, Brazil. The application will combine artificial intelligence-based plant recognition, collaborative data collection (citizen science), and a real-time interactive map showing identified species and their flowering stages. The main objective is to help beekeepers identify plants that bloom outside of spring, ensuring continuous honey production during the winter.

The application will allow users to record flowers found in the field by submitting a photo captured with their smartphone camera, with GPS enabled to automatically record the location, date, and time of the observation. After submitting the image, the system uses artificial intelligence to recognize the plant, returning one to five possible species with their respective common and scientific names, reference images, and a brief description. The user must choose which option corresponds to the observed plant, or mark it as "unidentified" if none are suitable, so that the image can be analyzed later.

After confirming the species, the app should prompt the user to select the flowering stage, displaying comparative images of the different stages: vegetative (no flowers), early flowering, full bloom, and fading flowers. Information on location, date, time, species, and flowering stage should be stored in a central database.

This data will feed an interactive map that will display, in real time, the distribution of floral species in the northwestern region of Paraná. Each point on the map will represent a recorded plant, allowing the user to apply filters by species, flowering stage, and period (month or season). By clicking on a point, the app should display detailed information about the observation, including photo, plant name, date, and flowering stage.

The system should also feature an optional web dashboard for beekeepers, which will display flowering zones by season, seasonal distribution graphs, and suggestions for ideal areas for hive installation outside of spring, based on the collected data.

The technical framework should utilize React Native (Expo) on the frontend, Node.js with Express on the backend, Firebase or PostgreSQL as the database, Firebase Auth for authentication, Firebase Storage or AWS S3 for image storage, and Mapbox or Leaflet with OpenStreetMap for the mapping system. Plant recognition should be performed using the PlantNet API or a plant classification model developed in TensorFlow or PyTorch.

The design should be simple, light, and intuitive, with a nature-inspired color palette of green, yellow, and lilac. The interface should be responsive for mobile phones and tablets and offer a fluid experience, with visual feedback and short animations when submitting photos or confirming identifications.

BloomMap should function as a citizen science platform that connects nature, technology, and beekeeping, promoting participatory environmental monitoring and providing useful data for researchers and producers. The system should allow the community to help map the region's flowers and understand flowering patterns throughout the year, contributing to the sustainability and continuity of honey production.

projectDetails.name: Project Urban Mind
projectDetails.summary:
Urban Mind is an intelligent dashboard designed to assess risks in expanding urban areas. It leverages satellite imagery and geospatial data to analyze environmental factors such as weather conditions, fire hazards, pollution levels, and other key indicators. By evaluating these variables, Urban Mind helps determine whether a specific region is suitable for urban development.
At the heart of the platform is an AI system trained on historical and real-time data. This AI collaborates with users—urban planners, policymakers, and developers—to offer actionable recommendations that support smarter, more sustainable city growth. The goal is to minimize pollution accumulation, reduce environmental risks, and improve the overall quality of life for residents.
Some of our key features are:
Satellite-based geospatial analysis
Real-time environmental monitoring
Predictive modeling for fire and pollution risks
AI-driven urban planning recommendations
Focus on sustainable and equitable development
Urban Mind empowers decision-makers to plan cities that are not only efficient and resilient, but also healthier and more livable for future generations.
projectDetails.details:
Urban Mind is an intelligent dashboard designed to support sustainable urban expansion. It integrates satellite imagery, geospatial data, weather patterns, pollution levels, and fire risk indicators to assess the viability of developing specific regions. The system uses machine learning models to analyze these data layers and generate actionable insights for urban planners.

At its core, Urban Mind features an AI assistant trained on historical urban development data, environmental trends, and predictive modeling. Users interact with the dashboard to receive real-time recommendations on where and how to expand cities while minimizing environmental impact and maximizing livability.

Benefits:

    • Risk Mitigation: Identifies areas prone to environmental hazards like wildfires or pollution accumulation.
    • Sustainable Planning: Encourages development strategies that reduce long-term ecological damage.
    • Data-Driven Decisions: Empowers urban planners with evidence-based recommendations.
    • Community Well-being: Supports healthier living conditions by avoiding high-risk zones.
    • Efficiency: Reduces time and resources spent on manual data analysis

Urban Mind aims to revolutionize how cities grow by embedding sustainability and resilience into the planning process. The project seeks to:

  • Reduce pollution and ecological degradation in expanding urban areas.
  • Improve public health outcomes by guiding development away from high-risk zones.
  • Foster equitable access to clean, safe, and livable environments.
  • Equip governments and developers with tools to make smarter, long-term decisions.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used

  • Programming Languages: Python (for data processing and machine learning), JavaScript (for dashboard interactivity),HTML and CSS for the page itself.
  • Frameworks & Libraries: Leaflet.js.
  • Data Sources: NASA satellite data, Copernicus Climate Data Store, OpenStreetMap, local environmental agencies.

How is the project creative ?

Urban Mind stands out by combining environmental science, urban planning, and AI into a single, intuitive platform. Its creativity lies in:

  • Cross-disciplinary integration: Merging satellite data with predictive modeling and user-friendly design.
  • Collaborative AI: The assistant doesn’t just analyze—it co-plans with the user, offering suggestions and adapting to feedback.
  • Visual storytelling: The dashboard uses dynamic maps and visual indicators to make complex data accessible to non-experts.

🧠 Factors Considered by the Team

  • Ethical Urbanism: Ensuring recommendations do not reinforce social inequalities.
  • Data Privacy: Respecting user and regional data regulations.
  • Scalability: Designing the system to adapt to cities of different sizes and geographies.

projectDetails.name: WindWhisper
projectDetails.summary:
WindWhisper is an intelligent air quality monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite data into actionable agricultural recommendations for Brazilian farmers. The system integrates real-time NASA TEMPO hourly measurements with ground-based OpenAQ stations to provide comprehensive air quality monitoring.
Key features include: real-time pollution tracking (O₃, NO₂, PM2.5), crop-specific risk assessment for 42 Brazilian crops, intelligent pesticide spraying windows calculation, fire and smoke alerts from NASA FIRMS, and an AI chatbot that answers farming questions in Portuguese.
The platform addresses critical agricultural challenges: Brazilian farmers lose up to 20% of production due to air pollution, but lack access to real-time air quality data. WindWhisper solves this by providing hourly satellite updates, validating data against ground stations, and offering 24-48 hour forecasts.
Built with Next.js 14, the system processes multiple NASA datasets (TEMPO, OMI, GEOS-CF, FIRMS) in parallel, ensuring sub-2-second response times. The rural-friendly interface features a 3D Earth globe, mobile-optimized design, and Portuguese localization.
Expected impact: 30% reduction in pesticide waste, 20% decrease in crop losses, and 60% reduction in environmental contamination. The platform democratizes access to space data, helping farmers make data-driven decisions to protect their harvests and increase agricultural sustainability.
projectDetails.details:
# WindWhisper Project Details

## What does it do and how does it work?

WindWhisper is an intelligent air quality monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite data into actionable agricultural recommendations for Brazilian farmers. The system works by:

1. **Real-time Data Integration**: Continuously processes NASA TEMPO hourly measurements, OpenAQ ground stations, and NASA GEOS-CF forecasts

2. **Multi-source Validation**: Cross-references satellite data with ground-based measurements for accuracy validation

3. **Crop-specific Analysis**: Evaluates air quality impact on 42 Brazilian crops using scientific sensitivity thresholds

4. **Intelligent Recommendations**: Provides optimal pesticide spraying windows, crop selection advice, and yield protection strategies

5. **AI-Powered Chatbot**: Offers natural language interaction in Portuguese for instant farming guidance

## What benefits does it have?

projectDetails.name: Project Agroguard
projectDetails.summary: AgroGuard takes on the challenge of easily obtaining past and current global weather data from NASA, integrating them with mathematical models and specific agronomic rules for sensitive crops, calibrated with historical data and local feedback. This is presented in a simple interface with an interactive map, push notifications, and straightforward language for quick decisions. This allows users to understand the likelihood of various factors, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and solar radiation. The importance of our application is to enable users to understand future weather conditions so they can prepare in advance and avoid losses.
projectDetails.details: AgroGuard uses NASA's POWER API (Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources) as its primary source to collect past and current global weather data, such as temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and solar radiation. Our application integrates this NASA data with mathematical models and agronomic rules specific to sensitive crops, calibrated with historical data and local feedback, enabling farmers to make important decisions in the field. Our simple interface allows farmers to select a crop and the exact location where it was or will be planted, providing accurate information about the climate in that location and enabling them to make important decisions. We also implement critical, high, or medium-level alerts for farmers to ensure they are not caught off guard. We also include a phenological calendar and graphs for improved data clarity. Our project is designed to understand the climate of a specific area selected on the map, helping farmers make the best decisions for planting or harvesting a sensitive crop, which has its own particularities and is susceptible to climate change. The intended impact of our project is to make advanced climate intelligence accessible to the smallholder farming sector, mitigate the risk of climate extremes, and stabilize production and income in critical agricultural regions of our state and country. Our research on sensitive crops was based on Google Scholar, articles, and recent news sources to validate scientific and market assumptions. The NASA challenge guided and motivated our work to deliver a solution based on advanced technology, real farmer needs, and social impact.
