projectDetails.name: OrbitShare — the Airbnb for satellites.
projectDetails.summary:
Our project was developed by students from UNESPAR (Brazil) for NASA’s challenge on commercial innovation in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

OrbitShare is an online marketplace that connects companies with idle satellites to customers who need orbital data — such as researchers, farmers, and startups.
By using open NASA data and APIs from space partners, the platform enables affordable, sustainable, and democratized access to space services.

We believe that by optimizing the use of existing satellites, we can reduce waste in orbit and expand the benefits of space technology for people on Earth — and beyond.
projectDetails.details:
5W2H – OrbitShare Project

1. What? (What will be done?)

The project consists of creating OrbitShare, an online marketplace platform for satellite capacity in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
The platform will enable on-demand access to idle space assets, turning unused satellite capacity into revenue for operators while reducing costs and time for end-users.
The service will include standardized contracts, a unified API with real-time NASA data, and a strong focus on sustainability by requiring end-of-life plans for satellites.

2. Why? (Why will it be done?)

OrbitShare aims to democratize access to space by creating a secondary market for satellite capacity.
The project addresses the problem of orbital idleness, providing a new revenue source for satellite operators.
It also encourages sustainability in the space sector and strengthens the Brazilian space ecosystem, aligning it with international best practices.

3. Who? (Who will do it / For whom is it designed?)

Team:

  • Technical Team: Software engineers, space specialists, and data scientists to build the API and manage the platform.
  • Legal and Regulatory Team: Professionals responsible for interpreting legislation, monitoring public consultations, and drafting contracts.

Target Customers:

  • Academic Institutions: Universities and research centers.
  • Startups and Entrepreneurs: Deep tech, IoT, climate analytics, and agri-space sectors.
  • Private Companies: Agriculture, mining, insurance, and telecommunications.
  • Smaller Government Agencies: Governments without their own satellite constellations.

4. Where? (Where will it be done?)

The platform will operate as an online marketplace, hosted on a cloud infrastructure to store Earth observation data, transaction logs, and telemetry.
Hosting will follow Brazilian data sovereignty standards.
Initially, OrbitShare will focus on the Brazilian market, with plans to expand to other Latin American regions.

5. When? (When will it be done?)

The project will be implemented in phases over 24 months:

  • 0–3 months: Research, legal and business planning, software architecture definition.
  • 3–6 months: Development of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
  • 6–12 months: Launch of a pilot project with nanosatellite operators and universities to perform simulated bookings and collect feedback.
  • 12–24 months: Platform expansion to medium-sized constellations and integration of additional services, followed by evaluation of international expansion.

6. How? (How will it be done?)

OrbitShare will be developed as a secure, cloud-based web platform integrating NASA APIs.
Standardized smart contracts with electronic signatures and payment gateways will simplify transactions.
Revenue will come from commissions per transaction (15%), premium subscription plans, and consulting or data processing services.
Risk mitigation strategies include engagement in public consultations, mandatory end-of-life satellite plans, and strong cybersecurity measures.

projectDetails.name: Project Protocolo Harpia
projectDetails.summary: Our project involves the development of a Real-Time Shark Mapping System, a crucial tool for both conservation and public safety. We created an integrated software platform that processes location data from acoustic or satellite tags fixed on sharks, translating this raw information into an interactive map displaying their current positions and migratory patterns. The system directly addresses the critical challenge of the lack of timely data on shark movements. This is vital because, by providing a clear, actionable visual of where sharks are, we enable researchers to establish more effective protection zones for threatened species and allow coastal managers to issue accurate, real-time safety alerts. Ultimately, our system promotes safe coexistence by improving marine wildlife management and reducing the potential for human-shark conflict.
projectDetails.details: Our project developed an Advanced Shark Monitoring Chip, a specialized hardware system that functions as a "marine black box." Attached to the shark, it uses an array of sensors—including heart rate monitors, accelerometers, depth gauges, and pH sensors—to collect unprecedented biological and environmental data. This approach goes beyond simple location tracking, allowing researchers to infer what sharks are eating and how environmental changes affect their health. The key challenge was achieving high-pressure resistance at a manageable cost. Our solution was to implement a two-version strategy: an initial, highly durable "Black Box" version (V1) for internal logging, built with rugged materials and coded in C/C++, followed by a more advanced, costly telemetry version (V2) later. This project is crucial because it provides the data necessary to accurately define Marine Protected Areas, understand true feeding ecology, and ultimately, reduce human-shark conflicts by improving conservation efforts and

challengeDetails.title: Embiggen Your Eyes!

projectDetails.summary:
The platform aims to transform data into territorial intelligence, enhancing the capacity for resilient, inclusive, and sustainable urban planning. More than a technological tool, it is a strategic instrument for reimagining the future of cities and improving citizens' quality of life.
  The platform proposes a new way to understand and plan urban spaces, integrating environmental, population, and socioeconomic data into a single interactive interface. Designed for urban planners, public managers, and researchers, it provides a comprehensive view of the municipality, promoting evidence-based decisions aligned with legislative norms and regulations.
We are a territorial intelligence platform that turns data into knowledge for the future of cities. Using information from NASA satellites and other global sources, we strengthen sustainable urban planning by integrating technology, science, and citizenship.
  More than a tool, we are a strategic instrument for rethinking urban development and fostering more resilient, inclusive, and humane cities.
projectDetails.details:
Territorial Monitoring: Real-time visualization of geospatial data, utilizing NASA's APIs.

Sustainability Maps: Identification of priority areas for preservation.

Urban Indicators: Interactive dashboards with metrics on mobility, water resources, air quality, and land use, integrating official data and satellite imagery.

Strategic Planning: Tools for simulating urban growth scenarios.

The benefits include providing urban planners and designers with clear, concise, and essential information for their work, all in one place, optimizing their processes. Our intended impact is to reach numerous urban planners and designers, transforming the way cities and urban projects are designed to become fully sustainable.

We used tools such as basic Google searches and AI research to develop the prototype, which was built using Figma and the Next programming language.

This project does not have a single application; instead, we leverage creativity, for example, in filters that incorporate data on population density, urban heat islands, green areas, and more.

We considered factors such as the needs of urban planners and designers, whether the solution was feasible, and whether it had viable applications.

projectDetails.name: Project THE BLACK HOLEEE
projectDetails.summary:
Florescer – Space-Based Digital Agronomist for Pollination-Dependent Crops

Florescer is an agronomic intelligence platform that integrates NASA and ESA satellite data (Sentinel-2, Landsat, SMAP, ECOSTRESS) with predictive AI to support farmers growing pollination-dependent crops such as fruits and flowers.

The system provides real-time monitoring of flowering and plant health (BloomWatch, BloomHealth), climate and pest early-warning alerts (BloomGuard), and advanced soil analytics (SoilSense). Farmers can register their farms, upload soil test results, and receive personalized recommendations through an intuitive, accessible dashboard designed for small and mid-scale producers.

Florescer tackles critical challenges in the sector: delayed decision-making, losses from pests and extreme weather, inefficient use of resources, and technological barriers. By delivering accurate satellite-driven insights and early alerts, it helps optimize pollination, reduce crop losses by up to 40%, save water and inputs, and protect pollinators and local biodiversity.

This matters because pollination drives 35% of global food production and represents hundreds of billions of dollars annually. Florescer turns space technology into productivity, sustainability, and profitability, strengthening food security and the future of agriculture.

FLOURISH - Detalhes do Projeto

O que faz e como funciona?

FLOURISH é uma plataforma de inteligência agronômica espacial que utiliza dados de satélites da NASA/ESA combinados com inteligência artificial para revolucionar a agricultura sustentável. O sistema monitora culturas em tempo real através de satélites SMAP, ECOSTRESS e Sentinel-2, processando dados de umidade do solo, estresse hídrico e imagens multiespectrais.

A plataforma funciona através de:

  • Monitoramento espacial contínuo das propriedades agrícolas
  • Algoritmos preditivos de IA que antecipam riscos climáticos e ataques de pragas com até 15 dias de antecedência
  • Gestão de floração com previsão precisa de picos de floração e otimização do manejo de polinizadores
  • Interface intuitiva com alertas instantâneos e dashboards acessíveis

Benefícios

  • Aumento de produtividade: 15-30% através de gestão otimizada e prevenção de perdas
  • Redução de recursos: 20-40% no consumo de água e produtos químicos através de aplicação precisa
  • Detecção precoce: Identificação de pragas e doenças antes de causarem danos significativos
  • Inclusão digital: Interface projetada especificamente para pequenos agricultores com linguagem acessível
  • Sustentabilidade: Soluções baseadas em manejo ecológico, sem dependência de produtos químicos agressivos

Impacto Pretendido

  1. Ambiental: Fortalecimento de populações de polinizadores nativos, aumento da biodiversidade em áreas rurais, conservação de recursos hídricos e redução da pegada de carbono agrícola
  2. Social: Democratização do acesso à tecnologia de ponta para pequenos agricultores que não podem investir em sistemas caros de monitoramento
  3. Econômico: Prevenção de 20-40% de perdas de culturas devido a falhas de polinização e ataques de pragas não detectados precocemente
  4. Escalabilidade: Modelo de negócio sustentável com planos acessíveis ($32-50/mês) e potencial de mercado de $1.7 bilhões até 2027

Ferramentas e Tecnologias Utilizadas

Dados Espaciais:

  • Satélites SMAP (NASA) - umidade do solo
  • ECOSTRESS (NASA) - estresse hídrico e temperatura
  • Sentinel-2 (ESA) - imagens multiespectrais

Stack Tecnológico:

  • Front-end: Next.js 15, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Inteligência Artificial: Algoritmos preditivos customizados para análise de dados satelitais
  • APIs: NASA Earthdata, Copernicus Open Access Hub
  • Processamento: Google Earth Engine para processamento de grandes volumes de dados satelitais
  • Hospedagem: Vercel para deploy e escalabilidade

Hardware/Infraestrutura:

  • Dados de satélites em órbita (SMAP, ECOSTRESS, Sentinel-2)
  • Infraestrutura cloud para processamento de dados geoespaciais

Criatividade do Projeto

  1. Primeiro módulo especializado em polinizadores: Única plataforma com foco integrado em gestão de polinizadores e floração
  2. Democratização de tecnologia espacial: Transformação de dados complexos de satélites da NASA em informações acionáveis para agricultores sem conhecimento técnico
  3. Modelo de negócio inovador: Combinação de SaaS acessível com licenciamento de dados e marketplace verde
  4. Abordagem preditiva: Não apenas monitora, mas prevê problemas e oportunidades com antecedência
  5. Design inclusivo: Interface projetada especificamente para usuários com baixa alfabetização digital

Fatores Considerados pela Equipe

Sustentabilidade Financeira:

  • Uso de dados satelitais gratuitos e abertos para reduzir custos operacionais
  • Múltiplas fontes de receita (assinaturas, licenciamento de dados, marketplace)
  • Planos escalonados para diferentes perfis de usuários

Impacto Social:

  • Preços acessíveis para pequenos agricultores ($32/mês para até 5 hectares)
  • Interface em linguagem simples com suporte técnico incluído
  • Foco em inclusão digital e capacitação

Viabilidade Técnica:

  • Utilização de infraestrutura existente (satélites já em operação)
  • APIs públicas e bem documentadas
  • Stack tecnológico moderno e escalável

Validação de Mercado:

  • Crescimento de 32% ao ano no setor AgTech
  • 67% dos agricultores globalmente já usam tecnologia digital
  • Testes piloto planejados com 50 agricultores no Q1 2024

Escalabilidade:

  • Arquitetura nativa da nuvem
  • Modelo de expansão regional progressiva
  • API para integrações futuras com outros sistemas agrícolas

O projeto FLOURISH representa a convergência entre tecnologia espacial de ponta e necessidades reais do campo, criando uma ponte acessível entre dados satelitais complexos e decisões práticas de manejo agrícola sustentável.

projectDetails.name: Meu Bairro Meu Mourão
projectDetails.summary:
Meu Bairro Meu Mourão is an initiative that connects technology and citizen participation to improve public management in Campo Mourão. The proposal consists of a digital application integrated with WhatsApp, where residents can record events, demands, and perceptions about their neighborhoods in a simple and accessible way. These reports, combined with public data such as those provided by NASA, are processed by an artificial intelligence system that learns from local patterns and generates interactive dashboards for municipal managers.

These dashboards provide a clear and updated view of the needs of each region, enabling faster and more effective decision-making. In addition, the AI can assist new residents in choosing the ideal neighborhood by providing relevant data directly through the WhatsApp conversation.

By using a widely accessible channel, the project democratizes data collection, strengthens active listening from the population, and promotes smart urban management based on real data. Meu Bairro Meu Mourão represents a step forward in building more connected and participatory cities, prepared to respond to community demands with efficiency and transparency.
projectDetails.details:
Our project connects municipal management with the population through a platform that collects direct feedback from residents. These records may include suggestions for improvement, complaints, or compliments, submitted in a simple way through a WhatsApp-accessible chatbot, which also identifies and records the location of the occurrence.

We also use data provided by space agencies, such as NASA, integrated with community reports. This combination supports public managers in making more effective decisions, based on intelligent reports generated by artificial intelligence. The system also enables automatic responses to managers with database information and guides residents toward the best areas of the city to live, according to their profiles and preferences.

Main benefits:

  • User-friendly experience, allowing residents to submit information easily and accessibly.
  • Low-cost data collection, eliminating expensive and bureaucratic traditional methods.
  • Intelligent and structured compilation, transforming scattered data into strategic reports for urban planning.

The intended impact is the creation of a more strategic, participatory, and effective model of urban development, where the citizens’ voices are directly connected to administrative decisions.

For the development of the project, we used Vite + React, CSS Modules, and JavaScript, which provide lightness, modularity, and speed in building the application. The creativity of the project lies in integrating different data sources — local feedback and spatial data — into a single, accessible, and scalable solution. Our team considered accessibility for citizens, cost reduction for public management, and practical applicability in the daily life of cities as key factors in its conception.

projectDetails.summary:
Developed by team 1719 — Carlos Fontes, Gustavo Praes, and Reinaldo Praes — this project presents an unprecedented proposal for total waste recycling on Mars, turning the challenge of space debris into an opportunity for self-sufficiency and sustainable innovation.

Using materials such as textile waste, metal, ceramics, and common residues, the team developed various manufacturing processes to create new functional composites applicable to tools, structures, and mission support components. Five main methods were employed: compression molding, cold sintering, resin infusion, 3D printing with filament, and 3D printing with resin. Each technique was explored in a complementary way, demonstrating how recycling can establish a closed-loop production system in extraterrestrial environments.

projectDetails.name: Project A FUN SOLAR JOURNEY
projectDetails.summary:
Our project was developed to stimulate children's scientific interest and natural curiosity in topics related to solar climate, an aspect often underexplored in schools.
The initiative arose from the observation that, although the Sun is one of the most present elements in our daily lives, its physical phenomena and impacts on Earth are rarely discussed in a playful and accessible way for children. Therefore, the project proposed an interactive, creative, and investigative approach, awakening in students the desire to understand the universe around them.
projectDetails.details:
Our project was developed with the purpose of stimulating the scientific interest and natural curiosity of children about phenomena related to solar climate, a topic of great scientific relevance, but still little explored in traditional school curricula. The proposal aims to present the Sun not only as a source of light and heat, but as a dynamic star, full of mysteries and direct influences on the Earth, including the effects of its solar storms, solar winds and variations in radiation.

We present to children complex concepts in an accessible and fun way, encouraging learning and stimulating research, critical thinking. Arousing interest in the study of the Sun and its effects, promotes the appreciation of science as an instrument for understanding the world and making conscious decisions on environmental and technological issues.

The intended impact is the construction of a scientific culture from childhood, encouraging future generations to explore areas such as astronomy, physics, meteorology and space technology. It also seeks to demystify science, making it closer and inspiring, and contributing to the formation of curious citizens, critical and aware about the role of science in everyday life.

For the development of the project, several tools and technological resources were used, such as AI Geminy, Canva, ChatGPT, Aconvert, CapCut, HeyGen, Genially, ElevenLabs, Pollo.AI and Remove.bg.

Creativity was a central element in the design process. The team sought to transform scientific knowledge into immersive visual and narrative experiences, using stories, characters and challenges that connect scientific content to children’s imagination. We considered factors such as the age of the target audience, the level of complexity of the concepts presented, the inclusion of different learning styles and the balance between scientific rigor and playfulness.

Thus, the project represents an innovative initiative that combines science, technology and art to awaken enchantment and respect for astronomical knowledge, making the study of the Sun a true adventure of discovery.

projectDetails.name: Bee Adventure
projectDetails.summary:
Our mission during this challenge was to create an immersive and meaningful experience that celebrates Brazil’s rich biodiversity. Through Bee Adventure, users explore an interactive environment where they can discover the flowers of the Cerrado and understand how their blooming seasons are connected to climate patterns.
Guided by a playful virtual bee, the experience combines art, data, and storytelling to reveal how temperature, rainfall, and other environmental factors influence flowering and, consequently, the life of pollinators.
By integrating datasets from NASA and other sources, the project transforms complex environmental data into a visually engaging and educational journey — one that encourages curiosity, environmental awareness, and appreciation for the natural beauty of the Cerrado.
Our goal is to inspire people of all ages to connect with nature and recognize the delicate balance that sustains Brazil’s unique ecosystems.
projectDetails.details:
Introduction

We are a team of students, with backgrounds in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, and Arts, who wanted to create an interactive and informative way to showcase Brazil’s biodiversity and the Cerrado’s unique ecosystems. 

Our main goal was to help people understand how flowering patterns are connected to climate variations and inspire curiosity about the natural world. To achieve this, we combined programming, data analysis, and design to develop Bee Adventure, an interactive experience that transforms complex ecological and climate datasets into engaging visual stories accessible to people of all ages.

Join us on a journey through the Cerrado, where flowers, climate, and curiosity bloom together!  

Exploring the Bee Adventure 

The experience begins by presenting the diversity and importance of the Cerrado biome through short videos and visuals that highlight its landscapes and ecological richness.The Cerrado is one of the oldest and richest biomes on the planet, covering almost a quarter of Brazil’s territory and hosting one of the greatest biodiversity in the world. It is the cradle of waters — the source of major rivers that nourish the country — and home to thousands of unique species of plants and animals.

The app introduces users to the natural rhythm of the seasons in the Cerrado: rainy summers and dry winters that sustain its balance. However, this harmony is now threatened by climate change, prolonged droughts, deforestation, and wildfires, which affect the soil, the climate, and the flowering of plants.

As the rains return, flowers bloom and bees emerge in a vital encounter — pollination, the process that ensures fruits, seeds, and the continuity of life. Yet, environmental disruptions are breaking this synchrony, making nectar and pollen scarce and threatening both bee survival and the biome’s equilibrium.

Through this experience, users are invited to see the Cerrado through the eyes of the native bee Melipona scutellaris (known as Uruçu), exploring how flowering events connect to the balance of life across the biome.

In the interactive exploration, the user takes the role of a bee. From the bee’s perspective, you explore Cerrado landscapes across different months and seasons, observing — through interactive timelines — the flowering cycles that define the rhythm of life in this biome.

The goal is to visualize current flowering patterns and future projections for the years 2026 and 2027, understanding how climate variations may affect plant–pollinator interactions.

On screen, the selected month provides descriptive information about the season’s temperature, rainfall, and ecological conditions, based on data from the NASA POWER dataset and MODIS via Google Earth Engine.

For each month, the app displays the predicted flowering events and key native species expected to bloom during that period. By clicking on the wildflowers, the user accesses short descriptions summarizing their flowering behavior and ecological importance.

Conclusion

As the exploration concludes, the app reveals how the balance of the Cerrado depends on the synchrony between flowering and pollination. Through visual comparisons between current and projected data, users can perceive the impact of temperature rise, reduced rainfall, and habitat loss on this delicate interaction.

The experience emphasizes that even small shifts in the flowering calendar can cause mismatches between bees and flowers, affecting food availability, seed production, and the continuity of life across the biome.

Finally, users are invited to reflect on the importance of preserving native vegetation and pollinators to maintain the Cerrado’s resilience. The journey ends with a message of awareness — that each flower, each bee, and each season are vital threads in the living network that sustains one of the world’s richest ecosystems.

Technical Details

In this section, we present the technical aspects behind Bee Adventure.To develop the application, we used JavaScript, HTML, and CSS to build an interactive and user-friendly interface. We performed time series forecasting using Python with the Pandas and NeuralProphet libraries, allowing us to analyze and visualize climate patterns over time and predict trends for the next two years.

For extracting and analyzing vegetation and flowering data, we used the Google Earth Engine (GEE) API together with Python and Scikit-learn. We processed satellite imagery from the MODIS dataset and calculated the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to monitor vegetation dynamics throughout the year. This index allowed us to identify the periods of higher greenness and potential flowering in the Cerrado, providing a quantitative basis to link climatic variations with ecosystem responses.

We also used Adobe Premiere Pro for video editing and storytelling, Adobe Photoshop for image editing and composition, Adobe Illustrator for vector graphics and illustrations, and Figma for interface design and prototyping.

projectDetails.name: Project Athena
projectDetails.summary:
Athena is a digital platform designed to empower girls and young women by sharing inspiring stories of innovators and changemakers. The app combines interactive content, practical tools, and a safe online community to promote self-confidence, leadership, and personal growth.

Athena addresses key challenges faced by girls—such as low self-esteem, lack of female representation in STEAM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Math), and limited access to mentorship. Through features like a Self-Esteem Journal, Gamified Challenges, Guided Meditation, and Inspirational Mentorship, Athena provides a fun and transformative experience that strengthens emotional intelligence, social skills, and resilience.

By creating a space where girls aged 13–17 can learn, connect, and grow, Athena contributes to building a more inclusive, confident, and innovative generation of women ready to shape the future.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works Project Athena is the prototype of a mobile application designed to empower and inspire girls and women. The app is dedicated to sharing stories of innovative women and girls to inspire others. Its target audience is girls aged 13 to 17 in Brazil, with the potential for future expansion. The platform provides support and resources in areas such as health, safety, education, and professional opportunities. It uses a fun, practical, and engaging learning methodology to help users build self-confidence and develop essential skills to face daily challenges.

Key features of the Athena app prototype include:

  • A "Self-Esteem and Confidence Diary" for users to record daily thoughts and achievements.
  • Gamified challenges and missions to encourage continuous progress in a fun way.
  • Interactive learning content, including articles, videos, and quizzes on topics like emotional intelligence and leadership.
  • A section for mentorship and inspiring stories from real women who have overcome challenges.
  • A moderated, safe community for users to share experiences and receive mutual support.
  • Tools for goal and skill planning to help users define and track their objectives.
  • Guided meditation and relaxation exercises to reduce stress.
  • A resource library with e-books, guides, and practical tips on personal development.

Benefits and Intended Impact The primary benefit of Athena is to help girls and women gain confidence and empowerment. It offers social connection, knowledge exchange, and the opportunity to set goals. The project's intended impact is to address the underrepresentation of women in critical fields like Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) by fostering confidence from a young age. By doing so, we aim to break cycles of inequality and promote healthier, more prosperous societies.

The project has already demonstrated a positive impact by engaging 200 adolescents in its development phase, with an estimated 2,500 total beneficiaries. Evaluations showed the project increased the girls' confidence to pursue their desired careers, including in STEAM. Our goal is to expand the project to a global audienceand promote its use in schools to open discussions on important topics like mental health and violence against girls through a program called "Clube Athena".

Tools and Software Used The development of the Athena prototype involved a range of design and programming tools. Our team gained experience with and utilized the following software:

  • Figma(for creating the app's visual identity)
  • Canva
  • Wix
  • Bravo Studio
  • Framer
  • Excel and Google Drive with its extensions

The team also studied mobile platforms like Google Play and iOS to understand deployment requirements. The first version of the project's website can be accessed at:

https://www.athenafortalecevoce.com.br/.

Creativity and Team Considerations Our project is creative in its use of a fun, practical, and revolutionary approach to building confidence. We intentionally integrated the "Learning through Play" concept, which helped our team better engage with adolescents by respecting their pace and demonstrating the value of collective work. The use of gamification is a core part of our strategy to make personal and professional development an engaging and motivating experience.

Throughout the project, our team considered several critical factors. We recognized that our greatest challenge was engaging adolescents, which required significant effort and a thoughtful strategy. We learned the importance of having an initial visual outline to present to participants to facilitate comprehension. The project's methodology was highly collaborative, involving initial meetings with girls to shape the idea, followed by prototyping, user testing, and feedback sessions to refine the app. To ensure success, we formed specialized teams for design, development, content, and emotional support, allowing participants to contribute based on their individual skills and interests.

projectDetails.name: Project A.T.L.A.S.
projectDetails.summary:
Project A.T.L.A.S. is an immersive web experience guided by NASA's Terra satellite, personified as a friendly 3D storyteller.

The journey begins with an interactive tour of the satellite itself, where Terra introduces its five "senses"—the instruments that make its stories possible (MODIS, MOPITT, ASTER, MISR, and CERES).

From there, the experience dives into two powerful, interconnected memories: the 2004 Amazon fires (“A Forest’s Fever”) and the catastrophic 2024 Southern Brazil floods (“A Deluge of Tears”).

Our story uses layered data to reveal a profound insight: how a wound to the planet in the past contributed to a tragedy in the present.

After the guided tour, the controls are handed over. In a free-explore mode, users can scrub through 25 years of Terra data, layer instruments, and make their own discoveries.

A.T.L.A.S. is designed to reduce data friction for educators, communicators, and citizens, turning NASA's vast archives into clear, actionable stories. We turn seeing into understanding, and understanding into action.
projectDetails.details:
INTRODUCTION

What if a satellite could speak? For 25 years, NASA's Terra has watched over our planet in silence.

Project A.T.L.A.S. gives it a voice, transforming its vast, silent archive into an unforgettable, guided story about our planet's health.

We solve the challenge of turning complex data into actionable understanding by making it personal, allowing users to witness the invisible threads connecting past environmental wounds to present-day climate tragedies.

THE A.T.L.A.S. EXPERIENCE

The journey is guided by Terra itself, personified as a friendly 3D presenter, and unfolds in three acts.

Meet Your Guide: The Five Senses of an Earth Guardian

The experience begins with an interactive 3D model of the Terra satellite. As the user rotates and explores the model, our guide introduces its “five senses”—the instruments that make the story possible:

  • MODIS: Wide-angle vision for true color, fire hotspots, smoke, and floodwaters.
  • MOPITT: A ‘super-sniffer’ for tracing invisible pollution like carbon monoxide.
  • ASTER: A zoom lens for detailed 3D terrain and heat mapping.
  • MISR: Multi-angle views for adding depth to clouds and aerosols.
  • CERES: A planetary thermometer for Earth’s energy balance.

Witness the Stories: A Tale of Fever and Tears

Next, Terra guides the user through a single, powerful narrative told in two parts, connecting a wound in the past to a tragedy in the present.

Memory I: "A Forest's Fever" (Amazon, 2004)

The journey begins by traveling back to 2004, where the user witnesses one of the most intense fire seasons in the Amazon.

Terra's narration frames the rainforest as the "lungs of our planet," and in a dramatic time-lapse, the user sees it "struggle to breathe" as MODIS data reveals vast plumes of smoke scarring the landscape and hotspots glowing like a "fever on the surface."

The experience is interactive; the guide asks the user to look deeper, triggering an animated "rewind" of the memory. As the timeline flows backward, the view shifts to Terra's MOPITT 'super-sniffer,' revealing the "invisible wound" left by the fires: a massive, suffocating cloud of carbon monoxide that spread across the continent.

The Bridge: An Unbalanced Sky

Having established this profound injury, Terra's narration explains how this wound, reopened over two decades, has helped unbalance the sky. The globe then rotates, moving the user's perspective from the Amazon in 2004 to Southern Brazil in 2024 to witness the consequence.

This narrative jump is the core of the A.T.L.A.S. experience: making the long-term, invisible consequences of climate change feel immediate and undeniable.

Memory II: "A Deluge of Tears" (Southern Brazil, 2024)

After a dramatic 20-year time jump, the story shows the consequence. Terra explains how the "unbalanced sky" turned a weather system into a weapon.

Using ASTER data for a 3D view of the Andes and MODIS overlays, the user follows the atmospheric river—part of a continental climate system known as "flying rivers"—as it’s funneled towards Rio Grande do Sul.

After the clouds clear, a blinking distress sign prompts the user to open a before-and-after slider. Using MODIS imagery, the user slides between the view of the land in 2023 and the devastating aftermath in 2024, as Terra's voice describes a landscape where the river has become "bruised blue sea swallowing the land".

Your turn: Become a Planet Guardian

After the guided tour, the controls are handed over. In a free-explore mode, users can select any official NASA GIBS/Worldview data layer and scrub through 25 years of time, empowering them to tell their own stories, whether it's tracking the spread of an urban heat island, heavy particles in the atmosphere, or the recovery of a landscape after a wildfire.

IMPACT: AN EMPATHY ENGINE FOR THE PLANET

A.T.L.A.S. functions as an empathy engine, translating cold data points into a deeply human narrative to extend Terra’s legacy beyond the lab and into the hearts of a new generation.

Our goal is to empower educators, journalists, and citizens to move from seeing data to feeling its importance, and from feeling to taking action. In the spirit of NASA's commitment to open science, A.T.L.A.S. is an open, beautiful, and actionable tool for everyone who calls this planet home.

TECH STACK

Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript, built with Vite.

3D Globe & Layers: Globe.gl (on Three.js) for the globe and tile rendering; integrates NASA GIBS/Worldview WMTS layers.

UI & Motion: Tailwind CSS for styling and Framer Motion for micro-interactions.

State & Routing: Zustand for app state/presets and React Router for deep links/permalinks.

Deployment: Static CDN hosting (Vercel) with HTTP caching for tiles and assets.

GitHub repository: https://github.com/gustavogitzel/atlas-webapp

projectDetails.name: Beware Of The Rocks
projectDetails.summary: Our project aims to create an engaging, interactive web application that allows its users to visualize and understand how meteor impacts can impact our lives on Earth and also learn how we identify these objects and possible mitigation strategies and ultimately raise awareness about this topic that is not discussed enough. We hope to accomplish this through our website that combines modern visuals, 3D and 2D visualization tools, and engaging narrative to create an intuitive experience for all users. To accomplish this, we garnered data from NASA and other sources to create our models and predictions. Only by community engagement and awareness can we mitigate the dangers that these extraterrestrial objects impose on Earth and its population; that's why we believe our project can have a global impact to further advance this objective.
projectDetails.details:
Disclaimer: For a better user experience, we recommend you run your project on a desktop with the tested browsers: Google Chrome, Firefox, and Brave.

Introduction

Our group is composed of 6 computer engineering students from Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) that wanted to take a chance at a NASA hackathon. Our project will take its user through a narrative starting from a warning that a meteor is on a collision course with Earth and tasks the user with taking a course on these objects and mitigation strategies.

After that, we can choose to take the Beware of the Rocks Training Course and look at an interactive simulation of Earth. There we can create meteors and see their trajectories. We also can choose to go to an Earth meteor impact simulation where we can define the parameters of the meteor that will impact Earth and where it lands, displaying a lot of statistics about the impact, including stats like the size of the crater and the force of the impact. The course is the recommended way to experience the project for the first time.

Training Course

There we will start the course with a simulation of the Near Earth Objects (NEOs), where we can see any NEO that are near us and information about them.

After that we have an interactive gallery about ways that we can identify these objects and learn about them.

After that we are taken to the Earth Impact Simulation, where we can visualize the consequences of a direct impact and associated statistics about it.

Finally we have a last presentation about ways that we can mitigate these collisions, so we can raise awareness about these ideas that may help humanity in the future.

Earth Impact Simulation

This is an interactive simulation that the user can choose the following parameters for the impact:
Meteor Diameter

Meteor Speed

Angle Of Impact

Material of the Meteor

Localization of the Impact
After that we can visualize the following impact statistics:
Crater Size and Depth

Blast Zones

Energy of Impact

Deaths Estimates

Meteor Orbit Simulation

This is an interactive simulation that simulates the earth orbiting the sun in it's real path. We can also add meteors with the desired parameters to see the trajectory it takes.

Conclusion

We expect that after experiencing our project, the users will have a deeper understanding of the NEOs and its dangers and also more educated about ways of mitigation about them. All this in hopes that the global community will have more awareness about this topic so that we as a species can continue thriving in our only world.

Next Steps

We hope that our project will be of great help to promote knowledge and raise awareness about Meteors, and to help in this journey, we have thought of next steps that couldn't be implemented due to the time restraints:
Mobile Port to help bring Beware Of the Rocks to more people worldwide

Support to other languages than English

Bigger Meteor Orbit Simulation with other planets and more advanced physics

Technologies

Our project was built using JavaScript and React to build the webpages. We heavily used Three.JS for the Meteor Orbit Simulation and Cesium for the Earth Impact Simulation. We also used Photopea, Beepbox, Suno and Gemini AI Image Generator to help with the visual, effects and sounds.

projectDetails.name: BioKnowdes - vish
projectDetails.summary:
We developed BioKnowdes, a platform that organizes and makes the visualization of scientific knowledge contained in NASA publications a pleasant experience. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques and Large Language Models (LLMs), we extracted keywords and scientific concepts from each article and constructed a knowledge graph, connecting different articles through shared keywords. 
This structure reveals relationships between research papers, enabling scientists, decision-makers, and mission planners to discover patterns, connections, and opportunities that might otherwise remain buried in a massive amount of textual data.
The user is also able to filter this graph by keywords and visualize the resulting subgraphs, or ask our Lumi chatbot to filter it for him. Not only that, but our assistant Lumi can help the user in selecting relevant articles for his purpose and downloading them.
projectDetails.details:
BioKnowdes: Mapping NASA’s Life Sciences Knowledge

BioKnowdes is an integrated web platform designed to help researchers navigate, understand, and uncover connections within NASA’s vast collection of life sciences research.

What is BioKnowdes?

Welcome to a new way of exploring space biology.

BioKnowdes bridges the gap between complex scientific research and accessible knowledge. Whether you're a researcher, student, or space enthusiast, our platform empowers you to navigate decades of NASA's biological discoveries through intuitive tools designed to spark curiosity and drive innovation. Dive in and start your journey through the cosmos of knowledge.

The platform is built around three main components:

1. Interactive Knowledge Graph

At the core of BioKnowdes lies a knowledge graph that represents research papers as nodes and their shared concepts as connections. This visual map helps users see how studies relate to one another and identify areas of overlap or emerging trends.

Building this graph involves a three-step data pipeline:

  • PDF Text Extraction: Using Apache Tika, we extract clean text from NASA’s life sciences papers, turning unstructured PDFs into machine-readable data.
  • Keyword Extraction: With KeyBERT [1] enhanced by SciBERT (a model based on Google’s BERT, but trained on scientific texts), we identify each paper’s ten most relevant keywords. We apply Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) to keep the results both diverse and representative.
  • Graph Construction: Using NetworkX, each paper becomes a node. Connections (edges) are drawn between papers that share keywords, with the edge weight representing how many concepts they have in common. The result is a dynamic, interconnected network of research topics.

2. Similarity Heatmap

The heatmap provides a high-level view of how papers relate to one another. It measures the similarity between top research articles and visualizes these relationships in an interactive grid, highlighting clusters of related work at a glance.

3. Lumi - our AI Research Agent

Lumi is our built-in conversational agent powered by a local Large Language Model (Llama 3.1) and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system. When a user asks a question:

  1. Retrieve: Lumi searches the database for the most relevant papers using a semantic ranking tool (ArticleRanker).
  2. Augment: The key content from those papers is added as context.
  3. Generate: Lumi produces a clear, concise answer grounded in those sources, citing exactly which studies it drew from.

A Walk Through BioKnowdes

Upon accessing BioKnowdes, you enter an interactive platform that transforms decades of NASA's biological research into visual and accessible knowledge. Navigate through the main sections, discover hidden patterns, explore unexpected connections, and transform raw data into meaningful insights. You can also interact with Lumi, our AI-powered Agent and request more information about the articles.

The Search button directs you to the Knowledge Graph, where you can explore NASA publications organized by organism, mission, keyword, or biological process. Each study is presented in summarized form and connected to related works, allowing you to visualize knowledge networks and identify relationships that generate new understandings in a dynamic and intuitive way.

The Heatmap provides an interactive map that reveals the areas of highest research concentration in space biology. With this tool, you can identify emerging trends, detect gaps in scientific knowledge, and understand which topics have received the most attention—all in a visual and intuitive manner.

You can use our Lumi assistant to select the articles that best match your question. The assistant will ask what your question or intention is, and based on your response, it will search our database for the articles that best fit the context you're looking for, giving you the option to start a conversation with Lumi. Lumi will then load the articles and begin a conversation with you, responding based on the most relevant articles for the topic you've chosen.

 

In Browse Articles, you can explore NASA's biological research publications in a structured and organized manner. Filter by date, topic, mission, or author to find exactly what you're looking for. This comprehensive library gives you direct access to the original studies that power our platform, allowing for deeper exploration and detailed analysis.

 In AskLumi, you interact with Lumi, our artificial intelligence assistant. Ask questions in natural language—such as "How does microgravity affect plant growth?"—and receive answers grounded directly in NASA publications. It's the fastest and smartest way to explore decades of accumulated scientific knowledge.

 The Help tab brings together a practical guide with step-by-step instructions, usage examples, and quick answers on how to take advantage of all BioKnowdes functionalities. Ideal for both new users and those looking to explore the platform's advanced features.

 In the About Us section, you meet the team behind the project: students united by the purpose of democratizing access to scientific knowledge. Our mission is to transform complex information into clear understanding and convert academic research into real impact for society.

obs: for deployment reasons we changed the local model for Openai API

Why It Matters

The main goal of BioKnowdes is to make space life sciences research more accessible and interconnected—to help scientists discover faster, collaborate smarter, and innovate further.

Key Benefits:

  • Faster Research: Find related studies and relevant information in minutes instead of days.
  • New Discoveries: The visual graph can reveal unexpected links between fields.
  • Broader Access: The AI assistant lowers barriers for students and interdisciplinary researchers to explore NASA’s data.

Intended Impact:

  • Support long-term space missions—like Artemis and future Mars expeditions—by helping researchers quickly build on existing work on human health in space.
  • Encourage innovation by connecting ideas across different scientific areas.
  • Translate space-based biological insights to improve health solutions on Earth.

Technology Stack

Backend: Python + Flask
Data Processing: Apache Tika (text extraction), Pandas, and NetworkX (graph building)
AI & Modeling:

LangChain to coordinate the RAG workflow

Ollama to run Llama 3.1 locally

Sentence-Transformers, KeyBERT, and SciBERT for semantic understanding
Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Visualization: Pyvis Network (interactive graph) and Plotly (heatmap)
Storage: JSONL and Pickle formats for quick loading and manipulation

What Makes It Unique

BioKnowdes combines three modes of discovery—a visual graph, a similarity heatmap, and an intelligent assistant—into one cohesive experience.

A researcher might begin by exploring a cluster of studies in the graph, zoom into a specific theme using the heatmap, and then ask Lumi targeted questions for deeper insight. This layered approach makes research exploration intuitive and engaging.

Design Principles

Throughout development, our focus has been on:

  • User Experience: Supporting different research styles—visual, analytical, or conversational.
  • Trustworthy AI: Lumi’s RAG system ensures every answer is backed by real, citable data.
  • Accessibility & Independence: The entire system runs on open-source tools, with no reliance on proprietary APIs.
  • Meaningful Representation: We use graph structures because science itself is about relationships—between ideas, discoveries, and people.

References

projectDetails.name: BioSpace Atlas
projectDetails.summary:
NASA holds an immense collection of scientific research and discoveries accumulated over decades. However, finding specific information within this ocean of data can be a real challenge.
With this in mind, we developed Bio Space Atlas, a web platform that transforms this search into a fast, visual, accessible, and engaging experience. Through it, users can explore the universe of space biology using dynamic filters, interactive timelines, word clouds, and simplified explanations.
The platform leverages RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architecture to generate contextual answers from NASA’s Space Biology Publications database, making science more understandable to the general public.
In addition, it offers two response modes:
Story Mode, designed for curious minds and beginners, and Research Mode, aimed at students and scientists.
To ensure knowledge is accessible to everyone, the system can translate complex scientific terms into clear, educational language.
Thus, Bio Space Atlas connects space science to people in an intuitive and interactive way — transforming data into accessible discoveries for scientists, students, and curious learners at all levels.
projectDetails.details:
Bio Space Atlas offers two learning modes:

Story Mode (for beginners):

A narrative experience where AI transforms scientific knowledge into engaging, illustrated stories — making learning light, imaginative, and accessible.

Research Mode (for advanced users):

An interactive chat environment where users can dive deeper into specific topics, access scientific sources, and explore related subjects in detail.

As users interact, they unlock “knowledge stories”, recorded in a Logbook that symbolizes their own scientific journey.

On the home screen, users can also take part in the “Mission of the Day” — a small challenge that tests learning and sparks curiosity.

Through these features, the project aims to make scientific knowledge more accessible, inspiring, and interactive — showing that for Bio Space Atlas, the sky is not the limit, but the entire universe.

Main Features

1. Knowledge Engine (RAG Engine)

At the core of the project is the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine, responsible for:

  • Processing NASA’s public dataset SB_publications.csv;
  • Generating semantic embeddings;
  • Indexing and retrieving information;
  • Producing contextualized answers.

2. Response Modes

  • Story Mode (for beginners): Translates scientific results into illustrated narratives with light, engaging, and educational text.
  • Research Mode (for advanced users): Provides technical answers, citations, links to scientific papers, and related topics, facilitating academic exploration.

3. Library and Logbook

Each new interaction generates a “knowledge story” that is recorded in a personal Logbook, representing the user’s learning journey. This mechanic transforms the experience into a scientific voyage, where every discovery becomes a new chapter.

4. Mission of the Day

The “Challenge Yourself” section presents a daily question related to space biology. Users can submit their answers and receive instant AI feedback — encouraging active learning and scientific curiosity.

Technical details

  1. Programming Languages:

Python 3.10+ (backend, data, ML)

JavaScript / TypeScript (frontend)

  1. Backend:

FastAPI (main web framework for APIs)

Uvicorn (server runner)

Argparse (CLI execution for workflows)

Logging (custom logs for process tracking)

Pandas (data manipulation and metadata handling)

Selenium (for NASA WEB data scraping)

PyMuPDF (fitz) and pdfminer.six (PDF text extraction)

tqdm (progress visualization)

Torch (embedding computation backend)

Transformers (for embedding and LLM loading)

Sentence-transformers (for BGE embedding model)

LlamaIndex and LangChain (for chunking and RAG orchestration)

FAISS (vector store)

SpaCy (NER and text analysis)

NetworkX (knowledge graph representation)

JSON (data serialization)

Requests or HTTPX (for external API calls)

Pytest (for unit testing)

  1. Data and Storage:

AWS S3 (storage for PDFs)

Local FAISS index (vector store)

JSON files (metadata, extracted insights)

Neo4j AuraDB Free (knowledge graph persistence)

  1. Frontend:

React (main web framework)

TailwindCSS (styling)

Wordcloud and Plotly.js (data and map visualizations)

HTML/CSS/JS standard stack

  1. Infrastructure / Cloud:

AWS Free Tier (S3 for data, EC2 or Lambda for backend)

A CONFIRMAR (frontend hosting)

Hugging Face Hub (model source)

GitHub (version control)

  1. Development Tools:

Git (versioning)

Black (code formatting)

VS Code and Spyder (IDE)

Conda (development environment)

README.md (documentation)

Data Sources

 Main Database: SB_publication_PMC.csv — a public dataset provided by NASA containing metadata of publications on space biology, such as:

  • Title, authors, and year of publication;
  • Abstract and keywords;
  • Studied organisms;
  • DOI and link to access the full article.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
A Inteligência Artificial foi utilizada no projeto exclusivamente para processamento e análise textual por meio de técnicas de Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Esse processo envolve a indexação semântica de mais de 600 artigos científicos sobre biologia espacial, utilizando modelos de embeddings (como BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) para converter textos em vetores numéricos que representam seu significado. Em seguida, um modelo de linguagem (LLM) é utilizado para gerar respostas contextualizadas com base nos documentos recuperados, garantindo que as informações apresentadas sejam precisas e fundamentadas em publicações reais.

Além disso, a IA é aplicada para extração de entidades e relações científicas (como genes, espécies, e experimentos) e classificação temática automática dos textos e perguntas em áreas como biotecnologia, neurociência, bioquímica, ecologia, microbiologia e genética. Essas técnicas foram implementadas em módulos específicos de backend, sem o uso de IA para geração de imagens, vídeos ou áudios, garantindo a transparência e rastreabilidade científica dos resultados.

projectDetails.name: AgroClimate Game
projectDetails.summary: AgroClimate Quiz is an educational game that transforms open data from NASA—including maps of warming, soil moisture, and precipitation in Brazil—into an interactive quiz-based experience. The goal is to bring complex scientific data closer to practical decisions in the field, helping farmers, students, and the general public understand how climate variables affect sustainable agricultural practices. The game directly addresses the challenge of integrating technology and data into agriculture, making complex information accessible and applicable. Its importance lies in enabling players to understand and use real environmental data, promoting learning, awareness of sustainability, efficient use of natural resources, and agricultural practices that are more resilient to climate change.
projectDetails.details:
The Game

Our project, AgroClimate Quiz, is an educational quiz game that helps players understand how climate variables affect agricultural decisions. It was created to make NASA's open satellite data — such as soil moisture, surface temperature, and precipitation maps — more accessible and applicable to farmers, students, and the general public.

The game presents challenges in quiz format, using real maps created with NASA data that show, for example, levels of warming, soil moisture, and precipitation in Brazil. Each map challenges the player to find the point of highest incidence of the variable in question (warming, soil moisture, or precipitation).

Several points are distributed across the map, only one of which indicates the position where the analyzed variable recurs most frequently. If the wrong point is chosen, the player immediately receives feedback to try again at another point. Similarly, when the correct point is chosen, the player receives feedback confirming the correct answer and is automatically sent to the next map.

The game was developed using the RPG Maker MZ application, which can be downloaded and installed free of charge from the developer's official website. The application features well-organized interfaces and offers countless possibilities for unleashing the creativity of those producing their games.

The end of the game provides a review of what has been learned about the use of NASA data in sustainable agriculture. It highlights that temperature maps help choose heat-resistant crops and plan planting seasons; precipitation maps guide the efficient use of irrigation or drainage; and soil moisture maps indicate how to adjust irrigation and fertilizer use.

It also shows that technologies such as controlled-release fertilizers, sensors, and drones allow resources to be applied only where they are needed.

The final message is that data is not just numbers, but information that guides smart decisions, allowing us to produce more, save resources, and preserve the environment.

Benefits

This project brings numerous benefits from various perspectives. Educationally, it brings scientific data closer to the public, helping to interpret climate maps and apply them to real decisions. The game raises awareness in a practical way by demonstrating how the use of data can improve sustainability and resilience in agriculture. In addition to being an inclusive game that is accessible to students, novice farmers, and rural communities, even those without scientific training, it can be adapted to different countries, agricultural cultures, and new data sets.

Impact

The AgroClimate Quiz transforms NASA climate data into an educational tool that brings science and agricultural practice closer together. Its impact is integrated, combining educational, environmental, economic, and social benefits. The game allows farmers, students, and communities to understand how variables such as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture influence crops and learn to make more efficient and sustainable decisions.

By promoting the conscious use of water and fertilizers, the project contributes to reducing waste, preserving soil, and decreasing environmental impacts such as pollution and ecosystem degradation. It also strengthens agricultural productivity by reducing losses and costs, especially for small and medium-sized producers, who often do not have access to complex scientific information.

In addition, AgroClimateQuiz democratizes climate knowledge by making satellite data accessible to a wide audience, including rural communities and young people, encouraging innovation and the adoption of agricultural practices that are more resilient to climate change. In the long term, the project supports the development of smarter and more sustainable agriculture, strengthening food security, natural resource conservation, and the resilience of agricultural communities in the face of global environmental challenges.

Motivating Factors


In developing the AgroClimate Quiz, the team considered key factors to ensure that the game was educational, accessible, and relevant to different audiences. The aim was to align the design of the experience with the goal of translating complex NASA climate data into clear information applicable to agricultural practice, while keeping the interface intuitive and attractive to players without technical training. The choice of the RPG Maker MZ platform as a tool was motivated by its ability to create interactive environments in an agile and accessible way. The reliability and limitations of the data used were also evaluated in order to present scenarios that reflected the real challenges faced by farmers. Another key point was the inclusion of the perspective of sustainability, considering how the decisions presented in the game could impact productivity, natural resources, and adaptation to climate change. Finally, we sought to balance playful and educational elements so that the experience would be both engaging and capable of raising awareness about the importance of agricultural practices based on science and technology.

projectDetails.name: Stranded: A Sticker Story
projectDetails.summary:
Stellar Stories is an interactive digital storybook designed to make space weather science accessible and compelling for high school students from ages 14 to 18 as target audience. It turns complex heliophysics into a narrative-driven story you can actually experience.

Our book follows Captain Juca stranded in space. Through a dialogue with a personified Sun, readers are introduced to core concepts like solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). The platform masterfully fuses storytelling and play, each mini-game helps the reader complete the adventure. Success is rewarded with collectible digital sticker packs, which are used to progressively complete the book's vibrant illustrations, creating a compelling loop that encourages players to fill their "cosmic album" and, in doing so, master key scientific principles.

Throughout the story, readers come across interactive models created from NASA’s Resources to better understand the concepts and impacts of space weather. Stranded ensures scientific accuracy while prioritizing emotional connection and intuitive design. It directly illustrates the impacts of solar activity on critical Earth infrastructure, including aviation, agriculture, and power systems. By transforming raw space data into a personal adventure, the story fosters scientific literacy and helps readers feel our real connection to the Sun.
projectDetails.details:
Team CaLiRaThAnCa | NASA Space Apps Campinas – Brazil

The project is the Storybook "Stranded", an interactive, comics-themed web platform that merges storytelling and gamification into a digital sticker album. Designed for high school students, it transforms NASA’s space weather resources into a fun and immersive learning experience about how the Sun affects life on Earth.

The platform invites users to freely flip through an illustrated, comic-style storybook that blends narrative with education. To unlock new stickers and complete their album, players must engage in mini-games and challenges. These interactive activities turn abstract science into a tangible experience, helping them absorb complex solar phenomena in a simple, visual, and immersive way.

Project Objectives

The project’s goal is to translate scientific information into accessible and emotionally engaging experiences, fostering public understanding of space weather’s impact on Earth systems. Using NASA’s open space weather resources, data from Heliophysics Focus Areas, Solar Storms and Flares, and the 2024 Space Weather Advisory Group (SWAG) findings, the narrative maintains both scientific accuracy and creativity.


Sticker Album - How the Story is Told


The platform invites users to freely flip through an illustrated, comic-style storybook that blends narrative with education. To unlock new pages and complete their album, players must engage in mini-games and challenges, having some special shiny stickers to conquer along the way. These interactive activities turn abstract science into a tangible experience, helping them absorb complex solar phenomena in a simple, visual, and immersive way.

The reader can also check the progress of his own sticker collection! The more you play, the more your album shines!

Open the Book: Initiation & Tutorial

The first page guides the reader into the dynamics of the storybook, introducing how to navigate, collect, and place their stickers. Through an interactive tutorial, players meet Captain Juca and learn how challenges and mini-games unlock new pages in the album. Friendly visual cues and animations explain each step, ensuring an intuitive start for all users.

The Story


In this Storybook, players follow Captain Juca, an astronaut capybara stranded in space after a radio signal malfunction. During his adventure, he meets the Sun and a lively Coronal Mass Ejection (CME), a personified solar storm. Together they explore how flares and CMEs travel through space, interact with Earth’s magnetic field, and affect daily life on our planet: from farmers and pilots to astronauts and power grid operators.

NASA’s Data in Action


To bridge the story with real scientific exploration, users can also explore a 3D interactive model that displays the Earth’s magnetosphere and the probability of auroral activity across different latitudes, allowing them to observe how solar storms influence our planet from a global perspective. By integrating datasets from NASA’s Heliophysics and Space Weather Prediction Centers, the tool transforms raw scientific information into a tangible, visual experience that complements the story’s educational goals.

Users can rotate, zoom, and navigate the planet in three dimensions, gaining an intuitive understanding of how variations in solar activity translate into visible auroras and geomagnetic effects on Earth.

Another model lets you visualize an interactive graph from NOAA’s D-Region Absorption Predictions (D-RAP), which forecasts how solar X-rays and energetic particles affect Earth’s ionosphere, increasing radio-signal absorption and occasionally disrupting communications and satellite systems like GPS and internet during strong solar events.

The Mini Games


To unlock new pages of the sticker album, players complete four short mini-games throughout the book, that transform NASA’s space weather data into interactive learning. Each game links a scientific concept to playful challenges, helping users understand how solar storms affect Earth and human technology.

NOTE: The non-completion of the games does not affect the reader's ability to read the story! The reader will only choose to miss out on the beautiful complete visuals curated for the best experience.

How It Was Made


Developed with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and designed with Canva, the prototype delivers a lightweight, browser-based experience that is interactive, visually immersive, and accessible on any device, from computers to tablets and smartphones.

The source code can be found on the link below: https://github.com/ThallesCansi/CaLiRaThAnCa.

Conclusion


Stranded reimagines science communication: Creativity lies in blending science communication with storytelling, where education meets play, and a capybara astronaut becomes the bridge between human curiosity and the Sun’s cosmic tales.
