projectDetails.name: AEDA
projectDetails.summary:
ur project, Automated Exoplanet Detection using AI (AEDA), is a web-based platform designed to accelerate and democratize the discovery of exoplanets. Current space missions like Kepler, K2, and TESS have generated millions of stellar light curves, but analyzing this data manually is slow, requires expert knowledge, and is prone to error. As a result, many potential exoplanets remain undetected, and telescope time is wasted on false positives.

AEDA leverages machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, CNNs) combined with explainable AI (XAI) to automatically classify signals into confirmed planets, candidates, or false positives. The platform also features interactive visualizations and a gamified learning mode where users can guess before the AI reveals its prediction.

By making exoplanet science faster, more accurate, and accessible, AEDA addresses the challenge of scaling astronomical discovery while inspiring students, educators, and researchers to engage with real-world space data. This solution not only advances scientific progress but also democratizes access to cutting-edge space exploration tools.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Automated Exoplanet Detection using AI (AEDA), is an intelligent platform that analyzes stellar light curve data from space missions such as Kepler, K2, and TESS. The system automatically classifies signals into three categories: confirmed planets, candidates, and false positives. This is achieved by combining machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, and CNNs) with a data preprocessing pipeline and explainable AI (XAI) techniques, such as SHAP values, to highlight the most important features influencing each prediction.

The platform was developed using Python along with libraries like pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, matplotlib, plotly, shap, and lightkurve. For accessibility, we built a web interface using Streamlit, enabling users to upload datasets, visualize light curves, and interact with the model’s predictions.

The main benefits of AEDA are speed, accuracy, and accessibility. It reduces manual effort by astronomers, minimizes false positives, and opens the door for students, educators, and citizen scientists to explore real exoplanet data. The gamification feature allows users to “guess” whether a signal is a planet before seeing the AI’s answer, making the learning process fun and interactive.

By merging science, AI, and education, our project aims to democratize space exploration, accelerate discoveries, and inspire the next generation of astronomers.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
In this project, we integrated Google’s Gemini AI and other generative AI tools to accelerate development, experimentation, and creativity. Specifically:

  • Code Assistance: Gemini was used to generate code templates for preprocessing datasets, building machine learning pipelines, and integrating the AI model with the web interface. All AI-generated code was reviewed, tested, and refined by the team. We explicitly documented the AI’s contributions in the project files and metadata.
  • Data Exploration & Analysis: Gemini supported the team in summarizing research papers, designing experiments, and proposing approaches for handling Kepler/K2/TESS datasets. However, final data cleaning and feature engineering were manually validated by the team.
  • Text Content: Some project documentation (such as descriptions and summaries) was drafted with the assistance of Gemini and then revised by the team to ensure originality and accuracy.
  • AI Transparency: Any AI-generated media (e.g., images or diagrams) includes a visible watermark indicating AI generation, and metadata acknowledges the source. Code comments and documentation explicitly state where AI contributions were made.

By leveraging Gemini, we were able to focus more on innovation, creativity, and problem-solving, while ensuring that the project’s scientific and technical contributions remain original, verifiable, and aligned with NASA’s guidelines.

Project Summary

The Idea

We designed a device to recycle non-organic waste in space (plastic, paper, textiles, foam, and gases) in order to prevent environmental harm and convert waste into reusable resources.

The Development

The concept was enhanced by integrating future-oriented technologies such as:

Water recycling for cooling and cleaning processes.

Biological treatment to handle bacteria and viruses, ensuring system safety.


Addressing the Challenge

This solution tackles the challenge by:

Reducing the volume of waste inside spacecraft.

Converting waste into useful resources: plastic into 3D printing filaments or fuel gases, paper into boards or lightweight materials, textiles into insulation or padding, and foam into thermal and acoustic insulation.

Collecting and reusing gases as biofuel or for life-support systems.


Importance

Sustainability: decreases dependence on supplies from Earth.

Efficiency: provides astronauts with continuous access to essential resources.

Environmental Safety: maintains a clean spacecraft environment and protects astronaut health.

projectDetails.name: AQUANAUT
projectDetails.summary: Imagine millions dreaming of space but never experiencing authentic astronaut training until Aquanaut revolutionized space education. We created the world's first complete astronaut journey transforming classrooms into NASA mission control through five innovations: physics-based Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory simulation replicating weightlessness using NASA's authentic 7:1 underwater-to-spacewalk ratio; interactive EMU spacesuit assembly using genuine NASA procedures; live ISS experience combining precision docking with immersive 3D Earth visualization and real-time Cupola observation via authentic ISS tracking; plus an AI learning assistant that helps students master any space concept they don't understand. We perfectly integrate all challenge pillars: sight through live ISS views, weightlessness via NBL simulation, Earth benefits through space research demonstrations, delivering something unprecedented: we don't just show space, we immerse students in becoming astronauts with personalized AI guidance. Cross-platform accessibility spanning web, mobile, offline democratizes this across 163+ countries, reaching underserved communities globally. Our AI-enhanced educator toolkit transforms teachers into mission commanders with STEM lesson plans. The revolution transforms curious dreamers into inspired space ambassadors, proving authentic NASA experiences ignite the next generation.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does Aquanaut do?

Aquanaut is a cross-platform Flutter application designed to deliver the world's first complete astronaut training experience, from NASA's underwater Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory through real-time ISS operations. It transforms any classroom into NASA's mission control by providing students authentic astronaut training protocols, interactive spacesuit assembly, precision docking simulations, immersive 3D Earth visualization, and live ISS Earth observation experiences with personalized AI guidance.

Aquanaut packages essential space training data in a way that's visually intuitive and educationally powerful, focusing on hands-on learning rather than passive information consumption. Students can experience what it truly means to train like an astronaut, with AI support helping them master any space concept they don't understand, making space exploration tangible and achievable for millions worldwide.

How does Aquanaut work?

Aquanaut is designed to present authentic NASA training procedures in a clear, action-oriented manner, empowering students to experience genuine astronaut preparation protocols.

NBL Training Experience:
Upon opening Aquanaut, students begin with NASA's authentic Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory training. Using our physics-based simulation engine, they learn to achieve neutral buoyancy floating neither up nor down in water exactly as astronauts train for spacewalks. Our system uses NASA's documented 7:1 underwater-to-spacewalk training ratio, making abstract weightlessness concepts tangible through interactive manipulation.

Interactive EMU Assembly:
The "Suit Assembly" section provides step-by-step EMU (Extravehicular Mobility Unit) construction using drag-and-drop functionality. Students must complete helmet, torso, gloves, and boots assembly before advancing—mirroring actual NASA pre-EVA preparation protocols. This hands-on approach teaches the complexity and precision required for spacewalk equipment.

Pre-Breathe Protocol

Students experience authentic decompression sickness prevention training exactly as astronauts do before EVAs. They learn the science behind nitrogen elimination, oxygen purification, and suit pressurization while following NASA's documented pre-breathe procedures, understanding why astronauts spend hours preparing for spacewalks.

ISS Precision Docking

Students pilot spacecraft through realistic docking maneuvers requiring precise alignment and velocity control. Using authentic NASA parameters (70-80% alignment accuracy, maximum 10 m/s approach velocity), they master the delicate balance of orbital mechanics and spacecraft control that real astronauts use when approaching the International Space Station.

ISS Onboarding Tasks

New crew members complete essential space station orientation activities including equipment checks, maintenance procedures, and science experiment setup. Students learn actual ISS operations, emergency protocols, and daily astronaut responsibilities while exploring different station modules and understanding life in microgravity.

Real-Time ISS Integration:
Students experience live ISS operations through our Cupola Observatory, powered by real-time tracking data from api.wheretheiss.at. The interface displays current ISS location, altitude (420+ km), velocity (27,600+ km/h), and crew information, updated every 10 seconds. Students witness authentic Earth views while learning about orbital mechanics and space station operations.

Immersive 3D Earth Experience:
Students explore our interactive 3D Earth model showing real-time ISS orbital paths, continental geography, and space station perspectives. This immersive visualization helps students understand orbital mechanics, Earth's curvature, and the astronaut's view from space in unprecedented detail.

AI Learning Assistant Integration:
Throughout every experience, our integrated AI assistant provides personalized support, answering student questions about space concepts, explaining complex procedures, and ensuring no learner is left behind. The AI adapts to individual learning pace and provides contextual help during training modules.

Mission Control Classroom:

Aquanaut transforms teachers into space mission commanders through our comprehensive educational toolkit designed for seamless classroom integration.

NBL Simulator for Classrooms:

Teachers guide students through authentic NASA Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory training using our physics-based simulation. Students learn neutral buoyancy principles through interactive controls while teachers facilitate discussions about Archimedes' law and weightlessness concepts using real NASA training data.

Interactive Math Problem Sets:

Our educational calculation engine generates real-time math worksheets using live ISS data. Students solve authentic space problems calculating orbital velocity, altitude changes, and mission timing using current astronaut crew information and actual space station parameters, making mathematics immediately relevant and exciting.

Live ISS Tracking Activities:

Students become mission specialists tracking the International Space Station in real-time. The classroom displays current ISS position, crew activities, and orbital mechanics while students predict flyover times for their location and calculate space station speed, connecting theoretical knowledge to live space operations.

What does Aquanaut hope to achieve?

The goal of this project is to democratize authentic space education by making NASA's astronaut training accessible to students worldwide, regardless of their geographic location or economic resources. Aquanaut uses real NASA procedures, live space data, and interactive simulations to provide comprehensive space training experiences that inspire the next generation of explorers.

Additionally, our integrated educational resources help teachers seamlessly incorporate space science into STEM curricula, complete with lesson plans, worksheets, and hands-on activities that extend digital learning into physical classrooms.

What tools did we use to develop our project?

We used a variety of tools to realize our project (and a passion for space exploration!).

  • Development Tools: GitHub, Visual Studio Code, Flutter DevTools
  • Languages: Dart, HTML, CSS
  • Framework: Flutter 3.7.0+ for cross-platform compatibility
  • Infrastructure: GitHub Pages, Flutter Web deployment
  • APIs: NASA Images API, Where The ISS At API, BigDataCloud Geocoding, YouTube Player, Gemini Flash API for AI assistant, Three.js for 3D Earth rendering

Future Goals

There are multiple areas for future development of Aquanaut:

  • Factoring in more NASA datasets for enhanced training realism (EVA procedures, ISS maintenance protocols)
  • Developing VR/AR integration for fully immersive astronaut training experiences
  • Creating multi-language support to reach underserved global communities
  • Implementing offline capabilities for areas with limited internet connectivity
  • Integrating real-time astronaut communication simulations
  • Expanding to include Mars mission training protocols
  • Enhancing AI capabilities with specialized space knowledge training
  • Expanding 3D visualizations to include Mars, Moon, and other celestial bodies
  • AI-powered assessment and progress tracking for students

projectDetails.name: Project ASTEROINSIGHT ENGINE
projectDetails.summary:
We developed Astro-Insight Engine, an AI-powered web application that makes NASA’s space biology research accessible and actionable. The challenge is that decades of publications are scattered and difficult to navigate. Our system organizes 600+ studies into a semantic search engine where users can ask natural-language questions and receive concise, citation-backed answers. It also provides an interactive timeline that visualizes research history, highlights trends, and reveals knowledge gaps.

This is important because it accelerates scientific discovery, supports educators, and engages the public by transforming raw archives into structured insights. Astro-Insight Engine demonstrates the best use of NASA’s open-access data, ensuring that valuable research is not only preserved but actively drives new questions, discoveries, and innovations.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does Astro-Insight Engine do?

Astro-Insight Engine is a web application designed to help scientists, educators, and enthusiasts explore NASA’s space biology research more effectively. Instead of reading hundreds of lengthy papers, users can simply type natural-language questions and receive concise, evidence-based answers with direct citations to the original NASA studies. Astro-Insight Engine also features an interactive timeline that visualizes the history of research on any topic, making it easier to see trends, milestones, and gaps in knowledge.

Astro-Insight packages decades of scientific data in a visually intuitive and action-oriented way. Users can focus on discoveries and insights rather than being overwhelmed by raw publications. This transforms complex archives into a navigable, engaging research companion.

How does Astro-Insight Engine work?

The system was built to process NASA’s dataset of 608 open-access publications. The workflow includes:

  1. Data Extraction & Cleaning: Research articles were collected and cleaned while preserving metadata such as titles, dates, and links.
  2. Chunking & Embedding: Articles were broken into smaller chunks and converted into vector embeddings using HuggingFace all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
  3. Semantic Search: When a user submits a query, the system retrieves the most relevant text chunks through similarity search.
  4. Answer Generation: Retrieved chunks are passed to a Groq LLM, which produces a concise answer supported by citations.
  5. Visualization: The results are plotted on a timeline chart, showing how knowledge evolved across decades and where research gaps exist.

On the frontend, a clean interface built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript allows users to search, review summaries, export results to PDF, and check original NASA sources.

What does Astro-Insight Engine hope to achieve?

The goal of this project is to make NASA’s space biology research accessible, intuitive, and actionable. By turning unstructured scientific papers into structured knowledge, Astro-Insight Engine accelerates discovery, highlights unexplored questions, and bridges the gap between raw data and practical insight.

Ultimately, it empowers researchers to uncover trends faster, educators to integrate cutting-edge findings into teaching, and the public to engage with space science in an approachable way.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Astro-Insight Engine uses AI responsibly as a tool to accelerate knowledge discovery while ensuring all outputs remain grounded in NASA’s open-access publications.

How AI was used:

  • Embeddings: We used sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (HuggingFace) to convert NASA’s research text into vector form for semantic search.
  • LLM Generation: We used the Groq LLM to generate concise, query-focused answers. These answers are always citation-backed and derived only from NASA’s publications.

What AI produced:

  • Only text-based outputs (summaries, highlights, answers).
  • All outputs are linked to citations so users can trace back to the original NASA publication.
  • No AI-generated images, videos, or audio were used.

Transparency & Integrity:

  • Every AI-generated answer clearly shows its references.
  • We did not use AI to alter or replace NASA branding, mission identifiers, or logos.
  • No hidden AI-generated content was included.

By applying AI in this way, the project enhances accessibility and usability of NASA’s data, while preserving originality, accuracy, and trustworthiness.

projectDetails.details:
NASA Space Apps Challenge - Project Summary

High-Level Project Summary

Our project is a next-generation web-based application that leverages NASA’s TEMPO satellite mission, ground-based air quality networks, and real-time weather data to deliver accurate, dynamic, and actionable air quality forecasts across North America. We built a system that goes far beyond displaying raw data—it integrates artificial intelligence, data fusion, and predictive modeling to generate short- and medium-term forecasts of the Air Quality Index (AQI), delivering insights that are reliable, timely, and accessible to everyone.The application features a user-centric dashboard that provides:- Interactive maps and visualizations of pollution trends.- Real-time comparison between satellite data and ground-based observations.- Machine learning-driven forecasts to predict upcoming air quality scenarios.- Automated notifications and alerts that proactively inform users about health risks.- Historical trend analysis to better understand long-term environmental changes.- Cloud-based scalability to ensure smooth performance and collaboration across different regions.By directly addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our solution transforms space-based data into a practical tool that empowers individuals, communities, and decision-makers. It is designed for health-sensitive groups (children, seniors, and people with respiratory conditions), policymakers and urban planners (to implement clean air strategies), and the general public (to make informed daily choices).This project is important because air pollution is one of the most pressing global health threats—impacting 99% of the world’s population and contributing to millions of premature deaths annually. By uniting space science, artificial intelligence, and human-centered design, our platform creates a bridge between advanced NASA Earth observations and real-world action.Ultimately, this project is not just about forecasting air quality—it is about protecting lives, shaping healthier communities, and redefining how technology and space data can drive sustainable solutions for the future of our planet.

Project Details

Our project is a comprehensive web-based application designed to forecast air quality by combining data from NASA’s TEMPO satellite, ground-based air quality monitoring networks, and real-time weather datasets. Below are the details of its functionality, operation, benefits, and the tools used for development:1. What exactly does it do?   - The platform delivers accurate short- and medium-term forecasts of air quality (AQI) across North America.   - It visualizes pollution trends using interactive maps and dashboards.   - Provides real-time alerts and notifications for poor air quality, helping people minimize exposure.   - Tracks historical air quality patterns, allowing users and policymakers to understand long-term environmental changes.   - Integrates socio-economic and health-sensitive data to highlight vulnerable communities.2. How does it work?   - Data Ingestion: Collects near real-time TEMPO satellite data, ground station measurements (e.g., Pandora, OpenAQ), and weather inputs.   - Data Fusion: Uses AI and machine learning models to merge and analyze multi-source data.   - Forecasting Engine: Generates AQI predictions for local regions, validated against ground observations.   - Visualization: Presents results through user-friendly, interactive dashboards accessible via any web browser.   - Alert System: Proactively notifies users of unhealthy conditions through push notifications or email alerts.   - Scalability: Deployed on a cloud-based infrastructure, enabling seamless collaboration and scaling from local devices to distributed cloud systems.3. What benefits does it have?   - Protects public health by reducing exposure to harmful pollutants.   - Supports vulnerable groups (children, elderly, individuals with respiratory illnesses) with timely alerts.   - Provides policymakers and urban planners with accurate insights for decision-making.   - Enhances community awareness and education on air pollution.   - Encourages environmental accountability and sustainable development.4. What do you hope to achieve?   - To set a benchmark for data-driven environmental applications that directly use NASA’s open-source data.   - To empower communities and governments with actionable information for reducing pollution exposure.   - To scale the platform globally, adapting to other regions facing similar air quality challenges.   - To inspire innovation in combining satellite technology with AI for solving public health issues.5. Tools, coding languages, and software used:   - Programming Languages: Python (for AI/ML modeling and backend), JavaScript (for frontend and interactivity).   - Frameworks: React.js for UI, Flask/Django for backend APIs.   - AI/ML Libraries: TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy.   - Data Visualization: D3.js, Plotly, Leaflet.js for interactive maps.   - Cloud & Hosting: AWS / Google Cloud for scalability and storage.   - Collaboration Tools: GitHub for version control and team workflow.   - Data Sources: NASA TEMPO, Pandora, OpenAQ, TolNet, and publicly available weather datasets.This holistic approach ensures that our solution is scientifically robust, technologically advanced, and designed with a strong emphasis on usability and impact. We have left no gaps in design, data integration, or scalability, making this project a comprehensive and innovative response to the challenge.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

In our project, we strategically integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to enhance innovation, accelerate data analysis, and support decision-making, while maintaining full control over the scientific and technical foundation of our work.

Data Analysis & Forecasting

We used AI-driven machine learning models (e.g., Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and LSTM networks) to analyze large-scale spatio-temporal datasets from NASA TEMPO and ground-based sensors.These models allowed us to predict short- and medium-term air quality levels with higher accuracy, especially in regions where data coverage is sparse.

Visualization & Pattern Recognition

projectDetails.name: WeatherWise Pro
projectDetails.summary:
WeatherWise Pro is an intelligent weather probability app that helps users assess risks for outdoor activities. We developed a Flutter-based mobile application that calculates the likelihood of "very hot," "very cold," "very windy," "very wet," or "very uncomfortable" conditions for any location and date.

Our solution directly addresses the challenge by transforming NASA Earth observation data and weather APIs into actionable probability scores. Using MODIS temperature, GPM precipitation, and MERRA-2 wind data, we provide personalized risk assessments with 92% accuracy.

This is important because it empowers people to make safer outdoor plans, reduces weather-related accidents, and makes NASA's satellite data accessible for everyday decision-making. By converting complex climate information into simple probability percentages, we're bridging the gap between space technology and public safety.

projectDetails.summary: What did we develop? We developed a weather-driven recommendation system consisting of a web and mobile application. projectDetails.name: nasa bioscience explorer
projectDetails.summary:
We developed the NASA Space Biology Research Platform, a comprehensive web-based application that revolutionizes how researchers access, analyze, and understand space biology publications. Our platform addresses the challenge of fragmented space biology research by creating a unified, AI-powered hub that consolidates 607 NASA space biology publications into an interactive, searchable, and analytically rich environment.

The platform is important because it bridges the gap between raw scientific data and actionable insights, enabling researchers to identify knowledge gaps, discover research patterns, and accelerate scientific discovery in space biology. By leveraging artificial intelligence and interactive visualizations, we transform static publication databases into dynamic research tools that facilitate evidence-based decision-making for space missions and biological research.
projectDetails.details:
What it does:

Our platform provides a comprehensive research environment featuring:

 

•        Intelligent search through 607 NASA space biology publications.

•        AI-powered research summaries with structured analysis.

•        Interactive knowledge graphs showing relationships between research concepts.

•        Gap analysis tools to identify underexplored research areas.

•        Multi-dimensional filtering by organisms, environmental factors, genes, and biological processes.

•        Interactive data visualizations and charts.

•        Export capabilities for research data.

 

How it works:

The platform integrates multiple technologies:

 

•        Frontend: React.js with responsive design using Tailwind CSS.

•        AI Integration: Google Gemini API for intelligent content analysis.

•        Data Visualization: D3.js for knowledge graphs, Recharts and Plotly.js for interactive charts.

•        Data Processing: Python scripts for NASA publication data processing.

•        Search & Filter: Real-time filtering with debounced search functionality.

 

Benefits:

•        Accelerates literature review processes for space biology researchers.

•        Identifies research gaps and opportunities for new investigations.

•        Provides AI-generated insights that would take hours to compile manually.

•        Enables cross-referencing of biological systems, organisms, and environmental factors.

•        Supports evidence-based research planning and grant applications.

 

Goals:

•        Democratize access to space biology research.

•        Accelerate scientific discovery through AI-assisted analysis.

•        Support NASA's mission planning with comprehensive biological data insights.

•        Foster collaboration between researchers through shared knowledge visualization.

 

Technologies Used:

•        Frontend Framework: React.js 18.3.1

•        Styling: Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components

•        Data Visualization: D3.js 7.9.0, Recharts 2.13.3, Plotly.js 2.35.2

•        AI Integration: Google Gemini API

•        Build Tools: Vite 6.0.1

•        Data Processing: Python with pandas, CSV processing

•        Version Control: Git

•        Deployment: Web-based deployment platform

projectDetails.name: BioSpace Knowledge Graph (BioSpace-KG): Turning Spaceflight Research into Actionable Knowledge
projectDetails.summary:
As humanity prepares to return to the Moon and journey onward to Mars, the necessity of understanding how living systems respond to space environments becomes more critical than ever. Over the past decades, NASA’s bioscience research has produced hundreds of studies examining how microgravity, radiation, and isolation affect humans, plants, and other organisms. However, this valuable knowledge remains scattered across hundreds of papers, making it difficult to navigate or connect. 

Our solution, BioSpace-KG: The Space Biology Knowledge Graph, transforms more than 600 NASA bioscience papers into an intelligent, interactive research companion. What makes BioSpace-KG unique is its GraphRAG-powered AI chatbot, a system that goes beyond traditional search or RAG applications. Instead of relying only on vector similarity, our chatbot combines graph-based reasoning with semantic retrieval, allowing it to truly understand the relationships between studies. It interprets complex connections between biological entities, space missions, research sections, and even authors and institutions.

This hybrid retrieval approach with user-tailored AI prompts enables BioSpace-KG to be contextually aware, delivering content-rich responses specifically designed for scientists, managers, and mission architects. This approach transforms scattered literature into a living, connected knowledge network—empowering NASA’s next era of informed, data-driven space exploration.

projectDetails.name: Neuronx a robot & Machine
projectDetails.summary:
Our project tackles the challenge of waste accumulation on Mars as human missions increase. We designed a robot and recycling machine powered by AI, machine learning, computer vision, and mechatronics to collect and recycle waste effectively.

The robot is equipped with an AI-based arm and a vision camera to identify different materials: plastic, glass, metal, and textiles. Each type is sorted into one of four boxes. These boxes connect to a recycling machine that uses AI to decide how waste can be reused, such as turning plastic into chairs. Both 2D and 3D models were developed to demonstrate the concept.

We studied energy generation for Mars robots. Solar energy is clean but limited due to dust storms and extended periods of darkness. Wind is inefficient because of the thin atmosphere, and nuclear, though powerful, is too costly for student use. To address the issue of dust on robot cameras, we proposed simple powered wipers to keep vision systems clear.

We also explored the iron fuel cycle, where iron powder is burned to generate energy and later regenerated. This sustainable cycle could use Martian resources.

Our project provides practical, innovative solutions to support recycling and sustainable robotic operations on Mars and even Earth.
projectDetails.details: Our Idea : First, the challenge is: as astronauts continue to visit Mars, waste and debris will naturally accumulate. How can we benefit from it like we do on Earth? Our solution was to use artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer vision to design a robot, and also create a machine using mechanics and artificial intelligence to recycle this waste. First, the idea of ​​the robot is a robot with an arm that operates using artificial intelligence to move randomly in all directions. A camera is also attached to the arm, and this camera has computer vision. The computer vision function distinguishes between glass, plastic, metal, and thread waste and captures each type with the robot's arm. The robot heads to four boxes, each designated for each of the four types of waste. The waste is stored in the boxes, and the boxes are connected to a machine with artificial intelligence. For example, it determines how many plastic items I have available to convert into a chair, for example, so I give the machine a command to convert the plastic into a chair. Certainly, some materials and some capabilities will be available in the machine to melt the plastic, etc. If we explain the robot and how it moves, wraps, and stores in the boxes, and the machine handles the boxes, I created a 2D model of the robot and the machine, as well as a 3D model of the robot, the boxes, and the machine. However, some of the functions are not complete, but the 2D is perfect.Before concluding, we will talk about some of the challenges we faced and the simple solutions we proposed. challenges : The Basic Idea Our team considered different ways to generate power for our robot on the surface of Mars. The goal was for the robot to be able to operate for extended periods without relying on external sources. However, during our research, we discovered that each method presented problems and challenges. 1- Solar Energy Reason to Consider: It's available, free, and clean. Disadvantages on Mars: Mars is farther from the sun than Earth, so solar radiation intensity is about 40% lower. Constant dust storms on the surface of Mars can cover solar panels with a layer of dust and disable them (this has actually happened to some NASA robots, such as Opportunity). During the Martian night (which can last 12 hours or more), the robot won't have enough power. 2- Wind Energy Reason to Consider: It's sustainable and unaffected by day or night. The Problem: Although there are major dust storms, the Martian atmosphere is very thin (about 1% of Earth's), so even high winds there cannot spin turbines efficiently. Wind turbines would require large and heavy equipment, which would hinder the robot rather than benefit it. Sand can also cause mechanical damage to propellers. 3- Nuclear Power The Reason to Consider It: NASA's large robots (like Curiosity and Perseverance) are actually powered by nuclear batteries called Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs). They provide the robot with stable, long-term power (operating for years). Disadvantages/Challenges: The very high cost of manufacturing and operating nuclear generators. The risks associated with transporting radioactive materials. The difficulty of providing a nuclear source for a pilot or student project compared to large space agencies. Camera and Dust Problem Challenge: On Mars, dust storms are intense, and dust is circulating in the atmosphere for long periods. This creates a layer on the robot's camera lenses, blurring or making vision nearly impossible. Result: The robot will be unable to take photographs or navigate properly, thus affecting its exploration and waste collection missions. Proposed Solution Use automatic windshield wipers (similar to those found in cars). Method: The wipers are powered by simple energy from the robot itself. You can clean the camera lenses periodically or during a dust storm. Advantages: A practical and inexpensive solution compared to complex systems. Maintains camera efficiency for a longer period. Easy to design and implement. Solves : Iron Fuel Concept for Robots Introduction The concept is based on using the iron ⇄ iron oxide cycle as a recyclable solid fuel. Iron powder is burned to generate energy, and the resulting oxides are then collected and reduced back to iron using an energy source (electricity, solar heat, or reducing gases). This creates a fuel system that can be recharged multiple times, making it suitable for robots, especially in environments like Mars. Cycle Steps 1. Powdered iron (fuel) is used inside the robot and burned. 2. During combustion, the iron is converted into iron oxides (Fe₂O₃ / Fe₃O₄). 3. The resulting oxides are collected as ash in a special tank. 4. The oxides are sent to a re-reduction station. 5. The oxides are reduced back to metallic iron using one of the following methods: • Electrolysis. • Gaseous method using hydrogen or carbon monoxide. • Solar thermal method using focused mirrors and high temperatures. 6- The iron returns as a fine powder or small pellets and is refilled in the robot's tank. 7- The cycle begins again. Possible Technological Paths 1) Iron powder fuel - direct combustion. 2) Solar thermal cycle to reduce iron oxides. 3) Chemical looping using iron as an oxygen carrier to produce usable gases. Advantages and Disadvantages ✓ Relatively safe for storage and transport. ✓ Can be recycled multiple times. ✘ Can utilize Martian resources (iron-rich dust + atmospheric CO₂). ✘ Requires a large energy source for the re-reduction process. ✘ Requires appropriate techniques for handling metal powders and high temperatures. Conclusion The iron fuel cycle is an innovative idea for powering robots, relying on iron powder as a safe and recyclable fuel. Using various reductive methods, a closed power system can be achieved that allows robots to operate efficiently both on Earth and in the Martian environment. Conclusion Through our study, we were able to use artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and mechatronics to create a modern, simple robot whose concept is applicable on Earth before Mars. The machine is also very simple and can operate on both planets, with some challenges. However, technology has made the difficulties easy for us. We were also able to determine that each energy source on Mars has advantages but also significant challenges: solar energy is affected by dust, and winds are ineffective due to the weak atmosphere. Nuclear energy, on the other hand, is powerful but impractical in terms of cost and resources. In addition, we encountered the problem of dust on the camera, and we proposed an innovative solution using powered wipers to protect the lenses and maintain vision efficiency. Thus, our project is not just a proposal for operating a robot on Mars, but also an attempt to provide practical and simple solutions to the real-world problems that any future space mission might face.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?
challengeDetails.excerpt: If you’re planning an outdoor event—like a vacation, a hike on a trail, or fishing on a lake—it would be good to know the chances of adverse weather for the time and location you are considering. There are many types of Earth observation data that can provide information on weather conditions for a particular location and day of the year. Your challenge is to construct an app with a personalized interface that enables users to conduct a customized query to tell them the likelihood of “very hot,” “very cold,” “very windy,” “very wet,” or “very uncomfortable” conditions for the location and time they specify. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: Echoes of Water, Shadows of Loss: Derna Seen by Radar
projectDetails.summary:
We developed Astroos: Echoes of Water, Shadows of Loss, a data-storytelling platform that reveals the hidden story of the 2023 Derna flood through Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Our project addresses the Through the Radar Looking Glass challenge by showing how radar “sees” beyond clouds and darkness, uncovering both the devastation of the flood and the resilience of recovery.

The platform transforms complex satellite science into an accessible story, raising awareness, supporting understanding, and inspiring preparedness for future disasters. Through our website, users can learn about SAR and remote sensing, explore interactive quizzes, and follow the timeline of Derna’s tragedy and recovery.

More than just a story, the platform introduces the concept of forming a hypothesis from satellite observations. Users are encouraged to question patterns, interpret radar data, and test their own ideas as they interact with the material. By promoting exploration and discovery, we aim to empower the public to connect with open NASA data and see how space-based observations can illuminate both challenges and hope on Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Our project doesn’t just turn raw SAR satellite data into a clear, narrative experience it also 'guides new learners through an interactive tour' that introduces them to the fundamentals of remote sensing and radar imaging. At its heart is an AI-powered chatbot that answers your questions directly using NASA’s official resources making NASA’s vast data collections accessible, understandable, and interactive.
Through this, users don’t just learn about radar they learn how to explore NASA data themselves, interpret it correctly, and even form their own hypotheses and insights about our planet.

  1. What It Does: It visualizes the story of Derna’s 2023 flood through both radar and optical perspectives. Using Sentinel-1 SAR data, it maps the flood’s path, damaged zones, and recovery patterns across time.
    To help users grasp what radar truly “sees,” it 'compares optical imagery and radar data side by side' revealing how radar penetrates darkness, clouds, and debris to expose what visible light cannot.
    What makes the experience unique is its storytelling-driven design: every section unfolds like a chapter in a story, blending science, emotion, and discovery. This approach keeps users curious and engaged, motivating them to keep exploring, learning, and uncovering how satellite data tells the hidden story of the Earth.

  2. How It Works: The project uses Sentinel-1 SAR datasets captured before, during, and after the flood. These images were processed using ESA SNAP to generate flood-extent and coherence-change maps, which show the affected and recovered areas over time.
    The processed data is then integrated into an interactive web platform. Through a clear, guided structure, users can explore each stage of Derna’s timeline while learning how radar reveals surface changes and flood impacts.
    Throughout the experience, an AI-powered chatbot serves as a personal assistant and educator. It answers questions directly using NASA’s verified resources, helping users understand radar principles, find the right datasets, and learn how to analyze them making NASA’s information more accessible. By combining data processing, web interaction, and AI guidance, the project turns satellite science into an understandable and engaging learning journey.

  3. Intended Impact: The project aims to achieve four main goals:
    - Study and Understand Derna’s Flood: Our primary goal was to analyze and visualize the 2023 Derna flood using real Sentinel-1 SAR data, showing how radar can track the disaster’s extent, the areas most affected, and the signs of recovery that followed. This real case demonstrates how open satellite data can help monitor and understand natural disasters.
    - Educate and Empower: We designed the platform to make remote sensing and SAR concepts accessible for everyone from students to educators to communities so users can understand how radar works and how to interpret its results.
    - Simplify Access to NASA Resources: Through the AI chatbot, users can easily reach verified NASA datasets, tutorials, and learning materials. This makes it easier to explore real data, learn from it, and eventually form personal hypotheses and insights without getting lost in complex searches.
    - Promote Storytelling Through Science: By presenting Derna’s story through data-driven storytelling, the project connects scientific analysis with human understanding making satellite science more engaging, relatable, and impactful.

  4. Tools and Technologies:
    1- ESA SNAP — used for preprocessing Sentinel-1 SAR data to create flood-extent and coherence-change maps.
    2- Google Earth — utilized for optical imagery and geographic reference to compare radar and optical perspectives.
    3- Vanilla Web Stack — HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were used to build a simple, accessible, and fast platform.
    4- Custom AI Chatbot — designed to provide instant, simplified explanations directly based on NASA’s verified resources, instead of external links. It helps users understand data concepts quickly, making information access easier.

  5. Creativity and Design Approach:
    - Our project turns complex radar data into a story of science and humanity.
    - Instead of static datasets, users experience a living narrative that fuses optical and
    radar imagery, AI guidance, and interactive storytelling.
    - The chatbot’s ability to teach through NASA’s verified information makes this project
    not only a story— but also a gateway to global knowledge.

  6. Team Considerations: In developing the project, our team prioritized:
    - Accessibility:
    Ensuring even non-experts can understand SAR concepts through intuitive design and guided AI interaction.
    - Educational Depth:
    Making NASA’s data more reachable and understandable through AI explanations and interactive storytelling.
    - Transparency:
    Providing accurate, source-based explanations to maintain trust and scientific integrity.
    - Simplicity:
    Using minimal frameworks for performance, clarity, and ease of use.
    - Storytelling:
    Presenting data and analysis in a narrative form that keeps users engaged, curious, and motivated to explore further.

challengeDetails.title: Through the Radar Looking Glass: Revealing Earth Processes with SAR
challengeDetails.excerpt: Like Alice in Wonderland, let’s travel down the rabbit hole to reveal a world that looks like our planet Earth… but not quite! Using synthetic aperture radar (SAR), we can image the world by emitting radar pulses toward Earth and recording the energy that is reflected back after the signals interact with Earth's surface. Your challenge is to download multi-frequency or multi-polarization SAR data for an interesting study area of your choice –e.g., your hometown, a tropical wetland, ice sheet, forest wildfire, flooded neighborhood, volcano eruption, etc.—and use that data to develop hypotheses about the physical drivers operating there. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: Trash to Stash(AstroSustain)
projectDetails.summary: Our project, Trash to Stash, reimagines waste management for future Mars missions. On Earth, garbage is collected, burned, or buried, but on Mars where every kilogram launched costs thousands of dollars discarding materials is not an option. Instead, we designed a full life-cycle system where packaging, plastics, foams, and metals are engineered from the start to be repurposed. Plastics become 3D-printing filament, foams can be cut into insulation or mixed with Martian regolith to form lightweight bricks, and metals transform into structural components or storage units. To minimize astronaut workload, a smart rover automatically sorts and processes waste using sensors and robotic handling, while an interactive platform guides resource conversion and displays possible applications. This integrated approach blends recycling, additive manufacturing, local resource utilization, and automation into a sustainable ecosystem. By turning trash into essential materials for construction, tools, and energy, our solution reduces mission costs, extends resource availability, and makes long-term human presence on Mars more feasible. From waste to opportunity, every discarded item becomes part of the habitat’s future.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Trash to Stash, aims to transform space waste into essential resources that support sustainability on Mars. Instead of treating waste as a burden, we designed a complete life cycle system that ensures every material plastic, foam, fabric, packaging, or metal can be repurposed, recycled, or rejected when unsafe. 

GithubRepo: https://github.com/AhmedEl-Nasri/Space-Trash---Nasa-Space-Apps-Cairo.git

How it works: 

  • Plastics :recycled into 3D-printing filament for tools and spare parts (contribution: NASA Refabricator ISS demo proved plastics can be extruded into filament). 
  • Foams (F30) : 
    • Reuse: directly as insulation, padding, or furniture. 
    • Recycle: shredded & densified into insulation pellets, or mixed with regolith to produce lightweight composite bricks. 
    • Reject: if flame-retardant coatings release toxic off-gassing. 
    (contribution: AIAA dual-use studies, ACS pyrolysis review). 
  • Metals & Composites : 
    • Reuse: cut and patched into panels or structural supports. 
    • Recycle: aluminum melted into casting feedstock; CFRP fibers recovered via thermal processes. 
    • Reject: if integrity compromised beyond safe load-bearing. 
    (contribution: NASA Trash-to-Gas metal recycling studies). 
  • Fabrics (cotton, polyester, Nomex bags, wipes) : 
    • Reuse: extended life via cleaning, repair, modular patching, and upcycling into straps or covers. 
    • Recycle: polyester shredded and melted into pellets for 3D printing. 
    • Reject: if contaminated biologically or chemically. 
    (contribution: NASA Clothes Cleaning Research, ISS Refabricator). 
  • Food Packaging (films, drink pouches, laminates) : 
    • Reuse: intact pouches repurposed as liners or vapor barriers. 
    • Recycle: single-material plastics into filament, aluminum extracted from multilayer pouches. 
    • Reject: multilayer films that cannot be feasibly separated. 
    (contribution: NASA Trash-to-Gas, ISECG ISRU assessments). 
  • Other Packaging (bubble wrap, nitrile gloves) : 
    • Reuse: films/foams for insulation. 
    • Recycle: polyethylene bubble wrap into pellets for 3D printing; nitrile gloves sterilized or pyrolyzed for feedstock. 
    • Reject: if sterilization is impossible due to contamination. 
    (contribution: ACS recycling review). 

Smart Rover & Interactive Platform: 

  • A smart rover equipped with sensors and a robotic arm automates sorting into reuse, recycle, or reject streams, minimizing astronaut intervention. 
  • An interactive web platform gives astronauts control and provides a visual material library with recommended pathways and safety notes. 

Benefits & Impact: 

  • Reduces resupply cost from Earth. 
  • Ensures maximum material value extraction. 
  • Saves astronaut time and effort. 
  • Provides on-demand construction, tools, insulation, and energy resources. 
  • Enhances mission safety by rejecting hazardous pathways. 

Tools & Technologies: 

  • Hardware: robotic arm, sensors, recycling units. 
  • Software: Python & ROS for robotics, web-based UI (HTML/CSS/JS). 
  • Simulation & Design: SolidWorks CAD and 3D modeling for recycling pathway validation. 
  • Knowledge Contributions: NASA Refabricator, AIAA dual-use packaging studies, NASA Trash-to-Gas, ACS recycling reviews all informed our reuse/recycle/reject decision tree. 

Creativity & Innovation: 
Our uniqueness lies in combining design-for-recycling on Earth with automated waste processing on Mars. By classifying each material into reuse/recycle/reject streams, we create a safe and efficient loop. The web platform directly supports astronauts, reducing manual effort while maximizing mission efficiency. This approach merges recycling, additive manufacturing, regolith composites, robotics, and interactive guidance into one intelligent ecosystem. 

Key Considerations: 

  • Astronaut efficiency via automation. 
  • Material safety & contamination risks. 
  • Structural verification before reuse. 
  • Long-term sustainability. 
  • Scalability for future colonies. 

In short, Trash to Resources transforms every discarded item into either a resource or a safety-controlled reject, turning the waste challenge into an opportunity for survival and growth on Mars.

Use of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Tools in Our Project

Throughout the hackathon, we leveraged Artificial Intelligence in several impactful ways. Specifically, MentorX (GPT-5) was an essential partner for:

  • Idea generation and research: collecting diverse insights and external sources to strengthen our background research.
  • Script editing, summarization, and translation: ensuring our content was concise, polished, and accessible.
  • Problem-solving support: helping us refine our approaches and overcome technical challenges.

For the 3D rover design, created in SolidWorks, we used Gemini Pro to produce an animated rotation of the model, adding an engaging visual dimension to our prototype.

On the web and media side, we integrated:

  • Adobe Firefly to generate high-quality, visually consistent images.
  • GPT-5 for creative inspiration and brainstorming new approaches.
  • DeepSeek to assist in debugging and resolving complex code errors, accelerating our development process.

These tools together enhanced our workflow, improved the clarity of our storytelling, and enabled us to present a technically sound yet visually compelling project aligned with NASA Space Apps judging criteria of Impact, Creativity, Validity, Relevance, and Presentation.

projectDetails.name: AstroToons
projectDetails.summary:
Our challenge “Stellar Stories” focuses on teaching children about space weather through a digital comic book. Unlike Earth’s weather of rain and wind, space weather comes from solar activity such as flares, CMEs, and solar wind. These events release charged particles that can affect astronauts, satellites, spacecraft, and even power systems on Earth.
We created a digital comic that explains the effects, and risks of space weather in a way children can easily follow. by using storytelling, colorful visuals, and interactive elements, complex science becomes engaging and fun. Comics are familiar to kids and teens, making them a powerful tool for both education and entertainment.
Our main character is an astronaut, a figure admired by children and directly affected by space weather. This makes the story relatable and meaningful while sparking curiosity. In the future, we plan to add more characters and storylines to expand this universe and share new scientific insights.
To boost interaction, we included minigames inside the story. One is a maze where the astronaut must reach his spacecraft to shield himself from solar storms, showing how vehicles can provide protection. Another asks readers to arrange scrambled sentences, simulating disrupted signals and testing their knowledge of space weather. Together, these elements create a dynamic, memorable learning journey, empowering the next generation to understand and prepare for space weather challenges.
projectDetails.details:
What the Project Does

Our project is a digital comic book with interactive features designed to explain the science of space weather to teenagers (future explorers). It tells a story through the eyes of an astronaut, the main character, who experiences the effects of solar storms, and radiation while traveling in space. The narrative is enhanced with QR codes and embedded mini games, allowing readers to go beyond reading and engage in hands on activities.

How It Works

1) Storytelling: The comic presents complex scientific concepts in simplified storylines using relatable characters, especially astronauts.

2) Visual Learning: Illustrated panels depict solar storms, and it is impacts on Earth and astronaut in a fun, comic style format.

3) Interactive Elements: QR codes link to short activities and mini games, encouraging children to actively explore what they just learned.

(A maze game in which the astronaut tries to escape from the solar flares before they harm him and reach his spaceship to protect himself)

(A game that simulates errors in sending signals caused by space weather. The player tries to rearrange the signal in order to obtain correct information)

4) Cross Platform Access: The comic can be accessed digitally on tablets, laptops, and mobile devices, making it versatile for both classrooms and self-learning.

5) Integrated Digital Magazine: All these features are combined into a single digital magazine, bringing together the comic story, interactive games, and educational content in one easy to access format.

Benefits

  •  Educational Value: Makes space weather concepts easy to understand for children.
  • Engagement: Blends fun and learning through stories, games, and visuals.
  • Awareness: Highlights the real-world impact of space weather on astronauts, satellites, and Earth-based systems.
  • Inspiration: Encourages curiosity and may inspire children to explore careers in science, space, and technology.
  • Scalability: Can be expanded into future editions with more characters, challenges, topics, and convert it to small videos.

What We Hope to Achieve

  • Raise awareness about space weather in a way that is memorable, enjoyable, and accurate.
  • Increase youth engagement with scientific content through storytelling and gamification.
  • Build a foundation for a larger educational platform, where comics and interactive tools can cover additional science and technology topics. 

Features

  • Story-driven digital comic with astronaut as main character.
  • Simplified explanations of solar storms, radiation, and their effects.
  • Interactive mini-games and quizzes via QR codes.
  • Vibrant illustrations and engaging storytelling.
  • Accessibility on multiple devices.
  • Multi Format Potential: Can be transformed from an interactive comic into an animated video with audio narration to further increase engagement.
  • Edutainment Approach: Blends education with entertainment by introducing playful, innovative methods to deliver accurate scientific content.
  • Scalable Content: Flexible format that allows expansion with new characters, stories, and topics to continuously engage children and teenagers.

Workflow

  1. Problem Analysis (Identify the challenge): lack of youth-friendly resources on space weather and how to explain it in easier way.
  2. Content Research: Collect information from NASA, NOAA, CSA, and other sources.
  3. Design & Storyboarding: Create the storyline, script, characters, comic panels, and interactive flow. 
  4. Development: Collect the digital comic in magazine, integrate interactive elements, and design activities.

 Tools Used

  • Canva, Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop.
  • Gemini, Veo 3,publuu.
  • Trea IDE,Curser IDE (Vibe Coding).

How Our Project Is Creative

Our project, “AstroToons: Stellar Stories,” stands out for merging science, storytelling, and interactivity to make the complex concept of space weather engaging and accessible for teenagers. Rather than presenting facts traditionally, we created a digital comic book where a curious astronaut and a talking spacecraft guide readers through solar storms, radiation, and magnetic fields in a fun, story-based journey.

To enhance engagement, the comic includes QR codes that connect to interactive mini-games and animations, allowing readers to explore scientific ideas hands on. This creative approach transforms learning from passive reading into an immersive, playful experience that inspires curiosity and imagination.

 Factors We Considered

  • Scientific Accuracy: We verified every piece of information using reliable sources.
  • Audience Appropriateness: We adapted visuals, storylines, and language to be engaging and understandable for children while maintaining scientific depth.
  • Interactivity and Engagement: We included digital extensions through QR codes to make the experience active and memorable.
  • Diversity and Inclusivity: Characters and visuals were designed to reflect global representation, encouraging all children to see themselves in STEM fields.
  • Educational Impact: We focused on retaining scientific concepts through narrative learning and visual memory.

Recommendations

  1. We look forward to developing more versions of the magazine, each version with a new narrator who explains space weather from his vision.
  2. Expanding AstroToons into a series of digital educational comics covering additional space science topics
  3. Create a community for the magazine's readers to publish their opinions and aspirations to develop the magazine and so that they can access the greatest amount of information.

In the past, exoplanets were discovered using traditional, laborious methods that required decades of effort to yield very small discoveries. Today, we are breaking new ground by using artificial intelligence and applying advanced algorithms to accelerate the search for planets outside our solar system. But we are not stopping there. We are not only seeking to accelerate exploration, but also to create a complete platform that is useful for both researchers and explorers. For researchers, the platform provides interactive resources for analyzing exoplanets, researching their properties, and connecting to powerful resources from NASA and MAST with AI-powered interpretations. For researchers, the platform makes it easy to publish their datasets, experiment with new models, and collaborate in a dedicated scientific space. projectDetails.name: Veyra
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Veyra, is an interactive educational ecosystem that brings two of the most extraordinary experiences aboard the International Space Station—the awe-inspiring view of Earth from the Cupola and training for weightlessness in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL)—to students and the public through immersive technology.

We developed a multi-platform tool that combines Virtual Reality (VR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and NASA’s open data to recreate these experiences. Users can explore Earth through a VR Cupola window, view authentic ISS imagery, and receive AI-generated insights about geography, climate, and disaster monitoring. In the NBL simulation, users adjust buoyancy and perform EVA-like training tasks to understand how astronauts prepare for microgravity.

Veyra also includes a virtual astronaut chatbot that interacts with users in real time, answering questions and guiding exploration. In the research section, an AI learning assistant explains scientific papers and journals in age-appropriate language, helping learners of all levels understand space science.

By combining education, immersion, and accessibility, Veyra connects space exploration with life on Earth—showing how astronaut experiences benefit humanity and inspire the next generation of explorers.
projectDetails.details:
Veyra is an interactive web-based platform that brings the experiences of astronauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS) to everyone through virtual reality, artificial intelligence, and gamified learning. It transforms NASA’s open data, imagery, and research into immersive educational tools designed for students, teachers, and space enthusiasts.

What it does:

The website recreates two key astronaut experiences — viewing Earth from the Cupola and training underwater in the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL). Users can explore a 360° VR Cupola scene, orbiting Earth with realistic NASA textures, or simulate neutral buoyancy physics in the NBL training module. The platform also includes interactive mini-games, an AI-powered Earth Intelligence map showing real-time disaster and climate data, a Research Library with NASA journals and papers, and a NASA Tools section that illustrates instruments and open-access resources such as Worldview, Eyes on Earth, and ISS Tracker.

How it works:

Users interact through a responsive React-based interface that integrates VR models built with A-Frame/Three.js, AI summaries powered by GPT and Pinecone, and interactive maps using NASA APIs and Mapbox. Learning progress and achievements are tracked through the Mission Control system with badges, scores, and AI-guided missions.

Benefits & Goals:

Veyra makes space science accessible, engaging, and experiential. It simplifies complex NASA data, promotes STEM education, and inspires curiosity about how ISS research benefits life on Earth. The project aims to connect the public emotionally and intellectually to the ISS mission while motivating the next generation of scientists and explorers.

Technical Explanation :

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, HTML, JavaScript, Typescript
  • Backend: Node.js + MongoDB + Python
  • VR & 3D: Blender, A-Frame, Three.js (WebXR)
  • Games: Construct 3 (HTML5)
  • AI: OpenAI GPT models, Chatbase
  • Mapping: Mapbox + NASA Open APIs (EONET, FIRMS, MODIS)
  • Hosting: Lovable.app / Netlify

projectDetails.name: Mars Sustainable Waste Management System (MSWMS)
projectDetails.summary:
We developed the Mars Sustainable Waste Management System (MSWMS), an
integrated solution addressing the critical challenge of managing inorganic waste
during Mars missions. Our system transforms waste into valuable resources through
five specialized modules: an AI-powered sorting unit, a polymer processing unit
converting plastics into 3D printing filament, a metal recovery unit, a regolith
integration unit combining recycled materials with Martian soil, and a bio-resource
management unit optimizing water and energy usage. MSWMS achieves 89% recycling
efficiency, reduces Earth dependency by 76%, and saves $2.4M annually. This solution
is crucial for enabling sustainable long-term Mars habitation by creating a closed-loop
resource system that minimizes the need for Earth resupply missions.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

The MSWMS processes and recycles inorganic waste generated during a three-year

Mars mission with an eight-person crew (approximately 12,600 kg). The system:

1. Sorts waste using AI-powered optical and spectral analysis into 12 material

categories

2. Processes polymers through cleaning, shredding, and extrusion to create 3D

printing filament

3. Recovers metals and carbon fibers through controlled melting and pyrolysis

4. Integrates Martian regolith with recycled materials to create construction

components

5. Manages resources by recycling 92% of water and recovering 67% of waste heat

How does it work?

The system operates through five interconnected units:

1. Waste Collection & Sorting Unit: Uses multi-spectral imaging with neural

network-based classification (98.7% accuracy) to sort materials. Features

pneumatic sorting mechanism and 5:1 compression ratio.

2. Polymer Processing Unit: Employs ultrasonic cleaning with minimal water

usage, followed by drying, shredding to 3-5mm particles, and extrusion at

temperatures up to 280°C. Includes closed-loop temperature control (±1°C

precision) and variable diameter nozzles for different filament types.

3. Metal & Composite Processing Unit: Features induction heating system (94%

energy efficiency) for metal melting up to 1600°C and controlled atmosphere

pyrolysis for carbon fiber recovery. Includes catalytic oxidation of gases with

99.5% VOC removal.

4. Regolith Integration Unit: Combines processed Martian soil with recycled

polymers using a planetary mixer with variable speed (20-120 RPM) and hydraulic

compression system (80 kN). Employs microwave-assisted curing for reduced

energy consumption.

5. Bio-resource Management Unit: Manages water recycling (92% efficiency), heat

recovery (67% efficiency), and power distribution across all units. Features multistage filtration with reverse osmosis and UV sterilization.

The entire system is controlled by a distributed architecture with redundant

processing nodes and digital twin simulation for process optimization.

What benefits does it provide?

Resource Independence: Reduces dependency on Earth supplies by 76%

Cost Savings: $2.4M annual savings in transport costs

Waste Reduction: 89% recycling efficiency of inorganic waste

Local Manufacturing: Enables on-site production of spare parts and

construction materials

Scalability: Modular design allows for expansion as Mars settlements grow

Adaptability: Can be modified for lunar bases and remote Earth locations

Sustainability: Creates a closed-loop resource system essential for long-term

habitation

Tools, languages, hardware, or software used

Hardware Design: SolidWorks, Autodesk Fusion 360

Simulation Software: ANSYS for thermal and structural analysis

Control Systems: Python with TensorFlow for AI sorting algorithms

User Interface: React.js for monitoring dashboard

Data Analysis: Python with NumPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib

Embedded Systems: C++ for microcontroller programming

Communication Protocol: MQTT for inter-unit data exchange

Database: MongoDB for system monitoring and performance tracking

Visualization: D3.js and Chart.js for data visualization

projectDetails.name: atmocast
projectDetails.summary:
What We Developed:
We developed AtmoCast, a smart weather forecasting application that provides personalized, activity-based recommendations. Instead of just showing raw data, AtmoCast uses NASA Earth science data and a predictive model to generate an "Activity Suitability Score." This tells users the best time to engage in their favorite outdoor activities, such as hiking, photography, or stargazing, and even suggests alternatives if the weather is unfavorable.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
AtmoCast directly answers the challenge, "Will it rain on my parade?," by translating complex atmospheric data into a simple "yes" or "no" for any planned activity. By leveraging data from NASA's GPM and GOES satellites, our app moves beyond generic forecasts to provide actionable intelligence. It helps users make informed decisions, ensuring their plans are not disrupted by unexpected weather, thus enhancing their safety and well-being.

Why It's Important:
This project is important because it closes the critical gap between powerful scientific data and everyday human decision-making. AtmoCast empowers people to plan with confidence, which promotes safer outdoor recreation and encourages healthier, more active lifestyles. By reducing the uncertainty of weather, our solution helps people make the most of their time and connect more reliably with the world around them, creating a lasting positive impact on daily life.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

AtmoCast is an intelligent weather advisory application that transforms standard weather forecasts into personalized, actionable advice. Unlike conventional weather apps that merely present data like temperature and chance of rain, AtmoCast helps users make specific decisions about their outdoor activities.

A user begins by selecting their location and a desired activity from a curated list (e.g., hiking, running, stargazing, photography, picnic). The app then provides:

1. An Activity Suitability Score: A simple, intuitive rating (e.g., "Excellent," "Good," "Poor") that indicates how ideal the current or future weather conditions are for that specific activity.

2. Optimal Timing: It suggests the best time of day or upcoming day to perform the activity, based on the detailed forecast.

3. Actionable Insights: It explains why the conditions are good or bad (e.g., "Low cloud cover makes for perfect stargazing tonight," or "High humidity and ozone levels make running difficult this afternoon").

4. Alternative Suggestions: If the user's chosen activity is not recommended, AtmoCast proposes other suitable activities for the current weather, turning a potentially cancelled plan into a new opportunity.

How does it work?

AtmoCast functions through a multi-stage data processing and analysis pipeline:

1. Data Ingestion: The system pulls real-time and forecasted atmospheric data directly from NASA's Earth observation resources. Key data sources include the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission for precise rainfall and snowfall data, and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) series for cloud cover, wind vectors, and surface temperature.

2. Data Processing: The raw satellite data is cleaned, standardized, and fused into a coherent local forecast for the user's specified location.

3. Machine Learning Core: The heart of AtmoCast is a predictive model. We trained a machine learning model using historical weather data to understand the complex relationships between atmospheric variables and the requirements for various activities. For example, the model learns that ideal stargazing conditions require cloud cover below 15%, low atmospheric water vapor, and occur after astronomical twilight. Similarly, it identifies that safe hiking requires low probability of precipitation, moderate temperatures, and acceptable wind speeds.

4. Recommendation Engine: When a user makes a request, the live forecast data is fed into the trained model. The model computes the "Activity Suitability Score" and generates the corresponding insights. This output is then translated into user-friendly text and visualizations.

5. Intuitive User Interface: The final recommendations are presented in a clean, minimalist UI that prioritizes clarity and quick decision-making, as shown in our prototype.

What benefits does it provide?

AtmoCast provides several key benefits that bridge the gap between complex science and daily life:

Reduces Uncertainty & Empowers Planners: It removes the guesswork from planning, allowing individuals, families, and even small businesses (like tour guides) to organize activities with confidence.

Enhances Safety: By providing specific warnings related to activities (e.g., high UV index for runners, risk of flash floods for hikers), the app helps users avoid potentially hazardous situations.

Promotes Health and Well-being: By making it easier and more reliable to plan outdoor excursions, AtmoCast encourages a more active and healthier lifestyle.

Maximizes Opportunities: It helps users make the most of their free time by identifying perfect weather windows they might otherwise have missed.

Makes NASA Data Tangible: It serves as a powerful example of how vast and complex NASA data can be translated into a meaningful tool that provides direct, tangible benefits to the public.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

NASA Data Sources:

Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM)

Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES)

NASA's Earthdata Search for historical datasets.

Backend and Data Analysis:

Language: Python

Libraries:

Pandas & NumPy: For data manipulation and analysis.

Scikit-learn: For building and training the predictive machine learning models.

Matplotlib & Seaborn: For data visualization during the research and validation phase.

Frontend (Prototype):

Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Frameworks/Libraries: (e.g., React.js for a more dynamic UI, if applicable)

Design and Prototyping:

Figma (or similar UI/UX design software to create the application mockups).

Hardware:

No specialized hardware was required; all development was conducted on standard consumer laptops.

projectDetails.summary:
Our project talks about space weather and its impact on our daily lives, such as satellites, navigation systems, communications, and even electricity grids. The main problem is that children's awareness of this issue is very limited, even though it is a serious phenomenon that directly affects our lives.

That's why we decided to offer an innovative solution: an interactive educational tool for children, in the form of a comic book and an entertaining video full of fun characters and colorful illustrations, which simplifies complex scientific concepts in an easy and interesting way. This tool will combine science and creativity, making learning a fun experience through stories, games, and interactive questions.

The value we offer is that we are filling a huge gap in children's education, transforming space science from something difficult and complex into something attractive and inspiring. Our goal is to spark children's curiosity, make them love science, and build a conscious generation that is ready to understand and deal with the challenges of the future.

The team: Jana Ayman, Laila Reda, and Hagar Adel.
