projectDetails.name: Aurora Tales
projectDetails.summary:
The challenge we chose is Stellar Stories: Space Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings, whose
basic idea is creating a tool that allows people, especially younger students, to learn about space
weather and its effects on us in an easy, simple way. The main problem we’re addressing is
teaching people the bad effects space weather has on our technology, and in some rare cases our
bodies, and to spread the knowledge of space weather and that it affects things we use daily like
navigation systems like GPS and Wi-Fi connection, in addition to many more things. The outline
od our idea is a game that tells a story of a young boy who faces a problem caused by space
weather, and then decides to explore the other effects space weather may have on other people
and if there are solutions to these problems. We chose this challenge because of the
consequences we may face after big events in space weather like solar storms, which send a lot
of particles towards the Earth’s magnetic field, and some of them manage to reach the Earth and
cause catastrophic problems that might take weeks to solve. So we should spread the knowledge
of space weather and its effects, and how to avoid its problems. Our solution meets the
requirements because it’ll be able to help people learn about space weather in an easy way using
a game and storytelling.
projectDetails.details:
The goal of the game is to quite interactively and also enjoyably introduce space weather to the children. The child meets characters that are affected by space weather then helps them through mini-games while learning how these events impact life on Earth and in space.

 

At the beginning of the game, the child will be exposed to a simple challenge through which he will learn about the concept of space weather in a deeper way and will begin to apply it through a game in which the player participates. The player contributes to protecting the Earth from harmful rays and particles and allowing the beneficial rays of the sun to pass through the Earth's magnetic field. Thus, the player learns that the particles that harm us and cause space weather are completely different from normal sunlight.This increases his understanding of the concept of space weather.

 

Exposure to dangerous radiation outside of Earth’s magnetic field makes that  challenge difficult. The challenge does involve an astronaut. The child is navigating in a simple maze. Through the maze, he reaches the safety room. The child collects five coins on the way to unlock the safety door. The astronaut needs this protection against harmful particles. In this stage problem-solving is taught and the risks of space weather in space are shown.

 

For a farmer with crops that are damaged by space weather is a challenge. Intact plants are kept while the child removes damaged plants in a mini-game. Clearing damaged crops before time runs out without harming good ones displays space weather's impact on agriculture. Finally, the child meets a scientist who explains that space weather is a real-world problem affecting  astronauts, farmers, communications, and the internet. The scientist also explains how researchers are finding solutions. By completing all stages, the child learns about space weather and its effects in a fun. We also wanted to make a scene for the scientist but we couldn’t make it due to limitation of time and the technical issues we faced with Unity, where we couldn’t access the license on Unity and this resulted in an inability to work from all of our devices,  and we had to use only one laptop, which reduced the efficiency.

As for the software part, we used Visual Studio, we relied on C# and

Unity to design the game and itch.io and Freepik for the free assets used in building and designing the game.

For the hardware part, we used our laptops.

projectDetails.name: Project AURORA TRAVELERS
projectDetails.summary: We developed a digital storytelling project called “Space Weather Storytelling with Leo the CME”—an animated, child-friendly narrative that personifies a coronal mass ejection (CME) as “Leo.” The project addresses the challenge of low public awareness about space weather by transforming complex science into an engaging, accessible story that shows how solar storms affect people’s daily lives, from farmers and pilots to astronauts and city residents. This is important because space weather risks are increasing in our technology-driven world, and educating children through storytelling builds early awareness, inspires curiosity, and promotes future resilience.
projectDetails.details: Our project is a digital children’s story video that explains what space weather is, how CMEs travel from the Sun to Earth, and what impacts they cause, including auroras, satellite glitches, aviation rerouting, power grid disruptions, and farmers’ GPS failures. It works by using a friendly character, Leo the CME, who narrates his journey in simple language, supported by cartoon visuals, voice-over, and music. The benefits include making abstract science tangible and fun, raising awareness in children and the general public, and sparking curiosity about STEM. We aim to inspire young learners while strengthening societal understanding of space weather. Tools and software used include Canva and PowerPoint for visuals, CapCut for video editing, Audacity for audio recording, and Google Drive and Slack for collaboration, without requiring coding languages.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used AI tools to accelerate creativity and storytelling development. ChatGPT was used to help script and summarize NASA and partner resources, Gemini was employed to generate cartoon-style concept art for Leo and his journey, and CapCut’s AI features assisted in aligning audio with visuals. All AI-generated outputs are clearly watermarked or acknowledged as AI-generated, and while AI supported visuals and narrative development, scientific accuracy relied strictly on NASA and space agency data. This ensured our project combined creativity with factual reliability.

projectDetails.summary:
High-Level Summary:

I developed an educational project centered around the Tera Telescope, aimed at making astronomy accessible and engaging for children. The project includes an interactive storytelling experience and a digital eBook, designed to explain the telescope’s functionality, its role in space exploration, and its broader scientific significance — all through a child-friendly lens.

This project addresses the challenge of limited early exposure to scientific concepts among young learners. By presenting complex astronomical ideas in a simple, narrative-driven format, it sparks curiosity and fosters a passion for science from an early age.

Its importance lies in its ability to bridge the gap between advanced science and young minds, promoting STEM education and encouraging the next generation to explore, question, and innovate.
projectDetails.details:
1. What exactly does it do?

My project focuses on the TERA telescope — explaining its importance, how it works, and its scientific role. The aim is to raise awareness about this advanced astronomical tool.

2. How does it work?

The TERA telescope operates using a combination of high-resolution optics and advanced sensors to detect cosmic radiation and observe deep space phenomena. It uses precise data collection and imaging technologies to study distant galaxies, black holes, and star formations.

3. What benefits does it have?

TERA helps expand our understanding of the universe. It provides valuable data for space exploration, supports scientific discoveries in astrophysics, and inspires innovation in optical and sensor technologies.

4. What do you hope to achieve?

Through this project, I aim to educate young minds and the general public about the significance of space exploration and inspire curiosity in astronomy and science.

5. What tools or materials were used?

The project is designed as an engaging storytelling experience, including a detailed eBook specially crafted for children. It simplifies complex scientific concepts in a fun and accessible way to promote learning.

projectDetails.name: FloraVision
projectDetails.summary: Our project utilizes NASA’s satellite data to analyze and visualize flowering phenology by processing large datasets to identify bloom timing and environmental factors. The workflow begins with collecting multi-source data from NASA EarthData, followed by cleaning, preprocessing, and exploratory analysis of vegetation indices such as NDVI, LAI, and SIF alongside dust observations. These datasets are integrated into a unified framework that allows us to study seasonal patterns and simulate interactions between dust, vegetation health, and flowering cycles. Using simulation models, we forecast blooming periods and pollen movement under different conditions and validate these predictions with real observations to ensure accuracy. The results demonstrate clear links between dust events and reduced ecosystem productivity, offering early warnings for individuals with respiratory sensitivities, practical guidance for farmers in planning their crops, and valuable insights for researchers studying climate change impacts. Ultimately, our work transforms raw NASA data into accessible knowledge with real-world applications.
projectDetails.details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?
Our project integrates advanced data analysis with interactive web visualization to study environmental and health-related datasets. We collected raw data (CSV files), cleaned and standardized it, then applied statistical methods and machine learning techniques such as clustering (KMeans). The processed insights were transformed into dynamic visualizations (maps, time-series charts, and heatmaps) and deployed through a Blot AI-based website, making the findings accessible in an interactive way.

2. What benefits does it have?
The project bridges the gap between raw data and actionable insights. It helps uncover hidden trends in large datasets, simplifies complex results into clear visuals, and provides decision-makers with tools to improve understanding of environmental and health challenges.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?
The intended impact is to make scientific analysis more transparent, interactive, and widely available. By combining data science with web deployment, the project promotes data-driven awareness in research, agriculture, and public health, while also encouraging collaboration across disciplines.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
We used Python for data processing and analysis, with libraries including Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Seaborn, Matplotlib, and Plotly. For visualization deployment, we used Blot AI to design and publish the website. GitHub was employed for version control and team collaboration.

5. How is your project creative?
Our creativity lies in combining technical depth with accessibility. We transformed abstract data into interactive maps and charts embedded directly into a live website. Unlike static reports, our solution provides a platform where users can explore data, test ideas visually, and understand patterns in real time.

6. What factors did your team consider?
We carefully considered accuracy of analysis, user experience of the website, clarity of communication, and the scalability of our methods. We aimed to balance scientific rigor with a design that non-specialists could also benefit from. Ethical use of data and reproducibility of results were also key considerations.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):
Machine Learning models (K-means clustering, regression, simulation) were developed and tested on Google Colab to identify ecological hotspots of mosquitoes, canopy cover, and dust. Additionally, we used predictive modeling approaches (OLS, RidgeCV, Bootstrap regression) to validate the negative impact of dust on vegetation indices (NDVI, LAI, SIF). Simulation models were also developed to forecast plant growth and flowering stages under varying dust conditions. These AI-driven methods enhanced pattern detection, ecological forecasting, and robust scientific validation.

Furthermore, we used Blot AI as an AI-powered assistant to generate, refine, and deploy the interactive website for our project. Blot AI helped in structuring project documentation, integrating analysis outputs, and presenting visualizations in a clear and accessible way. This accelerated development, improved usability, and ensured our findings were communicated effectively to a broad audience.

projectDetails.name: Project Bee-yound Sights
projectDetails.summary:
Bee-yond Sights is a dynamic, AI-powered Earth observation platform developed for the NASA
 BloomWatch Challenge. Our mission is to connect Earth, Air, and Life by transforming vast streams of
 satellite data into a clear, intuitive, and actionable pulse of our planet’s vegetation. Focusing initially
 on the African continent, our platform detects, monitors, and forecasts plant blooming events to
 provide critical intelligence for sustainable agriculture, public health preparedness, and climate
 resilience.
 By integrating a diverse suite of datasets from NASA, ESA, and other global partners, we have built
 a solution that moves beyond simple visualization. We employ advanced machine learning and deep
 learning models to deliver predictive insights, such as crop health forecasts for farmers, high-risk pollen
 alerts for allergy sufferers, and long-term desertification trends for environmental policymakers. The
 platform features an interactive dashboard, a deep data explorer, and a unique "Storytelling" mode
 that visualizes the impact of climate change on ecosystems over time. Bee-yond Sights is designed to
 be a scalable, user-centric tool that empowers a wide range of users—from local communities to global
 researchers—to make informed decisions based on the vital signs of our planet.
projectDetails.details:
2.1 Problem & Mission: Responding to the BloomWatch Challenge

The BloomWatch Challenge invites innovators to harness NASA Earth Observation data to build intelligent, data-driven tools that can visualize, detect, and propose solutions for monitoring and managing vegetation bloom events.

Bloom events serve as critical ecological indicators, influencing agricultural productivity, biodiversity, public health, and climate adaptation. Yet, despite the vast availability of satellite data, current monitoring systems remain fragmented and poorly integrated. This fragmentation limits our capacity to:

  • Accurately forecast crop yields and manage agricultural health proactively.
  • Predict pollen-related health risks affecting large populations.
  • Understand and mitigate long-term environmental threats, including desertification.

Our mission with Bee-yond Sights is to bridge the gap between data and decision-making by developing a unified, intelligent, and interactive platform capable of detecting, monitoring, and forecasting vegetation-related phenomena across both global and local scales.

By integrating NASA’s satellite observations with advanced artificial intelligence models, Bee-yond Sights transforms raw Earth data into actionable insights—empowering farmers, researchers, healthcare professionals, and policymakers to make informed, data-driven decisions that promote sustainability and resilience.

2.2 The Bee-yond Sights Platform: A Comprehensive and Multi-Dimensional Solution

Bee-yond Sights functions as a holistic ecosystem for environmental exploration, analysis, and prediction. The platform interconnects a series of intelligent modules that work in harmony to deliver a seamless and unified experience.

2.2.1 Africa Environmental Dashboard

Acting as the central hub for real-time environmental monitoring across the African continent, this dashboard aggregates and visualizes key performance indicators (KPIs) derived from NASA’s data pipelines. It highlights active bloom regions, climate variability trends, and includes a “What-If Simulator” that allows users to test how changes in environmental parameters could impact ecosystem health and agricultural productivity.

2.2.2 Data Explorer: Deep Dive Analytics

At the analytical core of Bee-yond Sights lies the Data Explorer—an intelligent engine that converts complex environmental datasets into clear, meaningful insights. It allows users to explore three primary domains:

  • Agriculture
  • Pollen & Health
  • Environmental Patterns

Each module features:

  • An interactive visualization map,
  • A dynamic control panel for filtering and overlaying data layers, and
  • A suite of advanced analytical charts, including time-series trends, regional comparisons, and risk assessments.

This component serves as the bridge between raw satellite data and real-world decision-making, empowering experts and policymakers to analyze and interpret environmental changes with scientific accuracy and clarity.

2.2.3 Storytelling: A Planet’s Pulse

To make complex environmental data more intuitive and engaging, the Storytelling feature narrates the evolution of Earth’s ecosystems over time. Through an animated global timeline, it visualizes changes in NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), rainfall, and temperature—turning raw data into visual stories that connect environmental patterns to real-world ecological transformations.

2.3 Predictive Services: Direct Model Interaction

To ensure accessibility and interactivity, Bee-yond Sights integrates four AI-powered predictive models that users can interact with directly. By inputting localized environmental parameters, users receive instant, model-based predictions across agricultural and health-related domains.

The models include:

  • Bloom Model – Forecasts and monitors water bloom occurrences.
  • Crop Health Model – Evaluates vegetation condition and crop vitality.
  • Irrigation Needs Model – Estimates optimal crop irrigation requirements.
  • Pollen Risk Model – Predicts pollen levels and potential health impacts.

This direct interaction closes the gap between large-scale satellite analytics and on-the-ground decision-making, enabling real-time, data-driven action.

2.4 Technical Architecture

The Bee-yond Sights platform is engineered for scalability, efficiency, and high performance, leveraging modern frameworks and cloud technologies.

  • Frontend: React.js, Mapbox GL / Deck.gl, D3.js
  • Backend: Python (FastAPI, Flask), PostGIS, Docker
  • AI & Data Processing: Python, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, Google Earth Engine API
  • Collaboration & Deployment: GitHub, Vercel

This architecture enables real-time data streaming, AI-driven prediction, and interactive visualization, forming a resilient digital infrastructure that supports sustainable environmental intelligence.

projectDetails.details:
Project Details

Beyond Pixels is an interactive web-based platform designed to make NASA’s massive image datasets—covering Earth, the Moon, and Mars—accessible and engaging to the public. The core challenge we solved is that these high-resolution TIFF datasets are too large to be visualized or explored efficiently in their raw form.

On the frontend, we used React.js with the Leaflet library to render these tiles with smooth zoom and pan functionality. This ensures users can freely navigate gigapixel and terapixel images without losing quality or performance.

The platform integrates storytelling and interactive quizzes, tied to specific map regions, to reinforce knowledge, spark curiosity, and improve memory retention. This gamified approach transforms data exploration into an educational and fun experience.

projectDetails.name: Project Beyond unseen
projectDetails.summary: High-Level Project Summary We have developed an innovative disaster-monitoring platform merging SAR imagery with optical satellite data to monitor floods and earthquakes over Egypt, along with all major disasters worldwide. The platform provides crisp before-and-after visualizations and translates SAR's very complex signals into layman terms, thus democratizing such technology. The whole idea behind this is to combat the problem of lack of visibility when disasters strike, with all sorts of complications like clouds and smoke blocking the conventional satellite observations or even it getting dark. By showing previously hidden changes on the surface, our platform aids the rescue operations, then decision making, and finally helps communities to realize, prepare for, and respond to natural hazards. This project matters as it is an enabler for advanced satellite technology into actual meaningful disaster response on the ground so that both local and global communities can respond faster, decide better, and mitigate the impacts of any catastrophic event.
projectDetails.details:
Our project outlines the ability and efficiency of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) in disaster response. It highlights the way SAR imagery can reveal the before and after contrast of a disaster, which allows the authorities and rescuers to react accordingly.
What it does:
The project shows that SAR captures images of the Earth surface before and after natural disasters such as floods or earthquakes. When comparing the two, differences in land structure, infrastructure, and water coverage are clear, even in cloudy or nighttime conditions.
How it works
SAR satellites broadcast microwave signals that bounce off the Earth's surface. They are transformed into images that are independent of weather or sunlight. When comparing two SAR images one captured before and one captured after a disaster our project detects impaired or changed areas, making it easy to find affected areas in no time.
Benefits:
Provides clear real-time visibility under any weather or daylight.

Enables faster and more accurate disaster response.

Removes the delay caused by missing or unclear optical imagery.

Aids governments and rescue organizations in making resource allocation decisions that are informed.

Our Goals:
We aim to educate everyone about SAR's ability to be an essential part of emergency response and demonstrate its ability to replace uncertainty with actionable clarity — viewing no disaster unseen.
Tools & Technologies Used:
NASA SAR Data Sets (e.g., Copernicus Sentinel-1, NISAR simulation data)

Copernicus Browser for SAR image comparison and visualization


GIS tools for overlaying before/after imagery

projectDetails.name: AERA (Air Environmental Real-Time Analytics)
projectDetails.summary:
From Cloud to Ground: AERA (Air Environmental Real-Time Analytics) is a web-based app built with Python and JavaScript that delivers real-time air quality information for both the public and scientists. It features an interactive map showing the Air Quality Index (AQI), allowing users to explore air quality via GPS, point selection, city search, or drawing custom polygons in North America. Data comes from the TEMPO satellite, validated with ground station measurements from Pandora for accuracy and coverage.

For the public, AERA provides clear AQI values for multiple pollutants, helping users decide when it’s safe to go outdoors, travel, or move between cities. Users can view current AQI, weekly pollutant forecasts via a U-Net deep learning model, and receive alerts when air quality is unsafe.

For scientists, AERA offers a comprehensive dashboard with time series analysis, pollutant trends, nearest ground station readings, and chart visualizations. Combining satellite and ground validation, it serves as a research-grade platform for studying air quality variations, climate impacts, and supporting informed decision-making.
projectDetails.details:
MOTIVATION & OBJECTIVE

GitHub Repo : 0xMotazMohamed/Nasa_Space_Apps-Big_Hero_6: Big Hero 6 Repo for nasa solution

Our Kaggle Pixels solution Dataset: TEMPO_Pixels_Data_Solution

Motivation

Air pollution is one of the biggest everyday health risks. From traffic and factories to wildfires and changing weather, the air we breathe is constantly affected. Most people don’t have an easy way to know if the air around them is safe, they either rely on scattered sources or technical data that’s hard to understand. At the same time, researchers struggle with fragmented datasets that make it difficult to track pollution patterns and study long-term effects.

Objective

AERA was built to close this gap. Our goal is to give people across North America clear, real-time air quality information so they can make simple decisions like when to go outside, whether it’s safe to travel, or how pollution trends affect their city. For researchers and scientists, AERA provides a platform that combines satellite and ground data, making it easier to study pollution trends, forecast future risks, and support public health and climate action.

HOW IT WORKS

Solution Diagram
Home
Solution (Interactive Map)

Dashboard (For Scientists)

About

DEVELOPMENT WORKFLOW

1) Data Acquisition (AWS)

We gather TEMPO satellite data from AWS, Pandora ground station data from AWS. to ensure that both satellite and ground-based are perspectives.

2) Data Preprocessing

Raw data is cleaned with quality checks, validated against ground stations, and transformed into a uniform 25×25 pixel grid. Missing values are handled through normalization and interpolation.

3) Modeling & Backend

Gridded data is processed with a U-Net model to enhance spatial resolution for accurate pollutant mapping, and a FastAPI backend serves predictions and data layers via ArcGIS.

4) Frontend & Visualization

An interactive Leaflet.js map displays real-time AQI overlays, while dashboards built with Dash/Plotly allow scientists and users to explore time-series data, charts, and pollutant trends.

TECHNICAL ASPECTS

Data Filtration (Using TEMPO User Guide for data V3,V4 )

No2 & HCHO :  main_data_quality_flag == 0 & eff_cloud_fraction < 0.2

When the main quality flag = 0, it indicates normal (good) data, for cloud fraction, only the highest-quality pixels should be used in analysis

O3 : “eff_cloud_fraction” > 0.5 & “solar_zenith_angle , viewing_zenith_angle” > 80 degrees

The user guide suggests this as the preferred filtering criterion.

Data Collection and Daily Averaging

TEMPO observations, from the mission start to present, are collected for all days and stored in AWS buckets. The data is then averaged daily to provide the AI model with stable, low-noise inputs.

Here is the full version of merged data in kaggle : TEMPO_Pixels_Data_Solution

Points Preprocessing and  Pixels Conversion

~22M observations are approximated into ~36500 pixels on a 25×25 grid, then reshaped (H=118, W=310) for structured input. Daily averaging, including irregular-hour data, yields a clean datetime-indexed sequence for the AI model.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

Deep Learning Model U-Net

U-Net, with its encoder–decoder structure to train the model fast, enhances spatial resolution by capturing context and details, enabling accurate pollutant mapping and reliable interpolation with limited data.

 

TOOLS USED

Data Acquisition & Storage: AWS (S3, EC2)

Preprocessing: earthaccess,Python,Xarrays, Pandas, NumPy, GeoPandas

Modeling: PyTorch, UNet

Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, ArcGIS Layers API

Frontend & Visualization: Typescript,Leaflet.js, Dash/Plotly

projectDetails.name: Skybird forecasting
projectDetails.summary:
Our solution, Skybird Forecasting, is a strategic weapon against weather uncertainty. Standard apps are useless for long-range planning, a gap that contributed to over 11,500 deaths from extreme weather in 2024. We developed an interactive web application that provides long-range weather risk assessments, forecasting conditions up to two years in advance. By selecting a location and future date, users get a personalized dashboard with statistical probabilities for core variables (rain, temperature, wind) and critical extreme events ("Very Hot," "Very Wet," etc.), along with user-friendly recommendations.

Skybird directly addresses the challenge by translating decades of NASA's MERRA-2 historical data into clear, actionable metrics for planners operating beyond the 10-day forecast window. Our probabilistic models provide the quantified risk assessment needed for confident long-term decisions.

This is a tool for preservation, not just planning. By quantifying the risk of events like the heatwave that killed over 1,300 people, we empower humanitarian organizations, agricultural planners, and public institutions to take preemptive action. It’s about mitigating disaster and using NASA’s data to safeguard communities in a volatile climate.
projectDetails.details:
What It Does & How It Works

Skybird Forecasting is a web-based decision-support system that provides long-range weather risk assessments. A user selects any location on Earth and a future date up to two years in advance. Our system then returns a personalized dashboard with statistical probabilities for key weather outcomes.

How it Works: The application is powered by a suite of probabilistic machine learning models. We do not perform simple historical lookups; we have trained our models on decades of NASA's MERRA-2 reanalysis data. Each model is a specialist, engineered to predict a specific phenomenon (temperature, wind, rain probability) by analyzing a curated set of scientifically-relevant predictor variables. When a user makes a query, our Flask backend processes the location and date, feeds it to the models, and returns a JSON object with the calculated probabilities to the React front-end, which then renders the user-friendly dashboard and recommendations.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Benefit: The primary benefit is quantified confidence for long-range planning. Standard forecasts are blind beyond two weeks. Our tool provides data-driven risk probabilities for events months or years away, allowing planners to move from guessing to making strategic, evidence-based decisions. This mitigates financial, logistical, and safety risks for events, agriculture, and humanitarian efforts.
  • Impact: The intended impact is to save lives. While convenient for event planning, the core purpose is to provide the foresight needed to mitigate disasters. In 2024, over 11,500 people died from extreme weather. Our tool can provide months of advance warning about the statistical likelihood of a catastrophic heatwave or rainfall event, giving institutions and governments the critical time needed to prepare resources, issue warnings, and protect vulnerable populations. This is a tool for building societal resilience.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Creativity: Our creativity lies not in inventing a new algorithm, but in the novel application of existing science. We creatively repurposed a complex, research-grade climate dataset (MERRA-2) into an intuitive, forward-looking risk assessment tool for the general public. The true innovation is in the translation layer—distilling petabytes of multi-dimensional atmospheric data into a simple, actionable percentage and a clear recommendation. We reframed the problem from "forecasting weather" to "quantifying historical risk."
    • The User: Our primary consideration was the non-technical user. We ruthlessly focused on hiding the immense backend complexity behind a simple, fast, and intuitive interface.
    • Performance: We knew the system had to return results in seconds. This dictated our use of pre-trained models and an efficient API architecture.
    • Scientific Credibility: We chose MERRA-2 for its scientific integrity. Our feature-engineering process was deliberate and based on atmospheric physics to ensure our results were scientifically sound, not just statistical correlations.
    • The Planning Gap: Our entire design was oriented around solving the single problem that matters: the inability of standard forecasts to provide guidance beyond 10-14 days.

Technology Stack

  • Backend & ML: Python, Flask, Scikit-learn, Pandas, Xarray
  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML/CSS
  • Data Source: NASA MERRA-2 (utilized collections: tavg1_2d_slv_Nx, tavg1_2d_rad_Nx, tavg1_2d_flx_Nx)
  • Database: SQLite (for caching)
  • Version Control: Git, GitHub
  • Development Tools: Cursor, Visual Studio Code
  • Hardware: Standard development laptops with local GPU resources for model training.

This AI-augmented workflow was not a replacement for human expertise but a deliberate strategy to accelerate our process. projectDetails.name: Space Biology Knowledge Engine.
projectDetails.summary: We developed an AI-powered knowledge engine that centralizes and summarizes NASA’s bioscience research. The system collects scientific papers and experimental data, processes and structures them, and delivers instant access through a user-friendly dashboard with advanced search, filters, and visualization tools. This addresses the challenge of scattered and hard-to-access space biology research, which often leads to wasted time and duplicated efforts. The project is important because it saves time, reduces redundancy, improves decision-making, enhances global collaboration, and supports both scientists and educators. Ultimately, it accelerates innovation in life sciences and strengthens preparation for safe and informed Moon and Mars missions.
projectDetails.details:
What it does

Our project is a centralized AI-powered knowledge engine that organizes and summarizes NASA’s bioscience research. It provides fast access to publications and experimental data through a user-friendly dashboard, enabling researchers to explore, visualize, and collaborate on space biology findings.

How it works

Data Collection: Gather research papers, experimental data, and bioscience findings.

Data Processing: Clean, organize, and standardize all information.

AI Analysis: Apply NLP and machine learning to classify, summarize, and extract insights.

Knowledge Integration: Store structured data in a centralized knowledge graph engine.

User Access: Researchers interact through an intuitive dashboard with search, filters, and visualization tools.

Collaboration: Teams share, comment, and build on each other’s findings across institutions.

Continuous Update: System automatically refreshes with new studies and experiments.

Benefits

Saves researchers time by providing instant access to space biology knowledge.

Reduces duplication of work through centralized and reliable data.

Improves decision-making with AI-driven summaries and insights.

Strengthens collaboration across global scientific teams.

Enhances transparency with secure storage and version control.

Supports education by simplifying complex research.

Accelerates innovation in life sciences and human space exploration.

What we hope to achieve

Our vision is to transform scattered bioscience studies into a unified, intelligent knowledge system that empowers scientists, mission planners, and educators, supporting safe and informed Moon and Mars missions.

Tools & Technologies

BioPython – Bio.Entrez:

It’s the main library we used to access PubMed and retrieve metadata directly from the NCBI databases.

BeautifulSoup (bs4): To parse the XML or HTML files and extract metadata fields manually when the data wasn’t clean or structured.

re (Regular Expressions): for pattern matching and text extraction — mainly to clean or capture specific parts of the article text.

torch (PyTorch): used as the backend framework for running the NLP (Natural Language Processing) models inside the transformers

pipeline : The function used to initialize the Pegasus model specifically for the text summarization task.

pandas : Used for data manipulation, reading the input CSV, applying functions column-wise, combining texts, and saving the final output CSV.

transformers :Used to load the Pegasus-xsum pre-trained model for abstractive text summarization.

PapaParse:

Used to read and parse CSV files directly in the browser, converting them into JSON format for easier data handling and display on the web page.

jQuery:

Used to simplify DOM manipulation and handle interactive elements or events on the webpage, and to support the functionality of DataTables.

DataTables:

Used to create interactive and dynamic HTML tables that allow searching, sorting, and pagination of the research data.

DataTables Bootstrap5:

Provides styling and layout integration for DataTables using Bootstrap 5, ensuring the table appears clean, modern, and responsive.

JavaScript (JS):

Used to add interactivity and functionality to the dashboard, handling user actions, dynamic updates, and integration of data visualization features.

TailwindCSS v3:

A utility-first CSS framework used for building a responsive, modern, and consistent design. It allowed rapid prototyping and ensured a professional UI aligned with NASA’s bold theme.

HTML 5:

The backbone structure of the web application, providing semantic markup for accessibility, searchability, and clean integration with styles and scripts.

projectDetails.details:
BioScope, is an advanced platform that revolutionizes access to space biology research by integrating NASA datasets with interactive, AI-driven features. It was developed to address the challenge of making biological research in space more accessible, inclusive, and actionable for a wide range of users.

How it works:
BioScope is designed as a dynamic research hub. It offers a Search Engine to simplify discovery through keywords and a Timeline Filter to narrow results by publication period. Research is categorized by discipline (plants, humans, microbes) and further refined with level-based filtering, allowing users to access studies tailored to their academic background.

The platform supports dashboard customization depending on the user’s role—whether a researcher, mission planner, manager, or citizen scientist. It also includes an AI Research Assistant (floating icon) that guides exploration, generates predictions, and provides intelligent summaries.

For accessibility, BioScope introduces a content listening (text-to-speech) feature, ensuring visually impaired and special-needs users can engage with the research. Users can also simulate experimental conditions to predict new outcomes, select studies and generate summaries, and visualize changes over time through a research timeline.

Beyond NASA data, the platform allows users to upload and analyze CSV files, providing flexibility for external datasets. Results and insights can be exported as PDFs, while an evidence access feature makes the research process more transparent and verifiable.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
BioScope democratizes access to space biology knowledge by making it searchable, customizable, and interactive. Researchers can accelerate discovery, educators can adapt materials to student levels, and citizen scientists can contribute meaningfully. The combination of inclusivity, personalization, and predictive modeling ensures BioScope goes beyond traditional repositories, transforming data into actionable insights that can support mission planning, research collaboration, and public engagement.

Tools & Technologies:
The platform was developed with HTML, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript (Fuse.js for search, Plotly.js for visualization, Lucide for icons). AI was integrated through external APIs to support intelligent summarization, predictions, and research assistance.

Creativity & Considerations:
BioScope is unique in combining 13 differentiating features—from keyword search and timeline analysis to AI simulations and accessibility tools—into one unified system. Our team considered usability, inclusivity, transparency, and educational value to design a platform that is not only a research tool but also an engagement and learning ecosystem for the global community.

projectDetails.summary: We developed an AI-powered web platform to automate exoplanet discovery by unifying NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS datasets into a single dataset manually, meticulously curated resource. Addressing data integrity head-on, we harmonized disposition labels and units (e.g., converting transit depth to ppm) and applied advanced, science-based methods from recent research to handle missing values, moving beyond simple imputation. We rigorously trained and evaluated multiple models—including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, and Neural Networks—ultimately deploying the best-performing Random Forest model. This model is integrated into an interactive Flask web interface that allows researchers to perform both single and batch predictions, receiving real-time disposition probabilities (Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive). By providing a robust, scientifically-grounded tool, we transform manual analysis into an efficient, automated process, empowering the accelerated discovery of new worlds hidden in vast astronomical data.
projectDetails.details:
### **Project Details: AI Exoplanet Hunter**

#### **What does it do and how does it work?**

Our project is a full-stack web application that automates the classification of potential exoplanets. It works through a streamlined, science-driven pipeline:

1. **Data Unification & Curation:** We integrated three primary NASA datasets (Kepler, K2, TESS) into a single, coherent dataset of 21,272 entries. This involved manually standardizing critical factors like disposition labels and units (e.g., converting transit depth to ppm) to ensure data integrity.

2. **Scientific Data Handling:** Instead of using simple averages, we addressed missing values using sophisticated imputation methods based on a 2024 astrophysics research paper, ensuring our data preparation was scientifically rigorous.

3. **Machine Learning Core:** We trained and evaluated multiple models—including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, and Neural Networks—as guided by exoplanet informatics literature. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior performance and was selected as our final classifier, capable of predicting a disposition of **Confirmed (1), Candidate (0), or False Positive (-1)**.

4. **Interactive Web Interface:** We deployed the model using a Flask server. The interface allows users to either:

* **Perform Single Predictions:** Input 10 key astrophysical parameters (like orbital period, planetary radius, transit depth) and receive an immediate classification with probability percentages for each class.

* **Perform Batch Predictions:** Upload a CSV file for bulk analysis, making it efficient for processing large datasets.

#### **What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?**

* **Benefits:**

* **Efficiency:** Drastically reduces the time required for initial exoplanet candidate screening.

* **Accessibility:** Provides an intuitive tool for both expert researchers and students, lowering the barrier to working with complex exoplanet data.

* **Rigor:** Leverages established scientific methods for data handling and model selection, making it a reliable tool for analysis.

* **Intended Impact:** To accelerate the pace of exoplanet discovery by moving beyond purely manual classification. We aim to provide the scientific community with a robust, open-source tool that can identify promising candidates from existing and new data, allowing human experts to focus their valuable time on the most promising targets.

#### **What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?**

* **Programming Language:** Python

* **ML & Data Libraries:** Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn

* **Web Framework:** Flask

* **Development Environment:** Kaggle Notebooks (for initial data analysis and model training)

* **Frontend:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript

* **Model Deployment:** Pickle (.pkl) for model serialization

#### **How is your project creative?**

Our creativity lies not in inventing a new ML algorithm, but in the **thoughtful synthesis and application of existing science to solve a practical problem.** Key creative aspects include:

* **The Unified Dataset:** We didn't just use one dataset; we created a new, more valuable resource by meticulously combining and standardizing data from three major NASA missions, which is what a comprehensive analysis tool truly needs.

* **Science-First Data Processing:** We prioritized scientific integrity by implementing data imputation techniques from recent astrophysics research, moving beyond basic data science practices.

* **A Tool for Discovery:** The web interface is designed not just as a demo, but as a functional tool that empowers users to interact with data and potentially make new discoveries themselves.

#### **What factors did your team consider?**

Our development was guided by several critical factors to ensure the project's usefulness and reliability:

* **Data Integrity:** We carefully mapped disposition labels across missions and unified physical units to avoid introducing errors.

* **Model Selection:** We did not rely on a single model. We tested several based on academic literature to empirically determine the best performer for our specific task.

* **User Experience (UX):** We considered the needs of different users, from astrophysicists needing batch processing to students experimenting with single predictions, leading to a dual-mode interface.

* **Interpretability:** The output provides probability percentages for all three classes, giving users insight into the model's confidence level rather than just a final label.

* **Scalability:** The batch prediction feature, though under development, was architected to handle larger datasets, a common need in this field.

projectDetails.name: Project BlackEye
projectDetails.summary: We developed BlackEye, a machine learning system that processes NASA's Kepler and TESS datasets to identify and characterize exoplanets. The system combines XGBoost classification and regression models to simultaneously classify exoplanet candidates and predict their physical properties, analyzing 17,232 astronomical objects with 12 raw features plus 3 engineered features. BlackEye addresses the challenge by automating the analysis of vast amounts of light curve data from NASA's Kepler and TESS missions, reducing manual review time and improving classification accuracy. It unifies data from multiple NASA missions into a single analysis framework, enabling researchers to process thousands of candidates efficiently while maintaining scientific rigor. This system is important because it accelerates exoplanet discovery by providing researchers with powerful, automated analysis tools that can process NASA's massive datasets in real-time. It advances our understanding of planetary systems beyond our solar system by making NASA data more accessible to the research community, supporting ongoing NASA missions and future space telescope operations.
projectDetails.details:
BlackEye is a machine learning system that processes NASA's Kepler and TESS datasets to identify and characterize exoplanets through a multi-target learning approach. The system analyzes 17,232 astronomical objects using 12 raw features plus 3 physics-based engineered features, then uses XGBoost to classify objects as CONFIRMED, CANDIDATE, FALSE_POSITIVE, or UNKNOWN while simultaneously predicting 7 key scientific parameters including orbital period, planet radius, equilibrium temperature, and stellar properties. The system provides a FastAPI backend for real-time analysis and web interface for visualization, with hyperparameter customization allowing researchers to configure XGBoost parameters for specific research needs.
The benefits of BlackEye include accelerated exoplanet discovery through automated data analysis, reliable classification and parameter estimation for scientific accuracy, making NASA data more accessible to the research community, and improved classification accuracy through machine learning. The intended impact is to contribute to exoplanet research and planetary system understanding, enable rapid validation of TESS candidates for follow-up observations, provide tools for astronomers and researchers worldwide, and prepare for upcoming space telescope operations and data analysis.
Our technical implementation utilizes XGBoost for gradient boosting, scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy for machine learning and data processing, FastAPI for the Python backend with RESTful API design, PHP, HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the frontend, Docker containerization for deployment, and NASA Kepler KOI dataset (9,564 objects) and NASA TESS TOI dataset (7,668 objects) as data sources. The system requires standard development machines with Python 3.8+, Docker-compatible systems for deployment, and processing capabilities for large astronomical datasets (17,232+ objects).
The creative aspects of our project include innovative approaches such as multi-target learning where a single system handles both classification and regression simultaneously, physics-based feature engineering with custom features based on astronomical principles, cross-mission integration for unified analysis of Kepler and TESS data, hyperparameter customization for researcher-specific model configuration, API-first design for programmatic access to research workflows, and Docker containerization for easy deployment and reproducibility. Our unique features include unified dataset processing that combines multiple NASA missions into a single framework, real-time analysis with fast inference on new astronomical data, confidence estimates providing reliability metrics for all predictions, and research-focused design tailored for scientific community needs.
Our team considered several factors during development, including technical factors such as ensuring all methods align with established astronomical practices for scientific rigor, implementing automated filtering and quality assessment for data quality, designing for growth with increasing dataset sizes for scalability, open-source implementation with comprehensive documentation for reproducibility, and optimization for fast inference on large datasets for performance. Research factors included focusing on astronomers and researchers rather than the general public for target users, using official NASA datasets for authenticity in data sources, basing methodology on peer-reviewed astronomical practices, implementing comprehensive cross-validation and performance metrics for validation, and creating detailed guides for the scientific community. Development factors included modular architecture with clean separation of concerns for maintainability, RESTful interface for easy integration in API design, simplified deployment and reproducibility through Docker support, comprehensive test coverage for reliability, and complete API and user documentation.

projectDetails.name: Project BlackVsion
projectDetails.summary:
BlackVision is a multi-spectral observatory designed to study black holes using synchronized optical, infrared, and radio observations. We developed a scalable system that combines CAD-based hardware designs with a 3D simulation engine to reconstruct event-horizon emissions in real time. Using NASA open-source datasets, including Sagittarius A* radio and infrared data, and insights from peer-reviewed Harvard research, BlackVision validates observational strategies and demonstrates how emissions may appear “frozen” from Earth’s perspective.

This project addresses the challenge by turning abstract, hard-to-access cosmic phenomena into observable, interpretable data, effectively “embiggening” humanity’s eyes. By providing a framework for multi-spectral observation, it democratizes access to frontier astrophysics, enabling researchers, students, and educators worldwide to engage with extreme cosmic events. The significance lies in expanding scientific discovery, fostering collaboration, and accelerating our understanding of black hole behavior, making complex astrophysical processes accessible and actionable for the global scientific community.
projectDetails.details:
BlackVision is a multi-spectral observatory that integrates optical, infrared, and radio modules to study black holes. It captures synchronized data across multiple spectra, reconstructing phenomena such as gravitational lensing and the apparent “frozen” emissions of matter near event horizons. A custom 3D simulation engine built in JavaScript and CSS visualizes these emissions in real time, supported by CAD-based designs that outline scalable observational systems.

We used NASA open-source datasets, including 2021 Sagittarius A* radio and infrared emissions, and referenced the 2019 M87 Event Horizon Telescope image and Harvard research leveraging NASA data to validate our models. This approach ensures scientific rigor while enabling real-time visualization of extreme astrophysical events.

The project benefits include democratizing access to frontier astrophysics, providing educational tools for students and researchers, and expanding the rate of scientific discovery. Creativity comes from merging multi-spectral hardware, simulation, and open datasets into an accessible, scalable system, allowing humanity’s first systematic observation of black holes beyond fragmented snapshots.

Visualizations and CAD Designs

Below are examples of the BlackVision system in action, including simulation outputs, CAD module layouts, and multi-spectral data visualizations. Each image highlights how the optical, infrared, and radio modules capture different aspects of black hole phenomena and how the data is integrated into a coherent multi-spectral picture

The BlackVision simulation engine provides a real-time, interactive representation of black hole emissions. Users can explore how matter near the event horizon behaves, observing gravitational lensing and apparent “frozen” emissions from different perspectives. This simulation serves both as a research validation tool and an educational platform for students and scientists.

The BlackVision project is supported and validated by peer and zenodo-reviewed research. Our primary reference is a paper detailing the conceptual design, observational strategy, and scientific motivation for multi-spectral black hole studies. This paper demonstrates how event-horizon emissions could appear “frozen” from Earth’s perspective due to extreme gravitational effects.

Key contributions of the research include:

  • Multi-wavelength data analysis: Techniques for optical, infrared, and radio observations.
  • Simulation validation: Using NASA open-source datasets to ensure real-world accuracy.
  • Event-horizon emission detection: Visualization of phenomena near black holes.
  • AI-driven reconstruction pipelines: High-precision imaging for scalable observation.

projectDetails.name: SkyShield
projectDetails.summary:
SkyShield is an air quality forecasting system in real time that integrates NASA TEMPO satellite data with ground sensors, MODIS/VIIRS products, and meteorological data. The platform translates state-of-the-art Earth observation into comprehensible, actionable information for policymakers, schools, and communities.

With automated data pipelines, statistical fusion, and AI-based forecasting models (XGBoost, LSTM), SkyShield provides short- and medium-term NO₂, O₃, and PM2.5 forecasts with continuous validation against ground stations.

An interactive dashboard (Next.js + Leaflet), intuitive to use, offers custom alerts, city search, and pollution hotspot mapping. The data is also available for researchers and agencies to obtain via an open API.

By linking NASA's cutting-edge datasets to public health decision-making, SkyShield allows communities to breathe safer, respond faster, and develop resilience to air pollution.
projectDetails.details:

Dashboard Development → install Next. js webapp, embed forecasts into Leaflet maps, use Framer Motion for interactive graphs. Validation & alerts → Real-time Validation against ground stations, real-time health alert notifications over the dashboard as well as SMS/Email notification. Deployment →with Docker, deploy on Kubernetes and monitor with Grafana/Prometheus. Features *Real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) reporting with Sparkline *Air Quality Map Filled and Unfilled style *Support on Apple Watch Real-time AQI updates for different cities AQI information sharing social plug-in What's New 1. More bug fix and improvement Health Almanac for color coded health alerts by category (GOOD to HAZARDOUS). Forecast & History Tabs to prepare and compare patterns. Multi-sensor satellite, ground sensor and weather data fusion. Clear and easy to understand infographics along with simple design and smooth animations. Benefits Allows school /early to protect themselves in time. Transforms complicated Earth observation data into easily understood, actionable information. Enhances public health preparedness by predicting hazardous air events. Earns trust with open sources, validated predictions and actionable recommendations.

projectDetails.name: Project Brain 2.0
projectDetails.summary: A meteor is a bright streak of light caused by a meteoroid entering Earth’s atmosphere at high speed. As it burns due to friction with air, it creates the glowing trail we often call a “shooting star.” If the object survives and lands on Earth, it becomes a meteorite. Meteors vary in composition—some are rocky, others metallic, and a few are a mix of both. Rare types even originate from the Moon or Mars. The process includes three stages: meteoroid (in space), meteor (burning in atmosphere), and meteorite (on the ground). These cosmic visitors help scientists study the solar system’s history and composition. Some meteorites contain ancient materials older than Earth itself.

projectDetails.name: Bonnie's Journey
projectDetails.summary: We developed an interactive educational website that tells the story of “Bonnie,” a solar flare brought to life as a character. Through a short animated introduction, Bonnie explains her impact on Earth, followed by an engaging game where players must help her avoid damaging satellites, power lines, and communication systems. This creative blend of storytelling, animation, and interactivity directly addresses the challenge by translating complex space weather phenomena into an experience that is fun, memorable, and accessible for the children . The importance of our project lies in its ability to raise awareness of space weather’s real effects on daily life—such as power outages, communication disruptions, and satellite failures—while also inspiring curiosity about science. By personalizing the science and giving audiences an active role in the story, we bridge the gap between technical knowledge and public understanding, ultimately promoting education, preparedness, and interest in space exploration.
projectDetails.details:
An interactive web-based children’s story and mini-game that personifies solar eruptions as “Bonnie” to explain space weather and its impacts on everyday life. It combines a 30-second apology/explainer video from Bonnie, interactive data visualizations, and a short game where players help Bonnie reduce impacts on spacecraft, communications, and infrastructure across different difficulty levels. Bonnie thanks the child by name after successful play, making learning personal and engaging.

How it works:
The platform integrates video, text, and interactive gameplay into a single website, providing a seamless educational experience.
The 30-second video introduces Bonnie and explains the effects of solar flares in simple terms.
The mini-game allows children to interact with the concept of solar eruptions, completing tasks that simulate protecting technology and infrastructure from space weather impacts.
Interactive visualizations present NASA and NOAA data in a child-friendly manner, helping players see the real-world relevance of their actions in the game.
Benefits:
Simplifies complex scientific phenomena like solar flares and space weather for children.
Encourages engagement through gamification and personalization, enhancing knowledge retention.
Bridges the gap between scientific data and public understanding by making learning interactive and fun.
Goals:
Raise awareness about solar flares and space weather impacts among children and the general public.
Provide a safe and engaging learning tool for educators and parents.
Demonstrate how storytelling, gamification, and accurate scientific data can be combined to teach STEM concepts effectively.
Tools, Languages, and Software:
Languages & Frameworks: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React (for website and game).
AI Tools: ChatGPT (for prompts, scripts, and code assistance), Gemini (for generating initial game code).
Multimedia Tools: Screen recording and video editing software for the explainer video.
Data Sources: NASA Heliophysics, NASA SVS visualizations, NOAA SWPC, and other official NASA/NOAA resources.

Asteroid Impact Simulator Summary
What It Does:
This web platform simulates the threat of near-Earth asteroids, like the hypothetical "Impactor-2025". It allows users to visualize an asteroid's 3D orbital path and the realistic, ground-level consequences of an impact, including tsunamis, seismic events, and atmospheric disturbances. It even has a gamified "Defend Earth" mode for testing mitigation strategies like kinetic impactors.

How It Works:
It fuses real-time astronomical data from NASA's NEO API with geological information from the USGS (topography, seismic maps, tsunami zones). The system uses established orbital mechanics and validated impact-physics models to calculate trajectories and accurately estimate things like crater size, blast radius, and seismic magnitude. The entire experience is delivered through an interactive 

Why It Matters:
Current tools are often too technical or too simplified, failing to connect an asteroid's path with its potential consequences. This simulator bridges that gap by translating complex data into an accessible, scientifically rigorous visualization. It empowers non-specialists and policymakers to properly evaluate threat levels, compare defensive strategies, and perform crucial risk analysis within their specific regional context.
projectDetails.details:

projectDetails.name: ClimaQuest
projectDetails.summary: Our platform is designed not just to give you the best travel experience, but also to raise awareness among young people and children about climate change because education and awareness are the key to our future. With our AI-powered weather prediction model, you can explore forecasts months in advance, even down to specific days. Using advanced analytics and satellite data, We provide Plan Your Journey tool where travelers can select a city and dates to receive accurate predictions, alongside essential safety tips and warnings ensuring every journey is safe, enjoyable, and memorable. For kids ages 6–12, our Tech Your Child section delivers a unique learning experience: animated adventures with a globe-trotting hero, interactive quizzes designed for their age, and a smart assistant that makes learning about weather and climate both fun and rewarding. Our My Weather page gives highly accurate 10-day forecasts including highs, lows, rainfall, and humidity based on your location. The Engineering Hub helps professionals design sustainable cities adapted to local climate conditions, while our upcoming Farmer’s Assistant will support farmers in choosing the best crops and planting times for their region. And for the curious, our Weather Science page reveals the algorithms and data driving AI forecasts, detailed visualizations, and interactive tools that let you see how predictions are generated in real time.
projectDetails.details:
Vision:

Our vision is to make climate and weather knowledge accessible to everyone, no matter their age or background.

We aim to create a platform that not only provides accurate and reliable weather data, but also helps users understand, learn, and plan their activities with confidence.

We believe that understanding the weather is not only for scientists — it’s for travelers, students, families, and professionals who rely on climate information in their daily lives.

Our Goal:

Our main goal is to create one unified platform where anyone can easily access everything they need to know about the climate and weather — all in one place.

Through our platform, users can:

  • View the weather forecast for their current location for up to 10 days.
  • Learn how experts predict the climate for future periods, including the scientific formulas and methods used.
  • Access educational content and safety tips for children, teaching them how to deal with different weather conditions.
  • Understand how engineers and specialists choose the right tools and equipment based on the local weather of a specific area.
  • Achieve the main purpose of our project — helping users select their destination and travel time, and instantly discover what the weather will be like during that period.

Our broader mission is to make climate knowledge accessible to everyone, in a simple, enjoyable, and interactive way — through a user-friendly interface that gathers all weather-related information in one convenient and trusted platform.

Mission:

Our mission is to make climate awareness and planning an easy and engaging experience for everyone.

We achieve this by combining scientific accuracy, modern design, and interactive learning tools within a single platform.

To fulfill this mission, we:

  • Use trusted data sources, including NASA and verified weather APIs, to ensure reliability and precision.
  • Design an intuitive and accessible user interface that allows users to find information effortlessly — whether they are checking today’s forecast or exploring deep weather science.
  • Provide educational materials for different age groups, helping both children and adults understand the science behind climate and weather.
  • Offer personalized travel insights, guiding users to plan safe and enjoyable trips based on accurate weather predictions.
  • Encourage environmental awareness by showing how climate affects daily life, technology, and human decisions.

In short, our mission is to turn complex climate information into simple, meaningful, and practical knowledge — all within a platform that inspires users to explore, learn, and plan with confidence.

Main Features:

Trip Planner:

Plan your travel easily — just select the location and time, and the website will show you the expected weather and personalized travel advice.

Weather Science Page:

Learn how weather forecasts are made, explore the formulas and concepts used by experts, and gain a deeper understanding of climate science.

Teach Your Child Page:

A fun and simple learning section for children, including short videos and quizzes to help them understand climate topics safely and easily.

My Weather Page:

Stay updated with the 10-day weather forecast for your current location at any time.

Destinations Section:

Explore suggested travel destinations based on weather conditions and trip types — perfect for users who are still deciding where to go.

About Page:

Includes a full overview of the project, a video explanation, our roadmap, and information about our team members.

Engineering hub:

A section that helps engineers choose the most suitable construction materials based on the climate of each region and It highlights the best choice of materials.

Theme Modes:

The website offers both Dark Mode and Light Mode, each designed with a unique and enjoyable user interface to match the user’s personal color preference.

Users can switch between the two modes easily — whether they prefer bright and clean visuals or darker, eye-friendly tones for more comfortable viewing.

This feature ensures that the overall experience remains visually pleasant and adaptable to different lighting environments and user preferences.

Website Structure:

Our website is organized into clear and user-friendly sections to ensure smooth navigation and accessibility for all users.

Pages Overview:

1. HOME PAGE

The Home Page is the main entry point of our website. From here, users can easily navigate to all other pages and sections.

At the top, the Navigation Bar provides clear links and guidance on how to make the most out of the website’s features.

This page also includes a Destinations section, which offers suggested travel locations. Each suggestion is tailored based on the general weather conditions of that destination and the type of trip you plan to take. This feature helps users choose a trip easily, even if they are not sure where or how they want to spend it.

The Home Page also highlights the main reasons why users should choose our website over others.

We use trusted and verified data sources, including information from NASA, to ensure accuracy.

Our system helps you plan your trip according to the weather, provides long-term forecasts, and acts as

“the last missing piece in your journey.”

2. WEATHER SCIENCE

The Weather Science Page provides a deep look into the scientific methods used to calculate and predict climate conditions.

It includes mathematical equations, graphs, and interactive visualizations under the section called Prediction Methodology.

Users can interact with the graph by entering custom data to view the historical average, actual values, and predicted results.

They can also choose to display or hide any of these datasets individually by simply clicking the desired option above the graph.

This page also presents detailed insights into:

  1. Wind Speed Analysis
  2. Weather Condition Distribution
  3. Prediction Algorithms and Equations

The purpose of the Weather Science Page is to help users understand the science behind weather forecasting in an interactive and educational way.

It aims to make complex climate models easier to explore and visualize, allowing users to see how data, formulas, and algorithms work together to predict real weather conditions.

By combining scientific accuracy with user-friendly interaction, this page bridges the gap between expert knowledge and public understanding of climate science.

3. MY WEATHER

The My Weather Page provides users with detailed weather information for their current location.

When the user allows the website to access their location, the page automatically detects it and displays local weather data.

If the user chooses not to share their location, the system automatically sets Cairo as the default city.

The page shows a 10-day weather forecast starting from the current day, including key information such as temperature, wind speed, and weather conditions.

Each day is displayed as a card, and when the user hovers over a card, additional extended weather predictions appear to give a clearer view of upcoming conditions.

Purpose of the Page:

The purpose of the My Weather Page is to offer users quick and accurate access to the weather around them.

It helps users stay informed about upcoming conditions and make daily or travel-related decisions more confidently.

By using location-based forecasting and a simple, interactive design, the page ensures a personalized and engaging experience for every user.

4. Teach Your Child:

In our website, we are not only targeting adults—we are also targeting children so we can build awareness of our planet's climate from childhood. This awareness grows with them, and they can make a real impact in the world.

We built an interactive learning journey that consists of several types of weather.

These videos are eye-catching, animated in 3D using AI, and include audio to explain to the children how to deal with different types of weather in the form of a story about a young boy who packs his suitcase and travels around the world to visit countries that have these different weather conditions:

  • Rainy weather (London)
  • Very cold weather (New York)
  • Windy weather (Shanghai)
  • Very hot weather (Cairo).

We also used both AI and voice-over to add audio to the videos to help demonstrate to the children how to deal with these different weather conditions.

To make the experience more engaging, these videos have two features:

a) ask for more

This feature provides an AI-generated summary of the video, in addition to a link to learn more about the topic from NASA resources.

b) Take Quiz (Optional)

A fun and engaging yet simple quiz that makes the experience interesting and more influential, since asking questions on a topic directly after listening to it makes the information more impactful and long-lasting.

5. Engineering Hub:

Of course, we will not forget our engineering community, so we added a dedicated page for engineers that helps them determine what type of material they should use to build buildings according to the country's climate. They can choose from 13 countries in our menu.

This page provides engineers with many material options and a quality indicator on a scale from 1 to 10. These points are calculated based on the material's durability, eco-friendliness, cost efficiency, lifespan, carbon footprint, availability, climate resilience, and regulations. This allows them to compare materials and choose the most suitable option according to these criteria.

We also added a feature that suggests the best option based on the quality points. It's not just about recommending the right materials—it also warns engineers about unsuitable ones and provides reasons, enriching their awareness of what materials they should and shouldn't use.

In addition, there is valuable information about the selected city sourced from NASA, including:

1. Climate Risk Assessment

  • Average temperature during the year
  • Aerosol Index
  • Flooding potential

2. Hydrological Insights

  • Drought
  • Rain
  • Wind
  • Groundwater stress

3. Renewable Energy Potential

  • Solar energy
  • Wind energy

4. Geotechnical Assessment

  • Seismic hazard
  • Predominant soil type

Engineers can also save this data and access it offline by downloading it in PDF or CSV format.

6. Plan Your Journey:

Plan Your Journey lets you design your trip with ease, confidence, and intelligence powered by AI. Unlike ordinary forecast tools, it uses an advanced AI weather prediction model that analyzes climate patterns months ahead, then translates them into practical insights tailored to your trip.

  • - Choose Your Destination: Pick your city from a destination box or directly on the interactive map, making it simple for any traveler.
  • - Set Travel Dates: Select the exact start and end dates of your journey to get forecasts that cover your entire trip, not just a single day.
  • - Select Trip Type: Define your travel purpose—business, leisure, family, or adventure—so that the recommendations adapt to your lifestyle and goals.
  • - AI-Powered Forecasts: Instead of only showing numbers, our AI model interprets huge amounts of weather and climate data, highlighting temperature ranges, rainfall chances, extreme heat or cold risks, and seasonal shifts.
  • - Percentage Ratings: Clear and simple indicators reveal how likely it is to be hot, cold, rainy, or pleasant, helping you prepare at a glance.
  • - Personalized Tips & Alerts: Based on your trip type and forecast, you’ll receive packing suggestions, activity recommendations, and vital safety alerts for severe weather conditions.

What makes this feature truly unique is the fusion of AI intelligence, interactive design, and personalization. It doesn’t just predict the weather—it adapts it to your journey. Whether you’re traveling for work, a family holiday, or adventure, Plan Your Journey transforms raw climate data into useful guidance.

Compared to standard forecast pages, Plan Your Journey stands out as your AI travel companion: interactive, predictive, and deeply personalized. It ensures every trip is safer, smoother, and more memorable.

6. About :

Our About Us page introduces ClimaQuest , our mission, and the passionate team behind it.

It starts with an introductory video that walks you step by step through how to use the platform—

showing how to plan trips, check forecasts, and explore all features in detail.

We then highlight the core strengths of ClimaQuest:

NASA Data Integration: Leveraging NASA’s Earth observation data for accurate long-term forecasts.

AI-Powered Predictions: Using machine learning to analyze historical patterns and predict future weather.

Global Accessibility: Turning complex climate data into practical insights for everyone—from travelers to farmers.

The Meet Our Team section introduces the talented individuals who brought the project to life, showcasing their roles and passion for climate technology.

Finally, our Journey Timeline shares key milestones: from forming during the NASA Space Apps Challenge, to building the first prototype, training AI models with NASA data, and achieving 85% accuracy within three months—culminating in our public release.

The page not only tells our story but also builds trust by showing the science, technology, and people driving ClimaQuest forward.
