projectDetails.name: climatour
projectDetails.summary: What did you develop? We developed ClimaTour, an AI-powered, web-based chatbot that functions as a smart travel risk manager. It leverages decades of NASA Earth observation data to provide travelers with long-term, probability-based weather insights and personalized, real-time travel recommendations.  How does it address the challenge? ClimaTour directly addresses the challenge by creating a personalized interface where users can query the likelihood of specific weather conditions ("very hot," "very windy," "very wet") for any location and time of year. It uses NASA datasets  to translate historical climate data into actionable travel intelligence, moving beyond standard 14-day forecasts to enable planning months in advance. The platform also provides data visualization and export options (CSV/JSON), as suggested in the challenge.  Why is it important? This project is important because it bridges a critical gap between vast scientific datasets and the practical, everyday decisions of millions of tourists and locals. By making NASA's Earth observation data accessible and understandable, ClimaTour empowers users to make smarter, safer, and more enjoyable travel plans. It mitigates the financial and experiential risks of unpredictable weather, turning complex climate science into a tangible tool for global travelers.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

ClimaTour provides users with a comprehensive travel planning service centered on weather risk management. A user starts by entering their desired location and travel dates. The AI chatbot then:

Analyzes Historical Data: It processes decades of NASA climate data to calculate the probability of various weather conditions (e.g., "a 22% likelihood of increased dust and wind").

Provides a Risk Score: It generates a unique Activity Risk Index (1-100) that quantifies the weather-related risk for specific activities like hiking or sightseeing.

Offers Personalized Recommendations: Based on the weather likelihood and the user's travel style (e.g., budget, interests), it suggests suitable activities, attractions, and dining options.

Creates Contingency Plans: In what we call the "Magic Moment," if a user's plan is at risk due to weather, the chatbot instantly generates tailored, real-time alternatives (e.g., nearby museums on a rainy day), complete with transit times from the Google Maps Places API.

How does it work?

The platform operates on a four-stage methodology:

Data Acquisition: It accesses key NASA datasets via NASA Earthdata APIs.

Data Processing: The raw data is cleaned and processed into probability distributions for specific weather conditions at given locations and times, then stored in a structured database.

AI & Recommendation Engine: A conversational AI (built with Rasa, Dialogflow, or OpenAI API) serves as the user interface. This chatbot communicates with a machine learning backend (using TensorFlow Recommenders, scikit-learn) that generates the risk scores and activity suggestions.

Visualization & Interface: A user-friendly web interface displays weather probabilities through charts and maps, provides clear textual summaries, and enables data export.

What benefits does it have?

Financial Protection: Helps travelers avoid investing in trips or events likely to be disrupted by poor weather.

Maximized Experience: Ensures every day of a vacation is optimized with weather-appropriate activities.

Enhanced Safety & Risk Mitigation: Provides scientifically-backed risk assessments, empowering users to avoid potentially dangerous conditions.

Efficiency: Integrates weather analysis, activity recommendations, and contingency planning into a single, seamless conversational interface.

What do you hope to achieve?

Our goal is to validate ClimaTour as a technologically superior and highly reliable service. We aim to achieve specific quantitative goals, including:

Historical Probability Accuracy: ≥92%

Tourism Recommendation Accuracy: ≥88%

Complex Query Latency: <3

 seconds

Contingency Plan Generation Speed: <1.2

 seconds

Recommendation Acceptance Rate: ≥45%

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

coding languages : HTML / CSS / JavaScript / JSON ( data exchange format )

projectDetails.name: Codeius
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Codeius, is an AI-powered web application designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Will It Rain On My Parade?”. We developed an interactive platform that helps users plan outdoor events by predicting rain risk using both NASA POWER data (precipitation, wind, temperature) and Open-Meteo forecasts, enhanced with NASA GIBS IMERG satellite overlays.

The system combines a transparent baseline risk formula with an ensemble machine learning model (Random Forest + Gradient Boosting with calibrated probabilities) trained on NASA POWER data from multiple cities. This dual approach provides more accurate predictions and confidence levels, while also explaining the contribution of each factor (precipitation, cloud cover, wind, nowcast) to the final risk score.

Codeius is important because weather uncertainty directly impacts safety, logistics, and community activities. By identifying low-risk “safe windows” and offering optimized scheduling suggestions, our solution empowers users to make informed decisions. The application also emphasizes explainability, user-friendly UI/UX, and reproducibility—making science accessible to everyone, powered by NASA data.
projectDetails.details:
Codeius is an AI-powered web application that forecasts rainfall risk and identifies safe time windows for outdoor events. The system integrates multiple data sources: NASA POWER (precipitation, wind, temperature), Open-Meteo forecasts, and NASA GIBS IMERG satellite overlays.

The application works by combining a baseline transparent risk formula with an Ensemble Machine Learning model (Random Forest + Gradient Boosting + Logistic calibration). The baseline ensures interpretability, while the AI model improves accuracy and provides calibrated probabilities. Users input their event time and location, and the system outputs:

  • A Rain Risk Score (Green/Yellow/Red).
  • A confidence level comparing forecasts with satellite data.
  • Optimized “safe windows” in the next 72 hours.
  • Interactive visualizations (risk timeline, precipitation charts, IMERG rain maps).

Benefits and Impact:

  • Helps communities, organizers, and families make informed decisions about outdoor events.
  • Increases trust in science through explainable AI.
  • Reduces safety risks and avoids logistical/economic losses due to weather disruptions.
  • Scalable to other hazards (storms, heatwaves, air quality).

Tools and Technologies:

  • Languages: Python (Streamlit, Pandas, Scikit-learn, Requests).
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS IMERG (satellite imagery), Open-Meteo API.
  • Visualization/UI: Streamlit with custom UI/UX design, Folium maps, charts.
  • Collaboration: GitHub for version control, PowerPoint/Slides for demo.

Creativity:
The project blends open NASA data with machine learning and delivers results through a user-friendly, modern interface. The team focused on clarity, accessibility, and impact—making advanced science approachable to the public.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of AI in Codeius

We used AI tools to accelerate development and creativity in the following ways:

  • Code generation & debugging: AI-assisted coding (ChatGPT) was used to draft initial versions of the Streamlit app (app.py), train_pro.py (model training script), and to optimize functions for data processing, error handling, and UI/UX design. All code was reviewed, tested, and refined manually by the team.

projectDetails.name: WeatherWise
projectDetails.summary:
WeatherWise is a weather prediction platform revolutionizing event planning by providing probabilistic weather forecasting months in advance using NASA Earth observation data and machine learning.

What We Developed:

Flutter mobile app with Google Earth-style 3D globe interface for global weather visualization, featuring real-time data and risk assessments

Django backend API integrating NASA POWER meteorological data with ML prediction models

Machine learning engine using MLP and LSTM models trained on decades of historical weather data

How It Addresses the Challenge:
WeatherWise tackles "Will It Rain On My Parade?" by providing long-term weather probability assessments using NASA's climatological datasets. Instead of binary yes/no predictions, it offers risk percentages and suitability scores with actionable recommendations like "Carry umbrella due to light precipitation."

Why It's Important:
Event planners and outdoor enthusiasts need reliable long-term weather insights for critical decisions about venues, contingency planning, and resource allocation. WeatherWise transforms NASA's decades of Earth science data into accessible intelligence that reduces financial risk, enhances safety, and democratizes climate data through intuitive mobile technology, enabling better weather-informed decisions with unprecedented foresight.
projectDetails.details:
How It Works

WeatherWise operates as a three-tier architecture combining mobile frontend, API backend, and machine learning intelligence:

Data Collection & Processing:

  1. System collects historical weather data for 7 specific regions covering the last 10 years via NASA POWER API
  2. Data acquisition requests single-day meteorological data iteratively, accumulating decade-long datasets into CSV files
  3. Local data storage: All historical data processed and stored locally (no cloud deployment currently implemented)
  4. Machine learning models train on this 10-year regional dataset to identify climatological patterns

User Interaction Flow:

  1. Users input location coordinates and dates via Flutter mobile app's interactive 3D globe interface
  2. Django backend receives requests and maps coordinates to one of the 7 supported regions
  3. Local ML models process the request using pre-trained patterns from historical NASA data
  4. System returns probability-based predictions with risk assessments and actionable recommendations

Core Functionality:

  • Regional Coverage: Focused on 7 key regions with comprehensive 10-year historical data foundation
  • Probabilistic Forecasting: Provides percentage-based risk assessments rather than binary predictions
  • Local Processing: All computations performed locally using accumulated NASA dataset
  • Interactive Visualization: Google Earth-style 3D globe for intuitive weather pattern exploration

Benefits

For Event Planners:

  • Reduces financial losses from weather-related cancellations through statistical analysis of 10-year patterns
  • Enables informed venue selection based on historical regional weather trends
  • Provides confidence levels derived from decade-long climatological data

For Researchers & Developers:

  • Demonstrates practical application of NASA POWER API for long-term weather analysis
  • Open-source codebase available at WeatherWise-NASA25 GitHub organization
  • Local processing model suitable for offline applications and data privacy requirements

Intended Impact

Proof of Concept:

  • Validates feasibility of using NASA Earth observation data for probabilistic event planning
  • Demonstrates scalable architecture that could expand to global coverage
  • Establishes foundation for future deployment and broader regional support

Technical Demonstration:

  • Shows integration between NASA APIs, machine learning, and mobile applications
  • Provides template for similar weather prediction projects using government Earth science data

Technology Stack

Data Collection & Storage:

  • NASA POWER API: 10-year historical meteorological data source
  • CSV Processing: Local storage of accumulated daily weather records for 7 regions
  • Python scripts: Automated data collection from NASA services
  • Local file system: No cloud deployment - all data processed locally

Frontend (Mobile App):

  • Flutter/Dart: Cross-platform mobile development
  • flutter_earth_globe: Interactive 3D Earth visualization
  • Provider: State management for regional data display
  • HTTP/Dio: API communication with local Django backend

Backend (Local API Services):

  • Django/Python: Local RESTful API development
  • Django REST Framework: API serialization for 7-region data
  • Local data integration: Processes pre-collected NASA CSV files
  • No deployment: Runs locally for development and testing

Machine Learning Engine:

  • PyTorch: Neural network development (MLP, LSTM models) trained on 10-year regional data
  • scikit-learn: Data preprocessing and model evaluation
  • pandas/numpy: CSV data manipulation and analysis
  • Flask: Local ML model serving for real-time predictions

Creative Elements

Decade-Scale Data Integration: Systematic collection of 10 years of daily weather data from NASA POWER API, creating comprehensive regional climatological databases

Local-First Architecture: Innovative approach prioritizing local processing and data privacy, demonstrating NASA data utilization without requiring cloud infrastructure

Regional Specialization: Strategic focus on 7 key regions allows for deep historical analysis rather than shallow global coverage, ensuring higher accuracy for supported areas

Iterative Data Collection: Creative solution for accumulating massive datasets through systematic single-day API requests, building comprehensive historical archives

Team Considerations

Data Scope Management: Consciously limited to 7 regions to ensure thorough data collection and model training within project timeframe

Local Development Strategy: Prioritized local processing to maintain data control and eliminate deployment complexities during development phase

NASA API Integration: Developed systematic approach for collecting decade-scale meteorological data through individual daily requests

Scalability Foundation: Architecture visible in WeatherWise-NASA25 organization demonstrates modular design ready for future expansion to additional regions and deployment

Open Source Commitment: Complete codebase transparency allows community verification of NASA data utilization methodology and ML model approaches

Resource Optimization: Balanced comprehensive data collection with practical development constraints, creating robust foundation for 7-region coverage

This focused approach demonstrates practical utilization of NASA's Earth observation data while maintaining realistic scope and ensuring thorough regional coverage through decade-long historical analysis.

projectDetails.name: ExoAI
projectDetails.summary:
The Cosmic Analysts ExoAI platform is a comprehensive Machine Learning (ML) solution that streamlines the entire model development lifecycle, from data ingestion to secure deployment. It offers a user-friendly, dual-mode interface suitable for both beginners (Guided Mode) and advanced users (Research Hub), making complex AI workflows accessible. Both modes have the quantum explorer, Kepli, an AI assistant. Uniquely, ExoAI also includes an interactive 3D model for exoplanets. Lastly, it fully supports Arabic.

Built on a modern, decoupled architecture, the platform utilizes a responsive React frontend and a scalable FastAPI backend that manages training via an asynchronous queue and maintains a version-controlled model registry. It supports a diverse range of high-performance models, including a novel Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (TabKANet), classical ML (LightGBM), and Quantum ML classifiers, with adversarial testing ensuring robustness.

ExoAI democratizes advanced ML by simplifying complex tasks like hyperparameter tuning and model exporting, empowering individuals and teams with limited expertise. For seasoned data scientists, it provides a flexible environment for R&D and robust performance benchmarking. It delivers state-of-the-art results while prioritizing data privacy through a focus on security and local-first processing.
projectDetails.details:
Repository: https://github.com/MohammadEmad2003/ExoAi

Key Features:

  • Data Pipeline: Drag-and-drop file upload (CSV, Parquet, JSON) with automatic schema detection, interactive data previews, and manual type overrides.
  • Training System: Asynchronous job queue for concurrent training, hyperparameter tuning with presets and an advanced editor, and real-time progress monitoring.
  • Model Management: A comprehensive model registry with versioning, tracking of performance metrics (Accuracy, F1), robustness scores against adversarial attacks, and inference benchmarks (latency, throughput).
  • Dual-Mode User Experience: A guided onboarding flow for beginners and an advanced research dashboard for power users, with a responsive design, 3D Models, and multi-language support (English/Arabic).
  • Kepli, AI assistant: A chatbot to help navigators learn about exoplanets.
  • Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A set of visualizations and simplified statistics to explain model's behavior.
  • Quantum Machine Learning: Trying the current quantum machine learning algorithms and hardware on exoplanets datasets.
  • Adversarial Machine Learning: Testing models against adversarial attacks to strengthen its defense.

Guided Mode

3D Models

TabKANet

Quantum Machine Learning

Adversarial Machine Learning

Workflow: A user's journey through the platform follows a logical progression:

  1. Upload Data: The user begins by uploading a dataset through the drag-and-drop interface.
  2. Configure Training: They then configure the training job, selecting a model type, defining the target column, and adjusting hyperparameters using either simple presets or the advanced editor.
  3. Monitor & Analyze: The user monitors the training progress in real-time. Once complete, they analyze the model's performance, robustness, and inference metrics in the model registry.

Benefits:

  • Accessibility: Lowers the barrier to entry for creating sophisticated ML models.
  • Flexibility: Supports a wide range of models and export formats to fit diverse use cases.
  • Efficiency: The asynchronous worker system and streamlined UI accelerate the development cycle.
  • Robustness: Built-in adversarial testing and comprehensive metrics ensure models are reliable and well-understood.
  • Privacy-Focused: Processes data locally by default, ensuring user data remains secure.

Tools Used:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, react-i18next
  • Backend: FastAPI, Python
  • ML Models: PyTorch, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Scikit-learn, PennyLane, ART Toolbox

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmic Canvas
projectDetails.summary:
Cosmic Canvas is a web platform making NASA's largest datasets explorable for everyone. At its core, a bandwidth-efficient "Infinite Zoom" engine uses dynamic tiling, loading only the viewed portion of an image. This minimizes internet use, ensuring a smooth experience even on slow connections.

A key feature is **Precise Discovery Labeling**, a citizen science tool allowing users to add annotations to exact coordinates to pinpoint discoveries and foster collaboration. Instantly switch between data layers (e.g., infrared, X-ray) with our Multi-Spectrum Overlay. A **Galactic Guide AI** offers natural language search ("show me star-forming regions") and a chatbot to demystify complex concepts.

By solving the challenge of scale and accessibility, Cosmic Canvas truly **democratizes discovery**. It removes technical and knowledge barriers, accelerates research through crowdsourced insights, and inspires the next generation of explorers by making the cosmos tangible and interactive.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

Cosmic Canvas is an interactive web platform that makes NASA's largest and most detailed images of space accessible to everyone. It transforms massive, trillion-pixel images—which are normally impossible to view on a regular computer—into a fluid, explorable map of the universe.

Users can:

Seamlessly zoom and pan across vast celestial images, from a wide view of a galaxy down to a single stellar nursery.

Search for specific features using natural, everyday language (e.g., "Find ice caps on Mars").

Add precise, location-based labels to pinpoint discoveries, ask questions, or collaborate with other users.

Chat with an AI guide to understand what they are seeing and learn about complex astronomical objects.

How does it work?

The platform is built on two core technologies:

Dynamic Image Tiling: Instead of attempting to download a single, enormous image file (which can be terabytes in size), our backend pre-processes the image into a pyramid of small, square tiles. Your web browser only loads the few tiles needed for your specific view and zoom level. As you pan or zoom, it seamlessly loads the new tiles required. This method drastically reduces internet bandwidth and processing power, making the experience smooth on almost any device.

AI Integration: The Galactic Guide AI connects to the Gemini API. When you type a search query or ask the chatbot a question, our Node.js backend sends your request with a set of carefully tuned prompt instructions to the Gemini API, which then provides a highly accurate and context-aware response.

What benefits does it have?

The primary benefits are centered around accessibility and collaboration:

Global Accessibility: Its low bandwidth requirements mean it's usable by people in rural areas, schools with limited internet, or anyone not using a high-end computer.

Democratization of Science: It empowers citizen scientists. Anyone with curiosity can now meaningfully explore raw scientific data and contribute to discoveries by labeling interesting features.

Accelerated Research: Scientists can sift through vast datasets more efficiently using the AI search and by leveraging the crowdsourced annotations to quickly identify points of interest.

Inspirational Education: It serves as a powerful, hands-on educational tool that makes learning about space engaging and interactive for students of all ages.

What do you hope to achieve?

Our ultimate goal is to create a living, collaborative map of the universe. We hope to build a global community of students, hobbyists, and researchers who are all exploring and charting our cosmos together. We want to transform NASA's incredible archive of data from a static repository into a dynamic canvas for shared discovery, ensuring that the wonders of space are not just collected, but are truly seen, understood, and appreciated by everyone.

What tools, coding languages, or software did you use?

We used a modern, JavaScript-focused tech stack to build Cosmic Canvas:

Frontend (Client-Side):

JavaScript with the React.js framework to build a dynamic user interface.

OpenSeadragon, a specialized library for viewing high-resolution tiled images.

Backend (Server-Side):

Node.js with the Express.js framework to build a fast, scalable, and efficient API for handling image data and user requests.

AI Integration:

Google's Gemini API. The natural language search and chatbot are powered by making structured API calls from our Node.js server, using carefully engineered prompts to ensure high-quality responses.

Database:

PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension to efficiently store and query user annotations and their geographic locations on the images.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI in Core Project Functionality

The primary AI feature in our project is the Galactic Guide AI, which powers our platform's search and chatbot capabilities.

Which AI Tool: We used Google's Gemini API.

How We Used It: Our Node.js backend sends user queries (from the search bar and chatbot) to the Gemini API. We developed a system of carefully tuned prompt instructions to ensure the API returns accurate, context-aware astronomical information, coordinates, and conversational responses. This AI is the engine that makes our platform's natural language interaction possible.

AI as a Development Assistant

We also leveraged AI as a collaborative tool to accelerate our development workflow:

Prompt Engineering: We used generative AI to help us brainstorm and refine the complex prompts sent to the Gemini API, allowing us to iterate quickly and improve the AI's performance.

Code Translation and Refinement: AI was instrumental in translating initial Python-based concepts and algorithms into our final Node.js backend. It also assisted in optimizing backend routes, debugging errors, and suggesting efficient code for certain UI elements in React.js. All AI-assisted code was reviewed, tested, and modified by our team.

Generated Video Content: The outro sequence of our project's demo video was created using a video generation AI. As per the rules, this segment is visibly watermarked as "AI-Generated."

By integrating AI as both a core feature and a development partner, we were able to build a more sophisticated and user-friendly platform in the limited time available.

projectDetails.details:
Space Biology Knowledge Engine (SBKE) Project Summary

The Space Biology Knowledge Engine (SBKE) is a semantic AI platform designed as the central nervous system for human deep space exploration, transitioning missions to Mars and beyond from merely ensuring crew survival to enabling them to "survive and thrive." The core functionality involves solving the pervasive data fragmentation problem by unifying over 500 omics studies from GeneLab with decades of human clinical logs from LSDA into a singular, integrated Knowledge Graph (KG), which is built on top of existing NASA archives to maximize investment utility. This KG provides the semantic backbone for our intelligence layer, leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and BioBERT models (Python, PyTorch) to execute advanced predictive physiological modeling (IPM). The project’s impact is to mitigate mission risk by forecasting complex, synergistic health trajectories for astronauts over long durations (e.g., 1000 days), enabling autonomous mechanism-based countermeasure prescriptions on the spacecraft, and accelerating scientific discovery by identifying causal relationships between molecular changes and clinical outcomes. Our team, COSMIC_PIONEERS, considered technical viability and scientific rigor by prioritizing Explanation Generation in our Inference Engine, ensuring all AI outputs are scientifically valid and traceable back to curated data sources, delivering a highly creative solution for autonomous, personalized space medicine.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We leveraged advanced AI language models (like Gemini) as a core part of our knowledge synthesis and information architecture design process. The AI was used for two primary functions: 1) Data Curation Simulation: Analyzing and synthesizing the vast, fragmented scientific corpus (from OSDR, SpaceLID, 200K+ publications) to identify critical gaps and structural relationships, directly informing the necessity for the Semantic Knowledge Graph (KG). 2) Structuring Complexity: Organizing the multi-layered technical details—including the five-layered architecture, the specific function of the SLSO Ontology, and the phased Roadmap—into a single, coherent, and strategically persuasive narrative. This enabled the team to rapidly prototype the project's conceptual framework and technical narrative, significantly accelerating our ability to present a viable solution.

node.title: Cosmic Query
node.excerpt: We are Cosmic Query, a team passionate about using AI to make NASA’s bioscience research more accessible and actionable.

projectDetails.name: Project Cosmic Query
projectDetails.summary:
Cosmic Query is an AI-powered knowledge engine that transforms 608 Space Biology publications published since 2010 on Pubmed Central from static PDFs into actionable intelligence. 

Our system reads, understands, and synthesizes research findings across multiple formats—from instant summaries to AI-generated podcasts.

The challenge: decades of invaluable research exists, but navigating it is like searching for specific stars in an entire galaxy. Scientists need to identifyknowledge gaps, mission planners need actionable insights, and students need accessible entry points. Cosmic Query addresses this through intelligent content
 transformations: 
1. Dense summaries extract key findings in seconds
2. Reflections identify research gaps
4. Analysis papers synthesize patterns across studies
5.  AI podcasts make complex research digestible anywhere, anytime.

As humanity prepares to return to the Moon and reach Mars, we cannot afford critical knowledge buried in PDFs. Every NASA experiment—from bone density loss in microgravity to plant growth in space—contains insights that could determine mission success. Cosmic Query democratizes this knowledge for scientists, undergraduate students, program managers, and life support engineers alike. We're not just organizing information, we're accelerating space exploration by making knowledge truly accessible.
projectDetails.details:
Cosmic Query is a multi-modal knowledge platform that ingests Pubmed Central's 608 space biology publications and transforms them into actionable intelligence. Users can upload papers or web URLs, and our system automatically processes them through multiple transformation pipelines:

  • Dense Summaries: Extracts core findings and methodology in concise form
  • Reflections: Analyzes gaps, contradictions, and areas needing further investigation
  • Analysis Papers: Synthesizes insights across multiple studies to reveal patterns
  • Sample Summaries: Provides quick overviews for rapid scanning
  • AI Podcasts: Converts research into engaging multi-speaker audio conversations

Beyond transformations, users can chat with their research corpus using natural language, search semantically across all documents, and receive answers with precise citations linking back to source material.

Workflow:

Our architecture combines cutting-edge AI with robust engineering:

1. Ingestion Pipeline: When users upload content, Firecrawl scrapes and cleans web pages while Docling parses PDFs and Office documents, extracting text while preserving structure.

2. Intelligent Processing: Our FastAPI backend queues jobs to background workers, which chunk content into semantically meaningful segments. Each chunk is processed through Google's Gemini API and Jina AI to generate embeddings— mathematical representations that capture meaning, not just keywords.

3. Hybrid Search: We maintain both vector embeddings (for semantic "understanding") and full-text indexes (for precise keyword matching) in SurrealDB, enabling searches that find relevant content even when users phrase queries differently than the original text.

4. Transformation Engine: When users request a specific output, our AI agents analyze the content and generate tailored formats. For podcasts, we create multi speaker scripts with ElevenLabs' text-to-speech, simulating conversations between scientists discussing findings.

5. Interactive Frontend: Our Next.js interface provides a sleek, space-themed dashboard where users navigate notebooks (project containers), explore sources, generate transformations, and engage in contextual conversations with AI that has "read" all their uploaded research.

Benefits:

  • Time Efficiency: Reduces literature review from weeks to hours
  • Accessibility: Makes complex research understandable for non-experts
  • Multimodal Learning: Supports different learning styles (reading, listening, chatting)
  • Gap Identification: Highlights areas where additional research is needed
  • Citation Integrity: Every AI response includes source references

Vision:

Our vision extends beyond this challenge. We hope to:

1. Accelerate Research Timelines: Help scientists avoid duplicating experiments already conducted

2. Inform Mission Design: Give engineers and planners instant access to biological constraints for spacecraft design

3. Identify Research Priorities: Help funding agencies see where knowledge gaps exist

Ultimately, we want Cosmic Query to become the standard tool for anyone working with space life sciences data—a living knowledge base that grows smarter with each new publication added.

projectDetails.summary: In Egypt, Helwan city suffers from pollution. Helwan is one of the most historical industrial cities, which has a high level of pollution, decline in green areas, and rise in temperature. HealCity converts this challenge to a chance as it is a website (digital twin) that diagnoses the town's health by using NASA satellite data. The website represents an interactive dashboard and avatar (interactive icons) that reflect Helwan's environmental status in real time. Citizens can help the city to be better by participating in gamification actions such as reducing emissions of factories, planting trees, and increasing green areas. The website allows seeing the impact on the emojis which represent the city's ecosystem. In addition, the website shows a comparison between the city's status before and after. The project combines data, engaging visualization, and technology to encourage citizens and decision-makers to work on the city and try to build a sustainable and livable Helwan city in the future. Decision-makers can use the platform to guide environmental policies, monitor progress, and plan initiatives that improve green spaces and reduce pollution.

projectDetails.name: Project CosmoCrafters_9
projectDetails.summary:
This project develops an automated exoplanet classification system using XGBoost machine learning to categorize celestial objects as FALSE POSITIVE, CANDIDATE, or CONFIRMED exoplanets. By integrating data from NASA's Kepler, K2, and TESS missions (21,271 ), the model achieves 77.93% accuracy in distinguishing genuine exoplanets from false detections.
The system addresses a critical bottleneck in astronomy: manually validating thousands of potential exoplanet signals is time-consuming and requires extensive expert analysis. This model streamlines the validation process by automatically prioritizing high-confidence candidates for follow-up observation while filtering out false positives.
The project employed advanced data preprocessing techniques including KNN imputation and Random Forest-based feature reconstruction to handle missing stellar and planetary parameters. Feature engineering created astrophysically meaningful variables like planet-to-star radius ratios and normalized transit depths. Hyperparameter optimization via randomized search identified optimal model configurations across 50 different parameter combinations.
This tool is important because it accelerates exoplanet discovery, optimizes telescope time allocation, and helps astronomers focus resources on the most promising candidates. With thousands of new signals detected annually, automated classification becomes essential for advancing our understanding of planetary systems beyond our solar system.
projectDetails.details:
How It Works

Our exoplanet classification system uses a multi-stage machine learning pipeline to automatically categorize astronomical signals:

  1. Data Integration Layer: Merges datasets from three NASA missions (Kepler, K2, TESS) containing 21,271 exoplanet observations with 15 standardized features including orbital period, transit depth, planet radius, and stellar properties.
  2. Intelligent Preprocessing: Handles missing data (up to 98% in some features) using KNN imputation and Random Forest regression to reconstruct stellar mass and metallicity from correlated parameters.
  3. Feature Engineering: Creates astrophysically meaningful variables like planet-to-star radius ratios, log-transformed distributions for skewed data, and normalized transit depths that enhance classification accuracy.
  4. XGBoost Classifier: Employs gradient boosting with 500 decision trees, optimized through randomized hyperparameter search across 250 model configurations to achieve 77.93% accuracy.
  5. Three-Class Output: Categorizes each observation as FALSE POSITIVE (instrumental noise/eclipsing binaries), CANDIDATE (requires follow-up), or CONFIRMED (validated exoplanet).

Benefits & Impact

Immediate Benefits:

  • Reduces manual validation time from hours per candidate to milliseconds
  • Processes entire TESS survey data (7,703 objects) in under one second
  • Achieves 86% recall for confirmed exoplanets, minimizing missed discoveries
  • Provides probability scores enabling risk-based prioritization

Scientific Impact:

  • Telescope Efficiency: Helps astronomers allocate limited observation time (James Webb, Hubble, ground-based facilities) to high-priority targets
  • Discovery Acceleration: With TESS discovering 200+ candidates monthly, automation is essential for keeping pace
  • Resource Optimization: Saves approximately $50,000-100,000 per avoided false positive follow-up observation
  • Democratization: Makes sophisticated classification accessible to smaller research institutions without large expert teams

Long-term Vision:

  • Integration into automated survey pipelines for real-time classification
  • Foundation for habitability assessment models (next phase)
  • Training tool for astronomy students learning exoplanet validation techniques

Technology Stack

Programming Languages:

  • Python 3.12 (primary development language)

Machine Learning & Data Science:

  • XGBoost 3.0.5 (gradient boosting framework)
  • Scikit-learn (preprocessing, imputation, cross-validation)
  • Pandas/NumPy (data manipulation)
  • Matplotlib/Seaborn (visualization)

Development Environment:

  • Google Colab (cloud-based training with GPU acceleration)
  • Jupyter Notebook (exploratory analysis)

Deployment:

  • Streamlit (interactive web application framework)
  • Joblib (model serialization)

Data Sources:

  • NASA Exoplanet Archive API
  • Kepler Mission DR25 catalog
  • K2 Ecliptic Plane Input Catalog
  • TESS Objects of Interest (TOI) catalog

Hardware:

  • Training: Google Colab GPU (Tesla T4)
  • Inference: CPU-optimized for real-time predictions

Creative Innovations

  1. Cross-Mission Data Fusion: First to combine Kepler, K2, and TESS data into unified classification framework, leveraging strengths of each mission's detection methodology.
    • Radius ratio relates to transit depth via physical laws
    • Normalized depth accounts for stellar brightness variations
    • Log transformations match power-law distributions in planetary systems
  2. Balanced Optimization: Tuned model to maximize recall for CONFIRMED class (86%) while maintaining precision, prioritizing "don't miss real planets" over "avoid false alarms" - reflecting real-world scientific priorities.
  3. Interpretable AI: XGBoost provides feature importance rankings, helping astronomers understand which parameters drive classifications and validate model decisions against physical intuition.

Design Considerations

Scientific Rigor:

  • Retained outliers (extreme but valid astrophysical cases) rather than blindly removing them
  • Validated that imputed values fall within physically plausible ranges
  • Cross-referenced classifications with published literature

Practical Usability:

  • Streamlit interface requires no coding knowledge
  • Accepts standard NASA Exoplanet Archive CSV formats
  • Outputs match IAU (International Astronomical Union) terminology

Scalability:

  • Model size (6.6 MB) allows deployment on standard hardware
  • Inference time <10ms per prediction enables real-time processing
  • Architecture supports incremental training as new data arrives

Robustness:

  • 5-fold cross-validation prevents overfitting
  • Tested on held-out data from different missions
  • Handles incomplete feature sets gracefully

Ethical AI:

  • Transparent decision-making through feature importance
  • Acknowledges 22% error rate to prevent overconfidence
  • Designed to assist, not replace, expert astronomers

Team Philosophy

We approached this project recognizing that machine learning in astronomy isn't about replacing human expertise—it's about augmenting it. Astronomers have limited time and cognitive bandwidth; our tool handles repetitive pattern recognition, freeing them for higher-level scientific reasoning about planetary formation, habitability, and mission planning.

  • These tools were not used to generate images, videos, or audio content .
  • All analytical work, feature engineering, and model training were designed, implemented, and verified manually by the team.

AI assistance was limited to textual support and code explanation only.

projectDetails.name: CTRL+Sky
projectDetails.summary:
CTRL + Sky is a web app that turns complex weather forecasts into simple, actionable insights for everyday planning. Instead of overwhelming users with data, it predicts if conditions will be too hot, too cold, too wet, too windy, or uncomfortable—helping people quickly decide whether it’s a good day for their outdoor plans.
From event organizers to families on a trip, CTRL + Sky makes weather intelligence practical, clear, and easy to use, empowering safer, smarter choices in a changing climate.
projectDetails.details:
CTRL+Sky

What Exactly Does It Do?

This website helps people plan outdoor activities by predicting whether conditions will be hot, cold, windy, wet, or generally uncomfortable at a chosen place and time. Users simply enter their location and date, and the site generates a clear, easy-to-read forecast. Instead of complex meteorological charts, it provides straightforward insights focused on comfort, safety, and confident decision-making.


How Does It Work?

The application starts with user input time and location, then calls weather data sources through APIs. The raw data, which includes values like temperature, wind speed, and rainfall probability, is processed and matched against defined thresholds. Each parameter is translated into clear categories that reflect how people actually feel the weather. These results are displayed through an intuitive web interface, making it quick and easy to interpret.

Benefits

Complex weather data is simplified into clear, actionable insights that help users plan outdoor activities safely and confidently. The app reduces uncertainty, saves time, and minimizes risks from extreme conditions. To make the experience more engaging, a mini weather-themed game was also added, turning learning about weather into something fun and interactive.

What Do You Hope to Achieve?

With CTRL + Sky, we aim to make weather forecasting more accessible and meaningful for everyday life. Our hope is to help people plan better, avoid risks, and feel confident about their decisions when scheduling outdoor activities. Beyond the hackathon, we want to show how technology and design can bridge the gap between scientific data and ordinary users. In the long term, the project could evolve into a widely available service with mobile alerts, multi-language support, and even smart recommendations for event planning.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Coding Languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for building the frontend and implementing core functionality.
    • VS Code: Integrated development environment used for writing and managing the code.
  • Data Sources: Live and historical weather data collected from Weather APIs. The data is processed and categorized into user-friendly weather conditions such as very hot, very cold, very windy, very wet, or uncomfortable.

projectDetails.name: Project Curiosity X Asteriod_Impact
projectDetails.summary:
Our project bridges the gap between scientists, decision-makers, and the public by creating a unified digital platform that communicates the real threat of asteroids to Earth in a way that’s understandable and actionable for everyone.

We developed an interactive web platform consisting of three main interfaces:

A dynamic 3D visualization that shows the real-time motion of asteroids and Earth in space, designed to engage and educate the general public.

A professional analytics dashboard that provides key data and insights to help decision-makers take fast, evidence-based actions.

A scientific interface that delivers detailed datasets and analytical tools for researchers to study asteroid behavior and improve prediction models.

This project directly addresses the challenge of improving communication and decision-making regarding asteroid threats. By connecting science, policy, and public awareness, it transforms complex data into a shared understanding — which is crucial for preventing future disasters and protecting our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an interactive web platform that visualizes and analyzes asteroid data to connect scientists, decision-makers, and the public through one unified system.

It works by collecting asteroid data from NASA APIs, processing it with Python, and integrating it into a 3D real-time simulation built with JavaScript and Three.js. The platform has three main interfaces: a public view that visualizes asteroid motion to raise awareness, a dashboard for decision-makers that displays key metrics like impact probability and asteroid proximity, and a scientific interface providing in-depth data and analysis tools for researchers.

The project’s main benefit is its ability to transform complex scientific data into clear, actionable insights, helping governments and organizations take early preventive measures.

We used Python, JavaScript, Three.js, Plotly Dash, Pandas, and HTML/CSS to develop and visualize the system.

Our creativity lies in bridging the gap between science, policy, and society — turning raw data into an interactive experience that makes space awareness accessible, understandable, and impactful for everyone.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used AI tools as supportive assistants during the development of our project. Specifically, AI was used to:

  • Refine, debug, and test Python code to ensure clean structure, accuracy, and efficiency in data processing and visualization.
  • Verify and cross-check scientific information related to asteroid data, orbital parameters, and environmental datasets to maintain factual accuracy.

No AI-generated images, videos, or NASA-branded materials were used.

projectDetails.name: CZMU
projectDetails.summary:
Exo Hunters is an interactive platform that brings the mystery of exoplanets closer to
everyone.

The story is written in three languages (English, Arabic, French) so the experience is
universal and inclusive.

On our website, users can learn through play with a quiz-based game, explore a galaxy map in 3D, understand how AI uses NASA’s real data to detect hidden planets, and connect with the legacy of Ancient Egyptian astronomy where pyramids were aligned with the stars.

Our approach combines NASA’s Kepler and TESS datasets with machine learning to analyze thousands of stellar light curves and identify faint signals of potential exoplanets. We translate this science into engaging experiences through games, visual storytelling, and cultural heritage, turning complex research into something anyone can enjoy and feel part of.

At its core, Exo Hunters is more than technology. It is about reclaiming the stars for everyone. Space exploration is often seen as distant, belonging only to scientists or astronauts. But we believe curiosity belongs to humanity as a whole. Every child who stares at the night sky, every culture that once charted the heavens, every person who has wondered “what lies beyond?” is part of this story.

By bridging ancient wisdom with modern science, we show that curiosity is timeless. We turn starlight into knowledge, and knowledge into inspiration, sparking a new generation to dream bigger, reach further, and see themselves as explorers of worlds yet unseen.
projectDetails.details:
🚀 Mission:

To make space exploration accessible to everyone by transforming real NASA data into interactive experiences that teach, inspire, and empower curiosity across cultures, languages, and generations.
We combine science with storytelling, technology with imagination, and learning with play to turn every user into an explorer of worlds beyond our own.

🌌 Vision:

To build a world where discovering the universe is not limited to scientists or astronauts but shared by every curious mind on Earth.
We imagine a future where AI, culture, and human wonder come together to reveal new planets, new knowledge, and a deeper connection under one infinite sky.


The CZMU Exo Hunters project provides a multi-platform exoplanet discovery system that allows users to:

1. Discover NASA datasets (Kepler, K2, TESS) through an interactive web dashboard.
2. Classify promising exoplanets using an AI model as Confirmed, False Positive, or Undecided.
3. Visualize planets in 3D along with orbits, sizes, and distances.
4. Engage with kids through a hardware-based game (ESP32 + TFT display) that turns discoveries into an enjoyable and interactive game.


5. Our hardware game tells a story about space and exoplanets, then asks the user a few questions to test their knowledge.


6. Planet game showing a correct answer and getting 5 points also showing the game level list

How Does it Work?

• Backend: Hosts data requests from the site and hardware, and returns AI model predictions.
• AI Model: Trained on NASA photometry features (orbital period, transit duration, radius, stellar properties) which called transit method to predict candidates with calibrated probabilities

Dashboard:

1- Scientist Mode: complete light curves, scatter plots, AI metrics.
2- Kid Mode: simplified findings, fun facts, emojis, and badges.
3- 3D Explorer: Planetary system map that is interactive.
4- Hardware Game: Tap buttons to select planets, see predictions, and trigger animations or sounds in real time.
Dashboard after discovering a candidate planet as a Confirmed with accuracy....


Benefits & Impact

1- Breaks NASA complexity to the understanding of all.
2- Encourages curiosity through gamification and 3D technology.
3- Connects history (Egyptian astronomy) with modern AI.
4- Supports global reach with English, Arabic, and French.
5- Encourages STEM learning, shaping future explorers.

Goals:

1- Determine the classification of the Candidate planet from the NASA Archive using our ML model to decide is it False-Positive, or Confirmed
2- Make exoplanet science accessible and engaging to all.
3- Show the power of AI in astronomy research.
4- Demonstrate multi-platform integration (web + 3D + hardware).

FUTURE CONSIDERATIONS:

Visionary Long-Term

1. “AI Astronomer” Assistant: a conversational AI trained on space data for research and learning.
2. Global Citizen Science Network: connect users from different countries to contribute live observations.
3. Cultural Astronomy Archive: unify ancient and modern sky maps in one immersive timeline.
4. Space Mission Collaboration: future tie-ins with ESA, SpaceX, or private observatories.

Software & Data:

1. Crowdsourced Training Data: allow scientists to help classify light curves and suggest reclassifications when human expertise overrides uncertainty.
2. Interactive Annotation System: enable scientists to add notes and insights to both confirmed and candidate
planets.
3. Planet Tagging Feature: allow users to save and label specific planets for continued study or collaboration.
4. Explainable AI: visualize why the model flags certain stars (heatmaps, attention layers).
5. Multi-language AI Interface: expand to Arabic, French, etc., for global accessibility.
6. Enhanced Visualization: VR galaxy maps with orbit simulations for each discovered planet.
7. Expansion beyond Kepler/TESS: include JWST, PLATO, and Roman Telescope datasets.


Hardware & Interactive Experience:

1. Physical Game Expansion: add sensors to simulate planet detection (light sensors mimicking photometric data).
2. Museum / Classroom Kits: educational setups for schools to teach AI + astronomy. Our goal is to make it into a classroom tool as universal as Kahoot, where quizzes and games teach space science.
3. Multiplayer Exploration Mode: introduce online or local co-op gameplay, allowing students to explore galaxies and make discoveries together.
4. Expanded Learning Galaxies: extend content beyond exoplanets to include NASA-related topics—from Mars missions to black holes.
5. Leaderboards & Challenges: motivate learners to stay curious and engaged through friendly competition and discovery milestones.



Statistics and Graphs :

1- Our Model Accuracy Reaches 92%

2- Testing our model on 876 candidate planet from the NASA archive, and we can determine the classification of 75% of them if False-Positive or confirmed as a planet

projectDetails.name: Project Data Wizards
projectDetails.summary: Air quality is not merely an environmental issue, it’s a daily human dilemma. Each breath we take may carry invisible pollutants that can harm our health. Even though NASA satellites already collect tremendous amounts of public atmospheric data, this information is typically very complex and far removed from communities that need access to this information. We have created a web platform that converts raw NASA EarthData into easily interpretable, actionable information and insights. AeroWatch integrates NASA satellite observations (e.g., TEMPO, MERRA-2, AIRS) with ground-based observational data to provide users with real-time air quality monitoring and predictions to help make informed and protective health decisions. AeroWatch uses an interactive interface, allowing users to quickly identify areas of air quality impact, understand air quality drivers (e.g., nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and ozone levels), and receive applied precautions. At an operational level, our system utilizes a custom API that meshes together applications and functionality of earthaccess, harmony-py, RSIG-py, ArcGIS-py, NumPy, and Pandas, ensuring accuracy and scalability. What distinguishes AeroWatch is its integration of weather influences, such as rainfall and humidity, into pollution forecasting, allowing for better estimates at the local, city, or even neighborhood level.
projectDetails.details: AeroWatch uses an interactive interface with easy-to-understand color-coded maps and alerts, allowing users to quickly identify areas of air quality impact, understand air quality drivers (e.g., nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and ozone levels), and receive applied precautions utilizing a custom API that meshes together applications and functionality of earthaccess, harmony-py, RSIG-py, ArcGIS-py, NumPy, and Pandas, ensuring accuracy and scalability. AeroWatch utilizes an API that uses earthaccess and harmony-py to get NASA TEMPO datasets, matplotlib to visualize data on map, NumPy, Xarray and Pandas for data analysis. They all work together to calculate the Air Quality Index (AQI), from which the air quality is identified. This API is combined with the backend to get, analyze, identify and show accurate, near real-time air quality to the user. This helps user to make decisions about the needed precautions to be considered as well as it makes scientists get make accurate analyses for pollution, resulting in more accurate and effective solutions for pollution. For the backend of the website, we used python for programming, earthaccess, harmony-py, Xarray, FastAPI, NumPy, matplotlib and Pandas libraries and APIs. For the frontend of the website, we used react.js, tailwindCSS and bootstrap5.

projectDetails.name: Monitoring Environmental Changes in the Nile Delta using Terra Satellite Data
projectDetails.summary:
The Nile Delta, one of the most vital agricultural regions in Egypt, is undergoing rapid environmental changes due to urban expansion, intensive farming, water mismanagement, and the impacts of climate change. These pressures are threatening crop productivity, water security, and the long-term sustainability of millions of people who depend on the Delta.

Our project addresses this challenge by transforming complex satellite data into accessible insights. Using NASA’s Terra satellite and its MODIS NDVI dataset (2000–2024), we tracked long-term vegetation health to detect trends and risks in the Delta. To validate and visualize these changes, we integrated NASA Worldview for satellite imagery and Google Earth Engine (GEE) for large-scale processing, enabling us to calculate annual averages and highlight areas of concern.

The solution is a visualization and analysis tool that simplifies satellite data into clear maps and charts. This empowers policymakers, researchers, and local communities to make informed, data-driven decisions about land use, agriculture, and environmental protection.

By leveraging open-access Earth observation data and cloud-based tools, our project demonstrates how space technology can directly support climate resilience, protect natural resources, and ensure a sustainable future for the Nile Delta.
projectDetails.details:
Project Title: Monitoring Environmental Changes in the Nile Delta using Terra Satellite Data

Problem Statement

The Nile Delta is facing rapid environmental changes caused by urban expansion, unsustainable farming practices, water mismanagement, and climate change. These factors are putting enormous pressure on agricultural productivity, water security, and the livelihoods of millions of people. Traditional monitoring methods are limited and often fail to capture long-term, large-scale changes.

Data & Tools

Satellite Data: MODIS NDVI (2000–2024) from NASA’s Terra satellite to measure vegetation health.

NASA Worldview: Used for visual validation and exploration of satellite imagery.

Google Earth Engine (GEE): Enabled large-scale processing, calculation of annual averages, and temporal analysis.

Visualization Tools: Maps, charts, and infographics created for clarity.

Solution

We developed a visualization and analysis tool that simplifies complex satellite datasets into accessible insights. By processing NDVI data over two decades, the system highlights vegetation changes, identifies vulnerable areas, and reveals long-term trends in agricultural land use.

Impact

The solution empowers policymakers, researchers, and local communities to make data-driven decisions about land management, agriculture, and environmental protection. By turning open-access satellite data into actionable knowledge, this project contributes to climate resilience and the sustainable future of the Nile Delta.

projectDetails.name: Shark Guard
projectDetails.summary:
Our project Shark Guard aims to protect sharks and understand their behavior using artificial intelligence and NASA satellite data.
Sharks play a vital role in maintaining the balance of marine ecosystems, yet tracking them is extremely difficult due to deep water movements and changing ocean conditions.
That’s why we designed a smart platform that combines real-time shark tracking with ocean environment analysis, using satellite data such as sea surface temperature, chlorophyll levels, and ocean currents.
The platform features:
- Interactive 3D Map displaying live shark locations and environmental layers.
- Smart Tag Device with sensors that measure depth, pressure, temperature, light, and ECG signals.
- Floater System that transmits tag data to satellites in real time.
- AI Chatbot designed for both researchers and students, with a Student Mode that explains shark science in a simple way.
- Educational Game that helps students learn about sharks interactively.

We used NASA datasets such as MODIS-Aqua, PACE, and OSTIA SST to build predictive models for shark feeding zones and migration patterns.
Our ultimate goal is to make Shark Guard a global platform that combines science, protection, and education, supporting sustainable ocean conservation for the future.
projectDetails.details:
Shark Guard is an intelligent system designed to track sharks in real time.

Tag Components:

It works through a small tag device attached to the shark that measures water depth, temperature, pressure, heart rate, and also includes a 360° camera that captures feeding and danger moments.

The data is transmitted to a floater, which sends it to satellites, and then visualized on an interactive 3D dashboard map with filters for environmental factors like chlorophyll, currents, and temperature.


How to Use 3D Interactive map:

You can easily explore our interactive 3D map by moving the planet with your mouse, zooming in to any ocean, then using filters (temperature, chlorophyll, ocean currents) to identify shark areas. Then, by clicking on any point, you can see shark data and details of its activity in real time.The project helps researchers and scientists better understand shark behavior, predict movements, and support marine ecosystem balance. We also added an AI chatbot

Student Mode with a fun educational quiz to teach high school students about sharks in an engaging way.

Using satellite observations and NASA APIs, the JSON points were constructed to reflect realistic oceanic conditions for monitoring shark habitats.

Data Sources: NASA OSTIA SST dataset, NOAA Climate Data Online (CDO), NASA MODIS-Aqua Ocean Color Data, NOAA Global Ocean Currents, IUCN Shark Species Distribution Maps, Surface Water and Ocean Topography, AO Global Shark Fisheries Data.
Technologies & Tools Used: React, Google Gemini, React-Leaflet, React-Icons, Flowbite React, React Globe, Figma, Recharts, Tailwind CSS.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We integrated AI technology into Shark Guard through a chatbot assistant that supports both researchers and students

For researchers, the chatbot can explain shark behavior, provide insights about environmental patterns (such as temperature or chlorophyll changes), and summarize satellite data in simple language.
For students, we created a Student Mode, where the chatbot offers interactive learning by answering questions about marine life, giving quick facts. This AI component, built using Google Gemini, enhances user engagement, makes complex scientific data easier to understand, and bridges the gap between science and education through a conversational experience.

projectDetails.name: DeepSpace ai
projectDetails.summary: Deep-space-ai is an AI model for classifying candidate signals as “exoplanet” or “non-exoplanet” using NASA’s open datasets (Kepler, TESS). We built a pipeline for light-curve preprocessing and feature extraction, then trained a deep neural network with uncertainty estimation and interpretability (SHAP). The system automatically ranks likely planet candidates and reduces manual workload for astronomers, accelerating the confirmation process and improving throughput on large survey datasets. (≈100 words)
projectDetails.details:
What it does & how it works:

  • Converts NASA light curves into cleaned, normalized time series, removes noise/outliers, and extracts time-domain and statistical features (transit depth, duration, periodicity metrics, etc.).
  • Trains an AI classifier (deep neural network / ensemble) on labeled examples from the NASA Exoplanet Archive to score new signals and output candidate likelihood plus confidence.

Benefits & intended impact:

  • Automates triage of thousands of signals to surface high-quality candidates faster, reducing manual review and increasing discovery rate.
  • Lowers false positives through multi-stage filtering and uncertainty estimation, making follow-up observation planning more efficient.

Tools & technologies:

  • Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, TensorFlow or PyTorch), astropy, lightkurve, matplotlib.
  • Execution on Google Colab / local GPU; CI via GitHub Actions.

Creativity & considerations:

  • Combined domain-specific feature engineering with learned representations.
  • Integrated SHAP explanations to make decisions interpretable for astronomers.
  • Addressed class imbalance and reviewed dataset licenses; adhered to NASA data usage terms.

How to use (workflow):

  • Upload raw light-curve files → preprocessing → model inference → ranked candidate list + HTML/PDF report for human review.

Demonstration of the DEEP Space model

projectDetails.details:
A Submission for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025

Team Name: Digital Minds

1. High-Level Project Summary

What did you develop?

We developed the Air Quality Monitor, a user-friendly web application created by our team, Digital Minds. It’s a complete tool that gives people real-time information about the environment around them. The main features include a live interactive map that shows the Air Quality Index (AQI) anywhere in the world, detailed weather information, and an advanced AI Assistant. This AI provides personalized health advice based on the current air quality and the user's specific health conditions, making environmental data easy to understand and use.

How does it address the challenge?

Our project directly answers the NASA Space Apps Challenge, "From EarthData to Action." We take complex environmental data from global sources and turn it into simple, actionable information that anyone can use. Instead of just showing numbers, our application explains what the data means for your health. The AI Assistant is the key feature that turns data into action, offering clear recommendations like whether it's safe to exercise outdoors. We make Earth data accessible and useful for everyday life.

Why is it important?

The Air Quality Monitor is important because it empowers people to protect their health. Air pollution is a serious global problem, especially for individuals with conditions like asthma or allergies. Our application gives everyone the power to see the quality of the air they breathe and make informed decisions to stay safe. By making this information free and easy to access, we raise awareness about environmental health and help build healthier communities for a better future.

2. Project Details

What does it do and how does it work?

Our Air Quality Monitor is a web app that helps you understand your local environment. It works in a simple way: you open the app and see a world map. You can click anywhere or search for a city to see the real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) and current weather, like temperature and wind. The most special part is our AI Assistant. You can ask it questions, and it will give you health advice based on the live data and any health conditions you share, like asthma. This is possible because our app connects to data sources for air quality (WAQI API) and weather (OpenWeatherMap API), and then uses the Google Gemini API to give you a smart, personalized answer.

What benefits does it have?

The main benefit is that it helps you protect your health. It gives you clear, simple advice that is made just for you. Because it's a web app, it's easy for anyone to use, and we made it in both English and Arabic to reach more people. It doesn’t just show you numbers; it helps you understand what they mean for your daily life, which helps everyone become more aware of the environment.

What is the intended impact of the project?

We hope our project will give people the power to make healthier choices every day. We want families to use it to decide if it's a good day for their kids to play outside. In the bigger picture, we want to make everyone more aware of air pollution. When people understand the problem better, they are more likely to support actions that lead to cleaner air for everyone. Our goal is to help build a healthier future, one person at a time.

How is your project creative?

Our project is creative because of how it connects data to real life. Many apps can show you the air quality number, but our app is different because of its AI Assistant. It doesn't just show you a number; it tells you a story about what that number means for you. By knowing if you have allergies or asthma, it gives advice that is truly personal. This changes the app from a simple tool into a helpful health partner, which is a new and creative way to use environmental data.

What factors did your team consider?

  • A Simple Experience: We wanted the app to be very easy to use for everyone, not just for tech experts. This is why we focused on a clean design and simple map.
  • Useful Advice: We knew that just showing data is not enough. We always asked ourselves, "How can someone use this to make a decision?" This led us to create the AI Assistant.
  • For Everyone: We wanted our tool to be useful for people all over the world. That's why we included two languages and added a feature that reads text aloud for people who need it.
  • Trustworthy Information: We used well-known public data sources to make sure the information is reliable.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Coding: We used JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3.
  • Styling and Maps: We used Tailwind CSS to make the design look good, and Leaflet.js for the interactive map.
  • Data and AI: We used the WAQI API for air quality, the OpenWeatherMap API for weather, and the Google Gemini API for our AI Assistant.
  • Other Tools: We used Visual Studio Code to write the code, GitHub to work together as a team, and Netlify to host our project online.

3. NASA Data

Our project, the Air Quality Monitor, was inspired by the main goal of the NASA Space Apps Challenge: to use Earth observation data to help people. While we use other data sources for our live numbers, our idea was shaped by NASA's mission.

The main NASA resource that inspired us was NASA's Earthdata, especially the Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). GIBS gives us pictures of our planet from space, showing things we can't see from the ground.

Our app is built to use these images to give a bigger picture. For example, a user could look at the Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) layer from NASA satellites to see where pollution is thick in the air. By combining these NASA images with the live AQI numbers, we can give a full and easy-to-understand view of air quality. This perfectly matches the challenge of turning "EarthData into Action."

4. Space Agency Partner & Other Data

Here is a list of all the data sources and tools we used for our project:

  • NASA Resources (Inspiration):
    • NASA Earthdata
    • NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS)
    • World Air Quality Index (WAQI) Project: For live AQI data.
    • OpenWeatherMap API: For live weather data.
    • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
    • Libraries: Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js
    • AI Service: Google Gemini API
    • Hosting: Netlify
    • Collaboration: Git & GitHub
    • Editor: Visual Studio Code

5. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Yes, Artificial Intelligence is a very important part of our project.

We used the Google Gemini API to create our AI Assistant, which is the main feature of our app. The AI is not just an extra feature; it is central to how our project works.

When a user asks for health advice, our app takes the live air quality and weather data for their location, along with any health conditions the user shares. All this information is sent to the Gemini AI, which then gives a personalized and smart recommendation. This is what makes our project special. The AI helps us turn complicated data into simple, useful, and personal advice, which is the main goal of the "From EarthData to Action" challenge.

projectDetails.name: Project Do Not Look Up
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Unidos: Earth Defense Simulator, is an interactive web-based visualization and simulation tool designed to model and mitigate asteroid impact scenarios. Using real data from NASA’s NEO API and USGS elevation and seismic datasets, Unidos enables users to simulate asteroid trajectories, predict impact consequences, and evaluate deflection strategies in an intuitive, educational interface.

The platform integrates orbital mechanics calculations to project an asteroid’s path and potential collision point with Earth, then estimates impact energy, crater size, seismic magnitude, and tsunami reach based on environmental data. Users can adjust asteroid parameters or test mitigation methods such as kinetic impactors to observe in real time how small changes in velocity alter the outcome.

By combining scientific accuracy, interactivity, and accessibility, Unidos bridges the gap between complex space science and public understanding. It empowers scientists, policymakers, and citizens to explore “what-if” scenarios and make informed decisions for planetary defense preparedness.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Unidos: Earth Defense Simulator, is an interactive web application that models asteroid impact scenarios and visualizes their environmental consequences. It integrates NASA’s NEO API for asteroid data and USGS elevation and seismic datasets to simulate realistic effects such as crater formation, seismic waves, and tsunami propagation.

The tool allows users to explore asteroid trajectories in 3D orbital visualizations and view detailed 2D impact maps showing affected regions. Users can modify asteroid parameters—such as size, velocity, or entry angle—or test deflection strategies like kinetic impactors to see how small changes in velocity can prevent catastrophic impacts.

Developed with Python (Flask) for backend processing, JavaScript (Three.js, D3.js, and Leaflet) for visualization, and HTML/CSS for the user interface, Unidos emphasizes both scientific accuracy and accessibility.

Our goal is to make complex planetary defense data understandable for scientists, policymakers, educators, and the public. By turning real datasets into interactive, visually engaging simulations, Unidos raises awareness about asteroid impact preparedness and highlights the importance of early detection and collaborative response strategies in defending our planet.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We used ChatGPT (OpenAI GPT-5) as a creative assistant during the ideation and documentation phases of our project. It helped us refine our technical descriptions, summarize complex concepts about orbital mechanics and impact energy, and generate explanatory text for tooltips and the user interface.

Additionally, we used Microsoft Copilot to assist with code autocompletion and debugging in our Python (Flask) and JavaScript (Three.js, Leaflet) modules. These AI tools accelerated development but did not generate or modify any NASA data, logos, or visual elements.

All project visuals, datasets, and simulations were created, processed, and verified by our team using official NASA and USGS open datasets.

projectDetails.name: Project Double Error
projectDetails.summary:
We developed an interactive web-based tool that allows users to design and visualize space habitats by selecting shapes, defining volumes, and organizing key functional areas (sleeping, hygiene, food prep, exercise, medical, etc.).

Our solution directly addresses the challenge by making habitat design accessible, fast, and intuitive — eliminating the need for advanced engineering software. The tool incorporates NASA’s habitat guidelines, ensures areas meet crew requirements, and provides immediate feedback when layouts are impractical (e.g., noise next to sleep).

This project is important because it helps students, designers, and professionals explore mission-ready layouts, encourages creative solutions for long-duration space travel, and sparks public engagement with human space exploration. By combining simplicity with science, our tool makes learning and designing space habitats both educational and impactful.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an interactive visual tool for designing space habitats. It enables users to:

  • Choose a habitat shape and dimensions.
  • Divide the interior into functional zones (sleeping, hygiene, medical, food prep, exercise, etc.).
  • Get real-time feedback on whether layouts meet NASA’s guidelines for crew needs, space, and mission duration.

The tool works as a web-based prototype, built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, enhanced using Gemini Studio for rapid prototyping and V0 for AI-powered layout suggestions.

The benefits include:

  • Accessibility: Simple to use compared to complex CAD tools.
  • Educational value: Helps students and non-experts understand habitat design constraints.
  • Practicality: Provides quick iteration for engineers and mission planners.

We hope to inspire innovative habitat designs for lunar and Martian missions while making space engineering fun and approachable.
