projectDetails.name: ProbCast
projectDetails.summary:
ProbCast is a web and mobile-friendly application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Will It Rain on My Parade?”. The project transforms complex NASA Earth observation data into simple, actionable insights about short-term weather events such as rainfall and heat waves.

Using data from NASA sources including OPeNDAP (MERRA-2), Giovanni, Data Rods, Worldview, Earthdata Search, POWER, and GLDAS, ProbCast provides forecasts that are both accurate and accessible. The system integrates a chatbot that explains forecasts in everyday language, offering tailored advice for general users and farmers. For example, the app can suggest carrying an umbrella, delaying irrigation, or checking severe weather alerts from CPTEC/INPE in Brazil.

Built with Python and Streamlit, the platform features interactive dashboards, maps, data exports, and multilingual readiness. This project is important because it bridges the gap between raw scientific data and practical daily decisions, helping communities adapt to increasingly unpredictable weather.
projectDetails.details:
ProbCast is an AI-powered weather application that helps people understand and prepare for short-term weather changes. The system collects and processes NASA Earth observation data, including precipitation, temperature, humidity, and soil moisture, from sources such as OPeNDAP (MERRA-2), Giovanni, Data Rods, Worldview, POWER, GLDAS, and Earthdata Search. Partner data from CPTEC/INPE provides high-resolution forecasts and alerts for South America.

The application translates this scientific data into clear, practical advice. A built-in chatbot explains forecasts in natural language, offering personalized tips for different users. General users may receive advice like “carry an umbrella,” while farmers get crop-specific suggestions such as delaying irrigation during heavy rainfall. Users can view interactive plots, maps, satellite imagery, and download forecast reports.

ProbCast was developed with Python and Streamlit, using libraries such as pandas, numpy, plotly, folium, earthaccess, and feedparser. It is web/mobile-friendly, supports multilingual expansion, and runs on personal laptops without specialized hardware.

The intended impact is to make NASA’s reliable data accessible to everyday people and farmers, increasing resilience to weather disruptions and supporting better decision-making. Creativity lies in combining real-time scientific datasets with an interactive chatbot and personalized advice, bridging the gap between raw climate data and daily human needs.

All AI-generated content is original and does not include any NASA branding, logos, or mission identifiers. Metadata and documentation clearly indicate where AI tools were used.

projectDetails.name: When the Sun Snaps Its Magnets
projectDetails.summary:
We made a video telling the story of space weather. The video discusses what is space weather, what causes it and how it affects humans on earth and astronauts in space.

This project is of great importance because it can raise the curiosity of the future generation about space weather and inspire them to learn more about it. Which can lead to a big number of thinkers and scientists specializing in space weather in the future.

These expertise in space weather which were ignited through a simple video discussing space weather can lead to huge innovations in the future protecting Earth's atmosphere from the dangers of solar storms or even lead to innovations about how to protect mars' atmosphere from these solar storms and return the planet to its previous state when it had an atmosphere and water was running through it.
projectDetails.details:
The project is a video hosted on YouTube. It discusses what is space weather, its origins, how it affects earth even though we are very far from the sun, various types of space weather such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar winds. The video also discusses the effects of solar weather on earth from beautiful auroras to complete power blackouts. Also, the video discusses how strong solar storms can affect people in planes or astronauts in space through radiation sickness or other forms of illness caused by these charged particles.

The project aims to raise the curiosity of young minds to learn and understand more about space weather, and how we can mitigate the dangerous effects it might have. If the project managed to reach to a big audience of children and young minds, this will lead to a generation who is interested about space weather which in turn might lead to innovative solutions as how to protect various planets' atmosphere from these solar storms, and in some cases we might be able to protect planets like mars and restore their atmosphere which degraded because of the continuous hits of these solar storms evaporating all water on the surface.

We used Canva and Kdenlive as software used to make the video, Audacity was used as the audio recording and editing software. The project doesn't contain any form of coding languages integrated into it right now but this is a future plan to make an interactive 3d game live on the web using the latest web technologies that children throughout the world can access from anywhere and anyplace to learn about space weather.

The project's creativity lies in its future impacts and how it is seen as a motivator and driving factor toward a better future for our solar system. Also the visuals and themes inside the project contain bits of creativity from every member in the team. The main factors the team considered while making the project were how to give appropriate background into what is space weather to let children understand what it is, what are the various forms of space weather and how do they affect us, and how we can raise their curiosities to further research space weather and be interested to learn it in the future.

Canva AI was used for some scenes and pictures in the video and there is an "AI Generated" watermark at the bottom of each of these scenes.

Audio, video making, video effects and everything else in the project is made by the team without the use of AI.

projectDetails.name: NASA Nova Farm
projectDetails.summary: Agriculture is the heart of the nutrition industry and provides raw materials for manufacturing. This vital sector of the economy must know how to improve both the quality and quantity of crops. The challenge is that many farmers around the world, especially in developing regions, lack education and access to modern knowledge. They need simple guidance to grow better crops. According to FAO, the global population will reach 9.1 billion by 2050, requiring food production to increase by 70% compared to today. Our project, NASA Nova Farm, addresses this need. It is an educational game with a friendly interface that integrates NASA datasets to guide farming decisions. Players experiment with choices through “Angel” and “Demon” advisors, showing sustainable versus harmful practices. The game teaches how to produce healthier, higher-yield crops using real data. Ultimately, players gain knowledge they can apply to farming at larger scales.
projectDetails.details:
Our game features a simple and interactive UI that hides complex agronomic calculations under a pixel-art world. The workflow begins with preparing characters and tile sets in Aseprite and building scenes and dialogues in the Godot engine. What makes the project unique is that each gameplay event is driven by mathematical models of crop growth. The soil moisture balance is computed each turn:

where Rainfall comes from GPM/IMERG data, Irrigation is the player’s choice, Evapotranspiration is calculated from NASA POWER climate data (using reference evapotranspiration multiplied by crop coefficient), and Drainage represents water loss beyond the root zone. If soil moisture drops below 20%, the game triggers stress, which is reflected in falling vegetation indices.

The health of the crop is visualised through NDVI, calculated as:

which is displayed in-game via satellite-like imagery. Every few turns, the player sees NDVI maps update, with Angel advising irrigation to restore canopy vigour while Demon suggests saving cost and risking further decline.

At harvest, yield is not arbitrary but computed from the FAO yield response equation:

where Actual Yield is the result of the player’s management, Maximum Yield is the potential under ideal conditions, Yield Response Factor is a crop-specific constant (≈1.1 for potato, 1.0 for carrot), and Actual Evapotranspiration versus Maximum Evapotranspiration captures how well water demand was met. Player choices across the season directly change Actual Evapotranspiration, thus determining final yield.

By embedding these equations into dialogues and pixel-art storytelling, our workflow bridges visual design with data-driven agronomic simulation, producing a game that is both engaging and scientifically rigorous. The logic and data processing were implemented in Python and T-Script within Godot, bridging the visuals with agronomic calculations.

projectDetails.name: Stellar Stories
projectDetails.summary:
In this challenge, we faced a specific problem:

How do we make the complex phenomenon of space weather understandable and engaging for Generation Alpha?

➡️After our deep reading of the challenge brief, what caught our attention between the lines was this: 
The true objective wasn't just storytelling, but rather bridging a massive awareness gap between NASA's scientists and this future generation. From that insight, we launched a vision that goes beyond simple information gathering: our goal is to adapt and reach, not just to present.

➡️We made a strategic decision:
To reach Gen Alpha through their most consumed platform(TikTok)

➡️This development relies on two key components:

⚫️Utilizing Storytelling in short TikTok clips as a magnet to capture the attention of this quickly bored age group.

⚫️Directing them to our trusted source: The website, which we see as a simplified, interactive curriculum for the young generation.

➡️By doing this, we ensure we are building a generation fully aware of the problems caused by space weather. This is where the importance of our project and its eligibility for support and implementation lie:
We have actively worked to bridge a major gap in space science and have provided an effective link connecting scientists with younger generations.

⭕️Note on the Prototype:
This is a functional prototype built under time limits. The core idea and scalability are clear, and we will fully develop it after the hackathon.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details:

➡️what exactly dose it do:
1. We transform complex scientific data into exciting, personalized stories told from the perspective of the space phenomena themselves, breaking down the barrier of boredom for Generation Alpha.


2. We connect NASA's scientists with this generation, using TikTok as a gateway for attention and the website as a hub for establishing trustworthy knowledge.


3. We measure via short quizzes to ensure the storytelling approach was effective in building an aware generation regarding the risks of space weather.

➡️How dose it Work:

We now move to the beating heart of our solution:
the Educational Website.
We designed it to be a complete narrative journey, told entirely from the perspective of the space phenomena themselves, which fulfills the requirement for innovative storytelling.

We didn't just compile facts; we organized the content as a series of flowing chapters that tell a cohesive story about our relationship with the Sun.

This is the structure of our Interactive Curriculum:
The Story Chapters

1️⃣ My Identity and Impulse.
The phenomenon introduces itself to the child, explaining its origin in the Sun, opening their mind to the idea that weather isn't confined to Earth.

2️⃣&3️⃣ My Nature and My Power.
Here, we personify Solar Flares and Solar Wind.
The phenomenon narrates its own strength and the reasons for its outbursts, relying on simplified scientific details taken directly from NASA data, but formatted as a story or personal journal entries.
This makes the complex concepts easy for the younger generation to grasp.

4️⃣My Unintended Impact.
In this part, the phenomenon recounts how its power can unintentionally cause harm on Earth, such as disrupting GPS signals or affecting power grids.
This crucial link makes the story relatable, ensuring the child feels the subject is relevant to their daily life.

5️⃣My Dazzling Apology.
We conclude the journey with a positive and enchanting note. The phenomenon explains how it apologizes in its own way through the Aurora Borealis (Northern Lights), leaving the child with a positive and magical impression of nature's beauty, even amidst its overwhelming power.

⭕️Measuring Impact and Learning:
After completing the narrative journey, the child moves directly to a short quiz. This test is not for grading or pressure; rather, it's to measure our success in effectively delivering the information and confirming that the story achieved its goal of building simple, smooth awareness

➡️ In this way, the website transforms into an integrated curriculum that feeds the child's mind with information through excitement and interaction, and then measures retention in a fun, pressure-free manner

⚫️Benefits and Value:
The Greater Impact of Our Project
​Our project isn't just about education; it's about investing in future awareness. We designed it to achieve three types of strategic benefits that extend far beyond the scope of this hackathon:

➡️1.Building a Risk-Aware Generation
(Benefit for the Child)

Our primary guaranteed benefit is transforming a vague risk into an understandable and relevant piece of information.

projectDetails.name: Nebulogy
projectDetails.summary:
Nebulogy is an AI-powered, interactive dashboard that makes NASA’s bioscience publications accessible, searchable, and role-specific for mission architects. Users can submit queries to receive flashcards containing AI-generated summaries, explore synthesized insights, and navigate a dashboard with knowledge graphs, analytical charts, and audio summaries. A RAG-powered chatbot allows users to ask questions naturally and receive context-aware, role-adapted responses.

By integrating semantic search, AI-driven summarization, knowledge graphs, interactive visualizations, and audio, the platform transforms hundreds of complex publications into actionable insights. Contextual hints, experiment spotlights, and “Did You Know?” tips provide additional guidance and engagement, making exploration both informative and user-friendly.

Neural Explorers addresses the challenge by enabling mission architects to efficiently analyze research, identify knowledge gaps, and plan safer, evidence-based space biology missions. Its combination of AI, visualizations, and interactive features bridges the gap between raw data and actionable knowledge, saving time and empowering informed decision-making in space research.
projectDetails.details:
Overview & Functionality:
Nebulogy is an AI-powered, interactive platform that makes NASA’s bioscience publications accessible, searchable, and role-specific. Users enter a query, and the system returns flashcards with concise, AI-generated summaries of relevant publications. The Insights tab synthesizes key findings, conflicts, knowledge gaps, and potential future research. The dashboard provides multiple visualizations, including a knowledge graph connecting topics and papers, analytical charts showing publication trends by year, journal, and topic, and an audio feature that reads summaries aloud for multimodal exploration. A RAG-powered chatbot lets users ask natural questions and receive answers tailored to their role as scientist, manager, or mission architect.

Flow of the Project:

  1. Search: User submits a query, then similarity search is performed and top relevant researches are displayed in the form of flashcards, with three different role-based summaries.
  2. Insights: Areas where science conflicts are present. It is supported by AI-powered proposals for future missions and researches, providing all required metrics for the three different roles.
  3. Dashboard: Insightful charts displaying important metrics and progress collected from across the 608 researches. Also, supported by a knowledge graph reflecting connections between researches.
  4. Chatbot: When user needs to ask, our Conversational AI delivers role-adapted explanations and insights to suffice all user inquiries.

Benefits & Impact:

  • Condenses hundreds of publications into actionable insights for scientists, managers, and mission architects.
  • Supports mission planning, research progress, and potential investments for space biology missions.
  • Makes NASA’s bioscience knowledge searchable, interactive, insightful, and AI-powered to cope with today's rapid revolution of AI.

Development Tools & Technology Stack:

  • Frontend: React for UI, dashboards, flashcards, and audio integration.
  • Backend & AI: LangGraph orchestrates AI pipelines; LLMs (GroqAPI/Gemini) generate summaries and role-specific responses, FastAPI for routers.
  • Databases: Milvus for vector embeddings; Supabase/Postgres for metadata and summaries.
  • Data Sources: NASA CSV of 608 bioscience publications, OSDR, NSLSL, Task Book.
  • Libraries: Python libraries for text parsing, preprocessing, and embedding generation such as sentence transformers.
  • Deployment: With the backend being hosted on hugging face while the frontend being hosted on vercel.

Creativity & Innovation:

  • Combines AI-generated summaries, semantic search, knowledge graphs, and interactive visualizations into a single platform.
  • Role-specific insights make it unique compared to traditional repositories.
  • Combines multiple visualization types (knowledge graphs + analytical charts) for an intuitive overview of complex data.
  • Contextual hints, experiment spotlights, and “Did You Know?” tips enrich the dashboard and make learning engaging.
  • Integrates audio that guides and navigates the user through the dashboard explaining the charts and the knowledge graph for engaging user experience.

Factors Considered by the Team:

  • User roles and their specific information needs (mission architect).
  • Accessibility and intuitive design for easy navigation and comprehension.
  • Scalability of AI pipelines and vector database for efficient semantic search.
  • Accuracy of data parsing, embedding generation, and summarization.
  • Seamless integration between frontend, backend, and AI modules.

projectDetails.name: Project NextDay Safe
projectDetails.summary:
Have you ever thought about planning your dream vacation, organizing a big family event, or just enjoying a peaceful day outdoors? Timing is everything. But there’s always that question: will it rain on my special day?

Traditional weather apps give you a short-term view—maybe a day, two, or at most a week ahead. But what if you’re planning something months in advance, or even a year from now? There’s no solution that tells you the likelihood of extreme heat, heavy rainfall, or strong winds on that specific day.

Here at the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we decided to change the game.

Introducing “Will It Rain on My Parade?”, a solution that combines modern technology with NASA’s treasure trove of historical climate data. We no longer rely on predictions—we rely on probabilities.

Imagine this… you’ve been planning your summer trip for months. Tickets are booked, bags packed, and excitement is at its peak. Then the big day arrives… and suddenly heavy rain or a heatwave ruins the outing. All your plans fall apart. We’ve all been there. The reason? Traditional weather apps only forecast for a week or two at most—no one tells you what might happen months ahead.

What if you’re organizing an outdoor event? A farmer preparing for the season? Or a traveler choosing the best time to visit a new country? This is where our solution comes in.
projectDetails.details:
Our proposed solution, “Will It Rain on My Parade?”, directly tackles the challenge by combining NASA’s long-term Earth observation data with an intuitive and personalized web application. The system empowers users to anticipate the likelihood of extreme or uncomfortable weather conditions and make smarter decisions when planning outdoor or indoor activities.

How the Solution Tackles the Challenge:

•By leveraging NASA’s historical datasets (temperature, rainfall, windspeed, humidity, etc.), our system calculates the probability of “very hot,” “very cold,” “very wet,” or “very windy” conditions at a specific location and time.

•The app provides clear visualizations (maps, charts, and probability indicators) to help users interpret climate data easily.

•It extends beyond simple forecasts by offering personalized recommendations for optimal activity times and suitable indoor/outdoor destinations.

•The system sends alerts/notifications for frequently searched places when conditions are favorable, making it proactive and user-friendly.

Steps to Implement the Solution Successfully:

1.Collect and preprocess NASA climate datasets.

2.Build APIs with Laravel (PHP) and store processed data in MySQL.

3.Implement a frontend dashboard in React, integrating Leaflet.js for interactive maps and Chart.js for visual analytics.

4.Apply data analysis/statistical methods (to be defined by the data analyst) to compute probability thresholds.

5.Design and refine the user experience in Figma, ensuring usability and accessibility.

6.Develop recommendation features for indoor/outdoor activities based on weather suitability.

7.Add export functionality (CSV/PDF) and notification services for user convenience.

8.Test iteratively under an Agile workflow, improving functionality through team feedback.

Alignment with the Challenge’s Requirements:

Our solution aligns perfectly with NASA’s challenge by:

•Using trusted Earth observation data to calculate long-term weather likelihoods.

•Enabling users to explore conditions for specific places and times via a personalized dashboard.

•Offering visual, downloadable, and user-centered outputs that go beyond standard weather forecasts.

•Providing both scientific accuracy and practical usability, ensuring users can plan better, safer, and more enjoyable experiences.

projectDetails.name: Are We Ready
projectDetails.summary:
We developed Nile Stars: Are We Ready?, an interactive simulator that brings asteroid science and planetary defense to everyone. Using real NASA datasets combined with USGS earthquake and tsunami data, the platform transforms complex research into engaging, visual, and hands-on experiences.

The challenge is that while near-Earth asteroids pose real risks, public awareness is low and most scientific information stays locked within research communities. Our solution addresses this gap by presenting accurate simulations, 3D visualizations, and simplified tools designed for students, teachers, researchers, and the general public. Users can run impact scenarios, explore real data, and understand both the threats and possible defenses in a way that is fun and accessible.

This project is important because awareness is the first step toward preparedness. By making planetary defense understandable, Nile Stars helps people see the reality of asteroid risks and empowers communities to think about how to protect our planet.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Nile Stars: Are We Ready?, is an interactive simulator that demonstrates the real risks of near-Earth asteroids. It works by combining real NASA API data with immersive 3D simulations built using React Three Fiber (R3F). Users can adjust asteroid size, speed, or trajectory and instantly see the resulting impact on Earth—whether ground shaking, tsunami generation, or atmospheric effects.

The benefits are twofold:

Education: students and teachers gain an engaging way to learn complex science through visual and interactive lessons.

Research & Awareness: researchers and the public can explore real scenarios with accurate data, fostering better understanding and preparedness.

The intended impact is to raise global awareness of asteroid hazards and to make planetary defense knowledge accessible beyond scientists.

Technically, we used FastAPI (Python) for backend services, NASA NEO API for asteroid data, and deployed via Railway. The front end is powered by React + R3F and hosted on Vercel.

The project is creative because it merges real science with interactive design, blending accurate datasets, storytelling, and gamified exploration. Our team considered accessibility, accuracy, and user engagement to ensure the tool is both reliable and inspiring.

projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

ClimaQuest is a mobile application that translates complex NASA climate and weather data into clear, actionable insights for both daily life and long-term planning. The app provides daily weather guidance by showing localized forecasts with easy-to-understand recommendations for clothing, activities, and safety. It supports travel planning by offering seasonal tips, climate trend insights, and personalized weather tracking to help users plan trips and outdoor activities effectively. Its smart navigation and safety features suggest optimal travel routes and alternative timings to avoid extreme weather conditions. ClimaQuest also emphasizes gamified learning, including fun weather games, quizzes, and challenges that build climate literacy while allowing users to track their progress and earn achievements. Additionally, users can search for weather forecasts anywhere in the world at any time of the year. Overall, the app bridges the gap between raw scientific data and practical, human-friendly decisions, helping users stay informed, safe, and well-prepared.

How Does It Work?

ClimaQuest is structured around several key pages, each designed to make weather information actionable and easy to understand:

Home Page: Displays the current weather forecast along with simple, human-friendly recommendations for clothing, activities, and safety.

Quick Insights Page: Provides an easy overview of weather conditions to help users quickly understand what to expect for the day.

Details Page: Offers an extended forecast with interactive bars for:

  • What Should I Wear?
  • Plan My Day
  • Stay Safe & Healthy
  • Plan Ahead

It also includes Smart Navigation & Safety, allowing users to select a destination and receive the best routes based on weather forecasts and alternative timing.

Search Page: Enables users to look up weather forecasts for any country and any time of the year.

Gamified Learning Page: Provides interactive weather games, quizzes, and challenges to help users build climate literacy while tracking progress and achievements.

This page structure ensures that users can access relevant weather information efficiently, make informed decisions, and engage with climate data in an interactive and educational way.

Value Proposition

ClimaQuest empowers users to make informed, safe, and practical decisions based on weather conditions. It provides personalized recommendations for daily life, travel, and outdoor activities, helping users plan clothing, routes, and schedules. The app also promotes climate literacy through gamified learning, enabling users to understand weather patterns, extreme events, and long-term climate trends in an engaging way. Overall, it bridges the gap between raw scientific data and human-friendly guidance, improving safety, preparedness, and decision-making.

What do you hope to achieve?

The project aims to make complex climate and weather data accessible and actionable for everyone. We hope to help users confidently plan their daily routines and travels, avoid dangerous weather conditions, and develop a deeper understanding of climate patterns. Additionally, through interactive games and quizzes, the project seeks to increase awareness of climate science and promote educational engagement with environmental data.

  • Flutter & Dart: For cross-platform mobile app development.
  • NASA Earth Observation APIs: To access and integrate historical and real-time climate data.
  • Backend Optimization: To efficiently process large datasets and provide fast, reliable recommendations on mobile devices.

projectDetails.name: NOFA: Rotating Sustainable  Space Habitat
projectDetails.summary: We developed NOFA, a rotating sustainable space habitat designed to ensure long-term human survival beyond Earth. With a 200-meter rotating sphere generating artificial gravity (1g), NOFA addresses the physiological and psychological challenges of space life. The habitat integrates a Solar-Hydrogen hybrid energy system, hydroponic farming for food and oxygen, and AI-based life support management. This solution is important as it provides a scalable model for sustainable, safe, and autonomous human habitation in deep space and planetary missions.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, NOFA, is a rotating sustainable habitat that provides a closed loop environment for long term space missions.

What it does:

Generates artificial gravity (1g) through a 200 meter rotating sphere.

Protects astronauts from cosmic and solar radiation using layered shielding with water and polyethylene.

Produces renewable energy through a solar-hydrogen hybrid system with wireless power transfer.

Supplies fresh food and oxygen using a hydroponic farm integrated inside the structure.

Uses AI management to control climate, optimize resources, and predict system failures.

How it works:

The habitat combines structural design (octagonal core + zero-G hub) with sustainable systems. Solar energy is harvested and stored as hydrogen, food is grown hydroponically, and life support is managed by AI for maximum safety and efficiency.

Benefits:

Preserves astronaut health and well being through gravity, nutrition, and mental balance.

Reduces dependence on Earth resupply, making missions longer and safer.

Scalable for Moon, Mars, or deep-space colonies.

Goals:

We aim to demonstrate a realistic, future ready concept for human habitation beyond Earth that combines sustainability, resilience, and AI driven management.

AI tools for visualization, video demos, and documentation.

AI visualization platforms for design and video creation Research integration from NASA/ESA datasets on radiation, life support, and microgravity.

Conceptual design of solar hydrogen systems and hydroponics.

projectDetails.name: Project Galaxy Zoom
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a web-based platform designed to make NASA’s large-scale planetary image datasets more accessible and interactive. The platform enables users to explore high-resolution historical planetary images over time and compare them side-by-side in a responsive, intuitive interface. By integrating OpenSeadragon and Leaflet, we ensure efficient zooming, panning, and smart tiling for smooth navigation of massive images. Users can select files via drag-and-drop, clipboard paste, or modal selection, and a timeline slider allows dynamic exploration of changes across years.

This solution addresses the challenge of navigating and comparing extensive planetary datasets, which are often too large and complex for traditional tools. By providing an efficient and scalable architecture built with Laravel, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS, our platform empowers researchers, educators, and enthusiasts to visually analyze planetary changes over time. The ability to compare datasets side-by-side fosters deeper insights, enhances educational engagement, and supports scientific discovery in an accessible, user-friendly format.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?
Our project, Galaxy Zoom, is a web-based platform that enables users to explore NASA’s historical planetary images over time and compare them interactively. Using OpenSeadragon and Leaflet, the system tiles large high-resolution images for efficient zooming and panning. A dual iframe viewer allows side-by-side comparison, with drag-and-drop, clipboard paste, and modal selection. A timeline slider dynamically updates the viewer, helping users analyze changes across different years.

What benefits does it have?
The platform makes massive NASA image datasets easily accessible and visually comparable. It supports efficient exploration of large-scale imagery, reduces technical barriers, and provides researchers, educators, and enthusiasts with a simple way to track planetary changes over time.

What is the intended impact of the project?
Our goal is to democratize access to NASA’s datasets, fostering scientific discovery, education, and public engagement. By providing intuitive comparison tools, we aim to support deeper analysis of planetary changes and make space science more approachable.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Backend: Laravel (PHP)
  • Frontend: JavaScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Visualization: OpenSeadragon, Leaflet JS
  • UI/UX Features: Drag & Drop, Clipboard Paste, Modal UI
  • Data Source: NASA’s planetary image datasets (via Worldview)

How is your project creative?
The creativity lies in combining web-based smart tiling, an interactive timeline slider, and a dual comparison interface into one seamless platform. The design is scalable, user-friendly, and extensible for future AI integration to automatically detect changes.

What factors did your team consider?
We focused on accessibility, performance, and scalability. Key considerations included handling massive image files efficiently, creating an intuitive UI for diverse users, and designing an architecture flexible enough to integrate AI-based image comparison in the future.

projectDetails.name: Numina's Exoplanet Classification and Exploration
projectDetails.summary:
Our project delivers an AI-powered classification system for exoplanet discovery, trained on NASA’s Kepler dataset. On the Classification Page, users can input new data, and the system applies our best-performing model (XGBoost) with an accuracy level of 95.19% for the multiclass classification to determine whether the object is a confirmed exoplanet, candidate, or false positive. This makes cutting-edge machine learning accessible for real-time scientific use. 
Beyond classification, the platform includes a 3D simulation tool that compares exoplanetary systems to our solar system in addition to a special feature allows users to see how a satellite observes a transit, the most successful technique for exoplanet discovery, This combination bridges rigorous science with interactive learning.
For deeper exploration, the Research Page features six individual machine learning algorithms — Random Forest, Stacking, Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Trees, and AdaBoost. Here, users can see how each algorithm works independently, compare their results, and even experiment with hyperparameter tuning to understand how models improve. 
This solution addresses the challenge by making exoplanet classification both rigorous and accessible: researchers gain open tools for experimentation, while students and enthusiasts can interactively explore how discoveries are made.
projectDetails.details:
This project implements a comprehensive machine learning pipeline for exoplanet classification using NASA's Kepler Space Telescope data. The system automatically categorizes Kepler Objects of Interest (KOIs) into three classes: CONFIRMED planets, FALSE POSITIVES, and CANDIDATE exoplanets. By analyzing orbital mechanics, stellar properties, transit characteristics, and signal quality metrics, the model can distinguish genuine exoplanets from astronomical false alarms with high accuracy.

What it does
The platform enables users to upload or manually input exoplanet-related data (from NASA’s Kepler dataset or new entries) and classifies the object as a confirmed planet, candidate, or false positive. The Classification Page uses our best-performing model to provide reliable predictions, while the Research Page introduces six machine learning models — Random Forest, Stacking, Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Trees, and AdaBoost — to demonstrate how different algorithms work individually. Users can also perform hyperparameter tuning to experiment with model behavior.

In addition to classification, the project includes a 3D simulation tool that visualizes exoplanetary systems compared to our solar system. A special feature illustrates how satellites detect planets using the transit method, the most successful technique for exoplanet discovery, showing how starlight dips occur when a planet crosses its host star.

How does it work?

The pipeline operates through several sophisticated stages:

1.    Data Preprocessing: The system begins by loading cumulative Kepler mission data and systematically removes irrelevant columns including identifiers, zero-variance features, and data leakage risks (like preliminary disposition scores). Missing values in numerical features are imputed using median values to maintain dataset integrity.

2.    Advanced Feature Engineering: The core innovation lies in creating 40+ scientifically-informed features that capture complex astronomical relationships:

o   Orbital mechanics ratios (temperature-period interactions, planet-star radius comparisons)

o   Logarithmic and polynomial transformations of period, depth, and stellar temperature

o   Habitability indicators (habitable zone flags, Earth similarity indices)

o   Signal quality metrics (SNR thresholds, signal strength categories)

o   Transit property calculations (duration-period ratios, depth-duration relationships)

3.    Feature Selection & Optimization: The system employs dual feature selection using F-statistics and mutual information scores, combining them to identify the most predictive features. It then generates polynomial interaction terms from the top 8 features to capture non-linear relationships.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

4.    Ensemble Model Training: Six state-of-the-art machine learning models are trained and compared:

o   Random Forest with hyperparameter tuning

o   XGBoost with gradient boosting optimization

o   LightGBM for efficient tree-based learning

o   CatBoost with automatic categorical handling

o   AdaBoost for adaptive boosting

o   Baseline Random Forest for performance benchmarking

5.    Evaluation & Visualization: Comprehensive performance metrics are generated including accuracy scores, confusion matrices, classification reports, and improvement percentages over baseline. The system produces six detailed visualizations comparing model performance, feature importance, and prediction quality.

What benefits does it have?

  • High Accuracy: Achieves classification accuracy exceeding 90% through ensemble methods and sophisticated feature engineering
  • Automated Discovery: Accelerates exoplanet validation by automatically flagging high-confidence candidates for follow-up observation
  • Resource Optimization: Helps astronomers prioritize telescope time on the most promising candidates
  • Scientific Insight: Feature importance analysis reveals which astronomical properties are most indicative of genuine exoplanets
  • Scalability: Can process thousands of KOIs efficiently using parallel processing and optimized algorithms
  • Reproducibility: Standardized pipeline ensures consistent results across different datasets

3D Simulation and Comparison between earth- sun system and exoplanet - star system (radius of exoplanet and star, distance from the star, transit period, orbital period, and temperature which are all features changes the exoplanet system):

3D simulation of the transit method (strongest identification method that discovered the majority of exoplanets):

What do you hope to achieve?

The primary goals of this project are:

1.    Maximize Detection Accuracy: Reduce false positive rates in exoplanet identification, ensuring that confirmed planets are genuine discoveries

2.    Accelerate Scientific Discovery: Enable faster validation of exoplanet candidates, potentially discovering Earth-like worlds in habitable zones

3.    Demonstrate ML in Astronomy: Showcase how advanced machine learning techniques can solve complex astrophysical classification problems

4.    Support Future Missions: Create a reusable framework applicable to upcoming space telescope missions (TESS, JWST, PLATO)

5.    Educational Impact: Provide a clear example of data science applied to space exploration for students and researchers

Tools and Technologies

Ø Python (primary language)

Ø Libraries: Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Seaborn, Matplotlib

Ø Web Interface: Streamlit, Three.js/Plotly for 3D visualization

Ø Development: Jupyter, Google Colab, and Kaggle Notebooks, GitHub for version control

Ø Hardware: Standard laptops + cloud resources for model training

Data Source:

  • NASA Exoplanet Archive – Cumulative Kepler KOI dataset (cumulative_2025.10.02)

Key Techniques Employed:

  • Stratified train-test splitting for balanced evaluation
  • RandomizedSearchCV for hyperparameter optimization
  • StandardScaler for feature normalization
  • PolynomialFeatures for interaction term generation
  • Cross-validation (5-fold) for robust model selection

projectDetails.name: Oblivara
projectDetails.summary:
What We Developed
Oblivara is an interactive, real-time 3D asteroid impact simulation and alert platform. It brings together multiple global data sources to visualize asteroid threats and simulate their real-world impacts at both global and city levels.
The platform models a full chain of consequences including crater formation, shockwaves, seismic activity, tsunamis, population displacement, and economic damage. Using advanced data integration and visualization technologies such as Three.js, Mapbox 3d Maps, presenting complex scientific data as clear, interactive stories that anyone can understand.
How It Addresses the Challenge
Oblivara closes the communication gap between scientific research and public awareness. It transforms technical orbital and geological data into intuitive visualizations and localized alerts.
Users can:
- Explore simulations by adjusting asteroid size, speed, angle, and material type.
- Understand consequences through side-by-side “what-if” scenarios and defense simulations (like NASA’s DART mission).
- Receive real-time, multilingual, and localized alerts—with voice support—to ensure public accessibility and safety guidance in over 50 languages.
Why It’s Important
When a rock from space can change life on Earth in seconds, awareness becomes our first line of defense. Oblivara turns distant data into real understanding—showing where an asteroid might strike, who could be affected, and how we can respond before it’s too late.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an interactive planetary‑defense platform that blends NASA real‑time asteroid data, physics‑based simulations, and machine learning to assess and visualize the potential impact of near‑Earth objects.

It pulls live asteroid approach data from NASA’s NEO API, calculates each object's impact energy (TNT equivalent), blast radius, and earthquake‑scale equivalence, then integrates USGS earthquake and population datasets to estimate human and economic consequences worldwide.

Built with Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit‑learn, XGBoost, FastAPI), PostgreSQL + PostGIS (Supabase), and an interactive React/Streamlit front‑end, the system delivers a real‑time, visually engaging risk‑assessment dashboard.

Our goal is simple: transform NASA’s scientific data into an accessible tool that helps scientists, educators, and the public understand, predict, and prepare for asteroid‑impact risks — turning complex space data into actionable planetary insights.

projectDetails.name: Project Olive BranchesHIML (Holistic Integrated Martian Living)
projectDetails.summary:
Introduction
Future missions to Mars face two major challenges: the massive accumulation of waste and the psychological strain of isolation. Traditional waste management is insufficient in such resource-limited environments.
What Did We Develop?
We created HIML, a holistic system that integrates two complementary approaches:
Circular Recycling Engineering – a tiered framework that repurposes waste at different levels of effort:
Immediate Reuse: Converting packaging or habitat parts into furniture.
Medium Recycling: Mixing plastics and foams with Martian regolith to form insulating bricks.High Transformation: Processing waste into 3D-printable filaments for tools, spare parts, or recreational items.Psychological Resilience Engineering – embedding recycling into social and cultural life. Activities such as creating decorations, building a communal coffee corner, or crafting games provide purpose, creativity, and team bonding, essential for mental health.
Why Is It Important?
HIML transforms waste from a liability into a valuable resource, reducing dependence on Earth and enabling sustainable, long-term missions. At the same time, it strengthens crew morale and cohesion, ensuring resilience in isolated conditions.
projectDetails.details:
in an isolated environment like Mars, where resupply from Earth is rare and prohibitively costly, inorganic waste is transformed from a logistical burden into a critical opportunity. Our project, HIML, provides a practical and sustainable solution by converting daily crew waste into vital resources, thereby closing the loop of a circular economy on the Red Planet.

What does it do?

The system processes mixed crew waste—including plastics, EVA suit textiles, packaging, and metal residues—and converts it into essential outputs. These include 3D-printing filament for on-demand manufacturing, building panels for habitat expansion, tools, and activated carbon for water and air purification.

How does it work?

The process is a seamless, automated pipeline:

1. AI-Powered Sorting & Identification: A deep learning model, trained for computer vision, automatically identifies and classifies material types via an integrated camera system. Robotic arms then direct each item to its corresponding processing module with high precision.

2. Advanced Separation:The system employs a multi-stage separation process, including magnetic separators for ferrous metals, eddy current separators for aluminum and non-ferrous metals, and air/density separators for plastics and fabrics.

3. Treatment & Processing:Materials are shredded and compacted. Notably, surplus carbon, a byproduct of oxygen extraction experiments, is thermally converted into highly porous activated carbon.

4. Conversion & Manufacturing: Plastics and foams are remanufactured into filaments for the integrated 3D printer, producing tools, spare parts, or composite building bricks mixed with Martian regolith.

5. Supporting Systems: The entire operation is powered by solar panels with battery storage, and waste heat is recovered to improve energy efficiency in the treatment stages.

Key Benefits:

Waste Elimination:Dramatically reduces waste volume and associated environmental risks.

Resource Independence:Provides a continuous, on-site supply of tools, building materials, and clean water.

Mission Sustainability:Significantly increases mission sustainability and reduces the mass and cost of Earth resupply missions.

Tools & Development:

The system was prototyped and simulated using a robust software stack: Python with TensorFlow for the AI classification model, Streamlit** for the interactive dashboard, and NumPy/Pandas for process simulation. A 3D interactive model demonstrating the material flow was created using HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

Ultimate Goal:

To establish a circular, self-sufficient waste management infrastructure that enables Mars and future planetary missions to achieve long-term sustainability and operational independence, with AI-driven intelligence at the very core of its sorting and recycling operations.

projectDetails.name: Orbit5 ExoML
projectDetails.summary:
We developed ExoML, an AI-powered platform designed to automate the detection and classification of exoplanets using NASA’s open datasets from the Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. 

Traditionally, exoplanet identification relied on manual vetting of light curves — a
slow and resource-intensive process.
ExoML tackles this challenge by combining machine learning and deep learning models in a unified, interactive web interface, which also provides interactive dashboard which includes insights and data analysis for the uploaded dataset. Researchers can select datasets, train or load models, and predict whether new data represents an exoplanet or not.

This platform saves time, reduces costly telescope follow-ups, and supports NASA’s mission to accelerate scientific discovery beyond our solar system — making advanced exoplanet analysis more accessible to scientists, students, and the research community.
projectDetails.details:
ExoML enables users to upload datasets, select or train ML models, and receive predictions

on exoplanet classification. It integrates a hybrid Ensemble Stack combining Gradient

Boosted Trees and 1D CNNs. The platform provides a Dashboard & Insights section to

visualize performance and understand how model features influence predictions. An

Economic Savings Calculator estimates telescope time and cost saved through automation.

How It Works:

1. Data Preprocessing – Cleans, normalizes, and prepares NASA datasets.

2. Feature Engineering – Extracts astrophysical features such as transit depth, duration, and

periodicity.

3. Model Training – Combines LightGBM/XGBoost with CNNs trained on phase-folded light-

curve signals.

4. Prediction Interface – Flask backend serves models to a React/Streamlit frontend.

5. Visualization & Reporting – Generates accuracy metrics, confusion matrices, and feature

insights.

Benefits:

• Reduces manual vetting time from hours to seconds.

• Increases classification accuracy and model flexibility.

• Helps scientists prioritize follow-up targets efficiently.

• Offers an educational interface for astronomy students.

Tools and Technologies:

Languages: Python, JavaScript

Frameworks: Flask, Streamlit, React.js, TailwindCSS

Libraries: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, Pandas, Plotly

Development: Jupyter Notebook, VS Code, GitHub

Storage: SQLite/JSON

Visualization: Plotly, Matplotlib, D3.js

projectDetails.name: Guardians of Weather: Accessible Safety, Earth Data Translated into Narrative Warnings.
projectDetails.summary:
We developed Guardians of Weather, an accessible, a web application that transforms weather forecasting into a story-driven risk assessment. It utilizes NASA Earth Observation (EO) data and AI prediction (VAE) to generate hyper-local, long-range forecasts for planned outdoor activities.

The solution addresses the challenge by integrating a Threshold Logic that maps predicted conditions (temperature, wind, humidity, precipitation) directly against known clinical risk factors for users with cardiac or respiratory conditions. Instead of raw numbers, users receive counsel from the personified Guardians and a final, unambiguous verdict from Terra.

This project is vital because it shifts the paradigm from complex data consumption to actionable safety. The narrative and personified weather conditions  friendly design makes the forecast fully accessible to the visually impaired, while the personalized risk score empowers vulnerable populations to plan outdoor activities independently and safely.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an AI-powered weather forecasting assistant designed to make complex climate predictions more accessible, engaging, and useful for everyday decision-making.

At its core, the system uses a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) enhanced with LSTM layers and attention mechanisms to predict future weather trends such as temperature, wind speed, and humidity. Historical weather data is preprocessed and normalized before being passed into the model, and outputs are rescaled for real-world interpretation.

What makes this project unique is how forecasts are delivered. Instead of presenting raw numbers, the system introduces “Guardians” — characters that represent different weather aspects:

  • Blaze --> temperature
  • Gale --> wind
  • Drizzle --> humidity / rain likelihood
  • Haze --> visibility and fog

These guardians provide friendly, story-like explanations of the forecast, alongside clear recommendations (e.g., “Carry an umbrella,” “Stay hydrated,” or “Wear warm clothes”). This makes weather information easier to understand and more engaging, especially for non-technical audiences.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Python for model development and backend.
  • TensorFlow/Keras for deep learning (VAE with LSTM + Attention).
  • FastAPI for serving predictions through a REST API.
  • NumPy, Pandas, Joblib for data handling and scaling.
  • Scikit-learn for preprocessing (scaler).

projectDetails.name: Project OxyGenZ
projectDetails.summary:
We developed PureAir, an integrated mobile application and AI-powered chatbot designed to address the global challenge of air pollution and its health impacts. The solution combines real-time air quality monitoring with personalized health recommendations, offering both a user-friendly mobile experience and a modular backend system.

The mobile application, built with Flutter and MVVM architecture, provides features such as onboarding with location setup, personalized health profiles, live AQI dashboards, and community-driven health insights. It connects seamlessly with external APIs (OpenAQ, weather services, and health guidelines) to deliver accurate and contextual data.

The AI-powered RAG chatbot enhances the experience by enabling users to ask natural language questions about air quality and receive tailored guidance based on WHO/EPA standards and individual health conditions. This makes the system accessible, interactive, and supportive of vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly, and people with chronic diseases.

By merging cutting-edge AI, IoT-ready infrastructure, and intuitive design, PureAir empowers communities to make informed decisions, raise environmental awareness, and protect public health. This end-to-end solution directly contributes to the goals of the NASA Space Apps 2025 Air Quality Challenge by turning complex data into actionable insights.

projectDetails.name: Project PAB ( Pioneers of Astrobiology )
projectDetails.summary: NASA has conducted numerous biological experiments in space, generating vast scientific data essential for lunar and Mars missions. However, this knowledge is scattered, highly technical, and difficult to navigate. We built the Space Biology Knowledge Engine — a web-based platform that empowers researchers to discover, analyze, and interpret space biology publications efficiently. The system organizes experiments into six thematic categories, summarizes each paper, and integrates a Gemini-powered chatbot for interactive exploration.
projectDetails.details:
Our project provides a comprehensive, interactive platform for exploring NASA publications. It collects, organizes, and summarizes scientific research, making it easier for researchers, students, and enthusiasts to access complex information efficiently. Users can search, filter, and interact with publications via a modern web interface, and engage with an AI-powered chatbot for contextual explanations.


1. Data Collection & Analysis

  • Collected and analyzed over 600 publications from NASA’s SB_publications dataset.
  • Web scraping (Python, BeautifulSoup) was used to extract metadata: title, authors, year, DOI, abstract, results, and conclusion.
  • Publications were categorized into six thematic domains for structured browsing.
  • Generated concise summaries of abstracts and results to enhance readability and accessibility.

2. Backend Development

  • Built with Java and Spring Boot, exposing REST APIs for searching, filtering, and chatbot integration.
  • Data stored in a relational MySQL database for efficient querying and retrieval.
  • Ensured scalability and maintainability through clean code, modular MVC architecture, and proper use of environment variables.
  • Tested endpoints using Postman to ensure reliable and smooth data transfer between the server and client.

3. Frontend Development

  • Developed with React, providing a modern, responsive UI.
  • Features include:
    • Search input for finding publications quickly.
    • Dynamic filtering tools by author, year, or category.
    • Rotating category sections for easy navigation.
    • Integrated chatbot panel for each publication.

4. Chatbot Integration

  • Embedded Gemini-powered AI chatbot for interactive support.
  • Enables users to ask questions about each publication, clarify methodology, and understand results.
  • Enhances accessibility and learning by providing contextual explanations.

5. Benefits & Impact

  • Makes NASA research more accessible and interactive.
  • Reduces time for researchers to find relevant studies.
  • Supports educational purposes, helping students understand complex research.
  • Encourages knowledge dissemination and informed decision-making in scientific communities.

6. Creativity & Considerations

  • Combined automated data extraction, summarization, and interactive AI assistance in a single platform.
  • Considered usability, scalability, and responsiveness in design.
  • Ensured accurate representation of data while providing easy-to-understand summaries.

To make complex research papers more accessible, we applied AI-based summarization techniques (using extractive and abstractive models) to the abstract and results sections of over 600 space biology publications.

An AI-powered chatbot (Gemini) was embedded into each paper’s page to provide interactive support. Users can ask questions about methods, results, or implications, and the chatbot retrieves relevant information from the paper to generate clear explanations.

NLP tools were applied to extract structured metadata (e.g., title, authors, keywords, and publication year) during data preprocessing.

projectDetails.name: AstroPass
projectDetails.summary:
We developed AstroPass—a comprehensive web-based educational platform that brings the International Space Station's most profound experiences directly to students and the public. Our solution features two immersive games simulating astronaut work in the cupola (disaster tracking from space) and NBL training (mastering neutral buoyancy), an interactive e-book revealing authentic daily life aboard the ISS, a visual carousel for swipe-based learning, and AI-powered personalized storytelling.
Addressing the Challenge: We don't just explain the cupola and NBL—we simulate their physical conditions while demonstrating real Earth benefits. Each game concludes with educational fact cards connecting space activities to humanitarian impact. The e-book immerses users in actual astronaut experiences, from brushing teeth in zero gravity to conducting life-saving research.
Why It Matters: Built entirely on official NASA resources, our platform ensures every learner—regardless of age, language, or learning style—understands how ISS observations save lives during disasters, how spacewalk training enables crucial maintenance, and how space research creates solutions for Earth's greatest challenges. We transform 25 years of ISS achievement into accessible, inspiring education.
projectDetails.details:
Project Details

Overview: Complete 360-Degree ISS Experience

Our platform delivers a comprehensive educational journey covering every aspect of the ISS challenge from multiple angles. We don't just show one perspective—we immerse users in the complete story through four distinct but interconnected approaches:

Games → Experience the physical reality of working in the cupola and training in the NBL while learning facts about their Earth benefits

E-Book → Live the authentic daily life of astronauts—from brushing teeth in zero gravity to conducting critical research

Carousel → Access the same deep knowledge as the e-book through visual, swipeable slides for those who prefer interactive exploration over traditional reading

Storytelling → Discover personalized scenarios and narratives connecting ISS activities to real human impact on Earth

Every learner finds their path. Every path leads to understanding. No angle is missed.

What It Does & How It Works

The Platform Structure

Users enter through a homepage introducing our mission and team, then explore four main sections that together create complete ISS understanding:

1. Cupola Earth Observation Game

A disaster-tracking simulation placing users at the cupola's seven windows, clicking on hurricanes, wildfires, volcanoes, and floods before they disappear. Three progressive difficulty levels (10→20→30 disasters) mirror the intensity of real Earth observation at 17,900 mph orbital speed. Each level concludes with fact cards explaining how astronaut photography directly supports disaster relief teams on the ground—connecting the game experience to tangible humanitarian impact.

2. NBL Training Simulation

A physics-based game replicating NASA's massive underwater training facility. Users control an astronaut, adjusting buoyancy with weights and floaties, collecting floating EVA equipment while staying in the safety zone. Sixty seconds, three attempts, and realistic physics teach why astronauts train seven hours for every one hour of spacewalking. Post-game screens reveal how this training enables the spacewalks that maintain ISS equipment for Earth-benefiting research.

3. Interactive E-Book with Audio

A comprehensive journey revealing the real human experience of ISS life—not Hollywood drama, but fascinating reality:

How astronauts sleep strapped to walls, eat floating food, brush teeth without sinks, and use specialized toilets

How they communicate with families across 250 miles, coordinate with Mission Control, and collaborate internationally

How they exercise two hours daily to prevent muscle loss and adapt to 16 sunrises per day

How they conduct experiments growing plants in microgravity, studying protein crystals for cancer research, and photographing climate change

How they prepare for spacewalks through intensive training and work in the cupola tracking disasters

Each chapter includes quizzes, audio narration for accessibility, and connections between daily activities and scientific breakthroughs that benefit humanity. From rocket launch to Earth return, users experience the complete mission lifecycle through astronaut eyes.

4. Dynamic Carousel

The exact same content as the e-book, redesigned as swipeable visual slides with stunning imagery and concise text. Perfect for visual learners and those who want knowledge without reading fatigue. Users swipe through the mission—daily life, scientific work, Earth observation, spacewalk training—gaining identical educational depth in an interactive format ideal for touch-screen displays at museums and events.

5. Storytelling Experience

Two complementary narrative approaches revealing ISS impact:

Interactive Quiz Stories: Users select topics they're interested in (disaster monitoring, space experiments, training challenges, daily life) and navigate decision-based scenarios. A student interested in weather might make choices about which hurricane patterns to photograph from the cupola. After each scenario, questions test understanding, ensuring active learning through decision-making.

Narrative Journeys: Compelling stories showing how ISS work creates real Earth benefits—drought-resistant crops from space plant experiments, life-saving water purification from ISS technology, hurricane warnings from astronaut photography, cancer treatments from zero-gravity research. These narratives make the connection between space activities and improved lives on Earth emotionally resonant and memorable.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Educational Coverage: Every learning style receives equal support—hands-on learners engage through games, deep readers explore the e-book, visual thinkers navigate the carousel, and personalized learners follow customized story paths. No one is left behind.

Physical Reality Connection: Games match actual ISS conditions—orbital speeds, viewing angles, buoyancy physics—while fact cards explain why these experiences matter for Earth. Users don't just play; they understand.

Human Authenticity: The e-book reveals unglamorous truths—space toilets, teeth brushing challenges, sleep difficulties—creating genuine understanding of astronaut life beyond stereotypes.

Invisible Learning: The carousel delivers comprehensive knowledge without feeling like education, perfect for learners resistant to traditional formats.

Earth Benefit Clarity: Every component answers "Why does this matter?"—games show disaster monitoring impact, e-books explain research outcomes, stories connect space work to saved lives and improved technology.

Intended Outcomes: Students gain STEM inspiration from real astronaut work. Teachers access comprehensive curriculum tools. The public understands why ISS funding matters. Everyone discovers that space exploration isn't escapism—it's solving Earth's challenges from a unique vantage point.

Technologies & Development

Core Framework: React.js for interactive components and dynamic content

Game Development: HTML5 Canvas for graphics, custom JavaScript physics engines for realistic buoyancy simulation and orbital mechanics

User Interface: Tailwind CSS for responsive design across all devices from phones to large displays

Media Integration: High-resolution NASA imagery throughout all components, video backgrounds for authentic cupola views, audio narration for accessibility

Carousel System: Touch gesture detection and smooth slide animations for intuitive navigation

E-Book Structure: Chapter-based organization with integrated quizzes, progress tracking, and bookmark functionality

Storytelling Logic: Customization based on user age, language, and interests to generate relevant scenarios and select appropriate narrative content

Data Management: In-memory state management for progress tracking and user preferences during session

Creative Innovation

Multi-Format Ecosystem: Most educational tools choose one approach. We built four complementary paths to the same knowledge, recognizing that learners need options, not restrictions.

Physical Condition Matching: Games replicate actual ISS experiences—orbital speed, buoyancy calculations, training ratios—making abstract concepts tangible through interaction.

Hidden Education: The carousel disguises comprehensive learning as visual exploration, bypassing "reading resistance" while delivering full e-book content.

Dual Storytelling: Quiz scenarios engage cognitive learning; narrative stories create emotional connection. Both are necessary—facts build knowledge, stories inspire action.

Strategic Fact Placement: Educational content appears at perfect psychological moments (after completing game challenges) when users are most receptive, transforming entertainment into learning.

The Mundane Matters: We highlight what typical space education ignores—how astronauts brush teeth, why plant experiments help farmers, how hurricane photos save lives. These "missing pieces" transform abstract wonder into meaningful understanding.

Key Considerations

Accessibility: Works on any device, supports multiple languages, provides audio narration, offers various complexity levels for different ages

Engagement: Short 60-second games for quick interactions, achievement systems for motivation, progressive difficulty maintaining challenge

Accuracy: All content based on official NASA documentation ensuring scientific credibility and educational trust

Usability: Intuitive controls requiring no instructions, immediate feedback to user actions, clear progress indication

Flexibility: Event-friendly short sessions for museums, deep-dive chapters for classroom use, multiple entry points for casual exploration

Impact Measurement: Built-in quizzes and completion tracking allowing educators to assess learning outcomes

Why This Works

By covering the ISS experience from every angle—games for physical understanding, e-books for human immersion, carousels for visual learning, stories for personal connection—we ensure complete educational coverage.

Users don't just learn facts about the cupola and NBL. They experience orbital observation pressure, feel buoyancy training precision, discover astronaut daily realities, and understand how every space activity benefits humanity on Earth.

This isn't just a visual tool. It's a complete gateway to understanding why the International Space Station matters—accessible to everyone, regardless of how they learn best.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

We utilized AI tools in three specific areas of our project:

1. Personalized Storytelling Content Generation

AI generates customized narrative scenarios based on user age, language, and interests through an API with our custom-designed detailed prompt. This creates personalized educational stories while maintaining scientific accuracy based on NASA documentation. All generated content is clearly presented as dynamically created experiences.

Human Role: Our team designed the prompt structure, validated accuracy against NASA resources, and ensured educational alignment.

2. E-Book Audio Narration

AI text-to-speech technology converts our e-book content into audio narration for accessibility. Metadata clearly indicates AI-generated audio.

Human Role: All written e-book content, structure, and educational messaging was researched and created entirely by our team using NASA resources.

3. Game UI Layout Assistance

AI provided design suggestions during the UI development phase for game interfaces.

Human Role: Our team made all final design decisions, implemented all code, and developed all game logic, physics engines, and educational content integration.

Summary: AI served as an acceleration tool for personalization, accessibility, and design iteration. The conceptual innovation, educational strategy, multi-format approach, NASA resource integration, and comprehensive platform architecture represent entirely human creativity and problem-solving.

projectDetails.summary:
What it does:
EXOplorer is an AI-driven platform enables both scientists and the broader public to analyze, classify, and interact with NASA's exoplanet data. The system classifies exoplanet candidates into categories which are either Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive and, crucially, provides SHAP-based interpretability, offering transparent explanations for each classification.
EXOplorer extends beyond basic categorization by fostering engagement through its interactive "Hunt Planets" educational game, which leverages authentic NASA discoveries. In this way, the platform bridges the gap between professional researchers and the general public, encouraging collaborative learning.

How it works:
From a technical standpoint, EXOplorer utilizes a Python/Flask backend equipped with a trained machine learning pipeline and SHAP explainer. The frontend, developed using React and Vite, seamlessly connects users to the system. The platform offers end-to-end functionality: prediction, explainability, dataset exploration, model retraining, and gamified education.

Why it matters:
EXOplorer combines scientific understanding, public engagement, and reproducible AI research. It gives scientists explainable ML tools and encourages the public to learn about finding exoplanets. This helps NASA's goal of making space science clear, collaborative, and accessible to everyone.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

EXOplorer represents a significant step forward in the study and public understanding of exoplanets. This AI-driven platform enables both scientists and the broader public to analyze, classify, and interact with NASA's exoplanet data. The system classifies exoplanet candidates into categories which are either Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive and, crucially, provides SHAP-based interpretability, offering transparent explanations for each classification.

EXOplorer extends beyond basic categorization by fostering engagement through its interactive "Hunt Planets" educational game, which leverages authentic NASA discoveries. In this way, the platform bridges the gap between professional researchers and the general public, encouraging collaborative learning.

EXOplorer goes beyond classification by connecting science and curiosity with an interactive "Hunt Planets" game that teaches and entertains users with real NASA discoveries. This makes it a place for experts and the public to learn together.

How does it work?

From a technical standpoint, EXOplorer utilizes a Python/Flask backend equipped with a trained machine learning pipeline and SHAP explainer. The frontend, developed using React and Vite, seamlessly connects users to the system. The platform offers end-to-end functionality: prediction, explainability, dataset exploration, model retraining, and gamified education.

*Benefits*

It turns black-box ML into auditable science, accelerating review and discovery. Scientists iterate quickly via one-click retraining and consistent, mission-agnostic preprocessing. Students and the public engage with authentic data through an approachable game, growing literacy while keeping scientific rigor.

*Intended impact*

Bridge researchers and the public around *explainable* exoplanet discovery; shorten the path from raw catalog data to trusted insights; provide a durable, extensible platform that NASA and partners can adapt to future missions.

*Tools, languages, software/hardware*

Backend/ML: Python, Flask, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, pandas, numpy.

Frontend/UX: React, Vite, Chart.js, Framer Motion.

Data/APIs: NASA KOI/TOI/K2 catalogs; NASA Exoplanet Archive API (metadata enrichment).

Services: Supabase (leaderboard).

Dev assist (non-core): ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini.

Hardware: Standard developer laptops/VMs; no special sensors.

*What makes it creative*

It fuses *explainable AI* with *gameful learning*—the same features driving scientific classification power an interactive quiz fed by real discoveries. The mission-agnostic schema lets one pipeline span Kepler, K2, and TESS without architecture changes, and the retrain-on-the-fly flow brings “living research software” to a public web app.

*Key factors we considered*

* *Scientific validity & transparency:* SHAP for per-prediction reasoning; sanity checks on physical bounds.

* *Reproducibility:* Versioned models/metrics/artifacts; consistent preprocessing.

* *Generalization:* Unified schema across missions; easy dataset expansion.

* *Accessibility & engagement:* Clear UI language, visual explanations, leaderboard motivation.

* *Ethics & openness:* Open data, documented methods, no proprietary training sets.

* *Performance & UX:* Fast API responses, animated but readable charts, resilient error handling.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
During development, we leveraged several AI-assisted tools to enhance productivity, code quality, and creativity throughout the project lifecycle:

ChatGPT (OpenAI): used for debugging backend and frontend logic, and improving technical clarity.

GitHub Copilot: assisted in writing and auto-completing repetitive code sections, optimizing API routes, solving errors, and ensuring clean integration between backend and frontend components.

Gemini (Google): used for brainstorming feature designs and verifying implementation details.

These AI tools supported the development process, but all core logic, model training, scientific analysis, and even documentation were designed, implemented, and validated by the team.

projectDetails.details:

VEGA is our solution to the “Your Home in Space” challenge, which is a visual, interactive web game/tool that makes complex space habitat design accessible and engaging for everyone.

Our tool empowers users to select habitat shapes, define their dimensions, and use an intuitive drag-and-drop interface to place essential modules like crew quarters, labs, and life support systems.

By gamifying sophisticated engineering principles, VEGA bridges the gap between highly technical CAD software and purely educational tools. It provides a fun, hands-on platform for students and enthusiasts to creatively design and validate the next generation of homes in space.

challengeDetails.title: Your Home in Space: The Habitat Layout Creator
challengeDetails.excerpt: Space habitats are “homes in space” that keep crew members healthy and able to execute their mission. Whether located on a planetary surface or in space, habitats must support critical functions such as waste management, thermal control, life support, communications, power, stowage, food storage and preparation, medical care, sleep, and exercise. Space habitat concepts can involve a diverse array of materials, geometries, and layouts.
