projectDetails.name: Project WALL-E
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a smart life jacket powered by machine learning and connected via Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. It integrates key survival technologies: real-time geolocation, continuous monitoring of vital signs, and data transmission through the RockBLOCK module over the Iridium constellation. The jacket includes a heating system against hypothermia, light signals for night visibility, an electromagnetic shark repellent, and flexible solar panels lasting up to 72 hours. Our AI model prioritizes rescues by analyzing location, vitals, and environmental data, ensuring maximum survival in minimal time.
Leveraging LEO satellites, we solved major maritime challenges—communication loss, low visibility, and delayed rescues—by transmitting live data from any sea point to rescue centers for rapid response. The project also showcases how LEO networks can be commercialized through direct sales and subscription models while maximizing real-world impact.
Drowning causes over 360,000 deaths yearly (WHO). Our system detects emergencies with 93% accuracy and a 15-second response time, reducing global rescue costs by $30 million annually. We aim to save one million lives by 2030 while proving that space technology can be both life-saving and economically sustainable, projecting $1.5 million in revenue with a 54% net margin.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a smart life jacket system designed to save lives during maritime emergencies. It automatically detects and monitors the wearer’s location and vital signs, transmits this data in real time to rescue centers via LEO satellites, and provides life-saving survival features to increase the wearer’s chance of rescue and survival.

The system works by collecting data through sensors embedded in the jacket that continuously monitor heart rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature. A RockBLOCK module transmits this information, along with GPS-based location, through the Iridium LEO satellite constellation to rescue centers and nearby ships. In addition to monitoring, the jacket includes several survival features such as a heating system to combat hypothermia, an LED lighting system that enhances visibility during nighttime rescues, and an electromagnetic shark repellent that protects against marine predators.

The machine learning rescue model analyzes each person’s location, health status, and environmental conditions to prioritize rescue efforts. It also forecasts ocean and weather hazards to guide rescue teams toward the safest and fastest routes.

The project offers several key benefits. It has a life-saving impact by reducing drowning deaths through improved communication, hypothermia prevention, and protection from shark attacks. It ensures faster response times, achieving 93% accuracy with a 15-second response rate that allows rescue teams to mobilize quickly. The system also helps reduce global rescue costs by up to $30 million annually and supports a scalable commercial model, proving the profitability of LEO-based services through product sales and subscription access for maritime operators. Furthermore, it provides safety and peace of mind to millions of seafarers, fishermen, migrants, and travelers worldwide.

Our mission is to rescue at least one million people by 2030 while demonstrating that Low Earth Orbit satellite applications can be commercialized responsibly to benefit humanity. We aim to establish our smart life jacket as a global standard for maritime safety, integrating it into shipping, naval operations, and leisure travel.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
An AI prediction model was developed to process real-time data from smart life jacket sensors — including heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), humidity, and sinking state — to automatically calculate a rescue priority score. This score classifies each individual into High, Medium, or Low priority, enabling faster and more efficient rescue decision-making.

Integration with the dashboard:

The trained AI model was deployed using a Flask API (/predict), which receives sensor readings and returns live predictions. The dashboard visualizes these predictions on an interactive map and priority table using Leaflet and JavaScript, allowing rescue teams to track and prioritize victims in real time.

Python (Scikit-learn / TensorFlow): Used to train and evaluate the rescue-priority model.

Flask: For deploying the model as a prediction API.

Chart.js: To display feature importance values from the trained AI model.

projectDetails.name: Project WALL-E: Landing On Mars
projectDetails.summary:
What did you develop?
We developed WALL-E: Landing on Mars, a semi-autonomous, integrated recycling ecosystem for Martian settlements. The system consists of a swarm of small, AI-powered collection robots and a central processing HUB that automatically sorts and recycles non-metabolic waste into valuable resources.

How does it address the challenge?
It directly tackles the critical problem of waste accumulation on long-duration Mars missions, where disposal is not an option. Our system transforms waste from a liability into an asset by automating 70-80% of the collection, sorting, and recycling processes. It converts materials like plastics, metals, textiles, and composites into essential products such as 3D printing filament, metal sheets for repairs, insulation panels, and even energy, establishing a circular economy millions of miles from Earth.

Why is it important?
This system is vital for mission sustainability, crew safety, and psychological well-being. It prevents habitat clutter and contamination, reduces the exorbitant cost and logistics of resupply from Earth, and frees up astronaut time for scientific research. By creating a self-sustaining resource loop, it is a foundational technology for the long-term goal of establishing a permanent human presence on Mars.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?

The system performs end-to-end waste management:

Collection: A fleet of 10-15 "WALL-E" robots autonomously patrols the habitat area, using LiDAR and cameras to detect, collect, and transport waste items to the central HUB.

Processing: The HUB uses an AI vision system (YOLOv5, EfficientNet) to sort waste with >90% accuracy. It then directs materials to specialized modules:

Plastics are shredded and melted into 3D printer filament.

Metals are smelted into sheets or powder.

Textiles are compressed into insulation panels.

Non-recyclables are converted into syngas (for energy) and vitrified slag (for construction) via plasma gasification.

Monitoring: A centralized dashboard provides real-time data on collection rates, sorting accuracy, material throughput, and system status for both astronauts and mission control.

How does it work?

Robotics: The robots use SLAM for navigation in Martian terrain. They are designed to be dust-resistant and energy-efficient.

AI Sorting: Trained on datasets like TrashNet and TACO, the AI classifies waste streams upon arrival at the HUB.

Modular HUB: Each processing unit (shredder, furnace, compressor, gasifier) operates within a standardized module, allowing for easy repair and scaling.

Human-System Interaction: Astronauts supervise the system via a dashboard and perform maintenance, accounting for 20-30% of the total effort, based on NASA human-factor principles.

What benefits does it have?

Operational Efficiency: Automates repetitive tasks, allowing crew to focus on mission science.

Resource Independence: Produces critical materials and energy on-site.

Psychological Well-being: Maintains a clean, organized habitat, reducing stress.

Scalability: The modular design allows the system to grow from supporting a single crew to a large colony.

Dual-Use Technology: The AI sorting and robotic collection have direct applications for improving recycling systems on Earth.

What do you hope to achieve?

We aim to establish the standard for sustainable waste management in deep space exploration. Our goal is to prove that a mission-critical, closed-loop resource system is feasible, making long-term human presence on Mars not just possible, but practical and sustainable.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

AI & Software: Python, YOLOv5, EfficientNet, OpenCV, Unity ML-Agents (for simulation), SLAM algorithms.

Hardware (Conceptual Design): LiDAR sensors, RGB-D cameras, induction furnaces, shredders, plasma gasification reactors, RTG (Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator) and solar panels for power.

Collaboration & Design: GitHub, Trello/Notion, Figma/Canva, Cursor, Google Drive.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Yes, Artificial Intelligence is a core enabling technology of our project.

How we used AI:

Object Detection and Classification: We utilized YOLOv8 and EfficientNet models to create a vision system that identifies and categorizes different types of waste (plastics, metals, textiles) with a target accuracy of over 90%. This is crucial for the automated sorting process in the HUB.

Robotic Navigation: AI-powered SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) algorithms allow the WALL-E robots to autonomously navigate the unpredictable Martian terrain around the habitat, avoiding obstacles and efficiently patrolling for waste.

Simulation and Training: We used Unity ML-Agents to simulate the Martian environment and train our AI models and robotic behaviors before deployment. This included simulating challenges like dust storms and low gravity (0.38g).

System Optimization: AI is used for predictive maintenance, analyzing system data to forecast potential failures in the HUB's processing modules, and for smart energy scheduling to conserve power during dust storms.

projectDetails.name: Project Waste to Wonder (RE_MARS)
projectDetails.summary:
We developed ReMars, an integrated recycling system that transforms inorganic astronaut waste into valuable resources on Mars. Our solution directly addresses the challenge by creating a circular economy where trash becomes manufacturing material.

The system begins with intelligent material sorting using advanced spectroscopy sensors. These sensors precisely identify and differentiate between various plastic types (such as ABS, PEEK, and PLA), enabling the system to automatically select and produce the most suitable filament type for each application. Printable plastics are converted into specialized 3D printing filaments, while non-printable materials like aluminum and carbon fiber composites are used as ready-made components. Through Integrative Hybrid Manufacturing, we create smart 3D-printed structures that mechanically integrate these components into functional products like storage containers and habitat elements.

This approach is crucial because it eliminates waste storage problems, drastically reduces the need to transport materials from Earth, and enables sustainable long-term presence on Mars. Our energy-efficient, adhesive-free system preserves material properties while offering maximum design flexibility - turning Mars missions from disposable to sustainable.
projectDetails.details:
During a single crewed mission to Mars, approximately 12,600 kg of inorganic waste are generated. To address this challenge, the proposed solution — Re-Mars — redefines the concept of waste by transforming every discarded material into a potential resource. An integrated recycling framework has been developed, designed to maximize material recovery and utilization in closed environments while minimizing energy consumption and waste output.

The process begins with an automated sorting and classification stage, in which an advanced spectroscopy sensor scans incoming waste streams to identify polymer types and their fundamental physicochemical properties. Based on this spectral data, the control system assigns each material to the most appropriate pathway for utilization.

Primary Pathway – Filament Production

Qualified polymers are directed toward conversion into high-quality recycled plastic filaments. Critical processing parameters—including temperature, pressure, and extrusion speed—are automatically optimized according to the identified polymer characteristics. The resulting filaments are suitable for additive manufacturing (3D printing) and enable in-situ production of functional components required during the mission.

Secondary Pathway – Hybrid Repurposing

Materials unsuitable for filament production are not discarded. Instead, they are integrated into hybrid assemblies as structural or functional components. This approach preserves the inherent mechanical properties of advanced materials (e.g., aluminum, composites, carbon fiber), reduces energy demands, and supports the creation of reinforced structures by combining recycled plastics with stronger inserts.

Recombinant Utilization Pathway

Beyond recycling and hybrid repurposing, a recombinant design approach is adopted to enable direct reuse of materials without additional processing. This concept draws inspiration from the Samsung × IKEA eco-packaging initiative, where television boxes were transformed into functional furniture and pet houses through smart design and simple folding instructions.

In a Martian context, such a strategy enables packaging and structural materials to be engineered with dual-purpose functionality. Examples include:

• Protective packaging reconfigured into storage modules, partitions, or insulation panels.

• Rigid containers repurposed as furniture, work surfaces, or experimental racks.

• Textile-based wraps adapted into personal gear, protective covers, or thermal insulation layers.

Through this multi-pathway framework, waste is not treated as an obstacle but as a continuous resource stream. By ensuring that all materials are either recycled, repurposed, or directly reused, the system promotes near-complete material utilization and contributes to the realization of a circular economy for space exploration.

projectDetails.name: WaveLens
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, SmartShark, develops a data-driven framework to predict shark foraging habitats using NASA satellite observations. Sharks are apex predators and vital regulators of marine ecosystems, but they face increasing threats from overfishing and habitat loss. Protecting them requires accurate knowledge of where they move and feed.

We combined data from multiple NASA missions: phytoplankton abundance from PACE and MODIS-Aqua, ocean eddy dynamics from SWOT, sea surface temperature from MODIS-Aqua, and bathymetry from GEBCO/ETOPO. Using these variables, we built a preliminary mathematical model that estimates the probability of shark presence based on oceanographic and ecological conditions. We visualized these predictions as hotspot maps and temporal graphs, making it easier to understand how sharks interact with their environment.

Additionally, we designed a conceptual Smart Tag that integrates GPS, depth, temperature, and novel feeding sensors. The tag transmits real-time data via satellite while harvesting energy from shark movement.

SmartShark combines space data, predictive modeling, and innovative technology to improve shark conservation and ensure healthier ocean ecosystems.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, SmartShark, predicts shark foraging hotspots by combining NASA satellite data with a mathematical model. We used PACE and MODIS-Aqua for phytoplankton abundance, SWOT for ocean eddies, MODIS-Aqua for sea surface temperature, and GEBCO/ETOPO for depth. These inputs are linked through logistic regression and machine learning to estimate shark presence.

The workflow, built in Python, produces heatmaps and time-series visualizations showing how environmental conditions drive shark movement. This helps identify critical habitats and foraging zones.

Alongside the model, we designed a conceptual Smart Tag with GPS, depth, temperature, and feeding sensors, powered by both battery and motion-based energy harvesting. It transmits real-time data via satellite, giving researchers immediate insights into shark behavior and diet.

The impact of SmartShark is to improve shark conservation and reduce bycatch, while highlighting the creative use of space-based Earth observations, ecological modeling, and innovative tagging technology.

challengeDetails.title: Sharks from Space
challengeDetails.excerpt: Earth’s ocean is one of the most powerful habitats in our universe, supporting a range of life that sustains ecosystems and habitability across the globe. It is common to measure photosynthetic activity in the ocean from space, but far more challenging to track top predators. Your challenge is to create a mathematical framework for identifying sharks and predicting their foraging habitats using NASA satellite data, and also to suggest a new conceptual model of a tag (a small electronic device that can be attached to an animal to track and study its movement) that could measure not only where sharks are, but also what they are eating, and in real time transmit that data back to users to enable development of predictive models. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: RainAware
projectDetails.summary:
RainAware is a web-based solution designed to make rainfall prediction simple and reliable. Using NASA IMERG precipitation data, our tool provides accurate forecasts that help people prepare for unexpected rain.

The platform offers clear probability insights, a weekly rainfall overview, and an interactive chatbot that explains the data in an easy way. This combination makes NASA’s complex datasets more accessible to everyday users, from farmers protecting their crops to communities and organizers planning events.

What makes RainAware different is its focus on trust, usability, and impact:

Data sourced from NASA ensures scientific accuracy.

A modern, user-friendly design makes the experience engaging.

The goal is to reduce risks, save resources, and support smarter planning.

RainAware helps people plan smarter and stay safe, turning advanced satellite data into real-world impact.
projectDetails.details:
RainAware Homepage – The main landing page of the platform, showing the project name, tagline, and a “Try Forecast” button to start exploring rainfall predictions.

Rain Probability – Shows the chance of rainfall for the selected date, helping users decide whether to prepare for rain (e.g., carrying an umbrella).

Expected Temperature – Displays the predicted temperature alongside a short description of the weather condition (e.g., moderate, hot, or cold).

Forecast Results & Features – An example of the weekly rainfall forecast displayed as a chart, supported by three core highlights of the project:

Impact – Helping communities and farmers plan ahead.

Innovation – A modern design combined with a smart chatbot.

Validity – Powered by trusted NASA IMERG precipitation data.

Forecast Input Section – The area where users select the governorate and date to get rainfall predictions. On the right, the interactive chatbot assists by answering common weather-related questions.

How the Project Works

RainAware collects rainfall data from NASA’s IMERG datasets and processes it through a trained AI model. The model analyzes historical precipitation and weather patterns to predict the probability of rain for a chosen location and date. The results are then displayed on a modern web interface, showing rain probability, expected temperature, and weekly rainfall trends. Additionally, an integrated chatbot makes it easier for users to ask about weather in different regions and receive clear answers.

Benefits

Helps communities and individuals plan outdoor events by reducing the risk of weather disruption.

Supports farmers and agriculture with rainfall insights to protect crops.

Provides early awareness for heavy rain, improving safety and preparedness.

Simplifies NASA data into an easy-to-use tool for non-experts.

Encourages trust by relying on AI-enhanced, NASA-powered datasets.

Programming Languages & Tools

Frontend: HTML, CSS

Backend / AI: Python (for model training, data processing, and predictions)

Data: NASA IMERG precipitation datasets

Visualization: Chart.js (for weekly rain forecast charts)
projectDetails.aiReferences:
AI Contribution in RainAware

In RainAware, we developed and trained a custom AI model using NASA IMERG precipitation datasets combined with historical weather records. The model was trained to recognize rainfall patterns and predict the probability of rain for specific locations and dates.

We applied supervised machine learning techniques to teach the model how different features (such as past precipitation, temperature, and time of year) correlate with rainfall events. After training, the model was able to provide probabilistic forecasts (e.g., “70% chance of rain tomorrow”) that were later visualized on the dashboard.

This AI layer ensures that the system does not only display static data, but actually analyzes and predicts future rainfall, making the solution more intelligent and reliable for end users.

projectDetails.name: Can We Go?
projectDetails.summary:
Can We Go is a creative mobile application designed to solve an everyday problem: how to know if the weather in a certain place is suitable for going out or not. Our aim is not only to help people avoid unexpected risks or disasters, but also to make sure that every outing and trip remains safe, enjoyable, and stress-free until the very end.
Unlike traditional weather apps that only provide raw numbers such as temperature, rainfall, or wind speed, Can We Go goes further by explaining what these numbers really mean. It translates complex measurements into simple, clear insights so that users of all ages and backgrounds can easily understand weather conditions and their possible effects.
In addition, the application highlights real examples of natural disasters caused by weather, which helps raise awareness about the importance and seriousness of the issue. To support this awareness, it also provides practical safety tips and advice that people can follow in daily life.
Most importantly, Can We Go is designed to be simple, easy to use, and accessible for all members of society. It turns a basic forecast into an engaging journey that combines knowledge, fun, and culture all under the umbrella of Can We Go.
projectDetails.details:
Visual Scientific Weather:Imagine opening a Can We Go app that doesn’t just tell you the weather and its forecast, but takes you on a scientific journey. From the very first moment, you step into a documentary style experience that brings the climate to life  the cloudy skies, the roar of thunder, the rush of rain, the fierce hurricane winds, the blazing desert heat, the warmth of a sunny day, the falling autumn leaves, the sparkle of morning dew, and the fresh bloom of spring. Each scene is not just data, but a visual story of our climate.

Learning and Weather Phenomena:As the journey unfolds, the app explains how weather phenomena actually happen  why it rains, what causes lightning, how storms are formed. Alongside, users discover valuable knowledge that enriches their understanding of the world around them. 

Climate Disasters:Then comes the storytelling part: real historical disasters caused by climate, reminding users of the impact weather can have on human life.

Safety Precautions:Finally, the app equips them with safety tips so that whether they’re planning a trip or preparing for an outdoor activity, they can stay safe and aware.

How it Works: 

This app works by letting you search for any city to see its current weather and forecast. You can use it by typing a city name..Use the interactive map to check the weather anywhere in the world. Simply click on any location on the map, and the app will show you the current weather conditions for that spot instantly.

This section features a documentary video offering a visual journey that connects space, Earth, and weather. Just click play to learn more in a visual and simple way.

This section explains basic weather phenomena like rain, wind, humidity, clouds, thunderstorms, and snow. Each card gives a simple description to help users understand how each one forms and its role in the climate.

This section shares real-life stories of natural disasters. Click through to explore events like Hurricane Katrina and learn how nature impacts communities.

This section explains the impact of real natural disasters and gives safety tips. Users can learn how to stay informed, prepare emergency kits, and make a plan.

Benefits of our solutions: 

Helps people plan events safely by checking accurate weather forecasts.

Increases awareness of natural phenomena and their effects.

Provides historical insights into weather related disasters to encourage better preparation.

We are committed to protecting people’s safety by providing accurate weather updates and essential safety precautions.

Easy to use interface suitable for both everyday users and students.

Our Goal: 

Our main goal is to create a smart and accessible platform that helps people make informed decisions about their activities and events by providing reliable weather information. We aim not only to reduce the risks associated with unexpected weather changes but also to raise awareness about natural phenomena and historical weather disasters. By combining accurate forecasts with educational content, the project seeks to make weather knowledge practical, easy to understand, and useful for everyday life. 

Tools and coding language 

Tools: React + Vite +Tailwind CSS+ Shadcn UI+React Router+Tanstack Query+ Leaflet +Lucide React

Canva:  For design, effects and music

Pixabay: To find and download videos

Languages: Javascript, Typescript

projectDetails.name: Weathix
projectDetails.summary:
In a world where the climate changes every day, where the winds shift from gentle breezes to storms, and the sun becomes a life-threatening hazard, our project was born from a simple question: Can we understand nature's wrath before it strikes?  

From this question, we began integrating human intelligence with the eyes of space. We used real data from NASA and global space agencies, and transformed it—with advanced artificial intelligence—into a lively platform that reads the future as a doctor reads a heartbeat.  

By analyzing weather and climate data in real-time, we don’t just tell you if it will rain; we tell you what it means for you—Is it a good time to travel? Is fishing safe today? Could the heat threaten crops?  

Our project is not just another app…it is a gateway between Earth and space, connecting humans to the universe's data to make more informed and safer decisions. We have made the data speak, telling the story of the weather… before its chapters begin. 🌦️🌌
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an intelligent climate insight platform that bridges Earth and space. It uses real-time satellite data from NASA and other global space agencies, combined with advanced AI data analysis, to transform complex climate information into clear, human-centered insights.

Here’s how it works:
The system continuously collects open satellite data—temperature, humidity, precipitation, air quality, and hydrology indicators—then processes it through a smart AI model that identifies trends, predicts weather patterns, and detects potential environmental risks.

Users can interact with the platform through explore live maps, and receive personalized forecasts based on their location, activity, and even age group.

The project’s core benefit lies in turning overwhelming data into understanding—empowering communities, researchers, and policymakers to act before climate threats occur.

Technically, it’s built using JavaScript, React, Node.js, and Python for data analysis, with APIs integrating directly from NASA’s OPeNDAP, EarthData, and Giovanni tools.

Creativity is at its heart — the platform doesn’t just show numbers; it tells a story of the planet through motion, interaction, and emotional design. We considered accessibility, inclusivity, and the psychological aspect of environmental awareness, making climate data feel alive and personal.

Our intended impact: to inspire climate action through understanding — because when people see data as a story, they begin to care, and when they care, they change the world. 🌎✨

projectDetails.name: Orbita
projectDetails.summary:
Orbita is an integrated AI-powered solution developed to address space-related challenges during the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 hackathon. The project combines three core components: a Flutter-based mobile application for cross-platform user interaction, a Python FastAPI backend with AI capabilities for intelligent data processing and analysis, and a robust backend infrastructure for seamless system integration.

The solution leverages NASA satellite data and machine learning algorithms to solve real-world challenges in space exploration and Earth observation. By implementing a comprehensive full-stack architecture, Orbita enables users to visualize, analyze, and interact with complex space-related datasets through an intuitive mobile interface. The AI component employs deep learning models to detect patterns, classify phenomena, and provide actionable insights from NASA's extensive data repositories.

This project is crucial because it democratizes access to space science data, making sophisticated space-related analysis accessible to broader audiences through mobile technology. The system addresses the growing need for efficient data processing and visualization tools in space research while maintaining scalability and real-time performance.
projectDetails.details:
How It Works

Orbita operates as an integrated three-tier intelligent system that transforms NASA's open satellite and space exploration data into accessible mobile experiences. The architecture consists of a Flutter-based cross-platform mobile application (iOS/Android), a Python AI engine for machine learning analysis, and a FastAPI backend server managing data processing and API orchestration.

When users launch the mobile app, they can select from multiple features: satellite imagery visualization, exoplanet data exploration, astronomical phenomenon tracking, or Earth observation analysis. The Flutter frontend communicates with the FastAPI backend through RESTful API endpoints, sending user queries and receiving processed data responses. The backend retrieves relevant datasets from NASA's open data APIs including APOD (Astronomy Picture of the Day), Mars Rover Photos, Earth Imagery, and exoplanet databases.

The AI engine processes raw NASA data using trained machine learning models that perform pattern recognition, anomaly detection, and predictive analysis. For example, when analyzing exoplanet data, the AI model identifies potential candidates based on transit signals and spectral characteristics. The processed insights, visualizations, and interactive charts are returned to the mobile app, where users can explore results through intuitive touch gestures, time-series animations, and 3D model interactions.

The system implements caching mechanisms to store frequently accessed NASA data locally, enabling offline functionality for users in areas with limited connectivity. Progressive data loading ensures smooth performance even when processing large satellite imagery files.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Educational Transformation: Orbita democratizes access to NASA's vast scientific resources, making complex space data comprehensible for students, educators, and the general public. By translating technical datasets into visual stories, the platform transforms abstract astronomical concepts into engaging learning experiences that inspire the next generation of space scientists.

Research Acceleration: Scientists and researchers benefit from AI-powered pattern detection that automates hours of manual data analysis. The platform's machine learning models can identify subtle anomalies in satellite imagery, detect exoplanet transit signals, and classify celestial objects faster than traditional methods.

Public Engagement: The mobile-first approach eliminates barriers to space science participation, allowing anyone with a smartphone to explore NASA missions, track Mars rover activities, and discover daily astronomical phenomena. This aligns with NASA's mission to engage global communities in space exploration and scientific discovery.

Real-World Applications: The system supports environmental monitoring through Earth observation satellite data, enabling early detection of natural disasters, climate change impacts, and ecological transformations. Decision-makers can access processed insights for informed policy development and emergency response planning.

The intended impact extends to fostering a global community of citizen scientists who contribute observations, validate AI predictions, and participate in crowdsourced space research initiatives.

Tools, Technologies, and Development Stack

Frontend Development - Flutter Framework:

  • Language: Dart programming language for cross-platform native performance
  • UI Components: Material Design widgets with custom visualizations for space data presentation
  • State Management: Provider or BLoC pattern for reactive UI updates
  • Key Packages: http for API communication, flutter_map for satellite imagery display, charts_flutter for data visualization, cached_network_image for performance optimization
  • Platform Support: Native compilation for iOS and Android with shared codebase

AI/ML Engine - Python Ecosystem:

  • Framework: PyTorch for deep learning model development.
  • Model Architecture: Custom Neural Networks (NN).
  • Data Processing: NumPy for multidimensional array operations, Pandas for dataset manipulation and exploratory data analysis (EDA).
  • Computer Vision: OpenCV for satellite image preprocessing and enhancement.
  • Training Datasets: NASA exoplanet archives, Mars rover imagery collections, Earth observation satellite data.

Backend Infrastructure - FastAPI Server:

  • Framework: FastAPI with Python 3.10+ for high-performance asynchronous API endpoints
  • Server: Uvicorn ASGI server handling concurrent requests efficiently
  • API Integration: Direct connections to NASA Open APIs (api.nasa.gov) for real-time data retrieval
  • Data Validation: Pydantic models for request/response schema validation
  • Caching: Redis for frequently accessed NASA data to reduce API call latency
  • Database: PostgreSQL or MongoDB for user preferences and processed data storage

Development and Deployment Tools:

  • Version Control: Git with GitHub repositories for code management and team collaboration
  • Containerization: Docker and Docker Compose for consistent development and deployment environments
  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions for automated testing and deployment pipelines
  • API Testing: Postman for endpoint validation during development
  • Cloud Services: AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure for backend hosting and scalable infrastructure

NASA Data Sources:

  • TESS Objects of Interest (TOI)
  • Kepler Objects of Interest (KOI)

Creativity and Innovation

Mobile-First Space Science: Unlike traditional desktop-based GIS tools and astronomical software requiring specialized training, Orbita pioneers mobile-native space exploration accessible through familiar smartphone interactions. This creative approach leverages Flutter's hot reload for rapid prototyping during the 48-hour hackathon, enabling iterative design refinement based on real-time user testing.

AI-Augmented Discovery: The platform innovatively combines multiple NASA datasets with machine learning to create predictive insights unavailable through manual analysis. For example, the AI model can correlate Earth observation data with astronomical events to identify patterns influencing climate or predict optimal viewing conditions for celestial phenomena.

Narrative Data Visualization: Instead of presenting raw numbers and charts, Orbita transforms data into interactive stories where users can "travel" through time-series satellite imagery, witnessing glacial retreat, urban expansion, or Mars surface changes over mission timelines. This storytelling approach makes science emotionally engaging and memorable.

Accessibility Innovation: The dual-level interface serves both casual learners and professional researchers through progressive disclosure—beginners see simplified explanations with visual aids, while experts can access technical metadata, spectral data, and raw API responses. Offline mode creativity ensures users in developing regions or remote field locations maintain access to previously loaded NASA data.

Open Science Contribution: By open-sourcing the codebase across three GitHub repositories, Orbita enables other developers to extend functionality, adapt models for regional needs, or integrate additional space agency data sources. This fosters collaborative innovation beyond the hackathon event.

Team Considerations and Development Factors

User-Centric Design: The team prioritized intuitive navigation patterns familiar to mobile users, conducting rapid usability testing during development to ensure features remained discoverable without extensive tutorials. Design decisions focused on minimizing cognitive load through progressive disclosure and contextual help systems.

Performance Optimization: Given NASA datasets can exceed gigabytes, the team implemented intelligent data streaming, progressive image loading, and aggressive caching strategies to maintain responsive performance on mid-range smartphones with limited memory. API rate limiting considerations shaped the backend architecture to batch requests and cache frequently accessed NASA data.

Scalability Architecture: The modular FastAPI backend design supports horizontal scaling as user base grows, with containerized deployments enabling rapid cloud infrastructure expansion. Database schema design anticipates feature additions without requiring breaking changes to existing mobile app versions.

Data Integrity and Accuracy: The team implemented validation layers ensuring AI predictions include confidence scores and uncertainty metrics, preventing misinterpretation of probabilistic outputs. All displayed data maintains traceability to original NASA sources through embedded citations and metadata links.

Ethical AI Principles: Model training considered bias mitigation across geographical regions, ensuring equal accuracy for Southern and Northern hemisphere observations. Transparency documentation explains AI decision-making processes and acknowledges model limitations.

Sustainability and Maintenance: Technology stack selection favored mature frameworks with active communities (Flutter, FastAPI, PyTorch) ensuring long-term support and security updates. The architecture allows individual components to evolve independently without system-wide disruptions.

Inclusivity Focus: Interface design supports multiple languages, accessibility features for vision-impaired users through screen reader compatibility, and offline functionality addressing users in regions with intermittent internet connectivity.

Open Data Compliance: All NASA data usage adheres to open licensing requirements, with proper attribution and respect for usage guidelines outlined in NASA's Open Data Policy. No proprietary or restricted datasets were incorporated, ensuring project reproducibility and legal compliance.

projectDetails.name: Project We Are Cooked
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a cross-platform mobile application using Flutter, AI, and a backend system that transforms raw weather and Earth observation data into personalized, actionable insights. Unlike traditional weather apps that only show general forecasts, our solution interprets data from the NASA POWER API to provide forecasts tailored to specific activities such as farming, traveling, or event planning.

This directly addresses the challenge of helping people move beyond “sunny” or “rainy” forecasts, focusing instead on what the weather means for them. For example, farmers can understand the potential impact of heat on crops, event organizers can assess risks for outdoor activities, and travelers can make safer decisions about their trips.

The project is important because it empowers users to make smarter, data-driven decisions, reducing risks, saving resources, and increasing resilience in daily life. By combining NASA’s trusted data with intelligent design, we make space technology meaningful and practical for everyone.
projectDetails.details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?
Our project provides personalized weather insights. It collects weather and Earth observation data, then uses AI to analyze it and give users customized forecasts based on their activities such as farming, traveling, or event planning.

2. What benefits does it have?
It helps users make smarter decisions. Farmers know how weather affects crops, travelers know if conditions are safe, and event planners know if their plans are possible.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?
The goal is to improve decision-making, reduce risks, and save resources by transforming raw weather data into useful, personalized insights.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
We used Flutter for cross-platform development, AI models for smart weather predictions, and a Backend system to manage and process data.

5. How is your project creative?
Unlike normal weather apps, our project doesn’t only show numbers. It interprets forecasts into actionable advice that is directly meaningful to each user.

6. What factors did your team consider?
We focused on data accuracy, user-friendly design, real-time performance, and making the system useful for different types of users.

projectDetails.name: ExoVision- Hunting Exoplanets Among The stars
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, ExoVision, empowers scientists and enthusiasts to classify newly discovered exoplanets using AI. We developed a Random Forest machine learning model, trained on NASA’s Kepler Archive, with a carefully selected set of core features that can be derived directly from light curve data or basic stellar parameters. These features are fundamental in astrophysical analysis and can be calculated early in the discovery pipeline, making the model highly practical for classifying new exoplanets without requiring complex preprocessing or advanced analysis.
We addressed data imbalance using SMOTE and fine-tuned our model through Randomized Hyperparameter Search, achieving strong performance. Our pipeline is designed to be reproducible, efficient, and adaptable to future missions beyond Kepler.

To make the technology accessible, we built a web platform where users can upload their data and instantly receive classification results. The platform includes an educational chatbot, powered by Gemini, that explains key astrophysical concepts, and a “Tales from the Stars” section that brings real discoveries to life through storytelling to inspire curiosity.

ExoVision uniquely blends science, AI, storytelling, and education, making exoplanet hunting more inclusive and inspiring the next generation of scientists and explorers to search for new worlds and look beyond the stars.
projectDetails.details:
ExoVision is an interactive web platform designed to make exoplanet classification more practical and accessible for scientists and enthusiasts. It integrates machine learning, education, and storytelling to empower users to analyze newly discovered exoplanets using minimal data — without requiring complex preprocessing.

---

How It Works:

The platform allows users to provide data through two options:

File Upload for CSV datasets containing light curve features and stellar parameters.

Manual Entry for directly inputting individual feature values.

Once data is submitted, it is processed through our trained Random Forest model, which classifies the exoplanet as Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive.

Model statistics, including a confusion matrix, are displayed to ensure transparency and interpretability.

---

Model Development:

Language: Python

Environment: Google Colab, VS Code

Libraries: Pandas, Scikit-learn, SMOTE

ML Approach:

Data was split, scaled, and balanced using SMOTE.

Random Forest was selected for its robustness and interpretability.

Hyperparameters were fine-tuned using Randomized Search, improving model accuracy and F1-score.

A core set of features was chosen specifically because they can be derived early from light curves and basic stellar data — making the model practical for new exoplanet discoveries without the need for advanced astrophysical analysis.

---

Educational & Creative Features:

- A Learning Tab explains transit methods, light curves, and exoplanet features for beginners.

- An integrated Gemini-powered chatbot answers user questions and provides guidance.

-“Tales from the Stars” features the story of Kepler-16b, complete with its complex light curve and audio narration, blending science with storytelling to inspire curiosity.

---

Impact:

ExoVision streamlines the exoplanet classification process, enabling early-stage analysis by researchers, students, and enthusiasts alike. By making the science behind exoplanets accessible and engaging, it supports both scientific discovery and public inspiration, aligning with NASA’s vision of collaborative exploration.

---

Future Vision & Impact:

ExoVision is not just a tool — it’s a foundation. Our platform is scalable and mission-agnostic, meaning it can be extended to work with future missions such as TESS, K2, and upcoming space telescopes. By designing a flexible pipeline, we’re paving the way for broader exoplanet discoveries and real scientific contribution.

We believe that science exists to make the universe more understandable and exploration more accessible. Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers — scientists, students, and dreamers — to keep looking beyond, to search the skies, and to uncover the hidden worlds waiting in the starlight.

-ExoVision isn’t just about finding new worlds — it’s about inspiring humanity to reach for the stars and write the next chapter of space exploration.

projectDetails.name: Project X nebula
projectDetails.summary:
Space Garden Box is a compact, smart plant-growing system designed to help astronauts produce fresh food in space. The project focuses on creating a small, automated garden that can grow plants in microgravity using limited water and energy. The system includes sensors to monitor light, moisture, and temperature, and automatically adjusts conditions to keep plants healthy.

This project addresses the challenge of food sustainability during long-term missions to the Moon or Mars. By growing food onboard, astronauts can reduce their dependence on supply missions from Earth.

It’s important because it promotes self-sufficiency, provides psychological comfort through contact with living plants, and supports research on sustainable life-support systems for future space habitats.
projectDetails.details: Our project, the Space Garden Box, is a small and smart plant-growing system made for astronauts to grow fresh food in space. It works by using simple sensors to check soil moisture, light, and temperature. When the sensors detect that the plant needs more light or water, the system automatically adjusts — turning on tiny LED lights or releasing small drops of water. The main benefit is that astronauts can grow vegetables or herbs safely in limited space without needing to care for them all the time. This helps save water, energy, and space while also giving astronauts access to healthy food and a touch of green life. We designed it using basic hardware like Arduino, moisture sensors, LED grow lights, and simple code written in C++. Our team focused on making it easy to build, lightweight, and adaptable for different space missions. What makes it creative is that it combines smart automation with emotional well-being — turning a small box into both a food source and a reminder of Earth. 🌍💚

projectDetails.name: Mission 25
projectDetails.summary:
It all started with a simple question: What does life in space really feel like?

For 25 years, humans have lived aboard the International Space Station, Imagine floating 400 kilometers above Earth, where sunrise happens every 90 minutes!, a home in orbit where thousands of experiments have reshaped life on Earth. But for most people, the ISS still feels distant. Mission25 bridges that gap by transforming space exploration into an interactive learning experience that anyone can feel and understand.

Our web-based platform guides users through an astronaut’s journey: starting with a personalized welcome, then training in a Neutral Buoyancy Lab simulation to learn balance and precision, exploring Earth through the Cupola module where each region reveals real ISS imagery and its contributions to humanity, and finally, learning through story-based videos or readings about NASA experiments that improved life on Earth.

The experience ends with a visual quiz and certificate of completion, celebrating each user’s achievement in “Mission 25.”

By combining storytelling, interactivity, and education, Mission 25 addresses the challenge by helping students and the public understand the sensory and emotional experiences aboard the ISS, showing that space exploration isn’t just about reaching the stars, but about bringing their lessons back home.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, Mission 25, is an interactive web-based experience that brings astronaut training and ISS exploration to the public in a gamified, educational way.

What it does:
The platform takes users on a journey with four stages:

1. Neutral Buoyancy Lab Mini-Game – a simulation of astronaut underwater training.

2. Cupola Map – users explore Earth through real ISS images using NASA’s Image API.



3.Stories & Videos – short-form storytelling showing how ISS research benefits life on Earth.
4. Quiz & Certificate – a final knowledge check where users earn a “Junior Astronaut Explorer” badge.


How it works:

  • A simple UI/UX guides users step by step.
  • NASA APIs provide real images and data.
  • AI narration explains benefits in easy-to-understand language.
  • Gamification elements keep users engaged.

Benefits:
The project makes space research tangible, connects ISS work directly to Earth’s challenges, and inspires students by showing real-world impact.

Our goals:
To celebrate 25 years of the ISS by increasing public awareness, sparking interest in STEM, and helping people understand how space exploration improves life on Earth and have impact on our daily life.

Tools & technologies used:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React, Next.js).
  • Backend: Node.js, Express.
  • AI: Gemeni NLP models for narration.

projectDetails.name: Project Z-MISSION
projectDetails.summary:
Our game, Z-MISSION, is an interactive, immersive game founded upon the typical model for games. It combines a suspenseful, narrative-driven story of a boy suddenly flown to space as an astronaut with the scientific underpinnings of the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) and the International Space Station (ISS) in concept and design. Astronauts are engulfed in the details of the ISS and NBL and, in particular, of buoyancy training and the breathtaking views of the Cupola module.
Z-MISSION is rising to the challenge to recruit and make science learning entertaining. A far cry from a stodgy study text or a distraction, it shows examples of the profound impact of ISS research, such as the Water Recovery System (WRS), on advancing science.
The value of the project lies in its ambiguity of entertainment and education by means of groundbreaking storytelling keeping science fact-based. It is aimed at entertaining anyone who ever had curiosity about space, 12 or 35 years young. By incorporating scientific facts within this engrossing "accidental astronaut" story, Z-MISSION inspires passive learning by means of an active, easy ride. It is the perfect entryway for everyone to pass into the universe.
projectDetails.details:
What exactly does it do?
Z-MISSION is an interactive adventure game that fuses Egyptian mythology and authentic space exploration facts. The game follows Zain, a young boy who, inspired by stories of NASA from his late grandfather, is somehow transported into a secret world. He will have to get trained at a facility inspired by the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory (NBL) before embarking on a mission or die endeavor to the International Space Station (ISS) with the ultimate mission of saving a secret world.
How does it work?
The experience is built with the Unity game engine to reproduce a compelling, story-driven 3D environment. The highlight is the Horus Chatbot (Anubis)—a "magical tool" that is the primary educational interface. During Zain's journey of challenges, the Chatbot teaches him (and the player) relevant real-world facts, physics concepts, and technical information about the NBL and ISS. Data management for the chatbot is carried out using Python libraries like Pandas and NumPy.
What are the benefits?
The basic benefit is Edutainment. The project battles the drudgery of scientific information by basing it in a thrilling fantasy quest. It positively ignites curiosity about space and works toward solidifying the dream of becoming an astronaut by connecting the grandeur of ancient civilization with the frontier of modern-day space science.
What do you hope to acquire?
The main mission of Z-MISSION is to be an immersion learning experience that promotes international awareness of space missions, namely those of NASA. Our goal is to demonstrate the powerful potential of combining imaginative storytelling with empirically verifiable scientific fact to inspire the next generation of space explorers and problem solvers.
What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
We primarily coded games and generated 3D spaces with the Unity game engine. We coded the core coding in Python, employing libraries such as Numpy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn for data handling and processing. Sketchfab (or other software such as skechtfap) and Maximo were also employed to model 3D, texture, and animate characters, as well as Python's re.library and collections.libr for basic programming needs.

projectDetails.details:
Project Name: BioMe: A Biology Knowledge Engine Dashboard

Overview:
BioMe is an AI-powered platform designed as a knowledge hub for researchers, students, and investors. It provides a reliable and organized source of biological research, enriched with advanced AI features to make learning and research more efficient, engaging, and accessible. Users can explore, search, and analyze scientific publications with the assistance of AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies.

Functionality & Benefits:
The platform allows users to sign in as guests or with personal accounts and navigate through an interactive dashboard with multiple features. Users can search publications and documents using text, image, or speech queries, ensuring flexibility in accessing information. Each retrieved document comes with AI-generated summaries, saving time and effort in understanding key insights. Users can also manage their reading history through features like "favorites" and "last read documents."

BioMe enables users to explore data in depth, compare research findings, and gain meaningful insights. With integrated AI assistance, the platform significantly reduces the time needed to analyze and interpret information, making research up to 100x faster and easier.

Intended Impact:
In the short term, BioMe helps researchers discover and analyze space and biological research, opening new horizons for exploration and learning. In the long term, it supports investors and entrepreneurs in identifying suitable research projects for potential funding and innovation. The platform is intended to bridge the gap between research, education, and real-world application, empowering the scientific community and decision-makers alike.

Target Users:

  • Students and learners seeking structured knowledge.
  • Researchers looking for advanced tools to explore and analyze publications.
  • Investors and business professionals evaluating research for opportunities.

Technical Implementation:
BioMe was built using a wide range of technologies to ensure scalability, performance, and AI integration.

  • AI & Data Processing: LangChain (LLM), LangGraph (agents), Ollama (text, image, and embeddings), RAG system (retrieval), unstructured library for parsing images/tables in documents.
  • Knowledge Representation: Neo4j for constructing and querying Knowledge Graphs.
  • Web Technologies: React, Express, TurboRepo, Prisma, Better Auth, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript.
  • Database: PostgreSQL for storing structured data.
  • Other Tools: Python for backend processing and web scraping for data collection and parsing.

Creativity & Uniqueness:
BioMe stands out by combining AI-powered search (text, image, speech), automated summarization, and Knowledge Graphs in one unified dashboard. Unlike traditional search engines, it contextualizes scientific data and links related research, giving users a more meaningful and connected understanding of the information.

Factors Considered:
The development team focused on performance, scalability, user experience, and security to ensure a smooth and reliable platform suitable for both academic and professional use.

Challenges & Solutions:

  • Handling complex documents: Many publications contained images and tables. The team used the unstructured library to extract this data, converted it into text with LLMs, and embedded it for AI-driven retrieval.
  • Building Knowledge Graphs: As a new concept for the team, constructing graphs with Neo4j was challenging but eventually led to a functional prototype.
  • Time constraints: Given the scale and complexity of the project, the team had to prioritize and implement efficient solutions within limited time.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We were mainly depending on Claude 4.5 Sonnet (preview) from GitHub Copilot Pro as our optimization and code refining AI helper. For the technical implementation, we utilized open-source local LLMs, mainly from Ollama. We were using gemma3:4b for summarization and construction of the knowledge graphs. For image understanding, we utilized llava:7b for generating descriptions of the image. For the transcribe model, we used OpenAI's open-source model Whisper to catch the text from a voice recording. For embeddings, we utilized embeddinggemma:300m for generating all the embeddings for our text, image description, and the transcribed text.

projectDetails.name: Henry's Farm Adventures
projectDetails.summary:
Welcome to Henry’s Farm Adventure!
For the NASA Farm Navigators Challenge, we didn’t just build a game, we built a global farming quest powered by space data.

Meet Henry, a struggling farmer whose crops keep failing. Instead of giving up, he sets off on an epic journey around the world, guided by real NASA satellite data. Along the way, he meets farmers on the frontlines of climate change, like Bilal in Pakistan, fighting the floods of 2022, and Ramesh in India, surviving brutal heatwaves.

But this isn’t just a story, it’s you in action. As the player, you step into Henry’s boots and take on mini-games that transform serious challenges into hands-on missions, by solving them, you learn how farmers adapt in real life, how NASA’s data reveals these risks, and how communities can fight back against climate change.

This is NASA data like you’ve never seen it before, not in charts or reports, but in the palm of your hand, as a playful, high-stakes adventure.
projectDetails.details:
Zumorroda-X's Project Solution

Henry’s Farm Adventure is an educational adventure game designed to teach players how environmental challenges affect agriculture turning real NASA satellite data into an interactive story-driven game. Players travel with Henry, meet farmers worldwide, and use hands-on mini games to solve climate challenges making science both fun and accessible.

How Does Our Solution Work

In the game, Henry is a farmer facing repeated crop failures, and he sets out on a journey to uncover the environmental challenges threatening agriculture as floods, heatwaves, droughts, and soil salinization. Along the way, Henry meets farmers from different countries who share their experiences and solutions, helping him piece together which challenge might also be affecting his own farm.

  • Heatwaves (India, 2021):
    Henry visits Ramesh, a farmer in India, who experienced the devastating 2021 extreme heat crisis. Ramesh shows Henry NASA's extreme heat map, in which player can see India suffering badly from heat in addition to other areas, then teaches Henry about techniques farmers use to protect crops from heats such as shade nets and mulching, after that Ramesh tests player with a quiz game.
  • Floods (Pakistan, 2022):
    In Pakistan, Henry meets Bilal, who describes how the historic 2022 floods devastated farmland. Using an image slider, Henry compares NASA satellite images of Pakistan before and after the flood, witnessing the disaster’s true scale. In the gameplay, players help Henry protect farms:
      Level 1: Navigate Henry to place straw in the areas hit by the heaviest rainfall.
      Level 2: Install drainage pipes to save waterlogged fields. Through this, players learn how farmers can adapt and reduce flood damage.
  • Soil Salinization (Egypt 2021):
    Next, Henry travels to Egypt to meet Mohamed, who shows him how irrigation practices are affecting farmland. Henry learns about soil salinization and explores live NASA satellite data that reveals how salt buildup reduces soil productivity over time. In the gameplay, players are given a time limit to save the farm from salinization by:
      Task: Implementing drip irrigation to revive the salty plants.
    Through this, players discover how efficient irrigation methods can protect soil health.
  • Drought (United States):
    Henry also visits the United States, where he meets an American farmer "Sam" struggling with drought. He learns how drought affects soil health and how scientists use vegetation indexes from satellite imagery to measure water stress and monitor crops.
  • Crops Management (Brazil):
    Finally, Henry visits João da Silva, a farmer and innovator. João explains how increasing CO₂ levels can sometimes stimulate plant growth. He also emphasizes the importance of adaptation to climate change, using fertilizers wisely, adjusting planting times, and adopting new techniques. João then reveals his AI model, which predicts which crops will survive based on country, year, CO₂ levels, and adaptation strategies. To make it hands-on, he shows Henry a NASA food supply table and turns it into a matching game, where Henry pairs crops with the right conditions, learning how to choose the best crops for each scenario.

When the player completes all the challenges, the farmers gather together for a lively catch-up!

The game benefits

farmers, students, and the wider community by:

  • Educating players on environmental disasters and their impact on crops.
  • Demonstrating practical, data-driven strategies for sustainable farming.
  • Bridging the gap between NASA’s datasets and real-world agricultural practices in a fun, engaging way.

Our goal

To make NASA’s open data more accessible, helping communities prepare for climate-related agricultural challenges while fostering awareness of global environmental issues. Despite our attempt to reveal agricultural difficulties globally, our game is limited to certain issues and didn't mention other calamities faced by other countries such as wildfires.

Tools and Technologies Used

Coding Languages:

  • Python → for the ML model.
  • JavaScript (with Phaser) → for 2D game development.

Data Sources:

  • NASA real-time datasets → for environmental and agricultural data. Through NASA’s data, we were able to access Landsat images that allowed us to compare countries' farmlands before and after enduring environmental issues, that go back to a farmland in 1984 and compare it with the same area about 17 years later. Furthermore, NASA provides data that allows us to check recent NDVI (Natural differentiation vegetation index) of different countries, which was integrated in our games using APIs. In addition, an artificial intelligence model was used and integrated with the NASA data to highlight the significance of CO2 on crops, and adaptation level on different types of crops. Finally, data was extracted from NASA’s US drought monitor, displayed in a map, and utilized for learning purposes in the game.

Character Design:

  • Piskel → for creating and editing pixel-style images and sprites.

projectDetails.name: Project Zyntra
projectDetails.summary:
Overview of the Proposed Solution
In this proposed solution, we provide an AI-based interactive dashboard that will turn NASA's 608 bioscience publications into an accessible and intelligent knowledge management system. Created as an interactive web app, the research platform uses strong artificial intelligence, knowledge graphs, and intuitive user interfaces to allow effortless exploration of research findings in the field of space biology.

Accessibility of Information
To address the challenge of accessibility, the solution incorporates AI-powered semantic search capabilities that defer from traditional keyword-based search models. Users will be able to ask complex scientific questions in natural language, and the system will intelligently retrieve and respond exclusively from information obtained through NASA's validated bioscience publications, maximizing reliability and ensuring scientific accuracy of responses.

Integrating Knowledge and Discovery
The platform addresses the problem of fragmentation in research by implementing automated summarization of content associated with individual publications which make it easy for researchers to find primary findings, methodology, and conclusions, in a timely manner. Furthermore, with advanced algorithms, the system will look for themes across these publications, indicating consensus, disagreements, and gaps in emerging research.
projectDetails.details:
What it does:

  • Provides AI-powered semantic search capabilities using natural language queries
  • Generates automated summaries of individual publications
  • Identifies themes, consensus, disagreements, and research gaps across the literature
  • Creates knowledge graphs connecting publications, experiments, and outcomes
  • Offers customized interfaces for different user types (scientists, managers, mission architects)
  • Provides interactive visualizations of research trends

How it works: The platform operates through four development phases:

1.    Data Infrastructure Preparation: Ingests all 608 NASA bioscience publications and integrates NASA resources

2.   AI System Implementation: Uses NLP models for content analysis, vector embeddings for semantic similarity, and intelligent query processing

3.   Dashboard Development: Creates user-friendly interfaces with interactive visualization tools

4.   Integration and Testing: Comprehensive system integration with performance optimization

Benefits:

1.    Reliability: Backed solely by peer-reviewed NASA database, eliminating AI hallucinations

2.   Intelligent synthesis: Knowledge graphs identify relationships between studies

3.   Multi-stakeholder support: Tailored tools for different user types

4.   Comprehensive integration: Incorporates NASA's entire research ecosystem

Goals:

  • Transform fragmented space research knowledge into accessible, actionable intelligence
  • Maximize utility of NASA's research investment
  • Minimize time to scientific discoveries and mission planning
  • Prevent duplicate research studies
  • Enable evidence-based decisions for lunar and Martian exploration

Tools and Technologies:

  • Frontend: React.js for dynamic user interfaces
  • Backend: Node.js for API and data processing
  • AI Processing: Google Gemini Pro for text summarization and analysis
  • OCR: Tesseract.js for text extraction from documents
  • Vector Database: Pinecone for semantic search and knowledge graph capabilities
  • NLP Models: Sentence Transformers for content embedding and similarity measurement
  • Design: Figma for UI/UX prototyping
  • Development: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub

Programming Languages: JavaScript (React.js, Node.js)

challengeDetails.title: Meteor Madness

projectDetails.name: skyra
projectDetails.summary: We developed a web application that allows users to input a location, date, and optionally an activity. Using these inputs, the app fetches historical weather data from the past 10 years via NASA POWER API and calculates probabilities for various weather conditions on the selected date.  The results are presented in a detailed dashboard, including an LLM-generated summary message for easy understanding. Additionally, the app features a chatbot interface that can provide personalized recommendations and suggest alternative activities based on weather conditions.
projectDetails.details:
Our

project is a web application that helps users determine whether a

specific location and date will have suitable weather conditions for

their planned activities.

- What it does:

Users enter a date and location, and the system fetches the predicted

weather data for that time using NASA’s API. The results are then

analyzed with the help of an AI assistant (Gemini), which summarizes the

forecast and gives the user a clear, human-friendly recommendation

about whether the conditions are appropriate.

- How it works:

The frontend, built with React, provides an intuitive interface where

users can submit their queries. The backend, implemented in FastAPI,

handles communication with NASA’s weather prediction APIs, processes the

data, and passes it to Gemini for natural-language summarization. The

final response is delivered back to the user in a simple “yes/no +

explanation” style.

- Benefits:

Instead of requiring users to interpret raw meteorological data, the

system provides personalized, actionable insights. This makes weather

planning more accessible, reduces uncertainty, and saves time—helping

people make smarter decisions about outdoor events like parades,

festivals, or gatherings.

- Our goals:

We aim to make weather forecasts more user-centered and practical,

transforming complex data into clear recommendations. In the future, we

hope to expand the tool to support more detailed planning (e.g.,

suggesting alternative times or locations).

- Tools & technologies used:

- NASA API for weather prediction data

- React for the frontend

- FastAPI for the backend

- Gemini AI for analysis and summarization

- Development tools: Vim, VS Code

- Deployment: VPS hosting with a custom domain
projectDetails.aiReferences:
We

did not use any AI-generated images, videos, or audio in our project.

Instead, AI was incorporated in two ways:

1. Development Support – We used tools such as GitHub Copilot and

ChatGPT to assist with writing and debugging code during development.

2. Application Features – We integrated the Gemini API into our web

application to analyze NASA weather data and provide users with

natural-language summaries and recommendations about outdoor

suitability.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?
challengeDetails.excerpt: If you’re planning an outdoor event—like a vacation, a hike on a trail, or fishing on a lake—it would be good to know the chances of adverse weather for the time and location you are considering. There are many types of Earth observation data that can provide information on weather conditions for a particular location and day of the year. Your challenge is to construct an app with a personalized interface that enables users to conduct a customized query to tell them the likelihood of “very hot,” “very cold,” “very windy,” “very wet,” or “very uncomfortable” conditions for the location and time they specify. projectDetails.name: Discovering the Sun
projectDetails.summary: This project presents an interactive educational story designed to teach children aged 7–10 about solar phenomena in a fun and accessible way. The narrative follows a curious child who, after seeing a funny meme about the Sun, embarks on an adventure.. Along the journey, the character meets different people as a farmer, a pilot, an electric grid operator, and finally an astronaut. Each explaining how solar activity, such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar particle events, affect their daily lives. Besides the narrative kids need to accomplish minigames to continue the adventure. By connecting real-world impacts with storytelling, the project addresses the challenge of engaging children in space weather topics through narrative-based learning.
projectDetails.details:
Our solution is an interactive storyteller that immerses users in an educational plot about space weather. Addressing a complex topic such as space weather can be challenging, especially with children aged 7 to 10, who are in a more concrete and curious learning phase. That's why our tool transforms the content into a fun experience, to make learning lighter and more meaningful. With the story, knowledge is presented in a playful context that is close to the child's reality, facilitating the understanding. Challenges by minigames stimulate reasoning, scientific curiosity, and problem-solving, while maintaining engagement. In addition, the use of videos and images promotes multisensory learning, helping children build connections between theory and practice. Thus, the tool not only facilitates the assimilation of complex information, but also the development of critical thinking and autonomy during learning.

The intended impact of the project is to make learning about space weather accessible by summarizing information obtained by NASA and making it palatable to children. Our goal is for the tool to be used in different educational contexts, such as schools, homes, museums, and science outreach centers, expanding the reach of knowledge and promoting the popularization of science. Thus, the project seeks not only to facilitate understanding of a complex topic, but also to inspire new generations of explorers and scientists, helping children comprehend the importance of studying climate and its impacts on Earth.

To develop the solution, we combined  programming languages with multimedia design and production tools. J. The languages used were JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. During the process, we used support software and platforms such as Cursor and Visual Studio Code (VS Code) for programming; Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Premiere, Adobe Podcast and Canva for creating and editing visual and audiovisual elements; and Word and Google Drive for collaborative planning and documentation. In addition, GitHub was used for version control and code storage, and OBS Studio assisted in recording and demonstrating project interactions. Text translation was done using Translated with DeepL.com (free version) and Google translator.

The creativity of our project is evident in its original storyline, which combines different narrative elements and features characters interconnected within the same context. In addition, it was necessary to create challenges in a creative way that was integrated into the story, in order to engage the user and ensure that each activity made sense within the proposed storyline. The base for these ideas came by analysing the background and objectives of the challenge proposed.We list each required point and insert them into the context of the narrative, using NASA data to support the information.
