projectDetails.name: Project ARCS Al Amal Haven
projectDetails.summary:
ARCS – Al-Amal Haven is a stunning innovation from the deserts of the UAE with humanity’s dream of living on Mars. Inspired by the UAE’s Hope Probe (Al-Amal) Mars Mission, our name reflects both “hope” and a “safe haven” for future explorers. Our project is a Smart Greenhouse Habitat Control System, designed to simulate how astronauts could grow food and live sustainably on Mars or the Moon. Just like a futuristic mission control center, our system uses real-time monitoring and controls to manage a greenhouse habitat.
🌍 Features of our design include:
A live dashboard showing environmental conditions like temperature, humidity, CO₂, light, and soil moisture.
Actuator controls for fans, lights, water, and ventilation.
A visual habitat simulation to show plant growth in space.
Auto vs Manual modes so astronauts can switch between automatic control or hands-on management.
Alert systems and failure simulations to test safety and resilience.
Energy tracking to keep the habitat sustainable.
Our vision is to create not just a technical system, but a futuristic mission experience with glowing indicators, Mars-inspired colors, and smooth animations that make science engaging and accessible. From the UAE desert to deep space, the ARCS–Al-Amal Haven team believes that with hope, creativity, and technology, we can design habitats that keep explorers safe and bring life to new worlds. 🚀🌱🪐
projectDetails.details:
🌌 ARCS – Al-Amal Haven

A Smart Greenhouse Habitat Control System for Mars & Beyond

What does it do / How does it work?

ARCS – Al-Amal Haven is a smart greenhouse habitat simulator inspired by the UAE’s Hope Probe (Al-Amal) mission. It demonstrates how astronauts could grow food and live sustainably on Mars or the Moon by creating a controlled, resilient, and sustainable greenhouse environment.

The system mimics a futuristic mission control center with:

  • Real-time monitoring of temperature, humidity, CO₂ levels, soil moisture, and light.
  • Actuator controls for fans, lights, water, and ventilation.
  • Auto vs Manual modes that let astronauts either rely on automation or take direct control.
  • Visual simulation of a space greenhouse with plant growth progress.
  • Alert systems and failure simulations to test how astronauts might respond to emergencies.
  • Energy tracking to monitor sustainability and power use.

Benefits

  • 🌱 Sustainability: Helps envision future farming methods in extreme environments.
  • 🚀 Space readiness: Demonstrates how astronauts can survive long-term on Mars or the Moon.
  • 🎮 Engagement & learning: Interactive dashboards, glowing indicators, and space-inspired visuals make science exciting and accessible to students and the public.
  • 🔬 Practical research value: Offers a testbed for ideas in agriculture, sustainability, and life-support systems.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers and innovators by combining hope, creativity, and technology. ARCS reflects the UAE’s vision for space exploration and sustainability, showing how desert innovation can reach into deep space. The project highlights:

  • The possibility of self-sustaining habitats beyond Earth.
  • The importance of resilience and safety in extreme environments.
  • A hands-on tool for students and scientists to explore space farming, environmental control, and mission design.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technology Used

  • Frontend/UI: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React (with Mars-inspired design & animations).
  • Hardware Simulation: Arduino/Micro:Bit/Raspberry Pi (for sensors like soil moisture, temperature, humidity).
  • Data Visualization: Chart.js, Recharts, or D3.js for real-time graphs.
  • Cloud/Database: Firebase / MongoDB for logging sensor values and system states.

Creativity & Innovation

ARCS is not just about controlling a greenhouse—it is about creating an experience of living on Mars.

  • Visual mission simulation: glowing indicators, Mars-inspired red-orange UI, and smooth animations to immerse users.
  • Dual operation modes: astronauts can rely on automation or test their skills with manual overrides.
  • Failure testing: built-in simulations of emergencies encourage resilience and creative problem-solving.
  • Inspiration from the UAE desert: connecting local innovation with humanity’s dream of interplanetary living.

Design Considerations

Our team carefully considered:

  • Realism vs accessibility: balancing accurate science with an engaging user experience.
  • Sustainability: tracking energy use to simulate long-term survival.
  • Resilience: adding failure simulations to test how systems recover.
  • User engagement: futuristic design that excites both students and professionals.
  • Scalability: system design that could grow from a classroom demo to a research testbed.

✨ ARCS – Al-Amal Haven is our vision of how hope (Al-Amal), creativity, and technology can turn deserts into gardens—on Earth, Mars, or beyond. 🌍🚀🪐

projectDetails.details:
Meteor Madness is an interactive, real-time web platform designed to track meteors and near-Earth objects (NEOs), simulate their potential impact, and educate the public about space hazards using open NASA data. It visualizes recent meteor events and asteroid approaches on a global map, allowing users to explore trajectories, sizes, and impact probabilities. The platform also features an impact risk simulator that estimates potential damage zones based on size, speed, and entry angle of hypothetical meteors.

The system fetches data from the NASA Near-Earth Object Web Service and Fireball database to provide up-to-date and historical meteor data. Users can input their location to receive alerts if a significant object is predicted to pass nearby. In addition, a crowdsourcing feature lets users report meteor sightings, contributing to citizen science and enhancing global awareness.

The project was developed using React for the frontend, Node.js and Express for the backend, and Firebase for real-time database and authentication. Visualization was achieved using Leaflet.js for 2D mapping and CesiumJS for 3D globe representation. Python was used for trajectory and risk modeling. All datasets were sourced from NASA’s open APIs.

Meteor Madness is creative in its fusion of real-time data, visualization, and public engagement. Instead of just displaying raw information, it transforms scientific datasets into accessible and interactive experiences, fostering awareness and preparedness. The platform emphasizes education by offering engaging infographics, historical insights, and quizzes about meteor science.

While developing the project, our team focused on accessibility, mobile responsiveness, data accuracy, and user engagement. We considered how to present scientific data to a non-expert audience while maintaining scientific integrity. Our goal is to make space data meaningful to people’s daily lives and inspire curiosity and understanding of our dynamic skies.

projectDetails.name: Project AstraRest: Rest Beyond Earth
projectDetails.summary:
Sleeping Orbit Coach transforms NASA’s International Space Station research into an educational wellness tool. For 25 years, astronauts have orbited Earth every 90 minutes, experiencing sixteen sunrises daily — a cycle that disrupts their circadian rhythm. Using NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and Environmental Data App (EDA), the project visualizes how light, temperature, and CO₂ affect sleep in space and on Earth.

The bilingual (English/Arabic) web app provides AI-guided recommendations that teach users how to align daily habits with healthy sleep patterns, inspired by astronaut science. It turns space data into interactive lessons that connect space exploration with wellbeing and education.

By celebrating 25 years of ISS innovation, Sleeping Orbit Coach bridges space research and human health — showing that the science keeping astronauts rested can help us all Rest Beyond Earth.
projectDetails.details:
I.Project Overview

For 25 years, astronauts aboard the International Space Station have experienced life in constant motion — orbiting Earth every 90 minutes, with sixteen sunrises and sunsets a day. That rhythm takes a toll on the

human body, especially on sleep and circadian balance. Sleeping Orbit Coach was born from the

question: What if the same data that helps astronauts rest better in orbit could also help us sleep better on Earth? Our app utilizes NASA’s open ISS sleep and environmental data to educate people on how

light, temperature, and daily routines impact rest. It’s a simple, bilingual (English/Arabic) wellbeing coach that blends space science and health education — turning ISS research into everyday advice for students, educators, and families.

II. Problem Statement

Astronauts struggle to sleep in orbit because their biological clocks lose track of day and night. Here on Earth, millions of people face similar issues due to stress, poor lighting, or irregular schedules. We realized the solutions used by NASA — like light control, CO₂ monitoring, and daily rhythm tracking — could inspire a smarter way to understand sleep for everyone.

III. Our Solution

Sleeping Orbit Coach is an interactive web app that:

• Visualizes 25 years of ISS environmental and sleep data, showing how astronauts adapted to microgravity life.

• Offers AI-powered sleep coaching based on these same principles — helping users build healthier rest habits.

• Simulates orbit conditions, letting users experience “sleeping in space” through light and timing cycles.

• Supports bilingual access (English & Arabic) to make space health more inclusive and educational.

IV. How It Works

We combined open NASA data sources to build a simple, visual, and interactive coach:

• NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Used astronaut sleep, circadian rhythm, and environmental readings.

• Environmental Data App (EDA): Linked CO₂, temperature, and humidity to comfort and alertness levels.

• ISS Benefits for Humanity 2024: Provided real-world examples of space science

improving human health. The app analyzes these patterns and translates them into human-friendly advice like: “Your light exposure today mirrors the ISS sleepcycle — try dimming your room an hour earlier tonight.”

V. Impact

This project celebrates 25 years of the ISS by reminding us that every bit of research up there has value down here.

• For Education: Turns astronaut data into interactive lessons about health, science, and wellbeing.

• For Health: Encourages self-awareness and healthier daily rhythms based on proven space research.

• For Inspiration: Shows students that space science isn’t distant — it’s personal,

practical and possible. Our long-term goal is to merge this coach with wellbeing apps and school health programs, empowering youth to learn through real NASA data.

Factors Considered:

  • Realism of farming simulation using actual NASA data.

projectDetails.name: Astro Atlas
projectDetails.summary:
Ten years ago, the Chelyabinsk meteor struck Earth, injuring over a thousand people and reminding humanity how unprepared we were for celestial threats. AstroAtlas changes that. Developed during the NASA Space Apps Challenge, AstroAtlas is a real-time asteroid tracking and impact simulation platform powered by NASA’s Near-Earth Object APIs. It brings space data to life through interactive 3D visualizations that allow users to explore every asteroid currently approaching Earth.

AstroAtlas calculates the exact time and potential location of impact, estimates the damage in megatons of TNT, and projects casualty ranges based on global population data. By visualizing this information dynamically, the app helps both scientists and students understand the power and consequences of near-Earth objects.

Beyond awareness, AstroAtlas also supports mitigation planning—suggesting defensive strategies and visualizing their outcomes in real time. The experience is immersive, educational, and intuitive, transforming raw NASA data into a visually stunning, accessible platform for everyone. AstroAtlas is equipped with an AI chatbot that helps the scientist retrieve important data, answer knowledge questions on astrophysics, and brainstorm on mitigation strategies.

Built by a passionate team of students brought together through their shared curiosity for space, AstroAtlas bridges the gap between science and imagination—helping humanity predict, prepare, and protect our planet.

projectDetails.name: Exo-Vision : AI Aided Exoplanet Discovery
projectDetails.summary: Exo-Vision is a machine learning model trained to identify potential exoplanets from NASA’s light curve data. The model analyzes subtle dips in starlight intensity to detect transit patterns that suggest the presence of orbiting planets. Using supervised learning on curated datasets of confirmed and false-positive signals, Exo-Vision learns to recognize genuine planetary signatures while also minimizing false detections. To detect vulnerabilities and analyze factors that influence the model’s decision to output whether the planet is an exoplanet or not, adversarial attacks are performed — these are subtle synthetic perturbations or patterns in the dataset that could influence inaccurate output greatly. Exo-Vision addresses the challenge by automating and accelerating exoplanet identification, helping scientists focus on the most promising candidates. By improving accuracy, transparency, and resilience, it strengthens the global effort to discover new worlds beyond our own.
projectDetails.details:
What does Exo-Vision do and how does it work?
Exo-Vision is a machine learning model trained to identify potential exoplanets in NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS light-curve datasets. It processes raw stellar brightness data by cleaning noise and isolating the small, periodic dips caused by planetary transits. The model extracts both time-domain and frequency-domain features using Fourier transforms to capture transit shapes and periodicity. It then classifies each signal as an exoplanet or false positive using a LightGBM classifier. Adversarial attacks are applied to introduce controlled distortions, revealing the model’s sensitivity and improving robustness. The final output is visualized in an interactive dashboard displaying predictions, confidence levels, and feature-based explanations for transparency and interpretability.

What benefits does it have and what impact does it create?
Exo-Vision enhances the accuracy and speed of exoplanet detection, helping researchers focus on genuine candidates and reducing false positives. Its explainable AI design builds trust by making model reasoning visible and interpretable. Beyond scientific accuracy, the project promotes open science and public engagement—allowing students and citizen scientists to explore real NASA data interactively. This combination of precision, transparency, and accessibility advances exoplanet research while inspiring broader participation in space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, and software were used?
Exo-Vision was developed in Python using LightGBM, scikit-learn, Lightkurve, Astropy, NumPy, pandas and matplotlib. Development and testing were carried out in a Jupyter/Conda environment with GitHub for version control and a hybrid CPU/GPU cluster for faster model training and adversarial attack simulations.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?
The project’s creativity lies in combining exoplanet detection with adversarial robustness testing—a novel approach in astrophysical AI applications. By analyzing how small perturbations affect model predictions, Exo-Vision not only improves reliability but also deepens scientific understanding of which features truly drive classification. The team focused on interpretability, scalability across datasets, and the educational value of open, explainable AI to ensure both scientific and social impact.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used AI tools including ChatGPT (3.5, 4.0, o1-mini), Perplexity, and GitHub Copilot for code generation, debugging, learning, and writing refinement.

projectDetails.details:
Project Title: Odyssey Asteroid Impact Simulator

Project Overview:
The Odyssey Asteroid Impact Simulator is an interactive educational tool designed to demonstrate the potential consequences of asteroid impacts on Earth and explore strategies to mitigate these threats. The simulator allows users to select asteroid parameters such as type, diameter, speed, and impact angle, and visualizes the resulting effects in a clear and engaging manner. It combines scientific principles with user interaction to provide a realistic estimation of impact outcomes, including energy released, crater size, potential casualties, and secondary hazards like tsunamis.

Objectives:
The primary goal of the project is to educate users about the science of asteroid impacts and the importance of planetary defense strategies. Users can explore how changes in asteroid size, velocity, and angle influence the severity of impacts. The simulator also emphasizes the effectiveness and limitations of various defense methods, offering a hands-on approach to understanding complex astrophysical concepts.

Features:

Impact Location Selection: Users can click on an interactive world map to choose the hypothetical impact site. The simulator tracks and displays the selected coordinates.

Asteroid Parameters: Users can select pre-defined asteroid types or input custom densities. Sliders control the diameter, speed, and impact angle, affecting the simulated results.

Impact Calculations: The simulator estimates kinetic energy, crater diameter, TNT equivalent, casualties, and tsunami potential using physics-based formulas. Shallow-angle impacts over water generate realistic tsunami estimates.

Defense Strategies: After initiating the simulation, a timed defense window allows users to choose from multiple mitigation methods, including Kinetic Impactor, Gravity Tractor, Nuclear Detonation, and Laser Ablation. Each strategy has a probabilistic chance of success, and successful defenses are explained to enhance understanding.

Safety Guidance: The app provides detailed evacuation and safety recommendations based on the severity of the impact. Advice ranges from minor local precautions to global emergency measures.

Asteroid Dataset: Users can view a curated dataset of near-Earth asteroids, including information on size, speed, approach date, and hazard status.


Educational Value:
The project bridges the gap between theoretical astrophysics and practical application. By interacting with the simulator, users gain insight into the physics of impacts, the importance of planetary defense, and risk management strategies. The simulator also encourages critical thinking, as users must weigh the effectiveness and risks of different defense approaches.

Conclusion:
The Odyssey Asteroid Impact Simulator serves as a comprehensive tool for both learning and engagement. It provides a scientific, visual, and interactive platform to understand the potential consequences of asteroid impacts and the strategies available to protect Earth. By simulating scenarios, users can explore the impact of varying parameters, making it a valuable resource for students, educators, and enthusiasts interested in astronomy and planetary science.

All coding, design, and testing were done by our team, and no NASA logos or mission images were used. AI mainly helped us understand concepts better and write clearer descriptions for our project.

projectDetails.name: Project AstroSweepers
projectDetails.summary:
Our project introduces a Modular Inorganic Waste Recycling System designed for long-term Mars missions. Astronauts are expected to generate over 12,600 kg of inorganic waste during a three-year mission, including plastics, metals, and textiles. Transporting additional supplies or returning waste to Earth is costly and inefficient, making on-site recycling essential.
The system features a shredder, sorting camera, and compactor that work together to process trash into uniform, reusable blocks. The AI-based camera identifies material types and directs them to the correct pathway for compaction. These compressed blocks can be repurposed for tools, construction, or 3D printing feedstock, supporting sustainable living on Mars.
By converting waste into valuable resources, the design minimizes mass, lowers resupply costs, and enhances crew autonomy. It provides a practical solution for closed-loop sustainability—a key requirement for future Mars bases and long-duration missions—and has potential applications for recycling systems on Earth as well.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, the Modular Inorganic Waste Recycling System, is designed to manage and repurpose inorganic waste generated during Mars missions. The system shreds, sorts, and compacts materials such as plastics, metals, and textiles into uniform reusable blocks. Waste enters through an automated shredder, where large debris is broken down. A camera-based sensor system identifies material types using image recognition, directing them onto specific conveyor belts leading to individual compactors. The compactors then compress the materials into dense blocks, which can be reused for construction, tool fabrication, or 3D printing feedstock.

The main benefits include reduced mass waste, minimized resupply needs, and enhanced sustainability. By turning trash into useful resources, it supports a closed-loop system crucial for long-duration missions.

We designed our system using 3D modeling software (TinkerCAD) and then used AI image generation to convert the CAD model into a realistic image. The concept shows creativity through modular design, automation, and adaptability to Martian conditions such as dust exposure and limited power.

Our team considered key factors including energy efficiency, astronaut safety, maintenance simplicity to ensure realistic and mission-ready functionality.
projectDetails.aiReferences: We used AI to transform our initial CAD concept into a realistic 3D visualization of the system operating on the surface of Mars. After designing the layout of the shredder, conveyor belts, and compactor, we used an AI image-generation model to produce accurate, detailed renderings that show how the system would function in a real Martian environment.

projectDetails.name: Gravitational Tractor system for Asteroid Deflection(GRAVITRAX)
projectDetails.summary:
The GRAVITRAX project presents an innovative method of planetary defense using a Charged Dust Amplified Gravity Tractor (CDAGT). Unlike impact-based approaches such as NASA’s DART, which deliver a single, forceful strike, GRAVITRAX relies on a continuous and gentle pull to adjust an asteroid’s trajectory over time. This is achieved by releasing charged nanoparticles between the spacecraft and the asteroid, boosting gravitational attraction and adding electrostatic effects. Together, these forces form a controlled “dust curtain” that gradually shifts the asteroid’s orbit.This method directly addresses threats from hazardous objects like the simulated Impactor-2025 (350 m wide, moving at 19 km/s). A collision of such scale would cause severe destruction, yet GRAVITRAX offers a way to avert disaster without producing dangerous debris. Its adaptable design works for larger asteroids, allows precise long-term corrections, and provides a safe, reversible alternative to explosive impacts.
By merging gravitational science with practical engineering, GRAVITRAX delivers a sustainable, precise, and innovative defense strategy. It advances humanity’s readiness against cosmic hazards and highlights a crucial principle of planetary defense: true security comes from knowledge and early action.
projectDetails.details:
The GRAVITRAX system is a non-destructive asteroid defense method. A spacecraft hovers near a hazardous asteroid releases charged nanoparticles (dust) into space. This dust amplifies gravitational and electrostatic interaction creating a “mass curtain” that gradually shifts the asteroid’s orbit over months or years, preventing a collision.The benefits of this method is summarised below:

1-Safe and reversible – avoids debris or unintended fragmentation.

2-Scalable – suitable even for larger asteroids (300–400 m+).

3-Precise – allows fine control of trajectory.

4-Non-contact – no need for drilling or landing on the asteroid.

5-Long-term effectiveness – ideal with years of preparation.

The intended impact of the project advances in planetary defense by providing a practical solution to protect Earth from catastrophic asteroid It combines gravitational physics, electrostatics, and space engineering while also raising public and scientific about asteroid threats.The tools that used in this project were:

• Simulation: Orbital mechanics software & physics models.

• Languages: Python, Matlab for trajectory and dust modeling.

• Hardware: Spacecraft with ion thrusters & nanoparticle reservoirs.

• Software: Microsoft PowerPoint, LaTeX, AI tools for visuals.

GRAVITRAX is creative because it enhances the proven gravity tractor concept with charged dust amplification.

This hybrid mechanism leverages gravity, electrostatics, and micro momentum transfer to increase effectiveness

without requiring massive spacecraft.Our team had to consider the following parameters:

• Asteroid composition and type (C, S, M, etc.).

• Size, density, and structure of the asteroid.

• Solar wind effects on dust stability.

• Precision and risk of misdirection.

• Timing – requires years of lead time for safe deflection.

node.title: AURORA-Suit
node.excerpt: Autonomous Unpressurized/Pressurized Recon & Oxygen-Reclaiming Astronaut Suit with Onboard Ice Harvesting and Hydrogen Propulsion

projectDetails.name: Project AURORA-Suit
projectDetails.summary:
AURORA-Suit is a self-contained astronaut suit concept that harvests ice from small meteoroids / ice-bearing regolith, extracts water, uses solar-powered electrolysis to split water into O₂ (for life support) and H₂ (propellant), stores and manages both gases, and uses the hydrogen (and optionally locally-produced O₂) in a controlled micro-propulsion system for suit translation and stationkeeping. The suit is designed for short EVA missions where resupply is limited and opportunistic in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) from ice-bearing bodies is possible.

Objective is to provide continuous breathable O₂ for one astronaut by producing oxygen from harvested ice. Produce and store usable hydrogen for on-demand micropropulsion (thrust for translation, attitude control, stationkeeping). Power the entire electrolysis and control stack using flexible high-efficiency solar panels integrated into the suit. Demonstrate a safe, redundant, and modular prototype capable of repeated harvest—electrolyze—thrust cycles.
projectDetails.details:
The AURORA-Suit is a next-generation astronaut suit concept designed to produce its own breathable oxygen and propulsion fuel in space. It works by harvesting ice particles from meteoroids or icy surfaces, extracting and purifying the water, and then using solar-powered electrolysis to split water into oxygen (O₂) and hydrogen (H₂).

  • The oxygen is fed back into the suit’s life-support system to sustain the astronaut.
  • The hydrogen is stored and used to power microthrusters for movement or stationkeeping in zero gravity.
    All operations—harvesting, water purification, electrolysis, gas separation, storage, and propulsion—are controlled by a smart onboard avionics system, powered entirely by flexible solar panels on the suit.

What benefits does it have?

  1. Self-Sustaining Life Support: Reduces reliance on external oxygen tanks, extending EVA (spacewalk) duration.
  2. In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU): Uses locally available ice from meteors or planetary surfaces, minimizing resupply needs.
  3. Lightweight Efficiency: Eliminates the need to carry large oxygen and fuel reserves.
  4. Safety & Redundancy: Continuous O₂ generation provides a backup in emergencies if primary life-support fails.
  5. Mobility Enhancement: Hydrogen microthrusters allow astronauts to maneuver freely in microgravity environments.

Problem / Challenge

  • Limited onboard consumables for long-duration or remote EVAs.
  • Need to avoid heavy, bulky life-support tanks for extended sorties.
  • Achieve reliable, safe harvesting and handling of cryogenic/flammable gases (H₂) in a mobile suit with limited volume and power.
  • Produce enough O₂ at a practical power and time budget using only suit-mounted solar panels.
  • Ensure propulsion uses hydrogen safely without endangering astronaut life support.

Solution

  1. Ice Harvesting Module (IHM)
    • A compact, articulated scoop + drill + heated nozzle unit mounted on the forearm and shoulder. For fragile meteor fragments: a scoop and harpoon; for compacted ice/regolith: a small rotary corer (needle drill) with local resistive heating to release volatile ice into a capture chamber.
    • Collected ice is transferred into a Thermal Sublimation & Condensation Module that gently warms samples in vacuum, captures the vapor, and re-condenses it into liquid water inside a small insulated tank.
    • Micron filtration + UV sterilizer + particulate trap to remove dust and contaminants before electrolysis. A small buffer tank (~1–2 L) provides continuous feed to the electrolyzer.
    • Flexible, high-efficiency photovoltaic cells laminated onto upper torso and backpack. MPPT (maximum power point tracking) and battery buffer (Li-ion or Li-metal hybrid) sized to supply electrolysis surges and reserve power for life support and avionics.
    • A PEM (Proton Exchange Membrane) or alkaline electrolyzer optimized for mass & efficiency, with gas separators, humidifiers, and pressure control. It splits water into O₂ and H₂; oxygen is routed through the life-support system while hydrogen is routed to a pressurized tank for propulsion or buffer uses.
    • Two small composite pressure vessels: one for O₂ (medical-grade, low-pressure feed) and one for H₂ (high-pressure composite vessel with burst/discharge protection). Redundant pressure relief valves, gas sensors, and a micro PLC for flow control. O₂ feed to the suit is regulated by standard life-support regulators.
    • Primary: A hydrogen-powered microthruster cluster (multiple vectored cold/hot gas thrusters). Two candidate modes:
      • Electrothermal microthruster: H₂ is resistively or inductively heated and expelled (moderate Isp). Safe, low-complexity.
      • Combustion microthruster: H₂ combusted with a controlled amount of O₂ to produce higher thrust/Isp (requires strict safety isolation between breathing supply and combustion loop).
    • Thruster pluming reroutes used reaction products (if combusted) or vents them away from suit intake.
    • IMU, LIDAR / optical flow for translation control, gas sensors (H₂, O₂, CO₂), thermal sensors, and an autonomous controller to prevent propulsion when suit seals/pressure or oxygen levels are compromised. Emergency jettison valves and passive safety (blast panels) incorporated.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is integrated into the AURORA-Suit to optimize performance, safety, and resource management. The suit’s onboard AI control module continuously analyzes sensor data to make autonomous decisions that support the astronaut in real time.

1. Smart Resource Management

  • AI algorithms monitor the levels of ice collected, water purified, oxygen produced, and hydrogen stored.
  • Using predictive analytics, the AI adjusts electrolysis rates and solar power allocation to balance the astronaut’s oxygen demand with propulsion requirements.
  • Machine learning models predict when resources will run low and automatically schedule harvesting or regeneration cycles.

2. Autonomous Safety Monitoring

  • The AI system constantly checks gas pressure, temperature, and leak sensors to detect abnormalities.
  • If hydrogen leakage or oxygen imbalance is detected, the AI instantly isolates valves and switches to backup systems.
  • A built-in fault detection and recovery (FDR) module ensures that the suit can maintain life support even during sensor or system failure.

3. Navigation and Propulsion Control

  • Using computer vision and AI-based navigation, the suit identifies nearby ice-rich meteoroids suitable for harvesting.
  • The AI autopilot controls microthrusters by calculating the most fuel-efficient trajectories in microgravity for small directional corrections or station-keeping.
  • Reinforcement learning algorithms fine-tune propulsion efficiency over time based on performance feedback.

4. Energy Optimization

  • The AI dynamically manages solar power distribution between electrolysis, life-support systems, and propulsion.
  • It predicts sunlight availability (based on position and rotation of the astronaut or object) and prioritizes critical systems during low-power conditions.

5. Human–AI Interaction

  • The astronaut communicates with the AI assistant through voice commands and a heads-up display (HUD).
    • “Oxygen level optimal at 96% efficiency.”
    • “Hydrogen storage nearing capacity—diverting power to electrolysis cooldown.”
    • “Incoming sunlight angle reduced—switching to power-saving mode.”

AI Tools and Technologies Used

  • Python with OpenAI API – for natural language processing and intelligent decision-making.
  • TensorFlow / PyTorch – for predictive models (oxygen demand forecasting, energy optimization).
  • OpenCV – for visual detection of ice deposits on meteoroids.
  • Arduino/Python integration – to control electrolysis, valves, and propulsion hardware based on AI outputs.

Impact of AI in the Project

By integrating AI, the AURORA-Suit becomes a self-aware and adaptive life-support system, capable of:

  • Operating autonomously in unpredictable environments.
  • Extending mission duration without constant ground control input.
  • Enhancing astronaut safety through early anomaly detection and automated decision-making.
  • Paving the way for intelligent, sustainable, and human-centered exploration systems for long-duration missions on asteroids, the Moon, and Mars.

The SpaceBio Knowledge Engine is an AI-powered research assistant designed to help scientists, educators, and students explore the effects of spaceflight and microgravity on living organisms.

Developed using FastAPI (backend), React (frontend), and OpenAI’s embedding models, it transforms scattered research papers into a searchable, intelligent database. Users can enter queries in plain language—such as “mice space missions” or “plant growth in microgravity”.

The project addresses the challenge of navigating vast scientific literature in the space biology domain by enabling faster, more intuitive discovery of insights. Its importance lies in supporting future space exploration, biological research, and education—bridging the gap between scientific data and accessible knowledge through the power of AI.
projectDetails.details:
The SpaceBio Knowledge Engine is an intelligent web-based research assistant that helps users explore and understand the effects of spaceflight and microgravity on biological systems. Using AI-powered semantic search and natural language processing (NLP), the system enables users to type research queries in plain language—such as “mice space missions” or “plant growth in microgravity”—and instantly retrieves the most relevant scientific studies along with concise AI-generated summaries.

How it works:
The backend, built with FastAPI, handles AI model integration and data processing. The frontend, created with React and Vite, provides an intuitive user interface for interactive exploration. The system computes similarity between user queries and stored research documents, delivering meaningful, context-aware results.

Benefits and Impact:
SpaceBio simplifies scientific discovery by turning complex, scattered research data into accessible insights. It saves researchers and students time, supports scientific innovation, and strengthens educational engagement in space biology and AI.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript
  • Frameworks: FastAPI, React
  • AI Models: OpenAI Embeddings
  • Database: SQLite
  • Hosting: locally

Creativity and Considerations:
The project combines AI, education, and space science into a unified interactive tool. It was designed with accessibility, simplicity, and scientific relevance in mind—bridging the gap between research data and user-friendly AI interaction.

projectDetails.name: Project Beyond Infinity
projectDetails.summary:
We developed ExoDetectAI is an end-to-end machine learning framework for automated exoplanet validation across NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. The system trains and evaluates state-of-the-art models—including XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and MLP—on real NASA catalogs to classify candidates as Confirmed Planets, Candidates, or False Positives. For TESS, we addressed class imbalance by downsampling Planet Candidates (PC) to 2,700 samples, while preserving confirmed planets and false alarms to reflect realistic vetting conditions. Our models achieve 93% accuracy on Kepler, 92.8% on K2, and 76% on TESS—performance that aligns with the increasing difficulty of newer, noisier TESS data.
ExoDetectAI tackles the core challenge of modern exoplanet science: data deluge. TESS alone has generated over 6,000 candidates, far exceeding human vetting capacity. By automating initial screening with physics-informed ML, our tool prioritizes high-value targets for follow-up, reduces false positives by over 60%, and preserves >85% of true planets—accelerating discovery while optimizing telescope time.

This work is important because it democratizes exoplanet research. Our open, reproducible pipeline—complete with pre-trained models and evaluation metrics—empowers citizen scientists, students, and researchers to participate in discovery. In the era of JWST and future missions like Plato, scalable, transparent AI vetting it’s essential to unlock the next generation of Earth-like worlds.

So in the last, we trained ML models on each dataset, Kepler, K2, and TESS. The impact is to help astronomers stop the tedious process of vetting the light-curves manually or by writing code. The Space Zoom Explorer is a self-contained interactive web application that demonstrates how massive NASA image and video datasets can be explored in an engaging and user-friendly way. Future Improvements may include advanced zoom and pan functionality for gigapixel imagery, saving/exporting labels, integration of additional datasets from Earth, Moon, and galaxies, and AI-powered feature detection to automatically identify craters, dust storms, or other phenomena.

projectDetails.name: Project Big Vision
projectDetails.summary:
Our project leverages NASA’s open exoplanet datasets from Kepler, K2, and TESS to develop an AI-powered classification system that distinguishes confirmed exoplanets from false positives. Using advanced machine learning models such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. We built a robust pipeline that cleans, aligns, and analyzes astrophysical parameters such as orbital period, transit depth, duration, and planetary radius.

This system addresses the challenge by automating exoplanet validation, a process that traditionally requires years of manual data analysis. By optimizing for Precision-Recall (PR-AUC), our models deliver over 90% accuracy across multiple datasets, enabling astronomers to prioritize the most promising candidates faster.

Beyond the models, we designed an interactive interface that visualizes predictions and insights, bridging data science and space research. This innovation accelerates exoplanet discovery, enhances scientific accessibility, and supports NASA’s broader mission to expand our understanding of worlds beyond Earth.
projectDetails.details:
Overview

Our project focuses on building an artificial intelligence and machine learning pipeline capable of automatically detecting exoplanets from NASA’s publicly available datasets. Traditionally, the identification of exoplanets has relied heavily on manual analysis by astrophysicists, a process that is both time-intensive and limited in scalability. By training models on datasets from the Kepler, K2, and TESS missions, we sought to replicate and improve upon this process by enabling automatic classification of candidates as exoplanets or non-exoplanets. The pipeline operates through several stages: preprocessing and cleaning of raw datasets, training of machine learning models, hyperparameter optimization, and evaluation using advanced metrics. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were trained and compared, with Random Forest and XGBoost undergoing hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV to maximize performance. The system outputs candidate classifications with associated probability scores, which are then visualized in an interactive environment to make the results accessible. 

Benefits

The benefits of this system are both practical and scientific. On the practical side, it dramatically accelerates the process of exoplanet candidate assessment, allowing thousands of observations to be classified in minutes rather than weeks. Scientifically, it supports the discovery process by highlighting the most promising candidates for verification while also offering transparent evaluation through confusion matrices, precision-recall curves, and PR-AUC scores. By automating repetitive aspects of candidate validation, our project allows researchers to allocate their time toward interpretation and exploration. Furthermore, by integrating the workflow into an interactive interface, we open up opportunities for students, educators, and the general public to engage with real exoplanetary science in an accessible way. 

Tools

The intended impact of this project is to accelerate discovery while democratizing access to space science. For researchers, the tool provides a scalable, high-accuracy system that can quickly surface potential exoplanets from large datasets. For educators and non-experts, the interface offers a gateway to understanding how AI can be applied to astrophysics, making complex methods like gradient boosting or hyperparameter tuning understandable through visualizations. By making the process transparent and interactive, the project fosters trust and curiosity around the role of AI in scientific exploration. 

Creativity

The technical development relied primarily on Python and widely used machine learning libraries. The models were built and evaluated with scikit-learn and XGBoost, while data preprocessing was conducted using pandas and numpy. Evaluation metrics such as precision-recall curves and PR-AUC were implemented through scikit-learn’s metrics module, and model persistence was achieved with joblib. The training environment was Google Colab, chosen for its GPU/CPU resources and accessibility. Visualization and interface design were implemented in Base44, which allowed us to create a structured, multi-page web application that integrates candidate tables, bar charts, and PR curves. Since Base44 does not natively support CSV uploads, we embedded data directly into JSON, ensuring that all results displayed were real outputs from our trained models. The project distinguishes itself through creativity in combining technical rigor with interactivity. We did not restrict our work to a single dataset or a single model; instead, we designed a unified framework that integrates multiple NASA missions and enables side-by-side model comparison. By moving beyond static charts and embedding real outputs into Base44, we transformed abstract performance metrics into an interactive user experience. Users can not only view model results but also explore how predictions vary across datasets, making the project equally valuable as a research aid and as an educational tool. 

Considerations

Throughout the process, we carefully considered issues such as data imbalance, computational cost, and user accessibility. Exoplanet datasets are skewed toward positive cases, so we optimized models using PR-AUC rather than accuracy alone, as this metric is more sensitive to imbalanced data. Hyperparameter tuning was designed to maximize predictive power while avoiding overfitting. For the interactive component, we prioritized simplicity, ensuring that novices could explore the outputs without technical knowledge, while researchers could still rely on the validity of the models. Because live retraining is computationally intensive, we balanced realism with practicality by precomputing results for large datasets while leaving the possibility of lightweight retraining with simpler models such as Logistic Regression. This balance allowed us to demonstrate interactivity without compromising the realism of our results. 

Summary

In summary, our project provides a practical, scalable, and interactive AI-based framework for exoplanet detection. By leveraging machine learning models on Kepler, K2, and TESS data, optimizing performance with hyperparameter tuning, and integrating outputs into a web-based interactive system, we met the challenge of automating exoplanet classification while ensuring transparency and accessibility. The result is a tool that not only accelerates the work of astrophysicists but also inspires broader audiences to engage with the possibilities of AI in space exploration.

Our models; Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were trained and tuned using NASA’s open datasets from the Kepler, TESS, and K2 missions. These algorithms learned from thousands of data points (such as orbital periods, transit durations, and light-curve features) to identify patterns that distinguish true exoplanets from false detections.

AI was also used to analyze model performance, generate Precision–Recall Curves, and compute PR-AUC scores, helping us visualize how accurately the models classified candidates. All code and results were generated programmatically, no AI-generated images, text, or NASA visuals were altered or used.

projectDetails.name: Project Breathe Clean
projectDetails.summary:
AirSafe Scheduler: Smart Activity Planning for Better Breathing

  I developed a web-based air quality monitoring and activity scheduling system designed to help individuals with respiratory conditions make informed decisions about outdoor activities. The application integrates real-time air quality data from the World Air Quality Index (WAQI) API and weather data from Open-Meteo to provide comprehensive environmental insights.

 The core innovation is an intelligent schedule analysis engine that compares users' planned outdoor activities against 7-day air quality forecasts. Using activity-specific AQI thresholds (based on exercise intensity), the system identifies potentially harmful exposures and recommends safer alternative time slots. Users can build weekly schedules, receive risk assessments (safe/caution/unsafe), and reschedule activities with one click.

  This tool is crucial for the growing population affected by air pollution-related health issues. By proactively preventing exposure during poor air quality periods, it empowers users to maintain active lifestyles while protecting their respiratory health. The system transforms reactive air quality monitoring into proactive health management, making environmental data actionable for daily life decisions.
projectDetails.details:
My application is a full-stack web solution combining real-time air quality monitoring with intelligent activity scheduling. The system operates through three main components:

1. Data Integration Layer (Backend - Python/FastAPI)

The backend fetches and aggregates environmental data from multiple sources:

- WAQI (World Air Quality Index) API: Provides real-time AQI measurements and 7-day forecasts for ground-level pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, O3,

NO2, SO2, CO)

- Open-Meteo API: Supplies comprehensive weather data including temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, and heat index

- Data is cached for 1 hour to optimize API usage and improve response times

- FastAPI handles asynchronous requests, enabling parallel data fetching for superior performance

2. Interactive Dashboard (Frontend - HTML/CSS/JavaScript)

The user interface presents environmental data through an intuitive, collapsible panel system:

- Left Panel: Displays real-time air quality metrics categorized by pollutant type (gaseous vs particulate matter), current weather conditions, and a 7-day forecast with color-coded AQI indicators

- Right Panel: Shows city-specific information with quick-switch functionality between Dubai, New Delhi, New York, and London

- 7-Day Forecast Grid: Visual representation of air quality trends with date-specific AQI values and health categories

3. Smart Scheduling Engine

The core innovation of our system analyzes user activities against forecasted air quality:

- Users build weekly schedules specifying activity name, time slots, location (indoor/outdoor), and intensity level (low/moderate/high)

- The analysis algorithm applies intensity-specific AQI thresholds:

- High intensity (running, sports): Safe ≤50, Warning ≤75, Unsafe >75

- Moderate intensity (cycling, jogging): Safe ≤75, Warning ≤100, Unsafe >100

- Low intensity (walking, yoga): Safe ≤100, Warning ≤150, Unsafe >150

- The system categorizes each outdoor activity and generates personalized recommendations

- For risky activities, it identifies safer alternative time slots within the week, checking for scheduling conflicts

- One-click rescheduling allows users to instantly move activities to recommended safer times

Benefits

Health Protection

- Proactive risk assessment prevents harmful pollutant exposure during outdoor activities

- Intensity-based thresholds ensure recommendations match individual exertion levels

- Particularly valuable for individuals with asthma, COPD, cardiovascular conditions, or other respiratory sensitivities

User Empowerment

- Transforms complex environmental data into actionable daily decisions

- Eliminates guesswork about when it's safe to exercise outdoors

- Supports maintaining active lifestyles while prioritizing health

Convenience

- Automated analysis removes the burden of manually checking forecasts

- Schedule persistence in browser localStorage enables ongoing weekly planning

- City-switching capability supports travelers and multi-location users

Educational Value

- Raises awareness about air quality impacts on health

- Teaches users to recognize dangerous pollution levels

- Promotes informed decision-making about outdoor activity timing

Intended Impact

Immediate Impact:

- Enable individuals with respiratory conditions to safely plan outdoor activities

- Reduce emergency room visits and medication usage related to air quality-triggered health episodes

- Improve quality of life for millions affected by urban air pollution

Long-term Impact:

- Contribute to public health data by demonstrating correlation between activity timing and health outcomes

- Support urban planning initiatives by highlighting areas and times with consistently poor air quality

- Foster community awareness about environmental health risks

- Potentially integrate with fitness apps, school systems, and workplace wellness programs

Scalability:

- Current implementation supports 4 cities; architecture allows easy expansion to hundreds of locations

- API-driven design enables integration with wearable devices and smart home systems

- Future enhancements could include personalized health profiles, historical exposure tracking, and community-shared schedules

Technology Stack

APIs:

- WAQI API: Real-time and forecast air quality data with token authentication

- Open-Meteo API: Free weather data service (no authentication required)

Development Tools:

- Virtual Environment (venv): Isolated Python dependencies

- Git: Version control

- GitHub: Repository hosting and collaboration

Creative Elements

1. Intensity-Based Thresholds

Rather than using generic "unhealthy for sensitive groups" categories, we developed activity-specific thresholds recognizing that

high-intensity exercise demands more air intake and thus requires stricter air quality standards.

2. Conflict-Aware Rescheduling

Our algorithm doesn't just find safer times—it checks for scheduling overlaps and only suggests truly available slots, preventing double-booking.

3. Dual-Panel Interface

The collapsible left panel design maximizes information density while maintaining usability, allowing users to focus on either environmental data or city information as needed.

4. Multi-Source Data Fusion

Combining air quality and weather data provides holistic context—high temperatures with poor air quality create compounding health risks that our system highlights through heat index integration.

5. Date-Synced Scheduling

Unlike generic weekly planners, our schedule builder dynamically matches the exact dates from the forecast, eliminating confusion about which forecast day corresponds to which scheduled activity.

6. Visual Risk Communication

Color-coded badges (High Risk, Caution, safe) provide instant visual recognition of danger levels, supplementing numerical AQI data for faster decision-making.

Design Considerations

User-Centric Design:

- Assumed users may not understand AQI scales, so I provided clear category labels (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy, etc.)

- Included activity examples (e.g., "Morning Run, Football Practice") to guide users in creating meaningful schedules

- Used emoji indicators for quick visual scanning

Performance Optimization:

- Implemented 1-hour cache to balance data freshness with API rate limits

- Used parallel async requests to fetch WAQI and weather data simultaneously

- Minimized frontend dependencies to ensure fast page loads even on slow connections

(Note - We were not able to add any of the nasa data into the project and instead used them as resources in our project)

Our project BrineLight is an interactive digital experience that explores the hidden biodiversity of remote, lesser-known islands around the world. Developed using Chronochrono, the platform allows users to journey through a series of unique ecosystems, uncovering endangered species, extinct fauna and the environmental effects of UV radiation and space-based influences on island habitats.

We developed this project to address the challenge of environmental awareness and data accessibility. By spotlighting these “hidden gem” islands we aim to bring attention to critical ecosystems often overlooked in global conservation efforts. Our platform combines science, storytelling, and design to create an engaging, educational experience that encourages users to think critically about biodiversity, climate change and the future of our planet.

This project is important because it not only highlights urgent ecological issues but also presents them in a creative, interactive format that is accessible to a wide audience. It empowers users to explore, learn, and connect with the natural world in a meaningful way—ultimately inspiring action and innovation for a better tomorrow.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, BrineLight, is a creative exploration of Earth’s “hidden gem” islands: remote, often overlooked ecosystems that hold unique biodiversity, endangered species, and critical environmental data. Through our interactive app built using Chronochrono we guide users on a scientific and visual journey to uncover the ecological significance of these islands and the threats they face, including UV radiation and space-related impacts on their ecosystems.

BrineLight works like a digital expedition: users explore different islands, learn about extinct or endangered species and dive into data-driven insights about marine life, climate effects and human impact. It blends storytelling, science and design to create an engaging and educational experience.

The benefits of our project are both environmental and educational. It raises awareness about critical conservation issues while also promoting curiosity and scientific thinking. Our intended impact is to inspire action and dialogue around protecting Earth's lesser-known ecosystems before it’s too late.

We used Chronochrono to build the experience—an intuitive, no-code platform that allowed us to focus on content, design, and storytelling. Our team combined research, creative writing, data visualization, and user-friendly design to bring the project to life.

What makes BrineLight truly creative is how it fuses art, science and technology. Instead of just presenting facts, we crafted an immersive journey that lets users feel like they’re part of the mission. We considered accessibility, visual clarity, and emotional impact—ensuring the experience is both informative and memorable.

projectDetails.summary:
AirLens — Sharjah’s Real-Time Air Quality Explorer
AirLens blends data, design, and purpose into one sleek dashboard that tracks real-time air quality across the UAE and major global cities. Built using Streamlit, it combines ground-level data from OpenAQ with live weather metrics and satellite-based insights to show accurate AQI readings and pollutant levels. What makes AirLens stand out is how it transforms raw scientific data into something people can actually see and understand. It bridges local and global perspectives—spotlighting UAE’s air quality while keeping a worldwide view. The polished UI merges clarity with creativity, balancing scientific accuracy and visual storytelling.

AirLens isn’t just a tech demo—it’s a small step toward healthier cities and informed citizens. It represents a thoughtful mix of science, data, and technology, with an artistic touch that connects communities through awareness.
projectDetails.details:
🌬️ Project Details — Sharjah Air Lens

Sharjah Air Lens is a real-time air quality and weather monitoring dashboard designed to help communities better understand the air they breathe. The app integrates ground-based OpenAQ data with live weather feeds from Open-Meteo and a simulated NASA TEMPO satellite proxy, providing a unified and interactive view of environmental health.

It analyzes pollutants like PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, SO₂, O₃, and CO, then calculates the Air Quality Index (AQI) using EPA standards. The app automatically adjusts its search radius to find the nearest available data, ensuring consistent readings even when local sensors are sparse.

Developed in Python using Streamlit, Plotly, Folium, and Earth Engine APIs, it blends scientific accuracy with a sleek, dark-themed UI to make complex environmental data simple and engaging.

The project aims to raise awareness, support smart city initiatives, and inspire data-driven climate action. Its creative blend of science, data, and technology aligns with NASA Space Apps’ goals of local impact and global connection — making air quality insight accessible to everyone.

We developed a Mixed-Media Educational Video (our MVP) that shows the real impact of solar flares and CMEs on pilots. We explain how these events increase radiation exposure on polar flights and threaten crucial GPS and radio comms.

By integrating visuals from NASA models like NAIRAS and instruments like ARMAS, our video demonstrates how airlines can use predictive data to guide pilots to safe altitudes or routes. This translates complex stellar science into a simple, actionable safety protocol, making air travel safer for crew and passengers.
projectDetails.details:
Core Problem

Solar flares release high-energy particles and magnetic fields that can:

- Disrupt communication and navigation systems

- Damage power grids

- Expose astronauts and high-altitude flights to radiation

Focus Area: Human beings

We are focusing on protecting humans, especially astronauts and high-altitude air travelers,

from radiation caused by solar flares. During solar storms, the increase in energetic

particles can pose serious health risks, including radiation sickness and long-term DNA

damage. Our goal is to develop better protection, prediction, and safety measures to ensure

human survival in space and during air travel.

projectDetails.name: Crash 'n' Course
projectDetails.summary: Our project takes you on a journey through space, where humanity faces two sides of the same cosmic story. On one side, Earth is under siege from meteors, and players must act fast to protect their home. This becomes “Asteriod Assult” a thrilling, reflex-driven game where every click destroys a meteor—reminding us that even small actions can matter in the face of overwhelming odds. But the story doesn’t end there. Beyond the chaos of the game lies “Asteroid Impact Explorer,” a space where science is in the spotlight. Here, users step into the role of researcher, entering real data—size, speed, angle, material, and location—to see what would happen if an asteroid truly hit Earth. The results are powerful, often devastating, showing the scale of energy released, the size of the crater, and the chain of global consequences. Together, these two modes tell one complete story: space is wonderful and beautiful, but it is also dangerous. By blending play with science, Crash ‘n’ Course transforms learning into an adventure—one that entertains and educates. It makes us think about our fragile place in the universe.
projectDetails.details:
Demo Video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FNhPj7cB19F3FI4TA4rO1VHNRAJwhDtJ/view?usp=sharing

🔹 What does it do or how does it work?

Crash ‘n’ Course is an immersive and interactive project designed to bring the wonders — and dangers — of asteroid impacts to life. The system operates in two distinct modes, merging entertainment with scientific exploration

  1. Game Mode 🎮 – In this fast-paced experience, Earth faces a barrage of asteroids hurtling through space. Players take on the role of a planetary defender, tasked with destroying incoming asteroids before they collide with Earth. This mode transforms the serious concept of planetary defense into an engaging and thrilling challenge that highlights the importance of swift action and strategy.
  2. Explore Mode 🔬 – In this mode, users step into the role of a space scientist. By adjusting parameters such as asteroid size, velocity, impact angle, material composition, and impact location, they can observe how each variable influences the magnitude of the collision, crater formation, and overall impact energy.

🔹 What benefits does it have?

  • Education & Awareness – Demonstrates real-world astrophysics concepts through interactive simulations, fostering a deeper understanding of asteroid behavior and impact science.
  • Engagement Through Play – Converts complex planetary defense mechanisms into an accessible and enjoyable experience.
  • Simulation Power – Provides a sandbox environment for testing “what if” scenarios, helping users visualize how small changes in parameters can lead to drastically different outcomes.
  • Public Outreach – Designed as an educational outreach tool that can be used in classrooms, museums, and exhibitions to inspire curiosity about space and planetary science.

🔹 What is the intended impact of the project?

The primary goal of Crash ‘n’ Course is to bridge the gap between science and the public through an experience that is both entertaining and intellectually enriching. The project aims to:

  • Promote global awareness about asteroid risks and planetary defense preparedness.
  • Spark curiosity and interest in astronomy, physics, and computational science among learners of all ages.
  • Serve as an interactive educational tool that allows users to visualize scientific concepts rather than merely read about them.
  • Encourage critical and creative thinking, showing how each scientific variable contributes to real-world consequences.

🔹 What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Python – Core programming language, powering both simulation and logic.
  • Pygame – Framework used to build both the Game Mode and Explore Mode, enabling real-time physics visualization and interactivity.
  • Streamlit – Used for the main menu interface, ensuring a clean, intuitive, and accessible starting point for users.
  • GitHub – For version control, collaboration, and maintaining a structured and transparent development process.

🔹 How is your project creative?

Crash ‘n’ Course redefines the way people learn about space science. It unites the excitement of gaming with the analytical depth of scientific exploration — transforming abstract concepts into something tangible, interactive, and visually stunning.

  • Seamlessly integrates fun and education, creating an experience that is both thrilling and enlightening.
  • Translates complex astrophysical phenomena into interactive visuals that users can manipulate and observe in real time.
  • Encourages experiential learning — empowering users to explore, experiment, and understand through discovery rather than instruction.
  • Blends storytelling, science, and simulation into a single, cohesive experience.

🔹 What factors did your team consider?

During development, the team emphasized a balance between scientific accuracy, engagement, and usability:

  • Accessibility – Ensuring the project runs smoothly with minimal setup, making it widely usable across systems.
  • User Engagement – Crafting captivating visuals and sound effects to enhance immersion.
  • Scientific Accuracy – Incorporating realistic impact physics and parameters inspired by NASA and ESA research data.
  • User Experience – Designing clear layouts, smooth transitions, and an intuitive interface through Streamlit and Pygame.
  • Dual Functionality – Building a unified platform that supports both adrenaline-filled gameplay and thoughtful exploration — blending fun, learning, and imagination into one experience.

projectDetails.name: Meteor Impact-Sim
projectDetails.summary: The Meteor Impact Simulation System is a data-driven project that models and visualizes the potential effects of meteor impacts on Earth. It processes meteor data, including size, speed, and impact location, to estimate the scale of destruction, affected areas, and possible casualties. Developed using Python, HTML, and JavaScript, the system provides an interactive simulation that allows users to visualize various impact scenarios. The project aims to assist scientists and decision-makers in assessing potential risks, planning disaster mitigation strategies, and increasing public awareness about meteor-related threats through an educational and research-oriented platform.
projectDetails.details:
The Meteor Impact-Sim project is an intelligent simulation system designed to model and visualize the potential effects of meteor impacts on Earth. By using past data, scientific resources, and user input, the system calculates the possible scale of destruction, the geographical areas that would be affected, and even the estimated casualties from a meteor strike. Through an interactive web interface, users can explore different impact scenarios and gain a deeper understanding of how catastrophic such an event could be. The project integrates NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) API along with USGS datasets to ensure data accuracy, while its backend is built using Python and JavaScript for calculations and processing, and its frontend employs HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for visualization.

The primary benefit of this project lies in its accessibility and practical application. Meteor strikes, although rare, can have devastating consequences, and there are currently few user-friendly tools that allow scientists, students, or policymakers to explore these scenarios. Meteor Impact-Sim helps bridge this gap by providing an interactive platform that not only enhances scientific understanding but also supports emergency response teams and government agencies in disaster preparedness. By simulating evacuation strategies, early warning systems, and resource allocation needs, the project demonstrates how data-driven insights can contribute to saving lives and reducing risks.

The intended impact of this simulation is twofold: to serve as a foundation for planetary defense research and to raise awareness about the importance of preparedness in the face of global threats. Creativity is central to the project, as it combines real scientific datasets with visualization techniques that make complex simulations both engaging and educational. The team carefully considered accuracy, usability, and public awareness, ensuring the system is not just a technical demonstration but also a valuable tool for decision-makers and the general public. Ultimately, Meteor Impact-Sim highlights how technology and creativity can work together to transform raw data into actionable insights that can guide future disaster risk management and planetary defense strategies.

projectDetails.name: Project ClearSky Coders
projectDetails.summary:
Our team developed ClearSky AI, a web-based application that forecasts air quality by combining NASA’s TEMPO mission data, ground-based air quality measurements, and weather datasets. The app uses machine learning models to analyze and predict air quality trends, providing real-time updates and alerts to communities and decision-makers.

The platform presents information through interactive maps, charts, and traffic-light indicators that make complex data easy to understand. Users receive timely notifications of poor air quality events, helping them make healthier choices, while policymakers and researchers can leverage the forecasts to design effective interventions.

This project directly addresses the challenge by making TEMPO’s revolutionary air quality data accessible, actionable, and scalable through cloud-based infrastructure. By transforming raw satellite data into insights, ClearSky AI empowers communities, improves public health decision-making, and advances NASA’s mission to monitor and reduce exposure to harmful pollutants.
projectDetails.details:
What Our Project Does

Our project, ClearSky AI, is a web-based forecasting app that integrates NASA’s TEMPO satellite data, ground-based air quality measurements, and meteorological datasets to provide real-time and short-term air quality forecasts. The system uses machine learning models to detect patterns in pollutants such as NO₂, ozone, PM, and aerosols, predicting poor air quality events before they occur.

Users can interact with an intuitive web dashboard that displays color-coded maps, charts, and forecast indicators. The app also includes a notification system that alerts users when air quality is predicted to reach unhealthy levels.

Benefits and Impact

  • For citizens: Offers clear, real-time air quality information so people can plan outdoor activities safely.
  • For public health officials: Provides data-driven forecasts that can inform health advisories and emergency responses.
  • For researchers and policymakers: Demonstrates the power of NASA’s TEMPO data by making it accessible and actionable for everyday decisions.

By improving awareness and response, our project supports cleaner air and healthier communities while showcasing how space data can be transformed into real-world impact.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python (data processing, ML), JavaScript/React (frontend), FastAPI/Flask (backend).
  • Data Sources: NASA TEMPO, AirNow & OpenAQ (ground stations), NASA MERRA-2 & IMERG (weather/precipitation).
  • Libraries & Tools: Pandas, Xarray, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch (ML), Prophet (forecasting), Mapbox/Leaflet (interactive maps).
  • Cloud & Scalability: Deployed on AWS/GCP using Docker; designed to scale for larger datasets and collaborative workflows.
  • Visualization: NASA Worldview integration for satellite layers.

Creativity & Design

  • Simplified complex satellite data into easy-to-read traffic light indicators (Green = Good, Yellow = Moderate, Red = Hazardous).
  • Designed a scalable pipeline that can grow from a city-level prototype to a national/global forecasting tool.
  • Combined real-time alerts + interactive visualization to make air quality data not just informative, but actionable.

Key Factors Considered

  • Accessibility: Non-scientists should easily understand TEMPO data through our interface.
  • Accuracy: Integrated ground-based data for validation of satellite observations.
  • Scalability: Built using cloud-friendly tools (Xarray, Docker, APIs).
  • Impact: Focused on improving public health decisions with space-based data.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Our project, ClearSky AI, incorporates Artificial Intelligence in multiple areas:

  1. Data Analysis & Forecasting
    • We applied machine learning models (e.g., LSTM, Prophet, Random Forest) to predict air quality trends using NASA TEMPO data, ground-based air quality measurements, and meteorological data.
    • AI was essential for identifying temporal patterns, correlations between pollutants, and producing short-term forecasts.
    • We used AI-assisted preprocessing tools to clean and harmonize heterogeneous datasets (satellite + ground sensors + weather). This improved accuracy and reduced noise.
    • AI writing tools (like ChatGPT) were used to draft and refine project descriptions, summaries, and team documentation. All technical contributions (data processing, ML models, code, and visualizations) were original work by our team.
    • AI-powered design tools were used to generate concept logos and visualization mockups. All generated images were watermarked to clearly indicate AI generation.

projectDetails.name: Project Cloud Six
projectDetails.summary: SkyCast Dashboard is a desktop application that helps users estimate the likelihood of extreme or uncomfortable weather conditions, such as very hot, cold, windy, or wet days for any location and date they select (up to six months ahead). Using NASA Earth observation data, the app allows individuals and organizations to make more informed decisions for outdoor planning, whether for vacations, field research, agriculture, or events based on long-term climate trends and environmental variables.
projectDetails.details:
Project Motivation and Purpose:

Most weather apps only forecast up to 10 days. SkyCast extends this by analyzing historical NASA climate data to estimate probabilities for future dates. It aims to make complex datasets understandable for the general public and assist outdoor planners, researchers, and travelers.

Functional description:

• Interactive map to select a location and date.

• Computes probabilities of “very hot,” “cold,” “windy,” or “wet” conditions.

• Displays intuitive charts and probability visuals.

• Allows users to export results as CSV or JSON.

• AI models analyze long-term climate trends.

How It Works:

The app collects location/date input, queries NASA data (MERRA-2, GPM, MODIS), and uses an AI model to analyze historical weather patterns. It returns probability-based insights visualized in a user-friendly dashboard.

Why It Is Important :

SkyCast bridges the gap between short-term forecasts and long-term climate awareness, empowering users to plan ahead using open NASA data.

AI Integration :

AI analyzes multi-year NASA datasets using regression and machine learning techniques to estimate probabilities of future weather events.

Tools and Technologies Frontend: React, Electron, Leaflet, TailwindCSS

Backend: Node.js, Express, Python (ML), Electron IPC Data: NASA MERRA-2, GPM, AIRS

AI Libraries: Scikit-Learn, Pandas

NASA Data Use

• MODIS – land surface temperature (heat/cold)

 • MERRA-2 – windspeed and humidity

• GPM – precipitation (wet probability)

• AIRS – atmospheric temperature/humidity profiles
