projectDetails.name: Project Stellar Techie
projectDetails.summary:
I envisioned the HoverTrack, a futuristic concept for sustainable personal transportation that merges clean renewable energy, AI, and immersive navigation. My project began with the film “Hot Sand, Cold Ice,” which connects the contrasting worlds of the Sahara and Antarctica to show how technology and the environment can find balance.

HoverTrack envisions a magnetized hoverboard track that uses repelling electromagnetic fields to lift and move a rider smoothly—without friction, fuel, or emissions. The system represents how transportation could evolve toward zero-emission mobility using renewable power and smart design.

To complement the track, I developed the NexRide app, built using "Base44" integration, which connects the smart helmet and hoverboard. The app provides real-time navigation, energy monitoring, and performance optimization through AI, while also offering a futuristic augmented experience during the ride.

This project demonstrates how innovation, creativity, and sustainability can merge to reimagine the way we move. HoverTrack and NexRide are designed to inspire a cleaner, smarter, and more connected future—where technology helps us travel without harming our planet.
projectDetails.details:
My project, HoverTrack, is a futuristic concept that demonstrates how clean energy, artificial intelligence, and magnetic technology can merge to redefine sustainable personal transportation. It envisions a magnetized hoverboard track powered by repelling electromagnetic fields, lifting and moving a rider smoothly without friction, noise, or fossil fuels. The concept represents a pathway toward zero-emission mobility where movement is powered entirely by renewable energy.

To bring this vision to life, I developed the NexRide app, built using "Base44" integration, which connects the smart helmet and hoverboard wirelessly. The app offers AI-driven navigation, real-time energy monitoring, and voice and haptic guidance for an immersive and safe riding experience. It adapts dynamically to route conditions and energy efficiency—showing how data and design can work together for sustainable innovation.

As part of the project, I created an educational short film titled “Hot Sand, Cold Ice.” The film connects the Sahara Desert’s hot sands and Antarctica’s cool air to teach youth about climate balance, renewable energy, and human responsibility. It encourages young minds to explore how technology can harmonize with nature rather than harm it.

This project is creative because it fuses science, art, and storytelling—using interactive technology and film to inspire the next generation to imagine bold, planet-friendly solutions that make sustainability both exciting and achievable.

Built with advanced multi-layered materials, AEROBUBBLE provides a pressurized, Earth-like living environment in places where there is little to no atmosphere.

projectDetails.name: Project Meteor-finder
projectDetails.summary:
The project Meteorite madness (app.py) creates an interactive visualisation for exploring the NASA Meteorite Landings dataset. It features:
Data Loading: Reads meteorite-landings.csv, converting mass and coordinates to numeric, with caching for performance.
Filters: Sidebar sliders for filtering by year and mass.
 Map Visualisation: Displays meteorites on a Folium map with clustered markers, sized by mass, and popups showing details (name, year, mass, class, estimated diameter).

Summary Stats: Shows meteorite count, mass statistics (min, median, max), and a table of the top 10 heaviest meteorites.
Data Export: Allows downloading filtered data as a CSV.

The app uses pandas, numpy, folium, and streamlit-folium for data processing and visualization.

projectDetails.name: Project Team Astroflora
projectDetails.summary:
Global pollinator populations are declining rapidly — honeybee numbers have dropped by over 30% in the past decade due to pesticides, habitat loss, and climate change. This crisis threatens global food security by reducing reliable pollination, while bloom asynchrony caused by shifting weather patterns further disrupts plant reproduction.

Our project, BLOOMBot, offers an innovative solution through a swarm of AI-powered robotic pollinators that integrate Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8 technologies for precise flower detection and readiness assessment. These eco-friendly mini-drones combine electrostatic pollen delivery, nutrient micro-dosing, and environmental sensing into a coordinated system that ensures each flower receives targeted care.

BLOOMBots use NASA and partner datasets — including Worldview bloom maps, Landsat imagery, and GLOBE citizen science observations — to forecast bloom timing and optimize deployment schedules. Visualized through Blender animation and a Figma dashboard, the system demonstrates real-time flower health monitoring, pollination progress, and nutrient distribution.

By merging robotics, AI vision, and NASA data, BLOOMBots address the pollination crisis with a sustainable, data-driven approach — advancing resilient agriculture for both Earth and future space habitats.
projectDetails.details:
BLOOMBots are intelligent, eco-friendly robotic pollinators designed to address the global pollinator decline and the growing challenge of bloom asynchrony caused by climate change. These bots perform precise pollination, nutrient micro-dosing, and environmental monitoring to ensure healthy and reliable crop yields.

Using advanced AI-based detection systems powered by Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8 technologies, BLOOMBots can recognize receptive flowers, identify bloom stages, and deliver electrostatically charged pollen directly and accurately. The system integrates sensors that monitor temperature, humidity, light, and soil conditions to optimize plant health and pollination timing.

Data from NASA’s Worldview, Landsat, and GLOBE programs enhance the bots’ decision-making, enabling adaptive responses to real-time environmental changes. The project was developed using Figma for interface and dashboard design, and Blender for 3D visualization and animation to illustrate BLOOMBot’s functions and environmental interactions.

Our team prioritized sustainability, creativity, and technological precision—designing BLOOMBots to work in greenhouses, orchards, and even space-based habitats. This innovation offers a sustainable, data-driven alternative to traditional pollination, aiming to stabilize food production, preserve biodiversity, and pave the way for future agricultural systems beyond Earth.

projectDetails.name: INTRODUCING OUR PROJECT-ANALYZING TERRA DATA TO FIND IMPACT OF GREENHOUSE GASES ON GLOBAL WARMING
projectDetails.summary: Our team has taken 2 sets of data from the MOPITT instrument aboard the terra  satellite for 2 sets of areas the mohn’s ridge of Svalbard coast and an inner region of the sahara desert.plotting area graphs for temperature and carbon monoxide volumes. We have concluded an interesting fact that concentrations of carbon monoxide(or any other green house gas) only has an impact on the temperature after a certain volume of CO is reached.This is against the popular belief that greenhouse gases are fully responsible for global warming .This finding will help us fight global warming in a more effective way and helps us use terra s data to understand the niche details of our climte and ecosystem.
projectDetails.details: Our project uses the NASA MOPITT instrument aboard the Terra satellite to find the actual impact greenhouse gases, specifically carbon monoxide, have on global warming and whether it is as profound as we make it out to be. For this, we gathered about 30,000 points along with their corresponding temperature and carbon monoxide readings from two locations: the Mohn's Ridge and the Sahara Desert. The benefit our project brings is that it reveals that CO volumes (and greenhouse gases in general) may not have an impact on the rise in temperature below a certain volume of carbon monoxide. This can help us shift our focus from industrialization as the sole factor and find other factors that may have a bigger role or can be more easily controlled. We hope to be able to use our findings to create a meaningful impact and help fight environmental issues in a more practical manner. In fact, further analysis of the data might reveal other hidden factors as well. We have used NASA’s data from the MOPITT instrument as well as a similar record from the Canadian space agency. Many of the results are generated using a Python program and Python libraries such as Matplotlib and SciPy. A spreadsheet software was also used to clean and sort the data.

projectDetails.details:
Aeris is an innovative air quality and weather monitoring application developed for iOS using SwiftUI, CoreLocation, and async/await networking in Swift. The app collects data from multiple sources including Open-Meteo, OpenAQ, and NASA TEMPO, combining it into a user-friendly interface that displays real-time AQI values, pollutant levels (PM2.5 and NO₂), and current weather conditions (temperature, wind speed, humidity). Aeris uses fallback logic to ensure the latest available data is always shown, preventing crashes when current readings are unavailable.

The app provides actionable health advice based on AQI categories, high AQI notifications, and a 12-hour forecast to help users plan outdoor activities safely. Its customizable settings, multi-unit support, and transparent source attribution enhance usability and reliability.

The intended impact is to empower users to make informed decisions about outdoor exposure, raising awareness of air pollution risks and promoting public health. The project demonstrates creativity by integrating multiple live environmental data sources, offering predictive and actionable insights, and presenting them through dynamic, visually engaging UI/UX elements while considering location accuracy, real-time updates, and accessibility.

projectDetails.name: CLAIRITY
projectDetails.summary:
Clairity is an advanced web-based air quality monitoring and forecasting platform that combines NASA’s TEMPO satellite data with real-time readings from IoT sensors and meteorological datasets to deliver precise, localized environmental insights. Designed to help individuals, particularly those with asthma and respiratory conditions, Clairity provides real-time air quality data, predictive forecasts, and personalized health alerts. The prototype uses an Arduino Uno integrated with a DHT11 sensor for temperature and humidity, an MQ-135 sensor for detecting harmful gases such as CO₂, NH₃, and VOCs, and a Raindrop sensor for monitoring precipitation. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud-based system built with Next.js, Node.js, and Python, enabling instant processing and visualization through an intuitive, user-friendly dashboard.

Artificial intelligence models analyze patterns in meteorological and pollutant data to predict air quality variations up to 72 hours in advance. Clairity’s dashboard displays real-time AQI levels, pollutant trends, and interactive environmental maps while sending automated alerts during unsafe conditions. Its scalable design supports city-wide sensor networks, mobile applications, and edge computing for rapid analysis. By uniting space data, IoT, and AI, Clairity transforms environmental science into real-world health protection, empowering communities to breathe safer and live smarter.
projectDetails.details:
Inspiration

Air pollution is one of the most serious global health threats, contributing to millions of deaths each year (WHO, 2023). For individuals with chronic respiratory illnesses, even small fluctuations in air quality can have dangerous consequences.

Team Singularity was inspired by NASA’s TEMPO mission, which provides hourly, high-resolution atmospheric data across North America. We envisioned a system that takes this data, integrates it with local ground sensors, and delivers real-time health alerts and forecasts directly to users. Clairity was created to make complex environmental information accessible and actionable.

Core Purpose

Clairity is designed as a personalized air quality intelligence system that transforms raw atmospheric data into practical insights. It empowers individuals, particularly vulnerable groups, to understand the air they breathe and take timely protective actions.

Key Features

  • Real-time air quality tracking with NASA TEMPO data
  • Integration of ground-based sensors for localized conditions
  • Interactive dashboards and pollutant trend visualizations
  • Predictive forecasting models for short-term air quality changes
  • Smart notifications and health alerts for at-risk populations
  • Data insights for researchers, policymakers, and healthcare providers

System Design

Clairity integrates multiple layers of hardware, software, and data processing to create a seamless monitoring and forecasting platform.

Hardware and Data Collection

The system uses an Arduino Uno microcontroller connected to precision sensors:

  • DHT11 for temperature and humidity
  • MQ-2 and MQ-135 for detecting gases such as CO, CO₂, NH₃, and VOCs
  • BMP180 for pressure and altitude measurements

These sensors form the foundation for localized environmental intelligence, with real-time transmission of data to the server.

Data Fusion and Processing

Sensor data is combined with NASA TEMPO satellite observations, OpenWeather, and OpenAQ datasets. Using Python and Node.js, interpolation algorithms synchronize multiple sources, producing accurate and evolving air quality profiles.

Visualization and User Experience

Clairity’s web interface, built with Next.js and TypeScript, converts complex atmospheric data into clear visual formats.

  • Interactive AQI dashboard
  • Dynamic graphs of pollutant trends
  • Color-coded air quality indicators
  • Forecasts based on predictive modeling
  • Customizable health alerts

The interface is designed to be intuitive, informative, and user-friendly.

Artificial Intelligence and Analytics

Machine learning models analyze historical and real-time data to forecast pollution levels. Regression models and temporal analysis help identify links between weather conditions and pollutant concentrations.

An AI-powered assistant enhances the platform by offering:

  • Health and safety guidance
  • Explanations of pollutants and scientific terms
  • Personalized tips to reduce exposure

Use of NASA TEMPO Data

TEMPO is the backbone of Clairity’s analysis, providing hourly satellite-based measurements of pollutants such as nitrogen dioxide, formaldehyde, and ozone. These are cross-referenced with ground sensor readings, meteorological inputs, and global databases. The integration creates hyper-localized pollution maps and reliable short-term forecasts.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Next.js, TypeScript, HTML, CSS
  • Backend: Python, Node.js, Express.js
  • Hardware: Arduino Uno with DHT11, MQ-2, MQ-135, BMP180 sensors
  • APIs and Data Sources: NASA TEMPO, OpenWeather, OpenAQ, Leaflet API
  • AI Tools: ChatGPT-5 for branding and content optimization, Perplexity AI for coding support
  • Development Tools: GitHub, Visual Studio Code, Figma, Vercel

Future Development

Clairity has the potential to expand into a globally deployable platform with the following planned enhancements:

  • Mobile applications for real-time access and location-based alerts
  • Advanced machine learning for more accurate forecasting
  • City-wide IoT networks for highly localized data collection
  • Partnerships with healthcare organizations for emergency notifications
  • Collaboration with governments for policy development and climate action

Scalability and Global Impact

Clairity’s modular architecture and cloud-based infrastructure enable it to scale from individual households to entire cities. Its ability to synchronize distributed data ensures both small-scale community use and large-scale institutional deployments. Beyond awareness, Clairity empowers proactive interventions, enabling individuals, healthcare systems, and policymakers to act before air quality becomes hazardous.

Conclusion

Clairity represents the convergence of space science, environmental engineering, and artificial intelligence. By combining NASA TEMPO satellite data with ground sensors and real-time analytics, Team Singularity has developed a system that goes beyond monitoring. It is an early warning ecosystem designed to protect lives and promote environmental awareness.

As air pollution continues to endanger millions worldwide, Clairity aims to make clean air a guaranteed right through the power of science, technology, and collective action.

projectDetails.name: Project AstroNests
projectDetails.summary: Our team embarked on an interdisciplinary project focused on space habitats, exploring how humans could live and operate in extraterrestrial environments. We began by designing a Roblox game obstacle course ("obby") simulating low-gravity.Concurrently, we developed a Scratch website with more games : a rocket simulation game highlighting the principles of propulsion and trajectory, and a clicker game where you have to click an earth to get points. To synthesize our findings and creative work, we prepared a comprehensive presentation detailing each component, highlighting the scientific concepts underpinning our designs, and explaining how they contribute to sustainable living in space. Complementing the digital projects, we created a detailed 3D model of a space habitat, illustrating both interior and exterior features. The model showcased modular living spaces, life-support systems, recreational areas, and structural adaptations for microgravity, providing a tangible visualization of potential human habitats beyond Earth. Through these interconnected projects, we integrated scientific reasoning, engineering design, and interactive learning, fostering a deeper understanding of human adaptation in space and demonstrating innovative approaches to habitat planning, resource management, and experiential simulation.

projectDetails.name: Project GeoPulse
projectDetails.summary: Our project, GeoPulse, is an app that helps users plan their events by using accurate and reliable data from NASA. Our app allows users to check the weather conditions of a specific place and time. To do this, users must pick a spot, then date, pick their preferred weather conditions or proceed with a preset, and then see what the weather is like at the location, and the odds of their preferred weather at that location and time. Users can also export this and share with other people. This app is important because it allows users to plan events such as weddings, birthdays, vacations, etc
projectDetails.details:
Our project is an app that allows users to determine the weather at a specific location and time. The app requires the user to input the area, the date and their weather preference. Using NASA's weather data, the app calculates the chances of rain and the temperature at that time, and also mentions if the weather suits their preference. While weather apps only predict the weather a week or two ahead, it is not effective because it means that the user has less time to plan their event, and the data is not even accurate. Because the app is using NASA data, it is able to provide accurate data of weather data at any time. This benefits the user because they can plan big events such as weddings, etc, months ahead. This website was coded using Swift on a MacBook. This is because Swift is a user-friendly coding language, and it is very professional because it is inspired by the Apple theme, which is preferred by many people. Our project looks very minimalistic, keeping the focus on the information itself. We've combined NASA POWER data and other NASA information to give users the best data possible, while keeping a sleek workflow.

Our App meets the following objectives:

- Obtains likelihood of certain weather conditions being met at the given time of a year and country

- Allows for advanced customisation to reflect user's requirements, while having preset data to allow for quick overview

- Shows probabilities with bar chart to improve visual experience, while giving text for dual coding.

- Has options for both drop pin and typing up a location, with auto-picker to pick best location, and a big enough map for scrolling through.

- Allows for data to be exported as a JSON for further analysis

projectDetails.summary: Our project “The Vanishing Green” uses Terra satellite NDVI data to visualize deforestation in the Amazon rainforest from 2000 to 2025. We created a 3D cinematic animation in Blender, mapping NDVI layers onto a realistic Earth model, and animating a flyover to show how forest cover has decreased over the past 25 years. By visualizing the impact of deforestation over time, our project demonstrates how NASA Terra data can be used to inform and inspire global audiences, promoting awareness of climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental sustainability.
projectDetails.details:
“The Vanishing Green” visualizes Amazon deforestation from 2000–2025 using actual NDVI data from NASA’s Terra MODIS sensor.
We mapped the NDVI images onto a 3D Earth model in Blender, applied realistic lighting and atmosphere, and animated camera flyovers to create a cinematic storytelling experience.
This project helps viewers see the dramatic loss of forest cover over time and its impact on climate and biodiversity.
Tools and software used: Blender 4.0 (3D animation), NASA Worldview (NDVI data), QGIS/Photoshop (data processing), DaVinci Resolve (editing), Audacity (audio markers).
Our project is creative because it blends real scientific data with cinematic storytelling, making complex environmental changes visually understandable and engaging.

projectDetails.name: Project Terrabind
projectDetails.summary:
Traditional construction materials consume vast natural resources, emit large amounts of CO2, and generate significant waste. TerraBind aims to solve this by transforming recycled concrete waste, fly ash, and natural fibers into durable, interlocking eco-bricks. These "snap-fit" bricks minimize the need for mortar, reducing both time and material usage during construction.

The composition blends recycled aggregates, hemp or coconut fibers for strength, and supplementary cementitious materials like GGBS and fly ash to cut cement demand while improving durability and long-term performance. The result is a lighter, stronger, and more sustainable alternative to traditional cinder blocks - reducing emissions by nearly 50% while enhancing ease of use and insulation properties.

Beyond material innovation, TerraBind promotes a circular economy by reusing waste from demolition and industrial processes. The interlocking design ensures faster assembly and lower costs, making it suitable for affordable, sustainable housing and infrastructure projects.

By combining engineering innovation with environmental responsibility, TerraBind offers a scalable solution to global construction challenges - building stronger foundations for a cleaner, greener future.
projectDetails.details: TerraBind is an innovative sustainable construction project that reimagines how bricks are made and used. It introduces interlocking bricks crafted from recycled concrete, crushed building waste, and natural fibers like hemp or coconut coir. This blend not only reuses waste materials but also enhances the brick’s strength, flexibility, and impact resistance. Through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations, TerraBind demonstrated highly uniform stress distribution across its interlocking geometry, confirming superior load-bearing capacity and structural stability compared to standard bricks. The interlocking design eliminates the need for mortar, cutting construction time, labor, and material costs while improving alignment and durability. The project integrates CAD modeling, 3D-printed molds for prototyping, and experimental mix design testing to optimize composition and bonding. Beyond engineering efficiency, TerraBind tackles global sustainability challenges by reducing CO₂ emissions from cement use and diverting construction waste from landfills. The result is a scalable, eco-friendly, and cost-effective building solution that embodies the future of green construction and circular innovation.

projectDetails.name: Project: Resilient Roots (digital story), Challenge: Weather through the eyes of earthlings
projectDetails.summary: "Resilient Roots" is a digital story created by Team TERRA METEO @WIN from The Winchester School, Jebel Ali, for the "Stellar Stories: Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings" Challenge. The project aims to raise awareness about space weather and its potential impact on interconnected global communities. The narrative centers on three individuals—Hemlock, a farmer; Eva, a pilot; and Marco, a taxi driver—whose lives are simultaneously thrown into chaos when their GPS-dependent technologies and systems fail due to a powerful space weather event.The story culminates with the characters attending a town hall meeting where NASA scientists explain the phenomenon of space weather, its causes (Solar flares, Coronal Mass Ejections, etc.), and its impacts on Earth's technologies, such as: GPS signal disruption (e.g., affecting farming, aviation, and transport logistics), Power grid stations turning off, Automated irrigation system failure, Radio communications blackouts.Crucially, the story emphasizes that basic skills and inner resilience are vital for problem-solving in a crisis, shown by the characters successfully navigating their way home using only a map and a compass. The project directly addresses the challenge by raising awareness, highlighting global technological interconnection, and informing the audience about the science and necessity of preparation. It underscores that understanding and preparing for space weather events is essential for modern society.
projectDetails.details:
Detailed Project Description: Stellar Stories: Weather Through the Eyes of Earthlings

The project Resilient Roots is a digital story presentation designed for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge by team TERRA METEO @WIN , comprised of passionate Year 6 students from The Winchester School, Jebel Ali. Our primary objective is to create a digital story that raises awareness about space weather by exploring its potential impact on our interconnected communities.

 The story centers on three characters—Farmer Hemlock (a modernized farmer relying on GPS for his tractor and automated irrigation) , his niece Eva (a pilot) , and their friend Marco (a taxi driver).

  • Conflict: It begins with the characters simultaneously experiencing technology failures: Hemlock's GPS signal vanishes, turning his perfect planting rows into a chaotic zigzag , Eva's flight is disrupted , Marco's cab GPS is dead , and Hemlock's farm loses power and irrigation. This also disrupts local logistics, like Hemlock's daughter's school trip.
  • Resolution & Education: The characters attend a town hall meeting where NASA scientists, Dr. Anya Sharma and Dr. James Span , explain the event as space weather. This part of story educates the audience on: Causes (Solar flares, Solar wind, and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) and The effects: GPS disruption (via the ionosphere) , power outages, telecommunication cable disruption, radio wave disturbance, and astronaut safety threats.
  • Key Message: The story concludes with the characters navigating home using a simple compass and map, emphasizing that while technology is powerful, basic skills and resilience are crucial when systems fail.

⚙️ How Does It Work?

The project works as a visual and textual narrative delivered through a presentation format (PowerPoint).

  1. Setting the Scene: The presentation uses rich imagery and prose to introduce the characters and establish their reliance on GPS and automated technology.
  2. The Crisis: The story builds tension by detailing the simultaneous failure of GPS across different sectors (agriculture, aviation, and transport), illustrating the vulnerability of modern systems.
  3. Scientific Explanation: It transitions to an educational segment, using diagrams, facts, and the voices of experts to clearly define space weather and its mechanisms, such as how CMEs can cause geomagnetic storms and affect the Earth's magnetic field and power grids.
  4. Real-World Context: It grounds the threat by citing historical events like the Carrington event , the near-fatal event in 1972 , the Starlink satellite loss in 2022 , and recent agricultural damage in May 2024.
  5. Mitigation and Future: It includes information on NASA and SpaceX efforts to forecast space weather, such as the SWIFT satellite constellation , and the use of AI-driven forecasts.
  6. Moral of the Story: The final scenes offer a powerful reminder about the enduring value of simple tools and human intuition over complex, vulnerable technology.

✨ What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Public Awareness: It translates complex astrophysics into an accessible, relatable narrative, making the abstract threat of space weather understandable to a general audience.
  • Promotes Preparedness: By illustrating the failure of core infrastructure, it encourages individuals and communities to consider non-technological backup plans and basic survival skills.
  • Highlights Interdependency: It clearly demonstrates the profound interconnectedness and fragility of global systems (transport, agriculture, power) in the face of a solar event.
  • Educational Value: It provides scientifically accurate information based on NASA resources about solar activity, its effects on the ionosphere, and the difference between solar flares and CMEs.

🎯 What Do We Hope to Achieve?

We hope to achieve the following:

  1. Inspire Action: To encourage citizens and policy-makers to recognize space weather as a serious, inevitable, and catastrophic threat that requires proactive preparation.
  2. Foster Resilience: To advocate for the blending of new technology (like AI-driven forecasts) with the preservation of essential non-tech skills.
  3. Increase Understanding: To successfully demystify concepts like the Carrington Event and the function of the ionosphere for a non-scientific audience.

🛠️ Tools and Technology Used

The project was developed using a combination of software and AI tools for research, content creation, and visual design:

projectDetails.name: SPACE WEATHER CHANGES EVERYTHING ; STELLAR STORIES
projectDetails.summary:
From Earth, space weather is invisible, yet its effects ripple through our daily lives. We don’t see solar flares bursting on the Sun, or streams of charged particles rushing across millions of kilometers—but we feel their impact.
When the Sun hurls a coronal mass ejection, Earth’s magnetic shield trembles. Satellites we depend on for GPS, banking, and communication may falter. Our power grids, the backbone of modern civilization, can surge with unexpected currents, leading to blackouts. Airline pilots flying near the poles sense invisible radiation pressing closer. Astronauts orbiting beyond our protective shield are reminded of their fragility.
Yet, space weather also gifts us with wonder. In the quiet skies of the north and south, auroras dance—green, purple, and red curtains shimmering in the night, telling us that the Sun is speaking to our planet.

projectDetails.name: R. O. M (Recycling on Mars)
projectDetails.summary:
For our summary:Millions of pieces of waste are produced annually by space missions, ranging from damaged tools and packaging to mission equipment. This issue will only worsen on Mars, endangering astronauts and squandering precious resources.
 R. O. M, our solution, is a straightforward yet effective recycling rover made to handle trash in space without the use of artificial intelligence. Around a Mars base, the robot, gathers waste materials and uses mechanical systems to sort them: metals are sorted by magnets, heavier items are sorted by density checks, and plastics and textiles are sorted by color-coded bins. 
After being sorted, the materials are melted and reshaped into tiles, blocks, or replacement parts. While the rover carries out instructions and transmits images and data back, the astronauts and mission control oversee the procedure and make all recycling decisions. R. O.M converts waste into resources.

projectDetails.name: Project The AICS sharkstronuts
projectDetails.summary: "Sharks from Space" is an innovative research project using satellite technology, AI, and drones to monitor and protect global shark populations. It started with studies like the Bimini Shark Lab’s work in the Bahamas, combining satellite imagery and field data to examine how coastal development impacts juvenile sharks. NASA expanded the initiative by adapting space technologies, such as the Centaur drone, to track species like great white sharks. The project blends marine biology with aerospace engineering, offering non-invasive methods for conservation and enabling data-driven decisions. It also promotes public engagement through citizen science and interactive platforms, showing how space tools can revolutionize ocean conservation.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

“Sharks from Space” is a research and technology project that uses satellite imaging, tracking devices, and data analysis tools to study sharks and their ocean environment from space.

What benefits does it have?

🦈 Conservation: Helps scientists protect endangered shark species by identifying important breeding and feeding zones.

🌍 Climate Research: Provides information about how climate change affects ocean life and habitats.

🧭 Better Ocean Management: Assists governments and organizations in creating marine protected areas.

🛰️ New Technology Use: Demonstrates how space technology can solve environmental problems on Earth.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The goal is to create a global understanding of shark movement and ocean health, using tools that allow scientists to see the bigger picture from above.

The project aims to:

Reduce shark population decline.

Inspire conservation through technology.

Encourage collaboration between space agencies, marine biologists, and data scientists.

How is your project creative?

This project is creative because it combines two completely different fields — space technology and marine biology — to solve a problem that normally can’t be seen from above.

It transforms the idea of looking up to space into looking down from space to protect life in the oceans.

It also uses modern coding and satellite tools in a new, eco-friendly way to promote sustainability.


What factors did your team consider?

Before developing the project, the team considered:

🌊 Environmental ethics: Making sure tagging doesn’t harm sharks.

💻 Data accuracy and privacy: Ensuring the data collected is secure and reliable.

⚙️ Cost and feasibility: Balancing technology cost with research benefits.

🤝 Collaboration: Working with space and ocean organizations to share data and knowledge.

🌐 Global impact: Making sure the results help not only scientists but also teachers, students, and conservation groups around the world.

It is common to measure photosynthetic activity in the ocean from space, but far more challenging to track top predators. Your challenge is to create a mathematical framework for identifying sharks and predicting their foraging habitats using NASA satellite data, and also to suggest a new conceptual model of a tag (a small electronic device that can be attached to an animal to track and study its movement) that could measure not only where sharks are, but also what they are eating, and in real time transmit that data back to users to enable development of predictive models. (Earth Science Division)

projectDetails.name: TerraBloom
projectDetails.summary: Terra Bloom is a web-based application developed to tackle the issue of inaccurate plant growth-to-land ratio data and the lack of accessible plant information. Using NASA’s satellite data, GPS, and environmental datasets, the app allows users to explore which flowers and plants grow in specific regions, track their yearly growth trends, and understand the environmental factors that affect their development. It also highlights underutilized areas where certain species could thrive but are not currently cultivated. By providing accurate, visual, and easy-to-access plant data, Terra Bloom empowers researchers, farmers, and conservationists to make more informed ecological and agricultural decisions. This project was created by The Code Ensemble — Sanaa Rehman, Huda Fathima, Maryam Musadiq, Sachi Shewale, and Nabila Nayaz Ahmed — as part of the NASA Space
projectDetails.details:
The Challenge

Accurately understanding plant growth patterns and their distribution across land remains a major challenge. There is often a lack of precise, accessible, and updated information on which plants grow where — making it difficult for scientists, environmentalists, and communities to make informed decisions about land use, biodiversity, and conservation.

Our Solution

To address the issue of inaccurate plant growth-to-land ratio data and the general lack of accessible plant information, we developed an interactive web-based application. This platform enables users to explore what types of flowers and plants grow in specific geographic regions — with detailed yearly progression data powered by satellite observations and geolocation.

Our app integrates NASA’s open satellite data, geospatial mapping via GPS, and other environmental datasets to accurately display:

* The types of plants and flower species in a given area
* How each species has progressed year by year
* Environmental challenges that hinder plant growth in specific regions
* Untapped potential: plants that could thrive in new areas but are not currently cultivated there

Users can also view different species variants, analyze growth trends, and identify ecological or agricultural gaps where planting could be expanded sustainably.
Innovation & Tech Stack

*Web App: React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Leaflet.js
* Data Sources: NASA Earth Observation Data, Satellite Imagery, GPS
Features: Interactive map, species browser, yearly progression tracker, plant growth challenges by region

This tool makes accurate plant data more accessible for everyone — from farmers and researchers to students and environmental planners.

TEAM MEMBERS:
Sanaa Rehman
* Huda Fathima
* Maryam Musadiq
* Sachi Shewale
* Nabila Nayaz Ahmed

projectDetails.name: The life of a Solar flare
projectDetails.summary:
Lamarada, a young flame flare who dreams of seeing Earth and its supposed aliens, launches from the Sun despite his parents' disapproval. As a relatively slow flare, traveling at 250 km per second, he calculated his trip would take 6.94 days. Along the way, he navigates dangers like unfriendly asteroids and observes fascinating real-life space missions like NASA's Parker Solar Probe and the ESA Solar Orbiter. He passes Venus, noting he wouldn't want to visit its hot surface, and uses Earth-orbiting satellites like the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Iridium to track his final approach. Lamarada muses on the vastness of space, the fate of other flares that didn't make it, and the possibility of lights from alien civilizations.
After days of travel, Lamarada finally reaches Earth's atmosphere, feeling the pressure and noticing the International Space Station (ISS). With his dream almost fulfilled, he sights his landing spot 2.5 km above ground. The adventure didn't quite end with his landing! The story explains that Lamarada was safely caught by some high-tech, futuristic gear. After scientists studied him in a lab full of space equipment, the little flare got a final rocket boost home to the Sun.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do or how does it work?

It is a creative narrative blending personal adventure with scientific facts about space, told from the perspective of a young solar flare. The story progresses chronologically over 6.94 days of travel from the Sun to Earth.

What benefits does it have?

The story makes complex astronomical concepts like solar flares, spacecraft, and orbital mechanics accessible and engaging for a young audience. It also offers a humorous and imaginative take on scientific exploration.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To inspire curiosity about space and science by personifying a technical phenomenon (a solar flare). The project also subtly educates readers about real-life satellites and space missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

-Capcut

-Canva

-Gemini

-Nasa Space App

-Nasa Original Resourses

How is your project creative?

It creatively uses a first-person perspective from a solar flare named Lamarada, a novel literary choice. It skillfully integrates specific, factual mission names like Parker Solar Probe into a fictional journey.

What factors did your team consider?

The primary factor was educational engagement, making sure the scientific details were accurate but not overwhelming. We also focused on creating a clear, linear timeline and a dramatic, yet safe, ending for the main character.

Our project is an interactive web-based tool designed to model and visualize the potential impacts of the newly identified near-Earth asteroid "Impactor-2025." By integrating real-time data from NASA's Near-Earth Object database and the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the platform allows users to simulate various impact scenarios, assess potential consequences, and evaluate mitigation strategies. Users can input variables such as asteroid size, velocity, and impact location to observe outcomes like crater formation, shockwave propagation, and population impact. This project addresses the challenge by transforming complex scientific data into accessible, interactive visualizations, thereby enhancing public awareness and supporting informed decision-making in planetary defense. Its importance lies in empowering communities and policymakers with the knowledge to anticipate and respond to asteroid risks effectively.
projectDetails.details:
Project Title: Impactor-2025 Interactive Simulation and Visualization Tool

Project Overview:
Our project is an interactive, web-based simulation tool designed to help the public, scientists, and decision-makers understand and mitigate the risks posed by near-Earth asteroids, using the newly identified "Impactor-2025" as a case study. The tool integrates real datasets from NASA on known asteroids and the United States Geological Survey (USGS) to model potential impact scenarios, predict consequences, and evaluate mitigation strategies. Users can explore how factors like asteroid size, speed, angle of impact, and location influence the outcomes of a potential collision.

How It Works:

  1. Data Integration: Real asteroid orbit and size data from NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) database are combined with USGS geological and population data.
  2. Simulation Engine: Users can input variables such as asteroid mass, velocity, and impact location. The engine calculates potential crater size, energy released, shockwave propagation, tsunami likelihood, and population impact.
  3. Interactive Visualization: The results are displayed dynamically on a global map with overlays for population density, infrastructure, and terrain type. Users can toggle scenarios to compare mitigation strategies like deflection missions or evacuation plans.
  4. Decision Support: The tool provides a risk assessment score and suggested mitigation actions for each scenario, helping policymakers prioritize response strategies.

Benefits:

  • Enables the public to understand asteroid risks visually and interactively.
  • Supports policymakers in planning and evaluating mitigation strategies.
  • Educates students, researchers, and disaster management professionals about the science and consequences of asteroid impacts.
  • Encourages data-driven decision-making for planetary defense.

Intended Impact:

  • Improve awareness of asteroid threats and preparedness for potential impacts.
  • Provide an accessible platform to test and communicate mitigation strategies.
  • Foster collaboration between scientists, emergency planners, and the general public.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • Programming Languages: JavaScript (React.js for the frontend), Python (for simulations and data processing)
  • Libraries/Frameworks: D3.js for data visualization, Leaflet.js or Mapbox for interactive maps, NumPy/Pandas for calculations and data manipulation
  • Data Sources: NASA NEO database, USGS geological and population datasets
  • Hardware/Software: Cloud-hosted web platform for accessibility, local development environment with VS Code
  • Optional Enhancements: WebGL for 3D impact visualizations, API integration for real-time asteroid data updates

Creativity:

  • The project merges real-time scientific data with interactive visualization for educational and decision-making purposes.
  • Users can experiment with hypothetical scenarios, making abstract risks tangible.
  • Combines planetary defense science with intuitive design to reach non-experts.

Factors Considered:

  • Accuracy of scientific models (impact physics, energy release, population effects)
  • Accessibility and ease of use for non-technical users
  • Scalability for different asteroid sizes and multiple scenarios
  • Visual clarity to ensure meaningful interpretation of complex data
  • Ethical communication of risk to avoid unnecessary panic

Conclusion:
Our tool transforms raw NASA and USGS data into an interactive, informative, and actionable platform. By enabling users to visualize and simulate asteroid impacts, it empowers society to understand risks, make informed decisions, and prepare mitigation strategies—turning abstract space threats into concrete, manageable scenarios.

projectDetails.details:
Project Details AirAware: TEMPO Air Quality Forecasting App

Overview:
AirAware is a web-based application that forecasts air quality in near real-time by integrating NASA’s TEMPO satellite data with ground-based air quality measurements and local weather data. The app provides an interactive dashboard with maps, pollutant charts, and personalized alerts to notify users when air quality becomes hazardous. The project aims to improve public awareness and assist individuals, researchers, and policymakers in making informed health and environmental decisions.

How it Works:

  1. Data Collection:
    • Satellite Data: TEMPO mission products (NO₂, O₃, HCHO, etc.) collected hourly.
    • Ground-Based Data: AirNow and OpenAQ station measurements.
    • Weather Data: Temperature, wind speed, humidity, and other relevant features from OpenWeatherMap or NOAA APIs.
    • Standardize and clean all datasets.
    • Align satellite data with ground stations using spatial collocation.
    • Merge with weather data to produce a fused dataset ready for forecasting.
    • Predict pollutant concentrations (PM2.5, NO₂, O₃) 1–24 hours ahead.
    • Baseline model: persistence (last observed value).
    • Machine learning model: XGBoost or similar regression model using fused features (satellite + station + weather + time).
    • Compute AQI based on predicted concentrations for user-friendly interpretation.
    • Frontend: React dashboard showing interactive maps, charts, and AQI forecasts.
    • Backend: Python FastAPI serving APIs for forecasts, ingestion, and alerts.
    • Users can subscribe to alerts (email or push) when AQI exceeds thresholds.

Benefits & Impact:

  • Provides accurate, real-time air quality forecasts across North America.
  • Protects public health by notifying users of hazardous air quality.
  • Assists researchers and policymakers with actionable insights into pollution trends.
  • Encourages data-driven decisions for environmental and urban planning.

Tools, Languages, & Software:

  • Frontend: React (or Next.js) + Mapbox/Leaflet for maps.
  • Backend: Python 3, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy.
  • Machine Learning: Scikit-learn, XGBoost, or alternative regression libraries.
  • Database: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB for time-series storage.
  • Data Storage: Local files or cloud object storage (S3-compatible).
  • APIs & Libraries: NASA TEMPO data, OpenAQ/AirNow APIs, OpenWeatherMap.
  • Dev Tools: Git, Docker (for local development & deployment).

Creativity & Uniqueness:

  • Integrates satellite observations with local measurements in real-time.
  • Provides user-friendly interactive visualizations and alerts for health protection.
  • Scalable architecture allows local testing and cloud deployment for public use.
  • Combines Earth observation data and AI forecasting in a public-access tool.

Considerations for Implementation:

  • Respect data licensing and attribution for TEMPO, AirNow, OpenAQ, and weather sources.
  • Ensure units are consistent (µg/m³ for PM2.5, ppb for gases).
  • Optimize for low-latency forecasting and responsive dashboard updates.
  • Alert thresholds should follow EPA AQI standards.
  • Provide clear documentation for developers to replicate or extend the system.
projectDetails.aiReferences:
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in AirAware

AirAware integrates AI to enhance air quality forecasting and data analysis. Specifically:

  1. Machine Learning for Forecasting:
    • We used XGBoost regression models to predict pollutant concentrations (PM2.5, NO₂, O₃) 1–24 hours in advance.
    • The AI model combines TEMPO satellite data, ground-based air quality measurements, and weather data to produce accurate, time-resolved forecasts.
    • Feature engineering and model training were conducted with Python libraries such as scikit-learn and XGBoost.
    • Predictions are converted to AQI categories, which drive user alerts and health recommendations.
    • AI helps identify patterns in pollution spikes that may not be obvious from raw observations alone.
    • All AI-generated code and predictions are clearly documented in the project’s README and code metadata.
    • No NASA branding, logos, or mission design elements were used in AI-generated outputs.
    • Images or visualizations used in the project (e.g., dashboard mockups) were created manually or via standard plotting libraries; no AI image generation was used.

Summary: AI in AirAware is primarily applied for forecast modeling and predictive analysis, assisting humans in making informed decisions, improving accuracy, and accelerating data processing. All AI use is documented to ensure transparency and originality.

projectDetails.name: Astro-Photocatalytic Urban Mapper (APUM)
projectDetails.summary: The Astro-Photocatalytic Pollution Remediation Mapper & Optimizer is a data-driven prototype designed to help cities reduce air pollution using insights from NASA Earth observation data. Our project identifies urban pollution hotspots and suggests where photocatalytic coatings (like TiO₂) could be applied to break down pollutants and create self-cleaning surfaces. Using datasets from Aura OMI (NO₂), CERES (solar irradiance), and MODIS (land surface temperature and land cover), the AI model demonstrates how zones could be prioritized based on sunlight, pollution intensity, and urban density. The results are visualized in an interactive website built with Canva Websites, designed for urban planners to explore potential solutions. While the interactive maps are currently example simulations and not yet connected to live data, the project addresses the challenge by showing how space-based material science and Earth observation data can guide sustainable urban growth. This approach is important because it provides a clear, data-driven pathway for cities to improve air quality, protect public health, and plan climate-resilient development, bridging the gap between cutting-edge space science and real-world environmental solutions.

projectDetails.name: Quantum Mood Tracker
projectDetails.summary:
Quantum Mood Tracker Summary 🚀

This interface uses quantum concepts as a metaphor to monitor the crew’s overall mental and emotional state. The idea is that the crew’s well-being forms an interconnected system, where each member’s mood can influence the rest — similar to quantum entanglement.

🔹 Quantum State Visualization

The system views the crew as one unified “quantum state” rather than separate individuals. Changes in one astronaut’s stress or focus instantly affect the overall team balance, giving mission control a holistic view of crew dynamics.

🔹 Optimal State Metric

The “X% Optimal” value represents how close the crew is to peak performance. It acts like a quantum equation for mission success, estimating the probability of maintaining ideal emotional and cognitive conditions.

🔹 Predictive Alerting

Using probabilistic forecasting, the system predicts potential issues before they escalate. Alerts like “Emotional Dip” are based on subtle changes in the crew’s collective “wave function,” allowing mission control to stabilize conditions early.
projectDetails.details:
The Quantum Mood Tracker is an AI-driven dashboard for Mission Control that provides predictive psychological monitoring of astronaut crews. It uses a custom-made watch to track vitals. We used React to create a highly responsive and intuitive website interface. The goal is to optimize well-being and performance on long-duration space missions, supporting the UAE Vision 2031 space ambitions for advanced human space exploration.

Key Features & Technology

Holistic Monitoring: Aggregates physiological data into a single metric, the Overall Optimal Well-being Score (e.g., 72%).

Predictive Alerts: Uses Quantum Machine Learning to detect subtle declines in individual metrics (Stress, Sleep, Cognitive Function), catching potential issues like "Increased Conflict Potential" before they escalate.

Actionable Interventions: Provides Mission Control with data-driven recommendations—such as assigning a "Group Cognitive Task"—allowing proactive support.

Development: built with React for a dynamic, single-page experience, ensuring fast, real-time updates for mission controllers.

Impact & Creativity

Proactive Approach: Moves from reacting to issues to predicting and preventing them.

Maximum Safety & Performance: Maintains crew mental health, reducing the risk of mission-critical errors.

Blueprint for Deep Space: Provides an objective tool for multi-year missions to Mars or beyond, aligning with the UAE Vision 2031 goal of leadership in human space exploration.

projectDetails.name: Project Stellar
projectDetails.summary:
Long-duration Mars missions face a critical problem: over 12,600 kg of waste, representing a billion-dollar launch investment destined for a landfill. Our project solves this by creating an integrated, closed-loop resource refinery.
Upgraded after NASA's MOXIE and following the path of the Sabatier, our system takes in the Martian environment and 100% of waste from habitation plastics to our modular R-CTB cargo bags—converting them to fuel, water, and life-supporting air.
The effect is an 80% elimination of waste going to landfills, and conversion of what is now a key liability into the very resources for a sustainable and long term human Mars presence.
projectDetails.details:
Our project addresses a paradoxical challenge for Mars missions: the 12,600 kg of high-value materials that become a hazardous waste liability upon arrival, representing a billion-dollar loss. We have designed an integrated, closed-loop resource refinery that transforms this waste from a mission-ending burden into the cornerstone of survival and self-sufficiency.

Our system functions by integrating two concurrent processes driven from a central energy center. First, following NASA's MOXIE, it employs water electrolysis and the Sabatier Pathway to synthesize Martian water ice and atmospheric CO₂ into methane fuel, oxygen, and water. At the same time, an entire waste management system treats 100% of habitat waste. Liquid waste is treated via an ECLSS, while solid waste―from plate scrapings to ourimaginatively conceived modular R-CTB cargo bags―is processed in a gasification reactor to yield more fuel and water, or fabricated in situ into finished goods such as chairs and 3D-printed parts.

The primary benefit is a radical increase in mission resilience and a massive reduction in launch costs and dependency on Earth. Our intended impact is a realistic 80% reduction in final landfill waste, transforming the Mars habitat into a sustainable ecosystem. By creating resources on-site, we minimize the mass of single-use items launched from Earth, ultimately conserving terrestrial resources. Our study made use of a state-of-the-art digital toolkit, such as Google Scholar and Perplexity for deep-diving NASA technical briefs, and NASA Image Library for visual resources. Generative artificial intelligence, in particular Google's AI Studio, helped in brainstorming, aggregating complex data, and building content for presentation.

Our innovation is due to our team's non-aerospace, diverse background, which made it possible for us to look at the problem from a brand-new angle. Instead of coming up with one brand-new piece of equipment, our innovation is in applying innovative combinations of available, proven technologies in one, unified system that treats all output as potential valuable input for yet another process. All along the developmental path, we took hard looks at issues such as feasibility by targeting high-TRL ideas, realism through use of an 80% efficiency factor in our models, and the essential nature of crew health and welfare in a clean, resourceful habitat.

We decided to create an app to explore different galaxies across the Universe. Seven galaxies are presented on the screen, and the user is able to click on each galaxy to find more information on it. Our user can then test their knowledge by doing quiz, solidifying what they have learnt and correcting any assumption they may have made about a galaxy. 

We decided to opt for the Create Your Own challenge, as it allows us to be creative with what we produce while being able to produce something we are passionate about.

It is designed for curious students who would like to know more about the different galaxies around the Universe, especially those that are not talked often about.
projectDetails.details:
Our project is a prototype of an app we designed, named Galaxy Exploration. It gives the user an opportunity to discover galaxies that are more unknown to the world.

How to navigate the app:

  • When you come into the app, you are greeted with a welcome message and a button allowing you to explore.
  • After that, the app takes you to a screen with 7 galaxies scattered across the screen. When you hover over a galaxy, it gives you a summary of its information. Clicking on the galaxy allows you to view more information about it. You can do this with all of the galaxies.
  • Once you are done reviewing the information, you can answer questions about what you have learnt using the quiz, which present questions about any galaxy shown on the screen. First you click on the quiz button on the top-right hand corner, then you can select what galaxy you would like to answer questions, and you answer several questions based on the information you have just read.
  • After reading and answering questions about the galaxies on the screen, you can reopen the app to discover new galaxies you have not seen.

For designing the prototype, we used the video editing software DaVinci Resolve to edit the video and add effects to display what our app would look like. We also used Canva to design the text boxes and button to display information in a more engaging manner.

If we were to actually create the app, we would use software like Flutter and Android Studio to create the app, and code in Java to create the functionalities we would like to include.

projectDetails.name: EarthWatch: Monitoring Earth's Crisis with Terra Data
projectDetails.summary:
We developed a two-part project to celebrate 25 years of NASA Terra satellite data. First, we created a compelling visual presentation that tells the story of Lake Chad's dramatic shrinkage, using Terra's long-term data to create an animated time-lapse. This narrative highlights the severe environmental and humanitarian impacts of climate change, showing how the lake has lost 90% of its surface area and affected 30 million people.

Second, we made "EarthWatch", an interactive web application model that brings this data to life. The dashboard allows users to monitor global resources like water levels and forest coverage in real-time, providing early warning alerts for environmental crises such as the critical water depletion in Lake Chad.

Our project directly addresses the Animation Celebration of Terra Data challenge by transforming complex satellite data into both a powerful story and an interactive tool. It demonstrates the critical role of Earth observation in understanding and solving our planet's most pressing challenges, making the data accessible and actionable for everyone.
projectDetails.details:
What does it do?
A presentation and interactive dashboard. The presentation shows Lake Chad's disappearance via NASA Terra timelapses, while the EarthWatch app monitors global water resources and environmental threats in real-time.

How does it work?
The presentation animates 25 years of Terra data. The EarthWatch app tracks resource levels and sends alerts for crisis zones like Lake Chad, Amazon, and Arctic regions.

Tools & Software:
Canva, Web development, NASA Worldview, Terra Satellite data

Creativity:
We transformed raw satellite data into both an emotional story and an interactive tool, making complex data accessible to different audiences.

Intended Impact:
Raise awareness about water scarcity and show how NASA data enables environmental monitoring and early warnings.

projectDetails.name: Design astro socks to protect astronauts’ feet in microgravity
projectDetails.summary: In space, astronauts’ feet are like hands. They use them to grip and grasp surfaces to stabilize themselves in microgravity. This use often leads to discomfort on the tops of their feet. We study the tasks that astronauts perform while on the International Space Station.We evaluate designs of performance footwear, gather user requirements and study foot anatomy. Then, we design and build a prototype to mitigate the pressure on their feet. By running trials using their sensorized sock,we test the effectiveness of our design in a simulated microgravity environment. Finally, we write and record an advertisement to explain their design.
projectDetails.details:
The Astro Socks project simulates a real-world challenge astronauts face aboard the International Space Station: pressure and skin damage on the tops of their feet due to prolonged use of foot rails in microgravity.
Students build sensor-enabled socks using Velostat and copper tape to detect pressure levels at four key foot zones: phalanges, metatarsals, tarsals, and ankle. These sensors connect to a microcontroller (Arduino Uno or micro:bit) and stream real-time data into Excel using the Data Streamer add-in.
The socks are tested with a cardboard “Space Gym” simulator, and data from multiple trials is collected and analyzed to improve the sock design and reduce pressure impact.

What benefits does it have?

  • Educational Impact: Teaches data science, electronics, and engineering in a real-world STEM context.
  • Real-Time Data Visualization: Helps students understand sensor input and pressure changes dynamically.
  • Hands-on Problem Solving: Bridges digital and physical worlds through experimentation and iteration.
  • Empathy & Innovation: Encourages students to think critically about astronaut safety and comfort.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The goal is to:

  • Inspire students to apply STEM skills in solving real-world problems.
  • Introduce engineering design thinking, sensor-based systems, and data interpretation.
  • Foster creativity and innovation in designing wearable tech.
  • Encourage exploration of space science and bioengineering.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

Hardware:

  • Arduino Uno or micro:bit
  • Velostat, copper tape, resistors
  • Jumper wires, breadboard
  • Cardboard (Space Gym), ribbon, Velcro
  • Wire strippers, hot melt glue gun

Software & Tech Stack:

  • Excel O365 with Microsoft Data Streamer Add-In
  • Arduino IDE (for Arduino Uno firmware)
  • .ino code or .hex code (depending on controller)
  • Astro Socks custom Excel workbook

Coding Languages:

  • Arduino C/C++ (for microcontroller firmware)

How is your project creative?

  • Integrates wearable tech into a space exploration context.
  • Combines DIY materials (Velostat, copper tape, cardboard) with real-time data science.
  • Encourages students to design, build, test, and iterate their own mitigation strategies.
  • Promotes empathy-driven innovation by addressing a human health issue in space.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Human factors in space – especially how microgravity affects the body.
  • Sensor accuracy and placement to get meaningful data.
  • Safety and accessibility in building the devices.
  • Iterative testing – baseline vs mitigation trials to compare designs.
  • Collaboration & roles – assigning tasks like wiring, coding, Excel setup, and design.

projectDetails.name: Desert Eye: UAE Orbital Environmental Hub
projectDetails.summary:
Our project, Desert Eye, envisions a commercial Low Earth Orbit (LEO) platform that transforms space into a driver for environmental sustainability. Designed as a UAE-led orbital hub, it combines three integrated modules: an Orbital Greenhouse that tests desert-resilient crops in microgravity to support food security; a Recycling Lab that captures and repurposes orbital debris by 3D printing to reduce space waste; and an Environmental Data Hub that monitors dust storms, coastal changes, and desertification using NASA’s open datasets (Worldview, EarthExplorer, ODPO).

Desert Eye addresses the Commercializing LEO challenge by linking sustainability, data, and innovation—creating an orbital ecosystem that benefits both Earth and space. The project demonstrates how microgravity research and debris recycling can become viable business models while contributing to UAE Vision 2071 and Net Zero 2050. By combining scientific insight with commercial scalability, Desert Eye shows how space commercialization can advance climate resilience and environmental stewardship for arid regions around the world.
projectDetails.details:
Desert Eye: UAE Orbital Environmental Hub

Desert Eye is a conceptual Low Earth Orbit (LEO) platform that turns orbital infrastructure into a sustainable business and research ecosystem. The hub integrates three connected modules: an Orbital Greenhouse for testing drought-resistant crops in microgravity; a Recycling Lab that captures and repurposes orbital debris through robotic collection and in-situ 3D printing; and an Environmental Data Hub that aggregates NASA and partner satellite data (Worldview, EarthExplorer, ODPO, Copernicus) to monitor dust storms, coastal change, and desertification across the UAE and surrounding regions.

Our prototype demonstrates how orbital assets can support food security, debris reduction, and climate intelligence simultaneously. Data from Desert Eye would flow to Earth-based dashboards for farmers, planners, and researchers, improving forecasts and sustainability decisions.

The team used Canva and PowerPoint to design and simulate system functions. The project’s creativity lies in linking environmental stewardship with orbital commercialization, showing how young innovators can align space entrepreneurship with the UAE Vision 2071 and global sustainability goals. By combining environmental data, microgravity biology, and circular-economy design, Desert Eye demonstrates a replicable model for responsible space commercialization.

projectDetails.name: BioBridge
projectDetails.summary:
Problem Statement
NASA’s space biology data (plants, rodents, microbes) is fragmented across different repositories like OSDR and Data.gov. It is difficult for educators, students, and citizen scientists to access, filter, and interpret these datasets quickly.

Solution
BioBridge is a simple, filterable knowledge engine that summarizes key space-biology experiments into kid-readable cards. Each card links directly to OSDR/Data.gov originals. A youth validator loop ensures accuracy through checkbox confirmation. A kids-friendly view makes findings fun and accessible.
projectDetails.details:
1. Problem Statement

NASA’s space biology data (plants, rodents, microbes) is fragmented across different repositories like OSDR and Data.gov. It is difficult for educators, students, and citizen scientists to access, filter, and interpret these datasets quickly.

2. Solution

BioBridge Junior is a simple, filterable knowledge engine that summarizes key space-biology experiments into kid-readable cards. Each card links directly to OSDR/Data.gov originals. A youth validator loop ensures accuracy through checkbox confirmation. A kids-friendly ‘Explain’ view makes findings fun and accessible.

3. Data and Tools

- Data Sources: OSDR portal (OSD-269, OSD-268, OSD-267, OSD-522, OSD-625, OSD-120, OSD-038, RR-23 payload) and Data.gov
- Tools: Glide (app builder), Google Sheets (data management), NASA Earthdata (optional visualization), OSDR, Data.gov

4. Technical Overview

The application includes:
- Explorer View: filterable cards of studies with summaries
- Kids View: simplified outcomes with Why it matters for Moon/Mars
- Validator Form: checkbox validation loop by youth participants
- Data Validation Screen: structured checks for metadata fields

5. Impact

BioBridge Junior makes real NASA biology datasets accessible to youth audiences, encourages STEM engagement, and provides structured datasets that can be reused by researchers and educators. It bridges NASA’s cutting-edge biology research with classroom learning worldwide.

projectDetails.name: ExoMind:AI-Powered Exoplanet Discovery!?
projectDetails.summary:
Project Idea Summary:
 our project uses artificial intelligence to analyze light curve data from NASA missions like Kepler and TESS to detect exoplanets—planets outside our solar system. When a planet passes in front of a star, it causes a small dip in the star’s brightness. Your AI model learns to recognize these patterns and predict whether a planet is present.
Goal:
 To speed up and improve the accuracy of exoplanet discovery using machine learning, helping scientists explore distant worlds more efficiently.
projectDetails.details:
Our project, ExoMind, is an AI-powered system designed to detect exoplanets by analyzing stellar light curve data from NASA missions such as Kepler and TESS. It works by identifying subtle dips in a star’s brightness—signals that may indicate a planet passing in front of the star (a transit event). We trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) using labeled datasets of confirmed exoplanet transits to recognize these patterns automatically.
The benefits of this approach include faster and more scalable exoplanet discovery, reduced reliance on manual analysis, and the potential to uncover previously missed planetary candidates. By automating the detection process, our model supports astronomers and researchers in exploring distant worlds more efficiently.
The intended impact of ExoMind is to accelerate scientific discovery in the field of astrophysics and contribute to the global effort of identifying habitable planets beyond our solar system. It also serves as an educational tool for demonstrating how AI can be applied to space science.
We developed the project using:
Programming Language: Python
Libraries: TensorFlow, Keras, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib
Platform: Google Colab / Jupyter Notebook
Optional UI: Streamlit for interactive predictions
Our project is creative in its integration of deep learning with real NASA data, and in the way it visualizes predictions through a user-friendly interface. We considered factors such as data quality, model interpretability, and accessibility—ensuring that our solution is not only technically sound but also understandable and usable by non-experts.
projectDetails.aiReferences:

projectDetails.name: ExoMinds AI
projectDetails.summary:
ExoMinds AI Summary:
ExoMinds is an AI-powered exoplanet discovery system that validates candidates from Kepler and TESS data using machine learning (LightGBM + Random Forest) combined with 8 physics-based calculations.

It not only classifies planets as confirmed, candidate, or false positive, but also evaluates habitability, including whether the planet could support liquid water, its temperature, and potential for a life-friendly environment.

Physics metrics include orbital distance (Kepler’s Law), equilibrium temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann), transit depth, habitable zone score, and other factors like signal-to-noise, impact parameter, bulk density, and transit probability.

Deployed via Gradio on Hugging Face Spaces, it provides an interactive UI for real-time exoplanet analysis with detailed reports and visualizations.
projectDetails.details:
Project Overview: ExoMinds – AI-Powered Exoplanet Discovery System

1. What does it do / How does it work?
ExoMinds is an AI-driven platform designed to validate exoplanet candidates detected by space telescopes like Kepler and TESS. It works by combining machine learning models (LightGBM and Random Forest) with astrophysics principles. For every candidate planet, it:

  • Analyzes transit signals and stellar properties.
  • Computes 8 physics-based features, including orbital distance, equilibrium temperature, transit depth, signal-to-noise ratio, habitable zone score, impact parameter, and bulk density proxy.
  • Predicts the likelihood that the candidate is a real planet or a false positive.
  • Assesses habitability potential, including the likelihood of liquid water and Earth-like conditions.
  • Generates a detailed scientific report and visualizations for each analysis.

2. Benefits:

  • Quickly validates thousands of candidates without manual calculations.
  • Reduces false positives from eclipsing binaries or stellar noise.
  • Provides a habitability assessment, helping prioritize targets for further observation.
  • Bridges machine learning and physics, making predictions more interpretable.

3. Intended Impact:
ExoMinds aims to accelerate the discovery of potentially habitable exoplanets, guide astronomers in follow-up observations, and serve as a research tool for educational and scientific purposes. By integrating AI and physics, it reduces errors and makes exoplanet research more accessible.

4. Tools, Languages, and Software Used:

  • Programming Languages: Python
    • LightGBM and scikit-learn for machine learning
    • Pandas and NumPy for data processing
    • Plotly for visualizations
    • Joblib for model serialization
    • Gradio for interactive web UI
  • Platform: Hugging Face Spaces for web deployment

5. Creativity:

  • Combines astrophysics formulas with AI models to create explainable predictions.
  • Visualizes both ML predictions and physics metrics side by side.
  • Allows real-time interactive analysis for researchers and students.
  • Habitability scoring is integrated directly into predictions.

6. Factors Considered by the Team:

  • Accuracy and reliability of ML models trained on NASA exoplanet data.
  • Physics-based validation to avoid false positives.
  • Clear UI/UX design for accessibility.
  • Interactive plots and reports for easy scientific interpretation.
  • Inclusion of habitability indicators, ensuring relevance for life-search missions.

projectDetails.details:
2025 NASA Space Apps Challenge – “Sharks From Space”

Team Members: Veer, Areg, Talha, Ali, Hayk

Challenge Overview

The team participated in NASA’s “Sharks From Space” challenge, which focused on

identifying shark foraging habitats using satellite data.

Foraging Hotspots

 The team compared sea temperature and chlorophyll abundance maps.

 Chlorophyll indicates phytoplankton-rich areas → attract zooplankton → small

fish → big fish → sharks.

 Sharks prefer warmer waters, usually near the equator.

 By combining both datasets, they found that the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans

are major shark foraging hotspots.

Why Track Sharks?

 Sharks are apex predators and help maintain balance in marine ecosystems.

 Tracking their movement helps scientists:

o Locate feeding and breeding hotspots.

o Understand ecosystem health and biodiversity.

o Measure impacts of climate change, overfishing, and habitat loss.

The Shark Tag – “SharkSense”

A smart tracking tag invented by the team to collect vital ocean data.

Features:

 Movement tracking: GPS + motion sensors.

 Temperature monitoring: Measures at different depths.

 Salinity & pressure sensors: Capture deep-ocean data satellites can’t.

Impact: Turns sharks into living ocean sensors, helping improve climate models and

marine research — supporting NASA’s Earth System Science mission.

Our Game – “Sharptrakz”

The team developed a game called Sharptrakz, inspired by their project.

It simulates shark tracking and ocean exploration.

(Download link was shared in the presentation.)

Acknowledgements

 Data and references mainly sourced from NASA satellite data.

 The project combines science, technology, and creativity to raise awareness

about ocean ecosystems and shark conservation.

challengeDetails.title: Sharks from Space
challengeDetails.excerpt: Earth’s ocean is one of the most powerful habitats in our universe, supporting a range of life that sustains ecosystems and habitability across the globe.
